incidentDescription:
I am reporting a thermal runaway fire involving an Anker PowerCore 26800 portable lithium-ion power bank, model A1277, rated at 26,800 mAh / 96.48 Wh. The SERIAL NUMBER of the battery is AFYJHX0E30581250. The power bank was purchased new in 2025 from what I believe was Best Buy in Crossgates Mall, Albany, NY.
The power bank was being used inside my parked [REDACTED] to provide power to a dash camera overnight. While the vehicle was unattended, the power bank caught fire inside the vehicles center console.
The fire caused substantial heat and fire damage in and around the center console and burned or melted nearby materials and contents. Although the visible fire damage was concentrated in the console area, smoke and residue spread throughout the enclosed passenger compartment. A noticeable film/residue was deposited on interior surfaces, creating concerns about contamination of the upholstery, carpet, headliner, HVAC system, ventilation ducts, trim, and other interior components.
 I have contacted restoration and hazardous-material cleanup companies because ordinary automotive detailing may not be sufficient for this type of incident, but CANNOT be fixed as insurance automatically deems the vehicle to be a total loss because there is no way to adequately clean the hazardous material.  We and the insurance company are unable to find anybody in any reasonable location who is willing to do the restoration.  The insurance company has totaled the car and it will be going to a salvage yard as a result.
I have preserved the damaged Anker power bank and have photographs showing the product and vehicle damage. I also have proof of purchase from Amazon. The power bank was approximately one year old at the time of the incident.
I am reporting this because a relatively new consumer lithium-ion power bank caught fire during use while supplying power to a dash camera and caused significant property damage to the vehicle. I am concerned that this may represent a product safety hazard.  [REDACTED] Insurance can supply documentation of vehicle being totaled due to defective battery/thermal runaway. (Please Let me know if the attached photos do not show and I can resend)

productDescription: XPedition 1.0 Cargo eBike purchased on October 4, 2024
incidentDescription:
I purchased a Lectric XPedition Cargo eBike in October 2024 and use it regularly to transport two children. Since the bike was purchased, the kickstand has been unstable and does not reliably support the weight of the bike during normal use.

The bike has tipped completely over on multiple occasions, and there have been additional instances when an adult was able to catch it before it fell. This creates a serious risk of injury, particularly while children are getting on or off the bike or are seated on it.

Fortunately, no one has been injured yet. However, given that the bike has already fallen completely over multiple times, I am very concerned that it is only a matter of time before someone is injured if this problem is not corrected. A large, heavy cargo e-bike falling onto a childor falling while a child is seated on ithas the potential to cause significant injury. The fact that we have avoided injury so far should not be mistaken for an indication that the product is safe.

I recently contacted Lectric to report the safety issue and request a permanent solution. The company offered to send a replacement kickstand but confirmed that the replacement is the same design as the existing kickstand and that they do not currently have another solution available.

Newer versions of the XPedition include a redesigned kickstand that appears substantially more stable and better able to support the bike. Seeing that Lectric has changed this component raises serious concerns about why owners of earlier versions have not been offered a comparable solution. 

I am reporting this because I am concerned this may be a broader product safety issue affecting other XPedition owners. The bike is designed and marketed as a cargo e-bike capable of transporting passengers, yet the kickstand on earlier versions does not adequately stabilize the bike during the ordinary process of loading and unloading. I am particularly concerned about families transporting children who may be unaware of the potential tip-over risk.

I believe this issue warrants investigation to determine whether affected XPedition bikes require a corrective action, redesigned component, or recall.

productDescription:
Product: Eureka PowerSpeed Upright Vacuum
Model: NEU280
incidentDescription:
On September 25, 2026, at approximately [REDACTED] PM, I was vacuuming underneath a couch using the hose attachment on my Eureka PowerSpeed upright vacuum, model NEU280. The vacuum was in its upright position, and the brush roller was still spinning.
While I was using the hose attachment, my 11-month-old son knocked the vacuum over. As I moved to intervene, his thumb became caught in the underside of the vacuum.
I immediately stopped and removed his hand. His thumb sustained a significant injury, with the outer layer of skin appearing to have been torn or removed. The injury initially appeared severe, and medical personnel were concerned about a possible fracture.
My son was taken for medical evaluation and underwent X-rays. The completed radiology report confirmed that there were no fractures. However, we were informed that ligament or other soft-tissue injuries may still be present and cannot necessarily be ruled out by X-rays.
The injury caused substantial damage to the skin on his thumb. Medical personnel treated the wound with ointment and a dressing.
Product Safety Hazard
The incident raises concerns about the accessibility of the underside and operating brush roller area of the vacuum when the unit is upright and in use.
The vacuum was being used with its hose attachment, while the brush roller remained in motion. When my infant son knocked the vacuum over, his thumb became caught underneath it as I moved to intervene, resulting in a significant injury.
This incident raises concerns about the potential for serious finger or hand injuries to young children who come into contact with the underside of an operating vacuum, particularly if the unit is accidentally tipped over.
I am submitting this report to document the incident and bring attention to the potential injury hazard associated with this product.
Injury and Medical Treatment
Significant skin injury to the thumb, with the outer layer of skin torn or removed.
X-rays performed following the incident.
Completed radiology report confirmed no fractures.
Possible ligament or soft-tissue injury communicated by medical personnel- extent not yet confirmed.
Wound treated with ointment and a dressing.
Supporting Documentation
The following documentation is available upon request:
Photographs of the childs injury.
Photographs of the vacuum and its underside.
Product identification and serial number.
Medical records and completed radiology report.
Additional information relevant to the incident.

productDescription: Foldable adult electric scooter with a saddle/seat. Black aluminum frame, 10 inch pneumatic tires, front and rear suspension, 500W motor, 48V battery, top speed 20 mph. Thumb throttle on the right handlebar, disc brakes front and rear, LCD display console mounted on the handlebar. Used as a commuter scooter on pavement. This particular unit was a refurbished scooter sent to me by the manufacturer as a warranty replacement rather than a new retail purchase.
model: Eclipse Ultra Electric Scooter with Saddle Attachment
incidentDescription:
The throttle on this electric scooter sticks in the engaged position. When I press the throttle and then release it, the scooter keeps applying power instead of slowing down. This has happened repeatedly, not just once.

I am an adult and I was the only person using the scooter. I was riding it normally on pavement, as a commuter scooter. It is rated for 20 mph. A throttle that does not release when the rider lets go creates a serious crash risk, especially approaching a stop or in traffic. No injury occurred. I stopped riding it as soon as I found the fault and have not used it since.

The scooter also has weak acceleration on inclines and a grinding noise from the brakes consistent with debris or misalignment in the brake pads. My main concern is that both of the systems that slow the scooter down are affected at the same time.

This unit was sent to me by the manufacturer on 9/21/2026 as a warranty replacement for an earlier scooter of theirs that had developed a hard jerking motion under throttle and braking along with a recurring E9 motor error code. The manufacturer later confirmed in writing that the replacement they sent was a refurbished unit. I was not told before it shipped that I would be receiving a refurbished scooter.

I reported the sticking throttle to the manufacturer by email on 9/23/2026. They suggested the handlebar grip might be pressing on the throttle. I adjusted the grip and it still sticks. They then directed me to purchase a replacement console myself rather than repairing or replacing the unit.

I have photographs and video of the fault and the condition of the scooter as received.

productDescription: ThermoFlask 20 oz. insulated food jars
incidentDescription:
On September 21, 2026, I used a ThermoFlask 20 oz / 591 mL insulated food jar to transport homemade chicken tortellini soup for my husband's lunch.
At approximately 5:00 a.m., I placed freshly prepared hot soup into the ThermoFlask food jar and secured the lid. At approximately 11:00 a.m., my husband opened the food jar at work and ate some of the soup. The insulated container had kept the soup warm, so the soup was not microwaved, reheated, or
otherwise heated while inside the container. After eating, my husband replaced the lid with the remaining soup still inside the jar. At approximately 5:30 p.m., after he returned home, I attempted to reopen the jar for the purpose of emptying and cleaning it.  The lid was unusually tight and I was unable to loosen it myself. My husband was lying in bed resting. He sat up and held the lower portion of the food jar while I attempted to turn the lid.

During that attempt, the container experienced a sudden and violent pressure release. The event produced a gunshot like sound. The lid and sealing components separated, and liquid soup and solid food contents were forcibly expelled from the container.  The expelled contents struck my husband and were projected across his clothing, the bed, sheets, bedding, and surrounding textiles. Photographs taken immediately afterward show liquid staining and solid food debris dispersed over a substantial area.  This was not a minor spill or leakage around the lid. The contents were forcibly expelled during
opening.  The container was being used for its ordinary intended purpose: storing and transporting hot food.
The soup contained ordinary ingredients including chicken, chicken broth, cream of chicken soup, cheese tortellini, garlic, Italian seasoning, lemon juice, parsley, water, chicken stock/bouillon, salt, and black pepper.  It contained no carbonated beverage, dry ice, yeast, or other ingredient intentionally intended to
create pressure. The food was never reheated while inside the ThermoFlask container.  

I am concerned that an unexpected pressure release of this nature could result in injury if a person's face or eyes were positioned over the container during opening, or if the contents were hotter when the release occurred.  The incident also resulted in soup and food debris being forcibly expelled onto my husband's clothing and multiple pieces of bedding.

I am reporting the incident primarily because of the product-safety hazard and potential for injury associated with the unexpected pressure release.

Product Identification
The bottom of the affected food jar is marked:
ThermoFlask 20 oz / 591 mL BPA Free Dishwasher Safe
The item was purchased as part of a two-pack from Costco.

productDescription: Google Pixel 6 smartphone, Stormy Black color, featuring a 6.4-inch display panel and a lithium-ion internal battery
incidentDescription:
I am reporting a severe product safety hazard regarding a Google Pixel 6 smartphone. The lithium-ion battery inside the device has catastrophically swollen and expanded, causing intense upward pressure that has physically split the chassis open and separated the display screen entirely from the frame of the phone.
I contacted the manufacturer (Google Support) regarding this hardware safety issue. Google Support explicitly stated in writing that their team determined a swollen battery is "not a safety concern." However, in a direct contradiction, they later explicitly instructed me that "for your safety, it is not recommended to charge or continue to use a device with a swollen battery."

productDescription:

incidentDescription:
Dear U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission:

Attached is my completed consumer product safety report concerning a Miele Guard L1
vacuum.

I am reporting that the Miele Guard L1 vacuum caught fire during use, resulting in property
damage to my home and a serious impact on my family.

Product information:

Manufacturer: Miele
Product: Miele Guard L1 – SUFEO PowerLine
Serial Number: 199264861
Material Number: 12811590
Article Number: 41UFE037
Retailer: Wayfair

Following the incident, the matter was reported to both the retailer and Miele. Wayfair
acknowledged my property-damage report.

Miele initially informed me that its Engineering department had determined that the electrical
issue originated outside the appliance and was not caused by the vacuum. However, Miele
subsequently acknowledged in writing that, because the original unit was no longer available,
it was unable to perform a full physical inspection or comprehensive evaluation and that its
assessment was necessarily limited to the submitted documentation and photographs.
I repeatedly asked Miele to identify the specific external source it believed caused the
electrical issue and to provide the technical evidence supporting that determination. I also
requested Miele’s formal position regarding the property damage. Those substantive questions
remain unanswered despite further escalation to Miele executive management and a final
written notice.

Because this incident involved a reported product fire and property damage, I am asking
CPSC to review this matter as a consumer product-safety incident and determine whether
further investigation or other appropriate action is warranted.

Please confirm receipt of this report and advise if any additional documentation or information
is required.

Thank You

Report Updated 9/30/26:
Based on what I personally observed, the Miele Guard L1 vacuum was operating when the fire began, and the fire appeared to originate in or at the vacuum. I am reporting the vacuum as the product involved and the apparent source of the fire. I do not have an independent forensic fire-cause determination, and the original unit was not available for a physical inspection.

brand: Vistefly V15 Pro Max cordless vacuum
incidentDescription:
On September 15, 2026, at approximately 5:30 p.m., a rechargeable battery supplied with a Vistefly V15 Pro Max cordless vacuum caught fire inside my home while it was charging. The battery was connected to the charger that came with the vacuum, and the charger was plugged into a wall outlet. We used the vacuum almost every day. I did not observe or report any modification to the battery, vacuum, or charger before the incident.
My daughters, ages 11 and 5, were sitting at the dinner table near the charging area. They called to me that there was smoke, and my older daughter then yelled that there was a fire. I immediately told both children to leave the area and the cords, battery, and other things close to the fire were thrown outside onto a concrete deck and I used a fire extinguisher to put out the fire. We were preparing to leave for a [REDACTED] karate class, so if we had already left, the fire could have continued unnoticed with our pets inside the home.
The fire and resulting smoke or heat damaged another [REDACTED] handheld vacuum, a pair of shoes, and a wooden dog bowl holder. The house had a strong, unpleasant odor and fumes after the battery fire, and fire-extinguisher residue covered the immediate area on the deck. No one sustained a reported physical injury, but the event created an immediate risk of burns, smoke exposure, serious injury, death, and a larger residential fire.
The burned battery was moved outside and placed in a bucket of cold water to help cool down the lithium ion battery. I retained the charger supplied with the vacuum. I contacted Amazon on September 16, 2026, identified the product, seller, purchase date, and order number, and explained that the battery had caught fire while charging and caused collateral damage. Amazon stated that the item issue was escalated and that an A-to-Z Guarantee refund request for $139.09 had been submitted. I am reporting this incident so the product and battery can be investigated and other consumers can be warned if a broader hazard exists.
Product Identification
Brand and model as listed in order: Vistefly V15 Pro Max cordless vacuum
Component involved: Rechargeable lithium-ion battery supplied with the vacuum
Charger: Original charger supplied with the vacuum
Retail channel: Amazon
Third-party seller: weilan tech

manufacturer: Shenzhen Yizhifangzhou Technology Co., Ltd dba VIBOFROST
incidentDescription:
I purchased a VIBOFROST countertop nugget ice maker, model VFI001, through Amazon on March 15, 2026. The Amazon order identifies the seller as LCY OFFICIAL. The product is designed to produce nugget/pellet ice for human consumption.

During normal household use, I discovered multiple small black plastic-like shavings/fragments in the ice produced by the machine. Some of the fragments were visibly embedded in or adhered to pieces of ice as they melted. The fragments include thin, curved/shaved pieces as well as smaller particles. I have photographs documenting multiple pieces of this foreign material in and among ice produced by the machine.

I am concerned that an internal component of the ice maker may be wearing, scraping, or otherwise shedding material during operation and that the resulting fragments are being dispensed with ice intended for human consumption. A consumer could potentially ingest these fragments without noticing them.

I stopped using the ice maker after discovering the foreign material. I have preserved the machine and photographic evidence of the fragments. The product label identifies the product as VIBOFROST model VFI001 and states a manufacture date of December 29, 2025.

I contacted Amazon Customer Service and specifically reported that the ice maker was dispensing visible plastic-like shavings/fragments into ice intended for human consumption and that I considered this a potential ingestion/product-safety hazard. I requested a refund and requested escalation of the safety issue. Amazon declined to provide a refund because the return window had expired. The representative also told me there was no one to whom the issue could be escalated and ultimately directed me to contact the manufacturer.

The products written materials state that VIBOFROST provides a 12-month product and labor warranty from the date of original purchase. I purchased this unit approximately six months ago and therefore discovered this issue during the stated warranty period.

I am submitting this report because I am concerned that the defect may not be unique to my unit and that other consumers using this model could unknowingly ingest foreign material in their ice. I believe the product should be evaluated to determine what component is shedding or being shaved during operation and whether other VIBOFROST VFI001 units present the same potential ingestion hazard.

incidentDescription:
1. What happened?

I purchased this hair dryer brush on Amazon US (Order ID: [REDACTED}, ASIN: B0DZ2DYF9N, Color: Black + Gold). It was delivered on August 25, 2026.

On August 30, 2026, I used it at my home in the United States. I found that the plug is a standard plug without the required GFCI (Test/Reset) protection. When I turned it on, all the lights in the room went out immediately. This indicates a serious risk of electric shock or fire.

The product is sold on Amazon US and is non-compliant with U.S. electrical safety requirements.

2. What type of product was used?

An electrical hair dryer brush (hair styling appliance).

ASIN: B0DZ2DYF9N

Color: Black + Gold

Intended Use: Hair drying and styling

3. Who was using the product?

I was using the product. I am an adult consumer.

4. How was the product being used?

I plugged it into a wall outlet at my home and turned it on. It immediately caused the room lights to go out.

5. Was there an injury, or could an injury have occurred?

No injury occurred, but there was a serious risk of electric shock and fire.

The product lacks required GFCI protection. When turned on, it caused the room's electrical system to trip. If used near water or if the outlet had not tripped, it could have caused electric shock or fire.

6. How did the injury happen?

No actual injury happened. But the incident created a dangerous situation:

The product was plugged in and turned on.

The room lights went out immediately.

productDescription: Hammacher Schlemmer best automatic cordless tire inflator 2023
incidentDescription:
My wife bought me a Hammacher Schlemmer automatic cordless tire inflator 2023 three years ago for a Father's Day present. I have photos. I have used it a dozen times over 3 years, and always kept it in my trunk. This is a safe, dry area just like the instructions say to do.

On 8/23/26 I used it on my outdoor driveway for 3 minutes to inflate my tires, and smoke started poring out the front side vents. The fire was coming from the display, which is now useless. The unit still smells of smoke. I pulled the Lithium Ion battery out of the base to stop the current flow into the unit. It continued to smoke for a few more minutes, before the fire went out on its own. 

Fortunately, I did not get hurt. I was able to disconnect the batteries from the unit before the fire spread beyond the display.

productDescription: Onewheel Pint S with a navy blue fender. Max weight 250 lbs. Max Speed: 20 mph.
incidentDescription:
On 8/31/26, my 13 year old son was riding his Onewheel Pint S that was purchased back in October 2025. He was riding it in a neighborhood, going straight, not swerving or going over any bumps. He was at a speed of about 15-18 miles.  Suddenly, the Onewheel locked up and dropped it's nose. It completely stopped at a high speed and launched him off the Onewheel onto the concreate.  

He had many road rash scrapes and cutes.  He luckily had his helmet fastened tight. It was very scratched up.  He had deep cuts/road rash along his left shoulder, left elbow, left hip, tops of both hands, tops of both knees, and the left elbow.  I took him to urgent care for evaluation. He had x-rays of his left shoulder and right pinkie.  His injuries were cleaned and bandaged. No concussion. 

The next day we had to go back to urgent care to get his left arm splinted because the x-rays showed that there might potentially be a fracture.  The following we day we went to an orthopedist. Took x-rays of his left elbow and shoulder, which was still hurting.  He was evaluated and luckily, no fractures. 

This could have been much worse had he been flung in front of an oncoming car and also his injuries could have been even more severe.  This product should not instantly stop at a high speed without any provocation from the rider.

I am requesting that the incident be formally documented and investigated, including whether the product or charging system had a defect or safety issue that contributed to the fire and explosion.

productDescription: Samsung 28 cu. ft. Family Hub 4-Door French Door Refrigerator with in-door ice maker and through-the-door ice/water dispenser, stainless steel finish. Free-standing residential refrigerator, approximately 36 inches wide and 70 inches tall. Model RF28NHEDBSR/AA. The defective component is the in-door ice maker assembly and its ice room housing, which feeds the exterior dispenser on the left-hand French door.
incidentDescription:
Samsung 28 cu. ft. Family Hub 4-Door French Door refrigerator, model RF28NHEDBSR/AA, serial 0A3K43BKA00371A. Purchased new from Home Depot in December 2018. Used normally in the kitchen of a private residence by adult members of the household.

THE DEFECT: The in-door ice maker repeatedly freezes over. The ice room frosts and fills with a solid mass of ice, the ice bucket seizes in place and cannot be removed, and the auger jams. When the dispenser is used in this condition, it discharges liquid water instead of ice, without warning, onto the person standing at the dispenser and onto the floor below.

THE HAZARD: Water pools on a hard kitchen floor directly in front of the refrigerator, in the exact spot where a person stands to use the dispenser. A member of my household has slipped on water discharged by this dispenser. No medical treatment was required. The hazard recurs continuously because the underlying defect has never been corrected. Guests and family members, including older adults, use this dispenser without any warning that it may discharge water instead of ice.

MANUFACTURER KNOWLEDGE: Samsung has documented this exact failure mode in its own [REDACTED], which states that the ice room housing allows warm, humid air to leak into the compartment, causing condensation and heavy ice formation.

REPAIR HISTORY - ALL FAILED: I contacted Samsung support on at least three separate occasions. Samsung performed service under [REDACTED], repair completed July 11, 2022. I separately hired an independent appliance technician at my own expense. In August and September 2026, having exhausted Samsung's channels, I purchased and installed genuine Samsung OEM replacement parts myself: ice maker assembly DA97-15217B and ice bucket DA97-14474C. The defect returned after every one of these repairs.

The manufacturer's warranty expired December 31, 2019, but the defect was present and known to Samsung before that date. Samsung has not offered a permanent remedy, a replacement, or a refund.

productDescription: SKIL 40V PWRCORE 40 5.0Ah Lithium-Ion Battery, model BY8708-00 (subject to Chervon North America's December 19, 2024 recall for fire/burn hazard)
incidentDescription:
The battery was on its charger in my garage when I heard a small "pop," immediately followed by fire shooting from the unit. I used a fire extinguisher on it, which appeared to extinguish the fire, but it reignited 3 or 4 additional times before I was able to fully submerge it in a bucket of water, where it has remained for over 48 hours as a precaution against re-ignition.

The battery and associated charger were destroyed by direct flame exposure. A nearby PVC electrical outlet box sustained scorching, soot and melting on its front surface. The receptacles and face plate are being replaced, and the wiring will be inspected and replaced as well, if warranted. This has not yet been done. Approximately half of a fire extinguisher was discharged to bring the fire under control. 

No injuries occurred, My hair/beard were singed while using the extinguisher, but no burns or medical treatment were needed.

I do not have a retained purchase receipt. The battery has remained fully submerged in water since the incident as a precaution against re-ignition, and I do not intend to remove it from the water to inspect the nameplate. I'm not able to provide the serial number/date code as a result.

I am also contacting Chervon directly to request a replacement battery and charger under the active recall.

productDescription:

The product is designed as a reusable insulated drinking bottle for cold beverages. The bottom of the bottle is marked Owala, 24 OZ, 710 mL, Hand Wash Cup, Dishwasher Safe Lid, Do Not Microwave, Do Not Freeze.
The bottle was received as a birthday gift approximately six months before the incident. The bottom base of the bottle has begun separating from the main stainless steel body. The separation has created a gap and a sharp exposed metal edge.
incidentDescription:
The product is an Owala stainless steel insulated water bottle that was received as a birthday gift approximately six months ago. The bottle was used normally as a reusable water bottle and was not subjected to unusual or improper use.
During normal use, the bottom base of the bottle began separating from the main body of the bottle. The separation created a gap around the bottom edge and exposed a sharp metal edge.
My 7 year old child was handling the bottle during normal use when their finger came into contact with the sharp exposed area created by the separation. The sharp edge cut their finger.
The bottle has some cosmetic scratches from normal use. However, the concern being reported is not cosmetic wear. The concern is that the bottom portion of the bottle physically separated from the body of the bottle and created a sharp exposed edge that caused an injury.
The bottle was only approximately six months old when this occurred. There was no known accident, drop, or unusual event that would explain the bottom of the bottle separating in this manner.
I contacted Owala and submitted a warranty claim with photographs showing the separation. Owala denied the warranty claim and stated that their warranty does not cover normal wear and tear, accidents, or non standard use or care.

productDescription: Concord 27.5" Step-Thru Electric Bike, 36V, Class 2, Aluminum, White
incidentDescription:
I was riding this Concord 27.5" step-thru electric bicycle on a flat,
dry, paved road under normal conditions. I applied the front brake
with normal, moderate lever pressure for a routine stop. I was not
braking hard and was not attempting a sudden stop.

The front wheel locked. I was thrown forward over the handlebars onto
the pavement.

I am not able to say what happened mechanically, and I am not going to
guess at it. What I can report is what I did and what I found when I
got up:

  - I applied normal brake pressure and the front wheel locked.
  - The front fork legs are splayed apart.
  - The front brake caliper is completely detached and is no longer in
    position on the rotor.
  - The front brake rotor is warped.
  - The front rim and tire are undamaged.

I would ask that the sequence be established by inspection rather than
by my assumption. I would note only that going over the handlebars
does not normally splay a fork apart.

I sustained a badly sprained toe, a right arm that was immobile for
approximately two days, and abrasions to my knee and inner leg. I did
not require emergency treatment. The bicycle is a total loss and
cannot be safely returned to service.

The bicycle was approximately five and a half months old. It had been
ridden only on paved roads, had never been crashed or modified, and
had shown no prior braking problems. The braking system is a
mechanical disc brake, front and rear.

I purchased this bicycle already assembled by Walmart. I did not
assemble it and have never adjusted or serviced the brakes.

I have preserved the bicycle in its post-crash condition, without any
repair or disassembly, so the front brake caliper, rotor, and caliper
mounting hardware can be inspected in the failed state.

I am reporting this because a front brake that locks the wheel
completely under normal, moderate lever pressure presents a serious
crash and injury hazard, and because comparable mechanical disc brake
caliper failures on other e-bike brands have resulted in formal
recalls.

incidentDescription:
On August 21, 2026, an Anker Laptop Power Bank (25,000mAh, 165W), model A1695, serial number 20PCN66F09100111, began smoking and ignited while it was being recharged.

The power bank was sitting on a flat, hard table and was being recharged using an Anker A2345 charger. It was not connected to any other device and was not under load. I was the owner and sole user of the product. It was being used as intended, indoors, at normal room temperature. The unit had not been dropped, damaged, exposed to water, or modified.

I noticed smoke coming from the unit and the unit then ignited. I extinguished it with a Fire Gone Fire Extinguisher Spray Suppressant. There were no injuries and no damage to anything other than the power bank itself.

I want to note the circumstances of detection. I only saw the smoke because I happened to be standing at an angle where the unit was in my line of sight. There was no audible alarm and no odor reached me before I saw the smoke. Had I been in another room or asleep, the failure would have continued undetected on a table indoors. No one was injured, but the potential for a structure fire and for injury was present.

I checked the serial number against Anker's published recall lookup tool and it returned no match. Model A1695 does not appear in any Anker recall to date.

I still have the failed unit. It is stored safely and has been photographed. I am willing to make it available for inspection.

incidentDescription:
I was using a Wyssay 75W USB Power Adapter/desktop charging station, model XLD-75W01A, purchased through Amazon. The charging station was plugged into an electrical outlet on my bedside table and had been in regular use for approximately two years without any previous problems.

During the night, my [REDACTED] was connected to the USB-C/PD fast-charging port using a charging cable. My phone's battery had been completely depleted when I connected it, and it had been charging for several hours.

I woke during the night and noticed a strong electrical/burning smell. My husband and I initially could not determine where the smell was coming from and walked through the house trying to locate the source. I eventually determined that the smell was coming from the charging station beside the bed.

Upon inspection, the USB-C/PD charging port had severely overheated. The interior of the port and surrounding material had melted and charred, and the connector on the charging cable was also heat-damaged. I immediately disconnected the charging station and have not used it since.

There were no injuries and, fortunately, the incident was discovered before a fire occurred. I am reporting this because I am concerned that the degree of overheating and melting presents a potential fire hazard, particularly because this type of charging station may be used overnight or while unattended. I have photographs showing the damaged charging port, damaged cable, and the manufacturer's label on the unit.

productDescription: EKX T1 electric bicycle, also called an e-bike. Adult electric bicycle with a rear hub motor driven through a 9-pin connector, a throttle, an LCD display presenting fault codes and parameter settings labeled P-00 through P-20, and brake levers with brake-cutoff sensors that disable motor power when a brake is applied. It shipped approximately three-quarters assembled. The front wheel and brackets required buyer assembly. No instruction manual, assembly instructions, warranty documentation, or manufacturer contact information were included in the box. Purchased new online in November 2024 for 854.09 US dollars.
manufacturer: Dongguan Xingji Outdoor Sports Goods Co., Ltd. dba EKX
incidentDescription:
I am reporting an electric bicycle (e-bike) that developed a brake and drive-system failure and was sold with no safety or operating documentation.

PRODUCT: EKX T1 electric bicycle, purchased new from an online retailer in November 2024.

WHO WAS USING IT: I am the owner and sole rider, an adult.

HOW IT WAS USED: Normal recreational and commuting riding on paved streets and paths. No off-road jumping. No modifications other than the attempted repair described below.

WHAT HAPPENED:

1. The rear brake stopped fully disengaging. Because the brake-cutoff circuit remained engaged, the throttle would not engage. A rear brake that does not fully release on a motorized bicycle causes brake drag, heat buildup, and unpredictable stopping behavior. I purchased and installed replacement brake levers to try to correct it. The condition persisted.

2. The rear hub-motor 9-pin connector, the controller, and the display all failed. The bicycle has been inoperable since approximately mid-2025.

3. The bicycle shipped with no instruction manual, no assembly instructions, no warranty documentation, and no manufacturer contact information. It arrived roughly three-quarters assembled. The display presents fault codes and parameter settings ranging from P-00 to P-20. Without a manual I had no way to interpret fault codes, verify speed limiting, or confirm safe operating parameters.

INJURIES: None occurred. The bicycle became inoperable before the brake condition caused a crash. The hazard is that a brake that does not fully release, combined with an unreadable fault-code system and no operating manual, could cause loss of control at speed.

OTHER OWNERS OF THE SAME MODEL REPORT THE SAME PROBLEMS. Two archived public discussions:

[REDACTED] (posted May 30, 2024) - multiple EKX T1 owners report receiving the bike with no instruction manual and no build instructions in the box, report error codes, and report no response from the company. Owners emailed the manual to one another because no official source existed.

[REDACTED] (posted October 25, 2024) - an EKX T1 owner reports a rear-drive clutch failure. The manufacturer shipped a replacement clutch whose shaft was warped, requiring a complete motor assembly. The same owner reports the manufacturer's U.S. website was offline because the hosting bill was unpaid, and that his open warranty case went unanswered for 23 days.

MANUFACTURER AVAILABILITY: The manufacturer's U.S. website was publicly reported offline for non-payment approximately two weeks before I purchased this bicycle. No manufacturer contact information was supplied with the product. To reach anyone connected to the brand I was eventually routed to an unrelated third-party seller. There is no functioning channel through which owners of this model could be notified of a defect or a recall.

I still have the bicycle.

incidentDescription:
I purchased a VOLPAM SP01 electric scooter (500W motor) in October 2025 for use as a personal commuting vehicle. Within months of normal adult use on paved roads, the motor developed a defect  producing loud irregular noises during acceleration and braking and losing the ability to reach or maintain speed. The scooter lost propulsion suddenly while in use on a public road. I was fortunate that no vehicle was immediately behind me at the time, as an abrupt loss of speed on a road with active traffic could have resulted in a serious collision.
I initiated a warranty claim with the seller (VOLPAM Direct, an Amazon third-party seller). After months of back-and-forth, the seller issued a prepaid return label and I shipped the scooter back in June 2026 in its original packaging for repair. The seller held the scooter for approximately two months with no clear repair timeline. Upon my request for a refund, the scooter was shipped back in August 2026.
When it arrived, the scooter was improperly packaged and sustained shipping damage. More critically, an internal wire was found severed  creating a serious electrical hazard on a 500W lithium battery-powered vehicle. When I reported this to the seller, they offered to ship replacement wires and $10 in compensation, expecting me to perform electrical repairs on a high-voltage scooter myself.
No physical injuries occurred, however the combination of sudden propulsion loss in traffic and a severed internal wire on a high-wattage electric scooter poses a significant risk of electric shock, fire, battery failure, or traffic collision to any consumer who uses or attempts to repair this product.

productDescription: The product is a Bromic Platinum 500 Series 39,800 BTU Mounted Outdoor Gas Heater.
productType: Gas or Lp Heaters, Other or Not Specified (392)
model: Bromic Platinum 500 Series 39,800 BTU Gas Heater
incidentDescription:
I have 2 Bromic Platinum 500 Series, 39,800 BTU Mounted Outdoor Gas Heaters on my screened porch.  Earlier this summer, one of the heaters caught on fire.  The Fire Department came to our house.  Fortunately, we were able to put the fire out with minimal damage because we were in the room when the fire started and we were able to act very quickly to stop the fire.  If we had not been in the room, my entire house could have gone up in flames because there was a hole in the RUBBER gas tube inside the heating unit which had a hole burned in it - and the open gas line was feeding a fire shooting flames out of the back of the unit.  If not caught immediately, the fire could have been even worse because the product uses an electrical switch to start - and the electric line was very close to the open fire (which could have also ignited an electrical fire).

Fortunately, we were in the room and quickly put our the fire, so there we no injuries.

A few weeks after the fire, we had the original gas professional installer take a look at both the product that started the fire as well as the other Bromic gas heater in the room.  The installer said that the second heater was also damaged and would have soon also caught on fire.  Clearly the heater is defective and if not remediated could burn down someone's home.

manufacturer: LIFESMART PRODUCTS / SOURCE NETWORK SALES AND MARKETING, INC
incidentDescription:
I am reporting a potential electrical/fire hazard involving a LifeSmart HT1109UV infrared heater manufactured/distributed by Supply Chain Sources LLC.

I purchased the heater from Menards in approximately September 2023. During normal household use, while the heater was plugged directly into a wall outlet, I observed sparking at the outlet. After unplugging the heater, I found visible scorching/damage to the wall receptacle. I immediately discontinued use of the heater and have not used it since. I did not observe any visible melting, scorching, or other damage to the heater's plug itself.

The heater had been plugged directly into the wall outlet and was not being used with an extension cord, power strip, surge protector, or timer.

I subsequently reviewed the owner's manual. The manual states that if heat, smoke, or signs of melting are detected at the contact point of the wall outlet, the consumer should stop using the heater immediately, contact warranty support, and have the outlet inspected/replaced by a certified electrician.

I reported the incident to Supply Chain Sources/LifeSmart and provided photographs and supporting information. The company confirmed in writing that my report was received, documented, and forwarded through its internal channels for review. The company stated that it did not require the heater to be returned or retained for further review and advised that I could dispose of it. The company declined replacement or other compensation because the heater is outside its one-year manufacturer's warranty.

No one was injured and there was no structure fire. I am reporting the incident because the sparking and visible scorching of the electrical outlet concerned me as a potential fire and electrical safety hazard.

incidentDescription:
I purchased a Nurecover steam sauna in November 2023 for home use. The unit includes a water-heating kettle that sits outside the sauna enclosure and delivers steam through a tube. In 2024 the water kettle was leaking steam through the top so I was sent a replacement.
In July 2026 the unit failed. The plastic housing surrounding the control panel and digital display of the water-heating kettle had visibly melted and scorched. The deformation and charring are consistent with sustained overheating at the control assembly rather than normal wear. The unit gave no fault indication, alarm, or automatic shutoff before the damage occurred, I discovered it visually when I went to use it. I always used this product exactly as described in the instructions. I always turned it off and unplugged it immediately after a 20 minute usage as I exited. There were no injuries involved in the malfunction.
I reported the failure to Nurecover on July 16, 2026, describing it explicitly as a possible safety concern and including photographs. In the company's reply, and in every subsequent message over the following four weeks, no acknowledgment of the safety issue was made. The response addressed only warranty status and replacement logistics. The company informed me the model has been discontinued, but did not state whether the discontinuation was related to any defect.
Because the company indicated a replacement would be sent, I disposed of the defective unit and no longer have it. I retain photographs of the melted housing and the complete email correspondence. They wasted weeks of my time with bad communication, and insisted that I pay for the replacement since the failure came after the warranty date. I ended up paying for a replacement, and they sent me a different unit that does not have the proper tube size for the sauna model I have. Now they won't pay for the return shipping needed to cover for their incompetence. I am reporting this so the failure is on record, and others can make more informed decisions regarding doing business with this company.
My concern is the fire risk, compounded by the absence of any fail-safe. This is a mains powered heating appliance that operates unattended on a floor surface for the duration of a session. Enough heat was generated at the control housing to melt and char plastic. Nothing shut the unit down or indicated a fault.

productDescription: Samsung Bespoke AI 22 cu. ft. Counter Depth 4-Door French Door Refrigerator with Zero Clearance Fit, Food Showcase Door, Dual Auto Ice Maker with Sphere Ice, in White Glass. The reported issue involves the Sphere Ice produced by the refrigerator's ice-making system.
incidentDescription:
I purchased a Samsung Bespoke refrigerator in December 2025. Approximately four months later, I discovered visible white solid particles remaining after the refrigerator's whiskey ice melted. The particles did not dissolve in the melted water and did not dissolve when rubbed or warmed in my hand.

I contacted Samsung and was initially advised to replace the water filter. I replaced the filter, reset the ice maker, and flushed the system several times. In July 2026, I checked the whiskey ice again and found the same white, non-dissolving particles.

I contacted Samsung again and requested an inspection. During the service visit, a Samsung-authorized technician melted the ice and personally observed the white solid particles remaining in the water. The technician also handled the particles and confirmed that they did not simply dissolve in his hand. Samsung then authorized replacement of the relevant ice-making component.

After the component was replaced, the white particles no longer appeared in the ice.

I do not know the chemical composition of the particles and am not claiming that they were toxic. However, this ice was intended for human consumption, and my family had consumed ice produced by this refrigerator for several months before the source of the unidentified material was corrected. I am reporting this as a potential product safety issue because unidentified, non-dissolving material appeared to be entering consumable ice from an internal refrigerator/ice-making component.

I have photographs showing the particles, although I no longer have a physical sample.

incidentDescription:
Using  Cuisinart WMR-CAP2 Classic Round Waffle Maker at home.

After making waffles, I unplugged the unit and lifted it by its factory-installed handle, using a potholder because the handle was hot from normal operation. While carrying the appliance across my kitchen, the handle suddenly detached, causing the hot waffle maker to fall onto a tile floor. The fall caused a small cosmetic dent in the appliance.

After examining the handle, I found that both molded plastic screw bosses that secure the handle had fractured around the attachment screws. The screws themselves remained intact, indicating that the handle detached because the plastic attachment points failed rather than because the screws loosened.

I had used the waffle maker approximately 15 times and had not noticed any looseness or other warning signs before this incident.

Fortunately, no one was injured. However, the failure created a significant potential hazard because the user is expected to lift and move the hot appliance by its handle. The sudden loss of the handle could have resulted in burns from contact with the hot appliance or hot cooking surfaces, impact injuries from the falling appliance, or damage to nearby people or property. I am reporting this incident because I believe failure of the load-bearing handle during normal use presents a potential product safety hazard.

productDescription:
Product Description: Cosori TurboBlaze 6.0-Quart Air Fryer

Model Number: CAF-DC601-KUS
Date of Incident: August 14th 2026

Description of Hazard:
While operating the air fryer, the appliance completed its normal cooking cycle. I removed the basket to retrieve the food. Approximately five minutes later, the unit experienced a catastrophic safety failure. The control panel displayed error code "E01" (indicating an internal temperature sensor/thermistor failure). 

Instead of shutting down safely upon detecting this sensor error, the appliance experienced a runaway heating event. The internal heating coils turned red hot while unattended, and the unit began pumping out large volumes of thick smoke accompanied by a heavy, burning plastic smell as internal components melted. 

This occurred while the basket was completely removed from the unit. The appliance failed to cut power to the heating element despite the cycle being finished and a critical sensor error occurring. I had to manually pull the power plug to stop the thermal runaway. This is a severe fire hazard that nearly resulted in a house fire and could have caused serious injury or death had I left the kitchen. 

Immediate federal investigation is requested to determine if this model requires a safety recall.
[REDACTED]

productDescription: Samsung residential French-door refrigerator with a built-in automatic ice maker and through-the-door ice and water dispenser. The dispenser allows the user to select different ice settings, including  Cubed Ice. The safety concern involves the ice-making dispensing system while the refrigerator is specifically set to dispense cubed ice.
model: Samsung refrigerator model RF28R7201SR Full model
incidentDescription:
I am reporting a safety concern involving a Samsung refrigerator with an ice dispenser that creates and ejects sharp, irregular pieces of ice while the refrigerator is specifically set to dispense Cubed Ice.

When Cubed Ice is selected, the dispenser does not consistently dispense ordinary ice cubes. It repeatedly produces a mixture of cubes, crushed ice, and sharp, jagged ice fragments. These fragments can eject from the dispenser with enough force to miss the drinking glass and land on the surrounding floor. This has occurred repeatedly during normal use of the refrigerator.

The problem creates multiple safety concerns. Sharp ice fragments can unexpectedly enter a drinking glass, creating a potential choking or oral-injury hazard. Other pieces eject outside the glass and fall onto the floor, creating a potential slip-and-fall hazard. This is particularly concerning in a household where a child may use or be near the refrigerator. My granddaughter is not tall enough to position her hand around the top of a glass in an attempt to contain the fragments.

I have personally resorted to placing my hand around the top of the glass while dispensing ice in an effort to prevent the fragments from flying out. Even with this precaution, pieces can escape and land on the floor. I have photographs documenting the irregular and jagged ice fragments produced while the refrigerator is set to Cubed Ice, including pieces that have landed on the floor.

I reported this problem to Samsung. On July 24, 2026, I participated in a live video support session with a Samsung representative. During that session, I demonstrated the refrigerator and ice dispenser in real time. The representative was able to observe the condition directly through the video call. Despite observing the dispenser's operation, I was told that what was occurring was normal and that the matter would be escalated to management.

I subsequently escalated the safety concern to Samsung and specifically explained the potential choking, oral-injury, and slip-and-fall hazards. Samsung's Extra Care representative acknowledged in writing the safety issues I described, including the potential slip hazard from ice accumulating on the floor and my concern regarding sharp ice fragments being dispensed while the unit is set to Cubed Ice.

Nevertheless, Samsung declined to provide a no-cost inspection or repair because the refrigerator is outside the manufacturer's warranty and instead offered to arrange a service appointment at my expense.

My concern is not simply that an older appliance requires repair. My concern is that a refrigerator being operated normally and specifically set to dispense Cubed Ice repeatedly produces and ejects sharp, irregular ice fragments, that Samsung observed the condition through live video support, and that Samsung subsequently acknowledged the reported safety concerns while declining to inspect or correct the condition without charge because of warranty status.

I am submitting this report so that the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission can document and evaluate this potential product safety hazard and determine whether similar incidents or complaints involving Samsung refrigerator ice-dispensing systems have been reported.

Photographs documenting the ice fragments and relevant written communications with Samsung are available and can be provided with this report.

incidentDescription:
Incident involving Instant Pot Viva 80 8-quart pressure cooker

I am reporting a potentially serious pressure-release incident involving an Instant Pot Viva 80, 8-quart electric pressure cooker, rated 1200 W with an 80 kPa working pressure.

During the last several uses, I noticed that the weighted steam-release valve was becoming unreliable about sealing. On the day of the incident, the valve initially would not seal while the cooker was coming to pressure. I adjusted/repositioned the weighted steam-release valve until it seated and the cooker subsequently pressurized normally.

Approximately 20 minutes later, while the cooker was operating under pressure, we heard a loud bang from another part of the house. When we entered the kitchen, a substantial quantity of chicken broth had been violently expelled from the cooker. Broth had sprayed high enough to reach the ceiling and was dripping from the ceiling, walls, and covering/flooding portions of the countertops and floor.

The weighted steam-release valve remained attached to the lid following the incident.

The cooker was not overfilled. I routinely clean the steam-release valve, steam-release passages and associated lid components after use, and the vent passages were clean.

There was also a potentially relevant symptom during the previous use of the cooker. I heard an unusual series of rapid repetitive clicking sounds from the appliance. I am familiar with the occasional clicking the cooker normally makes as the heating system cycles, but this was noticeably different and consisted of repeated rapid clicking ("click-click-click-clickidy-click-click") for a period of time.  It almost sounded musical.

I do not know whether the steam-release valve itself failed, whether the cooker experienced an abnormal pressure-control condition, or whether another component malfunctioned. I am reporting the observations rather than attempting to determine the cause.

Because of the force of the discharge and the amount of hot liquid expelled, I believe this could have caused serious burns had someone been standing near the cooker at the time.

I have discontinued use of the appliance and retained the cooker, lid, steam-release valve and other components in their post-incident condition. I can provide photographs of the appliance, model/data label, lid and components and additional information if needed.

Model: Viva 80
Capacity: 8 quart
Power: 1200 W
Working pressure: 80 kPa
Manufacturer/brand: Instant Pot

I have stopped using the heater. I still have the heater and power cord, my Amazon purchase information, the product listing information, and photographs of the injury available if CPSC needs additional information or wishes to examine the product.

I am reporting this incident because the product caused an actual burn injury during brief accidental contact while the heater was operating normally, and I am concerned that it could pose a burn hazard to other consumers.

productDescription: Oster Pro Series countertop blender with touchscreen controls and high-performance motor. Black blender base with preset blending programs, including a "Smoothie" mode. Product includes the personal/individual-size blending cup ("[REDACTED]" cup) with threaded blade assembly attachment. The incident occurred while using the personal blending cup attachment in Smoothie mode.
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription:
Urgent safety concern,  serious injury involving Oster Pro Series Blender.

I am writing to report a serious safety incident involving my Oster Pro Series Blender that resulted in a severe hand injury requiring emergency medical treatment.

On the morning of Wednesday, July 29, I was preparing a smoothie using the individual-sized blending cup attachment. I assembled the blender by attaching the blade assembly to the cup and securing the cup to the blender base in accordance with normal operation. I then selected the "Smoothie" preset and pressed the Start button.

Shortly after the blender began operating, the base started vibrating and shaking violently. The vibration became strong enough that the blender began moving across my countertop. I immediately reached toward the blender to turn it off.

As I did so, the blending cup suddenly detached from the blender and was propelled across the room along with its contents. The rotating blades were exposed, and my fingers came into contact with them, causing deep lacerations.

I was transported to the emergency room, where the injuries required stitches. My treating providers have advised that I will likely require physical therapy after the stitches are removed to help restore function to my fingers.

After returning home, I examined the blender. I observed that although the blade assembly appeared to remain threaded onto the cup, the cutter blade and the silicone sealing gasket were tilted upward on one side rather than sitting evenly. 

I also observed that during operation of the "Smoothie" preset, the blender repeatedly starts and stops while the personal blending cup rotates alternately in opposite directions. I do not know whether this operating sequence contributed to the detachment, but I believe the circumstances should be reviewed and investigated.

I have preserved the blender and all of its components in their current condition. I also have:

Photographs of my injuries.
Photographs of the blender and blade assembly after the incident.
Security camera video capturing the incident.
Medical records documenting my emergency treatment.

Please advise how you would like me to provide these materials and whether you would like the blender made available for inspection. I also request that this incident be documented as a product safety complaint and investigated by the appropriate department.

Given the seriousness of my injuries, I would appreciate a prompt response outlining the next steps in your investigation and claims process.

Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to your response.

productDescription: Casely Power Pods, Model Number E33A
incidentDescription:
I am writing regarding my Casely Wireless Portable Power Bank (Model E33A), which I have since learned was subject to a recall due to the risk of fire.

I was completely unaware that this product had been recalled. Given the severity of the known fire hazard, I am shocked and extremely disappointed that I never received any direct written notification warning me to stop using the product.

On the evening of Saturday August 1, 2026, I was sitting on my sectional sofa using my Casely Wireless Portable Power Bank with my Casely phone case to charge my phone as intended. Without any warning, the power bank suddenly burst into flames while it was beside me. I immediately threw it away from myself to prevent further injury. The burning power bank landed on the sofa and surrounding furnishings, igniting nearby materials. Within seconds, our smoke alarms activated, and I was screaming for help while my husband ran into the room to extinguish the fire. Our child and our three dogs were in the home and were understandably terrified by the incident.

The power bank was being used exactly as Casely designed and marketed it to be used, in conjunction with a Casely phone case for wireless charging. This was ordinary, intended use of the product. I had no reason to believe it posed an imminent fire hazard because I had never received any direct notice of the recall.

As a direct result of this incident:

My husband sustained burns to his foot while extinguishing the fire.
My clothing was burned and ruined.
Our sectional sofa sustained significant burn damage.
Our area rug was burned.
Our [REDACTED] blanket was destroyed.
Our home required cleanup due to soot, smoke, and lithium-ion battery debris.

I have retained the damaged power bank and the remaining battery fragments and have taken extensive photographs documenting the fire and the resulting property damage.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

incidentDescription:
Product: Frigidaire Countertop Nugget Ice Maker
Model: EFIC228-SS
Purchased from: Walmart
Approximate purchase date: 2023

I am reporting a potential choking hazard involving a Frigidaire countertop nugget ice maker, model EFIC228-SS.

After using the machine for some time, I discovered that small pieces of plastic were breaking off from inside the ice maker and ending up in both the water reservoir and the ice it produced.

The first time I became aware of the issue was when my young son drank water with ice from the machine and complained that something was stuck in his throat. At the time, I did not know what had caused it. After inspecting the ice maker more closely, I found small plastic fragments mixed in with the ice and water.

A few months later, the same problem occurred again. Once again, I found additional plastic pieces inside the machine and in the ice. I have photographs showing the plastic fragments.

My primary concern is that consumers, especially young children, could unknowingly swallow or choke on these plastic pieces. Because the fragments are mixed in with the ice, they can easily go unnoticed until they are already in a drink.

I have stopped using the ice maker because I believe it presents a potential choking hazard. I am submitting this report so the issue can be investigated to determine whether this is an isolated manufacturing defect or a broader safety problem affecting other units of the same model.

productDescription:
Onewheel Pint, made by Future Motion, Inc. of Santa Cruz, California. Serial number 2028162441. Manufactured July 2020.

It is a self-balancing electric skateboard, sometimes called a personal electric vehicle or an electric board sport product. It is ridden standing up, sideways, with one foot on each side of a single large wheel in the middle of the board.

Physical description. The board is roughly 27 inches long, about 11 inches wide and about 8 inches tall, and weighs about 23 pounds. It has one wide pneumatic tire, roughly 10.5 inches in diameter, mounted in the center of the board through a hub motor. On each side of the wheel is a foot pad, one of which has a pressure sensor that tells the board a rider is standing on it. The frame is aluminum rail with a plastic bumper at each end. Mine is sand colored beige, with a black tire and black foot pads. There is an LED light bar visible above the front foot pad that shows power and battery state.

The board carries a rechargeable lithium-ion battery pack of about 148 watt hours, housed in a sealed enclosure under the rail on one side of the wheel. The controller module, which contains the main circuit board, is housed in a matching sealed enclosure under the rail on the other side. The power button and the charge port are located on the controller side. It charges from a wall outlet with a supplied charger brick.

The board is self-balancing. It uses gyroscopes and an accelerometer to keep the rider level, drives forward when the rider leans forward, and slows when the rider leans back. Top speed is about 16 miles per hour and range is about 6 to 8 miles per charge.

The part that failed is the power button assembly, which is a small push button mounted through the wall of the sealed controller enclosure and held in place from the inside by a nut threaded onto the plastic body of the button. On my board that nut is metal. The button is wired to the main circuit board inside the same enclosure, which also contains the connector that carries battery power to the board.
incidentDescription:
The power button assembly on this Onewheel Pint failed structurally inside the sealed controller enclosure and released a metal fastener into a compartment containing an unfused lithium-ion battery power connection. The freed fastener came to rest across that connection and short circuited it. The controller board was destroyed and the battery pack no longer accepts a charge.

On inspection of the controller enclosure I found three things.

First, the plastic male thread on the power button body had fractured. It did not merely loosen. The threaded plastic broke and released the metal female nut that secures the button.

Second, the freed metal nut had migrated inside the enclosure and was resting across the contacts of the battery power connector, with corresponding marks at the contacts consistent with a short circuit.

Third, the power button wiring was torn.

The board operated normally and was charged successfully on the same day, July 26, 2026. It then failed completely. It will not power on. The LED light bar does not illuminate at all, not even briefly. The battery no longer accepts a charge. The charger does not change state whether or not it is connected to the board. The wheel spins freely by hand and the charge port pins are undamaged, so the failure is electrical and originates at the shorted battery connector.

The board has approximately 400 lifetime miles. It has never been in a collision of any kind. It has not been modified, was not opened before this inspection, has not been submerged, and has not been exposed to weather beyond normal riding.

WHY I BELIEVE THIS IS A SAFETY DEFECT

The hazard is not that the board broke. The hazard is that a conductive metal fastener was able to come loose inside a sealed enclosure that contains an unfused high current lithium-ion battery connection, and then bridge that connection. That is a short circuit directly across a lithium battery pack. In this case the result was destroyed electronics. The same event can produce thermal runaway, and it happens inside a sealed compartment where a rider cannot see or smell it developing.

This is a foreseeable and reportedly common failure rather than a freak event. The power button nut coming loose inside the Onewheel Pint controller enclosure is widely documented by owners. Published owner repair guides describe it as the most common problem with that enclosure, warn specifically that the freed metal nut can dangle on the power button leads and short components on the board, and report boards arriving from the factory with the nut already loose. The common owner remedy is to glue the nut in place, which indicates owners are compensating for a known design weakness rather than performing maintenance.

I further understand that the power button assembly Future Motion currently sells as a replacement part uses a plastic nut rather than the metal nut fitted to my board, which would eliminate this shorting mechanism. I have asked Future Motion to confirm this in writing and have not received an answer. If it is correct, then the hazard was identified and corrected in the replacement part, while boards already in service, including mine, retain the original metal nut and their owners were given no notice of the hazard or of the fix.

CONTACT WITH THE MANUFACTURER

I reported this to Future Motion on July 27, 2026 under support ticket [REDACTED]. Future Motion responded the same day. The response stated that the board was manufactured in July 2020 and is therefore out of warranty by age, and that the original warranty is non-transferable, so a secondhand owner is not covered. The response also stated that the controller module can sustain internal damage of this kind if the board has suffered extensive or repeat collisions. This board has been in no collision, and a collision does not fracture the threaded plastic body of a power button and then deposit the freed nut onto the battery power connector.

The warranty position may be correct as a matter of warranty, but it does not address the safety issue. Boards of this generation remain in service and are frequently resold, and their current owners have no way to know that a fastener inside the battery compartment can come free.

WHAT I THINK CPSC SHOULD EXAMINE

One. How many reports Future Motion has received of Onewheel Pint power button hardware coming free inside the controller enclosure.

Two. Whether the power button assembly was revised from a metal nut to a plastic nut, when that change was made, and whether it was made for safety reasons.

Three. Whether owners of boards built with the original metal nut were ever notified.

Four. Whether the battery power connection inside the controller enclosure is protected against a short caused by loose conductive hardware.

Future Motion and the Onewheel Pint were subject to the September 29, 2023 CPSC recall of approximately 300,000 Onewheel self-balancing electric skateboards. That recall concerned loss of balance control, which is a different hazard from the one reported here.

The board is preserved intact and unmodified and is available for inspection by CPSC. I have photographs of the fractured plastic thread, the metal nut resting on the battery power connector, and the torn button wiring.

productDescription:
The product is the Terraflame Hestia Bioethanol Fire Pit BioE Series, sold under the Terraflame and Solo Stove brand. It is a large, decorative, portable fire pit intended for residential use to create ambiance and warmth in indoor or outdoor spaces.
The unit I own is the 30inch round model, roughly 30 inches in diameter and about 12 inches high. It is a low, circular fire feature that sits directly on the floor or on a flat surface. The body is made of heavy, molded concrete often described as stone cast or concrete with a smooth, modern finish. The color of my unit is a light neutral rather than a dark graphite finish.
In the center of the circular concrete base is a recessed bioethanol burner reservoir. This is a metal insert designed to hold liquid bioethanol or similar alcohol based fuel that the user pours directly into the open container. The burner is then ignited to produce an open flame above the pooled liquid fuel. There is no chimney, no glass enclosure, and no mechanical fuel delivery system, the flame burns directly from the pooled liquid in the open burner.
The product is marketed as a bioethanol fire pit or BioE Series fire feature that is ventless, requiring no gas line or chimney, and is intended to be used as a decorative fire element for patios, living spaces, and similar areas. Its purpose is to create the look and feel of a real fire for relaxation and ambiance, using liquid bioethanol fuel that the consumer pours into the burner and lights.
manufacturer: Frontline Advance, LLC dba Solo Stove
incidentDescription:
I am reporting the Terraflame Hestia Bioethanol Fire Pit (sold under the Solo Stove and Terraflame brand) because I discovered that its design matches the exact hazard category described in the CPSCs consumer alert for alcohol and other liquidburning fire pits.

The product is a portable fire pit that requires the user to pour liquid bioethanol (or similar alcohol based fuel) into an open metal reservoir or bowl and then ignite the pooled liquid in the same place it was poured. It is marketed for home use, both indoors and outdoors, as a decorative fire feature.
I purchased this product in September 2023 and have used it personally as an adult consumer. My intended use was exactly as advertised: placing it on a stable, flat surface and using the manufacturers recommended liquid fuel for ambiance and warmth around my home/yard.
I later learned from the CPSCs public safety warning that fire pits which require pouring alcohol or other liquid fuel into an open container and then igniting pooled fuel violate voluntary safety standards and present a serious flame jetting and firespreading hazard. The CPSC has stated that these products have been associated with multiple severe burn injuries and deaths. Knowing that this design is inherently prone to flame jettingwhere invisible or low flames can ignite the stream of fuel as it is poured, causing explosive jets of burning liquid to be projected toward the user or bystandersI am concerned that this product cannot be used safely as intended.
I have personally experienced how difficult it can be to tell whether the flame is fully extinguished and how close hands and face must be to the burner area when refilling the reservoir. Even without an actual injury, these conditions put the user at clear risk of serious burn injury every time fuel is added, especially if any flame or hot surface remains.
At this time, I have not suffered a physical injury, but I believe injuries are likely to occur or could easily occur with normal use due to the products design. The risk is that a user, following typical instructions, refills the fire pit when the flame appears low or out, while vapors or a small flame remain, resulting in a sudden burst (flame jetting) that throws burning liquid onto the users hands, arms, face, or body, or onto nearby people and combustible materials.
I contacted the company (Solo Stove / Terraflame) to request a refund or remedy after learning of the CPSC alert. They confirmed there is no recall and refused to offer any remedy, instructing me only that they do not have a refund program tied to the CPSC alert. Because the CPSC has warned consumers to stop using and dispose of all such liquidburning fire pits, I am now discontinuing use and reporting this product so the Commission has a record that:
-The design appears to match the hazardous category identified in the alert.
-The product was sold for home use and used as intended.
-The manufacturer/distributor is declining to offer any remedy even though the product cannot safely be used as advertised.
I am submitting this report in the interest of preventing severe injuries and to help inform any future safety actions regarding this specific product line.

productDescription: Electric Scooter
incidentDescription:
I'm concerned there is an imminent safety threat to riders of the Segway model GT2 scooter. This is Segway's premium superscooter that is capable of going over 40 mph and rated for 330lb riders. Unfortunately there are multiple design flaws in the front suspension that make this model (and GT1) susceptible to a catastrophic failure event. I'm now seeing other GT2 owners have experienced the same catastrophic failure. I'm worried I am one of the earlier failures because I purchased the GT2 not long after launch (Aug 2023), used as a daily commuter (2.5 yrs, ~6000 mi total) and am heavier (240lb). 

On my commute home I hit a bump, one I've overcome hundreds of times before, two blocks from my home, and my steerer tube ruptured sending me to the ground hard at 20 mph. The handlebars and front forks essentially fell out of the frame, leaving me helpless.

I sustained multiple injuries including:
     -Four broken bones in my left hand (requiring two surgeries and screw in my scaphoid)
     -Chipped tooth
     -Face lacerations (requiring stitches and resulting in noticeable permanent scaring)
     -Broken right wrist

I've looked closely at the failure to understand better understand what happened.  I'm a Washington State board certified Professional Mechanical Engineer (Machine Design and Materials), so material failures interest me.  In summary, this catastrophic failure was 100% preventable. The design errors/negligence lead to the steerer tube being susceptible to fatigue (crack propagation) and will inevitably result in more failures. Additionally, the rupture occurs in a location that is not inspectable, so there is no way to assess a scooters current condition by inspecting for cracks. All GT1 and GT2 models should be recalled.
