incidentDescription: Bought this Coleman Triton 2-Burner Propane Gas Camping Stove through Home Depot to replace my 20 year old Coleman camp stove as it was showing signs of wear. The top grate of this stove has the grate bars bend in towards the burner on each side of the burner.  Hence, the pot or pan can easily tip over left or right spilling the contents creating a safety issue.  This happened to me on the very first time.  Even after using it and aware of the issue, it almost tipped over on my wife.  Luckily, no injuries.  However, someone could easily be burned by hot contents or start a grease fire.  A normal grate design will insure that the pot or pan weight is equally supported in multiple directions and thus avoids easily tipping over the pot.  Recommend not buying and Coleman should place a stop sell order on this stove.  The issue will be reported to the CPSC...Consumer Products Safety Commission.

productDescription: Char-Broil Patio Bistro 240 propane grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
I purchased a Char-Broil Patio Bistro 240 grill, model # 15601900 in June of 2025.  The grill never seemed to work properly but as I had never used a propane powered grill before, I assumed there were just some things I needed to troubleshoot on my own to get it to work properly.  The ignition button never seemed to work properly and would take numerous tries to get it to work.  At some points, the grill would start so forcefully that the internal grill plate would lift itself up and then back down.  I followed the instructions and troubleshooting information I found online, disconnected and reconnected the ignition mechanism, changed the batteries several times and even got a new propane tank at one point.  The issue continued to happen and sometimes it would not ignite at all.  I became frightened to continue trying to get it to work based on how forcefully it would start sometimes and noises it would make.  I stopped using it altogether and put it away for the season.  This season I tried to start it just once to see what would happen and it did not start at all.  I even consulted with my neighbor and told him what had happened previously and he said that was definitely something that should not be happening and sounded dangerous.  As I purchased the grill at a local hardware store in June of 2025, I know they will not accept a return for a refund.  I also didn't even attempt that because I felt that since this is clearly an issue on the manufacturer's end, that it is something they should resolve.  I reached out to Char-Broil and they told me they would only offer to possibly provide a replacement part.  They admitted in our online chat that this sounded like an issue with "repeated delayed ignition and it sometimes causes an excess of propane buildup."    I told them I would not feel safe using the grill even if  a replacement part was sent.  They told me that was basically the only option and there were no options for a full or even partial refund.  I reiterated several times how I feel this is a legitimate safety issue and could be specific to this particular grill.  They continued to repeat that the only option that could be explored would be a replacement part even though I stated more than once that I no longer felt safe using this grill.

This year when I decided the grill could definitely no longer be used I did a little searching online and found almost right away that there was an issue with what I believe is this exact same type of grill back in 2013 and that a recall was issued.  See link below.

https://www.cpsc.gov/Recalls/2013/Char-Broil-Recalls-Patio-Bistro-Gas-Grills

productDescription: Pororo THES10 Foldable Electric Scooter for Adults with Seat (350W / 8.5" Tires)
incidentDescription:
Incident Summary:
During the very first operational use of a newly assembled Pororo THES10 electric scooter, the structural support bolt securing the rider's seat failed under normal operation. The seat abruptly and violently tipped backward, causing the rider to lose control and be dumped backward directly onto the rear wheel. The rider was wearing a helmet and luckily escaped physical injury, but the mechanical failure presents an extreme risk of severe bodily harm or death to future consumers.
Technical Details of the Defect:
The failure stems from a critical manufacturing and packaging defect involving the 3-inch-long hex bolt with a matching 1/2-inch hex nut located directly beneath the seat assembly. This bolt/nut is responsible for locking the "fore and aft" tilt angle of the seat.
Factory Under-Torquing: The bolt/nut arrived pre-assembled from the factory but was under-torqued and insufficiently tightened to withstand standard rider load.
Missing Maintenance Tools: The product packaging failed to include the necessary 1/2-inch hex wrench required for a consumer to verify, adjust, or securely tighten this specific load-bearing bolt during initial assembly.
Risk to Public Safety:
The Walmart webpage explicitly advertises a maximum weight capacity of either 220 or 264 lbs. for the THES10 model. The 220 lbs. figure is in the Durable Construction section but under the specs pulldown, it says Max load 264 lbs. The reporter of this incident weighs just under 195 lbs. and still experienced an immediate structural failure of the seat.
For consumers approaching the upper limits of the advertised weight capacity, the factory-under-tightened bolt is virtually guaranteed to slip under normal riding stress. Because the seat collapses backward, this defect creates an immediate risk of a rider experiencing, catastrophic falls, head/neck trauma, or bone fractures.

productDescription:
Product information:

Manufacturer: Camp Chef
Products: PG24DLX Deluxe Pellet Grill and SmokePro BBQ Sear Box
Approximate purchase dates (March and April 2018).
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
model: Camp Chef SmokePro BBQ Sear Box
incidentDescription:
The  dangerous fire incident involved a Camp Chef PG24DLX Deluxe Pellet Grill with a Camp Chef SmokePro BBQ Sear Box propane attachment mounted on the side. Both products were purchased new in 2018. The pellet grill was purchased from Amazon in March 2018, and the SmokePro BBQ Sear Box was purchased from Dick's Sporting Goods in April 2018. The grill was equipped with the original propane regulator and hose assembly connected to a standard 20-pound propane cylinder.

Description of Incident

On July 6, 2026, at approximately 3:15 p.m., I observed a flame approximately 2 feet high coming from the right side of my Camp Chef barbecue while it was sitting idle on my backyard patio. The grill was not in operation at the time. It had last been used on July 4, 2026, when I cooked for approximately 20 guests.

The barbecue was covered with the original Camp Chef grill cover and was located in full direct sunlight. The outdoor temperature was approximately 94 degrees F.

When I saw the flames through my window, I immediately ran outside with a garden hose and extinguished the fire. I then shut off the propane supply at the tank. I normally close the propane tank valve after each use, but I had inadvertently left it open after using the grill on July 4.

After the fire was extinguished, I inspected the damage. The fire damage was concentrated around the propane hose and the gas inlet connection to the SmokePro BBQ Sear Box. The rubber propane hose was extensively burned and melted, and the grill cover was burned through on the same side of the grill. The pellet grill also sustained heat and smoke damage.

Based on the condition of the components after the incident, it appears there may have been a small propane leak at or near the hose connection to the Sear Box gas inlet fitting. However, I do not know the exact cause of the leak or the source of ignition. The metal hose fitting at the Sear Box remained very tight after the incident and did not appear to have loosened.

Fortunately, no one was injured, and the fire was extinguished before it spread to my home or surrounding property. Had I not been at home and happened to observe the fire shortly after it started, the consequences could have been much more severe.

I have retained the damaged grill, Sear Box, propane hose, regulator, and related components and have photographs documenting the damage. These items are available for inspection if requested.

productDescription:
Product is an Apple iPhone 13, model number MLMM3LLA. The phone is a smartphone with a glass front and glass back, metal frame, touch screen display, rear camera lenses, charging port, and built in rechargeable lithium ion battery.

The phone involved was not in a case at the time of the incident. The phone was powered on, not charging, and not on a wireless charger. The phone belonged to my friend.

The phone had a pre existing crack at the top right front of the device. To my knowledge, the phone had no known water exposure, no known overheating history, and no repairs, modifications, or battery replacement while my friend had it. The current battery health shows 79 percent, but I do not know what the battery health was at the time of the incident.

The phone currently displays an Apple battery health message stating that the battery health is significantly degraded and that an Apple Authorized Service Provider can replace the battery to restore full performance and capacity.
incidentDescription:
I am reporting a possible consumer product safety incident involving an Apple iPhone 13.

On the night of June 9 into the morning of June 10 2026, I was asleep in bed while my friends iPhone 13 was in the bed under or on the right side of my body. The phone was powered on, but it was not charging, not on a wireless charger, not in a case, and there was no other heat source nearby.

During the night I felt discomfort and a hot burning sensation, but I did not fully wake up or understand what was happening at first because I have a diagnosed sleep disorder that makes me difficult to wake. After several hours, the sensation became too uncomfortable. I removed the phone from my body and the hot burning sensation stopped.

Later that morning I noticed two small burn injuries on the right side of my body, one on my right arm and one on my stomach. The burns were blistered and raised. My right arm was bare and my stomach was covered by a shirt. The arm injury hurt more and burned badly when it touched anything. I took photos of the injuries the same day. The marks are still visible and look like scars.

I do not remember whether the front or back of the phone was hotter because I was not fully awake when I removed it. I also cannot confirm whether there was smoke. I did not observe burn marks on the bed or clothing.

The phone belongs to my friend, not me. To my knowledge, the phone had no prior overheating history while my friend had it, no known water exposure, and no repairs, modifications, or battery replacement. The phone currently shows battery health at 79 percent, but I do not know what the battery health was at the time of the incident.

I reported the injury to Apple and provided photos of the phone, photos of my injuries, medical documentation, the phone serial number, and completed Apples requested diagnostics by phone. Apples engineering team later requested that the phone be sent in for inspection, but Apple stated that the phone may not come back usable because it may be taken apart.

Because the phone belongs to my friend and may be key evidence, there is concern about sending it in without written replacement or reimbursement terms or written information about the inspection process.

I am reporting this because I believe the iPhone may have overheated or malfunctioned while not charging and caused burn injuries.

productDescription: RYOBI ONE+ HP 18V 4-Mode 1/2 in. cordless impact wrench, model P262, serial number NC22145N100078, powered by a RYOBI 18V lithium-ion battery pack
productType: Other Portable or Stationary Power Tools (809)
incidentDescription:
I was using a RYOBI ONE+ HP 18V 4-Mode 1/2 in. cordless impact wrench, model P262, serial number NC22145N100078, powered by a RYOBI 18V lithium-ion battery pack.  I am the owner of the tool and the only person using it. I am an adult with extensive mechanical and power tool experience.
The tool was being used for its intended purpose: removing suspension fasteners on a 2021 pickup truck in my driveway. It was fitted with a correctly sized impact-rated socket, with no extension bar or universal joint, running in reverse at mode 3. The tool had never been dropped, submerged, modified, or serviced, and had no prior damage or performance problems.

During normal operation, flame and smoke were emitted from the rear vents of the tool housing, at the motor and controller end, directly behind the handle. I immediately released the trigger, set the tool down, and removed the battery pack. The fire has to be extinguished by covering the device with a fire cloth.

No injuries occurred. However, my hand was on the grip and my forearm was directly behind the tool at the moment of the event, so the flame vented within inches of my hand and arm. Had I been holding the tool in a different orientation, or working in a confined space under the vehicle, burn injury would have been likely. There were combustible materials nearby (vehicle fluids, shop rags), and the tool was in close proximity to a vehicle at the time.

Neither the tool nor the battery pack has been disassembled, charged, or re-energized. Both are being preserved intact. The battery is isolated outdoors on a non-combustible surface and monitored for delayed thermal runaway. Photographs of the tool, nameplate, serial number, and battery are available.
I have separately contacted One World Technologies, Inc. to report this incident.

productDescription: YOZMA IN10 E-bike
incidentDescription:
The YOZMA IN10 electric bicycle, sold in the United States, appears to have a safety-related defect involving the chain tensioner pulley wheel. During normal use, the pulley wheel prematurely deteriorated and ultimately disintegrated after approximately 230 miles of operation.
The failure occurred while the e-bike was being ridden at approximately 30 mph. When the pulley wheel failed, the drive chain lost proper tension, derailed from the rear sprocket, and caused a sudden loss of propulsion. This nearly resulted in a crash and serious injury.
The YOZMA IN10 is advertised as capable of speeds up to approximately 40 mph. Failure of the chain tensioner assembly at these speeds creates a significant risk of loss of control, collision, and rider injury.
Replacement chain tensioner pulley wheels listed on the manufacturer's website are currently sold out. While the reason for the lack of availability is unknown, it may indicate increased demand for replacement parts consistent with similar failures experienced by other owners.
Based on the premature failure of a critical drivetrain component after only approximately 230 miles of normal use, I believe this condition presents an unreasonable safety risk and warrants investigation.

productDescription: ZEFIORA V12 electric bicycle, black, sold exclusively through Temu.com. Equipped with lithium-ion battery pack, BMS system, electric motor, and charger. Advertised range 80 miles. Actual range 23 km.
incidentDescription:
I purchased a ZEFIORA V12 electric bicycle from Temu.com (Whaleco Inc.) on March 16, 2026 (Order No. [REDACTED]) for USD 705.61. The bicycle was delivered on April 7, 2026. I am 64 years old. I am reporting multiple serious product safety violations that pose an imminent fire, explosion, and personal injury risk to U.S. consumers.

VIOLATION 1 - FALSE UL CERTIFICATION CLAIM (Most Serious)
The product listing on Temu.com explicitly stated UL Certification with the UL logo displayed as a product feature, alongside BMS Intelligent Safety and 80 MILES Long Range. Upon delivery and physical inspection of the battery pack, individual lithium-ion cells, BMS board, and charger unit, NO UL 2849 certification mark was found anywhere on any component. UL 2849 is the mandatory federal safety standard for e-bike electrical systems sold in the U.S. The physical mark is legally required on the certified product. Its absence renders the product legally uncertified regardless of any paperwork claim. This constitutes a false safety certification. The product was sold under deliberately fraudulent safety representations that endanger every consumer who purchased it.

VIOLATION 2 - BATTERY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (BMS) FAILURE AND FIRE HAZARD
The advertised battery range was 80 MILES (approximately 128 km). The actual range after a full charge was 23 kilometers, less than 18 percent of the advertised minimum. This is not a calibration issue. It is diagnostic of BMS failure. A malfunctioning BMS creates the following direct safety hazards - (a) uncontrolled overcharging of individual lithium cells creating fire and explosion risk, (b) cell voltage imbalance creating thermal runaway risk, (c) sudden power cutoff during operation creating accident and fall risk. This last hazard is not theoretical. On April 27, 2026, the bicycle died completely while I was riding it, despite the battery display showing 75 percent charge remaining. The display failure is itself evidence of a defective BMS. I was left stranded far from home. At 64 years old, I was forced to pedal the full distance back on foot under the Florida heat, creating a serious risk to my health and safety. I have photographic evidence of the odometer reading 23 km after a full charge and video evidence of the product defects.

VIOLATION 3 - DEFECTIVE AND DANGEROUS BRAKES
The brakes are dangerously ineffective and failed to provide adequate stopping power during normal use. This defect creates a direct and immediate risk of serious injury or death to the rider and to other persons in the area of use.

VIOLATION 4 - STRUCTURAL INTEGRITY FAILURE
The bicycle emits loud metallic squeaking and grinding noises during normal operation, indicating a complete absence of quality control and structural integrity that may lead to mechanical failure while in motion.

VIOLATION 5 - UNCERTIFIED CHARGER
The charger supplied with the bicycle displays no UL or ETL safety certification marks. An uncertified charger connected to an already non-compliant lithium battery pack creates compounded fire and electrical hazard.

VIOLATION 6 - MISSING SAFETY EQUIPMENT REQUIRED BY LAW
The bicycle was delivered without turn signals, which are required by Florida law and U.S. federal regulations for electric bicycles operated on public roads. I was forced to purchase turn signals separately at my own expense. Their absence at the time of delivery created an immediate legal and safety violation.

SYSTEMIC PATTERN - NOT AN ISOLATED INCIDENT
(a) In September 2025, the U.S. Federal Trade Commission assessed Whaleco Inc. a USD 2,000,000 civil penalty for INFORM Consumers Act violations, establishing a documented pattern of non-compliance with U.S. consumer protection laws. (b) On May 28, 2026, the European Commission fined Temu 200,000,000 euros under the Digital Services Act specifically for distributing unsafe products including e-bikes with non-compliant batteries through its marketplace. I have a copy of this EU Commission decision. The same unsafe product category, namely e-bike batteries sold under false UL certification claims, is being distributed at scale to U.S. consumers through Temus platform.

TEMUS RESPONSE AND BUYER PROTECTION FAILURE
I sent a formal Demand Letter via [REDACTED] Certified Mail on May 7, 2026 (Tracking No. [REDACTED]). Temu refused delivery on May 11 and May 16, 2026. I formally invoked Temus Buyer Protection guarantee. Temu ignored it entirely. The seller offered a reimbursement of only USD 20 on a USD 705.61 purchase. The seller also imposed commercially unreasonable return conditions, requiring me to ship the bicycle back to Zefiora at my own expense. I filed complaints with the [REDACTED] (Complaint No. [REDACTED]) and the Florida Attorney General under FDUTPA Section 501.201, with senior citizen enhanced penalty flags active. Temus only response to all of this was a generic template message with no substantive resolution.

WHY I AM FILING THIS COMPLAINT
I am not filing this complaint solely for my own benefit. Since discovering these violations, I have not used the bicycle because I know it is dangerous. I cannot sell it, because selling a product I know to be defective and falsely certified would make me legally liable. I am left with a USD 705.61 item I cannot use and cannot sell. I am filing this complaint because I cannot remain silent about a product that may have been sold to thousands of U.S. consumers who do not know their bicycle contains an uncertified lithium battery that can catch fire, explode, and cause serious injury or death. A defective BMS in a lithium e-bike battery is not a minor defect. It is a life-safety hazard. Every unit of the ZEFIORA V12 sold through Temu without valid UL 2849 certification represents a potential fire or explosion waiting to happen in a home, a garage, or on a public road.

I request that CPSC immediately investigate Whaleco Inc. d-b-a Temu for distribution of consumer products bearing false safety certifications in violation of 15 U.S.C. 2068, and initiate a mandatory recall of all ZEFIORA V12 units distributed through the Temu platform in the United States.

(7/2/2026): DESCRIPTION OF RISK OF HARM
This is not a single-unit malfunction or an isolated consumer complaint. It is a documented pattern of fraudulent safety certification combined with a battery management system (BMS) defect that creates a foreseeable, ongoing, and potentially fatal risk to an unknown but large number of U.S. consumers who currently possess this product without any awareness of the danger they are living with.
1.	NATURE OF THE HARM — FIRE AND EXPLOSION RISK
The ZEFIORA V12 was marketed and sold with an explicit UL Certification claim and UL logo displayed as a purchasing feature. Physical inspection of the battery pack, individual lithium-ion cells, BMS board, and charger confirmed that NO UL 2849 certification mark is present on any component. UL 2849 is the mandatory federal safety standard specifically written to prevent uncontrolled overcharging, cell voltage imbalance, and thermal runaway in e-bike lithium battery systems. A lithium battery pack operating outside this standard, paired with an uncertified charger, is a documented fire-ignition source. This is precisely the failure mode responsible for the e-bike and e-scooter battery fires that have caused deaths and destroyed homes in multiple U.S. cities in recent years. This is not a theoretical concern — it is the exact hazard the UL 2849 standard was created to prevent, and this product was sold without meeting it while falsely claiming that it did.
2.	EVIDENCE THE DEFECT IS ACTIVE, NOT LATENT
The battery's actual range after full charge measured 23 km, against an advertised 80 miles (approximately 128 km) — less than 18% of the advertised minimum. This magnitude of discrepancy is not a marketing exaggeration; it is diagnostic evidence of active BMS malfunction, meaning the cells are already being charged, monitored, and cut off outside safe parameters on every single charge cycle. On April 27, 2026, this manifested physically: the bicycle lost all power mid-ride while the display showed 75% charge remaining, a sudden and unexplained power failure consistent with BMS instability. The rider, 64 years old, was stranded and forced to travel the remaining distance on foot in Florida heat. A sudden, unpredictable loss of power is itself a road-safety hazard for any rider in traffic; combined with the documented brake failure described below, the risk compounds.
3.	COMPOUNDING MECHANICAL HAZARDS
The brakes provide inadequate stopping power under normal use, creating direct risk of collision, serious injury, or death to the rider and to bystanders. The frame emits structural squeaking and grinding under normal operation, indicating an absence of basic quality control that increases the likelihood of mechanical failure while the bicycle is in motion. The unit was delivered without turn signals, a feature required by Florida law and federal regulation for e-bikes operated on public roads, meaning every unit sold as-delivered is already operating in violation of traffic safety requirements, increasing collision risk with other vehicles.
4.	WHY THIS IS A COMMUNITY-WIDE RISK, NOT AN ISOLATED CASE
Temu is a mass-market platform, and the ZEFIORA V12 is sold at scale to U.S. consumers with no indication anywhere in the listing that the safety certification is false. This means the population of affected owners is unknown and almost certainly far larger than a single buyer. Most owners will have no technical ability to verify a UL 2849 mark and will trust the certification as displayed. This creates a population of consumers who are:
— charging an uncertified lithium battery pack overnight in bedrooms, garages, and apartments, unaware of fire/explosion risk;
— riding a bicycle with a documented pattern of sudden, unpredictable power loss in traffic;
— relying on brakes that do not provide adequate stopping power;
— operating without required turn signals, increasing collision risk to themselves and third parties.
Because these consumers do not know there is a defect, no self-correction is occurring. The risk is silent, distributed, and cumulative — every day these units remain in active use without recall or public warning, the probability of a fire, an explosion, or a road injury involving someone who never knew their bicycle was dangerous increases.
5.	THIS IS PART OF A DOCUMENTED CORPORATE PATTERN
This is not an isolated vendor failure. In September 2025, the U.S. Federal Trade Commission assessed Whaleco Inc. (Temu) a USD 2,000,000 civil penalty for violations of the INFORM Consumers Act. On May 28, 2026, the European Commission fined Temu €200,000,000 under the Digital Services Act specifically for distributing unsafe products — including e-bikes with non-compliant batteries — through its marketplace. Both actions establish, through independent regulatory findings, that the same category of product defect has already been identified as a systemic problem on this platform outside the United States. The ZEFIORA V12 fits this exact pattern and is currently being sold to U.S. consumers under it.
6.	WHY I AM SUBMITTING THIS DESPITE NO PERSONAL INJURY
I sustained no physical injury in the April 27, 2026 incident, and I want to be direct about that so this Report is evaluated on the correct basis: this is not a personal injury claim. I am submitting this Report because I have direct physical evidence — photographic and video — that a mass-marketed consumer product carries a real, mechanically-explained fire, explosion, and road-injury risk, that the product's core safety claim is false, and that an unknown number of other consumers currently possess this same product with no way of knowing any of this. I have kept the bicycle out of use since discovering the defect specifically because I consider it unsafe to ride or to resell to another unsuspecting consumer.
REQUESTED ACTION
I respectfully request that CPSC treat this as an active investigation priority given the fire/explosion hazard class involved, and that it consider a mandatory recall or public safety notice for all ZEFIORA V12 units distributed through Temu in the United States, consistent with 15 U.S.C. § 2068.
I am available to provide the original 21 supporting attachments already submitted with Report No. [REDACTED], and any further clarification CPSC requires.

productDescription: Tolooc ceepuy leaf blower
incidentDescription:
Battery charger caused a fire w/ Lithium Ion Batteries. Engine 6 dispatched for a building fire.

Arrived on scene of a 2.5 story middle unit townhouse with smoke showing, established command and stretched an 1.75 inch hand line.

The occupants were outside and advised everyone had evacuated and the fire was located in the back corner of the living room and one of the homeowners had used a dry chemical extinguisher to attempt to put it out.

We located the fire area and found that the extinguisher had knocked down all visible fire.

Continued the second due engine and first due ladder releasing the other companies.

Assigned Ladder 2 to ventilate upon arrival. Engine 2 took a hydrant on Westgate Crossing for water supply if needed.

Further investigation showed there was no extension to any of the surrounding material which included an end table with various items on it and a couch and love seat. There was some char on the wall and the cover for the baseboard heat was melted.

The cause of the fire was a charging Lithium Ion battery and I requested a K unit be notified and they could call C4's cell phone. K2 contacted C4 and after speaking with him photos were taken of the scene.

Released Engine 2.

The homeowner advised there were 2 cats in the residence and after searching by us and the homeowner both were located.

The homeowner advised that there was a battery fro the leaf blower plugged in and charging on the end table. We located the charger with the end that connects to the battery melted as well as the batteries with the exterior plastic housing melted away and the batteries separated from each other.

The leaf blower was a Tolooc ceepuy leaf blower, no data plate was found with any manufacturer information, model or serial number. The charger had no manufacturer information but was labeled Lithium Battery Charger model number LI13S50A(B) with a 5 amp output.

While investigating the area E6D advised the female occupant had reported some smoke inhalation and was requesting medical aid. I requested and ALS to respond.

After evaluation by the crew of Engine 6 she declined ambulance transport and the ALS was canceled. Refusal paperwork was completed.

Once ventilation was complete Ladder 2 was released.

Once photo documentation was complete and the area was rechecked for heat and extension with none found the property was released back to the homeowner.

Terminated command.

Capt.[REDACTED]

productDescription: The product is a Carbo E-Bike (carbon fiber electric bicycle) that I used for recreational riding and exercise. During normal operation, the bicycle seat unexpectedly detached, causing me to lose control and fall. I believe the seat assembly or its attachment mechanism may have failed during ordinary use.
incidentDescription: I was riding my carbon fiber electric bicycle at Delnor-Wiggins Pass State Park in Naples, Florida, on the roadway between Park Drive and the road leading toward the boat ramp. I regularly ride this bicycle for exercise, usually between 15 and 30 miles, and before this incident it had recently been repaired, including having new tires and brakes installed because of prior issues. On the day of the incident, I was riding at a low speed and coasting when I suddenly felt a bump. At that exact moment, the bicycle seat detached without warning, causing me to lose control and fall immediately to the ground. I also believe that a pothole in the roadway may have contributed to the seat failure. After I fell, the rear wheel of the bicycle ran over my right leg. I immediately realized my leg was severely injured because it was visibly deformed. I remained on the ground trying to stabilize my leg until bystanders came to help me and called 911. I was transported by ambulance to the hospital for emergency treatment. As a result of the incident, I suffered severe injuries, including a fractured tibia and a complete fracture of my femur. I underwent emergency surgery where two titanium rods were implanted in my leg, and screws were placed in my ankle to stabilize it. I remained hospitalized for about ten days before being transferred to an inpatient rehabilitation facility. I am currently unable to bear weight on my right leg, require a wheelchair and walker to get around, and continue to receive physical therapy at home. I am reporting this incident because I believe it may have been caused by a defect involving the bicycle seat.

It is an electrically powered cold plunge and chiller system designed to hold, circulate, filter, and chill water for residential cold therapy use. incidentDescription:
I am reporting a potential safety issue involving a Plunge All In cold plunge. The product is an electrically powered cold plunge and chiller system that circulates and chills water.

After removing the side panel, the leak appeared to be coming from the internal filter housing area.

My concern is that water is leaking inside and underneath an electrically powered product that contains a pump, chiller system, internal components, wiring, electrical connections, a GFCI plug, and moving fan components. Plunge troubleshooting instructions also require the unit to be filled, powered on, and leak tested while internal panels are removed and the chiller fan is exposed. This creates concern about possible electric shock, shorting, pump or chiller damage, slip hazard from water on the floor, or injury while troubleshooting around exposed internal components.

No physical injury has occurred so far. I stopped using the product because of the leak and safety concern. The product was being used in a normal residential garage setting for its intended purpose, filling the tub with water and turning on the chiller and circulation system.

This same filter housing issue was previously repaired during the warranty period, but the same area is leaking again. Plunge has now determined that the filter housing assembly needs replacement.

productDescription: OUPES Guardian 6000 Portable Power Station. Large-format home backup power station and solar generator. Black in color. Approximately 23.6 inches long x 11.4 inches wide x 15.7 inches tall. Weight approximately 132 pounds. Contains a large-format lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4) battery rated at 6,144Wh. Includes built-in AC inverter, AC charging input, solar input, and multiple AC and DC output ports. Sold as a new unit via oupes.com. Order number 38857, Serial number 97072604290123.
incidentDescription:
I purchased a new OUPES Guardian 6000 portable power station (Order [REDACTED], Serial 97072604290123) and within approximately nine hours of first use, the unit produced visible electrical arcing, a loud arcing sound, and a plume of black smoke from the rear AC area of the unit, filling my home with a strong burning electrical smell.
Prior to this event, the unit had exhibited abnormal behavior from first use: it would only draw 77-140 watts from a standard 120V AC wall outlet, far below the rated approximately 1,800W input. It also significantly under-pulled from a solar array compared to my other OUPES units on the same feed. The unit emitted abnormal repetitive beeping during a solar test earlier the same day.
The unit did not automatically shut itself off during the arcing and smoke event. I was required to manually pull the AC cord from the wall outlet and then physically press the power button to shut the unit off while it was still energized and smoking.
The unit was sold to me as new but arrived in visibly used condition, with coal-black casing already dusty and scuffed, and multiple long scratches on the plastic and AC outlet section inconsistent with a new product.
I am aware of at least two similar public reports involving the Guardian 6000 - a case documented by [REDACTED] involving a Guardian 6000 that caught fire within days of purchase under normal household use, and a post on [REDACTED] almost burnt my house down" describing a nearly identical event.
The unit is currently unplugged, powered off, and stored away from combustible materials. I have refused to ship it via standard retail return methods due to concerns about transporting a damaged lithium battery that has experienced a thermal event without proper hazmat classification and documentation, as required under DOT 49 CFR and IATA dangerous goods rules.

productDescription: Bertazzoni Range hood model KCH30XVPRO 30 inch stainless steel chimney hood, though this switch is used in other models as well.
incidentDescription:
While operating the Bertazzoni KCH30XVPRO range hood on its maximum setting (High), an electrical malfunction occurred within the internal control switch mechanism. The appliance experienced sustained electrical arcing, generating extreme, localized heat. This resulted in the catastrophic melting and thermal degradation of the plastic switch.

The failure occurred during normal residential operation under standard conditions. The failure mode indicates either an inadequate electrical component rating for the motors current draw, or a structural breakdown of the internal switch contacts, leading to high-resistance arcing.

Range hoods are installed directly over active cooking surfaces and are inherently exposed to flammable cooking grease and oils. An internal electrical failure that creates an open arc and melts plastic components introduces a direct ignition source into a high-grease environment, posing a critical kitchen fire and smoke inhalation hazard.

incidentDescription:
I am reporting a potential consumer-product safety hazard involving a Shark FlexStyle Air Styling & Drying System, model HD430, color Stone, manufactured by SharkNinja. The product was purchased from Amazon, ASIN B0B89P16MC. It is a 1300-watt, 120-volt hair dryer and multi-styler with three airflow speeds.

On June 20, 2026, I used the product during normal intended hair-drying and styling use, in close proximity to my head and ears. During a 30-second recorded session, I cycled through all airflow settings, including the three-dot maximum airflow setting. Because the product is designed for use near the ears, I performed a preliminary sound-level screening measurement using the [REDACTED] mobile app on an [REDACTED]. The phone was positioned at approximately the same ear-level distance and orientation as during normal use. The app was set to A-weighting, Fast response time (0.2 seconds), and +0.0 dB calibration.

The 30-second recording showed an average/Leq of 104.1 dB(A), a maximum reading of 116.2 dB, and a peak reading of 119.3 dB. The highest peak occurred while the product was operating on the three-dot maximum airflow setting. These are smartphone-app screening measurements, not certified sound-level-meter measurements. However, they raise a serious concern that this product may expose consumers to potentially excessive noise during normal intended use near the ears. This report concerns a potential noise-exposure and hearing-injury risk, including possible ear pain, tinnitus, temporary hearing changes, disorientation, or other auditory injury.

I did not see a clear warning regarding hearing damage, noise exposure limits, hearing protection, product decibel output, or safe exposure duration. After using the product, I experienced ear ringing, difficulty hearing clearly, and disorientation associated with reduced hearing clarity after use. I stopped using the product after observing these readings and symptoms. I have retained the product, packaging, Amazon purchase information, model number, UPC, and screenshots documenting the measurement settings and results, including A-weighting, +0.0 dB calibration, NIOSH dosimeter settings, 104.1 dB(A) average/Leq, 116.2 dB maximum, and 119.3 dB peak (peak occured right when 3 dot maximum airflow was pressed).

I request that CPSC investigate this with the Shark FlexStyle HD430 presents a potential excessive-noise exposure or hearing-injury hazard during normal intended use. I request independent sound-output testing at realistic consumer ear-distance conditions, including maximum airflow settings, and evaluation of whether warnings, decibel-output disclosure, safe-use or exposure-duration guidance, labeling changes, corrective action, or other consumer protections are warranted.


Here is the exact amazon link of what I purchased for specifications if needed: https://amzn.to/3SUhUbt

productDescription: Electric scooter
incidentDescription:
My daughter was riding the scooter, relatively low speed. She tried to stop and instinctively brought her left leg towards the rear fender. She got a deep laceration with lots of bleeding. My other kids got smaller injuries previously as well. This scooter has exposed sharp parts, the break, the edge of the fender. It is a major hazard. I am a physician, unfortunately I did not take a picture before applying glue and steri strips to the wound but it is a deep laceration, 3 cm by 0.5 cm, about 3 mm deep, heavy bleeding.

(06/29/2026) Product, GoTrax XR Advance Lightweight Electric Scooter, model GT-XRADVANCE-GRAY, serial GTSH8532503GRY03266, manufactured March 8 2025, purchased from BestBuy.com on August 3 2025 and delivered August 5 2025, Best Buy SKU 6574976.
I am supplementing to describe the hazard more completely than my first report and to refine the injury detail.
The core hazard is a cluster of exposed, unguarded sharp parts concentrated on the foot side of the deck. On inspection, the kickstand has several sharp edges, the rear fender edge is sharp, and the brake rotor has knife-like edges, all in locations a foot can reach if it leaves the deck. A rider does not contact a single isolated sharp point. There are multiple ways to be cut on this side of the scooter.
This is compounded by a braking defect. When the hand brake is applied, the scooter pitches sharply forward toward tipping over the front wheel, which makes the intended brake unsafe to use. My daughter, riding at relatively low speed, tried to stop and instinctively brought her foot down toward the deck, as one would to slow a non-powered scooter. Her ankle was deeply lacerated by one of the exposed sharp parts. The injury was severe enough that she cannot identify which specific component cut her, which is itself the concern. A foot leaving the deck on this scooter encounters several unguarded sharp edges rather than none.
Refined injury detail. The laceration is on the posteromedial aspect of the left ankle, just anterior to the Achilles tendon and approximately 1 cm below the medial malleolus, approximately 4 cm long and 5 mm deep, with heavy bleeding. This refines the initial estimate in my first report. As a physician, I closed it with tissue adhesive and Steri-Strips. The wound was of a severity that ordinarily warrants medical closure. She is currently unable to participate in gymnastics. Two other children sustained minor cuts on the same scooter on prior occasions.
A scooter marketed for this use should have no sharp, unguarded parts in locations a foot can reach, not several. Combined with a brake that deters safe braking, this is a design defect, not ordinary wear. I still have the product in my possession.
Attachments to this report include photographs of the exposed sharp parts, the kickstand, the rear fender edge, and the brake rotor, and a photograph of the injury.
I request that this hazard be recorded and evaluated for recall.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: Samsung French Door Refrigerator, Model RF28HMEDBSR/AA, Serial Number 065L43BJ600447J. Stainless steel finish, French door configuration with bottom freezer drawer. 28 cubic foot capacity. Manufactured June 2017 in Korea. Purchased new from Conn's Home Plus, Store #154, Phoenix, AZ on August 25, 2017 for $1,999.99. Refrigerant: R-134a. The refrigerator features a built-in ice maker in the upper left door compartment and an internal temperature display panel.
incidentDescription:
My Samsung French Door Refrigerator (Model RF28HMEDBSR/AA, Serial 065L43BJ600447J, manufactured June 2017) experienced a complete compressor failure at approximately 7 years of age. The refrigerator stopped cooling entirely while the internal temperature display continued to show normal temperatures (35F), creating a false sense of food safety. The actual interior temperature was significantly warmer, posing a food spoilage and potential foodborne illness risk.
The refrigerator was being used as intended  for household food and beverage storage in a residential home. No physical injuries occurred, however the deceptive temperature display prevented timely awareness of the failure, resulting in potential food safety hazards and significant food loss.
Additionally, the ice maker has required multiple replacements throughout the life of the appliance and continues to malfunction despite repeated repairs. This is a known defect in this product line.
Upon investigation, the compressor was found to have failed. This model (RF28HMEDBSR/AA) is among those specifically named in class action litigation regarding Samsung refrigerators failing to maintain safe temperatures. Both the recurring ice maker failures and the compressor failure appear consistent with known widespread defects in this product line affecting thousands of consumers.
That covers both issues and ties it to the known defect pattern which strengthens your complaint.

incidentDescription: Battleborn Model BB10012 battery failed with melted internal connection on positive terminal.

productDescription: It is a lithium iron phosphate battery that is designed for use in cabins, rvs and boats.
incidentDescription:
I have a [REDACTED] channel where I test batteries and solar equipment. I have found a major fire safety issue with multiple products from battleborn batteries. I am able to reproduce the issue in a brand new battery and I have my battery cycle machine to prove it. There are multiple spots on the product that can melt because the main terminal and supply connection has a piece of plastic that melts and creates a loose connection. Once this happens, the whole battery can melt and vent gases. I have multiple videos proving that this issue is reproducible and indeed a defect of the product. 

Once I posted my videos, many other people came forward with the same issue. I continued testing and found even more issues. Their larger battery does not have a mechanical connection between the cell packs, and if used in a high vibration environment, such as an RV or boat (which they are advertised to be used in), hot spots will occur and can cause a cell to vent. I had this happen in my backyard during testing and I captured the moment on camera. I have that posted in a [REDACTED]  video as well. 

There is a class action lawsuit named "[REDACTED]" where the plastic sandwhich electrical connection is called into question. The plantiff is the president of the [REDACTED]. He created many of the UL standards we use for this equipment, and even he is saying there is a major issue. 

For posting my videos, this company has filed a lawsuit against me for sharing the truth on this issue. I do not know what to do now because these batteries are in the field and people are still reporting melting batteries to this very day (this morning one was posted). Many people are also reporting that the plastic melts and the battery is dead without any abuse. One [REDACTED]even showed that 4 out of 6 of his batteries failed. Another member just posted that 11 out of 14 of his batteries are dead. When they are "dead" they have a loose connection and they are at risk for melting. This problem is found in the majority of peoples battery banks when they test them. There are many people who own these batteries and they are completely unaware of them having the issue. It is terrifying. When people reach out for a warranty claim, the company will blame them for improper installation. But it is a defect present in all batteries! They deny warranty claims left and right. 

I just dont know what to do anymore. I showed the issue, I tested new batteries and proved that it is a defect present in all of them, and now they are trying to sue me. These batteries are extremely dangerous and everyone doesnt know what to do. One of my forum members said I should post this to you guys and hopefully start and investigation. I have more proof than you can imagine. I have the test results, multiple tests on camera and more. I am also creating a database with users who are experincing these issues.

Also realize that this issue happens if you follow the companies advice for installation! And most of the failures that come to me are from factory installed systems. I will open a battery and find 2 sometimes 3 other hot spots and melting in the case. It is really bad.

The Defect: During factory assembly, the positive (+) and negative (-) wiring leads behind the main dual-battery connection port were crossed and connected in reverse polarity.
 The Incident & Progression: The vehicle initially exhibited irregular motor noise and progressive electrical resistance under normal operation. Upon attempting to isolate the issue with an authorized manufacturer-supplied component, the reversed polarity circuit caused a catastrophic backflow of current. This triggered a critical over-voltage loop, permanently destroying the electronic controller and locking out the main lithium-ion batteries.
 Certified Diagnostic Proof: A professional inspection conducted by certified technicians at an independent bicycle service center (LoweRiders Bikes & Boards) confirmed the reversed factory wiring loop. Testing of the heavy-duty lithium-ion batteries on the diagnostic bench revealed they are completely fried and permanently locked out, outputting an unrecoverable 3V due to internal protection circuit (BMS) failure caused by the manufacturer's surge.
3. Hazard Type & Public Safety Risk
 Primary Hazard: Electrical / Fire Hazard.
 Risk Assessment: Crossing positive and negative high-voltage lines on a high-capacity lithium-ion battery system creates an immediate risk of a catastrophic short circuit, thermal runaway, and battery fire. Had the internal Battery Management System (BMS) failed to sacrifice itself during the surge, a severe electrical fire could have occurred during operation or charging. This poses a systemic risk to all consumers operating the 2024 ENGWE LE20 model.
4. Manufacturer Response
The manufacturer was formally notified of the certified factory defect with photographic evidence of the dead voltage. The manufacturer refused to acknowledge the systemic assembly error or issue a safety replacement, instead using automated customer service scripts to run out the standard warranty timeline and shift financial liability for the hazardous components onto the consumer.

Where purchased- The Home Depot, Kauai, Hawaii

Genuine Makita 18-volt LXT lithium-ion rechargeable power-tool battery pack, 5.0 amp-hour capacity, with onboard LED charge-level indicator. Product identity is confirmed by the retained battery, which still bears the visible Makita logo and "5.0Ah" marking despite fire damage (photo available). The battery was being stored inside a parked work truck, with no tool or charger attached, when it underwent thermal runaway and ignited overnight, causing an explosion and interior fire. The damaged battery has been retained as evidence and is available for inspection.
incidentDescription:
A genuine Makita lithium ion battery that had been purchased new from an authorized retailer was stored in the back seat of our 2014 [REDACTED] pickup truck. The battery was not being charged, used, modified, or connected to any tool at the time of the incident. The truck was driven home at approximately [REDACTED], parked at our residence, and left unattended overnight.

Sometime during the night, the battery experienced a thermal failure and ignited inside the vehicle. The battery fire caused an explosion and burned through portions of the rear seat and surrounding interior components. The fire eventually self extinguished but continued to smolder.

The incident was discovered at approximately 830 AM on March 30, 2026, when my husband ([REDACTED]) opened the truck to leave for work and found extensive fire damage and smoke residue throughout the interior. Damage included burned seat materials, melted interior trim and plastic components, soot contamination, and a persistent chemical odor throughout the vehicle.

No person was using the battery when the incident occurred because it happened while the battery was being stored inside the parked vehicle. No physical injuries were reported. However, the incident created a significant fire hazard and had the potential to cause serious injury, death, or a larger structure fire if the fire had spread beyond the vehicle or occurred while occupants were present.

Following the incident, a licensed remediation company inspected the vehicle and classified the loss as a lithium ion battery thermal explosion originating from a Makita battery pack. The company found extensive soot contamination, chemical residue, and contamination of the vehicle ventilation system. The estimated cost of decontamination and remediation exceeds $16,000. The company further advised that complete elimination of odor and contamination cannot be guaranteed without replacement of major interior components, including seat materials and air distribution components. Based on the extent of the damage and remediation costs, we consider the vehicle a total loss. No mechanic shop will work on the vehicle until it is cleaned, and the cleaning costs sixteen thousand dollars just to address the toxic fumes. 

My husband relies on this truck for work and transportation. While we await Makita's response regarding this incident, he has had to continue using the vehicle because replacing it immediately is not financially feasible. We remain hopeful that the matter can be resolved promptly and fairly.

The battery and charger have been preserved and retained for inspection.

productDescription:

incidentDescription:
CPSC Office of Compliance and Field Operations,

I am reporting a substantial product hazard under 15 U.S.C. Section 2064 and
requesting investigation of manufacturer non-compliance with Section 15(b) reporting
obligations.

INCIDENT SUMMARY

On December 13, 2025, at approximately 40 mph 0.3 miles from my home during
normal operation, my InMotion V14 Adventure electric unicycle 50s
(Serial: A0311851800217C0, Activated: 2025-05-08, Mileage: approximately 1,292
miles) experienced a sudden, complete loss of motor stabilization without tilt-back,
audible warning, or pre-failure degradation. The controller ceased providing
stabilization instantaneously, resulting in a high-speed crash.
The crash as seen in the video is only 0.3 miles from my home, yet as the images show
below, it claims 1.6 miles which is what it would have been had I made it to the store
and back home. Luckily it was my father behind me in the vehicle recording and he
immediately brought me to the hospital as the injury images show, it would have been
impossible for me to have rode another 1.3 miles after the crash.

INJURY: acute radius break and ulna requiring four-hour surgery, a titanium plate and
eight screws, ongoing physical therapy, and pending hardware removal procedure due
to massive loss of mobility.
I am right-hand dominant and a sawmill owner. I am also an independent researcher
in HCI-IC. I have six years of college for a ba in math(csci major specializing in
robotics).
I am 42 years old and this vehicle was my main means of transportation and only
means of transportation to get to [REDACTED] over 12 miles away.
My riding data reflect my daily use and not a joyride for thrills.
My images of all seven months of my ride data show the hall sensor was silently failing
indicated by the mph spikes beyond the 43 mph so called tiltback and beeping alarm
you can hear and see was missing in the unedited video.
Medical records available upon request.
FAILURE MODE: Silent control-path failure - not envelope exceedance. Post-incident:
left hall sensor read error present; device exhibited uncontrolled motor runaway to
maximum RPM when powered. This indicates single-point control-path failure rather
than designed fail-safe behavior (torque reduction, speed clamping, tilt-back, or
degraded mode).
MANUFACTURER RESPONSE - DOCUMENTED EVASION AND ENDANGERMENT
I engaged InMotion customer support (Ticket: [REDACTED] / Request #[REDACTED])
beginning January 3, 2026, providing engineering failure report, video evidence, device
photos, and firmware information.
Critical timeline:
January 6-7, 2026: InMotion technical team reviewed available materials (video,
photos, cloud telemetry) and identified specific faulty hardware: Controller Assembly,
HMI Board PCBA Assembly, and [REDACTED] Display Board. Replacement of these
assemblies was advised to restore app connectivity and support further diagnostics.
January 7-14, 2026: Despite having identified faulty boards, InMotion instructed me -
while I was recovering from surgery to my dominant hand - to reassemble and power
the device to upload logs. Upon powering the controller with all components
connected, the wheel immediately accelerated to uncontrolled maximum RPM
runaway. I was fortunate my young son was not in the path of the device. This was not
a diagnostic step. This was energizing a known-faulty control system in a residential
environment. I refused further physical handling of the device after this event.
January 20, 2026: Without new technical evidence, InMotion pivoted to undetermined
cause framing - either due to faulty internal component or pushing the EUC over its
limits - and demanded I purchase a replacement controller to retrieve logs, despite:
(a) prior identification of faulty components; (b) documented runaway behavior
making the device unsafe to handle; (c) my surgical recovery status.
January 30, 2026: One-time exception offer: purchase new V14 50S for 2,499 USD
(standard market price).
February 28, 2026: New narrative introduced: Our technical team reviewed the
historical logs associated with the device and identified multiple instances of
overspeed riding, including recorded overspeed warnings. This narrative omits the
uncontrolled runaway triggered by their own instructions. It contradicts six months of
conservative riding, video evidence, their January 7 hardware-fault determination, and
the silent nature of the original cutout.
March 4, 2026: Formal evidence preservation notice issued. InMotion refused to
confirm preservation, refused corporate legal contact, and reiterated purchase
discount offer.
March 26, 2026: [REDACTED], Director of North America, initiated unsolicited P6 sales
outreach - side-channel engagement after safety-incident escalation was refused.
EVIDENCE OF DATA POSSESSION
Through network traffic analysis of the InMotion [REDACTED] application
([REDACTED]), I documented continuous real-time telemetry upload to
manufacturer-controlled cloud infrastructure ([REDACTED]) and
[REDACTED] infrastructure ([REDACTED]). This
contradicts InMotion's repeated claims that post-incident log upload was impossible
due to destroyed [REDACTED] connectivity.
Approximately February 2026, InMotion implemented certificate pinning/hardening in
the application, preventing further independent audit of data flows. A full application
overhaul followed. These actions occurred after I cited federal regulatory reporting
obligations and documented their data architecture.
REQUESTED ACTION
1. Open defect investigation of InMotion V14 control-path architecture, specifically
single-point failure modes resulting in instantaneous loss of stabilization without rider
warning or agency.
2. Subpoena manufacturer records including: raw ride telemetry for SN
A0311851800217C0; internal technical notes from January 6-7 review;
communications authorizing withdrawal of hardware-fault determination; and records
of any other V14 incidents involving silent cutout or control-path failure.
3. Investigate Section 15(b) non-compliance - InMotion had knowledge of hardware
fault and catastrophic failure mode by January 7, 2026, yet failed to report to CPSC
and instead pursued consumer-level containment.
4. Preserve third-party records - Notification to [REDACTED] of relevant data
custody for SN A0311851800217C0 telemetry.
5. Investigate manufacturer instructions creating secondary hazard - InMotion
directed a recovering surgical patient to re-energize a device they had identified as
containing faulty control electronics, resulting in uncontrolled motor runaway in a

incidentDescription:
While mowing my lawn with the Kobalt cordless electric lawn mower (Product# KSPM 1040B-03, Date code 0324 Serial # 001406), I released the bail control arm to stop the blades to avoid and clear a hazard, but the blades did not stop spinning.  I tried pulling and releasing the arm several times, but the blades continued to run. In order to stop the blades from running, I reached down and pulled out the battery. 

When the battery was reinserted, I was unable to get the blades to resume operation. The device powers on properly and is able to self-propel with the wheels, but the blades will not spin.

Earlier in the day, it had rained on the unit. I believe the issue was caused by water entering one of the safety interlock switches, holding the switch closed when the control arm was released. This obviously poses a significant safety hazard, if the blades do not stop when the bail arm is released, the blades cannot be quickly halted in the event of a child/animal/object entering the cutting surface of the lawnmower.

productDescription: Grilla Mammoth (vertical pellet smoker)
incidentDescription:
I purchased a Grilla Mammoth pellet grill in January 2025 (order number [REDACTED], serial code vs1c6920829f93, firmware version 1.0.26). As of the date of this incident, it had been used a total of three times.

On the night of June 7, 2026, I began an overnight brisket cook at approximately 11:30 PM. I monitored the grill remotely through the Grilla app overnight and observed no problems. The following morning, I found the grill door open and very difficult to close. Even when forced shut with the latch engaged, the door would not fully seal.

I have a [REDACTED] camera system that records the area where the grill is located. I reviewed the footage to determine what had occurred. The footage carries a burned-in on-screen timestamp and captured the failure as follows:

- At approximately [REDACTED] AM, the grill began smoking heavily, with smoke billowing out of the exhaust. The exhaust was not obstructed.
- At [REDACTED] AM, a first explosion pushed the door outward so that it was no longer fully sealed, though not fully open. Immediately after this, smoke began escaping from the seam of the door as well, whereas before the explosion smoke had come only from the exhaust.
- At [REDACTED] AM, a second, larger explosion occurred, producing a fireball that blew the door fully open.

I reached the grill approximately 20 to 25 minutes after the explosions. The door was open and light smoke was coming from the pellet hopper. I briefly increased the temperature to push the remaining fire out of the pellet hopper area while the door was open, then shut the unit down.

No one was injured and there was no damage to my home or deck. However, the grill had only been used three times since purchase in January 2025, and the failure, an unattended explosion and fireball, clearly presents a risk of serious injury and structural fire had anyone been nearby or had the unit been closer to combustible structures.

I have preserved time-stamped video footage of the incident, the grill unit, and the pellets used.

incidentDescription:
I am writing to report a burn injury that occurred when I came into contact with the exterior of a Solo Stove fire pit while visiting a neighbor's home.
I was not the owner of the product and had never used one before. I had no reason to believe that the exterior metal surface would become hot enough to cause a burn. Based on the appearance of the product and its double-walled smokeless design, I assumed the outer surface would remain relatively cool or at least would not present an immediate burn hazard from brief contact.

My concern is that visitors, children, and other individuals who are not familiar with the product may reasonably assume that the exterior surface is safe to touch or brush against. I believe the risk of contact burns could be reduced through more prominent exterior warnings, improved hazard communication, or design modifications that limit the temperature of surfaces that people are likely to contact. incidentDescription:
The product is a Bonavita 1L Digital Variable Temperature Gooseneck Electric Kettle, 1200 watt, stainless steel, model BV382510V. I purchased it through Amazon on November 25, 2025 and use it at home to heat water for coffee.

In early May 2026 it developed a hazardous defect. It continues boiling after the power is switched off and cannot be stopped using its controls. The only way to make it stop heating is to unplug it from the wall outlet.

The defect has worsened over time. The kettle has begun producing steam even when it contains very little water, has boiled itself dry, and on the most recent occasion I detected a smell of smoke. No injuries have occurred, but I consider this a serious fire, burn, and scald hazard. An appliance that will not stop heating and runs itself dry poses a significant risk of fire or injury, particularly if left unattended or operating overnight.

I reported the defect to the product's distributor, who acknowledged the hazard in writing, advised me to discontinue use and keep the kettle unplugged, and agreed to send a replacement. Several weeks later no replacement has arrived and the company has stopped responding to my messages. I have a video demonstrating the kettle continuing to boil after being switched off, along with the full email correspondence documenting the company's acknowledgment of the hazard.

productDescription:
The product is a MAXSHOT Electric Scooter purchased through Amazon from a third-party seller. It is a two-wheeled standing electric scooter intended for personal transportation and recreational use.

The scooter is primarily black in color and includes a metal frame, handlebars, an electric motor, front and rear wheels, a standing deck, and a rechargeable battery. The scooter is designed to be ridden in a standing position and is marketed for everyday transportation and recreational riding.

The product had been used for approximately 1.5 years before the incident occurred. The failure involved the main structural stem/frame area connecting the handlebars and front wheel assembly. This load-bearing component suddenly cracked and separated during normal use.

The scooter had not been modified, altered, or subjected to unusual use. It was used on normal paved residential roads and sidewalks in accordance with its intended purpose.

I can provide photographs showing the scooter and the structural fracture of the main frame/stem assembly.
incidentDescription:
I am reporting a potential safety hazard involving a MAXSHOT electric scooter purchased from a third-party seller on Amazon.

The scooter was used under normal conditions for approximately one and a half years before the main structural stem/frame suddenly cracked and separated during normal riding. The failure occurred at a major load-bearing part of the scooter.

At the time of the incident, the scooter was being used by a 13-year-old child. The rider was using the scooter normally on a paved residential roadway and was not performing stunts, jumping, racing, or misusing the product. The scooter had not been modified.

When the frame/stem failed, the rider lost control and fell from the scooter. Fortunately, no motor vehicles were nearby at the time of the incident. No physical injuries required medical treatment, and the rider did not need to visit a hospital. However, the structural failure created a serious risk of injury, including the possibility of head injury, broken bones, or being struck by traffic if the incident had occurred under different circumstances.

The product's main structural component should not fail during ordinary use. In my opinion, this represents a significant consumer product safety concern because a sudden structural failure can cause riders to fall without warning.

This machine has been used daily to brew beverages consumed by myself, family members, and visiting friends for an estimated 2-3 years or maybe more. incidentDescription: On Monday, May 25, 2026, my 14-year-old son was riding the Eskute RT-X 6500W electric motorcycle when two independent safety systems failed simultaneously, causing him to crash and sustain injuries.Product information: The product is the Eskute RT-X 6500W Electric Dirt Bike, manufactured by Eskute, purchased on Amazon.com. The bike has a 72V 30Ah battery, 6500 watt peak motor, 53 plus mph top speed, and is marketed to riders 5 feet 6 inches to 6 feet 7 inches tall.Who was using the product: My 14-year-old son, who is 6 feet 1 inch tall and 155 pounds, within the manufacturers stated rider specifications. He was wearing a helmet and protective equipment.How the product was being used: The bike was being used as intended for off-road riding under normal conditions. The bike was stock and unmodified, operating normally up to the moment of failure.Failure mode 1, Throttle stuck wide open: The throttle stuck in the wide-open or full power position with no rider input maintaining it. Releasing the throttle did not return it to the closed or off position. Power continued to be delivered to the motor without rider input.Failure mode 2, Brake-actuated throttle cutoff failed: The Eskute RT-X is equipped with brake levers designed to trigger an automatic throttle cutoff when brakes are applied, a standard safety feature on this class of electric motorcycle. My son applied the brakes in response to the stuck throttle. The throttle cutoff did not engage. Power continued to the motor despite brake application.Injuries: Unable to slow the bike, my son chose to lay it down to stop it, pinning the bike beneath his body during the crash. He sustained cuts and abrasions to his hand where his fingers were pinched between the brake lever and handlebar. He did not strike his head and was wearing a helmet. Injuries were treated at home with cleaning, antibiotic ointment, and bandaging. He has been monitored for 24 plus hours with no complications. Injuries are stable and improving.Concerns: Both primary safety systems failed simultaneously with no warning. This represents a serious safety defect with potential to injure or kill other riders, particularly young riders who may not have the experience to make split-second crash-avoidance decisions when controls fail. The simultaneous failure of throttle return and brake-actuated cutoff on a 6500 watt, 53 plus mph vehicle is a foreseeable injury or fatality risk that warrants investigation.Actions taken: Battery has been removed from the bike and stored separately. The bike has been preserved as-is with no further use, modification, or attempted repair. Photographs have been taken of the bike, throttle assembly, brake levers, crash damage, and injuries. The manufacturer Eskute has been notified by email at support.us@eskute.com on May 25, 2026. An A-to-z Guarantee claim has been filed with Amazon under order number [REDACTED].

productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
Under normal everyday use, the power cord and plug on this unit became extremely hot and began melting, producing a strong electrical burning smell. My wife and I discovered this as a fire hazard in our kitchen. No injury or property damage occurred, but the risk was clear. Photos of the damaged cord and plug were submitted to Cuisinart's consumer service team. Cuisinart declined to replace the unit citing the warranty period.

(07/17/2026) Following my initial report, Cuisinart's claims team contacted me and requested I send the unit in for engineering evaluation, which I did in good faith. I also completed their questionnaire thoroughly, disclosing all relevant details upfront.
Cuisinart's engineering team subsequently issued findings that contradicted my submitted documentation. They attributed the defect to the unit being placed too close to a wall, a conclusion that is physically inconsistent with the actual damage, which was isolated to the plug at the far end of the cord. My claim was denied a second time.
I formally disputed their findings in writing. Cuisinart responded with a form letter that addressed none of my specific points and blamed me for the issue.
Cuisinart requested I send the unit to them for evaluation using a prepaid label they provided. After completing their evaluation and issuing findings that I formally disputed, they have stopped responding entirely.
Cuisinart is now retaining my personal property without authorization. Despite multiple formal written demands for its return at their expense, I have received no response whatsoever.
It is worth noting that Cuisinart solicited the physical evidence of the safety malfunction, conducted a disputed evaluation, and then went silent while remaining in possession of that evidence. The unit, which documented the fire hazard defect I originally reported, is now in their hands with no path to independent verification of their findings.
A formal complaint has also been filed with the California Attorney General's office.
I am providing this update to ensure the complete record of Cuisinart's handling of this safety concern is documented

productDescription: Black Baseus battery
incidentDescription:
To Whom It May Concern,

This letter serves as a formal demand for investigation, accountability, and compensation arising from a dangerous and defective consumer product that resulted in a residential fire and placed my child at risk of serious harm.

I purchased a Baseus 65W 30000mAh Portable Charger BS-30KP365 through Amazon in December 2024. The original unit was later subject to a recall. On January 2, 2025, I was issued a replacement unit of the same model (BS-30KP365), Serial Number: FSD240906A.

At no time prior to or following the replacement did I receive any direct recall notice, safety warning, or instruction to discontinue use of the product.

In April 2026, the replacement battery catastrophically failed, exploded, and caused a fire in my daughters bedroom. This incident created an immediate threat to her life and resulted in significant emotional distress and property damage.

According to the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission recall notice, replacement units bearing serial numbers ending in A were distributed as a remedy and represented as safe. The replacement unit I received falls within that category. Despite this, the product failed in the exact manner the recall was intended to prevent. This constitutes a failure of the recall remedy and raises serious concerns regarding ongoing product safety and recall execution.

This matter involves, but is not limited to:
- Distribution of a defective and hazardous product  
- Failure to provide adequate recall notice and consumer warning  
- Failure of an official recall remedy  
- Negligence in product safety and consumer protection obligations  

As a result, I am demanding the following:

1. A full and documented investigation into the manufacturing, recall, and replacement process for model BS-30KP365  
2. All records related to the recall, including notification timelines, internal safety findings, and replacement distribution logs  
3. Preservation of all evidence and communications related to this product and my case  
4. Compensation for property damage, emotional distress, and any associated costs incurred as a result of this incident

productDescription: Oakford 1125
incidentDescription:
I am filing a complaint against Nexgrill Industries regarding repeated product failures and refusal to provide a fair resolution.

I purchased two Nexgrill Oakford 1125 pellet grills and, due to failures, assembled three separate units. After the initial failures, Nexgrill sent a replacement unit. That replacement also failed and showed the same issues, confirming this is not an isolated defect.

All units exhibited the same problems: inability to maintain temperature (dropping to ~120F unless set to maximum), repeated E4 error codes, and inconsistent pellet feed.

More concerning, I discovered what appears to be melted or deformed metal debris inside the firebox area, along with a strong burning electrical/metal smell that persisted even after the unit was powered off for several days. This presents a serious safety concern.

I provided photos, documentation, and detailed explanations. Nexgrill initially acknowledged the issue and issued a partial reimbursement (cover and taxes), indicating acceptance of the claim. However, they later reversed course, stating they are unable to validate receipts, and are now refusing to proceed.

They are offering further troubleshooting or retrieval of the unit, which is not reasonable after multiple failed units, including their own replacement.

I am requesting a total reimbursement of $1,300, which includes:

Cost of two defective grills
Grill cover
Multiple bags of pellets wasted due to product failure
Time and effort assembling three separate units

This is a documented pattern of failure, not user error. Nexgrills inconsistent handling and refusal to stand behind their product is unacceptable. I am seeking full and fair resolution.

UPDATED ON 5/6/2026: [Summary of Incident
During normal operation, the grill experienced a catastrophic malfunction that generated heat levels sufficient to melt internal metal components. This was not a surface grease fire or misuse scenario—this was an apparent internal mechanical or electrical failure.   They have attempted to fabricate that I introduced something to the hopper causing the malfunction and also that they cannot validate my purchases.  
The grill exceeded 550°F, and based on the observed damage, likely reached significantly higher internal temperatures. If this unit had been positioned closer to my home or any combustible structure, it could have resulted in a structure fire.
Additionally, I observed metal debris and abnormal material inside the unit, consistent with internal component failure (potentially from the auger or fire pot system). This raises serious concerns about:
•	Uncontrolled combustion
•	Component failure under normal use
•	Risk of fire and/or injury to consumers

•	Failed to offer a replacement unit or financial reimbursement
•	Avoided confirming how the unit would be handled or tested upon return

Given the nature of this failure and the potential safety risk, this request raises serious concerns about:

•	Lack of transparency in failure analysis

Safety Concerns
This incident presents multiple risks to consumers:
•	Fire hazard due to uncontrolled temperature escalation

•	Lack of safeguards to prevent catastrophic overheating
Request for Investigation
