It should be noted that this unit is a replacement sent to me by Ecowell after the first one suffered a melted tip-over switch, for which I filed a separate report at the time. The new unit was being used on short-pile office carpet under a desk. It has not been turned on in at least a day. It doesn't have any kind of timer function or thermostat. I smelled something burning and started immediately shutting off equipment, starting with the soldering iron on my bench, and as I was hunting for the source of the smell, the heater made a buzzing noise and the display flickered. The unit remains in our possession, and photographs of the damage are available. We also have a copy of the original purchase receipt, which was located in my mothers email records.

productDescription: Segway Ninebot Max G2 electric scooter
incidentDescription:
To the Office of Compliance and Field Operations: 

I am writing to formally request that the Consumer Product Safety Commission open an in-depth investigation into the Segway Ninebot Max 02 electric scooter and evaluate whether a mandatory safety recall is warranted. I make this request after experiencing repeated and identical safety failures across three separate replacement units of the same model. These failures are not minor inconveniences. They present a substantial risk of loss of control, rider ejection, and serious bodily injury. 

I am a California resident and purchased this scooter from Best Buy in San Carlos, California. I selected the Segway Ninebot Max 02 based on the manufacturer's marketing claims of stability, durability, and enhanced safety systems. Instead, what I have experienced is a recurring pattern of mechanical and firmware-related defects that make the device unpredictable and unsafe at normal operating speeds.

The most alarming issue involves what I can only describe as sudden and aggressive braking behavior at or near top speed. The scooter is advertised as capable of reaching approximately 22 miles per hour. In real-world use, particularly when riding downhill, the scooter may reach 23 to 24 miles per hour. Under these conditions, the regenerative braking system abruptly engages with excessive force. This is not a gradual or controlled speed regulation. It feels like an instantaneous braking event that causes a forward jolt strong enough to shift the rider's center of gravity. 

This braking action occurs without meaningful warning and without rider input. The handlebars lurch forward, the front end dips, and the rider must immediately compensate to avoid being thrown. In traffic or in a crowded pedestrian environment, such a sudden destabilizing force could easily result in a crash. At 22 miles per hour, the margin for error is extremely small. A momentary loss of balance at that speed can result in head injury, fractures, or harm to bystanders. 

The critical point is that this behavior has occurred on every replacement unit I have received. This is not an isolated defect tied to one serial number. It appears to be systemic, likely related to firmware calibration or a flawed implementation of regenerative braking logic tied to overspeed detection. Whether the root cause is software or hardware, the effect is the same: unpredictable, forceful braking that compromises rider control. 

The second ongoing issue involves persistent handlebar instability. On each unit, the steering stem either arrived with noticeable play or developed it shortly after minimal use. I followed all assembly instructions carefully. I tightened the fasteners using appropriate tools and confirmed that torque was applied correctly. Despite this, lateral movement in the handlebars remains. The play is not cosmetic. It affects steering precision. 

Even slight looseness in a steering column at higher speeds can amplify into wobble or misalignment. In an emergency maneuver, that instability can prevent accurate control. This is not a case of routine maintenance being neglected. It appears to be either a tolerance defect in the stem assembly or a structural weakness in the internal joint design. Again, the issue has repeated itself across multiple units. 

Compounding these safety concerns is the response I have received from the manufacturer. I have documented my complaints with Segway customer support on multiple occasions. In one recent case, the company returned a replacement scooter to me with a damaged display and continued steering instability. These issues were minimized as cosmetic, despite the fact that steering looseness is inherently a safety concern. The relevant customer service case number is [REDACTED]. 

From my perspective, the pattern suggests that Segway is aware of these recurring issues but continues distributing replacement units without implementing corrective design changes. Sending consumers additional scooters that exhibit the same hazardous characteristics does not resolve the underlying defect. It perpetuates it. 

As a California consumer, I am also mindful of the protections afforded under the Song-Beverly Consumer Warranty Act. When a product cannot be repaired to conform to express warranties after a reasonable number of attempts, the consumer is entitled to meaningful relief. However, beyond warranty rights, my concern here is public safety. Electric scooters are widely used by teenagers, commuters, and riders in dense urban environments. A systemic braking defect combined with steering instability creates a foreseeable risk of injury not only to riders but also to pedestrians and motorists. 

I have preserved all relevant evidence, including the damaged shipping carton, the defective unit, and correspondence with the manufacturer. I am fully willing to cooperate with any inquiry conducted by the Commission. If necessary, I would welcome a field investigator to inspect the scooter and observe the braking behavior under controlled conditions. 

This product is marketed as a safe and premium mobility device. In its current condition, it behaves unpredictably at normal operating speeds. The fact that three separate units have exhibited materially identical defects strongly indicates that the issue is not isolated. It is either a design flaw, a firmware calibration failure, or a structural weakness in the steering assembly. 

For these reasons, I respectfully request that the Consumer Product Safety Commission initiate an In-Depth Investigation into the Segway Ninebot Max 02 and evaluate whether a safety recall or corrective action is warranted. incidentDescription:

The product is a consumer smartphone (Google Pixel 7) used by an adult user as a personal mobile device for standard phone functions (calls, messaging, apps, and daily use). The device was not being used for any specialized purpose.

The issue was first noticed when the screen began separating from the device body, consistent with internal battery expansion. At that point, the device was immediately powered off and removed from use due to safety concerns. The phone has remained unused since that time.

No physical injury has occurred. However, the condition presents a potential safety hazard, as swollen lithium-ion batteries are widely known to carry risk of overheating, fire, or damage to property if continued to be used or left in an enclosed environment.

The issue was reported to the manufacturer, but no free repair or replacement was provided, and only out-of-pocket repair was offered despite the safety nature of the defect.

productDescription: RadonAway GX4 Pro Series radon mitigation fa
incidentDescription:
A RadonAway GX4 Pro Series radon mitigation fan was professionally installed by [REDCATED] in a private residence in September 2024 as part of an active soil depressurization system designed to protect household occupants from radon gas exposure. The fan failed completely within approximately five months of installation, in February 2025. A replacement GX4 fan was installed at that time. That replacement fan has also failed completely, in March 2026  less than 13 months after it was installed.

The product is a continuous-duty inline radon mitigation fan intended to run 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. The fan was being used exactly as intended  as a permanently installed, continuously operating component of a residential radon mitigation system.

No physical injuries occurred. However, each fan failure results in the radon mitigation system becoming non-operational, meaning radon gas  a Class A carcinogen and the second leading cause of lung cancer in the United States  is no longer being actively vented from beneath the home. During each failure period, household occupants are exposed to potentially elevated radon levels without awareness that the system has stopped functioning, unless they are actively monitoring with a separate radon detector.

The concern being reported is that the RadonAway GX4 is failing significantly short of its expected and warranted service life. Industry-standard radon fans are expected to operate continuously for 510 years. This product has now failed twice within 18 months under normal residential operating conditions. A review of consumer complaints submitted to the [REDACTED] and posted in [REDACTED] reviews for the installing contractor reveals a pattern of identical premature failures reported by multiple homeowners using this same product. The repeated failure of this product creates a recurring and unpredictable lapse in radon protection for household occupants.

productDescription: The product is an automatic baby formula preparation machine that measures, mixes, and dispenses powdered infant formula and water to prepare bottles for infant feeding. The unit uses an internal auger and mixing system to deliver a preset ratio of formula and water based on user-selected settings. It is intended to provide consistent, accurate, and safe preparation of infant formula.
incidentDescription:
We began using an automatic baby formula preparation machine (Baby Brezza Formula Pro) that had been received as a baby shower gift and was unopened prior to use. During normal operation, the machine consistently failed to dispense formula powder correctly.

The device performs only a partial powder cycle and dispenses mostly water into the bottle. There are no error messages or alerts, and the machine appears to function normally despite producing an improperly mixed bottle.

The product is intended to prepare infant formula by automatically measuring and mixing powdered formula with water. It was being used as directed to prepare bottles for infant feeding.

The product was being used by a caregiver (parent) to prepare bottles for an infant.

The issue occurs almost every use and is reproducible. The only temporary improvement occurs after running a water-only cycle, after which the problem returns within a few uses.

No injury has occurred at this time. However, the malfunction results in inconsistently diluted formula, which may pose a risk of improper nutrition for an infant if not identified. Because the device provides no warning and appears to operate normally, a caregiver may unknowingly feed diluted formula.

productDescription:
Product Name: 2026 Velotric Discover M
Type: Mid-Drive Electric Bicycle (Class 2 / Class 3 E-bike)
Color: Platinum Silver
Size: Large
Estimated Weight: Approximately 66 lbs
Key Components: Equipped with a mid-drive VeloCore motor and Tektro hydraulic disc brakes on both the front and rear wheels.

Purpose & Usage: This product is designed and marketed as an urban commuter e-bike. It is used daily for high-traffic city commuting in Manhattan and is equipped to carry a child passenger using a rear-mounted child seat.
incidentDescription:
What happened that made you want to report?
I am reporting a catastrophic structural failure and systemic factory assembly defect on a new electric bicycle purchased less than a month ago. While riding, the primary rear braking system completely failed. All six mounting bolts for the rear disc brake rotor detached or sheared simultaneously, resulting in a total loss of rear braking power and motor control. Upon inspection, the aluminum rear hub flange had fractured, with at least one bolt eyelet snapped off entirely. Additionally, inspecting the front wheel revealed that the factory-applied white witness marks (torque stripes) on the front rotor bolts had already drifted significantly. This proves the front bolts are actively backing out as well, indicating a severe factory-level failure to properly torque or apply thread-locker to critical braking systems.

What type of product(s) were being used?
A 2026 Velotric Discover M, which is a mid-drive Class 1/2/3 electric bicycle.

Who was using the product(s)?
I was operating the bicycle. I am a 40-year-old male.

How were the product(s) being used?
I was using the e-bike for my daily urban commute in high-traffic city streets in Manhattan, traveling at approximately 20mph. This bicycle is also heavily relied upon to transport my young child on a rear-mounted child seat.

Were there any injuries that happened or may have happened while using the product?
Fortunately, no injuries occurred during this specific incident. However, there was a critical, life-threatening risk of severe injury to both myself and my child passengers.

How did any injuries occur?
While no injuries occurred, a severe crash was narrowly avoided. If the detached rear rotor had jammed against the frame at that speed, it would have instantly locked the rear wheel in heavy traffic. Furthermore, because the factory assembly defect also affects the front brake bolts, an imminent failure of the front rotor would likely lock the front fork, instantly ejecting the rider and any passenger over the handlebars.

The unit is powered by an internal, non-user-replaceable lithium-ion battery rated at 3.7 volts and 3,000 milliamp-hours, charged from a 5V / 1.0A DC supply via the included cable.
The Parent Display pairs wirelessly with a companion nursery camera to stream live video and audio of an infant to the parent. It is designed to be carried throughout the home and placed on nightstands, counters, or similar surfaces. The housing is white plastic with ventilation/speaker grilles on the rear flanking a central battery compartment cover behind which the regulatory label is affixed.
Identifying markings on the unit include: Model MO183, Serial Number M0183MEAC235301155, FCC ID MNJ-MO183DTX, IC 4703B-MO183DTX, CAN ICES-003(B)/NMB-003(B), and "2023 Dorel Juvenile Group, Columbus, IN." The unit is labeled "Made in China / Fabrique en Chine."

incidentDescription:
On April 19th 2026, I observed that the Parent Display unit of my Maxi-Cosi See Pro 360 Baby Monitor (Model MO183, S/N M0183MEAC235301155) had come apart. The front bezel and LCD touchscreen assembly had been forcibly separated from the plastic housing. The device had been used normally  charged with the manufacturer-supplied cable, kept at room temperature, not dropped, not exposed to moisture, and not modified or opened. The unit was approximately 1 1/2 years old at the time of failure and was a gift from my parents for our newborn.

The product is marketed and sold for use in monitoring infants and is typically kept in close proximity to a sleeping child. The Parent Display in my home was used in the same room as my infant son. A swollen lithium-ion cell presents documented risks of thermal runaway, fire, and venting of flammable and toxic gases. Had the swelling progressed further  or had I attempted to charge the unit after the swelling began  the failure could have resulted in a fire or chemical exposure event in my child's sleeping environment.

No fire, injury, or property damage has occurred to date. However, the unit is no longer safe to use, cannot be charged, and cannot be repaired because the manufacturer's own user manual states that the battery is not user-replaceable. productDescription:
Electric self-balancing unicycle designed for recreational use, primarily marketed for beginners and children. The product operates using a single motorized wheel with dynamic balance control. It includes audible warning alerts and tilt-back mechanisms intended to prevent unsafe riding conditions.
The device is battery powered and controlled via a mobile application. At the time of the incident, the battery level was approximately 50 percent and the device was functioning normally prior to the sudden shutdown.
A critical safety concern is that under certain conditions, the device can abruptly shut down while in motion, which immediately removes balancing capability and results in a fall.
incidentDescription:
Product: INMOTION E20 Electric Unicycle
An abrupt shutdown occurred while my 8 year old son was riding the device on a slight downhill residential street. Prior to the shutdown, the device emitted warning beeps. However, before the rider had sufficient time to safely decelerate, the unit shut down completely.
Because this is a self balancing device, the sudden loss of power resulted in an immediate and unavoidable loss of balance, causing a fall and physical injury.
The device had sufficient battery at the time, approximately 50 percent, and there were no modifications or abnormal usage conditions beyond normal residential riding.
The incident was witnessed by two children, and photos and app data were captured immediately afterward without any modification to the device.
Manufacturer Response:
The manufacturer reviewed diagnostic logs and stated in writing that abrupt shutdown under certain conditions such as overload or overspeed is expected behavior and part of the system protection logic.
Safety Concern:
For a self balancing device, an abrupt shutdown directly causes a fall and creates a foreseeable injury risk. The warning system did not provide sufficient time or margin for safe recovery before shutdown.
This raises concern that the product design allows a failure mode where rider injury is unavoidable.
I am reporting this as a potential product safety hazard that may warrant further investigation and review.

incidentDescription:
A portable rechargeable lithium-ion battery pack purchased from Amazon ignited and caused a fire inside a
parked vehicle. The product is identified as: Brand: IGGPBB Portable Charger 50000mAh Power Bank, 22.5W
fast charging with built-in cables. The item was purchased on or around January 11, 2026 via Amazon and
was sold by a third-party seller identified as [REDACTED]. At the time of the incident, the battery pack was not
actively in use or charging. It was stored inside the vehicle on the front passenger seat area, within or near
personal belongings. The vehicle was parked outdoors and not in operation. There was no external
damage, impact, or known misuse of the product prior to the incident. The fire appears to have originated
at the location where the battery pack was placed. The product is believed to have experienced a lithium-ion
battery failure (thermal runaway), resulting in overheating and/or explosion, which ignited surrounding
materials including clothing and the vehicles interior upholstery. The fire caused significant damage to the

area, and heat/smoke damage extending upward to the headliner and overhead components. The extent of
the damage may render the vehicle a total loss. No individuals were inside the vehicle at the time of the

had it occurred while the vehicle was occupied or in motion. The product had been used in a normal and
intended manner prior to the incident. There were no modifications made to the device and no known
misuse. The remains of the battery pack and surrounding damaged materials have been preserved.
Photographic documentation of the damage and fire origin area is available. Amazon order details, product

request. This incident represents a serious safety hazard involving a high-capacity lithium-ion battery

brand: Starbucks 2026 White Icey Leak Proof SS 40 oz Tumb
incidentDescription:
NWT Starbucks 2026 White Icey Leak Proof SS 40 oz Tumbler with Handle
The images show a clear manufacturing defect in the straw assembly of the NWT Starbucks 2026 White Icey Leak-Proof Stainless Steel 40 oz tumbler. Specifically, the issue appears to originate at the screw-in straw seal interface, where the clear plastic outer housing meets the inner straw component.

At that junction, there is a visible gap and irregular sealing surface. The plastic components do not form a uniform, airtight barrier. Instead, there are small voids and micro-crevices around the seam. These imperfections allow liquid and condensation to migrate into the enclosed portion of the straw assembly.

Because the straw system is designed as a sealed, non-serviceable unit, this trapped moisture cannot be accessed or removed through normal cleaning. Over time, the retained liquid creates a persistently damp environment inside the sealed cavity. The second image shows dark discoloration forming in a ring pattern within the internal channel, consistent with mold or microbial growth developing in areas that remain wet and oxygen-exposed.

Additional contributing factors include:

The presence of textured or rough plastic edges inside the seam, which can trap residue and promote biofilm formation.
A lack of drainage or airflow within the sealed compartment, preventing drying after washing.
The inability to disassemble the straw for proper sanitation, making routine cleaning ineffective.

In practical terms, the defect results in a hidden contamination zone inside a consumer drinking component. Even when the visible portions of the straw appear clean, internal mold growth can persist and potentially spread.

This is not a typical wear issue. It is indicative of a design or manufacturing flaw in the seal geometry or assembly tolerances, where the interface fails to prevent fluid ingress while also preventing user access for cleaning.

productDescription:
Manufacturer: Ride1Up
Model: Roadster v3 e-bike
Size: Large
Purchased: June 27, 2025
incidentDescription:
Due to what I believe is a faulty design, my e-bike crashed on a busy paved road. I broke four ribs, two of them in multiple places, and suffered bleeding around my lungs as well as significant abrasions on my knee and elbow and minor hand and wrist pain (no additional breaks). I was admitted to the hospital and spent two days there for treatment of the injuries and the pain with morphine and fentanyl. Doctors prescribed me strong prescription pain meds. A week later I returned to the emergency room in severe pain, when a new set of CT scans and X-rays disclosed the extent of my injuries was worse than doctors first realized. I am still recovering more than five weeks later. The cause of this accident: The front fender/mud guard is attached to the frame by a single bolt between the forks. (Please see attached photos. Note that the horizontal arms attaching the forks to the fender/mud guard do not stop the fender/mud guard from dropping vertically into the wheel. They only dampen lateral movement of the fender/mud guard.) This single bolt screws in upward into the fame and away from the ground. Gravity pulls this bolt downward toward the ground and away from the bike frame. The act of riding the bike causes vibration that further loosens it. In my case, the bolt came completely detached from the frame while riding downhill. This caused the fender/mud guard to fall into the front wheel and instantly lock up the front wheel at 20-30mph. This sent me flying, and my body crashed violently onto the pavement on my back, breaking four ribs. The crash occurred on a busy road. Luckily, no car was immediately behind me on this narrow road, or it would have run me over. 
I first noticed the nut backing out a few months after purchasing the bike. What tipped me off was an odd rubbing sound coming from the front wheel. This caused me to remove the front wheel and discover the bolt halfway backed out of the frame. At that time I tightened the bolt back into the frame, which fixed the problem -- temporarily, as I learned when I crashed. 
At minimum, this bolt should be secured by Loctite or a similar compound. Ideally, the bolt should be redesigned so that it cannot be unscrewed or backed out without high torque. Vibration from riding the bike should never cause it to back out. I worry other riders of this bike are also at risk.

productDescription: The company name is WattCycle. Product name is "Wattcycle LiFePO4 2560Wh 25.6v 100Ah" and their similar product that is equally hazardous is "Wattcycle LiFePO4 1280Wh 12.8v 100Ah". The dimensions are 19 x 9.4 x 6.6 inches for the 25.6v 100Ah model. The 12.8v model is roughly half the size. The battery case is black, with the wattcycle logo on each side, with product specifications printed on the sticker.  These batteries are used in RVs, boats, solar energy storage systems, backup power, etc.
manufacturer: SHENZHEN WASHI ENERGY CO., LTD. dba WattCycle
incidentDescription: The battery company "WattCycle" is selling chemically unstable and unsafe batteries, advertised as "Grade A" (brand new). When a LiFePO4 battery is severely undercharged below 2.5 volts (the manufacturers specified max cutoff limit) the battery is to be considered scrap and must be discarded appropriately. I have recieved a lithium battery from them advertised as "like new" grade A cells. Each cell read .17 volts, which is 14 times lower then the absolute discharge safety limit. I contacted them in regards to this, and they told me to attempt to charge them fully and test them. Upon charging them, all 4 cells swelled severely and put much tension on the busbars. I told them I would like a replacement. Heres their response, quoted. "Thank you for your update. For the tension on the busbars, you can simply use cable ties to secure the cells together. This should keep them stable and safe for use. There is no need to return them or request a replacement." Cell swelling is caused by extreme gas buildup inside, causing delamination and potential internal shorts and is likely of thermal runaway. Now moving on to my real problem, as I bought more of their cells listed as "grade A" two out of a dozen i bought in a order were also severely undercharged. I contacted them, and they refused to replace them, saying its not covered by our warranty. As for one of the battery packs that had good testing cells like the rest of them, two have severely physically damaged cells. One, being crushed. The other, having very deep dents. I ended up using both of these damaged cells, since the internet for years has told me that the chemistry Lithium Iron Phosphate (LiFePO4) is very safe and unlikely to have mishaps. The cell that had crush damage, ended up having a thermal runaway, causing a fire in my trailer. The cell was installed in the center of my energy storage system, and spread to the neighboring cells. The fire department spent over an hour spraying the whole build in water, and it would continue reigniting. Luckily I have no injuries, however did breathe fumes, and was indeed in extreme danger due to the cell having a primary pressure discharge/explosion, taking a bright flash fireball to my face, luckily the flame was so brief it did not cause me to suffer burns. According to sources, obviously any physical deformation of these battery cells causes it to be hazardous and unusable due to the changes in shape internally. I am a very experienced battery builder, doing this for over a half a decade, and spending even more time beyond that watching thousands of [REDACTED] videos on battery builds and battery/energy science. My biggest point in this lesson, is that in my small sample of two dozen battery packs purchased from wattcycle (for pulling out cells for repurposing), BEYOND the fact that they are selling scrap unstable batteries and being encouraged to use them with no worry, is the companies dangerous act of using damaged cells in their battery packs that they cell across the nation and globally. If in my statistic of every 24 battery packs, there are two damaged cells, I cant imagine how many products with these issues are in the hands of consumers who are using them heavily each day, and in critical areas aswell such as a house and garage. I am trying to take this to court and get my losses reimbursed which is currently around 3,000 dollars. More importantly, they need to be investigated for recklessness and negligence with their products. This may warrant product recalls. I have documented absolutely everything from photographing the damaged cells even before my battery build began. Email logs from wattcycle, videos of the fire from minutes before the event, during the event, and after the event. Provided will be my phone number, I can answer any further questions and send all the evidence on request. The EPA had to get involved due to the firefighters water washing lithium battery material and chemicals down the storm drain on the side of the road, leading to lake erie. My residence is 8 minutes from shores. My local fire department was unable to take posession of these unstable batteries due to the risk. They for 4 days now have been laying distanced in my backyard. We still are not sure on how to get rid of them.

incidentDescription:
Product Safety Complaint  Chefman Power Infusion Plus 1.8L Electric Kettle RJ11-18-TI-KW

I am submitting this report to document a serious product safety concern involving the above-referenced electric kettle.

Summary of Incidents
Unit 1 After approximately two weeks of normal use, the kettle began emitting a noticeable electrical burning odor.
	The unit was returned and replaced through an exchange.
	Unit 2 Replacement Within approximately one week of use, the kettle partially melted and again emitted a strong electrical smoke odor, indicating overheating or potential internal electrical failure.
Safety Risk
These conditions presented a significant fire hazard. The situation required active monitoring to prevent escalation. A fire may have occurred had the unit been left unattended.
Electrical System Verification:
To rule out external causes, the residence electrical system was inspected by maintenance personnel. All outlets, including the GFCI outlet used, and the breaker panel were tested and found to be functioning properly. The GFCI outlet did not trip during either incident.
Conclusion:
Based on two separate failures under normal operating conditions and verification of a properly functioning electrical system, this appears to be a potential product defect and safety risk rather than an isolated environmental issue.
Request:
I recommend investigation into this model for potential overheating or electrical failure risks. I am requesting appropriate follow-up, including documentation of this complaint and any corrective actions.

UPDATED ON 4/10/2026: [As I had stated in my original report, we had our outlets and breaker box check by professional maintenance.  All electrical outlets are working properly.  
The manufacturer of the product did not address the defect in the rapid heating coil.  The pictures clearly shows that melting was from that plastic surrounding the heating coil.  My recommendation for the manufacture is to not use plastic, but a material that does not melt.  ]

incidentDescription: This is about a Breville Mini Smart Oven, basically a toaster oven, used in our family kitchen mainly by adults.    It gets extremely hot when used.  The product is made for use in small spaces.  The electrical cord on the rear of the unit is set up so that it can be plugged into an electrical socket without extending the cord away from the unit.  The plug attached to the cord is encased in soft plastic.  Because of the short distance between the rear of the unit and the electrical outlet, the plastic casing of the plug abutted the back of the unit. We were unaware of this, and there was no cause for concern because the unit was made to fit this way.  Over the months we have used the unit, the heat was high enough to melt the plastic casing of the plug to the metal rear of the unit.  The plug is now stuck fast to the metal unit while plugged in.  Eventually the plastic will melt through, and current will flow throughout the unit, which is all metal.  This is a very dangerous situation as it presents the potential for severe injury, as well as a fire.

incidentDescription:
Incident Overview:
While operating an electric kick scooter at a moderate speed on a flat, paved surface, the primary stem-locking bolta critical structural componentexperienced a catastrophic mechanical failure and sheared completely in half. This caused the steering column to collapse forward without warning.

Product and Usage:
The product being used was an NIU KQi3 Max electric scooter. It was being operated by a single rider for routine transportation. The scooter was being used exactly as intended by the manufacturer at the time of the hardware failure.

Injuries and Mechanism:
The sudden collapse of the steering column resulted in the rider being thrown forward over the handlebars. The rider impacted the pavement head-first and sustained a medically documented acute concussion involving a loss of consciousness. Additional injuries included significant abrasions to the right knee and right elbow. A full-face helmet was worn; it sustained a heavy impact and was structurally compromised during the crash.

Reason for Reporting:
The report is being filed due to a life-threatening structural defect in the stem-locking mechanism. The failure of a load-bearing steel bolt during normal operation represents a significant safety risk to the general public. Furthermore, the manufacturer has attempted to disclaim liability for the failure of this original hardware component because the unit was purchased through a "Renewed" (refurbished) program.

productDescription: Varla eagle one electric scooter dual motor, black and red
incidentDescription:
Incident Description:

I am submitting this report to document a hazardous incident involving a Varla electric scooter that resulted in a lithium-ion battery explosion inside my home.

The scooter had been stored inside our residence when the battery suddenly exploded. At the time of the incident, the scooter was not being charged, and the charger was not connected to the scooter or plugged into an outlet. This means the explosion did not occur during charging or due to any external electrical connection.

The explosion caused damage inside our home and created a significant safety hazard. Lithium battery fires are known to spread rapidly and can produce dangerous smoke and heat. The event occurred unexpectedly and without any prior warning signs that the battery was unstable.

The local fire department responded to the incident. According to the firefighters who assessed the situation, a battery exploding under these conditions is not considered normal. The fire department is currently reviewing the incident to determine the cause of the battery failure.

Product Age and Manufacturer Response:

After the incident, I contacted the manufacturer, Varla, to report what happened. During communication with the company, they stated that lithium-ion batteries used in their scooters have an expected service life of approximately 3-4 years and that risk of failure can increase as the battery ages.

The scooter involved in this incident was approximately five years old at the time of the explosion.

However, during ownership of the product there was no clear warning provided that the battery could become a potential fire or explosion hazard simply due to age, nor was there any communication advising consumers to replace or safely dispose of aging batteries to prevent safety risks.

The company ultimately concluded that the battery failure was due to natural aging and declined responsibility for the incident because the product was beyond the warranty period. They offered a 15% discount toward the purchase of a new scooter instead of addressing the safety failure or the property damage caused by the explosion.

Product Use and Storage Conditions

It is also important to note that the scooter involved in this incident was not used frequently. Although it was purchased approximately five years ago, the scooter accumulated only around 300 miles of total use over that entire period.

For the past approximately four years, the scooter was mostly kept in storage inside our apartment and was not regularly ridden. The apartment environment was temperature regulated, meaning the scooter and its battery were stored indoors under normal residential conditions rather than being exposed to extreme heat, cold, or outdoor weather.

Because the scooter had such minimal mileage and limited use, the battery failure and explosion were particularly unexpected. The scooter was not being actively used, ridden, or charged at the time of the incident. The fact that the battery failed in this manner despite limited use and indoor storage raises additional concerns regarding the safety and reliability of the battery system.

Consumer Safety Concern:

This situation raises serious safety concerns because:
		The battery exploded while not in use and not charging.
		The incident occurred inside a residential home, creating risk to occupants and property.
		The manufacturer attributes the explosion to battery age but does not appear to provide sufficient warnings or proactive replacement guidance to prevent such incidents.
		Lithium battery explosions present a significant fire hazard that could potentially cause injuries or fatalities.

Given the potential danger of lithium-ion battery failures, I believe this incident should be reviewed to determine whether additional safety warnings, product recalls, or battery replacement guidance are necessary to protect other consumers who may own similar scooters.

My goal in submitting this report is to ensure that the incident is properly documented and that any potential safety risks associated with this product are evaluated to help prevent similar events from occurring in other homes.

productDescription:
The product is a Type S Jump Starter and Portable Power Bank with an 8600mAh internal lithiumion battery. 

The device is designed to jumpstart a vehicle battery and also function as a portable power bank for charging small electronics.

The unit is a handheld, rectangular portable device, approximately the size of a small paperback book. It has a black plastic housing with molded edges and contains an internal rechargeable lithiumion battery. The jump starter includes builtin battery terminals/clamps for connecting to a vehicle battery and USB output ports for use as a power bank. The device is intended for automotive emergency use, specifically jumpstarting a car when the vehicle battery is discharged. The product is marketed as portable and consumeruse automotive equipment. Exact dimensions and weight are unknown. No external modifications were made to the product, and it was used as designed and intended by the manufacturer.
incidentDescription:
While using the Type S 8600mAh jump starter for its intended purpose (jumpstarting a vehicle), the device began smoking and melting.
At the time of the incident:

The device was NOT connected to a charger
The device was operating only on its internal battery
The device had been previously charged on an earlier date
The jump starter was being used normally according to instructions

Immediately after initiating the jumpstart process, the unit rapidly overheated, produced visible smoke, and the plastic housing began to melt. The failure appeared sudden and internal, with no external damage prior to use.
The device was immediately disconnected and moved to a safe location to prevent fire or injury.

Injuries or Damage
No personal injuries occurred.
No property damage, however the incident posed a significant fire risk.
The product itself is destroyed and no longer usable.


Safety Concern
This incident represents a serious safety hazard, as the product failed catastrophically during normal, expected use. Smoking and melting of a lithiumion jump starter creates a high risk of fire, burns, or explosion, especially given that jump starters are often used near vehicles, fuel vapors, and people.
The failure occurred without misuse, without charging, and without external power, suggesting a potential internal battery or protection circuit failure.

Actions Taken
Device was immediately removed from service
Device is being kept isolated to prevent possible reignition
Device will be disposed of as hazardous battery waste
Incident is being reported to warn others and support potential investigation or recall

Additional Information
The device was being used exactly as intended by the manufacturer.
The failure occurred under highcurrent demand typical of jumpstarting a vehicle.
There were no visible warnings or indicators prior to the failure.
This type of failure could reasonably cause serious injury or fire if it occurred indoors, in a garage, or near flammable materials.

incidentDescription:
I purchased the above-referenced electric scooter in July 2025 through an Amazon Marketplace seller. Approximately two weeks after receiving the scooter, it stopped functioning. I contacted the seller regarding the issue.

The seller shipped a replacement control board and instructed me to install it. After installation, the scooter still did not function properly. No further repairs were attempted.

The scooter was then left unused and unplugged next to the house. It had not been operated or charged for approximately four months prior to the incident.



Description of Incident

On Sunday evening, while the scooter was sitting unplugged and not in use, it spontaneously caught fire.

The scooter was not charging at the time and had not been used for several months.

Due to the severity of the fire and concern for the safety of the residence, 911 was called. Firefighters responded to the scene and extinguished the fire. Because of the lithium battery risk of reignition, firefighters buried the battery to prevent it from reigniting.



Additional Information
		The scooter was not plugged in at the time of ignition.
		The scooter had not been used in approximately four months.
		The fire originated from the scooter/battery area.
		Emergency services were required to prevent further damage and potential spread to the residence.

Supporting documentation available:
		Amazon order confirmation
		Communication with seller
		Photos of damage

incidentDescription:
I am formally reporting a serious fire hazard incident involving a Bella toaster that was purchased new only days prior to the event.

While being used under normal operating conditions to toast bread, the unit experienced a sudden internal ignition failure. The toaster began emitting extremely dense smoke almost immediately. Within moments, the exterior plastic housing began melting and deforming. The electrical cord burned and its insulation failed.

This was not minor overheating or food debris ignition. The appliance experienced a combustion-level internal failure.

The volume of smoke was severe enough to fill my entire two-story home (five bedrooms). All smoke alarms were activated throughout the residence. At the time of the incident, the home was occupied by an 83-year-old elderly family member, my 20-year-old son, and two household pets.

My son disconnected the unit and removed it from the home to prevent further escalation. The appliance was completely destroyed.

As a result of this event:
		The toaster casing melted.
		The electrical cord burned and was compromised.
		Kitchen cabinetry sustained visible smoke and heat damage.
		The residence filled with heavy smoke, requiring prolonged ventilation.
		There remains a persistent odor consistent with plastic combustion.

This appliance was used exactly as intended and had been owned for only a few days. A toaster designed for high-heat food preparation should not melt, ignite, or produce combustion-level smoke under normal operation.

The damaged product has been preserved in its post-incident condition and documented with photographs.

This incident posed a serious risk of structural fire and potential injury or loss of life. I believe this represents a significant manufacturing or electrical safety defect that warrants investigation.

Multi-function electric pressure cooker with programmable settings (e.g., rice, meat/stew, beans/chili, poultry, yogurt, slow cook, saut). Digital screen displays pressure status and cooking cycle information. Unit includes locking lid mechanism and pressure release/float valve safety system. Designed for household food preparation using pressurized steam.
incidentDescription:
On February 2, 2026, at approximately 7:35 PM, I was using the Gourmia Express Pot to prepare bone marrow broth. The appliance was being used according to standard operating instructions.

When the cooking cycle completed, the digital display indicated that pressure had been fully released. The unit screen showed Off.



2. Incident Description

After visually confirming that the display showed no remaining pressure, I rotated the lid.

The lid unlocked without resistance.

Immediately upon disengagement, the unit forcefully released a significant amount of steam and hot liquid outward approximately two feet.

The sudden release of steam and liquid resulted in a steam burn injury.



3. Injury Sustained

As a result of the incident, I sustained significant steam burns consistent with partial-thickness (second-degree) injury.

Medical-grade burn care was initiated immediately, including:
		Silver sulfadiazine 1% cream (prescription burn cream)
		Xeroform petrolatum non-adhering dressings
		Sterile wound care management

Photographic documentation of the injury and healing progression is available.



4. Safety Concern

The lid was able to unlock despite apparent residual internal pressure.

Electric pressure cookers are designed with locking and float-valve mechanisms to prevent opening while pressurized.

The ability of the lid to disengage and release pressurized steam presents a serious safety concern.

productDescription: HAONINYUE Car Jump Starter with Air Compressor, 3000A peak current, 150PSI tire inflator. Black, rectangular portable device measuring 5.5"D x 2.2"W x 6.7"H, approximately 2.30 lbs. Contains a 14.8V lithium polymer battery with 8000mAh capacity. Charges via USB-C. Includes built-in air compressor with pressure gauge, LED flashlight, and jumper cable clamps. Sold on Amazon.com under ASIN B0F2SBB9CJ by seller "Haoningyuedianzikeji" (brand: HAONINYUE). Device label reads "Made in China" with FCC, UKCA, CE, and RoHS certification marks, and a partially readable manufacturer name ending in "Electronic Technology Co., Ltd." Product listing advertises 10 intelligent safety protections including overcharge, overcurrent, short circuit, and high temperature protection.
manufacturer: Guangzhou Haoningyue Electronic Technology Co., Ltd.
incidentDescription:
On approximately February 4, 2026, the HAONINYUE Car Jump Starter with Air Compressor (purchased on Amazon.com, ASIN B0F2SBB9CJ) caught fire while charging via USB-C in my home in [REDACTED]. This was the device's second charge cycle.
The device was purchased December 17, 2025 and delivered December 29, 2025. I charged it once upon receipt, then used it three times to jump-start vehicles over the following weeks  all normal, intended use. After the last use, the battery display showed approximately 35-36% charge remaining. I plugged the device into a USB-C charger to recharge it, which is the manufacturer's specified charging method.
During charging, the lithium-ion battery underwent thermal runaway. The plastic housing melted and deformed. The battery cells ruptured through the bottom of the casing. The fire produced large volumes of dense, toxic smoke that rapidly filled the kitchen, living room, and surrounding areas of the house.
My household includes four people: myself, my wife, my newborn daughter, and my almost-3-year-old daughter. All four of us were exposed to the toxic lithium-ion smoke.
I attempted to remove the burning device from the house, sustaining a minor burn to my hand. I handed the device to our maintenance worker outside. We evacuated the house. I used a leaf blower and multiple fans to clear the dense smoke from the home.
The entire kitchen and living room were covered in soot, ash, and toxic lithium-ion particulate. Three household staff members spent the full day cleaning the contamination. My entire workday was lost managing the emergency.
Health effects: I experienced respiratory inflammation and a scratchy throat from prolonged smoke exposure. My wife had a full-body allergic skin reaction requiring antihistamine medication. Both children were monitored throughout the day for adverse effects. No emergency medical treatment was required.
The product listing on Amazon advertises "10 intelligent safety protections" including overcharge, overcurrent, short circuit, and high temperature protection. All of these safety features failed during a routine charge. The device was used entirely within normal operating conditions and manufacturer guidelines.
I have preserved the burned device as physical evidence. Photos of the destroyed device and property damage are attached. I have also filed a claim with Amazon.

incidentDescription:
Product Hazard: Toxic Off-Gassing & Negligent Safety Instructions

1. The Hazard (Chemical Exposure): The manufacturer (Instant Brands) admits in their California AB 1200 disclosure that this product line contains PFAS, specifically PTFE (Polytetrafluoroethylene) and FEP, in the food contact surfaces. Upon standard operation, the unit emitted thick, noxious chemical fumes that persisted for nearly a week.

2. The Injury (Polymer Fume Fever & Neurotoxicity): Exposure to these fumes caused immediate and acute physical illness. Even though I was working in a separate room at the opposite end of the house, the fumes were potent enough to cause severe physical symptoms, including pounding headaches, blurred vision, nausea, and chest tightness.

In addition to the flu-like symptoms consistent with "Polymer Fume Fever," I experienced distinct Central Nervous System (CNS) agitation. This manifested as a physiological sense of "unwellness" and extreme nervous-system excitability (feeling "on high alert"), which persisted throughout the exposure. The severity of the fumes made it physically difficult to enter the kitchen for nearly a week.

3. The Defect (Negligent Instruction): When reported, the manufacturer's support team admitted these fumes were "normal for new units" and explicitly instructed me to perform multiple "Dry Runs" (operating the unit empty at high heat) to "burn off" the smell. This instruction is dangerous. Heating PTFE coatings without food load causes rapid overheating (often exceeding 500F), which accelerates the release of toxic particulate matter. The User Manual (Page 9) contains NO instructions for this "burn-in" procedure, and Warning #19 forbids outdoor use, forcing consumers to perform this hazardous off-gassing procedure in enclosed residential spaces.

4. Pattern of Defect: Online consumer forums contain numerous identical reports of chemical illness from this product line, indicating a systemic manufacturing failure in the curing process of the non-stick coating.

incidentDescription:
My name is [REDACTED], and I own a landscaping company in Alabama called [REDACTED]. Our business uses Makita lithium-ion batteries to power professional landscaping equipment.

In the summer of last year, I purchased multiple batteries through Walmarts website. The online listing advertised the batteries as Makita brand batteries. They were not advertised as compatible with Makita or third-party batteries. Based on the listing, I believed I was purchasing genuine Makita products.

When the batteries arrived, they appeared authentic and looked nearly identical to real Makita batteries. There were no obvious signs that the products were counterfeit.

A few months later, a serious safety incident occurred in our shop. One of the batteries suddenly exploded and caught fire. Fortunately, no one was injured. An employee was nearby and was able to extinguish the fire before it spread, but the incident created a major risk of injury and property damage.

After the explosion, I contacted Makita to report the incident and request assistance. Makita has a team that investigates battery safety issues and examined the batteries we had in our possession. Makita informed me that some of the batteries were genuine Makita products, but others were not authentic and appeared to be counterfeit. Makita also showed us how to identify differences between real Makita batteries and counterfeit versions.

After reviewing our purchase history, we traced the counterfeit batteries back to the Walmart online purchase. Makita also informed me that Walmart is not an authorized Makita battery dealer.

I then contacted Walmart to report that counterfeit Makita-branded batteries were sold through their website and that one exploded and caused a fire. Despite multiple attempts to resolve this issue, Walmart has not provided a meaningful response or refund for the counterfeit products. The batteries also appear to still be listed for sale online.

I am submitting this complaint because the sale of counterfeit lithium-ion batteries marketed as a major brand is a serious consumer safety hazard and appears to involve deceptive advertising or misrepresentation. I am requesting that this issue be investigated and that steps be taken to prevent additional consumers and businesses from unknowingly purchasing counterfeit and potentially dangerous batteries.

incidentDescription:
On December 11, 2025, a residential lithium-ion battery energy storage system experienced an internal ignition and thermal runaway event resulting in a structure fire and total loss of the building.
The system consisted of four (4) stationary 48-volt LiFePO4 lithium-ion batteries, each rated at approximately 5 kWh (approximately 20 kWh total capacity), installed as a parallel battery bank. At the time of the incident, the batteries were fully charged and actively supplying stored energy to the residence during a system demonstration under normal operating conditions.
The fire originated at the battery level. According to the responding fire department and subsequent fire marshal investigation, multiple lithium-ion batteries ignited, with repeated re-ignition occurring despite suppression attempts. Firefighters were required to disconnect, remove, and bury the affected batteries in sand outdoors to prevent continued thermal runaway and re-ignition. The batteries reignited multiple times prior to burial.
A formal fire investigation conducted by Gainesville Fire Rescue determined the area of origin to be the southwest interior corner of the structure, where the battery bank was located. The fire marshal identified a lithium-ion battery as the probable item first ignited and eliminated inverters, upstream wiring, weather, and external ignition sources as causes. The fire was classified as accidental, with the probable cause being an undetermined internal battery failure.
The fire produced heavy smoke and combustion byproducts throughout the enclosed structure, resulting in widespread contamination. Due to the nature of lithium-ion battery fires and associated health hazards, the structure was determined to be a total loss. No personal injuries were reported; however, the incident presented a significant life-safety hazard and substantial property damage.
All physical evidence has been preserved. The batteries were being used as intended in a residential stationary energy storage application at the time of failure.

incidentDescription:
I am reporting a safety issue involving a residential, direct-vent propane gas stove (Hearthstone Waitsfield DX, LP) purchased and installed in early 2019 in what was our primary residence at the time. In 2024, the house became a rental, and the appliance was being used by our tenants as a primary heat source at the time of the incident which triggered this complaint, in December of 2025.

The stove operated for multiple years with a defective pilot assembly that was subject to a manufacturer safety mitigation bulletin requiring the unit to be shut off until the pilot assembly was replaced. During multiple service visits by the authorized dealer, this bulletin was not disclosed, and the stove was repeatedly returned to service. At no time were we notified of the mitigation program by the manufacturer. 

The defective pilot assembly was eventually replaced in October 2024 by a different service provider when the authorized dealer was unavailable. This replacement was paid for out of pocket and was performed without disclosure that the appliance was subject to a manufacturer proactive replacement program. By that time, the stove had already operated for years with the defective pilot assembly in place.

As a result, the appliance experienced prolonged abnormal operation, including over-firing and flame impingement. In December 2025, after a service visit in which the dealer again returned the stove to service, and again failed to notify us about the pilot mitigation program, my tenant reported that multiple panes of the sealed firebox glass developed spider-web cracking. It was only at this point that I discovered Hearthstones bulletin about a known defect and a pilot replacement program, by searching the internet myself for repeated pilot issues in this model.

The dealer later acknowledged in writing that the glass failure was due, at least in part, to the pilot assembly not having been replaced earlier.

Although the dealer returned the stove to service after discovering the cracked glass and without replacing it, I took it out of service myself once my tenants notified me about this condition. My tenants are currently using backup electric heat. No physical injuries have occurred to date, but the condition presented a serious risk of injury, fire, or carbon monoxide exposure due to compromised containment in a sealed combustion gas appliance.

In the wake of this incident, we notified the manufacturer multiple times and failed to receive any response beyond an automated notification of email receipt. I am reporting this as a failure of a manufacturer safety mitigation program and a resulting hazardous condition in a residential gas appliance.

Neither the dealer nor the manufacturer ever notified me of the mitigation bulletin at any time; I learned of it only by independently researching the problem after the glass failure.

The swelling also caused the ring to get stuck in the charging dock, making it hard to remove safely.

I contacted the manufacturer, Ultrahuman, and explained the situation in detail. The manufacturer acknowledged that battery swelling is not normal wear and tear and is a safety concern. They only offered a paid trade-in or a certified renewed (refurbished) unit without warranty, which I believe does not adequately address the underlying safety risk.

Given that this is the second battery-related failure and now involves physical battery swelling, I am concerned that the product may have a design or reliability issue that poses potential risk to consumers.

Its an unfortunate and frightening incident that has led to my writing you this letter. 
I own a Viking fridge.  I have loved the fridge and this is the second one that I have owned.   My Viking Fridge was purchased in 2016 from Best Buy, so it is 9 years old.  I have never had any significant issues with it. 
One day back in May of this year, 6 months ago!!, I started noticing a decline in its cooling abilityup until my fridge caught on fire.  I corresponded with the customer service team.  The Viking Company sent their licensed technician to check it.   The report was that the insulation on the top of the fridge fell down into the fan and made it catch on fire, destroying the fan and other surrounding parts and the fridge no longer cooled.  Additionally, had I not of been home, likely my entire house would have burned down.  The technician that Viking sent was astonished that there was not some kind of grate or other divider to prevent the insulation from ever coming in contact with the fan.  To make a long story short, I have been told by the Viking people that my fridge is unrepairable.  It is still under the sealed system warranty and now it is a total loss. However, Viking states that the fan is not part of the sealed system.  At this point, this is not about the warranty, but an unsafe produce for which I paid thousands of dollars and the company is unwilling to rectify the situation and either replace my fridge or make my fridge work again.  
The fridge is 9 years old but it should last for a minimum of 10 to 20 years, depending on factors like maintenance, usage, and model. While some Viking units can last longer with proper care, they are built to offer superior durability compared to the average refrigerator lifespan of 10-13 years, with many models engineered for 15-20 years of service. 
I have been going back and forth with this issue with different people within Viking for 6 months now.  The customer service team, often does not answer emails or messages, or have a comprehensive methodology to solve these issues.  The top manager,[REDACTED], does not even answer my emails. It has been a very frustrating experience because I am usually working and dont have a ton of time to take care of this.  But I come home every night with no fridge.  I have been using my garage fridge for 6 months now and I lost a significant amount of food in the whole process.   
The only thing customer service offered me a 25% discount on a new fridge.  While I appreciate the offer, I really cannot afford to buy 75% of a new fridge now nor do I think a life of 9 years for such an expensive fridge is a good thing.  The 75% would amount to about 8 or 9 thousand dollars!!  This fridge has always been in an air-conditioned house built into the cabinet.  There should have been no reason for this to happen.   This is faulty and deplorable engineering!!

productDescription: 2025 Blauwhal 50-Pint Dehumidifier with Pump, 8000 Sq. Ft. Coverage - Model PD14BS-B. Dark White. 14"D x 10"W x 24"H.
incidentDescription:
On February 2, 2026, I purchased a Blauwhal 150-Pint Dehumidifier with Pump, 8000 Sq. Ft. Coverage - Model PD14BS-B from Amazon, which was delivered on February 4, 2026. The side of the box containing the dehumidifier had a Warning label that caught my eye: "Risk of Fire due to Flammable Refrigerant Used. Follow Handling Instructions Carefully in Compliance with National Regulations."  Such warning was concerning to me, so I went back on the Amazon website and thoroughly reviewed the description given about the dehumidifier, including its Features and Specs. There was no disclosure given on the type of refrigerant used nor the risks associated with using that type. The refrigerant used, along with its associated risks, is finally disclosed in the Owners Manual found in the shipping box containing the dehumidifier, after it had been purchased and delivered. (The Amazon website did not include any link to an Owners Manual.)

The refrigerant used is hydrocarbon R-290, which is essentially propane gas and highly flammable. It appears that most portable dehumidifiers on the market today use R-32, which has much lower flammability and is considered only "mildly flammable." According to "combustion grade" classification by standards organizations such as ASHRAE and ISO, hydrocarbon R-290 falls in Class 3, whereas R-32 falls in Class 2L.

In my opinion, the Amazon website page on the Blauwhal dehumidifier should have disclosed the type of refrigerant used along with the elevated fire hazard risks associated with that type. Any potential purchaser should have that information to make an informed decision on whether or not to purchase it. My decision was to immediately return the unused dehumidifier for a full refund in light of the elevated fire hazard risk.

The scooter is powered by a 350W electric motor with a 36V 10.5Ah lithium-ion battery. It is marketed for adult riders with a stated maximum load of 120 kg (264 lbs).
incidentDescription:
I am submitting this report to document a serious safety hazard involving a Volpam electric scooter purchased through Amazon.

While using the scooter under normal riding conditions, I discovered structural instability in the frame and handlebar assembly. The scooter began to feel unstable, and the frame appeared to be separating. This created an immediate risk of collapse while riding.

In addition to the structural defect, the scooter experienced multiple critical component failures, including:
		Brake assembly failure: brake components loosened and fell apart while I was riding, requiring immediate repair to avoid an accident
		Brake light failure within the first week of ownership
		Throttle failure, requiring replacement
		Battery inefficiency, requiring daily charging despite normal usage

Because of these failures, the scooter is unsafe to operate. I weigh approximately 180 pounds, which is well within the advertised weight limits for this product.

After experiencing these issues, I reviewed product feedback and found multiple verified customer reviews reporting the same defect, including scooters snapping in half or breaking apart during use, resulting in falls, injuries, and hospital visits. This suggests a systemic manufacturing or design defect, not an isolated incident.

I contacted both Amazon and the manufacturer. Amazon declined assistance due to the return window expiring. The manufacturer refused a refund or brand-new replacement and offered only repair or a used replacement unit (90% new), which does not adequately address a safety-related structural defect.

Due to the risk of serious injury, I have stopped using the scooter entirely.

I am submitting this report to alert the Consumer Product Safety Commission of a potentially dangerous product currently being sold to consumers.

productDescription:
The product is a Mickey Mousethemed electric waffle maker designed to cook a single large waffle in the shape of Mickey Mouse. The unit features a clamshell-style design with a top and bottom cooking plate that close together. The exterior casing is primarily red plastic and includes a black metal edge that runs around the perimeter of the unit.

The waffle maker is marketed with prominent Disney/Mickey Mouse imagery and is visually appealing to children, although it is labeled as a household kitchen appliance. The unit does not include a latch or locking mechanism to secure the lid in either the open or closed position. When opened, the lid does not remain upright on its own and can move freely.

The product is powered by an electric cord and is intended for countertop use. Warning text is present on the side of the unit in small lettering, and safety information is included in the instruction manual. The model number shown on the product is DCM-12, and the manufacturer is Select Brands.
incidentDescription:
We experienced two separate injury incidents involving the same Mickey Mouse waffle maker, Model DCM-12, which was received as a Christmas gift.

First Incident  Burn Injury:
While the waffle maker was closed and actively cooking on the kitchen counter, our young son observed us making waffles. The product is brightly colored and prominently features Mickey Mouse imagery, which immediately drew his attention. He excitedly said Mickey! and reached toward the waffle maker.

Although the unit was closed, he made contact with the black metal edge that surrounds the exterior casing. The surface was extremely hot, and he immediately pulled his hand back and began crying in visible distress. He sustained a burn to his thumb and repeatedly stated that he just wanted to play with Mickey.

At the time of the incident, there was no prominent or clearly visible warning on the exterior of the product indicating that the outer metal surfaces become dangerously hot during use. The warning text present on the side of the unit is small and not easily noticeable, particularly given the child-appealing design of the product.

Second Incident  Pinch Injury:
In a separate incident involving the same waffle maker, my wife sustained a finger injury caused by the design of the clamshell lid. The lid does not appear to have any hinge tension, resistance mechanism, or locking feature to keep it open when raised. As a result, the top clamshell moves freely and can fall closed unexpectedly.

While the unit was turned off, the lid was in an open position and was inadvertently contacted, causing it to swing downward and close suddenly. Her fingers were caught between the top and bottom clamshell plates, resulting in a painful pinch injury.

There was no warning in the instructions or on the packaging indicating that the lid does not remain open on its own or that it presents a pinch hazard when open.

incidentDescription:
We purchased an electric bicycle from Amazon in November 2024 as a Christmas gift for our child. The product was assembled and briefly tested by an adult prior to Christmas by riding it once around the block for less than one minute to confirm it functioned. It operated normally at that time.

On Christmas Day, our child rode the electric bike for a short period, approximately 1520 minutes total, on flat residential streets. No issues were observed at that time. Due to living in Washington State, where weather conditions are rainy for much of the year, and due to our childs school and sports schedule, the bike was not used again for several months.

In early spring 2025, when weather conditions improved, the bike was ridden a few additional times. Shortly thereafter, one of the tires failed and went flat during normal use. A replacement tire was purchased and installed. The bike was then used again briefly.

Within weeks of the tire replacement, the electric bike began experiencing a significant loss of power. The motor would no longer reach its advertised or expected speed (approximately 21 mph), struggled to accelerate, and appeared to have an electrical or motor failure. This occurred during normal, light use by a child rider on flat terrain. No modifications were made to the bike, and it was not abused, overloaded, or used in extreme conditions.

Although no physical injury occurred, the sudden loss of power during operation presents a safety risk, particularly for a child rider, as unexpected deceleration or failure in traffic or near vehicles could result in serious injury. The product failed well within what would be considered reasonable consumer use and longevity.

Multiple attempts were made to resolve the issue through the retailer and seller, but the seller was unresponsive. The bike remains in excellent physical condition and is no longer used due to safety concerns.

UPDATED ON 1/5/2026: [Since submitting my report, I want to formally document that I am unable to obtain any resolution through Amazon, despite extensive attempts.

Amazon has:
• Refused to escalate this matter to its internal escalation or safety teams
• Refused to provide contact information for any escalation department
• Closed all A-to-Z Guarantee requests without accurately reflecting the history of seller non-responsiveness
• Directed me back to a third-party seller who is no longer reachable and has since been removed from Amazon’s platform

I filed a formal complaint with the Washington State Attorney General’s Office (Complaint File #708550). Amazon responded through that process but did not address the seller’s lack of responsiveness, the inability to obtain manufacturer support, or Amazon’s own role as the marketplace that facilitated the sale. The Attorney General’s informal resolution process is now closed.

Amazon has confirmed to me directly that they no longer have access to certain manufacturer or seller details, as the seller has been removed from their website. As a result, I am unable to provide some of the information requested in the product identification sections of the CPSC form because neither Amazon nor the seller can supply it.

The electric bike remains in my possession, unused and stored, due to safety concerns following mechanical and performance failures. I am not seeking sales, promotional, or warranty contact — only accountability and acknowledgment of the safety issues reported.]

productDescription:
The product involved is the Dyson Purifier Hot+Cool Formaldehyde HP09 (White/Gold). It is a multifunction household appliance designed for indoor residential use that combines an air purifier, space heater, and cooling fan in a single unit. The unit is tall and freestanding, approximately 30 inches in height with an oval-shaped loop amplifier at the top and a cylindrical base that houses the internal motor, heating elements, sensors, and filtration system. The color of the unit is white with gold accents, consistent with Dysons HP09 design.
The product uses a standard 120-volt AC power supply and is intended to be plugged directly into a wall outlet using its attached power cord and molded electrical plug. It contains a sealed HEPA and activated carbon filter system designed to remove particulate matter, gases, and formaldehyde from indoor air. The HP09 is marketed for continuous indoor operation in living spaces such as bedrooms, offices, and common household areas, and it is controlled via an onboard display and a remote control.
I own two identical Dyson HP09 units, both purchased in December 2024, and both still within the manufacturers 2-year limited warranty period at the time of the incident.
incidentDescription:
On November 27, 2025, I experienced a fire incident involving a Dyson Purifier Hot+Cool Formaldehyde HP09 (White/Gold). I own two HP09 units, both purchased in December 2024 (12/16/24 and 12/17/24) and both still within their 2-year warranty period. The incident occurred in my home during normal use. One HP09 was plugged directly into a standard wall outlet in my living/working area and had been running on a normal setting for approximately 25 minutes. I was seated about eight feet away when I heard an unusual noise. When I looked over, I saw an actual flame coming from the plug area of the Dysons power cord, at the point where the plug meets the outlet.
There was no prior sparking, smoke, or visible damage to the outlet before the ignition. The flame was clearly originating from the plug itself, not from inside the wall. I immediately ran over and unplugged the unit from the outlet; once the plug was removed from the outlet, the flame went out. The Dyson units cord/plug are damaged and unsafe to use. No one was physically injured, but this was a serious fire hazard; if I had not been present in the room, the outcome could have been much worse.
To reiterate, no other appliance has ever caused overheating, fire, or electrical disruption in this outlet before or after the incident. The pattern of similar complaints from other consumers, combined with Dysons past recalls for fire-related hazards, heightens concern that this may represent a broader product defect requiring investigation.
It is also important to note that Dyson previously issued a major recall on the Dyson Hot+Cool heaters (models AM04 and AM05) due to electrical shortcircuiting that caused fires. Although the HP09 is a newer model, this recall demonstrates that Dyson products have a history of thermal and electrical risks significant enough to warrant national safety action. My experience closely mirrors the symptoms that led to those earlier recalls.
Furthermore, Dyson, Inc. has over 3,000 customer complaints in the last three years on the [REDACTED] platform, many of which involve product malfunctions, warranty disputes, or service issues. This volume of complaints reinforces a broader pattern of unresolved product reliability concerns.
The product was being used exactly as intended: plugged directly into a wall outlet (no extension cords or power strips), running as an air purifier/heater in a residential room. The outlet in question has been used for other household appliances without any issues before or after this event. The only product that has ever caused overheating or fire at that outlet is this Dyson HP09. In addition, my second HP09 unit (same model) failed internally prior to this fire incident. It began displaying repeated error messages and stopped functioning despite following all recommended troubleshooting steps (power cycling, resets, filter checks, and cleaning). In summary, one HP09 failed internally and became unusable, and the other HP09s plug caught fire during normal operation. Because this product is designed for indoor, continuous use, and because the fire originated at the plug while the device was being used as directed, I am reporting this as a potential product defect and safety hazard.
