productDescription: Shark vacuum model number AZ4002, color is a deep brown approximately 4 foot high
incidentDescription:
Subject: Formal Complaint Against SharkNinja  Defective Vacuum and Unsafe Warranty Practices

To Whom It May Concern,

I am writing to formally file a complaint against SharkNinja Operating LLC (Shark Vacuum) regarding a vacuum cleaner I purchased in August [2025]. Since the time of purchase, this vacuum has experienced ongoing mechanical and operational issues, and it has now become a serious safety and fire hazard.

Most recently, when the vacuum is turned on, the motor will momentarily engage and then abruptly shut down, while the units lights remain on. Additionally, the electrical plug becomes extremely hot during use, which raises significant concern about electrical failure and fire risk.

Because of these safety concerns, I contacted Sharks customer service to request warranty support and to report what I believe to be a dangerous defect. I specifically explained that this vacuum may pose a fire hazard and requested that the company take the unit back for inspection so the defect could be properly evaluated and addressed.

Instead of offering a safe and responsible resolution, Shark representatives instructed me to cut the power cord off the vacuum and throw the unit in the garbage in order to receive a replacement. I was told that Shark would not honor my warranty unless I destroyed the product, and they refused to accept the defective unit for evaluation.

This response is deeply concerning for several reasons:
	1.	It prevents the manufacturer from examining a potentially dangerous defect that could pose a fire risk to consumers.
	2.	It forces customers to destroy evidence of a defective and hazardous product in order to access their warranty.
	3.	It raises serious questions about consumer safety, transparency, and corporate responsibility.
	4.	It effectively denies me full access to my warranty rights, unless I comply with an unreasonable and unsafe demand.

I believe Sharks handling of this matter is negligent and potentially fraudulent, as it appears designed to avoid accountability for a product that may cause property damage or bodily harm. A vacuum that overheats at the plug and shuts down unexpectedly should not be dismissed or disposed of without proper investigation.

I am requesting the assistance in addressing this matter and ensuring that SharkNinja:
		Properly acknowledges and investigates this safety issue
		Honors its warranty without requiring destruction of the product
		Takes responsibility for identifying and correcting potentially hazardous defects

I am deeply concerned not only for myself, but for other consumers who may unknowingly be using the same defective model.

Thank you for your time and attention to this serious matter. I am prepared to provide documentation, call logs, and any additional information needed.

incidentDescription:

There is an internal component within the water reservoir that cannot be removed or accessed, and the openings that allow water to pass through are covered by mesh, making it impossible to reach and clean the affected area. Because this area retains water and cannot be properly sanitized, the appliance cannot be safely used. After contacting the manufacturer, no cleaning method was provided for this internal component.

The appliance was used in my home by an adult (me) for normal, intended coffee preparation, following typical cleaning and maintenance. Once mold was discovered, I stopped using the product due to concern about contamination and potential exposure. No confirmed injury has occurred; however, the situation presents a potential health risk because it is a food-related appliance and mold was present.

I contacted SharkNinja for a resolution and was not offered any way to clean the affected component. I was initially informed that a replacement water reservoir would arrive within 10 business days. After that timeframe passed, I was informed the required part is on backorder with an estimated 2 to 4 week delay, leaving the product unusable for an extended period. At this time, the manufacturer has not resolved the issue, and the product remains unusable.

productDescription: It is a Wolf Gourmet, large, high end stand mixer,  Model WGSM100S
incidentDescription:
I sent the following message to Wolf Gourmet on 8 Dec '25:

Hi Folks,

This is the follow-up to my earlier call today concerning a potential safety issue with a loose/broken handle on a Wolf 7-Quart Mixing Bowl. The
background:

My wife has had a Wolf Gourmet WGSM100S for several years and loves it!
(Atch. 1) She is an accomplished cook and baker who probably uses the mixer at least once a week. On 26 November, while doing some holiday baking she commented to me that the "handle seems loose". I looked and sure enough it was not only loose, but a slight movement by me caused the upper 'attachment point' to separate completely from the bowl! Atch. 2 is the photo I took at that time while Atch. 3 is another photo I took today to more clearly show the problem. BTW, the bottom 'attachment point' is also loose but not yet totally separated. It appears to me that there is some kind of "screw mechanism" holding the handle to the bowl but no obvious way of "tightening"
it back on.

I don't think the handle should fall apart. Do you?  I believe this is a potential safety issue. If my wife was lifting off the heavy mixer bowl when the handle failed, she could have been injured. I told her to stop using it and I called you folks, but after 10 minutes of waiting gave up. Since she had lots more baking to do, I chose to immediately order an expensive
($263.95) replacement bowl. (Atch. 4) rather than deal with a potential safety problem. It arrived via UPS on 5 December and is working fine!

I'm not exactly sure when we bought the mixer but we still have the actual carton it came in.  Atch. 5 is from that carton and shows a "copyright of 2019" so I suspect our unit may have been bought in 2019/2020.  Thus, it is probably beyond the 5 year warranty period but I'm not sure this really applies in our case. If we hadn't noticed the failure when we did and stopped using the bowl at that time, the results could have been much worse.
Therefore, I am respectively asking that you consider refunding the $263.95 I paid for the replacement bowl. BTW, I still have the original "failed" bowl should you be interested in examining it. Thank you very much and we look forward to your reply.

[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]

They replied with this bland message:
[REDACTED] (Wolf Gourmet Support)

Dec 9, 2025, [REDACTED] EST

[REDACTED],

Thank you for your email.

Unfortunately, there is no way to repair/tighten the handle on the bowl.

With the appliance showing it is outside of the 5 year limited warranty we will be unable to replace the bowl.

We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience

Thank you for contacting Wolf Gourmet

[REDACTED]
Consumer Affairs

I then sent this reply back:

[REDACTED],

Interesting and disappointing. You completely ignored my central issue that Wolf has a SAFETY issue that could result in injury to your customers. I thought perhaps some "thank you for pointing this out" would result and maybe even as a gesture of customer goodwill reimburse me for having to buy a replacement bowl. You do acknowledge  "Unfortunately, there is no way to repair/tighten the handle on the bowl" which implies a design deficiency.
Bottom line, it appears that Wolf is more interested in quibbling over details rather than addressing a potential problem. So be it. Perhaps I will share this story with [REDACTED] and the Consumer Product Safety Commsision to see how they view the issue. Please reconsider your decision.

There has been no further word from them.
I can understand them not wanting to reimburse me for buying s new bowl, but cannot understand them ignoring a potential safety issue. I don't know if you have previous reports on this, but if I hadn't intervened, my wife could have been injured when the handle suddenly separated. Thank you.

[REDACTED]

productDescription: The product is a NeoCharge Smart Splitter 240V. It is a compact white electrical device designed to share a single 240V outlet between an electric vehicle charger and a household appliance such as an electric dryer. The unit has two 240V receptacle ports on the front and a single 240V plug on the back. It is rectangular with rounded edges and is roughly the size of a small brick, about 13 cm by 13 cm by 7 cm. The exterior casing is hard plastic. The device is meant to automatically switch between loads so only one appliance runs at a time. It is marketed as a safe way to avoid installing a second 240V circuit. The surface labeling includes the NeoCharge brand name and basic electrical information.
incidentDescription:
We began using the NeoCharge Smart Splitter exactly as instructed in their safety guidelines and through direct contact by email. The unit was installed correctly. Our EV draws about 22 amps during normal operation which is well below their recommended 24 amps. We never exceeded the load limits stated in their documentation. This is the 2nd unit they've replaced as the first just stopped working. 

After some routine use, we noticed a light burning smell coming from the unit. This was unusual because the previous replacement unit had been working normally before this. When we inspected the device, we observed clear signs of overheating at 145F and climbing on the outer shell casing. The exterior of the box felt hotter than expected and the plug area began melting. The smell continued each time the EV was charging.

We verified that the EV charger, the outlet, and the surrounding setup were all functioning normally and had no issues. There were no visible problems with the outlet or wiring. The only source of heat or smell was the Smart Splitter itself.

We searched online and found multiple reports from other customers describing very similar overheating and melting incidents with the same product. This raised more concern since the problem seems to repeat across different users.

No injuries occurred, but the burning smell and signs of melting created a clear fire risk. We disconnected the unit immediately once we realized something was wrong.

productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
manufacturer: Lagom Kitchen Company, dba Our Place
incidentDescription:
On the very first use of my new Our Place Large Wonder Oven Pro, I placed food inside, set the temperature and a 15-minute timer, pressed Start, and briefly stepped outside expecting the oven to shut off automatically when the timer reached zero.
Because food was inside from the beginning, the oven became permanently stuck in Preheating mode and never started the countdown timer. It continued holding the set baking temperature indefinitely with no auto-shutoff.
Within minutes the food severely charred, filled the entire house with thick smoke, and triggered every smoke detector. I returned to find the kitchen full of smoke and the food burned black.
The manufacturer has confirmed this behavior is by design and that there is no safety timeout if the preheat cycle never completes. This allows the oven to cook at full temperature (up to 450 F) for hours with no automatic shut-off  a clear and reproducible fire hazard.
I have video evidence clearly showing the display stuck on Preheating while the food continues cooking inside.

productDescription: Nebula Capsule 3 Laser portable projector. Cylindrical, compact portable projector designed for home entertainment use. Approximately the size of a beverage can, with a dark gray/black exterior and integrated internal lithium-ion battery. The device is intended to project video content and can be operated while plugged into external power via USB-C. The product includes internal electronics, cooling vents, and a rechargeable lithium-ion battery.
incidentDescription:
I am reporting a fire incident involving a Nebula Capsule 3 Laser portable projector.

The product was being used in my apartment for normal home entertainment purposes. The projector was idle at the time of the incident but was plugged into power, which is typical consumer use for this type of device.

On October 2nd 2025, around 1PM PST, the projector suddenly overheated and began to smoke and burn. I was present when this occurred and observed active combustion from the device. I immediately removed the projector from my apartment to prevent further damage or potential injury.

After the incident, I contacted the manufacturer (Nebula / Anker Innovations) and provided proof of purchase, the product serial number, photographs of the damaged device, and a detailed description of the event.

Despite this information, the manufacturer has repeatedly declined to proceed with a safety investigation unless I provide a fire department incident report or written confirmation from a fire station. No emergency response occurred because the fire was contained immediately and did not require dispatch.

Over an extended period of time, the manufacturer has continued to require documentation that does not exist and has not initiated a substantive safety review of the incident.

I am submitting this report due to concerns about the safety of this product, particularly the risk of fire while the device is idle or connected to power, and to help prevent potential harm to other consumers.

incidentDescription:
I purchased a brand-new Steam Deck handheld gaming device manufactured by Valve. Within the first day of use, the internal lithium-ion battery began to malfunction. The device would not hold a charge and could only operate while plugged in. Shortly afterward, the battery began visibly swelling, causing the back panel of the device to bulge outward near the left grip.

The swelling progressed over several days and made the device unsafe to handle. I stopped using or charging the product as soon as I noticed the deformation because I was concerned about the risk of a lithium battery fire. The device was used in a normal manner and was only a few hours old when the issue appeared.

There were no injuries, but the battery swelling created a significant fire hazard inside my home. I contacted the manufacturer, and they acknowledged the issue, but the return process was delayed for several days, forcing me to store a potentially hazardous product longer than appropriate.

I am reporting this because a lithium-ion battery swelling in a brand-new device is a serious safety concern. I want to ensure this issue is documented in case it reflects a broader manufacturing or battery defect.

productDescription: Mainstays humidifier (Model HF3190W-UL) White
incidentDescription:
On Friday, November 14th 2025, a White Mainstays humidifier (Model HF3190W-UL) caught fire in our home. At approximately 2:05 PM, my husband returned home and immediately smelled smoke in the house. Seconds later, the upstairs fire alarms activated. The smoke was coming from the humidifier located in our upstairs bedroom.

The device was actively burning from inside the unit. The plastic housing had melted open and flames were visible. My husband attempted to extinguish the fire using a fire extinguisher, which helped some but the flames continued. He then carried the burning humidifier with his bare hands into our hallway bathroom and placed it in the bathtub, where he doused it with water until the fire was fully out.

While he was working on the fire, I called 911 at 2:07 PM, and the fire department arrived within minutes to clear the home and ensure the fire was completely out.

The fire caused damage to the carpet, subfloor, hallway flooring, and a wooden bench. There is smoke odor throughout the second floor and faintly through the rest of the home. My husband inhaled smoke while suppressing the fire.

The humidifier bears an ETL certification mark, and it appears that the ignition originated internally. The top is completely melted, internal components are charred, and the wiring is visibly burned.

The unit was purchased approximately two to three years ago. We still have the burned device and can provide photos or the physical unit if needed.

This incident created a significant fire hazard, physical risk, and property damage.

incidentDescription:
I am reporting a critical and hidden electrocution hazard with a Kobe range hood (Model IN2648SQB-1200-1) 
The incident began when an individual with electrical experience came to install warranty replacement parts. As a safety precaution, he first unplugged the unit from the wall. Upon touching the internal components of the unplugged hood, he received a light electrical shock.
He then used an electrical meter to check for current but could not detect the source of the leak, as the charge appeared to have dissipated. Believing the danger had passed, he proceeded to install the new parts. After the installation, the hood was temporarily working. 
My mother then attempted to unplug the hood so we could screw the final coverings back on, but her hip was touching the metal oven and she received a stronger electrical shock. It was likely because her body created a path between the energized hood and the grounded oven. 
I then went to unplug the hood and after successfully unplugging it, I attempted to screw the final coverings back on. The moment I touched the hood, I received a third, light electrical shock.
While the shocks were not severely painful, they were distinct and alarming. This sequence proves an extremely dangerous and latent product defect: the hood was unsafe both when plugged in and, moments later, after being unplugged. It can store a dangerous electrical charge that dissipates upon shock, making it undetectable with standard tools, only to become live again unpredictably. The fact that it delivers any shock at all under these conditions demonstrates a fundamental failure of basic electrical safety, creating a hidden and unpredictable risk of more severe injury.

productDescription:
The Onewheel+ XR is a self-balancing electric skateboard (often called a one-wheeled skateboard) manufactured by Future Motion Inc., designed for recreational riding, commuting, and off-road terrain. Its a single-board device with a 750W Hypercore hub motor embedded in an 11.5-inch x 6.5-6-inch Vega off-road tire, powered by a 324Wh Nickel Manganese Cobalt Oxide (NMC) lithium-ion battery (63V nominal), and controlled via solid-state MEMS 6-DOF (degrees of freedom) footpad sensors for lean-based steering and speed control (up to 19 mph/30 kph top speed, 12-18 mile/19-29 km typical range, >30 max lean angle). The board charges in ~110 minutes via USB-C and includes a Maghandle for carrying.
Dimensions: 9.5 in x 11.5 in x 29.5 in (241 mm x 292 mm x 750 mm).Weight: 27 lbs (12.5 kg).Standard color: Black base with gray footpads (custom colors like blue or red available via aftermarket, but stock is monochrome).Size variants: None (one size fits all riders up to ~250 lbs recommended).Purpose: Urban and trail mobility, with app integration (Onewheel app) for ride tracking, firmware updates, and modes (e.g., Silent, Mission for speed). Hardware rev 4212 (as in your case) dates to mid-2020 production, known for fender-sensor interference without factory bumper pads.
This matches your serial 2118255594 and July 2025 support thread (FM confirmed the missing bumper pad defect causing footpad wear).
incidentDescription:
What happened that made you want to report?
I contacted Future Motion in July 2025 about footpad sensor wear caused by the fender grinding them (hardware rev 4212). They confirmed the missing bumper pad defect in writing but refused repair or warning, advising only to remove the fender and buy a new one. I removed the fender as a precaution. On October 26, 2025, it abruptly cut out on flat ground with no warning, ejecting me. After the fall, I researched and discovered Future Motion has known since at least 2020 about: (1) rev 4212 and earlier boards suffering fender-induced footpad wear leading to ghost-riding, and (2) balance wire failures causing sudden ejections. They never disclosed this despite my prior report. I emailed them again on October 29, 2025  no reply in over a week.
What type of product(s) were being used?
Onewheel+ XR (serial 2118255594, hardware rev 4212, FW 4165)
Who was using the product(s)?
I was using the product.
How were the product(s) being used?
Normal ride on level, smooth pavement at moderate speed (~84% battery, firmware 4165 active).
Were there any injuries that happened or may have happened while using the product?
Yes  head hit pavement first, then elbow. Helmet [REDACTED] cracked full-length down the side; I was severely dazed with possible concussion; elbow skinned and contused.
How did any injuries occur?
I was ejected when the boards power cut out without any warning, despite being well within operational limits. The ride log recorded only 0.63 miles and omitted altitude data entirely  never seen in 6712 lifetime miles.

UPDATED ON 11/18/2025: [I am writing to provide a critical update to my injury complaint (20251103-8998E-2147326613) filed on November 3, 2025, regarding my Onewheel XR (Serial 2118255594, Hardware 4212, Firmware Gemini-4165), which caused serious head trauma and injury on October 26, 2025.

TIMELINE: KNOWN DEFECT â†’ INJURY â†’ EXPLICIT REFUSAL OF REMEDY

Contact Attempt 1 - July 2025

I initially contacted Future Motion regarding accelerated footpad wear caused by the fender grinding. During this communication, Future Motion support staff ([REDACTED]) confirmed in writing that my board (Hardware 4212) has a known missing componentâ€”the fender buffer padsâ€”which is supposed to prevent the fender from contacting the footpad. Despite acknowledging this hardware defect, Future Motion refused to provide replacement parts. Instead, they advised me to either remove the fender entirely or purchase a replacement fender.

Contact Attempt 2 - October 29, 2025

On October 26, 2025, while riding on flat ground at normal speed, my board suddenly cut power with zero warning and ejected me, causing head trauma, helmet destruction, and elbow injury. Three days later, on October 29, 2025, I contacted Future Motion requesting board replacement under CPSC Recall 23-299. This formal demand was my second organized contact with the company.

No response was received.

Contact Attempt 3 - November 3, 2025

With no response after more than a week, I sent a third email to Future Motion on November 3, 2025, again requesting board replacement under CPSC Recall 23-299. This communication included detailed information about my injury, the incident circumstances, and my board's specific serial number and hardware configuration.

Again, no response.

Contact Attempt 4 - November 4-5, 2025

On November 4, 2025, I created a new email account ([REDACTED]) and submitted a fourth contact request to Future Motion's support address (support@onewheel.com), again requesting board replacement under CPSC Recall 23-299. I received an immediate automated response confirming receipt.

The next day, on November 5, 2025, Future Motion responded directly to my new email address via their support account. However, rather than honoring the CPSC-mandated recall remedy, support staff member [REDACTED] sent a response explicitly stating:

"...we cannot provide monetary compensation or a full board replacement..."

This statement represents a direct refusal to comply with CPSC Recall 23-299's mandatory remedy for defective boards. Rather than addressing the known hardware defect, [REDACTED] then proceeded to ask multiple questions attempting to shift responsibility for the board's failure to rider error, despite my extensive riding history and documented incident parameters.

WHY THIS WAS NOT RIDER ERROR

As a rider with over 12,000 miles of lifetime Onewheel experience, I have experienced approximately 20 prior falls and incidents. In all of those prior incidents which occurred across varied terrain, different riding conditions, and numerous circumstances I attributed each injury to my own riding error, judgment mistakes, or environmental factors. I have never sued or complained about those incidents because I understood I was responsible for those accidents.

October 26, 2025 was fundamentally different. In my 12,000 miles of riding experience, this was the first time I experienced a sudden power cutout with zero warning on completely flat ground. The incident parameters (normal speed: 9.3 MPH average, flat terrain, 84% battery remaining, no warning signals) were unlike any prior fall. My ride data clearly documents these parameters, proving this was not reckless riding but rather a product defect failure.

[REDACTED] attempt to characterize this incident as rider error is not supported by any evidence. It contradicts my extensive riding experience demonstrating responsible behavior, my ride data showing normal operating conditions, my own credibility demonstrated by taking responsibility for prior genuine rider errors, and the documented hardware defect (missing buffer pads) that Future Motion itself acknowledged in July.

MANUFACTURING DEFECT PATTERN

My initial CPSC report documented that Future Motion has known since at least 2020 about hardware revision 4212 and earlier boards suffering fender-induced footpad wear leading to ghost-riding (sudden power cutout with no warning) and balance wire failures causing sudden ejections. The defect I experienced on October 26, 2025 sudden power cutout with zero warning causing ejection on flat ground matches precisely the known defect pattern Future Motion has been aware of for at least five years.

(2) the second serious issue is about how the company custom programs their heaters thermostat to work which goes against how one should work, the standards, and the intuitive understanding of how all consumer's expect them to work. For decades any heater whether HVAC or a portable heater, the thermostat would only go to the users desired set temperature with the exception it might heat up to +1 degrees, but never higher. It would also never turn on again until the temperature fell below the user set temperature. This is part of regulations for a reason, if you have an infant a prodcut needs to be reliable so the user can ensure the device will keep there room within recommended temps; otherwise if the heater was to go higher (like dreo unit does) then it would put the life of the infant at risk possibly leading to Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS) because the high stress to the babys immature temperature regulation system leading to irregular breathing and heart rate. The reason the Dreo heater is so dangerous to infants is becuase the product  does not operate like a normal thermostat and instead the Dreo will heat up to +5 degrees from the set temperature. It will also go back on for 3min every 15min before it even falls back to the set temperature which completer defeats the point and shows that this company has no idea how to make a safe product and put lives at risk because they want to reinvent the wheel with no regard to safety and guidelines. Its also dangerous from the materials they are using that are creating hazardous chemical smells that make a person face numb. This is  why Chinese products should be banned in America. I contacted the company and there reasoning was it goes up to +5 degrees to help prevent temp fluctuations and significantly overshooting the goal temperature. productDescription:
The product is a Ninja Professional Blender purchased from Costco approximately [30 days before the incident]. It is a countertop kitchen blender with a large clear plastic pitcher (approximately 72 oz capacity), black base housing with electronic controls, and a removable stacked blade assembly. The unit is designed for making smoothies, crushing ice, and blending fruit or vegetables.

The blender came with a black plastic lid with a pour spout and locking mechanism. The blade assembly is a vertical multi-blade shaft that fits inside the pitcher. The base is rectangular, black in color, with Ninja branding in silver on the front.

The blender was sold in Costco's kitchen appliance section as a standard household blender intended for daily consumer use.
incidentDescription:
While making a small fruit smoothie in a Ninja blender purchased from Costco, the product violently failed during normal use. The blade assembly suddenly ejected from the container with explosive force. The loud noise was so strong that it caused ear pain, and the smoothie contents sprayed across the kitchen, covering walls, counters, and floors.

The blender was being used properly with fruit, ice, and liquid, nothing unusual or outside of normal use. In fact, I have blended much harsher items in the past (such as frozen bananas) without issue, so there is no reason this smoothie should have caused such a catastrophic failure. The unit was operated by an adult following normal instructions.

The flying blade scratched my kitchen floors, and the splattered contents permanently stained my walls and wood surfaces, leaving damage that will require resurfacing and repainting.

Although I was fortunate not to be physically struck, the blade assembly launched out at high speed directly toward the area where I was standing. It could easily have cut my hands, face, or even my neck and caused life-threatening injury. The sudden blast was loud enough to cause temporary ear discomfort. The incident created significant property damage and could have easily resulted in hospitalization or worse had the blade struck me.

The product has since been returned to Costco, which issued a refund and documented the incident, but this dangerous malfunction needs to be formally reported for consumer safety.

I pressed the brake lever repeatedly, but the scooter failed to slow down or stop. As a result, I lost control and was thrown forward onto the pavement.

I suffered bleeding from both knees and hands, along with significant bruising and emotional distress. I had to visit urgent care for treatment, and several personal items were damaged during the fall, including my [REDACTED] Watch, helmet, and clothing. The incident happened without any warning, and it could have resulted in more severe injuries. I believe this is a serious product safety concern.

I contacted Segway regarding this incident but have not received any response. I have also found similar brake failure reports associated with other Segway scooter models on public consumer forums.

productDescription:
The product is the ES4-800RN/ES4-800RB electric scooter, manufactured by Consumer Mobility Services. It is a foldable, two-wheeled electric scooter designed for personal urban transportation. The scooter has a black frame with silver accents (color may vary slightly by unit), foldable handlebars, and a standing deck for a single rider. It is powered by a lithium-ion battery integrated into the deck, with a motor that allows speeds up to approximately 1520 mph.
The scooter measures approximately 42 inches in length, 16 inches in width, and 45 inches in height when fully assembled. The handlebars include hand-operated brakes and acceleration controls, while the deck has a textured, non-slip surface. It has four points of contact with the rider (both hands and both feet) when in use, making structural integrity critical for safe operation. The screw assembly bridge connecting the handlebars to the deck is a key structural component that has failed in multiple instances.
The product is intended for individual adult riders on paved surfaces such as streets, bike lanes, and sidewalks for commuting or recreational purposes.
brand: The brand name of the ES4-800RN/ES4-800RB electric
incidentDescription:
I am submitting this report due to repeated, serious safety failures involving an ES4-800RN/ES4-800RB electric scooter provided by Consumer Mobility Services.
On the first incident in October 2021, while riding the scooter in New York City under normal usage conditions on city streets, the scooter snapped in half above the screw assembly bridge. This failure caused me to be violently thrown to the ground, creating a high risk of severe injury, dismemberment, or death. Following this incident, the company sent me a replacement model, which I used sparingly due to safety concerns.
On October 3, 2025, while riding the replacement scooter under normal usage conditions, the same catastrophic failure occurred: the scooter again snapped in half in a similar location. I was using the scooter on city streets at typical riding speeds of approximately 15 mph, with hands and feet in contact with the device. The structural failure created an immediate danger, as it could have caused death, paralysis, or other severe injuries. Fortunately, I was not gravely injured this time, but the potential for life-threatening harm was extremely high.
Attempts to contact Consumer Mobility Services following the second incident were prolonged and unsatisfactory. I was advised that I could pay for evaluation, shipping, parts, and labor to repair a device that they provided and had already demonstrated as unsafe. Given the repeated failure, I distrust the safety of the product and am concerned for both my safety and the safety of other consumers.
This report is intended to formally document the recurring safety hazard posed by this scooter model and to seek a solution that prevents further risk of injury or death.

productDescription: OL601 Series Ninja Foodi XL Pressure Cooker Steam Fryer with SmartLid 8qt
incidentDescription:
I was cooking food at home using a Ninja Foodi OL601 combination pressure cooker/air fryer when the top of the appliance emitted smoke, and I could hear electrical arcing.  
I believed that the lid heating element was soiled by food residue, so I unplugged the product and allowed it to cool. Then I detached some lid components in order to access and clean the heating element. However, I found that insulation on one of the electrical wires to the heating element had failed, causing the insulation to pull back and the bare metal conductor to be exposed inside the lid. The bare wire lead shorted out against adjacent metal inside the lid. 
Nobody was injured. However, I believe that this issue represents an electrical shock and fire hazard.  
The appliance was not repairable from this damage and was disposed of. No other property was damaged.

The product in question is a Frigidaire French Door Refrigerator, Model FRSS2623AW, purchased in September 2024. I am the primary user, and the appliance is used in a private residence by myself and my partner under normal conditions.

productDescription:
The product is a Vornado space heater, model TAVH10 (Type TAVH10, FC: WHL-TAVH10). It is manufactured by Vornado Air, LLC, Andover, Kansas, USA, and made in China.

The heater operates on 120VAC, 60Hz, 1500W and is labeled as thermally protected and conforming to UL Standard 1278. Serial number is JUN23-103351.

It is a portable electric space heater, designed for household use, intended to heat individual rooms. The unit is black in color (standard appearance for this model), approximately 1214 inches tall and about 10 inches wide. It is a floor-standing model with digital controls and a cord with a standard 3-prong plug.
incidentDescription:
A Vornado space heater was operating in an upstairs guest bedroom when I heard a loud buzzing sound lasting about 510 seconds. Shortly afterward, the smoke alarm went off. Upon checking the house, I discovered the guest bedroom was smoky, and the wall around the electrical outlet was charred.

The heater had been running unattended for about 15 minutes after my guest left the room. It was plugged directly into the wall outlet, not into a power strip or extension cord.

There were no physical injuries, but there was property damage. The heaters cord was melted at the prongs, the wall outlet and outlet cover were partially melted and burned, and the wall surface around the outlet was blackened. I was able to wipe away some of the charring, but not all.

When I found the unit, the plug had already come loose from the outlet, as if forced out during the event. I immediately turned off the circuit breaker to the room and aired it out. Later, once the smoke cleared, I began repairs. Testing confirmed the electrical line voltage was normal, and a new outlet functions properly under normal power load.

productDescription: Ninja Blast Portable Blender
incidentDescription: This is what I have typed up to email to attorneys. Can you tell me if this is good or not?   On Tuesday evening, my 10-year-old nonverbal son with Down Syndrome and Autism nearly severed his fingers with a Ninja Blast portable blender. I had bought it a year ago to make smoothies for my mother after her stroke, but she passed away before I had a chance to even use it. My kitchen is under renovation, so my appliances are all out of their normal place. This blender hasn't been out of the cabinet in a year, so when my son saw it, I assume it caught his interest, being new to him. I was preparing his evening medication with him standing beside me, and within an instant, he had picked up the blender and simultaneously turned on the blades with his hand inside. It happened so fast I couldn't even register what was happening. To my knowledge, it hadn't even been charged in the past year as it has been stored away in the cabinet. It did not have the lid on, so I also did not understand how the motor could turn on. Seven extremely traumatic hours later, two ER sedations and stitches, I arrived back home at 3am and crawled into bed to try to make sense of what happened. In my research, I discovered that this particular model lacks a safety latch to prevent the blades from turning on when the lid is open. Every blender and Ninja I have ever owned did. I am absolutely devastated that this happened to my son. He has endured so much in his life...being born with Down Syndrome and a heart condition, being adopted from China at 3, heart repair resulting in pulmonary hypertension at 4, epilepsy, leukemia at 7, which he fought bravely and is now in remission. He already has so much medical trauma that it is almost impossible to even succeed at basic well-child care for him. This should have never happened.

incidentDescription: I just received a pressure cooker that I ordered and I believe its an unsafe product. One of the first things youre supposed to do is to run a test by filling the pot 2/3 full of water and running a cycle. The pot is never supposed to be filled more than 2/3 full of anything. I noticed that the measurement lines in the pot are in 5ths not 3rds, so there is no clear indication of where 2/3 full is. So then I thought I would just use the cup measurement lines on the other side of the indicator and do a calculation. Since its a 12 quart pot, which is 48 cups, 2/3 full would be just under 32 cups. When I poured 32 cups in, it came up to a mark that said 20 cups. So the measurement lines are way off. Since pressure cookers can be very dangerous if used improperly, Im returning it without using. incidentDescription:
In December 2023, I recieved a phone battery pack() as a Christmas gift. I used it without issue until January 2025, when in burst into flames while charging at my workplace ([REDACTED]). It caught my clothing on fire, and I was able to pay myself out , unplug it from the power strip the charger it was plugged into, and blow out the fire so that it was only smoldering and not actively on fire. I evacuated with the rest of my lab, was checked out by emts on the scene, and did not immediately show any injuries, though my hands and face had soot from the fire on them, and gave a report to the fire Marshall, who collected my clothes as evidence, as well as the remains of the battery pack. I tried to show them
The item from my Amazon wishlist, but it was no longer sold, and we could tell from the vendor name that it was some Chinese company that did not advertise its contact number to report the incident. Upon returning home, my hands, especially my right hand tingled the rest of the evening, I suspect from either  a mild electric shock from unpluging the item, or from whatever was in the spot from the exploded lithium ion battery pack. My left eye was also sore and watering, so I repeatedly flushed it with water that day, and needed to reapply eye drops for 2 days afterward, and I suspect I had a bit of the soot in my eye. I have since been understandably traumatized and leary of anything containing a lithium battery, particularly while charging. Today, my father (who purchased the item as a gift for me) was emailed by Amazon that there was a recall for the product in question, and informed me I should report it here.

Incident Description: Our OneWheel GT-s appears to have a serious safety defect related to its battery and controller. The unit charges only to 90% capacity, according to the app. After charging, when my son attempted to ride, the board initially struggled to engage balance mode. Once it did, within 3040 seconds, the unit began to beep with a low battery warning, despite showing 90% charge. It then abruptly pitched back and forced a complete stop.

We attempted to reset the charge by leaving it on the charger for a full day, verified the 90% reading again, and repeated the ride. The exact same failure occurred  this time causing my son to fall and sustain injury due to the sudden stop.

At the time of the incident, diagnostics reported the following:

Battery Temperature: 75.2F
Controller Temperature: 80.6F
Motor Temperature: 73.4F

Hazard: The unit appears to falsely indicate sufficient charge while simultaneously triggering a shutdown protocol within minutes of use. The sudden, unannounced stop creates a high risk of serious injury to riders.

Outcome: My son was injured when the board abruptly powered down. The unit is unsafe and cannot be used.

Requested Action: We are requesting that the CPSC investigate this safety defect, as it may be systemic across the GT-s product line. The hazard mimics previously reported OneWheel nosedive incidents that have led to severe injuries and fatalities. We are willing to provide the defective unit for inspection.

productDescription:
Ninja Air Fryer Toaster Oven, purchased new from Amazon on December 2, 2024.

    Color: Stainless steel with black accents.

    Model: SP351

    Serial Number: S29UW302F2S0

    Combination countertop appliance with air fryer, toaster, bake, and broil functions.

    Includes a crumb tray, air fryer basket, wire rack, and bake pan.
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
What happened?
I purchased a Ninja Air Fryer Toaster Oven from Amazon on December 2, 2024. In July 2025just 8 months laterI discovered significant rust forming inside the cooking area, specifically underneath the heating element tray where food drippings and steam naturally accumulate. The product was used strictly as intended: air frying, toasting, and baking small meals. No harsh chemicals, soaking, or misuse occurred.

This rust poses a food safety hazard because its located where heat, moisture, and food contact happen. Rust particles can break loose during cooking and contaminate food. Ingesting rust can be harmful, especially for children, elderly, or those with compromised immune systems.

When I contacted Ninja, they refused to replace or repair the unit, even though its well within the standard 1-year warranty. Customer service gave conflicting and confusing information:

    At first said they could not help.

    The next day claimed it was registered but had no warranty.

    Suggested bizarre troubleshooting steps like reading numbers off the electrical prongs and doing a video call to prove the damage, despite already having clear photos.

    One representative implied the rust was my fault without any evidence.

The unit is still functional but unsafe, and the companys refusal to address a clear material failure leaves other consumers at risk.

Who was using the product?
I, an adult, used the product for normal household cooking.

How was it being used?
Used per instructionsair frying vegetables, meats, and baked goods. No submersion in water or harsh cleaning agents.

Were there any injuries?
No injuries yet, but the potential exists for ingesting rust particles if unnoticed in food.

incidentDescription:
We purchased a Keurig coffeemaker at Walmart in Murray, KY on July 4, 2025, and registered it online on the day of purchase.

Less than a month later the machine wouldn't brew and began to dump boiling hot water out the bottom and onto our counters while still plugged in, which is both a burn and a shock hazard making the product unsafe. Luckily we were able to unplug the machine before anyone was injured. Since the machine was unusable we decided to file for the one year warranty we had signed up for when registering the product. I called the company and was told by the agent that I could use a duplicate receipt from the Murray Walmart as proof of purchase, so I drove the 60 mile round trip to Walmart to generate the receipt. 

We submitted the documentation as required and were rejected via a form email - probably no live person even reviewed the claim. My guess is the company is implementing cost cutting measures by refusing to honor warranty even when they've sold a dangerous product. They should be focusing on getting these dangerous items off the market instead of telling consumers they're stuck with something that might shock or injure someone. There's a post on the Keurig [REDACTED] saying they had the same problem with their machine, so I wonder if this company sold a large number of these unsafe products.

This product could potentially cause illness to consumers who ingest the contaminated ice or water.  I performed regular cleaning cycles as recommended by the manufacturer. When the problem persisted, I followed online advice to run a water and bleach solution through the machine. This process flushed out a significant amount of black, mold-like material. I urge the CPSC to investigate this product and consider a recall to prevent other consumers from potential illness.

incidentDescription:
I have a serious concern and formal complaint regarding a Frigidaire ice maker, Model EFIC256, which I purchased from Walmart in May 2024.

The unit functioned properly for over a year. I have diligently followed all maintenance instructions and have only used double-filtered water to ensure its longevity and cleanliness. Recently, however, the machine began to produce an unusual noise. After an initial cleaning did not resolve the issue, I decided to remove the side panels to investigate further.

To my shock and disgust, upon opening the unit, I discovered an extensive amount of mold growth inside. It appears that condensation from the compressor combined with the warmth of the motor, created a breeding ground for this hazardous mold. This is not only a major defect but also a severe health hazard.

I initially contacted Frigidaire regarding this issue and was directed to Curtis International. Despite multiple attempts to resolve this, I have been met with various excuses and a lack of urgency. The serious health risks associated with a household appliance producing a product for consumption while harboring mold have not been adequately addressed.

productDescription: Ninja Foodi OL601 XL Smart Lock  14-in-1, 8 quart.
incidentDescription:
I am writing regarding my Ninja Foodi OL601C 14-in-1 Smart Lock 8qt (S/N: Q29RJ205Z1Q2), still in warranty registered with SharkNinja (Shark). My Ninja has developed concerning issues  heavy steam coming out of the dome lid while in the steam crisp mode. I have taken care of the product very meticulously and have looked through all available resources to troubleshoot. After much research, I have concluded that the product has malfunctioned in less than a year. Shark has recalled its OP models and discontinued all OL SmartLid/pressure cooking models due to injuries suffered by users. The heavy steam on the Dome Lid is very concerning to me.

On August 6, 2025, at [REDACTED] PM, I contacted customer service at Shark to resolve the issue.  He mentioned that I needed to cut the cord first, send an email to prove that it was completed before SharkNinja would send the replacement item. After almost half-an-hour interaction/ being held on call, he did not disclose until I probed further that no comparable replacement model was available due to the discontinuation of multi-cookers with the pressure-cooking function. The pressure-cooking function is a core feature that motivated my purchase. I find the withholding of critical information - the replacement is not the same item I bought-  misleading and deeply concerning.  After my third attempt raising my grouses with Shark, a representative emailed me on  August 12th .

Shark offered a 5-quart FD101 (pressure cooker + air fryer) plus an additional air fryer of my choice. This is unacceptable because:
1. FD101 is smaller (5 qt vs. my 8 qt) and cannot meet my original cooking volume needs.
2. The extra air fryer duplicates existing functions, adds clutter, and undermines my original space-saving purpose.
3. FD101 is older stock and future parts support is questionable, given current poor support.
4. Verified consumer reports show OL601C frequently fails within 1-2 years, often with identical lid/wiring faults.

I contacted Amazon 7 times (email/phone) for assistance with no resolution. This violates:
- Virginia Consumer Protection Act ( 59.1-196 et seq.)
- Magnuson-Moss Warranty Act (15 U.S.C.  23012312)
- Uniform Commercial Code  2-314

As the original retailer, Amazon shares responsibility. I request a full refund from SharkNinja or Amazon. 


Furthermore, there are widespread customer complaints online indicating that similar Smart Lock models often fail not long after the warranty period;  raising serious questions about the longevity and value of SharkNinjas high-end multi-cooking appliances.

As a resident of [REDACTED], I am protected under the Virginia Consumer Protection Act ( 59.1-196 et seq.), which prohibits deceptive or unfair business practices. I also cite the Magnuson-Moss Warranty Act and the Uniform Commercial Code ( 2-314), which guarantee consumers reasonably durable and functional goods.

Given:

The premium price of the unit,
Its in-warranty status,
The lack of a comparable price-point and functionality replacement,
And rather deceptive handling of my support interaction,
I believe a full refund is the most fair and reasonable resolution. Unfortunately, Shark has refused a refund.

productDescription: Mendodta Model No. FV44I-Mod Fireplace Insert Heater
incidentDescription:
When my wife got up on Sunday June 1st she called me right away to inform me that our fire place insert has self ignited and no one had turned it on.  I had removed the battery's from the remote which starts it to protect it from acid battery leaks.  Sure enough it was lite and the pilot keep trying to relight even thou it was lit.  I had to shut off the gas main valve to stop the flame. Then switch off the pilot lighting switch to stop it from trying to ignite it.  I felt this was very unsafe condition and called the installer (Schagrin Gas Company Middletown Delaware) and they told me it wasn't there problem it was the manufactures issue.
I then call them (Mendota  at Johnson Gas Appliance Company [REDACTED] - Cedar Rapids, IA 52405 and informed them of the unsafe condition that their Mendota Model FV44i-Mod ignited by it self and I was lucky we were home at the time. They informed me that they would have a technician check it out.  They sent a Schagrin expert to investigate the issue and he found the receiver for the mother board failed and when he turned on the pilot switch it tried to lite 
without the remote. He had to get a new receiver for the mother board and replace it.  I feel this is a very unsafe condition for public use and the Mondota company who design and built it should recall and reprogram the unit to shut off when a receiver or mother board failure not lite off. We were so lucky to be home when this happen.

productDescription: Segway Ninebot F3 eKickScooter, adult electric scooter, black with gray trim, folding handlebar design. Features a thumb-operated accelerator on the right handlebar, front and rear braking systems, and a digital dashboard display. Purchased new and activated on May 15, 2025. Scooter serial number is: 1EFBE2503C1089. Accelerator has a specific serial number imprinted: JNM25010534
incidentDescription:
On August 1, 2025, at approximately 6:20 PM ET, while operating a Segway eKickScooter Ninebot F3 (serial number 1EFBE2503C1089) activated in May 2025, the accelerator became stuck in the fully engaged position shortly after rainfall had stopped. The handlebar was slightly damp, but the scooter was not being ridden in the rain at the time.

The throttle lock caused sudden, uncontrolled acceleration. I was riding on a flat paved surface at moderate speed and had to bail off to avoid colliding with obstacles. This resulted in bruising and soreness to my right arm and hand from bracing my fall, as well as swelling in my left knee from my left leg absorbing the force of contacting the ground upon landing. Symptoms of these injuries persisted for over a week after the incident. The scooter itself sustained visible cosmetic damage to the handlebar, deck, and frame.

This malfunction is consistent with numerous publicly reported throttle-sticking incidents on Segway F- and G-series scooters, often associated with moisture or throttle assembly misalignment. In some cases, Segway has acknowledged the defect and replaced the throttle module. This defect poses an ongoing safety hazard to other consumers, as the failure mode could occur without warning during normal operation. Due to the serious risk posed, I have asked Segway to replace the scooter due to the faulty accelerator and cosmetic damage sustained during the incident, but they have failed to follow up with me in a timely manner.

Additional property damage occurred during the incident, totaling approximately $275, including torn or damaged clothing and accessories. Witnesses were present and can corroborate the events leading to and during the accident.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

manufacturer: SHENZHEN GUIYANG NETWORK TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD dba VAGKRI
incidentDescription:
I experienced a serious safety incident involving a dangerously defective VAGKRI 16-Inch Wall Mount Fan, which was purchased through a third-party seller on Amazon.

While the fan was in normal operation, mounted on the wall and running at a standard speed, the blades suddenly broke apart and were forcefully ejected from the unit. One of the sharp, jagged blades struck me in the face. More important though, at the time of the incident, I was seated nearby, and my 1.5-month-old infant daughter was also present in the room, although she was not physically harmed, the loud noise and flying debris startled her significantly. Since the incident, she has shown signs of ongoing psychological distress, including a pronounced fear of loud sounds and frequent emotional outbursts. These symptoms may require professional evaluation and treatment. The debris came extremely close to hitting her, and it could have resulted in a severe injury.

I initially contacted the seller on May 3, 2025, to report broken blades from the first unit. The seller sent a replacement. The incident described above occurred with the replacement fan. After reporting this to the seller on July 22, they offered only a refund and have taken no further action. Amazon instructed me to return the product, which I did, and I was informed that an investigation would be conducted. However, I have not received any report or follow-up from Amazon regarding the outcome.

This situation represents a serious product safety concern. The fan appears to have a significant design or manufacturing flaw that presents an ongoing risk of injury to both adults and children. I am requesting that this matter be thoroughly investigated to prevent further harm to other consumers. I have also reached out to product-safety@amazon.com to which I received a "full mailbox" message and it could not be delivered. A full inbox at your product safety department raises serious concerns about Amazons ability to handle active and dangerous consumer safety threats.

incidentDescription:
My son was riding a Ridstar Q20 Lite bike and the front wheel fell off.  The wheel was installed per the instructions and follow up instructional video, which I believe to be incorrect because the wheel retainer is not put into the axle in the instructions.

Update 8/7/2025: I’d like to add to the subject report that my son received 4 stitches for a laceration received when his face skid across the pavement after the front wheel fell off of his Ridstar Q20 lite while traveling approximately 15 mph.

 The instructions to assemble the front wheel of the bike aren’t just unclear. I think they’re actually wrong. 

  I’m an engineer with a professional engineering license. In my professional opinion, I believe there is a high likelihood that a child will die when the front wheel comes off of a bike traveling at close to top speed.  It will happen despite the fact that their parents installed the front wheel in accordance with the instructions.

productDescription: GE Monogram 48" vent hood
incidentDescription:
I own a GE Monogram 48 inch kitchen range vent hood and noticed that the grease baffle filters provided with the hood do not cover the entire air intake opening of the hood. I contacted GE regarding my vent hood, model ZV48SSF1SS, in which is found three 12.75 inch x 15 inch x 1 inch (25mm) [REDACTED] baffle grease filters, rated for fire prevention, and which according to the parts diagram of the hood should have only have three filters. The parts diagram states that the filters are GE part #WB02X10877. GE confirmed that the part number is correct, but upon pressing them for the dimensions they stated 13.5 inch x 16.5 inch x 2.25 inch which is clearly not the size of the filters I have. I then looked up the part number at repairclinic.com where a nice image of the filter laid on a grid confirms that the filter is 12.75 inches x 15 inches. I also confirmed that an internal ledge within the vent hood will not allow a filter greater than 30mm in thickness. So GE does not know what filter fits my vent hood and GE was not aware that three filters with a width of 12.75 inch each can only cover 38.25 inches of the vent hood opening leaving 7 inches of the 45.25 inch wide opening uncovered by a grease filter. This leads me to believe that when GE contracted with [REDACTED] for 48 vent hood filters they either transmitted an erroneous specification or thought they could get away using a filter for a narrower hood in the 48 hood. 

As you know know grease baffle filters must cover the entire opening of a vent hood to keep grease out of the vent exhaust duct that passes through an attic before exiting a roof. When the filters do not cover the entire opening, there are manufacturers who may provide spacers to fill in the gaps. Notably GE does not provide spacers. Because the filters serve to prevent a fire from passing up the duct, a gap may allow fire to travel into a duct and ignite grease in the duct which of course will burn down a home. 

This was a major design error on the part of GE. [REDACTED] provided what GE requested. Had GE provided three 15 inches x 15 inches  x 1 inch filters, homes could have been spared from burning down. A GE rep told me that there were no recalls on the vent hood; however, the lack of recalls provides no certainty that fires did not occur and that lives have not been lost because the causes of a major fire are often difficult to determine given the destruction of responsible factors. With respect to fires and there causes, I speak from experience as a former US Navy engineering officer responsible for fire prevention and fire fighting aboard a guided missile destroyer.

Of course having uncovered these facts, I will have to take 3 measures. Firstly, I will be engaging a consumer products tort lawyer for his opinion on the viability of a civil lawsuit. Secondly, I will be engaging the US Consumer Products Safety Commission (you guys whom I hope will take my concerns seriously) which has regulatory tools to uncover what injuries may have occurred and force GE to provide remediation. Thirdly, I will be engaging my own insurance company, [REDACTED], which is very interested in mitigating fire risks.

UPDATE 7/29/2025:
Dear CPSC Clearing House,

I have communicated with the maker of the baffle grease filters intended to keep fires from entering vent hood ductwork and they have informed me that the orientation of the filters in the image I provided you was incorrect. Both the prior owner and myself who followed his practice had the baffles incorrectly horizontally oriented.  When I rotated the filters 90 degrees such that the baffles were vertically oriented the gaps disappeared. 

I now see that on p 15 of the hood installation manual, which I recently downloaded only because I was searching for an electrical parts diagram, the orientation of correctly installed filters is depicted. As noted above, I also realize that they were installed incorrectly by the former owner of my home. I simply followed his practice and never thought about the gap until I began to wonder why there was a gap. Because it is obvious that filters can be installed incorrectly and not fall onto the range, perhaps GE could have provided a warning in the manual stating that filters must be installed as seen in the picture and that no gap should be present between filters when they are installed correctly. I installed them incorrectly just as the former owner did and I would never have noticed my mistake but for my conversations with the maker of the filters [REDACTED]. It is a wonder that the prior owner of my home didn’t burn the house down because he grilled meat on a gas range under the hood. Because purchasers of homes are also unlikely to be provided installation manuals on preexisting appliances, a permanent warning label on the hood and the filters would be a nice safety feature.

I have looked at manuals of current versions of the same GE hood and although they contain a diagram showing the vertical orientation of the baffles they do not contain warnings regarding incorrect filter baffle orientation and the necessity of not having gaps between filters caused by incorrect orientation of rectangular filters because the gaps create a risk of fires entering the vent ductwork. I am also concerned that the GE parts folks gave me the wrong dimensions of the filter after they confirmed that the filter part number was correct, and I am concerned that none of them could inform me that incorrect filter orientation was the cause of the gaps. It is only because I communicated with the USA rep of the Italian company which made the fire rated filters that I understood that the gap was due to an error by the prior owner and myself to properly install the filters. How not to do something is an important instruction that should accompany any instruction on how to do something. Unfortunately that type of instruction - which is necessary whenever it is physically possible to do something incorrectly - is rarely provided.  Image 2417 is an incorrect but physically possible  installation with gaps between filters apparent, and image 2422 is correct installation with no gaps. 

Thus, my only recommendation is that whenever fire is a risk, clearly worded warning labels with diagrams of correct and incorrect part orientations to advise users on proper installation be provided on or next to parts that can be improperly installed.

productDescription: Traeger Pro 34 Pellet Grill
incidentDescription:
Product: Traeger Pro 34 Wood Pellet Grill
Purchase Date: June 26, 2024
Retailer: Local hardware store

Summary of the Hazard:

Im reporting a fire hazard involving my Traeger Pro 34 grill.

On Mothers Day weekend 2025, during a long smoke of a brisket, the auger caught fire after about 12 hours of operation. The internal heat caused the grill to spike to unsafe temperatures and forced the lid to blow open.

I contacted Traeger support and was guided through a short test run, which seemed fine. After cleaning and waiting weeks, I re-tested the grill on July 29, 2025, with a new bag of pellets. The grill was set to 250F but continued to rise uncontrollably, eventually burning for nearly an hour after shutting it off. I estimate it reached 700F or more, damaging the structure and posing a significant risk to nearby people and property.

Despite proper maintenance, safe usage, and clear signs of a mechanical or design failure, Traeger has refused to take accountability, instead referring me back to a third-party store. Their support has not addressed the safety issue and appears to downplay the risk.

This unit should be investigated for potential fire risk or design flaw in the auger or temperature regulation system. I am concerned that this could lead to severe injury or property damage for others.

Injury or Damage:

Grill structure warped

Risk of injury from heat exposure

Unsafe temperature spikes and fire behavior

productDescription: Stand-up electric scooter designed for shared public use, accessed via the Bird mobile app. The scooter features a narrow standing deck, two wheels, electric motor drive, and handlebar steering with throttle and brake controls. These scooters are widely deployed in urban areas for short-distance transportation and are maintained by Birds internal fleet management team.
brand: Bird Rides Inc / Blue Jay Transit Inc (Bird)
incidentDescription:
Description of Incident:

While riding a Bird rental scooter in a bike lane on June 10, 2025, I experienced sudden instability with the vehicle. The scooter felt shaky from the start of the ride, and moments later I lost consciousness in a crash. There were no roadway hazards (potholes, bumps, or obstructions) present at the site. I was transported by ambulance and treated in the emergency department, where I was diagnosed with facial trauma and a fractured zygomatic bone. To date, I have incurred over $3,700 in out-of-pocket medical expenses, with additional radiology and surgical consultations pending.

Company Response:

Bird has denied responsibility, citing an internal post-incident inspection stating the scooter required no repairs. They have not provided documentation of this inspection, nor did they preserve the scooter for third-party review. Their only resolution has been to offer $175, conditioned on signing a sweeping legal release that includes full waiver of liability, confidentiality, and non-disparagement clauses  misrepresented as a simple form.

Safety Concern:

This raises serious concerns about scooter safety and Birds maintenance practices. Instability may stem from mechanical or firmware issues that are not detectable in visual inspections. The companys practice of returning scooters to service without independent verification, combined with aggressive legal tactics to silence injured riders, creates potential risk for other consumers.

Requested Action:

I am requesting that the CPSC investigate Bird scooters for safety and maintenance practices, and review their handling of injury claims and legal agreements. My concern is both for my case and for broader consumer safety.

productDescription:
The product is a Feekaa Air Fryer Oven  a black countertop convection-style appliance with four gold-colored rotary dials on the front (for temperature, function, timer, and toast shade).

The oven was approximately 15 inches wide, 12 inches tall, and 14 inches deep. It includes modes such as Air Fry, Bake, Broil, Warm, and Rotisserie.

The unit was gifted to us by a family member (our Nana), who originally bought it secondhand from a Goodwill thrift store.

There was no visible damage on the outside, and it appeared to be in normal working condition up until the incident.
incidentDescription:
I plugged in my Feekaa Air Fryer Oven into a grounded outlet that shares power with an air conditioning unit (using a heavy-duty extension cord). The unit was not even turned on yet, but it immediately sparked from the back and tripped the GFCI outlet.

I opened the rear panel to inspect and found multiple burned and melted wires, with signs of severe heat damage and no internal fuse protection. The main power input lines were scorched, and the neutral line had melted insulation.

The product was being used by an adult in a standard home kitchen environment. No one was injured, but the event could have easily caused an electrical fire.

I am submitting this report to alert the CPSC that this product may present a fire hazard due to poor wiring quality and lack of safety cutoffs. Photos of internal damage are available.

productDescription: Segway GT3 SuperScooter (Electric Scooter)
incidentDescription:
In July 2025, I experienced a power button failure on my Segway GT3 scooter. The unit began powering on unexpectedly during troubleshooting, even when not manually activated. During one of these episodes, the scooter jolted forward while I was straddling it, causing me to fall and sustain a facial injury. I was traveling at low speed on a pedestrian bridge at the time. My face and eye were injured, and I have photographic documentation of the incident.

Update 8/1/2025:
I wanted to add additional information - 

 What safety problem do you believe this presents?
The scooter is susceptible to uncommanded power-on events due to a defective power button or communication system. This presents a serious safety hazard, especially since Segway instructs customers to perform diagnostic disassembly themselves, even on high-powered units capable of sudden movement. The unit is not safe to troubleshoot in this condition, and I believe the defect poses a danger to other riders.

Has the manufacturer been contacted?
Yes.

What did the manufacturer say or do?
Despite multiple messages, Segway has failed to:

•	Provide a timely resolution,
•	Offer a verified replacement,
•	Or acknowledge the severity of the incident and resulting injury.


They sent a shipping label and asked me to box and transport a 100+ lb unit myself, despite my injury. I informed them that I would only release the damaged unit once a replacement is received, and that Segway must arrange pickup. As of July 28, 2025, I have received no response or resolution.

Injury details:
Facial injury including impact near the eye (photo evidence available). Injury was directly caused by the scooter powering on during diagnostic app use.

Do you have documentation?
Yes – photos of the injury, emails, chat transcripts, and technical instructions.

I am reporting a safety incident with an Easy Home brand Electric Fireplace / Heater Unit. The product was purchased from an Aldi store in approximately late 2017 or early 2018. I originally reported the incident to the customer service contact info provide by the manufacturer on Friday, 5/2/2025.
The product was not in use at all at the time of the explosion. I was in the same room as the product, sleeping approximately 8 feet away from the unit. There were no injuries, however, had I been within 4 feet of the unit, it is likely that I would have experienced injuries such as cuts or lacerations or other similar injuries.
Below is the text of the original report I provided to the manufacturer, and a second follow up email:

I immediately disconnected and removed the battery and am now storing it outdoors in a fire-resistant container, away from my home, due to concern over thermal runaway or fire risk.

incidentDescription:
I need to report a serious product safety incident involving a replacement
laptop battery I purchased through Amazon:

       *Product Name*: SUNNEAR L18C4PF3 Laptop Battery

       *Date of Purchase*: April 30, 2025

       *Product Link*: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08L7VYFWG?ref=ppx_yo2ov_dt_b_fed_asin_title

This battery was delivered on May 2, 2025, and was installed in my [REDACTED]
shortly after. About two months later, on July 7, 2025,
it caused a fire in my home while charging. The following is a detailed
incident report outlining the fire, resulting emergency room visit,
property damage, and emotional distress caused by this failure.

On July 7, 2025, at approximately 8:45 PM MT, I was at my desk in my
bedroom with my laptop charging beside me on my bed. Suddenly, the laptop
began to hiss and pop. As I turned my head, smoke started pouring from the
device. Within seconds, the computer violently burst into flames. Flames
approximately 2.5 to 3 feet high erupted from between the laptops lid and
keyboard.

I was so panicked that I do not fully remember how I got the laptop
outside. I acted on instinct, trying to prevent the flames from spreading
through my apartment. I tossed the laptop on the ground just a few feet
away from my apartment. I was shocked didnt suffer physical burns. When I
re-entered, my apartment was filled with thick smoke and the stench of
burning plastic. I immediately opened windows, turned on a couple of air
purifiers, and ran fans to clear the smoke.

My quilt was burned, and my backpack, which had been sitting on my bed, had
a burn hole in the back. I used a wet washcloth to cover the still-smoking
laptop to prevent re-ignition. Shortly after, I began experiencing a tickle
in my chest and a persistent cough that didnt exist before this incident.
I went to the emergency room to be checked for smoke inhalation. The doctor
confirmed irritation in my upper respiratory tract from the smoke exposure.
I can still smell and taste the smoke as I write this.

[REDACTED]  As
a full-time college student, I recently had my work hours reduced, and my
rent increased. I have no idea how I will pay this bill. That laptop was an
important tool for my education, and now I need to find a way to replace it.

After returning from the ER, I found a melted glob of melted plastic on the
rug next to my bed; likely dripped from the laptop as I carried it outside.
This rug has now also been damaged.

Its important to emphasize the seriousness of this incident. I live in a
building shared with six other residents. If I hadnt been present to
respond immediately, the flames could have spread to my bedding and nearby
furniture. My upstairs neighbors later told me they could smell the smoke
in their unit. This was not a minor malfunction. This was a violent,
extremely high-risk failure of a product that should never have been sold.

Since the incident, Ive felt extremely uneasy about using any laptop at
all. As someone who relies heavily on technology for school and work, this
fear is impacting my ability to function normally. The emotional distress
from the fire (and the thought of it happening again) has been weighing on
me.

I want to make it clear that I have never experienced anything like this
with my laptop before (it was originally purchased in early 2020). The
device had always functioned properly until I installed the new SUNNEAR
battery in May 2025. I followed all the instructions that came with the
battery and used it solely for academic and personal purposes. The fire
occurred while it was charging normally. There was no misuse or tampering
involved. This was the first and only time Ive ever seen my device (or any
device for that matter) behave like this, and the only major change leading
up to the incident was the installation of this battery. Ive worked in IT
support and device troubleshooting for the past two years, and Im fully
capable and knowledgeable on the proper installation of hardware components
such as laptop batteries. I handled this installation correctly and
followed all the manufacturer's instructions closely. I am confident the
incident was caused by a failure in the product, and not user error.

incidentDescription:
Lectric (a company making ebikes) sells an electric cargo bike popular with families with young kids. The model (the Expedition) I bought last fall, September 2024, has a completely inadequate kick stand. It very, very easily collapses while getting on the bike or loading cargo, including when putting a child on the bike. It's really unsafe- to the point where my wife and I haven't been able to use it without two adults. I went looking online and there is a ton of chatter about how unsafe the kickstand is, and options to try and replace it. Turns out, Lectric itself offers a free replacement to upgrade the kickstand and the new version of the bike is sold with an adequate version of the kickstand. But, there was never any communication about the issue- I reached out to ask after seeing someone on the street with a better stand, who said the company provided it. This didn't happen to injure my kids, because we were very cautious and recognized this danger, but the bike has fallen on me and caused a bruise/scrape, and just is not a safe option to be marketed to anyone using it for children as is- there should be a recall.
