productDescription:
Oklahoma Joe's Canyon Combo Gas Charcoal Grill and Smoker
Color: Black
SKU: 142109538
model: Oklahoma Joe's Canyon Combo Gas Charcoal Grill and
incidentDescription:
My wife and I purchased an Oklahoma Joes Canyon Combo Gas/Charcoal Smoker  Black from Academy Sports in May 2024. Since that time, we have experienced a serious and recurring safety issue with the gas portion of the unit.

When using all three gas burners, the flames intermittently extinguish without warning while the propane continues to flow. This presents a serious hazard, as the unburned gas accumulates in the enclosed grill chamber. On multiple occasionsonce by myself and once by my wifewe have experienced dangerous flare-ups that caused the grill lid to violently blow open upon re-ignition, due to this built-up gas.

We reported the issue to Oklahoma Joe/Char-Broil and followed all requested troubleshooting steps, including:

Purging the propane tank

Thoroughly cleaning the burners and grill

Installing a replacement gas manifold and regulator provided by the company

Unfortunately, none of these steps resolved the problem.

During our most recent communication, a Char-Broil representative insisted we switch to a 20 lb propane tank, rather than using the standard 15 lb tank provided by our local propane exchange service ([REDACTED]). At our own expense (nearly $80), we purchased a new 20 lb tank and began using it this season.

Despite this, the problem persists. Just one week ago, while using the grill with the new tank (which was still nearly full), my wife again experienced the flames extinguishing mid-cook with gas continuing to flow. When she attempted to reignite the grill, the built-up gas caused another dangerous flare-up, blowing the lid open.

At this point, we are extremely concerned that the gas side of this grill is inherently unsafe. The issue appears to be a design flawpossibly related to airflow, burner configuration, or a gas regulation failurethat allows the burners to extinguish during normal operation without shutting off gas flow.

We have cooperated fully with all of Char-Broils troubleshooting requests, yet the company continues to suggest redundant steps instead of taking responsibility for a potentially hazardous defect. We no longer feel safe using this product and are unwilling to continue risking our familys safety.

We are submitting this formal complaint to request that this matter be thoroughly investigated and addressed. We believe a recall or redesign may be warranted, and we are seeking a full resolution from the manufacturer, including potential refund or replacement with a safer alternative.

Thank you for your time and attention to this serious safety concern.

productDescription: Midea 50 Pint Cube Dehumidifier Model #MAD50PS1QGR, grey, 15x15x15
incidentDescription:
Midea 50 Pint Cube Dehumidifier Model #MAD50PS1QGR, manufactured 05/2021

Item was in use in basement area to dehumidify living space.

Unit was turned off but still plugged in. Heard drain pump cycle multiple times in an hour while I was in the other room, finally stayed on continuously and after a few minutes the room began to smell like something was burning.

After unplugging the unit and letting it cool down for an hour, I cleaned all filters, checked for clogs in the pump drain line, and reassembled but did not connect the pump drain line or inlet. When connecting back to power, the drain pump started up immediately and the unit began to heat up. Turned the unit on to attempt to reset, but now even with the humidity setting set to 80% the condenser starts immediately and will not turn off. Disconnected the unit from power after it began to show signs of overheating again (burning smell).

Dehumidifier was used around 12 hours a day, 6 months out of the year. 4th year that we've owned this particular unit and this is the first major failure we've experienced with the model.

No injuries or property damage to report, however this is solely due to the fact I was present at home when the unit began to malfunction. If I had been away for a few hours or if this had happened overnight there is a strong possibility that the unit could have continued to overheat and started a fire.

productDescription:
Product Description:

The product is a Hisense brand side-by-side refrigerator, model HRS290P5FSE, purchased from Lowes in June 2025. It is a full-sized, freestanding refrigerator designed for residential kitchen use. The unit features:

Color: Stainless steel exterior finish

Configuration: Side-by-side doors

Dimensions: Approximately 35.98" W x 33.86" D x 69.88" H (per manufacturer specifications)

Capacity: 20.9 cubic feet (13.25 cu. ft. refrigerator / 7.62 cu. ft. freezer)

Features:

Built-in digital control panel located on the freezer door

Exterior ice and water dispenser

Automatic ice maker (located inside the freezer door)

LED interior lighting

Spill-proof glass shelves

Factory-installed handles

The product is marketed as ENERGY STAR certified and includes a child lock, quick cool function, and door alarm. The serial numbers for both defective units included the same batch identifier B7BHO. The manufacturing dates were April 22, 2025 and April 23, 2025, respectively.
incidentDescription:
What happened that made you want to report?
In June 2025, my household purchased a Hisense side-by-side refrigerator model HRS290P5FSE from Lowes. Upon delivery and setup, the unit failed to cool properly in the refrigerator compartment. After more than 18 hours plugged in and empty, the internal temperature remained in the 50s Fahrenheit, despite the digital panel falsely displaying 34F. We verified this using multiple calibrated thermometers and confirmed food safety temperatures were never reached.

Lowes replaced the defective unit with another refrigerator of the same model and production batch (same batch number on the serial). Within the first 24 hours, the replacement refrigerator began leaking unprompted water into the ice chute and dispenser tray, even though the ice maker was off and the water had not been used. Soon after, a mechanical knocking noise began inside the unit, coming from the ice-making area. These symptoms strongly suggested a defect in the water inlet valve, sensor system, or internal cycling motor.

These are back-to-back product failures from the same manufacturer and model, with safety and reliability issues that could pose electrical risks, foodborne illness dangers, or mechanical damage due to faulty components cycling inappropriately.

What type of product(s) were being used?
Hisense HRS290P5FSE  20.9 cu. ft. side-by-side refrigerator with water and ice dispenser in the door.

Who was using the product(s)?
My father, a senior citizen with medical needs, and I were the primary users. The product was installed in a residential kitchen and was meant for normal home food storage and water/ice dispensing.

How were the product(s) being used?
The refrigerator was installed per manufacturer instructions, leveled, connected to a water supply line, and left empty to allow the internal temperature to stabilize. The first unit failed to cool adequately. The second unit was used in the same way  empty and monitored for cooling. The ice maker was never turned on, and the water dispenser had not been used, yet water pooled internally, and mechanical cycling noises began within 12 hours of installation.

Were there any injuries that happened or may have happened while using the product?
While there were no physical injuries, the defects posed serious risks of food spoilage, electrical hazard due to water intrusion, and possible malfunction of internal motors or fans due to repeated cycling or moisture exposure. Additionally, stress and anxiety were caused by managing appliance failures for an elderly household member on a special diet and strict medication schedule.

How did any injuries occur?
No direct physical injuries occurred, but unsafe food temperatures and internal water leakage created circumstances where injury, illness, or damage could have occurred if we had not vigilantly monitored temperatures and noticed the issues early. Water in the ice chute could also have presented a shock hazard if it had reached internal electrical components.

incidentDescription:
I am reporting a repeated cooling failure with a Samsung refrigerator (model RF29BB820012AA, purchased March 2022). On May 26, 2025, the unit began displaying a warm temperature warning and failed to maintain safe refrigeration levels. The failure occurred without warning and risked compromising food safety.

The refrigerator was in normal household use in a residential kitchen, used by two adults. No modifications were made to the unit, and it had been properly maintained. The products onboard AutoFill pitcher had previously failed, but this report concerns a separate, more serious cooling failure.

While no one was physically injured, the failure of the cooling system could have led to spoiled food consumption, posing health risks to household members, especially children or immunocompromised individuals.

Additionally, this is not an isolated incident. Many users of this same Samsung refrigerator model have reported identical premature cooling failures across online forums and complaint boards. The failures appear to happen shortly after the standard or extended warranty ends, indicating a possible design or manufacturing defect. Samsung has acknowledged the issue only partially  offering free parts but requiring customers to pay for labor and diagnostic costs.

This situation deserves review for potential product safety or reliability issues that may warrant broader consumer protection.

productDescription:
Samsung French Door Refrigerator
Model: RF28HDEDBSR

This is a stainless steel, 28 cubic foot, French-door refrigerator with a bottom freezer and an internal ice maker located in the upper left compartment. It features a digital display panel, temperature controls, and a twin cooling system. The ice maker is built into the refrigerator compartment rather than the freezer and is known to have performance issues.
incidentDescription:
My Samsung refrigerator (model RF28HDEDBSR) has a recurring issue with the ice maker freezing up. This causes it to stop producing ice and leads to fan and sensor errors, specifically codes 14E, 25E, and 32E. Ice builds up inside the unit and blocks airflow, sometimes preventing the fridge from cooling properly.

This problem requires me to manually thaw the ice maker every couple of months to keep it working. It's not due to misuse or wear  it's a design flaw that many other owners report online.

The failure risks food spoilage, water leakage, and possible electrical strain or fire hazard from the overworked components. Samsung sells a repair kit to fix this known issue, but refuses to cover the cost because the fridge is out of warranty, despite it being a design-related failure.

Product Details:

Product Name: UPPHETTA French Press Coffee Maker

Retailer: IKEA

Article Number: 002.978.50

Material: Heat-resistant clear glass pitcher with black plastic lid and handle, metal mesh plunger

Capacity: Approximately 13.5 oz (0.4 liters)  mini version

Size/Dimensions: Approx. 6" tall x 3.5" wide

Color: Clear glass with black components
incidentDescription:
While gently hand-washing a gifted to me IKEA UPPHETTA French Press Coffee Maker, I suffered a sudden, traumatic injury that changed my life. The glass carafe completely intact, with no chips, cracks, or visible damage, was unexpectedly punctured the palm of my left hand near the base of my thumb. The wound was so deep that blood spurted from it, and I entered a state of physical shock, barely able to stay on my feet. I had to self-administer emergency care before being rushed to urgent care by my brother for stitches.

Despite the external wound being closed, internal nerve damage was later diagnosed, requiring surgery and leading to ongoing numbness, pain, and a loss of function in my hand. Simple daily tasks are now a challenge. The emotional toll has also been significant  I live with constant anxiety about using glass kitchenware and performing basic household routines.

I am submitting this report because I believe no one should endure what I did from a product used as intended. The fact that such a severe injury could occur during normal cleaning of a product that appeared safe and undamaged is deeply alarming. This French Press poses a hidden design danger, and consumers deserve to be protected.

incidentDescription: In January 2025, I replaced all six smoke and carbon monoxide detectors in my home with Kidde combination alarms, model 30CUD10-V. It is now late May and three out of the original six have failed, and now one of the replacements that Kidde sent has failed. productDescription: Button cell batteries - fully intact in their packaging.
incidentDescription:
On 5/19/25, I received a small envelope of button cell batteries purchased through Amazon. The outer Amazon bubble mailer was clean, but the smaller manila envelope inside was covered with a black gritty substance that transferred heavily onto my hands. The material caused immediate skin irritation and got under my fingernails, requiring extensive washing to remove. Shortly after exposure, I experienced a spike in blood pressure and developed a lingering headache. The substance continues to shed fine particles if moved at all so it has been sealed in double bags to prevent further exposure.

I contacted Amazon and was told it could take up to 48 hours for a response. I am concerned this material may be hazardous, and the lack of urgency in their handling of the incident makes me question how often this might occur or go unreported. They sent me requests to process a refund instead.  I continued down the appropriate links to try to reach a different or more urgent response but instead received a message that they will contact me in another 10 days.   The headache I developed hasn't gone away since yesterday and my hands continue to feel sensitive, almost like there are tiny invisible cuts on them. 

Product Packaging:
Amazon-branded bubble mailer containing a smaller manila envelope and a blister pack of button cell batteries. Batteries appear intact and sealed.

Request:
I would like this investigated to determine the nature of the black particulate material and whether it poses a health risk. I still have the contaminated packaging available for testing if needed. I would someone to confirm what I have been exposed to.  I would like someone to tell me something other than to go get my vitals checked considering my blood pressure has returned to normal but I still have symptoms.

incidentDescription:
I am reporting a dangerous safety defect in a childrens electric go-kart manufactured by GoTrax, purchased in December 2024 as a holiday gift.

The issue is with the throttle system. When the go-kart is in use, pressing the acceleration pedal sometimes causes the vehicle to continue accelerating even after the rider has released the pedal. This malfunction causes the go-kart to move uncontrollably until it is powered off manually, which is difficult and unsafe for a child to manage in an emergency.

The go-kart was used exactly as intended  on a flat, paved surface by a child within the products stated age and weight limits, and under adult supervision. During one such incident, the faulty throttle led to the child losing control and falling, which resulted in a minor injury. This situation could have been much worse and presents a clear risk of serious harm.

I contacted GoTrax customer support multiple times to report the malfunction and requested escalation to their safety or product team. The company refused to assist, directing me back to the retailer (Target) for a return, ignoring the fact that this is a defect with serious safety implications, not a routine return.

Because GoTrax failed to address the problem or acknowledge the potential danger, I am submitting this report to notify the CPSC of a hazardous product malfunction in a children's electric vehicle.

productDescription: White Mainstays brand PTC Fan-Forced Heater 16621667, MODEL: WSH10C2AWW, ETL listed, conforms to UL STD. 1278, Made in China.  Also marked Intertek 3068797.  For product questions call customer service at 1-866-321-9509.  It is a white space heater with fan and ceramic / metal heating element, safety tip-over switch, approx. 4" x 6" x 8" in size
incidentDescription:
My son was using the space heater in his room.  The space heater is a Mainstays brand "PTC Fan-Forced Heater", date code 2106, purchased at Wal-mart.  It is a few years old.  After turning it on, he reported sparking and smoke coming from the appliance.  I checked, and it appears the cord developed a break and began to arc.  Since the cord lies flat against the carpet, it left a scorch mark on the floor where the cable had broken.

The product was being used "normally", placed on the floor a safe distance from flammable objects etc.  No injuries occurred, but the carpet was scorched, and I believe this could be a fire hazard.

I have looked at the point where the cable broke: it is attached to the device but passes through a plastic groove (channel) in the housing of the heater.  There are plastic nubs which are likely intended to hold the cable in place at that point.  However, I believe after normal use / transport of the appliance, over time the nubs become a stress point on the cable, eventually leading to the internal wiring breaking.  It seems to have improper strain relief at this point.

productDescription: Hamilton Beach BrewStation Programmable 12 cup coffee maker. This device is somewhat unique in that it has a reservoir for super-heating added water and then another reservoir for holding the final brewed coffee. The brewed coffee reservoir also has a heating plate to keep the brewed coffee warm. When you want to fill your cup with coffee, you hold the cup under dispenser as you press the cup against the dispenser lever.
incidentDescription:
We have a Hamilton Beach Brew Station Coffee Maker Model 48464 or 48465 (almost identical). The device has a water reservoir and a self-contained
coffee reservoir, where brewed coffee can be kept warm for preset number of hours until dispensed from reservoir into coffee mug.
When I awoke in the morning I started a morning routine to make fresh coffee. There was residual coffee in the "coffee" reservoir. The device was
powered (plugged into wall outlet), but had been in OFF mode since previous morning's brew cycle had ended. When I lifted the lid, condensed water
dribbles back down into the water reservoir (as it usually does). However, when the water dripped back into the water reservoir, the open lid shot
steam back out, as if the device was in brew mode. I felt the out side of the coffee maker and found that the lower half (where the water reservoir is)
was very hot. When I removed the self-contained coffee reservoir from the appliance, I found the left over coffee to be at room temperature. This
meant that the "coffee" heating element was NOT on, but that the "water" reservoir heating element (brewer coil) was on (and HOT). When I
mentioned the incident to my wife, she stated that the coffee maker had the same problem one week earlier.
I suspect that this malfunction could be a fire hazard and/or an injury (burn) hazard. I did read another consumer complaint that sounded like their
same device had similar issue (Incident Report | 5/18/2020 | [REDACTED]).

productDescription: Walmart Concord Commutr Ebike
incidentDescription:
Dear NHTSA Office of Defects Investigation,

I am filing a formal safety defect complaint regarding the Concord Commuter e-bike, sold by Walmart, due to a combination of catastrophic wheel failures and critical brake defects that pose an imminent risk of serious injury or death. Despite being made aware of these dangers, Walmarts manufacturer continues to sell this defective product.
Defect 1: Wheel Assembly Failure at High Speeds

    The rear wheel assembly repeatedly fails after approximately 1500 miles of use.

    The spokes start breaking in succession, even after replacements and truing, leading to complete wheel collapse.

    I have received five replacement wheels from Walmart, all exhibiting the same defect straight out of the box.

    These wheels come untrue from the Chinese factory and fail despite proper installation and maintenance.

    This defect is extremely dangerous at speeds of 20+ MPH, where a rear wheel failure can cause the rider to be thrown off the bike, leading to potentially fatal crashes.

    I have filed a complaint with the CPSC regarding this issue, yet Walmart continues selling the bike without corrective action.

Defect 2: Unrecoverable Brake Caliper Failure

    The brake calipers suffer from a critical failure where, upon the brake cable tightening and pads locking onto the rotor, something inside the caliper fails internally.

    This results in a sudden and total loss of braking force, making the bike unrecoverable unless the rider manually adjusts the actuating lever.

    This defect can lead to complete loss of control at high speeds, increasing the risk of serious accidents.

    I submitted video evidence of this defect to Walmart, proving that their brake system is unreliable and unsafe for consumer use.

Walmarts Response & Ongoing Sale of Defective Bikes

Despite being fully informed of these defects, Walmart and their manufacturer continue selling this product without addressing the serious safety risks.

    I have also filed a complaint with the Texas Attorney General, citing their failure to properly address warranty claims under the Magnuson-Moss Warranty Act after issuing multiple replacements of defective wheels.

    The fact that I have received five separate defective wheels proves this is not an isolated incident but rather a systemic defect in manufacturing and quality control.

Requested Action from NHTSA

Given the risk of severe injury or death due to sudden wheel failure or total brake loss, I urge NHTSA to:

    Investigate the safety risks posed by the Concord Commuter e-bike and its defective components.

    Issue a recall or mandatory corrective action against Walmart and its manufacturer.

    Require Walmart to cease sales of this defective e-bike until a proper safety solution is in place.

Supporting Evidence

I can provide video proof of brake failures, photos of broken spokes and defective wheels, as well as records of my multiple warranty claims with Walmart. Please contact me if additional documentation is required.

This is a serious consumer safety issue that warrants immediate attention. Thank you for your time and I look forward to your response regarding next steps.

Sincerely,

[REDACTED]

productDescription: Thermador ventilation hood (1000cfm)   Model PH36HS/02. Serial no. 921000034. Installed above a six burner gas range and oven about 36 inches wide, stainless steel housing and components.
incidentDescription:
A Thermador brand ventilation hood down left side spot light that illuminates the stove caught fire. The light was at times shutting itself off, however in early March 2025, the light started smoking as a fire had started in the housing.  The source of the smoke was discovered to be a plastic bag with papers showing schematics had made contact with the housing, igniting the papers.  

Thermador Customer service was contacted, although the regular warranty was expired. The customer service agent ( name is available) stated that it would not be a covered repair.   A repair technician who viewed the situation said it was a design defect he had encountered where Thermador or Bosch glued the schematic paperwork inside the ventilation hood, and the adhesive would let go. It contacted the halogen  light assembly and would cause a fire and damage the light assembly. An electrical fire could also occur.

This fire could ignite grease residue inside the ventilation hood that is ducted into the roof to an exhaust vent.

Product Name: DeLonghi Comfort Temp Full Room Radiant Heater
Model Number: EW7707CM-6A
Color: Light Gray

Features:
		Comfort Temp Technology: Automatically adjusts heat settings
		7 Oil-Filled Fins: Permanently sealed, maintenance-free
		Safety Features: Alleged overheat protection, thermal cutoff

Purpose:
This is an electric oil-filled radiator heater designed for indoor home heating, marketed as energy-efficient and safe for full-room heating. It is advertised to provide consistent warmth without requiring maintenance due to its permanently sealed oil reservoir.

Retailer & Purchase Information:
		Purchased From: Amazon
		Purchase Date: November 20, 2020
		Amazon Product Page:
https://www.amazon.com/DeLonghi-Comfort-Thermostat-Settings-Features/dp/B000TGDGLU?th=1

Defect Details:
Despite claims of safety and reliability, the unit unexpectedly exploded, releasing hot oil under pressure, causing property damage and ongoing exposure concerns.
incidentDescription:
What Happened?

On February 17, 2025, at midnight, a DeLonghi oil-filled radiator heater (model: EW7707CM-6A) suddenly exploded in a bedroom, causing hot oil to spray forcefully in one direction due to pressure buildup and leak onto the floor and surrounding area. The unit had been operating normally before the incident, with no prior signs of malfunction.

The heater was placed on a flat, wood floor, away from any obstructions, and was being used under normal operating conditions to heat a bedroom.

Damage & Health Concerns

The explosion caused oil to penetrate the engineered wood flooring, leaving irreversible damage despite extensive cleaning efforts. The room continues to emit a strong odor, raising serious concerns about potential health risks from prolonged exposure.

Impact on Household

The rooms occupant, a 12-year-old child, was present during the explosion. While no immediate physical injuries occurred, the sudden, violent explosion caused significant distress and fear, waking the entire household. Since the incident, the strong oil odor has made it difficult for the child to continue sleeping in the room, impacting her well-being and comfort.

Manufacturers Response & Safety Concerns

I reported the incident to DeLonghi customer service on February 18, 2025. The company acknowledged the failure but refused to provide written confirmation when I specifically asked whether the heater oil is non-toxic.

Additionally, DeLonghi has insisted on retrieving the damaged unit via regular [REDACTED] shipping, despite my concerns about further oil leakage during transport. They have ignored repeated requests for safe handling procedures and have not addressed potential exposure risks associated with the leaked oil.

Broader Consumer Risk

This product failure presents a serious safety concern that may impact other consumers using similar DeLonghi oil-filled heaters. I have found multiple reports of similar leaking, burning, and explosion incidents under reviews on Amazons product page:
https://www.amazon.com/DeLonghi-Comfort-Thermostat-Settings-Features/dp/B000TGDGLU?th=1
Given the potential fire hazard, exposure risks, and the manufacturers lack of transparency, I urge CPSC to investigate this matter to prevent further harm to consumers.

productDescription: Heated jacket. The jacket includes a rechargeable lithium-ion battery pack that powers internal heating elements.
incidentDescription:
On March 8, 2025, I was wearing a Svanur Heated Jacket that I received as a gift in December 2024. The jacket includes a rechargeable lithium-ion battery pack that powers internal heating elements. I was wearing the jacket without the battery turned on, simply driving in Naperville, IL, when the battery suddenly caught fire while inside the jackets battery pocket. No beeps, no warnings, just caught fire. 

What Type of Product(s) Were Being Used?
		Product Name: Svanur Heated Jacket with Rechargeable Battery Pack
		Product Category: Heated apparel / battery-powered clothing
		Power Source: Lithium-ion battery (specific brand unknown, but included with the jacket)

Who Was Using the Product(s)?

I was the sole user of the product. I am an adult male, and I was wearing the jacket in normal weather conditions while driving my car. Device was turne

How Were the Product(s) Being Used?

I was using the jacket normally and as intended driving my car while wearing it with the heating function turned OFF. The battery was not turned on when it caught on fire. The battery was properly connected inside the jackets designated battery pocket and had been fully charged two nights earlier.

Were There Any Injuries That Happened or May Have Happened While Using the Product?

Yes. I suffered severe burns on my abdomen when the battery burst into flames while inside the jacket. The fire burned through multiple layers of clothing and directly onto my skin before I was able to remove the jacket. The resulting fire also burned a hole in my car seat. 

How Did Any Injuries Occur?
		The battery overheated and ignited spontaneously while inside the jackets battery pocket.
		The flames burned through the inner lining of the jacket, my shirt, and underlayers, causing second- and third-degree burns to my lower abdomen.
		I had to urgently remove the jacket and pat out the flames before further injury could occur.
		I was able to drive myself to urgent care, where they told me my injuries were so severe I needed to go to the emergency room right now, where doctors confirmed that I suffered a mix of second- and third-degree burns.
		I am now undergoing burn treatment, which includes applying prescription burn cream, keeping the area bandaged, and attending follow-up medical visits. I may require a skin graft surgery depending on how the wound heals.

Additional Notes:
		The burned battery and damaged jacket are still in my possession for investigation.
		The incident occurred in public, near a busy intersection ([REDACTED] in Naperville, IL), which may have been recorded by nearby traffic cameras.
		This accident could have been fatal if it had occurred while I was asleep. 
		I am concerned that this product poses a severe fire hazard to consumers, especially given how quickly the battery ignited during normal use. I had this jacket in my use for 3 months.

productDescription: Titan Battery 18V 6.ah and Battery charger 2A for Ni-MH&Ni-CD
incidentDescription:
A Titan 18V 6.0Ah battery used with the Titan Pickleball machine was left charging on my coffee table in the livingroom. That evening, my daughter heard a hissing noise and, upon investigation, noticed that the battery and charger were glowing. She called out for the fire extinguisher, but before we could reach it, the battery continued to smoke and started sparking. My daughter grabbed a pair of sweatpants and rushed the battery and charger out of the house. As she threw it to the ground, it began to explode. My son used the fire extinguisher on it, but it continued to explode. We called the fire department, and they fully extinguished it.

Had it not been for my daughter's quick actions, the house might have burned down. Most importantly, we were unaware that lithium batteries could explode and continue to do so until fully extinguished. Thankfully, my daughter was not injured while removing the battery, and only some furniture, clothing, and plants were damaged. Additionally, my asthma was triggered, and I had to stay out of the house for at least 40 minutes to air it out and use my inhaler for the next two weeks.  My son, who was trying to extinguish the fire, and my daughter who handled the charger & battery, experienced throat and nose irritation for a few days.

productDescription:
The product involved in this incident is a Mr. Coffee Stovetop Kettle, a stainless steel tea kettle designed for boiling water on a stovetop. Below are the specific details:

Product Name: Mr. Coffee Stovetop Kettle
Brand: Mr. Coffee (Manufactured by Gibson Homewares)
Material: Stainless Steel (with plastic components including handle and lid)
Color: Silver (with black plastic handle and lid)
Size & Dimensions: Approximately 15.00 x 15.00 x 10.00 inches
Purchase Location: Walmart (In-store purchase, late 2024)
Intended Use: Heating water for tea or other hot beverages
This kettle is a commonly used household product, designed to be placed directly on a stovetop burner to heat water. It features a whistling spout that signals when the water reaches a boiling point. The handle and lid are made of plastic, which in this case, caught fire while the kettle was in use.
incidentDescription:
Consumer Product Safety Report
Date of Incident: Approx.. February 10, 2025

On approximately February 10th, 2025, while using a Mr. Coffee Stovetop Kettle (Stainless Steel, Silver, 15.00x15.00x10.00 inches, purchased from Walmart in late 2024), the product caught fire in my kitchen. The plastic components, including the handle and lid, ignited and produced 2-3 foot flames. The fire was extinguished, but the event posed a significant fire hazard and led to exposure to toxic fumes.

Details of the Incident
What happened that made you want to report?

The tea kettle unexpectedly caught fire while boiling water, an action for which it was designed.
The plastic handle and lid ignited, producing flames 2-3 feet high.
The fire posed a serious risk of property damage and personal injury.
Toxic fumes from the burning plastic filled my home, causing lingering health effects.
What type of product was being used?
Mr. Coffee Stovetop Kettle (Stainless Steel, Silver)

Who was using the product?
The tea kettle was used by me and my household members for boiling water.

How was the product being used?
The kettle was used almost daily before the incident.
On the morning of the incident, the kettle was placed on the stovetop with water in it.
The kettle was not left alone for an extended period.
Flames were noticed when my wife alerted me to the fire in the kitchen.

Were there any injuries that happened or may have happened while using the product?
I suffered headaches from exposure to the toxic fumes.
The home environment was contaminated with harmful smoke from burning plastic.
There was potential risk of severe burns or property damage if the fire had not been quickly controlled.

How did the injuries occur?
Toxic fumes from burning plastic filled the house, leading to health effects.
Exposure to smoke inhalation caused persistent headaches for about a week.

Manufacturer Response
Gibson Homewares, the manufacturer, attributed the incident to improper care, suggesting that the kettle may have boiled dry.
They acknowledged my concerns but refused to take responsibility, offering only a replacement kettle.
They claimed that no other reports of similar incidents had been received.
My request for a formal investigation and accountability was not addressed satisfactorily.

Conclusion & Request for Investigation
This incident highlights a severe product safety issue. A stovetop tea kettle should never ignite under normal use, even if water evaporates. This suggests a design flaw or use of flammable materials in critical components.

I request that the CPSC investigate this product for fire hazards and toxicity concerns to prevent future incidents. Consumers should be warned, and the product should be recalled or modified if found unsafe.

Sincerely,
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]

incidentDescription:
I am a cochlear implant user and need to replace four batteries every day. The new child-resistant packaging for these batteries is difficult to open, and the process poses several risks. Due to the packagings tight seal, it requires to use sharp scissors to cut it open. The required circular cutting motion caused sharp plastic shards to fly away, and I cut my finger on the packaging. Additionally, the force required to open the package caused some of the batteries to fly out uncontrollably, posing a sure danger of ingestion to a baby or child, something that was initially only a potential danger.

The old packaging was much more user-friendly, as it allowed us to not only store new batteries safely but also to put used batteries back in the same packaging, helping track their usage and prevent them from being lost. This made the process more efficient and safer overall. The new packaging, however, does not offer this functionality and makes it more difficult and dangerous to handle.

Once the packaging is cut, it becomes sharp and unsafe to carry around in pockets or store near children, as it can easily cause injury. The new design creates an unnecessary safety hazard that the previous packaging did not have.

This packaging is not only child-proof, but also adult-proof, making it dangerous and impractical for people like me who rely on these batteries daily. The excessive difficulty and risk involved in opening the package make it an unsafe design for medical device users.

incidentDescription: On November 25, 2024 I purchased a Weber Genesis SPX-345 Smart Gas Grill (Natural Gas).  The product was purchased through Lowes.com and was delivered to my home in a sealed box.  The product is a natural gas grill but came pre-installed with what I have now learned was a propane gas hose and propane gas regulator, rather than with one intended for natural gas.  The regulator was a .5 pound propane regulator; my natural gas line operates at 2 pounds.  Had this system remained in place, I faced what ultimately what would have been a serious explosion risk in the use of the product.  Additionally, Weber provided the incorrect schematic for the product and the wrong owner's manual.  When I contacted Weber about the problem, they told me it was my fault, not theirs, because there should not have been a regulator on the product.  However, the gas line and regulator were preinstalled when the product arrived.  I have had a professional plumber inspect and confirm the problem.  When I advised Weber that I was going to contact the CPSC its representative said goodbye and hung up on me.  I can't believe that this problem is limited to my gas grill and if it exists on others, it is in my opinion an inherently dangerous situation.  I do not know which Weber entity manufactured my grill, but I assume it was either Weber, Inc., Weber-Stephen Products, LLC, or Weber-Stephen Products, Co.

It became obvious to me that there is an engineering defect in these charging units.  I contacted BatteryEVO and explained the situation, and also suggested they contact their supplier/manufacturer of the charger units about this dangerous engineering defect.  Several days later after not hearing back regarding my issue, I called BatteryEVO and was told that they would not issue a working replacement, and apparently, have no intention of taking corrective action regarding this defective device. productDescription: Hunter Ceiling Fan, model # 54208
incidentDescription: I have two Hunter Ceiling Fans (model # 54208). The blades on this model of fan are ONLY held in place by a rubber grommet pushed onto a post. There is no screw or retaining nut on the post to ensure the blades remain firmly attached. After about 2-2.5 years of use, the blades are coming loose. This is a dangerous design, as the use of the fans puts downward pressure on the blades--which, then, are pushed off the posts. Had I not noticed this, the blades would shortly have come off while the fan was running. This is a highly dangerous condition, as the blades would be thrown across the room at great force--endangering anyone in the room and damaging property.

manufacturer: Shenzhen Yue Er Hua Trading Co., Ltd.
incidentDescription: Purchased 2 Givebest Heaters on October 9, 2024, from a 3rd party seller on Amazon, because I found them on sale and knew I would need some once it got cold. Received them on October 11, 2024. Did not need them until December, when it got cold. Opened 1 and plugged it in. The fan didn't come on to circulate the heat when I turned the switch to turn on the fan.... thought it may need to come up to a certain temp before the fan kicked on. Heater continued heating up, but can never came on, no matter where I turned the switch (it has an "Off",  "I", & "II" for off, low, & high). Picked it up to see if the "Auto Off When Tilt" would cut the heater off, as it was designed to do.... It did not. The heater continued to heat up to what I felt was a dangerous temperature, so I unplugged it & carried it with oven mitts outside to a sandy place in my yard for safety. Once it has cooled off, I brought it back inside, sat it and the one still in its box, on my fire place hearth. I contacted Givebest via information listed on label on heater and in the provided manual. Givebest told me to contact Amazon to return them. Contacted Amazon, who advised me that it was past their 30 day return policy and that I had  to contact the seller/manufacturer for return and full refund. Contacted Givebest again, who told me that they were aware of their products having issues, they couldn't help me because they had no storefront to return to, and they insisted that I had to return the heaters to Amazon for my full refund. In contacting Amazon again, explaining the fire hazards and other dangerous malfunctions with the first heater, that I was not going to chance trying the second. Amazon advised me to destroy and discard both heaters - as they were dangerous, and that they would take up all issues with seller - stating Amazon could not have sellers selling known dangerous products through Amazon. However, Amazon told me - again - to contact seller/manufacturer for my full refund, as my 30 day return window had closed and Amazon couldn't help me. After being run around by both Amazon and Givebest, I submitted my product review on Amazon - which made the seller/manufacturer contact me, upset over my review. I notified the seller/manufacturer of my intent to contact the [REDACTED] &  Consumer Affairs (now I know it's correctly called Consumer Product Safety Commission). I do not think a company should be selling products that they are aware of having dangerous "issues", as they stated to me via email. I think these heaters pose a real threat, as with none of the safety features working they are a fire hazard and I really hope someone doesn't lose their home - or their lives. I have myself (disabled), my adult son (disabled), and our dogs that live in this house, and had I not been leary of plugging in this new heater (as I am with anything that could possibly malfunction and cause damage), I might not have stood right there with it (had it sitting on the bar in the middle of my kitchen on a trivet) and it very may have caught my kitchen on fire - destroying our home, harming or killing us and our beloved pets!

productDescription: Labeled as 10w magnetic wireless charger for car
incidentDescription:
Subject: Safety Report for Magnetic Snap Wireless Charger (Tracking Number [REDACTED])  Fire, Shock, and Mislabeled Power Hazard

Product Details:
		Product Name: Magnetic Snap Wireless Charger
		Tracking Number: [REDACTED]
		Distributed by: Jem Accessories Inc.
		Purchased From: Five Below
		Input/Output Specs (as listed on packaging): 9V/2A, 5V/3A, 12V/1.5A (Output: 5W/7.5W/10W)

Description of the Hazard:

I purchased the Magnetic Snap Wireless Charger from Five Below, and after limited use, the device emitted a burning smell, suggesting a potential electrical short circuit or overheating issue. Upon further inspection, the charger fell apart, revealing twisted, uninsulated wires inside the device. These wires were completely exposed and poorly secured, creating a serious risk of fire and electric shock.

Additionally, I noticed several major safety and compliance issues with the product:
	1.	Invalid FCC ID:
THE FCC ID printed on the product is invalid. Since this is a wireless charger that emits RF energy, it is required by law to have FCC certification.
	2.	Mismatched Power Ratings (10W vs. 15W):
The product packaging states the charger provides 10W output, but the circuit board is labeled for 15W. This indicates a potential overpowering risk if connected to a higher-power USB-C charger, which could lead to overheating, thermal runaway, or fire hazards.

Photos and Evidence:

I have attached photos of the internal wiring showing the twisted, exposed wires, circuit board markings, and the packaging. The mismatched power ratings are clearly visible on the circuit board (labeled 15W) and the product packaging (stating 10W output).

Why This Is a Serious Risk:
		Fire Hazard: The burning smell and exposed wires indicate a serious fire risk. The charger could overheat and ignite, especially during overnight charging or unattended use.
		Electric Shock Hazard: The twisted, uninsulated wires pose a direct risk of electric shock if they come into contact with the metal charging surface or external components.
		Device Damage and Battery Explosion: The mismatched power ratings could result in overpowering connected devices, potentially causing battery swelling, leaks, or explosions.
		Missing FCC Certification: The lack of an FCC ID suggests the product may not meet U.S. regulatory requirements for wireless charging devices.

I respectfully request that the CPSC investigate this product for safety violations and consider issuing a recall to protect consumers. The product poses serious risks of fire, electric shock, and device damage, and the manufacturer and retailer should be notified immediately.

model: SafPow 42V 2A Battery Charger 3 Prong Universal Re
incidentDescription:
On September 18th 8:06PM a fire occurred in my garage caused by a defective SafPow 42V 2A Battery Charger. The charger was connected to electric scooter and malfunctioned, resulting in a thermal runaway event that led to a fire. The incident caused significant property damage, personal injury, and financial losses.

Sequence of Events:

1. Fire Origin:

The SafPow 42V 2A Battery Charger was actively charging the [REDACTED] electric scooter at the time of the incident.

The charger overheated and caused the scooter's battery to ignite, resulting in a rapidly spreading fire.



2. Spread of Fire:

The fire destroyed a [REDACTED] electric scooter and caused severe damage to three additional scooters stored nearby:

[REDACTED]

Despite attempts to mitigate the damage, all four scooters were declared total losses.



3. Personal Injuries:

While attempting to move the burning [REDACTED] scooter out of the garage to protect my family, I sustained multiple injuries:

Broken Nose: The burning scooter struck me in the face, resulting in a nasal fracture requiring splinting and pain management.

Burns to Both Hands: First-degree burns were sustained while handling the burning scooter.

Facial and Lip Injuries: A deep gash above my upper lip (now a permanent scar) and a bitten-through lower lip requiring antiseptic treatments and healing ointments.

Inhalation of Toxic Fumes: Prolonged exposure to smoke and hazardous fumes emitted during the fire.





Impact and Losses:

Property Damage:

The fire destroyed all four electric scooters, leaving no salvageable parts. The estimated replacement cost for the scooters is $8,898.


Medical Costs:

Out-of-pocket expenses for personal injury care include burn care supplies, wound treatment, nasal fracture care, and protective gear, totaling $165.


Emotional and Physical Strain:

The injuries and incident have had a lasting impact on my physical health, emotional well-being, and ability to conduct daily activities, including managing my business.



Attempts to Resolve:
I have made extensive efforts to contact Amazon regarding this incident. These efforts include speaking to numerous supervisors and managers, being referred to their partners such as [REDACTED], and repeatedly following up with their claims adjusters. Despite my persistence:

The claims adjusters have ceased responding to my inquiries.

Supervisors and managers have been unwilling to engage in direct communication or provide clarity on the resolution process.

Responsibility has been shifted to the third-party seller, despite Amazon's role in facilitating the sale and the product's inclusion in a global recall due to severe fire and burn hazards.


Additional Note:
The SafPow 42V 2A Battery Charger involved in this incident was recalled one week after the fire, underscoring the danger posed by this defective product. The lack of accountability and resolution has exacerbated the financial and emotional toll of this incident.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription:
The T-fal 3.5L Deep Fryer with Oil Filtration System is a stainless steel countertop appliance designed for home use. It features a 1700W heating element, adjustable temperature control, and a digital timer. The fryer includes an integrated oil filtration system intended to simplify the reuse and storage of cooking oil.

The oil filtration system uses a removable oil container with a built-in spout for pouring. The lid on the oil container is designed to secure the contents during storage and pouring. The product advertises dishwasher-safe parts for ease of cleaning and claims to deliver perfect golden crispy results.

Key Components:

Oil Filtration System: A removable container for filtering and storing oil after use.
Pouring Spout: Built into the oil container for transferring oil with minimal mess.
Lid: A plastic lid designed to cover the oil container, which should stay in place during pouring but has proven to detach easily during use.
Frying Basket: A stainless steel basket for holding food during frying.
Temperature Control and Timer: Adjustable settings to manage cooking temperatures and times.
Dimensions: Approximately 18 x 13 x 14 inches
Weight: 12.4 lbs
Material: Stainless steel body, plastic components for the lid and spout
incidentDescription:
Description of Incident:
While using the T-fal 3.5L Deep Fryer with Oil Filtration System, I attempted to pour peanut oil from the oil container using the built-in spout. During this process, the lid of the oil container detached unexpectedly, causing approximately one gallon of peanut oil to spill onto the counter and under the stove. This design flaw created a significant fire hazard, as peanut oil is highly flammable and could have ignited had the stove been on at the time of the spill.

Hazard Description:
The lid of the oil container does not secure tightly enough to withstand the normal use of the spout, leading to a high likelihood of accidental spills. Given that this product is specifically intended for use with flammable oil, the inability of the container to reliably prevent spills poses a serious risk of fire and injury.

Injury Details:
No injuries occurred during this incident. However, the potential for a fire or burns was substantial. Cleaning up the spill was time-consuming and required extensive effort to remove oil from the counter and under the stove.

Recommendation for Resolution:
The product design should be reviewed to ensure the lid secures tightly during use, particularly when pouring oil. Any features that compromise the safety of handling flammable liquids should be re-engineered to prevent similar incidents in the future.

incidentDescription:
Hello
On November 24th I bought a battery for a heated vest on Amazon ./ ... https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0DDPZX598?ref=ppx_pop_mob_ap_share
I wore it a couple of times as it powered a heated vest. 
On December 4th 2024, I wore the heated vest and battery for work. Got home after work and set it on the table next to my bed to recharge. I went to my bedroom at approximately 9:30pm. I unplugged the battery from the charging cable and left it on the table next to my bed.
At approximately 11pm. This battery spontaneously combusted.
The sound of the battery exploding and fire woke me up. I jumped up and ran from the upstairs bedroom to the garage to get a fire extinguisher. I ran back upstairs to the flames and put out the fire. 
I started a fan blowing the smoke and fire extinguisher contents out the windows.
I went to check on the carpet to make sure the fire was out. I discovered a pile of plastic burnt into the carpet. But it felt hot to the touch, At which point I ran back to the garage and got a hammer to remove the glob melted into the carpet. I discovered burning embers under the glob. I poured water onto this. Then cut out the carpet and carpet pad to confirm it was no longer burning.   

If this battery had exploded at 11AM instead of 11PM my wife and I would have been at work and likely would have lost our house. It's shocking to think a $60 item can destroy your home. 

I have been very disappointed with Amazon for not pulling this product off the site. And disappointed that the Seller has not made contact with me about the request to pull the product. And the requested refund and payment for damages.
Thanks [REDACTED]

productDescription: Cuisinart 14-Cup Food Processor (Model DFP-14BCN)
incidentDescription:
I would like to report a serious and dangerous small appliance malfunction that occurred with a Cuisinart 14-Cup Food Processor (Model DFP-14BCN).

We purchased this food processor just under 6 years ago.  On average, we use it once every other week.  We have had no problems with it in the past.  The appliance sits on a marble countertop with plenty of space around it.  It was plugged in as usual, but it was clearly turned off at the time of the malfunction.  It had last been used 24 hours prior.

During the afternoon of January 6, 2025, the food processor suddenly turned on.  The blade spinning noise was heard by multiple people in the house who went to the kitchen to investigate.  A few seconds later, the appliance started to emit heavy gray smoke and the scent of burning plastic.  We quickly unplugged it and placed it outside in the snow.  While moving the appliance outside, it was noted that the underside metal components were glowing red and sparking.

Afterwards, we checked the standard electrical socket that the appliance was plugged into in the kitchen wall and found no damage or abnormalities.  There was no lightning outside or any other obvious external cause.  No other electrical devices in the house were affected, and no house circuit breakers tripped.

To be frank, if we had not been home at the time, this event could have easily started a house fire.  Luckily there were no injuries.

productDescription: 4-Door Flex with Family Hub 27.9-cu ft 4-Door French Door Refrigerator with Single Ice Maker (Black) model RF28M9580SG/AA from Lowes
incidentDescription:
To whom it may concern,

We bought 4-Door Flex with Family Hub 27.9-cu ft 4-Door French Door Refrigerator with Single Ice Maker (Black) model RF28M9580SG/AA from Lowes for $3,704.05 on 08/14/2017.  We been having nothing but trouble with the ice maker, which started within 2 years of buying. The ice maker keeps over freezing and completely icing up the whole mechanism and harness.  We would constantly have to disable the refrigerator and to defrost it.  In addition, the unit also started to produce mold and mildew.  By the time this started, the warranty was already up. Additionally, the issue was not a hardware issue, but a defect in Samsung refrigerator which they wanted us to pay for them to resolve.  We finally just disabled the ice maker and bought an ice maker.  I am now seeing that the power consumption of the refrigerator started to increase.  I also ran a self-check, but Samsung's self-check says nothing is wrong refrigerator.  It was normally around 46.46 kWh - 54.96 kWh, but in May it began to rise.  It rose from 65.87 kWh to 98.13 kWh as of December 31, 2024.  This made me concerned as to why this was happening.  I was also hearing a louder humming sound coming from the refrigerator, which made me make sure the condenser coil was clean of dust, but no luck.  I also checked behind the triple & metal cooling to make sure it was not frozen.  It was little but was not bad.  I then checked the ice maker, which to my shock, the whole area was frozen even though the ice maker was still disabled.  Therefore, I disabled the refrigerator and unthaw the whole ice maker again.  In addition, I made sure to actually pull out the Refrigerator Ice Maker Assembly this time, in the hope it would stop it from causing this issue.  To my dismay, it did not.  So even though the ice maker is disabled, and the Refrigerator Ice Maker Assembly is pulled out, the ice maker compartment is still getting iced up.  I think this is a fault in the Samsung refrigerator and I want to bring it to your attention.  I have uploaded some images of the issue but if more is required, please let me know.

incidentDescription:
I purchased a Ninja Slushi machine in August 2024 and have used it approximately 10 times over five months. After each use, I have cleaned the machine thoroughly using multiple methods, including:

Running it through the dishwasher,
Soaking it with vinegar and dish soap, and
Using a sink hose and [REDACTED] to reach difficult areas.

Despite these efforts, mold and bacteria persistently grow inside the back of the vessel, a critical area that interacts with drinks. This defect poses a significant health hazard as the contaminated liquid is ingested by consumers.

I am allergic to mold, and this design flaw has placed my health at risk. The inability to clean this area effectively makes the product unsafe for its intended use.

Steps Taken to Resolve the Issue:
I contacted Ninja Kitchen customer support and was informed this issue was due to "normal wear and tear." However, this explanation ignores the apparent design flaw that prevents proper cleaning of the product.

Harm or Potential Harm:
While I have not yet experienced severe health issues, ingesting mold and bacteria could lead to serious harm, especially for individuals like me with mold allergies.

Requested Resolution:
I believe this product needs a redesign to ensure it can be cleaned effectively and safely. I also recommend the company issue warnings to consumers and consider a recall if this defect is widespread (which is seems like it is, just look it up on [REDACTED].. vessel bacteria / mold ninja slushi). I'm not the only one with this issue.

incidentDescription:
Hello, I purchased an Elite Gourmet coffee percolator on March 3,2023. Within one month the glass knob that goes on top of the unit randomly cracked when I took it off to clean it. I notified the manufacturer and they mailed me a replacement knob. On December 4,2024; the glass knob broke again and a sizeable piece of the glass was inside the unit on top of the metal coffee strainer. I didn't realize the broken piece was there, until I opened the flip top of the unit. This was disturbing, because I sometime reheat any coffee left in the percolator and I wouldn't have known if any glass pieces fell into the pot, if I then drank it. So I contacted the manufacturer again and submitted a screenshot of the cracked knob and the piece of glass that broke off. I also submitted a receipt from my original purchase  of the unit. I then discarded the unit, but I kept the cracked knob & the piece of glass that broke off. The manufacturer replied that I needed to submit a picture of the unit and I let them know I discarded it already. I did this because I really didn't want a third replacement knob, because I no longer feel safe using the unit; due to the risk of the knob cracking again and therefore; resulting in a potential injury to myself. Since I no longer had the unit, the customer service representative stated that it's not their policy to replace the unit and would only replace the knob. Again, I wasn't interested in receiving a new unit nor the knob. My intention was to emphasize to the manufacturer that there is clearly a defect with the glass knob, as I strongly feel it shouldn't crack and break so easily and at random. In my opinion, the unit needs to be recalled for consumer safety purposes. However, the manufacturer seemed completely unconcerned about the potential risk. So I'm requesting that you investigate this matter and if it's deemed necessary; immediately recall the product and/or advise the manufacturer to improve/modify the construction of the glass knob to prevent any injuries.

Opening the case, it appeared that the battery cells were loose in the case but it was difficult to be certain. I reached out to my bike shop. They reached out to their supplier, and according to them, there was a bad batch of the gel used to stick the battery to the case. productDescription: Ninja Professional Plus Kitchen System, 1400 watts.  This set contains a base unit, 2 smoothie cups, food processor container,  and 72 oz pitcher.
incidentDescription: I was using the Ninja Professional Plus Kitchen System to make smoothies.  I smelled an unusual smell that smelled like something burning.  I didn't see any smoke or any indication of a problem with the unit and thought the smell might be coming from outside my house.   I served the smoothies to my 2 sons.  One drank the smoothie; the other said it did not taste good.  When I smelled his smoothie, it smelled like the same burning smell I smelled while making them.  I put water and a few ice cubes in the Ninja smoothie container, put it in the base, and turned it on.  I was shocked to see the water turn blackish with sediments of a black substance.   I am very concerned because one of my sons drank the smoothie that had this substance.  I kept the smoothie container that has the water and black substance, hoping it would be analyzed to determine what it is.   The first week of November, when this occurred,  I immediately contacted the Shark/Ninja company.  The customer representative I spoke with told me they were going to expedite a return call to address my concerns and that I should hear back within two days.  I did not hear back that week.  The following week, I contacted the company again.  Again, I was told they would expediate a response and that I should hear back within two days.  It has now been four weeks, and I have not heard back from anyone at Shark/Ninja.  My concern is that something from the machine entered the container and contaminated the contents of the smoothies I prepared.  I am very concerned that this substance may have entered other food that I have prepared in the unit.  I am also very concerned that this could happen to someone else.  I offered to send my unit and the container that has the water and black substance to Shark/Ninja, but they have been unresponsive.  During the second call, they did offer to send me another unit, but I would never take a chance using this appliance again.  I hope that someone can help determine what this black substance is and whether it could harm my son's health.

incidentDescription:
Full story: [REDACTED]

My story and general info:

I'm an experienced rider.

Over 15,000 km on [REDACTED] 

Over 10,000 km on Segways: G30 (owned 2 of them), G2 (4,000 km), and GT2.

Ive never crashed any of them, maybe because I have 20 years and around 300k km of driving cars, without any accidents so far.

For context, I weigh 85 kg, so this isnt due to weight.

I never crashed this GT2, not even a simple bump or so just normal riding all the time.

Riding this Segway GT2, I'd say it was 70% city/asphalt roads and 30% dirt roads.

But heres the catch: the city is Lviv, where a lot of roads are made from cobblestone, and the GT2 felt really bad on them. Anyway, after 10k km riding Dualtron scooters on the same roads, there was never any serious damage like what I experienced with the GT2.

Basically, what I want to add here is that the roads were not always perfect, but more like average.

I see this as an engineering failure, since it broke at the specific spot where the bolt and hole are. This design flaw is quite frustrating. Segway shouldve done something like Inmotion did with their RS model, adds internal reinforcement inside the steering tube, cross-shaped.

I was lucky that my speed was only 30 km/h when it happened, so I just experienced almost fully blocked steering and nearly fell off the scooter. Fortunately, I managed to stop in time.

incidentDescription:
**Public Safety Notice Regarding Lasso Electric Space Heaters (Model #CT30710)**

Dear [Community/Customers],

We are writing to inform the public about serious safety concerns we have experienced with the Lasso Electric Space Heater, Model #CT307. After purchasing two of these units, we encountered two separate incidents of dangerous malfunction.

**First Incident:**
With our first heater, the plug itself melted during use. This raised immediate concerns, but we hoped it was an isolated issue and proceeded with caution.

**Second Incident:**
Unfortunately, the second unit posed an even greater danger. Not only did the plug melt again, but it also caused the outlet to overheat and ignite, resulting in a fire that spread to the wall. The fire was only contained because I had a fire extinguisher nearby and was able to act quickly to put it out. If I had not been home at the time, I fear the outcome would have been catastrophic, and our home would have been lost.

We urge anyone who owns or is considering purchasing the Lasso Electric Space Heater, Model #5586, to exercise extreme caution. We strongly recommend discontinuing use of the product until further investigation can be done and more information is provided regarding the safety of these heaters. 

If you have experienced similar issues with this product, we encourage you to report it to the manufacturer, your retailer, and the appropriate safety authorities. In the meantime, please prioritize fire safety by ensuring that all electric heaters are used according to manufacturer guidelines and are regularly monitored for any signs of malfunction.

www.pintxflaw.com
incidentDescription:
Unsure where to go for help with a consumer product sold by a predatory company adhering to gross negligence in regard to a manufacturing defect around a dangerously powerful lithium battery.

Future Motions sells products under their label OneWheel. One specific model, the OneWheel Pint X, has a well documented manufacturing defect with the 56V onboard battery - specifically the battery's balance lead wires. The plastic battery casing pinches and rubs the wires, causing them to tear and fray. This results in unsafe product operating conditions or complete product failure. Examples of this are product failure while riding, resulting in injury or death. 

This issue is well documented here: [REDACTED] 

Consumers have been struggling to get any kind of meaningful assistance from the company, Future Motion. Future Motion continues to deny any wrong-doing. Using scare tactics, they attempt in any way they can to ignore or deflect responsibility. 

I own an effected product. They told me to mail it to them at my cost to have it inspected with no guarantee they would fix anything. This is after I opened the product and sent them photographic evidence of pinched wiring. Furthermore, they confirmed if I inspected for the defect myself that I would be ineligible for any assistance. That I would need to pay for a new battery.

This issue has been going on for several years now with hundreds of people confirming they've had tremendous frustration dealing with Future Motion and their lack of meaningful support on these expensive electric vehicles.

Is there anything we as consumers can do to hold this company accountable for this manufacturing defect that they blame on their customers? 

Really, this should have been a recall years ago.

The cord looks exactly the same as the other unit did so that's why I'm writing this. I believe the problem is the wire is possibly undersized as well as the grommet that holds the cord into the unit is a pinch type grommet and so it compromised the inside of the electrical cord. productDescription: Purchased from Amazon.com.  Bali Outdoors 28" Gas Fire Pit.  Model #SRGF11626-XXX.  SKU #LGF06-0010
incidentDescription:
Several months ago, I purchased a 28 gas fire pit from Amazon, with model #SRGF11626-XXX .  I assembled the unit per the instructions and had to wait patiently for the Ohio weather to turn a bit cooler before using this fire pit.  

Recently, the weather did change, and I found an opportunity to finally use this fire pit.  I used the fire pit for several hours one evening, and after I turned off the gas, and as the unit cooled down, the tabletop insert, where the burner and beads are located, came crashing down onto the propane tank stored inside of the cabinet. 

After reviewing this, I observed that the burner insert was not properly installed from the factory.  This insert should have been anchored on top of the tabletop assembly with the four corner screws.  Instead, this insert was installed from the factory as an undermount to the tabletop, rather than a top mount.  This resulted in the pan crashing down onto the propane tank after the unit was turned off and started to cool down.  I re-read the assembly instructions again, and there is NO mention having to anchor this insert from the top down.  

Fortunately, this collapse occurred after the propane was turned off.  If this had collapsed while the propane was on and the burner lit, the result could have been catastrophic.

productDescription: This is a 2024 Lectric One ebike Long Range (Black) one-size fits all.
incidentDescription: I purchased a new ebike through pre-order on approx March 15, 2024.  Manufactured on April 15th.  Finally delivered approx Aug 2nd--  It was delivered and I put it together according to the instructions.  My partner rode it approximate 8-times for about 91 miles total.  In the most recent ride she mentioned that it lost power and was making noises.  On previous rides she complained of a knocking sound and it appeared to come from the rear wheel hub.  Each of the previous times this happened (three times I recall), I tightened the rear axel nuts to spec with a torque wrench.  So, back to the most recent situation.  The knocking sound was heard again and the she was complaining and we returned home and parked the bike in the garage.  Soon after I needed to move the bike to make space for other things.  I backed the same bike out of the garage slowly for a distance of about 6 to 7 feet.  As I did so, I heard a small piece of metal fall to the concrete.  Once I got the bike back in the garage I noticed that the Gates carbon belt drive (no metal chain on this bike) had slipped off of the rear cog wheel.  I then decided to look for the piece of metal that I heard hit the driveway.  I found it and discovered it was a steel spring wire that had been in the form of a ring but had be unsprung and was no longer round.  It seems that the diameter of this ring is the same as the rear axel of the ebike.  I put the ebike up on the bike stand to reengage the belt drive, which required the removal of the rear wheel and remounting the belt.  It was at this piont that I noticed that the rear cog ring (that the belt drive integrates into) had completely spun off of the axle.  I tightened up this cog, remounted the belt and put the bike together again for riding.  There was not locking piece available to keep the cog from spinning off once again.  I called the manufacturer and they asked me to send the ebike back to them for replacement.  I agreed to do so, but I have delayed as time is limited and I have to properly box it up to ship it.  I don't want to return it if CPSC wants to inspect it to determine if something more needs to be learned by the agency.  But, I am prepared to return it to them so I can either get a refund or a replacement.

productDescription: GE Profile Nugget Ice Maker Model UNC15NJII (or UNC15NJBII)
incidentDescription:
I own a GE Profile Ice maker, model UNC15NJII. That's the model number on the receipt, but the model plate inside the unit says UNC15NJBII. I bought it in April 2020 from Home Depot. It is a built-in ice maker installed under an island in our kitchen and is regularly cleaned and the ice is used for consumption all the time.

On Sep 25th 2024 I did a routine cleaning and noticed a fine gray substance in the bottom of the ice bin and along the lip that the ice slides over as it is produced. At first I thought this was mold or similar, and scrubbed it up with an abrasive sponge and paper towels. I could not get all of the gray material off the bin; there is still a "stain" of a gray line running around the perimeter of the bin near the bottom. However when I restarted the ice maker and observed the first pieces of ice falling from the hopper, I noticed black material suspended in the ice nuggets. I assumed again this was mold that may have somehow made its way into the machine. I unplugged the machine to try to further investigate. When that ice melted, I wiped up the black stuff, and realized on my paper towel that it was sparkling like some kind of metal. I got a magnet and confirmed it was metal shavings. Similarly, the very fine gray material that I had on a paper towel was also magnetic in nature. 

I tested this myself several times. When starting the ice maker with an empty bin from an empty tank, the first ice will have the most coarse shavings, and progressively the ice gets more clear, with the worse ice settling to the bottom of the bin where people are less likely to scoop it in most situations. However, the very fine gray metallic powder did coat the entire bin, which makes me suspect that the metal is always present, just to different degrees of fineness.

It is not clear for how long this ice maker has been embedding metal in the ice, whether coarse or fine, but it was an alarming discovery. The ice auger assembly is sealed and I didn't want to pop it open and void my warranty. So I contacted GE, who told me it was out of warranty for this type of failure, but that they'd send someone to look at it for free as it was considered a safety issue. The following Monday, a tech from a local authorized GE servicer ([REDACTED] Appliance) came by and reproduced the issue himself, again using a magnet to observe the metal shavings that were embedded in the ice.

After the tech left, he spoke to GE who advised that he would need to replace several parts in the machine at my expense. The parts alone were almost $3,000, nearly the cost of a new unit, and the tech suggested I pursue a claim through my Home Depot extended warranty instead. In the meantime I contacted GE's social media to let them know about the issue, with photos and videos. GE's social media team offered me a $400 coupon to help recover some of the parts cost. I refused that, and insisted it was a serious safety issue that should be investigated. Ultimately, they have agreed to replace the unit with a slightly newer revision. However I do not know whether the new unit has changed anything about the design, and I'm very concerned that GE Profile ice makers may have a design flaw that is resulting in the widespread consumption of metal particulate in water ice.

I cannot say for certain whether direct injury has occurred. I did get an MRI recently and, as far as I know, my stomach didn't explode with shrapnel, but I'm genuinely concerned for anyone who may consume the first ice of a batch when the shavings seem to be more coarse. I also suspect that machines that have been in service for longer may well show significantly more wear to the internal assemblies and thus more metal may be present.

productDescription:
NEWDERY for Apple Watch Charger, 10000mAh Portable Charger Power Bank
Sold by Amazon: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B0BZTXZZ77/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_search_asin_title?ie=UTF8&psc=1
incidentDescription:
This report pertains to a product sold by Amazon in United States. It is called: "NEWDERY for Apple Watch Charger, 10000mAh Portable Charger Power Bank". It's Amazon product page is here: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B0BZTXZZ77/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_search_asin_title?ie=UTF8&psc=1

Here is what happened. The product was bought in August, in USA where I reside. It was used sporadically in the last 2 months. 
We (my partner, our toddler son, and  I) traveled to Uruguay on September 27, 2024, and are staying until October 10.

At about 4am on October 1, while sleeping in a guest room of a family member's house,
we were woken up by a crackling hissing noise emanating from this Newdery charger (power bank). 
It was spinning around and it was on fire -- thin tongues of flame
were emanating from it. The fire resembled several firecrackers lit at once. It was emanating from the underside
of the unit and was extremely hot. It took us about 10 seconds to (sort of) put the fire out,
while the unit (on its own) was spinning around the floor, like a whirling dervish.  Finally, I used a large
pillow to extinguish the flame and then I carried (holding it between two shoes) the still glowing/hissing/crackling
carcass of the unit to the kitchen sink and immersed it in water. It continued to hiss for another 4-5 seconds.

It is an absolute miracle that the fire started with us being in the room. Otherwise, it would've burned down the entire
house where we were staying. It is also fortunate that the floor was tiled! If it was a linoleum, carpet, or wood floor,
much more damage would have been done. Another miracle is that none of us was burned, though it came close.
The damages amounted to burned sheets, a pillow, a mattress, and quite a few clothes. PLEASE NOTE that we
have photo evidence for all of this.

The entire floor where the unit burned was covered in black soot and the air stunk terribly. All 3 of us
inhaled some of that soot while putting out the fire. 

Also, when we originally went to sleep that night (4 hours before the fire, around 11pm) the unit was left *unplugged*,
meaning that it was not charging anything and it was also not being charged. It was on the floor in the middle
of the room near some of our suitcases  and clothes, but nothing was either touching it or covering it.

I tried to report this dangerous product to Amazon via its normal "product review" feature.
After I submitted a review, Amazon replied with an idiotic
form email saying that the review couldn't be accepted  because "it violated community standards"!!?

I believe it is imperative to (1) notify customers, both past and potential, about this dangerous product
and, (2) stop Amazon from peddling it to people.
