Report is regarding the Round Volumizing Brush attachment, which is one of many attachments or hair tools that connect to the main body of the machine for the purpose of styling hair
productType: Hair Curlers, Curling Irons, Clips & Hairpins (1682)
model: Dyson Airwrap multi-styler and dryer Straight+Wav
incidentDescription:
**Product Name**:Dyson Airwrap  
**Manufacturer**: Dyson

I have experienced repeated safety issues with the Dyson Airwrap, specifically with two round brush attachments. The attachment prongs, which appear to be made of plastic, lose their shape after the product heats up during use. As a result, the attachments no longer securely lock onto the machine and eventually dislodge. This issue first occurred with my original round brush attachment, which completely dislodged multiple times after losing its locking power. I had this attachment replaced after dozens of failures.

However, the replacement attachment, which I received about two to three months ago, is already experiencing the same problem. It frequently becomes loose during use, despite my efforts to be cautious. On a recent occasion, the attachment completely dislodged from the machine while it was in use, causing a significant safety hazard. The attachment flew off and burned my chin, as it was extremely hot. 

This presents a serious risk of injury. I am fortunate that it only hit me, as my young daughter was nearby, and it could have easily flown off and hit her instead.

The issue seems to lie with the material of the attachment prongs and the locking mechanism of the machine, which fail to function properly after extended use, particularly when exposed to heat. Given the potential for serious harm, I believe this product presents a safety risk and needs further investigation.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription: Electric Bike, Gray
brand: Hiboy EX7  Full Suspension Electric Bike
incidentDescription:
I purchased a Hiboy EX7 electric bike on Aug 20th. The bike came mostly assembled, after finishing set up I took it for a spin where it worked fine though the brakes were a little loose. Two days later the front AND rear brakes both failed while riding causing an accident. All the sudden I hear a little ping/click/pop sound and I notice that my rear brake lever has almost completely lost resistance, and that my rear brake seems to have little to no stopping power. Luckily I was able to pull over safely using my front brake alone and I spent a while looking at my bike to see if I could figure out what was going wrong.

At first I assumed that the brake cable must have snapped or something, but that doesn't seem to have been the case because each time I pulled the rear brake lever I could see the cable pulling the little "arm" (not sure what this part is called, but it's the little lever on the brake itself that the cable connects to) being pulled what seems to be the normal amount.

Looking into the rear caliper and pulling the handle, I could see a small amount of pad movement, and could even see the rotor move a bit so I know that some contact was being made. But just a short distance into pulling the brake I would hear that same ping/click/pop sound and it appears that the brake would just pop/slip back off, my hand would feel almost no resistance on the lever, and the brakes were barely stopping the bike, if at all!
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

incidentDescription: Dewalt 20v Max self-propelled mower - DCMWSP256. When the mower stayed engaged after release of the power, I removed the batteries and inspected the entire unit. I found that the control cable leading from the motor to the handle, was pinched in between the handle bar and the handle bar rest. It created exposed wires that penetrated the protective housing. When lifting the handle up to reposition the back of the mower, it creates a gap in between the rest and handle bar, allowing the cable to become pinched. I checked to ensure all screws were tight and cable guide was installed as pictured in the manual. This issue is a product design flaw. I have reached out to Dewalt to request a refund.

productDescription:
The product is a **Future Motion Onewheel GT-S Series**, a personal electric mobility device designed for outdoor use. It has a single large wheel in the center, flanked by footpads on either side for balance and control. The Onewheel GT-S is marketed as an all-terrain electric skateboard capable of handling various surfaces, including pavement, grass, and light off-road environments. It is primarily used for recreational purposes and commuting.

The board is **black and gray in color**, approximately **9.5 inches wide, 29 inches long**, and weighs around **35 pounds**. It is powered by a built-in lithium-ion battery and a motor housed inside the wheel. The GT-S model features a digital control system, including self-balancing technology and feedback via pushback and haptic buzz to alert riders of various operating conditions.
incidentDescription:
I am reporting a serious safety issue with the Onewheel, a personal electric mobility device manufactured by Future Motion. I experienced two significant crashes while using the product, resulting in physical injuries and loss of confidence in the products safety.

**Incident 1:**

I was riding the Onewheel over wet concrete, navigating shallow puddles as intended for outdoor use. While traveling at approximately 15 mph, the boards self-balancing system suddenly stopped working. The nose of the board dove into the ground, throwing me forward onto my right side. I sustained road rash on my leg, hand, arm, and shoulder, and a broken arm. My helmet also cracked upon impact. After the crash, the board was unresponsive and had condensation inside the casing, indicating water had entered the control board. The Onewheel is marketed as an outdoor product, and failure in such conditions raises serious safety concerns.

**Incident 2:**

After paying $180 to ship the board back to Future Motion for repairs, I received it and rode it once. During that ride, while stopped at a red light, the board unexpectedly accelerated on its own without any input from me. There was no haptic buzz, pushback, or other indication that the board would accelerate. This malfunction threw me off the board, re-injuring my already broken arm and furthering my distrust in the product. I had only ridden the board a short distance after receiving it from Future Motions repair shop.

**Product Information:**

The product is a personal electric mobility device known as a "Onewheel," which is designed for outdoor use on various terrains. It was being used by me, an experienced rider, in everyday outdoor conditions.

**Injuries:**

Both incidents resulted in physical injuries. The first incident caused road rash and a broken arm, while the second crash reactivated my previous injuries. The second incident highlights an ongoing issue with the products reliability, posing a serious risk of further injury.

**Conclusion:**

These incidents suggest that the Onewheel has significant safety flaws. The first crash was due to water exposure despite claims that it is built for outdoor use, while the second crash occurred after the board had been serviced by the manufacturer. Given the physical injuries Ive experienced, this product presents a serious risk to consumers.

incidentDescription:
I purchased a Case Logic phone charger at Meijer in July. I had it plugged in downstairs as a communal "where'd my juice go?" charging station. When we went up north, I unplugged it and opted to bring it with us. When I came home and went to plug it back in, I realized that I forgot to remove the protective film on the [REDACTED] charging base. As I started to peel it off, my hand started getting really really hot. When I looked down, the charging cord was smoking and had melted through. I contacted CaseLogic with photos and explained the situation, mostly because I thought a deeper investigation or recall should be issued so that other people don't leave this thing plugged in and start a fire in their home when they aren't there. They referred me  to Thule who manages their warranties. I have filled out the warranty claim form and am waiting for a response, but this whole process has already been going on for two weeks, and I really felt like people should know if they have one...to just keep an eye on it, and only leave it plugged in when it's within your line of sight. 

p.s. Thule said in their contact form that I will have to pay their standard shipping fee to return the charger to them before they can determine next steps.  Does that seem backwards or what?

productDescription:
This incident could have been caused by the battery and/or the charger, so details for both are listed in this field but it was the battery that exploded so I will devote the fields below to that product only.
-PKCELL ER14505 3.7V 2400mAh Rechargeable Lithium Battery,  AA size, Color - solid blue. (minimal info on label, obviously not labelled for resale)
-[REDACTED]
incidentDescription:
A rechargeable lithium battery exploded in my battery charger. No one was injured. There was no subsequent fire. I will provide details about both the battery and the charging unit.
The battery was an ER14505 size "AA" 3.7V Rechargeable Lithium-Ion cell manufactured by "PKCELL". I do not know if the cell had a Mfg. date or serial/batch info printed on it because the case was severly damaged in the explosion. The cell had no observable defects before being put into the charger. I did not personally purchase the PKCELL batteries, I acquired them from a releative who no longer needed them.
The charger was a [REDACTED]. The charger was purchased by me on February 28, 2024 and had been used about 3 times prior to this incident. This was the first time that I had charged 3.7V ER14505 cells in the unit. Following the incident the charger was intact, with some explosion residue on it. I immediately removed power from the unit, and after reviewing some MSDS information about the potential residue from the explosion the unit has been bagged and retained.
There were four of the "PKCELL" AA batteries in the charger at the time of the incident. The batteries were being charged at a level of 300mA. That charging value was [REDACTED]. 
I was not injured in the explosion, but seconds before it occured my hand and face were inches away from the unit. I was simply VERY lucky! There was no apparent property damage. I had just checked the progress of the charging unit without touching it, took two steps away and it exploded. Thankfully I was on the opposite side of a large vice on my workbench which shielded me from the blast. It was very loud, generated about a 2 foot diameter fireball and quickly filled my garage with acrid smoke setting off the smoke detector across the room. I set up fans to clear the smoke and left the room as quickly as possible. The three other batteries that were in the charger at the time of the explosion were ejected by the force. One of them landed about 8 feet away behind me. The cells that were in the charger next to the one that exploded were not visibly damaged but have also been bagged and will never be used again. The 8 foot ceiling of my garage and my entire work area was splattered with explosion residue (wet black fragments and dust) which I have been carefully removing.

productDescription: Ninga Woodfire  Grill. model OG7, series S5
incidentDescription: I bought a Ninja Woodfire grill, model numberOG7, SeriesS5, from Costco on June 17, 2024.  The materials  available  on line describing this product  say that the device requires a 15 Amp electrical circuit.  I have an outlet on my deck attached to a 15 amp circuit . So I assumed the device would work on my deck.  After using the device for about a month, it began to blow the circuit breaker every time I used it.  Then the circuit began to blow even when the grill was not in use.  Today an electrician  came to my house .  He determined that the device , which draws 1760 watts, is not safe to use on a 15 Amp circuit because the maximum continuous use wattage for a 15 amp circuit  is 1440 watts.  Additionally , he determined that the device burned the insulation off the wires in the electrical panel and  destroyed the 15 amp breaker , and came very close to starting a fire.  He said the device requires a dedicated 20 amp circuit  to operate safely.  I contacted Costco about this.  Costco agreed to allow me to return the grill and get a full refund.  I suspect Ninga knows that the device requires a dedicated 20 amp circuit but  it also knows that very few people have a dedicated 20 amp circuit available on their decks or patios, and so it  falsely claims the device can operate safely on a 15 amp circuit.  The materials available to the consumer by ninja , pre- purchase, say only that a 15 amp circuit is required. )

productDescription: 10 kilowatt home lithium ion energy storage battery
incidentDescription:
Six years ago I contracted with a local solar panel installer for a rooftop solar system.  I also had them add to that system a 10 kilowatt lithium battery to provide household power backup in the event of a power grid failure.  The battery was from LG Energy Solution and came with a 10 year warranty(Model RESU 10H).
     Three years later LG advised that my battery was part of a lot that was subject to a recall it was coordinating with the CPSC, due to a risk of the battery overheating and causing fire and harmful smoke.  It promised a replacement within a few months, but it actually took two years.  I see that LG was involved with CPSC three separate times for this recall, in 2020, 2021, and 2022.
     About a year later - Thursday, August 1, 2024 - I was summoned to the basement by a smoke alarm, to discover the replacement battery overheating and smoking.  Luckily I was able to contact the solar installer by phone and he guided me through shutting down the system, which cooled down the battery.  He came the next day to remove the battery, and one of the same ones he had installed as part of a solar system for my son.
     I am furious that a major company like LG would subject me or anyone else to this kind of risk, long after it became aware of the problem and said it had been fixed.  It is apparent that despite the documented risk of fire with this model, LG is issuing replacements of it instead of its newer models.  These older models constitute a clear and present danger of fire, without warning, to any household in which they are installed.  I would like LG to be forced to recall all of these batteries for anyone affected, and also refund the $7000 purchase price for me and my son.  Neither of us desire to have another backup battery from LG at this point.

GOTRAX GMAX Electric Scooter 
My child's excitement was palpable as he hopped on his GMAX Electric Scooter, eager to take it for a spin. But in an instant, his joy turned to terror. Without warning, the scooter suddenly folded in half, sending my child tumbling to the ground.

I watched in horror as my child struggled to get up, clutching his injured arm and leg. The scooter, which was supposed to be a fun and safe way for him to get around, had failed us miserably.

We rushed my child to the hospital, where he received treatment for his injuries. The incident left us both shaken and wondering how this could have happened. Was it a manufacturing defect? A design flaw? Or simply a case of poor quality control?

As we navigated the aftermath of the accident, I couldn't help but think about the trust we had placed in the scooter's manufacturer. We had assumed that the product was safe and reliable, but now we were faced with the harsh reality of a faulty product that had put my child's well-being at risk.

productDescription: The Lectric XP Trike is the ultimate eXPerience for all. It accommodates a wide range of abilities and preferences with our lowest standover height ever of just 13.8 inches. As the industry's first fully foldable and fully assembled electric tricycle, The XP Trike includes the award-winning features our XP series eBikes demonstrate, plus a bigger battery, hydraulic brakes, and a third wheel. A sturdy rear hub motor setup with a differential axle provides a whopping 65NM of torque - accommodating even the heftiest of payloads without a problem.
incidentDescription:
I purchased an Lectric Branded E Trike from a third party.  When we arranged for the test drive and purchase the odometer didn't even register a mile on it because this cute 81 year old man bought it for his dying wife who was unfortunately never able to drive it more than a short distance.  By the time we finished test driving it and agreed to buy it, the odometer registered one mile.  It's a beautiful trike.  I was so excited to be able to take it out on rides with my husband.  Our first couple of journeys we stayed close to home and took shorter rides while I got used to the trike and using the peddle assist feature.  On the third ride we took the trike out on an almost 12 ride on a paved bike path on along a river.  The trike nearly tipped twice on me.  The first time I hit a rock with the front wheel and the second time I tried to drive over an item that I could not navigate around.  I was going slow enough that I was able to slide off the seat and stand to stabilize the trike.  The last trip we were on a different section of the paved bike path and went on a 17 mile journey.  I was using the peddle assist and traveling between 10-11 mph when I came upon a root from a nearby tree that had grown under the asphalt and caused a slight buckle in the path.  I didn't see it in time.  I wasn't able to stop in time to avoid it.  I took a slight turn and the trike ended up toppling over on top of me.  At any rate of speed and a slight turn the trike is unstable.  The end result of that accident was a trip to the Urgent Care facility with a fractured elbow.  I have bone fragments still floating near my elbow and remain in pain nearly a month later.  I love the idea of this trike.  I love that I'm able to ride with my husband.  I just want a stable and reliable ride.  I've tried emailing the manufacturer of the trike multiple times trying to discuss with them ways that I can stabilize the trike so that I can continue to ride it but the only thing they want to tell me is that I voided the warranty when I bought it from a third party.  My point to them remains that by the time I test drove it and took it home it had ONE mile on the odometer.  I'm not asking them to warranty it for a return, I want help in stabilizing it so I can continue to ride it.  They just aren't interested in helping me do that and I am so disappointed at their apparent attempt to avoid liability.

I should interject that I am not new to adult tricycles.  I grew up with an adult tricycle.  I have moderate cerebral palsy which affects my lower extremities and somewhat my mobility.  That being said, I am not unfamiliar with riding, balancing and steering adult tricycles.  I do believe that I have a reasonable expectation that this E Trike would offer me the same stability and reliability that I am accustomed to.

incidentDescription: A five y/o girl received 3rd-degree burns to 19% of her face, torso, and legs. Her mother was using a "tabletop fire pit" that was marketed for indoor or outdoor use using isopropyl alcohol. The mother told me that she had purchased the product on Amazon and had purchased the bottle of alcohol at the same time. Unfortunately, family has since discarded the debris from the fire for any additional confirmation or reference. I was able to locate the product and identified it as a Weyland Table Top Fire Pit. The Amazon description states the product is to be used with 70-91% rubbing alcohol fuel. I attempted to locate additional product manuals or information, but I havent had much luck. I assume that you are familiar with how Amazon often advertises and offers the "Frequently bought together" option down on the product page. When you view this product, Amazon offers it and a bottle of fuel as a package option. My concern is that Amazon is packaging the product and a bottle of 99% isopropyl alcohol for the consumer to purchase together. Rubbing alcohol and isopropyl alcohol are clearly two different fuels with different chemical reactions to the flame, especially at 99%.

incidentDescription:
Product is a coffee bean grinder from Hamilton Beach. Purchased in 2021, but only used recently in the last 6 months. There is a hidden cord wrap mechanism that seemingly has a design flaw, as you wrap/unwrap the cord for us, the wire insulation deteriorated and exposed copper wire inside. I was only made aware of this after plugging in the machine, having it explode in my hand, and seeing the brunt and exposed wire inside. 

I had contacted Hamilton Beach support and they refused to provide a refund, only to replace the item with the same, or something of similar value. After experiencing this, and seeing the many online reviews of the same unsafe incident, I am not interested in their products, and they do not seem to be taking it seriously.

This could have resulted in electrocution, a kitchen fire if kept plugged in over night, or other unforeseen incidents. I have photos of the charred exposed wire, and record of their customer support response if needed.

incidentDescription:
On the evening of Sunday, July 21, around 5:15 PM, I was riding the scooter I purchased from Amazon a few months ago. My destination was the parking lot where my car was parked in [REDACTED]. While riding, the safety locker on the scooter unexpectedly opened, causing me to fall onto the street and sustain injuries to my hands, elbow, arm, and right leg. The wounds were significant, and I was both panicked and bewildered by how it happened. Considering the speed I was traveling at, which was approximately 15 mph, the consequences could have been much worse, so I am thankful for that. Despite the pain and bleeding, I had to drive for four and a half hours following the incident.

It is worth noting that the locker had opened on previous occasions, but I attributed it to my potential failure in properly securing it. However, on this particular instance, I made sure to lock it correctly, and it appeared to be in place. To my surprise, after the incident, I locked it again and gave the scooter a shake, only to find that it opened on its own once more. This poses a significant safety concern, and I strongly believe that a recall is necessary. I contacted the vendor, but their only resolution was to offer a replacement scooter. After reading reviews, I discovered that other people have also experienced similar issues. I kindly request that you thoroughly investigate this matter. The potential consequences were severe, and I do not wish for anyone else to endure a similar situation. Thank you for your attention to this matter.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

incidentDescription:
Dear Sirs,
I am writing to formally report a significant safety concern involving a Pentair Water Pool and Spa, Inc. product. This product, the Max-E-Therm Heater, has caused a fire at my residence, leading to substantial property damage and posing a serious risk to consumer safety.
Incident Details:
	Product: Pentair Max-E-Therm Heater
	Mdel Number: P/N SR400LP
	Serial Number: 44000492100293
	Incident Date: 09/16/2022
	Damage: Fire originating from the heater, leading to property damage and increased insurance premiums.
Independent Expert Findings:
An independent expert's report has concluded that the fire originated in the heater's upper housing area, specifically the combustion chamber. This is notably the same area affected by a recall by Pentair dated April 28, 2021. Despite this, my unit, manufactured slightly later, experienced the same defect leading to ignition.
Manufacturer's Response:
Pentair has acknowledged the potential defect and offered to compensate for the cost of the heater and its installation. However, they have attributed the fire to rodent damage without a physical examination and have only proposed a limited resolution. This speculative attribution raises concerns about the overall safety and design of the heater.
Potential Risk to Consumers:
Given the defect's potential to cause fires, this product poses a serious threat to all users, especially those with units manufactured around the same period as mine. The risk extends beyond financial losses to the safety and well-being of consumers.
Request for Agency Involvement:
In light of these concerns, I urge your agency to:
1.	Investigate the safety and design of the Pentair Max-E-Therm Heater.
2.	Ensure  Pentair extends its recall to cover all units manufactured around the same period as mine.
3.	Supervise the examination of my heater by Pentair to ensure transparency and accuracy. I have requested that experts from relevant consumer protection agencies be present during this examination.
Documentation:
I am in position of all relevant documentation, including the independent expert's report, correspondence with Pentair, and photographic evidence of the damage.
Conclusion:
Your agency must act to prevent further incidents and ensure consumer safety. I look forward to your prompt response and am available to provide any additional information or clarification.
Thank you for your attention to this urgent matter.

productDescription: 5-Burner Gas Grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
Issue Description:

After coating the grill plates with peanut oil to cure them, I heated the grill to maximum temperature for about an hour. Once the grill had cooled, I noticed that the internal structure had warped. This warping was so severe that three of the metal covers (heat tents) designed to hang over the flame emitters could no longer stay suspended via normal installation of them. Instead when installed as intended they would drop down on the back side of the grill and rest directly on the flame emitters.

Concerns:

Unsuitability for High Temperature Use:
The Char-Broil model 463448021-73 appears to be completely unsuited for high-temperature use. If a customer uses the grill at maximum temperature for between 45 minutes and 1.5 hours, the metal parts within the grill can irreparably warp. This deformation results in some of the heat tents no longer being able to stay suspended over the flame emitters, for where the heat tents are installed normally and fully inserted at the inside front of the grill.

Safety Hazards:

1. Falling Heat Tents: The inability of the heat tents to remain suspended poses a significant safety hazard. If the heat tents fall during high-temperature use, they could land on top of the flame emitters, which can result in uneven heating, potential flare-ups, and increased risk of fire or injury without the grill owner being aware that this has occurred.

2. Potential for Undetected Damage: During prolonged high heat use, the heat tents might fall without the user noticing. This can create hazardous conditions that are not immediately apparent, further increasing the risk of injury or fire.

3. Compromised Cooking Efficiency: With the heat tents unable to stay in place, the grill's ability to distribute heat evenly is compromised, leading to potential cooking inconsistencies and safety concerns.

Request for Immediate Action:

I urge a thorough investigation into this matter to ensure the safety of this and potentially other similar models. The potential for structural failure and the associated hazards necessitates a comprehensive review.

I request that the manufacturer review the design and material specifications of this model to address and rectify this critical safety concern. It is crucial to evaluate whether the materials used can withstand the maximum temperature settings for the recommended duration. What happens to this grill if its used at full temperature for 45 minutes? An hour? An hour and a half? Structural deformity resulting in heat tent failure & the tents falling onto the flame emitters? 

My estimated heat time was about an hour. This grill is easily structurally damaged via normal operation, damage which can easily result from what many people would do with the unit. The unit at present is designed-to-fail with a usage workflow which could be engaged by many consumers by default.

Please transmit this report to both companies, Char-Broil and Lowes.

The main assembly is a circular brushed (silver) metal housing that hangs "below" the  ceiling, shaped more or less like a wheel of cheese. D758FT02
GLN60BNK5CR <- this one is likely the model number as it also lists a phone number to contact for customer support that is also listed on Harbor Breeze's website.
incidentDescription:
I observed that our Harbor Breeze model fan was "listing" somewhat. Upon scaling a ladder and removing the decorative shroud around the "fan box" in the ceiling I observed that the fan had "slipped" one of its mounts in the mounting bracket over years of usage. I am unsure if the fan was improperly installed (a washer or screw with a wider head would have prevented the issue) or if the "slipping" through the mounting bracket was due to wear on the bracket from the screw during regular use. The entire fan assembly disengaged from the ceiling when I touched the mounting bracket. Had I not been up a ladder and waiting for it someone could have been killed.

This is a Harbor Breeze fan manufactured sometime between 2006 (year home was built) and 2017 (year we purchased the home). 

This was used about as typically as a fan could be. We did observe that it had a "rock" to it when operating shortly after moving in, but did not thing anything of it.

No injures thankfully, but it could have easily killed our toddler or infant if they had been under it when it fell.

incidentDescription:
I am reporting this incident because I was genuinely terrified. 

Product: Sun Squad Portable Fans (battery-operated handheld water misting fans). 

Both the fan blade and end cap popped off, exposing a blunt metal needle the length of an infant [REDACTED] syringe tip.

Full details of the event:
I purchased several Sun Squad handheld misting fans for a family party. It was purchased in-store at Target, beside Sun Squadpool toys and childrens flotation devices. I got these misting fans for the family (of varying ages, toddler to middle schooler). The end caps fell off during use but also easily pop off, exposing a protruding metal needle that spins. There are multiple hazards:

- The end caps can fall off, presenting a choking hazard.
- The caps are choking hazards.
- The protruding metal is a hazard.

There were no injuries during use, and I took them away. It was a terrifying experience. To be fair, you would think people would stop using a product when that happens, but they continued on. When the end caps came off, exposing the blunt needle, it didn't impact the functionality of the sprayer, so everyone continued using the product. 

The needle doesn't have a sharp tip. It is a metal needle the size of a syringe tip, protruding outward that doesn't retract. It could potentially injure an eye. The cap is a chocking hazard.

productDescription: the product is a hopper used to temporarily store whole coffee beans before they enter the grinder in preparation of a home-made espresso drink.
incidentDescription:
I believe there is a design defect with Baratza Coffee Hopper (model S012) intended for use with their Sette 270Wi coffee grinder.  Inside the hopper there is a small plastic cover over a second cover that is designed to allow the user to open and close the hopper for removal from the grinder.  The plastic cover is attached to the larger hopper via four half-inch plastic tabs.  The issue is that the plastic tabs appear to become fatigued very easily, break off and problematically fall into the grinding mechanism and ultimately brewed alongside the coffee, potentially introducing plastic shards or particles for ingestion by the consumer.  I have now personally experienced this issue with two identical hoppers over the course of 3 years of ownership of this particular device.  I've reached out to the company and they don't seem to take the issue seriously.  I have discarded the first defective hopper but have saved the pieces from latest issue for submission or review as needed.

Noting that no direct injuries have occurred but there is a small risk and also, with the awareness of microplastics on the rise, I wanted to share the concern with appropriate authorities for consideration.

incidentDescription:
U-Skooter/E-TWow dangerous sudden freeze up of front wheel purchased online from: 
ETWOW.COM
EL PASO, TX 79901 US
Support@USCOOTERS.COM
Shortly before noon on May 22, 2024, [REDACTED] was riding her U-Scooter/E-TWow on [REDACTED]. She was on her way to the [REDACTED] station as part of her daily commute to work. She had been driving this route for over a year without incident.
Suddenly, the front wheel of the scooter locked. Before [REDACTED] could react, she was thrown over the handlebars and onto the road. She sustained a broken orbital bone, a laceration over her right eye, and road rash/soft tissue damage on her hip, her right forearm and both knees.
 Thankfully, she was wearing a helmet, but the damage to her face was severe and paramedics transported her to [REDACTED]. Her pain was so intense that, in the ambulance, paramedics administered two doses of fentanyl.
At the hospital, [REDACTED] underwent a full CT scan and X-Rays, which identified the broken orbital bone in her face. In addition, she was given morphine and oxycodone to deal with her severe pain. She spent seven hours in the trauma ward of the hospital before being released. As a result of the accident, she missed several days of work and continues to experience debilitation and pain from her injuries. It may be months before she is back to normal.
 Upon doing some basic [REDACTED], [REDACTED] discovered that other ETWOW scooter users have experienced the same product flaw that resulted in her crash.  Here is the reference to others experiencing this product flaw:  
[REDACTED]
The scooter has not been turned on since the crash. [REDACTED] has photos of her injuries and documentation from the hospital as well.
The front motor wheel does not behave like a normal wheel.  When the scooter is off there is a lot of resistance to the spin.  So when the battery dies, i walk the scooter instead of riding it manually because of this motor wheel resistance.  It has been this way since i took the scooter out of the box and i believe is a normal part of the design.  I think this design is perhaps why there are problems with the front "wheel locking".  If I'm going 30mph and suddenly a fuse blows (or something), my wheel motor will die and go into its state of resistance.  The resistance at high speed could be creating the sensation of "wheel lock".

Here is [REDACTED] description of the accident:
I was commuting to work on my usual route in the bike lane, alert as always on the lookout for potholes and debris. Suddenly my front motor wheel locked and I was thrown forward onto the pavement. I was going roughly 25mph down an overpass. Though it happened in a manner of seconds, I was aware that this incident was caused by the front wheel locking up. I heard a noise that I am familiar with, a noise made by the regenerative braking system when it is engaged. But I was NOT pushing the brake lever. Then I heard and felt the front motor wheel skid on the pavement. The handlebars were facing perfectly forward throughout this and I was launched head-first over them. The first thing I saw after hitting the pavement was blood dripping from my eye onto the pavement. I could hardly breathe from the pain and shock. A man pulled over and engaged me in concerned questions. He gave me a clean washcloth to apply pressure to my bleeding eye. I was writhing in pain but conscious. A second man walked over and I watched him fetch my scooter that was on its side spinning in circles in the middle of the road. I don't know how it was spinning on its side without an operator pushing the lever, or how it got so far into the road. He asked me how to turn it off.  I felt too pained to answer, but the other man helped him and it was draped over the road barrier near me.  The first man stayed and engaged me until numerous police showed up. The police talked to this man and he may be a witness to the whole event. The ambulance arrived next. 

[REDACTED]

incidentDescription:
I am writing to file a complaint regarding the Samsung Family Hub 26.5-cu ft French Door Refrigerator with Ice Maker (Model #RF27T5501SR) that I purchased from Lowe's on 08/25/2020 for $2,454.18. The fridge's cooling system failed, causing loss of all my food and vital medication, including insulin, which I need to stay alive as a Type 1 Diabetic.

On 06/02/2024, my husband and I heard a strange noise from the fridge, but the temp readings on the Family Hub screen seemed normal. By 06/03/2024, the freezer contents were mushy, indicating a failure. Despite this, the fridge and SmartThings app did not alert us. I contacted Samsung in a panic, discarding all our recently purchased frozen food. They instructed me to reset the fridge via the breaker, but this did not resolve the issue. Later, the fridge's temp rose, causing further loss of perishable food and my essential insulin. I had to throw away both my frozen and refrigerated food.

As an immunocompromised individual, this situation is dire. Samsung's response has been inconsistent and frustrating. After being assured my case was a priority, I received no follow-up. When I called again on 06/04/2024, I was informed my case was not escalated. I uploaded my purchase receipt as requested, only to be told it was rejected and that my fridge was out of warranty. However, it is still within the 5-year warranty for the cooling system.

I was advised that no service technicians were available within 100 miles. Initially, I was told to hire a local tech and submit their diagnosis. However, the "specialty claims" department then informed me to wait an additional 24-48 hours for a manager to contact me with the next steps before hiring a tech, causing further delays.

The only acceptable resolution is a full refund for the refrigerator and compensation for the loss of food and medication. My health and well-being are at risk due to Samsung's defective product and inadequate customer support.

productDescription: Zephyr Savona ZSA-M90S, first generation, "Made in Italy", "Cod. K44.Z.902.300", "UL Listed"
incidentDescription:
With the light switch in the "off" position, I received a 110V shock while replacing a light bulb in a Zephyr Savona ZSA-M90S range hood.  The shock caused minor injury to my hand.  The circuit was not (nor was it required to be) a GFCI nor AFCI, so the circuit remained online even after I had received the shock.

...

I am the owner of the home and the appliance.

...

During the installation, I was following all labeled instructions on the unit, as well as all warnings in the manual.  I was also practicing basic safety techniques associated with changing a typical household (E26, Edison-base) light bulb.

...

Upon further investigation, I discovered that the circuit controlling the light is switched-neutral.  The same circuit also controls the motor, so the motor is also switched-neutral.  This appliance is thus unsafe by design; any attempt by an end-user to replace the light bulb would require de-energizing the entirety of the circuit at the breaker panel in order to avoid being shocked.  Further, any short to ground on the neutral side would result in, at minimum, the energizing of one or more elements of the appliance without any ability to turn them off, if not also electrical arc/fire hazards.

...

A retrofit kit, consisting of Zephyr part numbers 11000041 and 56210050, is available.  This retrofit kit maintains the switched-neutral configuration.  Figure 1 on Page 2 of the  the document "ZSA-M90S Switch Retrofit", labeled "MAY08.0301", shows a wiring diagram for the kit.  This diagram clearly shows that the intended wiring is that the white (neutral) wire from the AC supply goes to the switch, while the black (hot/line) wire goes directly to the lights.

...

Further, the design of the lampholder itself is problematic.  A [REDACTED]  (phenolic resin) lampholder base is attached to a "trapeze".  This trapeze is bent downwards to enable threading of the bulb, then bent back up so that the bulb fits snugly against the bottom plate of the range hood.  Performing this operation requires the user to place their hands inside the cavity of the range hood, increasing the likelihood of exposure to the live 110V leg of the circuit that is always present.  It also means that a user who wishes to have the lights sit flush as designed must carefully balance between screwing in the bulb further and retracting the trapeze.  These actions increase the likelihood of the E26 threads embedded into the phenolic resin breaking down/apart, as they did in my case; this was a contributing cause of the shock that I received, though in a different configuration, the broken threads could easily have provided a short-circuit path that bypassed the lamp, posing a fire hazard.

...

While rewiring the motor to no longer be switched-neutral is beyond my skills, I was ultimately able to effect a simple retrofit to remedy the issue with the lights.  With one of the traces on the PCB removed, I ran a separate wire for "hot" to the switch for the lights, and then reversed their positioning on the downstream lampholders.  It's probably not realistic to expect an end-user to be comfortable breaking traces on a PCB, but my retrofit demonstrates that Zephyr could at least partially resolve this issue for no more than the cost of a replacement PCB and a wire or two.

productDescription: Portable power station. Charges through 120VAC mains, or solar panel DC input. Supplies 120VAC mains power, 12VDC automotive power, or USB Charging. Also has a flashlight and wireless phone charger built-in.
incidentDescription:
Two technicians at my work cautioned me to be careful of the battery banks used on carts to charge/power laptops on the move, as they had both been shocked by power on the male wall plug while it wasn't connected to the wall. They described grabbing the plug so they could insert it into the wall receptacles in order to charge them, and getting shocked where their arms would go painfully stiff and numb. No lasting injuries were reported.
This alarmed me and as I have an electrical engineering background, I decided to quickly investigate. What I discovered is that all these units appear to have a design flaw that backfeeds 40-50VAC onto the input male power plugs across the live and ground, and and the neutral and ground prongs of the input cable when the 120VAC output is enabled from the battery pack. There should NEVER be live power of any kind on the charging cord EXCEPT when plugging into the wall to charge the units. I was able to replicate this problem across half a dozen different units so it's extremely unlikely it's a one-off flaw and not an inherent, dangerous design flaw. 40-50VAC is unlikely to permanently injure a healthy person, but this could certainly kill someone with a heart condition or a pacemaker. The products are being used as intended as mobile power supplies.
The units in question are the ALLPOWERS R600 available on Amazon with 4.8 stars. I also discovered checking a number of online databases, that the UL, CE and FCC certification markings on the product are most likely false as I've been unable to find and verify them for this product in any fashion.

incidentDescription:
Background:
The Fullstar Vegetable Chopper arrived a day before on March 7, 2024. Before purchasing the Fullstar Vegetable Chopper, I conducted extensive research over a course of months on various models (can confirm based on search history) where I assessed safety and user friendliness. I selected the Fullstar Vegetable Chopper due to its raving reviews on safety and popularity. The intention of buying the product was to help decrease cooking time, which turned out to be the worst decision of my life.

Saving myself 10 seconds of chopping time has resulted in a life altering event that has now impacted my body, personal life, functionality of my right-dominant hand,employment, and graduate school.

Packaging issue: 
As I began to open the packaging I realized that there were many red flags in terms of packaging.
The loose metal grid was wrapped in plastic. Compared to regular kitchen knives that have thick plastic coverings or sleeves. 
The spiral cutters had tape covering the sharp edges. Once again, no thick plastic round covering the entry compared to other brands.

It appears that  Fullstar Vegetable Chopper is more concerned about saving on packaging costs, rather than increasing their safety measures in terms of packaging. I have the vegetable chopper in a trash bag if needed for further investigation. 

Accident:
On March 8, 2024, I was working remotely from my house in [REDACTED]. 

As I began to open the packaging I realized that there were many red flags in terms of packing. The pieces appeared to all be improperly lodged inside of the chopper chamber, where only one of the grids was in a plastic thin sleeve and the exposed (piece that caused damage to my hand) was already attached. As I was inspecting the plastic grid attached to the top lever because it was detached, my right hand was unfortunately centimeters from the exposed grid when it pressed upon the lower side of my right hand below my pinky finger. I was unaware of the metal grid being exposed. Considering that all of the attached pieces were not attached, it never occurred to me that there would be one exposed grid without any safety coverings. Once again,  Fullstar Vegetable Chopper was more focused on cheap packaging. 


Hospitalization / Surgery:
I immediately called 911 for guidance because a significant amount of blood was gushing out of my hand. 

I drove myself to the hospital where I received temporary stitches and they were unable to operate on my hand, because there was no hand specialist available. I was told that my tendon was cut and likely to have nerve damage.

On March 18, 2024, ten days after the accident, I underwent surgery. The doctor was able to successfully repair the cut tendon and did not find nerve damage. However, the severity of the trauma to my hand has resulted in intense physical therapy to regain hand function. 

The seller has failed to respond to my messages and Amazon claims representative. This product is unsafe and they have been made aware of other issues (based on review responses) they need to be held accountable.

The relief valve on the unit was somehow compromised and the flame and gas was spewing up the wall. I immediately turned the gas off at the floor and the fire went out. If I had not been in my home, or if I had been asleep , the damages wouldve been much much worse. I would strongly recommend not using any Mr. heater products. My husband and I ran in there and found this brand new heater (just took it out of the box about a week ago)on fire. If I had used it in my coop my entire flock would have been killed before anyone even noticed a fire. Thankfully we caught the fire before it burned my house down or killed my baby chicks. It did however damage my hardwood floor. Thankfully, the fire tripped a breaker...sending my son looking to see what else in my house was effected and ultimately discovering the fire before the smoke detector went off.  I find it highly disturbing that when I went to contact Amazon, I noticed the reviews and ratings have gone down since my purchase. The listing I purchased from is now showing unavailable/out of stock with a 3 star rating.  However, with a quick search, I was able to locate the same heater, being sold by the same seller available for purchase and has a 4.5 star review. After speaking to Amazon today, I went back to that listing and now its not only available with a 4.5 star rating, but also being offered to me at 20% off.  Amazon resolution to this problem was to offer me an exchange for a new one or exchange for 80% of my purchase price, because I'm outside of their return window. ....which to me says, absolutely nothing is going to be done or followed up on. This thing needs to be recalled or something.  This could have been catastrophic. Had this been in a chicken coop like it's intended purpose it would have been catastrophic.  I have also attempted to contact the seller, but have not received a response yet. Listing does state that the heater is UL certified

incidentDescription: I just purchased a Cuisinart TOA-65 toaster/oven/airfryer. I noticed really hot air coming out the vent on the back so got out a thermocouple thermometer. When on the 450 degree airfry setting, after a few minutes the air coming out the vent on the back was 220 degrees F. This seems to be a fan forced airflow. I looked up the UL safety spec (UL 1026) and it said a maximum of 110 degree temperature rise was allowed. I also looked up the operating temperate specs of a [REDACTED] electrical outlet (the appliance may be placed in front of a kitchen counter outlet), and it was a lot less than 220 degrees. Common [REDACTED] wire used in homes is only rated up to 60 degrees C (140 F). People reported both on Amazon reviews and the Cuisinart [REDACTED]support group of melted outlets behind this appliance. I am returning the appliance to Amazon, as I don't want to risk damage to my home or my personal safety. I don't know if this is just something about the specific unit I have is defective or if this is a design defect of all TOA-65's. No injuries occurred and no damage occurred to my home, but potentially melting an outlet is not something an appliance should do.

productDescription: Ryobi 40V Volt Lithium-ion 6.0 Ah High Capacity Battery, Model 0P40602VNM, Black, 6inL x 3inW x 3inH, used for lawn equipment (mower, string trimmer)
incidentDescription:
On a Thursday afternoon, we suddenly noticed smoke in our kitchen. We were able to identify quickly that the smoke was coming from one of our cabinets. I opened the cabinet and found smoke forcefully flowing out of one of our Ryobi 40V batteries for our lawn mower and string trimmer. I was able to remove the battery to the yard, where the battery began to actually flame and burn. We called the fire department, who advised us to just let it burn out in a fire pit until it exhausted all of the lithium in the battery. 

We suffered some minor smoke damage in our cabinet, as well as some melting of the casing of the other two Ryobi 40V batteries that were in the cabinet. The batteries were all purchased new with new equipment in May of 2023, and used within manufacturer guidelines.  The batteries were kept on the charger only when charging, and removed once they were fully charged. We always stored them off the charger in a kitchen cabinet that is dry and maintained at 68-74 degrees year round. The batteries had stored for the winter and had not been disturbed since Oct/Nov of 2023, so there was no apparent event that would cause the battery to suddenly combust. We were lucky (a) to have been home to notice the smoke and remove the burning battery before it caused a house fire, and (b) to have enough time to research how to extinguish the battery and NOT use a standard fire extinguisher or water on it, which actually makes battery fires worse. If either of these things had gone differently, we could have had a lot more damage or injuries.

productDescription: Free standing Pellet Stove
incidentDescription:
I wanted to report a potential safety hazard with the following Pellet Stove. 

Stove:
Castle Serenity Pellet Stove (manufactured by Ardisam, Inc with headquarters in Cumberland WI 54829) Model 41278:  S/N: 041703 01021 071423 1333

My experience:
On Saturday 3/2/24 at ~11:30 AM EST I had the stove set to ECO mode with control by the thermostat.  We had just left our house for some shopping for a few hours.  Stove was off when we left.  Approximately -hour after we left, the stove turned on and began the ignition procedure.  It was likely about 2/3 through the "ignition" procedure, when the power blinked off for about 4 seconds.  I know this because I received a text notice from another appliance thats connected to the internet and sends a text message when the power is restored.and the firepot was full of pellets that were partially lit.  When the power came back, apparently the stove didnt.   Over the course of the next hour before we got home, the pellets continued to smolder in the firepot.  My house filled with smoke, all the smoke alarms in the house were going off.  

When we got home (around 1:15 PM EST), the smoke was so thick we could hardly make it through the house to get a dog out that was in her crate in the room where the stove is (downstairs in a large walkout basement) and get the windows open.

My house:
2,700 SF modern ranch constructed in 2007.  

My Installation (which is in accordance with manufacturers recommendations outlined in the Owners Manual): 
- Location  at the center of 37 long exterior wall within a walkout basement.  Its the on the walkout portion (not the buried portion of the basement).
- Exhaust - 3 Duravent piping with high temp silicone sealed joints with a 38 section of vertical pipe (greater than the 36 min. indicated in the Owners Manual) and vented out through sidewall.
- Intake - The installation instructions indicate that installing the 2 fresh air intake to the outside is NOT required for my situation (or at least it doesnt explicitly state that I must install the air intake to draw air from the exterior).  So, I did NOT install an intake pipe to burn exterior air, I let it utilize interior air from my house since I do have plenty of air leaks in my house.

Product Issue and recommendation:
Update the Power Outage/Restoration Safety Feature that is already part of the software that runs the stove.  Do this by updating the software for the fire-off procedure after power outage to LOWER the firebox temperature setpoint when power is restored from 120 deg Fahrenheit to 95 deg (which is an ambient temp that would NOT be typical in a house).

incidentDescription:

I was curious what had happened so I opened it to inspect it and found that the tip-over safety switch had completely melted and the leads had melted into the plastic plate the switch was mounted on.

I believe the problem was that instead of tipping over completely, the heater (being rather top-heavy) rocked back and forth, opening and closing the switch. It's also possible that the base of the heater might have landed on the heater's own cord and left the switch only partly open. In any case, it looks like there was arcing in the contacts that led to a high-resistance connection.

productDescription: Onewheel self balancing skateboard
incidentDescription:
Future motion taking away safety features 
We use to be able to use a 3rd party app to be able to see our individual cell voltages and make sure they were within safe operating range,
We use to be able to use the onewheel app to see overall voltage to make sure our boards were operating correctly 

Future motion has since enables updates that cause our boards to no longer connect to the 3rd party app to be able to see individual cell voltages and has since taken the feature of seeing overall battery voltage away from their own application

This makes the product alot less safe not knowing whether our cells are within a safe operating range, we just have to assume that they are, I have seen plenty of instances where this has led to problems

incidentDescription: I recently purchased a Lectric XP Step-Thru 3.0 White Long-Range eBike. When the bike was delivered, the rear tire/tube was deflated and separated from the bicycle. Upon contacting the company about this issue, I was informed that there was a known defect in the tubes and wheels for the bicycle I purchased. I was told that a batch of the bikes had weak tubes prone to rupture, burrs on the wheel rims that could lead to repeated tube punctures, and/or screws sticking out on the rims that could lead to repeated tube punctures. After I reported the issue, I received what seemed to be a form email about possible fixes for these issues. I had no idea that this was an issue before I purchased this bike, I was not informed about this issues before I received the bike, and I did not find out until I contacted customer service. As far as I know, no widespread notice has been sent out to customers about this issue as I have not received any such public notice even though the product I purchased was affected. I suppose I was lucky, because if my tire had not arrived deflated, I might have thought that the inevitable flat tire was due to user error or environmental hazard. I was never put in harms way because I have been unable to ride the bike even once. However, those customers that are not informed of these defects may repeatedly experience flat tires without understanding that the cause may be a defect with the bicycle wheels and tubes. Lectric offered to pay for me to get the problems repaired, but in the end I could not access a bike shop that would handle the issue. So that I could repair the bike myself, Lectric eventually agreed to send me new front and rear wheels, which are currently on backorder until the end of October. Originally I was told that there would be no point in them sending me new wheels because the new wheels might have the same problem. This indicates that they know there is a problem, but have not fixed it, and are not necessarily checking the products they send out to the public. I recently read about their disc brake caliper recall on the same model bike I purchased (albeit different dates), and this makes me worried about the safety of the product in general.

productDescription: Ashley Hearth 	DVAG11L Propane Direct Vent Wall Heater
productType: Gas or Lp Heaters, Other or Not Specified (392)
incidentDescription: Ashley Hearth direct vent wall mounted propane heater is the product; however, the concern is specifically regarding the pilot/igniter assembly. In October of 22 I purchased 3 of these at the same time from Amazon. Subsequently, all 3 have failed. I am a retired Master Mechanic/Machinist for reference. The Pilot Assy fails because of a design flaw in that the brass tube fittings are pressed then swedged into a steel plate. Heat from the burner; expansion and contraction causes the brass fittings to fall out. This misaligns the pilot burner, thermocouple and igniter. One unit simply failed to light because the piezo tip fell out. Another melted the end off the thermocouple as it misaligned directly into the pilot flame and would not light. The third, and most concerning failed as the flame supply tube fell out of the front and continued to remain lit in the heater bottom where it doesn't belong. If the flame tip would happen to come off, there would potentially be an open pilot flame outside the heater creating a very unsafe scenario. The overall function and quality of the rest of the heater seems adequate, although I will also say that when my units arrived, all the tube nuts that secure and seal the gas lines to the gas valve and the pilot assy. were too loose. All three units were like this, and I have done an Amazon review advising customers to check this before putting in service, as it could lead to a gas leak. I was able to loosen the pilot gas line by hand on two units. I suspect this loosening is caused from shipping, and there is little the manufacturer can do. Over tightening the tube nuts at manufacture is not a good option, and shipping always beats everything to death. Especially all the way from China were these heaters are made. In conclusion: At the very least, these heaters need an upgraded pilot assembly. There are two larger BTU sizes of the same style heater plus natural gas versions of all three. Simply search Ashley heater on Amazon to see them all. If they use the same pilot assembly all these products are suspect and need further evaluation to protect consumers. Respectfully submitted: [REDACTED]

I found mold floating in my coffee!!  
I clean my Breville Precision Brewer coffee maker (Model BDC450) every day before I brew my coffee.  I think I've brewed almost 800 carafe's of coffee in my coffee maker since I bought it in 2020.  I know this because I've bought 8 packs of 100 coffee filters.  I wash all components downstream of the hot water shower head.  Every surface gets cleaned with water and a paper towel, every brew.  I also run warm water through the coffee drip inlet on the top of the carafe lid to attempt to clean all of the fluid path.  I set the lid aside to dry while grinding my coffee beans.  

I recently (just today) found chunks things that were not coffee grounds in my coffee.  I researched online to see if anyone was having the same problem.  There were. Here is a link to what I found:
[REDACTED]

Based on everyone else's similar experience and troubleshooting methods, I made the decision to destructively inspect my carafe lid to see if there was mold.  I used a razor blade to carefully undo the ultrasonic weld that holds the lid together.  What I found was totally disgusting.  There was black, stringy mold inside of my coffee carafe.  And the only way to get to it was destroying the lid.  This uncleanable surface hidden away, which is introduced to warm condensate every day, harbors an unthinkably large colony of bacteria and mold.  This product needs to be recalled.  I'm not the only one who is experiencing this problem, clearly.  

The danger from this product is unavoidable and presents a high risk of longterm health problems.

I have pictures of the inside of the carafe lid, if this helps the CPSC issue the recall.  I am very seriously concerned that others will be hurt by this product.

incidentDescription:
I have a Fellow Stagg electric kettle which suddenly started violently spouting boiling water during the boiling process during which the electric base would be completely drenched in boiling water. Water would be spouted up to 1 foot away from the kettle. I reported this to the manufacturer immediately, recommending a recall due to this extreme danger of burning and electric shock, however they did not seem to be interested and blamed me for a user error instead.

As it turns out, this issue is due to a manufacturing error. incidentDescription:
For an extended period, we have routinely utilized blenders for tasks such as grinding spices, making sauce, and juicing. After thorough consideration, we opted to invest in a Vitamix, specifically the Venturist V1200 model in Red, purchased from Costco on November 29, 2020. This blender variant is equipped with three different jars, all of which my wife and I use regularly.

On January 5, 2023, while my wife was grinding spices using the [REDACTED] (nut butter jar), an incident occurred. This particular jar requires proper screwing onto the base with the blade and should be mounted upside down in the blender. Failure to completely secure or mount the jar correctly prevents the blender from initiating the grinding process. Unfortunately, during the grinding process, the jar unscrewed itself from the base. In an attempt to prevent spills and avoid spraying spices, my wife attempted to secure the jar manually and stop the blender. However, the jar dislodged from the base, resulting in severe lacerations to her middle and ring fingers. The injury caused significant blood loss, immense pain, and dizziness.

Swift action was taken, and my wife was immediately taken to an urgent care facility where she received nine stitches to mitigate further blood loss. Despite being prescribed painkillers, she endured constant pain and disrupted sleep for several weeks. Subsequently, she underwent a procedure at [REDACTED] Hospital to remove the stitches and realign the tissues, as they were not properly positioned due to the substantial blood loss. It took an additional month for her to recover and regain the ability to use her right hand for basic activities. Since the incident, her right-hand ring finger has not functioned normally, and she experiences intermittent pain.

I am prepared to provide medical treatment records and doctor's findings as needed by your office. It is noteworthy that the product details indicate that if a jar is not mounted or screwed properly, the blender is designed to detect this and should not initiate its functioning.

productDescription: Samsung 24.52-cu ft Side-by-Side Refrigerator with Ice Maker (Stainless Steel) Model #RS25J500DSR
incidentDescription:
On December 12, 2018, my husband and I purchased through Lowe’s a Samsung refrigerator (Samsung 24.52-cu ft Side-by-Side Refrigerator with Ice Maker (Stainless Steel); Model #RS25J500DSR), along with a stovetop/oven, microwave/convection oven, washer, and dryer—all Samsung—for our remodel. In total, we spent nearly $5,000 to have all matching appliances. 

After not even five years of use, our refrigerator started having problems. First, in the spring of 2023, the ice maker completely quit working. No ice was being produced at all. Then, on or about August 28, 2023, the controls on the front of the refrigerator suddenly began flashing, signaling an error code and failed to respond to touch. I contacted Samsung via online messaging on or about August 30, 2023. The service representative requested information from me regarding the problem and even collected a video from me showing the control panel flashing lights. He instructed me to perform a hard reset of the unit, which I did with no resulting change. The representative then advised that they would open a ticket and request service from a local repair technician. In the meantime, we continued to attempt several times to perform a reset on the unit, following the steps suggested by Samsung. We also ensured that the coils and filters were clean and free of debris. At that time, the refrigerator and freezer began having issues cooling adequately and holding a consistent temperature. We have verified that the unit is not cooling to an optimal temperature through the use of standalone thermometers. Obviously, this is very unsafe, and we have lost hundreds of dollars of groceries because of this. Thankfully, no one has gotten ill (yet). To this day, all issues with the ice maker, control buttons, and refrigerator temperature persist and Samsung refuses to help with repairs or acknowledge their defective product.

I knew I wanted it close but not too close. So I had the product about 6 inches from the grill.

I walked inside for a moment and found the fan was against the grill. Turns out it developed a vibrating type of movement where it pushed itself against the grill. After I finished cooking I couldn't replicate this behavior. So I tried it on the stove and sure enough, the fan vibrated to the stove. 

It seems to develop this issue near cooking surfaces when cooking temperature rises, which runs counter to the product's desired outcome. With no instructions or warnings, if this is even a normal behavior, I can see how this can be a significant fire hazard.

I have a video of this behavior I'd be happy to share.

productDescription: The product is a professionally manufactured griddle made up of 2 controls feeding gas to 4 burner tubes. The cooking surface is a 3/16" thick stamped steel plate formed to cover the burners, with a back and side splash lips to contain spatter and liquid. The product is well made, has a high reputation with existing users and appears in good repair throughout. No rough edges, no loose screws, all parts are properly assembled and it appears the griddle is capable of operating as designed. With the exception of control knobs which are not capable of withstanding the heat conducted through the control shafts. It appears to be a design/materials problem.
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription: After purchase of a brand new Blackstone Model 1666 22" griddle I connected propane (per instruction) and ignited the burners to heat the grill on high for 15 minutes to season the griddle. After the seasoning I attempted to turn the griddle off and the knobs could not press the burner control in enough to permit them to turn off. It is necessary to push the knobs "in - towards the griddle" to allow the controls to turn past the mechanical stop. Unable to turn off the griddle, I turned off the propane and allowed the griddle to cool. I removed the knobs and it appeared evident that the burner control shafts had  become hot enough to soften the plastic in the knob which prevented the knob from engaging on the raised part of the shaft. The knob could turn properly but could not be pressed far enough to pass the mechanical lock. There was no injury and it was later possible to install the knobs upside down from their initial orientation and the griddle could be operated, but with difficulty. IE if the knob was depressed very firmly, it could be turned to light and operate, but not consistently. At this time, I do not consider the griddle safe to operate.

productDescription: Hot Spring hot tub model Flair color Tuscan and Espresso dimensions 7’x7’x30” deep
incidentDescription: My wife and I purchased a Hot Tub from Regina pools and spa’s in Timonium MD on 7/25/23’ for $14,782. We received the hot tub on 10/06/23’ and was assembled by service tech’s from Regina. The electrical work was preformed at the time of delivery, by [REDACTED] a sub contractor recommended by Regina. Who we paid separately $2150.00 at the time of the installation. 10/16/23’ the Hot Tub tripped the 30amp GFCI circuit breaker in the sub panel installed by [REDACTED]. I reset the GFCI breaker two times and the breaker continued to trip. I notified [REDACTED] that night by text and they responded by phone the following morning 10/17/23’ stating that it was a spa issue not a GFCI Breaker issue and to contact Regina Pools and Spa’s. I contacted Regina they had me perform troubleshooting to the Spa to help resolve the issue which it didn’t the GFCI breaker continued to trip. 10/19/23’ a service rep from Regina came to our home to try to resolve the issue. He tried to have the breaker trip while he was here and he couldn’t get the breaker to trip. He stated that he would have to see the breaker trip in order to diagnose the issue. The service rep told me to continue using the spa which we did. Shortly after the Regina service tech left the breaker tripped again. 10/20/23’ I reported the breaker issue again to Regina and the rep said they would have a service tech out on 10/23/23’ ,and to leave the spa off. 10/23/23’ Regina service rep, arrived and began to try to diagnose the issue with the spa again. He could not get the breaker to trip again, and stated once again that, without seeing the breaker tripped, he could not begin to make any repairs. I noticed their service rep never had a meter to measure voltage with him either time he was here. I have a little electrical knowledge and the fact he never used a voltage meter raised some concerns. Again later that evening after their service rep left, we ran the hot tub . This time I had my cell phone with me and recorded video of the hot tub tripping the breaker multiple times that evening. 10/24/23 The owner of Regina pools and spa’s called me to tell me that he had spoken with the manufacture of the hot tub. Watkins wellness manufacturing and determined that it was more than likely a faulty GFCI breaker, and that he was going to send a service rep back out the following morning to replace the breaker. 10/24/23’ the same service rep that had been here two times before came again this time to replace the 30 amp GFCI breaker in the subpanel. After he completed swapping out the breaker, he told me to run the spa and let them know if there are any further issues. Later that afternoon, after running the spa, the breaker tripped again. I called and notified the owner of Regina pools and spas, and made him aware of the situation and that I was not happy and I did not have confidence that his service techs could resolve this issue and wanted a full refund for the amount of the hot tub. Later that evening a representative from Watkins Manufacturing called and stated their policies under warranty issues. Watkins mmfg does not do buy backs /refund money to the consumer, or swap out defective product for new. Essentially I was stuck with the spa that we bought and had to use Regina pools and spas to resolve this issue. I mentioned to the Watkins manufacturing representative that I didn’t feel that this was so much a warranty issue as it is a safety issue. Again she stated the company’s policy and what my option was. Contact Regina and have them fix it, and that ended the conversation.

incidentDescription:
10/4/2023:  The consumer’s 12 year-old, 186 lbs, 67” tall, son was riding the scooter down their street.  The son was on the scooter for approximately 2 minutes, when the front fork that holds the front wheel in place, snapped.  The wheel stayed attached to the scooter, but the bolt that supports the wheel/fork, broke.  A plastic portion of the fork is bent.  The son was riding approximately 3 miles per hour at the time of the accident.

The scooter is rated for 264 lbs., and can travel up to 20 miles per hours..  The scooter has never distributed any problems in the past.  The consumer’s children have only ridden the scooter on the paved street, in front of their home.  The scooter came fully assembled, ready to use.


The consumer immediately took him to a nearby hospital, but the first hospital transferred the son to a children’s hospital, which was an hour away.

The son sustained lacerations to the chin and fractures to both the right & left side of the jaw, as well as fractures to both his left & right wrist.  The son was kept at the hospital for 15 hours, while they searched for a surgeon.  After locating a surgeon, it was determined that it’s best to wait and see if the child will heal on his own.  The son was administered antibiotics and released the same day.

The consumer tried to call the firm, but was frequently told that no one was available.  She tried calling during the hours they were open on Hong Kong time, but still could not speak with anyone.  She was told that someone would get back in touch with her, but no one has.

She also looked up some of the reviews on-line and saw numerous other incidents, but they were not as severe as her incident.


She contacted the dealer and they offered a complete refund, but the consumer noted that she has 2 extensive hospital bills and her focus is also to warn other people about the hazard with this scooter.

productDescription:
LG LRMXC2206S French Door Refrigerator/Freezer  Stainless Steel,  Counter Depth     34-3/4" Wide, 31-1/4" Depth, and 69-3/4" High

We purchased an LG LRMXC2206S in April, 2022, and once installed, we placed digital thermometers in the fridge and also in the freezer to monitor the internal temps.  After a few days to equilibrate, the internal fridge temperatures recorded by the thermometer was 3-4 degrees F higher than the set temperature on the door control panel.  We called LG service about this and their tech came, took some temperature measurements and then explained that everything was fine since "the actual temperature inside the unit can be within 5 to 10 degrees of the set temperature" (We got the same reply when contacting LG service online and by phone).  We lived with a lower setting (34F) to maintain an internal temp of 37F.  In late April of 2023, we found that the internal temps were on the rise despite lowering the control temp to its lowest setting of 33F.  We were getting internal temps of 40-41F (with the control temp set to 33F), which is pushing against the max temp for safe food storage in fridges recommended by the US FDA.   Since the one-year warranty had expired three weeks earlier, we called a service person who replaced a fan, the back panel containing a thermistor, and finally the main control board.  All this took 4 months and cost us roughly $800.  When all the servicing was complete, we still had to set the control panel temp to the minimum setting (33F) to maintain a safe internal temperature of 37-38F.  As a result, we perceive a potential danger to others because of the inability of the LG LRMXC2206S to maintain temperatures that are safe for food storage as defined by the US FDA.  Please note that the freezer worked well throughout.
incidentDescription: Refrigerator would not maintain FDA safe temperatures for food storage (Below 40-41F) even when control temperature was set to lowest temperature of 33F.
