productDescription: Onewheel XR.  Guys, I'm not really sure how to pull all this data that you're asking for...
incidentDescription:
Hi.

I've been an avid rider of the OneWheel, made but FutureMotion.  Specifically, I have an XR.  I have over 1000 miles ridden across multiple devices.  I myself have purchased three XRs.

I've taken my licks on these boards - many of which have been my own fault, so I want to be clear about those wipeouts.

My complaint is not “nosedive” in and of itself, as I do understand that the device has limits and thresholds based on rider weight, wind, elevation and grade factors, charge level, etc.  My complaint is a specific scenario that FM refuses to acknowledge and I believe continues to be buried under 1) a financial burden for the customer and 2) gas lighting individuals.

I was riding my board around a 75% charge and going up a 1-2% grade rode (absolutely minimal for the eye to perceive, but a slow elevation incline).  I believe I was going roughly 10 MPH.  Mind you, my board was under warranty at this time.  

My board outright failed.  We’re talking just DIED.  Zero pushback.  Zero physical feedback.  I was riding with my wife and she witnessed this - and her observation was “you didn’t do anything, it just stopped working on you”.  The end result was completely flaying my skin on the asphalt and a concussion.  I still have the helmet with the gouge marks on it.  

If I were riding a bike and the forks failed, the vendor would lose their mind and offer to fix it free of charge.  FM doesn’t work this way.

Future Motion said the only way they could diagnose this issue was for me to send my board it, at my burden, for $80.00 USD.  
1. This is a massive financial deterrent that should not exist when a user experiences extreme physical injury.
2. FM removed the capability to provide remote diagnosis over time forcing me as a consumer to have to ship vs. sending a simple data file.  I believe you guys have records of their firmware updates and app updates doing so.
3. The only finding I had was after I crashed, my phone app showed an issue on the charge, yet simultaneously reported that the charge was fine.  Seriously?

I want to focus on the cells.  I believe that there are a some batteries that fail - maybe batch related, maybe a charge issue, maybe something else.  WHEN they fail, there is no recourse and the rider suffers personal and extreme injury.  I would know, as here in Albuquerque we had a rider DIE. (I don’t have context on the how or why, but come on, really?)


Aggregate issues like mine, plus documented problems with GT boards ghosting with the FSB, pint boards pinching and breaking their internal wirings - and their outright refusal to acknowledge that.  I had to seek 3rd party independent diagnosis, which now of course FM won’t support - the end result was a faulty BMS, but because I took the board apart I now have no recourse after being told they wouldn’t listen to me.

Haptic feedback is a good start for newbies and for overall helpfulness of the consumer, but it does absolutely nothing to address critical intrinsic issues with the underlying electronics, failing battery cells, failing BMS's and FSB's, and haptic feedback is not going to solve cases like mine.

THESE BOARDS HURT PEOPLE.  FM needs to be held accountable for their business practices.  We all understand there are implicit risks like any other sport, but come on.

How can a company show people doing hand stands without a helmet or protective gear on the main website?  How can they show women in bikinis “cruising” down the road with no protection?  How can the place a financial burden on someone that just dropped A FEW THOUSAND DOLLARS on the product to simply diagnose.  “Oh we put a warning”.  Okay.  Sure.

I would encourage you to see the stories coming out on [REDACTED] .  There is a plethora of people describing stories like mine, detailing broken bones, boards that fail for no reason, and antagonistic behavior from Future Motion.

I also find it hilarious that this “recall” is restricted to six hours a day to minimize their willingness/want to to work with customers.

I hope this helps someone from dying, because we had one death here in my local town and it sucks.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

incidentDescription:
I purchased "Vacplus Moisture Absorber Packets, Fragrance Free (10 Pack), Humidity Packs, Hanging Closet Dehumidifier Bags, Desiccant 9.8OZ (Nickname: VA-M158)" on Amazon. The product page lists the Seller as "Vacplus-BAYL" and states the product to be shipped by Amazon. When I received the product from Amazon, I was confused and became concerned. The product label does not tell me what the products is. I'm not sure how to handle and use the product . I'm also concerned about using the product safely because the label does not include any first aid information or tell me what steps to take if an accident occurs in my home or with my kids. I am not sure if this product is safe for my kids. The label states the product is not edible, but the product is small and capable of being ingested easily (either by eating or drinking), and I'm not sure what steps I need to take if one of my kids were to ingest these chemicals. I'm also not sure if the product is safe for the environment or what I should do to handle the product or discard the chemicals after use. 

The front label does not have a Signal Word or any affirmative statement of the principal hazards. I'm not sure how hazardous the chemicals are inside the product or on its packaging. I am unsure how to contact for further information about the product because the label does not tell me the name of manufacturer, and I'm not sure where the business is located. The sole information about the business appears in Chinese characters on the Amazon product listing. There is nothing on the label about who makes, sells or distributes the products in the United States.

This product is defective and its label is unacceptable. The product is misbranded. The product label does not have  a Signal Word and lacks all conspicuous warnings about potential product hazards. The label lacks proper warnings on both the front and back of the product. The label is also misleading and deceptive because there is no way for anyone to contact the company to obtain further information. 

Because the label is unacceptable, the product is misbranded and defective under federal law. Because its label fails to have cautionary language to help consumers handle and use the product safely and fails to give consumers the necessary info about first aid steps to take if an accident occurs, this product should not be available for sale to consumers in the United States, and it should be removed from our market.

productDescription: Samsung Refrigerator Model # RF27T5241. S/N 0B4M4BCW300969R. 27 CU, French doors, dual ice makers, stainless steel
incidentDescription: I purchased a Samsung refrigerator, model # RF27T5241, back in August of 2022. I kept finding flakes of some sort coming out of the water and settling at the bottom of our cups and glasses. At first I thought that maybe I didn't flush out the system enough when I first set it up. but no matter how much water I ran through it, the flakes continued to show up. I bought a couple of new water filters for it thinking that maybe it had a bad filter in it. I replaced the filter, and we still had the same problem. I finally called Samsung and reported it to them and they sent someone out to my home. The man they sent out the first time, paid more attention to the girl he was talking to on the phone than he was to the issue. He first said, what I was seeing were bubbles. After I showed him that those so called bubbles were settling at the bottle of the glass, he indicated that the particles I was seeing had to be calcium deposits coming through my water supply. I advised him that this is the 3rd refrigerator I have had in this home, and we never had any such issue with them. I also stated, that the water filter in the refrigerator should have caught the particles. He denied that and said that the filters don't always catch everything. He asked if I replaced the filter with a Samsung filter, and I advised him that I did. He obviously did not believe me and (without turning off the water supply as the manual indicates), he pulled out the filter, water started flowing out everywhere, and then he slammed the filter back in. So he still insisted it was just calcium coming through and left. I had to replace that new filter because dark water began coming out of the filter. Not to mention that the filter was not placed back on correctly and water was leaking all over the place. I reported all of this to Samsung, and they sent someone else out, who more or less did said the same thing as the first one. Again, I called Samsung because there was no way we were going to drink that water or use the ice from it. When I spoke with someone from Samsung that time, The lady on the phone advised me that if she sent someone out, I would have to pay for it because my 1 year warranty was up in April. I advised her, that I bought the unit in August not April, and if they have it registered to someone else, the unit must have been sold before, taken back to Lowe's, and resold to me. She then stated that someone else will come to the house and check it out again. So the 3rd person came to the home and guess what? He found that there were some damaged parts inside the water filter system and it wasn't calcium coming through the line. The next day, I received a call from Samsung, and was told that they were going to send me out a new unit. I asked if I could get a refund instead because I really didn't trust their product if it has issues this early in the game. The gentleman stated, that the unit will be brand new and last me for years, and not to worry because it will be under a new warranty. So, they sent Lowe's out with another unit and this one turns out to be worst than the last one. We received this one on 06/10/23, and at first, everything worked fine. But right around the 1st of July (the day before we left for our vacation), we noticed that some of the ice cubes in the bottom tray, were stuck together and it didn't seem to have made much more ice. I thought by the time we returned from vacation, the tray would be full again. But when we returned, it didn't make anymore ice. We also noticed that some of the items in the freezer were getting soft. So I called Samsung and reported it to them. They had me unplug the unit, wait several minutes, and then plug it back in. I did that and the temperature inside both the top and the bottom of the refrigerator were lower than they should be. So, I was instructed as to how I could reset the correct temperature on both the top and bottom, then told it could take up to 16 hours before everything was back to normal again. Well, I had to repeat that over and over again on the phone with them until I got fed up with it all. It was apparent, that the compressor was not working correctly. Again, I asked for a refund, but was denied. I asked if they were going to send a new unit, and I was denied that too. Now, we're are about to July 21st without a refrigerator or freezer working properly, and I was told that they will send somebody out to look at it. On the 24th, a man came out to look at it, and sure enough, the compressor was out. I asked if Samsung was going to send out another since we had food going bad, and he indicated that he was going to order the parts for it. I asked how long does that take, and he stated it takes at least a week, but Samsung is a little slower than most of them. As soon as he left, I called Samsung and advised them of what was going on, and could I please have a refund or an exchange, as this now seems like an emergency. And again, I was denied. They can't offer an exchange or a refund, until after the unit has been repaired (like they are going to refund or exchange anything after it's up and running again). I also mentioned (because during calls and waiting times, I did some research, and found that this model is the same as the RF27T5201, except the 5241 model has the dual ice makers, have been on your recall lists since 2020), that the unit has been on a recall list, and it should be handled ASAP. I asked them how soon can I expect to have something going because we need something now. I was then told that as soon as the repairman completes his report, and we receive it, which takes up to 48 hours, then Samsung will make a decision as to what will be done. There isn't anything else the can do until then. So here we sit in the middle of the summer 100 degree weather without a refrigerator. About a week later, I called the repair shop and asked if the parts came in yet, and I was told that the parts had been received, but the only person qualified to work on it could not get out to my home until the following Thursday (it was on a Friday when I called, so that meant it would be another week). Well, the following Thursday, the repairman came by. All he really did (that I could see), was shoot some Freon into the system. The repairman stated that the unit wasn't properly filled correctly from the factory. Then I waited about a week before calling Samsung back because one of the people that I first spoken with when I called about these issues, told me to make a list of all the food that gets spoiled because Samsung will give me a food voucher to replace it all. I advised my other half as to what I was told, so she began making a list. productDescription: ANKER POWERHOUSE 767
incidentDescription: Product is ANKER POWERHOUSE 767, ordered from seller "ankerdirect" on EBAY (identifies as FANTASIA TRADING, LLC), apparently a wholly owned subsidiary of ANKER INNOVATIONS LIMITED.  The product is an all in one portable power station (lithium iron phosphate battery pack, inverter, and associated electronics) which controls battery charging and subsequent output of stored energy through an inverter to provide power to household electrical devices which run on alternating current.  It is marketed to people desiring a source of electrical power during a utility power outage (among others).  I first tested the unit by plugging  three devices into it: cable modem, wireless router, and ethernet switch.  The router and switch powered up, the modem ([REDACTED]) did not.  When plugged into a household 120-volt receptacle, the modem powered up normally.  Having extensive electrical experience in my 76 years, I began investigating by plugging in my $5 three-light 120-volt receptacle tester, and found (to my amazement) hot and neutral reversed on this $2000 piece of gear.  An online search of "120 volt receptacle hot neutral reversed" will amply describe why this is incorrect and dangerous, so I won't go into that here.  I then searched online forums to see if anybody was talking about such a problem, and found multiple examples of people with the same experience who had made the company aware of the problem, and received replacement units without the problem.  Others who bought units long after the problem was made known to the company, and supposedly fixed, reported receiving units with the problem.  Apparently, the company produced many units, with the problem built into a random subset of the units, due to inadequate instructions and subsequent testing.  Then the units were sent to multiple stock points.  Upon learning of the problem, the appropriate action by the company would have been a recall and "stop sale" order, since detecting the problem is easy and cheap.  The complicating factors are that the unit weighs 67 pounds, and the packaging is heavy duty and strapped for [REDACTED] shipment, and the multiple stock points.  Opening the shipment units to do the simple test is taxing, so thus far, the company has just continued to ship out units like there is no problem, and replace the problem units as they are identified and returned.  The problem with this approach is that many devices will operate in what appears to be normal fashion, but with the risk of electrical shock that comes with the reversed leads.  The typical customer may have no devices (as I did) that check for the reversal and refuse to power up.  The typical customer will have no experience that leads them to look for such a problem, and no tools to identify it, and will suffer the risk without any warning.

productDescription: Blendjet 2 portable blender
incidentDescription:
My wife's Blendjet 2 started running on it's own yesterday, couldn't be shutoff for 10+ minutes, overheated, smoked and melted the casing!

My wife had used her Blendjet 2 for breakfast Saturday August 26th as per normal, cleaned it out and left it on the kitchen counter near the paper towel holder with the lid off but the main container still attached.

Over two hours later we were in the garage getting ready to leave the house and came back inside to get something and heard a whirring sound that we tracked down to the Blendjet running on the kitchen counter with the blades turning.  We pressed the button to turn it off and it sped up to normal mixing speed!  So we pressed the button again and it slowed down but didn't stop.  We repeated this process numerous times with similar results and were unable to stop the motor and the spinning blades.  We tried holding the button to reset it, nothing worked.  The lights flashing were sometimes red but nothing would turn it off.  

Not sure what to do we put it down on the counter away from other things hoping the battery would die soon.  A few minutes later my wife yelled out to me in the garage that the Blendjet 2 was smoking!  I grabbed it and took it out onto the driveway away from the house and cars.  I took off the clear plastic container part assuming there would be an automatic safety shutoff to protect users from the spinning blades, and it still didn't stop!

By now it was getting pretty hot to hold and so I dropped the base with spinning blades on the driveway to try to break it and stop it which didn't work.  We then thought to try to video it and managed to capture the last second of it running with the blades spinning as it rolled around on the sidewalk.  

After it finally stopped I tried to pick it up and it was too hot to hold.

I took a picture of the melted casing.  

My wife never dropped this Blendjet 2 or submersed it in water.  

Had this happened just a few minutes later, after we had left the house, this Blendjet 2 could have easily caused a fired which could have destroyed our house!

We also sent this report to the manufacturers customer support department.
We are not looking for a replacement.  We only want to warn others of this dangerous situation and the failure of at least two safety features on this Blendjet 2 (auto shutoff after 30 seconds, and a shutoff when the container is not attached).

productDescription: Ideal Living - Air Doctor air purifier
incidentDescription:
Air Doctor/Carbon Dust Contamination
Hi There,
I bought an air purifier from the Air Doctor store (Ideal Living, parent company) on Amazon about a month
ago. On July 3rd 2023, I vacuumed the filter because I have pets and they shed. Most people vacuum their air
filters to help keep their air machines running and in good condition.
After I vacuumed the filter, I noticed a cloud of black dust burst out of the carbon filter. At that time, the air
quality in my apartment had significantly changed for the worse. I opened both my vacuums and noticed that
the spongey vac filters were a darker shade of gray. And both of the reusable vacuum bags/containers had a
black fine particulate dust that lined the inside of them. That day I called my vacuum cleaner repair person and
she seemed to think that the gray saturation in the spongy filters and the canisters was not normal. She
recommended to wash the filters.
I called the Air Doctor customer service phone number and I talked to a representative who said, "Do not use
your vacuum in your home, after you use your vacuum on your filter because you will track carbon dust all over
your house." His advice was alarming but I listened to him and I did not use my vacuum again for fear of
spreading the carbon dust around further.
I began to vigorously clean up my floors with a mop, and started cleaning other parts of my apartment, I also
cleaned the insides of the vacuum cleaners. I was hoping that I could fix this terrible dust contamination
problem ??? until I realized that this was an unsalvageable situation. Unfortunately, there was a dust toxicity
exposure from this carbon filter accident.
I began to feel sick. My lungs started to hurt, I was having shortness of breath (constricted breathing), chest
tightness, brain fog, and my sinuses were completely clogged. On July 4th I called the [REDACTED] Nurse line.
The nurse asked me if I felt like I had shortness of breath. I said yes and went to the emergency room at about
12:00am on the night of July 5th. It was an extremely stressful situation to have to go to the emergency room to
get my lungs checked in the middle of the night while also trying to secure an emergency housing situation for
myself and my cats. Luckily, I am ok after leaving my contaminated apartment. I found a safe place to stay.
And I am still staying in a hotel at present.
I am in contact with a legal team (from Air Doctor/Ideal Living/Amazon) and am making a demand for their
insurance to financially cover the incurring expenses from this awful toxic exposure. I'll need funds for my hotel
stay, a mover to clear out my apartment, an industrial cleaner, as well as the replacement all of my contaminated
belongings.
In terms of witnesses, I have a long informative text from the vacuum repair person, several calls with Air
Doctor's customer service reps, as well as rep at the official Air Doctor online store whose name is [REDACTED]. I
have heard that she is aware of the malfunctioning carbon dust issue. I have a [REDACTED] post with comments
that state [REDACTED]knows several people who bought counterfeit machines (with hazardous carbon filters) from
the "Amazon" Air Doctor store. I found out about [REDACTED], through [REDACTED]. [REDACTED]and I know each other
from a [REDACTED] group.
I am trying to trouble shoot this nightmare. So, my plan is to hire an Industrial Hygienist to take a few samples
from my apartment before I get it professionally cleaned. I hope we can remedy this situation to help myself and
all of the other victims of this devastating Amazon air machine fiasco. It's unthinkable and so cruel that anyone
would advertise a product to help people but in turn actually harm them.
Thank you so much,
[REDACTED]

productDescription: Rec Teq, 1250 electric pellet smoker with ceramic heating element. The issues I experienced occurs on their other models for the same reasons.
incidentDescription:
I recently purchased a RecTeq 1250 electric pellet smoking grill. Upon my first ignition/startup I was able to quickly determine that the amount of fuel being fed into the fire pot was not appropriate to the amount of oxygen and heat source. This resulted in very large plumes of heavy smoke. When confined to a smoker this can and often results in a smoke explosion. 

I thought it was just because it was the first igniting, but on subsequent starts it has done the same thing. Upon doing further research I found this is quite a common phenomenon at start up with this brand of pellet smoker. All smokers run this risk, but it is usually caused by pellet voids or flameouts. Where these are happening at startup which shows their formulas and ratios are off.  The frequency this this happens also appears to be higher with this as a result of this. It's the design, not an anomaly or fluke.

When I wrote RecTeq about trying to return the smoker I was sent an automated reply, that was very similar to others I have seen who have reported this issue. This shows me that it is reported frequently enough that they had draft and modify an automated reply.

Upon further inspection of my smoker I discovered that the heating element was not installed correctly. It is not set in a way where it is making good contact with the pellets. It was actually installed recessed and this is why they were not igniting as they should. Again, this is a known issue within their community.

As a result of these incorrectly installed heating elements these units are at a high risk of fire, injury, and explosion right out of the box.  This poor contact also results in too many pellets being fed to the fire pot which also runs the risk of a backdraft, and also back burn. Back burn is when the pellets burn back into the hopper (pellet feed which holds 40 pounds of pellets) and again can cause significant fires. 

It does not seem that the company has not done much to address this quality control  issue. It is up to the consumer to take apart the fire pot and make the adjustment of the heating element. They do not warn consumers about this potential before starting up their smoker. In my opinion it should be something included in their manual to check before igniting.  

I am lucky as I have a cooking and fire science background, and I could see the trouble right away. Many others do not, and far worse many believe that it is normal. I understand that every smoker, grill, etc poses potential risks, this however is happening because of an assembly flaw that should be corrected at the factory. There is no excuse for these to roll out with the heating element, a key component installed incorrectly. It's far too dangerous.

productDescription: Li Poly Battery - See photos
incidentDescription:
July 23, 2023
1715 hours
Incident Number [REDACTED]
[REDACTED]

Notified at 1732 hrs. via cell phone by [REDACTED] to that a fire investigator was being requested at [REDACTED] for a lithium ion battery fire. (was later determined to be a Lipoly) I responded in [REDACTED] from my home.

On arrival out at 1807 hours I met with [REDACTED]. He stated that apparatus  responded to  a reported fire described as an electrical outlet fire that turned out to be a lithium ion battery fire. An occupant of the home remove the battery that was burning to the backyard. Crews then moved it to the front yard.

I photographed the remnants of the battery that had been moved to the front yard. It was undistinguishable. I then made my way into the house and photographed the living room on the first floor where the fire took place on the [REDACTED] of the building and the damage that was made.

I then went to the backyard and photographed the burn marks on the back porch and some clothing and towels that we used to bring the burning battery to the backyard.

I then interviewed an occupant of the home,  who stated that his girlfriend  cousin was down on the first floor when the fire occurred. He and XXXXXXX was on the second floor. The cousin  called up to her cousin XXXXXX once and then a second time which was described as being little bit more frantic.

When he and his girlfriend go down to the first floor they saw the battery burning on the floor. He put flour on the fire in an attempt to smother it. He then put a towel and clothing over it and brought it to the backyard.

The battery was plugged into the charging unit, but the charging unit was not plugged into the wall outlet according too XXXXXX. 
He stated that he had bought a remote control airplane on Friday at Hobby Quarters in Foxborough. He didn’t have paperwork as everything is electronic. He bought it on a payment plan. He was going to try to send me the information when he found it. 
There was a second battery that came with the Remote control airplane. I examined the second battery in photographed it.XXXXXX demonstrated how it was plugged into the charger and I photographed it.

I also went to the backyard and photographed the box that the RC airplane came in.

The plane was identified as a Star Max J3 Cub. The manual for same can be found here. https://rc-today.ru/UserFiles/Image/Instructions/382885194X592007X40.pdf

I  interviewed XXXXXXXXXX who stated that she heard a cackling sound, which I asked her if it was a crackling sound and she said yes. She stated it was like popcorn popping. It was coming from the area of the battery. All of a sudden the battery split in half and smoke and sparks started coming from the battery. Flames followed the sparks.

Photos can be viewed at [REDACTED].

[REDACTED] search for fires with this battery turned out to be negative. I found the following record on the Consumer Product Safety Commission website.

The submitter reports that thae responded to a residential garage fire that originated in the...
Incident Report | [REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
I will be making reports to both the manufacturer and CPSC.

I cleared the scene at 1835 hours.

Respectfully Submitted,


[REDACTED]

productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
Copied from the report I filed with the CT Dept. of Consumer Protection:

I purchased a gas grill from the Tractor Supply Company in [REDACTED], CT  on 5/19/23. It came fully assembled. A few days after I decided to grill, and
hooked up the propane. For some reason the grill would not light, and I could not figure out why. I looked underneath,
and the hose for the regulator was kinked as it was bent at a 90-degree angle. I called the store to see if they had one
from another grill they could swap out. They did not. I spoke with [REDACTED] in customer service who transferred me to [REDACTED]
who put the grill together. He said that "They all come in like that" and there was nothing he could do. So, he’s telling
me that every grill they have is defective, and a safety hazard, and the only way for it to work is to take a hose bend it
back creating even more stress on an already defective part that will eventually break. This is a safety hazard that can
result in an explosion. I contacted the [REDACTED] Fire Marshal's office. While they agreed with me they could not help as
they are in charge of grills assembled in a store. If It was in my house in [REDACTED] they could do something about it, but I
live in [REDACTED]. So I'm writing to this department to investigate, and take corrective action not only on this store, but
apparently ever single Tractor Supply Company in Connecticut as if these grills all "come in this way" it is a safety
issue, and an explosion waiting to happen. I am attaching pictures of the receipt, and damaged regulator in the
uploads.

I previously contacted the CT Department of Consumer Protection, but they said to contact you.

incidentDescription:
Hi There, I bought an air purifier from the Air Doctor store (Ideal Living, parent company) on Amazon about a month ago. On July 3rd 2023, I vacuumed the filter because I have pets and they shed. Most people vacuum their air filters to help keep their air machines running and in good condition.
After I vacuumed the filter, I noticed a cloud of black dust burst out of the carbon filter. At that time, the air quality in my apartment had significantly changed for the worse. I opened both my vacuums and noticed that the spongey vac filters were a darker shade of gray. And both of the reusable vacuum bags/containers had a black fine particulate dust that lined the inside of them. That day I called my vacuum cleaner repair person and she seemed to think that the gray saturation in the spongy filters and the canisters was not normal. She recommended to wash the filters.
I called the Air Doctor customer service phone number and I talked to a representative who said, “Do not use your vacuum in your home, after you use your vacuum on your filter because you will track carbon dust all over your house.” His advice was alarming but I listened to him and I did not use my vacuum again for fear of spreading the carbon dust around further.
I began to vigorously clean up my floors with a mop, and started cleaning other parts of my apartment, I also cleaned the insides of the vacuum cleaners. I was hoping that I could fix this terrible dust contamination problem – until I realized that this was an unsalvageable situation. Unfortunately, there was a dust toxicity exposure from this carbon filter accident.
I began to feel sick. My lungs started to hurt, I was having shortness of breath (constricted breathing), chest tightness, brain fog, and my sinuses were completely clogged. On July 4th I called the [REDACTED] Nurse line. The nurse asked me if I felt like I had shortness of breath. I said yes and went to the emergency room at about 12:00am on the night of July 5th. It was an extremely stressful situation to have to go to the emergency room to get my lungs checked in the middle of the night while also trying to secure an emergency housing situation for myself and my cats. Luckily, I am ok after leaving my contaminated apartment. I found a safe place to stay. And I am still staying in a hotel at present.
I am in contact with a legal team (from Air Doctor/Ideal Living/Amazon) and am making a demand for their insurance to financially cover the incurring expenses from this awful toxic exposure. I’ll need funds for my hotel stay, a mover to clear out my apartment, an industrial cleaner, as well as the replacement all of my contaminated belongings.
In terms of witnesses, I have a long informative text from the vacuum repair person, several calls with Air Doctor’s customer service reps, as well as rep at the official Air Doctor online store whose name is [REDACTED]. I have heard that she is aware of the malfunctioning carbon dust issue. I have a [REDACTED] post with comments that state [REDACTED] knows several people who bought counterfeit machines (with hazardous carbon filters) from the “Amazon” Air Doctor store. I found out about [REDACTED}, through [REDACTED]. [REDACTED] and I know each other from a Chemical Sensitivity [REDACTED] group.
I am trying to trouble shoot this nightmare. So, my plan is to hire an Industrial Hygienist to take a few samples from my apartment before I get it professionally cleaned. I hope we can remedy this situation to help myself and all of the other victims of this devastating Amazon air machine fiasco. It’s unthinkable and so cruel that anyone would advertise a product to help people but in turn actually harm them.       

Thank you, 

[REDACTED]

[REDACTED]

productDescription: Smoker grill
incidentDescription:
This consumer has owned a Pitt Boss Platinum Brunswick Wood Pellet Vertical Smoker (smoker) since
December 14, 2021. It has been used an estimated 12-15 times since purchase. On two of these uses,
the smoker had a serious "burn back" (described below), which resulted in an unreasonable risk of injury
to the consumer and damage to personal property. Additionally, throughout the approximate 1.5-year
ownership period, there have been repeated structural and mechanical issues. All mechanical and
safety issues were promptly reported to the company via the company's customer service group.
In general, the company was responsive to the mechanical issues, providing advice and numerous
replacement parts (including controller board, ignitor, temperature probes, and more). An estimated
20-30 hours of labor were required by the consumer to replace parts and make needed repairs
(including a malfunctioning door latch and seal). The company was not however, particularly helpful in
dealing with the burn-back fire issues (discussed below). Frustrated with the scope, frequency, and
severity of problems, the consumer attempted to return the smoker to Walmart (where it was
purchased). The return was denied as it was beyond the designated 3 (6?) month return period.
The smoker is fueled by wood pellets, which are stored in a large hopper located on the back of the
smoker. The pellets are transported internally via a metal auger. It feeds a small fire chamber where
the pellets are ignited producing heat and smoke. The burn back hazard is caused when the wood
pellets contained inside the auger become so hot they smolder and eventually combust. In a matter of
minutes, the fire can back up the auger into the storage hopper causing a serious fire risk.
The consumer was able to extinguish the two fires experienced by: removing the pellets in the hopper
(which is very difficult and dangerous while burning), unplugging the internal cooling fan (which was
making the fire worse), and cutting off all other outside air sources. The consumer was not injured in
either incident, nor was personal property significantly damaged. However, this outcome was only due
to the fact the consumer was still near the smoker when both fires stared and able to responded quickly
to remove fuel and air supply.

The consumer has followed all stated maintenance and operational guidelines found in company
manual/guides, on line, and from customer service representatives. The smoker was thoroughly cleaned
after each use, the wood pellets were sifted to remove excessive "dust" (which can clog the auger), and
all start-up and shut-down procedures were carefully followed. During the most recent call with
company representatives (5/29/23), it was also suggested that " ... perhaps the consumer(I) just needed
to invest in a better more expensive smoker." (The initial cost of this smoker was $579. 79.)
The burn back hazard with this smoker appears to be pervasive. The consumer conducted a very brief
search of the Pitt Boss internet forum (key words auger fire, back fire) and found 8 posts in the recent past 
on similar problems. Some posts indicated serious outcomes. The consumer strongly encourages
CPSC investigators to review this and other pertinent information (included past recorded calls between
the consumer and Pitt Boss representatives).

The consumer was told by Pitt Boss customer service staff (5/29/23) that the Platinum Brunswick
smoker is still being sold, and that it is not under any type recall. The consumer believes this smoker
unit is poorly designed and manufactured as evidenced by the numerous failures experienced. More
importantly, the consumer believes this smoker represents a very real, ongoing, and unreasonable risk
of injury and damage to property.

incidentDescription:
Viribus 26" Electric Bike - [REDACTED]

I was involved in a serious biking accident on my Viribus 26" electric bike the afternoon of (6/5/2023). The bolt and nut that secures the front fender to the fork worked loose while I was riding and the fender caught on the tire while I was traveling around 16 MPH.  This caused the fender to jam forward into the fork and lock up the front tire, resulting in the bike flipping over me, throwing me to the ground and landing on top of me.  I was pinned underneath the 50 pound bike and had to struggle to get out from underneath it. The bike had been delivered May 16th and we had already noticed the bolt had loosened twice prior and had retightened the bolt as tight as physically possible. 

We believe there is a serious defect in the way the fender attaches to the fork as the nut does not lock onto the bolt and easily works its way loose. 
I sustained a very hard blow to the head and have numerous strained muscles, bruises and scrapes.  Had I not been wearing a helmet I almost certainly would have suffered life threatening injuries.

We contacted the company and they claimed that they hadn't heard of this issue before. However, when looking on their website and on the amazon link we noticed that in one of their marketing photos the light has fallen over (presumably because the bolt loosened)  just like we mentioned with our issue.

productDescription: Homedics Ultrasonic 2 gallon Humidifier sold at Costco up until 2023. I do not have the original box that had the SKU number and UPC code
incidentDescription: We purchased two Homedics ultrasonic humidifiers from Costco this last fall and put both in service in late October. We followed the owners manual and used our tap water which it said you can do. By mid December I was having constant shortness of breath and a very productive cough. My wife experienced only the productive cough but I had one of the units right by my bed in my bedroom at night. Come January 1, 2023 I had to go to the ER, thinking I was having a heart attack with chest pain and difficulty breathing. I was not, and was sent home with instructions to see a cardiologist and a pulmonologist. After those visits I was put on night oxygen, an inhaler, given an EKG, a nuclear stress test, pulmonary function test, sleep study, two week heart monitoring, echocardiogram, and numerous other tests. I had the feeling that I was dying. It continued and on April 4th, 2023 I was again in the ER at the direction of my primary care physician to get a chest CT due to the doctor thinking I was having a pulmonary embolism. In early April I had indoor air quality monitoring done and found the indoor AQI was over 400 and PM2.5 was over 200. Thinking it was from dust we had all our carpets cleaned and no change to the indoor air quality. As the weather became warmer in mid April, we opened windows for the first time since November and the AQI and PM2.5 fell to near zero with the ultrasonic humidifiers off. That night it was cold so we closed the house up again and turned the humidifiers back on, only to see the AQI and PM2.5 climb to oner 100 with just a few hours. Mystery solved. The ultrasonic humidifiers were aerosolizing the minerals in our water to a toxic level indoors even with air filtration purifiers running. The pulmonologist says that my lungs may take up to a year to heal and may never return to what they were before the exposure due to the Homedics ultrasonic humidifiers.

productDescription:
26 cu. ft. French Door Refrigerator with Filtered Ice Maker in Stainless Steel
model RF261BEAESR/AA
incidentDescription: I purchased a Samsung 3-door Refrigerator in April 2020. The unit was within normal working parameters until April 2022. I began noticing ice build up in the vents at the back of the refrigerator section. This build-up did not affect any part or operation of the unit at this time. At the end of April 2022, I noticed my deli drawer at the bottom of the unit was stuck, it wouldn't move. Thanks to a layer of ice that formed, the drawer was going nowhere. I also noticed that food was going bad quicker than it normally would. The temperature from the top shelf reported 55F when the panel read 37F. Each week, I would remove the deli drawer and break out the layer of ice that had accumulated before drying it out. At the end of May 2022, food stored in the unit began to spoil within days of purchasing. A gallon of milk had spoiled within a day. In June of 2022, I had my first repair bill for it for $350. Samsung had scheduled the repair from a company on their authorized lists. Upon arrival, the repair person knew within moments of the issue, as they described this situation as the most common one they face: a faulty temperature sensor. This sensor messages the coolant system telling it if the fridge needs colder or to stand down. This fluctuation from the sensor's failure caused ice build-up that blocks the air vents, which raises the internal temperature. The fix was immediate and had no further issues until March of 2023. The ice build-up was back and I began removing it every two weeks. I reached out to Samsung asking for the repair to a device they replaced less than a year ago, but was told there was no authorized repairfolk in the {REDACTED] area so I would have to schedule my service and then file a claim to see IF the warranty of only the sensor would be covered (but there may be other 'issues' discovered'). At the time, the ice removal was not a huge issue so I did nothing In May of 2023, my food began to spoil within days of purchasing, again. Contacting Samsung, I was told there was now an authorized repair company that could schedule the appointment but I would have to pay $425 upfront to schedule it. I never had to do that with the first repair and this new appointment is essentially fixing the original repair's problem. Furiously, I decided not to continue the conversation with Samsung and attempt alternative routes. I concluded that if the sensor was the simple fix, then I could do it. After days of reviewing several videos and articles on the subject, as this issue with Samsung's units has been going on since 2017, I felt confident enough to screw off a panel, remove the ice build-up, and replace this sensor piece. The operation went text-book well. I was closing up the operation when I had not realized that the final 2 screws were not catching the receiving end for fastening. Realizing I placed the wrong screws in, I began removing the first incorrectly placed screw when a high-pressure burst of gas spewed out around the screw. I had punctured the coil which circulated the refrigerant gas. Unknowing the toxicity of the gas, I closed the unit doors immediately and removed my roommate and myself from my townhouse. After spending a wasteful 20 minutes with Samsung support on ascertaining how toxic this gas was, I discovered that we were in no danger by my research for an MSDS sheet on the gas. My issues are these: how are these products still being produced when they knowingly have continuous errors in their temperature sensors? If they claim they didn't, then their research department should be fired.  [REDACTED] knew that this has been an issue since 2017. The only logical conclusion is that Samsung has designed these units to fail on purpose. FOR EXAMPLE: why is there a vital tube behind a screw hole? Why need two different length screws when you could have designed it only to have one, eliminating the chance a consumer would be confused, [REDACTED] even a repairperson could get confused. I don't think I'm an Einstien-level genius, but as a licensed architect, I understand the purpose and why things are built the way they are. This product was designed to fail. That failure has costed me with lost food, pointless repairs, and poses a hazard to my health. This is not only unprofessional of Samsung but unethical. I am blown away that this has been allowed.

Temperature in the refrigerator is abnormally high. Please check if door is opened or hot foods are in the refrigerator, if this problem has been solved, the message will disappear, if the warning continues, please call a Samsung service center.
Press the ok button for 3 sec

The technician [REDACTED] said the compressor had failed and he would contact Samsung to get a replacement. Once they receive the replacement ( approximately April 11th) he would return to replace the compressor which is V covered under the warranty for 10 years from the date of purchase. On April 11th the repair man [REDACTED] came to make the repair on the refrigerator, in which when replacing the compressor, a dryer also needed to be replaced at which it was told to us came as a gift from [REDACTED] the repair technician. Then on May 15th 2023, the same warning message appeared on my refrigerator, again having to remove and dispose of all unsafe foods due to excessive temperature exposure, I contacted Samsung again, and a new  work order was created again, only the parts they replaced are not covered and I had to repay for the diagnosis of the refrigerator and they used the same company to come back out, and they are saying it’s a leak in the lines, yet the issues are the same.

productDescription: It is a hair crimper with a bright pink plastic outer housing, a black cord, a metal crimping surface, a blue interior plastic settings housing with one button to select multiple temperatures.  It has a non-polarized plug.
productType: Hair Curlers, Curling Irons, Clips & Hairpins (1682)
manufacturer: Jingdong E-Commerce (Trade) Hong Kong Corporation Ltd
brand: C(?)engli (The 'C' is stylized and I'm unsure)
incidentDescription:
I was using a hair crimper I recently purchased.  Instructions were included but aside from the title of the booklet (Operating Instructions) everything was in Chinese. I plugged it in, selected a heat setting, waited for it to heat up and began crimping my hair.
The crimper does not close fully with the force of one hand. I noticed a box on the end of the crimper that seems like it is intended for 2nd hand placement to fully close the crimper.  I gingerly tried this out and my assumption seemed correct.  However, after just a few minutes, the plastic housing on the crimper became too hot and I burned my fingers.  Not serious burns, thankfully, as I was being cautious.   It is worth noting that I had it on the 2nd to lowest setting, so I assume it can get much hotter; and the setting does not turn off when you unplug it.  There is one button that cycles through heat settings, and if you unplug it while it is on the 2nd setting, for instance, if you unplug it and plug it back in it remains ON.

Besides the casing becoming  excessively hot, I noticed that the plug is not polarized, and does not match the appearance of US standard plug prongs in that there are no holes.  I don't think this is a big deal, but noticed it as a warning of low manufacturing quality and lax safety.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

incidentDescription:
On the evening of May 5, 2023, I had started a fire in my Solo Stove which was placed on the pool deck behind my home.   We have approximately 10 fires a year at our home, but converted to the Solo Stove last fall.  My daughter who was 12 came down and was talking to me as she stood next to the fire pit, back to it, to warm herself.  Accidentally, she stepped backwards and made brief contact with the outer metal surface of the Solo Stove.  She received a 2nd degree burn approximately 4-5 inches long down her calf.  
We have had bonfires with our children present nearly all their lives, taught fire safety, and my daughter is more responsible than most.  There was no horseplay going on.  It's concerning to me that such a brief contact with this stove can lead to such a large and severe burn.  I think this product is defective and can lead to more injuries given the heat level and lack of cooling material around the stove.  With other traditional stoves we've never had an issue - they are either of a material that doesn't get extremely hot, have a ring around the circumference, or other safety mechanism.  Solo has released a surround now for its stoves, costing about as much as the entire stove itself.  It appears the company is attempting to profit from its inherent design defect.

productDescription: The product is a hair styling tool that combines a round hair brush and electric blow dryer.
incidentDescription:
I have an Amika hair blow dryer brush that I purchased directly from Amika in December 2020. While using the product last week, the dryer’s handle got very hot and I could smell a strong burning odor, then the dryer started to smoke.

The product is a combination hair dryer and round brush. My hair was tightly wrapped around the brush end of the dryer when the incident occurred, so I couldn’t just drop it. While I was unwrapping my hair from the brush, the handle got almost too hot to hold and the dryer started smoking. I immediately unplugged the dryer from the wall outlet.

I have not been able to reach anyone at Amika by phone, but did receive an email stating that they would like a photo or video of the entire dryer and a closeup photo of the dryer’s date code tag.

Yesterday, my husband (an engineer) took photos of the dryer and made a short video of the dryer in operation. He set the dryer on a non-flammable surface near our kitchen exhaust fan. He attached a digital thermometer to the dryer’s handle to record its temperature. The dryer started to smoke about a minute after turn-on and burst into flame 15 seconds later. He then immediately shut off the dryer and extinguished the flames.

The thermometer reading was 70 degrees (F) before turn-on, 96 degrees when the dryer burst into flame, and continued to rise for several minutes after the dryer was turned off. The peak temperature was 144 degrees.

The video that my husband recorded includes the entire test, from turn-on to shutoff.

After watching the video I realized that I had narrowly avoided serious injury during last week’s incident. The dryer was probably seconds away from bursting into flame while I was trying to disentangle it from my hair.

During a visit to the hair salon yesterday, my stylist said that the section of hair that was wrapped around the Amika dryer brush during the incident was badly heat-damaged.

Amazon product information (where we purchased the heater) shows ASIN B0BFBX1J3J.
There is no model number information on the outside of the heater.  If necessary, I can take it apart and look inside, but only if you truly need.
There is a sticker on the bottom of the heater with a bar code and the numbers "EC-99830-2201890611."  I believe this may break down as model EC-99830 and serial number 2201890611.
incidentDescription: We purchased a Mr. Heater Vent Free 30,000 BTU Radiant Propane Heater (bundle with fan blower) in November 2022.  Twice it has had a propane buildup which cause a flare-up where it basically went "whoomph" and blew a ball of flame 2 to 3 feet out of the front of the unit.  This only occurred when the thermostat was set to under their 2 setting (settings range from 1 to 5).  This is used in our living room as a secondary heat source.  Also note that in our correspondence with Enerco Group (the manufacturer), they state the cause was setting the thermostat to settings that were not whole numbers (i.e. setting the thermostat exactly on 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5).  Nothing in the owners or operators manual indicates the thermostat must only be set on whole numbers.  In our correspondence, Enerco states that even though they know this dangerous flare-up problem can be caused when the thermostat is not left exactly on a whole number setting, they have no plans to replace the thermostat with one that simply clicks into place on the whole numbers.  Enerco states they are changing their owners manual to indicate the thermostat should be set on whole numbers only, but, again, they are still going to leave the thermostat that allows unsafe settings.  This should be a simple hardware fix - replace the thermostat with one that does not cause an explosion of flame.  Enerco refuses.  No one was injured during the times this occurred, but the possibility is very high if someone had been in the wrong place at the wrong time.  I will attach copies of all email correspondence with Enerco representatives, both their emails and mine.

productDescription: RYOBI 40V HP Brushless Whisper Series 21 in. Single-Stage Cordless Battery Snow Blower
incidentDescription:
The second time I used a new RYOBI 40V HP Brushless Whisper Series 21 in. Single-Stage Cordless Battery Snow Blower it would not turn off.
I had been using the snow blower for a while. It then started struggling to blow snow. I released the bail switch and the machine continued to run. Actuations of the switch would not get it to stop. I had to remove both batteries from the machine to get it to stop.

I inserted the batteries again and I was able to switch the machine on and off a few times. The safety issue occurred again a few times, it intermittently fails to switch off. The fact that removing and then restoring the power source can restore the correct functionality indicates it is a software/sensor issue and not a hardware problem with the switch. It also suggests that the safety switch is NOT in series with the power source and they are using the switch as a sensor input to some software to turn the motor on and off.

I have contacted their technical support. I expected that the serious nature of the safety issue, would trigger a rapid response and investigation but they suggested I take it to a repair center (Home Depot). Home Depot no longer does repairs for Ryobi and there is no repair center near me. They have not made any effort to inspect the machine to determine the cause of the safety issue.  Twin 40V batteries produce a lot of power and having such a machine not switch off could cause some serious injuries.

productDescription: Nespresso Nomad travel mugs, all sizes with the pop top lid (which all have). My products are: 2 in 18 oz., and 1 in 13.5 oz sizes.
incidentDescription:
I am writing regarding extensive mold lurking in the lids of Nespresso's Nomad Travel Mugs. 

My husband and I have three Nomad mugs, two 18 oz., and one 13.5 oz. All three mugs have pop down tops with a center that depresses allowing for 360 degree drinking. We've had health annoyances and coffee that would curdle for one of us, but not the other on some days. When the coffee curdled again we decided to look into the lids. Prior to this, we have followed the directions that require only that the product is  soaked if not washed immediately, and if placed in the dishwasher that the lid is washed in the "open" position so water can flow through the cup. When we discovered mold in all three cups, I first pressure washed two of the three cups (cups A and B in the images) with the sink faucet before soaking in water and vinegar, then disassembling disassembling the lid as much as can be done (with the inner "pop" lid and outer spring removed, but the innermost spring locked inside). The third lid (lid C) was disassembled and soaked without any pressure washing, so the image shows even more of the mold and coffee left hiding in what appeared to be a "clean" mug.

Once soaked in vinegar and water overnight, I tried pressure washing each of the inner springs in the lids again and used bottle top brushes of different sizes and stiffness to try to clean the inner springs of the visible remnants within them. The photo of the inner springs is attempting to show you that there are still coffee and mold remnants stuck below that spring. Even the parts of the inner spring that look clean can be lifted and then scraped below with a toothpick to remove more residue. 

Which leads me to this:  these lids pose a serious health risk to consumers; they must be recalled.  The instructions do not tell consumers how to even clean as far as I was able to; they were disassembled by force and without direction. But more importantly, they ultimately cannot be FULLY disassembled. That inner ring that cannot be removed, that is tucked into the center ring, that every ounce of beverage passes through, harbors mold. These lids look this way after following the rinsing and dishwashing instructions as far as any reasonable consumer could be expected to do. 

I contacted Nespresso which then had a supervisor contact me. I was provided the first option of an identical replacement mug, an alternative mug, and then a refund. I was directed to email photos to an email address that, when attempted, blocks all incoming messages despite many attempts ([REDACTED]). 

I appreciated the money back, but I do not feel made whole. Unsuspecting consumers need to know of the incredible health hazard that lurks in their Nespresso Nomad travel mugs.

productDescription: Unagi Model One E500 electric scooter
incidentDescription: I was riding an Unagi Model One scooter at around 8mph, a car came out of a blind driveway about 30ft in front of me (plenty of time to stop). I engaged the brakes on the scooter, but nothing happened, forcing me to jump off the scooter to avoid the car,  badly injuring my knee and elbow as I landed on the pavement. On further investigation I realized that the scooter's electric regeneration-only braking is fatally flawed -- it doesn't engage immediately when the paddle is pressed, instead taking a critical moment or two to ramp up. This makes it essentially useless for emergency braking, and extremely dangerous. Almost all other scooters on the market have physical brakes -- drum or hydraulic. Note that the Unagi does have a "fender" brake, where you can press the fender into the rear wheel for additional braking, but this is useless in an emergency scenario since you can't shift your foot to the fender mid stop.

incidentDescription:
GE - General Electric;  Zoneline In-Wall Heat Pump Heater / Air-Conditioning Unit.  
MODEL #: AZ55H09DABM1
SERIAL #:  TF 650149 

Currently, there's an Open recall on limited Serial Numbers of the GE Zoneline HVAC Units listed on the following link's recall notice.       
https://www.cpsc.gov/Recalls/2016/GE-Recalls-GE-Air-Conditioning-and-Heating-Units

Our same exact Model Name / SAME EXACT BODY STYLE  Zoneline unit drips water  - in exactly the same electrical component AREAS mentioned in the Recall - and also above where the Electrical Plugs + Cords are located.   
HOWEVER, our particular Serial Number is NOT included in the Recall.  
I called GE's Recall Assistance Line ( 866-723-2697 ) and  GE has advised that they will not do a courtesy repair of the unit similar to the repairs being done on the Recalled Units.  

That being said, I do believe very strongly that the Existing Recall should be expanded to cover similar units.   
Such an expansion could affect tens of thousands of similar GE Zoneline HVAC Units.  
And it's curious as to how and why our unit / similar units are not included in the recall.  

Also noteworthy, is that our unit doesn't appear to have an "indoor-outdoor air vent" option.  Our unit heats and cools INDOOR AIR ONLY.   So there isn't an option to fix the problem by way of shutting a vent or a valve.  

ALSO NOTEWORTHY is how the water pools and puddles indoors, outside the view of most consumers.  
And also where a small child, pet, or adult could come into contact with the water and/or become electrocuted by the water pooling and puddling around higher-than-standard voltage plugs. 
 If the same unit leaked onto carpeting, there could be the creation of mold damage (we don't have carpeting in this area).  
The unit can and does leak into the surrounding wall right around where the electrical components are located.  
(When I noticed it in Summer 2022, I placed a large pan under where the dripping occurred.  But there's clearly signs of long term water dripping, out of view of the home's Senior Citizen Age Occupant - Owners.)   

GE Rep "[REDACTED]" advised that they won't perform a courtesy repair or modification to our unit.  She was also cagey about her location in the US, extension number, etc.  (but given her dialect, I surmised that she COULD be in the Dakotas. )

productDescription: Oster TSSTTVCG02 Oster 6 Slice Convection Toaster Oven with Integrated Broil Rack, Brushed Stainless Steel
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription: Oster TSSTTVCG02 Oster 6 Slice Convection Toaster Oven with Integrated Broil Rack, Brushed Stainless Steel. The oven's mechanical timer dial (lower right knob) is turned clockwise/ right to set for up to 60 minutes, ticking as it turns back to zero/Off position. Or the dial can be turned counter-clockwise/left to "Stay On". The timer has failed so that the dial keeps turning counter clockwise from any  set time, right past zero/off, in to the "Stay On" position.  If manually turned counterclockwise to Off, it no longer stays there and remains off, instead begins to turn toward the "Stay On" setting. Like other posters with similar models, I first thought this was my error until I observed and tested.  The oven can stay on past set time, indefinitely, and can turn itself on without residents knowing about it. The indicator light is off unless heating to set temperature, so user may not know the oven is not actually off.  This is a fire and smoke hazard in addition to ruining food and wasting electricity. In prior reports for similar models the maker has stated this is not a defect or hazardous. It clearly is a design flaw and an untended hot countertop oven is hazardous. The oven should have a failsafe against the timer dial moving from or past the Off position on it's own.

productDescription: Anker 535 Power Bank (power core 20K) with PD 30W Max Output, Power IQ
incidentDescription: As a Fire Chief and Fire Investigator, firefighters responded to a fire in a private, single-family residence for a reported structure fire. Upon the extinguishment, the undersigned conducted an origin and cause investigation for this fire loss. During the course of the investigation found that the cause of the fire was an Anker 535 Power Bank (power core 20K) with PD 30W Max Output, Power IQ. The power bank was not being charged nor charging any other device at the time of the fire any was found on the floor in the bedroom. It was obvious that the device experienced "thermal runaway" and internally exploded (photographs of the device are available by the undersigned). The device was left at the scene so private insurance company could see the cause of the fire. The homeowner reported hearing a "sizzling" noise and shortly thereafter a "boom". The structure filled with smoke and the device ignited Class A combustible materials to burn. No injuries to any civilian or firefighter. The homeowner purchased the device on December 7, 2002.

incidentDescription:
I purchased a GEVI Model : Nugget Ice Maker 1102
I purchased a GEVI model GIMN 1102 Ice maker 7/5/2022 when my [REDACTED] was acting up (because I didn’t properly maintain it- my fault)… I started the GEVI on 1/27/2023… I did as the instruction manual stated & ran the cleaning cycle before making ice- this caused some kind of malfunction and the unit kept telling me to add water when the reservoir was full. It was night time & I was too frustrated to call customer service so I [REDACTED] & saw this was a common issue that some resolved by removing the filter- which I did & it allowed ice to be made… 
on 2/27/2023, the unit started making an awful howling sound… I [REDACTED] & found that if you unplug the machine & plug it back in, the sound will stop… I then registered the machine so it could be under warranty if the issue came back.  It did a few weeks later and I reached out to GEVI for direction… they recommended that I clean the unit & gave me the link to what they recommended- they said if that didn’t resolve the issue, they would replace the unit or give me a refund.  I ordered the cleaner immediately.  Two days later a new sound woke me and when I checked the machine, there was little ice and a shiny metal blade in the ice!  GEVI apologized and gave me an immediate refund.  I found a similar blade in my water cup I had used the night before- thank God I did finish my water! I would have been seriously injured!
When I went back through Amazon reviews, I saw several people had the same thing happen & noted it in their reviews going back 6+ months!!! GEVI followed up with me to confirm the refund was processed, no need to send the machine back & apologized again for what happened.  I asked if they planned on doing a recall because it’s dangerous to still sell this item… they replied, “With regards to your concerns, please be advised that the GIMN-1102 ice makers have been upgraded since it has aroused great attention to whole GEVI team and at the same time, we are running a re-call project to take back defective ice makers and have them replaced with updated ones.”

I’ve notified Amazon of the issue in the hopes they stop selling this unit.  But when looking on line, it’s available on several different sites 

I forwarded the entire email string to Info@cpsc.gov at [REDACTED] 3/8/2023 & stated I would formally make a record on the official website.  [REDACTED] replied thank you to acknowledge receipt.

GEVI is aware of the safety issue of their ice maker, but continues to sell the dangerous model all over the internet!  And I do not see ANY recall on line at all… I cannot comprehend why they have not sent notifications to all customers that purchased this item telling them of the danger… It appears they are waiting to be put on notice which isn’t right

Update 3/10/2023
I left the following review on Amazon:

DANGEROUS- DO NOT USE!!!

This does make wonderful ice- but it is not worth anyone’s life! READ THE RECENT REVIEWS!! The blade is known to break & end up in the ice tray!!! Customer service was extremely apologetic & gave me an immediate refund
FOR YOUR SAFETY AND THE SAFETY OF THOSE WHO WILL USE THIS MACHINE, WAIT UNTIL THEY FIX THIS DANGEROUS ISSUE!!!!!!


I received an email a little bit ago from GEVI asking that I revise my review ??:
Dear [REDACTED],

Thank you for bringing your issue with our ice maker to GEVI attention and hope our solution and customer service has met your satisfaction. 


As for the concern you mentioned in the review, we are confident to share with you that we have had the blade issue fixed and there will be no further incident like this. We have also set up a re-call project to retrieve the ice makers with potential hazard and replaced them with the upgraded ones for their owners.


To grow to a reliable brand, we are committed to 100% satisfaction with our products and services for GEVI customers and we thank you very much for your voice.

Meanwhile, to help others understand that we have had the blade issue technically resolved, we'd be highly appreciative if you could take a few minutes to update your review via following link.
[REDACTED]
Contact Us – Amazon Customer Service
Looking for assistance from customer support representatives over the phone? Please call 1-888-280-4331 if you have any questions.
www.amazon.com
?
Should you have further questions, please feel free to let me know.
Kind regards,
[REDACTED]
GEVI Customer Service


I DO NOT PLAN ON UPDATING MY REVIEW - there is a review dated 7/17/2022 with photos stating they’re metal parts in the bin!  I believe the manufacturer should have recalled the machine at that time- or sometime after the dozens of similar reviews were posted!  I would not have bought this machine & almost swallowed part of a blade if they had taken the appropriate action!

GEVI states they have “have had the blade issue technically resolved”- NO! People bought the ice maker even after they were put on notice the blade broke into the receptacle.  Every person that bought this ice maker model needs to be put on notice of the potential danger & GEVI needs to remove it completely from their sale inventory. They state they corrected the blade issue with an upgraded model… I believe they should prove that to CPSC & then only offer THAT model for sale 


I was not physically injured - thank God I fell asleep before I finished chewing my ice I had in my water cup!!! But I can’t stop thinking every time I drink from my cup that a blade had been in it & could have cut my mouth & digestive tract if I had swallowed ??

Please make GEVI properly recall model GIMN-1102

Thank you

productDescription: Brezza
incidentDescription:
I gave birth to my son on [REDACTED]. His birth weight was 9.1lbs. We came home from the hospital a few days later on Sunday 2/12/2023. The days between birth and going home, I breastfed my son. On Sunday 2/12/2023, the day we arrived home, I began using the Brezza to formula feed every 2-3 hours in tandem with breast feeding and pumping. We began exclusively using the Brezza on Sunday 2/19/2023 and stopped breastfeeding. While using the Brezza, my son's weight either decreased or was slow to regain to his original birth weight each time we measured his weight. On Friday 2/24/2023, our pediatrician advised us to manually scoop the formula and increase the formula amount (increase the ratio of formula to water). That day, we measured out the dosage the Brezza was dispensing and learned it was less than half of the amount of powder recommended on the back of the formula package. After manually measuring and increasing the powder amount, he gained over 8oz in 48 hours putting him back on track to regain his original birth weight.

Pediatrician visits:
Monday 2/13/23 = 8.24lbs * First visit (routine wellness)
Wednesday 2/15/23 = 8.13lbs Weight check
Friday 2/17/23 = 8.22lbs Weight check
Friday 2/24/23 = 8.24lbs *2 Week visit (routine wellness) stopped Brezza, began manually scooping formula
Monday 2/27/23 = 8.78lbs Weight check

The injuries that happened are to be determined. At the 2 week check up, my son was supposed to regain all the weight lost and return to his original birth weight. Because of the Brezza dosage error, he did not. During the time we were using the Brezza, he slept poorly, and had unrest during his wake hours.

productDescription: Cuisinart "CGC-4PC5 4-Cup Mini-Prep Plus" food processor. The base/motor housing is silver-tone. Dimensions approximately 10"H x 5" W x 7" D.
incidentDescription:
This is a follow-up to an email I sent to Cuisinart, the manufacturer of the product. While I copied CPSC in that email, I'm also following up by submitting this form. This is what I sent them/you:

>>Having just spoken with someone from your Customer Service phone line, I have been redirected to your departments. This might also require involvement from your Legal Department.

I have a Cuisinart M/N CGC-4PC5 “Mini-Prep Plus Food Chopper”, S/N 3117Y, purchased at the local Costco back on 11/13/17. We use this device infrequently, for smaller food prep jobs, as we also have one of the larger Cuisinart food processors. So while it is 5 years old, it’s also received light use since it was acquired.

Yesterday, after my wife used the device to chop up an onion, I was cleaning it and noticed cracks in the “SmartPower” blade near where one of the cutters is mounted in its plastic housing. These cracks are now large enough to see with the naked eye. I caught it in time, but was concerned enough to take some photos after I finished washing and drying it, and they are attached below.

One of your customer service people tried telling my wife (paraphrasing) that if “you’re not comfortable using the product, stop using it. If you want to buy a replacement blade, it will cost $27. But the device is five years old and out of warranty.” When I called in a couple of hours later, I was told roughly the same thing and advised to write to these email boxes.

I want to make the point that THIS IS A SAFETY ISSUE. And Cuisinart has addressed a very similar safety issue with some of its older, larger food processors (in 2013 and 2016), involving the Consumer Product Safety Commission, and possibly product liability lawsuits that resulted in a mass recall of those cutter blades. I know, because we ourselves had to suspend use of our food processor device until Cuisinart could replace that blade assembly.

I’m not the kind of engineer that designs products such as food processors, but I am an engineer, and I can recognize a potential safety hazard like this when I spot it, wherein a device spinning a blade assembly at multiple hundreds of RPMs, and having said blade assembly suddenly and catastrophically fail, could see the blade slice through the plastic canister, potentially injuring (or even killing) the operator.

Again, look closely at the photos, which were taken (as the metadata will verify) yesterday evening, 2/02/23. One picture is worth a thousand lawsuits. And I’m forwarding six of them (photos, not lawsuits).

This email necessitates a response from someone high enough in your organization to recognize the seriousness of the situation. In case I haven’t made it clear enough, let me restate it bluntly: this is a ticking time bomb for you and for however many of your customers still own and use this blade assembly, regardless of the particular device models it came with. This should not be a situation where Cuisinart circles the wagons and stonewalls until someone – or their child – loses a limb or severs an artery.

I await your timely response. Thank you.

incidentDescription: I purchased a Bleame crystal hair eraser online a few months ago. The website says it works with gentle pressure. I tried it out, and couldn't get it to work using gentle pressure, so I set it aside. A couple weeks ago, I decided to try it again, this time using more pressure. I was able to get it to remove hair using more pressure, I tried various techniques (on dry skin, wet skin,  and with shaving cream) as directed on the package, and I ended up with really bad skin irritation on my right arm. I also got milder skin irritation and rash on my left arm and inner thigh. The skin irritation occurred when I used the product as directed on their package and website, I documented my rash. I did not get skin burns from using the product on my lower legs, but I did get burns on my arms and inner thigh. I did some looking around online and discovered that I am not the only person who has had skin irritation/friction burns from this product and similar products. Severe skin irritation is a common complaint with people who use these crystal hair erasers. The "crystal" is actually etched glass similar to a glass nail file and it's like sandpapering your skin, especially when used on wet skin, which they recommend. The Bleame company does not warn people of the high potential for skin irritation with their product and actually touts their product as 100% pain free (I have already filed a complaint with the FTC concerning their deceptive business practices).

Later in the evening - I was getting ready to go out and again I plugged in my hair dryer (I use it to heat up my eyelash curler) and this time when I went to unplug it - I squatted down so that I didn't lean over and pull the plug out.  Next thing I know - i was on my back again and I had blacked out for a few seconds.  My 85-year old mother and my sister both heard me fall on the floor....at that time - I still didn't know what happened.  Then I realized that I had blacked out and fallen both times that day at the exact same time that I was unplugging that hairdryer.  I had an electrician come out on January 30th and he said there wasn't anything wrong with the actual outlet and it had to be the hairdryer plug that was the problem.  I have a black eye from the fall (I don't know if the black eye is from me pulling the plug out and possibly hitting myself in the eye when I got electrocuted or I don't know if the electrical current went in through my eye.  All I know is that it was a scary situation and I am worried about my heart.  I already have a rapid heart beat (supraventricular tachycardia) and I am lucky that I didn't actually die from being shocked twice in one day.
