productDescription: Lawnmower Flex Bolt Battery charger and Battery
incidentDescription:
Consumer is reporting that the garage is located behind home, detached. Half is finished space. They keep washing machine, dryers and dog cages there. Husband used lawnmower during the day and used charger to charge battery overnight. The charger was placed on top of the washer. Consumer stated that they were getting ready to sleep for the night. Later that night, the husband went to the garage to let the dogs out for the night and when he opened the door lots of smoke came out. He immediately called for help from inside the home and they all began to drag the dog cages out of the garage. The consumer owned a total of three dogs, two were immobilized and one passed away during this incident. The fire department determined that the cause of this incident was something exploding on top of the washing machine as it had a big explosion hole. This is how the fire department related that the battery charger caused this explosion and incident. Consumer had to take both surviving dogs to the vet. Both are in severe conditions and the cost of keeping them alive is high.
Consumer was able to contact the company on December 20th, 2022, but they did not want to provide any help over the phone, consumer was referred to website report. The second dog succumbed to her injuries on 12/22.

incidentDescription: Fire department on NIH Campus responded to the report of an exploded Samsung A21 battery. Battery model #E8-BA426ABY. Battery was plugged in and charging at the time of the fire. Due to the phone sitting on a non-combustible surface, without and combustible materials around, the fire was contained to the battery/phone.

productDescription:
Its a small box shape air fryer with a stainless steel finish. the bottom is comprised of mostly plastic, and the display unit is touchscreen with white LEDs . 

Bella Pro Series 6.3 QT Air Fryer
Model : AF - 501C
Item : 90110
120V ~ 60 Hz 1700W
incidentDescription:
I was gifted a Bella Pro Series Air fryer for Christmas last year (2021). We have used our unit as normal and as the instructions require. As of 2 weeks ago our Bella air fryer unit caught on fire, from what I believe to be some sort of electrical or mechanical failure. I was using the unit as normal, and about 3 - 5 minutes into it heating up, smoke started pouring from the top of the machine. Where the cord meets the actual unit there was a fire, and the plastic and wires were melting. I grabbed an oven mitt, and a wet towel and had to throw the machine outside, and use a fire extstinguisher. The plastic on the bottom was so hot it was melting and dripping plastic on my kitchen floor. 

I have sent multiple photos and tried to notify Made by Bella / Bella Housewares for about 2 weeks now, only to have my message left for a supervisor who will not call me back. I feel as if some of these machines depending on when they were produced could have some sort malfunction to them. 

Injuries that could have happened - my girlfriend (32 y.o.) and son (1 y.o.) were in the house, and if I had left the room to go do something else the kitchen would have been on fire. 

No injuries were involved.

incidentDescription:
This email was sent on Friday, 12/23/2023 twelve (12) days ago to the Ovente Concerns & Support Department – [REDACTED] Request Number: [REDACTED] confirmations receipt email on Friday, 12/23/2022 2:14 PM PDT. 

If the OVENTE Customer Concerns and Support Department would have had the courtesy to respond to my email, I might not be posting this email. I tried. 

ORIGINAL EMAIL 

Friday, December 23, 2022, 1:30 PDT  

Re: Scalding Incident on Thursday, 12/22/2022 @ approximately 9pm PDT. The leaking hot water – from the Ovente Electric Kettles scalded the top and sides of Left Foot. It was caused by an inadequate top seal, while pouring the 212 degrees Fahrenheit – 100 degrees Celius Rapidly Boiling Hot Water. Instead of pouring through the center spout the boiling water came out from all around the top seal.  

OVENTE Customer Concerns and Support Department T: 1(855) 926-2626 M-F 8AM – 5PM PST Text: +1(213) 955-4545 Emails: Support - support@ovente.com Concerns: csovente.com 

AMAZON Order No.: [REDACTED] Price: $17.37 Date of Purchase: 09/12/2022 Item: Ovente Electric Kettle 1.7 Liter, Cordless Hot Water Bottle, 1100W, with Automatic and Boil Dry Protection, Fast Boiling, BPA Free, Portable Instant Heater for Making Tea and Coffee, Model #: KP72B  

Dear Ovente Customer Service Concern Department:  

I wanted to first email you to determine what type of response you will supply me regarding this profoundly serious matter.  

Scalding Incident on Thursday, 12/22/2022 @ approximately 9pm PDT. As I was pouring the hot water in my hot beverage mug, the leaking hot water – from the Ovente Electric Kettles Model #: KP72B scalded the top and sides of Left Foot.  

It was caused by an inadequate top seal, while pouring the 212 degrees Fahrenheit – 100 degrees Celsius rapidly boiling hot water. Instead of pouring through the center spout the boiling water came out from all around the top seal.  

Luckily for me, I was wearing leather shoes with socks. My left foot was drenched in this 212-degree Fahrenheit – 100-degree Celsius intensely hot water. I had to immediately take off my shoes, as my black cotton socks had absorbed a lot of the water. It was quite a frightening experience, as I live alone. Therefore, I am always extremely careful when cooking or pouring hot water.  

 This “Superficial Epidermal Scalding Burn” was A HAIR’ BREADTH from an immediate trip to the emergency room for second (2nd) or third (3rd) degree burns. Question: Would you reimburse me for any medical costs I might have incurred?  

Please do not inform me that I am the first customer who has ever mentioned this serious design flaw in the Ovente Electric Kettle. One experience and example are quite enough. I will not post an Amazon Review or post a video on my YouTube Account, until I receive some feedback and communication from you.  

 I will wait for your timely and prompt response. I am aware that we are all now in the activities which surround Christmas through New Year’s Eve. I still expect a timely response. I will gladly send you a video of how the Ovente Electric Kettle responds to pouring.  
 Your professionalism, solution-oriented approach, and support to my scalding experience and Ovente Electric Kettle spout and top seal pouring concerns will determine what my next steps will be: 

Consumer Product Safety Commission – USA GOV, Address: 4330 East West Highway, Bethesda, MD, 20814 T: 1(301) 504-7923 M-F 8AM – 5:30 PM ET, Toll Free: 1(800) 638-2772, Email – Website: https://www.usa.gov/consumer-complaints  

Thank you for reading this email. If you have questions or need clarification, please contact me.

Gray color
Lithium-Ion battery

incidentDescription:
My daughter received a Hover-1 Ranger Hoverboard for Christmas. We plugged it in to charge it for a few hours and then unplugged it, per the operation manual. My daughter rode it around for a bit and then turned it off, leaving it unplugged. 

We left the house and after a bout 2 hours, my husband got an alert that our smoke detectors were going off at our house. I called my parents to go check on our house because we were 20 minutes away. 

They entered our house and could immediately see smoke and smell the electrical burning. They found the hoverboard smoking and my dad pushed it out the door with his feet. Within moments it burst into flames. 

Thankfully no injuries occurred and our house is ok, just has a terrible electrical burn smell. We are attempting to clean our carpets, walls and coats that were nearby that all took the brunt of the smoke. 

If my parents had gotten to our house even 2 minutes later, our house would have caught fire. This could have been catastrophic. We could have lost our house and our 3 cats.

productDescription: The product was a rechargeable battery pack and it's charger...
incidentDescription: Our Fire Dept responded to a report of a fire in a lunchroom of a local bank.  On arrival, we found a small object burning on top of a microwave oven in a break room.  We removed the object and upon further examination of it, it was determined to be a rechargeable Li-On battery pack and it's charger.  The unit was left charging by the maintenance staff from use the previous night.  This was explained later to be a routine process for the last few years, since the COVID pandemic began.  There were no injuries and despite being told to leave the battery outside for the night and for additional follow-up the next day, the battery and it's charger were discarded by the maintenance staff.  Fortunately, a few photos were taken of the affected unit prior to our leaving the scene.

incidentDescription: I purchased From Lowes in Nov. 2021 a Samsung Jet 70 Pet Cordless Stick Vacuum (Convertible to Handheld). Regardless of the fact that the vacuum failed in an unsafe manner, and was covered under the 10 year written motor warranty sold to me by Lowes for the Samsung vacuum.  Samsung has a long history of "Bait and Switch," tactics covering their unsafe products. Plus: Lowes: which by selling these devices, is Samsung's legal agent. Lowe's is fully responsible for the safe non-defect manufacture of every product they sell. Both, should be heavily fined, Samsung's vacuum's should be recalled, and safety notifications should be sent to all of Samsung's dealers and distributors. Notifying them of this dangerous product, and reminding them of their legal responsibility to not sell defective or unsafe products.

productDescription:
I bought 3 Dollar Tree "Selfie Ring Light" that say "rechargeable using micro usb" but also use 2 AAA batteries.
When trying it out without the AAA batteries the light didn't come on, so I plugged it into a USB power bank and got a faint red glow, but it didn't seem to charge. 
After opening the product there is no internal rechargeable battery, and after installing non rechargeable batteries the light works, but when plugging it into the power bank the red charging light glows much brighter, meaning that it is trying to charge non rechargeable batteries.
Also the back of the package is confusing because it says "EXternal 2pcs AA battery, but you can not charger with AA battery ; (b) can be use rechargeable batteries;"
So they should say AAA not AA and that you need rechargeable batteries for it, normal batteries might leak or explode when charged.
I didn't let it charge them to see if they would leak or get hot but I imagine they will.
At best it's a confusing package that makes you think it's rechargeable out of the box, not that you have to install rechargeable batteries for it.

incidentDescription:
Product was an Echo Dot Gen 1 that I had been using in my guest bedroom for quite some time. I just happened to be in an area I could see into the room, thank god as this room isn't used much, and I noticed the Echo power bank was smoking while plugged directly into a wall outlet. I quickly unplugged the Echo and found that not only did the Echo produce enough heat to actually burn my outlet and turn it black but the power bank itself began melting. This product, as noted by Amazon, is intended to stay plugged in and always on. It was not "in-use" at the time other than being plugged into the wall.  

Had I not been in the room this malfunctioning power bank could have burned down my entire house, and taken the lives of everyone in this house and all our belongings with it.

To put in perspective the danger at play here let’s take a look at the Amazon safety and compliance standards where it says the echo dot gen 1 operating temperature is between 32°-95° F. [REDACTED] has informed me that plastic melts at anywhere between 175°-350° F.

incidentDescription:
Bradley XL smoker ignited and caught on fire.  This first occurred in 2019 while smoking meat.  The company explained to me that it was a user error related to keeping water in the bowl.  They agreed to sell me a replacement smoker at a discounted price since the original unit was destroyed by the fire.  This year I was using the appliance, being extra diligent about the water bowl, and despite close monitoring and following instructions, the unit ignited again!  Thankfully in both cases, I was able to quickly unplug the unit and move it away from my house.  If not properly attended, it could have burned my home down and caused significant injuries.  

In the first case the manufacturer explained it was due to a lack of water, but the circumstances were nearly the same. After doing several searches online, I can see that I am not alone in my experience with their smoker. This is clearly a design flaw and puts consumers at risk. This unit is not safe and presents a hazard to all that choose to use it. I have never heard of or personally experienced any other smoker with similar hazards.  

I contacted the manufacturer, explained the circumstances and they are unwilling to refund the money I paid for the second unit that ignited and caught fire.  I am reaching out for your help to conduct an investigation of this product in an effort to address a defective and unsafe product and avoid others from putting themselves and their families at risk.

incidentDescription: There is a potential deadly issue with the plastic grill burner knobs on the Weber Summit Grill . productDescription: Future Motion OneWheel+
incidentDescription: I've owned four models of OneWheel and have ridden them since the v1 came out.  I have lots of experience with pushback and know how to ride my OneWheels.  I can confidently state that the two times I experienced being "dropped" were not my pushing through pushback.  I alerted FutureMotion when it happend and they denied any issue with the board.  It is the only of the 4 boards I've had this issue with and I know it was not my riding.  One time I had just started off, hadn't even made it 10' and wasn't anywhere near the speeds where pushback would occur, I started going and after ~8' it just dropped the nose and I was on the ground.  The other time I was riding along the levy by the river and going under a bridge, there was  no pushback, the board just stopped.  I have let FutureMotion know when seeing class action suits that I strongly believe they should look deeper at a malfunction in their boards and not write off this issue but they continue to deny it.  I love the OneWheels and completely agree it is a risky sport and one should always wear protection.  I am also convinced that some of the boards are defective and can randomly stop.  Mine was a OneWheel+ model, but I'm sure 9x% of the Plus model and all OneWheel models are probably fully functional, but there is a percentage that are not.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription: oneWheel Pint, by future motion. Purchased in 2020.
incidentDescription:
I recently fractured my wrist after my oneWheel pint stopped short, without providing pushback while riding ~15mph on packed sand. The board’s battery was just under ~40% at the time, with just under than 2000 miles ridden so far. The stop / motor shutoff was so abrupt that I could not run it out. I caught my fall with my face and hand, and I now face the next 2 months with my dominant hand in a cast with a fractured scaphoid in my right wrist. 

Because the app does not provide ride diagnostic information about pushbacks that were triggered, I’m unable to determine why the board stopped, although I assume it is because of a reason that should have triggered pushback.

I wanted to report this incident because I don't think the oneWheel provides enough details in app to prevent or diagnose this kind of shutoff. I understand how the board is supposed to work, but if the single safety feature meant to prevent over-exerting the board is not triggered or goes unnoticed, a fall is almost guaranteed. I would consider myself an experienced rider.

incidentDescription:
I was riding my Onewheel on a walking trail when I was ejected, and was transported via ambulance to the ER as I took major damage to my head including vision loss in my left eye. I was wearing a skateboarding helmet, and being intentionally cautious to not push limits as I was still rather new to the sport with only 87 miles ridden. 

I have no memory of the accident itself. I took a picture of the Onewheel about 20 minutes prior to the accident, and afterwards, had returned to the walking trail I had already traversed on the Onewheel. 

I was riding on a flat, paved path away from car traffic. I didn’t observe any significant terrain issues, bumps, edges, or other obstacles which would have posed a problem for the Onewheel. I was being sure not to push the limits, and was familiar with “pushback” the device generates when it is operating past its limits. 

While I do not believe I would have ignored that feedback, I have amnesia of the accident itself. I remember being on a country road, safely getting off the Onewheel, and taking a picture at 5:05 PM of the Onewheel as I was enjoying my ride. My memory ends after getting back on, and riding back towards the walking trail. Between 5:22 and 5:24, I took 4 photos showing my head damaged and covered in blood. I have zero memory of taking these pictures, and not sure exactly when or where the accident happened. Metadata of those photos shows the exact location of the walking trail where they were taken. 

I was transported by ambulance to the local ER. My memory resumes in the back of the ambulance, informing the paramedics that I couldn’t see out of my left eye. They claim I had lost consciousness at some point, but didn’t know details of how my accident was reported. 
 I don’t know a detailed timeline due to memory loss. 

The ER informed me I had 4 fractures to my left orbital/sinus, and Traumatic Optic Neuropathy (TON). I was transferred to another hospital at about 2 AM to see specialists. Multiple ophthalmologist have confirmed that this damage is likely to be permanent, and I will never regain vision in my left eye. 

The only thing that really makes sense is despite my caution, I somehow experienced a “nosedive”, which Onewheel claims only happens after dramatically ignoring pushback functions. There are no other warnings or indicators thar you’re about to nosedive. I weigh 230 pounds which is within the operating limits the manufacturer reports. The app also documents I have never gone above 16 MPH in the 87 miles it’s logged. Its documented speed limit is 18 MPH.

productDescription:
The full product title is : APOKE 3 in 1 Hair Dryer Brush & Straightener Brush, Professional 1200W Powerful Ceramic Tourmaline Ionic Hot Air Brush, 3 Heat/2 Speed Settings One Step Hair Dryer and Styler for All Hair Types

It is dark grey and pink. It looks like a paddle brush, but it has air intakes and a rotating pink dial near the bottom (low, high, cool) indicating it's a dryer. It's 13in long and 2.8in wide.

Manufacturer's Address:

incidentDescription:
I'm writing regarding the APOKE 3 in 1 Hair Dryer Brush & Straightener Brush on Amazon at [REDACTED].

This product is a fire/burn hazard and claims UL certification when I don't believe it's actually certified. I use this product to blow dry and straighten my hair at the same time (reduces frizziness). I have not experienced any fire or injuries.

I am copy/pasting my [REDACTED] below.
---
Lot of twists and turns here, so bear with me!

Original review: Great product, I wish a reliable company made it. Used it twice, then I kept hearing a staticky sound. I believe it has a short in it. I was already on the fence because this is an unknown brand and there is NO thingy on the end of the cord. The sound only happens when I plug it in, so in the trash it goes.

UPDATE: I was sent a replacement...which is clearly used. It was not in the wrapper, and the cords did not have twist ties (the cord was sort of wrapped around the barrel). Ew.

UPDATE UPDATE: I was asked by the company if I used the used one, and if so, did it work? Who uses a used beauty product?! That's disgusting, and I told them this. They sent a replacement...which also makes the staticky sound.

UPDATE UPDATE UPDATE: The sparking sound defect is happening in the replacement's replacement. I know what's going on. It's related to something I mentioned in the original review because I thought it very strange when I pulled the dryer out of the box. If you look, you'll notice it, too.

*This hair dryer has no external ALCI.* ALCI stands for Appliance Leakage Circuit Interrupter, and it's what saves lives when an appliance is dropped in water for example. It's the little box on the plug with the "test" and "reset" buttons! It senses a problem with the circuit - moisture, a fault in the product, or a fault with the outlet - and shuts off the product. This dryer does not have the UL symbol because UL requires *all* hair dryers to have an ALCI to obtain certification.

This is why the dryer makes the staticky/sparking sound (like static electricity discharging) or just stops working. It has a fault, and when it recognizes it and shuts off, you can't push the little button and reset it yourself. On functional versions of this product, you may be fine the first 24 power cycles or so, but then you'll hear the staticky sound and a click not long after that. The sound stops after the click. That's the internal mechanism doing its job. Sometimes the product shuts off and does *not* fix itself, but that's somebody else's review.

On my first dryer, there was no click, ever. I'd plug it back in, the sparking sound began again. On the replacement, the click worked correctly. I'd plug it back in, and no sparking sound. This is supposed to happen every time, but it doesn't.

This is why *external* ALCIs are the norm.

This company (or its supplier) tried to cut costs, and they're gonna burn down your house instead. They made a defective product and put in their own defective safeguards to stop you from noticing until you are outside of the 90 day return window. Or they made a product to sell cheaply and intentionally did not include an ALCI so that you would just buy another one when it quickly fails. Either way, very shady and I'm looking into product recalls.

If it makes noise, but you still use it because your budget and options are limited, please be careful and unplug it after EVERY use. Please.

incidentDescription:
On July 17th, we purchased a Ryobi electric mower that came with two 40V battery packs and a charger. We did as told and made sure the batteries were not stored on the charger and kept inside at room temperature and await from moisture or high humidity. After the first use, both batteries would no longer charge. We contacted Ryobi and received two replacement batteries but they didn't ask for the batteries back or suggest there was anything concerning to them going into "sleep mode." Fast forward to October 27th. I happened to walk past our storage room and found it was filled with smoke and smelled horrible. One of the Ryobi batteries had melted a hole in the casing and was spewing smoke/fumes everywhere.  My husband grabbed our woodstove gloves, got the battery out of the house, and called the fire department. 

The fire department came out and checked out the whole house and confirmed the smoke and fumes were from the battery melting a hole. They used equipment to aerate the house so that we could get our pets and ourselves back into the house and advised us to run fans to continue airing out the melted plastic odor. They also recommended that we contact Home Depot and Ryobi, which I did, but Home Depot has yet to return our message and Ryobi passed us off to a safety group who have yet to get in touch.

As both battery packs that came with the mower were defective, the fire department told us to get the batteries into heavy-duty [REDACTED] bags, a box, and wrap that box in a heavy-duty trash bag. They told us where we need to bring them to ensure they're properly recycled and handled from this point on.

We rushed to get our children outside, then the pets outside, then we began ventilating the house. Thankfully my husband was able to use cardboard to extinguish the flames from burning too much in our house, but he is suffering for that now. My family and I are now suffering chemical fire inhalation, we have bloody mucus, eye/skin irritation, gastrointestinal symptoms, respiratory problems, central nervous system dysfunction, and I worry about the long term health effects this will have on our children-- who were in the vicinity when the device exploded. The air inside our house is still reading "poor" and the voc count has been the highest I have ever seen it for almost 7 days now. After calling poison control not many could help in knowing what to do when exposed to something like this, so now we are attempting to keep up with medical care while trying to figure this all out. The company has been hesitant to work with me and has off-put communications. This has been extremely difficult for my family and I; and we do not want this to happen to anyone else. We will never be the same from this.

productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
I bought a Cuisinart Toaster Oven Air fryer from Amazon. This is the letter that I sent to [REDACTED]:
-------------------

Dear [REDACTED],

I bought my nephew the Cuisinart TOA-60 Convection AirFryer Toaster Oven, Premium 1800-Watt Oven with Seven in One Functions and Wide Temperature Range, Large Capacity Air Fryer with 60 minute Timer/Auto Shut Off, Stainless Steel for $225.84 after coupon on January 15, 2022.  It was order number [REDACTED].

At first my nephew absolutely loved it. He is a home cook, and said it was the best gift he ever received. In July 2022 it caught on fire. He thought he did something wrong. He called Cuisinart and they said, Oh well, do not use it, throw it out. It was seven months old.  I checked the reviews before I bought it.  I researched the product all over.  I did not see mention of this issue except for “sometimes it runs hot”. He loved the oven so much he wants to buy a replacement.  I don’t trust the company anymore.

I have since looked at past reviews using your filter for “critical reviews”.  As of today, there are 3,574 reviews claiming that the oven burned their food or caught on fire. We are not the only ones that this happened to. It seems to be a known problem, and Cuisinart is not honoring anything. They wouldn’t replace it.

I am curious if you are aware that you are selling a product with a known defect, and that the company will not honor its warranty?  What bothers me the most is that we bought Cuisinart specifically because it is a good company.  Or at least it used to be.

After all my research, I believe I should be refunded the full cost of the item.  Additionally, I believe that you need to stop selling this particular product.

It seems that within the first year, the temperature controls stop working correctly, and the oven catches on fire.  In the reviews everybody loves it, until it burns up.  Luckily my nephew was in the kitchen when it happened, because the entire back of the unit was on fire.

It’s extremely disappointing that a company like Cuisinart would be selling this item.

I appreciate any help regarding this matter and look forward to hearing from you soon.
-------------------

Amazon fully refunded me. They do not have the item for sale any longer.  I am extremely concerned about these all-in-one toaster air fryers. They seem to run very hot. I have a friends who has one made by [REDACTED] and that one caught fire after 4 years. Somebody mentioned that there's no heat shielding, but honestly I don't know what that means.

I am wondering if there have been many house fires caused by these products. I have been trying to find one that is safe, but if you look at critical reviews, they all seem to have this issue. I cannot believe nobody's got caught in a fire caused from this yet. I think it's only a matter of time.

Thank you.

productDescription: Cyrusher XF650, Affordable Mountain Ebike, Black, 16-inch frame, fat tires
productType: Mountain or All-terrain Bicycles and Accessories (5033)
incidentDescription:
Cyrusher XF650, Affordable Mountain Ebike 
I bought two of these online at the end of May 2022. They came partially pre-assembled but had no instructions to complete the assembly. Once the bikes were completely assembled, as I was able to get the proper regs and instructions for the parts that I did need to assemble, I gave them to my two teenage boys. I have been mountain biking since 1995, never pro, but all over the country, and always did a lot of my own work on my bikes. With these two bikes, next to completely stripping the bikes down to check for any malfunctions or defects, I inspected them as they were, pre-assembled. I took my time and carefully adjusted, tightened, and put the right amount of air in tubes, test rides, etc...so that my boys would be as safe as possible with the functioning of the bikes. After a week of making sure the bikes were ready, the boys rode them that whole day and everything still checked out okay. The next day, on June 1st my son, took off on his bike to go to school in the morning. While riding in the bike lane, at around 25 mph, he said he was suddenly thrown from the bike but had no idea why. He ended up with a broken right knee, broken left wrist, and road rash on his right hand left leg, and left shoulder. He luckily was cleared from trauma 2 level and was discharged from ER that night. It took 6 weeks to get out of the cast and he had to miss going to his camp in VT that he had been going to since he was 8.
When I found my son at the site of the incident, I found the wheel completely flat, mind you I had just checked it the night before, and, the wheel was about 200 yards from where his bike was. No glass or any potholes around. No cars were involved. Nothing that would have caused his wheel to separate from the bike that was on the road or around him to go flat, or to cause a blowout. I have never had a quick-release separate like that in a blowout, but it did appear to be a blowout. When I took the tire and tube off the wheel the rim had this separation in the line where it looked like it was supposed to be connected. Like touching, or supposed to be welded. But it was not touching, and not welded. It just looked wrong and like it was different from the other rims. Next, I noticed that there was a pattern of holes in the tube, and on the inside of the rim were matching sharp bent mental pieces sticking up out of the rim. They were about 3 cm tall and exactly matched the tube holes. The quick release had no prior defects that I had previously Inspected, but now I could see it was looking a bit damaged, but still should not have dislodged. I started thinking was this my fault? No way. I made sure that the quick release was perfect and working. I checked the tire's air and all the parts the night before and I felt very secure with my work. The company Cyrusher tricked me into sending the bikes back saying that they would give me a full refund. As soon as they got the bikes they started giving me the runaround. They said I caused the injury to my son because I put the bike together wrong. Which didn't even make sense because how can they prove I did? Besides, I know I did right, and shame on them for even saying that. I think the quick release was just cheap and didn't hold up to the force that it was put under. They were fat tires and fat rims. They are heavy. So now Cyrusher is trying to trick me into "agreeing" that the incident was my fault for not assembling the bike correctly and that is why my son got hurt. They completely ignored the fact that the inside of the rim had these sharp metal pieces sticking up that were bent out of the rim, in a pattern, that perfectly matched the holes in the inside of the innertube. They should have inspected these rims before sending them out to the consumer population. I should have never trusted this company. They refuse to take responsibility. I am so scared that someone is going to lose their life because of this company. Please, please, please do not buy anything from this company.  They do not care about consumers at all. They wont respond and have kept all of my $3177.00 even though I returned them within my return policy rights. They are selfish and sadly part of this throttle-type mountain ebike that should be illegal. Obviously they are dangerous, but clearly a market that is not to be trusted with companies like Cyrusher and others. They are the only ones who make these types of bikes. [REDACTED] , [REDACTED], and other reputable names will not make this "throttle-type" ebike. They believe in participating in the work to peddle and these are called peddle assist mountain ebikes. I am now just learning. Integrity is not for sale and Cyrusher needs to be stopped.

productDescription: 5.7 QT Air Fryer
incidentDescription:
Something scary just happened with my Instant Pot Vortex air fryer.  I reported this to the manufacturer as well.

I turned my air fryer on and set the time and temperature.  Then I walked away doing other things, waiting for the beep saying it was ready for food.  This is the normal way to operate this air fryer, you preheat it and it beeps when it is ready (and the timer begins.)   Even if you walk away, the oven eventually preheats and the timer starts (and the air fryer turns off when the timer is done.)  There is no way to "keep it running" indefinetely.

So anyway 20 or so minutes later, I realized the beep never happened.  The air fryer still said "on" and was still preheating.  The scary thing is the cord was hot and when I unplugged it, the plug was hot.  Hot enough to blister you. Certainly something that could cause a fire.

It's almost like the heater turned on and just stayed on, but there was nothing inside to take all the heat!  And since it was stuck in pre-heat mode, it kept getting hotter and hotter and hotter.  When I say the plug was hot enough to blister, I'm not kidding.  If I had not found it when I did, there would have been a fire.

productDescription: Black and Decker toaster oven model TO1760SS
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
When I first received this new toaster oven, a replacement for another model which was defective, I top-broiled a piece of bread with pesto to warm it.  All went well.
When I did it again the next morning, the unit exploded, knocking off the handle and scattering glass up to seven feet away.
This happened as I was approaching the toaster oven to remove the heated bread…it was sheer luck that I was not close enough to be splattered with the glass.  It took me an hour to clean up the glass and deposit the unit safely into the original box.  Glass shards were all over my kitchen.

Report Update 6/30/22:
At my request, Spectrum representative “[REDACTED]” with the warranty division of Spectrum Brands, returned my request for a call. One of my questions was to be advised whether there had been other incidents e.g. explosions that blew off the door, shattering glass for six feet. I am awaiting word whether they want to have the damaged unit shipped to them so their Engineering and Quality Control team could examine it.

I was very disturbed to learn that whatever they learn is “proprietary” and would not be released to the public.  So there is no way to know how frequently this happens or has happened. I saw on your website reports of fires, of units being turned off, but not really turning off.  The units were not identified as to model.

I do not think this type of information should be withheld from consumers. I could easily have been badly injured or blinded when the glass door exploded and shattered as I was approaching the unit to retrieve the toast.

This is the second item, manufactured in China (which has special protections), that was defective to the point of causing damage to my wood flooring. The US company did not cover this damage, only a replacement.  It took me six months, working with an attorney, to receive payment to cover replacing my flooring. This was a brand new dehumidifier…the shut-off failed when the bucket became too full.

Consumers need protection!

Report Update 8/22/22:
They have not been responsible in either acknowledging the danger this product put me in—and potentially others, as well. The glass could have hit my face and eyes.
They refused to give information about whether or not this has happened to other customers using the same or other Black & Decker toaster ovens.
They requested I keep the unit until they decided whether or not they wanted to examine it to determine the reason for the explosion.  
There was no reply until I sent the email below (seven weeks later) on August 6th and then they sent only a label.  Nothing that acknowledged their interest or concern.

> June 13, 2022 - I reported the explosion and sent pictures.
> June 28, 2022 - I called to ask about returning the unit…[REDACTED](Engineering and Quality Control) called me and said there had not been enough time for them to know whether they wanted the unit to examine. 
> 
> August 6, 2022 -  I still have the large box in my dining room, waiting to hear back from [REDACTED] whether Engineering and Quality Control wants to figure out why the new toaster oven exploded the second time it was used.
> I am feeling that no one cares.  I was fortunate enough not to have the glass blow up in my face, but it seems that is what will be necessary for it to get attention.

I have contacted the manufacturer in request of a protective cage around the blades, which they do not offer.  This product does not meet basic safety protocol when installed as their provided instructions specify.  This is a product liability that their phone support denies.  I make this submission to you before someone becomes seriously injured.  The unit needs either:  A higher specification for mounting to ceiling, a protective cage, or a integrated clutch / sensor to prevent finger amputation.  A 6’ tall individual has a reach beyond 7’, and most others do as well.  The increased power of this fan makes a minor mishap critically dangerous.

productDescription: Char Broil Patio Bistro LP gas grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription: I recently took possession of a Char Broil Patio Bistro LP gas grill which was subject to recall in 2013 for possible burn hazard due to explosive ignition of gas. At that time, the company offered a replacement ignition-module repair kit, however the recall was not noticed and the repair was never made. My wife and I have experienced explosive ignition of gas from this grill on more than one occasion; fortunately no injuries have yet occurred. In trying to obtain the repair kit now, I have found that the manufacturer does not provide or sell it, and in fact continues to sell what appears to be the original defective/hazardous ignition module, as do other independent parts suppliers. productDescription:
The product consists of a pack of four self-adhesive stickers. The stickers have a metallic gold appearance and are round, about the diameter of a quarter. They are printed with an image of an outline of a human body (in a sort of Vitruvian Man pose). The stickers arrive in packaging consisting of a printed cardstock backer with descriptions of their alleged benefits, and suggested use cases such as sticking to cell phones or appliances. This backer is then enclosed in a plastic wrap envelope, with four of the stickers and backers inside.
The supposed purpose of these products is to protect the user from harm that may allegedly be caused by electromagnetic radiation associated with the 5G cellular telephone network. The package copy includes such phrases as "Negative Ion+Far Infrared," "Caring for Health," and "Preventing Radiation."
Here are some more phrases from the product's listing on Amazon:
"About this item
    Absorb and transfer electromagnetic radiation waves by using special materials
    Reduce mobile phone radiation injury on the human brain of 99.99%
    Applicable for Mobile phone, Laptop, Microwave oven, TV set, Refrigerator, Hair dryer and other electric appliances"
(This supposed use case is dubious--it may be appropriate to call these items a scam, as there is no scientific basis for the statements the product makes, or for the alleged issues the products claim to address).

Stickers like this appear to be sold under a variety of "Generic" brands on Amazon and [REDACTED]. This is just one example of "anti-radiation stickers."
model: EMF&5G Blocker 4 pcs for Mobile Phones 2021 Latest
incidentDescription:
Brief summary: I bought some stickers meant to be placed on a cellular phone on Amazon. They are radioactive, emitting beta radiation detectable with a Geiger counter.

- What happened that made you want to report?
I tested the product with a Geiger counter, and found that it emits harmful beta radiation. I used an antique [REDACTED]  Geiger counter, which is capable of detecting Beta and Gamma radiation. A metal shield can be slid into or out of position to block or allow Beta particles, so that only Gamma rays will be measured.
I checked the instrument against its included calibration test source and found it to agree within the specification written on the sticker. I then sampled the background radiation of my living room with the Beta shield open, and found a background activity basically too low to measure with my meter, well below .1 mR/h.
I then placed the instrument's probe with the Beta shield open against the pack of stickers, still in their packaging. My meter measured in the neighborhood of .1mR/h. I then closed the Beta shield on the probe and repeated the test, which was not measurably higher than background radiation again. I can conclude that the stickers emit Beta radiation, but not Gamma radiation.
- What type of product(s) were being used?
The product is a pack of four stickers that CLAIM to "Reduce mobile phone radiation injury on the human brain." They appear to be one of many examples of products marketed towards people who incorrectly believe that the 5G cell phone network is harmful to human health, and that these stickers will somehow prevent this harm.
The name of the Amazon listing of the product I purchased was:
"EMF&5G Blocker 4 pcs for Mobile Phones 2021 Latest Model – EMF Protection Cell Phone Stickers - 24K Gold EMF Pro Neutralizer - 5G Mobile Phone Protector - Anti-Radiation 7 Shilds for All Devices"
The URL is here: [REDACTED]
- Who was using the product(s)?
I personally examined the product.
- How were the product(s) being used?
I did not remove the product from its packaging, as I was suspicious that it might be radioactive. I saw a video on YouTube where an electronics hobbyist brought a Geiger counter near a pack of similar "anti-5G" stickers purchased from Amazon, and his instrument recorded a non-trivial amount of ionizing radiation being emitted by the stickers. That video can be viewed here: [REDACTED]

The stickers' packaging RECOMMENDS placing them on appliances and personal electronic devices, including cell phones. Given how cell phones are often kept in close proximity to the human body for extended periods (carried in a clothing pocket, charged on or near a bed overnight, held to the ear for calls), if these stickers were placed on a cell phone, the user would likely receive a concentrated dose of beta radiation near where the device is kept.

Additionally, given that stickers often appeal to children, who may place stickers directly on their own bodies or even ingest stickers, these items present a particularly great risk to children. If a child ate one of these stickers, the radioactive materials present in these stickers may settle in their bodies. The EPA warns that the greatest risk from beta radiation emitters is incurred when particles are inhaled or swallowed.

- Were there any injuries that happened or may have happened while using the product?
I did not experience any injury. However, sources of ionizing radiation, especially when kept close to the human body, ingested, or inhaled, present health risks due to the ability for ionizing radiation to damage human DNA. As mentioned, I think children would be especially at risk, as you children may sometimes eat small objects, which would cause radioactive material to come to rest in their bodies and present a long-term risk.
- How did any injuries occur?
N/A but see above.

productDescription: Ninja CE251 Programmable Brewer, with 12-cup Glass Carafe, Black and Stainless Steel Finish
incidentDescription:
Ninja Model CE251 drip coffee maker overheated approx. 45 minutes after brewing; boiled 8+ cups of coffee in glass carafe at time, melted plastic enclosure, significant smoke and smell, unit beeping softly (apparently a thermal alarm of some sort).  Unplugged and moved unit outside in time to prevent fire/flames.

Owner: [REDACTED], male, age 49
Affected product:  Ninja (American Ninja) Model #CE251 69, Serial # R06Q692AA0Z7, 12-cup drip coffeemaker
Other information:  Received as a gift from my wife at Christmas.  Used daily for 5 months before incident.  Unit is clean, in perfect condition, used in same location for entire life.  Unit is plugged into a GFCI-protected outlet that did not trip during the incident.

Sequence of Events:
- Set for delayed brew at 5AM, water filled to 8-cup line
- Coffee brew cycle completed normally at ~5:15am, "STAY WARM" light lit
- Poured 1 large mug (2 cups) at 5:15, replaced carafe
- at 5:50AM heard beeping, went over to check unit.
- unit making cracking sound), approx. 6 cups of remaining coffee inside carafe was boiling.  Removed carafe, saw smoke coming from plastic near rear of burner.  Unplugged unit and immediately took it outside, fearing imminent fire.  House smelled of strong acrid smoke.

No injuries, however the coffeemaker appeared very close to bursting into flames.  Had I not been in the same room at the time, I fear things could have been much worse. 

Note there are at least 7 similar reports of smoke from other owners of the same coffeemaker on [REDACTED]



I am amending the subject report, as requested, with the information needed for it to be published:

Description of Risk of Harm
1)	Fire -- until I unplugged the unit, the burner continued to getting hotter and hotter, plastic parts were melting and emitting noxious smoke, fire appeared imminent
2)	Burn/scalding -- coffee in the glass carafe was much hotter than normal (boiling); plastic parts around burner which are normally safe to contact were very hot and melting
Please confirm this is what was needed to publish the report.  The unit is in my possession.  If necessary, I can plug it back in and demonstrate that it catches fire.

productDescription: LG dehumidifier
incidentDescription: Purchased new dehumidifier LG model UD501KOG5 in September 2021. Because the unit is under LG warranty, I contacted LG customer service about the problem.  LG is taking the position that the issue is cosmetic only (without even seeing pictures or sending a technician) and is not covered by its 1 year warranty. The warranty states that it warrants against defects in materials or workmanship under normal household use for a period of 1 year from the date of purchase. The defect occurred after a period of normal use. In fact, the use has been light – only approximately 3 1/2 months out of the 9 months we’ve owned it because it is turned off during the dry winter months. The separation of the front from the back of the unit creates a dangerous situation. The gap is large enough for me, and therefore a child, to stick a finger or other implement into the internal electrical and/or electronic components. It also will cause dust and other debris to enter into the unit thereby interfering with its function and safety. The support of the top control panel containing the electronics is already compromised by the one side panel now being at an angle.

productDescription:
Samsung Refrigerator (Model: RF28R7201SG/AA; Serial: 0B2B43BM400093A)
28-cu ft 4-Door French Door Refrigerator with Ice Maker (Fingerprint Resistant Black Stainless Steel)
incidentDescription:
On May 16, 2019, I purchased a new Samsung Refrigerator (Model: RF28R7201SG/AA; Serial: 0B2B43BM400093A) from Lowe’s for $2,245.61.  This item was delivered to our home and installed in June 2019. 

I registered the warranty on this refrigerator with Samsung on June 30, 2019.  The warranty provided ne year parts and labor; five years parts and labor on Sealed Refrigeration System Only (Compressor, Evaporator, Condenser, Drier, and Connecting Tubing), and ten years part and five (5) years labor on Digital Inverter Compressor Only 

Over the last few years, the ice maker in the refrigerator has stopped functioning frequently.  Usually, we would do the reset process and it would start working again, but it is now completely dead and will not reset.  A couple of weeks ago, the freezer compartment also stopped being reliable, and we noticed the frozen foods were defrosting. 

Many other consumers have also reported problems with the ice makers and freezer temperature/temperature display.  There are several class action lawsuits pending and Samsung has been issuing refunds to consumers because the refrigerators are defective and not able to be repaired.  

We are now using a 10-year-old [REDACTED] refrigerator in our garage, because the Samsung is not working correctly. 

On May 8, 2022, I contacted Samsung online and requested service on this refrigerator.  I was given Ticket #[REDACTED], and service was scheduled on May 11, 2022.  Samsung then contacted me and cancelled the service, stating no parts were available to repair my three-year-old refrigerator. 

On May 16, 2022, Samsung offered me 50 percent off a new refrigerator purchased on Samsung.com via a text message, and said that they would send me a coupon code.  This coupon was never received. 

On May 18, 2022, Samsung called me and I was told again that they would provide the previously discussed 50 percent off coupon.  This coupon was never received. 

On May 20, 2022 at 10:54 a.m., I contacted Samsung again by phone (800-726-7864) and complained I had never received the offered 50 percent off coupon.  I was told that Samsung was now processing a refund of approximately $2,100, and I would receive a phone call from them soon.  I then provided Samsung with my bill of sale by their request via text message. 

On May 20, 2022 at 2:09 p.m., I received a call from Samsung.  Samsung told me they would not provide the refund which was just offered.  Samsung again offered only the 50 percent off coupon, and said I would receive it with two days. 

On May 25, 2022, I contacted Samsung again by phone and requested a refund instead of a coupon.  I told Samsung the freezer was also not working now.  I told Samsung I was not really interested in buying a new refrigerator from them since they would not repair the Samsung refrigerator that I already own.  I told Samsung the other models of refrigerators that they offered would not fit my cabinet space without over $1,000 in alterations.  Samsung said they would consider offering a refund again, and would contact me with their decision. 

On June 4, 2022, I called Samsung again about the requested refund.  Samsung refused to provide a refund because there had not been at least two repairs on the refrigerator.  I reminded Samsung that they refused to even conduct the first repair on the icemaker due to a lack of parts support, and they had also refused to make the second repair to the freezer when I contacted them on May 25, 2022. 

Samsung only offered again to send me a 50 percent off coupon.  They provided me with Ticket #[REDACTED]

On June 5, 2022 at 12:27 p.m., Samsung called me and said the call was being recorded.  Samsung said they were still working on the 50 percent off coupon.  I told them again I did not want the coupon, but instead wanted my refrigerator to be repaired, or to receive a refund.  I reminded them I’ve had two issues now, one with the ice maker and one with the freezer compartment.  I gave further details about the freezer compartment not maintaining the proper temperature and the temperature indicators being inaccurate.  I also told them about my food loss due to defrosting in the defective freezer compartment. 

Samsung told me they could not repair my ice maker or my freezer compartment.  Previously I’d been told if there were two prior repair requests, then a refund could be provided.  I told Samsung this, but they still refused to provide any refund or repair. 

Samsung told me my warranty was expired.  I stated the implied warranty, sealed refrigeration, and compressor warranty were still in effect.  I told them my refrigerator was only three-years-old and I know Samsung is aware of the manufacturer defects with this refrigerator, and Samsung has been refunding many customers with refrigerator’s that are more than seven-years-old. 

Samsung stated the only thing they could offer was the 50 percent off coupon, and I told them I would not accept this.  I told them I’d already complained to the Better Business Bureau, and would now take my complaint to the New Mexico Office of the Attorney General and the Consumer Products Safety Division. 

I also asked Samsung if I could speak to a supervisor and was told I would have to call back on a weekday for that. 

Since Samsung cannot provide service for my refrigerator, I am requesting a refund so I can purchase a refrigerator from a manufacturer that can support their products, with a working ice maker and freezer that will fit into my existing cabinet space without modification. 

Consumers are becoming ill due to consuming spoiled food from these defective refrigerators.  Please help me put a stop to this.

manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription:
Electrical safety hazard regarding FoodSaver Model FM-3945.  Want to bring to your attention an electrical safety hazard regarding my FoodSaver. The power cable insulation (16-month-old, moderate usage) has worn away leaving exposed electrical conductors.  If one reaches under a plugged-in unit to pick it up, contact with the energized conductors can be made, creating an electrical shock hazard.

Report Update:
The statement that the product does not present a hazard or unreasonable risk of death is inaccurate. The underside of the food processor has exposed electrical conductors, brought about by normal product usage, energized to a potential of 120 VAC when plugged in. Keeping in mind that a significant number of older homes do not have electrical GFCI protection, an individual could pick up the food processor by the underside, come in contact with the exposed "hot" conductor with one hand while touching a metal appliance (range or cooktop) with the other hand or bare arm (or even a stainless-steel kitchen sink - in some homes copper plumbing can provide a ground for the electrical system) completing an electrical path to ground through the body. The result being electrical current will flow through the body, potentially causing cardiac arrest which could result in injury or even death. Additionally, having damp hands will increase this risk.

incidentDescription:
3/20/2022:  The dehumidifier was in use (length of time unknown), when the consumer noticed the unit was on fire internally and emitting smoke.  She consumer quickly unplugged it and took it outside.  Once  outside, the flames died out on their own.

There is no visible exterior damage to the outside of the dehumidifier itself and there was no property damage to the consumer’s home.

The consumer did not use the water bucket for the dehumidifier.  It had tubing, which allowed water to go from the dehumidifier to a pipe in her basement.  So that is where the water from the dehumidifier drained directly into.

The dehumidifier model matched one of the recalled numbers (CPSC Release #[REDACTED]), but the serial number did not appear to be included.  Model # LAD504TDL Serial #KN01801706

The consumer said she contacted a company and they asked for pictures, but she hadn’t submitted them at the time she filed a report with CPSC.  The dehumidifier caught on fire 18MAR22.  Calls were made regarding the incident 19MAR22.

incidentDescription:
Our landlord provided us with 4 Delonghi Oil-filled radiator style electric heaters with the following model, type and serial numbers:
Model: EW6507L
Type: KH650715P
Serials: 42512 JN, 44312 JN DLT

These heaters all have serious defects and nearly caused a fire in our house. All of the power cords on these heaters get very hot when being used on the 1500W setting. The prongs of the plugs get extremely hot and all of them have melted the plastic surround the metal prongs causing them to come loose and some to even fall off. One of the heater plugs got so hot that it caused the outlet to melt and turn black. Still another one of the heaters had a wheel break off, causing it to fall over and start smoking. In all of these instances, we immediately stopped using the heaters.

We called Delonghi's Customer Support Safety line, and they assured us that none of these heaters are on their recall list and are "safe to use." Obviously they are not safe to use, and I am making this report to ensure that other consumers are warned of the dangers of these heaters.

productDescription: DR Power Walk Behind Lawn Vacuum Pro-SP model WL35008DEV. Large, orange, self propelled, gas powered lawn leaf vacuum with chipper capabilities. The parts that came apart were one of the leaf shredder blades which exited the machine and the flywheel that creates vacuum was cracked almost in half.
productSubCategory: Lawn Mowers, Leaf Blowers and Lawn Vacuums
incidentDescription: I was starting up my DR Power Walk Behind Lawn Vacuum Pro-SP. The flywheel has 5 leaf shredder blades welded to the flywheel. I was not even using the machine at the time, only starting it up. One of the blades came loose, came through the plastic cover on top of the machine, almost severed my left thumb, then impacted my chest. Damage to the thumb was extensive. The second joint was separated, at least one tendon was severed and reattached, one ligament was still attached to a severed piece of bone and re attached, one nerve was severed, there were several bone fragments, The second joint is current pinned while the bones heal. The impact to the chest resulted in two cracks in the sternum, internal bleeding behind the sternum, and a bruised lung. I spent two days in two different trauma centers. While the leaf shredder blade was the only piece to exit the machine and hit me, the flywheel, which is still inside the vacuum chamber, is almost torn in half across the middle. Without further examination, it appears to be a result of bad welds between the shredder blades and the flywheel.

productDescription: Harman Pellet Stove XXV-TC /  2018  S/N HF 1672177.   Built by Hearth and Home Technologies (352 Mt House Road, Halifax, PA 17032)    Black in color, 3 ft tall / 3 ft wide.
incidentDescription:
I have a Harman Pellet Stove XXV-TC / year 2018 (S/N  HF 1672177) by Hearth and Home Technologies. Installed June 2019.  The stove started to not follow the set room temperature by 10-15 deg or more on the hot side. Called the Harman technician and was told to load/reload new firmware (firmware update is 21.04.20) .  I did so 5 or 6 times, and each time something changed the stove settings (for good or bad) .   The last firmware download seemed to fix the "following the room temp" issues, but now the stove has safety issues.  
1. When the hopper lip is opened the fans (combustion and room) should stop as they did before.  They do not after firmware update.
2. When the load door is opened the fans (combustion and room) should stop as they did before, it does stop feeding pellets.   If the load door glass would break the combustion fan would not stop running (possible fire hazard).
3. The Touch Screen on/off "button" does not stop the stove. The stove keeps feeding pellets in the off position.  To stop the stove I must open the load door 
 and scrap the hot/burning pellets into the stove's ash pan. Leave the load door cracked open (so it will not feed pellets and start the fire up again) and let it cool for around 45 mins so it will shut down.  If I would unplug the stove it my damage it or smoke up the house.
4. You cannot tell if the firmware has been successful in its download (all downloads ended like they were successful).  You must run the stove to see what is fixed or not fixed. 
5. Was told by the Harman tech it maybe the Touch Screen if the firmware does not work, but the firmware seems to be the problem. Should the Touch Screens not be recalled if it is not the firmware? Or a new/better firmware to update with?
Read on web sites and [REDACTED] pages about the same thing happening to my Harman stove is happening the other stoves.

incidentDescription:
I rode my Onewheel XR, by Future Motion (the firm) and the front end of the PEV board nose dived and ejected me off the board while I was going less than 8 mph with a battery charge at more than 50%. It was windy so I was just going along against the wind which provided some resistance. I landed on the pavement and got lacerations on my left wrist, left knee, and right knee. I also sustained bruises on my left hand and both my knees and hip. The only way the product lets you know you are about to overload the hub motor, which keeps the board self balancing, is by subtlety raising the front end of the board up (The firm calls this "push back" and this wasn't very noticeable when it is very windy and providing lost of wind resistance).  There is no audible noise or light indicator informing the user they are getting close to the hub motor's upper torque limit.


                                   I also had a Onewheel Pint (another model by this firm) and had the same nose dive issue occur while I was going up a steep hill. I did not notice any "push back". When that incident occurred, I landed on my wrists and bruised both of my wrists and sustained some road rash on both of my wrists.

productDescription: Broan E64000 Series range hood
incidentDescription:
22 February 2021
Consumer Product Safety Commission
4330 East West Highway
Bethesda, MD 20814

Dear Sirs:
As part of a recent kitchen renovation I purchased a Broan E64000 Series range hood. I thought Broan sold high quality and well designed products. I was wrong. While probably not of interest to the CPSC, there are some design flaws that, while not dangerous, are very annoying.

First, the knobs controlling the light intensity and fan speed simply fall off . They appear to be secured with an impossibly small and virtually inaccessible set screw. So, they just fall off.

Second the bulbs in the under-hood lights fit so snugly in their recess they are extremely difficult to remove and even harder to install. Major annoyance,

But the real and dangerous design flaw relates to the under hood lights. These are not LEDs, they are incandescent bulbs and get extremely hot The problem is the switch to tum them on and off, and the knob to adjust their intensity are not in view, but are hidden on the under side of the hood. When groping to find the switch it is all too easy to easy to contact one of the bulbs and seriously burn your fingers. This is not hypothetical. Both my housemate and I have burned our fingers while attempting to turn the lights off.

I believe Broan should be required to recall these hoods and replace them, at their expense, with a redesigned model that does not present a danger to the public. 

[REDACTED]

[REDACTED]
Broan

productDescription:
Product is a double-door refrigerator with the right door having a quick-access panel for milk, creamer, juice etc. without having to open the entire fridge. The inside has a large cooling panel at the back boasting some kind of rapid cooling technology, and a small ice machine takes up the top left corner of the fridge interior. The left door features a touch panel with options for rapid-cooling, cubed or crushed ice, water dispensing as well as temperature controls for both fridge and freezer and a real-time readout of the current temperatures of each.

Freezer below has a slide out tray on top and two deep bins below as well as a secondary ice maker for bulk ice collection/production.
incidentDescription:
Refrigerator reporting stable temperatures of 34 degrees when internal temp and food temp is actually 56 degrees!

Quick research shows that the fridge has known issues related to a cooling system in the back icing over, as well as ice makers failing and freezing shut. We had been thinking for the last couple of days that the fridge was a little too warm and that our kid or my spouse and I had been in and out of it too much and made it warm, though each party denied using the fridge lately. Today we threw a thermometer inside and found that our food was being kept at well above safe temperatures and we had been eating improperly stored food for an unknown amount of time - at least a few days. It appears evident that the freezing over of the back also encases the temperature sensor in ice, displaying a consistent 34 degrees regardless of the actual temperature of the food or the rest of the refrigerator. I haven't looked any further into it yet, But evidently there is a [REDACTED] group upwards of 100,000 people seeking a recall due to this issue. Group linked here: [REDACTED]
I don't know if any of us is going to become ill from this, but it has certainly caused an exceptionally unnecessary risk, particularly when this has been a known problem for 5 years with over 20 models?! Please consider taking an action to prevent food poisonings or loss of large quantities of food - not knowing how long our food had been compromised, we just had to throw away our entire food supply and now don't have anywhere to put whatever we replace it with!

Samsung Model RF28HDEDTSR/AA
French door refrigerator with freezer below.

productDescription: Wall heater
incidentDescription:
Caller is reporting that the wall heater started emanating smoke similar to an incident involving a heater made by the same manufacturer (*recall 02-5 31).
PROBLEM: When an RM or ZM model heatbox (replacing a ZA or RA model heatbox) is inserted into a [REDACTED] wall can and wired through a fitting in the top-left wall can knock-out (see diagram below), the RM or ZM model has the potential for continuous heater operation, regardless of thermostat settings or room temperature. This can cause the heater to overheat and catch nearby combustibles on fire.

Caller stated that the smoke started filling up the room, the room was ventilated. The door to the room was opened revealing the smoke-filled room.

He stated that a electrician was present at the time and he was able to switch off the breaker.  Caller stated that he contacted the manufacturer and he was informed that the units were installed correctly but there may have been some sort of failure within the unit which caused overheating.

Caller stated that the heater has been uninstalled and stored.  He feels that these heaters are a fire hazard and should be reported.

*Recall 02-5 31: When an RM or ZM model heatbox (replacing a ZA or RA model heatbox) is inserted into a [REDACTED] wall can and wired through a fitting in the top-left wall can knock-out (see diagram below), the RM or ZM model has the potential for continuous heater operation, regardless of thermostat settings or room temperature. This can cause the heater to overheat and catch nearby combustibles on fire.

Report Update:

Intelligent fan-forced Heater, 1600/1500/1000W 240/208/120V

Model # CEC163TW

Summary

[REDACTED], homeowner [REDACTED], purchased 3 of the above heaters from SupplyHouse.com (order #[REDACTED]) which were delivered 12/2/21.

A licensed electrician, [REDACTED], installed the heaters 12/17/21 as per user manual instructions. He provided 220v to the heaters via #10 wire (oversized for additional safety). After confirming correct wiring he started the three units. Two units appeared to operate as designed, with the display starting at 62 deg. After 10 minutes the bathroom heater displayed 67 deg. At this time, [REDACTED] entered the adjacent bedroom to find that smoke filled the room. [REDACTED] immediately cut power to all three heaters at the breaker. Inspection of the bedroom unit revealed that the paint was scorched on the louvers and near the top of the heating element. [REDACTED] called the manufacturer’s technician who said that the units were apparently wired correctly and that, in the faulty unit, the thermostat was likely stuck on 120 degrees. On 12/28/21 [REDACTED] tech, corrected this by indicating that the problem was an automatic switch that was stuck on120v (all three were wired 220v).

productDescription: AC200 MAX  is a power station.  Power stations store power for emergency or recreational use such as camping, fishing hunting etc.
incidentDescription:
On Aug. 20, 2021 I made an online order of a product called the AC200MAX which is referred to as a Power Station.  Power stations store power for emergency use or recreational activities such as camping.  The AC200MAX stores approx 2,200 watts of power and is a product of Bluetti  The retail price of the AC200MAX is $2,099.00 and I purchased it at an online introductory offer of $1,699.00

After owning the product for several weeks, a [REDACTED] video I was watching titled "Bluetti's AC200Max Polarity Issue - How to check if you are affected"  web address ([REDACTED]) alerted me to the fact that the AC200MAX units had a Reverse Polarity issue.  With an Ohmmeter I checked and found that my AC200MAX had was wired with Reverse Polarity.  

I contacted Bluetti' via phone at their office in Las Vegas and through email correspondence with no satisfaction whatsoever.  I asked them for a replacement product and I was told that they could not guarantee that the replacement unit would not have the same Reverse Polarity issue.  

To sum up:  Bluetti's opening online discount opening offer for the AC200MAX was for a total sale of 500 units "first come first served."  Since Bluetti products are manufactured in China my assumption is that at a minimum, there may very well be 500 of these units out there with that are wired incorrectly with Reverse Polarity which presents the very real danger of serious injury or electrocution resulting in death.  

My AC200MAX still sits unused and with the Reverse Polarity wiring since it was ordered on Aug 20, 2021 and Bluetti.  I have complained to the Nevada Consumer Affairs Commission (since Bluetti's office is in Nevada and I have complained to the Arizona Attorney General's office and thus far I have not received results from either.  

I have exchanged over 40 emails with Bluetti and my AC200MAX still remains dangerous and unusable and I am absolutely sure that there are many hundreds, if not many thousands of the AC200MAX power station out there in consumer's hands that have a lethal potential.  One of my primary goals in all of this is to get Bluetti to issue a recall of said units but after many correspondences with them they are REFUSING to do so.  This to me, shows a blatant disregard for the health and safety of every consumer that owns one of these units in question.

PLEASE NOTE:  that I have in my possession ever correspondence with Bluetti and the preponderance of evidence that I have clearly shows that they know about this serious issue, yet, have refused to correct it by issuing a recall which is the only way to insure the health and safety of their own customers.  I am more than willing to share any or all of this information with your agency upon request.  I might also note that I also have emails from Bluetti stating the "management was negligent."  This statement came from a Bluetti employee in customer service and is entered in part of the record with both agencies that I have complained to.  The Arizona Attorny's General Office, by the way, has this case now in their Criminal Division from what I understand.

I will also tell you that the the attitude of Bluetti employees has been one of secrecy and arrogance across the board.  I have done my own research and  the only agency (as in UL) that ever examined this product was under the jurisdiction of Bluetti themselves (I could be wrong but that is the conclusion I came to) in other words, to the best of my research, the AC200MAX was never checked and tested by an independent testing company it was tested by their own "testing" operation.

productDescription: Roybi ONE+ 18V Cordless Orbital Jig Saw
incidentDescription:
I have a Ryobi Jigsaw with a quick change bit holder. I was setting up the jigsaw for cutting a board, with no battery in it.  

The jigsaw blade sometimes doesn't engage and flies out, so I check by tugging at the blade when I put it in.  This night, I couldn't get the blade to engage.  That is a danger in itself because I don't know what causes it to engage and what doesn't, and sometimes the blade goes flying when I start it up, or just after.  To try to"fix" that issue, I took the blade out and put the battery in.  I planned on triggering the tool with no blade, in hopes it would rattle the quick change mechanism into working order.  Then I planned to take the battery out and put the blade in and make sure it was secure.

I didn't get that far, as when I plugged in the battery I accidently hit the trigger while switching my grip.  I immediately felt pain.  My thumb was likely between the plunger and the guide for the blade when it engaged.  I went to the ER.  My nail is cracked, my thumb broken and there is a nail bed laceration.  

Unrelated to this issue, but I have accidentally engaged the lock off, causing the jigsaw not to turn off when I expect it to.  I feel like a better design would have a safety where the lock off is, like the one on the ryobi circular saw.

incidentDescription:
On duty staff heard a loud popping/breaking noise that they could not immediately identify the source of. After seraching to locate the source of noise, staff member found pieces of a 9v alkaline battery in a cupboard. Further investigation of the cupboard revealed that multiple Nuon alkaline 9v batteries had burst/exploded within the cupboard. These batteries were unused/unopened, individually wrapped, in the original cardboard container of 12 units, sitting in a plastic tray in the closed cupboard.

No injuries were reported, but the potential for injury or fire was present. Had a battery failed while someone had the cupboard open retrieveing materials, injury from debis, chemical content, or fire could have occured. Scorch marks were observed on the interior of the cardboard container, indicating flame was present at time of rupture. This could have started a fire in the materials in the cupboard, allowing extended growth before detection by personnel or extension out of the cupboard to sprinkler protected space in the office.

manufacturer: RAPID MEDICAL INC dba Mueller Co
incidentDescription:
For Christmas in 2020, I received the Mueller Austria Ultra-Stick 500 Watt 9-Speed Immersion Multi-Purpose Hand Blender Heavy Duty Copper Motor Brushed 304 Stainless Steel With Whisk, Milk Frother Attachments from Amazon- sold by Home Moderne. I have since used it only three times, twice for blending together butternut squash soup and this last being a few days ago 2/6/22 when smoke arose and the device nearly caught fire while simply mixing muffin batter. I was using the whisk attachment on the lowest speed setting and was only quick pulsing to combine my ingredients. At first, I thought it was the mix that had blown up into the air as I initially smelled the chocolate. I only used the product for all of 20 seconds when I started to smell burning and saw it was still smokey to which I unplugged the device and popped out the whisk attachment. Upon doing so, a piece of melted plastic fell out and an AWFUL burnt plastic smell arose from either end. You can still smell it on the product, I don’t dare use this again! 

The product features state the Mueller Ultra-Stick can be used to make delicious treats such as salsa, pesto, pancake and watter, batter, smoothies, cheese sauce, homemade tomato sauce, hollandaise sauce, whipped cream, apple butter, various Indian dishes, soups and cakes. Can also be used for chopping and making cocktails and much more though I can’t imagine how this unit would have upheld against something thicker.

I contacted the seller regarding this, however they said because it’s passed a year warranty, I could only purchase another unit at a discounted price as a means of a refund. There are several great reviews of this product, but MANY others have also had burning/fire issues like myself. I think this is a dangerous product and should be recalled immediately or at the very least looked into. I think it is irresponsible of the manufacturer/seller to only have a solution of purchasing another product exactly the same, so that I have purchased and spent money on two products with potential for both to catch fire. I do not see how this benefits or helps any consumer.

productDescription:
[REDACTED]
https://shopbvv.com/collections/glass-vac-aluminum-vacuum-chambers/products/glass-vac-5-gallon-aluminum-vacuum-chamber

BVV Glass Vac 5 gallon vacuum chamber. Glass lid with silicon gasket.
model: Glass Vac 5 Gallon Aluminum Vacuum Chamber
incidentDescription:
A Glass-Vac 5 gallon vacuum chamber (made by BVV) imploded during use, and the glass lid shattered sending glass flying. One of our technicians who was in close proximity to the vacuum chamber had glass fly into his eye and was taken to the hospital. He also experienced some hearing loss due to the implosion. 

Our engineering team ran an investigation and concluded that when the lid is placed off center it can lead to an implosion when the lid slips into the stainless steel chamber. The lid is 12" in diameter, so atmospheric pressure results in over 1500 lbs of downwards force. The engineering team recreated this failure with an identical Glass-Vac 5 gallon chamber.

This product is dangerous because there is no centering feature for the lid. Further, the rubber gasket around the glass lid hides exactly where the glass sits on the stainless steel chamber rim. I contacted the company and they sent me photos of identical failures that they received from other customers, so this is not a one-off incident.
