productDescription: Soleil Digital Ceramic Heater Model #PTC-915W (Date Code 0521) sold by Walmart
incidentDescription: On November 27yh, 2021 I purchased a Soleil Digital Ceramic Heater Model #PTC-915W (date code 0521) from Walmart in Cheboygan, Michigan 49721.  The heater was purchased for supplemental heat in my seasonal cabin.  The heater was used two times, once in late November 2021 and during the evening of January15th, 2021.  The heater was operated on the low setting throughout the night.  At approximately 4am on Sunday January 16th I awoke from sleeping and was a little chilled.  At  this point I changed the heater setting  to High and went back to bed.  I woke up at 7am to the smell of burning plastic and discovered that the heater had stopped working.  I examined the end of the plug which incorporates a GFI and discovered that one of the prongs was melted and that the plastic receptacle was melted and burned on the hot leg (small slot).  The 15amp breaker for this circuit in the load center was tripped.  This heater was brand new and not modified in any way.  I examined the receptacle for correct wiring, making sure there wasn't a loose Hot, Neutral or ground wire.  All wires were wrapped around the attaching screws and all screws were tight.  I replaced the burnt receptacle and cover.  I reset the 15amp breaker and plugged a different non-ceramic heater into the plug.  The prongs on the non-ceramic heater never got hot and the heater performed correctly.

model: WMD 200 B  (120Volt, 60 Hz, 1200 Watt, UL listed
incidentDescription:
I purchased a Black and Decker Double Flip Waffle Maker WMD 200 B  from JCPenny on Nov. 26, 2021. I used the waffle maker for the 3rd. time at my Son in Law and Daughter's house. on Dec. 22, 2021. I was at a gathering of 6 people including myself. I was seated at a card table with the waffle maker. The other 5 people were around in front of me. When the light indicated the waffle maker was ready, I put a normal amount of batter in the waffle maker, engaged the latch, waited 10 seconds, rotated it, an added a similar amount of batter to the empty side, and engaged the latch. 
About 1 and a half minutes later (time uncertain), The top of the upper chamber blew open and I felt a force hit my chest. The waffle maker lid had broken where it meets the rotation part of the waffle maker. The rim of the waffle maker didn't have any excess batter. Using a rag, I was able to turn the waffle maker and remove the lower waffle.
We were all shocked to say the least!  Later, after I removed my shirt, I was stunned to see shards of plastic fall from my shirt with some still embedded in my shirt.
If I had had the waffle maker on a kitchen counter, a higher height, the blast would have hit me in the face.
The Incident occurred on Wednesday, Dec. 22, 2021 ~ 5:30 pm. In Tucson AZ.
I believe this was a dangerous event and warrants immediate attention

incidentDescription: I purchased a high-end toaster oven/air fryer from a reputable retailer. I read the manual thoroughly, and the first time I turned the oven on, it exploded and sent shattered glass flying through my kitchen. There had not been any obvious defects with the oven prior to the explosion. We were working through the initial setup "Before First Use" steps as specified in the manual; specifically, we wiped down the interior of the oven, inserted the crumb tray, plugged it in, and set it for "pizza" which, according to the manual, was supposed to walk it through a 20-minute pre-use cycle to burn off a protective coating from the heating elements. After it completed the "preheat" phase of this cycle, it exploded. When I called Breville's customer service to report this dangerous incident, the representative informed me that the shattered glass was caused by the weather. To be clear, the oven had been in its original packaging and unopened shipping box under our Christmas tree for several weeks prior to first use, and first use occurred in the kitchen of our climate-controlled home. I am unable to view the serial number or other identifying details on the oven without exposing myself to broken glass.

productDescription: Food Processor
incidentDescription: I was using a Cuisinart food processor, model # EFP-14DC.  I had the grating disc in place and was grating a block of mozzarella cheese using the pulse function on the food processor.  The machine seemed to be laboring so i removed the cover and checked to make sure the cheese hadn't balled up.  Everything appeared to be ok so I replaced the cover and pressed the pulse function again and the processor started working.  Almost immediately, the cover broke off and several pieces of the cover and the bowl flew across the kitchen.  The processor had stopped as soon as the cover broke but not before the pieces flew about.   The plastic pieces were approximately 2.25 to 2.5 inches long and each had sharp points on both ends.  One of the release buttons on the cover and a spring also had come off.  I was not injured and no one else was in the room but I feel that the potential for a serious injury, particularly to eyes, could have occurred if a person had been in the path of the broken pieces.  I have always used my Cuisinart food processor with the assumption that the machine would not operate if the cover or the blades were not correctly in place and this safety measure protected the user from any possibility of injury.  I feel that the safety measures failed and that is why I am filing this report.

incidentDescription:
**PRODUCT & WHAT HAPPENED**: On December 30th at 2:30pm, my 6 year old son came inside recharge his main gift from Santa this year which was a "GoTrax GKS Kids Luminos eScooter" purchased via Amazon for $200. Upon opening the package we followed the directions exactly and operated it as described in the owners manual. That day, [REDACTED] had used his eScooter on and off for the couple hours prior to the incident and it was in need of charge. This worked because we were just about to pack up and leave the house. Since the chord was really short so the easiest place to charge it was the outlet in the foyer of our house. A few minutes later, sitting inside our house, the scooter EXPLODED several times. Not just little pops; the blasts could be heard several houses away and caused all of our neighbors to come outside to see what was happening. As I ran towards the smoke, I saw flames a couple feet high and tons of dark, thick smoke that smelled toxic. There were 5-6 explosions that shot flaming pieces of plastic in all directions. In between explosions I kicked the scooter outside where it exploded once more. I grabbed my phone to record the aftermath which I can send if needed. The firefighters arrived and informed me that in our town alone, they had 4 other recent calls related to exploding eScooters and hoverboards. I researched the scooter prior to purchase but none of this information was obvious as I wouldn't have thought to include the words "explosions" or "fire." This eScooter company is possibly the highest rated on Amazon.

productDescription: Apple iPhone Lightening Charge Cord
incidentDescription:
Apple (Authentic) iPhone Lightening Cable Charger
On Friday, December 17th my 13-year-old son came home from school and went downstairs to his computer where he also keeps his Apple iPhone Lightening Charger.  He picked it up and immediately dropped it because it was extremely hot.  He then realized he smelled something burning and looked at the cord to see that it had burnt through the rubber/plastic housing all the way through.  I called Apple’s Customer Support line on Saturday, December 18th and they didn’t seem all that interested, though they did take a report after being on hold for 40 minutes.  They told me they would not replace the cord since it was over a year old.  Later that day I went to the Apple Store in Reston Town Center, Virginia.  I was given an appointment to go back another time since I did not have an appointment.  I had no idea before this incident how dire this situation could have evolved into – such as burning down the house or harming my family.  I’m shocked this is a known issue based on all the exact same reports on this website alone, yet neither Apple nor any governmental agency is taking action on it.

There is NO language on the product packaging of the batteries which in any way warns against storing batteries outside of the manufacturer packaging. The only warnings are to not open the batteries or throw in a fire/keep in dry location. Only by luck did we avoid a house fire starting in a closet within a mere several minutes of putting some loose batteries in a drawer. As the manufacturer packaging is incredibly space-inefficient, it would be expected that other people will attempt to store the batteries together in a storage container of some sort. This is incredibly hazardous and there needs to be warnings against this practice on the packaging.

productDescription: Camping Stove, Coleman Dual-Fuel Model 424
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
Item: Coleman Dual-Fuel Camping Stove, Model 424

Background: This is the second Model 424 stove received directly from Coleman as a replacement for the initially purchased stove, ordered from Amazon on May 3, 2021 delivered on May 5, 2021, that was also defective.

Summary of Problem:

During a recent camping trip, October 10-16, 2021, the Coleman stove would produce a “puffing” sound that extinguished the burner flame.  This would normally occur when the flame was set to the low to medium range.  This required constant relighting of the burner.  At one point, on the second day, when relighting burner, the entire stove was engulfed in flames, reaching nearly two feet in height. Since this happened when under my camping canopy, I immediately removed the fuel tank, closed the stove lid and, with pot holders, physically tossed the stove away from my camp site.  It continued burning until the fuel had completed burned out.

Since early in my camping trip, once the stove had cooled, I reinstalled the fuel tank to determine if the stove was still operable. After approximately 10-minutes of operation I noticed that the table it was sitting on was wet with fuel that was leaking from the fuel tank. Obviously, I quickly turned off the burner.  What I found was the indentation on the fuel tank, where the generator assembly is attached to the tank, was filled with fuel and spilling over onto the table. Investigating the generator connections, I found that I could tighten the coupling near the fuel knob an additional ½ turn and the coupling from the long generator tube another ¼ turn. (Labelled picture available) This action stopped the leak. Regardless of evidently stopping the leak, I decided not to use the stove any further during this trip.

When this stove caught fire, it was under my camping canopy which was adjacent to my tent. This fire could very easily have resulted in an over $600.00 loss of equipment. Of course, this property damage is of little consequence when considering that I may have been severely burned when tossing the stove away from my campsite.

On 10/27/2021 I filed complaint to Coleman Consumer Service via the Coleman website and, through an automated receipt message, was assigned the reference number of [REDACTED]. As of 12/08/2021, 42-days after my initial submission, Coleman has yet to respond.  Therefore, I feel that I have no other choice but to bring this issue to your attention.

Without a doubt, due to either manufacturing or quality control problems, this defect is a safety issue that should be investigated before someone is seriously injured using Coleman Model 424 Dual-Fuel stove.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription: OXO Brew Adjustable Temperature Kettle, Electric, Clear, model 8716900.
incidentDescription:
We own an OXO Brew Adjustable Temperature Kettle (model 8716900) which has just experienced a disturbing type of breakage.  The kettle is approximately 18 months old (April '20 - November '21). It has never been used inappropriately or exposed to damaging conditions.

After a routine instance of heating water the kettle began turning ON full blast even while the base, which contains the control knob, is supposed to be turned OFF. In other words, it's permanently stuck on and heating/boiling, even though the on/off switch is left off. I've gone so far as to unplug the unit completely so it fully powers down, but as soon as the base is plugged back in to the outlet the kettle begins boiling again, even though the control knob is never touched. The unit gives no indication that the unit is in fact on; the control knob gives its usual "off" appearance. It does not appear that the control knob is stuck or damaged. There's no indication that the unit is on and heating except for the fact that it boils water and produces noise when plugged in.

This seems to be a fire hazard. There's no clear sign that the unit is powered, and there's no way to power the unit OFF without physically disconnecting it from power. It would be extremely easy for a customer to walk away from the unit while not realizing that it was still on and heating.

productDescription:
Glowforge laser cutting system

Model Glowforge Pro

I own a Glowforge laser cutting system. The company is based out of Seattle. After a little over a year of use I have come to the conclusion that these machines appear to be built using very unsafe design practices and their use could lead to catastrophic fire. Electrical faults are rife. The component layout is dangerous. The tube cooling capacity is poor and susceptible to overheating. The main cable that controls the laser head is exceptionally easy to damage during cleaning or maintenance, and the insulation wears off alarmingly quickly, exposing the conductor traces. The main cable also runs very close the stepper motor. These motors run very warm and there is not adequate separation between it and the cable to ensure safety (or reliability). The cable then runs through the drag chain, where it is subject to a great deal of friction and wear. In addition, the machine is advertised as a 'Pro' device that is able to cut wood, acrylic and more. However, the electronics, heat sink and exhaust fan are all located next to each other in the same area of the machine. The accumulation of dirt in fumes in both the fan and over those critical components is alarming. The design reduces cooling capacity over time. Finally, there is a red tension cable that carries around 26,000 volts and feeds the laser tube. This cable is not designed to be flexed or strained at all and is very fragile. However, the high tension cable is installed next to the main ribbon cable (mentioned above) which carry control signs. Mains and high voltage signals should also be separated by a considerable margin for safety - the potential for noise and errors passing between the cables could cause glitches, faults and represent a fire hazard. The final area I am concerned with is the ducting supplied with the system. The ductwork expands every time the machine is in use and the creasing and uncreasing cause punctures in the duct, allowing cutting fumes to vent into the user's work space. The ductwork is not rated for fume extraction. Overall, all of these flaws combined means not only is the machine being falsely advertised as a 'Pro' commercial production unit, it's incredibly unsafe. The vast majority of these lasers are sold and marketed to at-home hobbyists, teachers, and students who would not typically be familiar with the threat of electrical failure and fire these design flaws could lead to. The Glowforge Owner's forum (which the company runs) is filled with many comments/tickets about fires in these machines, so the company knows these can lead to life-threatening problems but has done nothing to correct these issues. I feel very strongly there should be a recall on these machines.

productDescription: Black & Decker 22 inch ceramic heater. Black. Use horizontally or vertically. BNVHC15
incidentDescription:
Black & Decker space heater model BHVHC15 may cause a fire due to confusing product electronic display that may lead consumers into thinking the product is OFF when in fact it is in STANDBY, able to come on by itself after a user goes to bed, leaves home or otherwise leaves the product unattended. The display does NOT work as indicted in the user manual.  The product also appears to occasionally draw more electrical current than indicated on the appliance and in the manual (exceeding 1600 watts)The company
s customer service phone representative seemed uninterested in hearing my concern. . The company, W Appliance, Inc. in New York City, has not returned my phone message in which I said I wanted to alert to a potential safety issue with the product. I purchased two of these, both of which have this problem.

ADDITIONAL INFO: The issue is the unit's electronic display shows a single red "plug" icon when the appliance is OFF but connected to a live outlet. It also shows the same icon when the built-in thermostat places the unit in STANDBY because the room temperature has reached the set level. As a result, a user could mistake that red light icon to mean that the appliance is OFF, when in fact it is in STANDBY, able to come on at any time by itself when the room cools down. If the user goes to bed, leaves the room or otherwise leaves the appliance  unattended believing the appliance is OFF when it actually is in STANDBY, this could create a fire hard, especially if the unit is set at 1500 watts and is aimed at a couch, bed or other combustible item. The user manual says: "To shut unit off at any time, press the POWER Button until all indicator lights go OFF. (see attached scan) " But all the indicator light do NOT go OFF. Instead, that one light stays on if the appliance is OFF and connected to live power. (Consumers have an incentive to leave the product plugged because it has a memory function that retains the  thermostat and heat setting unless the product is unplugged.)

productDescription:
I believe it is the  Segway/Ninebot Shared Scooter MAX model of electric scooter.

Model Shared Scooter MAX
incidentDescription:
I have made repeated complaints to the micromobility operator, as well as the appropriate agency at the City of Denver's gov site, but no response/action.
The product is the shared Lyft electric scooters in the City of Denver, Colorado.
I was using the product.
I was using the product to travel, in a legal and appropriate manner, in accordance with local regulations.
No injuries occurred, but there seems to me a high probability of one occuring.

In Denver, we have a pedestrian/shuttle mall, which is a restricted zone for electric scooters. My understanding is that the geofence is supposed to prevent shared scooters from riding DOWN (along) the mall, which runs NW/SE. However, every block there are roadways that cross the mall, including several roads with bike lanes (in Denver, scooters are supposed to use the bike lane if available, otherwise they are legal in the general lane—they are not permitted on the sidewalk).

On multiple instances, I have had the geofence restriction kick in while CROSSING the 16th St pedestrian/shuttle mall. The most likely scenario is if I'm riding a scooter and am stopped at a red light before crossing the mall—once I have a green light, the scooter will most likely not operate. Additionally, the wheels will lock, making it difficult to PUSH the scooter out of the geofenced area. This is not the most dangerous scenario, since being stopped at the light, it's easy enough to push the scooter (against the locked wheels) onto the sidewalk. However…

…if I have a green light, the geofence restrictions can kick in…at any point along the block after having crossed the mall. The most dangerous scenario that I have experienced (repeatedly) is on Stout St between 16th & 17th, which does not have a bike lane (I take this road because a) [REDACTED], and b) there's a protected bike lane that starts on 18th & Stout). Because Stout St between 16th & 17th has multiple lanes (and a light rail track), and has parking on the right-hand side, if/when the scooter cuts power and LOCK THE WHEELS while I'm riding down a general traffic lane, there's is literally nowhere to go except to dismount and slowly PUSH the scooter (against the locked wheels) down a half-block in the middle of a general traffic lane (frequently in heavy traffic) until I reach the end of the block and can either get to the sidewalk, or the scooter finally unlocks again.

While I understand the need to have areas where shared scooters are restricted from use, the implementation of the geofencing on the 16th St Mall by Lyft in Denver Colorado represents an extreme safety hazard, particularly for those who are unfamiliar with the misguided implementation of this restriction and are unprepared for their scooters to suddenly cut power and LOCK (resulting in a much faster than expected deceleration) while in traffic.

The model # of the bundle is RY40290VNM. The model # listed in field 4 is the model number of the power head itself (the component causing the shock).

Model RY40009VNM
incidentDescription: About 2 weeks ago I purchased a new Ryobi cordless lawn power head model # RY40009VNM serial # LT21086N120328 from my local Home Depot in bundle model # RY40290VNM . The first day I ran the power head I used several different Ryobi-made and approved attachments including an edger, blower, weed trimmer, and a pole saw. After about 40 minutes of use, the palms of my hands began to sweat a little - not dripping with sweat but slightly damp. I then began feeling sharp and painful shocks in my right hand (trigger hand) when gripping the trigger of the power head at full throttle. The first couple of shocks were so startling I jerked my hand away from the trigger and nearly dropped the entire tool. This power head runs on 40V batteries. With a little experimentation, I discovered I could run the power head without getting shocked if I held the trigger grip with my thumb and trigger finger being careful not to grip the rubber overmold near the recessed steel screws holding it together. Apparently, the shock is passing through these steel screw heads into the palm of my sweaty hand. I do not know why these screws are energized. Perhaps this a manufacturing defect (wire to the trigger assembly pierced by one of the screws) or a design flaw that is causing current to leak from the trigger/grip assembly. I do not know. I called Ryobi support and they promised to forward this report to their product safety department. I was told I would be contacted by safety directly. It has been a week since contacting them, and they have not reached out.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: The product is a Masterbuilt slow smoker model MB20100112 that is designed to be used as an add-on and alternative smoke source for most Masterbuilt smokers.  Once fitted alongside the existing smoker, it can be used for extended smoking time instead of using the wood chip dispenser on the original smoker. Dimensions: 10.4 x 10.4 x 18 inches, weight: 9.95 pounds
incidentDescription: My Masterbuilt slow smoker stopped working.  I found that it had tripped the gfci breaker on the outlet feeding it.  When I tested the power cord to the smoker with a multimeter, I found the the live and neutral power terminals were shorted to ground.  I opened the smoker and saw melted wires.  The internal wires to the electrical heating element have high temperature insulation, but the wires on the electrical cord powering the smoker do not.  The insulation had melted and the wires were shorted together and to the housing.  I contacted Masterbuilt customer service twice and only received one response stating the the smoke temperature  emanating from the smoker is less than 105°C.  They did not address the real problem that the power cable is held against the heating element with zip ties, causing the insulation to fail.  Their power cord insulation is the incorrect type for this high temperature application and poses a shock hazard to the user once melted through.  NEC table 400.4 states that thermoset insulation should be used for heater elements which this insulation is definitely not.  It seems to be thermoplastic from the way it melts.  Additionally, the use of this cable violates NEC article 310.15(A)(3) that states that the insulated conductor's temperature rating may not be exceeded.

productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
We purchased a Cuisinart Twin Oaks combination pellet/gas grill at the beginning of the summer.  We used the pellet side for a few small smokes. On our first 3+ hour smoke we had our first hopper fire once our food was completed. At the conclusion of cooking, we came inside and began eating.  I noticed a small amount of smoke coming from the hopper but the manual said this was “normal”.  When the smoke began getting thicker I checked on the smoker. Fire had consumed interior of the hopper.  I extinguished the fire and began looking for what I did wrong. After rereading the manual and doing some research I found that this was a common problem with the grill. A [REDACTED] video described a similar situation to what I believe happened in my grill.  I contacted Cuisinart customer service to voice my concerns. After much back and forth, I was told that fires are not covered under the warranty and that my issue could not be reproduced. As the grill could no longer be returned to Walmart, I purchased the necessary replacement parts. I continued to monitor my grill closely and follow the instructions from the manual in addition to the recommendations provided via email.  Since the initial replacement I have had two more hopper fires that I have been able to extinguish before damage to the grill.  After continued emails, cuisinart continues to claim this can not be reproduced.

The main issue comes from the fire pot not emptying when the clean out mechanism is used. If the grill sits for a period of time without use, particularly in a humid climate, the ash hardens and does not drop into the removal tray. When the ash remains, when one would think it’s empty, the ash accumulates until pellets in the auger catch fire.

productDescription:
BLACK+DECKER 4-Slice Toaster Oven with Natural Convection, Stainless Steel, TO1760SS
None of this is a joke. 
I think the only reason why no lawsuits is because item is cheap, just hurts the poor, and doesn’t kill just is a severe burn risk in many ways. Also, for those unconcerned about safety it is in a small category of inexpensive high wattage, small toaster-ovens. 

Why dangerous?
1) Leak from toaster heats knobs which get as hot as inside of toaster. Steam visible on knobs while heating.
2) Door does not open completely, so easily tips forward toward user and worse hot rack slides out toward user when tips.
3) Poor or zero tactile and audio feedback for off, and hard to turn-off.
4) Worse, just passed the off position is a permanently on position. So easy to accidentally keep on. Fire hazard. They even know it, and warn in big letters what to do in case of fire. Only indicator is subtle light, and very subtle in daytime since it dims (not kidding) when inside reaches set temperature.
5) Small, but BPA containing product poorly labeled.
6) Rack is in contact with glass. I could not maintain any space, even with effort. This is probably why negative reviewers report that glass shatters.

The main risk is obviously that heat leaks through backs of knobs to a a virtually unlimited temperature (maybe limit is 450 degrees F, I did not do an experiment) AND easily tips toward user spilling hot rack, and falling.

I am reporting this based on what the baby's parents showed me on a telephone screen featuring an add for the product. It looks similar to a [REDACTED] coffee maker.  I have not laid hands on one, nor have I reviewed instructional/product description literature.
brand: Baby Brezza Formula Pro Advanced Dispenser
incidentDescription: I am a pediatrician.  Parents of a newborn baby report they own a Baby Brezza machine (similar to a coffe maker, it 'brews' individual formula bottles for babies).  Apparently the machine is able to hold a water volume larger than an appropriately proportionate amount of powdered formula mix - which can result in the preparation of formula that is inappropriately diluted.  This apparently happened on two occasions during the night, and the father didn't realize it until after the bottles had been fed.  This is gravely concerning from a nutritional standpoint for sure, but also from a safety standpoint.  In the first 4 months of life especially, babies are reliant on a milk source for all of their nutrition, and each feeding serves a crucial role (during this time, babies must gain weight at 1/2 to 1 ounce each day).  From a safety standpoint, during the first 6 months of life the kidney function in babies is immature, and it is crucial they receive a proper electrolyte balance in any fluid they consume.  Blood sodium levels in newborns are prone to fall significantly with rather modest consumption of fluids containing suboptimal electrolytes (which can result in brain swelling and seizures).

incidentDescription:
The consumer has owned two 6-1/2 quarts, fish fryers that were made by this same manufacturer, which also had the same exact malfunction.  The manufacturer replaced those two, but the consumer did not have model/serial information on them.

12/2020:  The consumer got the first 6-1/2 quart fish fryer.

7/2021:  The first time he used the fryer, the regulator began to show signs of frost.  Within 5 minutes a large amount gas came though the regulator and  fire balls shot out the burners.  This happen several times within a few seconds.  The consumer quickly turned off the gas.  

7/2021:  The consumer called the firm and their rep. advised him to return it to the dealer for a replacement.  He took it back to the dealer and they provided him with an identical fryer.  

7/2021:  The very first time he used the 2nd fryer, the exact same problem occurred.  The regulator became frosted within 5 minutes and fire balls started shooting from the burner within seconds.  There was no property damage with the first 2 fryers.

8/2021:  The consumer called the manufacturer and reported the issue with this 2nd fryer.  Their rep. advised him to take it back to the dealer for an exchange or a refund.

The consumer took it back to the dealer and paid a little over $20 for a larger fryer (10-1/2 quart).

The very first time he used this 3rd fryer, the regulator began to frost up within 1 minute and fire balls began shooting from the burner.  The consumer quickly turned it off.

He said that the compressed air pipe, next to the ceiling in my shop,  is made of PVC and it blew up, as it got heated.   However, he also took pictures and made a video of the incident.

The consumer was using all 3 fryers indoors, but they are recommended to be used outdoors.


8/2020:  The consumer called the firm about this 3rd fryer.

8/17/2021:  The firm’s rep. returned the consumer’s call and offered to send a replacement regulator, which had been tested.  The rep. also requested his defective regulator.  The consumer agreed to this initially, but gave it further thought and decided he will not give the firm the part.  I did send them the third one but still have the 4th one that they sent.

The product’s packaging had the following:  Part # 716 of 2,374.  Therefore, he concluded that there are many of these items out on the market.

The consumer checked the Internet and saw that another person was selling theirs on the [REDACTED], but they also noted that the regulator didn’t work.  This added to his concern

His 10-1/2 quarts had: (SKU:  1631022)   UPC:  848696 002614

New information since our phone conversation ... 
Today is August the 25th. When I spoke with you on the phone I had mentioned that someone had called from the company that supplies the fish fryers. 
I had emailed the company and just now went back to find the emails so that I'd have the exact dates. There are no emails that I could find and I for sure didn't delete them. 
The phone number for the company that called and offered to replace the bad burner is (310)323-0888 and using the phone number, I did a search and it brought up the company name and address which is: 
New Legacy Industrial Inc. 
1618 W Rosecrans Ave 
Gardena , CA, 90249-3022 
United States 
The replacement burner that they sent, and stated that it had been tested (her exact words were "we're going to go ahead and pre-test it and ship it out to you") arrived about a week ago. The same day I hooked it up to a 20# cylinder and within a minute, the regulator began to frost up and after lighting the flame at 2:17:09 PM, at 2:18:20 it was getting a heavy layer of frost on the regulator. At 2:19 it was getting gushes of flame that got bigger as time went on so I did a 29 second video of it and shut it down once the fire gushes got close to the ceiling. I uploaded it to Youtube and this is the link to it. [REDACTED] 
I also uploaded a video of the second one from inside my shop where the flames overheated a PVC airline next to the ceiling causing it to burst. It was only about 4 seconds because I was in a hurry to shut it down. [REDACTED] 
On Monday I sent the regulator/burner back to the company in their prepaid UPS carton. I still have the one that they sent as a (supposedly tested) replacement. 

I do have some pictures that have timestamps in the photos if you need them? 
Thanks for looking into this and hopefully this hazardous product can be remedied,

productDescription:
Carrier Corporation Carrier Infinity Greenspeed 4 ton unit

Model 25VNA048A0030040
productType: Heaters or Heating Systems, Other or Not Specified (393)
incidentDescription:
I have a 3 year old Greenspeed Infinity system model #25VNA0 that completely stopped working on August 6 due to an inverter board failure.  After two authorized Carrier service technician visits, the heat pump unit was diagnosed with a failed inverter board, after initially showing a code 95 on the unit.  A code 95 indicates that there is high current above 257 volts ac being detected within the board.  

This same inverter board has been subject to a consumer product safety recall (https://www.cpsc.gov/Recalls/2017/carrier-and-bryant-recall-heat-pumps) of which absolutely no notice was formally sent to us that our unit posed a fire safety hazard.  The recall states the following hazard exists "The capacitors in the fuse boards in the heat pumps can stop working causing the unit to overheat, posing a fire hazard."  

Our service technician is having difficulty sourcing a new inverter board and contacts to Carrier directly have placed blame on distributors and not Carrier corporate for the issues in trying to source a known recall replacement product.

Hello,

I have a Samsung refrigerator model: RF260BEAESR, serial number: JKKM4BBD301439W, Date of manufacturer: March 2013. We have had constant issues with this fridge and freezer. Our refrigerator came with our home that we purchased 2 yrs ago. It was included in our settlement. I’m more concerned about the temperature being accurate then having ice, but it just adds to all the issues this refrigerator has. I’ve contacted customer service several times and all they say is it’s out of warranty. Well this fridge came with the purchase of my house and was included in our settlement. I’m more concerned about having a reliable refrigeration temperature for my daughter. I also have to be extremely cautious about who enters my home due to covid and the new delta variant going around so we must take extreme covid measures to keep her safe. I have a medically fragile daughter that needs to be taken into consideration as well as the health and safety of the food my family is consuming. This has nothing to do with a warranty when it’s a manufacturer design flaw this company should be taking care of its customers or they will eventually lose them all.

incidentDescription:
I was riding my 2018 Voltbike Enduro on a dirt trail when the frame snapped.  This ebike has full suspension, and was designed for trail use.  Fortunately, I was going slowly on a level trail when the failure occurred, so I was not injured.  The fracture in the seat tube opened up more than 1/2", so I was able to identify a manufacturing defect.  Evidently, the welding process distorted the tube, and the seat post would not fit.  The tube was reamed out, and they went too deep.  You can easily see that the tube was shaved eggshell thin where it began to curve, facing forward.
I told Voltbike exactly why the frame failed, and they told me the model had changed, and the old frame was no longer available.  I emailed my photos as requested, but they refused to respond with any remedy.   An investigation and potential recall may be warranted.

In the user's manual for this unit, there is statement #42 of page 3 that warns of this very accident, and advises to remove the blade assembly before emptying the pitcher's contents or you could receive a laceration.  But they don't tell you it is because the blade assembly will fall out and hit your hand or other part of your body.

The concept of having a floating/detached blade assembly is non-intuitive to the operator that will cause many accidents over time and it is a design flaw on the basis of safety of operation.

productType: Hair Curlers, Curling Irons, Clips & Hairpins (1682)
incidentDescription:
Product: T3 CURL ID (https://www.t3micro.com/product/curl-id-curling-iron)
Issue Overview: This curling iron has capacitive touch buttons on the handle that turn it on/off and change the heating setting. There is a safety feature to prevent heating the curling iron prior to locking the screen from these touch inputs. That safety feature is inoperable allowing the device to be turned on accidentally and immediately begin applying heat to the device.
Who was using the product: I was.
How were the products used: curling hair.
Injuries: cooked hair. Skin burns.
How: devices safety features are not correctly functioning.


Longer Description:

The T3 CURL ID does not have physical buttons to turn it on/off but instead has capacitive touch buttons that react to any touch. These buttons can turn the device on or off as well as change the heat settings. They are placed on the front face of the handle of the curling iron - where myself and other users hold the device.

The device allows you to lock the screen to disable these buttons from accepting input. According to the manual "Note: Screen must be locked to begin heat up". This is incorrect and the curling iron begins to immediately apply heat once turned on. The device does not indicate any way to lock the screen outside of the provided paper user manual.

When I used this device without locking the screen it behaved exactly as you'd expect a curling iron to behave. It heated to the temperature selected and let me start curling my hair. The device includes two modes: It's Smart and Manual modes. I used the smart mode on it's low settings. By holding the iron the device was switched to "manual" mode (because the screen does not require being locked to operate the device). The default setting for manual mode is the maximum heat setting which the iron immediately began to heat from the 260 degrees Fahrenheit I had set it to (measured via infrared thermometer afterwards) to 400 degrees Fahrenheit. In both cases according to the product manual: no heat should have been applied at all. The devices screen was never locked during my use. The temperature of this device can change by more than 100 degrees if you touch it wrong.

This change in temperature significantly damaged my hair and could have led to serious burns or fire if I had not been exceedingly careful.

productDescription:
Ninja Foodi Power Blender & Processor System.  It is black/silver in color and has typical dimensions for a home blender.

Model CO351B

UPC 1121
incidentDescription:
I purchased this Ninja Foodi Power Blender & Processor System on 5/28/21 and was injured the second time I used it on 6/2/21 while making a smoothie.  After removing the lid and while pouring, the razor-sharp blade assembly suddenly fell out of the pitcher and struck my right wrist, resulting in a deep cut needing three stitches.  I have a video showing how the blades fall out and razor-sharp the blades are, as well as pictures of my injury.  I was extremely fortunate that the blades did not hit a blood vessel/tendon/ligament and cause more serious injury.  

The design of this blender is absolutely terrible and a hazardous danger to users.  Every other blender I’ve used has blades that do not fall out and are part of the pitcher.  With this design, if you are pouring a thicker mixture (like a smoothie), you must reach into the pitcher with your hand to remove the blade assembly, causing a mess to your hand and contaminating the mixture in the process.  Otherwise, the razor-sharp blade assembly will fall out while pouring and cause an injury.  Your other option is to open the tiny spout on the lid, which does not pour out thick contents easily at all.

After getting hurt, I was initially shocked why the manufacturer wouldn’t have warnings to prevent this injury.  The fact that I had to carefully look for such warnings and instructions makes them defective.

The two warnings I could find were on the pitcher lid and the “Quick Start” instructions (I have pictures upon request).  

Its lid warning fails to comply with best standard warning practices and ANSI Z535 by failing to mention the specific consequences that result from exposure to the danger. Here, the warning only reads in incredibly small print buried among other instructions, “CAREFULLY REMOVE STACKED BLADE ASSEMBLY BEFORE POURING”.  A proper warning must explain the consequences and use design elements (such as bold print, contrasting colors, borders and underscoring for emphasis, or easily understandable pictures/symbols), for example, “BLADE ASSEMBLY WILL FALL OUT IF POURING WHILE LID IS REMOVED.”  Not mentioning the consequences and hiding the instruction in a sea of small print is like saying, “Do not eat this” in tiny letters – it fails to explain what will happen if you DO eat the item.

The “Quick Start” instructions are equally defective by putting its warning (which – unlike the lid warning – correctly states what the consequence is of failing to remove the blades while pouring without a lid) at the bottom of the page in even smaller print (see picture), FAR away from the main instructions for the blender.  The manufacturer should have used ANSI-required “embedded” warnings that are placed closely to the applicable instruction so that users immediately understand the danger associated with a particular step.  

Here, the instruction should have read (new language in ALL CAPS):

. . .  2.  Fill pitcher with desired ingredients.  Install the lid, then lower lid handle to lock in place.  WARNING:  LOCKING THE LID IN PLACE ALSO LOCKS THE BLADES IN PLACE.  UNLOCKING AND REMOVING THE LID ALSO UNLOCKS THE BLADES, WHICH MAY FALL OUT IF THE PITCHER IS TILTED TO POUR OUT A MIXTURE.

Even if an owner of the blender is fortunate enough to find, read and understand either the lid warning or the “Quick Start” instructions, the reality is that other casual users (such as guests or other family members) likely will neither see the incredibly small-printed defective warning on the lid or have the “Quick Start” instructions available to them.  The blender is therefore a hazard to both the party guest who makes a thick, slushy-type margarita, and takes off the lid to pour it out, and the visiting family member casually doing the dishes and washing the blender – both may be seriously injured by falling blades pouring out that margarita or water used to rinse the pitcher without the lid attached and blades removed.

THE MANUFACTURER HAS FAILED IN ITS DUTY TO REPORT THIS INCIDENT, NECESSITATING ME TO DO IT.

Report Update - 7/28/21

The defectiveness of the warnings and design accompanying the Ninja Foodi blender on which I was injured is established by the warnings that I believe were approved by the CPSC in connection with the Ninja BL660 series blender recall, which design is identical in terms of the removable stacked blade design.  

In short, despite knowing precisely what warning would be sufficient to users of the Foodi blender by way of the BL660 series recall, SharkNinja proceeded to use different and defective warnings.  

Attached are the warnings accompanying both the BL660 and the Foodi, and they are strikingly different, with the BL660 warning addressing several of the concerns noted in my report to the CPSC, including:
•	ANSI Embedded Warnings:  The BL660 warning has the warning language right after the appropriate instruction, whereas the Foodi warning has the warning language at the bottom of the page in smaller font away from the relevant instruction.
•	Pictograms:  The BL660 warning has pictograms showing exactly what should be done, whereas the Foodi warning does not.
•	Separate Pamphlet:  The BL660 blade warning was a separate pamphlet, calling more attention to the danger.  The Foodi warning again is all but buried and hidden at the bottom of a "QuickStart" pamphlet. If I had received a separate pamphlet, I more likely would have seen the warning and appreciated the risk.
Based on the above drastic differences in warnings, I strongly believe the CPSC should find Ninja's Foodi blender current warnings defective and deficient and order a new recall mandating inclusion of the "Stacked Blade Assembly" warnings that accompanied the BL660 series blenders.  The current warning on the Foodi blender is not embedded, located at the bottom of the page in smaller font, contains no pictograms, and does not adequately instruct users of the dangers of the defective stacked blade assembly design.

incidentDescription:
The manufacturer, Char-Griller, stated in an email that the reason why their Akorn Jr. charcoal grill caught fire and melted was because the grill exceeded its intended temperature. Amazon.com has stopped selling this model grill due to safety concerns and not due to a lack of inventory. 

On 7/4/2021 during normal operation of the grill, the grill caught fire  released toxic chemicals and partially fused into my deck. We were fortunate that I was outside putting the hot dogs and corn on the grill when I smelled a noxious odor moments before the grill caught on fire.

•	The grill’s ash pan and fire bowl emptied of any ash or residue as instructed on page C-4 of the Akorn Jr. instruction manual.
•	Standard hard lump charcoal was used, ignited with a single [REDACTED] paraffin wax lighter cube.
•	The grill’s vents were opened as instructed on page C-2 of the Akorn Jr. instruction manual.
•	Hard lump coal was placed in the center of the fire grate as described on page C-3 of the Akorn Jr. instruction manual.
•	The grill temperature did not exceed 600 degrees Fahrenheit when the unit began to melt and formed a toxic residue damaging my deck. The thermometer on the grill reaches 700 degrees Fahrenheit.
•	The product was significantly damaged and is unusable after it caught fire.
•	Damage was sustained to the grill itself and my deck

I was able to extinguish the flames using the garden hose.

incidentDescription: On November 16, 2013 we purchased a Samsung refrigerator from Lowe’s Apex, NC (store #0187) for $1,595.91. Model number RFG298HDRS/XAA. This particular model is a 28.5-cu ft French door refrigerator with Dual Ice Maker in stainless steel and has an energy star rating. The refrigerator began making a horrible noise, leaking water, not staying cool, and had ice building up in the back. We called Samsung and they scheduled repairs to be made to our refrigerator. Between April and August of 2017 we had 11 repairs, or rescheduled repairs, for our Samsung refrigerator. All of these repairs were scheduled through calling Samsung, or by the Samsung authorized technicians while they were at our house for further repairs because they were unable to repair the problem. (April 17, April 25, May 11, May 19, June 8, June 15, June 28, July 11, July 12, August 5, August 22.) Our Samsung refrigerator is now doing the same thing again, along with the upper icemaker has stopped working. We have lost hundreds of dollars’ worth of food, and thousands of dollars’ worth of medication because the refrigerator does not keep its temperature. My husband relies on his diabetic medication, and it became cloudy and no longer effective when kept in the refrigerator. This was an extremely dangerous situation! That, along with our family eating foods not being kept at safe temperatures is negligent on Samsung. Samsung has known about this defect in their product. There are several lawsuits against Samsung regarding this exact issue. This is a defect issue and Samsung needs to fix this issue.

productDescription:
Oster Blender | Pro 1200 with Glass Jar, 24-Ounce Smoothie Cup and Food Processor Attachment, Brushed Nickel from Amazon in August of 2016.

Model BLSTMB-CBF-000   Name: Oster Blender | Pro 1200
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription:
Oster Blender | Pro 1200 with Glass Jar, 24-Ounce Smoothie Cup and Food Processor Attachment, Brushed Nickel purchased from Amazon in August of 2016.  (Amazon lists it as BLSTMB-CBF-000).  10 months after purchase, the blades snapped off in my shake --which I did not know until I took a tablespoonful of my shake.  I alerted Oster and Amazon about this.  Oster removed my product review and sent a brand new replacement blender – the exact same model.  I assumed that because they sent the exact same model blender that meant the issue was an anomaly and not a design or material flaw.  

In 2021 3 ½ years after I received the replacement Oster Pro 1200 Blender, the blade broke in half in my smoothie and I did not know until I spooned the two pieces into my mouth.  Before having my smoothie, I even make a point of just checking the blade/housing.  It looked “fine” - the blades are layered so I couldn’t tell by sight that anything broke-until I found the blades in my mouth, again.  I have made smoothies every day for 3 decades using the single purpose, no frills Oster Blenders at work.  After thousands of days of daily use with plain Oster blender --- no blade ever broke.  This is a design flaw.

Another user, a mother of a 3-year-old shared same photos of broken blades coming off in the food she was about to serve her 3 year old son.  This is a hazardous design flaw.  Yet Oster continues to sell the blender on third party sites, like Amazon and [REDACTED].  I checked. They just restocked inventory on Amazon ~June 23, 2021 well after I notified them and flagged prior occurrences for me and for another user.

Oster has warning about sharp blades in their materials.  I am lucky I didn't cut my mouth either time.  Or start to swallow.  Oster knows about each incident.  I contacted them repeatedly to say this is a dangerous product.  I really  hope they  have their newer combo Blender/Food Processor evaluated in a lab to make sure the blades or the drive will not cause this to happen again to someone.

productDescription:
Char Griller propane grill. Model number 5030. Item was stated to be approximately 1 month old and was purchased new by the home owner.

Black with 2 burning areas or covers. Dimensions - 53.9 x 26.2 x 46.9 inches
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
We recently had a fire that I believe may have been caused by an out of place burner deflector on this grill. The grill was estimated to be 1 month old prior to the fire and had only been used 1-3 times prior to this fire. During my investigation, I did not find any other ignition sources that may have contributed to the fire.

We were called to a grill on fire on a deck that was connected to a single-family home. My engine company was the first to arrive. I found fire blowing from the relief valve of the propane tank connected to this grill. The fire from the relief valve was impinging on the the deck railing and communication lines running from the backyard power pole to the house. We extinguished the fire using a dry chemical fire extinguisher and cooled the railing and communication lines using a garden hose from the house. 

The homeowner stated the grill was approximately 1 month old and that they had used it 1-3 times, with no issues, prior to this fire. The person who started the grill stated it was heating up for only a couple of minutes when he returned outside and saw the fire near the propane tank. 

During my investigation, I found no other nearby ignition sources. There was a plastic handle grill scraper that was melted and laying on the floor of the deck, to the left of the propane tank. The scraper was directly below the hooks on the grill shelf that are intended to be used to hang accessories. The only other items to be damaged during this fire were the deck railing, communication lines, and the scorch marks on the left side of the grill and underside of the shelf. This area of the grill is where the propane tank was installed. 

I examined the grill and found it to be relatively clean with a minimal amount of burn food debris and grease on the inside bottom of the grill. I found the left burner heat deflector to be out of place. The deflector was still above the burner but was positioned slightly right of the burner and was rotated slightly in a clockwise position. This position would have deflected some of the heat from the burner towards the left side of the grill and towards a manufactured hole on the left side of the grill that was only a few inches away from the propane tank valve and the pressure relief valve on the tank. 

When I asked the person who started the grill about the position of the burner deflector, he was unsure what position the deflector was in prior to starting the grill. I asked the fire personnel who assisted in the extinguishment and overhaul of the scene if they moved the deflector or if they thought their extinguishment efforts may have moved the deflector. They believed their efforts had very low impact, if any, on the integrity of the grill or the items within it, and do not think the deflector was moved as a result. 

While I cannot state with absolute certainty that the position of the burner heat deflector caused this fire, I did not find any other ignition sources that could have caused this fire. I do believe it is possible that the heat deflector position along with the location of the manufactured hole in the grill side, and the location of the propane tank (fuel source), could have combined to cause this fire. I believe more testing of this product is necessary to ensure this issue does not happen again.

incidentDescription: My wife uses a Lakewood Model 5600/7 Oil-Filled Radiant Electric Heater (manufactured by Lakewood Engineering & Manufacturing Company of Chicago) at night to keep her bedroom warm. It was obvious to us that something inside failed, though it was still putting out heat.  We also opened windows in her room for cross-ventillation and put strong fans at the window sills to evacuate the strong odor.  During the removal of the heater and placing of the fan, the smell was so strong, I got nauseous and developed a headache, and my eyes began to sting and water profusely.  It took several hours of circulating fresh air into the room to make it habitable again, and many of the fabrics on my wife's bedding and clothing were saturated with the odor.  There was no obvious smoke, soot or aerosols visible.  This is the SECOND time a similar failure has happened with this exact brand and model of heater, but the first time (two years ago) the appliance was in use and we detected the smell immediately.  In both cases, we'd already been using the appliances for at least two years.

productDescription:
Name of Product: Blue Ember Gas Grills - Model # FG50069

Units: About 88,000 units in the United States (47,000 gas grills were previously recalled in October 2008) and 25,000 in Canada

Importer: Fiesta Gas Grills, of Dickson, Tenn.

Manufacturers: Unisplendor Corp., of China and Keesung Corp., of China

Hazard: The hose of the gas tank can get too close to the firebox and be exposed to heat, posing a fire hazard to consumers.

Incidents/Injuries: Fiesta has received 161 reports of grill fires, resulting in nine injuries, including two incidents of major burns on different parts of the body, six incidents of minor burns, and an incident involving temporary hearing loss.

Description: This recall involves Blue Ember liquid propane (LP) outdoor grills with model and serial numbers listed below. The cabinet style grill has two doors and is silver and black or silver and gray. "Blue Ember" is printed on the grill’s hood. The model and serial numbers are printed on a rating plate label on the rear of the grill. The rating plate label was destroyed in the fire/explosion.  The model number was provided by the home owner.
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
On Saturday night, May 22, 2021 the Fairfield Fire Department responded to a reported propane grill explosion at [REDACTED]. 

According to the homeowner [REDACTED] who is also the owner of the grill and the individual who reported the incident, he had just finished cooking his burgers and went inside to dine with his family.  He heard a loud “woosh” and saw flames in the back yard.  He evacuated his family from the house to the neighbors across the street.  When he was safely across the street he looked back and observed the size of the fire increase exponentially.  “All of a sudden it got really big.”
  
[REDACTED] recalled that he shut off the burners by closing the burner control valves but did not close the tank valve because the tank was located inside the grill cabinet and that it was too hot to turn it off.  He usually waited for the grill to cool down before closing the tank valve. 

Fairfield Fire Engine 1 arrived on scene and reported heavy fire in the back of the house visible from the street front.  Size up revealed a large gas grill had exploded in the rear yard, the relief valve from the 20 lb. propane cylinder supplying the grill had functioned, and a liquid propane fueled fire was burning from the tank which had fallen on it’s side.  Exposures included the fence, a large bush, the garage, patio furniture, and the house. 

Engine 1 crew stretched an 1 ¾ hose line to knock down the fire, cool exposures, and redirect the venting propane from the dwelling.  After the tank was cooled firefighters righted the tank, standing it upright on it’s base.  As the tank was cooled and the internal pressure dropped the relief valve reset and the leak stopped.  The tank valve was closed and the tank stabilized.  

The tank was examined and determined sound and safe for travel.  It was transported to the Fairfield Fire Training Center for safekeeping.  Initial investigation revealed that this grill was recalled by the manufacture in 2008 and 2009 for a design defect that resulted in fires similar to the one we experienced Saturday night. 

The grill was secured by the Fairfield Fire Department and transported to the Fire Training Center for safekeeping.  A fire and explosion investigation was performed, evidence collected was photographed, documented, and is currently being stored at the Fire Training Center.

Asst. Chief [REDACTED] DFM was the incident commander and also the investigating officer for this explosion.  Chief [REDACTED] is a certified fire marshal and fire investigator and has completed the FBI post blast investigation program.

I had cleaned the grill and checked the rotisserie motor to ensure that it rotated.  After putting the chicken on the grill rotisserie unit, I turned it on and put a pan underneath to catch the drippings.  I then turned on the rotisserie heating element at the back of the unit, and turned on the rotisserie motor to ensure it rotated correctly with the heat turned on.  After watching it for a few minutes, I closed the cover.  In about 10 minutes, I glanced over to see the grill and saw that it had caught on fire at the area where the plastic button is to ignite the rotisserie.  I quickly turned off the gas and cut off the cap that was burning on the grill to stop the fire.  The fire also burned the gas hose that goes to the lp tank, as well as the wire that goes from the rotisserie igniter button to the rotisserie heating element.  I feel very lucky that I saw the fire before it burned completely through the hose to the lp tank.  It might have caused an explosion or significantly larger fire.  I have pictures of the grill after the fire and fragments of the burned pieces.  I sustained some minor burns to my fingers trying to stop the fire before it spread, but just put them in water for awhile.

UPC 7852472231478
incidentDescription:
Ceiling Fan Warning – Fans made by [REDACTED] and Hubbell Incorporated are being sold by Home Depot and may break apart and seriously injure someone.  I purchased two of Hubbell’s 96-inch, indoor/outdoor fans, P250018, from Home Depot and after 1 week of use, one fan lost four of its six blades with the blades falling and damaging two classic cars.  I contacted Home Depot who opened a claim and referred it to the manufacturer, Hubbell, Incorporated.  After phone discussions with Hubbell and almost one year later, they claim no responsibility for the metal arms that hold the fan blades onto the housing breaking apart in the middle.  They claim that the thin aluminum blades hit an obstacle with enough force to break the metal arms yet also said that the leading edges of the blades do not show any sign of hitting an obstacle.  Hubbell has blamed me for improper installation but could not identify how a so-called improper installation could have caused four of six blades to come off the fan.  Interestingly, the so-called improper installation was also used on the second Hubbell fan which did not suffer any failure, and later used with three non-Hubbell fans that have operated fine for almost a year.  It is my opinion that one Hubbell fan experienced some type of metal fatigue possibly due to a bad batch of metal support arms.
I was fortunate that no one was in my shop when the fan blades came off.  Four-foot metal fan blades flying through the air could have caused very serious injury to anyone nearby.  I see reviews of this same fan where people have installed them in their living rooms.  I am sending this message so that anyone who has purchased or is considering purchasing a Hubbell fan will be aware that I experienced an extremely dangerous failure, and neither Home Depot nor Hubbell have offered to refund the purchase price of the returned fans, much less address the damages.

productDescription:
Hidrate Spark Steel Charging Cable (included charging cable also available for sale listed as HidrateSpark STEEL Charging Cable)

Model HydrateSpark Charging cable
incidentDescription: HidrateSpark is a Bluetooth-connected smart water bottle that reminds one to drink water through a smartphone-connected app.  The bottle reads the water level and calculates your water intake.  The charging cable provided does not have overcurrent or short circuit protection and is connected to the device using a magnetic connector with EXPOSED terminals.  Because it is magnetic, the connector is attracted to metal objects.  In the event that the terminals come in contact with exposed metal, an electrical connection is made and the connector then shorts the 5v power supply.  I had a bottle charging on my desk and disconnected it.  The cable came in contact with some exposed metal near my worksurface causing the power supply (phone charger to get extremely hot.  It happed again when plugged into a USB hub causing it to shut down the hub and all of the USB components on my computer including my mouse and keyboard.  Cables can be contructed with simple short circuit protection with the simple addition of a Polyfuse Resttable fuse that will disconnect the circuit due to overcurrent and reset once the fault is removed.

productDescription: Nutribullet baby bullet model number NBY50100
incidentDescription:
Product: Baby Bullet, Nutribullet model number NBY50100

This product may have harmed my child!  The washer/bushing on the blade does not completely seal the bearing.  This means that whatever grease is used in the bearing under the blade LEAKED INTO THE FOOD.  This is a health and safety hazard! I hope whatever grease was used is food safe as some of the tainted food was eaten before we caught this. 


To test/recreate - Hold the blade cap and push the bearing up as it would be during use.  If there is a gap as shown no matter how small, the food will be contaminated.  You can even see in the photo a line of the bearing grease on the blue part of the cap under the metal housing.


Likewise to test versus a control, fill the pitcher with water and blend for 30-40 seconds.  Place the water in a white dish.  If the water is CLEARLY AND VISIBILY tinted as ours was this indicates grease leaking into the food.  This is a product intended for babies, who knows what the long term impact of ingesting grease like this will be.

productDescription:
Tessan sells thru Amazon.com a large variety of 2 to 3 prong adapters. None of these have accommodations for the ground plug. 

Model TS-164US-JP

All can be deadly for the consumer. See Amazon (one example)   https://www.amazon.com/Adapter-TESSAN-Extender-Splitter-Philippine/dp/B08P6FDQYL
Another manufacturer is [REDACTED]
incidentDescription:
There are several versions of  dangerous electrical products on sale by Amazon. The devices are generally listed as “2 to 3 prong adapters”. One manufacturer is Tessan. I have tried to notify both with no response, The adapter allow a 3 prong grounded device to be plugged into a 2 prong (non-grounded) plug. There is no grounding tab to connect to earth ground, leaving the consumer at risk if the device develops an internal short. See [REDACTED] for reference: [REDACTED]
  Please note, I have not been injured, but I know of  people who have died using a 2 to 3 prong adapter w/o a grounding tab.

Which outlet I had the Delonghi Type 2507 space heater plugged in at
What I was doing at the time of the fire


The fire marshal then filed a report and it would be ready within a couple of weeks. The situation presented emotional and mental anguish to me.

Model Nutid article 60288701
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription: On Friday afternoon, March 19th, 2021, I was using the self-clean option on my IKEA Nutid (Whirlpool) 2016 convection oven on the shortest cycle available (3 hours) when I heard a loud explosion less than one hour into the cycle, presumably as soon as the oven reached temperature. The inner tempered glass door had shattered shooting hot glass all over the inside of the oven and across the floor in front of the oven. I am still finding shards of glass in distant places in my kitchen, and it continues to present a sharps hazard. The oven was less than 5 years old and was not often used and was not very dirty. In fact, the self-clean option had never been used before, although I have used self-clean options many times on other ovens. I had removed the grates from the inside of the oven and followed the instructions for the self-clean operation. The oven was not visibly damaged in any way prior to the incident. Luckily, no one was near the oven, but 500-degree Fahrenheit glass that shot out from the oven could have easily significantly injured anyone walking near the oven at the time of the incident, especially if it had been a pet or a child or if someone had been at eye level with the oven, bending down to grab a pan from a nearby cabinet or to sweep up dust from the floor. Additionally, my family has to wear shoes at all times, as we are still finding shards of glass despite having swept many times.

productDescription:
Bella Air Convection Fryer Oven 
Model: TXG WM10L - B2
Item - 14754
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
The "main" reason I am contacting the CPSC is due to the control panel to the toaster oven falling out, however, prior to this issue, there were other signs of product failure.  Paricularly, the toaster oven would autonomously change the time selected to a different time or it would go to the max temperature of 400 degrees without our input.  Additionally, when we noticed this / these issues were happening (there would be an audible beep when the change occurred - that we didn't select) we weren't able to go back to the original selection. nor were we able to adjust the time or temperature manually. The time and temperature issues of changing that occurred we thought that we did something wrong or hit the wrong button, but then it kept happening again and again, but still thought we weren't familiar with the unit and thought that it was intuitive or changed accordingly to product or internal temperature.  The most recent incident "control panel falling out / off", was something I know we didn't initiate and i know we didn't select the wrong selection.  This was a situation on the build quality and mounting quality of the main control board.  We do anything to promote the issue from happening; i.e.  Move it, clean it, bump it, drop it, slide it.  The only we thing we did is, open the door to the oven as the oven door is designed to open and then the control panel fell out hanging in front of the 380 degree oven itself  Fortunately, an adult was using the oven and knew to immediately unplug the oven and then remove what was being cooked,  Not sure my 13 year old daugheter would've known what to do or if she would've touched something that could've potentially caused her harm i.e burns or electrical shock.
To give a little info on the oven and when it was received,  my parents gave it to me for a gift for my birthday on 8/6/2020 (roughly a couple days before or after}.  Product was brand new, never used...prior to our use.   Product was placed on the counter and never moved since inception.  Overall, the Initial use of the product was great, and we were happy with it, until the snowball of issues started happening. 
This is the first time I've had to contact an organization about a product that I feel is safety concern.  I have pictures and the product available for review and testing if needed.  Please advise on the next step.

productDescription:
WASAKKY  "Pyramid Outdoor Patio Heater - 45000 BTU Stainless Steel Propane Heater with Cover, Glass Tube

Product names noted above.  Stainless steel color with 1/3 lower base consisting of solid metal pieces (4) formed around "pyramid" style structure of unit, with one side consisting of a "door" allowing access to control knob and propane tank.  The top 2/3's of unit consists of grated metal with a centrical glass tube that extends from the base burner to the top of the unit.     The brand name and the like were shown on Amazon website but little information on shipping container or packaging materials and no identifying information on the instruction manual.
productType: Gas or Lp Heaters, Other or Not Specified (392)
model: "Pyramid Outdoor Patio Heater - 45000 BTU Stainless Steel
incidentDescription: Using a recently purchased outdoor patio heater, in a pyramid design.  Using it for the fourth time at night, was trying to confirm if it was producing any discernable heat (it wasn't).  Pretty visual with the burner at the base, a steel pyramid  tower on four sides with visible glass tube from the burner to the top of the unit where the heat is presumably intended to release.  Video taping flame simply because it looked cool.  Over course of taping flame observed greater intensity burning, which I first assumed meant the unit was finally working correctly and would produce proper heat.  Then I noticed that it appeared the flame was no longer coming from the burner but  from an area around the perimeter of the burner, within the housing of the unit.  Intensity increased.  I went to shut off the gas from the plastic valve that is part of the unit.  The fire continued.  At this point I saw that the fire was coming from the end of the regulator hose that had been attached to the unit.  The rubber hose was burning slowly .  I estimated I had sufficient time to reach in and turn-off the propane canister - which I did.  The flame at the end of the regulator hose extinguished.  I had a minor burn to my hand that did not require medical attention and is fine.  There was no property damage beyond the unit itself.  The unit was on our backyard stone patio, about 10-12 feet from our home.  (I tried to file this report the night of the incident but when I went to attached the video files the system crashed and I had to start all over again.  The videos are telling and I can try to provide them separately but not with this report.  I am the homeowner and I was the only one using the unit at the time of the incident.  The prospects of injury seemed high had the fire continued to burn given that the flame was coming directly from the hose/regulator assembly that attaches to the propane tank.  The manual with the unit is titled:  "Quartz Glass Tube Patio Heater."  Oddly, the manual itself has no contact information nor does it identify any business or other entity.  The item was purchased from the Amazon.com website.  The item is listed as "Pyramid Outdoor Patio Heater - 45000 BTU Stainless Steel Propane Heater with Cover, Glass Tube"  When I spoke to Amazon to obtain the seller contact information to advise of this incident I was told that the company name was just a trade name and they did not have (or could not provide) a seller's name to me.  Via an exchange  with the Seller on Amazon platform seller simply indicated a refund had been granted and they would "check with factory."  I replied that i had specific information and was concerned about the product remaining available and in use.  No reply.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: Bissell Crosswave model 1785
incidentDescription:
Purchased a Bissell Crosswave (model 1785) in Dec of 2017. Had numerous problems with 1st machine, including giving me a small, stray electric shock when touching the revolving floor brush with machine plugged in, even though the machine was turned off. Bissell replaced the 1st machine. Second machine had several slightly-different problems in addition to the same small electric shock problem and failed within 6 months of replacing the 1st machine. Over the course of our two-year warranty from Bissell they  replaced the second and third machine under their warranty. Fortunately we purchased an extended warranty through [REDACTED] when we purchased the original Crosswave, so when the 4th Crosswave failed, we contacted [REDACTED], since Bissell's two-year warranty had just expired the month before the 4th machine failed. We expected [REDACTED] to repair our Crosswave, however [REDACTED] replaced it with a different Crosswave (our FIFTH Crosswave machine, possibly "factory refurbished", but I'm not sure of that).
This morning as I was using the latest Crosswave I thought I could smell smoke, but the machine was operating normally, so I continued to use it.  A few minutes later the Crosswave blew out a large puff of smoke, so I immediately shut it off. As soon as I shut it off I could hear a crackling sound coming from the lower part of the machine- the housing for the spinning floor brush. I then immediately unplugged the machine! 
A few minutes later after the crackling noise had stopped I removed the clear brush cover to check the spinning floor brush. Not only was the floor brush clean but it also spun freely, without any unusual resistance. In other words the floor brush was able to be spun normally.
I then plugged the machine back into a GFCI outlet, which immediately tripped. I unplugged the machine, reset the GFCI outlet and tried plugging the Crosswave in again, but the GFCI outlet again tripped off immediately.
It is now very obvious to me that our Crosswave would very likely have caught on FIRE if I hadn't unplugged it! The fact that it immediately tripped a GFCI outlet indicates that there is a serious electrical problem, which I firmly believe would have eventually caused our Crosswave to ignite and burn down our home!
This is not the first complaint that I have filed about these machines! I filed a similar complaint about the electric shock hazard, and had hoped to add this latest problem to that complaint, but I was unable to find it.
