productDescription:
https://www.renogy.com/2000w-12v-pure-sine-wave-inverter-charger-w-lcd-display/

Model R-INVT-PCL1-20111S


The Renogy 2000W Pure Sine Wave Inverter Charger can be used for multiple applications when going off-grid. A power inverter is an electrical device that transforms the DC power stored in a battery bank into standard household AC power for a user's electronic needs. This device can also charge and maintain a battery bank when connected to shore power and is now compatible with Lithium batteries. With a low transfer time, power remains uninterrupted when switching from solar to shore power. This creates clean and silent energy without having to worry about losing access to connected devices and appliances. The Renogy 2000W Pure Sine Wave Inverter Charger is a perfect back-up power source!
incidentDescription:
I purchased a Renogy inverter/charger (R-INVT-PCL1-20111S) on 11/30/2020 as part of a solar power and lithium battery upgrade for my RV.  The first unit that I purchased directly from Renogy was not working correctly, so I purchased a second one from Renogy and also a third from Amazon.  All three inverter/chargers had the same Issue.  There is a circuit within the unit called the Automatic Neutral to Ground bonding circuit that is a safety feature required by UL458 to prevent ground loops and ungrounded AC circuits in mobile homes that is not working correctly.  In fact, it is programmed to work backward, bonding when it should be unbonded and unbonding when it should be bonded.  This caused over $200 worth of damages to my RV, caused the GFCI circuit within my RV to trip constantly and posed the potential for electrocution hazard because it caused 60VAC to be present between ground an neutral of the AC receptacles.  I have since replaced the Renogy inverter/charger with a unit from [REDACTED], a competing manufacturer, which works correctly.  Renogy has denied the hazards I witnessed and has done nothing to correct the problem other than to provide a (yet to materialize) refund for returning the items.  I have lots of email correspondence with them stating UL458 compliance but at the same time discounting the need for this automatic circuit despite it being outlined in their user manual.  I have created videos of the issue:
[REDACTED]

incidentDescription: My Hamilton Beach Toaster/Convection oven Model 31103A turned itself on, in broil mode, after timer elapsed. There is a warning in the manual to not leave the product on in broil mode unattended. Additionally, the "always on" mode is essentially -1 on the timer dial, so intuitively turning the oven off by "turning counter-clockwise all the way" does not have the effect of "turning off", it has the effect of "never turning off". At least three time's I've accidentally turned the oven to "always on" mode despite intending to turn it off. The audible feedback of "off" is a bell, which sounds when the device transitions from "time remaining", through "off", into "always on" mode. Seems at least this latter design defect has been remedied by adding special grip buttons in a newer model, however the safety concern is still present on all previous not-yet-recalled models. I contacted their customer service department and they said the unit was outside warranty and offered a discount code to buy a new item.

productDescription: Room humidifier.
incidentDescription: My HoMedics UHE-WM350 Humidifier began to give off an electrical smell.  It was still running.  Since it sits on a Hardwood floor, I have an oval plant tray underneath in case of leaks.  The tray was full and slightly overflowing (maybe a pint of liquid).  I unplugged the unit.  I emptied the tanks and thoroughly dried the unit overnight.  I inspected the water channels under the tanks and the membrane for obvious cracks or leaks and found none.  I plugged the unit back in to see if it powered up.  It did.  I refilled the tanks, restarted it, and watched it carefully,  the same thing happened again.  I decided that the unit needed to be retired.  Out of curiousity,  I opened the fairing and discovered affected electronics from an unidentified internal leak.  The affected electronics were high in the compartment, and there is some sort of tray/cover that shows and ongoing leak.  The rust makes it appear that this was an ongoing issue, and a very likely fire hazard.  I contacted HoMedics via email with pictures.  They created a case number, but when I called 48 hours later, they still hadn't looked at the photos.  I informed them that I thought this unit may deserve a recall.

incidentDescription: My wife was riding her Pedego Interceptor on Jan 2, 2021 which she purchased in late 2018.  She was stopped at a traffic light and when the light turned green she began peddling when the e-bike accelerated rapidly.  It then came to abrupt stop without warning.  As a result she lost her balance and fell into the traffic lane.  Fortunately, traffic was light and she was not hit by a car.  However, she fell onto her knees and suffered pain and swelling.  She did not seek medical attention and after a few days of [REDACTED] and ice the pain and swelling subsided.  Prior to the accident the e-bike was not functioning smoothly.  The power seemed to lag and was not as responsive as usual.  Normally, she would set the power selector to the 1 or 2 position.  She thought that the battery might be nearly out, so she shifted the power selector to the highest level - 4.  It seemed to work until she came to the stop before the accident.  Additionally, in 2019, my wife experienced a similar problem with the e-bike.  When she would come to a stop, the bike's electronic pedal-assist would kick in and she could not control it.  I thought she might have inadvertently hit the throttle near the handgrip so I got on the bike and tried riding it and it happened to me as well.  We immediately took the bike into the store where we bought it and they "repaired it." I think they "reset" the computer on it and it seemed to work fine thereafter until the incident on Jan 2, 2021.  I would also wish to point out that even though the voluntary recall was posted on Sept 2020, we received no written or electronic notice of the recall.  It was only after the Jan 2, 2021 incident did I do a [REDACTED] search when I discovered the recall notice.  If purchasers of the product do not receive adequate notice of the recall, the recall is worthless.  The manufacture had all of our personal information to notify us and failed to do so.

incidentDescription: I purchased the Onewheel XR and it arrived last week. The safety flaw comes when the product either is pushed beyond the limits of product or if there is a failure in the computerized system. When either thing happens, the board immediately shuts down and the board tips forward at about 45-degree angle. This product reaches 20 mph.. As an example; please consider riding a normal four-wheeled skateboard: When it becomes necessary to bail off a skateboard, it is possible to jump off and outrun the fall because the skateboard remains level. But, the Onewheel tips forward at high speeds during a catastrophic failure (which can be caused by exceeding the product's capability-and if this happens it's at highest speed, 20+mph and suddenly it tips forward at the extreme angle and results in catapulting the rider headfirst into the groun). This is a fatal flaw as people have died because of this obvious flaw. Please refer to a huge number of [REDACTED] videos that clearly demonstrate the inherent danger associated with this terrible design flaw and safety hazard.

incidentDescription:
My furnace went out. My boyfriend and I used two Westinghouse ceramic heaters, model WHT0571, to heat my house until the furnace could be repaired. When one of the Westinghouse heaters stopped working, I gently tapped it on the floor and it started again. The second time it stopped, tapping it didn't work to restart it. It smelled like burnt plastic and never worked again.
The second heater worked well, until it, too, stopped yesterday. I tapped it on the floor, as I had done with the first heater. It started up again. A few hours later I noticed a strong smell of burning plastic. I didn't want to pick up the heater because that would shut it off. Once shut off, it might never start up again. So I pushed it across the floor a few inches. I saw a burn mark on my bathroom floor. The size of the burn mark was between a nickel and a quarter. I needed this heater to continue working to prevent my water pipes from freezing during the below-freezing temperatures we were experiencing here at night in Minnesota. So, rather than shutting off the heater, I decided to frequently push it a few inches  across my bathroom floor to prevent any one area from being burnt. I already knew my entire bathroom floor needed replacing because of the initial burn mark, and I didn't want my pipes to freeze, too.  Sometime before noon this morning, I smelled a horrible burnt plastic smell that permeated my entire house. I pushed the heater a couple inches and found the worst burn mark of all. If I hadn't been home I believe the heater would have started a fire.

productDescription: Rad Power Bikes RadRunner 1 ebike and passenger package with Kendra K-rad tire (20x3.3), manufactured and marketed by Rad Power Biles, radpowerbikes.com
incidentDescription: I purchased a RadRunner 1 from Rad Power Bikse along with the passenger package for the bike (early Nov, 2020). The bike is marketed as being able to carry up to 300 lbs of rider and  passenger load. With me (150 lbs) and a passenger (120 lbs) the bike went only a short distance before the back tire blew off the rim.  Upon changing the tube, I noticed the stock tire is rated for a maximum load of 198 lbs. The front tire is the same. Since the bike weighs about 70 lbs. a non-engineer may mistakenly believe that leaves 300 lbs for a rider and passenger. But an engineer would understand the load for bike, rider and passenger is not evenly distributed between the wheels. My estimate  is that 2/3 of bike and rider weight is on the back wheel and the entire passenger weight is on the back wheel. So, with a 150 lb rider, that leaved less than 60 lbs available for passenger weight within the load limit for the back tire. This limit is not noted in the marketing for the bike and passenger package, in fact, the marketing shows 2 adults as rider and passenger.

productDescription:
Cuisinart 2-Slice Classic Style Metal Toaster. Brushed Stainless Steel.

Model GB-CPT160P1ESP 15CE015765
incidentDescription:
Product: Cuisinart 2-Slice Classic Metal Toaster
Model: GB-CPT160P1ESP 15CE015765
Purchased online from Kohl’s, received the product on 11/24/2020

Timeline:
11/24/2020 – Received the product via UPS Shipment
11/27/2020 – Tested the product before giving it to adult family member. Testing the toaster raised safety and hazard issues.
11/27/2020 – Created and posted a 1-star review on Kohl’s website
11/30/2020 – Called Kohl’s customer service # to report issues, was given a full refund, safety issues were raised to Kohl’s customer service manager.
11/30/2020 – Called Cuisinart Customer Service # to report issues. The customer service representative told me that someone from corporate would call me within 48 to 72 hours. As of 12/4/2020, No one from the Cuisinart Brand management or Conair management has contacted me to discuss the product’s safety issues.

Safety Issues:
1)	Product seems to be drawing too much electrical current to not work on a GFI receptacle.
2)	Product isn't designed or insulated to keep the sides cool/warm to the touch, like predecessor older models
3)	Product can cause significant burns to your skin or possibly cause a fire to occur.

I've recently purchased this new 2-Slice Classic Brushed Stainless metal toaster (model CPT-160) for my son's college apartment. Before giving it to my son, I plugged it into my kitchen GFI receptacle to test it..... the same outlet that my current older 4-slice Cuisinart toaster is plugged into. With the toasting setting on 3, this new toaster wouldn't work on a GFI receptacle, the toaster levers wouldn't stay down, and the toaster would not function. I tested the toaster on several GFI receptacles throughout the house and the toaster would not function. I then tested it on a non-GFI receptacle, and the levers engaged, and the toaster worked. I then noticed a horrible chemical odor emitting from the toaster as it was being used for the very first time. After the toasting cycle was completed, I picked up the toaster and moved it back to the kitchen counter. I then noticed how incredibly hot the toaster's outer metal shell was, and this was holding it from the bottom. After placing the toaster on the counter, I felt the bottom portion of the sides and they were too hot to keep my hands there. I then did a quick finger touch to the top portion of the sides and it was extremely hot.... like a hot skillet, and if I kept my finger there long enough, I would have gotten burns on my skin. Keep in mind that this was the sides of the toaster, not the top. With my current older 4-slice version of this Cuisinart Classic Style toaster, you can safely touch the sides of the toaster during and after the toasting cycle.... you can actually hold your hand pressed to the sides near the top without getting burned, as the older version, model CPT-180 only gets moderately warm to the touch.
It seems to me that this newly manufactured toaster, model CPT-160 is drawing too much electrical current to not work on a GFI receptacle and isn't designed or insulated to keep the sides cool/warm to the touch during the toasting cycle, and the outer stainless steel metal shell is noticeably thinner compared to my older 4-slice Classic Style Cuisinart toaster.
Over the past 20+ years, I've bought two Cuisinart 4-slice Classic Style metal toasters and was always happy with the quality of this Cuisinart toaster. The predecessor, older versions were well-made.
This new 2-slice Cuisinart Classic Style metal toaster, model CPT-160 can cause significant burns to your skin or possibly cause a fire to occur. This newly manufactured product should have failed many safety tests, in my opinion, and should be removed from the market immediately. I can only assume that Conair Corporate and Cuisinart Brand management has decided to cheapen their products now, use lessor quality of materials, cut corners in the engineering and safety processes to reduce costs, and produce more revenue.

productDescription:
This was the product description as of 2019-2020 on amazon.com 

GETIHU Portable Charger, Ultra Slim 10000 mAh Power Bank, 4.8A High-Speed 2 USB Ports Battery Pack with LED Flashlight, Compatible with [REDACTED]
incidentDescription:
On Saturday, November 14th, 2020, our household had a GETIHU lithium ion battery explode in our kitchen. The battery made a pop noise and then there was a small flame. At the point where my husband tried to carry the battery out of the house (through a sliding glass door) with a spatula, it then fell on our hardwood floor and began spinning and spewing out ash and sparks. My husband was finally able to contain it by putting it in a bowl full of water. The damaged battery and two similar batteries now reside in a metal container on our driveway (concrete) out of fear of further combustion.

I want to report this because when I made the manufacturer aware of this through their customer service email, they have repeatedly tried to get me to send the damaged battery back to them in China via USPS (illegal). After my concern about illegally sending this damaged battery, they then suggested that I send it to a hub in California via UPS (I know that UPS allows for shipment of damaged lithium ion batteries under certain circumstances). However, they do not have the proper permits for ground shipping via UPS and they have not provided me with a safe container for transport. Moreover, they would be putting *my* name as the return address, making me liable for any damage that could happen en route.

GETIHU has pulled their listing of this product from amazon. com. I purchased one battery on August 18. 2018 and two similar batteries in June of 2019 (June 5 and June 22). The listing read as: "GETIHU Portable Charger, Ultra Slim 10000 mAh Power Bank, 4.8A High-Speed 2 USB Ports Battery Pack with LED Flashlight, Compatible with [REDACTED] 

After the battery exploded, I posted a note of warning to purchasers on Saturday, November14/ Sunday November 15 to the only listing for that battery that was still up on amazon. The listing has since been pulled from amazon. The manufacturer now sells another battery in its place, but I believe has not placed any warning to consumers of the batteries I purchased.

My concern is that there were many batteries of the kind I purchased that were sold in 2018-2019. I do not feel comfortable knowing that this incident happened to me and could happen to others in the future.

NOTE: The battery that combusted was unplugged/not-charging at the time and had been unplugged for over 10 hours. Previously it had been plugged into an outlet to charge overnight (necessary to get full charge) using a standard generic charging cable. In fact, two of these batteries had been charging in the same outlet with similar cables and were subsequently removed from charging after showing full charge. Only one of the batteries combusted.

After taking the food off, the grill caught fire and after reporting to traeger they noted the fire started in the fire pot due to too many pellets being distributed by the hopper. In researching, it appears traeger has a history of fire issues with their grills and I think this model should be investigated further

productDescription: Oklahoma Joe's pellet smoker grill . Model  600 Rider pellet smoker grill
incidentDescription: Pellet smoker grill caught fire. I've been in discussions with the smoker grill company about the failure of design and manufacturing of the product which has been completely manufactured in China and shipped perhaps without any oversight from them and only becoming aware of a possible problem after a great deal of failures/fires. They have only admitted that the replacement parts that failed are on back order and that they underestimated the amount of these parts that will need to be replaced. As a retired engineer and the lack of the product manufacturer to service the product I and many others have had to perform service on these products. I found the cause of the failure/fire to be the fan/auger motor assembly. The assembly motors that are found to be in these grills are not the assemblies that are outlined in their own wiring diagram. The failed units are with only one wiring terminal to operate the pellet auger feed system and none for the cooling fan on the assembly which possibly leaves the cooling fan inoperable or insufficient which leads to overheating and failure/fire of the product. They refuse to discuss my findings  or even listen to the fact that the motor they keep saying is in it in fact is not the motor in the product. I've even sent pictures showing this to be true. They have only expressed that they need a  great deal of replacement motor assemblies but thats where the discussion ends.  My findings and their refusal to talk about this is in my professional opinion is a clear attempt to stonewall for liability and or safety recall reasons.  In my professional career I worked directly with liability concerns as an engineer and their reactions and denials to answer my questions reflect nothing more than a coverup of perhaps thousands of defective/dangerous units.

productDescription: USB Type C Charger, ZeroLemon Removable 45W 4-Port USB C Charging Dock + 1 Removable USB Type C Travel Adapter for [REDACTED] and More-White
incidentDescription:
Purchased this Zerolemon charger on sale $6 on Amazon: USB Type C Charger, ZeroLemon Removable 45W 4-Port USB C Charging Dock + 1 Removable USB Type C Travel Adapter for [REDACTED]

Model # Y1010

There was a weird smell. My type C charging cable that I bought at the same time was hot. When I tried to disconnect it it had melted at the plugin. I pulled the plug from the outlet. 
It ruined my cable and also charred the connecting port on my phone. 

Perhaps the most disturbing part is that Amazon scrubbed that item from their site. They show most items even if they are not available for purchase but this item is nowhere to be found except in my order history. While it's not an admission of negligence, it's certainly suspect. When I called customer service they seemed familiar with the product bought me new cables and a new phone and refunded the $6 I spent on the shady charger.

Had I been asleep this could have killed my family. I can only assume it was the wrong voltage or amperage.

We are all in serious danger if Amazon can curate information about dangerous products it sells. If there were reviews for that product I'm sure my story would be one among many. I wouldn't be surprised at all if this product caused serious injuries and/or death.

productDescription: Ninja Foodi 64 oz Hot & Cold Blender with 1.4 kW motor & glass pitcher
incidentDescription: . I purchased a Ninja Foodi 64 oz blender [Model No HB152] and used it for ~6 months until the glass pitcher exploded in my face on 10/10/20. At the time of the incident, the blender was about 1/3 full & contained cold liquids, ice cream, chocolate chips & ice. This blender has a powerful 1400 W motor, but does not have speed variability finer than low, medium & high. Because of this lack of speed variability, the blender delivers its full force to the blades as soon as its turned on, and that force can be transferred to the contents inside. I was unfortunate to discover this when an averaged-sized ice cube was accelerated into the thick glass pitcher with so much force that it exploded. I was hit with glass in the chest, and glass shards & milkshake continued to fly all over the kitchen (the blades continued to spin until I unplugged it). I am so so thankful that I didn't lose my eyesight. A well-meaning customer service rep today told me that I was not eligible for a refund, & if I paid for shipping I could receive a replacement of the same model.

incidentDescription:

incidentDescription:

I believe based on when I saw it through the virtual visit it was this one "Formula Pro Advanced Baby Formula Dispenser"
It was black and white

Lot #: NWY-137
Item #: FRP0046
Made in October of 2018
model: I don't have this - can contact family if needed
incidentDescription:
At a child's 12-month well exam, his weight velocity had increased exponentially with no known cause. He had started to gain velocity in his weight around 6 months of age. At that time, there was no concern, as babies frequently change their curve and then curve off again as they get more active (crawling, walking, etc.). When I saw him for the first time, at his 9-month visit, the weight gain increased in velocity again. He was an overall happy and healthy infant, with a couple of minor developmental delays (again small concerns), and I didn’t see any major issues, so we just discussed proper nutrition for an infant and the division of responsibility, a common concept to assure there is no overfeeding, as well as mixing formula properly, etc. I expected his weight to curve off at our next visit. I told the parents if there were concerns before then, we could do another weight check, but they didn't come in sooner. He started working with a birth-to-3 program for the developmental delays in between the time I saw him at his 9mo and then at 12mo when he weighed in at 40 lbs. I ran a huge panel of labs to check for metabolic disorders, and the only abnormality was mildly elevated triglycerides (the lipid associated with consuming too much sugar). I was certain, at this point, the parents were either lying to me, and he was overfeeding (based on these results) or some piece of information was definitely missing. At the 12mo visit, they claimed he was taking 24oz of 20kcal formula and ~8oz purees per day (he wasn’t very into solids yet and was set for a feeding evaluation with the birth-to-3 program about this soon). I scheduled a virtual visit with them and had dad take me into the kitchen and show me the preparation of the formula to assure they weren’t making a mistake and giving him formula that is too highly caloric. As he was walking into the kitchen, he mentioned that for the past 6 months or so (the first time we noted his weight velocity increasing), they have been using the Baby Brezza. They originally bought it for night feeds, so they wouldn’t have to mix formula at night, but it was so convenient, they started using it all the time. He showed it to me, and I did a quick google search and found a couple scattered reports of inaccurate formula to water ratios. I advised them to immediately stop using this device and to come back in 1 month for a weight check. For the first time since his 6mo well exam, his weight curved off to what is considered a normal curve showing that this was almost certainly the cause of his weight gain and very likely why he hasn’t been interested in solids (he was too full to be interested). He has likely been receiving very highly caloric formula for >6mo. After further research, I found out there is a class-action lawsuit against the company for the opposite complaint of not enough formula to water causing failure to thrive in babies. This is an incredibly unsafe product if it is not able to be consistent with its water to formula powder ratio. Failure to thrive and excessive weight gain causing developmental delays (e.g. this child can't get from lying down to sitting at 12 months of age due to being too obese) are some of the less serious outcomes I could imagine. If a child has the wrong formula to water ratio, they can have kidney failure, receive too much potassium causing their hearts to stop, etc. I am incredibly fearful of this machine as a health care provider. 

For the estimated date below, I just went back about 6 months from when he came in for his 12mo visit, but I'm not sure when they bought the product.

productDescription:
Selectblinds.com 

Window blinds - cordless, pleated, "espresso" color.  Order information from SelectBlinds.com:
3/8" Cordless Light Filtering Shades, 38 5/8 W" x 61 H, Mount Type: Inside
productType: Window Shades, Venetian Blinds or Indoor Shutters (638)
incidentDescription:
My family has window blinds from SelectBlinds.com installed on almost every window in our home (20+ windows).  All installations used the provided hanging hardware, and followed directions as indicated from SelectBlinds.com.  All of the products were purchased approximately 4 years ago.

On the evening of Monday, September 14, 2020, my husband and I were sitting in our family room when a loud explosive/bang startled us.  A large metal spring (approx. 9 inches long and 1 inch thick) was ejected from the top of the window blind, broke through a plastic end cap on the product, and hit the window trim and opposite wall with great force.  The malfunction resulted in plastic fragments strewn about the room, and of course, a broken window covering.

Upon examination, we surmised that the large metal spring was under tension when the plastic "hook" that was holding it in place cracked and released it.  The potential for this malfunction, and the force at which the spring hit part of our window and wall is a major safety concern.  We have two small children who play in this room often, and we have the same product installed in almost every room of our home.

I immediately contacted SelectBlinds to notify them of the incident, and they replied that their Quality Control department would look into it and get back to me.  I found this response to be lacking and untimely.  

I truly hope that there is a way to quickly notify all customers of the potential for this to occur, the safety risk, and the danger to children for a significant injury.

productDescription: Glass counter top electric kettle
incidentDescription:
Here is my email to the manufacturer:


I just purchased a GK-17 ViewPro 1.7L electric kettle from Bed Bath & Beyond.

I ran the 3 full kettle cleaning cycles you recommend.

The kettle never automatically shut off as it is supposed to.  I let it run for multiple minutes at full boil and had to shut it off manually each time.

I tried it 3-4 more times, with varying levels of water, and still the same problem.

I finally tried it with very little water in it, perhaps 1/2”, and it shut off automatically.

Subsequently, after having done that test, it now shuts off automatically with any amount of water in it!  I fixed it, inadvertently, but it makes me wonder if there is an underlying defect to be concerned about.

The date code on the bottom says 1920 B.

I supposed in a sense it passed the safety test because it did shut off with a mostly empty pot.  If it never shuts off when it has a reasonable amount of water in it, then it’s just wasting energy by continuing to boil pointlessly.  I do wonder if like many products, it has a “duty cycle” where it is not designed to run continuously without a resting period?  If it is not designed to handle continuous running, then perhaps this is a potential safety issue all the way around.

In any case, I would suggest sharing this information with your QC and engineering department.

It is wayyyyy too easy to inadvertently release the baskets and the warning appears to be inadequate on user manual. We are both smart people and my girlfriend went to culinary school for 2 years and this was NOT AN OBVIOUS HAZARD.

The only warning I found in the manual was "use caution when shaking basket" and on page 8 warning #9 "extreme caution must be used when moving unit containing hot oil or other hot liquids"


There were no warnings about the inadvertent separation.
There was no pictogram showing we could be splashed with hot oil.

If we had a cat or a kid nearby it would have scalded them badly. We were lucky we were adults who just got sprayed on our legs -  it sucked a lot but aside from skin discoloration and the need to use ice packs we were fine a week later. 

I was horrified. Here are some simple solutions:
(1) how about a red release button so people are more conscious of the release potential
(2) how about a lock or button cover to prevent the thumb from accidentally releasing
(3) a specific warning would be useful about the need to not slip and hit the button and to keep the basket on a level surface.

I have emailed this to Costco and Customer Service. Hopefully this changes before someone else gets burned more badly.

My husband has had to force defrost the ice maker to keep the lines from clogging as it's too costly to have the Samsung technicians keep coming to our home to fix it. This item should be recalled as the engineering design defects are causing issues for many people. It is completely unacceptable that Samsung manufactures and sells a product they knowingly cannot repair. They have been aware of this for years but clearly they do not care about the consumer or the safety of its product. As consumers, we need to band together to voice our concerns about Samsung's fraudulent manufacturing practices.

productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
On or about June 5, 2020 I purchased a Cuisinart 3-1 5-burner grill from Walmart in Delavan, WI. The unit had been fully assembled by Walmart. The advertised price was $347 plus tax which I paid in cash. A Walmart employee named  -------helped load the unit into my vehicle.

I spent the next several days trying to absorb all the warnings and instructions contained in the Cuisinart Grill Operator booklet. I also stapled the purchase receipt into that booklet.

On June 9, 2020 I returned a propane tank to the Clinton, WI grocery store because it was malfunctioning in that it was not producing any gas. The store owner/mgr [REDACTED] provided me with a replacement tank. Both tanks were furnished by the [REDACTED]. Because it was starting to rain from the hurricane Cristobal which was just entering our area, I had the grill about 2-3ft. in the garage. I set the tank on the tray underneath the grill and connected it to the grill regulator. A soap test on the newly connected tank did not indicate any leak.

The new tank produced gas and all 5 burners on my grill ignited immediately.
The side burner, however, would not ignite. Per the instruction booklet, I proceeded to let the grill burn for 10–15 minutes. There was no obvious sign of any problem. I periodically checked the temperature of the grill on the closed lid thermometer and it eventually reached 500 degree+/-. At about
12 minutes, I decided to shut it down by turning off the tank valve first...
per the instructions. When I bent down, I saw yellow flames quietly burning in the area of the tank connection to the grill hose. I attempted to turn off the tank valve but it was burning hot.

I ran to the house to get oven mitts but by the time I returned, there was now a roaring jet of orange flame under the grill. I tried repeatedly to turn off the valve which required about 15-20 rotation attempts.  But when I succeeded, a new jet of flame blew out of the valve and the grill was fully involved in flames. I then managed to pull the grill out into the driveway and again ran to the house to call the [REDACTED] Fire Dept. By this time there was a loud siren sound coming from the tank which my wife heard from inside the house. She thought it was a tornado warning. I told her not to worry – it was just a propane tank fixing to explode.
It was now pouring rain. The fire dept. arrived and decided to spray water on the grill while they let the tank burn out from a distance. The chief in charge was [REDACTED NAME] who took my information for his report. As he talked to me in the garage, he asked if I was hurt because he could smell burnt human hair. I then realized I had burned my right arm and there was some pain.

I went to the Walmart store in Delavan on 6/10/2020 and after some difficulty, conveyed this information at 9:55 a.m. to “[REDACTED]” who said he was the assistant mgr. The booklet including my cash receipt had been sitting on the grill and most of it was consumed in the fire. I showed him my small bag of charred remains and he stated he could look up the purchase in their system. I gave him my contact information and said he might want to contact Cuisinart but he said we should wait for the fire report. He identified [REDACTED] as the actual store manager but said he wasn’t there.

I now have the fire report.

I unplugged the electrical device and saw a seriously corroded electrode. Only one electrode of the plug was impacted. The ground and the other electrode were fine. The corroded electrode was black and the plastic was melted around it. The area around the electrode was built up and not flat anymore.. The cord was also bent, suggesting that maybe the inside the cadding the wire was melting away.

When I unplugged the appliance.ade in China. I purchased two of these Emerson dehumidifiers from Brandsmart USA in West Palm Beach, Florida. Now I am concerned they are a fire hazard.

Taken from Amazon's description of this item as shown when I purchased it. Since I filed a complaint with them, this has been taken off of Amazon's site.

Model F-531
incidentDescription: I purchased an Opolar F-531 rechargeable fan from Amazon on June 12, 2020.  I charged it using a USB cable that plugged into a wall receptacle.  I would charge it during the day and use the fan at night.  Wednesday, July 30, 2020 approximately 15 or 20 minutes after turning it on, there was an explosion about 2 feet away from our bed at about 12:15am.  Smoke instantly filled the room and we eventually discovered that the fan had exploded, burning the rug it was on, shooting a piece of metal about 6 feet away which scorched our wood floor and several minutes later we realized that one battery was missing and found it under our bed.  It was searing hot and had burned down about 1/8" into our wood floor.  I have photos of the damage.  The battery must have shot up in the air from the floor and come across our nightstand, as a stuffed animal I had on there got burned as well.  There are a few small burn marks on our wall and soot covered much of the room.  This explosion was very violent and we are lucky that a fire did not start and that no one got hurt and that the damage is repairable.  We do not want this to happen to any one else. I did contact Amazon yesterday (July 30, 2020) and they have taken this item down from their site.  But we imagine that these batteries are in use in other items.  If we had not been home when this happened, it could have burned our house down and killed our cats.  I am shocked that these batteries can explode like this and are in use in many items.  These could seriously injure people, animals and property.  I understand the instances are rare, but the fact that they can occur seems reason enough to not allow these batteries to be in use. I feel that there should certainly be a recall on these batteries.

incidentDescription:
My wife,[REDACTED] and I purchased two (2) Samsung Galaxy Note-9 phones in November, 2018 from Best Buy in Lakeland, FL.  We entered into a two-year contract with Sprint. We each received a charger. During the week of July 20, 2020, my wife began getting shocked while she was talking on phone, with the charger plugged in. 

After examining the charger, we discovered that the wire was frayed, with the copper wiring completely exposed. My wife reached out to Samsung Corporation who only informed her that the phone and charger were no longer under warranty. However, when my wife put me on the phone, I informed the person, at an off-shore call center, that this was an existing hazard Samsung needed to address. 
 
I requested that someone in authority call me back or else I would file a grievance through the Consumer Product Safety Commission. I did receive a return call the following day, from a woman who said I should speak with someone from their "Product Liability" office. I informed this person that I did not have the time since the return call was received before the close of business. I wanted to reach out to you first before contacting Samsung. As previously stated, my wife sustained several painful shocks. Please note she has a formerly diagnosed cardiac condition that necessitated her being placed on disability nearly a decade ago.

productDescription: HP Envy X2 Detachable PC13  tablet silver with detachable keyboard
incidentDescription: We own an HP ENVY x2 detachable PC 13 tablet.  For several weeks before the incident my wife mentioned that her touch screen seemed to be pulling away from the body of the tablet.  We didn't pay too much attention thinking perhaps the adhesive was loosening and causing this to happen.  One day during the week of July 10, 2020 I happened to be walking past the tablet which was on my wife's desk and saw if from a side view.  I was stunned at how far the screen was pushed out from the body of the unit.  I was surprised the screen hadn't cracked yet.  I told the wife to immediately stop charging and/or using the tablet because clearly something has seriously gone wrong with the unit and I felt it was no longer safe to use.  I wasn't certain it was but i suspected the battery.  I disassembled the unit and indeed one half of the battery had swelled to the point that the vinyl covering the battery was very taunt.  Before I disturbed anything further I took several images of the battery still installed in the unit to show how distorted and expanded the battery was.   I then removed the original battery and placed it a safe area in the event the chemical/electrical process that was causing the defect would continue and possibly pose a safety issue.  At this point I purchased another OEM battery.  I replaced the battery and was able to gently push the screen and effected component back to there original position before the battery issue happened.  I didn't know how to dispose of the battery so i kept it for a period of time.  On Monday July 27, 2020 I was curious about what was causing it to swell thinking it was some sort of gas.  I wanted to release it before I deposed of it thinking it could cause an issue for some else if it wasn't released.   Not knowing what to expect I took it out to my drive.  At the urging of my wife I put on goggles and a face shield.  I took an [REDACTED] knife and punctured a small hole with the tip of the blade. I expect a small release of the gas inside.  Instead what happen was some sort of chemical reaction (i suppose) but it quickly got out of control I has shocked at the smoke, gasses and heat generated from this.  After a short time and after most of the smoke died down i thought to record what had happened using my phone. Even this video shows it still smoldering and melting.  If this has happened while still in the unit when it contacted a piece of material that punctured that vinyl covering or the battery exploded on it own the results could have been disastrous.  One or more of the following would or could have happened.  The gasses expelled are so toxic, it could in an enclosed area like a room in a house cause physical harm.  Or, since it would still be in the unit the heat could not have dissipated as it did outside of the unit and cause a fire.   With obvious results.  I checked the HP web site to see if this was a unit that was part of the recalled ones for defective batteries.  I was not.  Clearly, this situation with either this unit or these units collectively need to be investigated further.  This obviously is potentially a serious safety issue.  My hope is this bring attention to the matter.

Sadly, if Chef's Choice had used a more robust/appropriate plastic for the handle -- something like glass-reinforced PA 6/6 or Zytel (pennies more per unit), there wouldn't be a problem.

The metal stem that leads from the front steering tire up into the handles that give the rider steering control is secured using a very thin piece of plastic. Both the wheel stem and handle bar assembly are metal. Once this small plastic bracket breaks from use (my sons scooter broke after just 5 months of use while he was riding on a public sidewalk and was fortunate enough the scooter veered off into grass opposite the moving traffic in the street) the rider completely loses steering of the scooter. This can have very bad consequences for the rider considering these are usually ridden on public sidewalks and roadways sharing space with or in very close proximity to traffic. I have contacted the company with the issue and all they want to do is replace the plastic bracket with a new one. This is a serious design flaw that needs corrected with an appropriately designed metal bracket to ensure riders maintain control of the scooter at all times. The scooter has a folding design which likely leads to the stressing of the plastic bracket and eventual breakage. That and use of the scooter over sidewalks and streets with bumps and expansion joints which transmit energy up through the wheel into the bracket that is clamping the steering column into the wheel stem also stresses the plastic bracket.

incidentDescription: I purchased a Samsung French style 4 door refrigerator. The ice maker in the refrigerator portion started icing up and became non functional in less than 1 year. It was replaced under warranty 1 time but continued to freeze up over and over. Once the ice maker is frozen the refrigerator continues to ice up on the back wall Twin-Cooling system which freezes food against the back of the refrigerator, making it unsafe to consume. Once the back wall is frozen solid the drain freezes up too that forces water and ice under the crisper drawers, which affects the temperature of food stored in the drawers now sitting on an ice flow. When it gets full of water and can hold no more, it flows out onto the floor creating a fall risk. There are numerous Samsung service bulletins out to repair technicians about this know design defect. It is not a warranty issue which consumers hear ad nauseam when requesting assistance for these problems. This affects appliances dating back to at least 2009 and yet Samsung continues to sell the same defective refrigerators to unknowing consumers. The last stage of this flawed product is the ice maker fails in the freezer compartment, then the freezer itself fluctuates temperature regulation, periodically raising enough the contents start to thaw and/or then refreeze - another consumer safety issue. There is an LED display on the outside of the refrigerator that is to reflect the internal temperatures. It is no where close to being accurate as verified by placing thermometers inside the compartments. Another failed safety component, as I have become sick eating food I thought was cooled to a safe edible temperature. Numerous telephone calls, chats online, text message, reports to Better Business Bureau, New Jersey Consumer Affairs, Missouri and New Jersey Attorney Generals and finally the Federal Trade Commission have not address the problem for me, however it seems there are a few lucky people that are getting full refunds of purchase price.

productDescription: Propane Smoker built by Masterbuilt.  Model MPS 230S
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
This documents serves to capture an incident that occurred on Saturday, April 4th in 2020 with a Propane smoker from Masterbuilt.  The product I was using was the MPS 230S Propane Smoker.
On the evening of April 4th, at approximately 6:30 PM MT, the brisket and pork butt I was smoking  was taken off the smoker and into the house to rest the meat.
When I came back outside to close the smoker down, I re-opened the area of the smoker body where the meats are cooked.  Just as I was moving to close the door to to shut off the gas to extinguish the flame, the "Water Tray", which was filled with drippings from the meat that was just cooked, apparently sloshed slightly.  This cause some drippings to fall down onto the flame directly below, which was covered only with the Wood tray, which also is made to burn wood during the process.  This ignited and send a larger flame and caught the entire "Water Tray" on fire, which erupted into a very large flame and enveloped my entire face.  
I threw myself back away from the flame swatting to put it out and try to keep it from my face.  The grill, which was positioned 9 feet behind me and was not on at the time, broke my fall.  My wife, [REDACTED], was in the kitchen at the time and saw the eruption of flame and immediately came outside to see what was happening.
The entire smoker was instantly on fire.  My reaction next is probably what saved the entire situation from getting completely out of hand.  I moved toward the tank and shut the valve to stop the flow of propane gas.  I, then, removed the line and took the tank away from the smoker while the smoker was still fully engulfed.
My wife helped me get the entire flame out from the smoker after we took both the wood tray and grease pan out of the smoker completely.  We put a large pan lid from our kitchen on both trays in order to extinguish the flames, as we knew grease fires cannot be put out with water.  So, I know we did the absolute right things to get the situation under control.
Next, because she is a medical professional, she took me upstairs to look at the burns closely.  In her professional opinion, and because of the Covid-19 illness that was rampant during this time, she put some burn gel (aloe) over the areas that appeared affected, specifically the nose, cheeks and lips.  She applied it very liberally to help slow the burn process.  Since it was so late on a Saturday night, she thought it would be best to avoid the visit to the ER(again, because of Covid), unless symptoms got significantly worse.  So, we agreed we would monitor the burns carefully.  All went well, and when Monday morning approached,  I called my doctor as soon as the office opened and got an appointment for that afternoon.
My doctor agreed it was a really good call to not visit the ER and that everything [REDACTED] did worked wonders and prevented further damage to my face.
My doctor, then, prescribed some better face cream(Silver Sulfadiazine) with antibiotic and soothing properties to intensify the healing process.  
In the week I have been taking the cream it has improved the appearance significantly.  I am still in some pain from it, but it has come a long way, so far, and I hope the healing continues for it.
While my physical appearance has healed, there are lingering feelings on my nose and lips that I was told may take more than a year to fully heal, so time will tell on those.
My analysis of the product is that it is seriously flawed in 2 critical areas.  
First, the "Water Tray" is not deep enough to hold enough of the drippings that fall into it during the cooking process.    
Second, there is nothing to prevent or divert any drippings from the tray from reaching the flame below and causing it to ignite into such a monstrous fireball.
My situation is one that is only able to be shared because of how I reacted at the moment the flame erupted.  And, because I have more than 20 years of smoking experience, I was more prepared than most people would have been in this situation.  My exposure to the flame would have been significantly different with a much more catastrophic end result had I not reacted as fast as I did.
I truly don't want another person to have to endure the trauma this incident has caused me.  
And, again, my nose and lips will continue to heal, I hope, so I will eventually be fine from this incident.  
I am still very outraged at this incident and wish to have it resolved as soon as possible.  The company, Masterbuilt, has not offered an acceptable agreement on it, and they seem to be more concerned about my signing a form agreeing not to sue them.  They offered to replace it with a similar product to the cost of what I paid, excluding tax.  But, the features on the product they offered are the same, so I fear it could potentially happen again.
I have, since, purchased a new propane smoker from a different company, which is much safer and has a much larger "Water Tray" and has shields the trays below to deflect anything that may potentially fall toward the direction of the flame.    
I have disposed of the old smoker, so it is no longer in my possession.  The old one was unusable because of the amount of damage it suffered in the fire to the inside walls.
I would like this product investigated for the safety benefit, and I wish to have them pay me a reasonable amount for the suffering I've endured from using the product and trying to reason with them with no success.

productDescription: Baby Brezza Formula Dispenser
incidentDescription: I am a Primary Care Pediatrician practicing in Longmont, CO.  A 2.5 month old baby I care for in my practice was failing to gain weight for several weeks.  I admitted him to the hospital for Failure to Thrive.  After extensive evaluation, it was discovered that the source of his poor weight gain was improper mixing of his formula via the Baby Brezza machine the parents were using at home.  Per the Nutritionist's calculations, the machine was mixing the formula at 60% of the appropriate caloric strength, so he was receiving quite dilute formula.  This is exceedingly dangerous for a young infant, as it can lead to complications such as severe electrolyte imbalances and seizures in addition to restricted growth.  Per the parents' report, there was another baby on the hospital floor at the same time with the same issue with this machine.  It appears there have been many complaints and similar medical complications reported due to this machine working improperly in the past few years. incidentDescription:
Three times since we purchased our toaster on May 9, 2020 the toaster got into a dangerous state.  Each time the incidents occurred we were toasting bagels.  After several minutes we noticed smoke coming out of the toaster and the toaster had not automatically stopped.  Clicking the 'Cancel' button had no effect - the elements stayed on and the bagels continued to burn.  The only way I could get the toaster to stop was to unplug it.  The toaster itself became *extremely* hot to the touch, and there was a distinct smell of burning toaster parts (perhaps plastic, rubber, or metal).

After the toaster cooled down it appears the problem is that the metal piece the bread or bagel sits on gets dislodged easily and stuck on the inside of the toaster itself.  This must prevent the toaster from turning off and popping up the bagel/toast.  We had an older model that also had the metal piece dislodge occasionally, but it didn't prevent the toaster from turning off (it just made it hard to get the toast out).

I feel this is an extremely dangerous appliance.  If we had walked away or been distracted, there is no doubt the bagel would have caught on fire (it was very close).  I also am made to wonder what would happen to the toaster unit itself if it were left on indefinitely.

productDescription: "Rome Original Pie Iron"
incidentDescription:
"Rome" Brand Pie Iron.Manufacturer Code:  "Rome's #1605 Pie Iron Double Cast iron"  SKU # 29794-16059

Usage:  Pie Iron has two sections which fold over each other to hold a sandwich while the entire utensil is placed over a camp fire.  The cast iron sections had supported by two 24" metal handles.  The handles are supposed to be attached by roller pins press-fitted through holes in the cast iron to secure than handles.  The handles must support the iron as it is lifted out of the campfire, since the iron is red-hot from the camp fire.

One set of handles was unsecured, the roller pins were not installed during manufacture.  The other handle set was secured by roller pins but those pins were of a size which did not permit a solid press fit to secure the handle.

While lifting the iron from the campfire, one handle immediately detached out of the capture hole and the heavy iron rotated around the other handle.  This caused the iron to open and one side of the red-hot iron dropped onto the ground, very close to the foot of the person cooking over the fire.

This is a very dangerous manufacturing defect; post-manufacture quality control should have caught this deficiency.

model: Toastmaster Electric Coffee Maker 12 Cups TM-127KCM
incidentDescription: I bought an electric 12 cup Toastmaster coffee maker with a swing out basket from Dollar General ( https://www.dollargeneral.com/toastmaster-electric-coffee-maker-12-cups.html ). I ran a brew cycle using only water as the manufacturer recommended and had no problem. However, when I tried to brew coffee in it, the coffee did not flow out from the basket fast enough and overflowed the filter, nearly spilling out the top of the basket. I thought the coffee was just taking a long time to brew and decided to utilize the pause feature (meaning, the coffee is supposed to stop coming out of the basket while you poor a cup) but the coffee continued to flow from the basket. I wasn't expecting that so I opened the top and saw that the reason my coffee carafe was only half full was because it was all still in the brew basket. I emptied the carafe and basket and proceeded to attempt cleaning the grounds out of the basket by pouring water through it with the carafe in place. The water barely came out of the bottom, letting me know that the basket design was defective. It does not allow free flow of the liquid from the basket to the carafe, nor does the flow stop when you remove the carafe allowing the plunger to spring back into place. It appears that the weight of the wet grounds, combined with the heat of the coffee, causes the rubber stopper and/or spring to fail. This is dangerous in so many ways. First, you have the overflow hazard, then there is the burn/spill hazard when trying to utilize the pause feature. Then there is the added hazard of an electrical short if the liquid enters the bottom of the appliance when the carafe is removed.

It was plugged in to charge a phone, where it has been for the past year without incident. There had been no damage to the cord, and nothing was done differently than any other night. My wife went to plug her phone in, and the cord sparked from the middle, and got red hot, causing my wife to drop it to the floor. After hitting the floor, the cord sparked one more time, before exploding and catching fire. The explosion happened in the middle of the cord, and sent pieces of red hot metal across the room, melting my carpet and causing spot fires outside of the main fire where the cord is. 

Due to the cord being completely metal, if the middle of the cord is on fire the rest of it will be red hot. Unfortunately I was not able to pull the cable out of the wall without grabbing the cord, and was burned on my hands pulling it from the wall. Luckily they were small burns and did not require medical attention. After the cord was unplugged from the wall, I was able to douse the cord with a heavy blanket and put out the main fire. The piece of shrapnel that followed the explosion landed about 4 feet away, and was still red hot when I used pliers and a knife to cut out my carpet and remove the piece that was smoldering in the foam carpet pad. 

The cord was plugged into an indoor certified extension cord, with 1 other item (a lamp) plugged into that as well. There were no problems with the lamp, nor the extension cord.

productDescription: Samsung refrigerator, We have a Samsung refrigerator, Model #RF31FMESBSR that we purchased in 2014.  We couldn't figure out why our milk, fruit, meats and other parishables were going bad before the sell by dates and liquids seemed cool, but not cold when the temperature was set at 38 degrees (which is what the display showed)  We lowered the temperature and monitored it for several days with a digital thermometer.  The range was between 45 and 60 degrees.  Our food was spoiling and during this time with the Coronavirus, we could not go out all the time to get fresh food.  We stocked up on several items that all had to be thrown out.   In addition, the panel on the back of the fridge and the coils were frozen with ice coming through the hole.   My main concern was my food going bad.   I contacted Samsung asking for a service call, and they were not only rude, but indicated there was nothing that could be done by them because it was out of warranty.   We finally had to purchase a new refrigerator and we moved the Samsung in our garage for the time being.  The freezer portion still works but that is it.  I have done my homework, followed many social media sites with thousands of people have the same issue.  This is a safety issue.  This is not a warranty issue, it is a known design defect. The sensor that shows consumers what the temperature is inside the fridge is sending false and misleading temperature readings.  This is allowing people to think their food is being kept at a safe temp, when in fact it is not.  My son got extremely ill from drinking milk that went bad because of this defect.  Samsung needs to acknowledge their design flaws that allows the digital temp display to show normal safe temps yet in the refrigerator temps are actually 10-20 degrees higher.  In addition to these issues, the ice maker would no longer made ice and was frozen shut and could not be removed.   I did all the resets, unplugged and let defrost, then plub back in only for it to work for a day and then again freeze up.  Mind you this only allowed the ice maker to work again...the temps were still much much higher then what was indicated on the panel. On of the social media sites indicates that Samsung has refunded over $3MM to consumers because of these known defects, yet they wouldn't even send out someone to try to repair ours. If they are not going to offer me a FREE service call including any parts that might need to be replaced, then we should be refunded for the purchase of this faulty refrigerator, we should also be reimbursed for all of the food we lost.

productDescription: Wet Dry Vacuum Cleaner
incidentDescription:
RE: Vacmaster VF408 Wet Dry Vacuum by Cleva-na.com

This concerns use of the vacuum to pick up dry items. Due to the fact that the cord is not three-prong grounded type, I have not used it to pick up liquids.

Vacuum builds a static charge so large that:
a) When one touches the vacuum, the discharge is strong enough to move one's arm
b) The unit must be touched several times to completely discharge the built up charge.
     Example: If I use an alligator clip on a plastic part and touch a grounded surface, such as
       a cold water pipe or receptacle outlet ground prong, the spark is large and visible in
      daylight. The clip must be held on the grounded item for several seconds before the
      charge is completely dissipated.
c) The charge is also evidenced by the large amount of airborne dust, hair and lint that
    clings to the unit.
d) On one occasion, gypsum dust which was attracted to, and clung to, vacuum exploded in
    a small "pop".

If I leave a cord clipped to the vacuum body with the other end solidly grounded, no charge builds up.

Thank You for taking time to review this report. I appreciate your efforts to ensure safe products.

productDescription: Blender
incidentDescription:
I’m writing to you in desperation.  I have tried to work through Magic Bullet’s customer service department, but have not gotten any assistance.

I believe my daughter may have been ingesting fine metal dust as a result of using the Magic Bullet.  We had been using the Magic Bullet blender to make her daily fruit smoothies for years.  The blender had a fine, shiny metal dust accumulating at the bottom of the base but I didn’t think anything of it because I thought the cup was self contained.  It was bothering me, so I decided to run water in the blender as a test and the water came out grey with silver particles floating in it.  We tested the particles with a magnet and it stuck to it so we know it is a metal.

I immediately called the Magic Bullet company demanding to know what the metal is comprised of- it’s the inside metal housing inside the black plastic base where the blade shaft rotates that is deteriorating (not the blade itself).  I have been told by a product specialist that they are in the process of contacting the manufacturer but we have not heard back yet. The amount of time it’s taking to get basic information is not acceptable, especially when the request is relating my child’s health.  My child is undergoing a series of tests to evaluate her exposure to various metals and we are awaiting the results. This has been an extremely stressful time for me and my family.  We first contacted the company on December 23rd.  It has been almost four  months and I still have no answers from them and it’s just incomprehensible.  No one should have to endure this type of stress.

There were no indications that there was anything wrong with the machine other than it started producing a louder than usual sound.  The cup does not leak (we process fruit only) and it processes the food as expected.  The product specialists stated that the company “recommends” the blade be replaced every 6 months; however, this is purely a recommendation and is not disclosed as a safety hazard if not replaced.  I have spoken to many people that own Magic Bullets and they also were not aware that the blade should be replaced; many of them have never replaced their blades because the machine works properly.  Regretfully, I fear there are millions of customers may be ingesting this metal and have no idea.  This “issue” should have been escalated to the company’s top ranks on day one, instead they ignore me.  This is not just a customer service issue, this is a tremendous public health problem for users of this product who ironically are trying to promote good health.

I’m concerned for my daughter’s health as I do not know what she has been exposed to over the course of many years.  The lack of transparency and cooperation from the Magic Bullet company in obtaining this information is incomprehensible and it’s irresponsible, quite frankly.  The disclosures on the product are dangerous and deceptive- there should be a very clear warning sticker placed on the machine- that if you do not replace the blades every 6 months, there is danger that you may consume fine metal dust.

I am pleading with you, not as a customer, but as a mother who is very concerned about my daughter’s health.  Please help me find out what metal the product is made from so I can obtain the necessary measures to ensure my daughter’s safety.  I have been continually ignored by the company for almost four months and have gotten no information.

Your assistance is greatly appreciated.  Thank you.

productDescription:
13" W x 16.5"D x 16.75"H  Weight: 22 lbs.  Watts: 1,500
Amps: 12.5  BTU Rating: 5,000
productType: Heaters or Heating Systems, Other or Not Specified (393)
manufacturer: Better Living With Air & More, Inc.
brand: AirNmore Comfort Deluxe with copper PTC
incidentDescription:
Here's what I sent to AirNmore: Just wanted to give you a heads up that I discovered that I cannot use the Comfort Deluxe with Copper PTC (an electric space heater).  I have two of them.  I got the first one on 12-17-2019 (model YD-903G-CDA, serial CDA08194889) and then I got a second one (model YD-903G-CDA, serial CDA04191307) on 2-12-2020.  I only got the strange smell on the second unit when I turned the heater on and the smell did go away.  I have determined that both heaters must be emitting some toxic vapor because my bronchial tubes became irritated no matter which one I used.  
I have lived in a singlewide mobile home since 1991 so I know all about formaldehyde vapor.  I vapor-proofed the entire inside of my singlewide and also have a fresh air heat recovery ventilator with duct work putting fresh air right in where I sleep.  This problem is not formaldehyde vapor because formaldehyde vapor causes my nasal membranes to close up as if I had a cold, making it difficult to even breathe.  I got rid of my [REDACTED] infrared heater because it was housed in a wooden cabinet made of medium density fiberboard and it emitted some formaldehyde vapor.
This problem is different.  I can breathe OK but my lungs are getting irritated right at the top at the bronchial tubes right where the air first enters.  I quit using both units and felt better within hours.  I didn’t realize I had a problem with the first unit.  It must’ve been something that was accumulating.  I was only using the first unit during the day under my table in the kitchen and then I was using the [REDACTED] at night.  But I noticed both a reduced ability to breathe as well as the lung soreness in the morning.  But I attributed it all to the [REDACTED] infrared heater.  
When I got the second unit I used it during the day right under the table in my kitchen.  Then at night I used the first unit until my symptoms got so bad that I decided to quit using both units and just go back to my [REDACTED] 1500 watt model.  I got a new set of bulbs for it last year from you so it’s working fine.  I was keeping it as a backup and wanted to test out the new Comfort deluxe heater.  I also have a smaller [REDACTED] and changed those bulbs last year as well.  So I have heat.
I am NOT trying to return either unit.  I’ll probably eventually just disassemble them to at least recycle the metal.  My only hope is that perhaps the manufacturer is becoming aware of this problem and they might re-engineer the copper PTC heater element to correct the problem.  I noticed on your site that this same PTC heater element is used in several models, including the new smaller 1500 watt [REDACTED] heater that is about 12 inches by 9 inches by 9 inches.  So I don’t think I should get that model.  Right now the only model I would trust is another one with the six heater tubes, the 1500 watt model.  
Unfortunately these things do happen.  I had to get the [REDACTED] air bags replaced twice in my [REDACTED].  Then there was the formaldehyde problem with flooring from [REDACTED] that was in the news not all that long ago.  That flooring was manufactured in China.  The manufacturers in China like to cut corners to bring down the price.  But a bargain on something that you just can’t use is not a bargain at all.  I’ve always been more concerned about indoor air quality than price which is why I got the [REDACTED] in the first place.  
I was really excited about the Comfort Deluxe at first and even gave it a very good review at Amazon, even though I bought both units directly from AirNmore.  I’m going back to Amazon to adjust that review but I’m guessing that Amazon won’t post it.  I had a problem with some [REDACTED] blankets and they wouldn’t post that poor review.  They only want to post the good reviews.  I disassembled my second unit last night and it is not that much easier to remove that single fined copper PTC element than it is to replace six heater tubes in the [REDACTED].  I had to remove both right and left sides to remove that copper PTC element.  I put everything back together and it worked OK again.  I ran it in a separate room for a few minutes and then went in that room and got the lung irritation right away again.  So there is no doubt in my mind that something is wrong with the copper PTC heater element.  Again, both units give me the symptoms.  
So if the manufacturer recognizes the problem and comes up with a new heater element then I’d be interested in putting in the new copper PTC heater element and trying that out.  It makes no sense to just buy the same copper PTC heater element and put that in.  It needs to be something re-engineered and re-manufactured to correct the defect.  It’s probably whatever was causing the strange smell to begin with even though the smell went away.  The toxic, irritating vapor continues to be emitted even though you can’t smell it.  I admit that my lungs are more sensitive after living with formaldehyde in my singlewide for so long.  So perhaps I’m the first person to let you know that there is definitely a problem.  That is what needs to be addressed.  Perhaps they could make a glass-enclosed filament surrounded by the finned copper of the same size so I could just swap it into the two units that I already have.  
So, again, I just wanted to give you a heads up.  I am NOT trying to get a refund. Win some and lose some as they say.

LM-223 BR-26mm Electric Curling Brush

Model LM-223 BR-26mm
productType: Hair Curlers, Curling Irons, Clips & Hairpins (1682)
manufacturer: Shenzhen Lady Merry Technology Co., Ltd
incidentDescription:
I have a 2-year-old electric curling brush made by Phoebe.  It has a control to set it to various temperature settings up to a maximum of 430F, but defaults to 355F, which is what I always use.  The display lights up when it is on and displays the temperature.  I have it continuously plugged in, but am very careful to turn it off when I am done using it and have it sitting on a silicone pad.  

Last week I noticed that it was quite hot, even though it had been turned off for quite a few hours and the display was not on.  When I hit the on/off button, the display light came on and the temperature very quickly started to decrease, presumably to get down to the 355F default temperature.  I turned it off again (the display light turns off which indicates that it has in fact been turned off), and checked it again after a few hours.  The same situation occurred, with it still being on, despite the display being off, and presumably continuing to heat.  Same thing happened when I turned it off, with the display coming on and the temperature decreasing.  

At that point I unplugged it.  Thankfully I always have it sitting on a silicone pad, otherwise I think the wooden surface it was on would have burned or caught fire.  I contacted the company via email and their only solution was to offer to send me a free replacement.

I know I should always unplug this item, but a few things worry me about the situation.  

1.  The company was extremely quick to offer me a free replacement for a 2-year-old item.

2.  They did not request that I return the original appliance to them in order for them to diagnose what had occurred.

3.  I also just realized that there is no Underwriters Lab logo on it.

productDescription: BISSELL Cleanview Swivel Pet Upright Bagless Vacuum Cleaner, Green, 2252: [REDACTED]
incidentDescription:
I bought a Bissell Cleanview Swivel Pet Upright Bagless Vacuum Cleaner, Green, 2252 on Amazon on 1-4-20 and it was delivered shortly thereafter. I put it together and started using it soon after that. It worked wonderfully well at first, but within 3 or 4 uses the roller brush stopped turning and I noticed a burning smell. Upon investigation, I discovered that a mass of pet hair and other debris had collected around the motor spindle that turns the belt, which was causing the belt to slip and then to start melting from the friction caused by the spindle continuing to turn against the now stationary belt. I took it apart and cleaned it well, and used it a couple more times before it happened again.
People have reported in the product's reviews on Amazon that this design flaw- where the debris that is supposed to be channeled into the collection receptacle instead leaks into the belt housing- has caused their machines to malfunction, break, and/or catch fire. I had read some reviews on Amazon before making the purchase, but didn't see the ones warning of this problem, which appear to number in the hundreds as of today (one of which is mine). 
Many have also reported difficulty trying to obtain help from Bissell and/or Amazon, although Bissell has left replies to many of the complaints that the person should call them and they will be happy to help.
This product, which the manufacturer and Amazon appear to have known for at least a year poses a fire hazard under normal operation, is still on the market.
Please do something about this.

productDescription: Dash 6 Liter Air Fryer Family in Aqua (AAQP1095)
incidentDescription: On 2/19, I was using a Dash air fryer produced by storebound. Shortly after turning it on, it began putting off a strong burning odor similar to what would be expected of an electrical fire. Upon noticing the odor, my husband and I also heard a loud popping sound. We immediately unplugged the air fryer, but unfortunately it heated up to such an extent that my husband’s hand was burnt unplugging it, and the fryer cracked our 2 year old quartz countertops, causing $2,200 worth of damage. I was also able to locate two other consumers via product reviews who had similar issues with cracked countertops. [REDACTED] quartz countertops were cracked due to the air fryer over heating, and [REDACTED] countertops were cracked by the product.  I spoke with [REDACTED] at Dash about the issues, but unfortunately he dismissed the damage left by this product, claiming that the company had never heard of a similar issue with this product. This claim, however, was completely false as both [REDACTED] and [REDACTED] referenced speaking to corporate and having their concerns similarly dismissed. [REDACTED] from storebound (Dash) claimed that it was impossible for the base of the unit to have heated up to such an extent due to the fact that the heating element is located in the upper half of the appliance. While this may be true, the electrical components are located in the base of the air fryer. Upon unplugging the unit, my husband burnt his hand on the base of the fryer moving it, and the countertops were extremely hot. Based on these facts, in conjunction with the odor similar to what would be associated with an electrical fire, I assume that these units are prone to faulty wiring or some form of failure of the electrical components which are housed in the base of the air fryer. I have kept the product for reference and would be happy to submit it to the CPSC for further inspection. I believe this product to be dangerous. Not only did it cause costly property damage to our home, it is also a potential fire hazard and is capable of causing severe bodily harm due to the extensive heat that is produced upon malfunction.  I am also extremely disappointed that Dash cares so little about the well being of their customers that they would choose to lie about the safety of their products rather than investigating and resolving the apparent electrical malfunctions inherent to these appliances that are capable of causing extensive damage and bodily harm.

While doing this pre-heat my kitchen filled with a burning plastic odor and I got light headed and disoriented. I turned off the unit and went outside to breath fresh air, and ventilated the house. This is dangerous, particularly if there are family members who can not detect symptoms of airborne hazards. I am a veteran military pilot who has been through many training sessions in low pressure, high altitude chambers  for hypoxia and also exposed to burning oil fumes, jet fumes and solvents, and gasoline aerosol fumes. I do not want new arms to this horrible fan. It has been taken down. I cannot afford a new fan.
