productDescription: I purchased a Dyson Iron/Silver EX-QTV US fan/heater unit from QVC on 10/15/2018.   The serial number is SN3-US-KGA6252A.
productType: Heaters or Heating Systems, Other or Not Specified (393)
incidentDescription:
I am reporting an item that I believe to be unsafe.  I purchased a Dyson Iron/Silver EX-QTV US fan/heater unit from QVC on 10/15/2018.   The serial number is SN3-US-KGA6252A.

On the evening of 12/23/2019 the fan/heater unit was plugged in, but turned off.  The remote control was on the coffee table to the right of the fan/heater unit.  I was sitting in a recliner to the right of the coffee table approximately four feet from the fan/heater unit.

While reading emails on the laptop, I heard a noise.   I realized the fan/heater unit had turned on.   The light showed the heater was on set to 70 degrees.  I immediately utilized the remote to turn off the fan/heater unit and unplug it.

On December 26, 2019 at approximately I telephoned Dyson customer service and spoke with [REDACTED].  She said she consulted with the Support Team and could offer no explanation for the unit turning itself on.   She offered me a new and upgraded unit which shuts off automatically after eight hours.   I explained that I was concerned about the unit turning itself on and potential dangers if it were on for the entire eight hours unbeknownst to me.  Thus, I declined the replacement offer.  I, of course, realize if the unit was always unplugged except in my presence it could potentially mitigate the perceived danger.

I then telephoned QVC customer service on the evening of December 26, 2019.   The representative stated QVC would accept return not later than January 5, 2020 and refund purchase price.  The representative was not particularly concerned about the specifics of the incident and the potential unsafe product.

productDescription: Black & Decker Double Flip Waffle Maker, Black
incidentDescription: I was making blue berry waffles. I made the batter with blue berries. Before plugging the Black & Decker Double Flip (with duel cooking plates) product to the outlet to use for the first time, I read the product instruction book thoroughly, including the safeguards section, season the waffle irons as instructed, then wiped away any excess oil. I plugged in the product, then when the green indicator light turned on, I poured the first amount (3/4 cup) as directed in the instructions. I locked the product as designed and instructed. After 10 seconds (per the instructions), I turned it over to pour the batter on the other side. I locked the product as instructed, waiting 10 seconds, before turning it over to the side with the first cooking waffle. The first cooking waffle started to steam. At about one minute and a half later, it started to make a noise and was steaming very much. I backed away and the device exploded and jumped off the edge of the counter hitting the floor. No one was injured. It unplugged itself when it fell to the ground. I left it alone until it cooled off. I took two picture of the area shortly after the product exploded. I noticed that the plastic lock and one of the two handles snapped off and was left on the counter. I took additional pictures of the product after it cooled.

productDescription: T3 Single Pass 1.25" Hair Curler
productType: Hair Curlers, Curling Irons, Clips & Hairpins (1682)
incidentDescription: I recently purchased the t 3 Single Pass Hair curler at Ulta retailers. I had done some research  online before purchasing and had read that this expensive curler had some poor reviews due to fact that some customers were accidentally grabbing the wrong end of the curler when it was hot. The fact that the curling iron is white on both ends, and emits very little heat from the ceramic material, this was said to be very easy to confuse. I thought the design looked sleek  and figured I would not make this mistake myself. Well, not only does the design feature a completely white design on both ends that are shaped virtually identical, but typical curling irons would usually include a little metal stand that angles the hot end up and away from surfaces. This typical design subtly cues users as to which side is the hot end. The t3 curler sits nearly flush with surfaces and does not feature a way to prop the hot end up and away from surfaces. And sure enough, it proved to be easy to accidentally grab the wrong end. Within the 5th or 6th time using the curler, not only has this extremely hot tool fallen from the counter to the floor several times due to its improper anchoring system, potentially burning whatever it falls on, but today I grabbed the wrong end just as I thought I could avoid.  I badly burnt the entire gripping surface of my right hand after grabbing for the 410 degree end of the curler. I dropped the curling iron immediately, exposing my feet to potential threat from getting burnt, while simultaneously  creating a fire hazard.. My hand was in such pain it took me a prolonged period to react and pick up the tool off the the floor safely. This tool should be recalled for its lack of safety and knowingly exposing customers to danger, while charging a very high price tag for the product.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: WOLFGANG PUCK Pressure Oven,  Model BROR1002-A1
incidentDescription:
This item is a Wolfgang Puck Pressure/Toaster Oven. It has an “On/Off” Timer knob cook function, a light while cooking and a ticking sound during cooking. Normally when cooking is complete a bell will sound. At some point a while back unnoticed at first by me, the bell signal stopped functioning and later at times the Timer would not stop ticking. Gradually, the oven has become difficult to turn off. To clarify, when turning knob to off position, timer remains on and/or oven remains on. I’ve also discovered the slightest movement or vibration of oven causes the On/Off Timer knob switch on.
Also, if using auto turn off function, oven may shut off, timer stays on then goes to “Stay On” position which turns the oven back on. I tried it today. I turned it oven off. No light was on. I returned about 20 minutes later to a very warm 350 degree lighted oven. This is a hazard in my opinion. 
Even when  the timer continues to tick for an undetermined period of time. 
I attempted to contact W.P. Appliances to report this issue. The person I spoke with said there were no complaints of this type although she never asked my info, model number or any product details. I don’t understand how you can know if there are no complaints without product information. 
The only remedy I have is to unplug and discontinue use and report this issue.

productDescription:
Vacuuming Robot, Designed for carpets, rugs, hard floors. WIFI enabled, Automatic scheduling, 120 minute run time. 
IROBOT Roomba 980
incidentDescription: The IROBOT Roomba 980 series has been having charging issues for a period of time. I started doing some online research and have come across other people having the same issues. Some other people have taken there Roomba apart and have found that the electrical contacts on the bottom side of the Roomba are melted causing them to recess into the unit. I flipped my Roomba over and inspected for this. I found that the one contact has been melted\pushed up into the roomba a good amount. where the other electrical contact is still flat. This to me seams like a fire hazard. Even though this has NOT started a FIRE. I feel like there needs to be something done about this. Because there are alot of reported instances of this in online reviews of multiple different Roomba models. Not just the roomba 980. I contacted Roomba directly this morning and told them about what was going on with it. and also asked if they had any recalls for this happening. They said " this isn't a common case but a very common robot " That too me sounds a bit off. especially after finding multiple reviews with other people having the same problems. Roomba Customer service representative online said they will send out a new roomba and charging station. But will this actually prevent the new roomba from not having melted contacts?? I just feel like this is something that needs to be looked at by a third party. Because the worse case scenario is that a roomba can have a thermal event and cause a fire and burn down your house or apartment. This is why I am filling out this information.

productDescription: Hover-1 Eagle Kick Start Scooter. Black.
incidentDescription:
We have a Hover-1 Eagle electric kick scooter. We read a few online reviews that said they had issues with the electronic brake engaging suddenly causing the rider to fall and then the machine becoming inoperable. We figured the few reviews we read were one-offs, but we experienced the same problem with one of the two scooters we purchased. The first day my daughter rode it, the electronic brake engaged suddenly and caused her to skid to a stop. Luckily, it was at a lower speed than the scooter can obtain, and she did not flip or fall. After this happened, the electronic brake would not reset and the scooter would not work. We returned it and exchanged it for another. We haven't tried the new one yet.  

I am concerned about the safety of this scooter. It can go 15 mph, and if the electronic brake engages at that speed, it can cause serious injury. My kids wear helmets when riding these, but a fall at that speed can still cause serious injuries. 

Other reviews have had the same exact issues with the faulty electronic braking system on this scooter. This product should be recalled and replaced with a safer product.

productDescription: Great Value 9V alkaline batteries.
incidentDescription:
Walmart needs to check the polarity of the printed positive side of some Great Value 9V alkaline batteries.

The smaller circular (male) terminal is the positive, and the larger hexagonal or octagonal (female) terminal is the negative contact. 

I have the items and I took pictures.
On the picture you can see the polarity is reversed (wrongly printed).
These need to be recalled before people install them wrongly in their smoke alarms and do so on.

This is a waffle-maker of standard clamshell design, but there is no handle on the lower shell.
It seems perfectly fine and opens just by releasing the latch--until you cook a waffle. Then the waffle acts as a glue between the upper and lower shells, and releasing the latch does not open the waffle-maker. If you grab the lower half to pull it open, you will get burned, and with no handle on the lower half, there is no safe way to open the device. 

I managed to get a butter knife under the latch and lever the sections apart, but I had to pick the hot waffle-maker up off the counter to get the knife in there. Because it does not open easily once the waffle is cooked, this thing is a burn hazard.

productDescription: Rechargeable battery-powered tire-inflator
incidentDescription:
My wife bought me a Sharper Image battery-powered (rechargeable) tire inflator for Christmas 2018.  Its appearance is similar to a cordless drill but instead of a drill bit protruding from its nozzle, there is a short flexible tire hose with a valve that fits the standard Schroeder type used by all vehicles and most recreational products that have pneumatic tires on them.  It is in reality, a portable air compressor.

It features a digital readout which allows you to manually set your desired pressure.  Once set, you pull the trigger and let it run until the target pressure is reached. I had used it a number of times on my family's vehicles and enjoyed its convenience and efficiency.  

On one occasion I attached it to a deflated tire on a lightweight twin wheeled wheel barrow. I set the 22psi pressure recommended and left it alone to run until completed.  It ran for about 4 minutes and then stopped, having reached the desired pressure.  Instead of detaching the unit from my wheelbarrow tire, I left it there. No harm I assumed; job done.

A while later I set off my nearby lawn sprinkler.  Thinking nothing more about the lawn or the inflator after approx 10 mins, I was puzzled by a sound I thought may be at first was air caught up in the garden hose.  It was soon apparent that it was the SI inflator/compressor.  Realizing that I'd heard the noise for a while, I approached the valve with caution. When I tried to release the trigger, there was an almighty BANG!  It was so loud, my wife came running around from the front of the house thinking that a shotgun had fired very close to us!  

My assumption is that the water from the sprinkler shorted out the inflator's preset internal max pressure setting and allowed it continue until the battery would expire.  It completely ripped apart both the tube and the tire. 

Reporting the incident to Sharper Image, they, at first seemed concerned, telling me that they'd forward my unit to a special department. However,  their response to  a couple of follow up calls was ultimately to forward me a refund in the form of a credit.

In our town about 12 years ago, one tire dealer was killed when a regular hose was left on a wheel barrow tire that did not have the required safety cage over it.  Had this been set on a higher capacity tire typically found on a regular car or truck, the result could have been similarly catastrophic.

I belief that this product had not been thoroughly tested  prior to it being available for sale and so is extremely dangerous.  I also believe that other retailers sell the same unit under different names.

productDescription: Golf Cart King / Modz Maxx 36V 15A Battery Charger
incidentDescription: The following complaint against Golf Cart King & their Modz Maxx brand battery charger is on the grounds that this charger is unsafe for the end user, in addition to the fact that there are false claims on performance/efficiency, and insufficient information regarding what battery types can be charged. I also can find no record of it being in compliance with Department of Energy Battery Charger Efficiency Guidelines. The charger lists on it’s main label an efficiency of >93%. Furthermore, there is no information listed on the charger, the packaging, or the website stating what kind of batteries can be charged. Given this, it is inevitable that the end user could damage their vehicle and batteries, or injure themselves in several different ways, by any of several different mechanical, design, or marketing oversights. This charger is sold on Amazon.com and the Golf Cart King website alongside other “intelligent” chargers that actually do contain charge algorithms custom tailored to the battery application that end user will encounter with their golf carts. These other chargers can be found on the DOE public database listings for their energy consumption and efficiency with regard to specific battery applications. The Golf Cart King / Modz Maxx charger cannot be found on the DOE public database, it is not safe and can cause physical harm to the consumer, in addition to potentially damaging their equipment.

On the sales page the seller specifically warns potential buyers that the charger may get extremely hot and also cause the phone to become extremely hot.

I used this product for less than 24 hours before the supplied charging cable became so hot that it burned out and ceased to function. During that brief usage it caused the lithium ion battery to become so hot that the battery swelled popping the back cover of my [REDACTED] smart phone to pop off.

[REDACTED] smart phones can indicate when [REDACTED] charging is taking place. At no time did my smart phone indicate [REDACTED] charging was occurring despite the battery becoming almost hot enough to go critical and explode starting a fire. Had the charging cable not burned out and failed a fire could easily have occurred.

Unfortunately I no longer have this dangerous product as Amazon demanded I return it to obtain a full refund. I still felt the need to report this product because I believe it is dangerous and because the seller is telling potential buyers to ignore extreme overheating conditions which by itself is very dangerous advice to give to consumers.

productDescription: Gnome Pellet Stove, made by Thelin Hearth Products
incidentDescription:
After 5 days of using a new Thelin Gnome pellet stove, the stove mal-functioned by sending several cups of burning pellets out the air intake and causing a fire on the  pellet stove floor mat. The stove had been set to low when I left the house. I was burning the best quality pellets, douglas fir, the [REDACTED] Fire Marshall had been to the house 3 times during the install process, and finally to provide an approval of the installation. I arrived home, after leaving for approximately one hour, to a house full of smoke and my dogs coughing. The fire was extinguished and I notified the Fire Marshalls, the installer, and the distributor of the stove. I also called Thelin the following day but they would not discuss the incident and said I should speak to the distributor. I asked for the name of the person at Thelin, and she disconnected the call.  The distributor sent a technician the following day to look at the stove and told me that the stove mal-functioned and that it should have shut down before sending out the pellets. The fire basket was completely empty, so the stove finished the burn and,  did shut down and was no longer on when I got home, but the fire was burning underneath. There were two piles burning, one under the fan which was melted, and another under the air intake. 
There is no reference in the user manual or installation manual about the stove sending too many pellets out, closing the air intake (except if it is whistling), or the auger continuing to run when the pellet basket is full of pellets. A few days earlier, I had sent a picture of the flame to the distributor so they could see that it was burning well.
After looking at the stove, the distributore was instructed by the manufacturer to pull the stove from my home.

I called the manufacturer- Marley Engineered Products and was informed that it was a known problem and they would send out a wiring repair kit. They know the wiring is not able to stand up to the current draw of the heater yet are still selling them. I bought the unit 9/11/2019 and it lasted a month before failure. This seems to me to be a fire hazard. Unit was installed as per their instructions. incidentDescription:

It then began to leak from the part where the clear "fill line" window meets the stainless steel carafe. It leaks to the extent that it leaves a HUGE puddle of water around it, and the electrical base is sitting in a puddle of water, with plugged-in cords all around it. This could obviously lead to someone getting electrocuted.

This does not occur if there is only a very small amount of water in the carafe (about one cup).

I finally figured out exactly what was happening and called Hamilton Beach today. They said I was out of warranty, and offered to replace it for half price plus $11 shipping. Mostly, I am concerned that there is an extremely unsafe product on the market, and they don't appear to care. They did not put me on with any product people, just the regular call center. This product should be recalled.

productDescription: Instant Vortex Plus 10 Quart Air fryer oven. Black and chrome.
incidentDescription:
I purchased an Instant Vortex Plus air fryer on 7/29/2019. We have been using the unit daily since purchased. On 10/7, after cooking dinner for the kids, we had thought the unit had powered off as normal. It had not. About an hour later I could smell something hot and investigated. The light of the air fryer was on, and the control panel, which normally says “OFF” was completely dark. Upon approaching the unit, it was evident that the heating element was still powered on, and the unit was in a thermal runaway state. The unit was too hot to approach, and I unplugged it with an oven mit. I believe the unit was not far from catching fire when unplugged. 

After the unit cooled, I tested it by plugging it in. The internal light immediately turned on, and the heating element started heating. The computer interface was completely inoperative. It seems that the unit failed to the condition it was in when the control unit ceased function, causing a thermal runaway event. It is also evident that there is not mechanical thermal runaway protection on the unit.

Girl Scouts San Diego had an employee using a brand new Dewalt battery powered leaf blower, model DCBL772 to clear leaf debris from sidewalks.  The unit performed properly the first time it was used out of the box.  When used again, after several minutes of use, the employee felt an electrical shock through the handle of the unit.  The schock was severe enough to require a doctors visit as the employee suffered muscle disfunction in the right hand that was effected.  The blower was placed out of service and the battery removed.  The unit was inspected by a supervisor and the battery that was in use was found to be working properly and function normally in other battery power tools.  

A charged battery was reinstalled in the leaf blower in question and with electrical isolation gloves and isolation from ground, the leaf blower was tested.  The leaf blower no longer worked and did not appear to be providing any electrcial energy through the plastic handle.  The leaf blower remains out of service at the below address.  The employee continues under a doctors care and six days later has limited use of the right hand.

productDescription:

In addition, it happened when no one was home so we did not have physical problems caused by the fire that may have worsen the overall situation. But, we had to breath a very polluted air since the smoke and the soot went through the AC.

I immediately called the Amazon Customer Service and they opened a report to study the case internally with you. Moreover, since they are just a third party, they highly recommended to point this out to your Customer Service Team in order to solve this matter.

The fire caused damages in the apartment: the entry door has been forced; all the things close to the bike got burnt (window, curtain, wooden floor ecce). We are now paying all the expenses to fix and clean the unit as soot and dust are everywhere. Moreover, our lives are changed because we are still scared.
model: Folding Electric Bike 20" Wheels with 240W Brushless M
incidentDescription:
Two weeks ago, I charged the battery of the XPRIT Folding Electric Bike 20" Wheels with 240W Brushless Motor but, a few hours later, my boyfriend came home and found out that the battery exploded in our apartment. The police and the firemen had to force the door to come in and part of the living room has been damaged by this terrible accident. Please see attached the Police Report. Luckly, they arrived in time to rescue my place avoiding that the whole apartment would have caught fire. In addition, it happened when no one was home so we did not have physical problems caused by the fire that may have worsen the overall situation. But, we had to breath a very pulluted air since the smoke and the soot went through the AC.

I immediately called the Amazon Customer Service and they opened a report to study the case internally with you. Moreover, since they are just a third party, they highly recommended to point this out to the Customer Service Team in order to solve this matter.

The fire caused damages in the apartment: the entry door has been forced; all the things close to the bike got burnt (window, curtain, wooden floor ecc). We are now paying all the expenses to fix and clean the unit as soot and dust are everywhere. Moreover, our lives are changed because we are still scared.

productDescription: Pellet grill by Traeger, Silverton model. Black
incidentDescription:
On August 29 I cooked two salmon fillets on my new Traeger Silverton grill from Costco. This was the second time that I used this grill, I cooked the same items a week prior without a problem. I put the grill on "smoke" for about an hour, then turned it up to 350 degrees for the final 15 minutes of cook time. About 10 minutes after turning it up, I could see smoke pouring from the grill and heard noises coming from it. I opened the lid and flames were shooting out several feet. I shut the lid and turned the grill off, but it was still on fire. I opened the lid again pulled the salmon out, I had about 15 guests at my home and people were screaming. The fire eventually extinguished.
     The next several weeks were spent with innumerable calls to Traeger, they were completely unphased regarding the description of the fire. They finally agreed to replace this grill with an identical one, (after first offering to just replace the "burnt" parts, but truly did not care about the REASON the fire happened in the first place. So I then called and spoke with the Costco rep for Traeger, [REDACTED] (Sept 23, 2019) and described the grill fire.  This resulted in a call the following day from [REDACTED] in the Escalation Department at Traeger. I spent about an hour on the phone with him, taking the Pellet grill apart and texting photos of the burnt parts. I was naive in believing that they would be honest, but this was just a ploy to lay blame elsewhere. [REDACTED] decided that the fire was my fault and there was no defect in the grill design. He told me that the aluminum foil on the drip pan had a wrinkle in it, and that the aluminum drip liner (supplied by Traeger), had a wrinkle or fold which caused the fish grease to pool and catch on fire. First of all, the aluminum drip liner was so badly burned from the fire and was so distorted and charred as a result, there was no way to determine just how it was installed. The steel grill topper that I use for fish was also distorted and bent from the high heat of the fire, that was how hot it was. The tiny "wrinkle" in the aluminum foil could not have been the cause, so absurd! [REDACTED] (Traeger) sent [REDACTED] (Costco) an email essentially letting him know of his results. 
     I spoke with both [REDACTED] and [REDACTED] today (Oct 7, 2019), they are both happy to put the cause of the fire on the wrinkle in the aluminum foil and liner creating the pooling of grease which ultimately caused the fire. How absurd!
     Here is what I know:
1) I have had a Traeger grill for about 5 years and have cooked this same item on it hundreds of times without incident, I am not new to this. I've lined the drip pan with heavy aluminum foil for years without incident, wrinkles and all. 
2) I do believe that the fire WAS caused by the pooling of grease, as there was no grease flowing into the little grease bucket. But this was not a result of the little wrinkle in the aluminum foil, rather, it is a direct result of the angle (or lack of angle) on the drip pan itself.  When comparing the drip pan on the new grill as compared with my old Traeger grill, the pans sit at a completely different angle. The drip pan on the new grill is almost completely flat, there is hardly an angle to it at all. On the old grill, however, there is a distinct and visible angle to the drip tray allowing any grease to freely flow into the drip bucket and preventing the "pooling" of grease, thus preventing a fire. 
3) When I discussed my concerns with both Costco ([REDACTED]) and Traeger ([REDACTED) today, they were in denial and were both confident they had no responsibility. The "fix" for this defect is so easy, but imagine contacting every consumer that purchased this item for a retrofit repair to the grill....it is so much easier for them to deny there is a problem. My concern is that unsuspecting customers are currently subject to personal injury, property damage, or fatal injury as a result of this defective product.
4) Traeger was happy to send me another grill. After my first conversation with [REDACTED], he claimed that the Silverton had undergone some design changes and that I would not have a problem with the new grill. I had a handyman come out two days ago to put it together for me, and when I saw that it was identical to the one I currently have, I decided to send it back to Traeger. The freight company just picked it up a few minutes ago, and the driver told me he picks these up all the time because people are complaining that they catch on fire.

productDescription: Hoover Model UH71013 vacuum cleaner, upright, rewind, bagless
incidentDescription: The Hoover UH71013 cleaner I bought in the Fall of 2017 has a defective on/off switch. The original switch fell apart. I took it out and the plastic body was melted and the plastic insulators around the switch lead terminals were black. I ordered a replacement switch and installed and tested it. I ran the vacuum before mounting it on the handle to test it. I noticed the switch body and terminals were hot to the touch after only five minutes of operation. I then took the switch off the leads and clipped them directly together and ran machine for ten minutes. The terminals and wires were cool to the touch confirming the switch was too weak for the circuit. The cleaner is rated at 12 amps. I took the old switch apart and noticed the contacts were very tiny: about the size of a pinhead. This switch seems a bad design for this product.  This product should be recalled.

Without warning, while carrying a load of water and withOUT any sort of trauma, the handle of my teakettle completely came off, dropping the pot onto the ground. This represents a significant safety concern as there was absolutely no warning. Luckily, my pot only had cold water and not boiling water, so I was not injured and instead was merely splashed.

Where the kettle's handle fell off, it appears that the screws that were supposed to be holding the handle on were never attached through the wall of the tea kettle and that this is a manufacturing defect.

Looking at the Kate Spade website, it appears my tea kettle was not unique, as there are severa; reports of similar problems on their tea kettle review: https://www.katespade.com/products/tea-kettle/L857004.html

productDescription: Central Machinery 5-Gallon Wet/Dry Vacuum/Blower, Item # 61317
incidentDescription:
My client purchased a Central Machinery, 5 gallon Wet/Dry Vacuum/Blower from Harbor Freight in October, 2016.  The label describes it as a 120 volt, 8.3 amp, 60hz model, item number 61317.

Her daughter used the vacuum without incident for about fifteen minutes on September 22, 2019.  My client then plugged the vacuum in at another location in the same house, and it began to make a strange noise.  She could feel there was no suction at the end of the hose.  She turned the unit off and back on a couple times.  While it was on, she took hold of the handle at the top of the unit, intending to move it.  At that moment, she heard a "gunshot" noise, the top separated from the motor housing, and a metal disk in the motor essentially exploded, sending bits of metal shrapnel flying in all directions.

My client suffered deep lacerations to her left hand and right leg that necessitated emergency transport to a hospital and multiple sutures.

productDescription: Weber part number 83156 (Catch pan kit), belonging to Weber Genesis II E-310 Gas Grill (model number 61010001, serial number DW 5022256).
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
Sharp edges on Weber part number 83156 (Catch pan kit) resulted in a 1 inch hand laceration (left hand, index finger) during cleaning; the laceration required 4 stitches due to its depth and location.  In addition, the same part resulted in a minor cut (equivalent to a “paper cut”) moments later during in the opposite hand (right hand, thumb).

The part number identified above was removed from a Weber Genesis II E-310 gas grill (model number 61010001, serial number DW 5022256 ) for cleaning.  As the items was being cleaned in a kitchen sink with a sponge and soap, one of the sharp edges along the outer edge of the sheet metal catch pan cut through my index finger (along the side of side of the finger at the proximal interphalangeal joint).  After the bleeding was controlled, I returned to move the catch pan out of the sink and while simply grabbing the item (from the end opposite of the initial incident), it resulted in a minor cut in my opposite hand (thumb).

I went to an urgent care medical facility approximately 1 hour after the incident, due to the continued bleeding in the left hand, in order to seek medical attention; while at the urgent care facility, I received 4 stitches due to the depth and location of the laceration.  In addition to the stitches, the wound requires wearing a finger splint for 10 days (due to the location of the laceration).

productDescription: Dell Lithium Ion laptop batteries.
incidentDescription: Numerous reports of Dell 73XX, 55XX and numerous other model numbers for laptop batteries have swollen to a point of looking as if they are ready to explode.  I called Dell and they are not concerned about the Li-Ion batteries exploding and the only thing they do is offer a replacement.  I've got photos of these batteries expanding the laptop casing around the CD burner separating due to the expansion of the battery.  I'm in the Occupational Safety field and am concerned that if we take these laptops on aircraft or any other public transportation, there may be a catastrophic event.  I'm shocked that Dell hasn't self-reported this to CPSC yet as there are hundreds, maybe thousands of these computers in our Army Medical Command.  Our director of IT services is the one who brought this up to me and is also very concerned.  Thanks for your attention to this matter.

productDescription:
Lithium-ion Battery Pack for (OEM) DeWALT cordless drill.
18V 5000mAh Battery Pack
Direct replacement for OEM Part# DC9096
Sold by Amazon.com
Ordered on August 12, 2019 Order# 112-2568799-7477041 
Amazon merchant seller name: Jialitt
Amazon Merchant Info: https://www.amazon.com/sp?_encoding=UTF8&asin=&isAmazonFulfilled=1&isCBA=&marketplaceID=ATVPDKIKX0DER&orderID=112-2568799-7477041&seller=AGS089MMHXPF3&tab=&vasStoreID=
manufacturer: Dongguan Sanke Electronic Technology Co., Ltd
incidentDescription:
On August 15, 2019 I had a lithium-ion battery pack explode while in the charger which subsequently caught my house on fire. The battery exploded into a number of individual cells which continued to explode one-by-one starting several separate fires in my garage. It took two full fire extinguishers to put out the multiple fires over the course of 10 to 15 minutes . The battery pack had just been purchased from Amazon.com and installed into the charger about 6:30 pm on 09/14/2019. The battery pack exploded at 10:30 am the next morning 09/15/2019. The battery pack was an after-market direct replacement for a [REDACTED] cordless drill and sold as such. The battery pack was manufactured in China.  I had fire damage and some property damage to my garage. If my wife and I had not been home at the time, or had the battery exploded during the middle of the night while we were sleeping the entire house would have gone up in flames. It was very fortunate that we heard the explosion and that I had two fire extinguishers ready nearby to quickly put out the multiple fires. I’m also lucky that I was not seriously injured while doing that since I only had shorts and sandals on at the time. I only sustained small burns on one toe and the top of my left foot where I came into contact with some of the hot metal or plastic while extinguishing the fires.  There were lithium-ion cells still exploding while I was trying to extinguish the flames.  I reported the incident to Amazon’s customer service department shortly after the fire that same morning and they immediately removed the product for sale from their online store and refunded my purchase, but that’s all they would do. I’ve spent almost three hours on the phone during 3 separate calls and have been given different instructions and responses each time. In the end I received an email from Amazon’s Executive Customer Relations department stating that Amazon takes no responsibility for any damages or losses caused by merchants selling through the Amazon marketplace...and that I could contact the merchant in China (through their merchant link) if I wanted to pursue the issue further with them.

One more thing - there have been a number of incidents of lithium-ion battery fires aboard commercial and package carrier aircraft, I’d like to see some regulation against Amazon (and other online only retailers) to force them to take liability for selling counterfeit and poor-quality after-market products through their online store. If I had purchased an OEM battery from a brick-and-mortar store or directly from the OEM (even if the OEM product was manufactured in China) both companies would be liable for the damage and losses caused by their product. Why does Amazon get a free pass on incurring any liability for the products that they sell? That regulation needs to be changed.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

incidentDescription:
I bought 2 ea. 5V 2.5A Rhino wall power adapters to supply a micro-computer ([REDACTED]) . On both adapters the
5V outputs are not floating, They have 40V to 60V AC superimposed. Connecting the (-) terminal of the power
supply to real ground with 1kOhm made the resistor smoke, so there is not just static or a high impedance path.
When I first hooked up the power supply I got severely shocked and holding the connector (Mini-USB) to a known
grounded USB port it sparked heavily. It also damaged my entertainment system. By profession I am a physicist and
have a lot of experience with electronics. If someone uses these power supplies with toys it may be very dangerous.
I am willing to send the objects in for evaluation.

I run into my smoke and smell filled kitchen, pulled the cord out and knocked the coffee maker into the sink, I couldn't touch it, fire flames were reaching toward the ceiling. Took a long time to extinguish the flames. Because of the smell burned plastic we couldn't' spend the night at home. productDescription: I bought a brand new house from a developer that included a Samsung refrigerator, model # RF260BEAESR/AA. My husband had to go to work that morning and he was miserable. We reported this dangerous inability of the refrigerator to keep cold temperature and the refrigerator was repaired on August 29,2019. I haven't called Samsung again because I found out that there is no remedy for the problem but a refund. I don't want to schedule any more fixes on this as the problem is the flawed design of internal parts that freezes no matter what. If you need to view more evidence of my case, please feel free to contact me. Thank you.
incidentDescription:

It started making clanking noise randomly, then stopped maintaining temperature, then progressed to food poisoning and unable to make ice. RevoAce 6-Burner LP Gas Grill with Side Burner, Stainless Steel and Black, GBC1768WB

https://www.walmart.com/ip/RevoAce-6-Burner-LP-Gas-Grill-with-Side-Burner-Stainless-Steel-and-Black-GBC1768WB/55456047
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
Husband was putting pre-cooked ribs on the grill when grease dripped off the rack of ribs while he was placing them on the grill. That grease ignited into flames as he was moving the ribs onto the grill, ran up toward the ribs and his hand, and also down into the grill.

While it was scary that the grease burned up toward him, that is not the complaint. The complaint is that when the grease dripped into the grill, it ran right out the bottom of the grill body, and directly onto the gas hose and LP tank in the cabinet of the grill.

He then had flames in the grill itself as well as on the gas line and LP tank. He tried to close the lid on the grill to snuff the flames, but there is a huge gap where the lid and the body meet, as well as several large gaps at the bottom of the grill body. These let in tons of air, and fed the fire instead of snuffing it.

Worse still, he had to get into the grill with fire coming from everywhere, to turn off the valve on the LP tank and disconnect the hose. This was made even more dangerous, because the LP tank is physically clamped into the cabinet, so he had to unscrew those clamps before he could move the tank to safety. - All with flaming grease dripping down onto the rubber gas hose and LP tank, and my husband.

This all seems very wrong. We've owned maybe 6 or more gas grills over our 30 year marriage, and none were built like this, or would have EVER had a dangerous situation like this arise.

This could easily have burned down our house, seriously injured my husband, and even destroyed our truck. Totally unacceptable for a Walmart purchase.

productDescription: Bird (rebranded Mi Scooter)
incidentDescription:
On August 30th 2018 I was writing a Bird Scooter on [REDACTED] in [REDACTED] when the throttle stuck in the fully deployed position. Attempting to adjust it, I lost my balance and fell. I suffered numerous fractures to my right wrist and a very sprained finger and my middle left hand. I had to have a metal plate inserted into my wrist. I am still suffering the consequences almost a year later and will have to have another surgery to get the plate removed. 

Upon further investigation, it seems that these scooters are not meant to be stored outside. According to the manufacturer’s manual from Mi Scooter (see page 12 https://images-na.ssl-images-amazon.com/images/I/B12uhePLDnS.pdf), this subjects them to damage from heat. These are however, scooters that are available for rent, rebranded by Bird, and left on the sidewalks for public use. I rode them all summer without any problem, but on one of the hottest days in August, the throttle failed. 

It is my hope that you take this incident seriously, as there are many others who have been injured in a similar manner, due to malfunction of the scooters. Thank you for investigating this matter.

productDescription:
Lunar Bowl Fire Table by ELEMENTI
Propane fueled fire pit
2 units received,first serial # HSC-D20190700001.... SECOND UNIT, SEE SERIAL # BELOW
model: LUNAR BOWL FIRE TABLE (PROPANE)        MODEL# OFG101LP
incidentDescription:
Product: "Lunar Bowl Fire Table" by ELEMENTI, product # OFG101LP (propane fueled fire pit)

I ordered this fire pit through Amazon and it was delivered to my home.  It did not light using the ignitor, despite several attempts following the manual's lighting instructions. As I indicated to ELEMENTI, "IGNITION CLICKING HEARD AND PROPANE FLOWING, BUT UNIT FAILS TO FLAME. "

They responded by sending a second unit.  This had the same problem, as it did not flame in the fire pit following the lighting instructions.  I could hear the ignitor clicking, but it would not light.  I allowed the propane to dissipate as suggested in the manual, and then repeated this again, also as suggested in the manual, but it would not light. I then followed the alternative directions in the manual to light the fire pit using a handheld lighter. I was able to get the fire ring to light this way, but shortly after lighting it, a fireball exploded.  My son and I were seated next to it on the couch, and the fire appeared to come mostly from underneath the unit and caused burns to our legs.  It seared off the hair on our lower legs and resulted in second degree burns, mostly to my son's lower left leg and foot, and a smaller second degree burn to my right lower leg. The burns to my son's leg were treated in the Emergency Room at Rhode Island Hospital.

I had a fire pit/ gas service professional examine both fire pits afterwards and he detected heavy leaking propane from the air mixer (venturi) device underneath each unit. He reported them both to be unsafe and condemned them for use. Since the same issue involved BOTH units, from same part, I am concerned that there is a manufacturing design or part failure/defect.  Out of concern for others, I contacted Amazon and ELEMENTI, to let them know, as I am concerned there may be other units with the same propane leaking air mixer part and potential for injury to others.

incidentDescription:
Jetson Bolt ebike has a single brake. It is intended for light duty and relatively low grade inclines. However I am concerned that single brake (no redundant braking) is unsafe on downhill grades. I was on a hill using a lightly used (basically new) Bolt ebike. I was going down hill. The brake was unable to slow the decent and the bike continued to increase in speed. I was fortunate that half way down the hill, there was a fork and one of the paths went up hill (like a truck runout). I was not injured but it was terrifying. Reviewers of the bike noted problems with braking and expressed concern over its performance. (I won the bike at a workplace event.)

Note, my weight is equal to or slightly below the maximum weight rating for the bike. So fully loaded on a steeper grade.

I raised the issue with the company over facebook. They were responsive but I question whether they were really invested in investigating the matter. They stated that would look in to it, but did not ask questions, did not request contact information or have any desire to make arrangements to inspect the bike when I offered it. It was unclear whether they would follow up. They appeared to consider this more of a user error. I don't know -- it's in the factory configuration, has traveled maybe 2KM over its life, and should be in good mechanical order.

productDescription: 4 burner, stainless steel gas grill, with side burner and rotisserie searing burner, Kenmore model # 139.01566310, item number 640-04921798-7
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
A gas grill, sold by Sears, under model number 139.01566310 contains a defectively manufactured part, "Drip tray Assembly", part # CH3017361.  This part is a piece of shaped galvanized stainless steel, acting to catch grease/fat drippings from food during cooking. It also provides a thermal barrier between the burners and the LP tank.  Unfortunately, this part, through no fault of the consumer, or lack of maintenance, rusts away and disintegrates, allowing the flame from the burner to be unobstructed within inches of the LP tank. 
Sears has been made aware of this defect, and the grill has been the subject of a class action. 
However, Sears refuses to provide a replacement part, or to have a replacement part manufactured to address this defect. 
When I open the lid of my grill, I can see my LP tank, and have stopped using the grill. The bottom frame of the grill, below the firebox is enclosed so, even the slightest leak of propane, or an improperly tightened hose would result in a catastrophic explosion, due to this failed part. 
When I attempted to order the part from Sears, the order was taken, money was paid, but Sears had no intention of fulfilling the order - I eventually received a refund. However, Sears does not plan to address the safety issue with this grill.

productDescription:
Arm & Hammer OXI CLEAN Dirt Fighters PET FRESH CARPET ODOR ELIMINATOR
VACUUM BOOSTER Loosens & Helps Lift up to __% More Dirt
42.6 oz (2LB.10.6 oz) 1.21kg
UPC CODE 33200 11443
model: Arm & Hammer OXI CLEAN Dirt Fighters PET FRESH CARPET ODOR
incidentDescription:
On 8-8-19, my husband, [REDACTED],  purchased for the very first time, Arm & Hammer product Pet Fresh Carpet Odor Eliminator and in the evening, our pet dog urinated on the rug in our bedroom.  My husband followed the directions on the package and soaked up the urine and let it dry overnight.  

In the morning, about 6:00 a.m. he sprinkled the product on the carpet area which was about a 12" across and waited 15 min. as directed.  The next step was to vacuum the carpet.  As soon as he turned on the vacuum and disturbed the product, the odor produced was totally overwhelming and triggered in me an asthma attack.  

I immediately left the bedroom, closed the door behind me and took my inhaler to help me breathe.  My husband immediately turned off the vacuum and opened all the windows in the bedroom and turned on the fan to help remove the product from the room.  Then, he vacuumed the carpet area for about 5 minutes to remove the product.  The odor continued to be overwhelming!

He then called the Arm & Hammer customer service to report the incident and to find out if there was a way to neutralize the product to help clear the bedroom air.  By this time, [REDACTED] was beginning to feel a tightness in his chest and he does not have asthma.  

The customer service rep. could not find any information on how to neutralize the product and suggested cleaning the area but not to introduce a new product.  My husband inquired about using regular baking soda and the rep. thought it might work.  

My comment was to label the product SCENTED and to put a warning on the label that it is not to be used by customers who have asthma or allergies to scents.

Next, [REDACTED] called the Arm & Hammer Medical Line and reported the incident.  This rep. also could not find any information on how to neutralize the odor but suggested cleaning the area with dish soap & lots of water, soaking it up and letting it dry.  This was 3.5 hours later and the smell in the bedroom is still very strong.  Since the incident, we have opened every window and door in the entire house and have stood outside to clear our lungs.

It is now 5 hours later and [REDACTED] has cleaned the carpet with dish soap and warm water.  Then he sprinkled baking soda on the area and let it sit for an hour.  The odor is starting to dissipate.

I believe that if I would have been directly involved with this product, I would have ended up in the ER receiving medical treatment for my asthma attack.

No product should create a situation that causes an asthma reaction and takes 5 hours with additional cleaning for the odor to begin to dissipate!!!

The ingredients that creates this product need to be analyzed for health issues - I may not be the only customer that has had a severe asthma reaction to this product.

If the ingredients are not harmful to consumers, then this product definitely needs to be labeled SCENTED and carry a warning label that says that it causes allergy and asthma reactions!

productDescription: Saber Cast Black 3-Burner Grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
In August 2017, I purchased a Saber 3-Burner Cast Black Grill. During the weekend of August 11, 2018, when I attempted to light the grill, it burst into flames and exploded. We called the fire department, and the grill was left inoperable. I reported the issue to Saber, and they promptly sent a representative to pickup the grill and provide a new one. (Saber Case # [REDACTED])

This past weekend, on July 27, 2019, I went to light the grill that Saber provided in return for the defective grill in August 2018--and the same thing happened. A loud explosion, a fireball, and all of the grills were displaced when I attempted to light the grill. I called Saber to report the issue again; they declined to provide a refund, and explained that the issue is a "delayed ignition" issue which can be addressed by simply cleaning out the burners. 

There is a real safety issue with these grills. The two issues I have experienced in the last two years are identical to the issue described in the 2017 recall of Saber Grills, although neither one of the Saber Grills I used were within the scope of the recall. 

I requested a refund from Saber Grills, but they declined to provide a refund. They stated that any refund must come from the dealer where I purchased the grill. This grill, however, came directly from the manufacturer.

productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
Please see the email correspondence with the company.

I am concerned about two defects that I noticed in an LP gas replacement burner manufactured by GrillPro/Broil. King/Onward Manufacturing Company Limited. 

1.  The gaskets provided deteriorate within a few weeks of use to the point where they crack, break apart, and cause gaps that could allow gas to escape thereby allowing for the possibility of the gas to be ignited and flames to occur in the areas of the grill where they are not intended and may cause fire or explosion.

2.  The burner is intended for heating separately controlled sides of a grill.  However, I have received three of these  replacement burners over the course of less than two months and all three have had the same defect. The seperating divider within the burner, between the two halves, has large gaps that allow gas to pass from one side to the other when only one side is intended to be lit. Due to the proximity of the gas escaping to the flame on the intended lit side the escaping gas is ignited and either stays lit on the unintended side also or it ignites then goes out then reignites cyclically as the gas accumulates. The user may not expect the other side to be hot causing an accident.

productDescription: Hamilton Beach 1.7 Liter Glass Kettle
incidentDescription:
I purchases a Hamilton Beach 1.7L Electric Kettle for my wife to boil tea water, with an automatic shut-off as soon as the water boiled, to prevent injuries or the kettle boiling dry. At home, I filled the kettle, closed the lid, as pictured in the instruction (hearing and feeling a "click" as the lid closed), and turned on the power switch at the bottom of the kettle. After a few minutes, the water came to a boil, but the kettle would not shut itself off. I tried this sequence several times with the same result.

 I returned the apparently defective kettle to the store, bought another one, tried it out at home, and had the same problem of it never shutting itself off.

 I phoned the Hamilton Beach customer support number and was told I had squeeze two buttons on the top of the kettle's lid with my thumb and middle fingers, while pressing down on the lid with my index finger to get two small plastic latches on the right and left underside of the lid to engage properly with the top rim of the glass kettle. If only one of the latches engaged, I would still feel a "click" when I closed the lid, but the auto shut-off feature would be inoperable. (None of this was explained in the instructions, which simply indicated to close the lid before turning on the power.) I tried this sequence and indeed the auto shut-off worked when the kettle began to boil!

I then explained and demonstrated the procedure to my wife. Unfortunately, my wife is in the early stages of a common condition in older people called Parkinson's Disease. This disease causes gradual loss of sensation, muscle strength, dexterity, and agility. My wife tried to follow my instructions, squeezing the left and right buttons as she pressed the lid closed. She felt a "click" and turned on the power.  the kettle began boiling slowly, then progressed to a rapid, full, rolling boil, without shutting off. Realizing her mistake, my wife reached for the lid to squeeze the buttons and push down again, so both rather than just one latch would become engaged. However her hand was quickly scalded by the very hot steam spewing out  the spout and around the edges of the lid. 

In retrospect, when the kettle continued boiling,  it would have been safer to turn off the power switch at the bottom of the kettle than to touch anything on the lid to re-engage the auto shut-off function. However, I could imagine many others making the same mistake when the auto shut-off unexpectedly didn't work.

I understand that the lid should be latched when the water is heating, so that very hot water does not splash out of the kettle when one is trying to pour it slowly into a cup or pot. If the kettle can "tell" when the lid is only partially latched, why not prevent the heating element from even coming on -- rather than disabling the auto shut-off safety feature? 

If, for some reason, this arcane procedure must be followed to enable the auto shut-off function, it should at least be explained in the owner's manual.

productDescription:
Nutri Ninja Blender. It has a cup that has a blade assembly which screws onto the top. Like this:
https://www.amazon.com/Nutri-Ninja-BL456-Pro-Blender/dp/B076QGMGF7/ref=asc_df_B076QGMGF7/?tag=hyprod-20&linkCode=df0&hvadid=242218982356&hvpos=1o1&hvnetw=g&hvrand=8490414336739869759&hvpone=&hvptwo=&hvqmt=&hvdev=c&hvdvcmdl=&hvlocint=&hvlocphy=9016839&hvtargid=pla-404525030821&psc=1
incidentDescription:
I have owned a Nutri-Ninja blender for three years. it is the type that has a blade assembly that "screws on" to the top of the cup you drink out of. 
I've been meticulous about washing it really well after each use. It goes in the dishwasher each time and I also wipe it with a rag.
About a month ago, I started noticing some black flakes in my smoothies. At first I thought it was the fruit I was using. But, then I noticed that the black flakes were consistent, regardless of the fruit I was using. 
I washed the blade assembly very thoroughly and put it through the dishwasher multiple times.
It turns out the black flakes were mold growing inside the assembly of the blades! There is a rubber gasket that's about a half-inch wide that's shoved deep inside the blade assembly. Moisture gets inside this area and mold has been growing! (It doesn't look like I can upload a photo, but, I have a picture of this, it's super gross!)
I had no idea that this was supposed to come apart. There was nothing in the manual which says to wash this gasket. And, it took me using two screwdrivers in my workshop to pry that thing out, so, it's not something that an average person can easily fix. 
Shark Ninja Inc should be forced to recall these blenders or offer a new design on the blade/top of the cups so that people can actually clean these. At the very least, there should be a warning in the manual with instructions on how to clean this obscure part of the product.
This poses a health risk. Both my nine-year-old daughter and I drank smoothie after smoothie filled with mold as a result of this poor design. Something should be done.

Memorial Day weekend this year (2019) we brought it out of the garage, thoroughly cleaned it inside and out and began using it again this season. I’d say between last summer and this May/June we have used the grill maybe 20-25 times total. This past weekend, my husband was preheating the grill and within 5 minutes we smelled an awful burning smell. We opened up the grill and flames were everywhere. It was totally on fire. After turning off all the burners, we closed the lid to try to have the fire burn itself out. Nope. That didn’t work. Flames began shooting out the bottom of the grill (where the drip pan is). THANK GOD it put the whole fire out. The inside of the grill is destroyed. The cookbox is melted in several locations and melted to the drip pan. productDescription: 2-burner BBQ Grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
On July 1, 2018, I bought a Weber Spirit E210, 2-burner BBQ at Ace Hardware in Jackson, Wyoming.	For a variety of reasons, including the fact I have a larger, [REDACTED]grill, I did not used it very often. However, whenever I did use it to BBQ a whole chicken, grease seeped everywhere, and as the grease ran down its sides, it dripped onto, and burned, my deck. (I am enclosing 4 photographs .) Last summer, I was preoccupied with other matters, stopped using the grill, and did not contact Weber or the CPSC.

As we got prepared for this summer season, we thoroughly cleaned the grill. But when I BBQed another whole chicken, I had the same result - grease went everywhere . So, we cleaned it again, this time getting it as clean as it was when it was "brand-spanking new." Then I grilled another whole chicken, and again, lots of grease ran down its sides, and dripped onto my deck.

Accordingly, I called Weber's customer service line. The representative asked for photographs; I sent the ones attached hereto, and after he looked at them, he called and said, "when you BBQ fatty things, that will happen; it is normal and to be expected."

I responded: First, there wasn't much fat on any of those chickens, as I always remove the fat before BBQing.	WAY MORE IMPORTANT : Weber should not manufacture a BBQ that gushes grease when someone grills a chicken - I suspect, one of the most commonly grilled items .

Because I was taken aback at his response; I asked to speak to his supervisor and was transferred to her. She essentially said the same thing he had.

When I asked to speak to her supervisor, she said her supervisor had left for the day but would call me the next morning . She didn't!

It took a week before she finally called. When she did, she agreed there was a problem and said she would ship me a replacement unit, which has a slightly newer design, I said that would probably work and went to Ace to see how the new model differed from mine. The newer model has two wheels - mine has four and I need four - so I told her I would pay the difference and upgrade to the next model (a [REDACTED]), and that's what I did.
 
When I told the Customer Service Manager, she told me she would arrange tor Ace to refund my purchase price, pick up my Spirit, and destroy it.	I was shocked and said, 11 DESTROY IT! Don't you want to inspect it and see why it leaks grease?" "No," she replied.

My Spirit (and perhaps others) is extremely dangerous and I cannot believe Weber doesn't want to inspect it and figure out why so much grease escapes. Maybe it wasn't assembled properly (that was done by Ace), perhaps it has a faulty part, etc .? But SIGNIFICANTLY MORE WORRISOME : why does Weber want it to be destroyed without inspecting it? ASAP, NO LESS!

As an aside : two weeks ago, we had some young families and their kids over for dinner, and although I used the larger [REDACTED to BBQ, I realized those kids could easily have been seriously burned if I had been using the Spirit and they touched it.  Consequently, I contacted you.

I hope the Consumer Product Safety Commission will look into this matter - indeed, inspect the Spirit and determine if mine is the only one with an issue or if all 2-burner E210s need to be recalled.

Thanks,
[REDACTED]

productDescription: Portable outdoor gas grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
Charbroil grill2go x200 purchased approximately  May 25 2019 returned to retailer approximately  2 weeks later
2 major problems both concerning the regulator control

1. The grill, on low, would run over 600 degrees with no food inside, no grease fire, all from gas source

2. After weeks of ownership the fuel began bypassing the control valve on the regulator. This led to fuel flowing into the grill with the odor of gas (propane scent) noticeable 30 feet away. This occurred when the grill was turned to lock which is an extension of the off position. Fuel bypassed the control valve into the burner which had not been lit yet and was unattended and assumed off for 15 minutes. All fuel components were checked at for leaks at time of connection and none were detected, meaning the failure occurred after the grill was inspected to be safe within minutes of the failure. After failure fuel was only noticeable as coming from the brass nozzle that is inserted into the burner with the valve confirmed again as still off AND locked.  Valve was never handled with more than “fingertip” force and regulator never dropped or subjected to any damaging force since purchased.

3. Charbroil customer service advised of issue and questioned if there was another revision to the regulator.  Was advised that there were 2 revisions. CS advised that they could not trace by manufacture date code nor serial number what revision grill was equipped with when failure occurred.

4. Not wanting another regulator that may have the exact problem, grill was returned for exchange of different model.  Grill was purchased and returned to Lowe’s in Port Richey, FL. Lowe’s web page for the product shows reviewers making frequent complaints of overheating on low and other regulator related problems. Seemingly these are the only complaints about this product.

5. I am reporting this because I had adverted catastrophe with it is apparently far from isolated

incidentDescription:
Bought a Cuisinart DTC-975BKN Programmable 12 cup coffee maker.  I had read other reviewers Amazon complaints that it tends to spill over and has caused burns. The coffee maker kept spilling over, then the third time used, just stopped working.  Amazon exchanged it, and the replacement did the same thing.

productDescription: Gooseneck Kettle with pop welded handleAWK -210SB
manufacturer: Mirama Enterprises Inc. dba Aroma Housewares Company
incidentDescription:
The product of reference is Aroma Housewares. Model #AWK -210SB Gooseneck Kettle. The kettle sits on an electric hot plate configuration to heat the water placed within. The attachment of the handle is the concern. It is not mechanically attached. And I apologize but I believe is some kind of electronic weld, if you will. 
I’ve already sent a request previously (5 times ) to the manufacturer through their website, but I have had no response. THIS IS MY REPORT TO THE MANUFACTURER. I have your lovely gooseneck kettle for less than one year. When using it, full of hot water, the handle popped off (it was not attached by a screw to make sure there was what I would call a belt and suspenders in design) while I was transferring it full of “boiling” water to pour into my French press. You can tell how the unit was attached, the upper two nodules (of this perceived weld) barely had anything connected. This is a product defect. I am fortunate that I was not scolded with hot (boiling) water as most of it came out onto the floor. And I am fortunate that my dog was not injured either.  When it fell it could’ve easily damaged the floor but it did not, it broke its own fall and dented the base and part of the plastic piece of the base cane apart as well. I am requesting a new kettle from you, the manufacturer.  By the way in your description of the product to talk about safety. I would be concerned about using the word safety when the handles of these units can pop off. 

First of all, I’m fortunate I was not hurt, and was hopeful that the manufacture would care enough to contact me concerning this matter. If I wasn’t quick enough to jump out of the way, this hot boiling water could possibly had burnt me  significantly , broke small bones in my foot or severely hurt a pet or small child who frequently our at our feet, not to mention possible property damage. And here’s an opportunity to (I hope) make the Manufacturer pay attention to safety that they tout so much on their website. It’s honestly a simple manufacturing defect, it happens. But they should recognize the errors and Rectify any issues or concerns of consumers have

When I jumped off the scooter it was still moving and I was still trying to break with my hands. As a result the forward momentum pulled me down and my face hit the concrete curb. When I was able to sit back up I realized that the impact of hitting the curb had given me a large (2-3") laceration that extended from my upper lip to my left nostril (basically my lip was cut in half). I was fortunate that a taxi passed a minute or two after I fell - and I was able to get a ride to GWU hospital, here in Washington, D.C. A ENT surgeon at GWU repaired the laceration (with 30 stitches), but I will have a scar the rest of my life.

model HW1012T

incidentDescription:
At approximately 6PM on April 10, 2019 my wife came home to find our house smoky with a strange smell in the air. She sent our daughters outside and began a frantic search for the source. She finally found our EHEAT Envi Heater in our daughters' room charred, smoking and melted near the power switch for the heater. She shut off the break to the heater and removed the heater from the room, then notified me at work about what had happened. 

The heater was hardwired with power being fed off the GFCI outlet in my daughters sink area. This incident did not trip the GFCI on the outlet or the breaker in the main electrical panel. It also did not set off the smoke detectors (which have since been tested and found to be working with back up batteries dated 10-2018). The heater has a built in thermostat and is normally left in the on position. Until last week it had been "on" all winter, but I turned it off last week when we went out of town. I can't say for sure if cycling the switch last week contributed to the failure, but it seems like it may have. 

I was inform last spring of a recall on these heater and did, at that time, use EHeat's web site to see if my heaters (I purchased 3 originally) were affected by the recall. productDescription:
Honeywell heater
Model: 360 SURROUND HEAT
MODEL# HHF360V
Serial #: SPM13791125119
incidentDescription:
Heater was purchased from Target store in Lathrop, California (off highway 5) in November 2016.

The Honeywell heater was used from November 2016 to February 2017. The heater was purchased because the advertisement represented it to be a "safety" heater, and was made with:
1. A "cool housing";
2. "Over heat" protection; and
3. Exceeded "safety requirements.”

On the night of February 13, 2017, Ms. [REDACTED] took her boyfriend to dinner for his birthday and when they came back she was standing next to the heater talking to her boyfriend. Ms. [REDACTED] remembered saying the heater was kind of hot, so she stepped further away from it. She never touched the heater with her leg. She was always standing a few feet away from it. Ms. [REDACTED] and her friend talked for a few more minutes and then retired.

Her leg felt warm but not painful. She did not feel a burn and went to bed. When she woke up the next morning, she had "large blisters" across her leg. When she tried to turn the heater on the next day it would not turn on.

Ms. [REDACTED] stayed home from work and put a wet cloth on the blistered area. The following day, the blisters started to turn a dark color. Ms. [REDACTED] went to her Doctors for treatment. She continued to be treated by her Doctors every other day to apply bandages, and silver sulfadiazine cream.

Ms. [REDACTED] contacted Honeywell several times and reported the problem with the heater and her injuries. They did nothing to follow up with the product

For the next two months, Ms. [REDACTED] travelled to [REDACTED] two or three times a week for treatment of her "blister" burns. Her leg is still "pitted and ugly". Ms. [REDACTED] intends on obtaining a "skin graft" and/or "plastic surgery" treatments to try to make the affected areas of "discoloration" and "pitting" appear more normal.

The front of the heater is buckled and melted in minimally four places from the overheating. The switch is melted as well. The switch on the heater makes a loud unusual sound it when you try to turn it on and does not function.

There is no doubt, this Honeywell heater was (and is) defective and is not fit for its intended use. That is the commonality and similarity with many other Honeywell recalled heaters. This heater shares common problems with other defective
Honeywell heaters also.

productDescription: Kitchen Aid Artisan stand mixer with tilt head and metal bowl
incidentDescription: I recently purchased a new Kitchen Aid Artisan stand mixer with tilting motor head. Both times that I have used the mixer to mix dough, the mechanism that is supposed to lock the upper motor portion of the mixer in place during mixing has vibrated back in to the unlocked position within seconds of turning on the mixer. As soon as the locking mechanism springs back to the unlocked position, it causes the upper motor portion of the mixer to shoot up and cause the entire mixer to lunge forward. If you don’t literally stand there with your hand on the motor portion of the mixer holding it down during the use, the entire mixer “walks” across the counter from the vibration of mixing doughs. It is not inconceivable for this to send a mixer over the edge  of a counter.  The locking mechanism seriously does not work. In addition, twice while I’ve used the mixer for doughs, the failure of the locking mechanism to properly hold the upper motor piece down has caused the mixer to vibrate so badly that the pin that allows the mixer top to pivot in the stand base has vibrated almost completely out of the base. This is a brand new mixer, used maybe 4 times. There should not be mechanism failures like this. I have sustained no injuries as a result of the design flaws of the mixer, but I can very easily see one of these mixers lunging over the side of a counter during the failure of the locking mechanism or the pivot pin vibrating out causing the motor piece to fall off the stand base.

productDescription: A vacuum made for hard floors and area rugs that dispenses pulses of cleaning solution onto a rotating terrycloth roller brush. The rotating brush washes the floor, propels debris into the mouth of the vacuum and the rotating brush also picks up most of the cleaning solution and slings it into the mouth of the vacuum where it is eventually deposited into a receiving tank which is then removed and emptied.
incidentDescription:
I purchased a Bissell Crosswave floor cleaner in December of 2017.
These machines are a type of vacuum that uses a terrycloth roller brush to sweep debris into the mouth of the vacuum while dispensing short pulses of cleaning solution onto the spinning roller brush.
The idea is that the spinning terrycloth roller brush will wash the floor and then pick up most of the dirty cleaning solution and sling the dirty cleaaning solution into the mouth of the vacuum where the dirty cleaning solution is eventually deposited into a receiving tank, which is eventually removed from the machine and emptied.
Since buying this machine we have had to have it replaced by Bissell twice so far, and the third machine is in our dining room waiting for yet another replacement machine. Each machine has failed but for different problems. ALL THREE of these machines have a common problem, which Bissell chooses to ignore. ALL THREE of these machines have shocked me with a mild electric charge!
These machines do not suck up all of the cleaning solution! They are not only not capable, but not expected to suck up all of the cleaning solution. The floor is still slightly wet. Not just damp, but wet!
I have many times had to remove the front see-thru housing that encloses the floor brush to remove minor clogs; small twigs and long pine needles that the vacuum can't pick up are common in our home. When I touch the wet terrycloth roller brush I get SHOCKED! The only way to prevent this is to unplug the machine, but I don't think these machines should be shocking me even when it IS plugged in!
The flooring that we use this machine on range from sheet vinyl, real wood flooring, and "click-lock" flooring that is 95% PVC plastic with a very thin foam rubber backing. I have been shocked in all three rooms, on all three types of flooring! The machine has shocked me when plugged into  properly grounded outlets in each room, and I have even experienced being shocked when the machine was plugged into BOTH GFCI outlets! This happens in ANY outlet!
This electric charge has so far not been strong enough to hurt me, but strong enough to startle me! I find it very disturbing that ALL THREE of these machines have had this same problem!
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: Thermos® Foogo® 10-Ounce Leak-Proof Food Jar. Blue and yellow colors.
incidentDescription: I purchased 2 Foogo 10-ounce food jars and washed them as the instructions specified. The jars will grow mold because there is no way for the water to escape, and since this is something my children eat out of, it is a safety issue. After asking other mothers who have similar Foogo products, I learned their also have this problem. I also found several photos of people who broke off the bottoms to find tons of mold. This company is selling a line of products with a design flaw that allows for mold to grow no matter what you do to prevent it. My children and I were not injured but I could see others with mold allergies or sensitivities having dangerous problems.

incidentDescription:

I could not comb through my hair.
I can supply photos of the area where the hair got sucked in.
I talked with a Dyson representative. This is a KNOWN problem which the representative described to me.
I was able to replicate the safety issue of things getting sucked in at the top using yarn I have  a video of the issue.

productDescription: Vornado AVH10 Vortex Heater, a portable space heater
incidentDescription: On January 31, 2019, I purchased a Vornado AVH10 Vortex heater. After using the heater for about a month, on March 4, 2019, the heater stopped working. When I inspected the heater, I discovered that on the back panel, the vent had partially melted towards the top of the unit. This was alarming to me considering that I only used the heater for about two or three hours at a time at a temperature of no more than 72 degrees. (For reference, the lowest temperature of the heater is 65 degrees.) If I had been using this heater for longer periods of time or at higher temperatures, it's possible that the casing of the heater could have melted further and dripped into the heater itself, possibly causing a fire - or at least a fire hazard. I did some research online to see if anyone else has had a similar experience with their heaters of the same model. There are many complaints regarding the same issue posted by many reviewers on the product page for the unit on Amazon, where I purchased the heater. Some reviews include pictures showing damage from melting that is very similar to what I saw on my heater. A brand new heater should not be melting after one month of use for reasonable periods of time at relatively low temperatures. It appears that the problems that caused another Vornado heater to be recalled last year are still present in other units currently being sold. I would like for this issue to be investigated to ensure that this heater does not pose safety hazards to consumers. (Also, I have pictures, but this website will not allow me to attach them because I receive an error message each time.)

incidentDescription:
