It was left plugged in on our kitchen counter. At about 10pm I was in bed when my wife heard a grinding noise from the kitchen and went to investigate. The coffee grinder was on fire, emitting thick black smoke and flames which had just caught the cabinet above it on fire. Fortunately, I was able to put it out with a fire extinguisher, and pulled the plug on the coffee grinder and it stopped. It must have switched on by itself and ground until it overheated and caught fire. There was minimal damage, considering, only about $1000 worth of materials, and about $3000 worth of labor from a contractor to repair it. If we had not caught it when we did, it certainly would have caught the house and burned down as we slept.

I saved the coffee grinder, and took many pictures from every angle. I emailed the Mr Coffee company through their contact us form, but have not heard anything back from them for a week. Looking online, it did not seem like this was a common problem, but at least two other people reported the same thing happening on various websites.

Just recently I noticed that there was a tear in one of the corners - probably from the wind. Since the cover had a warranty of 5 years, I went to take photos of the tear for purposes of getting a refund. After taking the photos (attached) I noticed that my fingers were covered in a white powder / dust which concerned me. I then located the box which stated that the cover was made from polyester which is a plastic and coated with PVC (polyvinyl chloride) which is another form of plastic. I than went online to research and learn if PVC was toxic (I try to refrain from buying products made in China whenever possible - they paint our children's toys with lead based paint and put anti-freeze in our toothpaste).

It didn't take long to find out that PVC is indeed very toxic. 

After a little over a year of slight use, this product began to decompose emitting a poisonous dust. I do not want to breath it in - I don't want it on my cloths and I definitely don't want it anywhere near my food. When I tried to contact Kenmoore (several times - 866-872-7442 - the # on the box the cover came in) no one answered and no returned my call for several weeks. When someone finally did get back to me she said that she could not issue me a refund and that she was only authorized to send me a replacement. I explained to her that the cover was made out of a toxic material and I did not want a similar one that was destined to decompose and emit a poisonous dust just as the one I already have. This is a bad product and never should have been put on the market to begin with. Please help me get my money back so that I can purchase a BBQ cover that won't kill me - and this product should be taken off the market asap.

incidentDescription:

I was lucky to be sitting right next to the product when it caught fire.

I reported it to the manufacturer as well as amazon.  I took photographs as well.

Then, a second charger, identical to the first,  melted within two days of the first.  This unit was in my bedroom and caught my mattress protector on fire. (The cable that was attached to it was sitting next to my bed and melted onto the plastic protector)

Again, I contacted amazon and the seller/manufacturer.  I was refunded but the products are still listed for sale.

The company claims in their listings to be UL certified amongst other certifications.  I believe this to be false.

The company, upon seeing that I left negative feedback for them, offered me $200 as compensation for my damages (my computer cost over $1000 and was destroyed) IF I would agree to remove the negative feedback.
I did not accept and they had my feedback removed.  I added more feedback and to this date, it is still up- as well as others that have claimed fires, shorts, and melting.  

The products are dangerous- that I'm convinced of.  What are the odds it would happen not once, but twice with two different items in the same household?

incidentDescription: I want to report a potential fire hazard safety concern regarding the Belkin 27 Watt Power Adapter USB charger, model F7U011dq.  I plugged in the USB charger while in flight to an AC power outlet provided at the seat.  I connected the charger to an [REDACTED].  The USB charger was intermittent in charging. productDescription: Cordless Drill
incidentDescription:
The consumer indicates that he charged the battery to his cordless drill for approximately forty-five minutes and then proceeded to install the battery. The consumer placed the drill on top of a hat that was sitting on a chair afterwards. About four hours later, the consumer woke up to the smell of burning wires. When the consumer checked around his home, he noticed that the drill had caught fire. The consumer quickly picked up the hat the drill was in and threw it on his front yard. Ten minutes later the consumer removed the battery from the drill; the consumer states that the drill was still hot. The consumer notes that the drill had a hole in it approximately one inch in diameter.

The consumer states that the smell of burning wires still lingers in his home.

The consumer indicates that he has another one of these drills in his vehicle that he has since removed the battery from in fear of another fire.

The consumer indicates that, prior to the incident, the unit was used once or twice per month.

productDescription: Winplus car jump starter portable power bank
incidentDescription: Was charging the winplus car jump starter over night to use in the morning. At approximately 0800 in the morning (about 12 hours on the charger) I heard a bang shortly followed by the fire alarm. Saw on the kitchen the unit looked like it exploded from inside out and was on fire. Also the users manual next to it was on fire. I quickly put out the fire but there was still damage to the counter top where it was sitting.

productDescription: Dyson DC24 Vacuum:  530-US C31514
incidentDescription:

-there was a loud 'pop' and the breaker tripped
-one of the 2 pins was melted on the inside and disconnected from the plug when we unplugged the vacuum from the outlet
-one pin was left in the outlet, when we removed it, there were clear black with burn marks on the inside the pin - part typically covered by plastic
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: Space Heater
productType: Heaters or Heating Systems, Other or Not Specified (393)
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription:
The consumer indicates that his tenant called him because there was a burning smell in her apartment. When the consumer went to check, he noticed a distinct plastic burning smell, and once he looked around, he noticed that it was coming from the space heater even though the unit was not on. The consumer lifted the unit and noticed a burn hole in the carpet about one point five inches in diameter.

The consumer notes that he has purchased three of the same units in the past however they stopped working within the first year and a half. The consumer has an extra two units that are still functioning however he stopped using them because he is concerned about the fire hazard they pose.

11/15/2018 - The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation; the representative he spoke to unformed him that they stopped manufacturing this product two years ago. The representative did not offer any assistance for the unit in question nor the remaining three.

The consumer indicates that the space heater was used approximately every other day for about three to four hours during the colder months for the past two years. 

The consumer plans on keeping his space heater for at least the next thirty days in case in investigation ensues.

incidentDescription:

Everyone in the household was cautioned about turning the dial too far to the stay on position. Then the toaster was found on two more times long after it was used. The toaster oven is turning itself on from what is labeled “0” (zero) on the timer dial. This is extremely dangerous given how hot the toaster oven gets.

productDescription: Hand mixer
incidentDescription:
Caller stated that while using the mixer a piece of hard plastic flew out of the unit.  She stated that the object came from the opening of the back of the mixer which landed on the table top.  Caller stated that when took the casing off she noticed that blades were not attached to the fan and the plastic pieces were loose inside interior cavity.

Caller stated that she had made cookies using the mixer and is not sure if there are pieces of foreign objects inside the cookies.

Caller stated that she contacted the manufacturer and left a voicemail.  Caller feels that this mixer is unsafe and should be reported.

Caller mailed in an update to the report stating, "Just wanted to emphasize that I recovered 5 pieces of hard plastic that appear to be fan blades (see photo) but that is appeared that at least 8 blades were missing from the fans. The posterior fan had all blades missing (see photo). The fan blade pieces probably landed in food something although I can't be sure any landed in my Christmas cookies. However, I felt I could not take the change of serving them to my grandkids. I just threw them out. Also, this company had a problem similar to this in 1992 which was reported to CPSC and Hamilton Beach did a voluntary recall at that time. Although not the same model number as now, Hamilton Beach models 230 & 232 hand held mixers had broken cooling fans and broken fan pieces contaminated food & caused injuries in 15 incidents (Per news from CPSC - release # 92-043). I don't think this company had done due diligence in re fans/fan blade."

incidentDescription: A small 18 inch under-cabinet fluorescent tube light fixture became excessively hot when a bulb began to burn out. When the bulb started to fail, one side of the fixture became so hot that the plastic fixture surrounding the bulb warped, melted, and came in to contact with the bulb. The issue was discovered when a "hot plastic" smell was noticed and traced to the fixture. The plastic that was near to and in contact with the bulb turned dark brown and "bubbly" from the heat. productDescription: Lime electric scooter. Not sure if breaks malfunctioned but lost control around a corner.
incidentDescription: My 22 year old daughter was using a Lime Electric Scooter in Old Town, Scottsdale AZ. The sidewalk took a sharp turn and the scooter was unable to stop to slow down to take the corner. As a result, she was thrown off the scooter and was knocked unconscious for over 10 minutes. She suffered severe head trauma as well as trauma to the lower back, chest, arm and face. She was taken by ambulance, unconscious to the closest trauma ER hospital. She suffered a double skull fracture and brain bleed and swelling to the head. She remained in the ICU for 4 days and was sent home. Upon returning home, she suffered extreme pain which was uncontrollable from non IV meds, from the brain bleed "feathering" out in tight areas of her brain, and went back to the ICU in hospital again. She lost a month of work, and is looking at a 120K hospital bill to date.

productDescription: Heatilator gas fireplace heater
incidentDescription:
Heatilator  gas heater has leak in valve.  Valve is buried in concrete fireplace wall.  No way to discover leak in defective valve  until you smell gas.  By then, it may be TOO LATE!  BOOM !.   
Heatilator refers consumer to local dealer.  Dealer (Trinity Hearth & Home)  wants to charge $150 to inspect the  defective part.   Dealer says the  defective part is not part of a recall and no parts are available. Dealer denies liability and refers us to EBAY to search for a used  replacement valve.  Heatilator Company will not talk to us about the situation and says contact the dealer who again denies any responsibility.....thereby creating an endless loop of denial.
There is no way for a consumer to discover this defective valve unless he/she  smells gas or it goes BOOM!

Since the defect is not discoverable until the part fails, Heatilator is responsible to cure the defect even if is not part of a recall.  Like a defective part on an airplane...consumer cannot discover defect until the crash.  Heatilator should replace the defective valve before it causes an explosion.

productDescription: King Pellet Stove
incidentDescription:
I had purchased a King Pellet Stove in September or 2018, at Tractor Supply Co, the stove was installed in October of 2018 oer manufacturers instructions using the recommended ventilation kit purchased also at Tractor Supply.
Upon initial start of the unit , it had what was expected as a "burn in" period where you could expect  the burn off smell of a paint etc in a new heating product.
However, this unit shut down and failed to eject the smoke contained in the unit and smoke emitted into the basement area of my home. Also the unit burned extremely dirty leaving large deposits of unburned pellets and residue.
I also explained the unit was feeding pellets too fast,
I had made a call the following business day to the customer service number provided in the owners manual. I had an extremely hard time talking to a representative, and you do not know if you are actually talking to a technical agent or not, after spending hours both calling and texting messages. These issues were brought up in a BBB complaint, filed in November 2018.
Customer service personnel instructed me to make adjustments on the control panel, the unit (once I got a hold of one, and would not tell me if they were "technical" support or customer) in which resulted in the unit again burning off excess smoke filling my basement again with smoke, again many calls made back and once someone got back to me I explained the issues, not burning correctly( sent them pictures and videos of what was happening and the installation, also feeding too many pellets, again they gave me adjustment to make and finally it got to where the unit just filled and over filled the pellet bowl and would not light, and the one time it did an extremely large fire inside with all the pellets and I shutdown unit,
In the mean time the customer service representative stated they would first send me a new blower unit, now this is brand new barely 3 bags of pellets through it, and another stated they would send an ignition card, both times I explained how would I know how to install these, and they said to you-tube it!
I reminded them that in their instruction manual it specifically states to NEVER try to repair or replace any parts of the stove unless instructions for doing so are in the manual, in which  they are not.
This is stated twice in the manual, first page and page 17., thus contradicting their safety instructions.
I reached an exchange agreement with Tractor Supply since I was outside their 30 day return policy as well as filing a BBB complaint against the company which they said they would send me 300.00 for my trouble, in which they never did, again it smoked my house twice, and I had to pay for an install and uninstall, and another install!
Also my local Tractor supply stated they had several of the same units exchanged for the same reasons!
Representative did not respond to my question after that and have not responded to my calls or text.

Secondly, if you don't notice it right away (as in this morning), the electric cord where it goes into the unit sits in the water. Furthermore,  you can smell a burning scent as it is dripping on the inside of the coffeemaker and getting onto the internal heating element. The original date of my problem started in February of 2018. I notified the company in July 2018, replacement sent out on July 19th and now the replacement product has the same issue (January 2019).

productDescription:
Black and Decker Countertop Convection Oven 
12" pizza capacity
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
brand: Black and Decker Convection Countertop oven
incidentDescription:
In June of 2018, I replaced my former Black and Decker digital convection toaster oven with this new, out of the box, Black and Decker countertop convection toaster/oven (Model TO1640B).  
I purchased this current oven at BIG LOTS on North 72nd St in Omaha, NE in 2013.  (I stored it a few years because I thought my former toaster oven was failing, but discovered a button stuck on it, and once that was corrected the oven lasted another 5 years). 
After some months of using this current oven, it became apparent that there was some design flaws that gave me concern of its safety and potential fire hazard.
Two main problems have occurred repeatedly over the past few months, and it wasn't until recently that the oven was discovered ON and Very hot after having supposedly shut off over an hour prior.
This occurs in one of 2 ways:
1. If you are wanting to toast or heat and item for less than 10 minutes (as in a 2-3 minutes to toast an item and fail to turn the dial for the toast/timer far past 20 and then counter clockwise to the 2-5 minutes, the unit will stay on at whatever temperature the dial setting for TEMP is at, and will remain on for an infinite time. (this happened most recently on Sunday December 30, 2018, though it has happened on other occasions prior).  with this incident an piece of bread still remained in the oven and upon smelling the burning some long hour or so later, it became evident the oven was still ON.
Even though the appliance has a note to turn past 20 before setting the time, this seems haphazardly dangerous and has no safety measure to assure an operator has done so.  The oven will operate in the ON once the dial deviates slightly from the OFF point on the dial.

2. The second way this oven inadvertantly remaining ON unknown to the operator is that if you manually turn the TIMER/TOAST dial to the OFF point, it does not stop there, it will continue past the OFF point and turn the oven back in the ON status.  You do not have to turn it counterclockwise to the point where it says STAY ON for the oven to be turned back on with out noticing.  You think you have turned the oven OFF because an audible bell dings when you get to what you would think is OFF, except the dial doesn't have much of a safe check to keep you from overturning it.  I want to emphasize that you can just slightly over turn it counter-clockwise and it will turn the oven back on.  
Rotate it another half inch counter clock wise and you will reach the STAY ON point of the control.
The big problem here is you don't have to turn it all the way to STAY ON point for the oven to return ON, it only has to be just slightly a jar the OFF point.  
I keep my oven in a large appliance garage.  The door is open and has very adequate ventilation around it and above to operate safely.  A problem occurred when the unit was presumed off and the door was shut to the garage.
 It's not a safe appliance and I have removed it from my kitchen.
I spoke with Black and Decker consumer services regarding my concern and that do not intend to take any action over the matter.  I have asked that my complaint be brought to the attention to there product engineers and follow up with me.  There has been no correspondence what so ever.

productDescription: Forced Air Kerosene Space Heater
incidentDescription: I purchased a Master Industrial Products kerosene space heater model MH-75T-KFA, S/N 170722309.  The fuel tank's cap is made of a plastic that appears to be incompatible with kerosene.  What happens is that the portion of the cap that is inside the tank swells making it very difficult to remove.  Once you successfully pry it off the tank, you cannot get it back on because the "nose" of the cap is larger than the hole it goes in due to the swelling of the plastic.  So one has to operate the heater with an OPEN fuel tank or you can modify the cap by sanding off the swollen area of the cap to get it to fit for a short time, which most consumers would not think to try to do.  The locking pin in the cap's nose also falls out due to the swelling of the plastic.  The plastic continues to deteriorate due to being incompatible with kerosene, even after a sanding modification.  I called the manufacturer and found out that they offer a metal cap that you can purchase (they won't provide for free) which on face value, seems to indicate they know they have a problem with their plastic fuel cap.  This model (or the entire series that uses these plastic caps) should be subject to a recall before serious fires occur from people operating these heaters without the fuel cap.  I have the faulty cap in my possession.

incidentDescription: I bought one of the Red Stone 30,000 btu vent free gas wall heaters several years ago from Tractor Supply. The model number is MD300TBA-RS Serial #12542450. They are set up to use either Natural Gas or Propane depending on how you need it. Ours was natural gas. After the first couple years, it started flaring up in an uncontrolled manner, and luckily I caught it in time, so I contacted the company. They wouldn't make it right, but they did sell me a new gas control valve body to replace the original defective one. The unit functioned perfectly after that until today when the unit started venting raw, unburned natural gas into our garage and filled our house up. incidentDescription:
The product is a Cuisinart Mini-Prep Processor, Model DLC-1, Serial# 30928

This plastic hub assembly is cracked on both sides of the chopping blade and it appears the metal blade could separate when processor is at operating speed. So far the blades have not separated from the hub and no injuries occurred during its use today. 
Cuisinart had a similar recall for chopping blade assemblies back in 2016 but this specific model number was not one of the processors listed in that recall campaign. This unit looks as if it may have a similar issue which should be investigated before someone gets injured.
I stopped using the Mini-Prep and called Cuisinart about this issue. The rep I talked to at the recall phone number indicated that Cuisinart would replace the blade assembly free of charge and redirected my call to the warranty department. This representative was not interested in assisting me unless I could produce a receipt. I explained that this was a safety issue but this claim did not seem to convince her to help out in this situation and she repeated her mantra stating they would not replace it without a proof of purchase receipt (which I no longer have).
My concern is how many other blades are out there in this condition that could possibly cause injury to unsuspecting consumers.
I have photos of the defective parts but have not seen how to upload them for your review.

productDescription: Ninja Fit Personal Blender, Model QB3001SS
incidentDescription:
This product is in the category of personal blenders which generally include three main components: an ingredients cup, a cover with an integrated mixing blade, and an electric motor.  The latest iteration of these devices are marketed as personal juicers, pairing a high-wattage motor along with very sharp blades. 

The manufacturer provides standard cautions, however this device and seeming the majority in the category do not provide a cover or some means of shielding the blade mechanism when it is not in use.  As a result it is easy to cut or stab ones hands while using, cleaning, or storing the device.  That has happened several times resulting in minor injuries thus far.  Furthermore, the majority of these integrated lid/blade mechanisms tend to be black in color and camouflage their presence on a counter or inside a dark cabinet.  

I implore the CPSC and manufacturers (e.g. Ninja) to implement simple safeguards to reduce the likelihood of injury. Ninja specifically produces personal and counter top devices containing sharp mixing blades yet don’t include a protective cover to prevent users (and children)  from inadvertently contacting the blades.
.

My client owned a Medelco 8 cup glass stove top coffee percolator, model #PK008. The glass percolator was on the back right burner of the stove while she was cooking dinner on 10/14/2016. She noticed that the burner under the percolator was on. She turned off the burner and went to remove the percolator. The plastic handle was not hot to the touch. She lifted the percolator off to place it on the butcher block next to the stove, at which point the inside plastic parts including the plastic percolator basket and basket stand became liquefied plastic and erupted out of the glass percolator.
The liquefied plastic splashed onto her hands, causing third degree burns to her right right hand and fingers, as well as scarring and other injuries.
The product is manufactured by Medelco, Inc. It was previously sold under the brand name "One All" and now under the brand name "Cafe Brew". The company operates its manufacturing business out of a facility at 54 Washburn Street, Bridgeport, Connecticut 06605.
User reviews on numerous online retailers, including Amazon, cite incidents of the percolator's plastic parts melting. These user reviews reporting that plastic parts "melted" date back to at least January 2012. Some user reviews include photographs showing the melted plastic parts.

incidentDescription: Ok so I was unaware of this product recall until now! This is extremely crazy and I cant believe this is what caused the fire on my bathroom outlet! I had just gotten done blow drying my daughters hair got her dressed then went in the bathroom to blow dry my hair! Well the blow dryer was plugged in for about maybe 3 minutes between drying my daughters hair and then trying to do mine. I get back in the bathroom everything seemed normal. I flip my head over(like bent down forward with my head closer to ground) so I could blow dry my hair I picked the blow dryer up and turned it on high so I could hurry up. Well as soon as I turned it on I heard something weird then a loud pop. Immediately I thought what the [REDACTED] really the fuse just blew! So I yell for my boyfriend before I stood all the way back up (because I was going to have him check fuse box) and soon as I stand up and go to unplug the blow dryer I immediately seen fire! It wasnt huge but it was still fire. Well I guess I'm an idiot because I immediately threw water on it. I wasnt even thinking at all! We just have 3 little kids and they are my world. I guess I didnt really have time to think and my natural reaction to put out a fire is throw water on it if it's available.  I dont know I just didnt want the thing exploding I guess I just really wasnt thinking like I should have been. Well I guess I messed up by doing that because I [REDACTED] shocked the [REDACTED] out of myself (excuse my language). Well anyways I also I ended up burning my thumb pulling the blow dryer cord out because it was melted and AGAIN wasnt thinking. I just didnt want the fire to come back. Well anyways I ended up having to call an electrician and we were without power for a little over a week. Started by replacing the breakers one by one and then in the end had to get an entire new sub panel(breaker box is what I call it) with that and my bathroom outlet and wall I was out of pocket almost $4,000 then on top of that I had to get medicine/ [REDACTED] for my burn/blister on my thumb, and on top of that we had to stay at a hotel for a week.....so I guess I can say my 4th came in with a bang! (Me trying to make the situation less aggravating when I think about it) after all said and done we were out if pocket like $5,000. That was our vacation money....while I'm very sad we didnt get to go on vacation like me, my husbandn and our 3 kids had been planning and saving for, I'm glad it happened when it dis or we wouldnt have had the money(again me trying to make the best out of a bad situation) still to this day our kids are sad we didnt get to go to [REDACTED]! productDescription: Heatolator Cab50 wood pellet stove.
incidentDescription:
Hi,

I am the owner of a new Heatolator Cab50 wood pellet stove. When this issue occurred, I had only burned two bags of pellets in the stove since it was installed.  

To summarize the issue. I walked into my house to find the smoke alarm going off and the house smelling of smoke. I immediately went to where the pellet stove was located and could see that there was an issue with the stove. What I found was the electric igniter that is used to ignite the wood pellets was stuck on. There were no pellets in the fire pot and the thermostat was not calling for heat. 

Because the igniter was stuck on for apparently a long time all the metal in the stove was glowing red hot causing the stove to overheat and fill the room with smoke. 

I tried to shut down the stove down but was not able to, apparently the safety features built into the stove had failed preventing me from shutting down the stove. I was forced to unplug the stove to stop it from burning. After a few minutes I plugged it in again and the same issues occurred.
  
There is clearly a failure in the safety mechanism in this product and I was just fortunate enough to have come home in time before I had a major fire in my house. I strongly believe the manufacture should recall these stoves and correct this safety issue before more issues like this occur.

Thank you,
[REDACTED]

incidentDescription:
We have a gas fireplace made by Heat & Glo. The model number is SL550TRS-IPI-E, serial number 0023461841. The fireplace came with a remote control to turn the fireplace on and off.

On many occasions, the fireplace will turn on by itself. It can happen during the day, at night, evening, it's completely random. We've had service out, and they cannot pinpoint why the unit turns itself on. There is a replaceable electronic module inside, which appears to control the burner. 

Apparently this electronic module does not have a failsafe mode that if there's a problem that would prevent the fireplace from turning on.

The concern is if something combustible were to be placed in front of the fireplace too close to the glass, it could cause a fire. Additionally, we have 2 small grandchildren that play in our great room and we never use the fireplace when they are over. If this were to turn on, these children could get seriously burned. 

It's happened numerous times before, and it recently happened tonight. We were watching TV, and my wife commented the fireplace just turned on.

productDescription: Ninja Auto IQ 1000W Blender
incidentDescription:
***********DO NOT BUY A SHARK NINJA BLENDER***************IT WILL BLOW UP ON YOU!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
At exactly 5:15 P.M. on January 25th 2018, My Ninja Blender Auto IQ exploded during removal off the lid after blending and I suffered deep second degree burns on my wrists, hands, face, and neck.  The food that I put in the blender was room temperature and the blender heated up the food to the point that I was badly burned.  Luckily I am cautious with protecting my head/face in emergency situations or my face would be completely scarred.  I originally bought this blender to accommodate my daughter who is fed through G-Tube.  I purchased the blender a year prior to the incident and used the blender 2-4 a day EVERY SINGLE DAY. The first time I used the blender I blended some dinner left overs (that was refrigerated over night) and my daughters prescription formula.  When I went to take the lid off the pressure from blending it popped the lid off with a hard force and there was steam coming from the contents inside. I checked to feel the temperature and was surprised at how warm it was. I checked online to see if I could find any information on why it was making the food warm and with no luck, I just assumed that because the blenders blades rotated so quickly that it heated the content.  As time went on I noticed that it kept heating food a little warmer after every use.  I never imagined that it would have heated the food and exploded out of the container like it did, burning me in the process.  My attorney contacted Ninja and explained the situation and the product malfunction.  Ninja in no way accepted responsibility or even apologized.  However, Ninja did say they would be willing to work with our claim but only if we agreed to send them the evidence (blender) so they could have it tested in their facility (China).  My attorney is currently in the process of having the product tested through a forensic engineer.  My body is scarred and I am absolutely terrified to use any kitchen appliance.  I am also in the process of conducting a media campaign to show the true nature of SharkNinja Operating, LLC.  They do not care about the safety of the consumer and only care about the all mighty dollar from the consumer.

productDescription: Black+Decker electric griddle model GD2011B.
incidentDescription:
I purchased Black+Decker electric griddle model GD2011B from a Target store in Roseville, MN on 3/11/18.

The box for the griddle clearly advertises "Fully immersible base without probe makes clean-up effortless."

But the instruction book cleaning instructions say "DO NOT IMMERSE THE UNIT IN WATER." and the bottom of the griddle also says "DO NOT IMMERSE IN WATER."

This product has Intertek / ETL file 2003398.

I am more inclined to believe the manual and markings on the product than the box. This means that people just looking at the box will put themselves in danger by immersing the griddle.

productDescription:
Manufacturer:  Blackstone Products
Product Name:  36" grill surround table accessory
SKU:  1680
Product Web site: https://www.blackstoneproducts.com/product/36-griddle-surround-table-accessory/
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
Product Manufacturer:  Blackstone Products
Product Name: 36" Griddle Surround Table Accessory
Website:  www.blackstoneproducts.com

I purchased a 36" griddle surround table accessory for my propane Blackstone griddle.  The surround attaches to the Blackstone griddle to provide a work surface.  The issue with the accessory it closes off the ability for the exhaust heat from the propane burners to escape from the griddle such that objects and body parts that are near the griddle burn very easily.  The first incident occurred on June 22, 2018 when I first attached the accessory.  I was using the griddle and my hand was quickly burned while cooking.  I did not come into any physical contact with the griddle or accessory, simply having my hand near the edge in close proximity to where the exhaust heat escapes caused minor burns.  
The second incident occurred when I had plates lying on the accessory near the inner edge - the exhaust heat from the propane burners causes the plates to become very hot and I received first degree burns when attempting to pick up the plates.

This is a very serious safety issue that I brought to the attention of the manufacturer via email on August 10, 2018.  The manufacturer dismissed and did not address my safety concerns.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription: Char-Broil propane 4 burner gas grill. Product Model# 463376017. Serial # G470011803003760
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
I bought a Char-Broil grill on 6/14/18. I used it 4 times before a fire occurred in the right valve outside the intended area within six weeks of the purchase date. The knob that adjusted the flame melted and fire can be seen underneath the valve. Damage was caused to the grille itself. The company was contacted and opened a file up #[REDACTED]. Contact with the company via email and phone resulted in them sending me an entire replacement of the inner workings of the grille. I requested a new grille which they declined. I also asked for information as to who to report this incident to, they did not provide that information.
I decided to report this to you because I learned yesterday at Habitat for Humanities Restore located in Buffalo, NY there was another Char Broil grill someone had donated that was being sold for parts. I noted the similar damage to the gas control knob on the grill and a fire had damaged that grille as well. I inquired of the manager and was informed that they had seen several Char-Broil grilles being donated to them that had had similar damage from fires outside the intended grill areas. I therefore felt an obligation to report this defective product that could have led to an injury if the propane gas continued to teak out of the valve and caused an explosion or bodily injury to someone. I have taken photos of the teak with flame on my grille as well as the damage it caused to Char-Broil. I have also taken a photo of the Char-Broil grill in the Habitat store for prosperity purposes and will be available should you request same.
Judging by what I have learned recently it appears that this company is not reporting defective product of their grills that
seem to be more prevalent than one knows. Thank you.

productDescription: Espresso Maker
incidentDescription:
On September 20, 2018 in the early morning; I decided to have a cup of espresso.  I filled my Krups Espresso Machine with the proper amount of water.  Then added a modest amount of ground espresso to the filter holder.  Then I turned the machine on.  My 5 year old daughter and 3 year old son were curious as to what I was doing.  I picked up my son and my daughter stood next to me watching the machine work.  I explained to them that I was making Espresso.  The hot espresso began to slowly trickle into the glass carafe.  As my children and I watched and I continued to explain what was happening..something very unexpected happened.  A booming sound followed by hissing steam as the carafe exploded into hundreds of pieces.  Glass, espresso and ground espresso covered my kitchen counter, floor and walls.  Hot coffee sprayed onto my children and I.  My son was nicked by a small piece of glass.  We all were in shock as to what could have happened.

The broken glass only caused a minor cut on my son's leg.  Amazingly none of us were seriously hurt!  If we had been standing a foot closer...one of us could have lost an eye!  This should NEVER have happened!
victimSeverity: Injury, Level of care not known

productDescription:
Kobalt 80-volt Brushless Lithium Ion 21-in Cordless Electric Lawn Mower
Sold by Lowe's
productSubCategory: Lawn Mowers, Leaf Blowers and Lawn Vacuums
incidentDescription:
The item in question is a Kobalt 80-volt Brushless Lithium Ion 21-in Cordless Electric Lawn Mower, sold through Lowe's.  The mower was purchased on/about 16 Sept 2018 and used approximately 6h since.

On 23 Sept 2018, after using for approximately 1/2 hour, the mower was laid on its side for cleaning.  A hose was used to wash off loose grass clippings from the underside of the mower.  I had not removed the battery.  Less than one minute into the cleaning, the mower started spinning at full speed.

This mower is equipped with a safety lock-out button on the handle which must be depressed prior to the bail handle being pulled in order to engage the blade.  Neither the lock-out button was pushed nor the bail handle pulled at the time the mower started on its own.

I include a link from YouTube of another consumer who reports a similar incident:
    https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HL-hOO3GoOQ

This incident scared the living daylights out of me.  If any body part or animal had been in the vicinity of that blade, it would have been sliced to ribbons.

It appears from my experience and that of the person who posted on YouTube that water on bottom of the mower can override the mower's safety lockouts.  This is a VERY dangerous product that has an extremely high potential of causing traumatic injury.

productDescription: Panasonic NI-L70SRW Cordless Iron, Curved Stainless Steel Soleplate, White/Clear Green
incidentDescription: I was preparing to iron a shirt with our Panasonic NI-L70SRW Cordless Iron. I had used the iron many times before even on this shirt. I turned the iron on and prepared the shirt for ironing. After waiting until the iron was warm, signaled by a light on the iron, I picked it up and touched it to the shirt. The shirt instantly melted to the iron faceplate. I had not realized the iron overheated and should not be used. After posting a review because I could not find another way to contact Panasonic, I was contacted and returned the iron for assessment. After approximately 1 month, I was told that the iron performed as designed and their engineers are convinced I must have left the iron on the shirt for an extended period of time. I assured them that this was not the case and that the shirt had melted on contact. Instead of being concerned about the situation where the iron overheated to a point where it could have easily started a fire, I was being blamed as a consumer. I was told that Panasonic has nothing to gain from saying the iron worked fine if it did fail, so clearly I must be incorrect. I will be returning the iron if possible (or using the extended return period on my [REDACTED]), but I had hoped that Panasonic would take this seriously so that it would be investigated before someone had a fire resulting from a similar situation.

productDescription: Nutri Ninja Personal and Countertop Blender with 1200-Watt Auto-iQ Base, 72-Ounce Pitcher, and 18, 24, and 32-Ounce Cups with Spout Lids (BL642)
incidentDescription: I received a Ninja Blender Model: BL642 for a birthday present from my mother on 9/11/2018.  On 9/16/2018 at approximately 5:00 pm, I proceeded to open the Ninja Blender box and packaging for the first time.  I opened the top of the box and removed the top piece of Styrofoam.  I did not see any warning labels or instructions on how to un-package the product. I removed the blender carafe (72 oz. pitcher) from the surrounding Styrofoam packaging.  The carafe was packaged with blade assembly inside and the lid on.  The blade assembly had no sheaths or protective covers on the blades.  There was no warning label stating that the blade assembly was not attached or anchored to the carafe.  The carafe lid was not locked into the carafe upon initial removal from packaging.  I tilted the carafe, including blade assembly and lid, a little over 90 degrees from upright position to inspect the drive mechanism on the bottom of the carafe.  As soon as I titled the carafe, the lid and the blade assembly fell out of the carafe.  I was not aware and it was not made obvious to me through the packaging that the blade assembly is not anchored to the carafe.  As I witnessed the lid fall off, I reflexively tried to catch it, not realizing or anticipating that the blade assembly would follow it out of the carafe.  The blade assembly impacted my left hand on the way to the floor.  I felt a shock of nerve pain shoot upon my arm at the instant the blade assembly made contact with the inside of my left middle finger.  I immediately felt and saw blood gush out of the wound.  The blade assembly had produced a significant laceration diagonally across the first joint from tip of my middle finger.  I immediately grabbed some paper towels nearby, held the wound above my heart, and applied pressure with my other hand.  My wife took me to the emergency room at the closest hospital and I received 6 stitches to my finger.  Since receiving this injury, I cannot feel the tip of my finger.

productDescription: Pebble Time Watch Charger. Magnetic at the watch end. USB end at the other. [REDACTED] block used to plug into a surge protector. This cord and block have been used for aprox. 1 year.
incidentDescription:
My son uses a Pebble Time smart watch with an app that detects seizures on it. He has to charge it every night in order for it to work. 
He had the cord plugged into a charger block (with  two prong plug ([REDACTED])).  The [REDACTED] block was plugged into a surge protector. 
He was wearing the watch at the time. 
We got home around 6 pm and I noticed a slight plastic smell in our apartment. I took a walk through the rooms but did not locate the smell. 
About an hour later, my son walked into his room, and immediately told me that he smelled "smoke or something hot" and it was very strong  in his room.  Again I walked into the room and I could also smell it very strongly. I walked over to where his surge protector was, and went to check the plugs, and I burnt my hand on the exposed USB connector that had melted the cord right off of it.  I immediately cut the power by turning the surge protector OFF.  I was able to unplug that [REDACTED] block with the end of the cord still in it. We found the melted cord end on the floor in between his desk and the bed on the floor. 
This could have been very serious. 
None of the other plugs that were in the surge protector were warm at all and they seemed fine.
victimSeverity: Injury, Level of care not known

productDescription:
Oster Pro® 1200 PLUS Blend-N-Go® Smoothie Cup & Food Processor Attachment - Brushed Nickel - Glass Jar.
Oster® 5-cup Food Processor Attachment
Detailshttps://www.oster.com/jarden-master-catalog/oster-5-cup-food-processor-attachment/164205-001-000.html
164205-001-000
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription:
I was using my Oster 1200 blender with its food processor attachment setup with the slicing disk to slice mushrooms.  The processor made a brief louder chopping noise and then continued to work properly.  My wife and daughter later found plastic chips in their food.

After cleaning the food processor, I looked at it in more detail.  The slicing blade can move up on its shaft and chop plastic off of the edge on the bottom of the feed tube.  I requested a replacement and it looks like it has the same problem.  I believe the problem happened as a small piece of mushroom was in the tube and the random cutting and bouncing caused the blade to oscillate and ride up the shaft.

Attached pictures are taken with food processor attachment upside down to show blade contacting feed tube.  Blade may only contact the feed tube if it oscillates or gets food trapped between blade and housing. Problem would  be resolved if unit had a bushing to limit blade movement.

productDescription:
Kenmore Elite 600 series grills (Carbon grey metallic Model # 146.33578410,
64,000 total BTU, 4 - 13,000 BTU main burner, 12,000 BTU side Burner, Electronic Ignition System
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
On 9/29/18 i was grilling dinner on my Kenmore Elite 600 series grill.   However the flames were really high on the 4 end burners & more so on the end then in the middle of the burner even when turning back to low.     The next morning on 9/30/18 I cleaned the grill and notice the the firebox has a hole that rusted through right next to where you ignite the burner.    I contacted Sears by phone and the said I would have to have a service man come and look at it but it would cost $99.    

The grill was purchased in 6/18/15 but we did not receive it until late July.    I have the original packaging sticker and warranty that has 10/25 year warranty on parts.    This stick said the firebox stated on sticker "porcelain coated firebox".    The firebox should not wrought away.

After getting service repair man from Sears, he came out on 9/30/18 to look at grill charge me $99 that had to be paid then and gave me estimate for $452 to repair firebox that they say is not covered.

I did not repair and started investigating Kenmore Gas Elite grills on line and found that over 12-15 were in class action lawsuit that were handled by the [REDACTED] law firm and sears /kenmore had defective grills that caused firebox tray to corrode prematurely exposing the propane tank and hose connections to grills burners, potential creating a safety hazard.

I have sent a report and filed a copy of my info to the lawfirm.   In the suit on March 13, 2017 sears had to pay the cost for repairs and reimburse customers but not all the kenmore grills were recalled,   This started back December 2015 the same year I purchased my grill.   

Sears knew or should  have known that the grills are defective, not fit for their intended purpose, and unsafe to use as intended.  Sears routing failed to repair grills when the firebox defect manifests, and that owners of the affected kenmore grills had to spend around 300 per repair.   

I had a gas oven blow up in my face over 15 years ago and had 1st, 2nd and third degree burns on my face.   I do not need a gas grill that has an open hole and corroding above the propane tank to explode again in my face...

productDescription: 36 inch Blackstone Stainless steel Gas Griddle Grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription: I bought a Blackstone model 1560 36 inch stainless steel grill from Home Depot and used it first time on 6/30/18. It was scary and a big mess. Lucky I didn't burn the house down or get burned. This has a front trough that fills with hot grease that runs to the right and into an inadequately small catch container. Much of my oil ran out of the container, on to the deck and hot grease just went everywhere. The trough has a hole in the end of it and the grease runs out and turns back under, mostly misses the catch basin and ends up running all over. Next and worse, the consumer is then working over this big tray of hot grease with open flames a short distance away, right under the trough. If it were to  drip over the side, the whole thing catches fire. This is a HUGE fire danger. And since that trough isn't flat on the one I got, the center fills up and holds hot grease. No offense but this design is flat out dangerous. I've seen ads on TV that show a newer and safer designed unit that has a rear exit for grease with a one inch steel wall in front. But that's not what home Depot and many others are selling. I talked with Home Depot and their only solution is to return it. I told them its dangerous. We will be looking to obtain the model with the newer safer rear grease exit. But what about all those unsafe units out there?? I have tried to contact Blackstone but get no response either by email or phone.

incidentDescription: I have a oklahoma joes longhorn combo grill the lp regulator is defective. The model number of regulator is RA328. Model number of grill is 15202029. productDescription: Weber Genesis 310 purchased in 2013
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
Weber Genesis gas (propane grill) started up and within 5 minutes of operation the hose just downstream of the regular failed and propane was coming from the hose. The fire continued for several minutes until a small extinguisher was used to extinguish and get close enough to the valve so it could be shut off.

The concern is the flexible hose and regulator are attached to a metal pipe that feeds the ignitors. The rubber hose is in a area that is subject to thermal damage from other metal parts below the grill box. Newer models I understand are separated from the grill box by a piece of sheet metal and some distance. Realistically there's no easy way to shut off the gas since its also located right by the connection to the grill.

Of course the manufacture initially suggested  it was probably the gasket on the propane container and also said they didn't like those propane tanks with the gauges on the outside. Turns out both were ok.
Then they suggested it was a grease fire that caused it, but I doubt that as well. 
The location of the hose and regulator are to close to the heat source are of combustible construction and potential problems are endless. Bad design that was incorporated  now

productDescription: Molekule Air Purifier
incidentDescription:
Hi, 

I hope you are doing well. I wanted to write to you about the Molekule air "purifier" product that was recently approved for sale in CA. 

I wanted to reach out to you to let you know that there are many customers out there who have had a fairly negative experience with their device. The main concern being that the device continues to emit a foul odor / VOCs for many weeks after purchase. The company literature says that the unit is expected to off-gas for 24-48 hours. However, many of their customers (myself included) noted that the smell actually didn't go away for weeks. The problem is not just the smell, but the uncertainty around what actually is being emitted by the unit and whether it is harmful in any way.

The Company refuses to provide any info about why there is smell or whether there is any danger in inhaling that air. I, for one, can speak from experience that every time I entered the room where we were running the device I would break into incessant coughing. So there is something wrong in the gases being emitted from the unit but I am not sure what it is and dont have the means to test.

There have been folks who have been enterprising enough to do their own home tests. Many have found that Molekule has almost no impact on VOCs. In fact here is a link to a thread on forum, where a user "[REDACTED]" posts about his experience of thoroughly testing the unit and finding that it doesn't work. He then got in touch with Molekule and got their tech team to use sophisticated equipment to test his unit and they concurred with him that somehow his unit was defective. 

1: (http://hvac-talk.com/vbb/showthread.php?2254881-MoleKule-Update
"The technical folks at MoleKule took an active interest and contacted me in short order. I've been working with them for the last couple of weeks. After extensive testing at their facility, including Gas Chromatography (the gold standard for measuring VOCs) they determined my catalyst was defective")

2: (http://hvac-talk.com/vbb/showthread.php?2272161-Latest-MoleKule-Austin-Air-Test
Test 1:
At 70^F ~45RH with VOC levels ~300 ppb the 
MoleKule didn't register a significant change.
Austin Air showed a decrease of about 15 - 28%. I tested in a couple of rooms.

Test 2:
Same as above but added a small bowl of [REDACTED] equidistant from both devices.
MoleKule registered ~15% decrease.
Austin Air registered ~ 20 - 30 % decrease.

Test 3:
Same as test 1 except increase heat to ~ 80 - 82 ^F
Molekule didn't register a significant change.  )

This is most concerning to me and should be to CPSC too, and that is why I wanted to point it out to you. There was and is no indicator on the unit or the mobile app to detect whether the unit is working or defective. Most consumers aren't going to go to the lengths that [REDACTED] went to test their unit. So Molekule could very well be selling defective units without any oversight under the garb of being approved to sell these units.

I reached out to CARB earlier and they said they had no authority over them and they suggested I reach out to you instead. I have since returned my unit. 

Thanks,
[REDACTED]

Micro-Start lithium Ion Battery Auto jump starter and multi-function electronic equipment charger
or power supply.
incidentDescription:
On August 3, 2018,  at about 3:45 PM we were driving back from a hike in the Valles Caldera National Monument on High 4 near Los Alamos, N.M. when my wife heard a "pop" in the rear of our SUV and our vehicle immediately filled with dense white smoke. My wife yelled "stop the car and everybody get out". I was driving and thought the vehicle had caught on fire. Our son, my wife and grandchildren got out of the stopped vehicle immediately. Our son raced to the back of the SUV and opened the rear door which released a cloud of white smoke and one of our dogs. The other had jumped over two rows of seats and out the front passenger door. Our son saw the smoking Micro-Start XP-10 on the floor in the back of the SUV and grabbed a strap on it and threw it from the vehicle to the ground. It was still smoking. We had pulled over on this two lane road through the forest and were fearful the Micro-Start XP-10 might start a fire. We called the fire department and asked for help. They and the police arrived to direct traffic and inspect our vehicle and the "Jump-Starter". We had thrown it into our emptied cooler on ice packs and covered it with water. The firemen determined it was out and no longer a fire hazard then told us the smoke from the Lithium Ion battery was toxic. He suggested we monitor our dogs as they were close to the source longest and if they became sick we should seek care for them and ourselves. The firemen suggested we have the interior of the vehicle scrubbed out and replace the air conditioning unit air filters after we got home. We notified Antigravity Batteries by phone and left a V.M. about the episode and also sent an e-mail the night of August 3rd. They responded via e-mail August 6th and answered my phone call to the warranty desk. They e-mailed a Micro-Start Warranty Claim Form which we completed with all the requested information. We provided receipts for the expense of cleaning the SUV interior and the A/C Filter replacement. We have not shown any ill effects to the smoke nor have our dogs. 
The initial moving smoke filled vehicle and emergency exit from it could have resulted in more serious consequences.

Last year, I reported an identical incident involving a [REDACTED] brand product.  (See:  Report No. [REDACTED].)  The bases for the Krups unit and the[REDACTED] unit are identical except for the label and a metal trim strip.  In fact, they are interchangeable.  The Krups carafe is metal and the [REDACTED] carafe is glass.  but they too are interchangeable.

productDescription: Four-burner gas grill on rollers, collapsable metal side trays.
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
I was heating the grill yesterday (May 13, 2018) to cook a Mother's Day dinner for my wife and mother-in-law.  When I looked outside to check temperature, I saw dark smoke billowing from the grill and also could see flames in the undercarriage of the grill, far below the burners.  I was very concerned that the propane tank might ignite or explode.  I grabbed a fire extinguisher (dry chemical) and sprayed the front of the closed grill, then around the side.  I was then able to reach and turn off the four burner controls on the front of the grill.  The fire in the undercarriage (below the burners, above the propane tank) kept re-igniting.  After giving it a big blast from the fire extinguisher, I was able to manually turn off the valve to the propane tank to the fuel line.  I blasted it again with the extinguisher and waited a couple minutes before I went to disconnect the fuel line from the propane tank.  When I started to unscrew the fuel line, it fell to the side - the fuel line had been completely severed.  

My belief is that the fuel line was touching a hot part of the grill and that it ruptured and caught fire, spewing propane into the lower part of the grill.  

I purchased this grill in the spring of 2012 from Lowes in West Philadelphia.  I never received any information about a product recall.  I have children who are 7, 5, and 3; I am grateful that it was cool day and none of them were near the grill.  No one was injured, but we were all pretty scared.

It is about 2 - 3 years old.
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
I have a Cuisinart Toaster Oven, Model TOB-40, SN 20920. 
It is about 2 - 3 years old. 

On the morning of July 7th I used it to toast my breakfast.  As usual, after a few minutes, the little red indicator light went off and I heard a beep.  But I noticed the bottom two heating elements were still glowing orange, rather than cooling down.

I even moved the knob from “toast” to “off” but the elements stayed on.  At this point the toaster oven should have been off, and the red indicator light was off the whole time.

The only way I could get the two bottom elements to go off was to unplug the unit from the wall.

I think this is dangerous and possibly a fire hazard, as it means the toaster oven could be on continuously without the owner knowing.

incidentDescription:

This heater works very well with the exception, it continues to operate and produce significant heat, even when the heater's sole control knob is in the OFF position.  The control mechanism has no 'clicks'. 'stops' or other physical indicators which would show that the heater is in the OFF, HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW positions.
This morning I had the heater in the OFF position in my home office. My wife happened to push an office chair close to the heater.  The chair had my jacket hanging on it. Type: VH101

Cold, Low Heat and High Heat settings
incidentDescription:
A Vornado VH101 Personal Vortex electric space heater was purchased for me on Amazon.com 5 years and 5 months ago on November 27, 2012. I use it almost 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, however, because of a situation that caused me concern, I try very hard never to leave the unit running unattended without first turning off the heat.

1. When the unit tips forward onto its face, a safety switch located on the bottom always cuts the power as expected. This safety feature has never failed me.

2. When an object is placed too close, restricting the air flow, a thermal switch located inside cuts the power, and the power is not restored until the unit has sufficiently cooled. As far as I can tell, this safety feature appears to work consistently as well.

3. However, one day, after having owned this heater for approximately three to four years, the smell of burning plastic caught my attention, and I suddenly realized that the fan had stopped turning. I quickly turned off the unit which had become very hot to the touch. I later took the unit apart, lubricated the motor shaft and continued to use the unit. Within a year, the same situation occurred again. Since then, I have learned to continuously pay close attention to the sound of the fan, and whenever I hear it slowing down, I lubricate the motor shaft. I have not had any problems with the unit since. (Note: During both occurrences, there were no nearby objects obstructing air flow.)

productDescription: Greenworks 21 inch, 60 volt lithium-ion, brushless motor, cordless mower. Model M060L00.
productSubCategory: Lawn Mowers, Leaf Blowers and Lawn Vacuums
incidentDescription: My electric mower started spontaneously and without warning. I tipped the mower on its side to clear away already wet grass under the deck and was using water from a garden hose; I had not removed the battery yet. The blade went to full speed only inches from my hands. I had to place the mower back on its wheels and pull out the battery to get it to stop. I reinserted the battery and the motor started again without having to pull back the bail lever and/or press the safety lock-out button as usually required. I repeated this several times with the same result. The red safety key next to the battery was the only other way to stop the mower motor. I have a 572 MB video of this process. The mower is relatively new; purchased in June of 2017 and used about 6 times. Each use consumed only 1 indicator bar on the battery. That is about 20 minutes of run time x 6 total use. A warning in the manual says not to expose mower to water to "reduce the risk of electric shock" but does not mention unexpected or spontaneous starting of the motor. It also states to remove the battery before cleaning but again does not warn about unexpected or spontaneous starting. I am certain others will do exactly as I did and will suffer permanent injuries. This is a major safety issue and should be addressed. I checked the mower today and it appears to have returned to normal. It is obvious now that the water somehow got into somewhere it should not have. I was not injured and am not asking for compensation of any sort. This was truly a "Close Call" for me, a couple of inches would have change my life forever. You can be sure I will pull the battery at the drop of a hat from now on.

I assume the ENT did not bother to look at the CT himself. It was concluded and reported as negative for a foreign body in tongue. I then went to an oral surgeon whom upon taking a orbital CT scan saw immediately the lodged piece of grill bristle in the back part of me tongue. I then saw an another ENT who looked at the Yale CT (the 1st one) which clearly showed the wire bristle and from there 3 surgerys ensued and were all unsuccessful at removing the wire bristle.

Consequently, I STILL HAVE THE BRISTLE LODGED IN MY TONGUE...The trauma and swelling from the attempted removal and 3 surgeries performed within 1 week has resulted in me not being able to enunciate clearly; nor swallow without focused attention to doing so, severe pain, a numb tongue with minimal taste, swelling and severe mouth ulcers.

6-19-18 was the 1st of 3 surgeries and as of today, I am slowly recovering but still have te bristle lodged in my throat; and I am still looking for someone who can help me.
Products are recalled for being significantly less of a danger to the public than these steel-bristled grill brushes.  

These brushes NEED TO BE REMOVED FROM THE MARKET!

If you have any information on the  physician who successfully removed the bristle from the base of the patient's tongue (from the case reported in 2011), please contact me!
Thank you so much for your attention to this matter.

productDescription:

The contacts (less than a few mm wide) that clamp around the heating element, were made of too thin gauge material to provide enough clamping force to resist expansion of heat cycling. Problems didn't arrise until it was needed.
incidentDescription:
For order # ([REDACTED])
Amazon store

As an engineer, I had to say that the quality of the parts was underwhelming. 
   Months later, during the winter, the pressure contacts were heating up at the wires, glowing red hot, although seemed to be stable glowing like this but quite disconcerting having it in the house with the wife. "Is it supposed to do that?" was my first clue.

I believe in fixing what you have. 
  I brought in a few repair people to try to fix the problem. It didn't work. -The connections always wound up getting loose, causing increased resistance and glowing wires. Only it got worse, heating up more and more of the wire, shifting the heat output to just the topmost left of the unit. 

Not wanting to "burn" anymore time or money, I chucked it up to a loss and experience and sent the unit to my local plant to be recycled... that a few months later, the company calls me telling me about this fault. Alas.

I've called both apartments. They said you have to have the bottom of the unit for your CPSR to be allowed to take action. 

I am pleased to know my options are open and that this is a known issue
It's not critcial that action be taken for me personally, only that the engineers know and bulletproof the design more carefully in the future.

Blessings and good evening.
  -[REDACTED]

productDescription: Power AirFryer 3.4  Black with silver top, handle and buttons.  The product was purchased at Walmart and is product number 550564637.  The manufacturer part and Modle number is PAF-BLACK 3QT
incidentDescription:
My daughter was using a Power AirFryer 3.4.  She had put french fries in it and used the pre-programmed french fry setting.  Less than 5 minutes after the fries were put into the machine a fire started from the machine.  Within minutes the fire had spread and destroyed the whole kitchen.

The product was completely and totally melted in the fire.  The device is supposed to have a shut off mechanism if it gets too hot.  There was no warning or smoke that was visible before the fire started.

The smoke detectors didn't go off until the fire had spread throughout the kitchen.  The product was less than a year old and was not dirty or overfilled.  
 
The fire adjuster said that he thinks that something on the counter caught on fire due to the heat from the machine.  The machine was on for less than 5 minutes and cooks with hot air.  I do not believe that this is how the fire was started.  

There were flames at the back of the machine and a puff of smoke came out of the top of it after the fire had already started.

The consumer unplugged the unit and, upon inspection, noticed a burn mark around the ON/ OFF switch. The consumer plugged the unit back on and it immediately started sparking and smoking again; the consumer turned off and unplugged the hair dryer.

02/12/2018 – The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation. The representative she spoke to informed her they would get back with her however this has not been the case.  The manufacture subsequently contacted the consumer and asked her to send them the product.  She refused.

The consumer states the unit was used two to three times per week. The consumer plans on keeping her hair dryer for the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.

incidentDescription:
DeLonghi TRH0715 Oil-Filled electric radiator Type KH770715P  Serial 08218514

I purchased the heater on Amazon on September 7, 2017. It worked satisfactorily through the winter.
On Saturday June 23, 2018 the plug burst into sparks and flames, though the unit was turned off at the time.  I put out the fire with a hand-held extinguisher. Had I not been home my apartment would have been destroyed.

A professional electrician checked my outlet and wiring.  He said the fire was caused by the heater's un-grounded plug. He said the plug and its connecting wire were inadequate to the power requirements of the unit. It should have been sold with a grounded plug and a thicker wire.

productDescription: FAGOR (Electric Multi-Cooker) pressure cooker appliance. Model: 670041460, Made in China. Stainless Steel outer cover, black plastic cover, 9 button with 2 digit readout control panel.
incidentDescription: We experienced a serious issue with the power cord of our FAGOR (Electric Multi-Cooker) pressure cooker appliance. Model: 670041460, Made in China. This product utilizes a low quality undersized hard-wired power cord, and without proper strain release, actually caught fire at the cord entry to the appliance. It is a shame that a company such as FAGOR to allow production of such low quality short-lived and quite dangerous products. These products should NEVER utilize hard-wired flimsy light gauge zip-cord as power cords especially by a product rated to consume 1000 watts at 120VAC. Instead, utilize highly flexible 14 gauge round cable with extra length strain relief with at least IEC 320 C13/C14 or better connections. Power cords can then be easily changed or disconnected during storage. ALL products designed in such a way desperately NEED a national recall.  Do not allow dangerous junk sold to the consumer.  Do not purchase FAGOR or any other brand that produces products in such a manner.

incidentDescription: My instant pot purchased in December 2017 and used approximately a total of 8 times, self-destructed. I used it for the last time, to cook some artichokes for a family dinner the night of June 21st.  I turned off the Instant Pot when it was finished cooking but didn't unplug it. The next day after being in the kitchen all morning cleaning up, the Instant Pot showed no signs of any trouble. Sometime later in the early afternoon, I smelled smoke, upon investigation; I discovered the Instant Pot spewing acrid smoke.  The whole bottom of the Instant Pot had melted off and pooled in a smoldering mass of plastic and burning wires. The fumes where so bad, we had to wear masks with wet clothes underneath in order to enter the house and attempt to clean up the mess.  We had to leave the house for several hours with all the windows open and fans pushing the inside air out.  Even so, our home still smelled to the point of causing stinging eyes, headaches and coughing. Had this incident occurred during the night and gone undetected, I’m not sure we would have survived the toxic smoke that filled our entire house.  It was so bad that over 24 hours later, and cleaning all surfaces in the kitchen and adjoining rooms, it still is not cleared enough to spend more than a few minutes at time in the kitchen. It would appear that it will take several days or longer to have limited use of the kitchen. The Instant Pot also damaged the surface that it was on which may need to be replaced and professionally cleaned.

I immediately throw the dryer into the bath tub and unplugged it. I waited for it to cool down and took some pictures so I could send it to Revlon. A couple weeks went by and I heard back from them, and they were trying to blame ME for the incident saying that they found hair and lint inside the dryer...which, sure, they probably did, because there is no way to really clean out the bottom of the dryer. 

It has been about a month since this happened, and I now have a scar on my arm from this dryer.

This is very disturbing to us as I just happened to be home when this occurred; I will often brew the coffee and then leave the rest for my husband who gets up later. I have no doubt we would have had a kitchen fire with damage to our home if I had not been present when this issue occurred.

productDescription: 9020 Wood Fire Pro Pellet Grill
incidentDescription:
We purchased a model9020 Wood Fire Pro® Pellet Grill from Lowes (#3168 in Bear,
DE) on 25 March 2018. Upon its first operation, we experienced a flame out blast
which blew the lid open. There was a fire inside the main grill body. This fire had to be
extinguished.

We phoned Char-Griller's (C-G) Customer Service line and a Customer Service
Representative (CSR) told us the 9020 " ... is known for having been wired
backwards." The CSR talked us through disassembling the digital control unit and
reversing the power feed from the auger and draft fan. We became concerned that
such a "known" issue wasn't handled by a product safety recall or through some other
proactive corrective action. And that their way of repairing their products were to have
the consumer take directions by phone to rewire and repair their products.

Next we realized that the fire rod or igniter was not working as described in the
Owner's Manual. On the next call to their support line, the CSR explained how I
needed to, once again, disassemble the digital control and send pictures to C-G for a
visual review to determine if there were other problems with the assembly and
manufacturing of the grill. I was informed that C-G would not incur the expense of"
randomly shipping parts out in an attempt to correct every problem."

At that point I determined I was not about to act as a surrogate repair engineer to
repair a faulty product in hopes that all of the manufacturing errors would be
diagnosed from a smart phone picture.

Char-Griller issued an RTM statement to return the product to the place of purchase
but would not agree to reimburse us for all the C-G auxiliary products purchased -
vinyl cover {part #9155) & bag of pellets (part# 9620) and for the ancillary costs
associated with the purchase (transportation back to Lowes, etc ... ).

I believe that Char-Griller I A&J Mnf. is knowingly selling a product that was
manufactured unsafely and is negligent.

I feel the DE F&CPD should investigate this public safety issue.

additional emails: [REDACTED]; VP of Sales - [REDACTED];
Manager of Customer Service - [REDACTED]

Cuisinart Convection Toaster Oven
Manufacturer's Code:  TT40923
Other numbers from the unit:  2003464, TOB-160BCW, sec40923c
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
On Feb 4, 2018 my Cuisinart Convection Toaster Oven caught fire.  The fire was behind the control panel and smoke and flames were coming out the top of the unit.  I got it unplugged and out of the house where my wife deployed a fire extinguisher.  There were no injuries, but our cabinets and kitchen were inundated with an electrical/fire/smoke smell.  The oven was a loss, we used up our fire extinguisher, and the patio was a mess after the extinguisher was deployed.  

On Feb 5, 2018 I contacted Cuisinart and relayed the information above and all ID numbers on the product.  They volunteered to replace the product, supplied information on a replacement oven, and asked that I send the oven to them, which I agreed.  I said it was important I learn what happened as I have another Cuisinart oven and I need to know if it is safe.  

On Feb 7, my wife contacted Cuisinart about a replacement and they changed what was promised on Feb 5.  Now having no confidence in Cuisinart to provide me with information on the product, I opted not to return the oven.  

On Feb 13, I received a letter from [REDACTED] , Claims Manager with Conair the parent company of Cuisinart.  Now having a record of their request for the oven, I mailed it to them on Feb 26.  I again noted the need for information on the safety of this product as I have another one of them.  Since then we have heard nothing from Conair or Cuisinart.  Not sure how important this is to Cuisinart, but as it could have burned down our home, and we have another one of these ovens, it is important to us.  Can you help get some answers from Cuisinart or Conair?

incidentDescription:
I own an Outdoor Gourmet Island Kitchen sold by Academy Sports.  The side cooking burner is located on the left side of the grill assembly.  The inside grill has 3 more burners.  T

Problem - The gas supply pipe for the side burner one day just corroded and fell off while the burner was still on.  The right side inside burner was also on since I was cooking using a pot on the side burner and a small foil wrapped fish on the right side inside burner.

Luckily I was at the grill when this happened.  I hear a clunk and I immediately turned the left burner off.  Then I opened the doors and drawers to see what happened.  The right burner was still on.

I found the pipe and figured out it was the supply to the left burner.

Danger concern - if the pipe had fallen off when I was not at the grill, the remaining pipe section would have spewed propane into the grill chamber and since the right burner was on, there would have been an explosion.

incidentDescription: In Jan 2017 I purchased a brand new Pro Charging System's Eagle Performance series 48 Volt 15 AMP [REDACTED] golf cart Charger (Product # I4815YM619) (serial# 2016PCS3191081) for my six (6) new [REDACTED] batteries.
