Upon returning home I discovered these batteries were so hot from being overcharged I was afraid they would explode at any minute.   If we had not returned from our vacation when we did and stopped the charging of these batteries they would have no doubt have reached the point of exploding and causing a fire in my home. This charger's failure to properly shut down after a charging cycle is a serious safety issue, Golf cart battery chargers are suppose to turn off after completing a charging cycle not continuous charge as this brand/model did.   [REDACTED] golf carts do NOT have an on-board computer to control the charging cycles like [REDACTED] golf carts and must depend on the charger's abilities to accurately charge your batteries.  The manufacturer flat refuses to test this charger under the same type of conditions (40+ days), with the same equipment ( a [REDACTED] golf cart) and refuses to accept any safety concern for the consumers while using this model charger. productDescription: “Tassimo Cappucino Foaming Milk Creamer” discs/pods for use in the Tassimo coffee brewing system (16 count)
incidentDescription:
These incident concerns the Tassimo coffee brewing system, and milk pods/discs for their Cappuccino products that recently stopped working correctly and created a major safety issue caused by the explosion of the milk pods/discs during brewing, and causing hot steam and milk to spray outwards from the coffee machine.

Last week I  bought new milk discs for my Tassimo brewing system (which I’ve had for several years without problem - at least until,these defective milk pods).   started experiencing problems right away when I placed the milk pods/discs into the machine, and started the brewing process.  Immediately I could hear that something was not right because the machine was making strange noises I’ve never heard before, and I could tell that there was no hot milk going into the cup as it’s supposed to do.  Thus, it seems like the pressure in the machine was building up and not passing through the milk disc like it was supposed to.   I finally turned the machine off, and tried to open the Tassimo machine — whereupon there was an explosive release of steam and splashing of hot milk.  I was not injured, but I easily could have been if the steam or hot milk had hit my face.  

I thought that I mush have received a bad disc, or a bad box of milk discs.  So I opened another package of milk discs, and tried them....only to have the same thing happen yet again (although I stopped the process earlier to avoid any explosion I’d milk and steam, and I waited for the machine to cool down again before opening it.  I tried this process two more times with milk discs from the same and from different packages I had, and ALL of the milk discs seemed defective.  However, when I tried using other types of discs (or, coffee/espresso discs) in the machine, there was no problem whatsoever.

Upon checking the company’s website reviews for this same product (specifically “Tassimo Cappuccino Foaming Milk Creamer”), I discovered that the Gevalia/Tassimo company has been receiving complaints about these “exploding milk pods/discs” for approximately 6 month’s (i.e., since the end of 2017). 

However, there was nothing posted anywhere by the company in response to these customer reviews, and instead they simply replied by asking the customer to call them.  I tried posting two separate reviews with my experience, but both times I received an email from the company (which I cannot reply to) that stated my review “did not meet their website guidelines” due to “legally sensitive matter” (although there is nothing in their website guidelines that says anything against posting experience with my exploding milk discs, or against posting “legally sensitive material”.

productDescription: Silver Pressure Cooker
incidentDescription:
I have had a Cuisinart  EPC1200PC pressure cooker for a few months that I had received as a present.  Cooking was fast and healthy.  This unit has an internal pot and an outer shell.  The internal pot is removable and dishwasher safe.

When food is finished, it is well over 212 degrees fahrenheit due to the pressure.  One cools it down slowly or quickly, then opens it to release the pressure.  One can then serve the food.  It will stay warm as long as one likes.

The danger zone for food is between 40 and 140 degrees.  Once food cools to 140, bacteria begin to grow rapidly.  (Some would be more conservative and say 160.) Most are not going to stick a thermometer in there and wait.  Most will try to put it in the fridge sooner.  Botulism and Salmonella can be deadly.

The problem is that the design makes it impossible to remove the inner pot safely.  Imagine sticking . your arms out at shoulder height and lifting a 16 lb weight about a foot and a half and then setting it down.  It can be done. It can hold about 20 or more lbs.  Now consider that the space between the inner pot and the outer pot is one quarter inch high.   That means you somehow need to flatten your fingers to lift it.  The outer rim only sticks out about a quarter inch.  So you have to crush your fingers and keep them plastered to the teeny rim of the inner pot to lift it.  Did I mention that the inner pot can be close to 212 degrees and the outer pot even hotter?  So crush your fingers between two boiling pieces of metal and lift up to 25 lbs of sloshing boiling liquid.  

There is no way to do this safely.  Most people would grab a potholder.  But the potholder won't fit in that 1/4 inch slot.  You need to crush your fingers than wrap the potholder around them but now it's more to be put in there and you'd need to hammer your fingers down to paper thin size. 
 
Sounds pretty crazy, no?

I assumed I was missing some part.  THere would be something to grab the inner pot without fear of burning one's self.  One that would let one move 20 lbs of sloshing liquid slow enough so a gallon of boiling liquid  didn't pour all over oneself.  Perhaps it would even allow for some mechanical advantage so one didn't need to have 25 lbs pulling with arms at 180 degrees to the floor.  Maybe there was a lid to the inner pot and one could cover it before it cools down preventing bacteria from falling in.   Even so, the container must sit at room temperature for several hours before on can lift it.

So I wrote Cuisinart.  I asked how they recommended I get the food out before it was in the food safety zone.  I was told that I had to file a claim with their legal department.  I wrote back stating I would promise not to sue--I just wanted to know if I was missing a part.  Once again they refused tp respond and asked me to fill out a claims report.

I didn't ask for money.  I didn't want money.  I just wanted advice.  Now I recognize that know the unit is dangerous.  And they don't want this dangerous unit in the hand of someone wanting that the public should be protected..

I just noticed the newer version of the product...it features special safety handles so one doesn't need a "tea towel" to lift 20 lbs of boiling liquid sloshing and carrying at arms length and parallel with the floor.

It should be recalled.  There is no way to use it safely and the fact that they've redesigned it demonstrates they know it.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

I set it down and I reached over with my right arm to press the reset button and flames came out of the nozzle of the hair dryer. I immediately knocked it off the counter with my arm which pulled the electrical cord out of the wall and the flame went out. I looked down and my inner right arm was burnt black and it began burning pretty bad. I immediately put my arm under cold water and ran for ice in my kitchen. I took pictures of my arm right after, and also after an hour. My daughter who is a nurse felt I should have the burn evaluated by a doctor so I went to my closest urgent care. The doctor who saw me said it was 1st - 2nd degree burn so they put burn medication on my arm and bandaged it and also gave me a tetanus shot. I have paperwork from the urgent care emergency visit.

productDescription: GE Zoneline PTAC heating and cooling, through the wall unit.
productType: Heaters or Heating Systems, Other or Not Specified (393)
incidentDescription:
On December 14, 2017, we were informed that the GE Zoneline PTAC heating and cooling unit,  which was installed one year and two months prior in the bedroom of an apartment we rent in the District of Columbia, popped and started smoking.   The company that sold us the unit, Glenmont, inspected it on December 16 and stated the "control panel was burned."   

As several GE Zoneline units have been recalled for risk of fire, we called a GE customer service representative (1-800-386-1215, ext. 5031, Reference No. #[REDACTED]) for help.   The GE recall site states "Moisture from outdoor air can accumulate near the unit's heater when the unit is operated with the vent door continuously open. This, along with two shorted electrical components, can create an electrical ground path and arcing, posing a risk of fire."   

The GE representative stated the unit had not been recalled and therefore, GE would not repair or replace the unit.  He did say, however, the incident was most likely due to moisture.

Glenmont stated the unit did not have a warranty and also refused to repair or replace the unit.  

We decided to purchase another unit a little over one year after purchasing the one that burned and paid the tenants their demand of $1355 for rent credit, damages and for "stress and emotional" impact.

manufacturer: Mirama Enterprises Inc. dba Aroma Housewares Company
incidentDescription:
This morning our Aroma Kettle exploded with a loud bang. It wasnt in use but my wife place our kid's lunch bag near it and it may have pressed and held down the button for heating.

It was deafening, very scary and could have injured someone if someone was closer to the kettle as it sent a strange metal looking powder around which might have be hot or dangerous.

The kettle was less than a year old. Model no AWK-108. See photo to get serial number (not clear which number it is).

In all transparency, we did recently (a few weeks ago) also moved the kettle to a different plug inside the kitchen as it was always triggering a safety Ground Fault Circuit Interrupters of a plug with GFCIs. 
Nothing seemed wrong with the kettle. It worked on other plug in the kitchen. In hindsight, this seems like a very bad idea that we just ignored it was triggering the GFCI but it worked fine for weeks. 

Perhaps this safety (interruptor) should really be on the Kettle more than the plug itself.

So we are a bit unsure what caused this. We think it worth putting the word out regarding our safety concern with this product.

productType: Coffee Makers or Teapots, Not Specified (452)
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription:
We bought a Mr Coffee coffeemaker in July/Aug 2016 at Kroger in Columbus Ohio. 

It has sat on the kitchen counter used about once a day since then. Never fallen off the counter or had anything weird happen. Only used it to make regular black coffee with grounds from the store. Kept it reasonably clean. 

Today I made a couple cups of coffee in the afternoon. A couple hours later I heard the coffee maker making noises like it was still turned on. The little green light on the on/off button was not on, though. So I touched the button the way you would to turn it off, just to check. 

Sparks flew out of the button area in my face and up my arm-- my husband saw the light from around the corner. Not a couple of sparks. A ton, like a welder. 

It tripped the circuit, too. We unplugged it and contacted the company who has asked me to ship them the faulty machine. But I think you should know, too. 

This was a relatively new kitchen electronic, used as designed, and it electrocuted me when touching the on/off switch. Seems like a pretty bad flaw in a coffee maker. 

The model number is SK13 and the numbers on the plug were DG and H224. I don't know what that means but the company asked for it so maybe that's helpful. 

[REDACTED]

I reported the issue to Capresso and they were dismissive, concerned only with whether I could demonstrate if the kettle was under warranty.

Immediately after I started using it (switched to the "ON" position, grating disc in place on the motor shaft, work bowl and lid in the closed and locked position for proper operation) I heard a cracking sound, then a short creak. When I removed the processor work bowl, I discovered that the plastic on the motor shaft had failed, fracturing all the way through: back to front and top to bottom of the shaft. I was not injured, but a few jagged pieces of plastic from the shaft are missing. I'm not sure where they went, given how fast the motor shaft spins. This is a failure such that I can no longer safely operate this product. I use this processor frequently, but not for any "tough" jobs. I treat this product with kid gloves, so this hardware failure is an unpleasant surprise. It's Cuisinart model DLC-5BC. Color silver, 7 cup capacity, 120 V., 60 Hz., Max. 5 Amps. productDescription: 1 and 1/4 inch ceramic barrel clipless hair curler. This is a curling wand for your hair. The common name to refer to this product is a hair wand.
productType: Hair Curlers, Curling Irons, Clips & Hairpins (1682)
incidentDescription:
This morning, while styling my hair, I got a second-degree burn    when my forearm barely glanced- literally barely touched, the barrel of my clampless curling wand. I was wearing the safety glove, but it just covers to the base of the palm. My complaint and great concern is two fold. 1. The heat-resistant glove that comes with the product insufficiently protects consumers.
2. The product seems far to hot to be handled by the average consumer. While the temperature rating states that it heats to 450 degrees Fahrenheit, I question the safety of it given the extreme likelihood of a consumer accidentally burning themselves with it.
I am a grown woman. I was not goofing off or distracted in any way when I sustained the injury to my forearm today. On one prior occasion I burned my forehead and consequently my neck when I jerked from the searing pain. Those burns were terribly painful and were red and raised for quite awhile. However, after getting the terrible blistering, larger than a quarter sized  burn today,  I concluded that this product is simply unsafe.
The heat resistant glove provides a negligible heat barrier and I'm certain that one's hand would easily be burned if it came into direct contact with the heated barrel for more than 2 seconds. I've felt the burning on my fingertips several times myself while wearing. The glove length should most definitely be extended farther down the  wrist and Into the forearm inorder to provide the adequate protection needed from the 450 degree ceramic barrel! I have used heated styling products for years with no extreme burn incidents like what I have experienced with this product. It just seems extremely dangerous. I also question the accuracy and safety of the stated heating temperature. How on earth is it considered safe for the general public? I propose that this product's safety be reevaluated.
My injury is definitely very painful. I've been taking pain medication all day and can still feel the awful burning. I have looked up burn care for when and if the large blister pops. It is swollen and feels like it has fluid. I'm fairly sure it will also leave an ugly, visible scar. I have spoken to numerous women today who all share burn stories from using similar products. Some say my product might just be too hot, others say they have longer safety gloves. Taking their comments and my experience into consideration I decided to take action and report to your agency today.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

incidentDescription:

I am sending you these pictures of our Cuisinart DCC-1150 coffee pot (after 4 years of use) as I am

My husband, an aerospace engineer, said that if proper materials were used, there would not have

productDescription:
Follett 2013 Ice Machine
Model: 12HI 400 A
incidentDescription:
The Ice machine in the ICU started to smoke. The fire department and facilities management were notified. The Ice machine was taken out of service and the manufacturer was notified. No one was harmed and this did not disrupt patient care.
The Follett representative was contacted and stated that due to the previous ice machine fire they investigated, they found an issue with the relay and were in process of a recall to replace these defective part.
They started getting other facilities that were having the same issue. The root cause of the problem was that GE did not use enough copper wire in the windings of the relay when making the part, causing them to over heat and melt.
The ICU Ice machine was replaced, and 3 other ice machines had the defective part replaced.

As soon as the product is turned on, it produces a fine mist into the air.  Within a week of his initial use of the humidifier, the consumer noticed a dust on his furniture and other items that were near the humidifier.  He initially did not think much of this.  

He used the product for approximately 7 weeks and 5 week into using the product, the consumer developed a hacking cough (similar to a smokers cough).  The cough also continued to get worse over time.

Some of this dust was being sucked into his return-air duct.  This is when he identified that this mist floated in the air and remained for an unidentified amount of time.

3/2/2018:  The home heating system shut down and stopped working.  The consumer had to get a technician out to examine it.  The first tech. did not correctly identify the problem.  

3/3/2018:  The consumer had a 2nd technician come out, who was more experienced.  This tech. was able to identify that particles from the humidifier were being trapped in the home heating system's return-air duct.  The tech. also said that the consumer's filter was very tight and able to trap these particles.  However, lower quality filters may allow the particles to go into this home heating/venting system and could impact its’ operation.

Within 1 - 3 days of discontinued use of the product, the consumer began to feel almost 100% better.

3/5/2018:  The consumer contacted the manufacturer and spoke with a Customer Service Rep. and reported the issue and asked if he could be reimbursed.  The rep. took the consumer's information and told him that a supervisor would call him back, but he had not received a call at the time of this report.


3/8/2018:  The consumer followed up with the manufacturer again.  The consumer believes that their warnings are misleading and he inquired about getting reimbursed again.  The rep. asked him questions and told him that she had to pass his information over to a supervisor.

The consumer is extremely concerned because if this product affected his heating systems filter, he questions what the  health effects would be to homeowners.

3/4/2018:  The consumer returned the product back to the retailer and reported the problem as well.  The retailer took the product back and gave him  a full refund.

Intertek Tested:  4001372

PRODUCT WARNING:  If you have hard-tap water, stop using the water.

NOTE:  The consumer has soft tap water.

This product does not appear to be included in any CPSC recall.

representatives with a view to alerting the company about this dangerous
product;

outlet to a location assumed to be Hoover's factory. This was done

vary least, Inform me of of Hoover's findings In the matter. These requests
have, to date, been Ignored;

executive officer of Hoover. The requests In that letter have also, to date,
been Ignored.

This Information Is being provided to the Safety Commission for whatever use
It may wish to make of It, but I urge the Commission to Investigate the
matter. The Commission Is probably In a far better position than I am to get
Information from Hoover. All I can offer at this point Is that this product was/

With the torque of the rotating fan blades the unit could come out of the ceiling and injure someone.  Their engineers should have either used 2 screws or a nut and bolt to properly secure the fan motor to the ceiling.

I contacted Gree and completed the recall information. I received the recall package weeks later and promptly sent it in with all required information. It was explained to me at that time that I would receive my refund within 2-6 weeks. It is now January 12, 2018 and I have not received my refund as of yet. I just spoke to Gree and was told they did not receive the return package from me until October 16, 2017 and did not start to process the refund until December 1, 2017. Are you kidding me??? That is ridiculous. They stated they will get the refund to me as soon as possible.

If a company is involved with a recall such as this, they should be a little more attentive and ambitious to satisfy ALL customers in a timely fashion. This is NOT timely. Furthermore, they won't even refund the purchase price that I have on my receipt. They will only refund $229. Why?????

productDescription: CoolMist Homedics humidifier.
incidentDescription:
On March 26, 2018, a homeowner observed a flame emanating from the bottom of a Homedics humidifier,Model UHE-CM25TGTA. She immediately unplugged the unit. The home owner's husband, a fire chief for the local fire department, contacted this writer, (fire Marshal), re the incident. I advised him to bring it to the office, (fire marshal's office), and that I would examine it.

I disassembled the unit and observed burn/soot marks in the units interior. I removed a circuit board that was secured in place via two screws. When I lifted the circuit board off of its mounts, I observed a scorched wire in the two wire power cord, that was directly beneath the circuit board. I traced the shorted wire and found that it was the hot side of the power cord. The underside of the circuit board possessed many sharp edges. These edges were formed by the penetrations of the components that were soldered (bottom side)and mounted on the topside of the board.
The pointy projections sat directly on top of the power cord There was no protection afforded to the power cord. Without any buffer material to protect the cord from being abraded or penetrated by the circuit board components, the underside of the circuit board shorted out to the power cord.

I believe the home owner's presence in the room and quick action, prevented the event from growing into a larger problem.

Sometime later, he tried the hair dryer again and a shower of sparks flew from the place where there is a layer of plastic wrapped around the electric cord, near the area where the cord is connected to the handle of the hair dryer.  The sparks shower was approx. 2-1/2' to 3' (feet) in length.  The consumer immediately turned the dryer off and unplugged it from the wall outlet.  He then ran water over the bottom part of the handle, where the sparks shot from the cord.

NOTE:  The area of the cord, where the sparks shot from, has several holes.  One of the holes is a little larger than the others, since the incident.  He has not opened the dryer or the cord, but wonders if the wires became exposed in that area.

Above the handle, is the motor for the machine.  Above the handle is a disk 2/1-2" in diameter, which is used to blow air and cool down the motor.  However, this also blows dust inside the motor.

The consumer was not injured and there was no property damage.

This 2nd hair dryer may present a fire or burn hazard.

productDescription: Bodum Caffettiera French Press Coffee Maker
incidentDescription:
The hazard I wish to report concerns the Bodum glass coffee press. The main hazard is that the press, during regular use, is subject to extreme thermal stress when boiling water is poured into it, and in some cases is over stressed and fails.

Also, the glass craft is not secured into the cage, and can fall out while pouring. In both cases, the glass will shatter, leaving small glass slivers and pieces on the counter top, where food is prepared.

The first email attached is Bodums' response to my initial complaint, as well as my initial complaint. The second email
starts off with a more detailed description of the problem including the basis of a stress analysis indicating the over stressed condition.

Also included is a photo of a typical failure, this one due to thermal stress alone.  Please note that these products are similar to the product that Bodum previously recalled, the [REDACTED] coffee press, and has a similar defect. Also note that Bodum states that the product is subject to microscopic defects, not visible to the human eye, which could cause failure during normal use. Also note that Bodum does not include any warnings about these dangers on their products.

The first failure occurred when I poured boiling water into the craft. Boiling water, glass splinters, small glass cups, and
grinds were spread over the counter top, cabinets, and floor. The entire area had to be wiped with cloths which had to be thrown out due to the glass. Then the area had to be dried, vacuumed, and the wiped again. The glass chips were so
small, there is little assurance they were all removed.

Your assistance assistance is greatly appreciated.

[REDACTED]

productDescription: Pelonis fan-forced portable space heater, model# HF-0063, date code 1508; serial# appears to be 20215109Z
incidentDescription:
The product was a Pelonis space heater, model# HF-0063, date code 1508; serial# appears to be 20215109Z.  I bought this product @ Home Depot on or shortly before 2016-Feb-1.  

I've used this product in winter only.  This (winter 2017-2018) would be the 3rd winter in which I used the product (the heater is less than 2 years old).  

I've always used this fan-forced heater in its oscillation or swing mode, in which the body of the heater automatically rotates left & right using a motor.  

Today the heater turned off unexpectedly; its display was completely blank, and pushing the power-on button did nothing.  

I unplugged the heater & plugged it back in; the heater still didn't work.  

Thinking that the problem might be where the power cord enters the heater, I flexed the cord somewhat.  Soon the heater started beeping intermittently; it normally beeps when it's turned on.  

A few seconds later, with an arcing sound, a jet of flame, about 3 inches long, shot out of the point where the power cord enters the heater.  That flame might have caught something else on fire if there had been any such object close enough.  

After a couple of seconds, the flame seemed to extinguish itself the moment before I pulled the plug from the wall.  

This heater's predecessor, a similar unit by DeLonghi, also failed due to the power cord flexing, but didn't emit any flame.  Apparently it's possible to design this kind of heater so that it doesn't emit flame even if the power cord does fail.

productDescription: Capresso Iced Tea Maker Black 624.01
incidentDescription:
I was filling the pitcher of my iced tea maker with ice from my refrigerator door and noticed ice falling to the floor.  When I looked at the bottom of the pitcher, I noticed that an ice cube had broken through the glass, and glass shards were all over the floor.  I put the broken container in the sink and quickly cleaned up the glass before anyone was able to walk into the kitchen.  No injuries were sustained.

I am writing because my husband and I are concerned about the glass pitcher on this item.  This pitcher was not used outside of the manufacturer warnings and should not have broken with normal use.  Upon the first use, my husband and I were both surprised that the glass used on the pitcher was so thin - especially on the bottom.  However we (wrongly) assumed that because this iced tea maker was more costly than others on the web site, the glass must be stronger or of better quality.

We do not feel that an ice cube falling from a dispenser should have enough impact to crack or break through glass.  While no injuries were sustained with this incident, an injury could have easily occurred.  Since I did not hear the glass break, I could have easily stepped on broken glass.  I also could have easily cut myself on the bottom of the pitcher or while cleaning up the shards from the floor.  In addition, if a consumer happened to crack the glass with an ice cube, then continue to make tea (which adds hot water to the pitcher while it brews), the pitcher could easily shatter.  I do not believe the pitcher is tempered, which is a larger concern if children or pets are around when the pitcher breaks.

incidentDescription:
Dear CPSC Representative,

Calif. Dept. of corrections and rehabilitation (CDCR) changed the hotpot we are allowed to purchase to the one above.

All of us noticed that these hotpots developed small white round deposits all over the metal base inside the pot.  They're 1/16" to about 1/4" diameter.  They don't appear like mineral deposits, which look different and were more in a layer, with it being thicker around the heating element.  Vinegar will not remove them entirely, and the metal began to pit after only 2-3 uses.  No food was heated, only water.
We are concerned that these deposits are leaching from the metal itself, which appears to be a cheap quality.  Would this cause effects on our health?  Also there pits and the poor quality are causing leaks into the base.  This is a fire/shock hazard.  We cannot repair them, as the orange ring is a security feature which breaks if base is opened, thus custody staff would confiscate it.  Some have noticed mold or mildew growing in the base, as we can't access the insider to clean and disinfect.
What would you advise?  Can you obtain a hotpot and test it?  We inmates have no resources other than you.
Thank you so very much for your time.
Sincerely,
[REDACTED]

incidentDescription:
I purchased two SAMSONITE CONVERTER/ADAPTER PLUG KIT WITH POUCH (Item NO.: 495591073, http://shop.samsonite.com/exclusion-list-additional-sam25/samsonite-converter-adapter-plug-kit-with-pouch/495591073.html) on August 6th 2017 at Best Buy.

I lived in the US for three years and moved back to Germany in September 2017. I bought the converts to use it for some appliances I had purchased in the US. The product description states, that the adpater works with most travel products up to 1600 Watt.

I first used the adapter for an Air Bed (Insta-Bed Raised Air Mattress with Never Flat Pump). It ifrst worked fine and I was able to inflate the bed fully and also was able to add some air a few times. Also the built in never flat pump worked properly. But at some point there was a funny electric smell and the air bed pump stopped working. There is a fuse inside the samsonite adapter, but that one was perfectly OK. The indicator light on the adapter also still worked, but the air bed did not work at all anymore. 
To check if somehting is wrong with the converter I used it for my US shaver. The shaver basically blew up in my hand within a few seconds. I was not hurt, but I could clearly feel the impact. The fuse of the samsonite converter was still OK. I then checked the output of the converter with a Voltmeter and it showed about 230 Volts. This clearly indicated that the converter was broken as it should convert to 110 Volts. To compare it, I unpacked the second converter I had purchased and measured the output at that one. It gave me around 110 Volts.

I read some reviews on the Samsonite Homepage and there were customers that had similar issues. The converter simply does not work and can be dangerous in regards to fire or getting an electric shock.

Last week I sent a complaint E-Mail to costomer service at samsonite. No answer. Today I called them and the only thing they told me was, that I need to claim the product at Best Buy and there are no refunds for broken appliances that the converter was used for. I recommended them to take the product off the market, as it does not work and is dangerous. They want to get back to me within 48 hours. I already told them that I am very angry and will also file this saftey complaint.

productDescription: DeLonghi BCO330T, Serial Number 72825
incidentDescription:
On February 7th, 2018 at approximately 3:30 PM PST, I was operating an Espresso/Coffee Machine (DeLonghi BCO330T, Serial Number 72825).

I firstly began using the machine by adding water in the top reservoir of the unit, waiting about three minutes for the water to heat up, then I added almond milk to a frothing cup and heated up the milk with the unit's steam wand. 

Shortly after, I grabbed the espresso portafilter and added coffee using the measuring spoon included with the unit, enough to fill it at half capacity or for two shots of espresso coffee.

I began by priming the brew head to clean it. I then inserted the portafilter into the brew head, ensuring that the filter basket was properly inserted into the portafilter and that it it was flush, as I normally do when I operate the machine. I twisted the handle counter clockwise into the machine and ensured the handle was pointing to the arrow on the machine, so it lined up properly. 

I began the espresso brewing process by turning the switch on the side of the machine upwards and espresso began to brew and fall into a glass cup that was provided in the box for use with brewing espresso. 

As it was brewing, the unit had already poured enough coffee for one shot of espresso, and being accustomed to the machine, I knew it would take about a minute or two to finish brewing the full two shots of espresso, so I walked less than five feet away from the machine to another side of the kitchen and nearly two seconds after I walked away I could hear pressure build up in the machine, then suddenly heard a boom similar to a grenade exploding.

I stood there realizing and shaking by what seemed to be an explosion. I understood that I was lucky to have walked away for a moment as I could have been killed or seriously injured by the explosion's debris (the portafilter that flew from the blast of pressure, the hundreds of pieces of glass from the glass cup as well as the burning hot espresso grounds and coffee) which flew all over the room, the dining room, and the living room. 

I began by trying to clean up the mess and cut my finger with the broken shards of glass, so I consulted a cleaning lady and had her come clean up the debris which flew all over the room and previously prepared food and other kitchen items. 

I am writing this so appropriate measures can be taken to prevent this from happening to anyone else. I was left with a scene that looked like it came out of a Hollywood movie. Moments after the incident happened I contacted DeLonghi's customer service and spoke with a woman named [REDACTED] from Coffee Machine support and not only was my story not believed, but [REDACTED] asked me twice to plug in the machine again and attempt to brew a new batch of espresso, while she was on a video conference call with me although my repeated attempts to tell her that I was not comfortable with going through the experience again as I was almost seriously injured.

productDescription: Cuisinart Brew Central 14-cup Programmable Coffeemaker (model CBC-6400PC)
incidentDescription:
This morning I received second-degree burns when the bottom of my coffeepot spontaneously fell out, inundating my feet with scalding coffee. I'm wondering if I have an actionable case.

Details: At 6:15 a.m. I arose and went downstairs to get my first cup of coffee, as is my habit.

The Cuisinart Brew Central 14-cup Programmable Coffeemaker (model CBC-6400PC) had turned on automatically at 5:30 a.m., as usual, so the coffee was hot and ready. 

As I lifted the full glass pot from the coffeemaker and moved it toward my adjacent cup, the bottom of the glass pot broke out, and the hot coffee was released all at once onto my feet. I did not bump the pot against any other surfaces. There was no impact with anything.

I was wearing socks, and the hot liquid remained in contact with my skin until, in panic, I hurried into the bathroom and submerged each foot in the toilet in turn.

Both feet received second-degree burns, which were diagnosed and treated at a PeaceHealth urgent care center around 9:30 this morning. The left foot, of which I've attached a couple of pictures, suffered much greater damage.

Until it heals, which the doctor said would be possibly two weeks, I'll be unable to wear shoes and therefore unable to go outside or partake of my daily hikes or frequent bike rides or rounds of golf.

The pot that broke had no previous apparent imperfections and had been used and washed normally since we bought it from Costco on June 1, 2016.

The break in the glass followed the pot's lower metal band partway and also separated in a clean line along the bottom edge of the pot, as the attached photos show. I'm no engineer, but it seems that the nature of the break indicates a weakness in the glass rather than any accidental impact.

incidentDescription:
Our golf cart needed new lead-acid batteries, so the company that sold the cart to us, and continues to provide maintenance support, suggested we install six 8-volt batteries instead of the four 12-volt batteries that needed replacing.

While charging, potentially dangerous hydrogen gas is produced that made our carbon monoxide detector a floor above the cart garage alarm. Readings of 300 ppm were obtained in our house. When the detector was placed upon the batteries, the detector max'd out at 999 ppm.

I called the fire department, and their more sophisticated measuring device measured, and alarmed.
They said that firefighters will evacuate a building if hydrogen is measured above 50 ppm!

My cart company never received a complaint before about this, and didn't necessarily understand the gravity of the situation, but hydrogen gas had been escaping into my house for weeks!

incidentDescription:
Around August 15, 2017 I noticed my dehumidifier was not functioning correctly.

Around June 1, 2017, I started running the dehumidifier for the summer months in our basement. When I first plugged it in and started it, I thought the compressor sounded normal. The unit seemed to be running fine since I noticed water draining from the bucked to the floor drain. I have a basement office and I started noticing a kind of a low pitched "metallic" sound coming from the unit if I happened to be within earshot. It was one of those things you notice, but assume it is just "normal". 

Then around the 15th of August, I came downstairs and noticed the basement humidity was up and it had that "basement" smell. I could hear the unit's fan running, but the compressor was not on. I rotated the unit and kneeled down to check the floor drain to look for water coming out of the hose. There was none. I immediately noticed a "burnt, ozone, melted plastic smell" at floor level. I quickly unplugged the unit and began investigating. After taking the back panel off, I managed to pull off the black plastic compressor cap and found a horrendous site. One of the power leads had completely been melted, burnt, and was broken off of the compressor terminal. You can see in the pictures the melted wire, black scorching, and the melted plastic inside the cap. This is a complete fire hazard. I am lucky I was there when I noticed the unit not functioning.

productDescription: Keurig Single Cup Brewer Model B40
incidentDescription:
I was burnt by the hot water spurting from brewer leaking on countertop today. I notified Keurig and inquired if brewer was recalled because when I told my daughter what happened this morning, she stated a coworker told her her Keurig had been recalled. 
  When I contacted Keurig today, I inquired as to why wasn't I ever contacted regarding potential issues and a recall.  Keurig stated my brewer was not recalled. I provided my information and stated I had contacted them numerous times in past few years and each time I was accused of overfilling water reservoir too high, using brewer to much, or nit descaling. I told her the water spurting out from machine burnt me and she states "the recall was years ago". I then responded "I called you when recall was announced & was told my brewer was fine" and informed her that "I called 8 or 9 times after when brewer didn't brew 6oz or 8oz, brewed too hot, leaked,  and spurted hot water as brewing".   Keurigs response was your brewer wasn't recalled.   
  Prior to todays call,  I had contacted Keurig numerous times regarding my Keurig brewer leaking, spurting hot water, brewing really hot water, not brewing the correct amount (6oz/8oz) over the past few years.  On each and every occasion Keurig stated my brewer was fine. They stated it was my overuse, my not descaling, or my overfilling water reservoir. 
  When my brewer first leaked a small amount if water (not hot),  I called Keurig and was told to descale the brewer. I stated I follow the instructions to descale every 3-6 months and was told if used daily descale every 3 months. I have continued to follow the recommended descaling every 3 months since.  
  The problem slowly got worse and  I would call Keurig &  tell them its spurting hot water Keurig stated that I didn't clean it properly. I informed them I follow their instructions completely and inquired if my brewer was recalled.  Keurig stated "no"; I asked if anyone else is having problems like mine they stated "no". Every time I called Keurig, I was told it was my fault, "too much water in reservoir" "have an electrician check my outlets" (I did and my outlets have no short or faulty currents and electrician told me that I have a safety feature for outlet that shuts off power to that outlet to prevent fires/shocks etc). So the extremely hot water is the brewer not me or my electricity. 
    I called Keurig again and again as the leaking and spurting hot water slowly worsened.  Burning your tongue on a hot cup of coffee happens I know cause I own a Keurig that brews about 170-180degrees F (yep I measured the temp & Keurig has told me  thats the a normal temp) but getting scalded by  hot water leaking/spurting from brewer is not normal despite what Keurig said.

I was hoping that they had a fix for this and when to the store and looked at some new  Tragger grills. They still are manufacturing the with out any cover.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription: Ryobi Cordless Jet Fan Blower, Mod. P2108, Ser. No. EU 16192D150206, green
productSubCategory: Lawn Mowers, Leaf Blowers and Lawn Vacuums
incidentDescription:
The plastic fan inside my Ryobi Cordless Jet Fan Blower, Mod. P2108, Ser No. EU 16192D150206
broke, which caused the fan blades to be discharged from the front end of the blower tube. Luckily, no-one was near when this failure occurred.

I've contacted Ryobi Customer Service and filed a warranty claim. They in turn have forwarded the claim to the Ryobi "Safety" Dept who are supposed to handle the claim.

I'm contacting the CPSC because the same circumstances have resulted in the recall of a similar
Ryobi blower. The Ryobi [REDACTED], Mod [REDACTED] has been recalled, 
Recall No. [REDACTED]. The reason given in the CSPC recall notice is: " The plastic fan inside the electric blowers can break causing the fan blades to be discharged from either end of the blower tube.
This poses a laceration hazard."

productDescription: Cuisinart Smart Stick immersion blender, model CSB75(AD)
incidentDescription:
I recently purchased a Cusiinart Smart Stick immersion blender Model  CSB75(AD) and had used it perhaps a half dozen times for normal kitchen blending activities. I noticed one day that half of the very sharp blade had broken off and was missing.

 As you can imagine we were worried that the shards may have been swallowed since we can´t find the missing half of the blade. It does not appear that any injuries occurred.

Upon further review, it appears that this defect has been  noted by other consumers according to comments on Amazon.com.

productDescription:
26-cu ft Side-by-Side Refrigerator Single Ice Maker (Easycare) 
Item #: 488403 Model #: FFHS2611PF $958.62
incidentDescription: On Saturday, December 16th 2017 our brand new 26-cu ft Side-by-Side Refrigerator Single Ice Maker (Easycare)  Item #: 488403 Model #: FFHS2611PF purchased on 05/07/16 capacitor spontaneously caught fire. Was told there was nothing able to be done to resolve our issue and treated as if it were no big deal. Our house almost burned down, we could have lost our lives. Now we're out of a $1000 brand new refrigerator. The only option they offered would be to schedule a repair man to come check for $50 cash on sight. 6 months after our 1 year warentee, our faulty fridge catches fire, almost burns our house down and kills us all... and we have to pay to have a repair man come see what needs to be replaced (which I will have to pay for) upon further researched I learned this is a fairly common problem with this exact model of refrigerator, yet they are still being manufactured and sold. There needs to be a recall on this product and a class action lawsuit to prevent this from happening to other customers and to reimburse others who have suffered damages from this product with no resolution in the past.

productDescription: Range hood
incidentDescription:
Caller stated that his spouse turned on the unit and immediately there were flames emanating from the motor of the unit.  The fire extinguisher was used to contain the flames.  There were minimal property damages.  

The manufacturer was contacted  and a voicemail was left.

Caller feels that if he was not fire safety personnel this incident would have been worst and feels that this should be reported.

productDescription: Purchased from Kastar USA via Amazon.com on 8/21/17 as a set: Kastar SLIM LCD Charger (LCD3-S005) and 2 Kastar Battery rechargeable battery packs 3.6 V (For IA-BH125C)
incidentDescription: Purchased from Kastar USA via Amazon.com on 8/21/17 as a set: Kastar SLIM LCD Charger (LCD3-S005) and 2 Kastar Battery rechargeable battery packs 3.6 V (For IA-BH125C). I received the set on 8/25/17.  I immediately plugged the charger into my computer's USB port and began charging the first battery as the voltage appeared to be low.  About 15 minutes later, I heard a loud pop like a gunshot.  The battery had exploded and fallen to the floor on fire.  I immediately began putting out the fire with a blanket.  Luckily no one was sitting at the computer when the battery exploded.

productDescription: blender
incidentDescription:
The submitter said she was making a fruit smoothie and she had the blender on for about 10 seconds. She then tried to open it but it was very difficult and she indicated that it seemed like there was a lot of pressure inside. The submitter said after struggling for some time she was able to open it but the top exploded and hit her in the chest. The submitter described the incident similar to opening a champagne bottle. The submitter said the top flew off hitting her in the chest and the contents went everywhere. The submitter said had pains in her chest from the incident but she did not seek medical attention. 

The submitter said she used the unit again about 2 weeks ago and she has been unable to open the blender. She said she is scared to force it open because of the last incident. She said her husband has also tried opening it but he was unsuccessful. The submitter believes the product is unsafe and should be examined.

The submitter indicated that when she has used the unit in the past it would be a little hard to open but now it has become extremely hard and unsafe to open.

The submitter plans to contact the firm and notify them of her safety concerns.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: Oster Convection Countertop Oven, model TSSTTVF817
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription: My Oster Toaster Oven Model TSSTTVF817 timer failed and continues to run after reaching OFF.  It continues on to STAY ON which resulted in the oven being on all night.  It does not stay OFF when it is supposed to.

productDescription: Elite Platinum Maxi-Matic Electric Kettle EKT-200
incidentDescription:
While using the Elite Maxi-Matic electric kettle we noticed a strong odor of burning plastic.  When we looked at the bottom of the kettle we could see that it had melted a hole in the bottom plastic of the kettle and also in the base.
We did a web search on this product and discovered a review on Amazon saying virtually the same thing.  
We called the manufacturer's customer support phone number and the representative said they we not aware of any problems with this product.  I emailed them pictures of the melted plastic. 
They offered to replace the kettle, which we did not want.  They said we would have to go back to Kroger to get a refund, which we will do.  
We bought this kettle 9 months and we used it every day.

productDescription:
Soleus Air De-humidifier
Model SG-DEH-70-1
SN:54420000470
manufacturer: Gree Electric Appliances, Inc. of Zhuhai
incidentDescription:
Soleus Dehumidifier, 1 of 2 units being used in my finished basement.
Unit was making an unusual sound.
The fan was not running, there was a smell of melting plastic.
None of the control buttons worked and I could feel heat coming from the unit.
I unplugged the unit and monitored it.
When removing the water container I saw that the wall behind it was melting and too hot to touch.
Thank God I caught this before it started on fire.

productDescription: Broil King "Porta-chef 120" barbecue
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription: I am reporting an unsafe barbecue, " Porta-Chef 120 made by Broil King". It has no real grease drainage system. It stores grease in the bottom of the barbecue base, near the flame, until the grease reaches a depth of 1/4" with an approx. area of 135 sq inches. After it has reached this level it drips all over the floor. However, multiple times the grease has caught fire. It is a very ferocious fire and difficult to put out. If used near a building or an apartment it could easily start a fire. I was using this in 90 degree weather and it happened three times in a row. I stopped using it after I realized what was going on. Each fire was progressively worse than the last as the grease level increased.

productDescription: 120 VAC, 1500 Watts, electric space hater
incidentDescription: I purchased a Soleil  "Milk House Heater".  120 VAC, 1500 Watts, Model: TFH-203-S.  The fan on the heater seized causing the unit to overheat, tripping the circuit breaker.

productDescription: 6 gallon wet/dry vacuum
incidentDescription:
I have a Shop Vac model K12-300A purchased in 2013. When I turned it on recently the switch shorted, starting an electrical fire. Luckily I was able to disconnect it before anything besides the vacuum was damaged (the switch melted in the closed position). I contacted Shop Vac and was told I could purchase a new motor unit, which I have ordered. I asked them if they were going to respond to me regarding this serious safety defect (a switch shouldn't catch fire, as it's supposed to be within 1 wire, usually the black power line). They haven't responded.
If one panics for even a few minutes the whole motor assembly will burst into flames (it was starting to flame in the 10-15 seconds it took me to disconnect it).

productDescription: NutriBullet 900 Series blender
incidentDescription:
I pureed a soup in the NutriBullet 900 Series Blender.  When taking off the lid of the blender, it exploded like a bomb and caused 1st and 2nd degree burns across my chest, arms, neck and face.  I went to the ER immediately and they cared for my extensive burns.  That was a week ago - since then, I've had to do daily wound cleaning and dressing changes (at the ER or a wound clinic or with a nurse).

I have since found several other stories online in which other people (even a 4 year old boy in Florida!) suffered horrible burns like mine.  There are no warnings on this blender about putting hot liquids in it.  Unlike a [REDACTED] coffee cup, there is nothing that reads NO HOT LIQUID.  

In our litigious society, I am quite shocked that this company doesn't have such basic warnings about hot liquids...especially since I have seen multiple stories online about other burn victims.

This company should be required to add language in large bold letters to each NutriBullet device that reads NO HOT LIQUID.

It has been a very painful ordeal (second most painful event for me next to childbirth) and I don't want anyone else to ever suffer this pain.

I cannot work.  I cannot pick up my 2 year old daughter.  My burns hurt and itch.  I have limited mobility.  Please do something to ensure that others are warned about this kitchen device - no hot liquids should ever be placed in it.  The manufacturer must be required to add these warnings immediately...and a recall would be beneficial as well.

productDescription: Lithium rechargeable battery for an Apple MacPro laptop.
model: Temark New A1322 Battery - Item code: HSA07
incidentDescription: A local fire Chief reported that his adult daughter purchased a replacement battery online for her Apple MacPro laptop. She later discovered that the battery had expanded and distorted the plastic casing of the laptop. No fire was caused in the incident and no one was injured.

productDescription: Flexible hose to comect a 5 gal portable LPG tank to a BBQ
productType: Propane, Lp or Butane Gas Tanks or Fittings (131)
incidentDescription: 4 foot adapter hose from portable 5 gal propane tank to outdoor BBQ developed a leak at the end that was attached to the tank. No leak noted when it was hooked up but if the hose was touched high pressure propane would leak from the fitting. Removing the hose from the tank and cleaning all the fittings several times did not change the leak. No injuries or damage as I was checking for leaks after changing tank and noted the leak if the hose was touched. Leak was around the metal tubing running from the tank adapter into the hose. his hose has been in service for less than two years and shows no obvious damage. Hose in question was manufactured by Chen Fong Ent.  LTD. Model GHA1 Lot #031647.

productDescription: propane gas regulator
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
brand: Gaspro as advertised but is no where to be found on item
incidentDescription: Gaspro propane gas grill regulator failed and started leaking after 2 uses. Potentially explosive condition.

productDescription: Le Creuset Classic Stainless Steel Tea Kettle 1.6 quart
incidentDescription:
We purchased a Le Creuset classic stainless steel tea kettle in November of 2016.  Every time we used it for several months, we had the same problem:  every time the water in our kettle boiled this happened: when we started pouring into a cup, the hot water would spurt out of the spout, as if the spout itself were superheated.  It splashed out, partly into the cup, partly onto the countertop.  We quickly learned not to hold the cup with our hand.  I looked on line and found many descriptions of the same problem.  It seems to me someone could easily be burned by the hot water.
I contacted Le Creuset but they were not very helpful.  I returned the kettle to the retailer and bought a different brand.

productDescription: Ceiling fan
incidentDescription: The plastic support ball at the top of the down rod for the ceiling fan failed.   The assembly fell about 10 feet to the floor of the living room.  There was evidence of electrical arcing when the live wires pulled free in the electrical supporting box.  No electrical fuses were tripped.  The fan was running at its slowest speed when the failure occurred.  No one was present at the time.  It is a pretty heavy assembly.  If it had hit squarely on a child it could have caused a very serious injury.  There was also the possibility of an electrical fire.  I believe the fan is at least 10-15years old.  If you need pictures or additional information please contact me.

productDescription: SKY 2766  Better Choice Product Air Fryer
incidentDescription: I have a better choice air fryer.product number SKY2766. This is my second one in less than a year both have gone with a bang. This time there was lots of sparks. I was cooking pre made fries and following the manufacturer instructions. I have only used this replacement fryer about 6 times. This product is dangerous and I feel could cause serious injuries.

productDescription: Cuisinart 12-cup coffee maker #DCC-1100BK
incidentDescription: In normal use of my Cuisinart 12-cup coffee maker (once daily) I noticed that the power cord was deformed. Upon closer observation I discovered it it actually melting! This is the second time I've had an electrical problem with the same model coffee maker from Cuisinart. In fact a previous device (same modal) nearly caught fire in the base of the unit. Thankfully for me only smoke and stench without fire.

productDescription: Interstate 9V Battery
incidentDescription:
This is the 2nd incident that we reported to me. I have previously reported this to you via this website. 

We have had several 9V Interstate batteries fail. None have started fires. One did slightly injure an employee when it failed in his pocket. This was the case I reported to you earlier. The electrodes on the top of several of the batteries in different locations around the country are blowing off in some sort of small explosion/reaction.

productDescription: Revlon 1875W / Ceramic / Ionic Hair Dryer - Model RVDR5105
incidentDescription: Revlon 1875W / Ceramic / Ionic Hair Dryer (model RVDR5105)- noticed the the plug was so hot that I could hardly touch it after use. This had been going on for a while. Last week I went to use it and couldn't seem to plug it in. I looked at the plug and one of the prongs was completely misplaced and no longer lined up with the other. I looked at the outlet and noticed it had black residue on the same side as the misplaced prong was on. Luckily I unplug it after ever use. Otherwise it could have caused a fire.

productDescription: Bronze in color with 4 little round globe bulb type.  Harbor freeze ceiling fan
incidentDescription: In my home I have a total 6 harbor freeze ceiling fan.  I just recently started to pay close attention to the fan and had just discover the brand.  I was unaware of the brand because I didn't know how take it apart.  Anyways, the hazardous problem with these 4 bulb harbor freeze ceiling fan is that they get too hot and melts the connectors on the bulbs causing it to have loose connection or a short.  Like I said, I owned 6 total and have use different types of bulbs and have found them very dangerous when the ends of the bulbs are burnt off causing them to short.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: Small table-top room Humidifier
incidentDescription: Product has sharp plastic fin-like protrusion immediately adjacent to fill cap so that when I unscrew the cap to routinely fill the tank, I suffered a deep cut to my hand.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription: Red Copper Five Minute Grill
incidentDescription: I am reporting a very dangerous episode that occurred in my kitchen I had purchased a red copper Grill and was making an omelet, I have done this several times in the same fashion scrambled  the eggs placed them in the product closed and secured the lid set my timer for 1.50 minutes and then proceeded to flip the grill to cook eggs on the other side and again set the timer for 1.50 minutes about 45 seconds into the process a sizzling began to erupt as tho pressure was building up and suddenly the top blew open and the eggs flew off into the floor. Needless to say I wasn't standing in front of the incident or I would have been burnt by the hot egg. This happened and I thought well maybe I didn't secure the latch so a few weeks later I did the same exact thing and sure enough it built of pressure blew open the grill and once again the egg flew out of the grill and onto the floor. I called Red Copper and they couldn't explain it because I couldn't remember where I purchased it. I have used this for omelets and pancakes but never have I seen anything explode such as this.

productDescription: Toaster Oven
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription:
The consumer placed a frozen biscuit in the toaster oven to 375 degrees Fahrenheit. Approximately ten minutes later, the consumer heard a loud noise coming from the kitchen. When the consumer checked, he noticed the toaster oven door had blown off, with shattered glass everywhere in his kitchen floor, and some as far as his living room floor. The consumer immediately unplugged the toaster oven; the frozen biscuit had yet to defrost.

07/10/2017 - The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation; the representative he spoke to informed him they would send him a shipping label so he can send the toaster oven back so they can investigate the matter.

The consumer indicates that the same thing happened with a second toaster oven he purchased for his daughter several years ago.

The consumer is unsure if he is going to keep his toaster oven for at least the next thirty days.

productDescription: cell phone home charger
incidentDescription:
(07/28/2017) The consumer stated that the charger was plugged into the wall. When the charger was pulled out of the outlet, the plastic housing came apart. exposing the prongs in the outlet.

The consumer did not know how long the charger had been in the outlet. The charger was not connected to the phone.

(07/28/2017) The consumer contacted the firm and was advised that there was a 14-day guarantee on accessories.

productDescription: Red KitchenAid Tilt-Head Stand Mixer
incidentDescription: I was mixing cake batter with my Kitchenaid stand mixer. I forgot to tighten the attachment knob, so the metal attachment hub cover fell off into the bowl while mixing the batter. The metal cover hit the flat beater and flew sideways out of the bowl. I was standing in front of the mixer, so the metal cover didn’t hit me. A small piece of plastic came off of the flat beater. I don’t know if it ended up in the batter or where it went. I think it could be dangerous if the metal cover hit someone or if someone hurt their teeth when eating the baked cake.

productDescription: Quisinart DLC-7 super pro whisk attachment
incidentDescription: I was making pureed door for a neighbor in need. While whisking potatoes, the shaft teeth broke off into the food. It would have been tragic if not noticed as the pieces were sharp.

productDescription: Dehumidifier
manufacturer: EVA-DRY (EVA DRY) send to Momentum Sales
incidentDescription:
We had an Eva-Dry 2200 dehumidifier in 2 large walk-in closets in the second level of our home.   They had worked without incident for over a year.   On August 25, 2017, the one in our guest room totally disintegrated, causing severe damage to the closet and its contents, and also causing severe smoke damage to entire second floor of our home.  The fire chief stated that if the closet door had not remained closed, the damage would have been much greater to the structure, as well as to myself.  The fire chief also stated there was no indication that anything else electrical in the house had been affected and the breaker did not trip.
We looked on the internet for reviews of this product that might indicate someone else had experienced this problem but found none.  Also asked the question on the Amazon web site where we had purchased the product and no one said they had any trouble with it.
We contacted the company and spoke with an individual who suggested we not report it to our homeowners insurance but rather get estimates for repairs and let them know and they would send us a check, as long as it wasn't over $68,000.   They also made some sort of statement that we may have caused this to happen, on purpose.  The next time we spoke, we told them we had filed a claim and we have not heard from them since.  We still do not have the final costs associated with this fire nor do we know how much our insurance will pay to [REDACTED], [REDACTED] for cleaning of all of the clothing and textiles or for the complete rebuilding of the closet and repainting that had to be done in several areas.
We believe this product is dangerous in its design and/or use of certain materials.  I was home when this occurred and would not be here today if I had opened that closet door to investigate a noise I heard.  When I did investigate a few minutes later,  the smoke was so thick and so black in the bedroom, I could not even see light coming in from the windows....just smoke.   The remains of the dehumidifier were taken by someone from [REDACTED] to a lab to see if they could figure out what happened to it.  We have not heard back from them about the results.

productDescription: BLACK+DECKER 4-Slice Toaster Oven, White, TRO420
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription: Yesterday, I toasted an english muffin in the White Black And Decker toaster oven (BLACK+DECKER 4-Slice Toaster Oven, White, TRO420) which I purchased about a year ago. The toaster oven was definitely turned off and the over door was opened. I grabbed the toast and left the house and returned home the next day as I stayed overnight at a different location. The toast oven was completely on at full toaster heat with the door open and the knob past off. I felt relieved that a fire was not started. I've read on Amazon that many other reviewers experienced this same situation. The product should be recalled.

productDescription: ELITE KENMORE STAND MIXER
incidentDescription: WHILE MY KENMORE ELITE STAND MIXER IS PLUGGED IN IT WILL ME IN THE OFF POSITION AND THEN IT WILL TURN ON BY ITSELF. THEN THE SWITCH STOPPED WORKING AND THE LIGHT JUST FLASHES WHEN YOU TRY TO TURN IT ON

productDescription: Pink Mini-Prep Plus food processor
incidentDescription: Upon cleaning my blade, I discovered a crack in the housing that holds the blade. I fear that the blade will come out of the housing. I will no longer use this appliance.

productDescription: Shark Nija Professional Blender NJ600
incidentDescription: Brand new blender. I took it out of the box and the product was so difficult to put the plastic container on the blender motor that I was going to return to the store.When I turned it sideways to put back into the styrofoam packaging, I turn the blender container on its side and the inside blades do not lock, so they bounced out and made a large laceration and I had to be rushed to emergency for stitches.

productDescription: Revlon 1875 model RV473 Helen of Troy 125vac 60hz 1875 watts handheld hairdryer gray with black handle
incidentDescription: Revlon 1875 model RV473 hair dryer caught on fire while I was drying my hair. Smelt electrical smell and hand got hot; saw flames inside unit. Burnt hand slightly.  Dropped in sink and unplugged from outlet. Turned on faucet to put out flames.  Still have dryer for claims purposes. So glad it wasn't a little kid who could have been electrocuted.  I have owned it a year
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription: Grill Mark Tool for the outdoor cook, bbq grill brush with metal bristles, about 8" long and 3" wide
productType: Manual Cleaning Equipment (Excl. Buckets and Pails) (480)
brand: Grill Mark Tools for the outdoor cook
incidentDescription:
I write this letter today to also request your attention to a serious consumer safety problem involving brushes with metal bristles for grills, as did [REDACTED] attached.

My husband knew right away he had bit into a piece of meat with a bristle that buried itself inside his tongue.  We went to Exeter Hospital ER right away in August 2017 but nobody could see anything, so we were told to wait and contact an ENT Specialist if it continued to have the stabbing pain it would cause off and on.  Dr. [REDACTED] of Core Physicians in [REDACTED] was contacted a couple of days later.  He didn’t find anything but said we will monitor it more.  The stabbing pain continued until my husband insisted on an x-ray.  The x-ray did indeed clearly show the metal bristle lodged inside his tongue.  An MRI was then done soon after and finally surgery did successfully remove it on 9/22/2017.

Luckily it didn’t abscess or get infected during the month or so it was being investigated, or worse, come out and go into his stomach and larger organs where other people (see attached Victoria story) have reported this as well.  We have since heard many folks say they heard this story about these brushes with warning on news channels, and reports of people getting intestines removed and stomach surgeries, and terribly frightening, life threatening issues over it!

I am writing this letter to see where we are on [REDACTED] request and to ask why this product is still on the market at all.  The brush has a warning label on it, but it may take a lawsuit to finally stop this product from being sold in the US.  But why would this not be banned?  It seems like the best thing to do, as it would be if it were a child’s toy etc..

productDescription: It is a cast-iron grill / griddle from Walmart sold under the Ozark brand.
incidentDescription: I purchased a cast iron grill from Walmart. It is Ozark brand. The instructions say that it can be used on a stove top or on an open fire. I was using it on my stove top (for the first time) and after being exposed to the heat for less than 2 min, I heard a loud bang that scared me and my fiance. The grill had broken in two. The blast was loud enough to shake the electric heat sources on my stove loose. If I had been close to it, I have no doubt it would have caused bodily harm. There are absolutely no warning labels on the product.

productDescription: me Hair Removal System
incidentDescription:
06/15/2017 (Approximate) - The consumer indicates that he had just turned on the hair removal system when a few seconds later sparks shot out about six inches. The consumer instinctively dropped the unit to the floor. The consumer unplugged the device from the wall, noticing that smoke was coming out of it; burn marks were also evident.

07/05/2017 (Approximate) - The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation. The representative he spoke to informed him that the warranty does not cover the retailer he purchased it at so there was no assistance they could provide.

The consumer indicates that the product was used, on average, two to four times per month for approximately ten minutes each use prior to the day of the incident. The consumer plans on keeping his hair removal system for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.

productDescription: West Bend slow cooker model # 84367 (silver) "crockery cooker"
incidentDescription:
West Bend Slow cooker Model 84367

On 11/26/17 I had prepared a full [slow cooker] full of soup to take to a family gathering. It had been cooking on high. Went to lift it up off counter and into a towel lined laundry basket sitting directly beside [slow cooker]. As I lifted it over the basket and started to lower it down, the right side handle broke causing half the soup to mostly spill into the basket saving me from getting badly burned. Some did splash on my arms and clothing, but under other circumstances this could have had disastrous results. This [slow cooker] has gotten light use and always has been taken care of. I was shocked when this happened.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: DeLonghi TRD0715T Safeheat 1500W Portable Oil-Filled Radiator with Vertical Thermal Tunnels
incidentDescription:
Date: 11/28/2017
Time: 11:00 AM

Product: Delonghi Dragon Heater Model TRD0715TL 

Noticed a smell coming from heater. Noticed heater overheated the power cord, and melted at the 3-prong connection connected to surge protector. Potential loss of property and possible loss of life.

productDescription: Traeger grill sold at Costco and other retailers. This is the smaller one selling for $459
incidentDescription: We use our grill frequently and have used other smoker style grills. This traeger catches on fire extremely easily. We always have the grill cleaned and only use the appropriate pellets. While cooking the temp suddenly rises and then the inside of the grill is on fire and billowing black smoke. I have read many reports of this happening to others as well. It is something with this specific brand/model that makes it more prone to catching on fire.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: Ninja express chop NJ100 series food processor.
incidentDescription:
My mother in law bought a Ninja NJ100 series express chop food processor (NJ100GR 30).  On opening the product to set this up, prior to any use, the blade slipped and cut the back of her hand below her thumb knuckle, severing an extensor tendon (I believe the extensor pollicis longus tendon).  Fortunately we were able to see an ortho hand surgeon quickly and this was surgically repaired within a few days.  She is working on rehab now and should regain full functioning of the thumb, but has not yet - currently she cannot extend the thumb.  
The product contains a flyer that says "caution: open with care, contains loose SHARP blades." but this seems insufficient as one is already opening the product before one can see this and it is among several other pieces of paper one may not know to look at prior to inspecting the equipment.  My mother in law is very competent and watches our two young children during the day, I feel strongly this accident was not due to any negligence or aberrant behavior on her part.  As a physician I feel obligated to report significant safety incidents I know about as I would with any drug I gave.

productDescription: Keep warm 4 slice toaster
incidentDescription: On November 22, 2017, my toaster that was sitting on top of my stove caught fire from underneath. Thus causing a lot of damage to my home & stove/oven
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription: Ninja Coffee Maker CF 097 32
incidentDescription:
Received 3rd degree burn from steam from coffee maker while it was brewing.

This coffee maker vents steam from the top when it is brewing by design.   In the black plastic there are words molded-"CAUTION - HOT SURFACE".    But, black on black lettering is not very visible.   And, the surface itself is never hot, it is the stream coming from it, which isn't very visible.

The situation was;  the coffee maker has a water reservoir on the right side.   I was making coffee,  it stopped brewing and I noticed the reservoir was empty.   I got some water to refill and opened the lid of the reservoir.   The lid is hinged on the Left hand side to it opens to the left.  When I tilted the lid to the left, it then comes to rest on the surface where the steam is vented.   As I brought the lid over, this is when the steam that had been escaping burned my little finger.

I have been applying scar treatment for weeks now but still have a red mark on my finger.   I am concerned for others who may somehow lean across the top of the maker to reach for something in addition to the situation I had happen.

incidentDescription:
Raven Mower engine cam shaft blew up at church picnic. This mower has had several issues since replacement of original.
I purchased my original Raven in 2014, after less than a year, the generator portion of the MPV stopped working. At that time Denver Global Products (DGP) replaced the mower with a new one. Then at the beginning of 2016, the mowing deck stop working, I called DGP and found out that there was a recall on the deck at the end of 2015 and failed to contact me. They sent me a new mower deck mid-year 2016 after several attempts to contact them. Fast forward to this year. At the beginning of the mowing season, I had to "charge" my Raven so that I could mow, after several attempts to contact them due to voicemail issues or being on hold for an hour, they finally sent someone out. The tech was able to diagnose that the batteries had failed and that they needed to be replaced. They were changed on Aug 15, 2017. 6 days later, I was able to mow and the mower started cutting off on its own and would restart with no problems. This happened 4 times, then front right wheel came off the mower, WHILE I was mowing. I called for a replacement wheel and after several minutes they agreed to replace it. When I finally got the new wheel, I was finally able to mow again on Aug 28. Everything seemed to be going smoothly, until the mower started cutting off again in mid-mow. This happened 4 times, then on the 5th time the mower would not restart. I called and email DGP about what had happened, and they said they would get a tech out in 2 weeks. Since I had a Church picnic coming up on Labor Day and had no mower that would work, I had to borrow one to get the mowing done. At the picnic, several of the guys had heard me talk about the Raven and how much I had enjoyed the product asked to look at it. I showed them the features and they were impressed with the set-up. I attempt to start the Raven and low and behold it started. One of the guys said that it is sounding like a diesel engine, and said that it might be the cam rods. As soon as he said that the top of the engine blew off and several pieces flew 20' away and almost hit the kids that were playing nearby. One gentleman got hit on the forehead and is ok. Oil spew out all over the place onto our clothes and on my siding. I am absolutely shocked, but glad that no one was seriously hurt. 

I have email the above information to DGP and have not received any email back from them. I finally called and talked to [REDACTED], and she said that the engine is out of warranty and that I can buy a new engine to put in, but still hasn't emailed me.

 I am totally frustrated and actually scared of this machine. Plus, I want people to know that this could happen to someone else as well
