productDescription: Philips Fidelio docking speaker.  Built-in rechargeable Li-ion battery.  Used to play your IPod or IPhone music through.
productType: Stereo or Hi-fi Components or Accessories (546)
incidentDescription: 7/11/2014, I purchased a refurbished Philips docking speaker from Wal-Mart online.  I have used this unit coupled with Apple IPods, as intended, without any event.  There was never any glitch or abnormal behavior from the unit prior the the incident.  On the morning of 7/31/2017, I woke up to a strange sound coming from my bathroom.  I went inside and the room was smoky.  I heard a strange chirping sound and quickly realized the smoke was coming from the Philips unit.  I unplugged it and took the IPod off.  My hand was slightly burned, as the IPod unit was very, very hot.  I thought to videotape the unit smoking and chirping, because it was so strange and scary.  I have photos and the unit in my possession.  Upon inspection, after everything cooled down, the connector of the Philips unit and the IPod connector had both melted.  It was alarming, because had I not gotten up and gone to the unit, there, no doubt, would have been a fire.  I contacted Philips on 8/11/17 about this.  I let them know that I wanted to impress my concern for other people using this docking speaker model too. The unit was not in play mode at the time.  I take good care of my things, so I can't imagine what went wrong.  Maybe the device was not flush-on, possibly causing the IPod and docking connection to try to communicate and heat up?  I'm just not sure, as I'm not an electrical engineer. I strongly feel that this incident took place because of a Philips design flaw.  I let them know that.  If this was the impetus, had they had a click and release coupling mechanism, this likely would not have occurred.  I am not an electrical engineer.  All I know is that I used this product properly and it was heading toward a fire.  I have retained the video footage of this.  I felt they should have at least shown concern enough to inspect the unit.  They did not.  They closed the case because I could not produce the receipt in their time frame.  I do not know how many units were sold, but I had purchased a second unit new and let them know that I will retire that one for safety sake.  I was very surprised and found it disturbing that they just dismissed this without inspection.  I think that is very irresponsible and reckless.  I am bringing it to your attention because it was alarming and I am concerned for the public's safety.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription: 3 months ago we bought a Char-Broil Advantage 4 burner gas grill.  This grill is a fire hazard! We just replaced a grill we'd had for 8 years with this one. We have had several raging fires in it ( we NEVER had a fire in our last grill, ever). After the first time, we cleaned the grill thoroughly and according to instructions-- I'd only cooked on it 5x at that point, so we were surprised to need to. Then we had another fire. Another cleaning. So on. Last night we had ANOTHER FIRE, one that required a fire extinguisher, it was the first cook since I last cleaned it. The grill was spotless when I started the burgers, but the flame is just positioned too close to the bottom and the grease drainage is woefully inadequate; grease collected while I cooked and erupted in flames. My husband used to be a firefighter and he can't believe this design hasn't been recalled! I now see SO MANY reviews online with the same complaint. I called the company and after submitting photos they claim it was my fault because there was too much grease in the bottom of the grill.  The only great in the grill was the grease from the burgers I'd been cooking-- I had JUST cleaned it.  Plus, I've only cooked on the grill a dozen or so times, and I've cleaned it several.  CharBroil created a product that will catch fire if ther is any grease-- which is woefully inadequate for a BBQ grill!   I guess the company is waiting for a tragedy or a lawsuit before changing anything.

incidentDescription:
Running the Soleus Air dehumidifier Model # GL-DEH-70EIP-6 in my basement to lower the humidity level.  When opening the basement door, I smelled a strong "hot plastic" odor.  Tracking down the area where the odor was the most prevalent, led me to the dehumidifier.  No real warmth on the outside of the housing.  Turned the device off and removed the bucket from the unit. I could see that plastic behind the bucket had begun to deform and melt.

Given, I bought the unit because of the internal pump, I don't need to empty the bucket and visit the dehumidifier often.  Mainly only to clean out the air filter section.  I am glad this issue happened while I was home as I do feel continued operation of the dehumidifier was a fire threat.

productDescription: Black & Decker Toaster Oven, model TO2050S
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
My wife was using the Black & Decker toaster oven to toast a piece of bread. She assumed the toaster would stop when the toast was done. It failed to stop, and kept toasting. Eventually, the bread caught fire. Luckily, our nanny discovered it, and was able to unplug the toaster oven and stop the fire.

This model has a 'toast' timer knob with a poor design, insofar as it must be turned past the 4 minute mark and then back down, if the desired time is less than 4 minutes. There is mention of this in the manual, and in extremely small type on the face of the toaster. However, the type on the face is easy to miss, particularly for an appliance that should be as easy to operate as a toaster--my wife said she never knew that was required. (And how often will consumers fail to read the whole manual?)

This poor design and poor notice might not be so serious if, as I assumed, the consequence of failing to turn the knob past 4 minutes were that the unit would simply fail to activate, or perhaps that the time of operation would not precisely match the desired time. For the consequence to be that the unit toasts indefinitely seems a serious fire hazard. This seems all the more likely to cause problems given that most items only need to toast 2-3 minutes (in my experience, 2 for a piece of toast, 3 for an english muffin). 

In other words, consumers may be exposed to this potential hazard every time they are engaged in the most common use of the product--toasting bread or an english muffin for 2-3 minutes.

productDescription: 2 slice chrome toaster
incidentDescription:
Dualit 2 slice chrome toaster ASIN # B00009NROG – fire risk

There is a fire risk with this toaster and it should be recalled. Interestingly, the manufacturer is aware of the risk and has taken inadequate steps to address the issue. The problem occurs when the built in timer malfunctions and sticks which causes the toaster to remain powered on constantly. This poses an obvious fire risk although I did not experience a fire and no injuries were caused. The problem with my toaster occurred in May 2017 – the product was purchased in October 2014. A replacement part is easy to find online as are numerous reports of premature failure of timers and concerns about potential fire risk. Interestingly the replacement part has a warning of fire risk on the knob – “Unplug after use – fire risk” that was not on the original part - see photos below of new and original knob. This shows that manufacturer is aware of the issue. But this warning is inadequate as it is totally impractical in any busy household to unplug a toaster every time it is used. Also, by the time you purchase a replacement your original timer without the warning will have failed exposing you to fire risk. This product needs to be recalled and the timer redesigned with a built in fail safe so that if it sticks it powers down automatically.

productDescription: Kitchen Aid Commercial Style Dual Fuel Convection 30 Inch Range.
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
Roasted vegetables in brand- new Kitchen Aid Dual Fuel range using convection roast function at 475 degrees.  After completing oven cooking, turned oven off.   Excessive steam from a vent under cooktop front panel caused burner control knob on front panel to become excessively hot and unusable.  We called for a service technician through Kam Appliances from whom we had purchased new oven.  Service technician was able to replicate issue and measured knob temperature to be as high as 170 degrees.  Kitchen aid was notified by technician and, reportedly, was told that "oven is operating as designed" and that they are aware that the knob may actually become as hot as 190 degrees.  Consumer was told to wear oven mitt when using hot dial.  Kitchen Aid also sent technician new knobs which did not fit and were useless. 

As an elderly person with grand children, I am concerned about safety and, if I use the oven, can not turn it off if I am cooking something on the stove top.   Only after completing my stove-top cooking, can I turn off the oven knowing that the heat coming from that vent can cause potential harm when standing near that vent.  This is an unsafe range.

incidentDescription:
On 7-11-17 the Topeka, KS Fire Department responded to a structure fire located at [REDACTED].  The structure involved a detached garage and it was subsequently suppressed.  The Kansas Office of the State Fire Marshal was requested to conduct an origin and cause investigation.

The fire's origin was determined to have been upon a shelf within the interior of the garage.  Fire ignition was determined to have been from a fault within a Whistler Portable Jump Start & Power Supply.  The owner had plugged in the device for charging the evening before the fire.  

CPSC has reported certain models of this device have been recalled due to reported fires.  I was unable to obtain the model number from the product due to damage. No injuries occurred as a result of this fire.

The origin and cause report may be forwarded to your office if requested, when completed.

productDescription: Ryobi One+ 18-Volt Lithium-Ion Cordless Jet Fan Leaf Blower (Model # P2108, Serial # EU16291D080162)
productSubCategory: Lawn Mowers, Leaf Blowers and Lawn Vacuums
model: Ryobi Cordless Jet Fan Leaf Blower Model # P2108
incidentDescription:
Dear Consumer Products Safety Commission:

On July 5th I sent Ryobi Tools the following email:

Tonight July 5, 2017 my wife was operating our Ryobi One+ 18-Volt Lithium-Ion Cordless Jet Fan Leaf Blower (Model # P2108, Serial # EU16291D080162) that we bought at Home Depot in October of 2016 when the orange plastic fan inside the unit disintegrated into pieces which discharged through the housing and the electric motor started smoking. My wife immediately threw it down and ran. To say the least, she was shaken up, but fortunately not seriously injured. I have been a New Jersey attorney for over 35 years and can tell you this is definitely a defective product - for the exact same reasons as the electric one you previously recalled (MODEL [REDACTED]). You are on Notice, and this defective product should be recalled immediately before anyone gets injured by flying fan pieces or the electric motor catching fire or lithium battery exploding as a result. I just called this in to your 800-860-4050 # (Refer to Customer # [REDACTED]) and your representative told me to take it to a repair center in Somerville or Bound Brook be repaired. That is not acceptable! For the same reasons as you'll see below with your other recall, I demand a replacement; or a full refund for our cost of the blower, the 2 lithium batteries, and the battery charger. 
I checked in April or May and this unit was NOT of the Model # or in the range of serial #s of blowers being recalled. See Recall Date: March 2, 2017, Recall Number: [REDACTED], One World Technologies Recalls Electric Blowers Due to Laceration Hazard. But I now see that they were being recalled for the same defect.

"Hazard: The plastic fan inside the blower can break causing the fan blades to be discharged from either end of the blower tube, posing a laceration hazard. 
Remedy: Replace 
Consumers should immediately stop using the recalled electric blowers and contact One World Technologies, Inc. for a free replacement." 
[REDACTED]



Please confirm to me though your Safety Department whether I am to receive a replacement leaf blower or a refund; and how this leaf blower product defect is being addressed.

Thank you. 
[REDACTED]

_______________________________

Because this defect has already caused personal injuries in their electric cord model of the exact same design,  and because I’m receiving no response, I have called Ryobi numerous times only to be told by their Customer Service people that my complaint is at the Products Safety Department in a stack of complaints and will be tended to on an “as received basis which should be in 10 to 14 business days”.  They refused to escalate it nor allow me to talk to anyone in their Safety Department.  This is irresponsible and outrageous.  I ask that you folks contact them and request that they recall this product before more people get injured.  

Thank you.

productDescription: Krups Expresso Machine XP1000
incidentDescription:
On Sat Sept 16, 2017 I attached the filter holder to a Krup XP 1000 expresso maker but did not rotate it firmly into the locking position -- perhaps 10% short of the normal locked position. I used a finely ground Columbian coffee that I tamped down about 3/4 full. The coffee came out without a problem and was almost finished, just bubbles coming out, when there was a loud explosion. Boiling coffee and glass shards were sent flying in every direction including over me and my wife. Luckily I had just turned my back to get a coffee cup, and both of us were wearing long sleeves and pants. Neither of us were injured. The filter holder had blown out of the coffee maker straight down onto the carafe shattering it. If I had been standing watching/waiting as I normally do it is likely that I would have been seriously injured. Coffee was all over the 8 foot ceiling. I would strongly suggest that you put a VERY STRONG WARNING about the need to make sure that the filter holder is rotated as far as it can go. I have used this machine for 2 years without incident and tested it again after the explosion and it works fine. But older people might not have the arm strength to push the filter holder into the proper position or might just be lazy like me and not notice that it was not rotated into position before turning on the machine. 

So Krups knew about this problem in 1994 but still haven’t corrected it…. weird. There is no warning or instruction regarding this potential problem in the manual and I nearly lost an eye.... they should be punished.

https://www.cpsc.gov/Recalls/1994/cpsc-and-krups-announce-action-on-espresso-makers

productDescription:
Dirt Devil bagless upright vacuum
ModelUD70212
MFG Code K16AEU
manufacturer: Royal Appliance Mfg Co business as TTI Floor Care N. Am.
incidentDescription:
I purchased an upright vacuum cleaner online from Dirtdevil.com on 4/22/17.
It was brand new, not reconditioned.
I had it for 4 months, and soon after using it , it seemed like it was getting harder to push.
And then one of the wheels kept falling off.
To make matters worse, I was vacuuming up slivers of my vacuuming.
It was falling apart as I was using it.
So far, this is not your concern, until now.
I was really curious as to what was going on with my brand new vac, so I investigated further.
On my model, the motor housing sits very low to the ground, almost touching the ground.
The main wheel assembly is located too close to the motor housing.
If you run the motor for about 45 minutes, the housing gets so hot you can hardly touch it.
Bad enough that the motor is already almost touching the ground, but now the heat of the motor softened the plastic assembly that holds the main wheels.
Because the plastic has been softened due to the heat, the wheels tilt inwards like a car when it has Toe In.
The Toe In puts excessive wear on the contact surfaces between the wheels and the main body.
On one side, it looks brand new. 
On the other side, it is almost worn away.
This is a very dangerious situation for several reasons:
-the motor gets extremely hot. Is there no thermal cut-off
-the motor sits too close to the groung. Being so hot, this is very unsafe.
-after a few uses, the wheels develop Toe In, and now the motor actually scrapes the carpet.
TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE
Not to mention that the vacuum is tottaly useless with the motor scraping the ground and the eheel falling off.
All this from a 4 month old vacuum.
I contacted Dirt Devil and described the problem in great detail.
It fell on deaf ears.
They told me to take it to an autherized repair shop, which I did. All Brands vacuum in Lyndhurst Ohio.
They will not honor the warranty, they said it was just cosmetic, I believe.
Cosmetic? With a wheel falling off, and a very hot motor dragging on the ground?
I don't think so.
I was just going to toss it in the dumpster, and chock it up to poor business practices.
But I don't want to see somebody get hurt, or a fire start because of this.
I asked Dirt Devil if I was the only one complaining about this. She skirted the issue.
Its time for a recall.
They have a fee models where the motor is like mine. I bet they all have the same problem.

productDescription: The blender came with two containers for blending, chopping, and mixing – a large “Pitcher” and a small “Bowl.” Each container had its own blades and its own “Splash Guard.” An interchangeable “Master Pod” powers the blender in either configuration when users press the on/off pulse button. The Pitcher assembly includes an interlock system that prevents Master Pod activation unless the Splash Guard is affixed securely to the Pitcher, effectively shielding the spinning blades from user contact. Inexplicably, the Bowl assembly does not have any similar safety system. (See uploaded User Guide.)
incidentDescription:
On December 15, 2013, my client, 32-year-old [REDACTED], suffered serious injuries while operating a newly purchased Ninja™ Master Prep™ Professional blender in the kitchen of the apartment she shared with her husband [REDACTED], and 16-month-old son [REDACTED]. [REDACTED] bought the blender approximately two weeks before [REDACTED]’s injury. Before her injury,[REDACTED] had never used the blender.
 	
The blender came with two containers for blending, chopping, and mixing – a large “Pitcher” and a small “Bowl.” Each container had its own blades and its own “Splash Guard.” An interchangeable “Master Pod” powers the blender in either configuration when users press the on/off pulse button. (See uploaded User Guide.)

The Pitcher assembly includes an interlock system that prevents Master Pod activation unless the Splash Guard is affixed securely to the Pitcher, effectively shielding the spinning blades from user contact.

Inexplicably, the Bowl assembly does not have any similar safety system. 

If an inexperienced user attempting to assemble the blender in its Bowl configuration inadvertently presses the on/off pulse button after inserting the blades through the Bowl Splash Guard into the Master Pod, the exposed blades will activate, inflicting serious injuries.

Shortly before noon, [REDACTED] was attempting to feed [REDACTED], who was particularly fussy that morning. He was crying inconsolably; he would not eat his minestrone soup. She had an idea that if she pureed the soup’s vegetables and pasta, [REDACTED] might be more inclined to eat his lunch. She decided to try this using the new Ninja blender.

She retrieved the blender components from the counter, poured [REDACTED]’s soup in the blender Bowl, and attempted to put together the blades, Splash Guard, and Master Pod to complete the assembly.

She must have inadvertently pressed the on/off pulse button on the Master Pod, because suddenly, without warning, the exposed blades started spinning in her hand, inflicting severe laceration injuries to her right hand, index finger and middle finger.

[REDACTED] contends the blender was defective primarily because the blender Bowl configuration did not have an interlock system – like the Pitcher configuration – to prevent the exposed blades from spinning and inflicting injury when a user inadvertently presses on/off pulse button.

productDescription: Cuisinart CPK-17 PerfecTemp 1.7-Liter Stainless Steel Cordless Electric Kettle
incidentDescription:
The appliance in question is a Cuisinart CPK-17 PerfecTemp 1.7-Liter Stainless Steel Cordless Electric Kettle which we received as a gift in December, 2015. It has been used at least 4 times per day and almost every day since that time. The unit has an electronic temperature control module which operates a relay in the base of the unit — when operating properly, you can hear the relay click each time the controller wants power to be applied to or removed from the heating element.

For the last couple of months and with increasing frequency, the relay in our unit will get stuck in the "on" position. Regardless of the selected temperature setpoint, the unit will then heat to a boil, and if left unattended would boil dry. The controller has electronic "boil-dry protection," but if the controller cannot power down the heating element to prevent exceeding the temperature setpoint, neither can the controller power down the heating element to prevent meltdown and potential ignition of the plastic base after boiling dry. IMHO, this "stuck" condition therefore presents a fire hazard.

Cuisinart warrants this product for three years, BUT discourages warranty claims by requiring the customer to pay not only actual shipping cost to return the defective product, but also a fixed (and probably excessive) charge for shipping the replacement to the customer.

productDescription: Hot Headz Products hand held Cool Downz Personal Water Mister, red and clear plastic.  Pump on the bottom, water nozzle on the top.
incidentDescription:
We purchased the Hot Headz Personal Water Mister on 6/25/17.  We used the mister that day.  During the night, the mister was placed on the nightstand and exploded.  After a loud noise, shards of jagged plastic flew all over the room and bounced off the walls.  I have a photograph of the pieces.  Prior to the explosion, it had been a few hours since the mister was used or touched.  

The mister works by pumping the device to cause pressure, and then pressing the button releases a fine mist.  The product worked throughout the afternoon.  No one was hurt, but someone definitely could have been.  

I have photos of the plastic shards and the packaging labels, but am unable to upload to this report.

We still have the unit, and will keep it until we hear from you or the company,

productDescription: This was the stock phone charger adapter and cable that shipped with the phone. The actual damage was to the adapter.
incidentDescription:
Normally I will charge my cell phone completely in the evening, and unplug it overnight (so the battery doesn't get overcharged). In the morning while getting ready, I will "top off" the charge so the phone is at 100% when I leave. 

While traveling in March, I had charged my phone fully in the evening, and in the morning when I went to top it off, I noticed that there was significant melting to the power adapter. As this was an obvious fire hazard, I did not attempt to connect and charge the phone in the morning. 

I attempted to contact LG the next morning, and as this has still not been resolved (more than a month later) am I bringing it to the CPSC. 

The phone was less than a month old at the time of incident and there were no signs of damage to the charger when I used it the night before (when the incident occurred). 

I double checked the voltages on the adapter (as I was traveling) before using it, and it does indeed say it can tolerate 110 - 240v.

productDescription: White Breville toaster- 1510
incidentDescription:
We own two Breville toasters (model 1510, BTA630XL) and both of them have the same defect: on an inconsistent basis, when the toaster is ready to lift up the toasted bread, the grids lock up and the toaster begins re-heating at maximum power. The only way to get the toast out after unplugging the unit is to take a pair of tongs and force the grids open. The grids then snap right back together. Fortunately, no one has been injured and a fire has been avoided because we have been standing there and have intervened. 

This has happened with both toasters on several occasions and presents a fire hazard.  I have looked for recalls on this product and haven't found any but we can't be the only people with this problem. I have notified the company via email and have had no response from them.

Thank you.

(The incident date below is the latest---it has happened numerous times at both residences: our home and our vacation condo. The condo is located at [REDACTED]. The address below is our permanent address).

productDescription: 40 volt cordless dual-blade mower
productSubCategory: Lawn Mowers, Leaf Blowers and Lawn Vacuums
incidentDescription:
On 5/23/17 we had a fire at our house caused by a Kobalt Electric Lawn Mower. There were no flames per se but some heat and lots of acidic smoke/soot. The soot contaminated our entire house. 

The Fire Forensic Investigator ([REDACTED]) has determined that we were not at fault in any way. The mower was not on a charger (physically impossible) and had been setting unused in the garage for several days when the fire started. Additionally, the Investigator showed that Kobalt had issued a Consumer Safety Recall just the day before for this model mower because it had been deemed a “Fire Hazard.”

As a result of the fire we have had to vacate our home since the fire and a restoration company is currently working to clean our home and our belongings. Because the soot/smoke was acidic, may of our items are being deposed.

productDescription: Lasko ceramic oscillating space heater, tower-style, model 5362
incidentDescription:
I have a ceramic oscillating space heater by Lasko, model 5362.
There is a recall already for this model number due to cords overheating but Lasko says my unit isn't included in the recall (I have exact same included model number but they say mine was manufactured 2006 and affected units were manufactured in 2005).
My unit power cord had apparently overheated an unknown number of times causing the outer covering of the power cord to disappear/burn away, exposing the metal wiring inside the power cord. This has caused the metal to spark and arc wildly when the cord was moved, which caused slight burns to the carpeting it was sitting on as well as my hands/fingers when I attempted to move the unit to unplug it.
The unit overheated where the plug enters the base of the housing/grommet.
The unit has not been damaged due to abuse or misuse.
This unit *should be included* in the recall regardless if it was manufactured 2005 or 2006 as my unit OBVIOUSLY has the same issue that prompted the recall.
I was told by Lasko to stop using it and throw it away and buy a new one  (I personally believe they just do not want to cover this one with a free replacement even though it is the same model number as the recall with the same issues).
I have photos showing charred metal of the wiring/power cord but am unable to upload as I'm on mobile device (Note 5)... I can send via email or upload to file sharing website and share link(s) if needed.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

incidentDescription:
The product is the Evaco Whistling Kettle No. 20020-B.
Company address: Evaco, 285 Bel Marin Keys Blvd, Unite C, Novato, CA 94949-5763
800-7822738. Email: evacoimp@aol.com
The warranty for this tea kettle does not cover kettles boiled dry or subjected to excessive heat.

On Sunday, May 21, 2017 I boiled dry our tea kettle dry over excessive heat, both things that should not have happened. 
1) I had the heat too high
2) the whistle did not go off alerting me that the water was boiling.

Unfortunately, a flaw to these tea kettles (this is the second one I have owned) is that the whistle will not work unless the lid to the teapot is fitted snugly down on top of the kettle.

Because a recent guest had most likely taken the lid of the teapot off, there was not an adequate seal to have the whistle go off.

I picked up the tea kettle from the electric burner, noted that there was no water in it, and turned toward the middle of the kitchen. The bottom fell off the tea kettle, and layers of molten metal (tin?) hit the floor and splashed in small to 2" globs all about the floor of the kitchen, an approximate 6' radius. The hardwood floor in the kitchen burned underneath the molten metal.

Luckily one one splash landed on me which gave me a severe burn.

Even though I used the tea kettle as directions said not to by using excessive heat, it's a tea kettle and situations like mine are bound to happen because the whole point of a tea kettle is to put it on heat and boil water.

A better warning should be made to consumers, such as: Excessive heat will cause the bottom to fall off and molten metal will splash down causing possible physical burns and fires as a result.

Please have this company produce a safer Whistling Kettle, fix the flawed lid which stops the tea kettle from whistling, and issue warnings to what will happen is the tea kettle is overheated.

productDescription:
We bought a fan about 5 years ago that has been very problematic and downright dangerous.  The # is 0711569 and the UPC code is 082392247553.  We mounted this ceiling fan in our sunroom and about 2 years ago we found spackle on the coffee table and then looked up and saw that the fan was hanging by its electrical cords!   If that had fallen on someone it could have killed them or broken a neck.  At the very least it could have fallen on our glass coffee table in the middle of the night and given us all a good scare!  The problem is the mounting bracket.  It is open on one end and the post and spacer "wiggle" out of it over time.  All ceiling fans have to have some play to accommodate their natural wiggling.  We fixed it only to have it happen again a couple weeks ago.  Luckily my husband reinforced it with a metal chain if it happened again so no one would get hurt.  

 

This fan needs to be recalled, seriously.  It has the potential to be deadly.  I did contact Hampton Bay 2 times with their promise to get back to me and that has not happened.

incidentDescription:
I purchased a Char-broil Bistro Gas Grill from Amazon (model number 15601900) about a month ago and in that short time of using it, the grill has simply had the burner flame go out by itself, on full head setting at least three times now. 
The item instructs that user to pre-heat it at least 5 minutes before use, and so I go out and light it as the instructions tell, but turning it to light position and pushing the electronic ignition until I hear the burner light (on this grill, one cannot see the burner flame, so all I can go on is the sound and the feeling of heat being produced). I then go inside to prepare the food that is to go on the grill. I come back out and the first two times, it was obvious as the temp meter had not moved. I turned it off, opened the grill to air out the gas that had built up (yes, the gas is still coming out when the burner flame has stopped), and then I do the procedure again and wait.
The third time, it had apparently heated up some and then went out (again...the temp knob is set to the hottest setting)...so I did not notice that the flame had gone out. I opened the lid and must have caused a spark, because the grill top flew out of my hand and opened with a loud explosion and blew me backwards away from the grill. I did not notice that I had all the hair on my right arm sindged off up to my shoulder and that my watch has been been burned on the strap and had melted into my skin. 
This thing is a danger and should be recalled and fixed. I love the grill, it is the perfect size for us and cooks everything well ..but i afraid to use it.

productDescription:
Silver on the top, and black on the bottom.
Intended to be used with LP Gas
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
On 4/13/17 at 01:45 hours, a structure fire was reported at the location provided.  The fire was limited to a Char-Broil gas BBQ, and I was requested to investigate the origin and cause the following day.

BBQ Information:
Char-Broil, LLC
Model # 463633316
SN # G361011602010083

The owners purchased the BBQ in October of 2016 from Walmart for about $100. The owners had used the BBQ about 7 hours prior to the fire.  The BBQ reached 550 degrees or more before it was turned down by shutting off the right burner and leaving the left burner on. The food (fish in a marinade that included oil) was cooked once the BBQ reached around 350 degrees.The BBQ was in like new condition, and this was the first use, or one of the first uses. The owners turned off the BBQ after cooking (which was verified through observation during the investigation), but did not turn the LP cylinder valve off.  

I conducted an origin and cause investigation, and observed the following:
- Based on observed damage, patterns and indicators, it appears that the fire originated at or below the heat shield, which is below the fire box (where the food is cooked).  It also appears that the fire originated somewhere along the hose between the regulator valve and the connection to the assembly that connects to the main burners, and probably occurred where the hose was touching or near the heat shield or cart side frame.  Fragments of the hose and melted plastic and aluminum were discovered on the bottom shelf that holds the LP cylinder. Burn patterns indicate that the greatest damage occurred along the hose near the front left corner of the BBQ.  

Based on the timeline of the fire, the probable cause of the fire was overheating of the hose initiating smoldering combustion that eventually caused the hose to be compromised and allowed LP gas to escape.  It is probable that the smoldering combustion was the ignition source for the diffuse fuel of LP gas and air.  Since the LP Gas container was on, there was a supply of fuel for the fire.

Although turning the LP cylinder valve off would have caused the fire to not continue, there still appears to be a potential safety concern of conductive or convective heat igniting the hose.

I called the company and spoke to a [REDACTED] who in turn put me in touch with [REDACTED]. We spoke twice on the phone, first time she was very nice and asked lots of questions. Second time she had a very bad attitude and tried to deny that the curler was one of their products. I sent lots of pictures of my eyelashes and the curler at her request. She did email back and stated that they did identify the curler was "similar" to theirs from the photos I sent. She asked me to send the curler and pads to them for further investigation. I responded and said I wanted to consult with my attorney for advice as I did not want to send off my curler and have nothing to show causing the injury. Immediately she responded and wanted no further contact with me and said to deal with it through their legal department. I emailed her twice stating I was not retaining an attorney, just wanted to know the best way to cover myself prior to sending off the implement. Still I was faced with NO customer service. This is where I am at this time. Yes it cut chunks out of both eyelashes and thank GOD there was no injury to the skin of my eyelids, but that certainly could have happened. I have had to purchase special hair growth liquid to put on my eyelashes to help grow them out. This just scares me that it could have been much worse and how many other people this could or has happend to. This curler is junk and should be looked at from your department. I am lucky there was no further damage to my eyes, I can only imagine if I had put the curler closer to my eyelid and what could have happened. I have now consulted with my attorney and he suggested I contact your company first to see what my next step should be or what can be done.

productDescription: Gass Grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
Gas grill issues.

I purchased a charbroil 463268407 grill.  It immediately had burner issues with the 2 TEC glass burners.  I contacted Lowes and was told the unit should not have been sold and had been recalled.  I contacted Charbroil back in about 2008 and had a battle on the phone with them about the safety of the grill.  They sent me 2 burners and offered no help with installation even though it was less than 3 weeks old.  They also sold me several hundred dollars worth of extra parts in case I needed them.  I went back to Lowes a couple of months later and was told there was nothing they could do.

Finally in 2014, push came to shove and Lowes sent somebody out to repair the grill one again for the burner issues.  Last summer, I could not turn the gas valves (I have used under 3 tanks of propane at this point) and was told the heat from the burners backfiring has caused the valves internally to expand and seize up.

I contacted Lowes who looked up the item number and transferred me to Charbroil.  I explained everything to them (3 different people) and finally spoke with a manager who treated me like I wanted something for nothing.  Safety is very important to me and was willing to ship unit or parts back to them so they could see who the gas valve seized.  I live in Texas so major cold or rust is not an issue.  He would hear nothing except to say he would send new burners and I would have to buy the other repair parts.  He then eluded to a 75.00 trade in for a 1000.00 plus grill.  I purchased the best grill that was on the market and have had issue after issue with it.  The customer rep when I told him I was disabled, said can't your wife fix it?  I explained that working with propane is something that an inexperienced person should not "mess" with.

For the record, I can afford to buy any grill I want to.  As with my customers, they expect to get their moneys worth.  I am reporting this on the safety aspect and not the financial.  Charbroil automatically thinks you are out for something for free.

You need to investigate the replacement burners and the gas valves due to fatigue and heat stress.

productDescription: Defective product is a kitchen blender sold in various configurations including Auto-IQ 1500 watts.
incidentDescription:
This kitchen blender has a hollow pitcher handle with an opening at the top into which food migrates during blending. The handle isn’t user-openable, so the lodged food remains inside, rots, and molds. When the blender is used again the food inside the top of the handle can then remigrate into new food that is blended, introducing contaminants into mixture. The manufacturer sent me a replacement pitcher, but the same thing happened during the first usage. 

I spoke to the company’s customer service today and they acknowledged that the pitcher had been redesigned in a newer version of the product so that the handle no longer has the opening, but the unsafe product is still being sold at Costco and other retailers, and many thousands of the defective product have been sold.

productDescription: Keurig 2.0
incidentDescription:
This report is regarding a recent model Keurig 2.0 coffee maker product.

The design of the Keurig 2.0 coffee maker involves two thin hollow metal tubes that water passes in and out of the kcup through. These tubes have a tendency to clog resulting in building pressure inside the kcup. When the pressure reaches to great of force, the coffee maker begins spraying scolding water and scolding coffee grounds out all sides, several feet in distance. 

In my case, no injuries resulting however had I been standing next to the product it would have resulted in burns.

I have followed all cleaning instructions, never used off brand kcup items in the brewer, nor has the machine ever been misused. A quick check of the web reveals this is well known problem with other consumers having been burned.

productDescription: Cuisinart Mini Prep Food Processing Machine
incidentDescription:
I own 3 Cuisinart food processing machines.  One is subject to the recall and I had ordered the new blade through the established process.
The other 2 machines are not covered by the recall but also exhibit unsafe conditions with the blades. A 4 year old Cuisinart Mini Prep DCL 3 ACHC has a blade encased in plastic with no rivets.  The plastic is cracked, the metal blade is partially sticking out of alignment from the plastic and bits of plastic and metal are missing.
A 2 year old Cuisinart [REDACTED] has a blade encased in plastic with no rivets.  The plastic is cracked and a bit of plastic is missing.
The instructions for each machine do not state that the blades must be inspected before and after each use to be sure customers don't ingest bits of plastic and metal.  Meals are not often prepared in our home and the machines are used only 3 or 4 times a year, at holiday gatherings or family events like graduations.  We are careful to follow instructions on use and cleaning of all of our appliances.
I first tried to report this unsafe situation to the recall line at 877-339-2534.  They referred me to the company general customer service dept at 800-726-0190 and the representative was not at all concerned that there were unsafe products.  Her only interest was that I understood that I could buy a new blade, but because the machines are past the one year warranty and not covered by the recall there was not any other option.  I tried a second time to warn that customers need to know they can also be hurt by blades not covered by the recall, and there was no interest.  I asked for a supervisor and was told no supervisors were available.
I plan to discard all 3 machines as I am appalled by the lack of quality and the lack of concern in how the unsafe blades are being handled by Cuisinart.  I will retain them for a short while in the event you would like to examine the problem blades.

incidentDescription: We recieved a Self-balancing Hoverboard for my oldest daughter  from her Grandmother on 02/23/17  that she had purchased for my daughter's birthday in November of 2015 from Overstock.com. We set it up for my daughter to charge it next to her bed while she watched her bedtime movie. I tucked her in as always and sang her the bedtime song and made my way to my room. With the exhaustion of my daughters birthday I fell fast asleep. An hour or so later I was awoke by a heart stopping scream comimg from my daughters room! I run to her room and as I approached I see not only this hover board shooting sparks and on fire but my daughter's Trundle bed catching fire as well! I immediately grab my terrified daughter and take her to our room to mom and then run to the kitchen where we keep our fire extinguisher and return to my daughter's room and extinguish the hoverboard and the bed and mattress. Luckily my precious little girl was not injured and it was just material items! But what if we didnt wake ? None of us would be here! Its terrifying to know first hand that products are being released without proper testing that could actually "KILL" or badly injure a child or whole family. Although they are just material items and most importantly my daughter wasnt harmed we would like full compensation for said items! The hover-board $450.00 , Trundle bed $850.00, The dual [REDACTED] matresses $700, and Her [REDACTED] comforter set $169.99 for a total of $2,169.99.

productDescription: Retro Versal/Retro Bit Universal 3 in 1 AC Adapter NES/SNES/GENESIS used to power the Nintendo Entertainment System (NES), Super Nintendo Entertainment System (SNES), and Sega Genesis Model 1.  This power supply only supplies 9V DC, 350mA, which is insufficient.
incidentDescription:
A company called Retro-Bit (http://retro-bit.com/) is marketing and selling a transformer power supply for electronic game systems.  It is called the Retro Versal/RETRO BIT UNIVERSAL 3 in 1 AC ADAPTER FOR NES /SNES /GENESIS 1.  The model/PN is: RB-UNI-1361.  This power supply is specified to output DC 9V/350MA.  They can be found on Amazon at this link: https://www.amazon.com/Universal-Adapter-GENESIS-Nintendo-Entertainment-System/dp/B001S2VT6I 
and elsewhere.

The company advertises this power supply for sale to use with the Nintendo Entertainment System (NES), the Super Nintendo Entertainment System (SNES), and the Sega Genesis Model 1, all classic game systems.  The issue is that the NES and SNES, per their specifications pull 850mA of current.  The Genesis Model 1 pulls 1.2A (1200mA) of current.  When using these Retro-Bit power supplies they get very hot, probably due to the fact the power supplies are not designed to source more than 350mA of current.  An original NES power supply was specified to output 1.8A (1800mA), well above the NES's power requirements.  This Retro-Bit model is incapable of supplying even the bare minimum.  I am aware of no incidents of fire or injury.  But, I believe it is unsafe to use these power supplies in the manner in which they are advertised, due to the heat generated and the risk of fire.

productDescription: Outdoor gas firepit
incidentDescription: I ordered a BlueRhino outdoor gas firepit from Wells Fargo Rewards Catalog that is fueled by a propane tank. I assembled it exactly as instructed and used it right away. The instructions state to turn off the gas on the tank when finished. I attempted to do so but the tank knob was extremely hot due to the firepit. After letting it cool, I finally was able to turn the gas off. The next time I used this product, the flame went out. After trying to re-light it without success, I looked below in the cabinet where the tank is stored and i noticed that the rubber supply line going to the burners had melted to the bottom of the fire pan. This caused a kink in the line thus no gas could get to the burner. I then called Rhino and was told that the heat shield may have not been working properly so they sent me an entire new burner and register with pan. Again, I installed it as instructed and it worked fine for the first couple of times. On the third time I used it, the burner once again went out. I immediately looked below at the tank and once again the gas supply line melted to the bottom of the pan. Also, the tank was extremely hot to the touch. This is an extremely dangerous item and I was concerned that it could have blown up. I called Rhino once again and they refused to do anything stating to me that i would need to purchase a new register and pan. This product is extremely dangerous and i had no interest in purchasing anything additional for this unsafe product. I also have pictures to back up my claim

productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
I bought a Char-Broil grill and set it up.  This is a tabletop model with Model # 465133005 which is sold at both Lowes and Ace Hardware in different boxes .  Here is my video on youtube.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UqIMf5tsOpw


Here is Char-Broil's response to my complaint.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------  
Thank you for contacting Char-Broil. 

We apologize for the issues you've had with these tabletop grills. You are a valued Char-Broil customer and we want you to not only enjoy using our products, but feel safe while doing so. Fortunately, this is something that can easily be corrected, and we would be happy to help you with this. After reviewing your video, the reason you are getting turbulence in the burner's venturi tube is because the propane bottle is not flush with the unit and has no support. The grill will either need to be steadied in a way that the bottle lines up with the unit, or we recommend placing something underneath the LP bottle to support it and even out the connection.

If you have any questions or encounter any further issues, please give us a call at the number below and we will be able to best assist.

We appreciate your business.  If you have any further questions you may contact us by either visiting www.charbroil.com or by phone at 1-800-241-7548.  Our hours of operation are Monday through Friday 8am to 6pm EST, and 9am to 3pm EST on Saturday.

Sincerely,

[REDACTED]
Char-Broil Grill Service Specialist

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
I got a 2nd email directly after this one that with none in between that states case closed.

The video may not convey the flushness of their brass fitting but I have tried this grill with 2 different valves  and have pressed the brass fitting all the way in which is held in only by a dimple on the burner and a slot on the brass to allow it to go in.  The design of this fitting and the dimple is so loose that it can be either pulled out or fall out without the slot in the brass fitting aligning with the detente dimple.   This horrendous design while it back feeds and ignites in what Char-Broil refers to as a venturi the square hole which makes a rushing sound when it is ignited there can also actually light the valve outlet of the propane on fire too when the valve slides out entirely from the dimpled burner.  At that point you have short barrelled propane torch in your hand or its rolling around on the ground.  I returned both grills to Lowes 2 days ago as I was sick of the problem.  I was lucky they gave me store credit.  They were bought from different lots too.  It doesn't matter which position you attempt to put the brass fitting in as I tried placing it further out and further in completely flush and have the bottle up right or to front or back and this problem continues.  There is no magical flush position to stop this backflow ignition of the gas into the venturi.  What I call a air mixing bleed hole which is square.  The video was taken about 6:30 AM in the morning as the light was coming up to be able to see this burning problem not seen in the daylight hours.  

Here is a similar review on amazon about its behavior.


2) The dealbreaker: the grill kept "backflashing". This means that the flame would jump from outside the gas delivery tube (think the "spider legs", where they're supposed to be) to INSIDE the gas delivery tube. When this happened, there would be an initial flash backwards, towards the regulator/dial/fuel canister. Not safe. Then, you would hear a high pitched sound like a jet engine and the flame would be burning inside the tube. The instructions say this can happen if a spider spins a web inside the tube creating an obstruction to the flow of gas, but this happened to me right out of the box. This doesn't seem safe and I think eventually the gas delivery tube will fail, or the regulator will fail, because neither are designed to take direct flame.

and another reviewer said

Ok, so I bought this grill last week with plans to take it to a football game and do some tailgaiting. Put the grill together during the week, which was pretty easy, but the grill is CHEAP!! can't expect much for the price. Bought some propane to try out the grill on Saturday morning and the grill was making a loud hissing noise and I couln't see the flames. Tried several more times to get the grill lit without the hissing noise and was unsuccesful. Finally decided to call Charbroil and was told the grill is defective and they will send me out a new one. Have spent the last 3 days back and forth with Charbroil, getting the run around, ridiculous. If I do ever get my replacement I'll probably just give it away because this thing is a piece of crap. I'd return it but tossed the box and don't feel like deeling with repacking for the $20 refund. What a joke, do not buy.
 
and another reviewer said

We bought this grill for a camping trip. We built it on site. Overtime we tried to make it work it would make loud blowing noises; flare sounds like the gas would light all at once and then stop. It was simply a frightening experience. We called the help number, we tried everything they said and still nothing worked. I called them again explain the situation and they narrowed the problem down to the regulator. They said they were going to send us a new regulator within the week. We were hungry and angry and found other ways to cook our food for the weekend of our camping trip.They sent us a new regulator a week later but that still did not work. Even new propane tanks didn't make it work. This is the worst grill I could have ever purchased, and I feel lucky it didn’t blow up in our faces.

and another under 2 star reviews mentions

The back-flame issue others mention is clearly a design flaw. My grill did it within seconds of being lit, does it every few minutes, and does it about every other time I lift the lid. A quick puff of air on the gas tube usually clears it out, but that leads to the next problem... This thing blows out way too easily. I can't imagine trying to use it in a windy place - it sometimes goes out just taking the lid on and off. I bet I could make it back-flame or go out just by thinking about it.


and another
It also has a habit of randomly making loud jet blaster noises whilst grilling.


and another

When we used this we kept getting flare ups near the neck of the gas bottle.

and another

On our last outing, about 12 uses, the regulator valve got very hard to turn, and wouldnt press in. After looking at it a few days later, the knob broke off... I can see fire in the little hole next to it where the air gets mixed...

and another

The grill is a nice design, but the quality control stinks. I must have a bad burner, because the flame sometimes goes inside the burner. I can tell because it gets much louder and puts out less heat. If I cover the air intake holes with an oven mitt, it starves the inside of air, and I get a bright orange flame on the outside of the burner; then I uncover the holes and it goes back to a normal blue flame. This happens fairly often at random times, so I can't use the grill for roasting or anything like that. For steaks and burgers I just stay at the grill and babysit the entire time they're cooking.

In addition to my experience many of the reviews mention experiences with a valve (regulator) that was broken or would not stop leaking or delivering gas at what seemed full on status.  They had experiences with no being able to shut the valve (regulator) off.  If you combine the feature (flaw) mine has where the actual fire will go all the way back to the regulator and it comes lose from the burner as in the short barrelled torch I mentioned with the feature (flaw) of not being to turn off the regulator how would it take until the either the cheaply designed valve(regulator) melts or heats up the bottle or leads to something worse if they haven't screwed the bottle on tight enough. 

I just wonder how anyone is allowed to import such trash as this grill and sell it here and then claim it has not problem its ,"the reason you are getting turbulence in the burner's venturi tube is because the propane bottle is not flush with the unit and has no support." , when they built the thing with no support for the bottle other than the valve sitting in the burner with a small dimple which doesn't hold it flush anyway.  This not a scew on connection and various types of past similar designs included a clip to hold this regulator in place.  These are not designed to have the bottle held by anything ever.  The best brand Weber expects one to use the grill in such a manner.  This the difference between buying one that costs 2 to 3 times as much as a cheap Chinese designed and built knock off.  Its barely even that.

incidentDescription: January 22nd 2015, I was preparing beef stew in a Farberware  7-N-1 Pressure Cooker that I purchased from Walmart, manufactured by Midea. I then ensured the pressure release valve was positioned according to the included directions to release the all the steam from the beef stew that had been cooking. The reason I purchased this pressure cooker over the various others was the lid lock safety feature, in which the lid automatically unlocks only after all the extremely hot steam and intense pressure has been removed from cooker through an exhaust valve. Once this was complete, I went to remove the unlocked lid and the scalding hot content exploded onto my body severely burning my chest, stomach, hand, and tip of nose. I felt a searing pain to the skin on my nose, left thigh, chest, stomach, and left hand and I instinctively and immediately removed my clothing containing the scalding hot contents only to find the skin on my body had been violently burned away. This is a dangerous and defective product that is not safe. It caused me 2nd and third degree burns on my body and I am now left with ugly scars for life!

productDescription: Power Cooker Plus, Tristar Products, Inc., Model PPC780P
incidentDescription: Pressure cooker malfunction resulting in injury.  At approximately 5:50pm, I was cooking dinner in the Power Cooker Plus (Tristar) pressure cooker.  I have used it many times and I am very familiar with pressure cooker usage.  When the meal was done, I manually released the pressure using the valve.  Believing the pressure to be fully released, I attempted to turn the lid.  The lid is advertised as a safety lid that should not turn if there is any pressure.  However, the lid did turn and, as it did, the scalding hot contents of the pot erupted and shot out of the pressure cooker.  I saw another consumer say this effect was similar to a volcanic eruption.  That is the best description I can find.   Food was everywhere and I was hit in the stomach with scalding hot fluid.  I was burned with blistering 2nd degree burns across my abdomen even through 2 layers of clothing. My burns are significant, as are the accompanying blisters, with incredible pain.   At the very least, the safety lid malfunctioned.  It turned and open easily, despite the fact that the contents were obviously under pressure.  This is an unreasonably dangerous product.  (Note: I have pictures of the unit and the injuries, but I am having trouble with the photo uploader on this site).  Date of purchase provided is an estimate.  I bought it in the past year.

Energizer 2X Smart Charger 048-052-NA

Energizer® XBOX ONE 2X Smart Chargers used to charge XBOX ONE video game controllers. The chargers are black plastic and measure about 3.5 inches long, 5 inches wide and 11 inches tall.  “Energizer®” is printed on the charger’s label. Item number 048-052-NA is printed on the bottom of the chargers. The chargers hold up to two XBOX controllers.
incidentDescription:
Energizer 2X Smart Charger 048-052-NA:

Had product for approximately six months and product operated normally. One day we noticed one of the batteries was staying at approximately 15% charge even after several hours on the charger. I picked up the controller and immediately noticed a "hot electronics" smell. I opened the battery cover and the smell became intense. I burned my fingers attempting to remove the battery from the controller, which was difficult as the battery had begun bulging. I instituted thermal runaway procedures and immersed the battery in a bucket of water and baking soda until it cooled, then disposed of it normally.

Approximately two weeks later, the process repeated with the other battery. I again removed the battery from the controller and immersed it to cool it down, disposing the battery afterward.

There were no serious injuries from the incidents, though had the batteries ruptured or caught fire the damage could've been much worse.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

incidentDescription:
To Whom it May Concern:

Hello. I own a Ninja BL660 blender device. All seemingly was going well, until I poured the beverage into my glass, using my right hand to pour, and my left hand middle finger was lacerated by the nonfound warning extremely dangerous and falling out spiraling blade. The end of the finger was literally almost cut into, and in my hysterics, my boyfriend tried to stop the bleeding to no avail. I was inconsolable, and he commenced to drive me to our emergent care office at that time. It was approximately 5:20PM, on a Sunday mind you, and after my finger literally Pushing Blood out profusely allover our home, we arrived at the center and they were closed. At this point just by sitting down and calmly getting myself together and off my feet, the bleeding subsided and we decide not to head to the local hospital emergency room, as we are small business owners in the [REDACTED] area, and opted for a trip to our local pharmacy for liquid bandage adhesive and more products, and carried back home to clean up. 

I work with my hands Every Day, to provide for my family and pay my bills. I do computer hardware repair, and this literally put me down for a solid week, albeit my left hand.

Just Tonight, Again, a month later after being scared half to death by this expensive and obviously dangerous product, I thought Id give it one more try, being extremely cautious due to the last round of use. I went to pour my drink into my glass, still painful left hand so my right hand assisted. The blade this time literally dodged out of the blender housing, lacerating my Right Hand ring finger in the same way except way worse. Luckily, since my boyfriend was at work, my 17 year old daughter and her boyfriend were home with me, and helped me in my terrifying panic, blood is everywhere in my house, this time my good working hand. I will send you photos and dates of previous and current injuries, all scarring of the month ago event, bloody napkins, and this monstor device that now resides in my garage until I can have resolve on the issue. 

*Since yet another Sunday, no transportation to get to the emergency room, my hysterical child witness was able to calm me down and stop my bleeding once again. We are presently taking photos of this latest incident for your records.

I have never been a 'consumer complainer', in fact have Never conducted a full on complaint of any sort over a consumer kitchen appliance, but this is utterly ridiculous. And now my good hand, as I Am Right Handed, is out of commission until who knows when. I am requesting a formal complaint and assistance on what to do at this point, other than a lawsuit.

I need someone to contact me immediately, as I have an attorney I have notified and hired to help me with this issue. Im not sure if I need stitches, as every time I try to remove the bandages my distraught daughter helped me with, the laceration begins profusely bleeding again, and she has school tomorrow and I have my local small business to try to run. 

I would appreciate your prompt and immediate attention in this matter.

Thank you,

I quickly realized what was happening and I was able to unplug the unit before it got any worse, I am just thankful that I happened to come back into the kitchen at that very moment. I'm afraid what might have happened had I not been right there when this all started, I went on Amazon which is where I purchased the product and apparently this is a very commonly reported problem. Not even sure how this thing is still being sold. It is a fire hazard and is going to end up killing someone.

productDescription: Hoverboard
incidentDescription:
Dear Counsel:

This letter is to put you on notice of a potential claim regarding a product defect
as it relates to a hoverboard sold through Amazon.com, Inc. "Amazon" by
McFlyBoards.

On November 29,2016, the subject hoverboard exploded, sending flames into
the children's bedroom, causing a massive fire. While, thankfully, there were no physical
injuries, the family's apartment home and virtually all of their possessions were
destroyed in a matter of minutes. The Clark County Fire Department conducted an
investigation and determined that the cause of the fire was due to counterfeit component
parts utilized in the subject hoverboard. This constitutes punitive conduct on the part of
McFlyBoards. As a seller/distributor of McFiyBoards, Amazon bears a portion of
liability for this incident.

We are currently waiting for both the 'apartment complex and the client's home-
owners insurers to complete their investigation. At that time, we will have a better
understanding of the financial. loss suffered by the [REDACTED] family. Once we have a
computation of damages, we will submit a demand for your review.

If you have any questions or concerns, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Sincerely,
[REDACTED]

productDescription: Central heat/air conditioner. 3 TON PKG GAS 15 SEER 90K
productType: Heaters or Heating Systems, Other or Not Specified (393)
incidentDescription:
An apparent small fire started in my outside heat/air conditioning unit that resulted in filling my house with acrid smoke and triggering smoke alarms and the circuit breaker.
The repair man found that the electrical wire connecting the circulation fan to the main circuit shorted when a bare spot in the wire made contact with the metal fan support.  He said it was probably the vibration of the motor over time caused the sharp edged sheet metal to cut through the insulation.
The result was significant burning of wires and plastic in the motor housing.

incidentDescription: Krups FBC4 Toaster Oven will not turn off. incidentDescription:
I ordered an apple MacBook charger on-line through eBay. The charger was listed as a "new genuine original apple MacBook pro charger 85W Magsafe 2 A1424". However after using the charger for a short time, it became extremely hot and actually scorched my son's comforter on his bed. I returned this charger and stated what had happened. There are several comments on this sellers web site complaining of similar situations. It is my concern that if a child were to use this charger in their bed and fall asleep, it could cause a fire or at the very least burn the child. 
The seller is listed as 24hourchargers on the eBay web site and they also have their own web site 24hourchargers.com. They state that they have a 90 money back guarantee but did not honor this with my purchase. However I did receive a refund through my PayPal account after contacting them today. 
This guarantee provides a false sense of safety when ordering the item. This item is not a genuine apple charger and is not approved by Microsoft for use with their computers. It is misleading and could lead to dangerous results if left plugged into the computer for an extended period of time.

productDescription: Toast-R-Oven by Black & Decker
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
model: Only above information available on the unit.
incidentDescription:
On Sunday afternoon on January 29th my brother, [REDACTED], placed food to heat in a Black & Decker countertop over (a Toast-R-Oven) model and about 30 seconds after he turned on the unit fumes poured out the vents and a fire ignited inside. This appliance is several years old. (I think it is about 2 years old, but he believes it is closer to 5 years old so I using his estimated date).  My brother told me he purchased the counter top oven in new condition at a local store in Hastings, Nebraska. He said he cannot recall the name of the retailer right now, but suspects it was Walmart where he frequently shops. I carefully looked over the unit after the incident and could not find a serial number or a UPC code anywhere on the exterior.

I turned off the electricity and turned down the unit. The fire lasted inside the oven for about 3 minutes before dying out.  It was a fire (not a spark) and it blazed inside the product but did not consume the food item. I did not open the door, and fortunately the flames did not spread into the kitchen. However, a noxious odor and smoke permeated the area for several hours. I had contacted Black & Decker's website about 2 weeks earlier when I noticed a lot of smoke coming from the appliance and the heating element growing very white inside. Their customer service online chat/text service had referred me to an online vendor, support@spectrumbrands.com but I had not contacted that email since my brother had resumed using the unit and did not consider it unsafe to use. I had noticed it seemed to emit a smoky odor during use.  I did report the problem to the spectrumbrands email immediately on Sunday but have not yet received a response.

I wanted to contact you now because I am concerned about the safety of the product. The oven quite literally burst into flames in front of me on Sunday afternoon. Fortunately, I did not open the door- if I had, I think we would have had a potentially serious kitchen fire. We have since discontinued using the unit and it is available for technical inspection if desired.

productDescription: Ceiling fan with lights
incidentDescription:
We have a 6 yr old Hunter ceiling fan model 23903.  It has three lights with glass globes.  One of the glass globes fell off hitting our daughter in the head (the fan wasn't even running).  It shattered the bulb as it fell.  We had to pick bulb glass out of her hair.  Thankfully, she wasn't cut by it.

Each globe is held on by a 'globe assembly nut' -- a 2" diameter threaded flange that screws onto the threaded plastic bulb socket while the globe is held in place.  I assumed the nut had come loose.  I found that the nut could be slipped over the threaded light socket with minimal pressure and without turning the nut, as if the threads were stripped, but they weren't.  The nuts on the other two globes are the same way.  I can grab each nut and pull it right off the threaded light socket.  Of course I have no clue about whether they ever fit properly or the nuts had expanded or the plastic light sockets had shrunk.  Appropriate 60W bulbs had been used.

All Hunter fans that I now see have the globes retained by three radial thumb screws.  My guess is that they were all changed to correct the design flaw.  I contacted Hunter regarding a revised light assembly to replace my original one, and they said they don't have any of the newer design that would fit -- though, aside from the thumb screws, they look the same.  Newer model 52044 appears nearly identical.

productDescription: Ninebot One C+.  One wheel electric scooter
incidentDescription:
I ordered a product called a Ninebot One from an ebay seller called myfunwheel.  The ninebot is made by segway and myfunwheel is a U.S. seller.  

Their contact info is

Dion@myfunwheel
293 Washington Dr
Brentwood CA, 94513
1 925 493 0920

The Ninebot One is a single wheel device similar to a hover board except that it has a single wheel.  

While my son was riding this device, it stopped suddenly causing him to be thrown from the machine.  When I looked at the machine, I found that the battery was incorrectly installed.  The battery had quite a bit of double sided tape to hold it securely in the machine, but the backing was not removed from the tape.  This left the battery free to move around in the machine.  Because the battery was free to move, the power connection was ripped off the battery while he was riding it, causing the sudden stop and injury.  

This was directly the result of improper battery instillation by the supplier.  

Even though the machine was new, the battery also appeared to be an aftermarket battery.  

My concern is that this company sells hundreds of these machines on ebay, and I am certain that it is common for the batteries to be incorrectly installed.  I feel that there is great risk to other riders.  There is risk of injury or death as a result if this shortcut taken by the seller.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription: portable electric heater: "Optimus Digital Oscillating Heater Fan with LCD Display" but purchased through Houzz online:  shop@houzz.com
brand: Optimus Digital Oscillating Heater Fan with LCD Display
incidentDescription: I purchased two portable heaters.  I removed one from the box, and read the directions.  It said to plug it in and push the on button.  I did that.  The digital thermostat said 80 degree, and I pushed the button to lower that to 72. I then began to gather the plastic wrap etc to throw in the trash. In those seconds, I smelled a plastic-y or dust burning type smell.  I thought it might be because it was new and being turned on for the first time. I looked at the heater, and within a second or two saw a small wisp of smoke from inside the "grate" of the heater body.  Before I could react, at the base of the the wisp of  smoke emanated, a small flame erupted. I was shocked, and before I could react, the flame grew up rapidly, and black toxic smelling smoke began to pour from it. I kind of panicked, afraid to touch it with my hands, but had to move it aside to get to the cord to unplug it.  I hesitated but then just grabbed it from the sides. Luckily it was not hot yet at those spots, I guess, because I did not burn my hands. I unplugged it. By then it was really burning. I got the slider door open and got the heater onto the concrete patio.  I got a pitcher and began throwing water on it. My neighbors came out from the smell of the burning plastic, but we did not call the fire dept. because I got it out with the water. I immediately reported the product defect to the entity from which I ordered it, Houzz, although they are not the manufacturer or the direct vendor. I have the fire-damaged heater, and will hold it per your request for 30 days, and the other new heater is still unopened in the box.  PS [REDACTED] is my second home. Mailing address is on [REDACTED].
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

4 lbs tub of carpet cleaner

Rug Dry Cleaner
incidentDescription:
The consumer cleaned the walkways in his home.  He stated that he used 3 out of the 4 lbs. of cleaner that came in the tub.

Within a couple hours, the consumer's wife began to feel ill and he had to take her to Urgent Care on 10/20/2016.  The wife was referred from Urgent Care over to the hospital for an ultra-sound.  The wife was experiencing difficulty swallowing and shortness of breath.  

An ultra sound was taken and the consumers saw their primary care doctor the following day.

The wife was referred to an Ear, Nose & Throat doctor. It appeared that her thyroid was inflamed.  The consumer noted that his wife and he are both 64 years and haven't experienced this problem previously.

The EN&T conducted an ultra-sound and examined her throat, nasal passages.  Multi-adulor goiters (tiny bumps on her thyroid).  The wife was given 15 tablets of [REDACTED].  This did not alleviate her symptoms.  The wife was referred to Corvalus Hospital, where she remained for 2 days in their out patient program, where she stayed on 11/8/2016  & 11/09/2016.  

It was determined that the wife did not have cancer.

The wife later went to Lebanon Community Hospital.  A substance was administered to the wife, which enabled the doctor to see her esophagus.  

11/8/2016:  The wife then went back to her primary care physician.  

The physician suggested that the carpet cleaner was the culprit.

The consumer said that this material is even affecting his dog.

11/16/2016:  The consumer took his wife back to urgent care.  Anti-biotics was prescripted for the wire.

The consumer noted that this substance is sprayed on the carpet in a pre-soak fashion.  Then it is later brushed into the carpet for deep cleaning.  Anytime the consumer vacuums his carpet, this substance is raised in his home and his wife has to leave the home to avoid an injury.

This has impacted the wife's ability to sleep through the nigh.

productDescription: Kitchen Aid Artisan Stand Mixer (Model: KSM150PSWH, Serial #: WU0519544)
incidentDescription: I purchased a Kitchen Aid Artisan Stand Mixer (Model: KSM150PSWH, Serial #: WU0519544) in August 2008 at London Drugs in Vancouver. About 6 months ago I was using the mixer on high speed, whipping egg whites for a few minutes. There was a loud bang type of noise, a large spark and the breaker tripped. I thought it was a problem with the wiring in my 100 year old house. (But it was VERY SCARY.) Two days ago I was making cookies and sparks began to fly out of the back of the head of the mixer and the breaker tripped again. This time I realized it is a mixer problem. This poses an electrical and fire safety hazard for the user. I searched online and found a post about another consumer reporting the exact same problem. The mixer just before the most recent electrical issue,  developed what seems to be some kind of gear problem. I called the Kitchen Aid help line about the gear problem and since the machine is off warranty, they offered me a "Customer Loyalty Discount", to purchase a new machine. A can buy the same mixer locally here from Canadian Tire for less money, on sale. After the sparking and breaker incident, I realize this machine is not safe to use. I wrote about the issue on Kitchen Aid's FB page - they replied, saying that I had already been in contact with Customer Service and the best they could do was offer me the same Customer Loyalty Discount. This is a safety issue, which they do not show any concern about. They have not shown any interest in understanding the source of the problem, nor of protecting consumers who use this mixer and experience similar problems. This could have caused a house fire - and all Kitchen Aid has done is to offer me a discount to buy another mixer from them. I told them I will not be buying any more Kitchen Aid appliances! I think this matter should be looked in to, and the problem identified, consumers made aware, and affected mixers recalled. Thank you.

productDescription: Black and silver hair dryer, Revlon  RV544
incidentDescription: I was using my Revlon RV544 Ionic Ceramic Tourmaline hair dryer when it turned off. I looked at it and turned it off and on again and it resumed. The dryer has been carefully hung from the loop on a hook everyday and was well cared for. This was completely spontaneous and terrifying.
