productDescription: Cuisinart Smart Stick hand blender, model #CSB-76.  Exact location of serial number is unclear, but it is probably either 70807 or E143681.
incidentDescription: Cuisinart Smart Stick hand blender, model #CSB-76.  Exact location of serial number is unclear, but it is probably either 70807 or E143681.  The 3/4 inch long plastic collar surrounding the blade shaft just above the blade itself disintegrated into the food while pureeing well-done steamed cauliflower.  An hour-long phone call to Cuisinart was fruitless.  I was told they would not provide a replacement blade part as the item is out of warranty.  However, they could not even verify which number is the serial number so I have little confidence in their assessment that it is "out of warranty".  Regardless, however, of warranty duration, this is a safety issue.  (I am certain that my food processor from the 1990s is out of warranty, but they are still doing a massive recall when those are disintegrating into food.)  I understand a warranty limitation covering the motor, etc. in my hand blender, but this isn't that kind of issue.  If it just stopped working I wouldn't be notifying Cuisinart and requesting a replacement.  The problem here is that I almost fed my baby food with hard pieces of plastic in it.  Cuisinart should not be so cavalier about this and dismiss my call.  Look where that got them with the food processor blades.  Unbelievable.

productDescription: The product is a curling wand. incidentDescription:
On 2/25/2017 I was using an InStyler Auto Curler Tulip curling wand when a dangerous incident occurred as a result of using the wand.

The product was purchased by myself brand new from the store and it's seal was intact at time of purchase. Prior to using it the first time, I got out the instruction booklet that came with the wand and read it page by page, as I had never used a curling wand like it and wanted to make sure I did everything correct. To use the product, one places a strand of hair (there is a little guide included to ensure you don't put too much hair in the unit, which I was using) into the unit, pushes and holds a button. The wand automatically draws up hair into unit for a preset amount of time, at which point it beeps and you pull hair out to reveal a curl.

I had done several curls and thought I was getting the hang of it. I loaded another strand of hair into the wand, making sure I used the guide first, and the pushed the button. It pulled a little bit of hair into it then suddenly jammed, leaving it stuck on my hair with some of it sitting right on the 430 degree barrel, as I was unable to get it off. My friend who was at my home visiting helped me and we grabbed my hair with one hand and pulled the unit with the other and it let go of my hair, but not before it burned the portion touching the barrel beyond repair. I was shaken by the incident. I got back out the instruction booklet and read it once more trying to figure out where I want wrong.

There are no warnings on the box about the device having a potential to jam hair. In the user manual there is only a small warning that states "In the unlikely event of a tangle.." which made me feel a little relief thinking it was perhaps just a fluke thing.

I gathered myself and decided to give it another try about 10 minutes later. I reloaded a different section of hair into the device just as I had all the other curls, pushed the button, and it began pulling my hair into the wand. Then all of a sudden, again, my hair jammed with so much force that it hurt my scalp. I tried to pull the wand off my hair like the last time, but it was to no avail. The hair would not come out of the wand. I was freaking out. A large portion of my hair was wrapped around the hot barrel. My friend rushed over again to try and help me pull it off my hair but it was not budging. The more I pulled at the hot wand, the more it pulled at my scalp and the more pain it caused. I began crying and frantically trying to get it off my hair as I smelled it begin to burn it. I yanked the cord out of the wall. My friend grabbed a pair of scissors nearby and and to cut my hair. We had no other choice. This left me with a section of hair now cut half way up that looks absolutely ridiculous and also left me feeling pain on my scalp where we had pulled to try and get it off for a couple hours after the incident.

incidentDescription:
On Tuesday February 21, 2017 at approximately 11:00 am, I was using a 1/4 inch impact driver to install 1.25 inch screws when the tools battery exploded without warning in my hand. The tool is and 18 volt model made by Chicago Electric an sold by Harbor Freight Tools with a serial number of 363831451. The battery that exploded only has a part number of 68860.

The battery and driver was operating normal until this incident when there was a very loud bang very similar to a gunshot. I immediately felt pieces of debris hit my arms chest and face and was left unable to see from what felt like sand hitting my face and eyes. The tool was at most two feet from my face. My ears were also ringing from the sound as it was so loud. I was unsure the extent of my injuries until I was able to clear my eyes enough to see though they were blurry for some time.

It was at this time I found I was bleeding from numerous bleeding cuts on both arms with one cut having a small piece of the battery case stuck in it. My right wrist and forearm had both small cuts and burn on it as this was the hand I was holding tool in. My left arm had cuts on forearm and upper inside arm with some bruising starting. Both arms and face had a black powder which appeared to be from the actual battery insides that burned while on my skin. I needed to rinse eyes continuously to get out what felt like sand and was stinging seriously. My t-shirt had small pieces of debris stuck in the fabric.

The sound was loud enough to be heard from people both downstairs and another outside with closed windows that was there with me. Pieces of debris were scattered throughout the room I was in as well as hallway and room adjacent to hallway. The battery case is blown apart with individual battery cylinders missing and other material burnt and hanging out. The debris was made up of both metal and plastic including a metal cylinder that is split open into sharp edges and bulged out. It appears to be an actual battery casing.

I took pictures of injuries and the aftermath of incident including the tool and battery immediately after, as soon as I was able to. I also gathered pieces of battery debris and have kept them along with the exploded battery itself as evidence of incident.

It has been even more upsetting to find upon a Google search that this has happened before with these exact batteries and has been reported before. The injuries sustained by this failure could easily cause far more serious injury and needs to be dealt with. There is no warning prior to this an does not appear to have been in the other cases either.

productDescription: The smoke alarm is manufactured by Kidde, model P3010H, a photoelectric smoke alarm with a 10-year lithium battery. According to the label, it was manufactured July 5, 2014. I purchased it from a large retailer and installed it in March, 2016.
incidentDescription:
The smoke alarm is manufactured by Kidde, model P3010H, a photoelectric smoke alarm with a 10-year lithium battery. According to the label, it was manufactured July 5, 2014. I purchased it from a large retailer and installed it in March, 2016. 

Not quite one year after activation, the alarm sounded in the middle of the night. The "hush" button did not function as advertised. The detector was removed to another room and stopped sounding.

Today, it sounded again in the middle of the night (of course!), the "hush" button had no effect,  and was removed to another room, where it stopped. Two hours later, while on a table in another room, it sounded again. No response from the hush button. 

In each instance, none of the other five alarms in my home sounded (one is an identical model). I had a 35-year career in the fire service, and now six more years as a licensed and certified expert witness in fire investigation, and I'm pretty confidant that there were no products of combustion in the home during any of these alarm activations.

A quick check on the internet found numerous instances of consumers complaining of the same issues with this model alarm. No information about recalls was found.

Here is my concern: consumers dealing with this same issue might choose to deactivate or discard their smoke alarms as a false alarm is unsettling and annoying. If they do this, they will no longer have the protection of smoke detection in their homes. Over my fire service career I took part in investigating more than 60 fatalities from fire, and it is well known that the single most important thing that any of us can do to prevent a fire death is to have a working smoke alarm in our homes.

Additionally, if there is an issue with false alarms, I have no confidence that the detector will actually detect smoke. I have not yet tested this unit, but will if you choose not to.

I request that the CPSC investigate and evaluate this model smoke alarm to determine if there is any wider problem than my own detector failing. My faulty detector is still operational and available for evaluation and testing if necessary. I have, however, removed it from my home and will replace it before the end of the day.

Thank you for your consideration, and thank you for the work that you do to keep us all safer.

[REDACTED]

We contacted Shark Ninja about the problem on January 6 2017 via email (They asked for us to send additional information such as the model number. After they received that information they replied back on January 19 2017 and stated that they could not assist us. They told us to contact the Customer Service Department at 18776465288. 
We called the Customer Service Department on January 19 2017. They stated that they have not heard of the problem but when we searched online we found several online complaints regarding the machine turning on by itself. These complaints were posted on amazon.com and saferproducts.gov. The customer service representative offered to send a new unit at a discounted price of 87.00 with free shipping. I unplugged it and contacted Bonaire, who informed me it was not under warranty.  Despite this, I asked the representative to find out if they had other complaints similar to mine.  She talked with her supervisor and informed me they had no reports of any problem like this.  She did suggest I discontinue using the product for safety reasons. Everything turned off including the fan but the heating element did not turn off and started glowing red hot!  I quickly unplugged it and the element of course shut down.

productDescription: 5 QT. PROGRAMMABLE SLOW COOKER
incidentDescription:
This is about:

     AMBIANO 5 QT. Programmable Slow Cooker

     Model Number LY-5000DE

     Distributed By ALDI Inc., Batavia, IL.

The support structure on the bottom side of the unit consists of three(3) very small feet. Modest pressure applied to the left or right rear rim of the unit will cause the unit to tip.I used the word modest to give a sense of the situation, but it shouldn't matter as a unit like this full of hot materials should absolutely not tip at all under any circumstance.
 
Further, I filled the unit with 6 Qts of 57 degree tap water and chose the High setting which causes the unit to stay on for 6 hours.

The temp. of the water at 3 hours had not reached a temp of 150 degrees F which is below safe food temp.

During this time the surface or outer skin was at times higher than the internal temp.

By the sixth hour the internal temp had finally reached 195 degrees and the external temp. exceeded 166 degrees. 

As we understand it, thermal burn can start as low as 140 degrees. This is, of course, dependent of exposure time. It seems that 166 degrees would be of danger to small children and pets.

The ceramic pot appears to be suspended above the heated base unit. This would seem to account, in part at least, for the lengthy heating time of the contents and the high surface temp.of the outer skin of the unit.

Thank you!

productDescription: Duel fuel propane/natural gas unvented heater sold in 3 sizes, 6,000Btu (WDFT060-VF) 10,000btu(WDFT100-VF) and 32,000btu (WDFT320-VF) Its is not known at this time if any of the other units sold under the therma blaster name contain the same pilot design.
productType: Gas or Lp Heaters, Other or Not Specified (392)
incidentDescription:
As a HVAC Tech I have the job of installing many gas appliances in customers’ homes. I recently installed a Thermablaster heater for a customer. Upon Initial firing I was able to get the main burner to turn on but not ignite. After removing the front cover the locate the issue I determined that these units are being manufactured in a way that essentially bypasses the very system meant to ensure enough flame is present at the burner for proper ignition.

These heaters, manufactured in various sizes and sold both online and through major retailers are designed with 3 pilot systems. During operation on Propane, the pilot on the left is only designed to keep the gas control safety open. This pilot is placed several inches away from the burner and is not capable of properly igniting the main burner. The pilot on the right is enabled during ignition to shoot about a 3-4" flame to hopefully light the standing pilot located above and directly between both left and right pilot systems. It is this center pilot that ignites the main burner. The Issue with this unit is there is no way on ensuring that this center pilot is functioning properly or if it even lit during startup. As long as the pilot on the left is functioning gas can be turned on to the main burner and continue to flow until it locates a source of ignition. No injuries were sustained, but I cautioned this customer and subsequently a second customer to make sure the center pilot Is lit before attempting the use the unit. I have included a copy of page 15 from the WDFT320-VF Manual showing the pilot system in question for your reference.

productDescription:
FARBERWARE 4 LITER DEEP FRYER
Model Number: 103736
From WALMART
 on the back of the unit
incidentDescription:
On the night of December 21, 2016- (our second time using the Farberware 4 Liter Deep Fryer experienced no problem the first time we used the deep fryer) we decided to deep fry breaded shrimp in the Farberware 4 Liter Deep fryer. We filled the unit up to the maximum level line with [REDACTED] Vegetable oil. As per the instructions we set the temperature setting to 350 degrees and turned the unit on.
Soon after, a sickening smell/odor (like burning metal) spread throughout our entire house – My eyes began to burn, my head began to hurt, and I felt nauseated. My wife who has asthma was sitting well away from our kitchen in our living room and complained that it was hard for her to breathe.


We turned the unit off and tried to get rid of the sickening odor, but to no avail. We could not get rid of the odor throughout our entire house.  The next morning, I checked the set of  [REDACTED] FPR 10air filters (which I had installed on December 9, 20 16) located at the far end of our house. The air filters bad turned black (see enclosed picture). I went to Home Depot, purchased another set of air filters, and replaced the discolored black [REDACTED] FPR 10 air filters.

My wife and I left the house for the holidays. When we returned I checked the new air filters.
This time the set of [REDACTED] air filters had turned charcoal gray.
Before replacing another set of [REDACTED] FPR air filters, we called for our heating and air service man. Two days later, he came out and witnessed the 2 sets of discolored air filters. The sight of the discolored air filters puzzled him. He checked our heating and cooling unit. He found nothing wrong. (We were charged $67.29 for a service call). He could not determine what could have caused the air filters to discolor. He suggested we call an air quality expert for help. I have kept both sets of discolored air filters. I have reinstalled another set of [REDACTED] FPR air filters (FPR 10) on January 9, 2017. There has been no discoloration. To this day, my wife is still having trouble with her breathing.

Since the time of our bad experience with the Farberware 4 Liter Deep fryer my wife has had problems breathing and has experienced an asthma attack. She visited the pulmonary specialist once ( December 28, 20 16) and was given a prescription which has done very little to help her breathe better and has had a second prescription called in. She continues to cough and use a prescription inhaler. The Pulmonary specialist saw the pictures of the air filters and commented on them stating that "it was very interesting".

Before I replaced the second set of [REDACTED] air filters and determined to fmd out what could have caused the [REDACTED] air filters to discolor- I contacted [REDACTED] on January 7, 2017 and asked for their opinion. [REDACTED] answered me on January 10, 2017. I have enclosed their answer find their response to be very interesting. In the response from [REDACTED], an air specialist stated that the cause for the discoloration was a heavy metal captured by the air filters; He also stated that this could be signs of a Teflon coating burning off the coils of the unit which could and is hazardous to one's health. He also stated that Farberware is known to coat internal parts with Teflon. He also stated for us to stop using the Deep Fryer.

On the last page of the Farberware 4 Liter Owner's Manual there is a word of caution paragraph that clearly states that the deep fryer may give off an odor and emit smoke-- also stating that this is normal.

Enclosed you will find pictures of the discolored air filters and our response from [REDACTED].
Also, in the reviews of the deep fryer a customer states that they have experienced the same problem the second time just as we have experienced the problem the second time we used the deep fryer.

manufacturer: Royal Appliance Mfg Co business as TTI Floor Care N. Am.
model: Dirt Devil, Model:   BD10045 Plant U; Mfg Code: L 15B U
incidentDescription:
Below is my October, 2016 letter to the Chairman of Royal Appliance regarding the danger of their product, Dirt Devil, Model:   BD10045 that was ignored. Product can easily fall off the wall, injuring a child.

[REDACTED], CEO
Royal Appliance
1400 Salem Rd.
Cooksville, TN 38506

October 20, 2016

Re:  Dirt Devil, Model:   BD10045 Plant U; Mfg Code: L 15B U

Dear [REDACTED]:

I have purchased the above vacuum based on the good reviews I read on Amazon.  I have had many Dustbusters in the past, which did not have the problem reported below.

I mounted the unit on the wall, as per instructions; however, the unit is only held in place by very light charging contacts.  It falls off the base, landing on the switch, turning on the unit, draining it, making it a dangerous trip hazard.  

In September, 2016, I contacted your tech department and they offered to send out a new charging base—which solution I questioned, if it would be any better.  After many weeks, I called, as I had not received the base. I was told that the base was on back-order and may be available in November.  I was invited to peel off the label and cut off the cord off the unit.  I protested that I would not do this until I have the replacement unit, as the vacuum function still works, but I will give my credit card, which they could charge, to guarantee my compliance.  Once I returned the requested part, Royal could refund my money.  Your agent and supervisor, both told me that this was unacceptable. I had to disable to unit, while I wait the indeterminate time for the replacement. 

But more importantly, I explained that this 3.28 lbs. unit—more if it is filled with debris—can land on the head of a child, would that I mounted it higher.  One of my Dustbusters is mounted higher, but the unit slides securely into a plastic holster.  Is Royal so cavalier with the safety of children? I will ask that question to the Consumer Product Safety Commission, Consumer Reports and Amazon.  

Having still not heard from your company, I now await your response to my complaint.

Sincerely,




[REDACTED]

productDescription: ORiginal manufacture Apple iPhone 6c cellular phone, charger and lighting cable
incidentDescription: My Apple iPhone 6c was plunged into an Apple charger with an Apple charging cord which came with the original purchase of phone.  I had noticed the phone would become extremely warm if it was in use while plugged in.  This did not seem to be unusual.  My phone was plugged in and lying on my bed.  I got up to let my dog outside. After approximately 5 minutes I returned upstairs to my bedroom. I heard a hissing sound and thought it was the stool running. At the top of the stairs I could see an orange inferno covering my bed. I panicked and started to run and get the hose. Realizing it was unhooked and may have water in it that was frozen. I ran back upstairs for my phone to call the fire department an realized my phone would have been in the center of the inferno.  Black smoke filled the room with the distinct smell of an electrical fire.  To save my home from burning to the ground, I grabbed the side of my down comforter and flipped it over onto the flames. As I did that the fan of air to the flames whooshed out at me and caught the hair on the right side of my head on fire. I backed away to brush the fire in my hair off and noticed that covering the flames on the bed helped. I went into the hall for a breath of less smokey air and realized I must do this again if I were to save my home. This time I was more cautious as I flipped the other side of the comfort or over the flames. My beard melted to my face and all hair on my arms and chest was singed to the skin. Went for more air and saw this accomplished putting out the majority. I have a fire extinguisher down the hall but it all happened in a matter of probably under 30 seconds. Instead of grabbing the extinguisher, I rolled the comforter into a ball putting out the fire to a manageable level. I ran out for air. Knowing there may be smoldering cinders within, and there was upon inspection, a grabbed the black ball of what use to be a comforter and dragged it down the stairs and out the back door. At this point I needed to sit and breath for a moment before going at it more. I found a Cotten shirt with small flames on it and doused it with water using a cup in the bathroom. Almost 24 hours I am still in shock as to what happened. I went to unroll the comforter on the back lawn to see the Apple charger was completely fried. My phone was still plugged in yet is basically unharmed.  I have ruled out every possible reason for this occurance and come to the absolute conclusion that the Apple charger and or cord is 100% to blame. I am thankful I was not overcome by smoke and died and no other furniture or home was set ablaze. To this moment there remains that very distinct smell of an electrical fire.

incidentDescription: While using the Revlon (Ionic Tourmaline Ceramic/ Model #RvDR544) hair blow dryer, sparks and flame flew out of the bottom handle.  Distinct smell of electrical fire.  I immediately dropped the dryer in the sink and pulled the plug out of the wall.  As I did another loud pop.  After investigating the now cooled off dryer, there is a clear flaw in the design of this product.  Where the cord sparked and caught fire, it is visibly rubbing on the plastic part of the actual dryer.  In other words, everytime you move the dryer the cord rubs on this plastic part.  Considering that this is only about a year old, I would not expect this to happen.  This a a major design flaw with dangerous consequences.  I'm lucky the few times in the past couple weeks that I left this plugged in when I walked away that it did not catch the house on fire.  This product needs to be pulled from the market immediately

productDescription: Cuisinart Brushed Stainless Steel Custom 14-Cup Food Processor
incidentDescription:
I bought a Cuisinart 14-Cup food processor (model DFP-14BCN) in October 2013 in the U.S. (I currently live in Canada.) 

A few months ago, I had just made salmon mousse in it and was just putting it on the table for my children when I saw some rigid shapes in the mousse. I discovered that they were broken shards of the blade, which had cracked and come apart at the rivets. I had just served the mousse to my kids. Obviously, this was very upsetting.

I called Cuisinart's consumer line about this in August but did not hear back, and I just read about the recall for this blade defect, so I'm reporting it to you this time and will try sending the information to Cuisinart again. I'm also attaching photos.

The jagged edges of the blade also apparently left scratches on the inside of the work bowl, which I hadn't immediately noticed. I'm unhappy that I did not hear back from Cuisinart when I first contacted them, and I will contact them again today to ask that a new blade and workbowl sent to replace the defective/damaged ones. I will check back with you again if I still don't hear from Cuisinart. (I know you're aware of this issue because there is now a recall, but I thought you should know about yet another instance of the defective blade.) Thank you, [REDACTED] 

*IMPORTANT: If you need to contact me about this, please use email [REDACTED] . If you need me to call you, email me and we will arrange a time. (I will be travelling in the coming months.) Thank you.

productDescription: Lenovo Thinkpad Extended Battery 94Wh
incidentDescription:
Flight Information
•	Flight Date: 02 December 2016
•	Event Date: 03 December 2016
•	Flight: 836 (HNL-ATL)
•	Aircraft: A330-300 (Ship 3310)
•	Phase of Flight: Cruise
•	3 flight crew, 9 flight attendants, 259 passengers, 1 cockpit jumpseat

Preliminary Details (Subject to Change)
•	According to the flight crew, in the vicinity of SLC they were notified of a fire in an overhead bin.
•	The cabin crew initially observed a glow and smoke from the overhead bin near seat 3J.
•	The cabin crew then observed flames and discharged a halon fire extinguisher before opening the bin.
•	After opening the bin, smoke was observed from a passenger’s laptop.
•	At this time, the captain exited the crew rest facility and assisted the cabin crew in placing the laptop into a containment bag.
•	The cabin crew noted that they utilized three halon and two water extinguishers to extinguish the fire and cool the laptop.
•	Subsequently, the containment bag was moved to the mid galley and placed into a cooler with ice.
•	A flight attendant monitored the containment bag for the remainder of the flight.
•	At this time, the captain returned to the flight deck and contacted dispatch.
•	The flight continued to ATL without further incident.

incidentDescription:
There is presently a product recall on Cuisinart Food Processors that have a riveted blade.  The recall site states that if there are no rivets on your blade, then it is safe to continue use.  I have a Cuisinart Mini-Prep Plus Food Processor, Model DLC-2A.  Prior to the recall for the food processors with the riveted blades, I had noticed that mine which is not riveted is cracked in multiple places near where the blades insert and on multiple sites on that blade piece.

There has been no injury regarding my blade but clearly it could easily happen given the multiple cracks.  Of note, is that I have only used the processor for grinding herbs and fully cooked carrots.  As well, it has never been in a dishwasher.

I called your number as listed on your site yesterday 12.15.2016 and was told I would be able to attach pictures of my blade to this report.

In the area below for the incident report, I will have to guess when I first noticed the blade in this condition.  I was just planning on replacing the unit for another brand assuming this was a singular quality control issue.  As a physician, when I saw the recall for the riveted blades, I wanted to make sure you are alerted to the fact that the non riveted blades are most likely affected and would cause the same injuries as noted in the current recall.  Of great concern is the statement on the recall site that if you don't have a riveted blade, they are safe to use.  When you see the pictures of mine, you will understand why I am writing this. I tried numerous times to call Cuisinart but continued to get either a loud busy signal or a message that there was unusually high demand and to call later.  "Calling later" has not worked.  

Thanks for your work with protecting consumers.

productDescription: Cuisanart Food Processor Model DLC-& Pro with four rivet blade model DLC-7
incidentDescription:
Cuisanart Food Processor blade as reported December 13, 2016. The recall indicates certain models made in China from 1996 forward. We checked our unit / blade and it does indeed have the four rivets, AND THERE IS A CRACK RUNNING THRU ONE OF THEM.   Fortunately we have had no injury from this design failure. BUT.......YOU MAY WANT TO CONSIDER A RECALL EXPANSION. You see our  Cuisanart Food Processor , with Model DLC-7 Pro stamped on the bottom of the unit AND on the blade is ALSO STAMPED as having been  MADE IN JAPAN. Further there is an inspection tag still on the bottom of the unit bearing the date AUGUST 11, 1988. That is a full eight years earlier than the present recall. So, to reiterate, our unit : 
1. Was made in August 1988, not  July 1996 through December 2015 
2. Was made in Japan, not China
3. Has the same four rivet blade with beige plastic center
4. The blade has a crack through one rivet as reported in the recall

My thumb was badly cut by the preceding blade, even though I had placed it in a Ziplock 1 Quart Freezer bag since I recognized how sharp this blade was.

The cut to my thumb required 7 stiches to stop the bleeding and reattach my thumb tip.  I feel the Cusinart Cutting Blade, DLC-044TX 4mm should be sold with a hard clear plastic sleeve so a consumer handling the blade or placing the main unit in a drawer is protected.
Since, the manufacturer has such a particularly dangerous  Cutting Blade, DLC-044TX 4mm people owning this unit now should be supplied a protective sleeve for this blade.  The main chopping blade that was part of the recall due to metal fragments breaking off, normally sits in the chopping container/bowl so it does not present a hazard to a user when they reach for the handled chopping bowl

Cuisinart Food Processor

Pro Classic, Model DLC-10S TX (Type 25)

with Metal Blade FP-100TX
incidentDescription:
I own a Cuisinart Food Processor that is older than the advertised date range of the current Cuisinart recall, which is due to a riveted metal blade that can develop cracks and break.

I am reporting this out of concern that some owners of older Cuisinart food processors with defective and dangerous blades will not seek or will not obtain a new blade through the recall.

My blade unit also has cracks in the metal at each of the four rivets securing the lower blade. There are between one and three cracks at each rivet. The combination of cracks on this blade extends across about 90% of the blade. Although the metal blade is cracked, none of the blade has broken off.

I purchased this food processor in 1987. However, the advertised date range for the recall is July 1996 to December 2015.

The model number of the food processor is DLC-10S TX (Type 25). It is labeled the Cuisinart PRO Classic Food Processor, made in China. The blade is marked Metal Blade FP-100TX and it is also marked Cuisinart DLC-10.

For the Cuisinart recall form on the website, I selected model "DLC-10S" and my unit was considered eligible for the recall. There wasn't an option to select model DLC-10S TX. The website form did not ask for the date of purchase.

incidentDescription: I used my Cuisinart Mini-Prep Plus to chop some herbs for stuffed shells.   While eating dinner, my husband bit down on something hard in the stuffed shell which only has soft ricotta cheese and herbs in it.   He spit it out and it was a small white piece of plastic.   We were shocked and couldn't believe it came from the cheese.   We thought about how we made the shells and checked out the Cuisinart.   The plastic around the blade had deteriorated and parts were coming off during chopping.   While he hurt his tooth and it was sore for a few days, luckily it did not require dental work.   I looked into purchasing a replacement blade but it was $15 and I decided it was too much $. productDescription: Wood Pellet Stove
incidentDescription:
In November 2016, I took delivery of a wood pellet stove from a Home Depot Store in San Diego, CA, with order Nr. C53809356. This stove is made by US Stove Co., model Wiseway #GW1949.
When I fired it up on Nov.27,2016 the stove worked fine for three hours, but then suddenly emitted heavy smoke.
I closed the hopper, but the stove can not be shut off - it has to burn through the supply in the chute. It kept smoldering for 90 min., filling my house with heavy smoke. 
When I inspected it later, the fire had apparently reversed course and burned up the chute in direction of the hopper.
I notified Home Depot and US Stove Co. but got no answer as to how this incident could be avoided.

Conclusion: Had I not been present and closed the hopper, the fire would have burned and ignited close to 
50 lbs. of pellets, causing considerable damages.

productDescription: Boosted Boards, Dual, v1.
incidentDescription:
I purchased a Boosted Board powered longboard on 11/19/2014. I regularly used the product on a daily basis until 7/9/2015 in Foster City, CA when it caused me to fall and dislocate my left knee, including a full ACL, PCL, MCL tear in my knee.

This product is usually used in a "last-mile" commute to and from a destination. It has a dual 1500W remote-controlled motor sending power to two rear wheels. I rode my Boosted Board from my front door to reach my car parked a distance away on the morning of 7/9/2015. On this occasion I rode about 20-25 feet away from my apartment front-door when suddenly the board rapidly decelerated and made a loud grinding noise. I had no time to react and jump off. In the fall I injured my knee and I could not get up due to the pain and had to call for help.

I called a nearby building manager for immediate help and called a friend to take me to hospital. The next day I had an MRI which showed the extent of the injuries including a full ACL, PCL, MCL tear, impaction fractures, a grade II sprain of LCL, patellar retinacular tear, etc. (Full MRI report can be provided.)

On 12 January, 2016 I underwent a 9.5 hour orthopedic surgery to begin repairing my knee. On examination it revealed a full knee dislocation, with complete ACL, PCL, MCL, LCL tears. Full surgery report can be provided. I spent approximately 3 months on crutches, while awaiting a follow-up surgery to address the torn ACL.

On 8 December, 2016 I underwent a second surgery to reconstruct the torn ACL. Full surgery report can be provided.

On 13 July 2015, I provided Boosted Boards with an initial report of my injury and a concern that the product may have malfunctioned, I offered to them that I will return the board in an effort to allow them to investigate. After they received my board on 1 September 2015, they failed to contact me for several weeks while I asked for updates. On October 6 they said they haven't been able to figure anything out. On 16 October, the CEO of Boosted Boards contacted me saying no abnormal behavior was found in their logs and offered me a refund. 

I am aware of this happening to at least one other person. On 7/30/2015, another rider was commuting through San Francisco and described the following, "My board stopped suddenly with a screeching noise as if it were thrown into reverse. [...] I was thrown into scaffolding breaking a finger. I had surgery on Monday to set the finger straight. [...] It took some time to get my board and the remote back online with each other which led me to believe that my incident was most likely some of of RF interference." (More details on this incident can be provided however this is a separate incident and this person is not listed on this report.)

This report and its description of how the board malfunctioned correlate with my experience. Given that this has happened at least twice, I would like CPSC to investigate further, given how Boosted Boards has not been either willing or able to find the cause.

productType: Gas or Lp Heaters, Other or Not Specified (392)
manufacturer: Lennox Hearth Products LLC (Innovative Hearth Products)
incidentDescription:
We had a ventless gas heater that we had bought last year. We used it all last winter and this year had only used it about a week when the incident happened. When my son’s girlfriend came home our basement was filled with smoke and she went over to the heater and turned the main gas line off. We are not sure what happened with it but it is like it exploded inside. It was all burnt on the top and back of heater and caught the wall on fire.
 The company sent their rep to look at the heater last week but he didn't even really examine it nor did he even attempt to look at the inside of the heater. He just give us some b.s. that it was installation error. lt can be used for either propane or gas. There was a setting on the back and it was set to natural gas like it should have been. He then looked on the bottom where the fixtures for the lp and gas were. Since there wasn't anything in the propane fixture he said that the flame could get down in there and come out that hole. Well after he left we remembered from our pictures that there was something blue among some debris that was laying on the floor underneath the heater after it happened. We didn't realize what it was but my husband figured out that it was the fixture that was in the propane hole and it blew out when the explosion happened. I believe there should be a safety feature anyway so the gas wouldn't even go there if it is set to natural gas setting. We could have lost our whole house because of this heater. We even sleep down there where this heater is. I just want other unsuspecting families to be aware of the dangers of this heater. Luckily everyone was at work and school when this happened.

Report of Investigation
On 22 NOV 2016 at 19:15 hours the Fire Investigation Unit was requested to respond to [REDACTED] for a fire investigation. Scene access was by exigent circumstances, while fire crews were still working on scene. Weather at the time was 29°F, clear skies with winds from the WNW @ 14 MPH.
Upon arrival I was met and briefed at the scene by the IC, [REDACTED], [REDACTED]. Chief [REDACTED] detailed the WFD response and actions taken to the incident. The 911 caller was located in [REDACTED]. [REDACTED] had called her apartment maintenance person because she had a smoke odor and found soot coming out of her bathroom shower fixture. The maintenance man was [REDACTED] (xxxxxxxxxx). He observed the soot and smelled the odor and dialed 911.
Capt [REDACTED], commander of [REDACTED], was the first arriving WFD unit. He stated that there was an odor of smoke in [REDACTED] which is located on the second floor. After finding no cause for this odor or soot in [REDACTED], he ordered [REDACTED] to check the unit below this unit. [REDACTED] was commanded by Acting Lt. [REDACTED]. Acting Lt. [REDACTED] reported a neighbor said the unit was vacant. He forced the unit door open and observed soot covering all surfaces of the vacant unit. Further investigation revealed an extinguished fire in a bedroom ceiling. The adjoining walls were opened up in units [REDACTED] to check for fire extension until the companies were satisfied there was no active hidden fire.
Statements were obtained from the involved persons. [REDACTED] resident [REDACTED] was interviewed. She stated that she and her children had left the apartment at 05:30 hours. She returned briefly at 08:15 hours and at this time smelled the odor of smoke and heard alarms sounding in the downstairs unit which she knew to be vacant. She called her maintenance person; [REDACTED] who told her there was no concern because the fire department had already checked the property prior to her call and found a problem in the adjacent building. [REDACTED] then left for the day and returned at 17:30 hours to find soot on her shower fixture and the odor of smoke. She again called [REDACTED] who did respond to the unit this time and observed the conditions.
[REDACTED] was interviewed. [REDACTED] is the maintenance person for 22 of the 46 units within this complex. He does not have any affiliation with this fire unit. [REDACTED] has worked at this complex for 15 years and stated that he was aware of several fires that were caused by the ventilation fans located in the windowless bedrooms and common hallways. He reported that all these fans were installed in the same manner and of the same equipment when the building complex was first constructed. He also reported that as a result of his own testing and comparisons these fans did not have a thermal cut off switch within the unit, unlike the bathroom fans with lights that did have thermal cutoff switches. He opined that all the ventilation fans were dangerous and subject to overheating.
[REDACTED] (xxxxxxxxxx,xxxxxx) of [REDACTED] is the unit owner and she was interviewed at the scene. [REDACTED] purchased the unit on this day for $75,750, paying cash with no mortgage recorded. (Wdrd Book [REDACTED]; [REDACTED]). [REDACTED] did not have property insurance for this unit. She was advised that there may be an insurance claim under the master insurance policy, therefore she should not damage the fan or electrical wiring until it was approved and examined by the insurance company. The master insurance policy is held by [REDACTED] through the [REDACTED]. [REDACTED] is the local agent.
A systematic scene examination was then initiated in the area of least to most damage. No exterior damage was found on the building. Smoke staining was visible on the interior window surfaces of [REDACTED]. Interior examination of [REDACTED], located directly above the fire unit showed evidence of soot emitting from the shower head pipe fixture and concentrations of soot on the ventilation fan surfaces. Fire crews opened the walls in the area of the utility chase to check for fire extension. No fire extension was found in [REDACTED].
The interior examination of [REDACTED] revealed smoke and soot covering all exposed surfaces of the unit. Fire crews opened walls in the master bathroom to check for fire extension from the windowless bedroom. Upon entering the fire bedroom fire damage was observed to the carpet that appears to result from melting and pooling of a smoldering fire. The ceiling in the area of the ventilation fan was fire damaged with partial wallboard collapse. Fire crews pulled additional wallboard and insulation down from between the ceiling joists to expose the extent of the extinguished fire. The ceiling joists showed extensive char and fire extension to adjoining surfaces. The ceiling fan showed fire and heat patterns and the electrical wires were also burned.
Closer examination of the collapsed wallboard show smoke only on the interior surface indicating the fire began above the surface of the ceiling. The electrical wires were examined in detail. No beading was located on the electrical wires to signify an electrical arc or fault. Electrical wire damage was consistent with thermal exposure. The bedroom circuit breaker (#23) was found in the tripped position, also consistent with thermal exposure. Fire patterns on the ceiling fan housing indicate a heating event in the lowest portion of the fan motor area. The bedroom electrical switch near the door was in the on position.
MRIRS reports indicate that the Worcester Fire Department did respond to an alarm incident ([REDACTED]) at this building at 06:41 hours. Fire companies noted a smoke condition and alarms sounding in [REDACTED]. As they investigated the smoke condition cleared prior to locating the source. The building alarm was reset by the responding responsible party. The fire department left with no alarms sounding.
Based upon information obtained during this investigation it is believed within a reasonable degree of fire investigative certainty that the origin of this fire is the area of the NuTone ventilation fan and the cause of the fire is undetermined. The ignition source could not be identified. Faulty electrical wiring or a defective fan motor could not be determined without destructive examination. The first fuel ignited is most likely the thermoplastic cover, or dust contained within the grill. The ignition sequence is the thermal runaway of the ignition source. There is no evidence indicating a set fire. The burns on the carpet are caused by thermoplastic resin drop down fire that ignited a slow moving smoldering fire. This fire self-extinguished when it became ventilation limited by consuming all the available oxygen in the room. The incomplete combustion of the smoldering fire covered all unit surfaces with soot.
[REDACTED], xxxxxxxxxx is the Trustee for the [REDACTED]. He was advised of the findings of this fire and it was recommended to him to change all the fans in the common area and windowless bedrooms-24 fans in total and to add CO alarms within dwelling units. He was also advised that several of the emergency lights were not functioning and needed repairs. A complaint was filed with Fire Prevention for an Inspector to follow up with this repair.
This fire has been ruled undetermined and the case is closed pending further information that may
warrant its reopening. All additional names, photos, phone numbers, personal information, witness
statements, full narratives and notes are in FIU file or investigation report.
A notice of this fire and suspected product defect was made to the Consumer Product Safety Council.

productDescription: Fridgidaire FDL50S1 50 pint dehumidifier
incidentDescription:
For the past several years I have operated a Fridgidair model FDL50S1 dehumidifier in my basement.The dehumidifier was set to maintain 50% humidity and was hose drained to the basement sump. The manufacture date is listed as 03/09 which falls outside of the current recall on this particular model by Gree.

I arrived home for lunch to a strong burning odor and found my dehumidifier smoking slightly, but still running, in my basement. I immediately unplugged the unit and let it cool for 30 minutes.The dehumidifier was hot to the touch.I disassembled the unit the make sure nothing was smoldering before returning to work.The compressor was still too hot to touch,the plastic casing near the compressor was discolored, and the insulation on the wiring to the thermocouple (part of the thermal protection circuit) on the compressor was burnt.Oil was found in the plastic tray underneath the coils. Luckily I caught it in time and no injuries were sustained.

I called the Gree recall hotline at 1-886-853-2802 and provided my name,address,phone number,product model number,manufacture date,and serial number. I was told that it was not covered by the recall and that there was nothing they could do.

The blender blades has a hard plastic casing and a rubber o-ring to give a proper seal when using the blender for the NutriNinja cups.  The debris from blended food becomes lodged between the rubber ring and the hard plastic casing of the blade housing resulting in build up of decaying food, mold, and a putrid odor.  I contacted the manufacturer asking if there is a way to easily remove the rubber ring for proper cleaning and they informed me that the rubber ring should not be removed.  This leaves the consumer with the problem that food debris will become lodged there posing a health hazard.  I have looked online and found many posts from people with similar problems and they ultimately removed the rubber ring using a knife or other tool and found a large amount of rotting food matter.  The instructions that come with the product for cleaning (fill blender with soapy water and run it on the blender) only cleans the blade and does nothing for the debris that is stuck between the rubber ring and the hard casing.

incidentDescription: ITEM Oster Countertop Oven Model TSSTTVXXLL  I was cooking chicken cordon blue - (Frozen prepared version from [REDACTED]) on a flat pizza type pan.  I had preheated the oven. He twists it past the 20 minute point and back to off - no bell.  He turns off the oven.  Later we hear the oven running.  We check and the oven is on again.  We fuss with the timer again - past the 20 minute point going clockwise then back to zero (no bell ding).... then we notice that when we move it to zero - no bell dings, but the oven is off, you can still here the timer ticking though...... and it is slowly working it's way to the ALWAYS ON position and it turns the oven on again.  We reset the oven to zero (past the 20 min and back to zero) ... oven is off ..we watch it as it continues to tick and turn it self on again.. to the ALWAYS ON position.  We move it to zero, unplug it.... plug it back in 10 minutes later - same problem.  We unplug it and go to bed for the night.  The next morning. We twist it past 20 minutes in a clockwise manner, then roll it back to zero (no bell ding) plug it in and yep the timer is ticking and slowly as time passes... it moves to the ALWAYS ON button and it is on again.  Repeated a couple other variations but inevitably it turns itself back on if it is plugged in.  In my opinion, this is a huge fire hazard.

productDescription: Revlon hair dryer, grey color
incidentDescription:
On the evening of January 19th, 2016, I purchased a Revlon hair dryer from the Target in Medina, MN. After I returned home that night, I tried to use this hair dryer to blow dry my daughter's hair after she showered. I plugged it in and turned in on and immediately the hair dryer shot out fire.
My coat sleeve and my arm were both set on fire. I ran my arm under water. My daughter screamed and started crying. I was in great pain and was irritated by the Target. So I went to the Target to talk to the manager and explain the issue to him. At that time I noticed that the hair dryer seemed to have been used for a very long time. The handle was badly worn, the paint was off or faded, and it was repackaged. The Target manager was not sympathetic and was not willing to help me. He suggested me to contact the manufacturer of the dryer.

The pain kept getting worse at night, and I went to the urgent care the next day. The doctor gave me medications and a shot and I returned home. The next few days my arm became infected and the pain was getting even worse. I went to the urgent care again and the doctor diagnosed it as Second Degree Burn and Wound Infection, for which I was given more medications. In the
next three weeks, the infection and pain prevented me from doing most of my routine duties during the day and from sleeping well during the night. This incident also caused an emotional stress on the whole family. My daughter sustained a fear of hair dryers for a period of time after this, afraid of using hair dryers to dry her hair.

I contacted Target headquarters about this incident, and they also directed me to the manufacturer Helen of Troy. I contacted the manufacturer who asked me to mail in the hair dryer. However, I think it is the main evidence of this incident so I have been hesitant to mail it in. I have sought help from two different lawyers but neither was able to help. I believe that this incident should not have happened had either Target or the manufacturer been responsible. And I believe that by making both parties more responsible, it will help protect the rights of all the consumers and
customers of the two parties.

productDescription: General Electric 50 pint dehumidifier.
incidentDescription:
We have a GE 50 pint dehumidifier, model ADEH50LQQ1, serial number FZ053835, manufacture date 03/12.  The dehumidifier is connected to a ground fault interrupter in the basement.  It has been operating normally until recently  Now it now trips the GFI about once a day.  When it is running, it otherwise operates normally.

In about 2001 I had a similar incident with a GE dehumidifier.  At first I did not realize it was the dehumidifier that was tripping the GFCI.  When I plugged the dehumidifier into a non-GFI protected outlet, it started a small fire, which went out immediately when the unit was unplugged. It caused very little damage to the dehumidifier, and no injuries.  GE did send a courier to pick up the unit for inspection and provided a replacement.

I am reporting this incident because others may have the same model dehumidifier and may be operating it without GFCI protection, which may potentially lead to a fire.  

The product will be replaced, but I will save the old unit for possible inspection by the manufacture or the CPSC, as the unit appears faulty, but since it has not burned, it can be examined to determine which component(s) are faulty.

She saw smoke coming from the hoverboard; she grabbed a towel, threw it over the hoverboard and kicked the plug out of the outlet which caused sparks at the wall/outlet area.

She moved the hoverboard and used the towel to suffocate any source of heat that could cause it to burst into flames.

When she removed the towel she saw that the unit had melted in half with cracks on the halves.

When she tried to pick the hoverboard up after it cooled it broke in half.

She has now found that Swagway has recalled the unit and she is asking for CPSC to assist her with obtaining a refund for this hoverboard because both she and her now 15 year old son are afraid to have another hoverboard in their home.

incidentDescription:
Kenmore Elite Dehumidifier  Model 251.90701010  S/N  WNX5Y50000019

Electrical Shock Hazard

The Kenmore is about 7-9  years old.   Purchased about 2007-2009

 In is in the basement and performed well. 

On 9/14/16, the basement breaker circuit went out.  After repeated tests and disconnecting various electrical equipment the problem traced to Kenmore.  It has not been damaged and has been in the same place for years ... water goes automatically into a drain, so seldom touched or moved.    Electric cord was sound and had no defects.  

When I plugged the Kenmore in the receptacle, the breaker on the receptacle was activated and cut the electricity.

It cut off again when I tried to restart it.  Thinking it might be the receptacle, I ran a extension cord to another receptacle  in the basement.   

 When I tried to connect the Kenmore cord to the plugged in extension cord, there was a very large spark generated at the plug interface and a CRACK.  

 If I had not been holding the two ends at a distance from the connection point I would have been burned or severely shocked.   I was fortunate.

I noted other Kenmore dehumidifier  models have been recalled before due to hazard problems.  This was produced in Korea and might be from the same manufacturer.

productDescription: Conair hair dryer. Model 259Y. "Infinity Pro Conair"
incidentDescription:
This is the second time I am trying to send this message to you. The first time, your gateway server timed-out and lost all of my information.

Re: Conair Hairdryer Model 259Y “Infinity jPro”

I bought this hairdryer at CVS Pharmacy in [REDACTED] about six or seven months ago. It was on sale.

I’ve had no problems with it until today. While using it, it made a couple of popping sounds and then immediately flames and sparks started shooting out of the bottom of the handle. I dropped it and pulled the plug out of the socket.

I then went to the Conair website intending to report it and saw that many model numbers of the “Infinity Pro” had been recalled, but not my model number 259Y. The recall notice was very specific in saying that only models with one screw on the back of the handle were being recalled. My model 259Y has TWO screws on the back.

I telephoned the Recall Center and spent 17 MINUTES ON HOLD. Honestly, for a department that is entrusted with dealing with safety issues, this is quite unacceptable.

I hung up and proceeded to call the Conair Corporate Headquarters. I was transferred to a “Director’s” voicemail at extension #247. I believe that her VM message said that her name was [REDACTED] (phonetic representation). I left her a very long message with all of the above information and more along with my phone number which I repeated TWICE.

I demanded a call back and also demanded that the website recall information be updated to include this model 259Y with TWO screws on the back of the handle.

My feeling is that they will ignore me. I am VERY upset as this was a terribly scary incident that could have basically set me on fire. Conair needs a corporate standard that when consumers call that Recall Line, they get an answer within 1 minute. 17 minutes on hold is just absurd and suggests a reckless disregard for consumers who they have put a risk with their faulty products.

This message is to notify you that the battery EXPLODED!

incidentDescription: While on Toasting cycle, after finishing, there was an electrical fire behind the oven space. Could not be extinguished by fire extinguisher because of where it was. Turning off the breaker stopped the electrical arcing and fire stopped.

productDescription: Fan remote controller
incidentDescription:
Hunter All-Fan Control (model 27185, s/n 277076) failed while not being used.  I had this device installed in a fan canopy to control the fan and light kit via a remote controller mounted on the was switch.
On 8/24/16, I returned home from being away for a week, when entering, I noticed a smell of burnt electronics when entering the kitchen (where the device is installed).  A short time later, my wife tried to turn on the fan but neither the fan nor light would work, either with the remote or directly with the switches on the fan or light.
I removed power from the circuit and disassembled the fan and found the remote control unit badly burned and melted.
During the week I was away, there were no signs of a lightning strike to my home nor was there a loss of power.
I contacted Hunter Fan but they have not been very helpful in trying to figure out what happened.  All they have done is offer to replace the device.  
I have the failed device but they have shown no interest in having it returned for a failure investigation.

productDescription: portable pocket jump starter
incidentDescription:
This caller is reporting fault with his portable pocket jump starter that he received as a 2015 Christmas gift.
The caller hadn't used the portable jump starter until June 12th, 2016 when he went to  his truck and it wouldn't start.
[REDACTED] one ton pickup.
He decided to use his starter gift that morning to start the truck so he connected the cables then connected the other end to the portable starter.
He view the four blue lights indication the starter was ready with a proper connection and has turned itself on.  He tried to start his truck and could barely hear that the motor was trying to turn over.
He heard a "pop" noise, looked through the windshield under the open hood and saw that the portable jump starter had blown apart.
He went to the front of his truck and was going to pick the unit up but it was too hot so he let it cool off.
He has not attempted to reassemble the portable starter and he is reporting this unit as a possible burn and injury hazard.

There are no injuries being reported.  
The caller contacted the distributor to report this incident June 13th, 2015, he was informed by a female representative that [REDACTED] was owner of the company but did not provide another phone number.  She did advise him that his model number is not on an existing recall but that he could contact CPSC.

productDescription: Magic NutriBullet Model number NB-101B
incidentDescription:
August 19, 2016 at approximately 5:00 pm I was making a smoothie that consisted of almond milk, ½ a banana, peanut butter and ice.  When the blades stopped, which they usually due if I need to add more fluid, I went to take it off.  Although the NutriBullett claims it can crush ice without liquid, this is not the case.   I have found the blades frequently stop due to a lack of fluid and the blades being obstructed.  As I went to remove the canister, pushing down and turning to the left, enough fluid hit the blades and they started.  In the meantime the cup was not secured tight enough to the blades and the cup began to dislodge from the blades and the base.  Part of my shake came up the side of the cup and my right hand slid on to the partial exposed blades.  The blades continued to work because of at least one of the “nubs” stayed in the base until the cup became complete dislodged from the base.  The trajectory of my shake and blood from my hand went across the kitchen a minimum of 10 feet and as high as approximately six feet.  
The injury was to my right pinky finger and the base/palm of that finger.  I required 27 stitches. 

Witnesses:  [REDACTED] and [REDACTED]

productDescription: Ceiling Fan blades
incidentDescription:
This caller is reporting and incident with a ceiling fan purchased from retailer in and installed by the same retailer's tech around 2008.   

She has had no problems with this ceiling fan until the night of August 5th, 2016 when the caller went to bed with the fan running as usual then heard a loud sound and rose to find that two of the blades had fallen from the fan and had hit about two feet from her head.

When she woke the next morning she saw that there were two gouges in her wall that is about five feet from where she had been lying.

She is reporting this incident as a severe injury hazard.

Her small grandchild sleeps with her and she states that the child could have been seriously injured if the blades had come just two feet further.

There are no injuries being reported

She contacted the manufacturer Monday August 8th, 2016, she was offered replacement blades but then notified that the fan in question was no longer available.

They have asked for any information she has for the fan but they are questioning because she has no receipt from the eight year old purchase.

The manufacturer was contacted and they advised that a replacement would be sent to him, but they did not need the defective one to look at.

Caller feels that this vacuum cleaner is a safety hazard and should be recalled.

productDescription: portable gas grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
(08/02/2016) The consumer stated that he was cooking on the grill. He went inside for a few minutes. About 10 minutes later he looked out and saw flames on the top lid. 

The consumer went outside and shut the gas on the product. The consumer was able to blow the fire out.

(08/04/2016) The consumer contacted the firm. He was advised to send photos. The photos were sent to [REDACTED]. The consumer did not receive a response.

The consumer was cooking on this brand new BBQ a steak right in front of a kitchen window that looks out over the porch along the front of his house. He went inside to prepare the rest of his meal. He could see small flare ups from grease dripping on the burner cover. About 8 to 10 minutes he noticed a fire that did not look like a grease flare up. He went out to get a better look and that's when he notice the back of the BBQ lid was on fire. He turned the propane gas valve off but the fire did not go out. He was able to put it out by just blowing on it. He removed his steak and that's when he realized the BBQ lid had burned on the inside and continued up the lid to the top on the outside.
The consumer had to send the BBQ to Suntech Parts and Service Inc. of Canada to get a complete cash refund.

(with such force it blew the breaker on half of my house)  and probably saved my hair from catching on fire. productDescription: counter top portable coffee maker
incidentDescription:
I purchased a KitchenAid coffee maker.  The coffee maker has a hidden medal hinge pin in the top rear that protrudes out after about 3 weeks of daily use.  This pin is sharp and can puncture skin.  In addition, it is located where you hang the plastic water canister in the top rear of the coffee maker.  The protruding pin scrapes plastic filings into the water canister when you place it into the proper position.  Model KCM111OB, Serial # WF55202466.

I notified KitchenAid Customer Service who sent me a replacement coffee maker - I returned to them the defective unit.  After about 3 weeks of daily use, the 2nd coffee maker also had the same problem with the hidden pin that protrudes with the sharp point and escaping the plastic water canister.  I called KitchenAid Customer Service again and they sent me a different model replacement:  model [REDACTED], serial # [REDACTED].  After about 3 weeks of daily use, this 3rd coffee maker had the same exact problem as the others with a sharp protruding pin that can puncture skin and shaves plastic filings into the water canister that can be ingested by the consumer.  I notified KitchenAid and told them that they have a product design safety issue that needs to be addressed by their product design team.  They obviously are using this same hidden hinge pin on several of their models.  

I believe that they should be taking this product off the market until they can correct the safety problem.

The only thing he had running was the dehumidifier so he turned it off, unplugged then plugged it back in and within one minutes he saw a flash in the back of the unit, then smoke and a worsened acrid odor then he saw and orange glow and assumed that it was flames which prompted him to unplug it again.

incidentDescription:
Purchased a Bissell Proheat2x.  Used one time, two months later attempted to use again
when a smell of a rubber fire filled the room.  I shut it off within seconds. I then examined
the machine and realized my two brush bars were frozen.  I took off the bar guard to see if I could determine what the issue was.  It was then that I realized the bar that drives the belts was rusted stiff.  I spent several minutes calling the Bissell 800 help line.  They referred me to a service center that was two states away. Non the less I spent another few minutes calling the service center.  When I returned to the machine after speaking with the service center, I realized the machine was still smoking.  I then took the machine outside.

She makes a smoothie for breakfast every morning. The plastic is not detectable with the ice and she ground up a piece of the plastic and ingested a few pieces before she figured it out. She came to me alarmed that something was stuck in her throat.

I worked backward and found the shards of the plastic still in this ice bin.  I removed and took pictures of the broken pieces (attached).
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: Propane Gas Grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
This consumer is reporting his propane gas grill that he purchased from a retailer in Minnesota around November 2010 time frame.
He had no problems with this grill until around July 1st, 2016 when he placed his food on the grill then went inside to prepare other portions of the meal.
After just a few moments he looked out of his window and saw that the grill was on fire with flames close to two feet high coming from the back of the grill.
He immediately dialed 911 for the fire department who arrived in no longer than two to three minutes and checked the grill because the fire had extinguished itself.
The smell of the propane leaking from the grill was still quite strong.
The fire department firemen separated the tank from the grill and couldn't get the knob on top of the tank to turn off so the removed the grill and tank separately away from the caller's home.
There  are no injuries being reported.
The caller did contact the manufacturer July 21st, 2016 to ask if they would inspect the grill and repair it at their cost but they declined that offer and advised the caller that any inspection/repair would be at his expense.

I was having problems making it turn on.  After removing the “Start key” and putting it back in, the mower started running without the “bail” safety release or the “start button” being pressed.  The mower ran for approximately 30 seconds without the “bail” bar safely release being held down. This bail bar is the bar that is designed to stop the mower as soon as it is released. See video of the incident submitted.

Fire department and ambulance reported to the scene.  I was transported to the hospital burn unit.  I have found multiple complaints and issues regarding the design of the grill that have been reported online.  It has been banned in Canada.  It is still available for purchase at the Home Depot.  Please take this product off the market before another family’s life is changed forever or even worse, lives are needlessly ended.

productDescription: Cuisinart Custom Classic Toaster Oven Broiler, TOB-40
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
On Tuesday, August 9, 2016, I received an electrical shock when I turned off my Cuisinart toaster oven. The original Cuisinart TOB-40 toaster oven was purchased August 24, 2012. It had a 3 year warranty. Within the second year of use, one of the front bottom elements became warped. After the warping became severe, we contacted Cuisinart. The company sent a replacement oven in November 2014. We had to pay for shipping the original unit back to Cuisinart, $35.48. 

The front bottom heating element warped extensively on the replacement unit prior to the end of the second year of use. On August 9, 2016, when I turned off the toaster oven, I received an electrical shock. 

After this incident, I researched reviews on various sites where this toaster oven is sold and found numerous consumers reported problems with the heating elements warping. Some reported this resulted in fires and shocks.
victimSeverity: Injury, Level of care not known

the label calls this an "Outdoor Gas Grill" by CharBroil.

incidentDescription:
Our Char Broil gas bbq almost caused our house to burn down. 

I had lit the grill and gone inside to retrieve the food.
Apparently holes developed in the metal tube connecting the rubber gas line to the burners. 
There is evidence of charring under the grill, so flames must have been coming out of the
tube. It appears that those flames  melted the gas line, then ignited the gas flowing out of the severed gas line. (It must have been flames, not just heat from the bbq, otherwise the gas wouldn't have ignited.)
The propane bottle, unrestrained by the gas line fell over.  The lit gas line acted like a flame thrower, hurling flames at our house. Fortunately it had rained so the house was wet and we were able to grab a fire extinguisher and put this out. What a disaster.

incidentDescription:
I purchased a Jetboil Flash Personal Cooking System (Blue Desert color) from Backcountry.com on May 29, 2016. I noticed there was  a very strong plastic smell to it when I received the product, but the seller assured me it is common with new stoves. I did not attempt to use the stove until a camping trip on July 17, 2016. On July 17, 2016, I put cold water into the Jetboil cup and attached it to the Jetboil burner that is attached to Jetboil fuel canister. I made sure that the burner is at the lowest setting and pressed the igniter button that is supposed to automatically ignite the stove. 

What happened instead is I saw the whole stove go up in flames. I could not touch the stove or attempt to disconnect the fuel canister due to extremely high temperature and used whatever water I had at the campsite to put out the fire. Upon examination of the damage, I noticed that the igniter button completely melted off, plastic stand that the burner is attached to sustained substantial damage, and there was some damage to the wooden picnic table.  Upon first use, the whole plastic burner bottom went up in flames when I pressed the igniter. This sort of malfunction is a major safety issue, especially if I did not have access to water at the campsite (which is common on camping trips), the fire could ultimately lead to fuel canister explosion. 

I contacted the manufacturer Jetboil via email describing an incident and attaching photos of the damage but have received no response. Jetboil has previously recalled some of their product and it appears to be another instance of brand new stoves not being properly tested before being put on the market.

productDescription:
Red Folding Electric Lithium Powered Bicycle

305-209-4411
incidentDescription:
I purchased an electric bicycle back in December from farbike.com. I assembled it as per manufacturer's instructions and took it to a bicycle mechanic to be certain. The design of the bike is such that if you do not attach the battery just right, it will sit imperfectly but still run. I was riding to work one day and the battery fell off the bike. I took it home and attempted to charge and it started sparking, so I undid it and contacted the manufacturer. They asked for it back, so I sent it. 

Two months later, I finally get a new battery in. The new battery refuses to hold a charge, so I contacted them again, and suggested the charger might have been damaged as well. They sent me a new charger. With a new battery AND new charger, I then went to charge it overnight, as per the instructions. In the morning, I awoke to flashes of light and popping noises; the battery was sparking and jumping from the table I'd set it on. But I could not get close enough to unplug it as the sparks were too powerful. It set my couch, then my walls and entire home on fire and I lost everything. The Alamo Heights Fire Department has a report; they said if I hadn't awoken when I did I probably would not have awoken at all; the smoke and heat rising upstairs to my loft would have choked me.

We contacted the company, who passed us off to various sales reps but refused to answer our questions on liability or compensation, then passed us off to a rep in China who claimed to know nothing and has since ignored us. No refund on bike, no replacements, no compensation for thousands of dollars in damages to mine and my landlord's property. This company needs to be held accountable!

http://www.farbike.com/x-treme-x-cursion-xb-310li-folding-electric-bike

productDescription: Gold Chrome Plated, Self-Balancing Hoverboard, sold online by Hoverboard 360, with a mailing address in New York, New York. Arrived from Hong Kong in a box labeled IMOTO.
incidentDescription:
On December 2, 201 5, I purchased a hoverboard online for my 12-year-old son from Hoverboard 360 as a Christmas
present. The compnay had a mailing address in New York, New York and promised 2-day delivery on the item. The
company's website also advertised the hoverboards as complying with U.S. safety standards. Sometime around
December 17, 2015, I received a hoverboard in a box labeled IMOTO, shipped from Hong Kong. After closely
examining the hoverboard, I saw no manufacturer's label or branding on the item. I had no way of knowing what
type of hover board I actually received in the mail. That, coupled with all the safety issues that were coming to ligth
around that time, promtped me to contact my credit card company for assistance with returning the hoverboard.
My son was disappointed when he learned that I planned to return the hoverboard and, unfortunately, I elected to
keep it. After several months, I decided to allow him to practrice riding the hoverboard, but only with close
supervision. I noticed that after just a few minutes of riding, the bottom of the hoverboard would become
extremely hot. He was riding the hoverboard on a flat concrete surface in our garage. I also noticed the same issue
when he rode the hoverboard in our kitchen, which has flat hardwoord floors. Since he was just learning to ride the
hoverboard, he tended to ride very short distances before losing his balance. I did not understand how such limited
use of the product led to overheating. He is no longer allowed to use the product and we have wasted $498.99, as
the seller is refusing to provide a refund for the dangerous and defective item.

When comparing we weighed an empty bottle, dispensed 2oz of formula made by the baby brezza and weighed the bottle again and calculated the difference. We then did the same with a bottle made by hand using the formula scoop provided in the formula can. The difference was significant and shocking. Please look into this issue and research this on your own. Watered down bottles can be very dangerous for a newborn as you are already aware. I fear for the parents that do not think to evaluate what is being dispensed.
