productDescription: food processing machine Model#CFB-11ZBCPC Serial#41205 S  Cusinart
incidentDescription:
This is what I sent to Cuisinart customer service:

"I was gifted the food processing machine Model#CFB-11ZBCPC Serial#41205 S approx 8 months ago. I use it chiefly to make purees in preparation of our family meals.

Last night, about 4pm, I was making a puree of freshly-picked tomatoes--from my garden--including fresh herbs, garlic cloves and a can of tomato sauce and a little water. After 10 seconds of the machine being on, there was a giant bang and I saw a hole in the side of the Cuisinart clear plastic container/bowl; the blade had broken in half and part of it went through the side of the container. It had hit the stove and part the processor accessory case against the wall, behind the appliance.

I was standing right in front of it (making dinner) with my three children next to me, one of which is nine years old, and her head is about level with the appliance. If that blade had broken off just a nano-second earlier, it would have gone through her head, or my stomach.

We were all in shock, as this has never happened before. My mom had a Cuisinart for 15 years and it never anything did this. Today, I compared the thickness of this blade to her model (15 years old) and mine is far thinner and appears to be made of some kind of aluminum, not steel.

After a minute, I grabbed my phone and took pictures of the splintered pieces of plastic, the broken blade and the tomato sauce all over and was on the phone calling your customer service. The man on the phone was very aloof and did not seem to grasp the seriousness of the situation. He talked about replacement parts, but I informed him that I don't want another machine that will break apart again, and put us in such danger. I asked him if you were receiving complaints about this issue; he said "no". He put me on some kind of manager "24-hour call back list" which I have not had a call back from, as of yet.

The claim that no one else was complaining turned out to be a lie. I looked up this model online and found dozens of complaints (publicly listed) about the blade snapping half--even in processing soft items--and flying out the side of the container, just using the machine as the manual says it can be used. (And no, I did not list them here; I am certain your staff knows how to use Google)

Due to the number of public, visible complaints, it seems to me that Cuisinart is ignoring a serious danger to the consumer, knowingly putting out products that have two huge flaws.

Please tell your product development team, engineers and lawyers that:

1. the blade needs to be stronger (not so flimsy) so it wont snap in half
2. the plastic container/bowl need to be stronger to withstand the seemingly inevitable blade malfunction.

I do not want a replacement product that will once again put my family in danger again. I will not use it if I think the thin, cheap blade will snap in half. Any replacement parts offered must be stronger; the blade must be thicker and made of steel. If the motor is too powerful for the blade to handle, why did you put out an appliance that might fail?

Please get back to me quickly. I make food for my family three times a day and I use a food processor of some kind at least 4 times per week; I currently have no food processor and am having to work around it and alter the menu.

If you want me to send you the photos or the broken blade & bowl mailed to you as proof, let me know. I have also sent a copy of this email to a number of consumer affairs/safety watchdog individuals. If I do not hear back from your company in 24 hours I will write a consumer affair article on this model with the full breadth of the tale included and email it to as many media outlets as possible.

The public should be informed of the danger of this model, and God forbid it kills someone's little girl, and you knew about it, and could have prevented it.

Please immediately act to take this model off the shelves and inform the public of a nation-wide recall to replace these defective blades.

productDescription: 4 burner gas grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
I am a fire investigator for the State of Maine Fire Marshal's Office. On 04/12 I investigated a fire involving a 4-burner Master Forge (Lowes) gas grill. The investigation revealed that the grill had blown over in a heavy wind storm. When this particular grill falls on its control knob side, the knobs and electric igniter are in contact with the ground at the same time. This grill fell over on concrete with the tank valve still on. The grill slid across the concrete in the wind causing all four knobs to turn on as the igniter was firing. This caused ignition of the LP gas. Luckily the grill was lying on the concrete patio and the fire did not spread to an adjacent structure. I just wanted to make you aware of this as I was able to duplicate the event my first try. 

Mod#1010048

Ser#101CWIG0048119281

Office of the State Fire Marshal
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]

productDescription: Holmes Products convection space heater model HLH4422M
productType: Heaters or Heating Systems, Other or Not Specified (393)
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription:
I purchased a convection space heater at Home Depot, manufactured by Holmes Products, a brand of Sunbeam Corp doing business as Jarden Consumer Solutions, on March 5, 2015.  It is model HLH4422M.  When turning the heater on for the first time, it emitted a noxious, choking odor that also burned the eyes.  I placed it outdoors and ran it on a high setting for two hours.  The odor subsided significantly after this first operation, but it remains to an extent that causes coughing and airway irritation.  I am not overly sensitive to allergens or other environment conditions, and my workmates in the office also complained about the noxious fumes.  I use the heater sporadically, once every few month, and hoped that it would eventually “burn off” the irritant.  However, after a year and a half the noxious fumes continue.  After using it a week ago at a low heat setting, my throat became raw and my sinuses were irritated.  I decided that this product will never “clean up” and presents a consumer health danger.

I tried to return it to the place of purchase, Home Depot, but the 90 day return period expired and Home Depot said that the issue must be pursued directly to manufacturer, Holmes Products.  The manufacturer web page does not readily give contact information, I am still trying to make contact.  However, I feel that the CPSC should be notified of the health hazard.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

incidentDescription:
On 6/6 2016 I ordered a brand new shark navigator lift away vacuum, model NV352, from Home Depot.  June 14, 2016 was the first time I used it. This is not just small static shocks, but very strong electrical shocks, my hand and arm were tingling for about an hour after I stopped vacuuming. One was so strong that I actually let go of the vacuum handle and almost fell backwards.  This is extremely dangerous. After this happened I checked on-line and found out that Shark has had other vacuums that have been recalled for a shock hazard. I contacted Shark and this was their reply to me:

Dear [REDACTED],

Thank you for your email.

I am sorry to hear that. It is a normal occurrence and can be prevented by keeping hands moisturized, not wearing wool/polyester clothing while vacuuming. I apologize for the inconvenience this has caused. 

If we can be of further assistance please feel free to contact us at 1-800-798-7398, Monday to Friday, 8:00 am - 10:00 pm EST, as well as Saturday & Sunday from 9:00 am - 6:00 pm EST.

With regards,
Customer Service Team
SharkNinja Operating LLC


NORMAL OCCURANCE?!! Are they crazy??!! I have been vacuuming 40+ years and this is NOT normal. I can't emphasize enough how strong these shocks were!! Plus, I moisturize my hands and I was wearing cotton. I never wear wool or poly. To suggest this will fix this problem is insane. I'm hoping you can get a recall on this before some gets seriously injured. I will be returning it to Home Depot with a warning not to re-sell it!

productDescription: Frigidaire FAD504DWD 50-pint dehumidifier
incidentDescription:
I purchased a Frigidaire FAD504DWD 50-pint dehumidifier on Sept 1, 2014 through Amazon. I maintained the unit as suggested in the use and care manual (i.e., cleaning filter, dusting the cabinet, and clean the water bucket). On June 4, when cleaning the filter, I noticed a mildew smell emanating from the appliance. I disassembled the appliance and found that the front coil was covered in 1/8 inch layer of mold and sludge. As I started to clean the unit, I realized that there was also debris etc between the two coils and that there is no way to disassemble the coils from the appliance to clean/disinfect. 

My husband called Frigidaire (June 4, 7:15 pm) and was told that the appliance was still functional/not broken, so they could not issue a replacement under the 5 year limited warranty. On June 5, I emailed product support reporting what I had found and stating that I was shocked that Frigidaire considers this product functional in this state, rather than a product/health liability. On June 6, I received a response that "When the filter and coils of the dehumidifier are choked with dirt, it may not pull out moisture from the air properly. The efficiency of the dehumidifier gets decreased and the only solution is, to clean it thoroughly. In order to assist you with the cleaning procedure of a dehumidifier, following are a few tips..." One of these cleaning tips suggested that I "Use a vacuum cleaner to clean the evaporative coil/hot coil. Scrub off the dirt using a brush but make sure that you don't bend the fins while cleaning. Clean the condenser or the cold coil the same way." Given I didn't think the appliance could be dissembled allowing access to both coils, I requested detailed information on how to do this on June 6th. On June 8th, I received a response stating: "Do not try to remove the coils of the dehumidifier as this will ruin the appliance. You may use a vacuum cleaner to clean the evaporative coil/hot coil and condenser coil..." On June 8th, I responded and specifically asked for a refund given there is no way to adequately clean the unit without removal of the coils and removal of the coils would ruin the machine. In response, again on June 8th, I was told "I was happy to review your case with my supervisor. Regretfully, mold is not covered by your Manufacturer's Warranty, so Frigidaire will not be able to provide you with a replacement dehumidifier." I disagree. Given the current state of the appliance, it is not capable of performing its intended function without serious health ramifications. I contend that this is a direct result of the "defective materials or workmanship" (i.e., poor design) of the product.

Additionally, when purchasing this appliance, the website claimed (as does Frigidaire's current website) that this appliance "protects your home from mold and mildew caused by excess moisture" and "helps eliminate bacteria in the air that can make breathing difficult." Instead, this appliance became a major source of mold and mildew within my home. Further, I suspect that it was emanating bacteria into the air for months without suspicion as a direct result of these advertising claims. Given the design of this appliance is prohibits repair (i.e., cleaning), it is not feasible for the unit to function according to these claims, yet Frigidaire considers the unit to be functional in its present state.

I am currently working through the BBB to ideally obtain a refund/resolve my complaint, but think it is important that more people are warned so not adversely affected by this product.

productDescription: Weber Genesis 310 CNG grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
My Weber Genesis 310 CNG gas grill supply line caught fire on Sunday. The grill was completely destroyed and minor damage occurred to my home. The grill was not in use at the time and had not been in use for roughly 36 hours. 

As you can see, the grease is empty, the cookbox is relatively clean, and the origin of the fire is very clearly on the outside at the gas line. You can also see the melted wheel on the left side, which indicates the gas hose where it was near the ground was on fire. 

This is a defective gas line that seems to have started leaking underneath the cover. The combustion pattern is consistent with a gas accumulation under the cover below the velcro constraints beneath the side shelves. Splay patterns and flame spread are consistent with a fire point of ignition to the rear of the grill and in the gas line on the outside of the cabinet but roughly 2' from the supply line on the house. 

Weber states the supply line leaking from the center of the line was due to being left under pressure. The line, however, is designed to maintain pressure. ASTM standard indicates it should handle 105 psi for 10,000 service hours. The gas in my house is 0.26psi and the grill was installed approx. 8,900 hours prior. The line is installed per code and is a butyl core line, wrapped in corrugated steel, and covered in polyethylene. This is a clear defect. A storm was in the area, so ground static was high at the time. Weber states that this is an "act of nature", but a gas line that's not leaking won't ignite even under direct flame impingement.

The product is unsafe and Weber refuses to either honor the warranty, replace the grill, or deal with the problem.

Photos: https://www.dropbox.com/sh/nn6l4io51goc8mn/AADgo6u8PFblRxr6k2L8rSPra?dl=0

productDescription: Kenmore Propane Grill, Model Number 146.23680310
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription: Just over 2 years ago, we bought a Sears Kenmore propane grill (Model Number 146.23680310) thinking that it was a reliable brand which would last for awhile. We take very good care of the grill and from the outside it looks new. The inside, however, has completely rusted/burned through prematurely to the point that both the burners and the metal which protects the flames from the propane tank collapsed onto the tank, causing a huge fire hazard when the grill caught fire. Thankfully, we were able to extinguish the fire before anyone was hurt. Reading about this and other similar Kenmore models online, we were disappointed but not surprised to see that this particular model, along with a number of others, have had the exact same issue. It is clearly a safety hazard when the burn boxes are rusting/burning through prematurely. This and the other models at issue should absolutely be recalled.

productDescription: Cuisinart Food Processor. Model DLC - 5. Clear/gray bowl color. S blade in the bottom.
incidentDescription:
On Thursday, March 17th, my family and I began to cook dinner. We decided to make a sauce using our Cuisinart Food Processor model DLC - 5. We usually use our food processor when preparing dinner. While we blended up our sauce, one that we've made several times before, our processor began to make a sharp thumping noise. We stopped it, checked it, didn't see anything unusual, and tried it again. It made the sound again, so we shut it off to check around the machine and at the sauce inside. The sauce looked blended so we proceeded on with dinner. 

After dinner, we took the bowl off the processor off the base and as we went to clean it, we found a dark object in the bottom mixed in with leftover sauce. As we pulled it out, we realized that it was a piece of the S blade. When we pulled out the blade to look it over, we realized that on the bottom of the blade there are several rivets to hold the blade on. The blade had cracked along the thin edging where the rivets were. The piece we had identified in the bottom of our food processor bowl, mixed in with our food, was a piece that had broken off between two of the rivets. The sharp thumping sound we had heard, has been identified as the sound the blade was making as it spun around loose inside our food. It caused scratches and a huge dent inside the plastic of the processor bowl. 

At any point during our meal, this metal blade could have been consumed by our family, including our young children. The blade between the rivets can crack and break off and is extremely dangerous. We, as consumers, had no idea that was even possible. 

I contacted the company in April and did not hear back. I contacted the company again May 12th and we've exchanged many emails. The customer service is terrible. It takes about a day to get replies and every reply is from someone different so the emails are not cohesive. In one of the last emails, they told me I'd have to buy a replacement blade. I refused, because I don't believe we are at fault and we should not have to replace it. I also, do not want a blade with rivets on the bottom now, knowing the danger it poses to our family. 

Today, May 16th, I called customer service. It says in their emails that when you call, they will not know about the emails. As I explained my situation, the customer service representative said "So what do you want us to do about it?". When I told her I'd like my food processor replaced with one that does not have rivets on the bottom of the blade. She told me they couldn't do that, they could only replace the blade. She offered no remorse or apology. I asked to speak with a supervisor. She informed me that due to the volume of calls, she'd need to take my name and number and I would have to wait for a customer service supervisor to call me in 24 hours. 

Their Facebook page is full of negative feedback and other products that have broken or become dangerous, including a coffee pot that burst into flames. Many posts have not gotten any responses from customer service. This is a terrible way to conduct service. 

When I googled " Cuisinart Food Processor Blade Breaking" I came across many webpages with people that are dealing with the same situation for various models. It's extremely dangerous. I hope that you can help, since the company is unwilling to protect people.

productDescription: Smart Hoverboard w/ bluetooth
manufacturer: Shenzhen Better Power Technology Co. LTD.
incidentDescription:
To Whom It May Concern:

[REDACTED] represents [REDACTED], individually and on behalf of her daughter [REDACTED], in an action against 2 Smart Communications, LLC ("2 Smart") for selling her a hover board manufactured by Shenzhen Better Power Technology, Co., Ltd. ("Shenzhen") that caught fire while charging. 

As a Christmas gift this past Christmas, [REDACTED] purchased a hoverboard and charging unit from 2 Smart which were manufactured by Shenzhen.  [REDACTED] purchased the hoverboard for her daughter.  That hoverboard had a sensor that did not operate properly and was returned to 2 Smart.  On or about March 8, 2016, 2 Smart provided [REDACTED] with a replacement scooter and charger which were manufactured by Shenzhen (hereinafter the “Hoverboard” or the “Product”).  

On or about March 24, 2016, the Hoverboard was in the process of being charged in the Apartment.  The charger was plugged into an electrical outlet per the User’s Manual.  About 45 minutes later the charger emitted sparks.  The red indicator light was red, which according to the User’s Manual, meant that the charger was charging properly.  [REDACTED] observed the sparks and screamed for her daughter to get out of the Apartment.  The sparks then ignited wrapping paper within a nearby bag containing Easter clothing.  In an instant the bag caught on fire. As the flames erupted, [REDACTED] primary concern was the safety of her daughter.  She was able to get her daughter out of the house without being consumed by the flames or overcome by smoke. Once safely on the street a 911 call was placed to the Fire Department.  By the time the fire truck arrived, the Apartment was engulfed in flames and virtually all of Plaintiffs’ personal property was destroyed.  [REDACTED] and her daughter were left homeless.

incidentDescription:
Hello,

I purchased Ninja BL770 from Best Buy in November 2015. While the product is very good. The serious design flaw is that the blade can fall out while emptying the blended/processed contents from the jug.  This is because the blade is not locked into place. I understand that it is expected that the consumer removes the blade before emptying. We have been using the Ninja BL770 for 5 months now and every time the blade falls out. Twice now it has caused injuries because the blade falls on the thumb or finger. Today the blade fell out and caused a deep gash on my thumb. I had to use 2 bottles of hydrogen peroxide and 1 bottle of isopropyl alcohol to contain the bleeding. While the would is deep it cannot be stitched due to its location. 
This is a very serious flaw in the design of this product that the blade is not locked and can fall out. For years the blender industry has trained its users with locked blades - while it is possible to get accustomed to "unlocked" blades from Ninja, I worry that users like me are getting injured while using this product. 

Thank you

productDescription: BBQ Kitchen cover top made out of Alumawood by Amerimax sold by Tropicana Outdoor living Company business location is 949 N Cataract Ave, San Dimas, CA 91773; Phone: (909) 538·1414/(909)599-4211/(888) 849-1195
incidentDescription:
I bought an outdoor BBQ kitchen from Tropicana Outdoor Living Company and had it installed by their installers.
The kitchen top came off its footing with the winds we had two months ago. Luckily I was home to tight it down during the rain storm to prevent it from flying off to my neighbors' yard and possibly causing property damage and/or Injury to personnel. Enclosed are pictures of the top and screws used to attach the footing. I'm no engineer, but the size of the top overhang and footing are bad designs. This product should have never been on the market as designed; I was expecting a stronger footing design. Use of a metal plate with bolts would make a big different in the strength of the footing with a smaller top overhang. Notified the company of the Incident, talked to a person named [REDACTED], he stated that the design was safe and that the company's Installation team simply did not installed It correctly, maybe due to the installation team fatigue. I check with Amerimax engineering for specifications on size of overhang for the amount of spacing between posts for the patio top Installed by Tropicana 
Outdoor living installers and it specifies it should be no longer than 25% of post spacing (2 feet). Top installed has an overhang of over six feet, way beyond specs provided by Amerimax engineering and presents an extreme safety Issue and should no longer be on the market. Enclosed are Amerlmax engineering specifications. In addition, this company sale their products at home shows throughout Southern California. Yes, I would like to get reimbursed for the faulty product I bought from Tropicana Outdoor living Company, but most important is the unsafe condition that could exist out in the public in Southern California due to design of this product and faulty installation.

productDescription: Weber Genesis S-330 outdoor gas cooking grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
I spoke to [REDACTED] by telephone.  Mr. [REDACTED] told me that he was attempting to light a Weber gas barbecue grill on the deck and had just connected a new propane tank to the grill.  Mr. [REDACTED] stated that he did not hear any sounds indicating a gas leak after opening the valve of the cylinder.  He attempted to light the grill with the built-in igniter but was unsuccessful.  He knelt down in front of the grill and opened the cabinet doors to check the connections.  While he was kneeling in front of the grill, he opened a burner valve and pushed the igniter button.  He stated that the grill “blew up in his face.”  Mr. [REDACTED] stated that he had owned the grill for approximately 1 ½ years, and had no previous problems with it.  

After consideration of data collected for fire cause determination, and using the overall methodology by applying the scientific method as discussed in the 2014 edition of “NFPA 921- Guide for Fire and Explosion Investigation,” it is my opinion that the fire originated in the barbecue grill on the exterior deck on the east side of the structure.  The ignition source for the fire was a spark from the electronic igniter on the grill.  The first fuel ignited was uncontained flammable gas (propane) from a source other than normally intended at the burner, possibly due to a leak or improper connection at or near the container or piping.  The factors that brought the ignition source and the first fuel ignited together were the unintentional actions of a person or persons.  Using these elements, the classification of fire cause is ACCIDENTAL.

productDescription: CHI Turbo Low EMF Hair Dryer, red, by Farouk Systems Inc.
incidentDescription:
I had been blow drying my hair in my bedroom for about 8 minutes when I suddenly saw, out of the corner of my eye, an orange flash of light coming from the hair dryer. I simultaneously heard a sizzling, crackling sound coming from the dryer. It scared me, and I immediately turned it off and unplugged it.

-	I did not feel my hair being pulled, and I did not smell anything burning, so I’m sure there was no hair caught in the dryer. (I’ve had a piece of hair get caught in a dryer before during my lifetime, and I could feel it pull my hair out, and I could smell burning hair for a moment. That has not happened in a long time, and I don’t remember if it has ever happened with this dryer or not.)
-	I usually blow dry my hair for about 10 minutes almost every night. My hair is long, and thick, and completely natural. I use no leave-in products on my hair.
-	I do not remember how long I have had this dryer, but I will estimate about 4 years, maybe.
-	I checked the lint filter on the dryer, and it was not significantly blocked, as you can see from one of the attached images.
-	The ALCI plug did not trip, nor did the [REDACTED] Grounded power strip that I had the dryer plugged into.
-	I later noticed that the power cord coming out of the 2 inch rubber cord protector (I don’t know what it’s called) at the base of the dryer had partially melted, and you can just barely see a piece of copper wire showing through, and that the cord at that point appears to be permanently twisted about 90 degrees clockwise. (See attached images.)
-	Up until last year I did not realize dryer cords were not supposed to be wrapped around the dryer. So it is possible that years of wrapping a warm cord around the dryer for storage caused the cord to become twisted and weakened at that particular spot that melted. That may potentially have contributed to the dryer sparking.

However, despite my ignorance, I still feel this is a potential health hazard for consumers due to the significant number of similar and worse incidents reported on this sight and online from use of hair dryers of several different manufacturers.

Accolades to hair dryer manufacturers and government regulators for ALCI plugs, cord protectors, cleanable filters, safety warning labels, and safety instructions. Chi does state in their safety instructions #5: “Keep the cord away from heated surfaces. Do not wrap the cord around the appliance.” (See attached images.)

However, I don’t know any consumer that wants their hair dryer to be hanging up on their wall as a permanent part of their bedroom or bathroom decor. That would be a potential hazard also, because of all the constant dust getting into the vents. Most non-professional consumers store their blow dryers in a cabinet or drawer, and that requires folding up the cords to some extent, causing some twisting, even if they are careful to not twist the cord tightly around the appliance. I think this is conceivably and reasonably evident due to the significant number of similar and worse incidents reported online.

To protect the interests of all hair dryer manufacturers, and to prevent serious injuries to consumers in the future due to this issue, I would recommend that the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission require hair dryer manufacturers to manufacture stronger hair dryer power cords, or require that they include with the dryer some sort of simple storage tray or wall mount that would prevent cord folding or twisting.

productDescription:
Blender

Ninja Professional 1500 watts
incidentDescription:
Consumer stated that while the blender was in use for approximately 5 mins, he noticed sparks emitting from the bottom right sight side of the blender and there was a burning odor.  He then noticed that it had developed into a black smoke.  He immediately unplugged it and remove it outside.  He had the blender for over a year and there was no prior incident. 

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

Consumer feels that the blender is unsafe and should be reported.

This incident with Ninja BL770 occurred today while making a smoothie.
Ingredients being processed:
3 medjool dates
2 bananas 
Mango 
Coconut flakes 
Dried lime
Dried lime zest & orange zest
Quart of cold water

Because the consumer had brought the dates about an hour before starting to make this smoothie, they had not been soaked. Thus, he ran the blender on high speed for a couple of minutes to emulsify them with about 4-6 ounces of cold water.
Then added the bananas, dried lime sections, emulsified them on high.2-3 minutes.
Next, added the flesh from a decently ripe mango and a little more cold water. Emulsified on high 1-2 minutes.
Added remain of the cold water. Blended medium less than a minute. Tasted.
Decided not thick enough.
Pour out most of the smoothie to allow him to blend-in coconut flakes. After starting the flakes to blend, decided to add dried zest (lime & orange).
Added those ingredients; started blending on high. Because he had not ground the zest before adding it to the smoothie, the consumer figured he needed to run the blender a little longer than he would have otherwise.
It had been running 2-3 minutes when either sparking or the odor from the blender caught the consumer's attention from where he was standing at  the kitchen counter about 5-6 feet away.
The blender was still running.

The consumer immediately investigated. He had noticed on other occasions that the blender seem to get really warm. But, it had never shutdown; or, otherwise gave indication of overheating.
However, since he had ran it longer than usual, his initial thought was maybe it was beginning to overheat.
While the blender was still running, he saw what he believe was sparking coming out of the left rear side.
The consumer immediately turned the blender off and unplugged it.
At  this  time,  smoke  - noxious  smelling  like  'burnt  plastic'  - was billowing out of the blender.

Took the pitcher off.
Turned the blender over; and saw where the plastic center section had begun to melt.
There was still a lot of smoke being generated. 

Remove the blender base to my outside landing.

Decided to take pictures with his cell phone; and then, with digital camera.

Also, took pictures where the blender had been setting. There was substantial black dust on the pad I had had under it.
The consumer cannot say that all the black dust was from this incident because the reason the pad was under the blender was its history of making that black dust when used.

Attached are two pictures, The consumer has retained 10 other pictures.
If you need additional information about this incident, please contact me.

productDescription: Oscillating Space Heater
incidentDescription:
The consumer plugged in the space heater in his family room for use.  The consumer had the space heater placed on an open shelf. 

The consumer started using the heater on the evening of 1/17/16. The consumer would only use the heater in the evening.

Before bed on 01/19/16, around 10:30 pm, the consumer noticed that the heater stopped oscillating. The heater was still blowing out heat so the consumer went to bed.

At 1:30am (1/20/16), the consumer heard a loud crack sound come from the electric breaker. The consumer went to check and noticed that there were flames shooting up from the heater. The flames were reaching up to the ceiling. 

The consumer unplugged the unit and started throwing water to extinguish the flames. The smoke alarms went off.

The consumer had smoke and soot all over his home. He had to ventilate the area to get rid of smoke from the home.

The consumer has smoke/fire damage to the ceiling, wall panel, carpet and shelf in the living room. The consumer will have to have all of the wall panel replaced. The ceiling and molding is charred. The heater melted into the carpet.

The heater was originally about 12 inches tall. After the incident, the heater has melted down to just about 2 inches (only base remaining). 

The consumer called the retailer 1/20/16. He also contacted the manufacturer where he spoke to [REDACTED]. The consumer was asked the condition of plug, cord and outlet. The consumer informed her that all of those things were not damaged. The consumer explained the incident. The representative asked the consumer to send in photos and repair/clean up estimates. 

The representative also asked the consumer to send back the heater to the company for an inspection. The consumer refused to send it back and kept it as an evidence. The consumer informed the representative that they can send out an inspector to look at the heater. The representative informed the consumer that they may contact local fire marshall to come out to look at the unit.

The consumer received a call from the local [REDACTED] fire chief who was advised by the fire marshall to inform him that if the product has been boxed up, it would be considered tempering with the evidence. No one came out for an inspection.

The consumer contacted Service Master for an estimate. The consumer had them send photos and estimate to the Comfort Zone directly via e-mail. 

The consumer waited for a few days after sending the e-mail. He tried contacting the firm and was unable to speak to anyone. He constantly reached voicemail.

The consumer received a call about a week ago from [REDACTED] asking for photos. She stated that they only received the estimate. 

The consumer mailed photos to the company on 03/08/16 via registered mail. 

The consumer is waiting to hear back from the company. 

The consumer has the damaged heater at his home.

productDescription: Electric coffee maker
incidentDescription: We purchased a new Keurig coffee maker, from a local store, on 12/21/15.  The product was first used on 12/25/15 and was used once a day until 3/3/16.  One week prior to the incident, there was a faint smell of something burning in the house, but the problem could not be pinpointed.  On the morning of March 3rd, the Keurig coffee maker would not turn on.  As the machine was about to be unplugged, it was noted that the end of the power cord was melted.  After unplugging the cord, it was obvious that there was burning that had occurred. The outlet itself had a black burn mark, and the wires behind the outlet were burned back approximately 3 inches.  It was at that time that I did an internet search on Keurig and found that we were not the first to experience this issue.  Keurig was notified immediately of the defect.  They claimed they had no prior knowledge of this ever happening with one of their machines and would have FedEx to my home within the hour to pick up the defective machine; this is where red flags went up.  There are dozens of posts regarding this unit starting fires, some in which the entire house burned.  There are even more posts from customers that are on their 5th and 6th Keurig coffee makers because they stop working.  Keurig knows there is an issue, and it's a serious safety issue, yet their response is to sweep it under the rug, collect the defective machine and send the customer a new one in hopes that they will keep their mouth shut.  Well, that does not work for me. If a company is knowingly putting people in harms way and refusing to do anything about it, I will make sure the proper people know.  They did tell me they were going to send an engineer to my home to inspect the machine and outlet, but as the scheduled day approached, they changed their minds.  We are now at a stand still, and in the meantime, millions of people have these units in their homes and offices and have no idea that they could potentially be in danger of losing everything.  These machines are defective and need to be recalled before someone gets hurt.

productDescription: 5 Color LED Self Balancing Scooter Mini Smart Electric Hoverboard W/ Bluetooth Speaker
incidentDescription: I ordered a hoverboard over Thanksgiving and received it approx Jan 15th and have been trying to diagnose the problem since.   I thought it was a charging issue. I am located in Bermuda and could not send the product back to the US because of the hold on shipping the product. I finally found someone on island that had experience with troubleshooting them.  First he did not want to open the product because it looked like it had been already tampered with (missing screws and a variety of screws used.) Once the retailer was contacted, even though i had been in contact since it would not turn (Jan 16th) on even with the specified charging time, she advised me on Feb 2nd they became aware of that somewhere in the shipping process they the product was being opened.  In any event my technician opened the product and called to say that I would not be pleased with the inside of the machine. .  He said it is a huge fire risk as is and not willing to take that risk. The wires connected to both ends of the battery and motherboard are damaged (hot glue and kinks).  He said the hot glue will melt with every charge and cause damage. There is a chip on the board that he has never seen on any board and it is not connected to anything. It was wrapped around other wires.  He said of all the various boards he has worked on, none have had any hot glue used or been so complicated on wiring (unconnected or damaged).  He said he has never seen a battery so huge – all the boards he has serviced have had flat batteries.  He noted the missing screws and the incorrect screws used – varying types and not new screws as you can see the wear on the heads of them.  He was able to,  in my presence, to remove the screws with ease and he said that should not happen with electronics.  He also said the foot pads are not secure and they either are incorrect for the board or are on the wrong side.  The loose wires were also not connected to anything but hot glued down.  He said even if he fixed the charging mechanism, with all the hot glue used on almost every internal part, it would cause a fire and the heat would melt it and it would get into the motherboard etc and short out.  I just wanted to share the retailer/manufacturer and guts of the product.

incidentDescription:
I'm writing to inform you of a tragic mishap due to a manufacturing defect. My wife has had a Cuisinart 350 watt smoothie blender (Mod. CPB 300, Ser. 01023), for over two years which she has used almost every day. 
On the morning of Sunday August 16, 2015 she made her smoothie as normal. However, shortly after start up she heard an unusual sound and turned to find that the plastic blender cup had unscrewed from the blade holder and the ingredients were spewing all about the room. The powerful motor continued to run and the blade was exposed. The blade is positional (only goes into the blender one way) but has no safety interlocks what so ever. She, bowing to her instantaneous reflex came into contact with the blade with her left palm and was severely lacerated, severing 4 tendons and 4 or 5 nerves. I immediately transported her to [REDACTED] ER in [REDACTED]. where she received emergency care to include: 17 stitches, X rays, and a tetanus shot. The Bone and Joint Center of [REDACTED] was contacted and surgery was scheduled. We had a consultation on the 17th and the surgery on August 18, 2015. The surgery required 3 hours at which time tendons were repaired and nerves reattached. We have been informed that she will be in physical therapy for 6 to 9 weeks and probably scared for life. In addition, she will have limited use and sensitivity of at least two fingers. We blame the blender and its total lack of safety interlocks. Her medical bills will soon surpass $25,000, not to mention her pain, suffering and psychological trauma.

incidentDescription: I put my then almost 5-month old baby in his Davinci Kalani 4-in -1 convertible crib for a nap. About 10 minutes later he started screaming so I went in to check on him and his leg had gotten stuck between the slats on the crib. He could not get himself out because his thigh was wedged in the gap. This happened several times over the next few months including when he could roll over and stand up in hopes he could free himself. This was not the case. One incident he had both of his legs stuck pointing out the front of the crib between the slats. I had to stop putting him in it. He had some red marks on his leg but nothing more serious.  Had I not heard him though he could have easily broken his leg or cut off the circulation.  I'm not blaming the crib company because I know they conform to spacing standards. I'm asking the standards be re-evaluated. I've read a lot of people have had problems with their infants getting stuck, not just in this model crib but several others.  Or, since crib liners are not recommended, maybe a suggestion or article on the web site how to prevent this. I imagine many people now have cribs they will not use until toddler stage.

incidentDescription:
The power bank was purchased from a vending machine, which was located inside of a restaurant.  It is battery powered and it takes 1 battery, but the consumer is not sure of the size.  The bank can be plugged into an electrical outlet and it will recharge the battery that is inside of it.

The consumer's 14 year old son placed the power bank in an open area of the headboard of his bed.  The power bank was "not" plugged into a wall outlet at the time.  The consumer is not sure how long it was there prior to the incident and nothing was connected to it at the time.

The power bank make a loud popping sound and the consumer's daughters, who were in a different room, heard the noise.  It resembled a firework sound.  The power bank began to emit smoke and sparks flew from it.  Then it caught fire.  The son ran downstairs to get his mother (the consumer).  One of the consumer's daughter grabbed a waste basket from a nearby bathroom and filled it with water.  Then she and the consumer threw the water onto the power back.  There was charring to the headboard of the bed.  The consumer said that approximately 90% of the power bank is burned and discolored.  A spark flew onto the son's arm, but thankfully, he was not injured.

*  The consumer noted that was no information included with the product's package about potential hazards or overcharging the product.

The consumer has been attempting to locate contact information for the manufacturer, but since the product was made in China, it has been difficult.

productDescription: Cooling Heater
incidentDescription:
This caller is reporting that she purchased a Dyson Cool/Heater from QVC November 11 2015.

Around mid January 2016 the caller was sitting in her family room when her smoke detector sounded, she returned to the room where the unit was located and saw that the unit and her entire wall were both on fire. The submitter noted the unit was not on fire - the cord and socket were on fire.

She called the fire department. The submitter also noted she pulled the plug out to the wall and fire went out, then she called the fire department.

She contacted an electrician to inspect the wall electrical socket and replace it since it was burned.

The electrician informed the caller that the fire had not begun in the wall socket but by the heater that was plugged into it.

There are no injuries being reported.

The caller contacted the manufacturer, sent them the cooler/heater which they say they have disposed of when the caller told them she wanted it returned.

The manufacturer $257.77 and new Dyson AM09 Hot & Cool Jet Focus but the caller is afraid to have another one of their products in her home.

The submitter added she also requested many times a report of what was wrong with socket as they claimed that the problem was not the machine. The submitter stated she was told "we [FD] don't do that.."

incidentDescription: On January 18, 2016 my husband  was in our basement and was preparing to change our car's head light.  He was about to use a flashlight with a lithium ion rechargeable battery that is intended to be worn on one's head.  As my husband was lifting the flashlight to his head he turned on the flashlight and the battery exploded.  The explosion sounded like a bomb.  I was upstairs with my children and thought the noise was one of our basement windows shattering.  I came down to investigate what happened and saw my husband in shock and complaining of ear pain and grabbing his chest.  He had a burn on his chest; the chemicals had gone through his shirt.  Scattered on the basement floor and carpeting were tiny remnants of the battery.  There was a strong odor in the basement.  I contacted the fire department and they removed the pieces of the flashlight and battery.   They took up our carpet and removed it from the basement.  The fire department sent emergency medical staff who advised my husband to go the emergency room.  I brought my husband to the emergency room and he had a chest x ray and his ears examined.  My husband's chest x ray was negative but he was having ringing in his ears.    My husband visited an ear nose and throat physician assistant who ordered a hearing test.  The hearing test results showed considerable hearing loss in my husband's left ear. The physician assistant prescribed oral steroids to my husband and advised him to come back for a follow up appointment in two weeks.  My husband is still having hearing loss in his left ear, ringing in the left ear ,sensitivity to loud noises and generalized headaches.

productDescription: 6 quart programmable slow cooker
incidentDescription:
I bought my Hamilton-Beach slow-cooker 12/18/2016 at Wal-Mart in Concord, NC at their Concord Commons store. The CPC bar code number: 40094 33963 The box described it as a 275 watt cooker, type SC26 made in China.

I used it without incident according to the instructions 3 times. The 4th time, the ceramic pot cracked around the entire oval circumference of the shell and the bottom separated from the pot in one piece. I cut my finger slightly pulling the two big sharp ceramic pieces out of the metal shell. More importantly, under other circumstances, I might have cut myself very badly. I might also have burned myself badly. The leaking food juices might or might not have shorted out the electrical heater element in the metal shell (I don't know how well protected they are from liquids).

Sequence of events:
The ceramic pot appeared OK when I went to use it although I cannot rule out the existence of a possible unseen crack. It was clean and at room temperature. I poured into it the contents of a large casserole dish of cold meat, beans and vegetables I'd just taken out of the refrigerator; this just about filled the pot. I then ladled four small, drained, chopped, boiled onions on the top of the these other contents and mixed everything with a metal spatula. The slow cooker was completely full. Several minutes later, I went to plug in the appliance but I noticed brown juice flowing out the bottom. I opened it up and found the problem I described above. I did not plug in the appliance.

I took pictures. I have also saved the pieces for inspection. I'm an engineer with a little knowledge of glass and ceramics. I think this was a brittle fracture. There was a thermal gradient between the large mass of cold food and the small amount of hot onions on top, but I believe mixing the onions ingredients quickly reduced any gradient. The mixing I did was fairly gentle and I did not scrape the pot - I lifted the ingredients up from the bottom several times.

Whatever I did to cause this was well within the operating envelope one would expect for such an appliance -- most people are probably rougher with stuff.

This should be investigated as a hazard to users and a recall considered.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription:
Revlon 1875W Ionic Styler Hairdryer
Model RV474
Distributed by Helen of Troy L.P.
incidentDescription: On April 21, 2015 at approximately 8:15 p.m., I purchased a Revlon hairdryer from Walgreens store #[REDACTED] at 1300 Hazelwood Drive in Smyrna, Tennessee, model number RV474 for $19.99 plus tax.  A copy of the receipt is attached hereto as Exhibit 1.  A photograph of the hairdryer in its original packaging is attached hereto as Exhibit 2.   I left the hair dryer in its original packaging until the next morning, the morning of April 22, 2015.   At approximately 7:20 a.m., when I was ready to dry my hair, I unpacked the hair dryer, removed the plastic piece covering the prongs of the plug, plugged it in and turned on the hairdryer.  Immediately flames shot out of the front of the hairdryer where the air comes out.  Four separate burning particles flew out of the hairdryer and landed in three separate locations: one inside a basket near my vanity, two on the edge of a wooden vanity seat, and one on the bathroom floor.   The particles were not simply smoldering, but were actually actively burning with flames present.  I extinguished the particles that I could find immediately, (the one on the floor and the two on the vanity seat) and discovered that each burning particle was a tiny metal ring that had obviously shot out of the dryer.  I was aware of a burning smell, and upon further investigation found the fourth particle that had burned a hole through the side of the basket near my vanity.   I immediately unplugged the hairdryer for fear of injury, and was afraid to use it.   After attempting to clean the burned areas, repackaging the hairdryer, taking photographs of the damage, and locating my receipt, I plugged my electric toothbrush into the same socket of the same plug, and there were no issues, confirming to me that there was no problem with my outlet, and that the flames were a result of a faulty and dangerous hairdryer.  Moreover, I recently had an electrical inspection by a certified and licensed electrician, in which no problems with the outlet in which the hairdryer was plugged were discovered, further underscoring the certainty that the damage was the result of a faulty, defective, and dangerous product.

productDescription: LP Heating stove
productType: Gas or Lp Heaters, Other or Not Specified (392)
incidentDescription:
Our Jotul Sebago DV 400 (serial number 031793) started leaking gas on 1/28/2016 so we shut it off and called our dealer Woodburning Warehouse in Watervliet NY. They weren't able to come until 2/4/2016 so the stove remained off. When the repairman came he spent several hours trying to 
find the leak and finally said it has to be the gas valve as everything else checked out ok. I asked him how often the valves failed and he said rarely. He has worked 28 years repairing stove and has only replaced 3 or 4 in all that time and never in one as new as this (14 months old). Something failed internally in this valve. I talked again to the shop next day about this and they informed me they just had a call from another customer had had called about their Sebago 400 DV leaking gas.
   It appears to me they may have have batch stoves with bad valves that  are are prone to failure after a short time. This problem obviously can lead to catastrophic and fatal consequences if not addressed by the manufacturer.

productDescription:
6 quart pressure cooker.  "Denmark tools for cooks".
TTU-Q4907
UPC: 048552450881
incidentDescription:
Tonight, my wife, [REDACTED], was cooking chicken in this pressure cooker. She had stepped away from the kitchen for a few minutes only to come back to find fluid rushing out from the joint of the pot to the lid, shooting downward along side of the pot and fueling a developing fire on the range burner.

I immediately cut power to the range via garage circuit breaker, and sprayed water from the kitchen sink hose onto the flames to put it out.  The house was filled with smoke.  Presumably it was grease from the chicken that was fueling the fire.  

This is not the first time that this pressure cooker has acted strangely, but it is the most concerning.  In the past, [REDACTED] has finished cooking with this pressure cooker, carried it over to the kitchen sink where she would let cool water run over it in order to accelerate the cooling of the cooker so that it can be opened.  Several times when she has done this, suddenly fluid would start to shoot down from the pot-lid joint, and harmlessly into the sink.  

There is a definite design problem with this pressure cooker.  It is very dangerous.  Tonight's incident could have easily caused our house to burn if not caught when it was.

productDescription: KitchenAid 5 qt tilt head stand mixer
incidentDescription:
I am writing this letter regarding a recent experience with my KitchenAid Artisan series 5 qt tilt head stand mixer. Our family enjoys our mixer and uses it frequently without any mechanical problems. However, I have a serious safety concern with this particular model. When the head of the mixer is in the up position there is an open area that can easily entrap fingers resulting in injury. This was our recent experience with this particular mixer. There appears to be no safety mechanism or guard to prevent injuries from this area of the mixer.  The top of this mixer is extremely heavy and the weight contributes to injury.

               I was recently using my mixer and just lifted the head to remove the bowl. The head of the mixer is very heavy and easy to engage in the downward position. Since the tilt head does not have an upright locking mechanism my son was easily able to entrap his finger in this open area of the mixer. The entrapment combined with the downward force of the mixer head nearly resulted in a complete amputation of his finger. He required treatment at the local emergency department and received sutures from one side of his finger to the other. I believe that KitchenAid should look for some type of safety mechanism for this device to prevent future injuries of this nature. My daughter was also present during this incident and witnessed the near amputation, severe laceration and large amount of bleeding her brother suffered from the mixer. She really enjoyed helping to make various things using the KitchenAid mixer. However, she no longer wants to come anywhere close to the mixer for fear of the same injury occurring to her.

                I feel that this design can easily result in injuries for people of all ages. I am disappointed that this company did not see this as a design flaw or safety concern. As much as I hate that we experienced this event, I hope that our experience will raise awareness so that KitchenAid can work towards a solution that would prevent this type of injury to future consumers.

brand: KitchenAid coffee maker Model # KCM1110B Serial # WF23002531
incidentDescription:
KitchenAid coffee maker Model # KCM1110B Serial # WF23002531 

Coffee maker failed to shut down after brewing.    There is a switch with a small blue indicator on the front of the unit that is used to wake-up the device, to initiate a normal or a timed brew cycle.  (This indicator is being pointed as it is a visual indicator of the units status).  Normally and in all previous usages the coffee maker would turn off the heating element after brewing and plus approximately 2 hours warming time the blue indicator would then be turned off.  

We had made a pot of coffee, filled our "to-go" cups, turned off the unit and left the house.   When we returned four hours latter and we started to make another pot, I noticed the pot and burner were still very warn to the touch even though the heating indicator was extinguished.  After adding water to the reservoir the brew process started without the unit being turned on.  Not believing what I was seeing I unplugged the unit (app. 2 minutes), when I plugged the back in the brew process restarted once again without the switch being depressed nor the indicator being lit. This morning when I plugged in the unit it started to brew, without being enabled via the switch.  And once again  we returned home we tried for a fourth thing... same thing happened, plug it in and brewing starts. 

The concept of having a 1000watt heat source sitting on my counter top, generating hear for hours on end is worry sum as it could easily start a fire.  

I will admit that the owners manual states "Unplug coffee maker from outlet when not in use and before cleaning. Allow to cool before putting on or taking off parts"  If it should be UNPLUG WHEN NOT IN USE!!! Why then would it come with a clock and a brew timer? 

I am currently testing the unit (fourth test) to see if it continues to misbehave... After this test, the unit did act as it should have, after 2.5hrs the blue light was extinguished and within .5 hrs the heating plate was cool to the touch. 

Bottom line is that we no longer trust it not to burn down our home.

The incident occurred within about 5 minutes of me getting up to go to the bathroom and get something to drink in the middle of the night and when I returned to bed. There was no smoke when I left the room, and when I returned the hallway and bedroom smelled of burning paper/active fire and there was a haze of smoke in the bedroom. The fan motor was about one foot away from a wall and heat vent, which were also very hot as a result of the fan smoking/burning. I woke up my wife and she ran the fan outside, which was very hot, even on the plastic handle, while it was smoking and threw it in the snow, ending the incident. We were operating this fan in a safe manner and have had box fans for years without problems. Aside from a very minor amounts of dust on the blades, the fan was clean and in good condition and only about three years old from our time of purchasing it. I have no doubt in my mind that had I not happened to be up, it would have caused a house fire and was on its way to doing so. We're not negligent or stupid when it comes to fire or household appliances. We operate things safely and have never had an issue like this with any other fan we've owned.

incidentDescription:
In December 2015, I Purchased a KRUPS Espresso Coffee Maker Model / Type XP100, REF: XP100050 / 1P0-4513.  I have owned and operated other brands of steam type Espresso Coffee Makers for over 25 years.

In March of 2015, I unpacked the KRUPS and put it into service in my home using it without incident approximately twice weekly. I clean it thoroughly after each and every use.  My preferred brand of coffee is [REDACTED] Espresso Roast – ground for me by [REDACTED] specifically for use in a steam Espresso Coffee Maker.

On January 14, 2016, I prepared coffee as I normally do, turned on the KRUPS Espresso Coffee Maker; 2 or 3 minutes later the unit exploded propelling shards of glass, hot coffee, and hot coffee grounds a distance of 15 feet, covering the walls, floor, counters, appliances, and my back. 
Thankfully I had my back to the explosion.  It took nearly 2 hours to clean up the mess and I cut my hand on the broken glass in the process.

On January 15, 2016, I called KRUPS Customer Relations and was told:
1-	There are no safety concerns with this Espresso Coffee Maker.
2-	I probably caused the problem by tamping the coffee too hard or not cleaning the basket thoroughly (untrue and ridiculous).
3-	While there is a safety valve on the water tank, there is no safety valve on the brewing mechanism, that is why it exploded.
4-	KRUPS would not replace the Espresso Coffee Maker under the two year warranty.
5-	KRUPS would send me a shipping label to send the Espresso Coffee Maker to a service center for repair. I would need to pay for packaging of the unit. 

I feel that under the circumstances, I am entitled to either a complete NEW Espresso Coffee Maker or a complete refund of $100. If I had been facing the unit when it exploded, I would have been severely injured. Luckily I sustained only a cut to my right hand and a sizable mess to clean up.

productDescription: Yellow "MaxiZum" Zumaround electrically motorized scooter/kickbike/foot bike with 26" bicycle wheels, approximately 250 watt, Chinese made geared hub motor, unknown controller, two 36-volt, 9 amp-hour lithium ion "bottle" batteries that may be made by Panasonic but have no manufacturer ID other than a "Zumaround" sticker.
incidentDescription:
I was riding my new "MaxiZum" electrically motor-driven "scooter" (with 26" wheels, more properly a footbike or kickbike) westbound in a Class II bike lane when I had to merge into the main traffic lane at a point where the road narrowed to allow for reconstruction of a mid-block crosswalk near our main fire station.

It was the Thanksgiving holiday weekend, so no work was in progress. Thee excavation was covered by a smooth steel plate and the transition from the existing pavement to the plate was eased by a gentle, shallow, smooth graded asphalt ramp with no lumps, bumps, gaps or irregularities.

The line of traffic was moving very slowly and I had plenty of time to observe the construction work as I approached.  With nearly 60 years of cautious and safe cycling experience, and the knowledge that the footbike had an advertised ground clearance of 4 inches, I judged that the very minor elevation change was perfectly safe to ride over at a slow speed. I was wrong.

As my front wheel mounted the incline, two tube ends projecting below the floor frame of the footbike grazed and dug into the asphalt, bringing the MaxiZum to a sudden halt and slightly lifting the rear wheel from the ground and causing it to rotate, airborne, to the right, around the axis of the bike's headset.  I was able to quickly step/jump off to the right and prevent myself from falling all the way to the ground, although my right knee did collapse, resulting in a strained/sprained medial collateral ligament, which is still a bit sore.  following traffic, also moving slowly, was able to stop without hitting me, and I dragged myself and the scooter/footbike off to the side of the road. Not a catastrophe, but it certainly would likely have been if I and/or following traffic had been traveling faster.

When I got home, I put the footbike on a bench, removed the footboard, and inspected the (minor) damage to the tubes that had contacted the pavement.  With the footboard removed, I was also able to measure the actual ground clearance of the device.  As can be seen in the photos I took (if I can find a way to share them with you), the tubes that struck the asphalt provides less than 3" of clearance.  Further, a travel-limit tab on the center kickstand measured about 2 5/8 " ground clearance, but it also shows signs of having struck the pavement (perhaps when the airborne rear wheel came bouncing and sliding back to Earth), so it's quite likely that the original clearance there was even less.

The close examination I was able to do on the bench made it clear that it is not only ground clearance per se that makes this motorized (to approx. 20 mph) device unsafe to operate on US streets and paths with the usual bumps, uneven pavement, projections, etc.  The very design and geometry of the frame makes it dangerous, as well.  The near-90-degree junction of the vertical tube cluster with the floor frame, combined with tube ends and other projections *below* that frame, means that almost any contact with an irregularity or projection from the surface will be, effectively, a "head-on" crash.  With no leading curve or angle, and with the afore-mentioned projections below the frame, and with no skid plate, there is almost no chance that the footbike would be able ride/slide over even the slightest obstacle.

When I contacted the manufacturer, he (trying to prevent me from filing this report, no doubt) promised a detailed written response within a few days.  He then said he was going to Israel for a couple of weeks but would try to write when he was there. From Israel (presumably) he told me he had been busy, but would try to write "soon."  When he returned from Israel, he again promised a letter in a few days, which started and email exchange in which he arrogantly assured me that the problem is with my expectations, not with his product.

Full disclosure: While waiting for resolution of this issue, I raised it in an online forum for scooter enthusiasts, without identifying the brand or model of the product (it turns out that some of the members of the forum, including the forum operator, are friends/customers of the manufacturer, so they probably knew which product I was talking about).  Virtually every response I got was, more or less "That's just how kick scooters are; you have to be constantly alert and ready to stop and dismount at the sight of any obstacle."  I tried to explain that is an unreasonable position to take when talking about a 20 mph motorized footbike, as big as a full-sized bicycle, that is advertised for use on the streets and will likely encounter minor obstacles frequently, and often be surrounded by auto traffic.  They just kept repeating themselves.

In the intervening period, I have test-ridden electric footbikes that have none of the inherent defects of the MaxiZum.  They have more than twice the ground clearance.  They have curved/angled junctions between the vertical members and the floor frame.  They have no projections below the floor frame.  They have skid plates.  They would have been ridden safely over the little construction rise that threw me from the MaxiZum without even noticing it.

Today, I contacted the seller.  He told me what the manufacturer and the forum members told me: that's just the way kick scooters are.

But, no matter how often they call it that, the MaxiZum is NOT a "kick scooter" -- it's a motorized, full-sized footbike.

I appear to be the only person who thinks the device is inherently dangerously flawed, so you may be tempted to just let this go.  Or you may simply not be able to investigate such a "minor" matter.  However, I am quite certain of this:

If very many people ride very many MaxiZum powered footbikes over very many miles of ordinary American roads and trails, there will be serious injuries and, probably, deaths.  How many will simply be a matter of how many scooters he manages to sell and how far the customers ride them.

productDescription: Dual Fuel Gas Space Heater (Non Vented)
productType: Gas or Lp Heaters, Other or Not Specified (392)
model: 32,000 BTU Blue Flame WDFT320-VF (Dual Fuel LP or NG)
incidentDescription:
I purchased and had installed Thermoblaster 32000 BTU Blue flame dual Fuel (Gas) heater in my garage this past weekend and found a issue with the unit that I believe is potentially extremely dangerous! This unit has 2 pilots one that is for natural gas and one for liquid propane. When the unit is started in the proper sequence for Natural Gas both pilots light and should stay on. The problem is when or if the Natural gas pilot goes off for what ever reason the LP gas pilot can stay and does stay lit. This allows the thermocouple to stay latched and in turn allows the main gas valve to open and for the gas to flow out. The problem is the LP pilot flame is smaller and located below the burner outlets as normally LP gas is heavier than air but because the unit is hooked up to natural gas which is lighter than air the gas rises quickly and does not ignite. In my case when the garage reached temperature the unit shut down and the natural gas pilot is going out constantly but the LP pilot stays lit. As stated this keeps the gas valve open and then the whole garage filled with gas to the point where we could smell it outside. I was very lucky that I went out to check on it when I did and that the gas did not build down to the point where the LP pilot could have ignited the gas. If it had I am sure it would have leveled my garage.I did speak to a couple of representatives at Thermoblaster at including the president and they recommended that the LP pilot be capped to prevent this scenario from happening and they even have procedure for doing this. I think this procedure would work but my concern is what if someone does not catch this issue in time. Someone or many could die using this product!
I was able to duplicate this issue a few times and have removed the heater and returned it to Lowes. I think it is also very important to mention that there are a couple of other reviews on the Lowes web site that indicate others have had the same or similar issues with this heater. They should be forced to remove the heater from the market until this safety defect is resolved. rous.

productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
I purchased the Breville BOV800XL at Bed Bath and Beyond and the unit was operating normally for about 12 months. I told everyone that would listen how much I loved this product, citing that the price was absolutely worth it. One day the unit was working correctly, the next day it wasn't. The LCD screen still functions properly, as do all the knobs and buttons, but upon pressing the start button (which activates the burners) electric popping can be heard and sparks can be seen shooting out from an area under the LCD panel. I had my hand on the side of the unit and it shocked me pretty hard.

I've actually never had an appliance do this, I certainly didn't expect it to happen from this device when it's a very high end purchase from a reputable company. (around $220). After looking into getting the unit serviced, I decided to call Breville to see if they'd take care of this issue since it is most certainly a design flaw, a VERY DANGEROUS design flaw. Breville's phone support suggested that I PLUG THE DEVICE BACK IN and try different settings to see if I could get the heating elements to heat up.

This is very irresponsible and dangerous advice, I honestly fear that this unit could catch fire if I plug it back in. 

Breville, you should stand behind your product. I've read other stories online where this exact same issue is happening to other people with the Rev. A version of this oven.

incidentDescription:

I am concerned that this could result in energization of the tray - a major problem, since the device is not grounded.

A second issue is that the rear of the oven gets so hot that it melts everything in contact with it - enclosing the power cable.  Our previous appliance even melted its own cable to the point that it suck to the oven and almost exposed the inner wiring to the oven housing - again a major problem due the lack of a ground.  I just noticed that the cable of the replacment machine is also melted - although not so badly that the wires are showing.

productDescription: Haan FS-20 Steam Mop
incidentDescription:
I have been using various brands of steam mops for quite some time, [REDACTED] and my Haan  FS-20 which I had used for a few months, on a regular basis of about 2-3 times a month.   Upon pulling out the mop one day, I noticed that it kept tripping my circuit breaker whenever I would plug it into a GFI outlet.   Thinking that my house was just old or that I had a lot of other appliances connected to those outlets, I moved the mop to a regular outlet where I was luckily able to clean the floors.   

Upon doing further research online later to determine what the problem may be, I came across several reviews from other users that the inside corrodes causing the electrical components to malfunction.   I decided to take apart the bottom of my mop (of which coincidentally they use special screws that are not easy to get off.  Must be to just have users purchase a new one instead of trying to fix a broken mop??) to find that the entire inside of the mop was in fact corroded.  While there is a small O ring around the hole where the steam comes out, it is obviously not enough to keep water from getting inside the unit and therefore corroding all the interior components in due time.   In reading other complaints where others have been injured by either using this mop in bare feet where water gets left on the floor or touching the metal part of the mop, I'm glad to say that I did not encounter this of which is rare as living in Florida we are in bare feet a long portion of the year.

I feel that this is a major design flaw or negligence in the part of Haan to ensure that a device that they sell is not better sealed or protected from water and electrical components to come into contact with each other and cause not only a short life span or issues with the mop, but also potentially dangerous conditions for a user!    I would hope that the new Haan mops are much better made however in looking for a new steam mop currently, I am very hesitant to put my hard earned money out for another Haan if they can allow these things to occur.

incidentDescription:
Was entertaining friends watching weekend bowl games.  As it was a bit chilly I brought out Kerosene heater to help keep guests warm.  When lit there was a fair amount of black smoke coming from the heater.  We waited a bit thinking it would burn off as it had not been used in a while.  The smoke got worse and started seeing flames shoot out the sides.  
At first I tried turning down the heater but nothing happened when I turned the knobs.  I then attempted to shut off the heater but the cut off valve fell off when pushed down (melted).  Flames got worse so moved the heater further away from guests and house.  
A friend grabbed fire extinguisher from house and we used on heater.  Flames went out but a few seconds later came back.  Then we sprayed again with fire extinguisher and same results.  
Finally moved further into the yard and watched as flames kept shooting out the top and sides.  We waited for the fuel to run out.  
As Kerosene heaters can be used indoors I am seriously concerned about these heaters.  
I purchased the heater in November of 2014.  Looking at the reviews for the heater on Amazon there are many, many complaints of the exact scenario I have outlined.  One reported major damage to home from the heater burning out of control and not able to shut off.

incidentDescription:
While pureeing some Fava beans (a very soft food) in my Cuisinart Prep 9 food processor, I began to hear a clanking sound. The puree, which I was preparing as a filling for dinner with my wife and two-year-old son, had small shards of sharp metal scattered through it. The product is only three years old, has never been abused, and has been used only lightly to moderately, usually with soft foods. I shudder to think of all the times I have made purees for my child, that on any of those occasions I could have failed to hear a clanking sound and served a possibly fatal meal to my baby.

I called Cuisinart, and they were not even willing to replace the flawed part, though I think I will be switching to a different brand anyway. Still, it is astounding that the only response offered to me by this dangerous company was an attempt to get more money out of me for a replacement of the same faulty part.

incidentDescription:
Breville Lift and Look Touch Toaster purchased 12/11/2015. First used 12/26/2016.
Design of toaster has buttons for operation on top of toaster towards the front. The buttons are approximately 1mm raised and only take very light pressure to activate which starts the toaster, lowers bread and turns on heaters inside. 
Due to the ease, location, and raised feature of the start button, it is very easy to inadvertently brush up against the button and turn it on. Even a child could do this. If a lightweight toaster cover, or anything else is on toaster at time, It will start a fire.

This is exactly what happened. A toaster cover was placed over toaster and just the weight of the lightweight cover had activated the start button and a fire ensued.

This would not have happened if the buttons were recessed, even by 1mm. There would have had to be direct pressure placed on it to activate the button.

Very dangerous design..

productDescription:
The product is called UWheels - it's a Hoverboard.  It's red and black and contains blue tooth and lights.  
Here's the description from their website:

• Get up to 15 mile travel range on just one charge
• 36 Volt 4.4A Samsung Lithium long-lasting battery
• 700 watts of power
• Fully charged in just  2 hours
• Maximum Speed up to 9.3 mph
• Up to 265 lbs maximum load
• Lightweight frame weighing just 24 lbs
• Bluetooth Speaker System that easily connects to your smartphone

UWHEELS are outfitted with high-quality gyro-tech computer sensors that are able to recognize weight differentiation. This state of the art technology helps the rider keep their balance and provides an easy and safe rider experience.
incidentDescription:
I purchased a Uwheels hover board for my husband in late October - he received it three weeks later even though they charged my credit card the minute I ordered it.  

The product is totally inferior. It started with a simple problem where the plastic covers popped off and could not be replaced.  Soon the problems became much more serious The Battery charger melted and was smoldering nearly starting a fire in my garage.  If you go to their Facebook page you'll see that many people have had the same experience with their inferior battery packs.

Third the product is unsafe.  We have another hover board from a different manufacturer that is not at all like this one.  With the other one when the battery is getting low it beeps and blinks and tells you the battery is getting low. It also simple slows down until it finally stops - a safe approach. The Uwheels on the other hand provides no warning. It simply goes from full speed to STOP! My husband was riding on it and it came to an abrupt halt!  He was thrown off the product and sprained his wrist.  

Fourth, I have been trying to return the product to no avail.  I submitted a ticket and they simply closed it out with no resolution. I have called both of their retail offices and nobody picks up the phone. I also called the VP Sales - no returned call there either.

This company needs to be STOPPED!  They are manufacturing UNSAFE products that will create fires AND hurt riders!
