productDescription:
Cuisinart 7 cup food processor Model # DLC- 10 STX Serial # 11010

Blade #FP-100 TX
incidentDescription:
This is a 7 cup Cuisinart food processor with a stainless steel blade. It was manufactured in China in 2011 and purchased approximately in 2013. It has been used very little as the blade is still as sharp as when new. We were pureeing a can of diced tomatoes when the blade simply broke. In looking at the unbroken part, I now see that the blade under the rivets that attach it to the round plastic base of the blade assembly is cracked under the two (of a total of 4) remaining rivets. It is clear that the four rivets that affix the blade itself to the round plastic part were pressed on using too much pressure. Cuisinart refused to replace the broken blade as it is no longer under warrantee.

Extremely sharp blade parts in the food one provides to one's family is an obvious safety hazard. This is a manufacturing defect and should be recalled with the blade replaced by a properly riveted blade.

productDescription: Xnow 2 hWheels Self Balancing Electric Scooter with Smart Key, Red
incidentDescription: My son's friend received a Hoverboard from his grandma for his birthday on November 20th, 2015.  He went to her house after school to pick it up.  She had ordered it on Amazon and it came in the mail earlier that day.  On the way home, they stopped by our home.  He ended up staying.  About four hours after he got the board, he plugged it in to charge in my son's room.  We went to his house to get stuff for him to spend the night, within an hour, we received a call from my husband that the house was on fire.  He heard a noise and thought it was my son and his friend rough housing.  He yelled at them to knock it off.  When the noise didn't stop, he got up to investigate.  He saw flames coming from underneath the door.  He kicked the door open and the hoverboard had exploded.  It was shooting fire, later we realized they were the burning batteries.  My husband carried the burning board through the house and threw it outside.  He went back to the room to put out the fire.  He then went outside to check on the hoverboard and it was still on fire.  He used the garden hose to put it out. He called 911.  The fire was out before they got here but we needed them for smoke removal.  The hardwood floor needs to be replaced, the walls fixed from the shooting batteries, the blinds melted and his futon couch was burned.  He also lost clothes and Xbox games that had melted.  My husband was seen in the ER for smoke inhalation.  If my husband wasn't home, the house would have burned down.

productDescription:
Revlon, Ionic, 1875 watt hair dryer.  It is turquoise in color.  Has two switches.  One for speed, and one for heat settings.  Along with a "cool shot" type button that allows you to give a shot of cold air, without changing the settings.  It came with an oval diffuser, which no longer stays on; and a lint cage that falls off regularly.

Model RVDR5036 Type VD781BL
incidentDescription:
Not long ago, my Revlon hairdryer started having some issues (the plug in had to be wiggled a lot for their to be a full connection to the outlet and maintain power).  So, I opted to replace it.  I chose another Revlon product, having been generally satisfied with my previous model (I actually bought that one twice).  Anyway, the replacement was a Revlon Ionic 1875W model, that came in a turquoise color.  

Recently, I started using the medium setting vs. the high setting, so that I can hear my radio when getting ready in the morning.  Over the last few days of use , I noticed that the "high" setting, was actually feeling more like "medium".  The button was set to high flow, but was not coming out as such.

The hair dryer also started intermittently changing heat settings, it would be warm, then hot, or give me a shot of cold, or whatever it felt like doing.  No discernible pattern, that I could tell.  The issue only happened a few times, and I couldn't make it repeat on purpose.  But, I did start paying attention to it, because it was just weird.

Today, everything changed.  I typically dry my hair most of the way without styling tools, and just when it's almost done I use a round brush to style it.  I started with the front bang area of my hair, everything seemed fine.  Two round brushes further back, I noticed a smell.  Burnt smell.  I turned the hairdryer off and set it down.  Started brushing my hair and saw a big glob of hair on my brush.  Pulled it out and put it in the sink.  Started running my fingers through my hair, and pulled out chunks (that somewhat resemble a hair extension with glue on the root end).  Chunks were coming out, strands were coming out, and tiny pieces were breaking off as I touched the root ends of my hair.  It was very alarming.

I have very fine, very thin hair.  I'm in my mid 40's, so I'm well aware of how to blow dry & style my hair.  I know not to stay in one spot for long, and I didn't do that in this case either.  I wear my hair just past my shoulders (appx 2.5-inches), in a slightly layered style.

I have a small spot just above the bang line where the hair was burnt down near the scalp.  That area is maybe an eighth of an inch long.  Another area, which is quite a bit larger, is at the top/crown of my head.  Most of that hair is burned down to less than half of an inch long.  There may be a few strands longer (hard for me to see).  But, the area itself is approximately the size of golf ball.   The third and largest area, is damaged and still falling out.  The best way to describe location on this, is half way between the crown & nape of my neck.  In this area, the hair is damaged, and like I said, still falling out.  The most disturbing part about this last area described, is that I hadn't started styling that area yet.  So, either a spark flew down from when I was styling the top, or it flew up when I was doing a general dry and moving all around.  Either way, it's scary to thing that this incident could actually have been worse.

I have emailed Revlon, and am awaiting their specific response (only had an auto email so far).  

This unit isn't that old - a few months or so?  I'd have to try to locate my receipt, and I'm not sure that I have it.  It's not a heavy use item either.  One person usage, approximately 5 days a week for 5-10 minutes off & on.  I don't dry & style at the exact same time.  And, I rarely use on the weekends.  So, in my opinion, this is a potentially serious & dangerous equipment malfunction - not user error.

I would like to recommend investigation and recall of this unit.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

Model is 4644 30111 0484
 serial number is 101CWI J0006 019447A
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
I purchased a Kenmore 4 Burner plus side burner LPG Grill (P/N 307010030) manufactured by Char-Broil from Sears on 3/7/12. At the beginning of it’s third grilling season, Spring of 2015, I put some pieces of chicken on the upper rack to slow bake using the two end burners on low. The temperature was reading about 350 degree F. After about ten or fifteen minutes, I went inside to answer a phone call. I returned a few minutes later to find the grill and the side of my house ablaze. 
Severe and unexpected corrosion/rusting of interior parts had deposited a heavy layer of rust and rusted metal debris covering the drip pan and causing fat to accumulate, rather than be conducted to the center drip cup and removed. A large hole had rusted through along the back edge of the pan, through which an updraft intensified the flames as they blew out the gap between the back edge of the cover and the rear top edge of the firebox, quickly igniting the wooden siding of the building. 
I filed a complaint with Char Broil. Customer service requested photos, and more photos, but three months later, has not settled my case. In fact, it is no longer accessible to customer service, who claimed it has been removed from their system to “corporate”. I believe this product is poorly designed and manufactured, and is a severe fire hazard, and a danger to the public.

productDescription: See Information Below.  It is a Purple Revlon Ceramic / Tourmaline/ Iconic / 1875 W Hair Dryer.
incidentDescription:
Revlon Hair Dryer Model RVDR5141 has a risk of electrocution.

We started using this hair dryer about one month ago.  As we used it, the motor started cutting out more and more frequently.  I thought that there must be a loose connection inside, until I saw smoke and sparks where the electrical cord entered the rubber stress relief tube on the handle.  The electrical  cord was about to break in two.  Bare copper wire was exposed from both leads.

I started to re-package the hair dryer in its original box and noticed that the box will not close unless the power cord is bent at a sharp 90 angle where the cord enters the stress relief tube.  I have surmised that there are two problems.  1.)  The extension cord insulation is made of a more brittle and less flexible material than other cords, and 2.)  The box the hair dryer is packaged in is too small and forces the power cord to be bent severely, in order to close the box.  This severe bend essentially breaks the cord insulation.

Please take action to force this company to issue a RECALL.  Many other consumers are experiencing the same problem and nothing is being done about it.  Revlon is clearly not taking any responsibility based upon their corporate BS response.

incidentDescription: We awoke this morning to a very strong smell of propane gas. A spark, perhaps a static spark from clothing, could have touched off an explosion and fire. This is the second time this has occurred. We believe that the burner controls are too easily turned on in such a situation and are extremely dangerous. We believe that there should be a positive stop of the controls in the off position that would require some explicit action to overcome. This event, and the previous occurrence, scared us deeply. We believe this to be a design flaw and a very serious safety risk.

productDescription: Cuisinart "Total Touch" Convection Toaster Oven Broiler, model CTO-140PC
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
brand: Cuisinart "Total Touch" Convection Toaster Oven Broiler
incidentDescription:
On Nov 20, 2015, I was preparing toast with my Cuisinart "Total Touch" Convection Toaster Oven Broiler, when I heard the oven make an odd electrical sound.  Upon examining it, I noted that the oven appeared to have shorted internally - I could see flames inside, and smoke started billowing out of the top vents.  I immediately unplugged the product, and took it outside - where the smoke continued.  I poured water on the product (not a good move for an electrical fire, I now recognize), and finally noted that all activity with it, had stopped.

There was no previous damage noted to the product, and it had performed quite well for the several years we have owned it.  To see this event take place - risking my home, and the health and safety of my 5-year-old son especially – was very troubling.

I called Cuisinart at 800-726-0190, and reported the issue, providing my model and serial number:
 
Model: CTO-140PC
Serial: 30412

The agent [REDACTED] took my name, address, and phone number, and indicated I would be contacted by corporate in two to three days.

However, a week later, I still had yet to hear anything back.

So, I called them again on Nov 27, 2015 at the same number.  The agent this time,[REDACTED] , took my name and phone, again confirmed the model and serial, and asked for details of the situation.  As before, she asked if there was any injury or property damage.  I indicated "no", and indicated that I have photos and video of the results of the incident.

Apparently, NO RECORD of my previous call was available in their system. She asked for my address, and again logged my phone number.  Also asked for a email address - I provided them [REDACTED].

While on the phone, I also reiterated that the Cuisinart rep at Bed Bath and Beyond (on the previous Friday, 11/20) assured me that Cusinart Corporate would take care of the situation - no matter how long ago we purchased the product.

She (as [REDACTED] did before) indicated they would call me back within 2-3 business days.  I indicated my lack of confidence in this process, but she indicated she "guarantees" that someone will call me by Tuesday, Dec 1, 2015.

It is now after close of business on Tuesday.

I am obviously very concerned at the problem encountered with the product - but especially troubled by the lack of engagement of Cusinart.  They appear to have phone representatives who take down information, ask questions of the consumer to flesh out their report, and then completely ignore the resulting information.

I am therefore reaching out to the Consumer Products Safety Commission for assistance.  Not only do I want Cusinart to take this incident seriously, but I need them to answer as to why I've experienced so much frustration in simply trying to report the issue to them.

Please advise.

productDescription: Gas hose that links disposable propane cylinder to a a camp stove.
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription: I purchased a Brunton propane stove a couple years ago and the gas hose leaked from the over-pressure valve. Primus, the parent company sent me a replacement stove, a Primus Profile and hose. I was about to use the stove 2 days ago in below freezing temperatures in [REDACTED]. When I screwed the propane cylinder onto the hose, the over-pressure valve failed and a jet of propane came shooting out - same problem as with the first stove. It's pretty clear that the hose assembly has a sacrificial part in the over-pressure valve and that this part fatigues and eventually fails. Under normal use, the valve freezes due to the expanding propane gas, and my guess is that these freeze-thaw cycles are what fatigue the part and lead to failure. If someone were to leave the hose attached to the cylinder while they were camping, the valve could fail and fill a car or camper with propane. In addition, if the valve fails while cooking, the jet of propane could easily reach the flame of the stove about 2 feet away. I have the second hose that failed if you need to examine it

productDescription: Breville Lift and Look Toaster
incidentDescription: Our Breville Lift and Look Toaster self activate in the cabinet and caught fire.  We kept the unit in our appliance garage in the corner of our kitchen.  Monday morning my wife got out of bed and poured a cup of coffee.  A few minute later the house filled with significant smoke and the smell of wire was strong through the house.  The Battlefield Missouri Fire Department responded to help track down the source but never found anything so they told us to get our furnace checked out.  The fire had apparently went out where ever it was and the smoke in the house started to clear.   We called a local HVAC company who gave our furnace a clean bill of health ($73.00 charge).  About 5 pm my wife called me to tell me the furnace test out fine.  I told her to check every outlet in the house and check every device plugged into to those outlet as whatever had caused the problem may have just burned up.  When she got to the appliance garage the door would not roll up, but as soon as she attempted to roll it up smoke started to pour out and the fire started once again.  She determined the toaster had apparently activated itself.  We had to break into the cabinet as the plastic channel the roll up door used had melted closed.  When we finally go into the cabinet we found a box of coffee creamer had fallen over an was laying on the switch which apparently started the toaster.  The toaster is a total loss and the inside of the cabinet us burned up.  I had an incident once before when I accident touched the toaster getting something out of the appliance garage it activated itself but I was able to catch it.  This is a great toaster but it is no a safe design.   My wife does have photos of the toaster on her phone.

incidentDescription:
Text of Submitter's e-mail message dated September 29, 2015:

Subject: Formal complaint / recall required MotoTec 1600w Dirt Electric Skateboard DUAL MOTOR

I'm lucky to be alive writing this. Through walmart, I purchased the MotoTec 1600w Dirt Electric Skateboard DUAL MOTOR. After my 10th ride or so, I was riding down the street going 15/18 mph. I accidentally touched the top of the controller and hit the speed button. The wheels instantly locked up. You can imagine what happened next. I barrel rolled down the asphalt about 40ft. I have scrapes and road rash and internal bruises all over. I am an adventurous person and also an engineer. I know that these types of remotes need to have a failsafe in case buttons are accidentally or intentionally pressed. It should absolutely not lock up the wheels if I press ANY button. It needs to disable all buttons while the board is in motion. This is the worst safety oversight I have ever seen in a product. I am 35 years old. I cringe when I think of a kid using this, accidentally (or even intentionally) pressing a button and then possibly getting hit by a car. I very strongly urge you to stop selling and distributing this until this problem is fixed. You also need to notify those that have purchased it of this problem. This needs to happen immediately. Go ahead and test one, but if mine did it, others will do it too.

After pooring my second cup of coffee, I switched off (toggle on front of machine) the coffemaker and went upstairs.  About 4-5 minutes later I smelled a burning electrical/plastic odor.  When I went downstairs to investigate, acrid smoke was pouring out of the coffee maker.  I unplugged the unit and placed it outside.  I've been airing out the smoke to try to remove the smell from the house.

If I had not happened to be home, I believe this would have ignited the kitchen cabinetry and possibly destroyed my home.

I've spoken with Cuisinart customer service. They've offered to replace the machine with an alternate Cuisinart coffee maker.  I asked them if they wanted me to save the machine so they could analyze it for the problem.  They've asked that I cut the cord and send the cord back to an address in Arizona.  Instead, I think I'll play it safe and purchase a different brand.

incidentDescription: I have a Frigidaire dehumidifier model #FDL50S1 serial #KN90602955 with date code Feb 2009 manufactured by Gree.  There was a recall in 2013 for their dehumidifiers overheating and catching fire.  I called Gree on 9/12/13 and they said my dehumidifier was not part of the recall.  They gave me a reference #[REDACTED].  Last week I went down to my basement and smelled something burning.  It was the dehumidifier and it was smoking. When I tried to turn it off by the button on the unit it would not turn off.  I had to pull the plug out of the outlet to turn it off.  I called Gree today and told them what happened and she said the year 2009 dehumidifiers are not part of the recall, the recall only goes up to the year 2008.  I told her the same thing is happening with my dehumidifier as the ones already recalled, and she said she would have to send something to their other department and for me to call back in four weeks!  I think they need to put another recall out for year 2009 also!

incidentDescription: As my wife, newborn baby, and I were in the living room of our home, we heard a "crack" sound from the kitchen. When I went into the kitchen to investigate, I didn't see anything that had fallen on the floor or anything that seemed like it would have caused this sound. Then we heard a loud "bang" sound, in similar sound and loudness as firecracker or .22 caliber rifle. When I looked around, I saw that a Duracell Ultra M3 9 volt battery that I had removed a few days ago from a smoke detector (due to the smoke detector beeping as an alert that the battery voltage was reduced beyond usable condition) had exploded. The battery was sitting on our wooden kitchen table, not touching anything, and when I touched it, it was not hot or even warm. One of the inner "cells" was a few inches from the battery, and another one was visibly ruptured, still within the metal casing of the battery. This was a very scary incident as we didn't know if more "cells" would erupt, and it was frightening to us as we have a newborn child, and this could have been very dangerous if the baby was nearby when this occurred.

productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
Dear Customer Care:

My husband and I purchased a Brinkmann Elite Dual Sear Gas Grill from Home Depot on 05/03/14 for our family grilling needs.

On Saturday, 9/26/15 we proceeded to turn on the grill to pre-heat it prior to cooking our baby back ribs (no added oils, just dry rub) like we have done dozens of times before.

No sign of anything being wrong.  We put the ribs on, checked ribs at normal interval and turned them. When we went out to turn again , the entire grill was engulfed in black flame, the outer metal was bubbled and charred to black and white, the smell of burnt metal and plastic from handle and thermometer, etc. was strong, the heat was so dangerous we were grateful our children weren't outside playing or that the propane tank didn't explode and injure or kill anyone, the heat also blackened our outer stucco wall , and warped our window and melted seal to window.

I am a director for a marketing and advertising company and work with attorneys across all 50 states so I've seen cases involving gas grills and we could tell there was a defect in where the gas line runs through the grill.

We paid a total of $357.49 including buying the Premium Cover for the Grill.

We are routine in our cleaning of the grill in-between uses, we are responsible BBQ/Grill/Chefs and have a taste for high end, gourmet products. We made no error, this grill is dangerous.

I'm going to now turn this over to you to handle in the immediate, appropriate manner as you see fit.

I also typed this up in the customer service section of the Brinkmann site and only get an error message stating my message did not go through.  When calling you have to give your phone number and are placed in some sort of queue in hopes to be called back. Horrible service.

Thank you

[REDACTED]
Purchase Info: Receipt # 6964 06 99611 
Item Code: 039953529641 & 039953522161
Purchase Date: 05/03/14
Purchase Location: Home Depot, Newark, CA

productDescription: EcoHeater NA400S
incidentDescription:
Initially purchased 3 of these units for the bedrooms in our newly purchased home. Noticed a wisp of smoke staining the wall from one of the units. Assumed it was a defect so replaced with a 4th unit. These units were less than 18 months old when a second one failed. Fortunately there was someone home to unplug the unit before our home burned down. I contacted Eco-Heater along with pictures and spoke with an "I don't give a damn" rep, [REDACTED]. All they wanted was:

1. Please provide the serial number of your heater. The serial number is located on the carton and on the rear of the switch junction box. 
2. Please provide a copy of your proof of purchase.
3. Please let us know which model you have

I could not provide a complete serial number since part of it was burned off. I could not immediately provide a proof of purchase as I was out of state for 4.5 months. And the model was an easy one. Within the first 3 emails, all they asked for were those 3 things above and they tried to take possession of the burnt heater in an attempt to take away the only evidence. I told them I would not be sending them the unit unless they repaired my wall. After 17 emails, they refused to repair the damage to my wall and offered to replace the 3 units instead. Why would I want to replace the units when 2 out of 4 caught on fire (1 was in the master bedroom and the other in my infants bedroom)? They gave me the run around and I can only assume they were hoping I could not provide a proof of purchase (the accountant at the business I purchased them from was kind enough to go back into their database and provide the original receipt and purchase order). They have stopped replying to my emails and my numerous requests to repair the damage to my wall (not even both, just the one that is burnt in the picture).

I'm sure their customer service is great for little things. But when it comes to accountability and the well being of others, they could care less. I brought up the request to repair my really burnt wall in every email but they refused to acknowledge that it was their unit that damaged my walls. Dishonest, no accountability, do not deal with this company!

productDescription: Weber Genesis Silver A Grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
The Bottom fell out of my Weber Genesis Silver A Grill on (8/23/15). Burning
debris was scattered over my wooden deck. I was able to put the fire out using a
garden hose, but my deck has numerous burn marks.
Weber was contacted on (8/24/15). A full set of pictures and an explanation was
furnished to them via email on (8/31/15). I can furnish a copy of that
correspondence - Basically, it shows that rails that attach the bottom of the burn
box which are used to slide in/out a bottom hopper-like piece, are spaced to far
apart to properly secure this bottom piece. This, I consider to be a design flaw.
The Weber representatives [REDACTED], in a subsequent
telephone conversation (8/31/15), did not acknowledge this as being a problem,
saying that age was the issue, not design. [REDACTED] offered to replace the rails for
free even though they were only warrentied for 2 years. My response was that I
didn't think that that would solve the design issue.

I asked to speak to a Supervisor and was referred to [REDACTED]. We covered
much the same ground. He indicated that in addition to the rails, I might need to
replace the bottom pan. I would have to buy the pan. If the rails were to be
furnished to me for free, I would have to sign a product liability wavier. At this
point, I suggested that I believed the problem was serious and perhaps the
Consumer Product Safety Agency should be contacted. At no place in the
Owners Manual, does it suggest that there could be a safety issue relating to
parts of the grill aging and warping or that inspection for this problem should be
carried out by the owner. Basically, they denied that the product was at fault and
any damage caused to my deck was not their fault.
I would be must happy to furnish a copy of the email correspondence with Weber.

[REDACTED]

productDescription: Operate 110/120V AC heating appliance (1600 Watts max) from 220/240V AC. Use for hair dryers, steamers, electric curlers, immersion heaters, lamps and food bottle warmers, contact lens sterilizers, etc.
productType: Electric Wire or Wiring Systems (Excl Panelboards Recept (4062)
incidentDescription:
I plugged the converter into a European wall outlet (240VAC). I then plugged a USA surge-suppressor power strip into the converter's 110VAC outlet. (Note: As the converter's outlet was for 2-pronged plugs, I put a plug adaptor on the power strip's 3-prong, grounded plug.) Immediately after I flipped the power strip's switch to "on" there was a bright blue flash and a "poof" sound. The circuit breaker protecting that European outlet had tripped, apparently by my actions. The converter's internal fuse was not blown. I suspected that the power strip had been damaged, so I discarded it.

I acknowledge possible user-error. However, Samsonite should provide warnings to preclude such configurations. In my opinion, the converter's internal fuse should have blown first, preventing possible harm to the user/equipment/electrical supply. That the circuit breaker tripped first seems to indicate existence of some electrical sneak path that effectively shorted the outlet.

productDescription: Black & Decker Smart Brew Coffeemaker.  Model DCM2000B
incidentDescription:
This morning, after brewing a pot of coffee as usual in my Black & Decker 12 Cup Smart Brew Coffee Maker Part #: DCM2000b Type 1, the upper plastic handle retainer broke loose from the pot. productDescription: GREENWORKS 40-VOLT 20" DUAL-BLADE Li-ION BATTERY-POWERED LAWNMOWER, MODEL 25302.
productSubCategory: Lawn Mowers, Leaf Blowers and Lawn Vacuums
manufacturer: Greenworks Tools Inc. / Sunrise Global Marketing
incidentDescription:
The product in question is the GREENWORKS 40-VOLT 20" DUAL-BLADE Li-ION BATTERY-POWERED LAWNMOWER, MODEL 25302.

I bought this lawnmower, serial number GWT0510399-02/20/14, through Target Stores (on-line mail order, with order number 102506043369) on April 30, 2015.  When the lawnmower developed a serious safety problem (see below), a similar replacement lawnmower (Model 25302) was sent to me by Greenworks' post-sales support representative, Sunrise Global Marketing Inc., in June 2015.  The serial number of the replacement unit is GWT0510445-02/20/14. 

The total area of my lawn (total of front and back) is about 4,800 square feet.  This area is flat, except for a steep slope on one side of the front yard.  

I used the first lawnmower (above) several times, with no problem.  However, on or about May 21, 2015, I noticed that the bail was repeatedly failing to electrically disconnect the electric motor when the bail was released.  (The bail is the safety bar that must be kept depressed in order to maintain an electrical connection to the motor.)  When the bail is released, it is supposed to disconnect the electric motor.  Failure to disconnect is a SERIOUS SAFETY PROBLEM because, in the event that the lawnmower starts to slide back toward the user on a slope, the electric motor must be quickly stopped to prevent extreme injury.  When release of the bail fails to stop the electric motor, the only way to stop the motor is to manually pull out the circuit key, or manually pull out the battery, either of which takes a number of seconds to perform.  

I called the Greenworks support representative, Sunrise Global Marketing (telephone 888-909-6757) and explained the safety problem to them.  They made arrangements for a replacement unit (see above for the S/N) to be sent to me through their office in Mooresville, NC (telephone 704-660-2800).  I received the replacement unit on June 9, 2015.  The Sunrise Global Marketing reference number for this transaction is 1133884.  During June, July, and August, I used the replacement unit several times with no safety problem.  

Then, on September 19, 2015, while I was mowing my lawn, the replacement unit repeatedly displayed the same safety problem as the original unit: RELEASE OF THE BAIL WOULD NOT STOP THE ELECTRIC MOTOR.  

On September 19, 2015, I called Sunrise Global Marketing at telephone 888-909-6757, and also the retailer, Target Stores, and reported the latest safety problem.  I sought to return the lawnmower and obtain a refund.  Both organizations advised me that the lawnmower could not be returned.

incidentDescription: I’m writing this letter to let you know that I’m concerned about the safety of the product that I purchased. Throughout the years, the power cord got stripped and we put electrical tape over the area that the metal inside was exposed. Cord itself is so flaky that you bend the cord a little bit and it gets easily stripped that we had to kept wrap the electrical tape to fix the issue. The issue started within one year form the date I purchased it. I recently contacted Dirt Devil and explained what happened and they told me that since this vacuum was made in 2005 and it’s not within the warranty period, they told me to bring the vacuum to the repair shop to see if that issue was cause by the manufacture. But the catch is that if it’s not, the cost for the repair shop to even look at it cost $25 and it’s on us.  If it’s cause by manufacture, they would pay for the parts and repair. Dirt Devil told me that they offer 30% off of the new purchase if we decided to buy a new vacuum from them. Considering all the possible cost of fixing the existing vacuum, I decided to purchase a new one. Now I have a new vacuum cleaner and everything is fine, but it doesn’t erase the fact that I electrocuted by my previous vacuum cleaner, and that vacuum cleaner is not safe. If I had not quickly put my hand away from the cord, I could have been seriously injured. I should not take this type of thing lightly, so should Dirt Devil. I’m reporting this incident mainly because I don’t want the same thing happen to other people. I just think that particular cord wasn’t safe and Dirt Devil should do something about it. And to be nice, they should pay for repair shop to just take a look to see if it’s caused by faulty cord.

productDescription: Frigidaire 70 Pint White Dehumidifier, Model FAD704DWD, Serial Number KN50700665, manufactured in China and sold by Electrolux.
incidentDescription:
Purchased this Frigidaire Dehumidifier, Model FAD704DWD, Serial Number KN50700665, manufactured in China and sold by Electrolux, from Amazon on July 02, 2015.  Further tag information lists a "Service Model No." as FAD704DWD12, a UL Identifier as SA11089, Design Pressure of 300 Low, 560 High, RA10A:8.820Z and EEV-1.85L/KW.H, AMPS - 7.8A. I could not find  UPC Code. This dehumidifier was used on the first floor of our two story, wood frame, 2500 sq. ft., three bedroom home, to control indoor humidity during humid summer days and evenings. It was ordered from Amazon, July 02, 20125 and received July 06, 2015, unpacked, plugged in, and I set humidity level to 45%. The unit worked flawlessly until today, September 13, 2015, when this exact unit, Frigidaire Serial Number, KN50700665, appears to have experienced an electronic control failure accompanied by a mechanical failure, of some kind. Operating for several hours today, around 5:30 p.m., Sunday, September, 13, 2015, it suddenly began making a loud, low frequency, drumming kind of sound. I immediately investigated and discovered the unit's fan was no longer operating, the display read 30% instead of the 45% it was set for and it could not be turned off. The On-Off switch was unresponsive despite being pressed repeatedly. The unit continued making the noise described above and began to smell like it was overheating and very hot. The filter was perfectly clean and was not a contributor. The bucket was virtually empty and not a contributor. The only way to turn it off was to unplug it. The back panel of the unit felt hot and the entire unit smelled hot. The back panel is easily removed by loosening 7, highly visible, chrome plated, Phillips screws and simply lifting it off. I removed the back panel and the interior was spotlessly clean but the compressor was extremely hot, too hot to even lightly touch. I stood the unit up and let it cool down for about 15 minutes, then replaced the rear cover and all of it's screws, plugged it back in and pressed the On/Off switch. The unit immediately started up and operation was normal for approximately one minute when the display again reverted from the preset 45% to 30%, the exhaust fan again coasted to a stop, the loud, low frequency drumming sound returned and the On/Off switch was again inoperative and again it was not possible to switch the unit to an Off condition with the On/Off switch. This dehumidifier had electrically and mechanically, locked itself up in a way it could not be turned off, reset, or stopped, without unplugging it and the sound it was making is consistent with a motor driven mechanical device that has mechanically failed but the motor is still trying to drive it. Because the On/Off switch was again inoperative, I had to again unplug the unit to shut it down and it again smelled like it was overheating and excessively hot. I checked the exhaust fan for freedom of movement and it spun very freely when I used a small stick to move the squirrel cage, accessing it from the grill opening on the top of the machine, thus eliminating the fan as a potential source of the problem. 

We had received a rebate for a prior Frigidaire dehumidifier recalled by the Consumer Product Safety Division for causing several fires and were informed the unit had been redesigned and was no longer a fire hazard, so we used the rebate to purchase this replacement. However, the same fire hazard condition appears to still exist. If we had not been home to unplug the unit when it overheated from an obvious electronic and mechanical failure, I am 100% confident it had every potential to set itself on fire and potentially burn the house down. I have now completely lost confidence in the Chinese manufactured Frigidaire brand of dehumidifiers labeled as Frigidaire and sold by Electrolux, believing the unit we currently have to again be a serious fire hazard and a threat to occupant safety, not to mention property damage with the potential for catastrophic loss. In my opinion, based on real life experiences with these Frigidaire dehumidifiers, these units are a fire hazard, a threat to family/public safety, and should be removed from the market place.

productDescription: Propane Gas Grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
The consumer stated that an incident occurred with her gas grill. 

The consumer stated that her husband replaced the propane gas tank with a new, full tank. He turned on the grill and came into the house. The consumer's husband heard a pop and a hissing noise while he was inside of the house. The consumer's husband came outside to check on the grill and noticed that the grill was on fire.

The consumer's husband quickly yanked out the gas tank from the grill and put out fire with extinguisher. The consumer stated that the attachment in the grill that was connected to the tank was leaking gas.

The consumer's husband was able to avoid a more serious explosion by removing the gas tank. The consumer stated that the stainless steel panels and the top of the grill is scorched. The plastic control knobs are melted and do not work.

The consumer contacted Nexgrill to see if they can get replacement parts for the grill. The consumer was informed that they did not have anything available to provide them. 

The consumer's husband bought a hose from Amazon but it did not work on their grill. The consumer was able to get a refund for the hose from Amazon.

The grill does not work anymore.

The grill does not appear to be recalled.

productDescription:
Portable jumpstart (Whistler Jump 'N' Go)

Manufacturers phone number:  479-273-6012
incidentDescription:
Caller stated that she experienced a fire due similar problems of release#15-123.
Hazard:The jumpstart’s lithium battery can overheat and cause the units to melt, catch fire and ignite nearby items, posing a fire hazard to consumers.  She stated the product was being charged in the basement, she was alerted by the smoke alarm.  In her investigations she noticed flames as high as 3 feet.  She stated that she contacted the fire department who came out and contained the fire.  (See enclosed Professional Engineer report)    

Caller stated that the battery caught fire while it was being charged,  She stated that the property damages are estimated at $11,000 and that there was black chemical all over the  basement and everything in the basement and the electrical circuitry in the basement had to be completely repaired by professional electricians.  In addition, the freezer in the basement had to be replaced because its wiring is completely destroyed.  The house had to be professionally cleaned at the time of the call.  She stated that the retailer from whom she obtained the product was not mentioned in the recall.   There was no information identifying the model or serial numbers because it was burnt.  That information was found subsequently on the retailer's confirmation email.

The manufacturer was contacted when she found out there was a recall and she was informed that the recall was posted on their website.  The insurance company now have the product in their possession.  Caller stated that she was never contacted about the recall.

incidentDescription:

The consumer stopped using the drill and waved it around in the air to put out the fire. 

The consumer has tried to use the drill after the incident and the drill works. The consumer stated that he does not plan to use the drill because it is a fire hazard.

The consumer's drill does not appear to be affected by any recalls.

The consumer will contact the manf in regards to the incident.

productDescription: Smoke Alarm (Lithium Battery Operated)
incidentDescription:
The caller is calling from Pelham Fire Department. They are currently installing these smoke alarms under the Turn Your Attention To Fire Prevention program.

The caller stated that they have received 3 calls where the smoke alarms have gone off without any presence of smoke. They have to punch through the plastic tab and disconnect the battery to turn off the smoke alarm. The caller stated that users tried other ways to turn off the alarm (air out the area, reset, etc) but those ways did not work. The alarm gets destroyed when the plastic tab is punched through. The users are unable to use the alarms. 

The fire department purchased these alarms from Home Depot (Pelham, Alabama). The retailer replaced the alarms. The fire department contacted Kidde and was informed that they were not aware of issues with these alarms. 

The caller stated that their department has only received 3 calls, but they are aware of other area departments that have received many calls. The 3 calls they received were for the same model.

The battery comes sealed into the alarm. The caller believes that there is an issue with the battery that the manufacturer needs to acknowledge.

productDescription: 9-cup, Prep 9 Food Processor
incidentDescription:
I have a 9-cup Cuisinart Food Processor with a steel metal cutting blade. Where the rivets hold the blade to the spindle mechanism there were apparently stress cracks. When using the processor, a sharp piece of metal, about 4mm wide broke off and ending up in the batter of some scones. I bit down on the metal shard, and was able to spit it out before swallowing it.  When I examined the underside of the blade, I see that almost all of the other rivets had similar stress cracks. 

I called Cuisinart and it seemed to know all about this problem. Also, all over the internet, especially on Amazon reviews, there are reports of these stress cracks. I found these after the incident.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

incidentDescription:

My 9 year old son came and brought the larger pieces of plastic to me. The 5 year old emptied her water and ice out...when I asked her why, she told me that there was something floating in her water. I then took pictures of the ice and plastic because I realized that it was pieces of the ice maker itself that was being broken up and dispensing out with the ice.

I called Sears to check for any product recalls to no avail. They told me they would send a technician out on September 28 to check my problem.

I feel this is a huge safety hazard.

incidentDescription: Today, I noticed the smell of smoke in my house, and I traced it down to my basement. When I entered my basement, I found it heavily engulfed in smoke. I was able to trace the smoke back to our dehumidifier, which we purchased from Sears approximately 4 years ago. It has been 12 hours and we are still running fans to empty the smoke from the basement. I am extremely agitated that it would break in such a manner as to cause harm to myself and my family. If we werent home, the house would have burned down.    It is a Kenmore Elite Dehumidifier Model Number 42-99701. Thank you and we would appreciate a response.

productDescription: Grill Mark Stainless steel bar burner
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription: I replaced the original burner on my [REDACTED] [REDACTED]Bar-B-Que about 18 months ago with a Grill Mark stainless steel BAR burner. Part Number 81282 which I purchased at the local ACE hardware. I was cooking on the Bar-B-Que when suddenly the outside of the BBQ was engulfed in flames. Turning off the gas by using the burner control knobs on the front of the BBQ stopped the flames. There were no injuries or property damage. The burner was a "universal" burner so they used an accordion type gas pipe between the burner control and the burner. This type of gas pipe was used so it could be bent to fit any type of Bar-B-Que. Upon inspection I found that the gas pipe had broke at the connection on the bottom of the burner.

productDescription: Countertop oven
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
I have a Black & Decker oven, model #CT0650.  It recently gave me an electric shock by just touching the handle.  I unplugged it immediately   When my husband came home from work, he tested it with a meter and found that the outside of the oven was ”live.”  I contacted Black and Decker and received a phone call from [REDACTED].  He said there was nothing they could do because it was out of warranty but offered me a discount on a new one. I found this response very irresponsible.  This is a dangerous issue.  A discount or replacement was the least of my concerns.

(photos) Here is what we found after taking the side panel off the oven.  My husband, an electrician, believes the terminal block, which has melted, is underrated for this oven.  Without taking it apart further, his theory is, that during the melting process, one or more of the screws may have “floated” down making contact with the metal frame of the oven.  Even if his theory is incorrect, this should be of concern to someone!  There were no signs that this melting was accurring   No smell or smoke and the oven was operating as it should.  Even though the shock hurt tremendously, my ears popped and I had chest pain for approximately an hour, had I NOT been shocked, this melting could have continued without our knowledge and turned into a fire.  Also, it was fortunate that it was me that got shocked, as my husband has epilepsy and who knows how he could have been affected.  We have used the oven responsibly.  It has never been dropped or abused in any way.  It has never even been moved from it’s present location.  It has always worked well and we’ve been pleased with it otherwise.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

incidentDescription: While trying to help someone with a dead battery in their van - my Jump and Go Portable Charging Device began to smoke and expand.  I immediately disconnected the device from the vehicle and let it fall to the ground.  No damage other than the device occurred.

 Staple item # 1694123

model: Soundlogic 2600mAh Executive Leatherette Power Bank Blue
incidentDescription: I was using this to keep my phone charged and felt it getting hot.  I unplugged the charger and placed it in my pocket.  A few minutes later, while in the University of Detroit Dental School's Orthodontic Clinic, I felt it getting warmer and removed it from my pocket.  The middle section of the cell was extremely hot and had expanded from 1/4 inch to well over an inch thick.  Within a half a minute the unit began to smoke heavily and then blew open filling the clinic with an acrid smell.  I quickly went to a sink, turned on the water and dropped it into the sink.  About 15 seconds later I picked it up and since it was still very warm, I held it under the running water.  I then placed it in a zip lock bag.  Two of these were bought from Staples and my account was credited early this morning informing me to dispose of these power cells.  So I have 1 intact and the other in an exploded form in a zip lock.   I would like to be given instructions on how to send these in for proper inspection.  These were bought less than 2 months ago during which time I traveled from Detroit to Ft Lauderdale with Delta Airlines with these batteries.

The unit had automatically turned itself off as it does every day so it wasn't on, but it was plugged in. I went to check and see if something had gotten on the hotplate. It was super hot and smoke was rising from it. Then I noticed smoke coming out of the back of the coffee maker where the plug comes out. I immediately unplugged it. If I hadn't been home, this most certainly would have caused an electrical fire.

productDescription: FRIGIDAIRE SIDE BY SIDE WITH ICE MAKER AND COLD WATER DISPENSAR
incidentDescription:
August 16, 2015 my Frigidaire refrigerator caught on fire in my kitchen. I awoke to the sound of crackling, fearing I had left something on the stove top I entered the kitchen quickly. The room was already full of smoke but there was nothing on the stove top. I began checking my small appliances   (toaster, coffee maker, microwave) Seeing nothing wrong I began checking the outlets. When my husband began helping me I had an opportunity to listen for the noise again which to my surprise started again from the rear of the refrigerator. Along with the noise the smoke began again.
This came as a complete shock to me as this identical thing occurred August 14, 2014 to the Frigidaire I had purchased 14 months earlier. According to the technician that fire began with the compressor. A new Frigidaire Model FFHS2611LBLA was delivered to my home in September of 2014. Therefore that unit has been in my kitchen just shy of 1 year. 
August 16, 2015 it appears that the fire began from the same location as the first fire however when a technician can visit (delay because of the rural location I live in) that will be confirmed. 
I am grateful I was home each occasion because the outcome could have been entirely different. The model of refrigerator is FFHS2611LBLA. I am at a loss to understand how the identical unit has self-ignited twice.  I cannot come away with any other explanation other than design defect?

productDescription:
Black and Decker (UPC 885911221450)19 in. 36-Volt Self-Propelled Cordless Electric Mower with Removable Battery 

Model number: SPCM1936
productSubCategory: Lawn Mowers, Leaf Blowers and Lawn Vacuums
incidentDescription: On July 31, 2015, there was delivered a Black and Decker (UPC 885911221450)19 in. 36-Volt Self-Propelled Cordless Electric Mower with Removable Battery to my address. I tried it out and found its mowing performance to be acceptable.  A few days later, I decided to store it by taking advantage of a function advertised for this model, the handle that folds up for better storage. The metal handles consist of two pieces each, one of which has a pin or bolt in the middle, the other a corresponding hole. To disengage the pin and fold the handle, one turns a knob located on the handle a quarter-turn, grips the handle pieces and pries them apart. Once the pins are disengaged, the handle can be folded in half, the pins popped back into place, and the knob reset to lock the handle. I managed to disengage the pins and fold the handles. I re-engaged the pin on one side and turned my attention to the other. The instructions warn the user to be careful during this procedure not to "pinch" ones finger between the handle and the plate, so I was being careful when I did this. When I went to pry the handle piece in order to pop the second pin back into the hole, the considerable tension created by the force required in the maneuver propelled my index finger between the two handle pieces, shearing off a piece from the side of my finger. It's been two weeks and my finger is still trying to heal. Frankly, I could easily have lost the finger. I feel this incident should have been anticipated by normal testing and that it is a product defect (engineering/design). I am keeping the mower because of the difficulty in returning it and because I need something to mow my lawn.  I will not be using the foldable handle function, however, as soon as I figure out how I can re-extend the handles to mow the lawn without taking off a piece of me. This device should be investigated for this danger. Perhaps they could devise a simple tool to do the job rather than manual force.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription: Breville BOV800XL
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
Toaster oven door falls wide open during operation

I own a Breville BOV800XL toaster oven - convection smart oven 1800 watts. Recently I placed a food item in it, closed the oven door and walked away. Upon returning 20 min later, I found the door wide open and the oven full on!  I closed the door and it immediately fell wide open. The oven is designed with a heavy bar handle, located up high on the door.  The design Places the center of gravity up high on the door, requiring an appropriately designed closure spring to hold the door closed.  

I called Breville to notify them of this design flaw and request a replacement oven.  This is a widely distributed product carried by Bed Bath and Beyond - I wasn't sure of purchase date. As I communicated to Breville, this is a design flaw - a weak spring not capable of holding this heavy door; over time the spring breaks allowing the door to simply fall open.  Breville customer service as much as admitted the spring has since been redesigned. I provided a number from the back of the oven and was told it was manufactured in 2010. Breville is unwilling to replace or repair the oven unless I pay a $120 service charge (the eventually agreed to do it for $90).

Frankly, I don't care about the money.  I will likely ship it back and have it repaired because otherwise I like the item.  But, I do not have young children in our household so this enables me to consider the problem from a different point of view.  What shocked me was Breville's complete lack of acceptance of the fact this design flaw could result in a serious burn injury.  I would think this rises to the level of a recall for a repair.  I have worked as a Product Manager for over ten years; telling consumers to pay to fix a serious safety design flaw seems, well, flawed!

How many thousands of these ovens are in consumers homes, being used daily, with the potential the door will flop open at any moment?  Shouldn't Breville at least issue a safety warning?

I would be happy to send you an iPhone mpg of the door falling open (immediately after it is closed) if this is helpful.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription: Cuisinart TOB-40 Custom Classic Toaster Oven Broiler

incidentDescription:

This was a major product failure that could have easily caused harm had I not noticed what had happened right away - combined with the fact that this same product has failed for so many other people in the same way, perhaps there should be a recall of the product.

incidentDescription: I went into the garage about 5:30am this morning and the garage was full of smoke and had a strong odor.  After searching the garage I found my Kawasaki cordless drill, model #691761 on my work bench with a hole melted through the plastic near the trigger.  The battery was quite hot, so I removed it to prevent any further issues.  The battery and drill have brown burn marks on them. productDescription: Portable Gas Grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
The consumer stated he was using the grill to cook some hamburgers. 

He stated that the way the grill is designed, the propane gas tank hangs over the table where the grill sits. 

The consumer moved the burgers to the side where the tank is located. The consumer stated that the grill flipped off of the table. As the grill was falling, the consumer grabbed onto the propane gas tank. The consumer stated that the tank came loose and caused a large flame (about 2-2.5 ft). 

The consumer stated that there is a safety hazard with the way the grill is designed.

The consumer will also contact the manf and inform them about the issue. 

The consumer notified the manufacturer of the incident.  Their response was that the tank could be turned at an angle so it rests on the table however fuel efficiency might be negatively affected.

They further stated that the design meets all safety standards and no further action would be taken.

The simple solution would be to make the legs of the grill long enough to allow the tank to remain vertical while sitting fully on the table.

productDescription: Frigidaire De-humidifier. caught fire and tripped the GFI
incidentDescription: The frigidaire dehumidifier tripped the GFI. When I attempted to reset and plug it back in the GFI tripped again and I could smell the dehumidifier burning.

productDescription: a mini-dehumidifier for single room/space use
incidentDescription: I ordered this unit the end of March 2013 and used it during the spring and summer only to avoid any chance of freezing.  I realize it is out of warranty, but I think you ought to know of a safety issue.  The unit was never misused or placed in any unusual situations.  The plug that attaches to the unit semi-melted down and the unit quit working.  There were burn marks around the plug at the unit.  I had noticed the adapter always seemed hot to touch.  There was no other damage unless it is inside of the unit.  I recommend you review this product as I see others have found the same damage to their units (see saferproducts.gov report # 20130209-ACB4E-2147458946).  I am surprised there is not a recall as it could easily have created a fire.

productDescription: Breville BOV800XL/A countertop toaster oven
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
On 07/23/2014 I purchased a Breville BOV800XL/A toaster oven based on the high recommendation published in Consumer Reports magazine. Generally, my complaint has to do with it gets VERY HOT on the outside. 

When I first used it the following morning, when I opened the door to remove my toasted English muffins, my finger touched metal door frame and I got a painful burn. I then ran another cycle and my laser thermometer indicated between 110 and 120 degrees. Subsequent test yielded temperatures on the outside door frame of 109 degrees (top) 96 and 99 degrees (sides), and 141 degrees (bottom). The metal frame inside of the door ranged between 140 and 160 degrees. The top of the oven was 162 degrees.

I then ran a ten minute broil cycle at the 500 degree setting and the door frame was about the same as with the toasting and the sides and back were between 90 and 110 degrees. However the tip was 185-290 degrees.

There are warnings in the manual on page 4 and 5 under a column title "important Safeguards" and made reference to exceptions for top storage on page 47. They also made reference in that section to a bamboo cutting board designed to fit on top. Some of the consumer comments on the Amazon.com web site indicated the cutting board was of marginal quality and the feet on the bottom elevated it that made it appear to be a heat shield.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: Honeywell Air Genius 4 Air Purifier
incidentDescription:
I purchased a Honeywell Air Genius 4 Air Purifier at Walmart. I read all directions and operated the 
purifier as directed. Within 24 hours of turning the air purifier on I began to cough and had a tightness in my 
chest. I did not associate the symptoms with the air purifier until the next day. The coughing got 
painful, my chest and lungs felt inflamed, my sinuses felt burned. I searched the internet to see if 
there was any problems with using an air purifier when I discovered the ionic air purifiers have 
been identified for years to have caused similar symptoms, and are banned in some states. Why is 
there not warning labels required on these product? Why are they still for sale to the public? 
I took the produce back to Walmart and complained to the store manager and she said that there was 
nothing she could do to remove these dangerous products for there store and that it had to be 
removed by the manufacturer. How many more consumers have to have their lungs destroyed before this 
product is removed?
It's now been over ten days since I stopped using the air purifier and all of the symptoms have 
remained. How many others have had their health effected because if these products?

productDescription: Jenn-Air Stainless Steel LP Gas Grill Model 720-0163 Serial #DG-002 034610 Lowe's item 18852
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
On 8/26/2006 I purchased a Jenn-Air Stainless Steel Propane Gas Grill from Lowes in Lake Ozark, Missouri. The Item Number is 18852 Model 720-0163 Serial Number DG-002 034610. Last fall when we went out to use the grill my wife said the grill smelled like gas. I checked out the grill with all the burners and valves in the off position we could still smell gas. We shut off the main gas valve and the valve to the BBQ as we were going to Florida for the winter. This spring when we came back I disassembled the grill checking all the hoses and fittings as well as individual gas valves on the BBQ with soap and water. I found one of the Main gas valves to one of the burners leaking propane, while in the off position. This unit has never been damaged or misused. In my 67 years I have never had a BBQ gas valve just start leaking. I believe you may have a very serious safety issue with the gas valves on this unit. Hopefully this will help before any damage (fire or explosion) or injury can be caused by this faulty item. 

As of right now I have been waiting over six weeks for another part (main Gas Valve) I ordered from nex-grill on June 15, 2015 and the date is now July 27, 2015. As of today they are telling the parts are still on Back order and they don't expect to receive them until September.

incidentDescription: Weber Grill Model SP-310.  When grilling and lid is open, user can easily burn hand when reaching to close the lid. I owned a previous Weber grill (Genesis 1000) which was designed so that the handle extended sufficiently beyond and below the lid, and the user would grab the handle without touching the hot lid. This problem on the newer SP-310 model could be fixed by Weber engineering by designing a replacement handle which would extend lower over the lid, allowing the user to grab the handle without touching the lid. productDescription: Side by side window fan.
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription: We were given 3, Holmes window fans last summer that were purchased from Walmart in Butler Pa.  2 of our 3 window fans have gone bad and nearly caused a fires.  The first (which was in my toddlers bedroom) stopped running and began to produce a burning electrical smell which woke my son who then alerted us, this was apriximataly 2 weeks ago (July 2015).  Today (2 weeks later, August 4, 2015) the second of the 3 fans began to produce a electrical fire smell that filled out entire residence.  This unit was still running.  Both units, the plastic foam insulation around the motors was discolored on and appeared to be starting to melt and were isolated to be the the source of the smell.  The plastic fan slats at the motors were extremely hot to the touch, actually too hot to touch for more than a second or two.   With both incidents the walls around the electrical outlet became hot over where the wires run through the walls however we caught the problem prior to the breakers tripping.  I attempted to contacted the manufacturer today and am awaiting contact back from the company.  After reviewing product reviews on the manufacturers site and various other sites searching for possible recalls I found an identical incident on a review on Target.com website from a person who also purchased 3 and had 2 fail similarly to ours shortly after purchase.

productDescription: Dehumidifier
manufacturer: Gree Electric Appliances, Inc. of Zhuhai
incidentDescription:
The consumer indicates that although his unit sounds like it is working properly, for the past two weeks it has not been removing moisture from his home. The unit runs twenty-four hours a day, seven days a week.

06/16/2015 - Curious as to why his unit was not working properly, the consumer proceeded to check his unit. At first, he had to wait for it to cool down as he noticed how hot it was to touch. When he opened the unit, he noticed several components inside it that were either losing their form from excessive heat; the compressor was so hot that the housing was melting because it was touching the compressor. The water pump was also affected.

The consumer indicates that he never noticed any smoke surrounding the unit. He informs that the fan was working properly.

The consumer contacted the manufacturer and explained to a representative the issues he has been having with his unit. Upon looking up his specific model, he was informed that his dehumidifier is not included in a recall. Because his unit is not recalled, he was not offered a remedy but was informed that he should unplug and stop usage of his unit, as well as that he will be receiving a call from the manufacturer the following week.

The consumer has no injuries nor previous incidents to report. The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard.

productDescription:
POD (Power on Demand). A compact charging unit designed to charged small electronics and jump dead batteries in autos. Also contains a built in flashlight.
Note: I have a photo but your sites 'Add File' is not working
incidentDescription:
I purchased a P.O.D. X4 (Power on Demand) Feb 22, 2015. I've used it a few times. Mostly camping charging cell phones. I've jumped my Goldwing twice and my car once. The second time I jumped my car, I had just fully charged the unit. I connected it to my battery posts, and had it in my hand trying to press the button to turn it on. The button would not press, only to find out it was swelling in my hand, popping the case apart. It immediately, got hot and started billowing heavy white smoke. I dropped it and disconnected the leads to the battery and dropped it to the ground. It popped and fizzled spewing heavy white smoke, so heavy I thought someone was going to call the fire dept. Within seconds it got extremely hot and melted. I could have easily burned my hand, or worse, catch my car on fire if I had left it unattended.

I've tried connecting the manufacturer, but no response.

It's too bad about the defect, it was a nice unit and was very convenient.

I have not found any information on any defects for the P.O.D. I would hate to think it could catch on fire sitting in my car of motorcycle saddlebag.

productDescription: Nostalgia Electric "Retro Series" electric ice cream maker
incidentDescription:
Product is a Nostalgia Electrics "Retro Series" electric ice cream maker.  With this product, the lid/motor assembly screws onto the base counter clockwise.  The machine also churns counter clockwise.  While trying to churn my first batch of ice cream I heard the lid separate from the machine and begin to spin on top of the machine.  By the time I ran into the kitchen to turn it off, the machine had spun enough to pull the cord into the bowl assembly and reeled the cord into itself like a fishing reel.  Once it reeled enough cord inside itself, the machine pulled itself a couple feet across my counter and fell into my kitchen sink.  Had my children been doing dishes as the time this electrical appliance walked itself into my kitchen sink, the unthinkable would have happened.  All they had to do was have the lid/motor assembly locked onto the base in the opposite direction of the machine rotation, this would never have happened.  In my opinion, this machine needs to be pulled from shelves before someone gets seriously hurt or electrocuted.  

Part number is ICM150RETRORED
UPC code is 0826677217912

productDescription: GreensWorks 3-in-1 blower, mulcher, and vacuum.  The blower has 2 settings, low and high.  An attachment was included for the vacuum that is added to the bottom of the unit.  A bag for the leave/mulch came with the product as well.

The smell persisted so I looked at the blower and could see it smoking.  I immediately stopped using it and when I attempted to remove the extension cord it was melted onto the prong.

productDescription: 70 pints dehumidifier
incidentDescription:
This caller is contacting the CPSC regarding her daughter's Kenmore dehumidifier which was purchased September 15th, 2013 after her previously owned unit was recalled.
Her daughter had no problems with the new dehumidifier until her father went to her basement Monday, June 22nd, 2015 to empty the water container and found that it had overflowed and that the dehumidifier was overheating.  The unit was not smoking, however the fan was not running and the top of the unit was very hot.

With the thought that the unit may reset and work properly it was left plugged in but it continued to overheat and so the caller's husband unplugged their daughters dehumidifier Wednesday, June 24th, 2015 and it remains unplugged for fear of fire.

The manufacturer was contacted around June 22nd, 2015 but was believed to be unconcerned.

productDescription: CHI Professional Hair Dryer with Diffuser, Fuchsia Couture 841385
model: Chi Pro Low EMF Professional Hair Dryer Model GF6852
incidentDescription: I received a CHI hair dryer for Christmas, purchased from Sam's Club.  When I use it, my hair is almost dry and it takes me less than 5 minutes to use a round brush and finish styling my hair by drying it with the dryer.  For storage, the dryer has been hung on my wall by the loop the manufacturer provides that is permanently attached to the dryer.  The cord is not wrapped or anything.  Today I was drying my hair and had been using the dryer probably 3 minutes when I noticed an orange spark fly out of the dryer.  I held it away from my hair, in front of my view, and tried to turn it off.  I accidentally turned it to low instead of off (the switch position is low to one side, high to the other, off in the center).  Another spark flew out before I could get the dryer turned off and unplugged.  I was very startled.  I believe this could easily have set my hair on fire and have never had a hair dryer do this before.  Since the dryer was only 8 months old and in perfect condition, I believe this is a serious safety issue and a recall should probably be issued.  I will be returning the item to Sam's Club as soon as possible.

productDescription: Proctor-Silex slow cooker. Type SC19; Model number: 33275Y; series number: E0331DJ.
incidentDescription:
Today, July 26, 2015, the glass lid on our Proctor-Silex slow cooker exploded.
The handle on the lid hit the bottom edge of the microwave (about one foot away to the left) and partially dislodged a filter screen, then landed on the counter top nearby, to the right of the slow cooker. The glass lid is completely shattered. The pot had not boiled dry, there was plenty of liquid.

No one was nearby, so no injuries were sustained, just lost a pot of beans!

Had anyone been close to the slow cooker when the top exploded, serious injury could have been sustained.

The model number is 33275Y; series number is E0331DJ.

productDescription: Smokey Joe 14" Charcoal Grill
incidentDescription:
Dangerously Hot Glass-Reinforced Nylon Lid Handle - Weber Smokey Joe 14" Charcoal Grill

In September 2014, I bought a new Weber Smokey Joe 14" basic model to replace a 20-year old one as I was moving out-of-state. I was using the new one for the past few months without a problem. However, I recently bought the Weber coal Chimney Starter and tried it 2 nights ago. The coals heated up very quickly and I grilled meat with the lid off. Then I put slices of bread w/cheese on top on the grill and put the lid on for no more than one minute (to melt the cheese on the bread). When I went to take off the lid, the handle was so hot that I burned my hand and instinctively flung the grill cover away. It could have hit my feet/legs and I could have had serious burns. 

I've written to Weber about this on their company website.  However, I received their response today saying "Sorry to hear about that accident you had with your grill...The use of a heat-resistant BBQ mitt or glove is recommended when operating the grill.  These warnings are outlined in the owner's manual for your grill." 

Following Weber's response, I have accessed several websites to read consumer complaints about this product and this same issue of the overheated handle has been noted since 2010.  How can the company continue to ignore this?

incidentDescription:

incidentDescription:
We recently purchased from our local Austin, TX Lakeline Target store a pre-assembled, floor model of a 32" Threshold Fire Column in the Garden section, retailing at $129.99. It is Store Item Number (DPCI) 009-07-0769 and Online Number: 16538881.

http://www.target.com/p/threshold-fire-column/-/A-16538881?lnk=rec|pdp|viewed_viewed|pdpv1

I read the user’s  comments/warning about holding the ignition before starting the gas,  this didn’t seem to help.   The directions didn’t seem to indicate this, either. 
 
After about two seconds of holding down the ignition we had a large fireball that came out of the fire column and ended up with non-serious burns on my fingers.  
 
I’ve operated gas grills for years and haven’t ever seen anything like this.   It is a very dangerous product and I did contact the Retailer to express my concern of an unsafe product. 

To date, I have not received a response from Target, though I contacted them on Sunday, July 12.

I’m wondering if Target has had other complaints about this product in addition to the comments on their website. I believe it merits further investigation.

productDescription: I'm inquiring about a product we own: a Ryobi Model RY14110A 48 volt 20-inch self-propelled lawnmower (Serial# BMP0780024). Our batteries weren't charging and my husband pulled them out. They are bulging and look dangerous. I started researching the internet including Home Depot where we bought it, as they are a Ryobi distributor. Many people on the reviews complained about their batteries not holding a charge, some posted pictures of the bulging, and others stated their batteries leaked acid in the garage. Supposedly a poor charger was the cause but Ryobi didn't contact us. The reviewers also said that Ryobi Customer Service hasn't been helpful, but a Ryobi Facebook e-mail address was. My husband e-mailed them today and they weren't helpful and told him to call Ryobi Customer Service. My husband called Ryobi Customer Service and they basically said since our lawnmower was built in 2011 that we are out of warranty. However, we were never notified of a recall and I don't see one on this website, either. Many reviewers bought new batteries but they just stopped working due to the malfunctioning charger which was causing the batteries to go bad. Some of the Home Depot reviewers had Ryobi reply on the website and suggest they buy a different Ryobi lithium model--even thought they had already spent $400-$500 on this model, plus any battery replacements at $129 a crack. Aren't companies supposed to replace defunct products/issue a recall? Reviewers commented that there was a recall but hardly anyone (including us) knew about this. I put the bulging batteries in a box in our cool basement. With temperatures hitting 90 degrees this weekend, I didn't want to risk an incident in our garage due to overheating. However, I also don't want to get rid of the evidence in case someone wants to see it. I took pictures but the bulging doesn't show as well in the pictures. Please advise if there is an investigation regarding this product and/or the battery charger. Note: If you look on the Home Depot product site this product has been discontinued: http://www.homedepot.com/p/Ryobi-20-in-48-Volt-Cordless-Self-Propelled-Lawn-Mower-DISCONTINUED-RY14110A/202042176. Thank you.

productDescription: Kit used to convert grill from propane to natural gas.
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
KitchenAid markets a conversion kit (model 71 0-0003) to convert their model 72900891 B grill from propane to natural gas fuel. I purchased the kit and during instillation, I discovered are two dangerous defects in the kit.

First, the natural gas regular hose is too long. It is supposed to measure 150 mm, but actually measures 190 mm. Therefore, when attempting to attach the regulator to the grill side panel (instructions page 6, step 7), the hose kinks badly. This can weaken the hose and result in a gas leak.

Second, the kit contains a 10ft supply line hose which is properly rated for natural gas; however, the regulator hose is marked for LP not NG use, and this kit is intended for use with natural gas as a fuel

No incident occurred. Once I discovered the defects, I simply stopped installing the conversion kit (leaving the grill in propane fuel mode), notified the manufacturer and you.
