productDescription: Eveready Energizer 9v
incidentDescription:
June 22, 2015 
Subject: Possible Problem with [REDACTED] Model No. [REDACTED] Fire Alarms and 9v Batteries 
This home was built in 2008 and First Alert Fire hard wired alarms on all three floors. Recently we purchased a 4-pack of 9v [REDACTED] batteries to have on hand and the first one used was installed about a week ago on the first floor. The alarm seemed reset properly after a test press of the test button but started intermittent alarming from then on. [REDACTED] online suggestions were tried to no avail after loss of sleep, thinking the problem was fixed. 
The new 9v battery tested good with my voltmeter. I took the alarm apart and noticed positive leaf spring was not vertical and not protruding as far as the negative. In trying to find out how the pin got bent, I also noticed the [REDACTED] negative battery spring posts was also different when compared to an Eveready Energizer I had on hand. The [REDACTED] has a square post. Having roughly measuring the 9v negative and positive post the dimensions of the [REDACTED] versus Energizer, they are about the same. 
What I learned in placing either battery in the [REDACTED] alarm was the positive and negative leaf springs are bent near the end and goes inside the battery post holes leaving the only lower one edge to touch the posts. The lower edge allows for less tension resulting in a poor contact. The bend of the leaf spring needs to be made at a lower point and possibly lengthened to make contact at both ends of the battery posts. 
My view is this is a defective product and a recall may be in order. Please notify me of your findings as I am interested in knowing what needs to be done to replace all of my alarms. 

Sincerely, 
[REDACTED] 
Phone: [REDACTED] 
Email: [REDACTED] 

Sent to: http://www.cpsc.gov/ 
Consumer Safety Product Commission 

[REDACTED]

productDescription: Vita-Mix 7500 blender, black (I have since packaged the blender to return it, so I don't have access to the serial number or manufacture date)
incidentDescription: I purchased a Vita-Mix 7500 blender online based on Consumer Reports high rating.  After cleaning it, I tested it out.  Tiny black particles were emitted into my food; about the same amount on each of 5 tests (maybe 30-50 visible particles in 2 cups of water in a white bowl; the water was free of visible particles prior to being blended).  Online research finds many such reports; apparently Vita-Mix has told consumers the particles are Teflon shards coming from an O-ring on the blade assembly.  Not every individual blender is affected, but all models may be involved.  They have not recalled the blenders, stating Teflon is inert and therefore safe for consumption.  A redesigned container and blade apparatus is being worked on and may be ready at the end of 2015.  I notified Consumer Reports for their awareness in rating these blenders, and they suggested I contact CPSC, as well.  Teflon may be inert, but it seems irresponsible to sell a product touted as useful for healthy eating, even as you're aware that parts of the apparatus are being consumed with that healthy food.

productDescription: Stanley SL18130 5-Gallon 4.5 Peak Portable Stainless Steel Series Horsepower Wet/Dry Vacuum Cleaner
incidentDescription:
This is a Stanley Shop Vac Model: SL-18130 and could apply to many steel can vacuums

I have been an electrician for over 20 years and use all sorts of tools including vacuums to clean up all sorts of different materials in the past.  This one incident is pretty serious.  The voltage and arc generated could be, in my opinion, lethal. 

This electrical charge was repeated several times and observed open air arc was 25-45mm from another grounded appliance (furnace duct work).  The ignition coil on a car idling won't discharge an arc like this at 20mm.  The accompanying arc snap volume was quite alarming.

The material being cleaned up was 1950's vintage plaster and dust which settled over a hot air furnace.  In one respect, Tesla would have been pleased.

Ungrounded metal catch can will generate dangerous capacitive voltage depending on the material collected.  None of my test equipment had the range to measure voltage, current or joules. This information is based on my own experience (getting zapped) and then actually causing the situation to occur several times while observing the arc's behavior.

To sum this issue in a few words:  It doesn't matter how the electrics are protected.  Double insulated motors or grounded motors.  The point is the metal can was ungrounded and the materials being cleaned up caused a rare but dangerous situation.

Here's the thing.  National Electrical Code clearly states that all metal for any electrical device must be bonded to ground.  This is a safety issue.  Had this particular model simply put on any sort of ground to the can, the charge generated would have been safely discharged through the ground.

If I am not mistaken - Underwriters Lab also has rules for metal encased appliances - I.E. the use of a grounded power cord.  I test grounds on all 3 prong tools on job sites (as per OSHA).

This vacuum has a 3 prong cord (NEMA 5-15p) but the ground was never extended to the metal can.  

MY FIX: 16ga wire to a small copper strip positioned across the gasket.  When the vacuum lid is closed, the strip comes into contact with the can.  The copper strip under the seal provides an adequate ground path to discharge any stray or capacitive charges.

Such a fix should be used on any metal can shop vac, especially those used to collect WATER.  120v traveling through water could cause the metal can to become energized.  Why?  Some unsuspecting homeowner cleaning up water ... well, lets see ... water on the floor ... feet in the water ... metal can becomes full and stop float fails to work.  Water is drawn through the motor armature.  That situation is becoming dangerous.  I have had shut-off floats fail in the past during a flood water cleanup.

Some sort of mechanism should be developed to ensure the safety of metal can vacuums, especially any vacuum that could be involved with water. 

I hope this information is useful in preventing someone from getting injured or worse.

Thanks,
[REDACTED]

I closed the tank valve and extinguished the flames. The next day I could see that the spark igniter unit was burned and melted, the on-off switch for the grill light was melted and had dripped onto the deck, the gas regulator hose was circumferentially burned and melted and the main gas manifold tube had perforated with rust and corrosion. I believe that the gas regulator hose was moments from burning through and allowing gas to flow freely from the tank. The grill is kept on a wooden deck next to the house.

incidentDescription: I seriously cut myself twice within 15 minutes while using this blender for the first time.  I would not recommend this blender for anyone.  In my opinion it is defectively designed.  The Ninja uses a long attachment with concentric circular blades much unlike the normal blade design typically used in blenders.  The Ninja's "razor blade Christmas tree" design provides no discernible benefit over the normal blade design yet increases the risk of injury exponentially.  I seriously cut the index finger on my right hand while inserting the blade attachment into the pitcher.  Minutes later, the attachment fell out of the pitcher into my left hand while I was pouring the contents of the pitcher onto a plate (the poorly mixed, half-blended contents, I might add).  It caused a deep gash in my palm requiring four stitches to close.  The attachment fell out of the pitcher because it is designed to sit loose on the base of the blender with no secure connection whatsoever.  Not surprisingly, a quick review of Safer Products complaints shows others have been injured in the same manner and even more seriously.  I was lucky to escape with only four stitches.  I immediately returned the blender to the place of purchase for a full refund.  Avoid at all costs.  The Ninja blender is needlessly dangerous, almost as if the manufacturer set out to create a booby trap.  Mission accomplished.

incidentDescription:
Fire on June 11,2013 at residence located W 131 S 8448 Eagles Way, Muskego, Wisconsin. Smoke and fire damage
exceeded $500,000. The fire was caused by an arcing incident within a dehumidifier. The dehumidifier was
examined and determined to be the cause of the fire. Attached is the Report of the two experts.
My law firm, Greg Cook Law, S.C. first became involved in this incident in late April. We gathered the information
and learned that similar dehumidifiers manufactured by the same company had been recalled for fire hazards. See
Release #01-130, 10-096 and 11-324.
This unit model number does not appear on any of the recalls. This unit is described in the report as one SIMILAR to
Model LHD459EL dehumidifier manufactured by LG.
My concern was that the engineers referred to manuals for models LHD30, LHD45EL, UD65EL, LD450EAL, and
LD451 EGL as well as the schematics for Model LDSOELY6 since the homeowner did not have any manuals in his
possession. Homeowner purchased unit in 2006-07 from a Home Depot, according to his recollection.
I suspect the other recalls involve similarly designed machines with almost identical wiring problems that were
found in this unit. Arcing was the reported cause in other fires and from what I could see it may have been a similar
defect.
The unit is in the custody of State Farm Mutual Fire Insurance company. We are trying to verify if the serial number
or other information can be gleaned from the unit.

Space heater had not been turned on or used for around one month, although it was left plugged in. The On/Off switch in the OFF position, thermostat set to the lowest setting, Hi 1500w/Low 1250w switch set to Hi, unit in standby/off mode, with only power running to the on off switch on the unit.  The room temperature was around 70 degrees Fahrenheit, so there was no attempt for the heater thermostat to activate due to temperature change.

With no indications of a problem, the male end of the units electrical cord shorted, made a buzzing sound, followed by a bright arc like an electric welder, the plug started blazing.  I pulled the cord causing the plug to release from the female receptacle, extinguished the flaming plug end without further damage to the house, myself or anyone else. The arc burned away one of the plug prongs, melted and burned the plug end leaving a burned out void where the prong would normally protrude out of the plastic. Luckily, this occurred while I was home, and awake, sitting 3 ft away, where I had a chance to take action. I'd hate to think what the outcome would have been had I not been able to intervene, or worse yet had I been asleep.

incidentDescription:
The consumer stated that he plugged the unit in for use in his secondary bedroom. The consumer turned the heater onto 70F degrees and fan at low speed. 

The consumer stated that the unit was being used as a secondary heating source. The consumer had a pellet stove being used in his living room.

The consumer stated that after several hours, he smelled plastic burning. The consumer searched the house and found out that the breaker box had an incident occur with it.

The consumer stated that he uncovered the breaker box and noticed that the wires were glowing brightly. The casing off of several wires had melted. Back plastic casing had also melted. The consumer stated that as soon as he turned off the heating/cooling/dehumidifier unit in the bedroom, the wires stopped glowing. The breaker box finally cooled down.

The consumer turned on the heater again to see if that really was the issue. The consumer stated that the wires started glowing again when he turned on the heater. The consumer concluded that the heating/cooling/dehumidifier unit was the issue.

The consumer checked all the plug-ins and breakers for any problem. The consumer stated that there is nothing wrong with any of those and they work properly even with melted components.

The consumer stated that he travels for military, so he has barely used the unit about 5 times.

The consumer stated that he has never used the dehumidifier feature.

The consumer has not tried to use the unit since the incident occurred.

The consumer sent an e-mail to the manf. He has not been able to find a working contact # for the manf. The consumer asked the manf to buy back the damaged unit and provide a replacement breaker box.

productType: Beds or Bedframes, Other or Not Specified (4076)
incidentDescription:
We recently purchased a bed frame from Crate and Barrel. The bed was assembled by the people who delivered it. The bed was meant for our guest bedroom and was only slept on once by one person of approximately 160 pounds. This was about 30 days after the bed was delivered. We noticed later in the day that there were 2 small pieces of metal on the floor near the corner of the bed. We removed the mattress from the bed frame and found out that the pieces of metal are the ends of 2 screws which are meant to hold up the side board.

The screws which held up the side board had broken in half and the side board was only held up by two very small screws. Upon taking the bed apart, the other 2 screws broke as we disconnected the size board from the foot board. We then found another corner of the bed had screws which were broken in half. In my opinion this bed is unsafe because the screws are defective/unable to hold the weight of the bed on it's own. We feel fortunate that the bed did not collapse as someone was sleeping on it, otherwise the headboard would have come slamming down on the occupant.

productDescription: Small, rectangular white portable power source.  Says "POWER BANK"
incidentDescription:
A portable battery charger branded "Power Bank" spontaneously exploded approximately 2 weeks after being charged.  After being charged in a regular 110-volt home outlet, it was not plugged in again nor used to provide power to other devices before the explosion.  (It would typically be used as a way of charging a cell phone or other small electronic device.)

We traveled overseas with the device but didn't end up needing to use it.  Hours after arriving back in the US it spontaneously exploded on a counter top.  It was not plugged in to anything at the time it exploded.  The fire was quickly contained but smoke and other damage occurred.  I am horrified to think what would have happened if the device had exploded in my carry-on during the flight, or while I was carrying it in my backpack.

I immediately alerted the accounting firm of BDO about the incident since they had provided it as a gift.  They put me in touch with Office Depot, the distributor of the device, and another group called [REDACTED] who sourced the devices for Office Depot.  All parties have claimed that they have had no other reported incidents with the device in question but I am pressing BDO to issue an alert to all of the recipients of the device.

productDescription: NutriBullet 900
incidentDescription:
02/16/2015 - The consumer used her blender before she went to work. The consumer indicates that while the unit was blending her smoothie, she heard an unusual sound coming from it but did not think much of it. Though the consumer usually drinks her smoothie right from the blender glass, she was running late and had to place its contents in a mason jar. When the consumer was in her vehicle, she started consuming her drink via a straw. At one point, she noticed that no juice was coming from the straw even though the container was not empty. Believing that possibly a vegetable had gotten stuck, the consumer proceeded to try to extract it with her hand. When the consumer got her hand out, it was actually one of the six prong blades that had broken off.

02/17/2015 - The consumer contacted the manufacturer via e-mail and explained what had happened with their unit. The consumer received an automated response from the manufacturer indicating that they would contact her within twenty-four to forty-eight hours. 

02/19/2015 (Approximately) - The consumer received a call from Products Specialist [REDACTED]. He informed the consumer that he was very sorry she had to go through what she did and that it was the first times that it had happened. He asked the consumer that she should mail them her unit. The consumer informed him that she wanted to receive something in writing indicating what they would do should she send them the unit. [REDACTED] agreed to her request.

02/25/2015 - The consumer had not received an e-mail or any other notice from the manufacturer. She proceeded to e-mail them once again informing them that she was rather upset she never got any response from them and that she would take the matter to a higher level. 

03/11/2015 - The consumer e-mailed them once again as she had not received any response, She asked to speak to the [REDACTED] of the company as she was surprised by their apathy. 

03/15/2015 (Approximately) - The consumer received a call from what she believes was a [REDACTED] but he was unintelligible. She tried contacting him several times and was not able to. 

03/18/2015 - The consumer e-mailed the manufacturer and informed them of the [REDACTED] incident and how she had been trying to get a hold of him.

The consumer received a very nasty e-mail from "[REDACTED]." He indicated that she must have been dialing the wrong number. "[REDACTED]" also informed the consumer that he wanted to speak to her directly as well as verify the legitimacy of the blender.

The consumer contacted [REDACTED] and their conversation was almost an interrogation. The consumer felt like she was being accused. [REDACTED] asked her what she wanted them to do was she looking for money and later asked the consumer if she had read the consumer report on the item. After the consumer answered that she had not, [REDACTED] informed her that they had done a "ridiculous test" and that after numerous times of blending some contents with an x number of ice cubes, a blade would break off. The consumer did not understand everything [REDACTED] was saying. He asked her if she could send him pictures as well as a picture of the serial number on the blade. The consumer also learned that [REDACTED] is the [REDACTED] of the company. He offered to give her the same blender model she owns.

When the consumer got home, she took some pictures of what was asked of her and sent them to [REDACTED]. The consumer then later looked up the consumer report on the unit and after having read everything, she was left flabbergasted because what happened on the testing they did was exactly what had happened to her blender.  Same model!  900. ... except the fact that the consumer did not use seven (possibly twelve - she does not remember the exact digit) ice cubes when the incident occurred (the consumer indicates that she always uses three iced cubes).

03/22/2015 (Approximately) - The consumer contacted the manufacturer and spoke to [REDACTED]. She asked the [REDACTED]'s address ([REDACTED]) because she wanted to to send him a personal letter. [REDACTED] informed her that she is not at liberty to give her that information. [REDACTED] said she could provide her [REDACTED] and/ or [REDACTED] contact information, to which the consumer declined. 

03/24/2015 - The consumer was contacted via e-mail by their [REDACTED], [REDACTED]. He informed her that he was aware she wanted to speak to the [REDACTED] and not him nor [REDACTED]. He informed the consumer that her case would not be escalated any further. He expressed his disappointment that the consumer did not do as she promised - send them their unit - though the consumer indicates that she never promised such a thing.

03/25/2015 - Several e-mails were exchanged later on. The consumer thanked [REDACTED] for his time and enlightening her on the consumer report. He wrote her back and she responded that she want all consumers to be reimbursed for their faulty blenders as well as recall her blender model.

The consumer indicates that she uses her unit once a day. 

The consumer has no injuries to report nor other incidents. The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard.

http://www.amazon.com/Cuisinart-TOB-40-Classic-Toaster-Broiler/dp/B004JMZGM2/ref=cm_cr_pr_bdcrb_top?ie=UTF8
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
Some time after using our "Cuisinart TOB-40 Custom Classic Toaster Oven Broiler" for toast at 7:30pm the device activated itself and the heating elements became red hot.  We awoke at 9:30pm that evening to the smell of burning plastic and general "hot" smell.  We found the toaster with hot elements glowing in the dark kitchen, even through all control dials and lights indicated the toaster was off.  The only course of action was to unplug the device after which it cooled normally and displayed no damage.

This is a HUGE concern to me as this presents a sizable fire hazard and it frightens me to think how many times this toaster may have activated while I was not at home.

Reading one star reviews of this product on Amazon.com show many users with similar self-activation complaints, and still others with deformed heating element issues. I obviously have no way of knowing but it seems those issues could be caused by self-activation and over heating cycles while the user is not present.

Please investigate this product to protect consumers who, like me before yesterday, are not suspicious that this appliance could destroy their homes and loved ones.  I will not be leaving this product plugged in any more, and will consider whether to discard it completely.

Thank you,
[REDACTED]

brand: Lifesmart Largre Room Infrared Quartz Fireplace
incidentDescription: I bought a LifeSport 1500 KW fireplace heater for a room in my house in November 2014.  In February 2015 the heater quit working.  I called the company support line on March 2, 2015 and talked with an agent who ran through a predetermined script to see what needed to be done to fix my heater.  At the end I was told that I would need to send a copy of the invoice to her and once she received that she would start the process for sending me a new heater - which would include via the mail system a letter on how to dispose of the old heater.  On March 9 I got a call from LifeSport saying that they had determined that the thermostat was bad and was going to send me the part.  I asked if a technician was going to come out and install and they said no that I would do the work.  I told them that I couldn't believe that the consumer would be the one to have to repair the unit.  I got the instructions, ahead of the part coming in the mail, on March 10.  The instructions are 7 pages long and the thought of this being a common practice on the consumer repairing a heater sent all kinds of red flags up for me.  I told myself that I need to do something because there were many, many people that would not be able to perform this task if their heater had failed for the same reason.  I think it is an unsafe act to have a consumer repair a room heater when there are many statistics about room heaters causing issues when professionals put them together.  I would like to attach the instructions but I don't see a way to do that.

productDescription: Primus Firehole 200 Propane Camping Stove
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
I purchased the Primus Firehole 200 stove brand new from REI (Recreational Equipment Inc.)

I used the stove for cooking on three separate occasions. On the first occasion, the stove worked fine.

On the second and third occasions, I noticed the flame sputtering on both of the burners, indicating that they weren't receiving sufficient fuel.  On the fourth occasion, when attaching a propane fuel bottle, the gas immediately began leaking from inside the stove.  This was not a small leak, but a full-on flow of propane.  The smell of propane filled the air around me.

I immediately disconnected the fuel bottle from the hose attachment.  After disassembling the panel from the bottom of the stove, the cause was very clear.  The copper tube that carried the gas from the fuel source to the first burner had broken at the soldering point where it attached to the brass fitting that the rubber fuel hose connects to.  

This caused propane gas to spew into the interior of the stove unhindered when a propane bottle was connected to the hose.  Had I made an attempt to light the stove, it almost certainly would have resulted in an explosion.

incidentDescription: While blow drying my hair, I suddenly noticed a burning odor. I was blow drying my hair upside down with my eyes closed. productDescription: 1500 watt, 4 element infrared quartz heater
manufacturer: LIFESMART PRODUCTS / SOURCE NETWORK SALES AND MARKETING, INC
incidentDescription: On March 6, 2015 I purchased a 4 element infrared quartz heater manufactured by "lifepro" trademark of lifecorp products from Menards (Model #LS1002HH, Serial #MM281405981).  The product was moderately used to supplement my whole house furnace in a dining room where my parrot resides.  I would estimate that I used the heater less than 100 hours since purchasing at a modest temperature of 72 degrees.  The unit can be set as high as 90 degrees.  On March 27, 2015 I powered off the heater which appeared to be operating fine.  It had been running throughout the night with no issues.  This particular heater has a blower that remains on 90 seconds after powering down to cool the unit off. The heater was in that cycle when I walked away from it.  At that time I was loading up the car for work and walked back inside to discover an overpowering smell of burning plastic.  The smell was coming from the heater that displayed an error message of "E1" on the LCD screen.  I immediately pulled the plug and had to take it outside as the smell was still permeating from the unit.  Upon removal I noticed that the metal grill/grate where the heat blows out had blistered paint and the plastic surface above the grill was significantly melted.  This damage was not on the heater prior to the incident.  The plastic appeared to be borderline of getting hot enough to start dripping onto the floor. This heater clearly has defective parts and its very alarming to think that the heating elements weren't even operating when it started to burn.  I'm thankful that I was home at the time of the incident.  Who knows how much further this could have gone if I hadn't been there to pull the plug. I hope that you investigate the matter further.

productDescription: Pellet Stove
incidentDescription:
This caller purchased her pellet stove around the autumn of 2012 and had no problems with it until after an electrical issue that had been covered by the warranty.
Two different electrical repairs completed by the hardware store she purchased the unit from.  They were in touch with the manufacturer during these two incidents of repair under warranty.
On Friday, February 20th, 2015 the caller started the pellet stove, went to the other side of the house.
After approximately one half hour the caller smelled smoke and went to investigate, the lights of the control panel were all blinking and the stove was out.
Since there was no fire she decided to trouble shoot and re light the stove.
Approximately one half hour to one hour she smelled smoke again. 
She returned to the stove and found her bedroom where the stove was sitting engulfed in gray smoke but no fire again.
She continued to investigate and realized that the plastic compartment that hold the pellets had a hole in it and that the pellets had been sifting down into the motor like an hour glass.

This caller is reporting this as a severe safety hazard and is asking for her monies.to be returned for this product.and for her bedroom to be repainted at manufacturer expense.

The consumer provided photos and added: photo #1 - stove functioning properly; photo #2 - inside the hopper, still smoking pellets have poured down hole; photo #3 - after the fire was out, she removed the pellets and discovered the hopper floor had melted a huge hole; and photo #4 - left side-fire melted the insulation and wood placed in the window opening.

productDescription: White 4 slice toaster by Rival model # RV949 plastic.
incidentDescription: A four slice toaster Model # RV949 purchased at Walmart was in our breakroom heating without either one of the bread plungers pushed down.  The heating elements should not have been heating without the plungers being pushed.  The toaster became very hot and we could smell the scent of something burning.  THis is a fire hazard for a toaster to remain on and heating after the plungers have popped up.  We had to unplug the toaster to shut it off.

productDescription:
Ryobi battery charger
part of a Expand It grass trimmer/tree pruning kit
incidentDescription:
On Sat, March 7, 2015 at approx. 2:30pm., I discovered  my garage fully engulfed in white smoke,
I immediately called 911 and  Montgomery County MD Fire Dept.(MCFD) responded. Upon arrival, the 
cause of the smoke was determined to have been  a Ryobi 40 volt lithium battery charger located 
on top of a refrigerator in the garage.  It should be noted the charger was NOT plugged  in and  
battery had last been utilized  in Oct. 2014 prior to being cradled in the charger for the winter.
MCFD determined the charger overheating had caused  the resulting small fire/smoke to burn  the
plastic (charger/ battery)  and  paint (top of refrigerator). MCFD utilized  a heat seeking device 
to locate the  source of the fire/smoke after first ruling out the refrigerator plug as the cause. 
The charger/battery were destroyed and refrigerator damaged. Additionally, smoke damage was
evident  behind  the  refrigerator, which leads directly into the family room  of the residence. 
MCFD also  indicated  that  the  timing of my opening  the garage  doors after smelling  the smoke 
in the family room  limited the fire/smoke damage from spreading to other locations inside the  
residence. I purchased the Ryobi charger & battery  in Sept. 2014 from The Home Depot as part of a 
Ryobi Expand It grass trimmer/ tree pruning kit.

On  March 7,  at approx. 3:30pm., I  contacted Ryobi Customer Service and  the CPSC to report  the incident. I was told by Ryobi that the incident was being forwarded to their Safety Division and that a Safety Officer would contact me within 48 hours. On Mon., March 9 the CPSC contacted me; however, I have not been contacted by Ryobi as of this writing (March 10 & 11) to no avail. Ryobi customer service will not allow the consumer to speak with the Ryobi Safety Division. 

The weather conditions were dry, approx. 40 degrees, with snow on the ground.

incidentDescription:
I own a Kenmore Stainless Steel gas barbeque model #148.23683310. I purchased it two years ago. Last night while cooking for my family the floor of the fire box collapsed. The smoldering hot metal showered onto the propane tank and hoses below. This could have been a life threatening situation for all of us. I shut off the burners. I could not shut off the propane tank valve because it was covered in shards of smoldering hot rusty sheet metal. I had to anxiously wait far away for it to cool so I could shut the valve. I cannot fathom why a grill would be designed so poorly. The metal between the actual flames and the fuel source is paper thing steel that rusts away in less than two years creating a potentially grave situation!!

My attempts to resolve this issue with Sears have been less than satisfactory. I am one of thousands of consumers experiencing this based on my own internet research. There needs to be a product-wide recall on these life threatening appliances.

Thank you.

productDescription: Fan
incidentDescription:
The owner bought the house in March 2012 as repossession; the house was built 2002; when he bought, he had to totally remodel everything, i.e. the house had been destroyed inside; The closet in the laundry room was an area used for a salt water aquarium, most likely built-in when the house was originally built; The wall where the aquarium would have sat was open like there had been a window. There was no aquarium in this space when he bought the home, just an opening in the wall; He replaced the drywall where the opening had been, did not have to do any electrical or plumbing work to finish the wall;

The fire occurred in the middle of the night, when he woke up to his dogs barking like crazy; He said he couldn’t turn any lights on in the kitchen and saw an orange glow under the door into laundry room; He said when he first opened the door the exhaust fan was burning and fire was dripping on the floor along with plastic & aluminum metal.  He said with-in seconds the plastic cover fell & he was burned on the leg from the splashing molten plastic; He said he threw water on it from floor level but it didn’t do much; He said he got the ladder & using a bowl of water got up to closer & he was able to control the fire with several bowls of water; He said he got it out and never felt the need to call the FD.

productDescription:
Utilitech Space Heater sold at Lowes Home Improvement (I think its a house brand)
Item #0485219
Model# H-7247
DateCode# 0513

The product somehow carries a lab accreditation (Not surprisingly... its not UL listed) with ETL/Intertek #3125218  

There is an internal sticked under the light that reads in two lines:
LQ13
0377411
incidentDescription:
Had a space heater running in my bathroom, there was a large arcflash from inside the unit and the 20amp branch circuit feeding my bathroom GFCI's did its job and tripped. 

I opened the space heater and the mains wires are not thermally protected from the ceramic heater element, the "hot" wire was laying directly across the "neutral" wire of the ceramic element terminal. The heat conducted via the terminal caused a breakdown of the insulation that resulted in a direct short.

I infrequently use space heaters, but I am appalled that a company would forgo the 20cents required to thermally insulate the mains wires going past a ceramic heating element.

She flipped it over to a book and took it outside the house, the battery burnt through the book as well.   The battery was still sizzling when she took outside.  She stated that there is burnt marks on her bed headboard, black soot on her clothing in her room and 3 spots on her carpet were burnt.  The room had a overwhelming odor of smoke and she had to ventilate it.

productDescription: Ninja Professional blender
incidentDescription:
The consumer wanted the report to be worded exactly how it is written below.

The 6 Blades Assembly of this blender slipped right out of the Jar/Pitcher while I was emptying a fruit shake and severely cut my left thumb. The laceration was so deep that I was bleeding heavily and I couldn’t stop the bleeding. My wife had to rush me E.R to get stitches and medical treatment. As a result of the accident I was unable to move my thumb, I had no sensation/feeling and the pain was awful. Due to the seriousness of my injury I was sent by the hospital to see a Hand Surgeon. 

After having a physical examination by the hand specialist, he determined that he needed to proceed surgery on my thumb to explore damage of the tendon and nerve. Indeed, during the operation he noted that my radial digital nerve was transected and I had scar tissue. He had to repair the radial digital nerve and removed the scar tissue. I have gone through hand therapy, numerous doctor visits and to this day my left thumb hasn’t come back to its normal functionality. This accident occurred over a year ago and I’m only reporting it now because I was not aware of the Consumer Product Safety Commission. 

This blender is a dangerous hazard to consumers because its 6 Blades Assembly is extremely sharp and does not have an interlock/securing mechanism, it slips right off jar/pitcher. Until this day I have a hard time performing normal activities like I used to; I cannot even execute some at all because my left thumb has been permanently injured. I’m shocked to see that there have been many critical injures like mine reported here and this flawed product stills on shelves for resale. This sharp blade assembly could fall on someone’s arteries causing life-threatening hemorrhage, it should be recall immediately and removed from the market to prevent future injuries.

productDescription: Harbor Breeze ceiling fan
incidentDescription:
I have Harbor Breeze fans throughout my house. My understanding is that this brand of fans is a private brand sold by Lowe's.This past weekend one in a bedroom began making noise and made a loud eruption noise emitting a large amount of sparks onto a bed directly below with someone in it.
I do not feel comfortable turning on my other Harbor Breeze fans around the house.

productDescription: Off white with gray accents electric hair dryer with an approximately ten foot cord with safety device at receptacle end of cord.  External material is primarily hard plastic.  Has a removable, gray "concentrator" that fits on the output end of the device.  Additionally, there is a removable lint screen on the input end of the device, also gray plastic with a metal screen suspended within the ring.  Sold exclusively at Sally Beauty Supply, current version of device available at http://www.sallybeauty.com/hair-dryer/JLBERE30,default,pd.html
model: Jilbère de Paris Porcelain Series Hair Dryer
incidentDescription: My wife was drying her hair after showering with the Jilbère de Paris (produced by Conair, sold by Sally Beauty Supply) Porcelain Hair Dryer (called Jilbere Porcelain Series Hair Dryer at Sally Beauty) and after a few minutes of use the rubber/plastic insulation on one half of the cord began to catch fire.  Our toddler age daughter was sitting next to my wife at the time of the incident.  It caused no personal injury, nor any property damage beyond the unit itself. This continued until the unit was shut off by flipping the power switch on the unit.  Upon unplugging from the wall, an inspection revealed that one half of the power cord had frayed causing the insulation to burn.  This area of damage was just below the point where the cord entered the base of the handle of the hairdryer.  The unit was immediately removed from use and a replacement unit purchased.

productDescription: Sunbeam Heritage Series Stand Mixer; black color; 120 volts
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription:
On 02/23/15 the consumer used the unit to mix the ingredients he had to make muffins. The consumer put the muffin mix on a muffin tray and left it in the oven for about 20 minutes. The consumer removed the muffins from the tray and noticed a silver item on the bottom of one of the muffins. The consumer took the screw out of the muffin but did not know where the screw came from until he was cleaning the unit and noticed a screw missing on the bottom of the mixer blade. 

On 02/24/15 the consumer contacted the firm and informed them of the incident. The firm offered to sell the consumer a replacement blade for about $10 plus shipping. The consumer did not want to purchase the replacement blades. 

The consumer uses the unit frequently and has not had any prior incidents.

The consumer has some safety concerns with the unit.

productDescription: Black & Decker coffee maker model 1050B Type 1
incidentDescription: My coffee maker was plugged in but not on; I had put water and coffee in it for the morning, but had not programmed it. I heard a funny noise from the kitchen around 10pm and when I investigated, there was pungent-smelling smoke (it smelled like burned plastic) coming out of the bottom of the unit. I unplugged it and dumped out the grounds and water. The unit continued to smell so I took it outside.

productDescription: Aroma brand rice cooker model ARC-757SG
incidentDescription:
I have an Aroma brand rice cooker model ARC-757SG.
It is about 2-1/2 months old.

On Fri 3/6/15 when using it at usual, instead of shutting off when the rice is done as it is supposed to do, the heat stayed on at full power and the unit starting burning the rice and smoking very profusely. 

If I had not unplugged it, it would have continued heating until the rice caught fire, at which point it could have burned the house down. It would be a huge understatement to say that this is completely unacceptable.

Obviously this unit does NOT have an over-temp or over-heat sensor which would shut if off when the primary heat sensitive shut-off fails, as it clearly did in this case.

I still have this unit with the burned rice in it. I would be very pleased to send it to you for investigation.

This unit should not be allowed to be sold. All such products should have fail-safe circuits that prevent them from overheating to the degree that they could start fires.

This unit's label indicates that it is UL listed. How could such an poorly designed unsafe product have a UL listing? This should not be possible.

I am a very experienced electrical engineer with some experience in electrical safety design requirements.

PLEASE take strong corrective action immediately. This product is very dangerous and could easily kill people and cause large amounts of property damage.

productDescription: Keurig  mini. It's gray and silver. The model number is K10 and the serial number is 31.2004.0908341
incidentDescription: Hot water is coming out every where. Most of my coffee ends up on the counter and not in my cup.

productDescription: Dirt Devil upright
manufacturer: Royal Appliance Mfg Co business as TTI Floor Care N. Am.
incidentDescription: I wrote an entire page and could not "send". I was electrocuted by a dirt devil vacuum. The I was using the "hose" attachment when the vacuum rolled over it's own cord (I did not move it) I felt a shock in my arm, tingling pins and needles. The roller piece sucked the electrical cord, sparked, flamed then a loud "pop" and exploded. The frayed cord split in two. My small children were home when I yelled for help. This vacuum is extremely dangerous, and my entire right arm is still tingling off and on. I have photographs. Very frightening and potentially deadly. This product really needs to be recalled to prevent another consumer from getting hurt or God forbid, killed by it. Please help.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: electric skillet 12x16 inches
incidentDescription:
(02/13/2015) The consumer stated that he had the skillet set at 350 degrees. He was frying eggplant in vegetable oil for about 30 minutes. When he finish frying the egplant he noticed that the surface underneath the skillet was extremely hot. The skillet was on the counter and the heat from the skillet caused a crack in the counter top. 

The consumer stated that he has used the skillet before.

The consumer thinks that the product should be tested in the CPSC labs because it is unsafe.

(02/13/2015) The consumer contacted the manufacturer. The company offered to replace the product. He was asked to send in the electric cord.

productDescription: Krups Thermal drip coffee maker  #KT720D   This is a thermal glass lined carafe in a stainless steel outer casing with the rest of the coffee maker being stainless steel
incidentDescription: My husband and I had just made a pot of coffee in our Krups thermal drip coffee maker, model KT720D. My husband decided to open the coffeemaker and add a little cinnamon. When he attempted to lightly stir this, the coffee pot exploded with a huge noise. Glass from the lining blew out all over the kitchen, luckily missing ourselves and our dogs. the bottom of the pot totally cracked. Hot coffee was pouring out from everywhere. This morning I am still finding small pieces of glass, the size of glitter, all over the kitchen. We were so lucky someone did not get hurt. This needs to be corrected or taken off the market. We still have the outer heating part of the coffee maker but not the carafe.

productDescription: Cuisinart toaster oven, model TOB-40, 120 VAC 60 Hz 1800 W. Black sides and top, brushed stainless front. Three control dials, one red indicator light, and one start/stop button.
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription: This incident involves our Cuisinart toaster oven, model number TOB-40 120 VAC 80 Hz 1800 W. On Thursday, February 19, 2015,  while we were toasting bread, one of the bottom heating elements caught fire without any apparent cause. There was nothing touching the element when it ignited. I quickly shut off the toaster and unplugged it, and the flame slowly dissipated. The heating element is now deformed (bubbled). We have not used the toaster since. This is a major product safety hazard because, not only because of the spontaneous fire, but the speed at which it occurred. Had I not been standing right at the toaster, I would not have been able to put it out.  Please look into this product.

productDescription: Slow Cooker
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription:
The consumer stated that the handle on the slow cooker broke off. The consumer stated that this happened to the right side handle (when facing the front of the cooker).

The consumer stated that she was taking the slow cooker out of the cabinet. When she lifted the cooker, she noticed that the handle had broken.

The consumer stated that the cooker was not hit or it did not fall.

The consumer contacted the manf. and they informed her that her slow cooker has not been recalled. They informed her that there were no other complaints about this year/model. They offered to sell another one.

productDescription: Air Purifier
incidentDescription:
Consumer stated that his air purifier overheated, causing the plastic housing to warp and at some point shut off before causing a fire.  The unit was on for approximately 6 hours before the incident occurred.

(2/3/15) The manufacturer was contacted and he was informed that he would be sent a mailing label, he would need to find a package to mail it back to company.


Consumer feels that this air purifier is a fire hazard and should be reported.

productDescription: Portable Heater
incidentDescription:
The consumer stated that she was using the heater. The consumer woke up in the morning and noticed that the plastic around the heater door had melted.

The consumer contacted QVC and they informed her that they will pass it on. The consumer then contacted the president at QVC. The consumer was provided a refund.

The consumer contacted the manf. They kept asking her for a ticket number. The consumer was unable to receive any assistance.

The consumer called QVC again and informed them that she is unable to speak to anyone at Twin Star. The person at QVC informed the consumer that they will pass on the information to their legal team. 

The next day, consumer received a call from [REDACTED] at Twin Star (e-mail [REDACTED]).  [REDACTED]apologized for the issues and informed the consumer that this has never happened before. The consumer was concerned about breathing in the melted plastic. He asked the consumer to send back the product.

The consumer did not want to return the product. She will hold onto it.

The consumer added the company, Twinstar International, did not take her issue seriously until QVC legal contacted them directly..Consumer noted she not only worry for her safety, but the safety of others who purchase this heater which is an obvious safety hazard.

productDescription: 31.3002.0211564 	red  bought 03/17/2014 	from Keurig.com
incidentDescription: I was on the phone with the Keurig company and the customer service rep has been check different things with a paper clip.  I tell him that water is dripping out from the bottom.  He says well empty the drip tray.  I did and more water was dripping.  I turn the machine to the right and lots of hot water just rolls out onto my fingers rolling on my palm to my wrist.  The rep could of said becareful that hot water may pour out further.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription:
DeLonghi SafeHeat. 
Model: EW6507L
Type: KH650715P
Serial Number: 61114 JN (there appears to be a larger sticker next to the ending of JN that says JQ)
incidentDescription:
The heater keeps making a popping noise and it periodically sparks. When it is dark, this is very noticeable as the sparks will flash brightly. I only notice this when it is dark and I am facing the heater, but it has been happening on a daily basis for the last 2 months and they appear to becoming more frequent, so I doubt that it will stop or mitigate.

It seems as if the sparks are coming from the heater itself, since it stands about 3 feet or so from anything else and the sparks are not coming from the ground but rather a foot off the ground. 

The wire is not damaged and completely fine, so I doubt it is coming from there. It is not coming from the outlet as the sparks do not come from the wall.

productDescription: Cuisinart Toaster Oven Broiler, model number TOB-40. Silver and black. http://www.bedbathandbeyond.com/store/product/cuisinart-reg-custom-classic-trade-toaster-oven-broiler/1017958909?showRatings=true
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription: I have a Cuisinart Toaster Oven Broiler, model number TOB-40. The product is barely 8 months old now. The other day I used my oven, and the temperature was VERY off, my food was burned even though I cooked it for less time than I usually do. I turned off all of the knobs and turned around to tend to my burned food. About five minutes later I looked back at the toaster oven and the top coil was still on, despite ALL KNOBS being in the off position. The only way to turn the coil off was to unplug the machine. I contacted Cuisinart and they declared it a "warranty issue," which is disgusting because this is a clear fire hazard. I did a search online (Amazon) and it turns out several people are having similar issues with their products. This needs to be researched and recalled and Cuisinart needs to be fined for continuing to sell a product they know contains such a gross hazard.

productDescription: 1.5 quart, porcelain enamel, whistling tea kettle
productType: Coffee Makers or Teapots, Not Specified (452)
incidentDescription:
The tea kettle has a minimum and a maximum fill line.  Regardless of how much water was poured into the kettle, water spewed out it forcefully when it was poured.  The consumer said that she could not figure why the water was dispensed so forcefully.  The user could risk either getting burned or water could spew all over the counter.

The instructions for use suggested that the kettle came with a squeeze and pour handle.

The consumer said that she pours the water out of the tea kettle at night, but it took several months for her to figure out it contained rust.  The consumer is unsure when she discovered the rust, but it may have been mid-year 2014.

Consumer has ingested rust and maybe black coating inside of tea kettle unknowingly

1/7/2015:  The consumer called the manufacturer and explained her problems with the product.  The rep. agreed to send the consumer a replacement with a different design.  The rep. asked the consumer if she could send this one back to them so that they could analyze it and the consumer agreed.

Please see addendum as to what didn't happen!

The consumer said that she has burned her hand while using this kettle.  The consumer used burn cream for her injuries.  The consumer said that she burned her hands multiple times.  The consumer said that the cream made her hand feel better in a day or so, but she had to apply a bandage and it actually took several days for her burn to heal.

[REDACTED]
Addendum to report #20150108-D3755-1461149

Jan 30, 2015 consumer didn't receive new stainless steel tea kettle as promised.  She called and was told the company doesn't have any.  Consumer asked "why didn't anyone from the company call to tell her that".  On 1/7/2015 they promised it 10-14 days .  The Rep stated their "backup".  Consumer at this point requested a cash refund.  The rep agreed but it's going to take 6-8 weeks.  Seeing is believing.  The rep never requested the old tea kettle back to analyze it so nobody else gets burned.  The company original was suppose to send her prepaid postage and instruction.
Thank you
{Redacted]
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription: Honeywell Personal Heater HZ-315
incidentDescription:
Product: Honeywell Personal Heater Model HZ-315

I had been using the product for a few years without any trouble.  One day I noticed a smell, but I associated it with the usual heater smell.  Later in the day I went to run it off and almost burned my hand. The knob used to control the temperature was literally melting and was no longer attached to the metal post. I was able to turn it off and unplug it, and afterwards you can tell that the plastic around the metal post is completely burnt. It is as if the control electronics were in contact with the heating element. Not cool. This other link seems to report this problem.

http://www.saferproducts.gov/ViewIncident/1170824

productDescription: Electronic fireplace with built-in electric heater
incidentDescription: I returned home and found that the lights in my living room did not work. I checked my circuit breaker panel and found the living room circuit breaker had popped. I tried to reset it and it would not reset. I found a flashlight and investigated. There was smoke coming from behind my Dimplex electric fireplace. I pulled the plug and was able to reset the living room circuit breaker. When I left the house, I had shut off the fireplace using its remote control. I reported the incident to Dimplex and was told that this had never happened before and it could not have happened as I described because the fireplace had been shutoff. The fact that the main on/off switch was in the on position and that the remote on/off switch may have failed did not persuade them to assist me.

productDescription: this  was a Cuisinart DCC-1200 Brew Central 12-Cup Programmable Coffeemaker
brand: Cuisinart DCC-1200 Brew Central 12-Cup Programmable Coffeema
incidentDescription:
Purchased a Cuisinart DCC-1200 coffee maker in Feb, 2011. Hardly used at all till sometime 9/ 2013 and then daily.  In Feb 2015 started smelling something that was hot in kitchen. Then one morning there was smoke and coffee maker smelled terrible and could see base looked melted, quickly unplugged unit and took it outside to get it out of house.. 
Throwed miserable unit away.

productDescription: Cuisinart Griddler is designed to be used as a contact grill, pannini press, full grill, full griddle and have griddle
incidentDescription: I purchased a Cuisinart Griddler GR-4N at Bed Bath & Beyond on 2/25/15.  On 2/26/15 I was using it to make pannins.  Per the product directions it was normal to expect some smoke on the first use so I didn't think too much about it when it started to smoke. However as I continued cooking the unit shot actual flames out of the back.  I unplugged it took a picture of the burned out unit and emailed Cuisinart Customer Service.  After 3 canned response emails, the last of which told me I needed to pay to mail the unit back to them, I finally called.  I was told on the phone that I needed it to take the product back to Bed Bath & Beyond for a refund.  Beyond the bad customer service I received, I believe this product is unsafe.  Flames shooting out of the unit certainly would indicate to me the possibility of a larger problem.

productDescription: Rigid Tool Brand (18 volt Lithium Battery) Rechargeable
manufacturer: Emerson Tool Company, a division of Emerson Electric Co.
model: Rigid Tool Brand (18 volt Lithium Battery) Rechargeable
incidentDescription: Home fire started by an overheated Lithium Battery. Ignited a tool bag containing tools. No serious injuries reported.

productDescription: This is a Tozai oscillating fan, white in color.
incidentDescription: On the evening of February 14th, our department responded to an apartment fire.  Fire crews quickly made an interior attack and the fire damage was kept very minimal.  I was called to investigate this fire and arrived about 30-45 minutes after the initial call.  The area of origin was quickly determined to be a chair sitting on an angle in the room.  I found there to be two possible ignition sources.  One of them being a fan that was plugged into the wall, and the other being a wall mounted furnace.  There is not much left of the fan, basically just the motor and a little bit of the cord.  The residents stated that they had not been home since 0900 and the call came in at 1603.  Video surveillance verifies this information.

productDescription: Personal Blender
brand: Black & Decker Fusion Blade Personal Blender
incidentDescription:
The consumer noted she was preparing to make a smoothie and plugged the base of the blender in the wall electrical outlet...Immediately the blender turned on...She reached with her left hand to press the silver button to turn it off and an exposed blade lacerated her palm...She then had to reach with her right hand to unplug the machine...She was taken, by her husband, to the North Florida Regional Medical Center Emergency room for wound care and stitches...Upon returning home she looked at the blender and saw that the lid was on the base with the blade exposed. She received stitches and later on had to receive follow up surgery from a specialist on 2/2/15.

Caller feels that this blender is a safety hazard and that it should have been designed not to operate if the product is not closed properly.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

The consumer added the product was purchased in Summer 2014 by her mother, and she gave it to her the day she was injured.

productDescription:
Toaster Oven

Information off of the plug:
ETI 
CAT-07 E143469
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
The consumer stated that an incident happened with the first toaster oven in 2013.

The consumer stated that piece of toast caught on fire.

The consumer contacted the manf and they asked the consumer to cut off and return the end of the cord. The consumer was provided a replacement toaster.

The consumer stated that he started using the replacement toaster and the same exact incident happened with the replacement toaster in Jan/Feb 2015.

The consumer stated that he put in 4 pieces of bread to toast. The consumer turned the setting knob 2/3 way. The consumer stated that he went into another room and then smelled smoke few minutes later. The consumer went to the toaster and noticed that the toast had caught on fire. The consumer unplugged the toaster, opened the door and tried to suppress the fire. The consumer moved the toaster outside and dumped it in the snow.

The consumer stated that the toast setting knob is supposed to also act as a timer and eventually turn off the toaster after certain time (depending on the setting of toast). The consumer stated that the spring failed in the knob and failed to turn on the timer. The toaster stayed on the same setting until the consumer got to the toaster and unplugged it.

The consumer stated that this is exactly how the toast caught on fire in the first toaster as well.

The consumer contacted the manf in regards to this incident as well. They sent him a pre-paid mailing label and box to return the toaster. The consumer will be provided a refund.

productDescription: Wahl - WAH 9818 - Stainless steel battery-powered (lithium ion) trimmer.
incidentDescription:
Summary: The trimmer turned itself on and will no longer turn off.

Found battery-powered trimmer running in drawer after arriving home from work. It had turned itself on and would not turn off. This seems like a fire hazard given the lithium-ion battery and constant unforseen run-time.

productDescription: Honeywell Surround Heat Personal Heater Space Heater
incidentDescription: I am writing to inform you of a product malfunction with the Honeywell Surround Heat portable heater. Last night, 2/28/2015, the heater was in use and the thermostat set at the halfway mark. After about an hour of use, the thermostat triggered the heater to start up. I heard sputtering and then blue flames were visible through the vents at the bottom of the heater. The next moment, flames shot out of the base of the machine as I leaped out of my chair and disconnected the heater from the power source. I only removed this heater a week earlier from the bedroom my two young daughters share, and I can't even imagine the horror that could have possibly unfolded had this happened while they slept.

productDescription: Cyclonic Digital Ceramic Heater with Remote Control Model 5841
incidentDescription:
Lasko Brand -- Cyclonic Digital Ceramic Space Heater Model 5841

We have been using this space heater at home for the last few cold months.  Recently it was placed bedside.  Last night, I awoke to a strange, foul smell.  Without turning on the lights, I tried to locate the source of the smell -- and not thinking straight, simply turned off the heater and went back to bed.  Forgetting about this incident, I turned the heater on again tonight.  The odor appeared within minutes, and I immediately turned off the unit and located the odor source.  The heater plug is connected to a heavy duty extension cord which is plugged into the wall behind the headboard of my bed -- and where that connection lay on the carpet, both the plug and the carpet were melting/melted.  What I smelled were the fumes of melting carpet and plastic.  The plugs of both the unit and the extension cord are fused/melted together (unable to be separated) and the carpet has a burn the size of a "cigarette burn."  I am certain if this unit was left in on in an unoccupied room, it would have eventually set fire to the carpet.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: Stainless Steel 6.5 quart slow cooker
incidentDescription: I was cooking chili in my Cuisinart CSC-650 slow cooker when it stopped working.  The cord failed to retract and I removed the cover on the bottom over the retractable housing.  What I found were corroded wires that were continually overheating until they finally broke off free of their connectors.  On the white retractable cord spool, the power cord had melted, along with the plastic disc which was also burned housing.  The yellow disk, which should be white, suffered long-term heat damage and is where the unit is fed from the retractable cord, it too suffered long-term heat damage and was burned.  The saving grace is when this shorted out, the burned components and live wires were all housed in sheet metal.

productDescription:
14.5 inches wide, 10.5 inches long.  0.25 inches deep in the forward part, going upwards to 1.5 inches in the far side.

Dark grey, covered in holes for ventilation.  2 inside fans, both at the far side of the device.

A dark grey band of rubber, saying "belkin" on the forward front of the unit.

On the back, in the indentation, it reads "N10117  FOR HOME OR OFFICE USE US Patent 6,527,241"

On the back, outside the indentation, it reads "US Patent 8,061,679  Made in Taiwan   Model: FSL 103

Additionally, when I tried to upload my pictures to your website, it froze my screen, an error message flashed for half a second, and I had to recover the page.
incidentDescription:
Near the very end of 2013, my dad and I bought a Belkin cooling unit for my laptop computer.  For most of the year, while it worked, it did not work well.  I began to notice lighter marks on the grey plastic, about half a year in, and thought nothing of it.  I'd thought them the result of wear and tear on the thing, and probably from continually setting my computer down on it.

Apparently, they were singe marks.  Because on January 29th, at some point between midnight and 5am, my cooling unit caught fire, directly next to my left hip.  I heard sputtering, and wasn't sure what it was, but then noticed the little trail of smoke, emitting from my computer.  Looking down, I saw the open flame, which had burned the USB plug off of its wire, and was spraying flame out for about an inch, next to my flammable pants and blankets.

Immediately, I shut down my computer, to end the power source, and the flame died out.  I wasn't burned and nothing (except the Belkin cooling unit) caught fire.  It caused more white singe marks, around the area where the plug caught fire.  They match the previous singe marks, near the top of the unit.

We took the unit back to Wal-Mart the next day, but they said that it was not their job to report such things, and that we would have to do so.  They encouraged me to take photos of what happened, and contact Belkin directly.  But I did not wish to do so, because I have noticed that most companies do not like admitting to fault, in cases of dangerous incidents.  I doubted that anything would be done.

After some asking around, no one knew where to report this to, so I just typed in "Where do I report dangerous products?" into Bing, and it gave me your site.  Several other sites, listed beneath it, also referenced your site as the place to go.  So.

I've got 3 pictures of the singe marks and melted cable on my Belkin unit.  I'd imagine that several people could be harmed, by the sudden appearance of an unexpected flame.  I hope you guys can use my report, to stop this problem from hurting anybody.

productDescription: It's the Crock Pot Original Slow Cooker.  Stainless steel with a glass top, black handles.
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription: The crockpot was being used to cook chicken. It was on high and had been cooking for 3 hours when it suddenly exploded.  Glass flew 5 feet from the location of the crockpot and the lid shattered causing most glass to fall into the crockpot.

manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions

incidentDescription:
This is concerning a replacement decanter for a MR. COFFEE 10 and 12 cup. for Coffee makers :
EJ,ET,IS,LM AND VM series.

productDescription: Red and white  plastic [thermal container] approximately 8 oz.
incidentDescription:
Purchased plastic  [thermal container] insulated snack jar from Dollar Tree. 
Filled with boiling hot water after cleaning to see how long it would stay hot.
After filling, I tipped the container to check for leakage. The contents spilled
Onto my hand due to the product's lid not sealing.
Burned hand but not requiring treatment.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: Single serving blender
incidentDescription: I was using my Ninja Professional blender. I mixed the pancake batter and was unable to remove the top. I tried several grippers in order to remove it and it wouldn't bufge. I sat it upright on the counter and turned to do something else. All of a sudden there was a loud bang. The top flew off and went about 12 feet. The top contains the very sharp mixing blades and fortunately it did not fly in my direction or hit someone. The blades and force could have killed a child, pet or severely cut someone. Batter flew everywhere. I know that the lid was on straight. I have used this to mix this batter many times. I feel this is a great safety hazard. I did call the company about this incident but they seem to only be interested in settling a claim for damages. I do not feel that is an issue, but product safety is the issue.

productDescription: Cuisinart 1100 coffee pot, black
incidentDescription: We brewed our usual cup of coffee this morning and about 10 minutes after it finished brewing, I heard a crackling noise. I went over to the coffee pot and saw it was off but the coffee was boiling and i saw smoke forming around the base. I pulled the coffee pot off and the heat plate was smoking. Then I saw the back of the coffee pot was smoking, where the electrical cord comes out of the pot. I unplugged it and it was still smoking, got worse and was smelling really bad, like an electrical fire and plastic (this all happened within a minute, so, very quickly). My husband grabbed it and put it outside in the snow. It continued to smoke for at least 30 minutes afterwards.

productDescription: Aldi's Kitchen Living Turbo Convection Oven Model Number:4881,11/14,KHC-625
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
I was using my new Kitchen Living Turbo Convection Oven that I bought at Aldi's to cook chicken breasts.  The scant directions in the user guide recommend a 400 degree setting for 40 minutes on the top rack of the cooking bowl.  I set the chicken on the top rack and started the cooking process.  This was only the third time that I used this cooker since buying it in December.  
 I lifted the lid up, by the handle, after 20 minutes of cooking to turn the chicken.  To do this, I had to turn the lid upside down to rest on the counter top.  You can't just set it upright as the cooking element light won't turn off.  
As I lifted the lid by the handle, the handle completely pulled out of the lid!!! I was shocked but managed to catch this heavy glass lid, which weighs almost five pounds, before it could fall and shatter onto my ceramic tile floor.
I was able to complete the cooking of the chicken after carefully setting the lid back in place.

After the lid cooled, I examined it.  This is a very dangerous product that should be recalled from the US market.  The handle on the lid is held in place with two cheap plastic pegs that are under 3/8 of an inch long.. I also found that the metal holding the handle in place had cracked and the handle was no longer secure.  As the lid is used and heats up, the plastic becomes pliable and the pegs are not effective in holding the lid.  The handle is what controls the on and off operation of the cooking device and also the mobility of it.  If this lid had fallen onto the floor, the glass lid would have shattered, the light bulb within the lid would have shattered, and the electrical connection in the lid may have caused a shock or short.  I really would like to see this product removed from our US stores.  Thank you

productDescription: Sunheat heater model sh-1500
incidentDescription: We were using a Sunheat Portable heater to heat our daughters room which is a second story bedroom.  The thermostat was set to keep her room 60 degrees.  The heater did not run often as we burn wood and is used for supplemental heat.  On Sunday, February 15th, 2015, I awoke to a funny smell.  At the time it was faint but I could smell something.  I went to our basement thinking maybe someone laid something too close to our woodburner.  The smell was not in our basement.  I went back up to the main level and awoke my husband telling him something smelled like burning plastic.  He also immediately suspected the woodburner and I told him that I had already checked.  We checked the main floor and was unable to find the source.  I went to the second story, our oldest daughters bedroom.  Immediately after opening her bedroom door I could smell the burning plastic.  I immediately went and unplugged everything that was plugged in.  Plugged in items included an [REDACTED] in one outlet, a TV and DVD player in one, an [REDACTED] in one and the Sunheat heater in another.  The room stunk so bad and our daughter and her friend, both almost 15 years old, were asleep and unaware something was burning.  We woke them up and told them to get out.  We immedietly suspected the heater but when I unplugged it, it was not running, nor warm so we really didn't think it was the problem.  Unable to find where the smell was coming from we were ready to call the fire department but decided to remove the heater from the room and disassemble it.  Upon taking the heater to another room we could smell the same smell inside the heater.  We took the heater apart and realized that the quick connect for The power cord and the thermostat had melted and burned badly.  I called a few local dealers and they seemed to not be concerned.  I contacted the manufacturer and they stated they would send me an email showing us how to remove the quick connects and hard wire it.  No concern that it was a safety issue.  The employee I talked to stated it happens in some earlier heaters that they put the quick connect in.  We received the email showing us how to hard wire it but feel thhis is a major safety issue.  What if we had not been home??

incidentDescription:

We have a 
Black & Decker Toaster Oven  approximately 5 to 7 years old.  Here are all the numbers on the bottom of the oven:  CAT. No. cto612ob  --  type1 -- miramar -- fl. 33027 --no.1335.1&1335.2.9 --
3099249.  This number is on the end of the cord that goes into outlet -- 747x0.

You turn the oven on, then when it is supposed to stop automatically, it keeps moving to the position of stay on.  which means the oven will then stay on until you shut it off, but if you put it to the off position, it will move again to stay on. plastic dispenser push valve that releases hot water. Internal threads failed and it released from internal male bolt. This allowed boiling water to shoot out of tank in a straight line toward user resulting to burns to the hands. 
 Plastic threads either disintegrated or were factory defective allowing valve to fall off. Unit was less than one year old.

productDescription: Dehumidifier
incidentDescription:
Caller purchased his dehumidifier in May 2012.
The unit remained on but set to automatic so when needed it ran and when not needed it did not run.
This caller had no problems with it until December 10th, 2014 when he noticed that the plastic on the top melting.
He removed the top of the dehumidifier then observed that it was also melting inside.
He turned it off then unplugged it to prevent a fire and it has remained unplugged.
He is reporting this unit due to the potential for fire and burn hazard.
There are no injuries being reported.

He tried to contact the manufacturer but at this time has been able to obtain a live person only one time and that person told him they would call him back but has not.

productDescription: Vacuum
incidentDescription:
The consumer has owned the unit for approximately ten months. After about six months, the consumer noticed that the two contacts in the base of the vacuum were getting very hot during charging - hot enough to create a burn blister on his finger. 

The consumer indicates that the corresponding contacts on the charging unit are metal with a plastic form underneath. Some time later, these corresponding contacts began to distort and the plastic was distorting as well, which caused the corresponding contacts to fail to retract into the charging unit.

 The consumer was able to reshape them for a while. Eventually, they were so out-of-shape from the overheating that the consumer had to order a new charging base. A day later the consumer discovered that one of the contacts on the underside of the vacuum had melted into the plastic housing and was depressed by nearly ¼ inch. 

The consumer indicates that during charging, one would typically leave the unit alone for an hour or more. He is concerned because if the unit gets hot enough to create a burn blister to his fingers, he believes it could get hot enough to set fire to rugs, drapes, paper, etc. The consumer indicates that he uses his unit once a week but that it is charged six times a week after he vacuums each room (which is when the unit overheats, when it is being charged).

12/31/2014 The consumer contacted the manufacturer and after explaining the situation, they informed him that they would ship him a complete new vacuum and charging base and, in return, the consumer is required to send them back the defective unit. 

Because the manufacturer made an instantaneous decision on the warranty return, the consumer believes they already knew about the problem with these units and he suggests CPSC address the issue with the manufacturer. 

01/08/2015 (Approximately) The consumer states that his unit was shipped and he will have to ship back his original unit once the new one is delivered. 

The consumer states that he feels uncomfortable now with these products. He indicates that his new unit will only have a remainder of two month’s worth of warranty on it. 

The consumer has no injuries to report. The consumer believes the overheating on the vacuum may pose a safety and fire hazard.
victimSeverity: Injury, Level of care not known

incidentDescription: Product: Bodum French Press, large size - completely broke today while I was making coffee - the crack is a "U" shape that runs from one side of the canister across the bottom, and up the other side, a perfect crack that essentially split the glass in half. productDescription: Hamilton Beach Slow Cooker- plain metal finish. Two carrying handles. 5 quart capacity.
incidentDescription:
I have a Hamilton Beach-brand slow cooker, model 33156SZ. I conducted slow-cooking for approximately 2 cups (soaked) of garbanzo beans, at low heat, over a period of six hours. I left the slow cooker for that period of time, on "low" heat and with five cups of water for the two cups of beans. I went to check the slow cooker after that time, and found that the lid had fragmented. A hole, approximately two inches in diameter, had opened in the lid, and several shards of glass had fallen into the beans. Very small shards of glass had fallen on the counter.

I could not lift the lid by the handle, as the handle came detached from the lid. I had to remove the lid by holding the edges.

Neither myself nor anyone else was injured in this incident. The slow cooker had been on a "low" setting for six hours, and approximately 2 inches of water remained above the beans at the time of my checking the slow cooker. The beans were, however, ruined.
