productDescription: Blendtec Total Blender Classic with Wildside Jar - The jar number is: 12351 - it is 36 ounces - Wild Side
model: Blendtec total Blender Classic with Wildside Jar
incidentDescription:
The Blendtec Wildside Blender jar exploded while I was operating it in my kitchen on Monday, January 12, 2015.  
I purchased the Blendtec from Costco approximately two years ago. I make a protein shake every morning with the following ingredients:  ice, water, zucchini, spinach, beet, carrot, small baby cucumber, banana, frozen berries, and protein powder.
I generally “pulse” the shake a number of times, to cut up the big pieces, and then press the button for “whole juice” or “crush ice/shakes.”  I did that on January 12, and, within a few seconds of putting the machine on “crush ice/shakes,” (my hand was still on the lid), the jar exploded with a ferocity that sounded like a bomb going off.  It just so happened that the side of the jar which exploded was facing the windows in my kitchen and the wall.  My arm was in front of the jar, so it “broke” the explosion a bit from spreading even further.  My arm was covered with a thick, fuzzy jacket, so the plastic and food hitting me did not cause any harm.  Unfortunately, in addition to the walls, floors and everything in range, my bench seat (with custom made cushions, one chair cushion, and one of my two blinds in the kitchen were covered with the contents of the shake.   

Of great concern, of course, are the safety issues.  As is obvious to me, if the rupture had been on the side where I was standing, the plastic pieces could very well have exploded onto my face.  The plastic pieces, are shaped like shards of glass – with sharp points.  With the force of this explosion, and an unlucky spin of the plastic, an eye could have been lost.  This is the gravest apprehension I have with continuing to use the Blendtec.  

I also have great concern that the manufacturer told me they were "sorry," sent me a new Blender Wildside jar and did not explain why the jar exploded.

productDescription:
Whirlpool side-by-side refrigerator with door ice maker.
Model number:  ED2NHGXVQ01, 21.8 CUFT, White
incidentDescription:
Our Whirlpool refrigerator caught fire in the ice maker.  While we slept at night, something seemed to explode in the freezer.  By the time we got woke up and came in, we assumed it was the ice maker dropping ice, as it is usually loud.  
In the morning, we were overwhelmed with a gas-like smell.  When I found the smell originating from the freezer, I opened it and everything was black.  There was a large hole in the ceiling of the freezer, and melted plastic throughout the upper section of the freezer.  
What really concerns me the most is that the seal was almost completely burned through.  If it had continued through that seal, it would have easily spread to our wood cabinets directly above the fridge, and throughout our home--as we slept.  
Ultimately, we contacted Whirlpool who sent out a repairman.  He determined that the fire started in the ice maker, not the relay switch as we assumed (after reading about all of the recalls from Whirlpool and Maytag previously due to relay switches catching fire).  I can only trust that we were told the truth about what started the fire.  
However, in any case, an ice maker should not be the cause of a fire inside your fridge, especially not a well-respected name brand like Whirlpool who is all too familiar with freezer fires.
We were also told by Whirlpool that the side by side model we have is made to contain the fire inside. In our case, this was true, but this was only by luck I believe.  I will be attaching pictures showing the freezer's seal almost completely burned through.  
 
Thank you for your attention to this matter.

productDescription: Space heater

incidentDescription: Last Wednesday (01/21/2015) we smelled something burning in our home. We started going room to room till we reached the basement. When we got in the basement the smell of something burning or melting was very strong. productDescription:
Ceiling Fan with light, four blades, 42 inch diameter, indoor, flush mount.

Note:  Label lists manufacturer as:  Hong Kong China Electric Appliance Manufacturer Co. Ltd.
model: 40016 in manual, H42-4B/1L on product label
incidentDescription:
FIRE HAZARD! - When the ceiling fan was turned on at the wall switch a loud pop was heard.  The circuit breaker was found in the tripped position.  The circuit breaker was reset and the wall switch was turned back on.  The ceiling fan blades rotated but the light did not illuminate.  The voltage at the light bulb socket measured 75 vac.

The metal cap on the metal switch housing was removed.  Soot was observed on the wiring and the inside housing surfaces.  The insulation on the black wire to the light bulb was indented, partially melted, and ruptured.  On the cap, to which the light bulb socket bracket attaches, small metal beads and a pit, indicative of arcing, were observed.  It was also observed that the crimp on the bracket, which attaches to the housing cap, contained sharp edges.  The sharp edges of the bracket along with the tight packing of the wires inside the housing resulted in the abrading of the wire insulation.  As a result bare wire contacted the bracket crimp resulting in arcing and tripping of the circuit breaker.

An identical fan purchased at the same time and used in another room was disassembled and the same sharp edges were observed on the bracket crimp.  The sharp edges on the bracket crimp were created during the manufacturing process.  The electrical short was caused by the manufacturer making a defective crimp on the bracket.

This is a serious problem and could have resulted in a fire.

productDescription: Vitamix 5200, made by the Vita-Mix Corporation headquartered in Cleveland, OH
incidentDescription: We bought our 80+ year-old mother a Vitamix 5200 blender for Christmas (made by the Vita-Mix Corporation headquartered in Cleveland, OH).  The first time she went to use it, she had the idea to remove the lid (while it was still running) to help stir the mixture of vegetables she was grinding up in the Vitamix, using the plastic pusher device that comes with the machine. You can imagine the scenario from there, but the worst part is that the plastic food pusher shattered when she unintentionally contacted the in-motion chopping blade.  The pieces of the shattered food pusher became high-speed projectiles that went everywhere.  By the grace of God, none of the flying pieces of sharp-edged shattered plastic hit my mom, which was a truly miraculous escape of injury. That the Vitamix machine is able to operate even with the lid removed is a real concern because I know my mom will not be the only person out there to try that stunt, and in all likelihood, others will unfortunately not be as lucky as my mom was in avoiding injury.  In seeing those shattered pieces of hard, sharp-edged plastic, and how far they flew across the room, I can tell you that anyone being hit with any of those pieces would have every potential to sustain serious or even life-threatening injury.  This product is excellent for its intended purpose of grinding food, but the lack of a safety switch to prevent its operation with the lid off is a serious safety omission that needs correcting to prevent severe and life-threatening injury to consumers.

productDescription: Lorex baby monitor, Model # WL4320, 4.3" digital wireless LCD color monitor - malfunctioning rechargeable battery pack

After a few days of use, the battery would not keep a charge (NOT safe to have a baby monitor shutting off shortly after being removed from the AC cable).  Got a replacement battery from Lorex.  A few months later the 2nd battery wouldn't hold a charge and expanded breaking out the battery tray cover (? fire risk).  Got a 3rd battery from Lorex.  Over the past week the 3rd battery is expanding again, and won't hold a charge.  CLEARLY this product should be recalled entirely as a safety risk.   Please CPSC: even if the device does not catch fire, it is a risk to infants if the monitor shuts off very prematurely when on battery power-- you have an unmonitored infant.  As a board certified sleep disorders specialist, let me also add how extremely dangerous this is, to have a completely unmonitored infant, when parents falsely believe their monitor is working.  NOTE: after contacting Lorex today to find out about getting a 4th battery, and finding out they have a technical bulletin on this, isn't that enough for the CSPC to force a mandatory recall and refund program for parents owning this flawed device?

productDescription: Hamilton beach [slow cooker], "set and forget" 33967
incidentDescription:
I had a Hamilton Beach [slow cooker], the "set and forget" 33967. I had it for five years, and hadn't had any problems, until yesterday. It had been set on high, for four hours, to cook a broth.  My husband was home at this time, and with in a 30 minute period, it went from "just fine" to explosion of broth all over the kitchen. 
First of all, the lid was not clamped down, so there was no reason for it to explode due to pressure. Second, I was cooking the broth in four hour increments, because I am cautious. 
According to my husband, it started beeping, didn't stop beeping, and when he came in to see why, it was frothing over with extreme heat. He managed to unplug it without burning himself. 
Now why, when this [slow cooker] started to malfunction, would it lock into an extreme heat, unlike anything we'd ever seen before? Why wouldn't it just shut off? The broth managed to hit items 2 feet away, which is quite unlike anything I've ever heard off. 
We've gotten a new [slow cooker]. I will never buy anything by Hamilton Beach again.

incidentDescription:
Re: Safety Hazard, Best 48" Stove Vent
P/N: Model K260A, K260A, Rev-G

Dear U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission

The attached memo to [REDACTED] Broan-Nutone describes how I seriously lacerated two of my fingers (total of 19 stitches) on an unprotected, raw stainless steel sheet metal edge inside my Best 48" stove hood (P/N referenced above). This occurred in mid-July 2013 when I was trying to replace one of the four the removable vent baffles after cleaning, and it was catching on some hidden obstacle in the vent assembly (...turned out to be dangling 120V power cord assembly).
 
The unit was purchased from Ferguson Enterprises on 28-Dec-2013 (invoice Nr.2736968), and installed on February 5, 2014 by Greg Georguson Summit, Inc, [REDACTED] of Lodi CA.

Also, be aware that when trying to replace on of the (four) halogen lights, the light socket installed in the hood broke free as I tried to "push and twist'' a new light bulb into place, potentially exposing me to yet another raw stainless steel sheet mental edge, as well as the now exposed, internal120V AC electrical circuits. [REDACTED] sent me a replacement light socket that I self installed. The old one is still trapped somewhere inside the vent unit. This latter event occurred in mid October, 2014.

I believe there is a simple fix to the exposed, raw sheet metal edge on which I lacerated my fingers: simply roll over this sheet metal edge by ~6mm prior to assembly. I recommend that this unit be recalled until the above issues are addressed and fixed.

Sincerely yours,
[REDACTED]

productDescription: Oster Toaster Oven, Model number TSSTTVCG03. Color: Silver.  Purchased at Costco, Brick, NJ
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription:
I purchased an Oster Convection Toaster Oven, Model number TSSTTVCG03 from Costco about a month ago.  I had purchased a similar one for my mother in the past and thought they were the same.  

Last night, we awoke to the smell of burning electrical wire at 4 a.m.  We discovered that the oven was still on from dinner the night before.  Upon inspection, we realized that the bottom dial, which you turn to set the time for your cooking, had a peculiar and very dangerous feature:  If you turn it to the right, you choose the number of minutes it is to run and then it turns off automatically when it hits zero.  This is the customary feature on these ovens with dials. However, on this model, to the left of the Zero, there is a "stay on" feature that allows the oven to keep running.  Problem is, if you need to manually turn the oven off because you overestimated the time, and you accidentally turn it a hair too far to the left, the oven does not turn off.  The ticking sound is so faint or nonexistent that you would never know until you smell burnt wires or your house burns down.  This is VERY DANGEROUS and we are lucky to be alive. This is particularly dangerous for older people;  the reason I bought this for my mother is because she forgets to turn the toaster off.  However, on her model there is a "hard" off -- you can't turn it left past off because there is a stop feature at zero.

I'm not sure why the "stay on" feature is necessary -- this is a toaster oven not a professional oven so the timer  should be required.  In this case, the oven no longer works so "stay on" resulted in it burning up after a few hours anyway. However, if I'm missing something and manufacturers want a "stay on" function,  then it should be accessed in one of two ways: 1) by a clearly marked additional button; or 2) by having to turn the dial all the way around (one full turn) to access it.  The oven should have a hard stop when turned left to zero.

I do want to say that Costco has excellent customer service and will take this back  no problem but I am concerned about other stores that sell this and the possibility of people dying in their homes.

productDescription: Eden Pure GEN3 Model 1000 Quartz Heater
incidentDescription:
My mother-in-law was using a Eden Pure Model GEN3 manufactured in 2011 to heat her living room. The unit was purchased new last year (2013), and had been used only a few times prior to 12/13/14. The few times that the heater was used prior to 12/13/14, my wife's mother had always commented that the cord was very warm during use. On 12/13/14,  while the unit was operating normally, the circuit breaker suddenly tripped. I went out to reset the tripped breaker and noticed that the panel was warm in the area of the breaker. I felt the breaker and it was hot to the touch. I went back to the living room and began to unplug the heater, when I noticed how extremely warm the cord was. The wall outlet face was warm and also the entire receptacle was giving off a substantial amount of heat. I removed the outlet cover to assure that no burning or arcing had occurred at the outlet. The entire assembly was just warm like it had been overloaded. The circuit in use was a 15amp branch line in a home less than 15yrs. old. No other high draw appliances or lamps were in use at the time of the tripped breaker. No extension cords or any adapters were in use with the heater at the time of the incident, it was plugged directly into the wall. I advised her to not use the heater until I could verify that it was operating correctly and I had checked for a recall. 
Several days later I began to research this product and found some shockingly similar stories from many other customers. It seems that this is a common issue with this product and it has already been attributed to at least (1) serious fire. I also found some recall information involving the same manufacturer with another product. 
Needless to say, I am wondering why this product is still available to the public and why a recall involving all similar types of their products has not been issued. This appliance very well may have caused a serious fire by merely operating under normal circumstances. I am not sure if the appliance is UL approved, but it certainly would not be considered safe. See links below:

http://www.consumeraffairs.com/homeowners/edenpure.html

http://edenpure-heater.pissedconsumer.com/

productDescription: Fahrenheat FUH54 5000-Watt, 240-Volt Garage Heater
incidentDescription: I purchased a Fahrenheat FUH54 5000-watt electric heater from Home Depot in January of 2014 and had it installed in my garage.  I ran the unit to keep the garage at about 50-degrees through the winter.  This fall I turned the unit back on to again keep the garage slightly heated.  On two occasions the heater thermostat failed to turn off the heater.  The last time it happened, the garage was close to 80-degrees before I discovered it was stuck on.  I turned off the breakers to the heater to shut it off.  I then opened the bottom of the unit where the thermostat and wiring is located.  I found that one of the wires that goes to the thermostat had the insulation charred off on the thermostat end, indicating it had overheated a lot.  I did some research online and found that the thermostat in the unit is known for this defect...that there is a flaw with the thermostat that causes arcing and overheating.  This is a HUGE fire hazard.  There was enough heat in the wire to destroy the wire insulation which is also enough to start a fire.  The serial number on the thermostat is 5813-11002-000, thermostat model number is ATC-26B SPST.

productDescription: Gas heating stove, freestanding
productType: Gas or Lp Heaters, Other or Not Specified (392)
incidentDescription: We purchased a new Jotul free-standing gas heat stove to replace a wood stove.  It was finally up and running with a new gas line on December 1.  We had it set on a thermostat to keep the basement room at a steady temperature.  Upon returning from an errand on Dec 3, we entered the room to find the flame considerably larger than it was set, and there was a sound like a blow torch coming from the stove.  It was quite alarming.  My husband set the flame level back, but that did not correct the blow torch sound.  We turned it off, turned it back on and it was okay.  This has happened four times now since Dec 3. Today is December 19, and it happened this morning.  We no longer leave the stove set on a thermostat unless we are in the room.  I did a search online and found a forum where others with Jotul stoves were discussing this issue, and one of them had contacted Jotul and spoken with an engineer.  The first post on this forum was 2005.  Several comments were posted about this issue, in 2007, 2010, and the latest in 2011.  The findings were that the engineers confirmed there is a problem with the burner, and that there could be some damage to the stove from repeated blow torch effects.  So, we shared this with our dealer, who called Jotul and had it confirmed with them by telephone.  A new burner is on order and will be installed as soon as the part comes in.  We are sharing this issue because we see this as at least a costly problem with the stove over time, and possibly a potential fire hazard.  It is alarming to us that this issue was first mentioned in the forum 9 years ago, and that it has been ongoing, and yet our dealer had never been provided information about this.  We believe this is worth some investigation by some organization.  If that is not you, please advise so we can pursue this.

The consumer stated that the powder got to the walls, counter, ceiling, pots and pans. The consumer stated that when they try to clean it up, the powder just spreads more. 

The consumer stated that he contacted [REDACTED] on 10/1/14. The consumer spoke to [REDACTED] in Product Service department. The consumer also spoke with [REDACTED], who was an engineer. productDescription: Goal Zero 11002 Sherpa 50 Battery
incidentDescription:
Bought Goal0 Sherpa 50 Battery approx 4/29/2012 from Amazon.com    

I bought the Sherpa 50 for my bug out bag. I took the Sherpa 50 on a camping trip, and it worked well for that trip. I used it to power some Bose speakers mounted on my backpack for a trial run. A year rolled by since then and I wanted to take it to the beach the following morning to give the Bose speakers some extended play. So, I plugged the Sherpa 50 it in at 11:30 pm. About 2 hours later my sister awoke me that she was nauseous that some noxious burnt electronic smell was coming from my office where she was sleeping near. I rushed into the room where the battery was being charged only to be sickened by the odor coming from the room. The battery had melted from the inside, and produced such a terrible smell, that I had to evacuate the house to a nearby hotel for 2 days to let the house air out. I placed the battery outside. I can still smell traces of the odor in room where I left it about 2 weeks later. When I contacted Goal Zero about the battery problem the next day, they knew all about it...I asked if it was toxic and would I need treatment for the 5 people that were present when the device failed. They stated it wasn't toxic that it was some sort of sodium battery and that it only happened on a few of the batches. They said that what happened was a few cells went dry over the course of a year and that the charger was trying to fully charge the dysfunctional battery bank, that's when the meltdown would occur. They have known about this problem for some time. I was LIVID when I realized that they didn't issue a recall or warning about the battery. It could have saved me a lot of headaches and money at 2:00am. It could have burned down my house if I was not home, killed the family pets, or worse .... if it turns out to be toxic it could have sickened family members. Even after my call to them, they didn't seem to interested in contacting Amazon to issue a recall. Seems morally bankrupt to me. I feel like my family's safety has been priced, a calculated risk because "only a small number fail". Well, that's great, unless your unaware and the owner. I find it criminally negligent not to issue at least a warning to watch it or charge it outside. I own dozens of cordless tools, not one battery charging failure there. I am going to make Amazon aware of this issue. Let me know if your experience was similar. Rest assured this product won't be there for you when you need it the most. It's an expensive hazard in my book. They company took my name and address, and said they would replace the product. So Far, nothing has come through. Empty promises. I'll issue an update on here if they make good on their promises. I'm interested to see if they issue a recall after this or after I flag it for Amazon to examine.

*** AMAZON DIDN"T GET OFF THEIR FATT [REDACTED] TO RECALL THIS PRODUCT AFTER I TRIED TO TELL THEM MANY TIMES ***


http://www.amazon.com/review/R2RR0P83CMB67I?ref_=pe_623860_70668520

incidentDescription: I am writing in regard to a warm mist humidifier model #HWM-340 manufactured for/by Kaz USA that resulted in fire during normal operation last week.   The humidifier was filled during the day and then we had forgotten to refill before we went to bed.  Normally if the water level got too low the unit would shut off and the refill light would come on, but overnight the auto shut-off function failed and all the water boiled off resulting in the unit overheating.  I awoke at 6:30 AM last Tuesday to the fire alarms going off in my house and my living room filled with smoke.   When I went downstairs, the humidifier was in full flames but luckily I had a fire extinguisher handy and was able to put the fire out before my house or furniture caught fire.  The unit has water level indicator that shuts the unit off when the water drops below a certain level, but the unit does not have any type of overheating protection if the unit is run without water.  There are warnings in the manual not to operate without water, but if the fill level system fails, then there is nothing to prevent the unit from overheating and catching fire. The 15 AMP circuit breaker to the outlet also tripped but not before the unit caught fire. The unit is about 1-1/2 years old.

productDescription:

Unit fed 240V/ twin 50Amp circuits to electrical resistance heater coils in forced-air heat pump HVAC system.  (electrical resistance heat used as "back-up" heat source to HVAC system)

The Siemens 240V 50A circuit breakers date code is 07/99

I will post a picture if that feature is available. It broke at one rivet and is cracked around two others. I'm really lucky I didn't break a tooth, cut my mouth, or swallow a piece of metal! 

When I went to buy a replacement blade, I learned that it is common for these blades to break, and people have reported this to Cuisinart and to you. See http://www.amazon.com/Cuisinart-FP-100TX-blade/product-reviews/B000TENO5A/ref=cm_cr_dp_qt_hist_one?ie=UTF8&filterBy=addOneStar&showViewpoints=0 and http://www.amazon.com/Cuisinart-FP-100TX-blade/product-reviews/B000TENO5A/ref=cm_cr_pr_hist_2?ie=UTF8&filterBy=addTwoStar&showViewpoints=0&sortBy=bySubmissionDateDescending
Altogether, 19 of 68 reviewers mention their blade breaking or cracking.

My blade broke from the underside, which is not someplace I ordinarily see. Cuisinart should include a warning to inspect all parts of this blade after use.

Didn't understand, it was essentially brand new as it was just purchased 2 months ago. Decided to locate Conair's consumer phone number and called.  Absolutely rude service, told my product was not covered in a recall as it has 2 screws (didn't know until today when I called that there was one), I asked if there is another number I could call to speak about my issue and he said no. This time he unplugged the battery itself from the charger and replugged it back into the charger(Red light flashing now). Owner watched the charging light for 5 minutes then left. Upon investigation by the owner, he noticed the battery on fire. He retrieved a dry chemical extinguisher and used it to extinguish the fire. Owner's sister called 911 to report the fire. incidentDescription:
I was riding my electric bike down a paved street when the folding frame cracked at the weld 
connecting the front part of the frame to the hinge that was still attached to the rear part of the frame. While I was able to coast onto the sidewalk, the bike split in half before I could stop so I was still moving about 8mph. I suffered cuts and bruises on my right arm, stomach and ankle. This bike 
was well maintained and had about 2300 miles on it, mainly street riding and paved bike paths.
I contacted the company on 7/28/14 and sent a customer service representative [REDACTED] the 
photos of my bike, but not of my injuries. The company response was to send my an upgraded 
full frame, not folding and  I would have to transfer the existing parts to the new frame. I did
not get the name of the witness who saw my crash, so I have not pursued legal action.  At this
time I am trying to warn riders of this bike of the potential danger, since the company has not sent
any warnings so far to registered owners like myself. They posted an updated manual on their
website noting that the frame could crack on this bike, but they do not notify registered owners
of this, for obvious reasons.

productDescription: Toaster Oven
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
I was using the toaster oven to reheat pizza.  I set the timer dial to 10 minutes and after that time heard the bell go off signaling it was done.  I was working on something else in the kitchen so I didn't get the pizza out right away.  A few minutes later I smelled something burning & went to the toaster oven...The timer dial had gone past the 'off' point and continued all the way to the 'Stay On' position.  Moving the dial back to the 'off' didn't turn the device off, the timer again travelled to the 'Stay On' position.  Not having any other means to turn the device off, I unplugged it.  

This is a faulty design that could have caused a fire.  This spring-loaded timer dial works by turning it clockwise from 'Off' to set a specific time and turning it counter-clockwise from 'Off' to have the oven be constantly on.  Unfortunately, a faulty 'stop' at the Off position causes the unit to go to the 'stay on'  position indefinitely.  The failsafe 'stop' position on an oven like this should be OFF, not ON!

incidentDescription:
The Kenmore 2 Burner Grill Patio Grill first caught on fire on either July 5th or 6th when being used to grill hamburgers.  With approximately 8 burgers on the grill, the entire grill caught on fire during our party.  We had cleaned the grease trap prior,  but we figured it may have caught on fire due to the extreme heat that day.  We were able to put the fire out without too much incident, but the frame definitely had been on fire.  Then, using the grill again on August 31st, we tried to slow cook ribs.  Again, we cleaned the grill thoroughly before use.  After about 30-45 minuts cooking on low, the entire grill, frame and all, caught on fire a second time.  This was the last time we used the grill.  We were able to put the fire out with minor incident.  My friend helping put it out was burned.
We contacted Sears about the grill since it is under a year old.  Sears sent out 3 repairmen.  We have been told that the grill caught on fire because we used meat on it and it is not designed for anything with fat content even though the manual shows that it is a standard grill designed for meat and fish products.  In response to the burn marks on the frame, Sears has notified us that although it appears the frame has been on fire, they have no way to prove we did not light the external part of the frame on fire ourselves.  We are obviously done with Sears on this product, but we are more concerned that owners of this grill will face potentially dangerous situations when using it.  The frame appears to be structurally unsound in that is cannot handle the heat of a grill.

productDescription: Hoover  (also known as TTI Floor Care) vacuum Model # UH70820
incidentDescription: Earlier this year (March 3, 2014) I bought a new Hoover  (also known as TTI Floor Care) vacuum Model # UH70820 from Target. Immediately out of the box the motor made a humming noise. A few months after owning it the vacuum Model # UH70820 it overheated on the bottom and burned holes or roller marks in to my shag rug. I filled out a complaint form on their website June 25, 2014.I did not hear back from Hoover/TTI Floor Care so I emailed them again on July 18, 2014. I didn’t hear from Hoover/TTI Floor Care until late August 2014. The lady who called me was very kind and informative. She knew a lot about Hoover/TTI Floor Care products and explained to me that Model # UH70820 doesn’t have an automatic roller shut off feature. That when you are using the hose feature the rollers continue to roll, causing the bottom of the vacuum to overheat. She explained the damage claim process and that she would send me model that was redesigned with an automatic roller shutoff so that when I use the hose the replacement won’t further damage my property. I received my replacement much sooner than expected, I was told 7-10 days from the date Hoover/TTI Floor Care ordered it but it was here in 2-3 days. Again immediately out of the box the replacement has a humming or vibrating noise coming from the motor. I’ve not yet used the hose attachment feature, mostly out of fear of further damaging my property.Last week I’d realized it had been 5 weeks since I filled my damage claim against Hoover/TTI Floor Care and I was supposed to hear back from Hoover within 2-3 weeks with a determination of my claim. I emailed my Hoover/TTI Floor Care representative and she called my fiancé back this morning. The Hoover/TTI Floor Care Engineer could not find anything wrong the vacuum so my property damage claim was denied. I called back and a request was submitted for a supervisor to call me back. I spoke to a Hoover/TTI Floor Care supervisor today and she informed me that the engineer can’t duplicate this in his lab which means I must have used it incorrectly. They claim you have to use the vacuum with the back turned towards the object you’re vacuuming with the hose. This is not in the manual but non sequential because the hose is short and that’s the only way you can reach the back of the couch I was vacuuming any way. They further claimed that you have to have it tilted slightly back which is contradictory to the manual that states, “Brushroll continues to turn while product is turned on and handle is in upright position. To avoid damage to carpet, rugs, furniture and flooring, avoid tipping cleaner or setting it on furniture, fringed area rugs, or carpeted stairs during tool use.” I assured them that it wasn’t tipped and that it was in the upright position which is what the manual advised. She read the manual with me and noted my use. I requested that the engineer test on a high area rug like mine and not your standard carpeting but I’m not optimistic that will change his mind. Hoover/TTI Floor Care doesn't feel that a vacuuming overheating is a safety or fire issue but I disagree. If it got hot enough to melt my rug and turn it into what feels like hard plastic this definitely is a safety issue. A vacuum has no business getting that hot.

brand: rc3 GPS with heart rate monitor
incidentDescription:
I suffered a serious burn injury from a heart rate monitor I was wearing during the Portland Marathon on Sunday Oct 5, 2014. 

I purchased the RC3 GPS watch and heart rate monitor on Friday Oct 3, 2014 from a company called Polar www.polar.com  

Polar had a booth at the Portland Marathon bib pick-up festival and I purchased the watch and monitor there. 

I followed the instructions carefully.  I set up the watch and heart rate monitor.   I moistened the strap as directed.  I attached the battery component to the strap and connected it around my chest with the battery component facing up and positioned just over the xiphoid process at the lower part of my sternum.  

Everything seemed to be working fine and I was tracking my heart rate, mileage, and time for over 20 miles of the marathon. 

It was a hot day so some of the residents of the homes along the marathon route were standing by the road with hoses to spray down the runners. 

One of them sprayed me with the hose and at that moment I felt an electric arc on my chest immediately under the part of the strap where the battery attaches.  I felt severe pain and there was the smell of burnt skin.  

When I finished the race, I looked at my chest which was then hurting pretty bad and I had sustained a nasty burn in 2 horizontal strips across my chest. I was up all night with pain.  I attached a picture that I took this morning with my cell phone. 

Has this been reported before?  I am fearful that I bought a defective product and that others might suffer a similar fate.  After all runners routinely run in the rain and on hot race days, it is very common for the spectators to hose down runners.

productDescription:
Holmes Low Profile heater
Model HLP3300B

Metal and plastic housing, black, with rotary control knobs (off-low-high and thermostat).  NEMA 1-15P polarized plug.
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription:
I recently received a Holmes electric space heater as a gift.  The very first time I plugged it up, within minutes the control panel caught fire.  Fortunately I am both a nurse and a volunteer firefighter/officer and was able to remain calm, unplugging the heater and carrying it outdoors to the front porch until the flames self-extinguished.  As I write this, I have extraction fans running to suck the cloud of noxious, choking smoke from my home.  The incident affected two victims, myself and my adult son who resides with me.  Symptoms included coughing, respiratory distress, eye irritation, and headache.  Respiratory symptoms were alleviated by removal to fresh air pending the extraction of the smoke.  Both of us still have headaches and eye irritation but no acute distress and normal vital signs.  Because the event was quickly limited by unplugging the device and removing it from the structure before flame spread could occur, fire/EMS activation was not required. (As a fire lieutenant, however, the incident will be reported as a "near miss.")

I am horrified that in the year 2014 we still have so many poorly made, outright unsafe products flooding the American market.  This is by no means the first space heater I have seen catch fire, but it is the first one I have seen to do so within minutes of its first use and the first one to do so in my own home.  I am just thankful that, as a firefighter, I have a very high index of suspicion when testing any new appliance.  Because I was directly observing the heater when the flames broke out,  I was able to take very swift action before any flame spread could occur.  Had this heater been purchased by a typical American purchaser who naively trusts the safety certification marks to actually mean anything, the outcome could have been tragically different.

The product information follows:

Holmes Products (div. Jarden Consumer Solutions), Boca Raton, FL
Product made in China (*sigh*)
Model number HLP3300B
Date code from plug blade:  D200 TET
Supplier code from plug blade:  GEM
Additional codes from plug molded housing:  KAI HUA KH-9921 E25426

Since so much hot steam is shooting from the exposed connection, it's very hard to hit the stop button since you're most concerned about getting your hands anywhere near the shooting steam.  I sent the product in for repairs and made specific note of this problem.  I did some reviews online to see that this flaw was not uncommon and reported on Amazon among other sites.  The coffee maker was returned quickly and everything seemed to be working fine. The repaired unit included a brand new nozzle that I assumed was reengineered to fix the earlier separation problem.  After several uses, it separated once again shooting hot steam on my hand and hot milk all over the counter and my clothing. 
I contacted the company and complained about the problem and repeated burn danger.  The service team was very responsive again but simply sent my another new nozzle.

When I approached I could see coffee in the carafe was almost boiling and the maker seemed to be turned off. I reached to unplug and noted smoke pouring from the opening where the cord goes into the back of the coffee maker. Bottom of the coffee maker was burning. Rancid burning plastic electrical smell. I was fortunate to be in the kitchen when this happened. The amount of burning in such a short time would have caused a house fire had I been upstairs on a work morning. This happened on Sunday so I was downstairs in the kitchen. Scary to think it could have burned me, my husband, my pets, my house and property. 

Upon researching for possible reasons I found this has been a common occurrence with a variety of models and sizes of Cuisinart coffee makers. It appears that Cuisinart should recall coffee makers.

She saw the fan blade on the floor (directly under the fan, a straight drop) and the remaining three still spinning, but wobbling. The fan blade did not hit her or anything else in the room. I saw that the bracket holding the fan to the rotor had snapped. I turned off the fan and did not see any cracks in the other brackets. 

The customer service representative I called within a week of the incident was really unhelpful.  According to the rep, all she can do is sell me another part ($5 for part, $7 for shipping). The company takes no responsibility whatsoever, even when I pointed out that this was a very dangerous situation. The rep was really unmoved and completely unconcerned that someone could have been badly hurt. She denied that there have been any other incidents like this. 

All the rep wanted to do was sell me a replacement part, and kept denying any responsibility, saying that the fan was not covered under any warranty. I mentioned the Limited Warranty listed in the manual and the rep said since the fan wasn't broken when I got it, and since I installed it, Lowe's is also not responsible (since apparently I am assumed to have installed it incorrectly). I even got further clarification that if I had purchased a “lemon” and it had broken a day after I got it, the company would still refuse to replace the fan. productDescription:
Kenmore 4 Burner Gas Grill Model # 720-0830A
Sears Link:
http://www.sears.com/kenmore-4-burner-all-stainless-steel-gas-grill/p-07133492000P?sLevel=0&redirectType=SKIP_LEVEL
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
On April 18, 2014 I purchased a gas grill from Sear's store located in Seaford Delaware a Kenmore Model#  720-0830A.  I used my grill over the next few weeks and had intermittent problems getting it to light. Sometimes it would light on the first attempt like you would normally expect and other times it took several attempts to get it to light.  On July 8, 2014 I attempted to light the grill at approximately 1850 hours. My first few attempts to get the grill lit were unsuccessful.  I tried several different burners thinking there may be a problem with one or two specific burners. I then took the regulator off of the LP gas tank, I remove the tank to feel it's weight. After verifying the tank was heavy and had plenty of fuel I reattach the regulator and install the tank in the grill.  I again attempted to light the grill and was unsuccessful.  I turned on several burners in an attempt to get fuel to the burners.  When I pressed the igniter a large ball of fire came out of the top of the grill (which was open) as well as the bottom of the grill (where the gas tank is stored).  I was blown back a bit.  Once I stood up I found I had sustained burns to my left leg, left arm, neck and face.  I was immediately taken to the emergency department at my local hospital.  From there I was transferred within the hour to a specialty burn care hospital in Baltimore, Johns Hopkins Bayview Hospital. I spent the next two days in the burn intensive care unit. I had sustained second-degree burns over 6% of my body.  After being discharged and recovering for the next few weeks I again attempted to use the grill.  My first attempt at using the grill after my recovery was successful. The grill lit just as anticipated and had no problems.  My second attempt at using the grill was unsuccessful and I again could not get it lit after multiple attempts using multiple different burners.  After being frustrated from spending $400 on a grill that I could never longer use I started looking for remedies.  I was strongly suspicious of the gas regulator being faulty.  My reason for the suspicion was the fact that at times when lighting it you could not even smell gas. I felt as though the regulator would not always pass fuel.  I purchased a new gas regulator and hose I installed it on the grill and I've now been using it for several weeks with no issues at all.  I strongly suspect the gas regulator has some type of defect. I contacted Sears and was transferred around amongst many departments finally landing in the recall department.  I spoke to a gentleman and told him my story I gave him the model number of my grill he responded with "yes your grill has a recall". The gentleman stated that parts would be sent out to my home and once I receive them to call the numbers provided and a technician would come out and replace the faulty parts.  I asked him to elaborate on the recall because I wanted to know if it was safe to use or what parts were involved in the recall. He stated he only had part numbers and had no further information, he then transferred me to the service department. I spoke to a very nice gentleman there that put the model number into the computer and then told me there was no recall and had no idea with the other gentleman was talking about. He did suggest that I contact the Consumer Product Safety Commission and file a report.  I simply don't want this to happen to anyone else.  I have retained the original gas regulator should your agency want it for testing purposes.  I would be happy to answer any questions or provide additional documentation such as receipt for the grill, medical records, and pictures of my injuries. Thank you for your time and looking into this matter.

Home Depot refused to exchange the product.
victimSeverity: Injury, Level of care not known

productDescription: Dehumidifier
incidentDescription: We left our dehumidifier on and found it emitting a burning smell and a faint white smoke when we arrived home.

productDescription: Large slow cooker, oblong, silver with black trim.  "Hamilton Beach STAY or GO" imprinted on lid in white lettering.  Black handles and silver lid locks on sides.
incidentDescription: After four hours of cooking a pot roast on high setting, with lid locked, the glass in the lid shattered into tiny shards.  They held together but bowed inward and crumbled into pieces when we pressed lightly on them.

productDescription: Weber Titanium Cast-Aluminum 2-Burner (21,700-BTU) Liquid Propane Gas Grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
At approximatly 3 pm, I turned on my Weber gas grill to preheat for 30 minutes.  After 30 minutes, I heard a crash and went outside to investigate and found my grill tipped over and on fire.  After calling the fire department, the grill exploded, sending a ball of flames up the side of my house, setting the house on fire.  There were two explosions that followed.

After the fire was put out, I inspected the grill, finding that the bottom of the body of the grill had melted, which caused the grill to tip over in the first instance.  I note that the grill was two years old and clean.  Also, the grease pan had been replaced less than 8 weeks ago and the grill had undergone light use during that period.

Based on the manufacturers specifications, the grill body was made of aluminum, which has a melting point of 1400 degrees.  I stongly suspect that the body is not, in fact, made of aluminum, but rather tin which has a melting point of 500 degree.  There is no other explanation that I can descern since is it clear that it was the melting of the body that caused the grill to collapase and later igntire the propane tank.

productDescription: Soleus air dehumidifier model# GM-DEH-45-1, serial# 10007930825
manufacturer: Gree Electric Appliances, Inc. of Zhuhai
incidentDescription: Fire involving Soleair Dehumidier model# GM-DEH-45-1 on 8/22/14 at 11:30AM CST.

productDescription: 2014 Weber Genesis three burner propane grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription: Homeowner had purchased this Weber Genesis propane grill online from Lowes around July 4, 2014. He stated that he had used it approximately 6 times since he had purchased it. Homeowner and his wife both stated that at least three out of the six times the grill was used they could hear a hissing noise coming from the connection between the gas hose and the tank. On the night of the fire very shortly after lighting it to cook dinner, they noticed it on fire. The homeowner noticed the flames had traveled down from the burners towards the propane tank. Homeowner extinguished the fire with a dry chemical extinguisher prior to FD arrival. No injuries, but the grill did suffer fire damage.

productDescription: Cuisinart Compact Single Serve Coffee Maker Model SS-300
brand: Cuisinart Compact Single Serve Coffee Maker Model SS-300
incidentDescription:
My Cuisinart Compact Single Serve Coffee Maker Model SS-300 normally, after brewing a cup of coffee, automatically turns off. Two weeks ago, I made a cup of coffee and was about to leave the house when I smelled something burning. I returned to the kitchen to find the Cuisinart coffee maker smoking and when I lifted the brewer head and looked inside, it was glowing bright red. I immediately unplugged it and took it outside. If I had not returned to the kitchen and unplugged the machine, I fear that my home could have been damaged or destroyed by a disastrous fire.

I have pictures of the melted inside parts of the machine below the filter compartment and the melted filter holder that sits on top of it that I can provide.

productDescription: The defective battery was purchased from BJ's Wholesale club.  8 of the 12 batteries in the package had been used without incident.  The package indicated "Best if used by 2015".
incidentDescription: I bought a package of 9v batteries by Berkley & Jensen from BJ's. I used a battery to power a CO2 detector in my home.  In the middle of the night, I awoke to a loud pop like breaking glass.  Immediately thereafter my CO2 detector produced a low battery warning. When I opened the CO2 detector to replace the battery I discovered that the battery had exploded.

productDescription: Kenmore four slice digital toaster oven.  The model has changed a little since this one but I've attached a photo.
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription: I have had the Kenmore 4 slice digital toaster oven for over a year and a half.  On 8/14/14 30 minutes after using it I heard a noise from my kitchen and walked in to discover the glass door had shattered.  The handle was on the counter and there was glass strewn 3-4 feet around the kitchen (it is small so couldn't go any further).  It was still making noise and crumbling slowly.

productDescription: Coffee maker
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription:
I have a Mr Coffee VBX23 model coffee maker.  I've had it for about 2 years.  While using it today, the unit start producing smoke.  

It had completed the brewing cycle about 5 to 10 minutes before the incident and the hot plate was on to keep the coffee warm.  I noticed that it was producing quiet popping-like sounds, and shortly later, I smelled the smoke.  Smoke was quickly coming out of the rear of the unit, where the electrical cord goes into it.  I quickly unplugged the unit, brought it outside, and hosed it down to prevent a fire.  I double checked and there were no items resting or close to the coffee making that would have been the source of the smoke.

incidentDescription: We started hearing noises in the blender but did not know what it was. We noticed a metal taste in our smoothies and then the whole blade unit came apart in pieces.  My husband almost got cut collecting the pieces not knowing there was two loose blades.

productDescription: Bonavita Thermal Glass Carafe Coffeemaker
incidentDescription:
I was rinsing out my Bonavita Glass Carafe with warm water when it suddenly exploded with  glass shards.  The carafe was last used at 10 am that morning and it was being washed out after the dinner dishes at 7:15 PM. 

No brush or other item came into contact with the inside of the carafe.  Luckily, my face was turned away when the explosion occurred.  The carafe was the last item in the sink and it was sitting by itself with only the water inside the carafe, the sink did not contain water.

productDescription: Cuisinart Classic Toaster Oven / Broiler, model # TOB-40
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
In December 2011, I purchased a Cuisinart Toaster Oven, model # TOB-40, through Amazon.  In July of 2014 I noticed the lower heating element had warped upwards and the insulation had split about 1 1/4 inches, exposing the element.  In seeking product info on Amazon, I noticed about 25 user complaints documenting the same problem that I experienced.  Some of the users noted they had received an electrical shock or had seen sparking, in addition to the obvious fire hazard.  Personally, I experienced sparking.  Here is a link to that web page:

http://www.amazon.com/heating-warped-upwards-through-problem/forum/Fx18TEHZUNAHXJ8/Tx2D06DTFL9WTPF/1/ref=cm_cd_dp_aar_al_a?_encoding=UTF8&asin=B004JMZGM2

The unit was still under the 3 year warranty and I contacted Cuisinart.  They offered to replace the unit with the same model.  I inquired whether they had modified or corrected this model to address the defect and they had not.  I declined their offer to replace the unit with the same model #TOB-40.

productDescription: Blender
incidentDescription: In April of this year I purchased a new blender through Amazon.com.  The actual seller is STL Pro, Inc.  The blender cost $124.99+shipping.  Yesterday, 8/18/14, as I was using it to blend some almond milk, oats and blueberries, it began to burn.  I pulled the plug, but I have severely damaged lungs from my military service and was driven out of the house by the smoke.  I went to Amazon.com and looked at the user comments for this particular blender.  There are 85 comments of which 3 mention that the unit started to burn when they used it.  I contacted Amazon who referred me to STL Pro.  STL Pro wrote that because the 30 day return policy had expired I had no recourse.  I assume they will continue to sell this product which is clearly defective and dangerous.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription:
Hose regulator assembly (LP Hose, CHLO251-Q)

Part # 30500002
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
The consumer stated that she purchased Ducane gas grill in 2007.

The consumer stated that she had an issue with leakage in the hose. The consumer contacted the manf. The consumer was offered a free replacement hose assembly under warranty. 

The consumer ran into the same issue again in May 2014. The consumer purchased a new hose assembly from Ducane for approximately $30. The consumer stated that the hose assembly failed within few months (started leaking).

The consumer contacted Ducane with the issue. The consumer was sent a free replacement hose assembly with some other additional parts that she purchased. They informed her that they will test the assembly before they send it out. The consumer received this hose assembly around 7/25/14. 

The consumer stated that she put the new parts on along with the new hose assembly. The consumer stated that she used it once. The consumer stated then she heard leakage and tested it with soap water. The consumer stated that this assembly failed as well (started leaking).

The consumer contacted the manf and asked for her money back on the hose assembly purchase. The consumer was informed that she would receive her refund. The consumer believes that this assembly is hazardous and informed the manf to look into the issue.

The consumer purchased a new hose assembly from [REDACTED], made by [REDACTED] (made in Canada). The consumer stated that she has not had any issues with this assembly. The consumer stated that this assembly is made slightly different from the previous ones she had by Ducane/[REDACTED].

productDescription: Ready to go at a minute's notice, the Dremel 7700-1/15 MultiPro Cordless Rotary Tool Kit is perfect for a variety of hobby, craft, and light-duty home improvement projects. The two-speed rotary tool is capable of doing almost anything the standard MultiPro does, but with cordless convenience. The kit comes with a carrying case, battery pack, charger, one attachment, and 15 accessories that give you the option of cutting, grinding, sanding, polishing, routing, drilling, and carving--so you'll be ready to tackle whatever project you dream up next.
productType: Other Portable or Stationary Power Tools (809)
incidentDescription:
I purchased this "Dremel 7700-1/15 MultiPro 7.2-Volt Cordless Rotary Tool Kit" from Amazon in November, 2013.

This rotary tool has a removal battery that also doubles as a hand grip. However, I noticed that the battery cannot be locked to the tool properly. This is quite dangerous as the rotary tool runs at 20K RPM and some of the tools are used for cutting wood and metal. Depending on how you grab the tool, when the battery come loose, the top portion could come off and cause damages.

I called customer service and it seems they are aware of the problem but I think they should issue a recall to the product.

On August 4, 2014 at 10:30 pm, my SaFPWR leather case with rechargeable battery for iphone 4 burst into flames a foot high!!!!!   I awoke to the noise and was able to douse the case with water and put out the fire.  Luckily I awoke and was able to avert a real tragedy.   The case is completely destroyed.  

The case was plugged in for recharging.  My iphone was in the case.  The area around the camera lens of my iphone melted.  I do not want this to happen to anyone else.  They may not be as lucky as I was!

My Mr. Coffee coffee maker overheated to a degree that could have caused burns or a fire. I purchased the coffee maker only a few months ago. productDescription: Kenmore Elite Red Stand Mixer 400watt, 5quart, 120Va.c, 60Hz. Serial #100.8920890A
incidentDescription:
Kenmore Elite 400 watt 5 quart Red Stand Mixer
Product faultiness description
Serial #100.8920890A / 120Va.c 60Hz
Made in China
8/9/14

To Whom it May Concern;

I was given a Kenmore Elite 400, 5 quart Red Stand Mixer as a gift from my then boyfriend in the Christmas of 2010. I haven't used it since 2012, the last time I video taped it spinning out of control. 

This mixer will suddenly speed up in the middle of mixing something on slow speed. I would be mixing say, some cake batter on #2, it immediately would speed up to #9 in half a second. Very quickly! It would fling batter or flour everywhere. My son would be baking with me and he got really got scared of it. I would stop it immediately of course. It scared me too! The mixer is pretty heavy duty and something really serious could’ve happened, fingers hurt, parts could’ve come undone, who knows. No injuries have occured. I tried to use a few times after but it would speed up even more frequently. This mixer is really dangerous and unpredictable. I do not recommend buying this product and I hope there is a recall on it.

Thank you, 
[REDACTED]

productDescription: 12 cup programmable coffee maker
incidentDescription:
My few months old programmable coffee maker somehow became defective and defaulted to the ON position with the heating element being on. Tried to turn it off, but stayed in the ON position. Tried to unplug and plug it back to see if it cleared, yet still stayed in ON position.

This seems to be a serious safety issue, as the defect caused the coffee maker to default to the ON position. Luckily we were home and noticed this, but I can only imagine the results if we were out for a prolonged period and the coffee maker sat on counter top getting hotter and hotter.

productDescription: Harbor Breeze Celing Fan - manufactured by Lowes.
incidentDescription: The metal bracket securing the ceiling fan failed and the ceiling fan was then held in place by electrical wiring.

productDescription: Dehumidifier
incidentDescription:
The consumer stated that she noticed the dehumidifier was too hot to the touch. She then checked to see if the unit was dirty. She looked in the back of the unit cleaned the fans, where the water drips. She states that the unit was not excessively dirty.   There were no prior incident with the unit.

Consumer stated that approximately after an hour and a half of use the dehumidifier became extremely hot which can cause burning. She feels that the unit poses a fire hazard. 

The manufacturer was not contacted.

productDescription:
Parrot ar.drone battery and wall charger

Parrot ar.drone product... serial number PS720000AH0K166430
Model # of suspect supply/charger: CHA012008  with a date stamp of 1247D
incidentDescription:
I have a recently purchased (date uncertain, seeking records) Parrot ar.drone battery/charger set that experienced a significant failure of the battery cells and housing during charge.  3 LiPo cell packs are severely swollen, splitting open the battery case.

I removed the battery from the charger, photographed the item, contacted Parrot support who advised to contain it in a saline solution to render it inert.

At this point, regardless of warranty, etc. Parrot seems unconcerned about safety or root cause (which I would believe to be a failure of the charger to stop charging.)

Had I not noticed this sudden condition I fear that explosion, fire, property or personal damage may have occurred.

Significant concern that Parrot may have many of this product in the hands of consumers unaware of the potential danger/life-safety issue.

I have pictures and the defective item intact for inspection/analysis.

productDescription: 6 quart, oval black shaped crock pot
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription: Almost three years ago my friend bought me a crock pot from Walmart on Black Friday. Ive used it about 10 times since ive had it and almost always cook food at a low setting. Well I haven't used it in about 2 or 3 months. I live in Phoenix and usually made soup in it,  and since the last time its been washed, sitting on my counter near the sink (for a lack of space) with the lid sitting on top, upright with the cord laying inside. This evening for no apparent reason it suddenly cracked into a thousand pieces but stayed put together.  Luckily there was no food in it and no one was near by. After looking online and asking a few friends I guess this does occasionally happen.  Ive never, in my 28 years of living, seen or heard any of my mother's crock pots do this. Im assuming it's the brand.

productDescription: Cuisinart pod type coffee maker
incidentDescription:
Bought a Cuisinart pod type coffee maker a few weeks ago.  One morning, July 21, 2014, I had used it, making three cups of coffee.  Then it shut off automatically, as it was supposed to.  About an hour later I happened to be in the kitchen, heard a noise and looked over to see the unit steaming and smoking.  The heating element at the top, under the water reservoir was bright orange and red.

I removed the unit outdoors, so keep the smoke alarm from activating.  I phoned the company, which said they would send me a replacement unit, but that they would not pay for return shipping of the defective unit.  I will not return the unit at my cost, since I did not manufacture and sell a defective product.

I seems very irresponsible that the company would not want the unit back to examine, and perhaps help avoid fires at future customers' residences.

The model # is SS-300.  Serial #31200 (or 31206 - difficult to read on the unit).

6/22/14 The retailer was contacted and he was informed to file a complaint with the agency.  He feels that this leaf blower is a fire hazard and should be reported.

productDescription: 45 pint Dehumidifier
incidentDescription:
The caller, a private fire investigator, states nobody was home when a small fire originated from the location of the dehumidifier. The dehumidifier is always plugged in. The unit is automatic and turns on automatically.  The location of the dehumidifier is where the primary damage occurred. The caller states that as the fire progressed, it melted a plastic water supply line which sprayed water and extinguished the fire. 

The owner plugged the 3 prong plug of the dehumidifier into an adaptor that allowed it to be plugged into the 2 prong female outlet in the wall.

The unit is damaged internally and the label with the unit’s identification information is no longer there. The owner of the unit obtained the units information (product overview print out of the unit) from Home Depot, where she purchased it from. The owner made a visual identification of the unit to obtain this information. 

*  There were no injuries.
*  The model number did not appear to match any of the CPSC recalls.

incidentDescription: We were given this dehumidifier from my "elderly" mother and father-in-law and was using it in our basement..It worked FINE for a while and then started to smoke, so we unplugged it right away. Took it apart and the thermostat wires were literally, burnt off.. I went on the website to see if I could get the part for it and saw that it was recalled due to this happening. I know it has been a while since it was purchased and has the date, 2000 on it, but wanted to see if something can be done to compensate me for the damages to the humidifier..The model number is AHG4OLAG2. I am afraid to buy the part for fear that this might happen again and do not want to waste money putting into it, if this is going to happen again..PLEASE HELP ME!!!!!!!!!! I was upset that this happened because it was hardly ever used prior to this happening and dehumidifiers are expensive...Thank You

productDescription: Dunkaccino Machine at Hess Gas Station
incidentDescription:
BELOW IS A COPY OF A LETTER SENT TO DUNKIN DONUTS 1/8/14:

Dunkin' Donuts

Canton, MA 02021

Dear Sir/ Madam:

I am writing regarding your Dunkaccino machine at the WilcoHess location.  
We visited this store (#4001) on 12/31/13 @ 3:15PM.  This is a self-service Dunkin Donuts location.  
My son attempted to get a Dunkaccino.  The instructions on the machine stated that you should push the button to release the liquid but stop when the cup was half way full.  He went just past that halfway point when filling his cup before he released the fill button.  When the cup began to overflow onto the counter, he panicked, grabbing the cup from the machine and scalding his hand.  The salesperson quickly came out to check on us & cleaned up the spill.  My son immediately ran his hand under cold water, took Tylenol for the pain & inflammation, & was given an ice pack by the store manager for the drive home.  His entire hand up to mid forearm was pink & edematous.  Fortunately, he did not blister.  He had discomfort for the remainder of the day & a few days later had peeling of the skin as if he had a sunburn.

I felt it necessary to contact you to ensure this does not happen to anyone else.  The store employee stated that this has happened before, indicating that this is not an isolated incident.  

Safer practices should be put into place.  It would make sense if the machine had a button the customer could press based on the cup size.  The cup would be placed onto the machine, a button pressed for size, and no further interactions would be required by the consumer until the machine is finished.  No gray areas for someone to have to look into the cup for a halfway point or misjudge the level to stop the machine before it overflows.  
 
There also seems to be no safety switch to prevent a young child from quickly pressing the button without even having the intent of getting a beverage.

I urge you to look into this hazardous issue.  I would appreciate a response with a plan on what will be done to keep this from reoccurring.  I look forward to hearing from you.

productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
I purchased a Jenn-Air Built-In Gas Grill Model # 750-0142 Lowe’s SKU # 168935. As I understand it, this grill was manufactured by NexGrill and sold under the Jenn-Air brand name. 

After replacing the steel rod cooking grids on at least three occasions, it has become apparent that there is a serious manufacturing defect in this portion of the product. 

What has me very concerned is how they are manufactured. The grids are advertised as Stainless Steel. I am no expert, however, it appears that they are actually made of steel rods that are then “dipped” with a stainless steel coating. The end result is that after about 4-6 months of normal usage the outer stainless steel coating begins to separate and razor sharp pieces of steel flake off of the grids. This is bad enough, however, even more dangerous is the fact that those razor sharp pieces stick to the food you are cooking, causing an extremely dangerous hazard should someone ingest or swallow a piece of this steel flake. I have photos to illustrate the issue visually if you would like me to send them to you.

productDescription: Danby 60 pint dehumidifier, model DDR6009REE
incidentDescription:
Lights dimmed briefly, then the circuit breaker blew.  Not being positive what blew the breaker, I disconnected a few things, turned off the lights and reset the breaker.  After about a minute, it blew again.  That time I saw a flash (the dehumidifier was near the breaker box) and I realized the dehumidifier was the cause.  I also detected a slight smell of heat/burnt wire insulation.

Since the unit was out of warranty, I decided to open it up to see if it was something as simple as a short in the power cord where it entered.  It wasn't.  What I found disturbed me and makes me concerned that the unit has been a potential fire hazard all along.

One of the wires running to the compressor had its insulation worn through, presumably due to vibration over time where it rested against a metal stud that holds a cover over the wiring where it enters the compressor.  Due to the arcing, the metal stud was mostly burnt through!  The insulation of that and the other wires going to the compressor also seemed hard/brittle from heat at the last couple inches before the compressor.  I can't say for sure whether it was from heat over a long period of time or heat from the short that blew the breaker, but typically insulation doesn't get stiff like that from one brief heating, and therefore I suspect the wires had been getting hot over time, which could also explain why the insulation wore through and allowed the short circuit.  (I would think this issue could have been avoided if it had been manufactured with better quality wire -- better insulation and/or heavier gauge wire, and some foam or heavy heatshrink insulation over the stud....or routing the wiring so it couldn't come into contact with the stud and wear.  Minimal cost at time of manufacturer.)

I immediately checked to see if the unit had been recalled, but it was not one of the models that are part of the current Danby / Gree recall.  I can't help but wonder, however, it the problem is similar to what happened in the recalled models.

I called the manufacturer, Danby, gave them this information, and then emailed the representative pictures of the burnt wiring.  The manufacturer's representative was very kind and interested in the issue, but said she could do nothing since the unit was out of warranty, but that she would forward the information and the pictures on to the appropriate people to look at the info from a safety issue.   

I have not heard back yet, but that was only yesterday.  In the mean time, I decided to file this report to serve as a warning to others to at least be on the lookout for the issue.

This appears to be something that can likely be repaired, and if done properly, repaired in a way that it won't happen again in the future, BUT as manufactured, I believe the dehumidifier to be unsafe, especially since dehumidifiers are often located in basements and areas that are generally unoccupied and therefore less likely to be noticed if giving off smoke, sparks, or a hot smell.

productDescription: All Clad slow cooker ceramic crock
incidentDescription:
My complaint is in reference to the All Clad slow cooker, model SERIE SC01, which has a ceramic insert.  Twice the insert has mysteriously cracked out of the blue after cooking for several hours.  It was not due to cold or heated ingredients being added, nor from careless mishandling or accidentally knocking against other hard surfaces as I am very cautious about this.  During the first incident, I happened to notice a small crack near the handle (which did not leak liquid) but I believed could eventually expand and lead to a safety issue.  I ordered a new (and expensive) replacement crock through All Clad – alarmed, but not throwing in the towel just yet.  After using the replacement crock for one and a half years, it mysteriously cracked while cooking on low after two hours.  Fortunately I was home when it happened.  I heard a loud pop in the kitchen and knew right away what it was.  By the time I made it into the kitchen, I saw liquid pouring out onto the counter.  There was a sizable crack down the side and across the bottom of the crock.  Within seconds the hot liquid contents were spilling out of the crock into the bottom of the metal cooker, through a spill hole onto the counter top and streaming down onto the floor.  The mess, albeit a real pain to clean up and a ruination of my anticipated dinner, was the least of my concerns.  What if I had not been home to see this problem and the contents continued to cook without liquid?  Would this start a fire?  Could the liquid spill onto an electrical cord nearby and cause an electrical fire?  Would the crock break apart in my hands spilling its hot contents all over me as I tried to dump them into another container -creating a burn incident?  I plan to keep the crock as evidence.

productDescription:
Harbor Breeze Bellevue Ceiling Fan, white matte, 44," has drop option, but was installed flush to ceiling
Item # 0096982
Model # E-BE44MWW5C
incidentDescription:
Our Harbor Breeze ceiling fan was installed by a professional electrician in September 2012 (purchased August 2012), but has not been used very often (it has maybe been on between 10 and 20 times total), because the nursery was not in use until our baby was born and sleeping in his own room, and the fan was not needed during the winter.  The fan/light is connected to a wall switch which controls the light, and the fan speed is controlled with a pull chain.  The fan and light have worked well since installation, with no noise or wobbling when the fan was in use.

Late in the evening on June 25, 2014, I went to my infant son's nursery to prepare the room for the night by turning on the monitor and turning on the fan.  Because my son had fallen asleep in another room, I went upstairs without him in my arms, which is normally not the case, so I could turn the light/fan on, then turn the light off with the pull chain to avoid waking him with the bright light.  With the light still on, I pulled the chain once for the fan, which put it at high speed.  After waiting a second, I pulled the chain again to reduce the fan to medium speed.  With the second pull, the fan, still spinning, can tumbling out of the ceiling onto my head.  I was able to protect my face from the spinning blades and light kit with my hand, and am so grateful I was not holding my son and that he was not in his crib to be hit by the falling debris.  

The fan stayed connected to the electric wires in the ceiling, but I was able to turn the wall switch off and eventually prop the ceiling fan on a ladder until an electrician could come to remove it.  We found the metal mounting bracket had snapped and a piece of it was on the floor.  Our electrician said he had never seen anything like it in 30 years.  I called the company and they said they would send a replacement part.  I asked if there were any recalls for this, as a newish fan should not have parts that break in such a dangerous way.  I was told no and that it is often because electricians use old mounting brackets when installing new fans.  I can attest this was NOT the case for us, as I was present for the installation and know all parts were new and from the fan box.  I told the customer services representative that we were lucky there were no more serious injuries than the very minor injury to my finger when deflecting the falling fan and encouraged them to investigate the mounting bracket.  To date, I have not been contacted for further information.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: Revlon Ionic / Ceramic / 1875W Hair Dryer Model RV484
incidentDescription: The incident involves a Revlon RV484 Hair Dryer. The hair Dryer was bought new approx one year ago and has been used daily since it was purchased. On the incident date, when my wife was using the hair dryer, it began to vary in speed and power by itself, then began cycling off and on during use, until the unit failed completely. I took a look at the hair dryer and could see that the wire insulation looked like it was failing where it enters the strain relief on the hair dryer handle. I took apart the hair dryer and tested the components with a multimeter. I isolated the failure as an intermittent break in the copper wiring under the insulation. By twisting the cord while connected to the meter, I could make or break continuity. The insulation, which appears to be a rubber-like material, at the point of failure appeared deteriorated. The remainder of the wire insulation (the complete six feet from the integrated GFCI to where the cord enters the hair dryer) just didn't look right either. It wasn't as deteriorated as the insulation at the point of the wire failure, but it appears to look like the early stages of deterioration. Thinking that this hair dryer power cord failure was just a fluke, I went onto amazon.com to read reviews about this particular hair dryer to see if others had experienced this failure. I found that mine was NOT an isolated incident. Others have had the same issue with the power cord, including smoking and sparking, from the wire insulation failing where the cord enter the handle of the hair dryer.
