manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription: we had a Sunbeam ceramic heater in our bedroom. Model number SCH4062-WM2. we were very careful to make sure nothing flammable was near the unit due to a chance of fires. I put my daughter down to sleep at 9:30pm and turned on the heater because the room was cold. i went out to use the computer prior to going to bed. 10 minutes later the fire alarm went off. I rushed into the room to find it full of smoke and the back of the heater on fire. my husband quickly grabbed our fire extinguisher from the kitchen and put out the fire. thankfully we were all sleeping and our fire alarm was working or this could have ended badly for us. upon closer inspection of the unit, you could see that the inside of the unit had caught fire. this could be very dangerous for others owning the same unit as me.

productDescription: Duracell Batteries
incidentDescription: I got my son the [REDACTED] I had just put brand new Duracell batteries in it and with in a week they were going dead so I opened it up and the batteries were leaking acid and it felt warm RECALL!!!!

productDescription: Farouk Chi Rocket Low EMF Hairdryer
incidentDescription: I have been using this hair dryer for around 2 years. It is a Farouk Chi Rocket Low EMF. As I was using it, the electrical cord broke at the strain relief fitting on the handle and produced a spray of sparks, almost electrocuting me. The attached GFCI apparently did not trip.

productDescription: Boxed Fan
incidentDescription:
The consumer stated that he was using the fan for about 3 minutes before it caught on fire. 

The consumer stated that he saw the fan turn off. The consumer went to check to see why the fan turned off. The consumer stated that he saw sparks and then flame in the center of the fan.

The consumer unplugged the unit but that did not stop the fan from burning. The consumer stated that he put the fan in the shower to put out the flame. 

There are no recalls on this product

The consumer stated that he was unable to speak to anyone when he contacted the manf (the manf is no longer in business)

productDescription: Electric Radiator heater
incidentDescription:
Consumer stated that the heater malfunctioned and started to overheat and smoke.  He noticed that the control switch did not function properly, if low heat was selected it would go to medium high after using it approximately 3 weeks ago.  This incident occurred when he used the control switch and there was an odor of something burning, he immediately unplugged the heater and return it to the store. 

The manufacturer was contacted and he was informed by a representative that he would relate the issue to his supervisor.

He is concerned that this heater is a fire hazard and should be reported.

The product is not part of a recall.

productDescription: Oster Electric Skillet CKSTSKFM-1216. 120V
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription:
We were operating a brand-new electric skillet. I plugged it into the wall to cook some chicken and vegetables
when the coil on the bottom of the skillet melted and the inner coil was exposed. It was red-hot and flakes of red-hot metal dropped from the coil onto the counter. I immediately unplugged the skillet and put it in the snow outside to cool it down. Had my wife not noticed the red-hot coil, it could have caused a fire. I have pictures of the skillet and can provide upon request. This is the third time using since purchasing the item as a Christmas gift on Kohl's.

productDescription: Honeywell Low Profile Silent Comfort Heater, HZ-617
model: Honeywell Low Profile Silent Comfort Heater, HZ-617
incidentDescription:
Honeywell Low Profile Silent Comfort Heater, HZ-617
I purchased this heater on 8 January 2014 from Amazon. It was used for occasional supplemental heat in my daughter's bedroom which is above the garage and colder than other rooms. On the morning of 28 February I went into her room to wake her and noticed the heater's fan had come on even though the switch was not on that setting. I tried to turn the switch and there was an electrical shortage followed by billowing clouds of acrid smoke. I am sure it was about to catch fire. I unplugged the heater and rushed it outside. Obviously I wish I had paid more attention to the other reviews on Amazon citing the same and similar issues with this heater. My experience was clearly not the first.  I can only conclude that there is an issue with this heater which renders it UNSAFE.

productDescription: Holmes Humidifier Model # HM5250
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription:
Holmes Humidifier (Model # HM5250) caused fire in the house. burned the carpet in the family room. Had I woke up 5 minutes late, the whole house would have been in fire. 

Filed complaints to the company (800-546-5637) on 2/27/2014. The company representative reported to their supervisor and the supervisor told me the company will call me back within 48 hours and they did not call me. I called again on 3/4/2014. They said that they will call me back soon and they failed to call me again today.

productDescription: coffeemaker
incidentDescription:
The consumer stated that the problem occurred about five years ago The plastic pour- in bowl has melted. The consumer stated that it might be an electrical failure.

He stated that he was going to donate it and looked on line for parts and discovered the recall-rel#05-189.

(02/12/2014) The consumer stated that he contacted the manufacture and was advised that his product was not involved in the recall. He was also advised that no parts were available for the unit.

productDescription: Cuisinart convection toaster oven
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription: After using my cuisinart convection oven to warm up pizza, my three year old sustained 2nd degree burns from touching the outside of the oven after it being turned off 10+ minutes.

productDescription: Magic Bullet blender
incidentDescription:
Using the "Majic Bullet" blender to make baby food. This small blender has stabilizing ridges on the inside of the detachable jars. Placed semi frozen fruit into the blender and pureed the fruit into baby food. While trying to feed my baby I found a piece of this plastic had broken off and I nearly fed it to my child. I immediately strained the rest of the food and found that one of the ridges had shattered into 3 small pieces that are easily lost in small spoonfuls of baby food.
No injuries occurred as I fortunately found the pieces just before feeding them to my child.
I have photos of the parts and the pieces available if requested.

productDescription: Bionaire® BCH9208-UM Ceramic Tower Heater
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription: Operating Bionaire Heater as directed by manufacturer, Model BCH9208.  During operation heard an arcing sound and unit began to smoke and smell of burning plastic.  Immediately unplugged from wall outlet.

productDescription: Holmes Ceramic Heater model HCH1823M. Black portable Heater
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription: Was notified by owner of a Holmes Ceramic Heater, model # HCH1823M, that they had it plugged in under their kitchen table and heard a popping sound. When they looked down flames were starting to come out from around the knob on top that sets the temp. The unit is about 6 months old. When I went to look at the heater it smelled of burnt plastic and owner stated that unit will not work now.

productDescription: Lasko ceramic air heater Model number 5367
incidentDescription: My toddler daughter was burned by an electric space heater that had no warnings on it that the surface of the heater would get hot enough to cause burns. It is a Lasko heater model number 5367 and was in use for less than 30 minutes when she touched it with her leg, leaving (on her backside) a burned imprint of the metal lattice cover from the front of the heater, which I thought was plastic until this incident. I was standing 3 feet away from her and the heater so she was not unattended or being reckless, this is just a very, very dangerous product without any labeling. I have other Lasko heaters in my home that do not get so hot because they are plastic on the front but an amazed that they can produce such a dangerous product and not put a label on it stating the surface is hot enough cause skin burns. Obviously heaters get hot and they do put a label on all their products to keep combustible material away from heaters, but my daughter isn't combustible.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription: Dehumidifier
manufacturer: Gree Electric Appliances, Inc. of Zhuhai
incidentDescription:
Caller stated that the dehumidifier was in use for 3 months constantly and he returned home to an odor of burning plastic.  His spouse tried to power off the unit but it would not power off it had to be unplugged.  The following day it was re-plugged and the same incident occurred. 

2/17/14  The manufacturer was contacted and he was advised that the unit was not part of a recall and to return it to the store because it was under warranty. 

Caller felt that he experienced similar problems of Recall number 13-283: Hazard:The dehumidifiers can overheat, smoke and catch fire, posing fire and burn hazards to consumers.

productDescription: Pelonis Oil Filled Radiator Heater Model HO-0218H
incidentDescription: I have a Pelonis Oil Filled Radiator Heater Model HO-0218H which is approximately 1 to 2 years old. Saturday night 15 February 2014, the heater started to smoke a little and filled the room we were in with a extremely acrid smell with what I will guess was some sort of electrical problem. I immediately unplugged the heater and removed from the house. I have tried to call the company but have not been successful in reaching them by phone. Have also sent an email to inquire as to remedy or would they like the product back for examination. This product is out of warranty, which is 1 year.

productDescription: Harbor Breeze Clearwater ceiling fan 3578978
incidentDescription:
I purchased a Harbor Breeze Clearwater (Item #3578978) ceiling fan from Lowes.  I had it installed by a certified master electrician.

After mounting the fan and checking everything he left the sun room we are having built. Approximately one hour later my contractor entered the sun room and noticed an electrical burning smell and saw the sparks coming from the fan motor.

He immediately turned the switch off.  If he had not gone into the room we very likely would have had a house fire.

Once the fan cooled he dismounted the fan.  I returned it to Lowes this morning for a refund and made them aware of the issue.

productDescription: Vicks Warm Mist Humidifier
incidentDescription: We have had a couple of issues with our Vicks Warm Mist Humidifier.  At first, the handle to the water tank broke and almost landed on my wife's foot.  Needless to say it busted and spilled water everywhere.  Secondly, which is the latest incident, the unit leaked water into the electrical switch, and even when the unit was off, it was running(fire hazard).  It also continued to leak and ruined my daughters night stand and also leaked water onto the carpet.  I have dealt with KAZ the manufacturer on the handle issue, but this is unacceptable that water can leak into the electrical circuit.  This is highly dangerous, due to the fact that water and electricity do not mix.  Also, houses do not have GFCI outlets in the bedrooms.  What is someone would have gotten electrocuted or a fire would have started from the heating element heating up the plastic after all of the water had leaked out!  It really scares me to think what could have happened.  Very concerned consumer.  Now I am nervous, as I have a newer model in our bedroom.

productDescription:
Optimus Electric Heater, Oscillating Pedestal Digital Dish Heater with Remote, Model Number H-4501, 120 VAC 60 HZ 1200 W   Date Code 2011
UPC code 6-30326-145019
Confirms to UL Std 1278
incidentDescription:
Regarding electric heater, Optimus Model H-4501, Oscillitating Pedestal Digital Dish Heater.
While heater was in operation in our living room, noticed a bright flash of light in direction of heater.  Initially did not recognize that flash was coming from heater.  Approximately 1-2 minutes later saw 2-3 Inch sparking flame coming from back of heater.   Immediately unplugged heater and flame stopped.  Inspected heater.  The area where the plug attached to heater was charred and melted.  Very small pieces of charred material had fallen onto floor.

productDescription: Slow cooker 3 qt oval shape, glass lid, lift out ceramic insert.
incidentDescription:
This is about the slow cooker brand Proctor Silex.

Monday, February 24th, 2014 I cooked chicken in my Proctor Silex [slow cooker] for 10 hours on Low. Food was good. Everything was good. Our dishwasher person forgot to wash the lid that night and it was left in the kitchen on a table until Tuesday, February 25th, 2014. 

Tuesday we had our person dishwasher wash the lid by hand. Upon inspection Wednesday it was discovered still a little dirty. 

Saturday, it was re-washed by hand (using only liquid dish detergent, warm water, and a wash cloth). Upon inspection Sunday morning it appeared still a tiny bit dirty. Our person washer RE-WASHED it Sunday morning and stood it to dry in the dish drainer/rack with other clean plastic dishes. That was 8:30am. 

Sunday 12:30pm on March 2nd, 2014 when we returned home from church, the lid was still standing in the drying rack but the glass had completely shattered. Pieces were everywhere in the clean dishes, in the sink, and on the floor. I was concerned because we have 5 children that all entered the kitchen not knowing what we were walking in to. We also have a puppy that we're raising for the Seeing Eye and I was worried she'd get glass in her paws.

productDescription: Coffee Maker
incidentDescription: I made coffee with my Cuisinart Grind and Brew DGB 700BC this morning - there was still about 2 cups of coffee in the carafe and the warm function was on.  Luckily I was nearby - I heard a boiling sound and went toward the sound which turned out to be the coffee which was boiling in the carafe.  As I approached I noticed smoke coming from the base of the unit and a smell of burning plastic/electric components.  I quickly unplugged the unit and removed it to a safer surface.  I am sure that there would have been a fire if I had not been close by and acted quickly.  I have investigated and note that there are others who have had this same problem with this coffee maker as noted on Complaints.com and Amazon.com.

productDescription: Small red hairdryer. Hand Held.
incidentDescription:
Babylisspro Tourmaline 1500 HairDryer exploded in my hand during use. Smoke came out and filled the bathroom. Plastic bits flew all over the floor and sink. The Item came apart into two parts. It made a loud bang/pop noise. I unplugged it quickly but this could have been a terrible thing if i had it near my eyes.
I was not injured, however

productDescription: Hamilton Beach 10 Cup Food Processor
incidentDescription: The motor shaft on Hamilton Beach 10 Cup Food Processor with Compact Storage Feature disintegrated into very small pieces.  I would have not noticed the broken pieces in my food except for the fact that I was shredding yellow cheese and the pieces stood out amongst the cheese.  I very seldom use the processor, maybe 1 time a month.

productDescription: Breville BTA630 Lift and Look toaster
incidentDescription:
Breville BTA630 Lift and Look

The Breville BTA630 Lift and Look toaster turned on by itself. I had just awoken and was in my kitchen, washing a pan. I smelled a slight burning odor and at first I thought it was food from the skillet. But the burning smell got worse and was smoky. I checked my coffee maker because it was brewing. Finally, I started looking around my kitchen and found the toaster was on and BLAZING hot. I had to unplug it to get it to turn off.

productDescription: Frigidaire Dehumidifier
incidentDescription:
I had a problem with a dehumidifier made by Gree. This unit is approx. 4 1/2 years old. I checked  your website, and noticed that other similar models were recalled due to fire hazard, but not this size.

It was plugged into an GFI outlet, and it kept tripping the GFI breaker. When I plugged the dehumidifier into a non­ GFI outlet, the unit would run, but with some serious growling noises. Needless to say, I'm not using this anymore, due to the fire hazard associated with Gree units. Unfortunately,I don't qualify for a refund under the existing recall because this particular size (25 pint) is not included.

I still have this dehumidifier,and I am going to keep it in case you want to examine it.

productDescription: AZ Patio Heater Model # HDLS01-CGT4. It is a propane patio heater with a base that holds the tanks.  Inside the base is the regulator and the hose travels up the pipe to the upper assembly.  Along the side is the pilot ignitor button and the flame control.  The upper assembly has a flame ring with mesh around it and a pilot in one spot.  Around that is a metal cover to protect from the flame with holes in it.  Above that is a reflector plate to force the heat downward.  Still available on website.
incidentDescription: I purchased a outdoor patio heater at ACE hardware in Daleville, PA.  After bringing it home and assembling it per the instructions we began to use it.  Within a week we started having issues with the ignitor not working properly.  It was inconsistent as I would have to keep pressing it sometimes without lighting or wait them try again.  I was concerning with the accumulation of propane until it lit.  The patio heater has a tray for setting drinks on it while standing beneath it and we used it as such.  After a short time we observed metal pieces dropping on us and the tray.  Upon further inspection of the flame area I observed the mesh around the flame was melting and dropping pieces down on us, some of which were hot or could have dropped into our drinks.  I contacted AZ Patio Heaters http://www.azpatioheaters.com and spoke with someone named [REDACTED] there.  I explained the issue and forwarded pictures to review.  In the meantime, we observed that where the screen was missing a flame was protruding out the safety cover and burning the upper heat reflector cover, which could harm a rather tall person or someone standing on a stool.  I contacted AZ patio again and was told by [REDACTED] to remove the screen.  I was not comfortable rigging it because it still did not address the ignitor issue or the flame shooting out the side.  I contacted him a few more times with no response, so I called this morning and spoke to a management person.  He told me they were aware for a while of the issue (did they contact you?) and were telling consumers to remove the screen.  What effect that will have on windy days?  Will the flame shoot out the side and burn the flame reflector like mine?  Do you want inexperienced consumers trying to fix this item?  Next, he told me the he thought the flame was caused by the regulator, but could it be that it is from the missing screen that burned off?  Unknown.  Why was this not reported as a safety issue to you if they knew it was a problem for a while with hot metal pieces falling on people or possibly ending up in drinks and consuming?  I will be contacting consumer reports as well.

productDescription: Gree dehumidifier GE brand. Bought for finished basement.
incidentDescription: GE dehumidifier gets extremely hot. Hazard of smoking or catching fire could result injury or loss of human life and pets, home, non-replaceable item and materials. Gree recall on GE dehumidifier.

I was cooking a large batch of soup at 'high' temperature in the crock pot. The soup was boiling and I heard a soft "pop." When I looked over at the crockpot lid it was full of spider-web cracks. When I tried to remove the lid several pieces of glass fell into the soup. I later pried the edge of the lid up and slipped a pizza pan under it to remove the lid. productDescription: Cuisinart coffee maker DCC-1100 black
incidentDescription: My coffee pot was on when I noticed a strong smell coming from my kitchen.  It smelled like burning plastic and was very strong.  I finally realized it was my coffee maker and by that time the outlet had turned the coffee pot off.  Upon inspection of the coffee pot, I noticed that on the bottom of the hotplate was where the burning had been.  It was discolored and the smell was very strong.  I called Cuisinart and reported the problem and they informed me they would send me a new one after I gave them the model number of the coffee maker.  I am concerned, however, that they would send me one with the same problem that could cause a fire in my home.  I have 3 children and am concerned with their lack of concern with this problem.  Tonight I was doing research and found that many people have had the same problem.  Why is Cuisinart still allowed to sell such a dangerous product?!

productDescription: waffle maker
incidentDescription:
This information was transferred from an email to the CPSC Information Center.

When the product is in the opened position, the lid doesn't have anything to keep it opened. This means that when you are trying to remove waffles, the lid slams down onto the users hands.  The consumer believes that a person would need three hands to remove waffles safety from the maker.  The consumer has looked at several different websites and found that it received very poor results for this same reason.

The consumer claims that she received minor burns as a result of this issue.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

Ultra Glide Easy Cord Iron

Ref: FV4379 u0/90-1810R
120V
1700W 50/60 Hz

Electronic Shutfoof Flat iron
incidentDescription:
The iron was turned off and setting on air provided cooling plate in order to cool down after ironing was completed.

It had been setting on the cooling plate for approximately five minutes when it burst into flames six to eight inches above the iron.

The caller and her helper who had been ironing ran to the iron and began blowing on it to get the flames to subside.

The flames appeared to be out, the caller unplugged the iron and carried it outside to the courtyard.

It is raining where the customer lives but the iron burst into flames again.

They then opened the doors and windows, turned fans on to rid the house of smoke and odor.

Caller has not contacted the manufacturer and does not intend to contact them.

There are no injuries being reported

While sitting in the charger, the battery for my cordless drill started on fire. I did manage to get it outside. The smoke set of all the detectors in the house. The charger and battery were brought back to the service center. They told me that the battery and charger could be sent to the manufacturer but that the manufacturer was not interested unless I paid the shipping cost to send it both ways. Thank you.

incidentDescription: the switches are going out and some are arking fire and smoking

manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription: Bought a crock pot.  I used it once.  A week later I used it again but this time I came home from work to find the lid completely shattered.

productDescription: Space Heater
incidentDescription:
On January 28th, 2014 the caller's 32 yr old son turned his space heater on then left the room to take a shower.
In the ten minutes he was out of his room the space heater caught fire and when he returned to his room this heater was in flames going about three feet high and spread about three feet.
He yelled fire to his family and his father/the caller grabbed the fire extinguisher while he also called 911 for emergency assistance.
The fire department arrived within minutes and extinguished the fire.

The space heater had been recalled in 2004 with release # 04-191 by Vernado and at that time this unit as well as another.
Both were repaired and returned to the consumer.

The heaters have worked well after the remedy repair was completed until the time of this fire.
There are no injuries to report
The caller did not contact the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.

The caller states that the unit is beyond repair, he, his wife and his son have all lost work and he is open to any options.

productDescription: Portable electric heat
incidentDescription:
Consumer stated that she turned the heater on and approximately 2 seconds it went off.  She flipped the switch on and off and she noticed smoke and she unplugged it and removed it outside.  She also smelled an overwhelming odor (electrical fire).  She placed it on the grass and within seconds it erupted into flames and a black smoke with a toxic smell.  She contacted the fire department immediately who came out to contain the fire, the fire was contained which left a big burnt mark on the grass and broken glass pieces.  The product was destroyed in the fire.

12/13-1/14  The manufacturer was contacted  a few times before they informed her to send photos of the incident.  They eventually advised her that her claim was denied and she should contact the retailer for a refund.

She is concerned that this heater could have caused a house fire and serious health issues. 

The product is not affected by a recall.

productDescription: Gold Star Dehumidifier DH305T7
incidentDescription:
(8/2011) The consumer stated that his dehumidifier was on for approximately 5 hours during the day. He went to turn the unit off and unplugged it, he noticed that the plug was burnt as well as part of the electrical cord. 

The consumer feels that he is experiencing similar problems of Release #11-324.  The power connector for the dehumidifier's compressor can short circuit, posing fire and burn hazards to consumers and their property.
 
The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

productDescription: Surround heat
incidentDescription:
The consumer was given the heater as a gift. 

The consumer stated that she saw a dent on the side of the heater. The consumer went to examine the dent and noticed that heater had melted in that area. The consumer said that the plastic case melted on the right of the temperature dial.

The consumer stated that the spot that melted is extremely hot to the touch. 

The consumer contacted the manf and they informed her that there was no recall on her model.

The consumer informed the manf that she used the heater in the bathroom. The consumer was informed by the manf that because she used the heater in the bathroom, her warranty is void. The consumer was informed that the product is not meant to be used in moist environments like bathroom.

The consumer stated that she did not use the heater in the bathroom for long periods of time. 

The consumer was informed the manf that as a courtesy, if she sent the heater back, they will replace it.

The consumer plans to send the heater back to the manf.

The consumer's model is not included in recall #12-087.

productDescription: 70 pints
incidentDescription:
Caller is reporting fire from 70 pint malfunctioning dehumidifier that burned the serial number off of the unit, and caused a fire.  
This fire caused smoke and fire damage serious enough to cause the family to be displaced from their home to a hotel.

Dehumidifier normally was on timer but caller happened to be up on Sunday around 3:30PM, turned the dehumidifier off to lessen the noise so that she could hear her children who were still upstairs while she was in the laundry room.
She would turn it back on normally but she didn't this day because she was moving clothes and checking on the children.
They went to bed that night and were awakened by the smoke alarm around 3:00AM Monday morning, February 10th, 2014.
The caller rose and began trying to find the source but when she arrived at the steps to her basement she saw an orange glow.
She flipped the lights on, crept closer to the source then saw that the dehumidifier was on fire.
She looked for the fire extinguisher but when she couldn't find it she began screaming for her husband to get the children out of the house.
She grabbed the kitchen fire extinguisher, ran back downstairs, saw that the flames were now almost to the ceiling.
The smoke was very thick, she was still screaming for her husband and children while she put the fire out.

productDescription: It's a white warm mist advertised as 25 gal but holds only 1.5 gal water Optimus U32000 Humidifier
incidentDescription:
I bought a Optimus 15Gal Warm Mist Humidifier White SKU: 1648407 online from www.bestbuy.com on Dec. 18,2013. Several days later it was delivered and I set it up two days later after reading the instruction booklet. It did put out a good amount of mist and was fairly quiet. I did notice that it had three lights on top, one for on/off, one for humidity, and one for refill. The humidity and refill light did not go on even when it was no longer producing steam and out of water, but otherwise it was working. Thought maybe it has to be completely dry for these lights to activate, but there was always residual water in the tray. I removed the water tower and steam tower looking for calcium deposits, but there were none, just a little brown sludge. 
I noticed a somewhat pungent, acrid smell from when I first started using it. I thought it was from the plastic and new parts and that the odor would go away. When I saw that it was out of water, I would refill it, or turn it to "off' and fill it a several hours later. The smell was irritating my sinuses and lungs. It caused shortness of breath that is still affecting me. On Jan. 26, 2014, I turned it off, waited 30 minutes and removed the two towers. The heating element was still very hot, and the "white" filter was brown and had a burnt smell. So I unplugged it to cut the electric power since obviously the on/off switch not turning off and stuck "on." I tried to remove the filter, but it was fused to the heating element. I soaked the filter in some vinegar water and finally able to remove it, but it looked brown and burnt, and found some brown stained calcium deposit on the projected heating element around which the wrap around filter goes with a [fastener] strip. By comparison, the [REDACTED] humidifier I bought at Best Buy at the same time still works well and never had an odor, and has no filter and the heating element is cleaned once a week or so with vinegar water depending on the amount of calcium deposit.
My complaint is that I think there is a design flaw in this humidifier and it is unsafe since it never turns off and out gasses fumes from the overheated filter. Perhaps the closely fitting filter is causing the overheating problem? It kind of frightened me that it could possibly have caused a fire and burned down my house. I don't know if it is the only one, or there might be thousands of malfunctioning units of this model, or similar units, out there endangering people. That is why I am reporting it. I contacted the manufacturer, who has not replied. I contacted Best Buy, and about an hour later I received a phone call asking me more questions and they were concerned and would give me a refund. They had UPS send me a return label that is good for ten days. Of course, once I send it back, it can no longer be examined, so I am wondering what to do.
Humidifier manufacturer: Optimus Enterprise, Inc., Customer Service Dept., 2201 E. Winston Road, Unit #J, Anaheim, CA 92806 Tel: 1-888- 672-5832 E-mail not listed in booklet, but found website through a search: www.optimusent.com

productDescription: Kerosene space heater, unvented.
incidentDescription: Purchased SENGOKU CV-2230 kerosene heater to provide supplemental heat bduring recent cold weather. Had originally owned this type of heater back in the 80s-early 90s.  Used high quality 1-K kerosene and burned heater for a total of about 24 hours on 3 separate days. Flame and burner operation appeared to be perfect but after that time my apartment was was filled with uncombusted kerosene/ emissions product. I observed the combustion burner of this heater during actual operation and found the following; unlike the older [REDACTED] or [REDACTED] heaters, this heater had a combustion chamber screen diffuser with no catalytic activity during burning. The use of the catalytic combustion diffuser in the older heaters assured a combustion efficiency of greater than 99.9%. Not the cse with this heater. It is just a cheap imitation of the older efficient heaters. Also, this heater had both UL cert markings and NKHA (National Kerosene Heater Association) markings. Basis observed combustion performance, It is my belief that UL has not tested this item for performance in several years. Further, I have been unable to verify that there is even something known as the NKHA which is still in existence.

productDescription: Hamilton Beach Stainless Steele 12-Cup Percolator, 40614, SILVER
incidentDescription:
Dear [REDACTED]

Enclosed is the Hamilton Beach Stainless Steele 12-Cup Percolator that I reported to you on November
27th as causing a sever burn across my abdomen to which I emailed pictures to you.

The burn occurred on the evening of November 26th when I accidently spilled coffee while sitting down
on the couch. I was clothed in pajamas and a cotton robe tied in thE front. When the liquid spilled out
of the cup onto my robe, I immediately felt it come through to my skin and jumped up and tore my robe
loose and pulled my pajama pants away while screaming in pain. My husband was sitting in the recliner
next to the couch and jumped up to assist me and noticed the immediate blistering.

On November 27th, I visited my doctor's office and Dr. [REDACTED] classified the burn as a 2"d degree with the
blisters and recommended to keep aloe lotion on the burn and [REDACTED] as needed and take [REDACTED] for
pain.

Prior to sending you the percolator, I experimented following the owner's manual and comparing to my
Hamilton Beach coffee maker. Using a meat thermometer, I determined that the percolator reaches
195 degrees after percolating at the point the light indicator changes from blue to green signaling ready
to pour contents. Then, I waited 2 hours and retested the coffee temperature and it was still 185
degrees. My Hamilton Beach coffee maker averages 165 degrees from the time it stops processing
throughout the time the warmer is on.

This test concluded that there is a significant difference in temperature between my Hamilton Beach
coffee maker and the enclosed Hamilton Beach percolator. I truly had no idea the temperature
difference since there are no warnings or information regarding the scalding heat level and serious burn
risk.

Based on consumer market research, the average age of purchasers of this percolator are between 54-
65 years old. As we age, our skin thins and burns become more severe and healing takes longer so I take
this very personal and am concerned that there simply is not enough warnings on this percolator. The
only warning in the manual and on the pot is to not immerse in water because of the electrical base.

A disturbing statement contained in the manual and as part of the specifications is, "coffee stays hot
with a gentle keep-warm heater." In the instructions, it also indicate the liquid stays "warm" without
warning of just how hot the liquid is kept at on the warmer. I can assure you that there is nothing
"gentle" about the keep-warm heater and the liquid is not kept warm, but just below boiling
temperature. The only mention of scalding is if the cap is removed during the percolation cycle, not
from the liquid after the light turns green.

There is a negative impact to my life since this incident occurred. I am not able to wear normal clothes
because of the location and size of the burn across my stomach. Instead, I am wearing elastic band
workout pants with the elastic pulled down below the burn. While I am able to work remotely at home,
I have had to cancel several face-to-face meetings and decline certain holiday functions. Today, I will
email you an updated photograph of the burn so you can see that even after 8 days, there is little to no
improvement.
 
I am forwarding a copy of this letter to an attorney friend as I believe this is a serious matter that
requires escalation.

Thank you for your kindness and immediate response to my report of this incident on November 2th.

Sincerely
[REDACTED]

Dear [REDACTED]
I received your reply letter and must admit that I am disappointed in the lack of data to support your
short statement concluding that the percolator was not defective. I took the time and effort to conduct
a series of tests between the Hamilton Beach percolator and our Hamilton Beach coffee maker to
determine the temperature differences and would have appreciated at least the same level of data to
support the ruling of "not defective" based on your internal testing.
I am not looking to fight or sue Hamilton Beach. What I am expecting is reimbursement for the
purchase, doctor's appointment and the few medical supplies to soothe the burn and pain along with a
promise that Hamilton Beach will apply more warnings to this percolator raising awareness of potential
scalding.
I can assure you that as a home-based worker for 13 years that consumes either hot tea or coffee all
day, I have spilled my share of liquid on myself. However, I have never experienced a burn such as the
one I did with the coffee from this percolator. It has been over 5 weeks since the accident occurred and
the burn is still very red and continuing to heal. Enclosed are a set of the time-lapsed photos taken
immediately after the burn on 11/25 through 12/31 evidencing that I am still healing. It just amazes me
that I sustained a burn such as this through my robe and pajama top. I cannot imagine how severe it
would have been if I had not had my robe on at the time of the spill.
I remain very concerned that Hamilton Beach refuses to acknowledge that they have insufficient
warnings on this percolator and in my opinion has the following false statement in the instruction guide,
"How To Heat Water I Step 8: Ready Light will glow when water is hot, and percolator will automatically
go into a keep-warm mode." The liquid remains extremely hot, not warm.
Based on my tests and comparisons, the water heats to scalding and the warmer maintains a very hot
heat level. Therefore, by stating gentle keep-warm heater misrepresents the hot temperature that is
continuously maintained by the warmer. The only reference to scalding is if the cap is removed during
the percolation cycle.
Since Hamilton Beach insists there is nothing wrong with this product and refuses to acknowledge the
potential for scalding if spilled, I am reporting this to the North Carolina Consumer Protection Bureau
and the United States Consumer Product Commission in hopes they will encourage Hamilton Beach to
improve their warning and avoid others from experiencing such a painful ugly burn.
I am enclosing receipts for the expenses I've incurred due to this accident I sustained by purchasing this
percolator and am requesting full reimbursement at your earliest convenience.

Sincerely
[REDACTED]

incidentDescription:
We bought a NEW Gas Grill and were using it for the FIRST time (we have had other grills for years.)
The grill spewed a LARGE flame, caught the tank on fire and melted the coupler around the tank.
We had to let the tank empty itself.

It has been looked at by engineers from the Tank company, Uhaul where the tank was inspected THE DAY OF THE INCIDENT and Brinkman, the manufacturer of the grill.

Brinkman has blamed the tank from day one, despite it passing inspection on two occasions.

They refuse to pay to reside our home, as the fire damaged it (It is a new home, just bought in May 2013)

They admitted the tank was neither overfilled, nor out of recertification - yet blame them and deny our claim without an explanation as to WHY it should be the tank's fault.

During inspection, by Brinkaman's OWN engineer, the regulator on the grill caught fire, and spewed flames.

Despite this obvious flaw, they refuse to acknowledge it and said the regulator on the grill (Made in China) is not significant.

THis is on tape, and was witnessed by myself, an engineer from Uhaul, and Brinkan's rep.

They refuse to give me the evidence nor any reports.

Brinkaman had a similar issue with other regulators and had to recall them for the same reason.

There is NO DOUBT from myself and Uhaul's engineers that this caught my home and the grill on fire, and it is a danger.

Please help us get this resolved, and these grills off the market!

productDescription: Twin Star 10Q1071ARA space heater
incidentDescription:
[REDACTED]     
December 31,2013
          
Consumer Products Safety Commission
Washington, DC 20707
Re: Dangerous or defective space heaters

Last winter, I bought a space heater from a local hardware store. It indicates that it
is a Twin Star 10Q107IARA with UL listed at 3RE7 E 335639, made in China.

I used it in my kitchen, which is at the far end of my forced air heating system. I
plugged it in a GFCI receptacle. The heater warned that the plug should be checked
periodically to see if it was warm.

On December 1, 2013, less than half an hour after I plugged this into the GFCI
receptacle, I smelled something burning. When I felt the plug it was HOT! The GFCI
receptacle was destroyed. The insulation on the receptacle had melted off.

I promptly turned the circuit breaker off to that receptacle to avoid a fire, and
possible further damage to the electrical system and the house. That circuit is now
useless, but my house wasn't damaged further, as far as I know.

These space heaters should be carefully checked and removed from the market if
they aren't safe. I could imagine what could happen if it was plugged in to heat a
bedroom at night while the occupants slept.

Sencerely:

[REDACTED]
CC: WV  attorney general, consumer protection
Pendleton County OEMS
Selling store

incidentDescription:
I purchased a Dimplex Electric heater (it is large and burgundy) a few years ago. It looks like a wood stove. For the past few weeks, it has been randomly kicking off and no heat would come out but it would still run. I would unplug it for a bit and then restart the stove. It would have good days and bad days and sometimes would run with heat all day without disruption while not working at all other days.

Last night, I heard a loud pop. I looked over and the unit was flaming from inside. I immediately unplugged the unit. It also put some burn marks on the outlet. Luckily, I was able to unplug the unit, lift it and get it outside right away. I opened the front door of the stove and smoke was billowing out and it was flaming slightly. It did stop. I think because I was able to open the door, it allowed for air to get in and release everything. 

The unit is Dimplex Air Heater Model Number DS5629CR

The Serial Number is 123110D3F  178

I did contact the company this morning to notifiy them of what happened. I believe that if I was not present when this happened it would have definitely caught my house on fire. Luckily, I was home and the fire for the most part was contained inside the unit. The number that I called was 1-800-668-6663. I spoke with a rep named [REDACTED] at extension [REDACTED]. She opened a report and asked for me to send pictures and said she was not aware of any issues with this unit. She asked for me to unscrew the inside piece to try and get pictures of the inside and also whatever other pictures that I could so she could show her supervisor. I told her that if this hasn't really happened before that perhaps they need the unit back for technicians or engineers to take a look at and evaluate. Pictures don't really represent the issue.

productDescription:
Central Boiler Maxim M250 wood pellet boiler.
www.maximheat.com
incidentDescription:
On 8/19/2011, I bought a Central Boiler Maxim M250, serial #M00377 from [REDACTED], Frontier Heating Concepts Inc. On 11/7/13 the product caused a serious fire that destroyed the boiler and threatened structures and personal belongings at my home. The fire originated in the boiler and was contained by the metal enclosure. 
After extinguishing the fire, I contacted the Central Boiler dealer, [REDACTED], who came to my home and took pictures. An investigation was not performed. Pictures of the boiler were sent to Central Boiler (CB) on 11/8/13. I made inquiries about the fire through the dealer on 11/13, 11/20 and 12/4 with no reply from CB to that point. On 12/4, [REDACTED] instructed me to contact the dealer directly. 
I sent an e-mail inquiry to [REDACTED] of CB on 12/12/13. [REDACTED] replied on 12/16, briefly explaining that a determination was made from photo’s that the fire was caused by lack of maintenance and that damage would not be covered by the furnace warranty. I replied to [REDACTED] the same day, stating that recommended maintenance was thoroughly performed just prior to the fire and that close examination of the boiler would affirm that. [REDACTED] has not replied to this message that was sent more than two months ago. 
I sent an additional e-mail to [REDACTED] on 1/2/13 to ask if he would explain the sequence of events he believed would occur from lack of maintenance that would cause a catastrophic failure and fire. I also asked if the Maxim M250 has any engineered features or safeguards to prevent fire from occurring outside the burn chamber? If yes, I asked if he would explain what those features are and how they work? [REDACTED] has not replied to this message that was sent three weeks ago. 
At this point, attempts to resolve this with the manufacturer are being repeatedly ignored. 
I believe this fire resulted from a failure to regulate temperature. The Maxim M250 is a pellet boiler comprised of a 90-gallon water tank surrounding the burn chamber. During normal operation, when the thermostat calls for heat, pellets are automatically introduced to the burn chamber by a feed auger accompanied by fan-forced air. As the fire intensifies and the water temperature rises to a set point (180°), thermostatic control ceases both pellet and air introduction to the burn chamber and the boiler idles down until another call for heat occurs.  
During suppression of this fire with a dry-chem extinguisher, it was found that the furnace had boiled dry as evidenced by large amounts of water on the concrete floor where it is installed. This was confirmed by physically examining the water tank. Additionally, areas around the water jacket are the most heavily charred, indicating an area of origin. Fire eventually burned through auger feed tubes to the pellet hopper and heat caused a propane regulator to fail which then resulted in fire damage to the electronic controls compartment. 
If a thermostat or other burn cycle controller were to fail, tank water would heat to the boiling point and much of it be forcefully ejected from the fill port. As the burn cycle continues, remaining water would escape as steam and the steel water tank itself would heat to the point that foam insulation surrounding chars and burns. Extremely hot metal will conduct heat to ultimately affect anything that is either combustible or can melt. Evidence and examination of the boiler suggest an overheat condition that eventually led to a fire that involved several major boiler components. 
This product is installed in an outbuilding that in addition to the boiler and pellet fuel contains other combustible materials. If the fire had not been noticed when it was, the outbuilding could have been involved in fire which then may have threatened my home as well. I consider this a grave life-safety concern.

I have a Cuisinart 12 cup food processor and I am disappointed in one aspect of its function that I believe is a grave safety concern.  This model has push button on and off.  There is no way to tell that this machine is on or off because it has flat "buttons".  

I plugged in my Food Processor, then attached the large work bowl with the work bowl cover attached (because of how I store the work bowl and cover and blades to keep them with the food processor away from my children, I had the large chopping blade and the Shredding disk inside the work bowl). 

My machine was plugged in and as soon as I connected the work bowl to the machine, the chopping blade and shredding disk went spinning and swirling about inside the work bowl.  I immediately unplugged my machine.  My work bowl is scratched.  My work bowl cover has the plastic rim shredded.  I have a damaged chopping blade and damaged shredding blade.

I find this to be a huge safety issue as there is no way to tell that this machine is actually clicked into the "ON" position prior to plugging it in or connecting the work bowl.  God forbid if this had continued and shattered my bowl sending metal blades through my kitchen.

There is no way to actually tell on this machine that the ON button is actually deployed.  I find this feature to be a pure disregard for safety.  There is no switch.  I thought, given the structure of these buttons, that when unplugged, the "ON" switch would reset to the off position (or at least, this is what it would appear to do) so I thought the machine would not defaulty be "ON" given the fact that there is no way to tell (ie:  a switch or other way to look at the machine to realize it's turned on).

The space heater was immediately unplugged and all signs of smoke and red glow dissipated.  Fire Protection Engineer and Safety were called to investigate.  Supervisor notified.  Investigation reveals that the Bionare Model BCH9208 shows evidence of blackened wire insulation internal to the heater.		
The affected wire is a white wire, 16 AWG size, directly connected to the power cord. The blackened portion is limited to about 2 inches at the end.  The wire has a crimped-on female spade connection.  The spade connection is tight, but the wire has come apart at the end of the spade connector, making it appear that the crimp has failed.  Appears that either heat destroyed the wire at the connector crimp or else the crimp was poorly made at the factory. This particular heater is approved for use and meets the requirements of ISPM-6.  The unit	was plugged directly into an outlet as required.  The unit had a clear space behind of at least 18 inches and in front greater than 36 inches.

productDescription: small portable electric  heater
incidentDescription:
The consumer noticed a chemical odor after operating the heater for approximately  3 hours. 

 He then also noticed  a few sparks coming from the control panel. The heater was operating on the low setting  when the failure occurred. 

The consumer powered it in the off position. He has not used the heater since the failure occurred.  

On 3/13/2012 the firm was contacted and the consumer states that he was advised to mail the heater back into the firm. The consumer states that he declined in sending it back and knows what he needs to do to fix the failure. 

No further information was provided.

UPDATE FROM CONSUMER:

Heater is approx. 8 3/4" high and molded feet (front to rear)
light weight
L.H. 2 3/4" long
RH 3 3/4" long
Easily tips over, on hard surface and worse on rug

I am considering adding a board under heater to reduce possibility of tipping over.  There is more than enough room in heater base for some screws and still stay well away from internal parts and wiring.

The odor first noticed appears to have come from charring of heat-shrink tub insulation on the connector- no fire resulted. 

Local retailer had obtained more of this heater and exchanged my heater (with bad connection). I also purchased an extra heater.  These heaters are expensive and have a low setting of 600 watts, which will be useful in warming storage areas.  The heater with the defect may have been a rare anomaly and was not a design defect but was an assembly error and I know what to watch for.  If connector parts are misaligned when they are pushed together the spring tension is reduced and connection will heat up and deteroriate further.

The element wires (that produce the desired heat) do not get hot enough to show any visible light.  Heater should last a long time.  Some radiant type heaters' elements can burn out.

Use of the replacement heater shows no problem to date, but I will add a comment/suggestion.

productDescription: Convection toaster oven
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
We were broiling some fish for dinner with two guests  in the toaster oven when we started to smell a strange electrical burning smell.  We turned off the broiler and removed the fish, and sat down to eat dinner.  However, the smell lingered and when my husband and I went into the kitchen to check the toaster oven, we saw that the heating elements were still red, even though the oven had been turned off.  (Normally, the elements stop glowing red almost immediately after turning off the oven.) We tried turning it on and off again, but the elements simply remained on.  The only way to turn off the elements was to unplug the toaster, which is of course what we did.  The next morning, to see if anything had changed, I plugged the oven back in and immediately the elements started glowing red without my having turned the oven on.  My husband then took the oven apart to see if he could identify the problem, but after reading information about the oven online, we found out that you cannot replace the circuit board, which we assume had shorted out.  The oven is, I believe, between five and six years old, but this model is still for sale.

This is an extremely hazardous situation -- what if we had left the house thinking the oven was actually off? The potential for burns is also significant --fortunately I was wearing an oven mitt when I took the fish out of the oven.  There is clearly something wrong with the wiring in the oven and just brief internet research indicates that other people have had this problem with this model.  Krups should recall this model.

issues and was replaced under warranty. No less than a year later, the warranty replacement full size dryer began arcing and sparking from the nozzle, making loud snapping noises and gave me a shock. I sent it back for warranty replacement 3 weeks ago.

I began using my T3 travel dryer (purchased the very same day as the full size) and it caught fire while I was drying my hair! First, the dryer began turning itself on and off. Then, a flame jetted out of the handle area and it started smoking, filling my apartment with hazardous, irritating smoke. I had to open all the windows and doors to clear it because it burned my eyes, nose, and lungs, and smelled terrible. It also made me be late to work.

I requested a full refund from T3 for both dryers and the shipping costs I incurred, yet they will not help. Instead, they keep asking me for the serial number, which is too small and illegible for me to read.

I believe you must force recall on these dryers. There is quite obviously a serious wiring fault and they put consumers' lives and safety in real danger!

productDescription: Optimus Heater Fan Item H-1382 with oscillating heat and auto-shut off feature (which did not shut off as plug was burning up)
incidentDescription:
This is regarding an Optimus Heater Fan with plug burn damage. It is item # H-1382. I purchased this fan heater to use at my work. I use it just about an hour or two in the morning to take the chill out of the air. Yesterday I smelled plastic burning coming from the unit at the electrical outlet and immediately pulled out the plug and I had the electrical engineer examine it. He said it was not the electrical outlet, but rather the plug that was burning up (internally). Part of the burn discoloration extends up the cord for about an inch or so. Most of the burn was located at the end of the plug which even melted the electrical wall socket protector. I have photos showing the burnt plug.

This unit has only been used less than a year and not used but just 5 days a week for about a couple of hours (at the most), and even less usage in the warmer months… It was a good thing that it didn’t happen while I was away from my desk as it could have started a fire. Please let me know if there was a recall or others that had this same issue with their units. I bought this unit because it had the safety features (like tipping and auto-shutoff) but even now, I will try to remember to turn any heater fan off when walking away from my desk, even for just a few minutes, as it was a scary moment….

This is NOT an issue with the electrical outlet. It has been thoroughly examined and the issue is the Optimus PLUG, which is shown to be burnt from the inside and even along the cord, as it melted onto the electrical outlet. The engineer that investigated said that the only damage on the electrical outlet is the plastic that melted from the cord, as he physically examined booth the electrical outlet and then the Optimus unit. No spark or fire occurred because I was in my office and was available to turn the unit off and unplug immediately after smelling burnt plastic. This would have resulted in something far more serious had I left my office! 

I contacted Optimus and sent photos showing the cord (burning INSIDE the plug and ALSO burn damage inside the cord). 

I bought a new [REDACTED] unit (in operating order with the red light on) and working just fine plugged into the other electric outlet that was not melted due to failure of the Optimus unit. The burnt remains of the Optimus plug is just below the current outlet used by the new [REDACTED] unit. Optimus stated that is was a faulty electrical outlet that caused their unit to burn up, but this would NOT be possible since I'm currently using the same outlet with another heater/fan unit.

Please let me know if you need photos of the Optimus unit that almost caused an electrical fire!
Thanks for your time in reviewing this.

Char Broil called it a [REDACTED] fire and requested that we send photos, which we did.  The company refused to do anything but sell us a new knob and new wire.  They claimed that the fire was caused by an obstruction in a conduit (we removed the conduit and saw no obstruction) probably a spider web, they said.

This dangerous product should be removed from the market.

incidentDescription:
I wanted to register with you that within the past 3 months I've have 2 CrockPot brand crock pot lids shatter into small shards of glass.
Neither was being used in any way against their instructions. The first was cooking a pork tenderloin (on low). I complained to the company - they sent me a new one. Within 3 uses the lid of the new one shattered on Thanksgiving Day. The CrockPot contained mulled cider.
I will be calling the company again on Monday to complain, but I will not use their product again. It is very dangerous, aside from the fact that I lost some expensive food to the debacle. I have no faith that it will not happen again.
One concern I have is that people may try to wash the broken glass off the food rather than lose the money. One of our guests suggested i strain the cider and we continue to drink it. Obviously I didn't do that, but it was disturbing that an otherwise intelligent person would think that would actually be ok to do . Someone is going to get hurt.

productDescription: Cuisinart Custom Classic Toaster Oven Broiler TOB-40
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
brand: Cuisinart Custom Classic Toaster Oven Broiler TOB-40
incidentDescription:
Cuisinart TOB-40 toaster oven purchased less than one year ago (December 18, 2012). One of the four heating elements developed a split in the outer covering which started glowing very hot and red (what I call a "hot spot"). This is a serious fire hazard.

Looking at the reviews of this product on Amazon.com, there are many people who have reported the same problem with this product many times. If you look at just this one thread on Amazon ( http://www.amazon.com/review/R29PS611BJCV75/ref=cm_cr_pr_viewpnt#R29PS611BJCV75 ) you will see 14 reports of TOB-40 elements that developed "hot spots" (not counting those that just stopped working). 

When I called Cuisinart customer service, they were very familiar with the problem and offered to send me a new TOB-40 immediately. They already had my name and address on file. So the company knows that they are selling a defective and dangerous product but is taking no steps to recall it. This is unacceptable. 

Please investigate this product quickly before someone gets killed in a house fire!

productDescription: CritterZone Pet Air Purifier
incidentDescription:
I purchased the CritterZone Pet Air Purifier Wall Unit from Litterboy.com and plugged it in and set it on low. It produced an awful metallic chemical smell that made me extremely ill. The smell has lingered in my condo unit and is in my clothes in the closet, couch, bed, EVERYWHERE.
The first night, I woke up in the middle of the night with shortness of breath and an insane headache. When I got out of bed I was dizzy and began to feel nauseous. I immediately unplugged this toxic product. I could not get back to sleep and the headache lasted for 3 days.
This product also made all three of my dogs sick. My dogs were lethargic and did not eat or drink for 2 days and were breathing heavy. My pitbull vomitted. 
The next morning my neighbor came over because the stench had seeped through into her unit. I showed her the product and she said that it was an ozone generator and was illegal to have those in California, that they had been banned a few years ago.
I've done everything to get this smell out out my condo. I've had every window open and have been freezing. I've had to wash EVERYTHING and spent 4 days doing laundry. When I leave and return home I get a headache after being home for awhile and have woken up with a headache every morning since. I can't believe this product caused this much damage in a day and a half. It has  been over 2 weeks and the chemical odor this product produced still lingers in my condo.
What was even more upsetting then the damage this product caused to my health and home was the customer service I experienced from Litterboy.com. I contacted them and notified them of what happened and said that maybe the unit was defective to cause so much harm. I requested to return it and receive a refund. In their reply they refused to refund me because they said the product was used and that it may be defective and I could call and have them trouble shoot it. Why the heck would anyone want to plug that harmful product back in, unless they were suicidal?
I didn't bother arguing with the company because it was clear they did not care and had no intentions of providing the proper customer service to resolve this issue . I did research on the internet and found through product reviews that other customers had similiar experiences from this product. The company is mismarketing this product and should make it known that this product produces ozone which is harmful and even fatal.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription: 52" Edenton Aged Pewter Fan (Harbor Breeze - Hunter)
incidentDescription: I purchased 3 Harbor Breeze (Hunter) fans in June 2010 from Lowe's.  About 5 months ago I had one of the fans blow out.  I turned the light on and right away I could smell electrical burning and then a loud pop and all the light bulbs filled with smoke.  We don't use that fan much so we hadn't done anything about.  Then on October 20, 2013, we had a similar incident with another fan but this time the lights actually flixered on and off and made a buzzing sound before the loud pop and smoke coming from fan.  Once again electrical burning was smelled right away.  I had an electrician over to check out the fans and what he found was scary.  He showed me Part No. 98480-02 in both fans which had been fried.  The part inside of these had been flattened and still smells like electrical burns.  He stated that I was extremely lucky that my house didn't catch fire from this.  I also have a third fan that I bought at the same time which hasn't had any issues but I am just waiting.  This is a fire hazard and since my incident I have actually done research and found a LOT of problems with this part.

productDescription: King Electrical Manufacturing Company, Seattle, WA Pic-a-Watt 240V electric wall heater model PAW 2422 complete with wall can and controlled by King thermostats.
incidentDescription: My house is all electric and has King Pick-a-Watt electric wall heaters, 240V, model PAW2422. My house is not a manufactured home or a trailer.  I have been vacuuming the dust out of the inside of the heaters once a year as King recommends.  Two of the heaters have caught on fire, one in the bathroom and one in the kitchen .  I did see and hear the kitchen heater fail.  I was sitting across from the heater in the kitchen when I heard a pop noise, like a small firecracker, looked over at the heater and saw the metal rod that goes through the heat fins glowing bright red on the right side, followed by flames coming off the rod for about a third of its length.  The bathroom heater also glowed bright red in the same place, followed by flames, but I did not hear a pop noise.  The heaters did not shut off, I turned them off, and neither heater dropped its breaker in the main electrical panel.  I have wired in smoke detectors, one very near both heaters, and it did not go off.  I have two more heaters that were turning themselves off and was told by an electrician that the heaters have a thermal switch that should shut them off if they malfunction.  I had a licensed electrician replace all four heaters.  One of the new heaters failed after about 3 hours' use and I returned it and bought another one - which is a 25% failure rate for this King product.  The new unit that failed started making screeching noises, like a dry or worn out bearing, and a thumping noise.  It also smelled very strongly  and set off the smoke detector. Eventually there was a tan stain on the grille on the right side and the paper label on the back was scorched.  I had that unit replaced and had to pay another service call for the work.  I contacted King by email through their web site on November 6 because I was and am concerned about the fire danger from these product failures.  I would expect that any malfunction would shut the heater down.  If I had not been at home when the heaters caught fire they likely eventually would have set the wall framing and sheetrock on fire.  King offered to replace four heaters, but by that time I had already bought and paid for the installation of new ones - it is winter and cold where I live.  I asked them to pay for the service call to replace the new out of the box defective heater and so far they have declined to do that.  I was without heat in the kitchen and bathroom for about four days until an electrician could do the replacement work and had partial heat in the living room where the other two heaters were replaced.  There have been multiple emails and phone calls between myself and a representative of King but as of today  their only response has been to ask me to return the kitchen heater that I heard and saw fail so they can examine it and to ask for photos of the kitchen and bathroom walls.  They have not compensated me in any way for the service calls, the defective new product, the four defective heaters, or the danger to my property and my life.   Because no one can tell me why this happened or why the two heaters did not shut off when they failed I live 24x7 with the stress of wondering when the next failure will occur, and I'm reluctant to leave the heaters on at night or when I leave my house.  As it's been almost three weeks since  I notified King and they've been indifferent to or very casual about my situation I thought I'd better file a report in case this happens to someone else or someone's home does catch fire.  I have photos of the kitchen and bathroom walls and the kitchen heater but can't get them to upload or attach.

productDescription: Kuuma portable gas grill.
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
The product is a portable gas grill manufactured by Kuuma Products/Camco Manufacturing, Inc.
This grill has a built in Pezio igniter which sometimes works, sometimes doesn't.   When it does function, it ignites propane at the burner.  When the lid is shut on the grill the flame is extinguished but the gas continues to build up inside the grill.  Only by looking at the temperature gauge (built in to the lid) can you determine that the flame is out (the temperature goes down).  After five minutes with the gas turned off,  the flame may be relit.  When opening the lid, you have access to an access hole to be used to relight the flame by sticking a lit match or utility lighter through the hole.  Residual gas still inside the burner area ignites all at once with a loud noise (whump) and a fireball which singes the hair on your arm.  This happens often while cooking.

Additionally, the wire which connects the Pezio igniter to the sparking head lies close enough to the flame that the insulation on the wire catches fire.  The operator cannot see this take place.  The insulation continues to burn until it reaches the ignitor button and then the plastic housing for the spark generator catches fire.  Again, the operator cannot see this happening while cooking.  After the gas is turned off and the cooking flame is extinguished there continues to be black smoke coming from the ignitor button area.  By inspecting the inside of the unit, I found the Pezio ignitor had burned into an unrecognizable black blob of plastic.  When I contacted the manufacturer to obtain a new ignitor, I explained what happened.  They sent me a new ignitor which I installed according to the directions provided.  After using the grill a few times, the second ignitor caught fire and melted.

productDescription: Quality Craft QC888HB Portable Heater
incidentDescription:

After about 20 minutes, we smelled strong smoke from another room, and ran into to find the QC888HB on fire internally and throwing mass amounts of smoke.  We quickly unplugged it and carefully got it outside.

I called Quality Craft, and their first reaction was that their are safeties on the unit and it can't catch on fire.  Their second reaction was to say the unit was out of warranty.  I explained that this is not a warranty issue - this is a product safety issue as my house was moments away from catching on fire.  They then asked for pictures, and after reviewing - offered to send me some internal electronic parts to replace inside the unit.

I stated I am not authorized or certified to repair appliances, and was dismayed that they were not interested in finding a root cause.  After much back and forth, they finally agreed to have me ship the unit back - but only after putting legal forms (liability waivers, releases, etc) in front of me.  

I told them before ever plugging in a Quality Craft unit again and placing my family at risk, I would need to understand why this happened in the first place, is it happening to other people, and lastly - I'm not releasing them if it catches on fire again.  Communication has since ceased.

productDescription:
Product # 08 89257
Bubbling over with MacKenzie-Childs style, our Courtly Check® Enamel 2-Quart Tea Kettle will have you finding new reasons to put the kettle on to boil. The heavy-gauge steel underbody is hand-painted with our color-dragged Courtly Checks® and ceramic glaze, and rimmed in bronzed stainless steel. With a wood handle, and a lid topped with a carved faux-cinnabar bead, you may find yourself leaving this charming piece on the stovetop for kitchen beautification. Or place it on display, filled with fresh-cut flowers or greens. Our iconic MacKenzie-Childs kettle makes a perfect gift for seasoned collectors, or a welcome invitation for a friend new to our Courtly Check® wares.
incidentDescription:
On August 4th, 2013, I took a week’s vacation to visit my Mother.  That morning I heated up some water using her two-quart Courtly Check Enamel Tea Kettle, product # 08 89257.  

While using the teapot, I thought it strange that it was taking so long to heat up, as I didn’t hear any whistling or boiling noises. After a few more minutes I figured the water had to be ready and I took the teapot off the stove to pour into my coffee cup.  At first, no water came out. I assumed this was due to the steep angle of the pourer, so I attempted to pour at a slighter greater angle. Suddenly, the super-heated teapot saucer lid popped off and landed on my finger, causing immediate blistering with 2nd degree burns.  In addition, scalding water poured out of the teapot and caused first degree burns on a good portion of my hand (see attached picture of my hand 10-days after the injury).

This experience, along with being extremely painful, ruined my vacation as I wasn’t able to go swimming, with my family.  I had to watch from shore as my niece and nephew splashed away in the water.  

Having safely used teapots for over 35 years, it is very clear that the MacKenzie Childs Courtly Check teapot is a dangerous and unsafe product for the following reasons:

•	No whistle feature: One doesn’t know when the water has boiled and is ready to use.
•	Unsafe Loose saucer lid:  The lid on the teapot comes off easily, unexpectedly and at the worst possible times. This was confirmed by my sister who had a similar experience, thankfully she wasn’t burned as the top landed on the counter.  

Upon doing some research, I discovered that MacKenzie Childs has known or should have known about this product defect as early as June of 2009 (See links to Amazon review below) yet has done nothing to my knowledge to correct these defects. 
http://www.amazon.com/gp/cdp/member-reviews/A20WX5NVTUHWC7/ref=cm_cr_pr_auth_rev?ie=UTF8&sort_by=MostRecentReview

A simple product modification of installing a small latch on the inside of the ornamental top saucer to keep the lid on could’ve avoided this painful injury.  
In the interests of consumer safety, I hope Mackenzie Childs will discontinue selling the Courtly Check and other teapots with these design flaws until a latch or other safety features are installed along with a whistle mechanism.

I used a fourth circuit that was 20A and the humidifier ran for 5-10 minutes (again seemingly "working") and then it made several loud popping noises (that we could hear from upstairs, the unit was in our basement) and smelled like it was burning.  It was still running when I went into the basement, and continued to seem like it was running fine until I unplugged it. productDescription:
Electrolux W touch counter depth French Door Refrigerator
Model #-EW28BS85KS

I had my kitchen remodeled in September 2011. The appliances were supplied by the contactor. The freezer of the new Electrolux refrigerator didn’t work right from day on and after several attempts to repair it was replaced by the above brand new model in December 2011.
This unit worked well until 10/5/2013 when while filling a glass with ice the entire system shut down. No ice-no lights-no sounds-nothing! A rectangular piece of [REDACTED] had dropped into my glass so I reached up into the ice chute to see if anything was stuck. All I got was a major shock and jolt. I unplugged the refrigerator at that time and removed the ice tray. I found two wires hanging down from the top that had arced to the metal ice auger and shorted the entire system out. This was what was responsible for the shock I got. In the tray were the temperature sensor/thermometer and a rubber hose. 
Reconstructing the events;
The restraining piece of [REDACTED] was dislodged allowing the sensor and attached wire to hang down into the ice tray.
The auger caught the senor and wires and tore them apart allowing the bare wire to arc on the ice auger causing the short.
The short may have killed not only the ice maker, but the major and auxiliary circuit boards and the compressor.

Model #-EW28BS85KS

I had my kitchen remodeled in September 2011. The appliances were supplied by the contactor. The freezer of the new Electrolux refrigerator didn’t work right from day on and after several attempts to repair it was replaced by the above brand new model in December 2011.
This unit worked well until 10/5/2013 when while filling a glass with ice the entire system shut down. No ice-no lights-no sounds-nothing! A rectangular piece of [REDACTED] had dropped into my glass so I reached up into the ice chute to see if anything was stuck. All I got was a major shock and jolt. I unplugged the refrigerator at that time and removed the ice tray. I found two wires hanging down from the top that had arced to the metal ice auger and shorted the entire system out. This was what was responsible for the shock I got. In the tray were the temperature sensor/thermometer and a rubber hose. 
Reconstructing the events;
The restraining piece of [REDACTED] was dislodged allowing the sensor and attached wire to hang down into the ice tray.
The auger caught the senor and wires and tore them apart allowing the bare wire to arc on the ice auger causing the short.
The short may have killed not only the ice maker, but the major and auxiliary circuit boards and the compressor.

The consumer called the brand name company on 7/19/2013, but they were not open.  He reached the firm on 7/22/2013.  The firm's rep. The rep. at Archway told the consumer that his grill was "not" under recall, but as a 1 time curtsey, they would replace his hose with a new one at no charge.  The consumer said that his model was similar to the one in the recall and suggested that they take the grill back.  The consumer believes that another rubber hose will eventually present the same problem.  The consumer told the rep. that he could send the hose, but unless it is metal, he has not confidence in the grill and will not use it again.

The consumer was given a confirmation # 34475436.

The consumer believes that the recall needs to be expanded to include other rubber hoses on these grills.
