productDescription:
Cadet CEC163TW Com-Pak Energy Plus dual voltage electric wall heater (white).  1 year old.  Purchased through Build.com on 10/8/12.

?Complete unit with wall can, heatbox and grill.  Digital thermostat included.
?1600W at 240V/1000W at 120V
?Rough In Dimensions: 8" W x 10.25" H x 4" D
?Multi-Volt, Multi-Watt: Factory set at 240 Volt
incidentDescription:
At approximately 5:00am on 10/8/13, my wife and I were awakened by our fire alarm.  We jumped out of bed and immediately noticed the smell of electrical smoke.  After a quick look around the house, my wife identified the source as being our Cadet CEC163TW Com-Pak Energy Plus electric wall heater in the living room.  The top of the heater element was glowing red hot, and the cover grill fins had begun to melt.  I quickly ran into the basement and turned off the dedicated breaker for the heater.

The wall cavity above the heater felt really hot, and so we were worried that there may have been a fire smoldering inside the wall cavity.  We live in a rural area, and the volunteer fire department response time is not good.  So we monitored the temperature of the wall cavity for about 10-15 minutes and it slowly cooled off easing our fears of a house fire.  I believe that we were extremely fortunate that our house didn’t burn down that morning.  If the heater’s breaker had been left on for just one or two more minutes, I believe there would have been a fire in the wall cavity that we would not have been able to put out.

Here’s the disturbing part….
Although the heater’s breaker was on (so we can monitor the temperature in the living room), THE HEATER’S SWITCH WAS TURNED OFF!  We had not yet used the heater for this cold season, so the heater had been switched off since April 2013.  Why does a heater that is switched off, spontaneously start overheating?

I purchased 2 of these heaters on 10/8/12.  The other heater is installed in our kitchen (also wired 220 with its own dedicated breaker).  The heater in the living room had acted flaky before this incident.  About a dozen times over this past year, the heater has failed with a F8 code showing on the front display.  According to documentation, an F8 code is described as follows:   INTERNAL CONTROL FAULT  - Disconnect power, reconnect power.  If F8 code returns, replace heater assembly.  I called Cadet customer service about the F8 code, and received a brush-off response.

Tonight, I wanted to double check, so I plugged it in and turned it on. There was a sizzling sound and a flame shot up from the wires inside. The heater is less than a year old and has hardly been used. It has been taken care of and is not dusty or dirty, nor was it placed near any walls or objects.

One always assumes that these things are tested and safe, but apparently that is not the case. We could have been burned to death. I'm pretty shook up.

I store my grill near an air intake vent for my furnace room, so when the gas is accidentally turned on, the gas leaks into my basement near the furnace creating a potentially dangerous situation.

I try to remember to turn the gas off on the grill after each grilling session, but on three occasions have forgotten and smelled gas in my basement soon thereafter.  I'm afraid one of these times the gas will ignite.  I have seen  other reports online about this and weber customer service just recommends remembering to turn the gas off at the source each time.  Seems like some sort of recall to make the knobs harder to turn is in order.

incidentDescription:
My family and I were at our camp on Hinckley lake.  The nights started to get cooler, so we plugged in our CALORE portable heater that I believe we purchased from Wal-Mart.  We placed it in the center of the living room.  The heater was on a medium setting, but does have a thermostat, so will turn of when temperature is reached.  My husband and I were in our room, and our children where in their bed/bunks.  I awoke from my husbands coughing, which at that time I smelled something horrible.  I woke him and we went in the other room.  The camp smelled very badly of burning plastic.  The heater was still running, but was MELTING.  It was partially charred, and misshapen.  We pulled the plug from the outlet.  Again, It was STILL running.  We awoke the kids and opened up all the windows.  The smell was disgusting.  We took kids to Dr.'s just to make sure they were fine from inhaling fumes from melting heater.  I have heater, and took pictures.  Could not find any information on company to notify them.  This was a very dangerous situation and could have been much worse if my husbands coughing from the smell did not awake us.

I hope this matter can be looked into.  Please contact me with any information.

Thank you,
[REDACTED]

incidentDescription: I purchased the "Jetboil-Zip Cooking System" last year. I used it successfully 3 times. Last month, the stove malfunctioned on my 4th attempt. I was in the Adirondacks backpacking with friends. I was relying on the Jetboil stove to heat water. After setting up the stove and attempting to light it, the flames shot out around the stove. Fire was coming directly from the fuel canister and encircling the stove in a tall fire. I was afraid that the fuel canister was going to explode and catch our tent, or our faces, on fire, or worse - start a forest fire. We got the stove detached from the fuel canister using a stick and our boots and doused everything with water. It was horrible. The stove had malfunctioned, though it previously worked, leading me to believe that there is a material in the stove that cannot stand up to heat and use, therefore allowing it to malfunction over time.

productDescription: Backyard fire pit with pink colored faux brick facade and black metal bowl and frame.
incidentDescription:
I bought a backyard fire pit from Christmas Tree Shop a few weeks ago.  It is made by Nantucket Distributing Company.  It is an iron frame that a round pinkish colored faux brick facade sits in and then the bowl that the fire goes in sits in the facade.

We intended to use it just for small fires, the roasting marshmallow kind.  And also clearing out some small branches that have accumulated over the summer.

I started the fire and put some branches, small logs, and a cardboard box in the bowl.  Everything seemed fine until I heard this huge 'POP' sound.  At first I thought my husband might have put a log on too and the wood had a knot in it, since that's a noise I have heard in the past when burning knotted wood.  

Didn't really think much about it until a few minutes later when another huge 'POP' sent a piece of the fiberglass facade whizzing past my face and half way across the yard.  I stood there in shock since I had just bought this, it was our first fire in the darn thing and now it was exploding all over my yard.  Pieces of the facade began flying everywhere and the noise it made sounded like I had bullets in my fire pit!

I don't know how a fire pit can be sold that explodes upon actually using it for what it is intended.  I am so grateful that my 3 year old was not in the yard with me at the time of all this.  If she would have gotten hurt from this I don't know what I would have done.

I called the store I bought it from and the manager said that he would tell his manager about it and so on, but I can't take the chance that he doesn't.  I have to tell everyone I can think of about this because it is incredibly dangerous and I couldn't handle it if a child were to get injured by this.  

I don't have any item numbers or anything like that, we recycled the box and contents after we put together the fire pit.  But if you need any further information, please let me know and I will do my best to obtain it for you.

productDescription:
Hamilton Beach small food processor, model 72610, type FC05,
Series A1940BB
incidentDescription:
I had a small Hamilton Beach food processor model 72610, type FC05, series A1940BB. On August 28, 2013 I went to use it. The bowl and blade were already on it but the lid was not. When I plugged it in it immediately came on even though I did not turn it on and had not yet put the lid on.  If my fingers were further in the bowl I would have lost my fingers. The only way to shut it off was to unplug it. I called Hamilton Beach to tell them what happened. They said to mail it to them which I did. After over a month of not hearing back from them I called them back. They said they would replace it if I paid for shipping. I told them I didn't want a new one I was more concerned about all the ones that were out there still and worried that someone would get seriously hurt. They said they no longer make them but they would send me a replacement if I paid postage. I told them again I was not interested in a replacement what I thought was necessary was a recall. They said once again they no longer make them and I told them once again what about all the others still out there. After many back and forths like that I finally said I was contacting you. Both safety features, only on with lid on and button held down, both failed. I could have or someone could loose their fingers and they don't care. I really think it needs to be recalled. I no longer have it because I had to send it back to them but I did take a video before I mailed it in case you are interested in seeing it. 
Thank you for your time.

productDescription: Hamilton Beach Slow Cooker - Model #33162H - Gray and Black with glass lid
incidentDescription: I have a Hamilton Beach Slow Cooker, model #33162H.  It is about 2 years old.  I used it on the 'warm' setting for about 8 hours one day.  The next day, I cleaned it, in warm soapy water, and rinsed it with warm water.  I then had the glass lid in my hand, and was drying it with a cloth towel.  It spontaneously shattered into thousands of small pieces, in my hands, and onto the kitchen floor.  Luckily, I had on pants, socks and slippers.  I had small cuts on my hands and one on my ankle.  It could have been a lot worse, had I been barefoot and in shorts.  Also luckily, there was no one else in the kitchen at the time.

productDescription: Cuisinart 12 cup programmable coffee maker
incidentDescription: I brewed coffee this morning in my Cuisinart Coffee Maker and went upstairs to shower.  I came down to plug my cell in and my kitchen was filled with smoke that was coming out from under the unit.  The unit sounded as if it were trying to brew again, popping noises and steam sounds, even though it already had brewed an hour earlier and the carafe still had several inches of coffee in it.  I unplugged the unit, removed the carafe and ran with it to my garage.  The underside has a metal plate and it was incredibly hot to the touch (I burned my hand when my thumb accidently hit the underside running with it to the garage.  Despite being unplugged, the unit continued to smoke for about 5 minutes.  I honestly believe that it could have started a fire had it not been on a granite counter and had I not come down to find the smoking unit.  The unit did sustain high use - every day for about 3 years, but I've never had a small kitchen appliance behave that way.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: Krups Espresso carafe XP1505
incidentDescription:
I am reporting the second failure of the handle on a Krups XP1505 Expresso carafe.  The glass unit consists of a glass carafe, a metal band, a screw and a plastic handle/lid assembly.  The handle/lid attaches to the metal band by means of the screw.  The band goes around the glass and the screw tightens it until it is secure.  The glass, the band and the screw seem reasonably robust.
The screw passes through a thin and weak part of the handle/lid assembly to attach to the metal band.  After less than two months of use the plastic around the screw has separated from the rest of the plastic of the handle/lid assembly.  The weight and heat of hot (steam produced espresso) in the carafe make the most dangerous time for this item the most likely time for it to fail.
The user could be easily scalded.  Worse, as most coffee is made at "adult height" little people below that adult in the kitchen are exposed from head to toe.  The falling carafe and the broken glass after it lands also present a danger.
I have had this failure occur two separate times.  The first time I did not know the age of the unit.  The second time I know the replacement unit was in service less than two months.  Two month or two years, the failure is unacceptable.
Krups is aware of this problem and will not remedy it.  There was a previous complaint (not by me see, 20121029-0D5C0-2147462420; 20120308-8079A-2147469460; ) of this precise problem.  However when I reported this to Krups they (representative [REDACTED]) denied it had ever been reported to them before and that, although in no way defective, the carafe was not warranted to be either fit for the intended purpose or merchantable.  (To be fair, Krups maintains that using the carafe with Krups machine X instead of Krups machine Y makes my complaint void.  They dod not explain how espresso made from machine X differed in its impact on XP1505's durability from espresso made by machine Y.)
The Krups response to the first complaint is virtually the same as their response to the second complaint and both are belied by their response to my complaint.

On the way to the game tonight, my wife and I toasted some pizza.  This time was different though, we shut it off after toasting and it gives a beep signal to know it's off.  But then as the cab arrived, I smell a little smoke.  It was coming from our Krups toaster oven!  I looked on the front and there were no lights and it appeared to be off.  But looking inside the oven, it was blazing hot with the filaments that bright fiery orange.  We had to unplug the Krups toaster to turn it off, pushing the buttons had no effect.

As we jumped into the cab, all I could think about was what would have happened to our helpless cat and dog had our house caught on fire.  Not to mention the other tenants in the house.  Very disconcerting to say the least.

productDescription: Wood Pellet Grill
incidentDescription:
The product in question is a Traeger Little Tex Elite wood pellet grill.  This unit's firing cycle and subsequent cooking temperature is controlled by a simple digital that controls the operation of the wood pellet feed auger which delivers the pellets to the combustion chamber.  One setting of the thermostat is "smoke" which is time-based, in default, the auger operates delivering wood pellets for 15 seconds out of 90.  This setting is practically useless as the fire goes out.  If the restart procedure is executed, the unit can burn internally very aggressively and unexpectedly as the accumulation of unburnt wood pellets begins to burn.

Typically when the unit is operated in in non "smoke" or temperature cook mode, the thermostat will try to control the firing cycle via cooking chamber temperature and not by a set time cycle.  Today, the unit while operating in temperature cook mode unexpectedly went out.  I noted the the pellet hopper was empty and subsequently refilled it and executed the restart procedure as published by the manufacturer.  I checked on it after approximately 20 minutes only to find very heavy smoke and flames issuing from the unit.  I foolishly opened the lid at this point to find the interior of the unit engulfed in flames and a temperature reading of 521 degrees F on the thermostat readout.  Fortunately there were no combustible surfaces within three feet at the time of the incident save for some garden plants.  I believe that given the quantity of fire present and it's intensity that this unit which has no provision to shut the induced draft fan off in the case of fire constitutes a fire hazard.

productDescription: Dehumidifier
incidentDescription:
Smelled odor in basement.  Inspected dehumidifier and found it was blowing warm air but not condensing any water.  Removed water tank and found inside plastic very hot.  Immediately unplugged and took to garage.  Disassembled plastic panels.  Placed thermometer on compressor.  Read 275 degrees F.  This overheating compressor would have started a fire had we not noticed it.  WOW we dodged a bullet!

Condenser and evaporator were not plugged however drain line was half plugged with slime.  About 2 weeks ago drain line had totally plugged and lower part of evaporator was all froze.  Unclogged line and restarted, seemed to be working then.

The compressor says it is thermally protected, Guess NOT.  The contacts on the thermal protection device were probably stuck together because they were made of silver with impurities or not made of silver or even silver plate, or just too small for the amperage. If you don't want the unit to inspect it I will probably cut it apart to see what caused the failure.  Yeah you guessed it, I'm and engineer, and just have to know what would have probably burned down our house.

We had gotten 4"-8" of water on the floor during snow melt and after dewatering the shop used the humidifier to try to dry out the drywall on the walls.  We placed the unit in the middle of the shop floor and shut the doors and kept the unit operating 24 hours a day, checking on it often. After a week or so we were distracted by work and did not check it for a day or so.  Upon going into the garage we found a strong small of burned electrical parts and the unit was badly charred.  The paint had blistered off except for the very bottom of the unit, the bucket was a melted mass of plastic.  The unit was still plugged in and the breaker was not tripped.  We assumed the unit had overfilled, spilled and then shorted out the unit and caught fire.  We discarded the unit and aired out the garage by opening the door and turning on fans.  There was no other damage except for the humidifier which my late wife had purchased in Anchorage for about $300 and sent up to Kotzebue. 
We attributed the problem to our failing to check on the unit frequently enough and felt ourselves lucky that when the unit burned it was on a concrete floor and nothing else caught fire.  It was only upon reading about your recent recall notice that I looked and found the Owner's Manual for the Dehumidifier and found it on your recall list: Frigidaire Model FDB70R1. We cannot say with certainty that the unit malfunctioned which caused it to catch fire, but it does seem odd that the breaker did not trip and the unit failed within weeks of having been purchased.  We had otherwise maintained the unit properly, regularly draining it and cleaning the filter.

incidentDescription:
I'm writing to you today to inform you of the explosion I had in my house due to your Mr Coffee Espresso Maker Model # BVMC-ECM260.

I purchased this machine at Walmart about 1 week ago because it was a name I thought I could trust in an appliance and the fact that it was black and stainless steel and matched my kitchen.

On 9/8/13 I took it out of the box for the first time and set it up. I read the instructions and did everything it said to do. I set up the machine and walked to the other side of my kitchen to finish cleaning. The machine starts to pour coffee and I walk back over to the machine. All of a sudden it explodes in my face! Glass hot coffee hot coffee grounds are now everywhere all over me and my kitchen. 

The glass didn't just break the actual filter holder flew off just missing my face and the glass shattered and flew everywhere. I had coffee and glass in my hair and all over my kitchen. From the ceiling to the other side of the kitchen.

My 1 year old daughter was right behind me and thank god she was not touched by anything. I took the full hit. 

I was not harmed enough to seek medical attention but this could have been much worse. I have used a different brand machine for years and have never had this issue. I know I put the filter holder on correctly as I have used many espresso machines. 

After the hour and a half it took to clean my kitchen and myself I sat down to look up why it could happen (which I am still finding coffee and glass everywhere). What do I see but more and more stories of the same thing happening with Mr. Coffee machines. 

Each time all I see is the same response to every complaint please contact us. I want this product recalled. No one should have this happen to them! Some one can get seriously injured and your company having known of the issue for such a long period of time (I see complaints as far back as 2011) could be facing a ton in damages.

incidentDescription:
This incident occurred while I was toasting a bagel in a "Euro-Pro Toaster Over" Model TO1612. This toaster over was bought at the Sears Grand store at the Pittsburgh Mills on May 11, 2011.

I noticed some light blue-white smoke coming out from behind the upper (temperature control) knob. Seeing this I quickly remove the plug and the smoke stopped. Thinking the something may have gotten into the area behind the knobs, I removed the outer metal cover from the toaster over to see if the area needed to be cleaned. However, the area behind the control knobs was clean.

Next I decided to find out what would happen if I turned the toaster over back on. I took it outside to the concrete patio and plugged it in again without changing any settings of the three control knobs. Within a minute or so the backside on the middle control (function: keep warm; broil; bake; toast; grill) burst into flames. I removed the plug and the flames went out.

From what I have observed, this toaster over could have caused a fire if I had not been near-by when the first smoke appeared. I do have a smoke detector in the area so I think I would have eventually been alerted to the problem, but, significant damage may have occurred to my kitchen first.

I have taken some pictures of the toaster over and I will hold onto the over and the pictures just in case you would want me to send them to you for further investigation.

Thank you for your attention,

[REDACTED]

productDescription: Weber One-Touch Silver Charcoal Grill 221/2 inch, serial number AU
incidentDescription:
The handles on Weber Charcoal Grills either absorb or conduct heat and become too hot to handle. This issue is the
result of a design flaw in the grill top. Formerly these handles were made of wood which did not create a safety
hazard. However, because of the need to label these handles with county of origin (this is what the customer service
representative reported) they are now made of a different material which becomes too hot to handle with ones
hands. This issue is not random or inconsistent but happens whenever these grills are used.
My experience result in three burned fingers and a dropped grill cover causing minor product damage.

These handles are not merely warm but too hot to handle causing burns.

After speaking with the customer service representative I was told to use a glove or pot holder in the future.

This issue is easy to resolve with a handle that does not absorb the heat from the grill. In fact such a handle did exist
when they were made of wood.

11 August 2013
[REDACTED]

[REDACTED]
V .P. of Customer Service
Weber Stephen Products, LLC
90 West Hillcrest Blvd.
Schaumburg, 11. 60195

Dear [REDACTED]:

I was referred to you by one of your on-line phone customer service representatives.
Last evening, while using my recently purchased, One-Touch Silver charcoal grill 22 Yz"
(serial number AU purchased at the Green Thumbers in Davenport Iowa on 5.11.13), I
lifted the lid to remove the meat and burned my hand. Three fingers were burned as I
tried to escape the heat from the handle. The lid was dropped causing a minor amount of
damage to the lid.

It is clear that this handle conducts heat or absorbs heat to a level that cannot be tolerated
by your customers.

The purpose of this letter is to call your attention to this very serious design flaw and to
correct the issue. I did a search of the internet and this issue is common among your
customers. It is absolutely amazing to me that a company like Weber that manufactures
products that get hot, would design a handle that conducts or absorbs intolerable levels of
heat.

I spoke to two customer service representatives. The first representative indicated that I
should wear a glove or use a pot holder. This hardly seems like an appropriate design
solution. The second service representative indicated that this has been a known issue for
some time. She added that 5 or 6 years ago Weber discontinued the use of wood handles
as there was a country of origin issue related to the labeling of the handles.

I can only conclude that you have cut corners to save on product costs putting your
customers at risk. From my perspective it is unthinkable that a manufacturer in good
conscience could allow this known product defect to exist. These grills are not highly
engineered products - a simple solution is available. The risk of injury is not random but
rather it is known and expected! When injuries can be significant and the cost of fixing
the problem insignificant, the solution seems obvious.

I look forward to your response.

Very truly yours,
[REDACTED]

CC:
[REDACTED], General Council & Secretary to the Board of Managers
Weber-Stepen Products
200 East Daniels Road
Palatine, IL. 60067

productDescription: Apple Computer 17-inch MacBookPro Rechargeable Battery (serial number W0115094Z9DA). Model Number A1189 10.8V 68Wh
incidentDescription:
MacBookPro battery is bulging out of its metal casing: In early 2008 I purchased a MacBookPro from Apple, Inc. Since then the battery that came with the aforementioned MacBookPro has been replaced once (by Apple) due to it reaching the "end of its life cycle" and presenting extreme bulging out of its metal encasing and consequently the slot in which it's located.
Last week the same issue started to develop with the replacement battery, serial number W0115094Z9DA, about a year since I began using it. I believe there's an intrinsic manufacturing defect on these batteries rendering them unusable after they've reached a percentage of their "life cycle". 
Most importantly however, these batteries seem unsafe to consumers using them under normal operation specifications. As described above, the initial battery that came with the laptop battery bulged so much that I feared for my safety. 
Regarding the early stages of bulging presented by the current battery, I was reassured by Apple's Employee ([REDACTED] at Portland's Pioneer Square Apple Store) that battery serial number W0115094Z9DA remains safe to continue operations for "several more months or years". He reassured me specifically that there is no risk of the battery exploding or leaking its contents.
My uninformed guess is that these batteries aren't safe for use and therefore I hereby submit this unsafe product report to further evaluate the safety of this battery.

the item number is: 54-4241436
incidentDescription:
My 16 month old son was using the Pottery Barn Larkin crib. On 8/5/13, my wife awoke to our son crying and screaming. When she went into his room, she discovered that my son's left leg had become stuck between the slats of the crib. His leg was stuck at the thigh. My wife was unable to free his leg and was forced to contact the fire department. The slats of the crib had to be forced apart by crow bars to free the leg. 
That night, a mesh bumper was placed in the crib to prevent my son from putting his leg through the slats again. The next day, I was driving to work when my wife called to tell me that our son's right leg had become stuck in the crib again despite the use of the mesh bumper. I came home and had to use a hammer to break one of the slats to free his trapped leg. 
He has not been in the crib since. Our concern is that this crib could seriously injure a child by trapping legs. This problem could be solved by allowing for quick and/or easy removal of the slats.

productDescription: Eureka Airspeed Rewind Pet Upright Vacuum
incidentDescription:
On 7/14/13, the first time I was using my brand new Eureka pet vacuum right out of the box, I had selected the “tools” option and was using the hose with the attachment to vacuum unwanted pet hairs from the corners of the walls.  I heard my 14 month old son screaming, who was approximately 1 - 1.5 feet away from me, and when I turned around, he was on the floor with the tower which had also fallen over, however his foot was caught up inside the vacuum.  I am still shocked that it was continuing to spin and motor, being I had selected “tools” and the hose has a 12 foot extension on it. How can an everyday household vacuum be as dangerous as an unattended power tool?   

The bottom of my 1 year old son’s right big toe looked like shredded lettuce.  He saw his pediatrician three times that week (who said it was one of the ugliest injuries he had seen), and on day 5 of the injury, in which it was STILL bleeding (it bled for SEVEN days total), our pediatrician referred us to see a plastic surgeon immediately.  We opted out of a skin graph, and then followed up with the plastic surgeon for two additional visits (so 3 visits with the pediatrician and 3 visits with the plastic surgeon).  I have photographs, doctor records, co-pay receipts, etc to validate my cause.    

We are fortunate that the vacuum was brand new and clean, in which we avoided a bacterial infection.  He was not allowed to wear shoes, or go in the water, for 2 weeks, to avoid the risk of contracting any other infections.  ).  It is 4 weeks later and his toe is healing beautifully, although not 100%, and we are at the stage of applying Vitamin E oil on it to help with the scarring and skin repair.

As a consumer, I am appalled that the safety shut-off is NOT an industry standard, AND that there was NOT any warning on the vacuum, or anywhere in the paperwork, to caution walking away from the upright tower (while using the tools selection).  My [REDACTED] vacuum DOES have this safety feature so I am perplexed as to why they all don’t?   I am going to petition and move forward doing EVERYTHING that I can do make this an industry standard for ALL vacuum cleaners.  It would cost the manufacturers approximately $2/vacuum to put this in place.  As far as I’m concerned, this is the same thing as using an electrical sander with my children in the room, and then walking away 12 feet (the length of the hose) to turn on an electrical saw. 
Please make the right choice for the consumers and make this an industry standard!  A small cost for the good of the people.

productDescription: the manufacture is Char-Broil. This grill is made specifically for Lowes Home Improvement stores. The Char-Broil model number is 463247311 and the Lowes Item # is 154596. It is the Commercial series 4 burner TRU infrared grill with the side griddle and cost was $499.00

incidentDescription:

The knobs on my grill are very close to the grill surface and heat exit of lid therefore causing them to get to an extremely unsafe temperature.  The new model has these knobs moved significantly lower and further out from the grill/lid surface.  This appears to be a resolution to the safety condition I am experiencing.

incidentDescription:
Order# [REDACTED] from Amazon.com--a Primula glass teapot, 40 oz., advertised as microwave safe.  Notification below just sent to Amazon.

Dear Amazon,
I'm not asking for replacement or return, but want Amazon to know of a safety issue with the product-- a glass teapot made and sold under Primula brand. Though listed as dishwasher and microwave safe, the entire handle simply separated from the pot as I was pouring microwave-heated tea on Sunday, leaving a hole in the side of the glass pot as it fell to the table. 
   I had only a couple of small burns from sloshes hot tea and two tiny finger cuts (like paper cuts, so not serious) from the ragged edge  where I picked it up after it fell--very lucky. The main part of the pot did not break-- It appeared the handle bond just failed with no warning-- apparently from cumulative microwave use..?
   I will be happy to send a photograph to you or the maker, but definitely recommend you remove the "microwave safe" from the product listing and warn the maker. I will do a review (my first) to share the warning, but worry about others who already have purchased. productDescription: Master Forge Gas Grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
This incident is concerning the Master Forge 5-Burner Gas Grill, model # L3218 sold by Lowes Home Improvement between September 2009 and November 2009, manufactured by the Sagittarius Sporting Goods of China. This first recall was "fixed" by using a longer regulator hose.

My second incident occurred approximately 4 years after the first .  The first incident was resolved by replacing the regulator hose with longer hose.

I was having problems with the grill to come up to temperature and noticed the flame from the burners were low.  Decided maybe the burners were clogged with spider webs or something.  Removed all the burners and cleaned out the bottom (which is rotting away and becoming another hazard).  Reassembled everything and turned on the grill.  

The temperature didn't come up.  So, this time I was going to attack the valve regulator as perhaps good ol spidey took shelter there as well.  Removing the regulator hose first, I noticed the end that goes to the valve regulators (the rubber part) was slightly melted.  

This is why my flame was low it was constricted from a melt down from a burner that was too hot as a result from poor construction of the unit. Albeit it was 4 years however, this "first fix" did not fix at all.  It seems there is a space (3/4") between the bottom (dripping area) of the grill and the area that the valve regulators go through into the burner (firebox) section. 

This space is only visible when lying on you back to replace the hose (if one's not injured by now) and not visible at all from viewing down.

I'm fairly handy when it comes to replacing the hose however, this is a race to see whether or not one does get injured by a unit that's still working, or one that haven't rusted out yet in 4 years.  My simple solution would be to have a thicker base for the firebox, and extend the connector for the regulator hose down and away from the flame source with a metal gas line.

Your original recall site was:

http://www.cpsc.gov/en/Recalls/2010/Sagittarius-Sporting-Goods-Recalls-Gas-Grills-Sold-at-Lowes-Stores-Due-to-Fire-and-Burn-Hazards/

I've seen the original recall report and decided to add to this units' demise.  Never again for the imports.

After removing the plastic wrapping and the sticker from around the food processor I pressed the lid release button that holds the lid to the food processor on.   The lid wouldn't open up easily so I tried to use both thumbs to apply more force to the release button.  As I did that, the lid came off, the food processor fell on it's side on my kitchen counter, and the food processor blade came rolling out of the food processor, right on top of my left foot. I was rushed to the emergency room and received treatment which included wound irrigation, Tetanus shot, antibiotics shots, multiple anesthesia shots directly around the wound area.  The end result was 6 hours of emergency room and hospital time, 16 stitches in my left foot, a completely severed tendon to my left toe that had to be reattached, and loss of feeling in the foot and several toes. productDescription: Kitchen ventilation fan, down draft, sits behind (but sold separately from) a five burner stove.  Fan designed to raise and lower, and has three speeds - H, M, L.
incidentDescription:
I have a Thermador product with a melted circuit board that I am concerned could cause a fire if I continue to use it, and I have gotten nowhere with the company as far as acknowledging this risk and providing a remedy.   Ultimately I would love if Thermador would remedy the situation, but more importantly I want others who own one of these or are contemplating the purchase of one.   I am still uncertain if it is a defect in the circuit board or a design flaw in the product. 

We moved into our home in 2007. Previous owner had just redone kitchen, went high end on appliances not knowing they were going to have job transfer.

Recently Thermador downdraft fan stopped working properly. Figured it was out of warranty by now, I took a look to see if it was a switch I could replace - discovered it had a circuit board. I was shocked to see that the circuit board had started to melt along with the wires leading to it. I called Thermador, said I knew it must be out of warranty by now - but it seemed like a defect in manufacturing or design flaw and a fire hazard.

After many calls, Thermador reluctantly agreed to send someone at their expense to "diagnose". The technician informed me it happens all the time:. 

I maintain for the amount of money spent on this type of product one should expect it to last longer than five or six years, and of all the appliances I have ever owned, it is the only one that has ever had a part that melted and posed a fire hazard|. Thermador refuses to make good - "it is out of warranty" and it is "normal wear and tear".

I recorded my last conversation with Thermador! The audio, as well as pictures of the melted circuit board and wires and a video of it sparking and smoking can be found on you tube under the user [REDACTED]. I now have a stove in the middle of the kitchen with no ventilation;.

productDescription: Cuisinart food processor prep11 plus
incidentDescription:
My wife owns a Cuisinart Food Processor about six months old.  I was helping my wife in the kitchen.  I removed the basin from the motor base to pour out the semi-liquid contents into a storage container.  As I poured about half the contents in the bowl the razor sharp blade fell out bounced off the counter and landed on the top of my right foot.  I am aware that the blade just sits by gravity onto the motor shaft.  However, when the basin is full you can't see the blade.  I was so surprise and disgusted with myself to see the blade literally shoot out and bounce off the counter.

It was late at night.  The cut was very deep in the top of my foot on the highest point in line with my big toe.  A compression bandage stopped the bleeding after losing 750cc of blood.  I went to my doctor who butterflied and redressed my wound.  It has been two months and my big toe is no longer controlled by the flexor tendon.  It appears my Flexor hallucis longus tendon was either severed or damaged so badly I can't lift my toe. The flexor tendon does not pull up making a ridge like it does on my uninjured left foot.

I believe that having a razor sharp blade held in place only by gravity, in a container designed to be tipped over to transfer processed food, is dangerous. The blade should be mechanically held in place to resist falling out.  It makes no sense that you need to blindly reach through the processed food, that obscures the razor sharp blade only held in place by gravity, before you pour out the contents safely.  

My foot will likely never be the same.  I have intermittent sharp pain across the deep scar in my right foot.  I would not consider surgery to repair the injury.  Surgery could make it worse.  The biggest bummer is the effect my injury has on my passion for rock climbing. The big toe strength is essential for free climbing. I am optimistic over time it will get better some or I'll learn to compensate for the reduced big toe strength.  

Please fix this problem with your food processor.  Good Design does not cost much.  Engineers, like myself, and manufacturers, like Cusiniart, have a duty to protect the public.  As a licensed California Structural Engineer I take that responsibility very seriously.

sparking/flaming motor on U5018-900

Last night I changed the bag on the Hoover vacuum we have. The changing was uneventful. This morning I operated the vacuum and noticed a burning smell. I took off the belt cover to see if anything was blocking the movable parts from moving. Next I removed the rotating bush and the belt and I was able to see back to where the motor was. A plasma (flame looking) light source could be seen from where the motor was. 

Thus it very much appears to me like the motor for this vacuum is sparking when it's in use. This is a new occurrence for us. The vacuum has worked from before this morning. 

The sparking (plasma flame looking light & burning smell) from the motor is of course a fire hazard. 

Due to the nature of this failure I wanted to request assistance from you in this matter, with either repair or replacement.

Flame type light & smoke is definitely being emitted from the motor for this vacuum.

---end of quote

I received a response from TTI Floor Care North America, the makers of the Hoover vacuum in question, first to call their customer service department via phone. Then when I called they said they could not help with a sparking motor over the phone. 

Here is one thing they could have done "over the phone:" Offer to have the vacuum repaired or replaced. These words could have passed from their mouths into their phone and then into my ears. But, they refused to do this, even though the vacuum is now a fire hazard.

Here is the product info for the vacuum:

serial number 050400043453

The fire was under the control knob area and the flames were coming out of the right rear area where the gas line enters. My father had been using the grill at our house the week before and mentioned he was worried about flames from the back.   I opened up the Weber after that, took out the grate, flavorizer bars (they are both new this year) and looked around for any debris, etc.  I also had cleaned the grease pan and ensured nothing was in there.

I had lit the grill and was playing with our dog for a minute.  As it was still coming up to temperature, I went in side for ~5 mins, when I came out flamers were coming out of the back right area of the grill (under the control knob table and the back knob had already started to melt.  I quickly reached under, avoiding the flames and turned off the gas at the tank. The flames went out in the grill when the gas was shut off, but one of the knobs was actually on fire. Fortunately, I saw the fire before it burned through the gas supply hose. The fire burned the control knobs, the ignition wiring and it appears to have scorched the gas supply hose from the gas fuel tank. 

I contacted Weber and they asked me to send photos, which I have done. I am concerned that this is a safety issue that could result in a home fire, or possibly an explosion if other consumers experience the same issue.

productDescription: Char-Broil Patio Bistro TRU Infrared Gas (LP) Grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
model: Char Broil Patio Bistro Gas (LP) Grill, Model 126015 Series
incidentDescription:
I purchased a CharBroil Patio Bistro TRU-Infrared Gas Grill (Model 126015 Series) from The Home Depot online that was delivered to my home on/about June 6, 2013. Upon opening the packing box and before assembling the unit, I noticed that the valve was not correctly positioned inside the burner tube (where the valve coming from the gas supply meets the aerated burner tube which then leads into the kettle)  I carefully but firmly repositioned the two parts into the correct position.  There is no hard connecting point here, just a matter of positioning the two gas lines to ensure proper gas flow.  THIS IS NOT COVERED IN THE ASSEMBLY GUIDE OR THE GRILLING GUIDE THAT CAME WITH THE PRODUCT, HOWEVER, AND IS ONLY MENTIONED IN THE PRODUCT GUIDE UNDER THE SECTION ON "CLEANING THE BURNER ASSEMBLY" ON PAGE 9.  THE CONSUMER SHOULD BE EXPRESSLY WARNED TO CHECK THIS PARTICULAR VALVE/BURNER TUBE ASSEMBLY EACH TIME THE GRILL IS USED AND SHOULD BE WARNED OF THE DISTINCT POSSIBILITY OF A SEVERE AND INTENSE FIRE.

 Problem 1:  An inexperienced assembler would not necessarily notice that the valve was not positioned correctly into the burner tube while unpacking the unit from the original box which was exactly the situation I faced.  I suspect the proper alignment was dislodged during routine handling and shipping.  That misalignment can produce a serious fire hazard WHICH I LEARNED THE HARD WAY SHORTLY AFTERWARD (see next paragraph).

 

After first assembling the grill per the Assembly Guide and connecting a new 20# propane tank, I used the grill on 3 or 4 occasions during the remainder of June without any problems.  The assembly worked perfectly and the grill lived up to the good reviews we had read.
However, on July 4th, I gently moved the grill approximately one foot (the grill is equipped with wheels for the express purpose of moving it) to make room for other items on our rear deck and prepared for a family cookout.  UNBEKNOWNST TO ME, the valve/burner tube "fitting" described above became dislodged.  I started the grill with the electronic igniter and brought the grill up to cooking temperature per the instructions .  I left the grill for appromixately 2-3 minutes to bring food from the kitchen to the deck to cook.  As I was loading my first food items, I realized that an intense fireball, approximately 6 inches in diameter, was roaring directly under the heat control unit and coming from valve/burner tube assembly area.  The fire had already severely damaged the control assembly, had burned through the igniter wires, and was rapidly devouring the gas supply line from the propane tank.    I first grabbed the burner controller which had already warped from the heat and was "frozen" in place (i.e., useless at this point) and then immediately reached underneath the fireball to turn off the gas from the tank (praying that the fire wouldn't reach the propane tank itself).  The grill and fully charged propane tank were less than 15 feet from the back door to my home and family during this episode.

 Needless to say, the grill is now ruined.  The gas feeder hose from the tank, the entire control assembly,and the igniter assembly are completely burned and unusable.  I do not trust this grill and will not have it near my family in the future.

 Problem 2:  Even an experienced person may not know how to control or extinguish a fire that can start so easily and was caused simply by moving the grill one foot and inadvertantly jostling a critical mating of gas lines (again there is no hard connection; the two lines are simply nestled together).    The engineering of this connection should be examined and changed.  Clear warnings of possible fire based on my very real expereince should be provided to the consumer.



I have contacted the Arlington County, Virginia, Fire Department/Fire Prevention Unit and am copying their representative on this email.  I am also submitting a copy of this communciation and reporting this incident to the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission  U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission using their online reporting system (the action being taken here). 


I have asked The Home Depot to have a Customer Service Representative contact me to discuss how best to return my burned out yet "still new" grill.  I am equally concerned that other consumers be made aware of this dangerous situation which in my case became a real incident even when I followed all published safety procedures.  I will henceforth check the valve/burner supply connection before each use with any grill that I purchase and use in the future.

 

Sincerely,

[REDACTED]
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: food chopper
incidentDescription:
The consumer stated that his wife was using the food chopper to prepare a meal. The consumer stated that when she was done cooking he went to eat the food and found sharp plastic pieces in the food. The consumer stated that he had placed food in his mouth and he felt the plastic pieces inside of his mouth. 

The consumer stated that he wasn’t sure where the plastic came from and he decided to look at the inside of the chopper. The consumer stated he noticed the broken pieces that came from the collar (see picture).  There is a ridge on the collar.  Pieces of plastic chipped off of the ridge.

The consumer stated that no one was injured. Some of the plastic may have been swallowed.

The consumer stated that he contacted the manufacturer on May 10 2013 and the representative informed him that there was no problem with the food chopper. The consumer stated that the representative informed him that they were only aware of incidents in which the consumer did not properly use chopper. The representative clearly indicated that plastic pieces break off the collar- if the blade guard is not seated adequately or if it is missing.

The consumer stated this product should be investigated do to the safety hazard that it poses to consumers.  The plastic pieces which are chipped off are dangerous if they are swallowed by an infant of by anyone.

productDescription: Sunjoy outdoor wood burning fireplace Description: This recall involves "Garden Treasures Living" steel outdoor fireplaces with a bronze finish chimney and slate colored accents. The wood burning fireplace is approximately 24 inches deep by 35 inches wide and 57 inches tall, has two glass doors and a tile back inside. Item number 0027705 and model number L-OF082PST-3 are printed on the front page of the product's instruction manual
incidentDescription:
Back when this fireplace was originally recalled in 2011, we hadn’t yet used it.  So, the replacement hood that was sent to us, is working fine.  However we are now experiencing other issues with the fireplace body itself and have safety concerns.
 
We have used this fireplace about 10-15 times in the last year (which isn’t much).  We didn’t start using until 2012.  It is covered and protected from the elements when not in use.
 
We used it this past Saturday evening, were surprised to see some bubbling & smoking of paint near the bottom, and also the stone work started falling off (I can providee pictures).  It would appear this is another recall type event, and would like to have a replacement bottom sent to us.  This should not be happening with a fireplace that costs the amount of money that this one, with the limited use we’ve given it.  
 
We are now not using it, feeling there may be another safety issue and are concerned with it starting to now fall apart.

productDescription: Dehumidifier
incidentDescription:

The "fix" cost me $90.54 (receipt enclosed) and never did fix the problem. Go figure! Two years later, a recall was issued on the dehumidifier. I knew nothing about the recall until going through an old issue (November 2012) of Consumer Reports magazine. A special thank you to them for bringing this problem to my attention. 
On this date, I contacted Sears National Customer Relations at 1-800-549-4505 and spoke with a very pleasant and accommodating representative who, at my request, provided me with the Sears' Customer Solutions address. By copy of this letter, lam asking Sears to fully reimburse me the 2010 out-of-pocket costs ($90.54) I incurred in my fruitless attempt at "repairing" the defective dehumidifier.
Please reference Service Order #[REDACTED]. 
I will note that r have been a loyal customer of Sears for many years. In addition to two (2) dehumidifiers, I have purchased refrigerators, ranges, a microwave, a dryer, vacuum cleaners etc. Whenever I was in need of a major appliance or a small appliance, my first thought was Sears. Hoping I can.

UPDATE FROM CONSUMER:

While I thought the "settlement" cound have/should have been more (as outlined in my 6-13-13 letter), I am 'satisfied' with the prompt response from the mfr.  The matter has been resolved. On 6-8-13 I received a call rfom Sears advising me my credit card would be credited the full amount of the repair in 2010- $90.54. As of this date, the credit has not been applied.

productDescription: Weber liquid gas freestanding outdoor grill - 2 burner
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
On Saturday, July 6, 2013 we used our new weber grill for only the 4th time since purchase from Lowes in Egg Harbor Twsp, NJ on May 25, 2013.  

We turned it on, the automatic igniter lit and we let it warm up for about 2 minutes.
Upon putting 2 steaks on the grill, the entire grill became engulfed in flames.
The fire was shooting out from under the grill where the b ase of the burners were located and where the propane tank was stored.  Meanwhile  the steaks were located on the grill and the fire shot out the sides of the grill......it was not a grease fire.

The fire began burning a coating of metal material from inside the grill which emitted billowing gray smoke for at least 5 minutes. It was noxious.

It billowed into the neighborhood and made me sick.   A friend ran forward and turned off the propane using the knob located on the front. I thought the grill was going to explode on my deck and kill us.My husband said the temperature gauge was at the manimum of 600 degrees. It could have been hotter.

After the supply to the propane was shut off, the grey smoke continued to billow out.

Upon cooling, I noticed the inside of the grill which was supposed to be stainless steel was turned a medium brown color which did not rub off like soot.

I read tonight online that the grill grates are coated with something to promote flavor.Whatever that was it is completely burned off.

I was really scared and have owned a grill for 40 years. This type of incident has never happened.

The design of the grill is such that there is no bottom to the housing...essentially the housing consists of 2 sides and a lid which you pull shut   With no iron or other metal barrier between the propane tank and the burners directly above - the grill looks like a fire hazard. There are 3 removable teepe shaped metal parts which are to be cleaned periodically located directly under the burners. These were covered black.

Again the material burning and billowing out gray smoke was not grease from new steaks just put on.

Thank you for listening. 
[REDACTED]

productDescription: Pampered Chef Food Chopper
incidentDescription:
We started noticing hundreds of little opaque *lines* in the bottom edge of the housing (the part that actually sits on your cutting board) and were like, "What's that?" After investigating, in slow motion, we realized what was up.

The outsides of the waffled blades are so close to the edges of the clear plastic housing that they inadvertently collide, thus shaving off little bits of the plastic housing and intermixing them in whatever food we're chopping.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: Babyfood Cooker-steams, cooks, and purees food for babies.  Similar to a blender, but includes a special steaming function and type of plastic bowl with measurements for baby food.
incidentDescription: I purchased a Beaba Babyfood cooker in January 2013 to puree and steam food for my infant son.  In less than six months of use I discovered major cracks underneath the blades in the plastic bowl used to puree/steam the food.  Had I not been tipped to remove the blades for cleaning I would not have noticed this cracking.  These cracks have led to food seepage along the outer rims of the bowl, creating mold (even with cleaning in the dishwasher after each use).  Also, due to the number and size of the cracks I am highly concerned small pieces of plastic could break off and go into the baby's food, causing major injury if ingested.  I would NOT recommend this product and believe it should be recalled due to this issue.  I have a number of friends who also purchased this product (at my initial recommendation), their Beaba's have all had the same issue.

productDescription: Baby BEABA baby food cooker (steamer and blender in one)
incidentDescription: I purchased a Baby Beaba cooker to make fresh food for my baby. I have owned it only 2 months and the bottom plastic (around the blade) is cracking. This poses a big safety concern as pieces of this plastic once broken off will end up in my baby's food and pose a choking hazard, and potential for internal injury if ingested. I have a friend who purchased the same cooker with me and her product is already chipping, she noticed missing plastic pieces and immediately notified me. Upon inspection of my own unit I noticed dozens of cracks in the bottom of my unit, thankfully no (visibly) missing pieces. My friend had to throw away all her baby food and is unsure how long her unit has been flaking plastic into her baby's meals!

productDescription: Summer Infant Slim and Secure handheld color video monitors (model #02800) - Type 3.7V Li-ion Battery
brand: Summer Infant Slim and Secure handheld color video monitors
incidentDescription: Yesterday, I went to turn on our Summer Infant Slim and Secure handheld color video monitor (model #02800). I noticed that the back of the battery compartment was almost off of the back. When I went to re-secure it, I noticed that the battery appears to be bloated, which caused the back of the monitor to crack and the battery door to become unattached. I remembered that these monitors and their rechargeable batteries had been recalled in the past, but ours was not included in that recall b/c it was marked w/ "TLC." I am glad we found this defective battery before it ruptured, which could have either causing me harm (b/c it rests on a table beside my head at night) or damaged the monitor itself. Thank you.

productDescription: Black and Decker Toaster Oven
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
Toaster Oven would not turn off and toast almost caught on fire.  This was a brand new BD Toaster Oven with three knobs.  There is nothing on the toaster oven which indicates that the oven is set to off.

I called BD Customer support and they explained that the bottom knob should be turned parallel with the countertop.  Going all the way over leaves the unit permanently in an on position.  There is a O which is supposed to indicate Off but the word Off does not appear on the Toaster Oven.  This is a terrible design flaw.  Even the DIrections for Use are not clear on this.

productDescription: 4 burner gas grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription: The consumer says that flames shot out of control panel.  Her son shut it off and turned it on again, yet the same thing happened.  She says she will never use it again.  She contacted the manufacturer who said that they will offer to send a technicican for a fee, she refused.

productDescription: Basic [slow cooker]
incidentDescription: I had my [slow cooker] at a picnic. It was just the [slow cooker] and lid, not the entire unit (so obviously it was not plugged in). It had been sitting on a table for several hours. The [slow cooker] was completely cool at this point. I was standing about 8 feet away talking with a group of people when we heard an explosion. We all looked at each other and walked over to the table (no one was around the table at the time of the explosion thank God). Here the lid to the [slow cooker] had exploded all over the place. It was in and on other food and all over the table. We had to pitch some food and take the table cloth completely off because there was no way to clean up all the glass as it had flown everywhere. It was very scary to think my kids or other kids or even adults could have been in the path of the flying glass!

productDescription: Black & Decker Toast-R-Oven, Model# TR04075B with a QC Pass 2 sticker on it.
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
I am once again writing to inform the public of yet another fire we experienced while making toast on 6/11/13, with
our free replacement Black & Decker Countertop Oven. Needless to say, after three different model replacement
ovens from Black & Decker (Model #TR0480BS on 7/5/10 and Model# TR0480BS on 2/23/11, referred to in Report
No. 2011 0323-6D9C3-1172288 filed with the U.S. Consumer Products Safety Commission and recent Model#
TR04075B with a QC Pass 2 sticker on it), I am totally convinced- Black and Decker/ aka Applica- is making junk. At
one time, I had confidence in buying the Black and Decker brand, but no more. The fact that we live in a throw
away society and the fact that the government does not recall these products is appalling to me. To make matters
worse, the internet is full of reviews concerning fires with these products and they continue to remain on the shelf.
After filing and researching my two previous complaints, which requested an investigation into this matter, I was
told that only the most serious complaints are investigated. Therefore, the products remain on the shelf. The
remedy to the problem was two-fold. I could either file another complaint and/or stop buying the product.
Needless to say, I filed another complaint, bought the #1 rated toaster oven, and will never buy an appliance from
Black and Decker again.

incidentDescription:
My Cuisinart coffeemaker nearly caught fire this morning. If I hadn't been home, it would have likely caused a serious fire in my home. 
I was walking past and it started crackling and smoking, huge billowing smoke. I immediately unplugged it and took it out to my lawn. It took a good 1/2 hour to cool down completely. The heating element was glowing and it was extremely hot.

productDescription: Propane Grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
Caller received grill on Father's Day 2012 and had no problems with it until Father's Day 2013.
Caller was grilling, walked inside for a few moments then back outside.
He saw that the grill had dark smoke coming for under the hood.
He opened the lid and aside from the normal flames of grilling there were flames with black smoke coming from beneath with the cooking area.

There have been no injuries
Caller has not contacted the manufacturer yet but does intend to contact them.

productDescription: toaster oven broiler
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
(06/17/2013) The consumer stated that she had brussel sprouts and carrots warming in the oven at 200 degrees. The consumer stated that she took her son upstairs to put him to bed. She stated that she was only upstairs for about ten minutes.  When she came back downstairs the food in the oven was smoking. The heating elements  were on bright red as if they were on broil. The indicator still showed 200. The consumer stated that she unplugged the oven. She stated that she took the food out. The consumer stated that she tried it again the next day to see what would happen. The same thing happened again. The consumer stated that she turned the oven off at the switch. The consumer stated that she did not unplug the oven. Later on in the evening, the consumer stated that she heard a high pitch noise that sounded like a fire alarm. The consumer stated that it was the toaster oven making the noise.

(06/18/2013) The consumer stated that she called the company She spoke with a customer service representative. The consumer asked to speak with a supervisor. The consumer explained the situation. The consumer was advised that there was a three year warranty on the product. The consumer was advised that nothing could be done about the problem.

(06/19/2013) The consumer stated that she sent a letter to [REDACTED] , the Director of Business Development. The consumer have not received a response. 

The consumer stated that there are several customer comments on the Amazon web site.

productDescription: Propane Grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
The consumer stated that he purchased a grill approximately 10 years ago and he the burning assembly was worn out and he decided to replace the burners. The consumer stated that the manufacturer sent the replacement burners and the consumer found that the new burners are approximately 4” smaller than the original. 

The consumer stated that since the burners are smaller when you try to turn the grill on with the “match in the hole” the grill can fill up with gas and explode. The consumer stated that because the burners are smaller there was an increase in the buildup of gas inside the grill, which can lead to an explosion. 

The consumer stated that no one was injured. He stated that there were no damages to his home structure.

The consumer stated that he stopped using the grill. 

The consumer stated that he contacted the manufacturer and they informed him that the burners should always be lid by the ignited and if that fails use a match extension (Approx. 6” long). The consumer stated that the manufacturer provided instructions on how to use the match extension. 

The consumer stated that he received an email back from the engineer who informed him that the new burners were tested and should works as good as the original. 

The consumer stated that he believed that this product should be investigated. 

UPDATE FROM CONSUMER:
Also the new burner kit came with installation to replace, but no warning on how to light the grill.

productDescription: Propane powered portable grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
RE: Char-Broil TEC grill Model 463268307 S/N G508010704002246

I have had this problem on this grill on two occasions.  

With a mild breeze coming in from the backside of the unit the controls on the front panel get hot enough to burn the fingers, hot enough to melt the knobs and trim and the electric igniter gets so hot that it has exploded.  The explosion is the result of the battery inside overheating.  The explosion cause the parts of the igniter to be shot directly into the face of the operator.

I replaced these parts once but the problem reoccurred.  I just spoke to the manufacturer and their response is to not use the grill in the presence of wind.  This is an outdoor device and there is always the possibility of a breeze outdoors.  I have another similar grill from another manufacturer that does not have this problem since it incorporates a simple heat shield between the burners and the controls.

productDescription:
Shop Vac 4 hp wall hanging

incidentDescription:
This is a ShopVac wall hanging wet/dry vacuum purchased from a Lowe's store approximately 5 years ago.  It is used in our garage to vacuum out our vehicles and clean up small messes from projects. However it has never been used as a wet vac. This is the second time this particular problem has happened with this vacuum.  The first time the housing around the On/Off switch got so hot it melted around the switch.  This time it got very hot to the touch and my wife said when she went to turn it off she felt a mild shock.

After that incident we always unplugged the vacuum after use.
When it use it did not trip the GFI outlet it was plugged into nor did it pop the circuit breaker.
ShopVac 4.0hp  Model# QPSH400 or Model# 87707-91. I can not locate a serial number on the unit.

productDescription: Outdoor Gas Grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
I'd like to alert you to a defective and potentially dangerous product. 

I purchased a very expensive ($3,000+) Capital Cooking Outdoor Grill. Several times the igniters have burnt out and even the plastic coating on the electrical wires leading to them have been totally burnt off due to inadequate insulation between the grills themselves and the igniters. The igniters have been replaced twice but the company refuses to correct the problem. The danger comes from the fact that gas does not ignite and there is the real potential for an explosion. Furthermore the knobs at the front of the grill become so hot that they cannot be touched without an insulated glove and in fact I have burned my fingers twice.

I have had several discussions with the president of the company however his response is that the grill must have a surround built around it. I have owned a few other far less expensive grills and never had this problem. I though you should know so that you can test this make yourself and alert your readers to this deficiency and danger.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription: Upright Stand Blender
incidentDescription:
This is a Kalorik Model BL-16909 Blender.  It was purchased new in May 2012, and has been used infrequently.  Lately I have been using the blender, about 3-4 times per week to make smoothies which requires crushing @ 5-6 ice cubes first, before blending in the other frozen and fresh ingredients.

Yesterday, I was fortunate in that I looked into the glass blender jar to inspect the ice.  Inside the ice were several pieced of black material.  Upon closer inspection, what had happened was a black plastic washer that keeps the three metal blades separated, braking off from the cutter blade assembly.  There were three to four pieces.  

Had I not noticed this, and added the other ingredients I might have swallowed the washer pieces.

Although I don't think this rises to a choking hazard, it certainly is not something I want to ingest.

productDescription: Cooler Master M/N: NotePal X- Slim laptop cooling fan
incidentDescription: Cooler Master model  NotePal X-Slim laptop cooling fan (flat flat sits under the laptop) has 3 distinct problems: 1) The USB female port is sharp, it cut both my wife and my 5 year old daughter during regular use of the product 2) the wires that power the fan are in the housing right next to the fan, which caused it to fail and lockup 3) My wife (not realizing the fan being plugged in was a problem) left the unit plugged in and left. When I came home to check the unit I found the round metal motor housing on the bottom to be extremely hot, it burned my finger to touch it. Luckily there was nothing overly flammable nearby and my children weren't playing it. This thing is junk.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription: Jenn-Air built-in outdoor grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
In mid-May, I was making steaks on my new Jenn-Air gas barbecue. I put the steaks on and walked back into the house to check on the rice. When I returned, literally minutes later, the patio was full of smoke and there were flames shooting out of the barbecue.

I went to shut off the gas burners, but they had become so hot you couldn't touch them without a hot pad. Worse, the controls inside them had apparently melted -- the nobs spun like [REDACTED]'s head in [REDACTED]. 

Fortunately, I have my gas shut-off valve right next to the barbecue, so I didn't have to call the fire department. But it was tense.

Still, I would have thought it was some weird anomaly if the company had responded differently when I called to report the problem. Instead, when I told them the barbecue had imploded, they started asking questions: How much ventilation is it getting?  Can you send photos of how the BBQ is set up -- from every side? etc.... 

When I asked what was up, they said: Well, if its not well ventilated, the heat can go down through the back and out the front....burning through the mechanism. In other words, this has happened before. So I started searching for complaints about this BBQ. I couldn't find the exact model number, but this struck me as interesting, since the second review came so close to what happened to me: http://www.consumerreports.org/cro/home-garden/lawn-garden/gas-grills/gas-grill-ratings/models/overview/jenn-air-720-0709-sams-club-99030943.htm

Un-plugged and tried exercising the timer knob, tried plugging it back in and it again began to smoke. Un-plugged it and permanently put it out of service.

productDescription: Oscillating table fan, AC power
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription:
My Holmes Oscillating Fan Model HAOF87 "Blizzard" has been working fine since we bought it new several years ago.  However recently I accidentally stepped on the cord barefoot and got a 60-cycle shock in my foot.  (I'm a retired Electrical Engineer and I _know_ what 60 hertz current feels like.)

A visual inspection of the chord shows no wear or breaks in the insulation (but my eyesight ain't what it used to be).  It was plugged in with the polarized plug in the correct direction and the outlet is properly grounded.

I would be happy to mail you the fan if you wish.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: purple & gray steam mop
incidentDescription: I put water in my steam mop and plugged it in.  Usually it starts steaming within a minute or two.  It didn't this time.  I got closer to see if I could hear it.  Then all of a sudden the mop head blew off across the floor and then the steam came out.  I was not hurt but felt that the product was unsafe to use.

productDescription: 16" Oscillating Stand Fan/White
incidentDescription: I have the 16" Climate Keeper fan in my office cubicle. I have had it for about 3 years. I have only used it a handful of times. Two days ago I was sitting in my office and heard something just shatter. It was the plastic blades on the fan. All the blades just disintegrated as I had the fan on. Which caused the blade pieces to fly everywhere. Even though pieces flew into my hair ,it was a good thing I had my back to it. But my niece was looking at it straight on and she was lucky to be far enough from it that she didn't have a pieces fly into her eyes.  I couldn't believe what I saw. That is absolutely ridiculous that that piece would be so brittle that it would break like that.

Crock pot brand crock pot. purchased approx 1 year ago but I no longer have the receipt. I was cooking frozen butter beans, with plenty of water, had them on low for about 4 hours. I heard a loud crash, went in the kitchen, and the glass lid to the crock pot had shattered into a million pieces. still somewhat holding together in a lid shape until you touch the plastic handle. 

I did nothing to the crock pot before it broke. i had not touched it in a couple hours. it was not bothered in anyway, just sitting on my counter cooking on LOW. I have used this crock pot plenty of times before this incident.

productDescription: ceiling fan with light fixture with antique glass shades
incidentDescription:
The consumer stated that his ceiling fan was installed 05/28/2013 and after approximately 10 minutes he noticed a burning plastic type smell. The consumer stated that he noticed that the fan was emitting the odor and he decided to turn off the circuit breaker. 

The consumer stated that he tried to make sure it was installed properly and turned the fan back on. He stated that the fan started to emit the same burning odor. 
The consumer stated that he believed that the smell was being emitted from the antique shades. He stated that the glass shades were turning a brown color as if it was burning. 
The consumer suffered irritation to his eyes, sore throat and headaches. The consumer stated that he did not receive any first aid or medical attention, along with a friend who came out that night.  Consumer did contact poison control and they informed himto vacate home.  HIS home.
The consumer stated that the manufacturer informed him that they would contact him back.

He's contacted them a more more times and they still have not resolved the issue or contacted me.   They are very rude.  To resolve the issue, they must 1) fix product and 2) let him know what he was or could be exposed to.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: four burner Gas Grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
The consumer says the original gas tank was empty.  He exchanged the gas tank with the retailer.  He used it for the first time on Memorial day (5/27/13).  

Once he used it he smelled the presence of a gas odor.  After twenty minutes he noticed flames shooting out of the outlet where they attach the regulator to the tank.  

The consumer acted promptly and shut off all the four burners on the top.  He extinguished the flame by pouring water on the unit.  He received minor burns on his fingers on his right hand.  

The attachment of the grill to the cylinder has a gas leak which caused this to happen.  The entire plastic that is holding to the cylinder is completely burned.  

The incident has been communicated to Brinkmann and [REDACTED].
victimSeverity: Injury, Level of care not known

productDescription: Gas Grill

They contained the flames by using a fire extinguisher.  She feels that she experienced similar problems of release 12-152..Hazard: The regulator on the grill can leak propane gas, which can ignite, posing fire and burn hazard to consumers.

6/3/13 The manufacturer was contacted and she was advised to send pictures of the incident and someone would contact her.

The caller feels that this gas grill should be included in the recall.

The unit is unplugged and sitting on my counter and could be made available, upon request.

productDescription: Lasko model 5165 ceramic tower space heater.  S/N H2511071056
incidentDescription:
I have a Lasko model 5165 ceramic tower space heater.  We used it in a small room of the house during the past two winter seasons.  A few weeks ago, I wanted to unplug the heater from its extension cord in order to reuse the cord.  That extension cord is short (about 3 feet) and heavy duty, designed for use with a portable air conditioner.  It should be able to handle the load of this heater.

When I tried to unplug the heater, I was unable to do so by hand as the plug was stuck.  I used tools to separate them.  I was then able to see that the plug had overheated and melted to the extension cord.  The metal plug prongs are charred.  

I checked the Lasko web site and found that several other models, some similar to this one, had been recalled for similar problems.
