productDescription: 14" Oscillating Pedestal Dish
incidentDescription:
Consumer states the initial incident where the wires fell from the motor of the heater happen 1/15/12. The consumer sent the heater to be repaired, but received a refurbished heater in April 2012 instead.

The consumer stated that the heater was then only used once or twice because it was not needed because of the season change. 
Consumer reported the heater was now being used to heat the living room area of the home after 8 months of storage. The consumer had the heater plugged in  for about 12-14 hours consecutively, but the heater has a temperature control. Therefore the heater only comes on when the temperature is below 75 degrees. 

The consumer stated the wires that connect to the back of the heater seemingly broke out of the motor, while it was still plugged in. The wires began to spark and the consumer unplugged the heater.
 
(12/10/2012)  The consumer contacted the mfr. and spoke with [REDACTED] (Last name not given) and was told the problem was a user error.

Consumer stated the heater is not functioning and has been sent to a personal acquaintance for repairs.

There was no property or physical damage.

productDescription: Vacuum cleaner
incidentDescription:
The consumer is concerned because he feels that this is a safety hazard. He also stated that he will not buy another Sears product. 

The consumer stated that there was a short in the handle of the vacuum cleaner which was repaired in 2009. About a year ago the light on the attachment for the powermate began to blink off and on. The motor would cut in and out. 

The consumer stated that there was a smell coming from the handle on August 1, 2012. 
The consumer turned it off and unplugged from the outlet. The consumer stated that the handled was warm to the touch at the connection to the pipe. The consumer disconnected the hose attachment and found that the electrical plug was melted.  

The consumer stated that the manufacturer was contacted on August 7, 2012. The consumer was advised of 90 day guarantee on the repair which was in 2009. The customer was advised that he could bring the vacuum in for repair at a cost to him. The price would be upward of $90.

productDescription: Krups espresso machine FNC2 machine.
incidentDescription:
I had made an espresso; lucky for me I had not stirred it up well with the sugar as when I had finished drinking it, I noticed a sharp piece of plastic in the sugar.  I thought at first that it had not come from the machine as I knew that it had an o ring that was soft, this was hard.  So I made another one, then another piece was in my next cup this time larger and really sharp.

I contacted the manufacturer after I turned the machine up side down to see where it came from and asked about the part number that I needed to replace.  They said they did not have that part available (they had lost of other parts, but not that one) ...which made me think that many others had the same thing happen.

It is a hard plastic like [REDACTED] that would be bad if someone ingested it.  I have the unit still and the broken parts if you want pictures.

productDescription: George Foreman Grilling Machine
incidentDescription: I was cleaning up my grill. After removing the plates and the drip catcher, I saw some oil (grilled salmon with olive oil) had spilled on my counter. I ran my dish cloth underneath the grill and my right ring finger made contact with a plastic piece under the grill that has an opening. The edges of the plastic are sharp and I cut my knuckle. The cut is approximately 1/8 of an inch deep and it was hard to get the bleeding to stop due to being on the knuckle.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription:
Bodum (brand) Tea For One:  Glass with tea strainer, double wall
Had one orange and one black
incidentDescription:
Had purchased 2 Bodum Tea For One glasses (double-wall glass with tea strainer).  Used for a couple months with no incident.  I had always hand-washed them.  One time, after finishing my tea, I was handwashing with those plastic soap wands with sponge at the end.  As I was turning the glass with one hand and using the soap sponge wand on the inside with the other hand, the outside shattered where I was holding.

I looked down and the outside layer of glass had shattered.  I did not use any heavy pressure and did nothing that should have put enough pressure to shatter the glass.  I did get a minor cut on my hand - luckily there was not hot tea liquid in the glass when it happened.

I threw out the glass and have not used the other one since.  I have sent two messages to Bodum about the incident through their website contact form but never got any response.

When it shattered, I noticed how thin the layers of glass are on the double layer and I can see that it probably could break if you held on too tight while drinking tea which is why I don't use the other one anymore.  The glass is much thinner than the [REDACTED] glass tumblers (which I also owned) that were just recalled.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: Food Processor, chrome, 9 Cup
incidentDescription: When purchasing an item I have a tendency to read the good reviews and overall ranking and discount the poor ones because as a rule it is hard to please everyone. I am not one to complain but I feel it is my duty to write this review to prevent one from getting hurt by this machine. I have had the Prep 9™ 9-Cup Food Processor for about 2 months and I use this food processor only to process vegetables to make soups. The machine does a wonderful job as many reviews describe. I operate and clean this item as instructed. Yesterday while processing tomatoes I heard something that sounded like a pebble bouncing off the inner bowl as the unit was operating. When investigating I noticed that a sharp piece of the blade (about the size of half a [REDACTED]), broke off from its base and was lose in my processed tomatoes. Upon further review I noticed stress cracks around all four rivets that are used to attach the base of the blade to its crème colored plastic anchor. I escalated this issue to Cuisinart customer service and will be returning the Prep 9 to Crate and Barrel later today. Unfortunately due to the severity of this issue I will be purchasing another branded food processor. What scares me is that if I didn’t catch this I easily could have eaten/ ingested the piece of the blade with my food and who knows if I would have been around to write this review. Very Scary….. As stated before, I feel obligated to voice my concern with this product.

productDescription: 22.5" dia. Black, Weber Charcoal grill with glass filled nylon handles.
incidentDescription:
PRODUCT:  Weber Charcoal Grill with glass filled nylon handle on lid.
While the instructions (fine print) instruct one to use a mitt, I think reasonable person would assume that the handle provides some insulating value.  It does not.  I touched it lightly and dropped the lid but burned my fingertips.  If someone gripped it tightly without a mitt (seemingly impossible based on space limitations), a serious burn would be the result.  In the past, the metal handles were covered with wood.  I don't believe the average consumer is going to realize that the glass filled nylon handles are heat conductors.  
I reside in Warsaw, IN.  The incident happened in Waterloo, IA.  Both are the same Weber Charcoal grill.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: Bunn Coffee Maker
model: Velocity Brew 10-Cup Thermal Carafe Brewer, Black
incidentDescription:
Text of consumer's e-mail message dated May 10, 2013:

Subject: sickening smell from Bunn Coffee Maker
We purchased a Velocity Brew 10-Cup Thermal Carafe Brewer, Black on April 13th of this year. Both my daughter and I got headaches from the smell that emanated from the brewer and it only got worse with each passing day. That unit was returned to Amazon with the explanation that the smell was obnoxious. A new brewer was received as a replacement with the same problem. I called the Bunn customer service line and complained about the smell and was told that it was from the glue used in China and it would go away with frequent use in three or four weeks. We tried to run the brewer about twenty times and the next morning the smell was worse than ever. I have had a headache for two days, daughter cannot stand the smell in the house and my wife came down with a sore throat to the point she lost her voice.
I have returned the second unit and this time I asked for a refund. I believe there is a problem with the glue being used and Bunn knows about but continues to keep the unit on the market.
victimSeverity: Injury, Level of care not known

productDescription: Size D Battery, 8 pack
incidentDescription:
Within the last 6 to 12 months I purchased a package of
Ray-0-Vac, D batteries, expiration 12-2017,lot RG6F.
They came in a plastic package which contained about 8
batteries. They were probably purchased from Ocean
State Job Lot or Wal-Mart, but I cannot be sure. I
placed them in various flashlights in our home and
cars. One of those flashlights was placed upright on an
end table near my bed. Recently I noticed a ring on
that table under the upright flashlight. I opened the
flashlight and observed that one of the batteries was
leaking a fluid. That fluid caused severe damage to the
finish on the table. I then we to observe the
remainder of the batteries remaining in the container.
Another one was leaking and some of the fluid spotted
my jeans.
In May, I call the company and reported the above
details. They asked me to return the batteries for
replacement but I choose instead to report it to this
Agency.

productDescription: Mr. Coffee Espresso machine
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription: I purchased a Mr. Coffee espresso machine from Wal Mart on 5/27/13.  I followed the instructions included with the appliance, including performing the 'test run' using just water.  I brewed my first pot using espresso coffee and just before the end of the brew cycle, I turned away from the machine to get a coffee cup.  Right after I turned, there was a huge exploding sound and the brew basket blew off the machine, the glass carafe shattered, and hot espresso went everywhere.  There was broken glass, coffee grounds, and hot espresso all over me - my kitchen - and even in my dining room.  The walls and ceiling in my kitchen were covered in grounds and espresso.  If I had not turned away from the machine when I did, the flying glass and metal parts would have hit me in the face.  NOT A SAFE APPLIANCE!

productDescription: GE 12 cup digital coffee maker
incidentDescription:
(04/20/2013) The consumer stated that she started brewing coffee. She had been using it every morning. She followed the manual instructions. As it was brewing, she smelled smoke after about five minutes. Behind the plate where the pot sits, she saw flames. The plastic behind the pot and underneath the plate was melting. She unplugged the item. Her husband took it outside and hosed it down. She had to open all of the windows due to the smoke from the burning plastic. The damage was contained to the coffee maker. 

The consumer took the coffee maker back to Walmart.  She spoke to the manager on duty. She was given a full refund.

productDescription: Silver cover three control knobs on the side
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription: I was preheating the grill to get ready to cook. Went into the house to get the meat to put on the grill and noticed the flames shooting out from under the control panel. Had to turn the gas off in order to be the flames to stop shooting out toward the second knob which was totally melted. This is the second time this has happened.   The first time I thought maybe I needed to clean the gas tubes and replaced the regulator hose thinking it was the hose.  Obviously it was neither the tubes or the regulator. It is frustrating as the first time I called Weber, I told them what had happened and all the lady said was what parts do you need. Didn't even acknowledge that there was a a potentially dangerous fire.

productDescription: Black and Decker Toaster Oven
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
I put a slice of toast in oven as I always do. I Smelled smoke while in the room next to kitchen. I Ran into kitchen now in thick smoke, smelled burning wires and saw flames inside toaster oven that were coming out of sides of glass door. I unplugged the oven and watched closely. The flames went out and I then waited until it was cool to inspect oven. 

I called Black and Decker and made a report. I kept the defective toaster oven in case it needs to be inspected.

productDescription: BonaVita BV1800TH 8 Cup Coffee Maker with Thermal Carafe
incidentDescription: Glass lining of thermal carafe of the Bonavita B1800 8-Cup Coffee Maker exploded (imploded) while being rinsed with warm water.  Glass flew out, hitting me and landing a couple of feet away.  The carafe was never dropped or damaged in any way. There are numerous other reports of this problem in online reviews, and at least one other recent CPSC report published (20130410-3D5C5-2147457124 ).

productDescription: Tea Kettle
incidentDescription:

She tried to contact the manufacturer but she only finds web sites that sell the product but she cannot find contact information for them.
victimSeverity: Injury, Level of care not known

incidentDescription:
Own a Optimus Infrared Quartz Radiant heater model number H-5210, purchased on January 20, 2012.  The unit was mainly used in the garage of the home.  On one occasion the unit was facing some shop rags and a rag was slightly burned.  It did not combust, but was smoking and appeared to be about to combust.

Calphalon Coffee Maker

12 cup coffee maker; Stainless steel finish; 12 cup glass carafe
incidentDescription:
Calphalon Coffee Maker - Mod:HE121cmg - Build Date: 37th week of 2012 (3712b)
This model of coffee maker has failed on us twice.  First unit just would not turn on after three months.  Retailer (Bed Bath & Beyond) replaced the unit.  Second unit operated for less than nine months. Second unit brewed coffee morning of 5/29/13 and we took our first cup into living room.  About ten minutes later we heard popping sounds from kitchen and upon investigating found coffee in carafe boiling the remaining coffee and smoke emitting from coffee maker unit.  Unplugged unit and took outside, perhaps none too soon as the unit was very hot and we speculate was ready to catch fire.  Called Calphalon and they are sending shipping tag to us to return unit for refund, as we clearly do not intend to consider another unit from them.
Calphalon representative mentioned that there have been known issues in both scenarios their staff has been aware of and are investigating and is why they want unit back.

productDescription: Gas grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
My Weber Spirit 310 grill caught on fire yesterday, 5/27/2013. It was not a grease fire. The fire was under the control knob area and the flames were coming out of the manifold area. I was able to carefully reach under, avoiding the flames and turn off the gas supply. The flames went out immediately when the gas was shut off. Fortunately, I saw the fire before it burned through the gas supply hose. The fire burned the control knobs, the ignition wiring and the gas supply hose from the gas fuel tank.

I contacted Weber and they asked me to send photos, which I have done. I can send those to you as well, if you need them. I am concerned that this is a safety issue that could result in a home fire, or possibly an explosion if other consumers experience the same issue.

productDescription: Kenmore Liquid Propane Gas Grill Model # 119.162310
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription: I was planning to grill on my Kenmore grill model #119.162310 yesterday afternoon. I opened the propane tank valve, lit all four burners and closed the lid before returning to the house. After 10 minutes I stepped outside to check the temperature on the grill to find it engulfed in flames. The flames were coming from both the firebox assembly and the cabinet assembly where the propane tank is located. Initially, I was afraid that the entire propane tank may catch fire, injuring myself and our property. Luckily, I keep a fire extinguisher nearby in the kitchen and was able to locate it and extinguish the fire. My concern is that this grill caught fire rapidly and had I not had the presence of mind and the access to an extinguisher, a similar incident could have easily resulted in serious injury to person and property. I would like other owners to be notified of this products defect and possibly have the grill recalled if it is a prevalent defect.

productDescription: Hand held rechargeable battery operated device.  The Prosonic Cleansing and Exfoliation System for Face & Body has a rotating brush to clean off dead skin and stimulate your skin.
incidentDescription: I was using the Prosonic Cleansing & Exfoliation System brush I had recently purchased.  I was holding it in my right hand and had it turned on for less than ten seconds and was using it on my neck when it exploded in my hand.  There was a loud bang, like a gun shot, I think.  I had shooting electric shock waves up my arm and a strong burning smell.  I could not hear for several seconds and one day later still have some ringing in my ears.  My neck was bright red and the palm of my hand, too.  My daughter ran upstairs and said it smelled like something burning.  WE have collected and saved all the pieces.  The device blew apart along its seams so no piece is actually broken.  WE have contacted the website and phone number of the manufacturer's representative who asked us to return the device but i am trying to find someone to look at it before I return it.  If I had been using it on my cheek or forehead I could have seriously damaged my eyes!

productDescription: Cuisinart coffee maker model DCC-1200, silver and black
model: DCC-1200 Brew Central 12-cup programmable coffee maker
incidentDescription: Our cuisinart coffee maker, model DCC 1200 serial number 00816h, that we purchased in September 2011 broke his morning. By broke, I mean it became a serious fire hazard! My wife and I brewed a full pot, 12 cups, this morning and after drinking approximately 5 cups the coffee began to boil and the pot began making loud cracking noises followed by smoke.  I immediately associated the smell of the smoke to burning electronics which I have experience dealing with due to my work in military aerospace.  I am scared that if we hadn't acted quickly to unplug the electrical power that a fire would have started and possibly caught our kitchen cabinets on fire.

productDescription: Breville BJE510XL Juice Fountain Multi-Speed 900 Watt Juicer
brand: Breville BJE510XL Juice Fountain Multi-Speed 900 Watt Juicer
model: Breville BJE510XL Juice Fountain Multi-Speed 900 Watt Juicer
incidentDescription:
I was using the brand new Breville BJE510XL Juice Fountain Multi-speed juicer. This was the first time that I had used it.  I read all the directions, unpacked, cleaned and assembled it before the first run. There were no left over packing parts. Everything was seated correctly and the safety arm was in place.
 
I was juicing ginger root which has about the same consistency as carrots so the machine was set on 5. Initially, I was not at all impressed with how much juice was coming from the juicer. I was using it 4-5 minutes when my wife said she smelled electrical burning. She was about 10 feet away in back of the juicer. At that time, the warning E did not appear on the LED screen. I stopped the juicer, refitted the parts. I did not smell any electrical burning smell anywhere around the juicer. I believed she smelled the ginger.  I started it up again, and within half to one minute, my wife said the juicer sounded as if it were straining. As I was looking down to the LED screen again to check, the plastic filter bowl exploded with an extremely loud noise, showering me on the chest and abdomen and about a third of the kitchen with plastic shards, wire mesh shards and ginger pulp. It was fortunate that the juicer was on a low counter so my eyes were not level with the filter bowl.
 
I sorted through the debris and collected as many pieces as I could find as well as spent 45 minutes cleaning walls, cabinets, and large appliances that were in the direct line of the explosion. I searched carefully through the pulp container and all of the dispersed pulp looking for any possible foreign body that might have been in the ginger but found no hard or metal objects other than the remnants of the micro mesh filter basket.
 
To say the least, under the wrong circumstances, the explosion could have blinded me or caused facial damage, not to mention that the sound scared the hell out of both of us. I have reported this to the Consumer Product Safety even though you said that this was a rare event, as I feel that your product could inflict serious injury on another customer.

I bought a BBQ grill from Lowes last year in April 2012. Every time I use the grill and pre-heat the grill it starting burning and starts a fire inside. I complaint last year to Ducane and they sent a tech person home in November last year to clean the grill and fix the problem. 
I used the grill again this year and have used it 2-3 times. When I heat the pre-heat the grill the after a few minutes there is fire in the grill. I called Ducane company and they said that they cannot do anything about it and are very arrogant in their stance. 
I informed them that I am very concerned that this is a major fire hazard issue but they are not listening. 
What are my options.
I can provide all videos that I have taken while the fire comes up.

Thanks,
[REDACTED]

productDescription: Weber Performer Gold 22-1/2" Charcoal Grill in Black
model: Performer Gold in Black, Model Number: 1431001
incidentDescription: I had recently purchased a Weber Performer Gold grill from Home Depot and was using it for the very first time.  I removed the lid and stored it on the storage bar on the lower half of the grill.  I removed the upper grate and poured charcoal ([REDACTED] [REDACTED] charcoal, which does not require liter fluid) into the grill.  I ignited the charcoal and it flamed upped and I walked away to allow the charcoal to burn down.  Shortly thereafter, I detected the order of burning plastic and turned toward the grill.  I noticed the charcoal was still flaming up, but I also noticed the two plastic standoffs on the lid storage bar were on fire.  I immediately closed the lid on the grill to smother the flame, however the standoffs were still burning, so I put them out with a glass of water.  I am reporting this because when I called Weber they only offered to send me two replacement plastic standoffs and said they would report it, however there was no genuine concern that this was a real issue and the representative said a couple times this has never happened before, coming across as though they thought I was not being truthful about what had occurred.

productDescription: Kirby Model G4 vacuum cleaner
incidentDescription:
I was vacuuming with my Kirby G4 vacuum when the power fluctuated a second later a heard sparks and the vacuum power cord caught on fire.  I turned the vacuum off, blew out the fire and ran to unplug it.  I came back to look for fires, and luckily non were discovered.  I looked at the cord and damage to the unit.  Where the cord was manufactured to hook onto the handle of the vacuum in a plastic swivel connection, the cord was burned in half with back powder coming out.  

I called Kirby and they offered no concern about the fire hazard in their power cords.  I was told that I could replace the cord for $31 from them or take it to the local distributor 30miles away.  I said that I was told that I have a lifetime warranty.   I was told that they offer lifetime rebuilding warranties.  They checked my record via SN, then said it would cost over $260 to rebuild it not including shipping to the southern states.  

I’m outraged, not just because of the inherent risk of the manufacturing of their vacuum cord, but for obvious disregard to safety with their G4 power cord specifically modified for hooking into a swivel that over the years causes the power cord to break or fray, spark and catch on fire.  Even if I purchased a replacement cord, it would only take so long for the same thing to happen again.  

Kirby needs to recall this power cord on all units sold and replace it with a proven safe power cord for free to its consumers.

productDescription: Hamilton Beach 6 Slice Capacity Toaster Oven. Model 31507, Series A1901DV
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
Hamilton Beach 6 Slice Capacity Toaster Oven. Model 31507R, Series A1901DV

Timer failed, such that timer continues past the "Off" position and continues until it stops at the "Stay On" position.  Oven then continues to operate indefinitely.  On testing for the problem, the timer consistently failed to stop at "Off", failed to sound the bell, and continued to "Stay On".  This failure is not obvious to the operator until the contents of the oven begin to burn.  This is a serious fire hazard as well as a burn hazard for anyone who, unaware the oven is still operating, touches the outside of the appliance.  Once the failure occurs, the oven cannot be turned off, except by unplugging the power cord.

Today it started shooting sparks out of the bottom where the cord is inserted into the dryer.  This is a fire hazard. The sparks made contact with my skin and I have stopped using the product because of this.

The last dryer I had lasted me over 5 years and the only reason I got rid of it was because I wanted to upgrade.  I am disappointed with this product and I don't think I will buy this brand or anything else manufactured by Helen of Troy again.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription:
Espresso Golden Baby Sorelle Verona Lifetime Convertible Crib

Dimensions: 61.5"L x 31.3"W x 50.7"H

http://www.toysrus.com/product/index.jsp?productId=11363879&gcsct=0ChMI8PiR87GYtwIVS0HmCh1JCAAAEAE

Manufacturer Date/Code  112011     37611JW
model: Golden baby Sorelle Verona Lifetime Convertible Crib
incidentDescription: At approximately 9:30 pm I checked on my 14-month-old son, who had been in his Sorelle Verona crib for two-and-a-half hours. He was sleeping on his back at an odd angle with his left leg dangling through the slats. His leg was pushed through past his knee and bent at a 90 degree angle. Not wanting him to injure himself by attempting to re-situate himself, I tried to lift his leg out for him. My son would not budge (please note that I did not pull very hard - didn't want to wake him). He woke up at this point and began screaming. After carefully trying to manipulate his knee and leg back through the slats for a few minutes, I cut off his pajama pants. At this point I found his knee was incredibly swollen from the pressure of the slats. I briefly tried icing it to bring down some swelling, but that did not help. He was still screaming in pain and frustration. While inspecting his knee, it appeared its bones and structure were a bit wider than the slats themselves. I'm not sure how he managed to get it through in the first place. At this point, there was no choice left other than to dismantle the crib. I used a hand saw to remove one of the offending slats to free my son. He limped at first, but after a few minutes that was gone. The swelling was almost gone the next morning and completely gone by the afternoon. Aside from bruising on both sides of his knee, there does not appear to be any permanent damage. Fortunately I discovered his leg was stuck before he woke up the next morning, energetic and ready to go, and decided to extricate himself. There is no telling what kind of damage he could have done to his knee, leg, and even his back if he had been left to his own devices.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription: Crock-Pot Slow Cooker
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription:
My wife received a burn while attempting to remove the lid. The burn was a result of touching the side of the cooker.

The Sunbeam d.b.a. Jardens Consumer Solutions would place a visible warning on the outside of the box warning consumers of the potential of receiving a burn while using this device.
victimSeverity: Injury, Level of care not known

productDescription: Krups Coffee Maker Model KM405, Part Number KM405550/5CA. programmable 12 cup coffee maker with auto program features such as strength of coffee, time to heat after making coffee etc. Purchased as birthday gift for wife in Sept 2013.
incidentDescription:
On 14 May 2013 my wife made her daily pot of coffee using her Krups KM405 coffee maker (KM405550/5CA). It was a birthday gift for her purchased in Sept 2012. She made coffee about 11 AM. At about 12:30 PM she left house to go shopping. The coffee maker has auto shut off after 1 hour (Programmable 1, 2, or 3 hours). The carafe had about 1/3 pot of coffee left in it.
I was working in yard and came back in house about 1:15 PM. Nothing appeared out of ordinary. I left house to go to store about 1:30PM. Upon returning I was in house and nothing appeared out of ordinary. I went out and was working in front of garage. At about 2:15 PM I heard a strange sound and went to investigate. As I walked on porch I realized it was our house alarm, fire alarm going off. As I entered kitchen flames were coming out of coffee maker and going up front of cabinets and to ceiling. I grabbed the kitchen fire extinguisher and put out fire. Heavy black smoke was throughout downstairs.
The damage was: 1) large burned spot on cabinet top, 2) soot over cabinet fronts and bottom, 3) soot on ceiling and 4) large hunks of melted plastic all over the counter tops. l started to clean up mess. I was able to get most of soot from cabinets and walls as well as the small splatters of melted plastic from walls and cabinets. The ceiling (white) is too covered so I will have to paint it. The burned spot on counter top will require new counter tops.
I touched coffee maker after fire was out to take it out of house and burned tips of two fingers.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription: Green, Hoover Windtunnel T Series upright vacuum with rewind cord.
incidentDescription: My son (17 year old) was vacuuming this afternoon when the unit started to "smell like fire". He unplugged it and it burned his hand. I called Hoover and they said this unit was NOT recalled but many of the same model are with the same issue. This model needs to be added to that list immediately!
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription: Cuisinart Food Processor UPC 86279-04924-7

After the incident I also washed and dried the disk and found that it was necessary to concentrate so as to not cut your fingers where you naturally hold it on the bottom.

I plan to return the appliance to the store.

flames and the proof is that there is soot all over my apartment. I will need to clean the walls, perhaps repaint, and
empty the cabinets. We put the fire out with salt and then a wet cloth. I'm just grateful I got to it on time before it
spread.

It just broke apart and the blades detached from the fan when operating.  The consumer turned it on and the blades just fell out.  The consumer says she was not injured but she could have been.

productDescription: Shark "Professional" steam mop
incidentDescription: We have a Shark brand steam mop ("Professional" model) purchased at Costco in Santee, CA.  After just 3-5 minutes of normal use (cleaning small kitchen floor), the plug on the mop is extremely hot to the touch. Tonight (5.13.13) it burned the finger of my 9-year-old son when he was unplugging the mop from the wall outlet.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription: Oil filled electric heater, model #HZ709
incidentDescription:
I bought a Honeywell heater, model #HZ709 last year, using it for several months as an auxiliary heater to my furnace.  I have used it this winter except for the last month.  I turned it on tonight and noticed that it was getting very hot, not stopping at the temp I set it on.  I unplugged it and noticed that there was black around my electrical outlet.  I then examined the plug to the heater and found that it was slightly melted.  

I then did a search to see if there was a recall and found a lot of complaints that have been made on this same problem.  Thankfully, most of the people caught it before this product caused a fire.  I know that Honeywell has been notified over several years of this same problem, but they are still selling the product.  This product will end up causing a fire and possible loss of life and needs to be recalled.

productDescription: canister vacuum cleaner
incidentDescription: On several occasions the vacuum cleaner started by itself - once during the day , and twice in the middle of the night. The cord was plugged into the wall plug. In all instances there were people home to unplug the vacuum cleaner.

productDescription: Char-Broil Gas Patio Bristo, model #12601558
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
My concerns are in regard to the Char-Broil Gas Patio Bistro, model #12601558. 

I would categorize two safety concerns with this bbq. The first is the cooking grill. It is a stainless steel accordian/fan type design with small perforated holes. While it's not completely solid it is enough that it traps propane underneath it if the flame goes out and the knob on the bbq is still on. You also can't see enough through the grill to see if the flame/element is lit which is also tricky when trying to ensure that it's lit or not. 
The second concern is the design of the controls on the knob. To turn off the gas flow into the bbq with its knob, you have to go by the ignition setting. So what has happened to me on 3 different occasions is that I'm pre-heating the grill, I go out and see/feel that it's not heating, so I turn the knob off, and it just hits the ignitor enough to explode the trapped propane. While I've been fortunate not to have been burned, I have lost some facial and forearm hair. When this happens it also projects the cooking grill from the bbq.

productDescription: Ryobi One+ Charge Station
incidentDescription: One World Technologies Inc and CPSC issued a recall for Ryobi 1+ charge centers. It limited the recall to model P108 number 130429028. The recall should be expanded based on my experience with model P113 number 140501013. Description follows:  My Ryobi battery charger began smoldering as I awaited a battery to recharge so I could finish weedwhacking my property. At first I smelled what resembled ammonia or urine as in when my dog had had an accident and lifted his leg to mark territory. Then I realized the odor that was by then burning my throat and causing a headache was more like that of a corroded battery compartment in a small unit like a flashlight. I approached my sitting room window seat where the charger was plugged in. The unit was smoking copiously and the odor very intense. I knew it was smoldering to catch fire but was more afraid it would explode. I am a 65-plus female homeowner living alone and cannot afford to be incapacitated. So despite my fear of explosion I opened a nearby window, unplugged the unit and gingerly tossed the hot object out the window onto the grass below. Several hours later, still fearing it might burst, I approached for a closer look. It was cooled off but I was unable to release the battery. It had fused to its compatible Ryobi charging unit. My local mechanic pried it apart and verified that the battery and charger were compatible based on the information printed on each. Home Depot would not hear of any compensation or replacement without a receipt which I did not have. They made no mention of problems or warnings regarding their Ryobi specialized product. I searched the internet to reveal the recall information. I will be writing to both Home Depot Corporate and to the listed distributor, One World Technologies of this Chinese-manufactured product to document my incident and to notify them of this e-mail to you, the CPSC. My photographic documentation is entitled THE RYOBI FIRE STARTER. I would attach a copy of the graphic representation here but there seems to be no mechanism for doing so. The melted and disfigured components are quite obvious.

productDescription: Portable electric heater. Manufactured by Patton. It is a PattonPUH680 1500W heater at 60 Hz. Gray in color. 120V AC
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription:
Two years ago I purchased a portable heater made by Patton. The heater was purchased at walmart. It is a: Patton, PUH680, 60Hz,1500W heater. The heater received light to moderate use during the cold months as a supplemental room heater.

I turned on the heater on the lower setting and left the room. Upon returning about ten minutes later I smelled a very bad fishy type smell (burning wires) and a smoky smell as well. I immediacy turned the heater off and threw it outside.

The next day I took the heater rear cover off to see what had happened and I discovered that one of the lead ins to one of the heating coils had burned through the protective wiring cover and was shorting out. This heater was adult owned and used, it was never abused in any way. To have the wire burn through was a cause of serious concern for me. There were no electrical storms nor service interruption in any way.

No room damage nor structure fire occurred because I was nearby. However a structure fire may have developed if this was not noticed in time.

productDescription: coffee maker 14 cup
incidentDescription:
Incident Description: On January 7, 2013, I purchased a brand new Kitchen Aid Empire Red 14 cup
coffee pot (Model #KCM1402ERO) (Serial #WE23207957) from Target. The very first time I used the
new coffee pot, it malfunctioned. This coffee pot has a spring loaded basket where you place the coffee
grounds. I was standing at the kitchen counter making toast, which was right next to the coffee pot,
when all of a sudden, the basket door of the coffee pot flew open. It was filled with hot water and hot
coffee grounds, which splashed onto my left wrist/hand area and down the left front of my shirt,
burning me with scalding hot liquid and hot coffee grounds from the basket. Hot coffee grounds and
hot coffee splashed on me and all over the kitchen counter and down the fronts of the cabinets. I
immediately put ice on my burns, (my left wrist/hand area and a quarter size area on my stomach).
After cleaning up a huge mess in the kitchen due to this incident, I made a second pot of coffee,
thinking that maybe I didn't close the basket door properly the first time. Not more than 2 to 3 minutes
into the 2"d attempt to brew a pot of coffee, the exact same malfunction happened again. Once again, I
had a big mess to clean up. I called Kitchen Aid and reported the incident. They gave me a report #
(SR# [REDACTED]) I talked to "[REDACTED]". She told me that they did not have any other complaints
or reports on that model coffee pot, therefore she suggested that I return to them that coffee pot and
they would send me a new one. I was reluctant at frrst, but she assured me that I was the only one that
had a problem, thus far.
They frrst had to send me a FedX shipping label so that I could return the non-working coffee pot to
them, and once I did that, they sent me a new one. This was a 6 week timeframe.
I received the new coffee pot, exact same model (KCM 1402ERO) and the new Serial # is
WE24141881. The very frrst pot of coffee that was made with the new pot, the exact same
malfunction happened. Five minutes into the brewing time, the basket door flew open with hot coffee
grounds and hot coffee splashing everywhere. On March 27, 2013 I contacted Kitchen Aid once again
and this time I requested a refund. Kitchen Aid wanted to send me a THIRD coffee pot. I refused. I
talked to "[REDACTED]" and he told me that I had to give them my original receipt from Target in order to get a
full refund. I did not have the receipt to give them so after a lengthy argument, Kitchen Aid agreed to a
full refund. Once again, I will receive a F edX shipping label to return the coffee pot to Kitchen Aid
and once they receive it, they will process my refund. I strongly suggested to Kitchen Aid that they
recall this coffee pot before it harms another consumer. They continue to suggest that they have not
had any other complaints on this Model. I do not believe that and I am convinced that there is a design
flaw with the basket door. I had 2 brand new models and they both malfunctioned. Once the basket
fills with hot water, the weight of the coffee grounds and hot water causes the basket door to slip below
the latching mechanism thus releasing the basket door allowing it to open, filled with hot liquid and hot
coffee grounds that splash out during the force of the door being released. The spring on this basket
door is a heavy duty spring. I was a Target yesterday and this Kitchen Aid Model Coffee Pot remains
on their shelves. I have included copies of my correspondence from Kitchen Aid and also pictures of
the coffee pot. I sincerely hope that the Consumer Product Safety Commission takes whatever action
necessary to force Kitchen Aid to recall this dangerous product. Please note ... the scald burns that I
received from this incident was bad enough that the area on my left wrist/hand peeled, and I still have a
quarter size scar on my stomach. I medicated myself and did not seek outside medical treatment. I was
lucky that the burns where not more serious. I told the personnel that I spoke with at Kitchen Aid that
the next consumer that gets burned by this design flawed coffee pot might not be so accommodating.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: Single making blender, comes with 4 individual cups, 2 blade heads, and an extra rubber gasket.
incidentDescription:
I purchased the GE single serve blender at Walmart's for 19.99. It comes with 2 sets of blade covers (one laying on top of the other to form a +) and they each have rubber gaskets in them to prevent leaking when it's turned on. It also comes with a second gasket in a little plastic bag.  
1...While blending, the blades separated and the rubber gasket came loose and got chopped up by the blades. I thought the unit was just a bad one, and threw it out.  
2...Because it was the size unit I wanted, I decided to give it another try and bought another one. After a couple of weeks, I thought this new blender was ok but one day, after blending another drink, pouring it into a glass and drinking a few sips, I noticed the gasket was wrapped around the blades again and torn apart. After fitting the gasket pieces back together again, I was missing one tiny piece so I know I drank the piece of rubber!!! 
3... To see if it would happen again, I put in the new gasket and every day blended just plain water (without drinking it)...and about a week later, it happened again. THE GASKET WAS WRAPPED AROUND THE BLENDER AND TORN INTO PIECES!   
I honestly feel this could present a MAJOR CHOKING HEALTH HAZARD...IF NOT DEATH...if you were not aware this could happen and just mixed the drink and drank it right away.
This product should definitely be taken off the market.  It's a great idea but also a great health hazard!

productDescription: WAHL Groom Pro Head & Total Body Grooming Kit (it includes a hair clipper, trimmer, multiple attachments, and a carrying case).  I believe the product is located here:  http://www.wahlhomeproducts.com/Products/HairClippers/ClipperTrimmerCombo/79520-3101.  The large hair clipper is what caught fire (not the smaller trimmer).  The incident also involves the WAHL "Total Care" all in one cleaner, lubricant, & coolant spray designed to clean the hair clipper.  The clipper caught fire after being sprayed with the cleaning spray.  There is a link to a similar cleaning spray on their website (http://www.wahlhomeproducts.com/Products/HairClippers/ClipperAccessories/3772), but I can't find the same one with the same label as what I bought from Walmart.
model: Wahl® Groom Pro™ Head & Total Body Grooming Kit
incidentDescription:
I purchased a WAHL Groom Pro Head & Total Body Grooming Kit (it includes a hair clipper, trimmer, multiple attachments, and a carrying case) at Walmart located at 1220 Old Country Rd, Westbury, NY 11590.  I also purchased from the same store the WAHL Total Care cleaning spray which is designed to clean the hair clipper.  I purchased both products approximately one year ago.  

In the early morning hours of April 5, 2013, at approximately 1:40 AM, I was sitting in my bedroom in my house cleaning the WAHL hair clipper.  I had just used it minutes before to trim my chest hair.  I was cleaning the hair clipper using the WAHL “Total Care” all in one cleaner, lubricant, & coolant spray.  I purchased the WAHL cleaning spray because I had assumed that the spray made by WAHL would be the best product to use to clean the WAHL hair clipper.  

I followed the instructions on the spray can exactly.  The WAHL Total Care spray can states, “Turn unit off and brush hair from blades.  Next, holding the unit in a downward position and with the unit running, liberally apply solution to blades to completely flush out all foreign matter.  Allow Wahl Total care to remain on the blades for 2 minutes.  Turn unit off and wipe clean.  Unit is ready for use.”  I brushed hair from the blades while it was off.  I turned the clipper on, held it in a downward position while still running, and I began to liberally apply the solution to the blades.  At that exact moment, the head and blades of the hair clipper caught on fire.  

I attempted to blow out the fire, and it would not blow out.  I had been cleaning the hair clipper over my garbage can.  After I realized I could not blow the fire out, I dropped the flaming hair clipper into my garbage can to avoid being burned while in a state of panic.  I had no safer place available to drop the flaming hair clipper.  The only alternative place to drop it would have been my bedroom floor, and this might have caused my entire house to catch fire.  After dropping the flaming hair clipper into my garbage, the contents of my garbage caught on fire, and in a moment a very large fire was inside my garbage bin.  My garbage bin is a large approximately 13 gallon plastic garbage bin I previously purchased from Target.  I began to shout “Fire” and my mother and brother came running to my room with fire extinguishers.  They used the fire extinguishers to put out the fire in my garbage.  The garbage was still smoking after the fire was extinguished, so I then poured water inside the garbage.  Fortunately, the fire went out.  I placed the smokey garbage bin and clipper outside my house, because I was afraid it would reignite.    

As a result of the fire, my entire bedroom, and the second and third floors of my house were filled with smoke.  We opened all the windows and waited for the smoke to dissipate while choking on smoke in the air.  When the smoke finally dissipated, I saw that my entire room was covered in a layer of smoke dust/residue.  I have numerous electronics in my bedroom (television, desktop computer, laptop, printer, speakers, cable box, DVR, blu-ray player) and I do not yet know what effect this residue will have on my electronics.  Furthermore, I believe it is likely my room will need to be professionally cleaned.  I also do not know whether I will need medical treatment, as I unavoidably and inadvertently breathed in a large amount of smoke during the fire.  I do not yet know the full extent of the damage of this fire.

When the unit was new, letting go of the throttle caused the motor to disengage, allowing the scooter to slow down and even coast to a stop.  (Pressing the brake lever also disengages the motor.)

The throttle is now sticking.  That is, simply letting go the throttle does not cause the motor to disengage.  The rider must now press the brake lever to disengage the motor.

The E100 scooter is designed for kids (weight limit 120 pounds).  This problem with the throttle first occurred when my 11 year old grandson was riding the scooter.

The unit is just over a year and has had very little use.  There are no visible signs of damage, and as far as I know, the unit has never been wrecked or misused.

I called Razor and they are going to send an "electrical repair kit."  However, I'm not sure that I will trust the unit even after the kit is installed.

At approximately 10:30 AM on the morning of March 30, 2013, I walked into the kitchen and found smoke coming up from my Cuisinart coffee maker.  I immediately unplugged the machine, but smoke continued to waft upward from the bottom of the machine.  I moved the coffee maker into the sink and submerged it in water, and after a few minutes, the electric fire was finally doused.  

At 11:00 AM, I called the Cuisinart customer service number and reported the fire.  [REDACTED] answered the call and apologized for the situation; he asked for the model number and serial number, and then apologized again because he said that there was nothing that could be done.  [REDACTED] explained that because the serial number indicated that the coffee maker was one year outside of the warranty period that there was nothing that he could do because it was “too far outside” the warranty period.

productDescription: Counter-top oven
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
I had quite a scare this morning.

I put a piece of bread in my KitchenAid Countertop oven, set the position switch to “toast”, and set the timer for 6 minutes.  When the timer is up, the machine “dings” and turns itself off.  There is nothing abnormal here.

This time, the appliance did not “ding”, and did not turn off.  And I forgot about the toast.  After maybe 15 minutes, I smelled something burning, and found heavy smoke pouring out of the countertop oven.  I noticed the timer was still set at 6 minutes, and the oven was still on and really hot.

I turned the appliance off, and left the door closed.  I did not want to introduce oxygen to the mix.  But the smoke was extensive and continued to pour out, and I knew I had to get the toast out or my house would smell for months.  I opened the window, grabbed a hot pad, opened the oven door, grabbed the toast, and flung the really burnt toast out the window.  There were no flames, but I suspect ignition could not have been more than moments away.

After the oven cooled, I cleaned it up, and examined the timer switch.  The timer is a mechanical spring-wound clock-like device that ticks as it counts down.  It operates without electricity.   When the timer times out, it opens a set of electrical contacts to shut off the power to the heating elements.   

I rest the timer numerous times.  Ninety percent of the time, the timer would ”tick” and  run down normally, but twice, when setting the timer at 6 minutes, the timer would not start ticking.  It would just stay at 6 minutes, with both top and bottom elements on.  The oven would have stayed on indefinitely.  I have not found a one-line diagram or traced the internal circuitry, but I expect the thermostat is only in the circuit when the oven is used for baking, not when used for toasting.  For toasting, all elements are on full power continuously.  

I reviewed the owners’ manual, and found it suggests for times less than 5 minutes, moving the timer switch to greater than 10 minutes, and then turning it back to the time desired.  But my problem was at 6 minutes.

The oven is Model KCO1005ER.  The serial number (WGT2610420) dates the appliance to 2006.  No recalls were found.

I see this as a definite fire hazard.  I welcome your comments, questions, or suggestions.

[REDACTED]

productDescription:

The model  number is CSB-76 and the Serial # is 20921C
incidentDescription:
I was cleaning out the base of the smart stick with my left hand and held the top portion of the stick with my right which turned the blender on while my finger was in the blade. I immediately went to the Emergency Room where I was told they were not sure there was enough to my finger let to put back together. They were able to place 13 sutures and I sustained an open fracture. I have had multiple ER, MD and physical therapy appointments. I now have vascular (venous) congestion where my finger turns blue if it is not in the upright position. I was told it will be up to a year to determine if I will regain feeling as there was also a severe crush injury (nerve injury). 
If I was able to sustain this injury, imagine if a child got a hold of a smart stick while someone was not looking. 
I notified Cuisinart who sent me a letter stating in the manual it states you should unplug the device.

productDescription: portable electric heater
incidentDescription:
The consumer stated that she started feeling bad after she purchased the first heater. She first used the heater in November 2012. She set it up in the kitchen near the window and the exhaust over the oven, where she would have some ventilation.  The consumer was using 3 of these heaters in her home at the time and all of them were identical.  The consumer stated that there was a chemical burnt plastic odor coming from all of the heaters. The heaters were in different areas of the house.

The week before Thanksgiving she got a sore throat, congestion in her lungs, sinus congestion and burning eyes.  She went to the doctor on 11/16/2012, and saw  [REDACTED] in West Monroe LA.  She was diagnosed with a sinus infection and bronchitis.  She stated that she got an injection of [REDACTED] and was put on an antihistimine and antibiotic.  

The consumer stated that symptoms got really intense after she purchased and started using the second two heaters (1/3/2013). She went back to the doctor on 1/8/2013. The congestion was worse and the coughing was worse. She was given a prescription for [REDACTED], a cough suppressant.  She was put on allergy medicine and an antibiotic.  She had burning, watery eyes.

The consumer stated that three other people in the family were congested. Her brother went to see [REDACTED] on 1/23/2013. He was diagnosed with bronchitis and sinus congestion. 
The consumer stated that the others were affected after they had a cold spell last week.

The consumer stated that she had to go to the emergency room on 1/12/2013. She was taking her medicine on schedule from Tuesday to Saturday, but she felt like she was not taking them at all.  
She was treated at St. Francis Medical Center, Monroe, LA. by [REDACTED]. She was put on an inhaler and [REDACTED] and [REDACTED].  

The consumer stated that at that point she still had not connected her health symptoms to the heaters.

On about 01/21/2013, she suspected that there was a connection with the heaters.  The consumer stopped using all of the heaters and boxed them up and placed them in plastic bags.  The adverse health symptoms began to improve for everyone in the home shortly afterwards.

The consumer stated that she never had a reaction like this before. She stated that [REDACTED] even asked her if she had been around chemicals and she told him no.  She stated that she has an allergy, but it was nothing major.  

On 1/29/13, she saw a doctor about sinus congestion, persistent cough, though her lungs were better.  Told him about the heaters; was asked if they had been removed from use.  Prescribed another antibiotic, continued antihistimine and congestion medicine.

As of 2/28/12 everything seemed better.  Occassional hard cough.  Would still like to know what odor was from and how dangerous it really is.

productDescription: 8 qt. Pressure Cooker
incidentDescription:
Caller's dad purchased an 8qt pressure cooker and presented it to her July/August 2012 and although she has only used it a couple of times she has had no problems with it until March 1st, 2013 when she was cooking beans in it with plenty of water and her child was sitting about 2 feet away playing with magnets on the fridge.

After cooking approximately 30 minutes with the units temperature set to medium, the caller heard a sound like pressure and spewing liquid and she turned around to see steam and water spewing and billowing all over the kitchen.  Initial sound was a loud pressurized release.  

The steam filled the room during the 5 to 10 second spewing the water out of the pressure cooker. steam was very thick fog. Almost looked like smoke, but wasn't.

Once it stopped spewing the water out, she then grabbed a kitchen towel to reach over and turn the pressure cooker off.

After it cooled a bit she began trying to open the cooker, she had a lot of trouble opening but after 20 or 30 seconds she got it opened and found that there was almost no liquid left in the cooker. It was pressure sealed shut even though all steam had left.

Caller has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.

There were no injuries.

productDescription: Hunter Litex Fans 52" ceiling fan model # E-BDB52MWW5BC4. White finish with 5 fan blades and 4 socket light kit.
incidentDescription:
Product is a Hunter Litex Fans 52" ceiling fan model # E-BDB52MWW5BC4. I purchased this product on 8/20/2009 from Lowes. I installed the fan with the included 4-socket light kit in our daughter's bedroom soon after purchase. The unit has been in typical residential use since then.

About 3 days ago we smelled an odor that seemed electrical in origin. We localized the odor to this ceiling fan. Only the light was in use at the time. The fan motor has not been used for quite some time. We observed that turning off the light reduced the odor somewhat. Today I removed the light kit and discovered an internal component that apparently got hot enough to melt the plastic housing. This is the likely source of the odor.

At the time of failure only 3 of the 4 light sockets contained a light bulb. Each bulb is 40W incandescent type bulb with candelabra base (within the load limits specified per product labeling). 

There are obvious concerns here of a RISK OF FIRE involving this product.

I have documented the incidents with photographs and I still have the faulty product.

productDescription: Natural gas grill.
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription: I own a Weber 310 natural gas grill. Several times when I put the Weber grill cover back on the unit, it bumps the burner knobs and turns the gas on. This has happened three times since owning the grill. This last time it was on for over 24 hours. It's winter and I just happened to go out back where the grill is and got a strong odor of gas. I called Weber and they said it is not a manufacturing defect. While it not be a defect, it certainly is a safety problem. The knobs turn very easy. There is no locked position. My past grill, it was required to push down to unlock and then turn. These just turn and once the cover is on there is no way to tell if the burners are on. Weber says to turn off my natural gas supply to the grill when it's not in use. While this is the fix to stay safe, it is not practical.

productDescription:

Purchased at Sams Club, Dale City, VA.
incidentDescription:
I purchased a new Hamilton Beach Coffee Maker Model 43254R, Series A4011DT from Sams Club in Dale City, Virginia a few months ago.

I made coffee in the morning.  I always make enough for two days of coffee and just microwave the remaining or make iced coffee with it later.  I left in the morning for the day.  I came home late at night and it was only because my child wanted a dinner at 9:30 p.m. that I was even in the kitchen.  After making dinner I kept hearing the pop of a heating element.  I searched everywhere - no heating element indicator lights on anywhere in kitchen.  I gave up, shut off all lights and started to go upstairs for the night, heard the heating element sound again.  So I started touching things - and this coffee maker, all lights off, was on and HOT!  It had evaporated my half pot of coffee during the day and all that was left was a welded black hardened mess at bottom.

I have unplugged it, but this is new, and shouldn't be happening.  The auto-off feature has ALWAYS worked.  I almost never turn it off manually.  There is no auto-off override.

productDescription: Ceiling mounted heat/vent/light.  Self contained.
incidentDescription:
On Sunday, March 10th, 2013, I was awakened by my wife telling me that there was a fire in the house.  She led me to the bathroom where a NuTone ceiling mounted heat/vent/light unit is installed.  Looking into the interior of the unit through the grill/cover, I observed fire within the unit.  Burning material was dripping out of the unit.  The combustion was audible as a crackling sound.  While I turned the wall heat and light switch off, my wife retrieved a fire extinguisher.  A quick burst of retardant from the extinguisher extinguished the flames within the unit.  While conducting this exercise, some of the melted, dripping material resulted in burns to my hand.  This same material also adhered to the bathroom floor.

Once the fire was extinguished, I removed the unit cover.  The assembly's "B" unit, the heater component, seems to be the cause of the fire.  The electrical wiring and plastic enclosure were charred and melted.  The adjacent fan module showed partial melting.

Since my wife was in the room when the fire started, our response was rapid and the resulting damage minimal.  If the fire had started while the room was unoccupied, I believe the results could have been much worse
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription:
'Electri-heat' in-wall heater, model # CFW2-15, 240 VAC, 60 Hz, 1500 W.
TPI Corporation
Johnson City, TN 37601
productType: Heaters or Heating Systems, Other or Not Specified (393)
incidentDescription:
'Electri-heat', model CFW2-15, 240 VAC, 60 Hz, 1500 W, in-wall heater caught fire and began to burn the wall. The
circuit breaker for the in-wall heater did not trip. The coils glowed red hot and flames began to appear from within
the wall.
Upon manually de-energizing the electrical circuit at the breaker, the fire stopped and the unit was removed. The
metal frame of the heater appeared to have been exposed to enough electrical energy and heat to appear melted.
The plumber was working on a on a shower installation kit in the same condo, on the opposite side of the wall as
the in-wall unit. The plumber insists that the wiring inside the wall was not compromised. He also insists that the
heater unit was not deliberately turned on at the time of the fire.
The in-wall heater is old enough to be part of the original 1970's era construction. The in-wall heater appears to be
connected to a 120 VAC circuit although it is labeled for 240 VAC.

productDescription: Crock Pot brand Smart Pot
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription:
I have a stainless steel crock pot brand smart pot. I bumped the pot with my hand while using it and now have a 2nd degree burn on my hand which is about 1 inch long by 1/2 inch wide. This burn became infected and I have had to be on antibiotics. Additionally, when it does finally heal, I will have a good size scar on my hand.

My concern is that I had no idea that the outside of the crock pot was so hot during use. There are no safety warnings on the pot itself. If I received this type of burn, I can only imagine what would happen if a child touched the pot while in use.

No counter top cooking device should become so hot on the exterior that it can cause this type of injury or certainly should have a large warning on the outside about the potential danger if touched during use.

productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
Dear US CPSC,

I'd like to report a problem with a Black and Decker toaster/convection oven that I believe is a hazard.  This is in reference to Model #CT04400B Type 1.  This toaster oven has a unique issue with its on/off button.  If you turn the dial ever so slightly past the off setting, the toaster oven remains on, and I believe that this is a significant fire hazard.  We found that frequently, the toaster oven would remain on for very long periods of time and get very, very hot.  It was very easy to mistaken leave the oven in the on setting, when you meant to tum it off.  I have enclosed a couple of pictures of what I mean.

I wanted to let your organization know about this dangerous appliance.

Sensio, Inc.
Item: 18014
incidentDescription:
Food Network Slow Cooker
Sensio Inc. 
Model: YDE-1006
ITEM: 18014

I've had the slow cooker for approx. 2 yrs.  

I noticed that the slow cooker had not heated the food after 4+ hours.  I checked on it several times throughout the day & the display was working normally.  My husband, who has some experience with electrical work, took the slow cooker apart & discovered that in two places the insulation appeared to be burned through & the wires were charred. The wire insulation is brittle & falling to pieces along the length of the wire. What was left of the wire was black & very brittle.  We are very glad we found this b/c it stopped working as opposed to someone being shocked b/c of the short. We are keeping the slow cooker for a while and would be happy to send pictures.

I bought it new & since I've had it I don't believe it has had any abnormal use (used dry, on too long, etc.).

The consumer stated when the vacuum exploded it emitted a strong gas odor. One of the accessory parts popped off of the vacuum and hit the consumer in the right eye.

productDescription: DeWalt 18 volt XRP NiCad battery pack model DC9096, DeWalt model DW9116 battery charger
incidentDescription: I was charging a Dewalt DC9096 18 volt battery in a Dewalt DW9116 charger.  When I entered my workroom about 2 hours after the battery was placed in the charger, I could smell an acrid smoke in the room.  I went over to my workbench, and the smell was very strong.  I attempted to remove the battery from the charger, but it was so hot that I couldn't hold on to it.  I unplugged it, grabbed a pair of gloves, and put the battery/charger outside to cool.  I brought it back in to the house after an hour, and was able to remove the battery from the charger.  Both the battery and chargers plastic cases has started to melt, neither is usable.  The date code on the battery is 200725.  I suspect that if the battery had been charging much longer that it would have started a fire.  I had used the battery in a DeWalt 18 volt cordless drill earlier in the day without incident.  I contacted DeWalt customer service through their web site, and their e-mail reply indicated no concern about this serious safety issue.

productDescription: Crane Warm Mist One Gallon White Humidifier, Model EE-5200W
incidentDescription:
We smelled a toxic electrical burning smell which was coming from our 1.5 year old daughter's bedroom.  It turns out that the plastic on the bottom of the humidifier had melted and oozed out onto the hardwood floor.  The inside of the humidifier is black and charred from an electrical issue.  I have attached a few pictures of the bottom of the humidifier.  

I feel very fortunate that no one was injured in this incident.  I do feel strongly that this and similar products that are manufactured/sold by Crane need to be investigated and recalled so that no one is harmed or possibly killed by these products.  

In looking into this issue a bit further I have found that our incident is not the only one of its kind.  I see that there are at least 10 customer reviews since December 2011 on Amazon.com, where our humidifier was purchased, that indicate similar issues of melting/smoking/fire.

productDescription: Gevalia Kaffee-branded [REDACTED] single use coffee pods for use with Keurig coffee makers.
incidentDescription:
Gevalia manufactures "[REDACTED]" single-serve coffee pods for use with Keurig-style coffee makers.
These pods are a thin plastic container having a sealed foil lid on the upper surface. Inside is a
porous filter that is connected to the upper, inner surface of the plastic container. There is an air
gap between the lower end of the porous filter and the bottom of the plastic container. A single
use portion of ground coffee is placed in the filter, and the foil lid is sealed.

In use I placed the [single serve coffee pod] in my [REDACTED] coffee maker as directed. This coffee maker has a top
puncture to pierce the foil lid and allow hot water (192 F) to enter the container and brew the
coffee in the container. The coffee maker has a lower puncture to pierce the bottom of the
container to allow the brewed coffee to flow into a mug/cup.

On the 17th of February, while using a Gevalia-branded [single cup coffee pod] the coffee stopped flowing after
approximately 4/5 of a typical brew. I opened the [REDACTED] coffee maker (as designed) to remove
the [single cup coffee pod] and throw it away. Upon opening the coffee maker hot water immediately splashed on
me and about the area of the coffee maker.

I inspected the [single cup coffee pod] by removing the foil liner and disposing of the used coffee grounds. I
noticed that the inner filter had been pierced by the lower puncture. This allowed for coffee
grounds to fill and clog the lower puncture so that coffee could no longer be dispensed. The
undispensed hot water was essentially a pressurized water source that was released when I
opened the [REDACTED] machine. Had I not been wearing a long-sleeve shirt and glasses I might have
been burned/injured by the hot water/coffee that splashed.

I have used many different [single cup coffee pods] "flavors", and they have typically been [REDACTED]
-branded. These [single cup coffee pods] have never had their inner liners pierced by the lower puncture.
It appears that the pressurized hot water, the weight of the brewing coffee grounds, the the
flexibility of the inner filter allowing for the filter to "stretch" while the brewing process was
occurring thus allowing the lower puncture to pierce the filter.

As of right now I still have the defective [single cup coffee pod] and the remaining, unused [single pod coffee pods].

productDescription: Single cup coffee brewer
incidentDescription:
My Keurig B70 brewer stopped pumping water for the brew cycle.  I called Keurig customer support and the representative walked me through several trouble shooting tasks.  The unit still failed to function and the representative said that it was not repairable.  She offered me a replacement brewer at a reduced cost as the warranty had expired on mine a few months earlier.  I accepted the offer and was instructed to return only the K-cup holder and then dispose of the old brewer.

Prior to disposing of the old brewer I took it apart out of curiosity.  I found what appeared to be two electrically actuated water valves at the top of the brewer.  Both valves had stains and corrosion consistent with long-term water leakage at the lower seals.  The valves had been leaking directly above a transformer which was also water stained.

Below the transformer was a pump which was stained and corroded, and appeared to be the component that had failed.

I own two brewers identical to the one that failed, and I am concerned that there may be a safety issue if they also contain leaky valves.

Carafe extremely hot, and machine would not turn off without unplugging. Spoke with HB - replacement to be sent under warranty for cost of shipping.

12/20/12 - received replacement. Within 1 month, noticed auto shut-off feature not working - light shuts off, but hot plate remains on and won't shut off without unplugging. After this, kept unplugged, though we bought this product for the timer feature and it would need it to be plugged in to use this. Took out filter basket to clean (did not touch the front of the machine) and the machine immediately got very hot and began steaming (must have had water remaining in the system). Coffee maker was not turned on. I hurried to fill the water and place filter and coffee while steam coming out. Made entire pot of coffee without ever turning on the machine. Emailed HB again, with product info (43254R, A4221D). 

Seems to be a hazard to have a coffee maker that comes on and gets very hot when not in use. Now, looking at reviews online, I'm not the only one this has happened to.
