This causes an unsafe condition as it allows the burners to pull out of the connections in the front of the grill wherein the gas enters the burners.
Have had to stop using because the burners have pulled out and allowed fire with going into the burners

productDescription:
Product Details for attachment that turned on blender without safety guard:
http://www.tribestlife.com/productcart/pc/Mason-Jar-Attachment-BPA-FREE-3p624.htm#.USRPCqU3u8A

Use the Mason Jar Attachment to blend and grind your recipes in glass mason jars. 
The Tribest Personal Blender Mason Jar Attachment allows you to blend, serve, and store your favorite recipes in the same glass mason jar.  The Mason Jar Attachment connects the Personal Blender blade assemblies with most regular-mouth mason jars, so the upgrade possibilities for your Personal Blender are virually limitless.
Mason Jar attachment is compatible with regular mouth [REDACTED] or [REDACTED] brand mason jars only. 

BLENDER:
http://personalblender.com/main.asp
incidentDescription:
I am writing about horrible safety negligence in the design of a product that injured my boyfriend last night. He is in extreme pain due to a mangled hand, and cannot type due to his injury, and asked me to write on his behalf. 

I bought a personal smoothie blender called “Tribest” found online at www.personalblender.com, the one that came with the mason jar attachment (very important).  My boyfriend was assembling the pieces yesterday while I was at work, and the blade started spinning as he fit the blade into the base. The instructions said to plug the blender in and put the blade into the base, on the first page of the manual!! The blades stuck out about an inch above the well that houses it, and spun at a very high speed (it is designed to also grind coffee and chop nuts), cutting deeply into his right hand and forefinger. The blade was activated because he had placed the mason jar attachment, which fit into the tab that turns the machine on perfectly. He went to the ER and had over 20 stitches and an arterial vein cauterization.

We do not know yet the extent of his injuries, but the doctor said that he would likely have nerve damage and loss of feeling in his index finger.  He was trying to assemble the unit, and the first page of Safety Guidelines in manual reads to plug unit in first, but once you see the device, you can see how easily it is to chop your hand up with the blades, and that there is a lack of a safety mechanism. In other words, he simply assembled the parts that went with the blender into the holes they fit into, and the blade started going with nothing inbetween his hand and the very fast blades!!

 We would also like to make an impression on Tribest to add safety features to their products to ensure no one else is hurt in this situation.

productDescription: Juicer
incidentDescription:
Caller is reporting his Juicer that was sent to him by the manufacturer around September 26th, 2009 as the remedy for his juicer that had been recalled with release# 02-041.
He had no problems with the replacement juicer until January 28th, 2013 when he was using the juicer, he heard a loud pop and noted that the juicer "jumped" a bit then the top portion of the plastic clamp which is used to hold the top portion of the unit in place to the bottom portion.
A piece of plastic went shooting past his head.
He is reporting because if the piece of plastic had hit his eye or throat etc. he or anyone standing near him could have been severely injured.

He contacted the manufacturer 01/28/2013, notified that his juicer is not one recall, not on warranty but that they would be happy to provide him with a 30 day only offer for another juicer at only 50% cost to him.

No injuries have been reported.

productDescription: 12 cup coffee maker
incidentDescription:
The consumer says the coffee pot turned on ten minutes before he got out of bed.  He walked into the kitchen and noticed the coffee pot was on fire.

The consumer says that he unplugged it and threw it in the sink to put the fire out.  The flames were shooting out from the bottom of the pot.  it melted the side of the unit.  He says that it was burning internally.  

He contacted the manufacturer who advised him to take it back to the store.  The consumer says his unit looks exactly as the one pictured in the recall.

productDescription: Professional Chargriller BBQ model2121 is the current version.
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
I bought a Professional Chargriller made in China.
The first time I used it we detected a gas leak. It turned out that the Regulator was defective.
In a haste to cook the food, I went down and bought a new one and put it on and it worked fine for a couple years. The first time it overheated due to chicken grease, it melted the internal lines inbetween the 3 burners. I did not turn the main tank off but, turned off the three burner knobs in the front. My neighbor came to me the next day saying he smelled gas and sure enough the thing was leaking again. If this had been put in a garage, it would have been catostrophic.
Luckily enough it was sitting outside. I am going to destroy the BBQ so no one trys to use it.
Mine was three years old, the current model of it is a 2121. I went to Lowes Department store 2 months after I purchased it and reported it, I went back months later and they were still being sold.

productDescription: Toaster oven Broiler
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
The consumer was making toast.  She went into the bathroom for a moment.  She heard alarms go off and her home was filled with smoke.  She went to the kitchen and saw flames shooting out of the two vents on the side and the cracks near the front door.  

She smothered the fire with a towel.  The consumer says the unit was on for approximately a few minutes prior to the incident.  She only used the unit a handful of times.  The consumers says that the timer on the oven never moved.

productDescription: ninja kitchen system (blender)
incidentDescription: I was using the blender for the first time. I put it together as shown in the quick start guide. After blending my smoothie I tried to pour some of it through the small flip top lid but it was too thick so I had to remove it. the blade tower seemed to snap into place when I placed it in the unit and I thought it secured. As I poured some of the smoothie into a cup to check the consistency the blade tower came out slicing my thumb. When I contacted the company I was told that I should reach into the blender and whatever is in the blender to remove the blade tower before pouring anything. This makes no sense since the blades are covered by in this case a thick, viscous and opaque material ie... fruit smoothie. I could not see the location of the blades in the unit nor would I stick my hands in and grab them if I could. This product is inherently unsafe and the company should know that.

productDescription: Propane BBQ
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription: When lifting the lid a large fire had broken out subsequently into the propane chamber melting the regulator hose/knob and a portion of the main lid and accompanying lid of sear burner.  When lid was opened a large fireball blew out and burned hair/face/arms of my wife.

productDescription:
Primula 6 cup aluminum espresso coffee maker. Espressly made for EPOCA 
Boca Raton FL 33487
incidentDescription:
I recently purchased a Primula 6 cup aluminum espresso coffee maker and at my first use I almost burnt my hand the coffee came out fron the side of the spout and the middle, I made sure that it was closed good as I have been making espresso coffee for the last 33 years.

*see attached e-mail address in google site but undeliverable.
victimSeverity: Injury, Level of care not known

productDescription: Lasko Ceramic Element Heater MODEL 5586
incidentDescription: I bought a Lasko Ceramic Element heater about 2 months ago. I had it plugged in using a heavy duty extension cord. I use it in my basement workroom. I wanted to unplug it from the extension cord and it wouldn't come apart. Using a screw driver (it was unplugged from the wall), I had to pry it apart. The plug from the heater had melted on to the other cord.

productDescription: silent room heater with remote control
incidentDescription:
Consumer stated she plugged in the heater at night. Just to warm up the room and it was on for about 15-20 minutes. When she came back in the room she smelled something burning. 
So she turned off the heater with the remote and went to unplug it, but the cord was too hot. So she grabbed something to pull the cord with. 
The consumer noticed that the flat prong looked charred and blackened. The prong was burned at the base; the base also seemed to have melted.
Consumer stated she has not contacted Lasko yet, but does intend to. 

There were no damage and no injuries.

UPDATE: Consumer spoke with (REDACTED0 at Lasko on 11/29/12.  She spoke with someone who said that the problem was the "resistance heating" and she should have an electrician check the outlet for "poor connection" and also check the wiring.  The electrician came on 11/30.12 and said there was nothing wrong with the outlet or wiring.  [REDACTED] said this would be processed through claims and they sent a mailing label. She will return it to them.

productDescription: battery for Apple iPhone 3GS White 16GB for ATT
incidentDescription:
I had a Apple iPhone 3GS, out of warranty, where the battery was swelling.  It caused the back of the phone to expand.  I googled this and saw where other 3GS phone cases cracked, glass fronts came off, and some even exploded (battery exploded).  I took it to an Apple store and they would only replace the battery for $150.  An authorized Apple repair center told me to go to another Apple store ASAP because the expansion of the battery causing the hard plastic case to expand around the battery (very visible) indicated that the battery was seriously swelling and could explode.  (the case seemed expand over a period of only a few days after noticing a dark spot on the screen, the first sign of the battery swelling)  I took the phone to another Apple store and they acknowledged a battery problem and offered to sell me a replacement phone for $80.  
The fact that batteries can explode after 2 - 3 years of use of a very expensive phone AND the fact that the manufacturer does not disclose this to consumers is egregious.  They should issue a recall for all phones with this battery and replace the phones.  This is a dangerous situation and Apple should not just sit by with a sketchy program to replace the phones only to those who scream loud enough or have the insight to take the phone to less busy stores that are more service oriented.  What if the phone exploded in my pocket or my hand?  People are using older phones either as phones or ipods so they're not being quickly retired.
I tried to find some information on Apple's website and the only thing I found was in the user support community where a few people - in the US and abroad - had registered incidents.  I am fortunate to have learned of the problem before it became a hazard.

productDescription: SPT Mini Dehumidifier Model: SD-652
incidentDescription: Bought the SPT Mini Dehumidifier Model: SD-652 circa September 2012.  The unit was used almost daily from November until February 2013 during the day only. It was used in a small bedroom closet during this time. On February 7, 2013 the unit would not turn on.  After close examination it was discovered that the plug that inserts into the unit had "shorted" causing the rubber/plastic of the plug to melt onto one of the prongs. The plastic around one of the holes on the plug was melted and blistered. There were no injuries or fire damage cause by the unit. It was always used in a safe manor and in a dry closet. In fact, it was rarely moved other than emptying the water tank which would take well over a week to fill halfway. It should also be noted that during the last month to month and a half of use, I did notice the motor running louder than usual when first turned on. However, after several minutes, the motor would resume its normal sounds.

productDescription: Revlon Ion RV484 hairdryer pink/gray
incidentDescription: While using the Revlon RV484 Ion hair dryer I would notice pops and then a spark would shoot out the end of the blower. This happens when the Ion switch is both on and off and also when it is at set on all the different temperatures. I am now fearful to use my hairdryer as the sparks could potentially set my hair on fire or worse. This hair dryer has been used for less than 6 months. My previous dryer lasted 15 years. This new dryer is horrible quality and a safety hazard.

productDescription: TIGI Wave Runner in Pink
productType: Hair Curlers, Curling Irons, Clips & Hairpins (1682)
incidentDescription: Purchased a TIGI Brand "Wave Runner" for my hair this morning and came home to try it out and use it. Upon plugging it in and trying on low first, per instructions with the product, was not satisfied with the results. The product seemed very cool and I expected it to be hotter, so I turned it to high. I then took a strand of hair and began to use the product which was now approimately 1 inch from my head. Immediately a large white flash and a loud pop and crack was heard. I was startled and jumped back into a wall approximately a foot back. My boyfriend then ran into the room hearing the popping noise and found that the cord was severed from the product approximately 2 inches below where the cord joins the handle of the product. The cord was melted, severed and had tripped the GFI outlet. Had the cord been touching my face, I could have been burned or electricuted, or blinded from the flash of the arc. There was no water or moisture near the product at the time of use. The product was properly removed from its packaging, inspected, instructions read and plugged into wall for use.

productDescription: 120 volt, 700 watt Digital five function multi cooker
incidentDescription:
On October the 18th 2012 his wife was making a pot roast when a hold was melted through the bottom of the cooker and burned a hole in the countertop.  The cooker never shut off.  It was on roughly 4 hours prior to the incident.   

Had his wife not discovered this it could have caused a serious fire.  he contacted the retailer who said that they were not very concerned.  

He said they were more concerned about getting the product back into their hands.  He contacted the manufacturer's representative and they did not seem very concerned.  

Approximate cost of damage $6,600.00

productDescription: Propane barbecue. Char-Broil Patio Bistro.
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription: The propane barbecue has one knob controlling ignition and gas flow. When turning the knob to ignition and then to gas flow it seemed that the barbecue did not ignite. I therefore turned the knob to off but cycled past the ignition point which blew the barbecue grate into the air. Seems poorly designed and that the ignition and gas flow should be on separate controls. It is a Char-Broil Patio Bistro barbecue.

productDescription: 5 qt. 3 setting Slow Cooker
incidentDescription:
Consumer started to cook a roast in the slow cooker on the low setting and placed the lid on. Within 5 minutes the glass lid shattered and the handle on the lid flew off. The lid still remained on the cooker, but it was shattered. There is a 3 inch wide hole where the handle once was secured to the lid.  Some of the pieces of glass near the handle also separated from the rest of the glass.

After cleaning the kitchen twice to remove the fragments of glass; the consumer's daughter [redacted] , sustained minor cuts to both hands by untraceable pieces of glass. The cuts on her right wrist and left thumb were rinsed off and bandaged; no medical attention was needed. 
Consumer has only used the slow cooker about 4 times, since receiving it as a gift before the holidays. There were no known cracks or blemishes on the slow cooker. 

On the same day the consumer spoke with mfr ([redacted] operator#[REDACTED]) who stated she could send a replacement lid and it would be referred to the Claims Mgr [redacted].  The consumer did not indicate whether or not he would accept the replacement lid.  He was more interested in speaking with [redacted].  The consumer was told that [redacted] would call him back at a later time.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription: Progressive Microwave Tea Kettle
productType: Coffee Makers or Teapots, Not Specified (452)
incidentDescription: I had used my Progressive Microwave Tea Kettle for years without a problem, but the top caught on fire tonight.  Electrical arcing was visible at the site of the burn.

productDescription: Dust Buster
incidentDescription:
We purchased a Back&Decker Dust Buster Model  CHV1410 and hung it on a wall at a convenient height of approximately 54 in.  The hook provided was used, and the included instructions were followed.  When the Dust Buster was lightly bumped, it disengaged from its hook and fell on the foot of the user, resulting in a broken bone. Medical treatment, and therapy were required to restore optimal function.

On examination, the hook and it's mating slot on the Dust Buster do not provide a secure connection.   A minimal move from true vertical allows disengagement from the hook, resulting in this incident.  
This design does not prevent any sideways movement of the Dust Buster in relation to true vertical.

productDescription: Grill Cleaning Brush
productType: Manual Cleaning Equipment (Excl. Buckets and Pails) (480)
incidentDescription: After cleaning my grill grates approx. Nov 8th or 9th, I grilled a London Broil. Ate London Broil on Nov. 8th or 9th with family at dinner time.  Stomach and abdomen had severe stabbing pain next day.  waited for pain to go away but it did not. went to see family doctir who took an x-ray and saw nothing.  He gave me a prescription to help ease stomach pain.  Did not work. Pain returned.  Went to the ER Nov. 11, 2012, Sunday morning.  They took 2 CAT scans.  Film and report stated metallic pin or object lodged in small intestines, poking through somewhat- hung up.  Admitted for surgery.  8 days in hospital. Surgeon removed wire bristle and later told me the hospital pathologist had it and it did look like it came from a grill cleaning brush.  Wife checked out grill later and found several wire bristles stuck to the grill grates. She also picked off loose bristles from the brush. We still have the grill brush.

productDescription: Automatic coffee maker
incidentDescription:
Recently ordered Cuisinart model DCC-2800 coffeemaker, serial #20112.
Product appears to have been assembled incorrectly at factory.
Appears to be a DCC-2800 body with a DCC-2900 control panel installed.
Cannot set auto off time for the warming plate.

productDescription: Shark Steam Mop Model # S3501CO
incidentDescription: Steam & Hot water built up in the reservoir. Steam started escaping from the sides & hot water was spraying out of the front. Then the mop head popped off with hot steam shooting out from the pressure.

productDescription: Hair Dryer
incidentDescription: Turned on my BabylissPro TT hair dryer and immediately lifted near my head to dry my hair. Within about 2 seconds, the dryer sounded odd and then it exploded. Pieces of the dryer flew all over the room I was in. I picked up approximately 7 different pieces of the dryer. It appears the plastic fan on the inside broke which then caused the exterior to explode as well.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: Lasko Space Heater
incidentDescription:
Caller purchased space heater November 9th, 2012 brought it home and began using it for heat with no problems until November 22nd, 2012 when it began sparking and instantly caught fire.
She jumped up grabbed her three yr old grandson who was standing very near the fire then she threw salt on the fire to put it out.

Caller unplugged the heater and stopped using it noting that a portion of the plug had broken off and that portion was blackened.

She has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.
There were no injuries

She is reporting this heater because she purchased it new from the retailer just two weeks ago and she is asking that she be reimbursed at manufacturer expense.

productDescription: 5 speed electric hand mixer 125 watts motor
incidentDescription:
The consumer tested an electrical hand mixer on 12/13/12.  She stated that the mixer sparked when she plugged it in the wall outlet.  The consumer was not mixing any hand ingredients at that time.  

The consumer tripped the GIV outlet and reset the circuit breaker.  She stated that she then tried the mixer again and it sparked.  She reinserted the mixing blades believing that it would help, but the breaker tripped again.  The consumer discontinued use of the mixer at that point.

The consumer plans to contact the retailer (Target) at a later time.

No injuries or property damage.

productDescription: vacuum cleaner
incidentDescription: About December 8, 2012, my wife was using her Kenmore vacuum cleaner when it caught fire around the wand/cord area.  It is a kenmore Model: 116.25512506, Part CO1ZCYKOOUOO-KCO1ZCYKZO.NO.  I purchased it on 06/10/2006 from Sears in King OF Prussia, PA.  I brought the unit outside and put out the fire with a wet towel.  No injury or damage occurred except for the vacuum.  I sent an email via their site in December but never received a reply.  Recently, I contacted them again and they advised no recall was issued and because the warranty expired, no replacement was offered.  I expressed my concern about safety and the incident was reported to the company safety officer.  Note; I will be in Florida until mid April and return to PA at [REDACTED] in mid Arpil. Thank you.

productDescription: Stick Hand Blender
incidentDescription:
On Saturday, December 8th, 2012 the caller was using her stick blender when she began to smell a burning odor and saw a small amount of smoke, she stopped the unit and turned it off.

After the unit cooled off, she removed the attachment and saw that the coupling that connects the attachment and the motor had melted and stripped itself of all threading.

Blender is no longer usable without being a fire hazard and this is why she is reporting.

She contacted the manufacturer Tuesday, December 11, 2012 and was advised by a representative and a supervisor who advised that there is nothing that can be done because it isn't on warranty and they have no known issues with it.

She did not obtain names.



There have been no injuries

productDescription: Ecoteck (Ravelli) Pellet stove
incidentDescription:
Our home has an Ecoteck (Ravelli) Pellet stove.  The model name is "Monica".  The pellet stove was operating normally when the power failed.  After the power returned, the stove's display indicated “Black – Out”.  The instruction manual solution for this message is “Press the OFF button and repeat switching ON the stove”.  After doing this, the display indicated "Final Cleaning" which is the message normally displayed while it is in its shutdown phase.  After stove shut off, I restarted it and checked it a few minutes later.  The stove interior was filled with smoke & fire, smoke was seeping from the seams of the flue inside the house and smoke was billowing outside the house from the flue.  There was also a detonation of combustible gases in the flue which blew the bottom cover off the flue at the base of the stove.  I opened the stove door and used a fire extinguisher to put the fire out.  The fire pot was entirely filled with pellets, which apparently led to the runaway fire.  I called 911 and had the fire department make sure everything was ok.

Later investigation showed that the power failure created a failure mode in which the stove's electronic controller continuously loads pellets in the fire pot leading to a dangerous runaway fire condition in the stove's interior.  The intensity of the resulting fire is beyond the design limit of the stove and could easily have led to a structural fire in the home had I not contained it.

productDescription: Five cup General Electric coffee maker
brand: General Electric 5 cup digital coffee maker, model # 898677
incidentDescription:
I purchased a 5 cup coffee maker, made  by General Electric, at Walmart about 2 years ago. In less than a year the cover for the pot broke off.  I called GE and then returned the coffee maker to Walmart, where it was replaced. That was in February, 2012. On Feb. 5, 2013 I made a pot of coffee, and when I went to pick up the pot, the one piece handle and lid broke off, leaving several small pieces of plastic and the screw which tore loose from the metal band around the pot. The pot fell forward, and I was scalded from my ribs down to about the middle of my leg.  I was wearing only underwear because I had planned to drink the coffee while I got dressed. I immediately got in a cool shower (painful burn) and when I could stand to touch the area  used [REDACTED] cream.
I am writing because two of these pots broke in a very similar way. With the first one, the lid broke off when the plastic didn't hold. With the second one, the entire plastic mechanism broke as soon as I lifted the pot of scalding coffee. I think these pots should be tested for inferior quality plastic, which can result in serious damage.
When I called GE at [REDACTED] and told the robot the model number printed on the front of the booklet, it insisted there is no such number, but obviously there is. The model # is 898677.Below that is UPC605388986771.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription: battery pack (np-fx110) for sony portable dvd player
incidentDescription:
The battery lid attached to the sony portable dvd player got bent and wouldnt close from one side.
The battery model is np-fx110.

The battery pack wouldnt fit. Upon opening the lid, we found that one of the two cells inside had puffed up.

Replacement batteries cost almost as much as the dvd player. This is a product defect and potentially dangerouns since the product is mainly used for kids.

I hope sony issues a recall and gives a replacemnt battery for all customers facing this issue.

productDescription:
CHI Velocity Hot Shot Ceramic Hair dryer (black & red).

Taken from website Online "Product Description":
 Produces far infrared heat with negative ions to reduce drying time
2 speed settings & 2 heat settings
AC motor for more power
Available in Red/Black and Black/Red
120 Volts AC, 60 Hz, 1800 Watts

http://www.farouk.com/CHI/Discontinued-Products/VELOCITY-by-CHI-Hot-Shot-Tourmaline-Ceramic-Hair-Dryer.aspx
model: Velocity Hot Shot Ceramic Hair dryer
incidentDescription: Within the last three months, my husband had contacted the manufacturer of the CHI Velocity Hot Shot Ceramic Hairdryer to tell them that the Hi/Low pressure had stopped working on the hair dryer.  They were not interested in fixing or replacing the hair dryer at that time as we were just outside the warranty period.  However, this did not render the hair dryer unusable.  Unfortunately on Friday, my son was using the hair dryer and sparks, as well as black smoke started coming out when he screamed down to us as he was unsure of what to do.  We told him to unplug the hair dryer and ran up.  You can see the black burn marks on the middle red button which is the hi/low pressure button.   I will be happy to send the hair dryer to you for your evaluation.  This product is defective and a potential fire hazard.

productDescription: Toaster oven
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
I have used Black & Decker toaster ovens for years.  Sometime in late summer I noticed a toaster oven with a timer which I thought would be a helpful feature so I purchased one- I believe the model number TO1412B.  I gave the old toaster oven to a family that had lost everything in a fire.  The first few times I used the toaster oven I had no problems but then I was summoned to the kitchen by the smoke alarm.  On arrival I noted smoke and flames coming from the toaster oven.  When I grabbed the handle to pull it away from the wall to unplug it (as the instructions state) I sustained 1st degree burns on the back of my fingers.  When the fire was extinguished the inside the toaster oven was covered in a layer of black soot.  The charred remains of the bread I had attempted to toast sat on the rack.  Although I was fairly sure I had set the timer I couldn’t be certain.  I cleaned the toaster as well as I could and tried to use it while I stood by and observed, it worked as intended.  Thinking that I had been mistaken about setting the timer I didn’t return it at that point.  I used it a few times after that but was always hovering nearby observing because I didn’t trust it and then it happened again i.e. the timer reached time zero and failed to turn the toaster off- I returned the toaster oven to Walmart and was given a replacement which has worked OK for the last 3 months. 
Since I ‘ve had toaster ovens in the past I note that the temperature selection knob is not as tapered at the selection end as it was on previous models.  This makes it a bit difficult to see the temperature it points to at a quick glance. I have since painted a dot on the temperature selection end.  Nor do I like the fact the the heating element seems to come on at full power to get the unit up to the set temperature as this results in burning any items that are on the rack when the machine is turned on.
victimSeverity: Injury, Level of care not known

productDescription:
Sony Model No. NP-FX110 Lithium Ion Rechargeable Battery Pack for a Sony portable DVD player
Made in China DC 7.4V 3800mAH
incidentDescription:
The Lithium Ion Rechargeable Battery Pack ( NP-FX110 ) for our Sony DVD player has had one of it's cells expand to the point that it has cracked the plastic case that houses the cell.  It is pressurized to the point that it seems like it will explode if anything punctures the cell's membrane.  The unit is now inoperable.
It's safe to say that this is happening with MANY other units and this is not a fluke occurence but a manufacturing defect that could potentially hurt someone.  Sony has to realize that these DVD players are primarily used by children and a curious child whose DVD player stopped working could potentially puncture the pressurized cell, exposing the child to its chemicals.
I'd like to know what Sony will do about this and if they are interested in keeping a long time customer.

productDescription: Keurig B40 single cup coffee maker
incidentDescription:
I have a Keurig Elite Coffee Maker that is about 4 years old.  It has started coming on by itself.  I press the power button to off but if I leave it plugged in it will come on, heat the water and dispense the hot water continually until the water storage bin is empty, then it will continue to try to pump.  

The first time it started on it's own I was within hearing distance and hear the sound of the water running out.  I have been unplugging it since but the other day I forgot and the above episode happened where it kept pumping out hot water till the bin was empty.  However, you could hear the pump trying to pump more water.  Since the unit has a program that is supposed to stop pumping when the water is low and engage a warning light to tell me that it needs more water, that function must not be functioning either.

It works if I make a cup and unplug it when I'm done but if this is happening to others....as it is because there are movies of it happening on You tube....if this had happened when I wasn't home I fear it would have caught fire as the water bin must have been hot because it is not a little warped.

productDescription: Perfect flame model GAC3615, 4 burner gas grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription: Was bar-b-queing chicken hind quarters on low, right before they were finished the top of the small side of the grill ( Perfectflame model # GAC3615)  seemed to explode and caught on fire.  The house and deck caught on fire, my husband was able to disconnect the propane tank before it exploded also.  We were able to get the BBQ grill off the deck and dragged it out to the driveway were it continued to burn, putting water on it made the flames brighter and it was difficult to put out.  We are very upset our house smells like smoke inside, we had to tear our our melted and burned vinyl siding to see if there was a fire underneath and our our brand new freshly painted deck now has burn holes. Not to mention we now had no dinner.  After the fire was out I called Lowes - [REDACTED] at store # 1559, said that it was not their responsibility after one year.  I told her that I had talked to my son who lives in another state and he told me that they had a lot of recalls on that brand.  She said they were still not responsible and gave me the number to the manufacturer.

productDescription: Portable Buddy propane space heater
incidentDescription:
Saturday, November 17th, 2012 while caller was in his deer blind and just after he changed the propane then lit the portable heater being used he heard what sounded like a mini explosion.  He looked down and saw that the propane heater was on fire with the flames being small but hot enough not to catch him afire.
He grabbed the heater and threw it out to the blind then stepped out and poured his coffee over the fire to put it out.

If he had not been right in front of the fire or the heater had actually exploded he could have been burned severely.
He is reporting this product as a fire hazard.

He has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.

I ran to her bedroom only to find the Sunbeam SWM-5251 humidifier was on fire with flames about 2 feet high. My wife was right behind me,she grabbed her I unplugged the unit and ran for an extinguisher and put it out. productDescription: GE Profile Model #JVM1790SK01 combination microwave/convection oven, installed above a range.
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
The convection oven of my GE Profile microwave/convection oven self-started, while not being used.   It became so hot that the fan came on.   I was in another room and heard the fan running, I went into the kitchen to find the oven extremely hot.   I could not turn it off, so unplugged the it, and did not use it anymore.   I reported the problem to GE as a safety problem, because the convection oven had only been used one time since I had purchased the unit.  It was a little over one year old.    

I told GE Consumer Hotline that I did not want the unit repaired, but wanted them to know that it had self-started, because it is a safety issue.   They did send a technician, who did not inspect the appliance, but said it was a bad circuit board, and wrote a repair estimate for over $500.   He said that any circuit board could malfunction at any time, whether the unit was in use at the time or not (which mine was not).     I absolutely did not want to keep it, it was out of warranty, but I got rid of it anyway, and purhased a counter-top microwave, without a convection oven in it.   (That was what the technician suggested would be my best solution, if I didn't want another expensive unit with a convection oven in it.)     

The model number of the GE Profile microwave/convection I had was JVM1790SK01.   Both the technician and the sales person at Home Depot were very unconcerned about the danger of a heat-producing appliance that would come on by itself and could not be turned off.   I was absolutely concerned about a potential fire, which they said could not happen.   I don't believe that for a minute.    My sister and a good friend both have this same model, and I am genuinely concerned that this could happen to them.    We have since learned that there have been other instances reported of this happening.

productDescription: Larger cooker of Fagor Rapida 5-pc Pressure Cooker Set
incidentDescription:
My two-year-old Rapidia pressure cooker exploded (seal broken). 

There are two reasons why I want to report this incident. First, I believe that the cooker wasn't designed properly. Its safety valve should have prevented the incident to happen by releasing the steam pressure, or a stronger seal needs to be used.

Second, I believe there is a design flaw in the location of the safety valve which is bundled together with the normal steam outlet. This design can prevent people from telling if the steam is from the normal outlet or the safety release valve. Because of the design flaw, it's very hard for most users to tell the difference between steams released from the safety valve and from the normal valve. As a result, it'd be impossible for most users to tell when the safety valve is open and when to remove the heat from the cooker. If the steam is out from the safety valve, users would be able to identify the problem in time and remove the heat to avoid the explosion.

productDescription: Bradley BTIS1 Original Fully Automatic 4-Rack Outdoor Food Smoker (black)
incidentDescription: I purchased a Bradley BTIS1 Smoker as a gift in November 2011. We used the smoker twice last summer. The second time we used it, it went up in flames. We cleaned it thoroughly after our first use and monitored it while it was in use. We didn't try using it again until this past Christmas and needless to say, it didn't work. I emailed the company but haven't gotten a response. Our one year warranty has expired so I'm not expecting a replacement. In doing some online research, I have found that several other people have had a similar experience and for safety reasons, I feel this product should be recalled. Had we not been outside when our smoker caught on fire, we could've lost more than just the smoker.

productDescription: Outdoor Barbeque
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
I have been using the GrandTurbo BBQ (from Barbeques Galore) for approximately 3 years and have had occasional problems with the barbecue knobs becoming too hot to touch and ultimately melting to the point that they slide off.
Also during that time, I have seen the stainless steel cooking grids slowly loose their structural integrity resulting in them "peeling" apart, and getting steel in the food. 
Early on in my ownership of the grill, the company that installed the grill replaced my control knobs.  Most recently, I have contact the manufacturer about replacing them again (the installation company is no longer in business), in addition to addressing the issue of the cooking grids.
However, my email exchange with them have only resulted in a position that I need to purchase replacement parts (even though the product has a lifetime warranty).  At first, I thought this was just a warranty issue.  Then I realized that I have been tolerating a product that is supposed to be used for cooking, but can result the food being injected with steel from the grids and knobs that are melting or too hot to turn off.... and that is a safety concern.

productDescription: High-power universal TV remote with non-replaceable, rechargeable battery.
incidentDescription:
The 'Pro' version of the TV-B-Gone has a non-replaceable, rechargeable battery. My unit was charged and used a total of 6 times. For the initial use, I charged it per the instructions. It worked as advertised. Two days later, I went to use it again but the battery was dead. I charged it and again, and it worked. The unit was dead again after the 2nd day. It was very frustrating to use as I always had to 'anticipate' its use by re-charging beforehand. I could never pick it up and have it ready. After the sixth charge, I discovered that the battery had expanded to three times its width. The battery had also melted the front and rear covers. It created so much pressure that it popped off the back cover and landed more than 2 feet away. I've sent repeated emails to the company, as well as [REDACTED], the president. After several weeks, still no response.

I am very lucky that the battery did not start a fire. I charged the unit according to the instructions, and had around 10 minutes of total use. The idea is great but the implementation is not. I have included pics of the damaged unit with the swelled battery and separated cover.

productDescription: George Foreman Grilling Machine, model GRP99 B, silver in color, LED display

The temperature of the grill was higher than I have ever used it, which means it exceeded 400 degrees Fahrenheit.

After the grill cooled off, it seems to operate correctly, though we are nervous using it now.

The space heater was the only item at that outlet. It was ~3 feet away from the wall, and at least 18 inches away from anything. There was no extension cord or power strip; the unit was plugged directly into the wall.

productDescription: Helen of Troy Professional thermal hot air brush
incidentDescription:
Saturday morning, 1/26/2013, I was drying my hair about 7:15 a.m. using my approx. 6-month old Helen of Troy tangle-free thermal hot air brush. It takes about 20 minutes to dry my hair, and I usually read the paper or a book while running the brush through my hair. I just turn my hair under so it's pretty easy to use. My hair was almost dry when I noticed white globs caught in the curls. I was trying to figure out what they were when I looked down at the hair dryer and noticed that there was a large hole melted into the plastic brush. I immediately turned off and unplugged the dryer; the brush and tip were burning hot to my touch. I think in another second or so my hair might have caught fire. I worked to free what I realized were parts of the brush that had melted in my hair. I do feel very lucky not to have been injured, though I tore some hair pulling out the plastic bits. I was going to a meeting so I plugged in a different brush dryer and finished my hair.

I've taken pictures of the flecks in my hair that remained last night after removing most everything else. I also took pictures of the hair dryer.

I think the dryer overheated but the reset button did not shut it down. 

I've used dryers like this for many years, and during this time have gone through seven or eight of the lower-cost [REDACTED] models. These do overheat and will shut down until they've cooled down. If they do that several times, it's my cue to toss the dryer and replace it with another from my stock (several years ago I bought about ten [REDACTED] dryers on sale at WalMart, but I haven't found them there in years). 

However, the Helen of Troy is a Professional model and had never shut off/overheated during the six months or so I've owned it. I liked it very much. In the last week, however, I had noticed that the plastic had become discolored, and I had planned to take off the roller brush this weekend to clean it. The only hair product I use is [REDACTED] shampoo (I don't even use hair spray) so there was nothing new in my routine that might have caused the discoloration.

Since this is a relatively new -- just six months old -- dryer, I am wondering whether what happened to me might happen to some other user if this is a design and/or production flaw.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: AUTOMATIC RICE COOKER
incidentDescription:

 1) Automatic shut-off  failed to work after cooking cycle so it burns the rice. We had to unplug the unit from the AC outlet.
  2) Does not go to keep warm mode. When it does it has a tendency to switching to cooking mode by itself.  We had one night we woke up with a non stop beeping sound of the cooker and smell of burning rice.
 
I refused to accept anymore replacement this being the 3rd time because I'm afraid given the above repeated incidents that this product is not safe to use and will put me and my family in danger.

I just want the distributor (Fry's) to replace it with another brand.

productDescription: Bathroom Ventilation Fan
incidentDescription:
On August 11, 2012 and again on January 26, 2013 the City of Carrollton Fire Department responded to [REDACTED]  to reported residential fires.  On both of these responses the bathroom exhaust fans had overheated or had a fire inside their plastic enclosures.  The plastic enclosures themselves were melted causing considerable smoke inside the apartment buildings.  On January 30, 2013 I made an investigative visit to the apartment complex and with the owners permission checked several of the apartments to determine fan manufacturer, model, and condition.  The majority of the fans that I checked, which was only a small sample of the 50 or so apartments, showed signs of poor maintenance with heavy dirt and dust accumulations inside the fan housings.  The fans involved in the fire incidents were not recovered at the time of the incident and it is not possible to determine if poor maintenance could have been an issue with these fans.

Aubrey Manufacturing
Model # 7550 Vent Fan

incidentDescription: Using an Andis Elevate Ionic Hair Dryer at 6:45AM 1/18/13: Turned on unit and within 5 minutes of use it made a bang sound and the right side of the unit approximately 2x3 inches blew out, with shattered plastic pieces of plastic and metal following that. I unplugged the unit immediately but it did continue to run before I did unplug it and there was a smell of burning. Their office is in the midwest and was closed by the time I got off of work on Friday - I live on the west coast.

productDescription: Dehumidifier

Caller was upstairs crafting and smelled a burning odor, she opened her basement door and was met with a chemical smelling smoke.

She ran downstairs, found that the smoke was coming from her dehumidifier and while leaning over the dehumidifier to turn it off then carrying it outside with pot holders she suffered an epithelial corneal chemical burn in her left eye which took three days to resolve with steroid eye drops and an antibiotic eye drops prescribed by doctor.

Caller is asking that this dehumidifier be recalled with replacement.

She tried numerous numbers to contact retailer with no success.

The only person she was able to contact was the manager of the day at the Cape Cod Store named [REDACTED].

[REDACTED] advised that she would have the appropriate department contact this consumer, however no one has contacted her.

Heater uses thermostat and automatically turns on and off to maintain selected temperature setting, so heater is left plugged in. Returned to home after approximtely 24 hours away and could smell smoke as approached house. Upon entering home, the house was filled with smoke and smoke alarm was sounding. Smoke was coming from heater and element was bright orange. Immediately unplugged heater. Top and sides so hot they could not be touched, so consumer had to pick up heater by bottom and carried outside to cool down. Owner's manual states that a thermal protection device will cut off the product when overheating to avoid fire, etc. but it appears that the safety device did not work.

productDescription: Lawn Blower/ shredder /Vacuum
productSubCategory: Lawn Mowers, Leaf Blowers and Lawn Vacuums
incidentDescription:
The caller stated that the portable lawn blower vacuum zipper malfunction after using it for approximately 1 hour, causing debris (sands, wood etc.) to disperse from the unit.  There were particles all over his body, face, some content got in his eyes, he was able to wash it off.  He stated that he received minor bruises around his left eye.

11/26/12 The manufacturer was contacted and he was offered a replacement bag which he declined because he feels that the incident will re-occur.  He feels that the manufacturer is aware of the safety hazard of this product.

Under incident details:  Consumer insisted that the replacement bag not be the same model bag.  Consumer informed Black & Decker customer service that he wanted the bag that is used on the LH 5000 model which has a slide bas VS zipper closure.  They verified that bag used on the LH5000 model would in fact fit the consumer's LH4500 machine.  Consumer received LH5000 model bag via UPS on 30 Nov 2012.  It is obviously a much more sturdy design than a zipper closure.
victimSeverity: Injury, Level of care not known

productDescription: Duracell Alkaline AA Batteries
incidentDescription:
This is one of several incidents I have experienced involving leaking Duracell batteries in the past year.

The device is a [REDACTED] LED headlight for bicycles, which is powered by 4 AA batteries. The batteries in the device were dated to expire on March 2012. The device has been used as a general purpose flashlight for inside the house rather than as a bicycle headlight.

The flashlight has been in regular use and today my wife informed me that it had stopped working yesterday. Because I have seen many devices damaged by Duracell batteries recently, I immediately opened the flashlight to assess the damage. 

The inside of the battery compartment is contaminated by a white material that has leaked from the batteries and has begun to corrode the battery contacts in the flashlight. This material irritates the skin and I am concerned it may contain toxic chemicals.

The leaked material has pooled on the surfaces of batteries, contacts, and the inside of the flashlight. This flashlight was working less than a day ago, so the leakage was not caused by the flashlight sitting unused for weeks or months. The batteries possibly started leaking before the light stopped working, because the leaked material has a dry crystalline quality to it, although the flow of the residue suggests that the material was fluid at the time it first leaked.

I was born in 1950's and leaky batteries were common in the 50's and 60's. Since improvements to batteries in the 70's and common use of Alkaline cells, battery leakage has become very rare. But now many Duracell batteries are leaking and are leaking much sooner in their lifespan. 

I have opened four devices in my home this month with similar damage. One of these devices was a valuable guitar with active electronic circuitry inside.

I think Duracell batteries may be unsafe and may put consumers at risk for burns and toxic effects. Please follow up with me to discuss what can be done about this problem. If you go on the Duracell website you will see that many consumers have the same problems.

incidentDescription: In early December, 2012, I purchased an outdoor patio heater from Costco online. The product is Costco Item # 514537.  The heater is manufactured by Fire Sense Model # 60688.  The product requires some assembly.  I believe the product has a serious design flaw that could result in a fire hazard. The unit was designed so that the purchaser does not have the ability to test the upper hose (where it connects to the igniter and on/off switch for gas leaks. The owner's manual diagram shows that the hose is accessible through a hole in the housing and should be tested for leaks. The actual design is such that there is no testing hole and the entire unit must be dissembled, placed on the ground and tested and then reassembled. This is not practical.  The part of the unit where the hose connects comes already assembled and is very difficult to take apart.  I did in fact experience a gas leak but was fortunate enough to detect it before I experienced a fire or explosion.  I attempted to post a review of the product on the Costco web site describing my issue but Costco chose not to post it. I returned the product to Costco without a problem. I called the manufacturer customer service line.  They told me that they would have to replace the entire burner/valve portion of the heater but that they did not have any in stock and wouldn't for over a month as other customers have experienced similar issues.    I expect that most customers who purchase this product will not test the hose coupling for leaks as it is not accessible and they will not take the time to disassemble the unit.

Her lawyer contacted the manufacturer 10/05/2012, was informed that they were coming to the lawyers office to examine the fan motor, photos etc., however, they provided no date, have not called again or come to the lawyers office.

productDescription: Battery charger and tender, 12 V, 5 A
incidentDescription:
As an amateur radio operator, [REDACTED], I run my station on batteries so that it can be available in an emergency when no utility power is available.  

To charge the batteries and maintain their charge, I bought a 5 amp BatteryTender Part No. 022-0157-1, S/N 3412-100698C, from Amazon.com on 7 Dec 2012 and connected it to a [REDACTED] battery.  To test the charging, I deliberately ran the battery down to a 12 V level.   The wiring was standard for the setup in my upstairs radio room.

I woke up in the middle of the night and smelled an acrid odor in the house and found the BatteryTender warm, but not hot, and the battery warm.   The red light on the BatteryTender was on continuously, as it had been all day.  The red light indicates the charging mode. The battery had boiled over, warping the top.

Apparently, the BatteryTender had failed to go from the charging mode to the maintenance mode, over charging the battery.The battery's internal water was converted to hydrogen and oxygen.  The result is well known to be an explosion or fire hazard.  The BatteryTender should have stopped charging and gone to a maintenance mode automatically.  That's why it's called a "Tender" not a "Charger".

This is a product which is dangerous when it fails to work as intended.

I sent an e-mail to service@batterytender.com on 12/18/12 and have not had any response.

I immediately removed the cord and contacted Target to let them know this device is defective.  I will also contact Lasko via email.

This product needs to be removed from the market before it burns someone's home down.  If left unattended, the electrical outlet will overheat causing internal wiring to catch fire in homes that do not have AFI outlets.  AFI outlets will short the wiring before it catches fire.  Most homes built prior to 2010, do not have these upgraded outlets. 

I took a photos of the burnt cord, the ceramic heater, original box and the damaged outlet.  Did not see a manufactured date on the product or instruction manual.

I will be returning these products to Target for a full refund or give Lasko 7 days to respond to my email.

productDescription: Cuisinart CSB-76 Smartstick Hand Blender (Immersion Blender), made in China
incidentDescription: The incident involves Cuisinart CSB-76 Smartstick Hand Blender. Severe finger laceration requiring approximately 9 stitches occurred after the device failed to turn off while being disassembled. It is possible for the main power switch to be in the "on" position, allowing the blade to continue turning while a second "detach" button is pressed. The detach button is not properly designed, because when pressed, that button should de-energize the appliance before it can be disassembled. I note there have been at least 3 other similar incidents located on the CPSC website, but could find no corrective measures or recalls to date.  I recommend that the company be required to recall these devices and install a properly engineered safety interlock device that makes it impossible to energize the blender while it is being disassembled. This would make it impossible for injuries such as this to occur in the future. The instruction manual's advice to unplug the device is important, but fails to meet widely accepted safety engineering standards. Please advice on CPSC's action in this matter. Thank you. Sincerely, [REDACTED]

productDescription: Optimus H-5210. 400/800 Watts Infrared Quartz Radiant Heater
incidentDescription:
I purchased two Optimus Quartz Radiant Heaters Model: H-5210 in December 2011 from Walmart.

The heater that is used the most is very hot to the touch and shuts itself off after in use for a while.  I believe that its "Thermal Cut-Off Safety Device" cuts the heater off due to overheating. (The other heater is just a backup and is hardly ever used.)

Subsequently, I read a report on page 52 of the November 2012 issue of Consumer Reports magazine which indicates that this heater is a Safety Risk and a Don't Buy.

It also indicated that it contacted Optimus and Optimus claims to have fixed the problem on 2012 models. However, there is no way to tell the model year from the box.

When I contacted Walmart it said it can't help at all because it is past 90 days from the purchase date.

I contacted Optimus which said if I want to ship it back to them in California it will fix it. The problem with that is that the shipping cost is almost as much as the purchase price.

However, I am more concerned with overheating and the safety of this product.

productDescription: Hunter Outdoor Ceiling Fan. Model # 21318, Captive 52"
incidentDescription:
I purchased multiple Hunter Captiva 52" outdoor ceiling fans, Model # 21318 about 3 years ago. They have had very little use, but this past weekend 2 blades broke off of one of the fans, and went flying like missiles across my porch. Upon inspection, I found more blades cracked across where the mounting screws attached the blades to the fan bracket.

I looked up the fan on the Hunter web site, and found where multiple people have had this same problem. One individual said he had filed a complaint with you, and suggested others do the same. Hunter is not acknowledging the problem, and continues to sell the fan as is. Of course, they were happy to sell me more blades. One set cost $60, plus tax and shipping. So much for the "lifetime" warranty.

This is a danger to everyone that has purchased this fan over the last several years. Especially children. Please follow up with them on this! 

Thank you in advance for your help with this,

Respectfully,

[REDACTED]

productDescription:
Cuisinart Pro Custom 11" food processor
White
Model #DLC-8S
90409 Serial #
incidentDescription: I purchased model # DLC-8S serial #90409 Cuisinart Pro Custom food processor in September 2009.  While using the plastic work bowl, pieces have continually fallen off into the food I am preparing.  The first time it happened soon after purchase, the plastic was found in our meal.  Subsequent times I have been able to catch the broken pieces and disposed of the food.  This work bowl is clearly defective.  The cracking includes both small internal fissures around tension points (crazing) and actual broken/cracked pieces.  The final piece that engages the lock to operate the appliance has broken and the appliance is rendered inoperable.

productDescription:
Le Creuset 1.8 Quart whistling kettle

product number: SKU SS3102P
incidentDescription:
I bought  a 1.8 quart stainless steel whistling tea kettle manufactured by Le Creuset in September. On first using it I was alarmed to find a serious and dangerous design flaw. After the water has boiled, and when you try to pour water into a cup or bowl, the water fizzes and bubbles out of the spout in an arc of boiling water that goes all over kitchen surfaces. It is highly dangerous because any hand close to the kettle risks severe scalding. In my view this product should be recalled immediately.
   I thought I might have been sold a single defective kettle, but looking at recent reviews on Amazon shows that other people are suffering the same problem, and danger. I refer you to the Amazon reviews dated october 16 by [REDACTED] and september 13 by [REDACTED].
  I emailed le Crueset's customer service department pointing out the risks of this product and calling on them to withdraw it. I received in return a message that did not address this issue but offered me a credit note if I returned the product and they found my complaint valid.
   I have not taken this up because it misses the point. A child could be scarred for life by this product. It is should be withdrawn from sale immediately.

productDescription: Magic bullet, Baby Bullet baby food maker
incidentDescription:
I was using the Baby Bullet, baby food maker to puree some food for my 6 month old daughter.  I had only used it a few times.  This was the third time.  I had followed all of the manufacturers guidelines on how to use and clean the device (hand wash, and top rack dishwasher safe). 

I was feeding my daughter her food and she was struggling with something in her mouth so I reached in and pulled out a piece of plastic/silicone.  This was from the units blade component. There is a plastic/silicone gasket around the blade.  It had popped off and had been cut into pieces.  I am very upset about the whole thing.  I was about half way done feeding her when I noticed something was wrong,  so it is is possible she might have eaten a piece earlier.

I tried to call the company but they are closed until tomorrow.

After some investigation on the Internet I have discovered that many other people have had similar stories about this unit malfunctioning and causing a choking hazard.

Please feel free to contact me about this report or my incident.

productDescription:
Nyko Charge Station.
A base station to charge remotes for the [REDCATED] console. Plugs into wall, comes with two rechargeable battery packs. White with blue lights signifying dock connection. Holds two remotes.
incidentDescription:
A fire was sparked in my home at 12am when I was not there. I believe it was caused by the NYKO charging [REDACTED] charging base station I purchased in 2008 or 2007. I recall the [REDACTED] being very hot after charging them on the station fro a while, even burning my hand a few times. 

And after perusing the internet, today I found out that they have been recalled, which I did not know previous to this. 

My base station was plugged into the wall next to a strip outlet that held other electronic devices. The chargers were charging, as nothing was since I was away and when I came home the next morning I found out that a fire had occurred overnight and me entire apartment was a total loss. This product is extremely unsafe and should be taken off the market.
victimSeverity: Injury, Level of care not known

incidentDescription:
I have a Kenmore 30 pint dehumidifier, model 580.52300200. 
The power cord has been working off and on for a few months, and recently when I moved the cord, it exploded, sending embers in the air and smoke everywhere. I'm so glad my hand was back a few inches from where the cord exploded.
I see there's a recall on newer models than mine, but that they have the same issue as I just experienced. I'd like to warn you about this problem with the model I have, and see if there's a solution for the unit I own.
I sent the above text to Kenmore's customer service a week ago and received no response whatsoever.

productDescription: Euro-Pro Shark Steam Mop, Model S3250 Purple & grey handle, purple base where water tank and heating element are, grey mop bottom where mop attachments go.
incidentDescription: I was using my Shark Steam Mop, Model S3250 and as it was warming up the hissing noise it usually makes as it releases steam seemed muffled.  The sound is usually loud(ish) and you can usually see the steam being released.  As I pumped the handle I saw no steam and began to feel concerned that something was wrong with the mop.  I unplugged it right away and seconds after I did so, the cap to the top of the water tank popped up and loads of steam was released through the water tank as well as out of the seams of the base of the mop where I assume the heating element is.  The mop base was so hot it was literally melting the paint and dripping purple all over the floor.  While this portion of the mop usually gets hot, this time it easily would have left burns if touched.

incidentDescription: I have a GE brand Food Processor bought at Walmart a year ago or so.  It is 14 cups and model number 169203.  I have been having trouble with the plastic parts of the processor chipping off and getting into the food product, putting my family at risk for ingesting plastic shards. I had this happen right when I got the unit and then was careful to watch for additional chips and not use that food.  Yesterday the plastic post that the chopper blade seats down on failed and put lots of little plastic shavings and powder into the food.  This is a repeating problem so yesterday I searched the internet for the modle and found that it had been recalled for a different propblem, but I thought you should be aware of the food contamination issue as well.  I wonder how many times I missed very small plastic chips getting into food?

incidentDescription:
Several years ago,  I purchased a Soleus Air Heater HGW 308, MD 000081509000, S/N 504700100829.

When I attempted to use the unit late in the 2012 heating season, it malfunctioned and failed to heat. I stored the unit without further inspection.

In mid-November 2012, I re-inspected the unit and noticed that on the exterior of the unit (plastic side control panel, lower portion), I noticed that the plastic had discolored and slightly melted outward from the unit.  Upon opening the side panel for inspection, I noted that the power cord had become brittle at its connection with the unit's internal wiring. There were obvious char marks on the wiring at the junction of these wires.

While there was no fire with the failure of the unit, charring of the plastic did occur. I am not in a position to determine if greater damage would have arisen if the wiring had not completely charred.

Pictures were taken and the unit remains in my possession.

productDescription: Vacuum Cleaner
incidentDescription:
Caller purchased vacuum in 2004 and had no problems with it until Thursday, October 4th, 2012 when she was vacuuming and a spark then fire came from the bottom portion of the unit.

When she saw fire she immediately unplugged the unit and then threw the breaker.

She has commented that she was just beside her curtains when this occurance happened and it could have resulted in a damaging fire.

She is asking that this model be investigated and recalled.

productDescription: Kaz Vicks cool mist humidifier model v400
incidentDescription:
On the evening of 11/13/12 I was putting my 5 1/2 month old son to bed. He had his baby congestion so filled up his Kaz Vicks model V400 humidifier and placed it approximately a foot from his head near the head of his crib.  This is a common suggestion from all pediatricians.  After putting him down to sleep  I turned it on, turned off the light and began to walk out of the room. When I had the door closed about 3/4 of the shut I heard to motor drone down in sound.  I opened the door back up and say sparks flying out of the unit.  I immediately ran and turned it off and unplugged it. Upon inspection the electrical wiring on the inside was burned.  Mind you this all happened about a foot from my sleeping infant.  Had I not heard the motor I fear a full blown fire would have erupted and with exceptional damage or death to my son!  After checking to see if it had been recalled I emailed the manufacturer with photos and an explanation of the incident.  I have finally heard back from them a full week after the incident! Obviously not a high priority for them.  

I have had trouble sleeping since this event and their lack of response has not helped.  I also cannot imagine putting another humidifier in his room.  This is causing me a great deal of stress since i know he will need one once again sometime in the future.  Something needs to be done to insure this model and this risk is not putting other families in danger.

Best regards,

[REDACTED]

productDescription: Portable heater
incidentDescription:
The consumer stated that he purchased two portable heaters in 2010, however, one of them was replaced because it caught on fire and the other because it stopped working.  

The replaced heater was on for approximately 1 hour, he smelled an odor of burnt plastic and smoke had dispersed in the rooms, he unplugged the unit and ventilated the house.  This incident triggered his smoke detectors as well.

There were no visible property damages, just the smell of smoke.  The heater was scorched and melted from overheating.

The manufacturer was contacted the following day of the incident and he was informed that it would be replaced.  Caller is concerned that these heaters are being replaced by refurbished heater which will cause a house fire.

productDescription: Perfect Flame gas grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription: I was using the Perfect Flame gas grill to make dinner for my family. There are 4 knobs across the front pf the grill, the knob 2nd from the left sounded as if the propane was getting low so I shut the knob off and just continued making the burgers. When I was done I left two of the burners on low so I could burn off the cheese, as I have done this many times before and then cleaned the grill with the brush. My daughter said the grill was on fire and I walked out the door and lifted the lid and sprayed a little water on it and the flame at first went down but then it came back even bigger, and thats when I realized the flame wasn't in the grill it was on fire underneath the grill. I could not turn off one of the knobs because the fire was shooting a flame out. I looked down under it so I could shut the gas off but that's where I realized the grill was on fire from the line of the grill to the propane tank. I kept a steady stream of water on it as I had just called for my husband to come quick and he just instructed me to keep the water spraying and he stuck his hand in where the fire was to shut off the propane. The whole right side of the grill is charred and melted.

productDescription: Electric, portable, space heater. Apx. 2.5 feet long. Black, digital thermostat and timer, tip-over cut-off, mesh grille, no fan. No serial number.
incidentDescription:
Electric portable heater labeled under "Soleil" brand. Model LH-875A, date code 0810, 120volt, 60hertz, 1500watt, Made by Shanghi Limach Manufacturing. No serial number listed. This heater served me well, but in the last few uses, I noted an orange glow from on of the small wire elements inside. I had not seen this before. I started unplugging it after use. Tonight, on low setting, automatic mode, set to 70 degrees, the heater clicked on, and orange and blue small flames and sparks started shooting from the bottom toward my carpet, and flashing out of the top, at the same location I saw the consistent orange glow, about four inches from the left end of the actual element inside the case. It was also crackling. I jumped up, and pulled the very warm plug out of the wall. I have never reported a product defect before, but never had one that nearly burned my house down. I read about this heater online, which with all reviews, must be taken with a grain of salt. (Everyone online thinks they are an expert). But I did notice that Home Depot, where I purchased the product, had terrible customer reviews for this particular unit, nearly all stating that it had failed at some point, a HUGE failure rate. Other similar heaters by different manufacturers, had consistently high ratings. I am concerned these units may lead to other incidents. Had I been using it in my bedroom and sleeping, it almost certainly would have caught the carpet on fire. I do not have the box or receipt, but I did purchase it in-store from a local Home Depot in the fall of 2010. It worked well until recently. It is used a few nights a week in either my master bedroom or living room, to take the chill out of the air. This incident occured in my living room, with it installed about a foot from my glass patio door, no where near drapes or other compustables. And using common sense, was plugged directly into a standard, grounded, 120 volt outlet, no extention cord or "power strip." I have good electrical knowledge, and know that would be terribly dangerous. There was no outside infulence from water, dampness, etc. That is what got me so upset, since the only fault of this near blaze was that of the heater itself. I am saving the unit, obviously not being used after this. I would be happy to ship it for inspection, as I am certain the same result will be recreated as soon as it is powered on. Any further questions, I am happy to oblige. I work during business hours, so e-mail is the best way to reach me. I appreciate your time and consideration. Happy Holidays.

[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]

productDescription:
Oster Toaster Oven
Model: 6058-126-001
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription:
Wife cooked 2 pizza bread slices at 350 deg. An hour later she noticed the oven seemed very hot. 
I placed cooking thermometer in oven: 347 deg. 
Checked further discovered that all indicators were in their normally off setting. 
Pressing Stop/Cancel had no effect. 
Unplugged oven and inserted power tester inline with power cord. 
Replugged and found oven drawing 551 watts. 
Tried controls again - set oven to broil, timer to 0:30 (seconds), start - did not count down, Stop/Cancel did turn element off. 
Power reduced to ~4 watts. 

Left thermometer in oven with alarm set to 122 deg. 
Checked several times during the night. 
21 Nov 2012 11:00 oven turned on without being touched and thermometer sounded alarm, Power = 530 watts.

productDescription: GE (made for Walmart) coffee maker overheated and melted the plastic housing around the plate.  we disconnected it.

We have an 18 month old 12 cup automatic coffeemaker.  It has the GE logo on it but on the data plate says made exclusively for Walmart.  It is a model # 898682.    Using it sunday it made a pot but the burner was stuck on high and it melted the plastic housing and was cintinuing to put out a very high heat melting the pot before we unplugged it.    

We showed the manager at Walmart and he said there was no rrecall on it, but perhaps there should be in the future if enough fail like this.

productDescription: Laptop Acer Aspire 5740-6491  Battery
incidentDescription:
My laptop Acer Aspire 6740-6491,  Shut down on its own while a child was using it on a hard table with adult supervision doing his homework.  When they picked it up,  they received a burn on their thumb bad enough to blister from the battery.  I do not see any recall notices on this make and model.  It is a few years old and out of warranty, I get that, but that does not make it alright to physically burn a consumer.  The battery is the original battery,  works fine and  holds a charge that lasts a couple of hours.  The system does not overheat and the battery does not get hot when you are using battery power only.  The problem seems to be when the unit is plugged in.  It was not a one time event.  It happens all of the time now.  The power cord sometimes gets hot, but not always.   The power cord gets hot enough that it is uncomfortable to hold but it does not cause burns.  It takes about 20 mins of electrical power for the battery to get to the burning point.  It does not seem to get hot if the unit is powered down  and but left to charge the battery.   So it is either the battery or the powercord, but I am thinking it is the battery.

I tried calling the toll free number for Acer multiple times but could not get past their automated phone system to report it.  [REDACTED] I am very disappointed in this company, who is not responsible enough to take consumer hazard calls regardless of warranty dates.  That makes Acer all the more at fault.     Had someone talked to me I would have been happy to accept a replacement battery and to send the current battery back so the issue could be researched and verified with appropiate recall notices issued.     I tried and email address that I found on a 3rd party recall site, and they replied back telling me to use there automated system.  Real bad.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

incidentDescription: Purchased Master Forge Stainless Steel Portable Gas Grill Model # GR4039-014247 from Lowes in Amarillo Texas. Regulator freezes up when using full 16 oz porpane cylinder. productDescription: Vacuum
incidentDescription:
We purchased an Oreck XL vacuum from the Oreck factory dealer in Salem, NH in the last week of June 2012. We have regularly used the vacuum since then on a daily basis. The vacuum is used for a few area rugs and 3 bedrooms.

On November 29, 2012 we realized the power cord was completely frayed at the handle area. We only noticed this on accident. The rubber outer insulation is breaking away from the harder rubber going into the handle. This exposes the the white and black wires inside as well as some strings that we are guessing they use to prevent the wires from being bent inside the cord.

We took the vacuum back to the dealer and he reluctantly said we could leave it with him for a few days and he would attempt to repair. He really didn't seem like he wanted to repair the vacuum.
We contacted Oreck customer care and they only referred us to a different dealer in Nashua, NH which is a 30 minute drive from here.

We believe that with such a possibility of having exposed A/C electrical wires that the dealer or Oreck should have given us a new vacuum (since it is less than 5 months old) instead of offering to repair over several days. What are you supposed to do? Go and buy another vacuum while they repair a basically brand new vacuum that could cause electrocution? We don't even know how long the power cord has been like this as the place where it is falling apart is under the handle and hard to notice. 

We believe other people must have seen similar problems with their Oreck XL power cords (near the handle).
