incidentDescription:
U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission
Attn: Reports
4330 East West Highway
Bethesda, MD 20814

Customer Service Center
Lowe's Companies, Inc.
1000 Lowe's Boulevard
Mooresville, NC 28117

Garden Treasures 11000 BTU Tabletop
Liquid Propane Patio Heater
Item #: 48221 I Model #: HPS-C-PC
I bought one of these from Lowes and after several months it quit.

I called three different times 888-775-1330 and the first time, they had me disassemble
the top portion to expose the pilot and use compressed air to blow it out.

The next day they had me disassemble it and expose the copper tube & orfice and blow
them out.

When I lit it, flames came out the lower section of the burner box at the top of the
extension tube.

I called a third time and the tech started into another fiasco and I told him, hell this is a
relative new unit and I don't want to be doing a bench repair on a product you should be
fixing or standing behind.

I bet there is a recall on it or there should be.

When I worked on it the third time I discovered that there was a main burner tube
connection that apparently is a slip fit and was most of the way out.

This is not safe and I refuse to go another hour on it.

Lowes should not be selling these unless they take responsibility.

My unit is serial number 20110710674 Model HPS-C-PC.

Your website had one purchaser state: "it just shut down all gas went off including the
pilot light. Thinking it may be a problem with the mechanism I called Lowes, the
manager told me it may be a bad thermo-coupler, to bring it in for an exchange. I did.
The new one has the exact same issue! I called the support number on the
instruction/warantee book they are AWESOME by the way. Come to find out, this is a
known issue with these heaters!

NOW WHY IS IT THAT LOWES SELLS THIS AND HAS "QUESTIONS
PROBLEMS MISSING PARTS ETC. CALL 1-888-775-1330"?

Maybe I should have done what that guy did and call Lowes, but I did not; I invested
three days of my life trying to fix a propane driven appliance that could become a bomb.
What do you want to do about this or should I turn this over to a consumer regulatory
body for a safety check?

productDescription:
Heat n Glo Vienna II gas LP green cast iron stove - vented
Glass door and side shelves
productType: Gas or Lp Heaters, Other or Not Specified (392)
incidentDescription:
I have a Heat n Glo Vienna II green cast iron gas LP stove. I bought it in December 2001 from the dealer Frederick Block in Winchester VA. It was installed in January 2002 by an HVAC/plumbing/electrical contractor into a new home that we built. We moved into the house in March 2002 and since winter was over, the stove was not used for the first time until the following winter in 2003. It is located in our family room. This stove has had normal use - primarily for pleasure - it was never the main heating source for the room it is in. Since 2003 it has been used maybe a total of 20 hours a week during the winter months of November - February, operating via a remote control/thermostat setting that turned it on/off automatically based on the temp setting. In the past week I was having trouble with it not lightning properly when I used the remote to turn it on, and pilot light went out for no reason, and I noticed that it also looked like the logs had moved inside the stove. I called a technician who looked at the stove on Friday, Nov. 23rd. He found the following:

* The metal plate the logs rest on is rusted very badly - tech said due to the condensation of the water in the LP gas before it burned off. I would have thought Heat n Glo would have taken that into account in the stove design and would have used a metal that would not corrode from the water in the gas. One of the pieces that was designed to hold a log had completely rusted through and a chunk had broken off, which is why the logs had moved. 

* The pilot light kept going out when the tech tried to light it. Upon investigation, he found that the burner pan had many cracks in it and the gas was seeping through the cracks with enough force to blow out the pilot - instead of coming through the holes in the pan as it should have. Tech said WE COULD HAVE HAD A CATASTROPHIC EXPLOSION! He said the stove was totally unsafe to use, was at high risk for an explosion, and he turned off the gas to it. Where did the cracks come from? We didn't do anything to cause it. It had to be defective from the manufacturer.

Tomorrow I will be calling Heat n Glo and also the dealer who sold it  (they were both closed due to Thanksgiving till 11/26) to see if there is any warranty or recall on this stove. I wonder if there aren't other Vienna I and II stoves out there where this is also occurring, which is why I am filing this report with you. I am very sad about this because I loved that stove, but I believe it is a disaster waiting to happen to someone - could have already happened for all I know. And even if under warranty and the parts or stove itself can be replaced, I don't want another stove with the same faulty design that might blow us up. So I may just be out my $2000 I paid for this stove, unless there is a newer stove with a better design that Heat n Glo is willing to give me to replace this one. 

I also have 2 of the Heat n Glo 6000TRI gas log units in fireplaces - 1 in living room and 1 in master bedroom - that I am having checked out to see if they might have burner pad/leaking gas defects. They were also installed new when house was built in 2002 but have rarely been used. FYI all the Heat n Glo units are vented to the outside and are plumbed directly into the 1000 gallon underground propane gas tank in our yard that also provides gas to the hot water heater, house furnaces, and backp generator. 

I have seen that there are recalls on some Heat n Glo units - but I don't know if there are any recalls on the ones I have. Are there recalls on the 6000TRI fireplace logs or Vienna II stove? 

Does a manufacturer have to stand behind a defective product, such as this stove that could have blown up and killed us, or am I just out the money and left with a green cast iron piece of junk that I'm afraid to use, and Heat n Glo walks away without any responsibility to make it good? I have seen some dealers online that are still selling Vienna I and II, although the stoves are no longer listed under those names as available products on the Heat n Glo web site. Are they perhaps still being sold, but under a new name?

Mintek Portable DVD Player model # MDP-1815 (together with rechargeable battery pack RB-Li 55, which has serial number 24D0510250877L) gave off burning odor and smoke during use.  

CPSC already has posted a recall that describes the same kind of incident, specifically for the rechargeable battery pack (Release #05-187).  However, the recall refers to different model numbers for both the main product and battery pack.  Your recall specifies DVDs with model number DVD-1710.  However, the model involved in this incident is MDP-1815.  Your recall specifies battery packs marked RB-LiP01 or RB-LiP02, but the battery pack attached to the model involved in this incident is marked RB-Li 55.  

Release #05-187 appears to be the only CPSC recall for a Mintek product.  Therefore, I am providing this information because you may wish to amend and/or widen your advisory information to consumers.  

Please note that the relevant fields below do not permit me to note the following information: what appears to be the DVD player serial number is printed on a white sticker placed in a black box outline that is printed directly on the bottom of the product.  Directly over the box outline, also printed in black directly on the product, is the phrase "DATE OF MANUFACTURE".

productDescription:
Honeywell oil-filled digital radiator heater
Model HZ-709
Manufactured by KAZ Inc. - sold by Honeywell at Wal-Mart
incidentDescription:
Honeywell oil-filled digital radiator heater
Model HZ-709
Produced by KAZ Inc. - sold by Honeywell at Wal-Mart

I own several Honeywell oil filled digital radiator heaters. One of them nearly burned my house down yesterday and I thought you should know what happened.
I had run the heater overnight and in the morning turned the unit off my pushing the on/off switch as usual. The unit clicked off, all the lights went off as usual and the unit appeared to be off. I left home for several hours, came home and went into the bedroom which was very, very hot and had a strange smell. I went to the heater which still had all of its lights off, still appeared off, and yet the unit was too hot to even touch. Obviously the on/off switch had shorted out and so too had obviously the thermostat. The unit was stuck on and was heating all day. This was a very dangerous situation and I an afraid to think what might have happened had I not come home early.

This has happened more than once.  This happens with the water below the level of the spout, and has happened when the burner on the stove was on "medium".

productDescription: It is a Grillrite propane gas grill made by Fiesta Grills.  2-burners only.
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
Defective propane gas regulator model RA329 manufactured by Ningbo Wanan, China. Product was included in the purchase of a Grillrite brand outdoor gas barbeque grill. Regulator functioned well several times before failing. On or about the 7th use, the regulator failed upon ignition of grill. Uncontrolled flames shot out from regulator where it connects to the propane tank.  I was able to access the main valve at the 20-lb propane cylinder to shut-off gas flow.  Fortunately there was no explosion and no injuries occurred.  Just lucky I guess.

The second occurrance was on 11/01/12 but this time I hear the propane gas escaping from the connection where the regulator meets the propane tank.  I was able to shut it off and disconnect the regulator unit.  This was a replacement that I purchased but made by the same company, in Ningbo Wanan, China.  

something needs to be done to stop this company from exporting defective regulator units before someone gets killed in an explosion.  I am surprised that the agency has not stopped the import of this product as I am not the only one who has reported the same problem.

Minor injury (burns to hand) ocurred as user tried to  Replacement of regulator with a different brand/model resolved issue.

productDescription: Electric steam mop
incidentDescription:
While using a EuroPro Shark steam Pocket Mop, the steam channel melted and became clogged.  Upon inspecting the unit as to while it was not functioning and releasing steam, the mop head exploded away from the unit, and steam was release in an uncontrolled fashion.  Luckily, no one was hurt, but the steam jet was about 1-2 feet in the air as reflected off of a tile floor.  Any hands in the way would have been scalded and burned.  Small pieces of the melted plastic steam channel had broken off, and were found on the floor after the steam had finished releasing.  If the mop had been pointing up as opposed to at the floor when the explosion occurred, these may have become projectiles.

This mop had been replaced under warranty for a similar clog which resulted in the non-function of the unit.  The first mop had internal tubes rupture, without outward explosion.  However, that unit was broken at that point.  The replacement unit failed outwardly, which is considerably more dangerous.  Both units had been filled with tap water with each use.  I would believe that calcification due to tap water minerals would have clogged the first unit, but a melted steam channel in the second would not be caused by minerals in water.

productDescription:
Baby Bullet is a food mixer that is designed and marketed to make pureed food for babies. The piece that is defaulted is a removable clear plastic ring that is in outer edge of the blade attachments  
for the blender. It seals the bottom blade attachment to the blender cup.
incidentDescription:
I purchased my Baby Bullet in December 2011 and was using it as instructed when the inner plastic sealant ring came off and was blended into the food I was making for my 7 month old daughter. Not only did the ring get chopped up and mixed with the food but it is also clear in color and hard to see. I have read many reviews of this product and this exact issue happening with other people on sites for Target, Babies R Us, Amazon and more. While Baby Bullet is now making this item so that the sealant ring is permanent within the mixer, many people still own the earlier version of this product where it is not permanent. This is a very hazardous issue and I would like this to be recalled and for people who own the baby bullet to be made aware of this possible risk.

______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________



Reports Department of Consumer Product Safety Commission,

I own and have been using the "Baby Bullet" product to make my daughter's  food for about a month. 
The other  day I was using the "milling blade" (there is more than one blade attachment that comes 
with the baby bullet)  in the short cup to blend her food and the sealant ring came off while the 
food was blending, and was cut up by the blade and mixed with the food.  I noticed the plastic 
pieces in the food and luckily did not serve that to my 7 month old daughter. I had followed the 
washing instructions and also checked this ring to make sure that everything was properly secured 
and this still happened.

Today I spoke with a lady in customer  service named [REDACTED] at [REDACTED] and I told  her of my ring 
coming off and being blended into the food.  She offered to replace my part with  one that has the 
permanent sealant ring.  I told her that I would indeed like this part replaced, but in addition to my 
replacement part, I would  like this hazardous issue to be addressed and recalled publically. I mentioned 
to her that I am aware that there have been multiply reports  of this exact incident happening  to other 
people and she said she was unaware that this was an issue. I asked her to have someone that has that 
authority to please contact me so that I can make this same request of them. I received a call from [REDACTED] 
and made the same request that this item be recalled and he said this was not something that felt 
necessary to do. This is a choking hazard and I expect this item to be publically  recalled so that, in the 
future, no person is at risk of unknowingly serving their  baby small pieces of plastic that could 
potentially cause harm and choking.

I have read reviews of this same thing happening to other  owners of this product on the websites 
of Target, Babies R Us, Amazon and more. This is unacceptable  that this has been happening  and, 
up to this point, nothing has been done.  Please help me in having this product  recalled and 
owners of this defective  blade with removable sealant ring be made aware of this hazard.

productDescription: Black & Decker LH4500 Type II Leaf Hog (leaf blower and vacuum).  Hand held, electric motored unit.
productSubCategory: Lawn Mowers, Leaf Blowers and Lawn Vacuums
incidentDescription: I was using a Black & Decker LH4500 Leaf Hog to vacuum leaves when a heard a loud "bang" and was knocked to the ground by an impact on my right leg.  When I was able to get up I discovered that the cast aluminum impeller in the unit had come apart.  The largest fragment was embedded in the units housing while a smaller fragment (about 2" X 2 1/2") had gone through the housing and hit me in the leg.  I was wearing very heavy work pants but still experienced broken skin in a "check mark" shape on the right leg about 4" above the knee.  The area around the point of impact (about the size of my hand) started to swell and bruise.  Now (5 days later) some swelling persists, the bruising has become deeper, and I still experience some discomfort with every step.  I was very fortunate to have been hit in the leg and be wearing heaving pants.  Had this fragment hit me in the face, neck, ankle, or knee, it could resulted in a significant injury or even death.  I have been in contact with Black and Decker and am providing the unit for engineering analysis.  As a former engineer I consider the unit unsafe (refusing B&D's offer to provide a replacement) because of the relatively brittle properties of cast aluminum, its use in a corrosive environment under cyclic loads (with the potential for fatigue failure), and a plastic case that is obviously incapable for containing such a failure.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription: HEAT RECOVERY SYSTEM
productType: Heaters or Heating Systems, Other or Not Specified (393)
manufacturer: Venmar Ventilation - Venmar CES - Broan Nutona Canada
incidentDescription:
2000 we built a home.  We installed a heat recovery system HRV by BRYANT. The system worked for about 3 years, we notice it was running all the time and it did not work right with the wall control. 

(1) 2004 We called a heating guy out, was the same one that installed the system, the board in the HRV was bad and had a burnt spot on it. He check out all controls and replaced board, it worked fine for two years. 

(2) 2006 We notice again it was not working, this time we called the wholesaler and Venmar in Canada about the problem along with pictures; All Air put that board in. He checked all controls everything good. 

(3) 2008 We had the same problem and again we put this board in. We pulled out all controls to check is there was a short; everything was clean. 

(4) 2009 Again the unit was not operating by the control. We again talked to the distributors also Venmar they sent me a recall part to have installed on the motor by the heating guy and a new board. T and T Heating did the work. I shipped the board to Venmar for inspection, did not hear from them for a year, we called them and they had no information for me. Our home is very tight and needs the HRV to bring in fresh air, again the part went. 

(5) The system worked for just over a year and now has quit working. We are stump on this Bryant HRV, have called T and T Heating to come out, they are avoiding us…small town only a few heating guys here, have no faith in them. I had electrical out to check my box...everything clean, I am suspecting something is causing the board to blow, could it be motor, I think we replaced that a wild back. The place where the board was seem very warm. I am calling Venmar in morning, my concern is the air quality and the tightness in home also possibly fire. If you can give me any info I would appreciate it.

productDescription: Venmar  Model AVS Duo 1.9; Serial # 9N 08000621435  Heat exhanger/ventilator
productType: Gas or Lp Heaters, Other or Not Specified (392)
manufacturer: Venmar Ventilation - Venmar CES - Broan Nutona Canada
incidentDescription: While investigating why my garage unit heater (natural gas) was not turning on I discovered a tripped breaker.  The Venmar Heat recovery/ Ventilation unit was plugged into the same circuit as the heater.  through process of elimination I found the Venmar to be the cause of the breaker tripping.  I then removed the front cover of the Venmar AVS Duo 1.9 as in performing the annual cleaning, and found the motor to be ~150 degrees F.  I verified that the fan was free to turn (though somewhat stiff) and tried to run it while observing.  The motor appeared to get power, move a few degrees, and lock up.  I isolated the power, removed the motor and lubed the bearings with a couple of drops of oil and was able to free up the shaft to spin freely.  I reassembled and tried powering it up again without the fan cages on the shafts and it immediately bumped, froze up, and heated up.  I did not let it go long enough to trip the breaker.  the motor is apparently not as thermally protected as it should be, and though I haven't disassembled it yet, it may not be designed to be used in a vertical installation.

productDescription: Kenmore vacuum cleaner Model 116.27514
incidentDescription:
I purchased a Kenmore Model 116.27514 vacuum cleaner in Feb 2010.  This is a cannister vacuum with the sweeper mounted on a handle.  The sweeper can be detached to allow different attachments to be fitted to the handle.  In Aug, 2011 I noticed that the light and vacuum were turning on and off on the sweeper as I pulled it back and forth.  When I investigated I found the insulation on the electrical cord that connects the sweeper to the handle completely worn through.  There were wires bundled in that sheath and the insulation on the wiring was also worn though.  There was a black area as if something had arc-ed.  I called Sears and ordered a replacement part figuring that the cord had been damaged or mishandled by me.  I installed the replacement part and have used the sweeper roughly 50 times since then.  Last week I noticed that the same wear had occured.  I caught it early enough that the insulation on the wires is not worn.  I know that I have not mishandled the vacuum or done anything unusual that would have caused this.  I attribute the wear to poor design and feel continuing to use this product poses a risk. 

I sent an email to Sears today alerting them to this problem.

productDescription: TEC Char-Broil Grill - Model Number 463268407 - Part Number 80008993 is the one leaking the gas.
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
TEC - Char-Broil Gril - Model Number - 463268407 - 

The heads of the bolts are falling off the TEC Infrared Burners.  They are coming off due to the heat generated by the burners themselves.  The bolts fall onto the top of the TEC Burner. This is causing movement in the burners themselves.  Making matters worse, the burners themselves are flaking apart allowing gas to come up in bursts.  The burners will go from working fine, to having a rapid popping noise as the gas escapes from the burner in small bursts, then a flash explosion on the grill surface will shoot a flame approximately 1'x1' across the top of the burner.  The burner then blows out with the gas still flowing.  The burner must be then shut off and relit.  It will go back to working fine, then popping, then explosion, and blowing out.

I thought this was normal until I read the other filed complaint and spoke with where I purchased the grill.

productDescription: Black & Decker Spacemaker Coffeemaker Model #SDC740B with a plug #940YA
incidentDescription: I own a Black & Decker Space saver  Coffeemaker of which the handle of the Carafe broke while I was pouring a full pot of coffee spilling hot coffee on my wife's lap and my self.   When I tried to order a new carafe from the company they told me there was a recall of that particular machine.  They then told me that they were going to replace same of which I was satisfied. [REDACTED]

incidentDescription: We are writing this on behalf of our son.  This matter concerns a TEM 500 Back to Basics toaster (originally purchased by my wife and myself years ago but since passed on to our son in very good condition).  Our son has reported to us that this toaster had come within seconds of self igniting into what could have become a serious apartment fire here in Seattle.  Here is a quick summary of the situation:  On 5/22/2012 our son was awakened from his sleep at exactly 2:24 am by a loud electrical buzzing noise coming from the plugged in TEM 500 toaster.  Yes, the toaster was plugged into the wall socket but it was definitely in the "off" position.  The toaster had apparently reached a very dangerous hot temperature and was emitting noxious fumes.  In short, the toaster was aggressively burning itself from the inside out.  Our son told us he was severely shaken up mentally and unable to concentrate properly at work the next day from lack of sleep and emotional exhaustion.  Our son still is in possession of the toaster.  Like the prior complainant (here at safeproducts.gov) we had contacted the company who wants us to mail back the toaster which we are still mulling over.  In reply to our complaint the company rep has told us that the toaster instructions call for the user to unplug the toaster after every use to prevent such incidents.  We ask you...is this ever a cop out or what?  Seriously now, how many people would go ahead and buy a toaster or any kitchen appliance for that matter having known in advance that unless the appliance was unplugged after each and every use a fire might result! We think this is a very convenient way for this company to cover their you know what.  And, indeed, it was not terribly difficult to find out about other very similar self igniting scenarios with the TEM 500 with a simple [REDACTED]  search.  As a concerned family we are not exaggerating when we say this could have been a disaster if the toaster self ignited while our son was away at work during the day. At the very least we felt this merits reporting to the federal government for a possible recall on the TEM 500.

productDescription: 1.2 litre Deep Fryer
incidentDescription:
Following is CC of correspondance with manufacturer;

Good morning;

 

My wife and I received a Bella Kitchen 1.2 liter fryer from our daughter and her family as a Christmas gift last year. The unit is your model number XJ-6K116G. 

 

It has had light use  and has been cleaned in accordance with the instruction manual and towel dried after each use. It has not been immersed in water. Up until last night it has operated to designed intent. 

 

Please refer to the attached photos. There is one each of the front, the base, and of the interior of the appliance.

 

Last evening I experienced an unacceptable failure. I plugged the fryer into the outlet and set the thermostat to high in preparation for use. The indicator light came on and I went about preparing the rest of the meal. When the preheat cycle was complete and the light went out, I placed the chicken in the fryer basket, lowered the basket into the hot oil and installed the lip on the fryer. I set the timer  for four minutes and went on preparing the meal. When the timer went off I turned around and was greeted with the sight of 350* oil pooled on the countertop beneath the fryer, across the countertop and down the face of the cabinetry, which was on the countertop adjacent to our Jenn Air gas cook top. 

 

I immediately pulled the plug out of the receptacle in order to shut off the power to the unit and grabbed the fire extinguisher. This morning, after the mess was cleaned up, I washed the fryer and examined it carefully. The aluminum interior housing, which serves as the oil vessel, has numerous small holes in it, which allowed the oil to leak out of the fryer. See attached photos. The largest areas of aluminum decomposition are noted by the red arrows. 

 

This failure poses an unacceptable safety hazard due to the potential for accidental contact with superheated cooking oil flowing over the countertop, not to mention damage to cabinetry and the potential for fire when the oil comes in contact with the adjacent gas cook top.

 

Your prompt reply to this matter is requested.

 
[REDACTED] 

CC; US Consumer Product Safety Commission

productDescription: 23" Round Fire Pit
incidentDescription:
I recently purchased the Round Fire Pit (SKU: 2595032, Model: DS-4724) from my local Menards, and have found it to be both a highly inferior as well as downright dangerous product.

I realize that this is an inexpensive firepit ($49), but I do not think I have unrealistic expectations even given the price level.

The first issue was assembling the firepit, which was no easy task give the incredible poor craftsmanship, which left many screw holes un-punched, and dimensions that were not to-spec, making things much snugger fit than they should have been.  After assembling the unit, we placed a grill cover over it to protect it from the elements and to prevent rust. A week later, we decided to have our first fire in it.  We took the grill cover off, and placed three small logs in, and got a fire going. Just about the time that the fire had caught, one of the legs snapped off. In one week this pitiful excuse for a firepit had rusted through its leg, spilling flaming logs and hot ash everywhere. Honestly, I cannot believe how horribly irresponsible and negligent Menards has acted in selling such a poorly made and dangerous product, all in the name of making an easy buck.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription: DoughPro SL1577A Grill
incidentDescription:
I purchased a clamshell grill model SL1577A from DoughPro in Perris CA. It was duly delivered. We plugged it in and set the operating parameters, but did not put it into use immediately.
On June 23 of this year we experienced a power failure at our place of business. We closed the business and went home. Later my wife had occasion to return to the place of business. Power had been restored and the place full of smoke. The source of the smoke was the mentioned grill - I had left some papers on the grill surface. Checking it the following day I determined that the grill would activate whenever power was connected and run up to its pre-programmed temperature, in this case 450 degrees. I initially thought that the unit had possibly been damaged by a power spike and consulted with the manufacturer on Monday June 25. To my astonishment, the company confirmed that the appliance was working correctly since it was programmed to respond as it did. I told them that it was an unacceptable fire hazard, and that I would not be using the appliance. They agreed to send me a revised chipset. I have rechecked the unit different times and its response is allways the same. Disconnect the power - plug it back in and the unit heats to its programmed values. Any power interruption has the same effect. 
Two months later I again spoke with the same person and she indicated that she would need to speak with a supervisor before taking any action - she had apparently done nothing. Two subsequent voicemail messages went unanswered. 
My next course of action was to contact INTERTEK, the testing agency. Their concerns involve client privacy issues, and informed me that they may not be able to inform me of their investigative findings. 
Meanwhile I will not be using this product until its safety deficiencies are addressed. 
I am, of course, aware that many users of this appliance are likely unaware of this hazard and solicit the assistance of your office in facilitating a solutiom to this problem.

[REDACTED]

productDescription: Eureka Air Speed 13 Amp Vacuum Cleaner Black and Yellow in color.
incidentDescription: We purchased the Eureka Air Speed 13 amp vacuum cleaner (Model AS1000, Type A, Serial # UU321219000949) at Walmart on August 11th of 2012.  After approximately 4 uses significant wear began to show on the vacuum cleaner's power cord.  The rubber coating on the outside of the cord appeared to have been damaged by the vacuum cleaner when it was accidentally run over.  In 3-4 spots on the cord the entire protective outer sheathing of the wire was gone exposing the smaller inner wires.  On 3-4 other spots the rubber outer protective sheathing on the wire showed significant wear/chaffing.  This is an electricution hazard for consumers.  The outer sheathing of the wire is not durable enough and should not be that easily damaged when it is incidentally run over by the vacuum.  The wire appears to have a material flaw.  This is a very popular vacuum used by many consumers.  Some one could be seriously injured or killed if this problem is not addressed promptly.

productDescription:
Whirlpool 50 Pint Dehumidifier Model AD50USL3
White plastic, approximately 2 feet high
incidentDescription:
Items: 2 Whirlpool 50 Pint Dehumidifiers Model AD50USL3
Serial Numbers: QP1820933 and QP1821048

Both units were in use in my basement. When I went into the basement I noticed an electrical burning odor. I eventually determined that it was coming from one of the dehumidifiers. I looked up any recalls on these units and found that a recall Release #02-096 was for serial number beginning with QL, but not for units beginning for QP like my units. Seeing that the recall stated that the units were overheating and causing fires. I also found a Whirlpool document that stated "certain internal components including wire terminals and switches can overheat.  This can result in fire and cause personal injury or property damage."

I was concerned that my dehumidifiers might have the same problem, so I took the cover off the units to see if there was something that needed to be cleaned. I also took the cover off the compressor and found that the wiring on the overload switch on both units was brittle and bare and had shorted against the metal rod coming from the top of the compressor that it was tightly pulled against (I have photos showing both overload switches). I assume that the burning odor was from the bare wire that was shorting against the metal rod, which I believe is an electrical and fire hazard. On both units this wire as so short that it was pulled tightly against the metal rod. In addition, other wires and terminal plugs on both units were brittle, cracked, and broken - which are also electrical and fire hazards. That area was also very hot.

She doesn't remember what did happened, she was only aware that the index finger on right hand on the side in a triangle which is why the skin popped out and the pinkie then ring finger on the second joint,  on her left hand were cut and she was bleeding.

Her ring finger on her left hand is remaining numb and she can't straighten it and her pinkie on the left hand is sliced vertically as if a knife or cutting utensil dropped sliced and folded her skin, the cut is down to her first knuckle.

She cannot remember what happened, she remembers only that she was holding it one second and the next second it was lying in four pieces and she was bleeding profusely.

Caller's 8yr old daughter called an ambulance and caller was transported to the nearby hospital emergency room where she was given strong pain medication and received 18 stitches total for the three fingers.

She was released later that night being advised that she would need to speak with a plastic surgeon within just a couple of days because they are not positive that they were able to repair it adequately.

She would ask that an investigator look at these slow cookers for weak spots or defects and recall them.

She has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.

productDescription: Char Broil Patio Bistro Infrared Gas Grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
Char-Broil Patio Bistro Gas Grill

I purchased the above model grill from Amazon on May 23, 2012. Yesterday I had an incident while using the grill. After the grill was lit and warming up, for some reason the flame went out. I noticed this because after about 5 minutes, the grill was cold. I went to turn off the gas and the explosion that resulted could have seriously injured me. I firmly believe had the cover been closed, which is what I normally do when warming up the grill, it is probable that a serious perhaps even a fatal injury could have occurred. 

The grill has a design defect that must be corrected. Until this defect is corrected, the grill should be removed from the market. I am certain others must have experienced this problem.

The design defect is as follows:
When you turn on the grill using the control knob, the first position you come to is the igniter. This ignites the gas. The problem and defect is that if for any reason the flames goes off,  gas continues to flow into the grill. When you go to turn off the gas, you must pass the same igniter position to turn the gas off. This ignites any accumulated gas causing a potential life threatening situation.
I believe this grill should be removed from the market.

productDescription: Infinite Hot Pink Curling Iron manufactured by Royale USA www.royalusa.com  1-800-965-0302
productType: Hair Curlers, Curling Irons, Clips & Hairpins (1682)
incidentDescription:
Royale Infinite Hot Pink Curling Iron.  www.royaleusa.com  Family member purchased this product and sustained a burn to the hand/wrist during use. It presents a burn/safety hazard in the following 3 ways and should be taken off of the market.

1.  The "curling" part that gets extremely hot has no cover at all, it is completely exposed. There is nothing to protect a small child from grabbing the end and sustaining a burn.
2. It lacks an indicator light. There is no light to indicate if it is off or on and could be extremely hot.  
3.  No temperature setting to control/regulate how hot it becomes. 

I have spoken to the company directly and was told there was nothing they could do and they would not refund my money.  The retail price on this poorly made and dangerous product was $130.  

Thanks for your attention to this matter.

productDescription: Hoover Platinum Collection Carpet Cleaner    Manf code:  F10A   Model:  F8100900   Series BB10.5
incidentDescription:
Bought Hoover Platinum Collection Carpet Cleaner about 1 1/2 years ago.  Used about 5 times since then.  Cleaner still like new.  

On 9/18/2012 began to clean carpet in bedroom 1.  Cleaner began making a really loud rumbling noise.  I stopped the cleaner to make sure that I had all containers for solution, water, and dirty water in properly.  They were.  Turned cleaner back on.  Noise began again and grew even louder.  

Then machine began bellowing out white - horrible smelling smoke - enough smoke to fill up the second level (2300+ sq ft) of my home.  Just as I thought "what in the world?" here come some flames shooting out toward me and then toward the drapes.  Scary!  

I immediately turned off the machine, ran and unplugged it, and began to move it away from the bed and drapes and toward the tile in the master bath.  As I was doing this I noticed the carpet in this bedroom was charred black!! 

The machine was so hot that - as I was attempting to get it into the master bath - it even charred the carpet in the master bedroom just by rolling over it!!!!   

I finally managed to get the machine into the bath, turned it on it's side to get the "hot portion" of the unit off the floor and into the air and the ran to the windows to open them and turn on the ceiling fans to get the smoke and the smell out of the house.  

God was with me.  There is no other explanation.  Otherwise the drapes, the bed, the carpet, and me would have caught on fire!!!!!    Plus the smell...oh my.  I get migraines and needless to say this scare and smell triggered a fantastic one that stayed for two days.  

Once I had done these steps, I called the 800 number for Hoover to report what just happened.  They could have cared less.  They told me to take photos - I did.  They asked if I wanted to file a claim on the damage.  I do.  They then stated that I should get a repair/replace estimate.  I have.  They also stated they would contact FedEx and have FedEx email me a shipping label to send the machine back to them.  

To date I have NOT received the label yet.  I have called and emailed Hoover several times.  They ignore me.  The only response I get is one rep did leave a message and said the label was sent to me last Tuesday and if I did not have it I must have deleted it.  

I received 2nd and 3rd degree burns last year from a brush fire on both my legs.  Needless to say when this carpet cleaner did this I nearly went into shock!  I want this dangerous machine out of my home.  However, Hoover is doing nothing to help this process along.  

I sincerely think something should be published on these machines and this company should take responsibility for making such a dangerous piece of home cleaning equipment.

productDescription: Kitchenaide Electric Countertop Coffee Maker, Model #KCM111OB, Black and Silver with a round digital clock display, push button controls and a removable water tank in the back
incidentDescription: I purchased a Kitchenaide Countertop Coffee Maker (Model # KCM111OB) in May of this year. About two months later, I began having issues with it. It shorted out just after it finished brewing. I unplugged it and let it dry throughly and began using it again. It seemed okay until about a month later when I tried to run it through it's first cleaning cycle. After the cleaning cycle, it would no longer brew. The water would not filter through the maker and when I touched it, it was incredibly hot. I did not actually burn myself; but it was much hotter than any coffee maker I've ever used has gotten. At that point, I contacted Kitchenaide via e-mail. I described the issues and asked them what we could do. we went back and forth a bit because I actually wanted my money back so I could buy a different coffee maker. However, all they would do was send me a new one of the same thing because that's all their warranty allowed for. I was not pleased; but I accepted the replacement. I have had the replacement one for three weeks now. At the end of the first week, it began doing the same things as the original one - it shorted out once and sometimes does not filter the water through when it should be brewing. I think this coffee maker is dangerous and could easily result in a house fire or burn injury.

productDescription: Cuisinart classic 12 cup Programmable Coffeemaker DCC-1100 (black)
incidentDescription:
This morning, my Cuisinart DCC-1100 Series coffee pot (of several years) began to smoke. I regularly set it to brew automatically in the morning. As I was sitting at the kitchen table, I noticed that the machine was making an unusual popping/clicking sound. I didn't pay much attention until I heard it again, and the noise didn't sound like the normal clicks of brewing, since the coffee was already made. I noticed the red "on" light was off, which I didn't do, and the pot wasn't set to turn off automatically for another hour. (We just had GFI outlets installed because we just moved into an older home). Then as I went over to inspect the machine, I noticed and smelled plastic burning and saw smoke coming up around the coffee pot. I immediately unplugged it, and took it outside. If I had not been at home or if I had forgotten to turn it off today and waited for the auto shut-off, I could have had a kitchen fire after I went to work. Nobody would have been home!

I researched online and found a thread of similar complaints:
http://www.consumeraffairs.com/homeowners/cuisinart.html

Thanks for your time,
[REDACTED]

incidentDescription: The fire department purchased 234 [REDACTED] smoke alarms to distribute to low income and elderly families in the community. incidentDescription:
In May 2012, we purchased a Webber (Genesis E320) from Home Depot. We soon noticed that the “grease tray” which is supposed to direct away the grease into the waste container, has a few design flaws. 
1. The Grease Tray was not properly directing the grease away and into the waste container; causing the grease to remain in the tray.
2. Grease Tray was located too close to the heat source; causing the grease to burn and make gross smelling smoke.

We had to manually clean the grease tray after each use since the grease was not led to the waste container.

On Wednesday September 12, we grilled 2 T-bone steaks. The meat had some fat and the drips were creating some smoke. I opened the BBQ to check the meat and suddenly the whole BBQ went on "FIRE"!!! I am pregnant (on a high risk pregnancy) and I was totally shocked and scared. I turned off all the keys and shut the door and turned to run inside to inform my husband. But as I turned I caught into a chair and fell on the ground. My 7 year old daughter just opened the door and called for help. My husband helped me move away and got the fire extinguisher and turned off the fire. Although he also burned the palm of his hand as the handle was too hot and the fire was everywhere.

We are totally frustrated to be sold an “unsafe” product which has a fire safety issues. We would like to get our money back and also an investigation be issued on the safety of this product and a possible "RECALL".

productDescription: The product is a new HEPA filter insert (HON24000) for my 10-yr old [REDACTED] air purifier. I purchased the product from Amazon.com, and their supplier was AllergyBeGone (866-234-6630). The product came with a small identifying sticker: RPS Products / BestAir / 847-683-3400. The new HEPA filter insert is white overall, and donut-shaped about 16-in in diameter and 12-in tall. The interior hole diameter is about 10 inches. The product is flat on top and bottom, and covered on top and bottom with what looks like white rubber. The inner and outer sides of the product are covered with what looks like clear/white plastic mesh. Inside the mesh is what looks like close-folded vertical folds of stiff white porous paper.
brand: unknown, did not save box. Invoice calls product HON24000
incidentDescription:
I purchased a new HEPA filter insert ([REDACTED]) and charcoal pre-filter (HON38002) for my old [REDACTED] air purifier. The products came from AllergyBeGone (866-234-6630) via Amazon.com.  I am reporting the HEPA filter insert (HON24000) as unsafe. It came with a small identifying sticker: RPS Products / BestAir / 847-683-3400. The new HEPA filter insert is white overall. All previous HEPA filter inserts I have purchased for the air purifier have been black outside. I first used the new HEPA filter on 8/13/12. 

I have operated my air purifier with the new HEPA filter in place three times. All three times when I turned on the unit I immediately noticed a strong organic chemical sort of smell, a smell too objectionable for me to remain in the room. Never before have I experienced any sort of smell when using the air purifier (I have owned it since it was new, perhaps more than 10 years ago, and have purchased and used several replacement HEPA filters and charcoal pre-filters through the years). 

I ran the air purifier for 3 hours each time on two different days and in two different rooms. The smell was just as strong after each time, so I turned off the air purifier, opened the windows and, after a time, was able to return to the room. On both occasions the next morning I awoke with a sore throat, which was gone by later that morning. 

A third time I ran the air purifier in my bedroom for 1-1/2 days while I was out of town. The same strong smell was immediately present, and remained as strong after 1-1/2 days of operation. I turned off the air purifier, opened the windows and, after a time, was able to return to the room. I later went to bed in the room. The next morning I again awoke with a sore throat, but this time by midday I was experiencing such low energy that I spent much of the rest of the day lying down. I developed a runny nose and scratchy throat during that day. All my symptoms worsened over the next several days, and I developed a significant cough and experienced much-interrupted sleep as well. 

One week after the 1-1/2 days of running, with continuing bad cough and very low energy, I realized that if the replacement HEPA filter were related to my symptoms, perhaps my paper hepa furnace filter had picked up contaminants and was continuing to spread them through my home. I replaced the furnace filter with a new paper hepa furnace filter and, on lying back down, had the sense of breathing more easily for 20 minutes or so (though I had not previously been aware of breathing difficulty). That same evening I had more energy and my cough had improved. I noticed significant improvement in both by the next morning, though my energy level was still at perhaps 50% of normal. 
After two more days I realized that though I had washed my sheets since the 1-1/2 days use of the air purifier in my bedroom, they had not been washed since I changed the furnace filter (my sheets are left open to the air during the day, and the air conditioning ceiling air ducts in the bedroom discharge directly onto them). I washed the sheets and that night my sleep was dramatically improved. 

Now three days later I am still experiencing fatigue – improved though still significant – I spend much of each day lying down. I sought help from my medical doctor yesterday, and it was her opinion that I am dealing with a two-fold trouble: a viral infection AND the effects of using the HEPA filter. I sincerely hope that no one else will need to suffer such effects.

productDescription: Weber Spirit Gas Grill Model E-210
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
On March 24, 2012, I purchased a Weber Spirit E-210 gas grill for $399.00 (before tax) at the Home Depot store located [REDACTED] Fort Worth, TX 76137 [REDACTED]. In addition, on the same date, I purchased a propane tank pre-loaded with propane gas at the same Home Depot for 43.92 (before tax).  I also purchased a long-handled grill brush (9.99 before tax) and a 4-piece BBQ tool set (9.97 before tax).

I used the gas grill on several occasions between the date of purchase and September 9, 2012, and never noticed any problems or had any issues with the grill.  However, when I went out to grill two hamburger patties and one link of [REDACTED] sausage on Sunday, September 9, 2012, I heated the grill up and cleaned the grates as I normally do.  Once the grill had been pre-heated (about 5 minutes), I placed the food on the grates.  I sat out by the grill as I was cooking because I always turn the meat over after it has cooked 6 minutes on the first side.  After my food had been on the grill for 5 minutes, I started hearing this “whooshing” sound and jumped up to see what was happening.  I went over to the grill and noticed flames were coming out the sides of the cooking area.  I was going to open the lid to the grill to alleviate the flames, when I noticed flames were also within the bottom cabinet area (where the propane tank sits).  I would have attempted to turn the propane tank off; however there were too many flames within the cabinet area to stick my hand in there.  As these few seconds went by, I suddenly heard a loud popping sound, like a firecracker.  At that point, it was very clear to me that the grill was about to explode.  So I ran into the house and called 911.  While I was on the phone with 911 within by kitchen, I heard a loud boom.  That’s when the first explosion took place.  So I ran out to my front yard to get as far as away from the grill as possible while I was on the phone with the fire department.  At that time, I heard a second loud boom while I was on the phone with 911 and told the fire department to hurry.  I was fairly certain that the back part of home was going to catch fire from the explosions, but thankfully that did not happen.
I was not injured.

incidentDescription: I purchased a Mr. Coffee Espresso maker Model # BVMC-ECM 260 at Walmart. It exploded on its second use. We immediately unplugged the unit and took it outside.  After the smoke subsided and the unit cooled down, we inspected it.  The problem seemed to be in the heating element of the unit where the burner was causing the plastic base of the coffee maker to melt and subsequently smoke around the electrical cord of it.  

After this happened, we found on the Cuisinart website under Consumer Affairs that there are many reports indicating a similar problem with this model.  This is very disappointing as it appears to be a somewhat common issue, and this coffee maker is also rather expensive.  This is the second coffee maker by Cusinart (same model) that we've had within six years.  The first one was the same version of this but stainless steel versus plastic.  That one just stopped working after about 3 years.  When looking to replace that one, it appeared that Cuisinart replaced it with this plastic version.  

Thankfully, we were nearby the kitchen when our coffee maker started burning and smoking so we could take care of it immediately and avoid a larger fire.  We will no longer purchase Cuisinart, and hope that this specific make and model coffee maker will be recalled to protect other consumers.

productDescription:
The Jenn-Air® grill has corrosion resistant commercial grade 445 stainless steel construction. This grill comes equipped with a total of 78,000 BTU’s of heat and over 828 sq in cooking area, infrared searing side burner and infrared rotisserie burner, radiant heat, Continuous electronic ignition , tank pull out tray 
•Dual energy valve for converting the grill from propane to natural gas
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription: I purchased a Jenn-Air Gas Grill Model Jenn-Air 720-0709 sold at Sam's Club.  After four months of use, we stopped using the product due to the propensity of the unit to catch on fire even under controlled conditions.  We experienced two serious fires.  After the first incident, I inspected the unit for debri, leaks, or any other defect and found none.  However, I did noticed while attempting to clean the unit, that the design of this unit has two layered grease pans at the bottom of the firebox.  The layered pans are fix welded to the unit and spaced in between about 1/2" with the top one having a center drain sloping toward the center in which drippings fall to the next layer.  We believe the root cause of the fires is the design of these two layers.  The concentration of the right amount of drippings, heat, contiguous fire source, and spacing of the drip prans appears to be condition leading to these two fire events.  During both incidents, flames and black smoke occurred.  The flames spread to throughout the unit shooting out from behind, on front of the control knobs, and under the firebox.  The biggest concern for safety was the risk associated with flames reaching the hose and propane tank underneath considering that we were not able to control the fire after turning off the valves.  We were required to use a fire extinguisher to put out the fire.

The regulator leaked as soon as the propane gas tank was opened. Lowe's was informed the same day and the grill was replaced on 09/01 at around 9 AM. This one did not leak after original installation and passed the soap-solution test.
At 6 PM on 9/1 the grill was put to use. After about 30 minutes, the regulator attached to the propane cylinder caught fire, with the fire engulfing the interior of the grill cabinet. The thermal nut did not shut off. The flame kept on increasing for about 6-8 seconds during the time it took to access the grill, get the protection and shut off the tank tap.

Melted plastic is still stuck to the cloth used to shut off the valve and the hand suffered scalds with burnt hair. The regulator periphery has melted.

Hopefully this will be investigated.

incidentDescription: I purchased three MC_ZS_E Verona 150cc motor scooters from Sunny Sports Inc. of Chino California. They were delivered by private shipper. and getting extremely hot while using attachments.

incidentDescription: Toaster failed and combusted inside.  Printed circuit actually combusted at take-off for quartz heating elements.  Reached temperatures high enough to melt lead.  Circuit board was actually burned and powdered.  Very dangerous considering that there are flamable bread crumbs inside.  Fortunately it was unplugged before any fire was started.  I am not alone. Please see:  http://www.fixya.com/support/t8782546-krups_sensotoast_deluxe_just_stopped

productDescription: Chefmate electric blender model BL-10
incidentDescription: I have had my Chefmate BL-10 blender from Target for 2 years. Today the connection from the blade to the motor split apart and sent shards of plastic across my kitchen, as the recall stated could happen with this blender. I hadn't heard about the recall until this happened. Would you please distribute this recall again, so people don't get hurt? Fortunately the plastic shards didn't hit us, but they certainly could have.

productDescription: Gas Grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
On June 30th, 2012 the caller turned his grill on, cooked food for party then turned valves off.

Did not notice right away that the heat just kept rising, after about five minutes later he saw heat coming from grill, went to it and viewed thermometer which was reading over 500 degrees.

He looked underneath and saw that the rubber hose was in flames and leaking propane.

He then shut the valve off to the propane also, the flames then extinguished but caller took the hose and sprayed the entire grill down with water.

July 5th, 2012 He contacted the manufacturer via phone and email, spoke with female named [REDACTED] who told him this grill is not on warranty, not on recall so they could not help him other than to sell him the replacement parts needed to repair grill.

He discovered through this contact that the rubber hose on his grill is now replaced with a flexible metal hose.

He states that he is an engineer and that if the rubber hose was replaced by metal hose then it has been replaced due to an issue of some sort with this product.

Caller would like the public notified of the danger, his grill repaired or replaced at manufacturer expense.

productDescription: Electric Coffee Maker
incidentDescription: I brewed a pot of coffee like normal yesterday morning.  About an hour after the pot finished brewing, I heard a splattering noise in the kitchen. It sounded like eggs frying in a hot pan of butter.  I found that the sound was coming from my coffee maker.   The coffee was boiling!  Smoke was billowing out from the burner.  The smell was awful.  The on/off light was not on.  I switched the lever back and forth and the light wouldn't come on.  It looked off, but the boiling continued until I unplugged the coffee maker.  We will not use it again.  I hope you will recall the coffee maker before someones house burns down.  I am so thankful I was home when the incident happened.  This coffee maker has an auto shut off feature, but it failed and can't be trusted in the future.

productDescription: Cuisinart DCC-1200 Coffee Maker
incidentDescription: Cuisinart DCC-1200 coffee maker overheated and started smoking. Had brewed a pot of coffee and the carafe w/ coffee in it was on the warmer. Heard sizzling noises from the coffee maker, saw smoke/steam/fumes coming from the warmer plate area and smelled smoke or burning electrical component. Clock had shut-off. Unplugged unit immediately. Unit was 2 years + 2 months old. No prior problems. Researched unit on Amazon and discovered similar reports from other consumers. Then searched Cuisinart DCC-1200 fire hazard and found many other instances. Cuisinart claims their built-in safety feature automatically shuts-down the unit in case of overheating.

productDescription: Cuisinart Coffee Maker model DGB-700BC
incidentDescription: We own a Cuisinart Burr Grind & Brew model DGB-700BC coffee maker. My husband is awake for work day around 4:30 a.m. and I normally sleep until approximately around the time my husband leaves, or shortly thereafter. The program was set to start the brew process at 4:30 a.m., as is customary in our home. My husband awakened me in a bit of a panic to say that he, needed my assistance to determine the root cause of the smell of electrical smoke in our kitchen. We quickly determined that it was the coffee pot, and observed a thin trial of white smoke arising from the lower back portion of the unit. The unit was immediately unplugged, never again to be plugged in; at least not in our home. I was unnerved to imagine how the story would be told if the unit over-heated after my husband left if I were not yet awake! After locating online similar stories from various other consumers, I called Cuisinart. The agent never requested the age of the unit nor purchase date, but I assume this is because we are on file with their company - the unit in question was the replacement of a warranted unit that failed less than two years before. I was advised that I'd receive the shipment in 7-10 business days. Outrageous!! Surely Cuisinart, if any company, can understand the plight of a rural-living, work-from-home, happily-caffeine-addicted customer who would have to travel approximately 10 miles one way for a commercially made cup of Joe! What's more, I would hope that my circumstances are not so usual and customary that they would have great difficulty meeting the demand of expediting a shipment to customers who experienced their unit over-heating. After failed efforts with the CSR, her supervisor promised 5-7 business days. It took a voice mail to the director of customer service (which was rapidly returned), and a call to a very competent professional in risk management who was able and willing to do the needful before I was assured that I should expect the package about 1 business day later. I was advised that Cuisinart coffee makers are equipped with 3 (I assume that 2 are for fault tolerance) thermal fuses that prevent the unit from actually catching fire, and to Cuisinart's credit, I do not find any reports of consumers observing flames after such an incident. However, it's worth noting that the unit does overheat enough to generate smoke. Also, sparing the minor details of difficulties such as receptionists who want to route you back to customer service or keep you on indefinite hold, or CSRs who direct the customer to corporate, but cannot provide the contact telephone number this experience was akin to a tooth extraction minus even local anesthesia. Compare this to my original warranty replacement was very easy and uneventful, and I'm left baffled for an explanation.

productDescription: This is an under the counter space saver coffee Pot made by Black and Decker.  It is the SDC 740B
manufacturer: Applica Consumer Products, Inc. - NOTIFY SPECTRUM BRANDS
incidentDescription: Making coffee with the Black and Decker Space Saver Coffee Pot ( SDC  740B )  Once the coffee was ready and I picked up the carafe to pour some coffee, the handle broke away from the glass carafe causing the hot coffee to pour all over the top of my counter and down between the stove and counter as well.  Fortunately,  I was not burned, but that is only  because I acted quickly and put the carafe down on the surface as fast as possible.  We were lucky we did not get injured, however, we had an all day cleaning event as we needed to remove the electric stove and cabinet from the wall for cleaning as hot coffee poured everywhere.

productDescription: MY SEARS KENMORE DEHUMIDIFIER MODEL 580.54501400 LOOKS EXACTLY LIKE A SEARS MODEL [REDACTED] DISPLAY PANEL, EXCEPT FOR THE DIMENSION SIZE WHICH LOOKS LIKE A [REDACTED].
incidentDescription:
I HAVE A SEARS KENMORE DEHUMIDIFIER MODEL 580.54501400 PURCHASED MAY 26, 2004 FOR $159.99 FROM THE LOCAL SEARS.  I CONSTANTLY MONITOR THE HUMIDITY IN MY BASEMENT.  LAST WINTER, THE UNIT DID NOT SEEM TO WORK PLUS IT  DID SEEM TO BE QUITE HOT ON TOP.   I THOUGHT THE ROOM TEMPERATURE WAS TOO LOW.  I PURCHASED A DIFFERENT BRAND, LARGER UNIT.  AS SPRING BROUGHT WARMER TEMPS, I DECIDED TO RETRY THE SEARS UNIT.  AGAIN, I KEPT A CLOSE WATCH TO ITS PROGRESS.  GOOD THING, AS ON ONE TRIP TO THE BASEMENT, THE UNIT WAS SO HOT ON THE TOP, I COULD NOT TOUCH IT.  WITHIN SECONDS, I SMELLED SOMETHING LIKE IT WAS BURNING INSIDE.  I QUICKLY SHUT IT OFF AND UNPLUGGED IT.  I KEPT THE UNIT TO RECYCLE THE PARTS THIS SUMMER WHEN I FOUND OTHER SEARS BAD UNITS ON THE NET.

I THINK SEARS SHOULD REFUND MY INVESTMENT ALONG WITH THOSE OTHER UNITS.  OTHER CONSUMERS NEED TO CHECK THEIR UNITS AND FILE A REPORT LIKE I HAVE.  THANK YOU U.S.CPSC.

productDescription: Blow dryer. Porcelain Ceramic by BaByliss PRO. Small, compact blow dryer, pink.
incidentDescription: I was blow drying my hair with a small, Porcelain Ceramic blow dryer by BaByliss PRO when a bad, burning smell filled the room. The dryer was shaking and sending small shocks down my arm. I turned it off to let it cool as I thought it had gotten overheated. I waited about 10 minutes and tried again. It was ok for about 20 seconds and then it started making a grinding noise and smoke began to come out. I turned it off, unplugged it and put it aside. The next time I tried to dry my hair, the same thing happened. I knew something was very wrong and I was afraid to ever use it again. It was a very powerful dryer. I liked that it was lightweight and easy to use. I figured it was just getting old. I went online to see if I could buy a new one just like it and there were a few on amazon and eBay. I read some reviews and saw where another person had the same experience. Then I saw the recall notice. I'm so glad I saw it as I was about to buy another one just like it!!  It seemed to be a great little blow dryer but I was truly terrified when it started smoking and sending shocks down my arm. I think the review and this recall saved my life.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription:
BonJour 2-Quart Stainless Steel Tea Kettle with Copper Bottom was left on the stove too long.  Link to the model on Amazon.  Our purchase was from a local kitchen supply store.

http://www.amazon.com/BonJour-2-Quart-Stainless-Kettle-Copper/dp/B002LGFF6U/ref=cm_rdp_product_img

This model kettle does not have any whistle and the water boiled all out.  The bottom overheated and the inside layer (lead? Tin?) portion of the bottom, between the copper cladding and the steel body and inside bottom had melted.  The copper cladding failed when the over heated kettle was moved and spilled out liguid metal onto the stovetop and splashed onto the floor near the stove.  The person who moved the overheated kettle also got some second degree burns on the bottom of a couple of toes as they moved away and stepped on a metal splashing on the floor.  

The stove and the burner had quenched metal on various portions, but did not appear to suffer any real damage.  The linoleum floor has some scorched marks where the metal splashed.  

The concern here is the low temp metals used as a heat sink in the base of the kettle that liquified with just stove top temperatures.  Combined with the rupture of the copper cladding, this created a very hazardous situation.   There was no indication of this other lower melting point metals beyond the steel and copper components on the literature we had for this item.
