productDescription: Weber Spirit Grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
Our weber grill (spirit) caught on fire. The fire destroyed the control knobs and the lines from the propane gas to the control knobs. Thankfully, we saw the fire and immediately took the propane gas away and contained the fire.  The grill was turned off but the propane gas was not. We are not sure what caused the fire but it could have been out of control if we were not in the immediate area to douse the fire. We only had the grill for two years and used it at least an average of two times during the summer months. 

Thank you.

productDescription: Electric Bike wheel that you add to a pre existing bicycle.
incidentDescription:
The consumer stated he was riding his bike and he took the finger of the on/off switch and the electric wheel continued running when it should off stopped.

The consumer stated that the wheel turned itself on when it was not switch on. The consumer stated this incident happened approximately 10 times.

The consumer stated that he was not injured.

The consumer stated that if a child was riding this product and the wheel turns on by itself it can cause the rider to shoot off un-expectantly and lose control of the bicycle. The consumer stated that this product poses a crash hazard. 

The consumer stated that he contacted the manufacturer and they informed him to mail the electrical component of the wheel back to the manufacturer. The consumer stated that he contacted the manufacturer several times and once they told him to fix it himself.

productDescription:
VACUUM COFFEE MAKER, HIGH TEMP GLASS. TWO PIECE.
ITEM WAS NEW!
incidentDescription:
This is in regard to a "BODUM" vacuum maker, the model being a "SANTOS" model. 
This model is currently marketed under the "PEBO" designation.
It is a glass model of the metal type of vacuum makers popular during the 30's, 40's
and 50's designed for range top use.
The top or funnel, as is the lower unit, is made of high temperature glass.The lower unit 
holds the finished coffee after brewing. The lower unit has a narrow collar in which
the upper unit fits. The lower unit has a black plastic handle aroung its filler neck.
The owners manual does not have any prohibitions against heating the unit in a 
microwave oven. It is because of this, I decided to heat clean water in the lower
unit for the purpose of cleaning the unit.
I filled the lower unit, or carafe, to a water level of 10mm below the filler neck top.
I placed the unit in the microwave oven, set the timer for four (4) minutes and 
observed the water being heated , the purpose being to prevent the water from
boilling over the filler neck.
As I was watching the unit, I heard a muffled "pop". I immediately shut of the
oven. I thought the glass might have cracked. Using oven mitts, I carefully removed
the carafe. There did not to be any indication of the glass being damaged!
Removing the carafe, I did notice a stream of hardened plastic coming from a
small hole, approx. 5mm, dia. in the handles plastic collar , located along the
horizontal line of the handle collar.
The hole did not appear to go all the way thru the collar.
There two things that could caused this to happen.
1. The collar had an implanted RFID chip. (not likely though)
2. A small piece of  a metal substance contaminated the plastic "shot" during molding.
I am concerned about the integrity of the handle as hot liquids are involved.
If it will be of assistance to you, I can remit images of the unit.

productDescription: Gas grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
The consumer stated that the regulator on the grill leaked gas posing a fire hazard. He stated that he was affraid that if it leaked inside the grill it could cause an explosion.

The consumer stated that he tested the regulator with soap bubbles to verified that it was infact leaking gas. 

The consumer stated that he was not injured. The consumer stated that there was no damages to his home structurer. 

The consumer stated that he contacted the manufacturer and they mailed out a new regulator on 07/23/2012 (est.). 
The consumer stated that when he installed the regulator to the propain tank it was still leaking gas. 

07/29/2012 The consumer stated that he decided to go to the retailer and they informed him that they would provide a new regulator. The consumer stated that he installed that new regulator and he has not had any problems. 

The consumer stated that he believes this product should be investigated due to the fire hazard that it poses.

productDescription:
Replacement laptop battery, part # LHP200L-AP
"powered by Leydenenergy" on label
Assembled in China
no other manufacturer information
brand: None listed powered by Leydenenergy on Label
incidentDescription:
The battery in my laptop computer exploded in flame
I suffered a 3rd degree burn on my leg which required medical treatment.
The computer was damaged beyond repair
After I dropped the computer on the floor and went to tend to my burn it burned the hardwood floor
The computer was a [REDACTED], however the battery was a generic replacement made in China and purchased on the internet

productDescription: silver and black hair dryer
incidentDescription:
I was using my Revlon 1875 hairdryer this morning. I noticed it wasn't blowing very hot on the low fan speed. When I turned it up to the higher speed, an explosion occured in the handle - and a flame and smoke shot out it - and the dryer turned off. 

I immediately unplugged the device - but I have to say it was extremely scary because the flame  that discharged from the handle was very close to my hair and face. My teenage daughter has the same model of hairdryer, so I am concerned that this is a dangerous product.

productDescription: steam mop for hard floors that also has a vacuum feature
incidentDescription: I was steam mopping my floors with the product, and my older child let my one year old through the baby gate.  When I saw him coming towards me I stopped mopping and put the handle upright, reached to get him a cookie off the counter.  He slid on some water as he came towards me and his toes slid under the edge of the steam mop.  I grabbed him up immediately, and ran cool water over his toes, but the damage was done.  He sustained 2nd and 3rd degree burns to both feet.  After a trip to his pediatrician, then a pediatric surgeon in a neighboring town, we were sent to a burn center in Augusta, Georgia (about 4 hours away).  [REDACTED] (my son) was admitted and had surgery to debride his burns and apply gamma-overlying silver grafts.  He was bandaged, redressed, and assessed once a week, requiring multiple drives back.  He has handled this ordeal better than his parents, we are thankful that his grafts did well, he does have  keloid scarring on one toe, the others fared better.  We are unsure of the nerve damage he has sustained, but are hopeful to not require any further treatment.  The safety feature of the steam vac is that the steam stops when the handle is upright- clearly, that did not function properly, and the warnings in the manufacturer book are not adequate in my opinion.  It never occurred to me that anything could slide under the edge, since it appears flush with the ground until close inspection.  I just hope the warning labels can be adjusted to adequately warn future consumers.  I do not want this traumatic event to happen to any other child or family.

productDescription: Vacuum cleaner
incidentDescription:
The consumer stated that she was using her vacuum cleaner and the handle became extremely the hot. The consumer stated that she was using the vacuum cleaner for approximately 5 minutes. The consumer stated that she was using it on a carpet surface. She stated that there was nothing stuck in the vacuum to make it overheat. 

The consumer stated that when it became hot she immediately turned off and let it cool down. The consumer stated that it took approximately 30 minutes for the handle to cool off. The consumer that she did not see any smoke of sparks, she stated that it only becomes extremely hot. The consumer stated that she used the vacuum in other surfaces and the same incident happened. 

The consumer stated that she was not injured. 

The consumer stated that she had been experiencing this issue for approximately 6 months. 

The consumer stated that she researched online this particular model and many reports are available online stating that they were experiencing the same issue of the handle becoming extremely hot. 

The consumer stated that she contacted the manufacturer and they informed her that they had never heard of the problem. The consumer stated that she should take it to one of their company authorized repair locations. She stated that the representative informed her that she would have to pay for the repairs (amount of the payment was unknown). 

The consumer stated that she contacted the local repair place for the company and they informed her that they were very familiar with the problem and that they had replaced and repair many of this model vacuums. 

The consumer believes this product should be investigated due to the burning and fire hazard that it poses.

productDescription: White Bosch Tassimo T20, bought in July 2011 at Bed Bath and Beyond.
incidentDescription:
I received the new T disc holder because my coffee machine was affected by the recall of the disc holder. The new holder does absolutely nothing to fix the described problem. My coffee maker spilled ground coffee and hot water before and does so after I installed the new part. 
I feel like this fix is just a pacifier for consumers but not a fix to a bad product. I still believe that the machine is dangerous and that I could get burned from it. I always stay 2 feet away from it when I am making coffee. 
I called Bosch and informed them about the problem but they don't seem to care and don't want to take care of my issue. 
It is unfortunate that I have to go this route but a dangerous product needs to come off the market. 
I wish I could just return the machine and buy a different coffee maker.

productDescription: Electric coffee maker, drip style, 12 cup Model DC 1100
incidentDescription: Coffee maker overheated. Liquid in pot began boiling, smoke emitted from back of machine. Odor indicating electrical fire or smoldering was detected. Power switch apparently inoperative. Power indicator light not functioning.

productDescription: Cuisinart model DCC-1100 12-cup programmable coffee maker, black.
incidentDescription:
My wife made a small pot of coffee successfully but before removing pot to fill cup was confronted with tremendous odor as though something was burning and/or melting. Didn't recognize source immediately but became bad enough to alarm children upstairs. Upon realizing coffee making was to blame, unplugged unit and burned hand trying to move off counter. Pot holder needed to remove unit outdoors. Very surprised counter top didn't melt. Warming plate beneath carafe was clearly so hot as to  melt unit's internals. Second unit to suffer similar fate. Good unit but not worth potential grievous injury.
Unit involved is Cuisinart programmable drip coffee maker perhaps 3 years old.  Whether it be 3 months or 5 years, I don't believe there ought be a time limit attached to consumer safety.
victimSeverity: Injury, Level of care not known

productDescription: Cuisinart DCC1200
incidentDescription: This morning I was brewing coffee in our Cuisinart DCC1200.  It started gurgling, the warmer plate got extremely hot, the power light went off, there was a strong electrical smell.  I've now read that this is not an isolated experience with this product.  It obviously could have burned our house down.

productDescription: Cuisinart Coffee Maker, model number DCC 1200, serial number 00917h, black & chrome model.
incidentDescription:
I have the Cuisinart DCC 1200 in Black & Chrome, purchased at Macy's in 2010.  I programmed the coffee maker to go off at 6:30 a.m.  I was in the kitchen making breakfast at 7:20 when I started to smell something weird & then heard some popping & crackling noises.  Upon looking around, I noticed the smoke coming from the coffee maker!  I unplugged it quickly and took it into the garage before it woke up my 4 children from the smoke alarm and burned my hand in the process.

My concern is that if I hadn't been awake yet, the potential for a fire could have caused more serious damage, including being life threatening.

Upon googling this, I found numerous complaints about this particular model from Cuisinart and it's disheartening to know that this is something that's a known problem yet still being sold.  I have left a message at Cuisinart and have no idea what their recourse is but I'm concerned about purchasing another one of their products.
victimSeverity: Injury, Level of care not known

productDescription: Outdoor Gas Grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
The consumer says that the burners are too short to go into the gas manifold.  He says that this creates air space where gas can escape, instead of going into the burner.  He says this cannot be seen normally.  He only noticed after thorough inspection.  He feels that there needs to be a recall on this product.  He says the company is aware of the issue and changed the model number of the product to keep this information a secret.   


The consumer contacted the manufacturer last Friday 07/13, who told him they would pass the information along.

productDescription:
Char-griller Duo 5050
It is a combination gas & charcoal grill with a side burner
incidentDescription: We were using the side burner on our grill to do a seafood boil.  The gas hose melted at the connection to the burner and caught on fire.  The hose was shooting propane & fire on our wood deck.  Luckily we were standing near it and could shut off the valve on the gas tank.  No one was injured.  2 months later, our friend with the same grill had the same thing happen to him.

productDescription: 1875 Ionic Ceramic Blowing Dryer
incidentDescription:
Caller was unable to hold onto her blow dryer due to extreme heat coming into the handle.

She was blow drying her very short hair around July 11, 2012 however, after only five minutes the heat became unbearable and she had to turn it off and put it down.
There were no flames just extreme heat.

She has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.

She is positive that the blow dryer would have caught fire if she had not turned it off quickly.

Caller would like to have this blow dryer investigated, recalled and replaced at manufacturer expense.

productDescription: White in color, handheld hairdryer with 2 speeds, 10 ft power cord with GCFI
incidentDescription: Plugged in hair dryer and turned it on.  It made a loud cluncking sound and sparked.  I immediately turned it off and unplugged it.  Saw that the blade had come off and was broken in half.

productDescription: Mr. Coffee Coffeemaker BVMC-SJX33GT. GLASS CARAFE
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription:
Mr. Coffee coffee BVMC-SJX33GT had just finished brewing and was on warming cycle when I heard a strange popping noise. I looked at the machine and saw what I thought was steam. But upon closer inspection realized the coffeemaker was actually smoking and emitting the smell of melting plastic. I unplugged the machine immediately.
The coffeemaker was 3.5 months old. It was used once daily and cleaned regularly.

productDescription: Ceiling Fan
incidentDescription:
The caller stated that while the fan was in use, the metal arm that connects the fan blade to the base of the fan snapped in half.  The fan blade projected across the room.  Fortunately no one was hit because this could have caused serious injuries.  The blade landed against the drapery on the wall.

My son [REDACTED] (16), was in the bed at the time.

6/2012  The manufacturer was contacted and she was informed that someone would contact her.
7/9/12  The caller contacted the manufacturer again and she was informed that the fan would be replaced but that the incident was rare and there was nothing else that could be done.
The caller feels that the failure of the fan is a safety hazard and should be investigated.

productDescription: Cuisinart Model DCC-3750 coffee pot, thermal pot elite brew
incidentDescription: All of a sudden I smelled smoke and being in the kitchen I saw my coffee pot billowing smoke from underneath and behind unit. The pot was not turned on, nor programmed to be turned on. It also had not been used for many hours prior.  There was a horrid smell for many hours  and it smoked for a while even after it was unplugged.

productDescription: Product is a Cuisinart Convection/Toaster/Broiler oven that sits on a countertop. It is style number TOB-195. This is the expensive stainless steel unit that is sold at better department stores and kitchen stores, not the cheaper version sold at Walmart and Costco.
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
I have a broiler/convection/toaster oven from Cuisinart that sits on a counter top. The style number is TOB-195. It is an expensive all stainless steel unit. It is seemingly a nice oven, but there is a defect in the design that can prove to be EXTREMELY dangerous, especially to CHILDREN. The elements of the oven are at the top of the unit and very close to the exterior steel casing. There does not seem to be any insulation between the steel and the elements, and if there is - it does not work as it is insufficient. As a result the outside of the unit gets extremely hot when in use to the point that it cannot even be touched without actually causing a burn to the skin. It can actually cause second and third order burns to the epidermal and dermal layers of the skin. That is how hot it gets. Other toaster broilers I have had and still have may get warm but not so hot you cannot even touch the unit. The Cuisinart is of poor design and poses a very serious risk to children in the home, and adults who may inadvertently touch the outside while in use, which is an easy thing to do. It also poses a fire risk, and will melt any plastics that you may place on top while in use. My wife and I have both burned our hands on the unit. We stopped using it, as we did not want our small and teenage children to burn themselves.
    I contacted the company and they gave me a pat, flip corporate answer which of course absolved themselves of any responsibility in the matter, even though I know they receive the same complaint all of the time. I personally know several people that have the same complaint, including my sister who was also duped into believing the most expensive toaster oven on the market, would actually be a good product. Supposedly Cuisinart knows how to make small appliances, but apparently not. What I do not understand, is why they are still allowed to make and sell this product, and what's even more - is why they would willingly still make and sell this product after knowing about this problem and receiving complaints.
    It is a poorly designed product, it is a dangerous product, it is a very expensive product. It is a product we and others cannot use, because of concern for our safety. It is a product that will eventually harm children, if it has not done so yet - however, I think a child somewhere has already been burned by this product. 
    I contacted the company and they gave me a pat, flip corporate answer that admitted the problem, but takes no responsibility and blows me off:

"    Thank you for your inquiry. With this toaster oven you have, the heating coils are right at the very top of the toaster oven. The heat from those coils will make the outside extremely hot, due to the stainless being a conductor. There is no manufacturers defect with the unit as it is operating as it is intended. It is strongly recommended not to place anything on the unit due to the high heat. If you have any further questions please reply, with history, to this email. We invite you to call our Customer Service Department at 1-800-726-0190 , if you prefer. Please keep in mind the Customer Service Agent will not have access to your e-mail information. The hours of operation are 7 AM -11 PM EST Monday through Friday and 9 AM - 5:30 PM on Saturdays and Sundays, excluding major holidays."
    Really? They know it gets extremely hot, they intended for it to get extremely hot, and apparently it is operating as it should - which means it is OK to burn people. And the only thing they could say is not to place anything on top. What if my 11 year old decides to touch it for whatever reason? Am I supposed to constantly police my toaster oven? I should not have to have a special protocol in use just to use a countertop appliance. How ridiculous!
    So basically, they admit and know the unit gets extremely hot and can even explain why, and they admit this is exactly how they intended for it to be - to get so hot that it can actually burn people, and yet all they can do is tell me not to place objects on top, as if I am an idiot and cannot figure that out. That isn't the point. The point is that I should not have to worry about the obvious unsafe functioning of a product like that, especially when the company is aware of the problem. And especially in a product that cost $175.00 - which is three times the price of their competitors that do not seem to have the problem of burning people.

productDescription: Cuisinart CBC-4400 14-cup coffee maker, black, glass carafe (sn 70412c)
incidentDescription:
My Cuisinart CBC-4400 coffee maker (sn 70412c) malfunctioned yesterday.  This unit has never been abused or improperly used.  

Approximately 30 minutes after brewing a pot of coffee, I walked into my kitchen to find smoke billowing from the unit and the acrid smell of burning plastic.  I unplugged the unit and moved it outside where it continued to burn for several minutes.

I was lucky to have caught this. Had I used the timer to automatically brew my coffee while my family and I slept, this could easily have led to a fire resulting in injury or death.  At the least, had I left the house with the unit on, there would have been a catastrophic fire.

This is entirely unacceptable and, from what I've found online, all too common.  There is absolutely no reason to engineer a product in this way in this day and age.  The engineering and parts cost to make sure this can never happen again is trivial.

incidentDescription: Aug. 9, 2012, approximately 12:30 am, I had just filled a glass with crushed ice from my GE refrigerator’s ice maker, model no GSH25JSTASS.  I then poured a can of Pepsi over the ice, and proceeded to drink it.  As I drank, what I thought to be small pieces of crushed ice entered my mouth, and as I chewed the ice, I bit down on something hard.  Upon closer examination I realized that it was a sharp piece of plastic about the size of a pencil eraser.  I immediately drained the rest of the drink into a strainer, and found that a larger piece had also been dispensed into my glass.  I examined the ice maker discovered that the plastic on the Ice Dispenser Bucket Auger GE Part Number: WR17X11705 had broken into three pieces.  I believe that the fact that these pieces of plastic can break off and be dispensed into a persons drink poses a serious danger for choking or injury.

productDescription: The Baby Bullet is a food processor designed to prepare homemade baby food.
incidentDescription: My husband and I received a Baby Bullet food processor as a baby shower gift.  We read the manual thoroughly and cared for the product and prepared all of the food according to the instruction in the manual.  We have used it a total of 6 times.  The 6th time of use, we pureed sweet potatoes for our son.  While feeding him lunch the next day he began to choke.  I was able to dislodge what he was choking on and pull it out of his mouth.  I, at first, thought it was a sliver of potato, but upon closer inspection realized it was a one inch piece of rubber.  That rubber was a piece of the rubber gasket on the Baby Bullet that had been chopped up and made its way into my son's food.  Who knows how much he actually ingested.  My husband, [REDACTED], called the Baby Bullet company to file a complaint about the product and we were informed that a "couple of months ago" the company had changed the care instructions in the manual because the heat from dishwashers was causing the rubber gaskets to fail and they have also changed the structure of the product and instead of using a removable rubber gasket, they are now permanently seated.  We did register our product when we received it, yet we were not notified of these changes.  The company told us that there was such a small percentage of occurrences that they did not send out notifications.  Had they sent us a notification, the incident of my son choking could have been avoided.  How is it determined what is an acceptable percentage to not have to notify consumers or initiate a recall?  I feel like any percentage of failure that could be hazardous to a human life is too high of a percentage.  Baby Bullet has requested that we pack our Bullet up and leave it on the porch so that they can send FedEx for it and we have complied with their request.  I did take pictures of the product showing the broken gasket and the piece that my son choked on.  I want other parents to know that this product can be dangerous.  Not only should parents be informed, they should also be sending out these replacement parts.  I do not want any other parent to have to go through this.  Next time it could result in something much worse, like the death of an innocent child.

incidentDescription: My toaster oven switches itself on. The only way to keep the toaster oven from heating is to keep it unplugged. The toaster oven has 3 dials, one of which controls power state. From the "off" setting, you can turn the dial to the "on" setting on the right if you want the oven to stay on, or you can turn the dial to a "Dark...Medium...Light" "toast" setting on the left. The "toast" setting is controlled by a mechanical count-down timer that rotates the dial back to the "off" position. Now instead of stopping at "off", the dial continues to rotate to "on", where it stops. The same thing happens if you manually set the dial to "off".

This caused a gas leak at the end of the burners that allowed the gas to escape and catch fire around the knobs used to control the temperature and shut off the gas.

productDescription: Char Broil Commercial Series (Infrared Gas Grill)
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
I have owned a Char-Broil Commercial Series infrared grill for almost 3 years, so it is beyond the 2 year warranty.  Recently when removing the grill grates, emitter surfaces and flame tamers for cleaning I noted that the firebox flange which supports the flame tamers had corroded sufficiently to become detached from the firebox itself as the welds attaching it were completely destroyed.  This allowed the flame tamers to drop closer to the burners which I believed might create a safety hazard.  In June I reported this to Char-Broil through an on-line chat at their website and the technician I chatted with agreed that it may make the grill less safe.  He offered to sell a replacement firebox but could not tell me whether the firebox had been revised to prevent this problem from recurring 2½ years from now.  He also suggested calling customer service directly as he could not do anything but sell the parts.

Today I spoke with their customer support and confirmed that purchasing an entire firebox is the only option I have.  I also confirmed that there had been no design or material improvements to suggest that the replacement box would last any longer than the original.  The customer service rep did seem concerned whether I was using the grill at a temperature too high, suggesting that high temperatures may be at issue here.  I responded that the maximum temperature capability of the grill would be determined by the orifice diameter that Char-Broil provided in the natural gas conversion kit and that I could find nothing in the literature provided with the grill that even hinted that using the grill on high would present a problem of any sort.  Since the grill is an infrared model, much is made of the benefits of searing the meat.  Further, the four temperature gauges on the front of the grill stopped working the first year I owned it.

I called 911 and my husband managed to get to it, felt that it was not too hot on top to touch, unplugged it and dragged it out through the garage into the driveway where the smoke continued to pour out of it. incidentDescription:

I noticed on the Internet that there has been a problem with the regulator, maybe leaking gas.  I have worked with Lowe's to return the grill (manager was helpful) but I'm trying to understand more about the grill and other issues as I have seen some incidents reported on the Internet.  

Because Master Forge grills are made in China, they do not have a headquarters here in the U.S.A. The # that is inside the door to the grill is the parts department and appears to authorize RMAs to Lowe's -- they are not Master Forge.  

You call Lowe's Corp Office, they have you work with the local store, then local store sends you to the parts #.  With this being a Lowe's brand, my initial thought is Lowe's corporate would be handling this situation.  

I had to replace some siding because of the heat from the fire was very intense.  My concern is there could be a global issue with this grill.  Lowe's is still selling it.  I'm thinking their thought is since the regulator has been replaced in future grills, it is ok to sell.

incidentDescription: I own a Black and Decker Spacemaker White coffeemaker, Model #SDC740, on several occasions for no reason I will make the coffee and walk off, or set it to come on automatic in the morning and come back to the coffee grounds and hot water coming from the basket area and not going in to the pot but flowing all over the counter top. The thing that caught my attention the last time it happened is it smelt like the house was on fire.  The coffee grounds had dripped into the surge protector (which is now black in the areas the appliances were plugged in), I assume than burning out all of the appliances connected into the surge protector (the spacemaker toaster oven and coffee bean grinder).  So, I went on the internet to search for new appliances, not at all thrilled that all of our appliances were ruined and found that Black and Decker had a recall in 2009 for a different model coffee maker with a very similar problem. productDescription: Outdoor Gas Grill Appliance
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
This complaint is about a safety issue with a Sears Kenmore Outdoor LP Gas Grill.  It concerns the gas coupling/regulator assembly that appears to be OEM from GLOBAL ILLIDA.  Note: This part may be commonly used on many makes and models of gas grills that are sold by many different companies under different names. 

The gas coupling/regulator assembly "blew apart" under pressure after it was attached to the LP Gas Tank OPD and the valve was opened.  The failure was not instantaneous.  It "blew apart" after the valve was opened and the system was under pressure for a few seconds.  The black plastic gas coupling thread assembly remained attached to the LP Gas Tank OPD valve and the regulator assembly broke away and was forcefully ejected from the OPD valve.  I did not notice anything wrong with the unit before using it.  It was last used the weekend of June 23rd.  The unit is stored indoors and wheeled outside and connected to the LP tank prior to each use, usually on the weekends.

The regulator just missed hitting my face.  I had been bent over to open the tank valve and was returning to an upright position.  My hand was removed from the valve and I was starting to stand back up.  The coupler/regulator assembly  "blew apart" approximately two seconds after opening the valve.  There was a loud popping sound as the assembly failed and the regulator was ejected.  Since the regulator remained attached to the flexible rubber gas line, it whipped in an arc and I dodged back and out of the way.  No one was injured.

I contacted Sears Kenmore to report the failure and request repair/replacement of the part.  They refused citing the fact that the product was purchased on 6/2/2011 and it was now 6/29/2012.  The product is covered by a one year full warranty and five year limited warranty on the burners.  I was requesting a courtesy repair since the failure occurred so closely to the one year anniversary.  The product was purchased on 6/2/2011, but was assembled later and placed in service approximately 6/11/2011. 

I attempted to report the safety defect to Sears Kenmore, but was given "the runaround". Seven different 800 phone numbers were provided and all were contacted.  Finally, a Sears/Kenmore customer solution representative took my information and promised to forward it to her supervisor.  I requested that someone from Sears/Kenmore call me back to follow up to report the safety defect of this gas coupling/regulator assembly.

Model: 415.16128010
S/N:  G550011104016135

The part that failed appears to be manufactured by "GLOBAL" or "GLOBAL ILLIDA" and has this information imprinted on it:
On Coupler:  GLOBAL ILLIDA 80GK Adapter for  LP-GAS YS900A
On Regulater: GLOBAL Low Pressure LP-Gas Regulator Listed 9T82

I would like to be reimbursed for the cost to repair or replace the grill.

Thank you.  
[redacted]

productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
model: Kuuma IR Stow and Go Grill Model Number 83726
incidentDescription:
I purchased a Kuuma Stow and Go Grill from West Marine on 9 July 2009.  I was not aware until 12 July 2012 that there had been a recall of this product: Release #10-196.  I have had an occasional problem with flame that seemed to back out from the lit grill towards the control knob.  When that happened, I tried to make tighten the gas connections and that seem to help enough to allow time to cook a hamburger or piece of chicken.  We only use the grill 4 or 5 times a year in the summers aboard our sailboat, so it has not been a major issue until yesterday, 11 July 2012.  Upon lighting the grill, which was attached to the cockpit aft rail on our boat, I turned away briefly to pick the food I was about to cook, when the entire side of the grill where the propane tank is attached burst into flame.  The fire quickly engulfed the entire side of the grill where the propane tank is attached and melted the plastic gas control knob, so I could not twist the control knob with my hand without being burned.  I feared that the propane tank would "cook off" in an explosion, but was able to finally get the gas shut off by using a pair of cooking tongs.  I believe I and my wife were in grave danger of having our boat catch fire, since the flames would have quickly heated the cloth Sunbrella bimini top.
Last night I went on line to report this to the CPSC and discovered that the item had already been subject to a voluntary recall.  I do not remember seeing anything about this recall from either Eastwind Industries, or West Marine.
This was a life threatening incident and more aggressive action should be taken against this product.

The fire flared up quickly and we were able to shut off the gas before it got any worse.  When we inspected the situation, we found the tubing to now be melted.  The Southern California Gas Company was contacted and after their inspection, indicated to us that they had to shut off the gas feeding to the barbecue and "red tagged" the barbecue indicating that it was unsafe for any further barbecue use.

productDescription: Battery for HP Pavilion dv6000
incidentDescription:
I own an HP Pavilion dv6000 purchased during the summer of 2007. This is around the time HP laptops were sold with batteries that were later recalled for issues with over-heating and fire hazards. The CT number for the battery in mine does not match those included in the expanded recall despite being purchased during the same time period as the defective ones. Mine begins with 62941 instead of 62940. I called HP in regards to this recall when it first came out. I was reassured that despite the battery in my device having the same over-heating issue that it was unaffected by the recall. The recall was later expanded to include more batteries but mine still did not fall under it.

My concern is that despite the battery for my device not being included in the recall of HP batteries to date, something may still be seriously wrong with it. The entire unit including the laptop itself, the removable battery, and adapter all over-heat from time to time. More often than not, I'm forced to use a laptop cooling fan or place it on top of a cool surface to avoid over-heating. Sometimes, it gets so hot that my laptop will shut down completely. 

I am worried about being injured or having my computer damaged if something were to explode or otherwise seriously malfunction because of this issue. In the meantime, I also have an HP Pavilion dv2000 which uses the same type of battery. I use the battery from that device or take out the battery and run my computer off the adapter to minimize the risk. However, that battery is getting old and dies quickly and the adapter over-heats as well.

I'm putting the incident date was May 2010 because that is when I called HP about the problem. It has been an intermittent issue for a few years now. The injury I am reporting is minor at most. If it starts to over-heat and is placed on my lap, it does begin to burn them. This "burn" is similar to the feeling a person gets when touching something very hot and pulling their hand away quickly. It is uncomfortable for a short time but leaves no lasting injury.

productDescription: Kawasaki cordless drill
incidentDescription:
I own a Kawasaki cordless drill model # 691220.  While using the drill in my garage to drill through thin plastic, I started smelling a burning smell.  I thought it was the plastic burning around the drill bit and kept drilling the holes.  The smell became very strong, and I noticed a lot of smoke coming out of the vent holes at the back of the drill.  I stopped using the drill and switched batteries, and made sure the forward, and speed switch were fully engaged.  I used the drill again and brown smoke started coming out of the drill.  I have not used the drill since.

The drill motor turns, but slower and makes a weird sound.  The closest thing I can relate to it is when you attempt to use the drill with a battery that is almost dead.  But these batteries were fully charged and hold a charge for hours.  I don't feel the batteries are the problem at all.

I bought a new drill and was going to sell the batteries and charger since they are still good.  When I did a search online I noticed a recall for Kawasaki drills model # [REDACTED].  The reason was for a bad switch.

I researched my model drill online and found that many have failed for the same reason, although I don't see complaints of smoke like mine.

My concern is where there is smoke, there is fire, or about to be fire.  I feel a person who is working outside in a breeze won't notice the smoke, and the drill may catch fire.

I bought the drill at Costco.  I thought it was about two years ago.  I tried to return the drill without the receipt and was told that they couldn't find a record of my purchase, and assumed it was purchased over 4 years ago.  They don't maintain purchases past 4 years.

incidentDescription: Cuisinart DCB-700BC Grind & Brew coffee maker.  We purchased this coffee maker approximately 6 months ago. We traced the smell back to our Cuisinart DCB-700BC Grind & Brew coffee maker located on our kitchen counter that was smoking and extremely hot.  We immediately unplugged the coffee maker and cleared the smoke smell from the house.  I looked the problem up on the internet and was very surprised to see all of the complaints about the Cuisinart coffee makers over heating, smoking and catching on fire.  I am very upset that these coffee makers are still on the market. have not been recalled and that Cuisinart has no concern for consumer safety.  I can only imagine what may have happened if we were drinking our coffee on the patio this morning and not caught the problem before the pot went up in flames. productDescription: Hand Blender
incidentDescription:
I was making guacamole and I noticed that a piece of avocado was stuck under blender blade. Blender was off but plugged in. I used my left index finger to dislodge avocado. As I rotated blade the motor engaged and started. One of the blender blades became embedded in my finger and I could not remove my finger as I realized the blade was probably stuck in the bone.
I rinsed off my finger and placed a towel around. My husband rushed me to the ER. The ER doctor had no idea how to remove the blender. My husband went home to retrieve a tin snips and special wide edge pliers. The Dr. and my husband and the male nurse took turns cutting the housing down in sections and removing it like peeling a banana. Then the dr. held onto one blade with a pliers as he rotated the embedded blade to remove it from my finger. Xray was taken and I had a stabilized fracture as a wedge of bone had been cut out from my finger and two tiny bone fragments were visible on the xray. I had to get a tetanus shot. I received several IVs of antibiotics while in ER. I also received two stitches and an RX for 10 days of antibiotics. This happened June 30th, 2012, approximately 4 pm. My biggest concern now is for infection in the bone/stitches area. I am taking the antibiotics and keeping injury as clean as possible. Stitches are to be removed in 7-10 days from injury.

productDescription: GRACO Lauren Classic Crib, espresso
model: Graco Lauren Classic Crib, espresso, Model 3251635
incidentDescription:
This is the second occurrence of a child entrapment injury with this same GRACO crib.  I filed a prior CPSC report on 2/17/12, including photos, when the first incident occurred and I never received a response from CPSC investigators or the manufacturer.  See CPSC report 20120217-BC4A4-2147470080.

On or about 4/23/12 (similar to the 2/17/12 injury) my wife placed our 17 month-old daughter in the GRACO crib for a nap.  We generally stopped using the crib after the first injury, but my wife was washing the sheets of the another portable crib that we were using for our daughter, so this crib was the only option.  About 5 to 10 minutes later, my wife heard a loud and distinctive scream from our daughter.  Our daughter almost never cries or screams, even when she injures herself.  This scream was distinctive and left no doubt that our daughter was in extreme pain.  My wife ran into our daughter's bedroom and found our daughter trapped in the front rails of the crib.  Our daughter's leg was pinned between the wooden rails and her body was twisted, trapping her in such a position that her neck was twisted.  The screams became muffled as our daughter's airway closed off, beginning to suffocate her.  My wife worked frantically to dislodge our daughter from the rails, but she described the process as "very difficult" to dislodge our daughter.

Again, our daughter suffered deep bruising on the area of her leg that was trapped, along with swelling and pain.  Fortunately, my wife was nearby and was able to dislodge our daughter before she became unconscious from her neck being trapped in a twisted position.

I do not believe the CPSC, GRACO, or LAJOBI (the manufacturer) have taken appropriate steps to prevent these serious entrapment injuries.

On 6/26/12, I phoned GRACO and notified them of the two injuries associated with this model crib, knowing that many other children must be suffering similar or more serious injuries.  I have now disassembled the crib completely and will no longer use it.  THIS CRIB DESIGN IS UNSAFE AND HAS INJURED MY ONE YEAR-OLD DAUGHTER TWICE.  GRACO was entirely uninterested in investigating or correcting the hazard, and they refused to offer replacement or refund money for the crib during my phone conversation.  GRACO directed me to contact the manufacturer, LAJOBI.

LAJOBI showed even less interest in doing anything, while admitting that they receive a high volume  of calls regarding children being injured by these cribs.  The LAJOBI representative I phoned blamed the CPSC, explaining that LAJOBI crib rails are designed from CPSC standards and until the CPSC changes those standards they will continue to market and sell these cribs.  LAJOBI said they will not replace any cribs or refund any money, citing the CPSC standards.

I told the LAJOBI representative that it seemed odd that a manufacturer would knowingly continue to sell a product that is injuring a high number of children, and again she explained that it was the CPSC's fault, not theirs.  She said the CPSC was aware of the injures and has failed to changed the standards, so there is nothing the manufacturers will do.

Based on my initial investigation, there is plenty of liability to spread around (between GRACO, LAJOBI, and CPSC) and finger-pointing, but everyone is missing this goal of protecting our children - - very odd, since all the parties involved have children as their primary responsibility.

incidentDescription:
I have a Hunter ceiling fan:  Model #25658 (The Lancaster).  It was sold through Lowe's (their item #14651).

The light kit comes with 4 Kraft paper shades that over time have basically been toasted by the heat from the light bulbs.  Recently I have become concerned that this is a potential fire hazard.  I have also had to remove one of the shades since it has come apart at the top and it is in danger of coming into direct contact with the bulb.

I have tried contacting Hunter about this directly, and I have received no response from them.  A search on the internet has revealed that others have experienced the same problem, and that Hunter was not helpful about correcting it.

The shades are uniquely designed; they are secured to each light socket with a screw-on locking ring.  I have tried replacing them with glass shades, but the locking ring does not allow for a traditional glass shade to be securely fastened (at least the ones that I have tried).  This is also a safety issue since this is a ceiling fan and subject to vibrations.

I would like to see Hunter replace the shades with ones that will tolerate the heat from the bulbs, and that can be securely fastened to each light.  I believe that this is a basic design flaw in the product.

productDescription: MVS 10 red and black gasoline powered stand-up scooter
incidentDescription:
I purchased the Motovox MVS 10 gasoline powered stand-up scooter on April 11, 2012 from Sears. On about May 15, 2012 the metal gas tank bracket failed and broke into causing the gas tank to fall off during operation of the scooter. I called the company and a warranty repair was initiated by a local repair shop approximately 10 miles from my home. The Motovox Company replaced the gas tank and paid the repair shop labor for the service. It took approximately two weeks for the repairs to be completed. 

One week later, (approximately June 1, 2012) after the first gas tank repair, while the scooter was in operation the bracket that is part of the scooter frame broke into causing the gas tank to swing out away from the scooter. The tank is bolted on with two bolts and the frame bracket broke in between the two bolts causing one to remain in place and the other to swing out with the gas tank. I called the company three times to date and left messages each time. I haven’t received a call back from the company in reference to this problem. I feel this is a defect and is a direct result of the excessive vibration caused by the normal operation of the scooter engine (two cycle engine) and the lack of protection of the gas tank.

The first time this occurred the tank fell completely off and was being pulled along the sidewalk before the scooter could be stopped. It was still connected by the gas line to the carburetor. This problem has a great risk of the gasoline spilling from the tank and being ignited by the metal gas tank being dragged across the concrete and sparks from the friction. If the gasoline spills when the tank falls off and ignites the gasoline an explosion and resulting fire has the potential to be disastrous. 

The gasoline level measuring unit has fallen loose into the tank on both gas tanks causing the round plastic lens to just lay on top of the tank loose. This allows gasoline to splash out and spill from the tank. 

With the first instance of the bracket failing and now after the repair the frame mounting bracket failing, I feel this is a defect. I want the scooter repaired but I feel this will continue to be a problem with this design and would rather receive a refund from the manufacture and a return of the product to the manufacture. 

Something must be done to ensure the safety of our youth riders of this scooter. They are standing on a problem that when it fails can/will cause a fire/explosion to be literally at their feet. I'm a career firefighter of 20 years and a fire prevention specialist for a metro Atlanta fire department. I can see a huge problem brewing with this defect.

productDescription: Perfect Flame 4 burner with right side additional burner.  Silver with gray, drawer below the unit with double doors below that.  4X12,000 BTU w/ 12,000 BTU side burner - propane only
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
We own a Perfect Flame model SLG2006B outdoor gas grill.  When I went to buy the grill, I went for an upper level grill, liked all the features and design of this particular grill and have been fairly happy with it until about 1 1/2 years ago, it caught on fire while we were cooking on it.  Thankfully we had a fire extinguisher in the house to put it out.

Thinking that it was just too much marinade on the tenderloin and aluminum foil that aided in it catching on fire, I took the unit apart, cleaned it, replaced 1 bad burner, replaced the burner covers and put it back into action.  Then, on Fathers Day, my daughter went out to start warming up the grill.  Again, it caught on fire, this time with no food on it at all.  The thermostat registered over 800 degrees.  This time, I used the dogs watering bucket that happened to be sitting on the deck to drown out the flames.  (Getting a little tired of having to put out flames and clean this grill!)
So, I called the company today, read off the grill numbers, asked if she wanted me to read her the serial numbers - she said, that's not necessary.  We will send you new burners, you just pay for the shipping.  How much is the shipping, I asked?  29.95.  Really - from the reviews that I have been watching and finding on the internet - they want to charge another $30.00 to send you replacement parts b/c they have defective ones?  

Come on... This is a grill with propane and flames.  They are really lucky that the grill did not catch totally on fire, burn up, burn up my deck, explode the propane and wipe out my family and house.  And their response is, we will ship you new burners for $30.00?
I just went out and tested my grill.  2 burners are cracked, a 3rd now not working, the flames got so hot that it is now causing the controller on the left hand side  to not release, therefore keeping the ignition flame going until you pull the controller back.  The racks are now rusted out b/c of the heat and all of my coverings are shot.  Oh, but I could just pay another 12.95 for each heat plate.

So, in order for me to get this grill back up and running - 4 free burners, but $30.00 in shipping, 4 heat shields at 12.95 each = $51.80, the grill racks - over $100, new burner for left hand side control unit - would guess anywhere from $25-$45.  So, for about $225 - $250 I could correct this issue, get my grill back up and running - and possibly use it again.  HMMMMM.  Why would I trust that this would fix the problem and not catch on fire again?  

I am just so thankful that nobody got hurt during either one of these fires and that my house is still in tact.  Also, that my wife and I have been around during BOTH of these episodes.  What would have happened if one of my kids decided to grill something - even though they are young teens - I would have lost everything, house and family included.  And the companies response is... we will give you the burners, but you have to pay for the shipping.  Sorry, but that just [REDACTED}me off - It should be, hey, we are glad that everyone is o.k.   We had a recall on those units, we will be more than happy to either replace your grill with another one that we have or if you would rather continue to use that grill, we will make it right.  

What ever happened to a company doing the right thing?  After 2 fires, I would rather recycle that grill in the scrap yard and get what I can out of it before I buy any more parts for it.  

Here's a recommendation - [REDACTED].  That's Right!  They know how to make grills that don't catch on fire and burn up!

I would send the unit in for repair if I thought that would take care of the problem. Because of the design I feel this will continue to happen. The photo is the mount for the pressure release knob. In the lower part of the photo you see a metal cup the site on the metal lid. Inside that medal cup is where the plastic mount goes that holds the whole assembly together. This plastic mount is about 2cm thick and will not stand up to constant heating and cooling. You can see that it wasn't just a random piece of plastic braking the whole assembly disintegrated. All of the little pieces of plastic should be one piece. What would have happened if that failed under pressure? Deni concern for their customers safety should include this piece. productDescription: Unvented gas log heater, 24 inches wide
productType: Gas or Lp Heaters, Other or Not Specified (392)
incidentDescription: I was exposed to a low-level, injurious concentration of carbon monoxide (CO) over a 4-month period by daily use of a gas-log fireplace heating system installed in the un-vented mode.  I believe this system lacks sufficient safeguards to maintain the high efficiency necessary to be used un-vented.  I learned that a change in position of the logs results in sooting, which is a visual indicator that CO is being produced.  In my case, a fairly heavy soot coating on the walls and windows finally alerted me to the hazard, but it was not until after I suffered a sudden 90-percent loss of hearing in my left ear on December 23, 2011.  I subsequently learned that long-term exposure to low concentrations of CO can lead to health problems because of the cumulative effect, with a retention time in the bloodstream of several hours.   In my case, it was four months of daily exposure each evening to a low-level of CO (our CO detector, with a threshold of 100 ppm, provided no indication).  The result, as verified by a physician, was nerve damage that caused hearing loss along with unsteadiness and vertigo.  I've attached a technical paper that describes the link between CO and hearing loss.  When the heating season began, I moved the logs to relight the pilot after turning it off for the summer.  The owners' manual presents vague warnings about moving the logs and an incomprehensible diagram of log placement, but there is no warning that directly relates to a specific hazard of CO.  Later, after the logs were reset and cleaned by the original installer, they shifted on their own to again cause sooting.  There is no way to lock the logs in place.  Had this been a vented installation, there would have been no problem, but the dealer's selling point was that the high efficiency of the burner makes it perfectly safe to be un-vented.   When it is vented, of course, it provides substantially less heat to the room/home.  Beyond the direct effect such as I experienced, it is known that CO exposure during pregnancy can lead to fetal poisoning or death.

productDescription: Storkcraft Sheffield Stages Crib- espresso 2010
incidentDescription:
I am having a really big issue with the crib that my 1 year old son sleeps in. When he is playing in it after or before sleeping his legs get stuck in the rails! It is not like they get stuck once or twice here or there, but many many times a day. They are getting stuck in the sides so bad that his legs turn blue. In order for me to get his legs out I have to put a lot of lotion on his legs and the rails and slowly work them out. I am so scared that he might end up breaking his leg! I have e-mailed the crib company about my concerns and the reply I got was the following; "We recognize and appreciate your concerns regarding your son’s leg getting stuck between the railing on the crib sides. As children grow and start to become active they begin to explore their environment which includes their crib.
Please be assured that all Stork Craft cribs, including your Sheffield Stages Crib, meets or exceeds safety standards for both Canadian and  United States.  Government and Industry standards regulate the design and construction of cribs in Canada and the U.S., these regulatory requirements stipulate, among other things, the dimensions and spacing.  The spacing between the spindles in the rails or panels must not be more than 6 cm or 2 3/8 inches.  The intent behind the specifications regulated by the standards is to protect infants from life threatening or debilitating injuries such as head entrapment."
I understand that they have to make it to where young ones don't get hurt. But my son is getting hurt! He has bruises on his legs from them getting stuck. I have gone to look at other cribs but I can not afford a new one. What am I suppose to do?

productDescription: Kenmore liquid propane gas grill sears model no. 415.16649010
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
My Kenmore gas grill bottle emptied in a matter of minutes while cooking last Sunday afternoon.  This fire caused  our families' deck to burn as well as scorching other established bushes.  Since there was no other way to quelch the flames while securing the gas bottle, this person's arm suffered second to third degree burns in doing so..  The grilll experienced an unconrolled spike in temperature, so intense that the foods, in a  matter of minutes, became scorched beyond recognition.  In fact what remained, resembled carbon lumps  and a aluminum pan that we were using, simply melted.  In addition to suffering from the burns to my arm and having our dinner ruined, we were forced to incure additional expenditures just to replace our meal.. Additionally, the shrubs in question, are highly valued Gardenias.  These bushes have been very well tended but such a broad, intense fire, resulting from this defective gas grill are problematic for a number of reasons.   Such unrestrained heat and fire damage is disturbing, at the very least, as well as life-threatening. 

In summary, as a result of this life-theatening event, the pricey beef ribs to be barbecued were ruined, my deck was on fire and one railing damaged by the intense flames. Additionally, my wife's highly valued Gardenia bushes were batterd by this intense fire.  This Kenmore defective grill appears to have, as they say, gone super nova - meaning that more than  3/4 -full gas bottle was instantaneously  depleted.

productDescription: food processor marketed for babies and toddlers
incidentDescription:
We blended cooked food and water in the "baby bullet" food processor. While feeding our 13-month old son, we noticed he was having difficulty chewing. He finally let us look into his mouth and we noticed a piece of rubber that was approximately an inch long. (It was the gasket to the food processor that sits at the base below the threading where the cup screws into the blade.) We matched that piece with the remaining gasket that had broken and found that there is still a one-inch piece missing. The remaining gasket was still firmly seated in the bottom of the base. We believe the missing piece was swallowed by our child. Fortunately, he did not choke on it necessitating an ambulance to help in a lethal situation. Our pediatrician indicated that since this material is plastic, it will not appear on an x-ray. We can only watch our son and wait to see if he has any side effects or if the piece will pass through his intestines. 

Before using the processor, I had removed the gasket to clean it since food was trapped underneath it. Replacement gaskets were included with the box. Again to reiiterate, I firmly inserted the gasket back into the bottom after washing it. 

The "baby bullet user manual and cookbook" indicates to inspect the gasket before using. It does not instruct on whether or not the gasket needs to be replaced at set intervals nor does it give instructions on how to replace it. This would be helpful information since food does get trapped below it regularly causing bacteria to build if not removed and washed.

This product needs to be taken out of distribution immediately. This information needs to be reported to the news agencies.

Please respond to us as soon as possible.

Thanks
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: electric Smoker
incidentDescription:

He used the replacement smoker possibly 8 times, however then he had been cooking ribs in the smoker in April 19th, 2012, turned the smoker off but didn't unplug it.
He came out to put the dog out around six hours later and realized that the smoker, although turned off was running strong at around 300 degrees.
He unplugged the smoker and sat it to the side to cool off.
Caller has not used the smoker since then but has plugged it in to test whether this incident would be repeated and it has.
He received payment from the retailer as refund, he has no financial request but would request that the public be notified of the fire danger this grill has.

Propane Grill

incidentDescription:
Like many others that purchased the Perfect Flame Double Lid Four Burner Gas, model GAC3615, we also experienced this product burst into flame and engulf the entire cooking chamber exactly as described by the other complaints, with flame involving both interior and exterior surfaces. In our circumstance this dangerous event has now occurred three times. This grill is manufactured by Lucas Innovation Inc., of China, distributed by BBQTEK Enterprise, Inc. and sold exclusively by Lowes is apparently incredibly dangerous. 

At first it was presumed a cooking error had been committed, however after the third occurrence where our home almost caught fire, we became suspect and discovered this model grill is subject to a partial recall due this specific issue. Lowes was incredibly helpful once we discovered the recall however BBQTEK refused to honor or acknowledge the recall of their product unless it could be specifically identified as being a part of a particular manufacturer’s serial number string and date code. Due to cleaning efforts and weathering the label on our particular grill was worn and torn so only the model number is identifiable. This complaint has been added since apparently the entire product line is deficient not only part of it as in the present recall. We encourage any one that has purchased this model grill to file a complaint to expand the recall to the entire product line.

productDescription: Revlon 1875 Ionic Ceramic blow dryer, silver & maroon, manufactured by Helen of Troy, their model # RV484.
model: Revlon 1875 Ionic Ceramic Blow Dryer model RV484
incidentDescription:
I purchased a Revlon 1875 Ionic Ceramic blow dryer approximately 1 1/2 years ago. For the last couple of months it stops working when I'm using it and if I move it around it starts working again, like there is a problem with the cord. Also when I change the setting from hot to warm it smells funny. Yesterday I was in the store with my sister, who also owns this exact dryer (purchased around the same time), and she tells me there is something wrong with her blow dryer. In her word "it's possessed". She then described the exact same problem I'm having. I decided to call Revlon and when I [REDACTED] the blow dryer model I found product reviews for this blow dryer, dating back to 2007, where people tell stories similar to mine, many have worse stories where this blow dryer catches fire, burns their hand and/or hair. Many people have the blow dryer for only days or months. I know that mine is 1 1/2 yrs old but that's not really old for a blow dryer. My last one was a Conair &  I had it for years. With all the problems this blow dryer causes it makes me wonder why it is still on the market and hasn't been recalled. 

I called Revlon, who directed me to call Helen of Troy because they manufacture Revlon's small appliances. When I called Helen of Troy I was instructed to send the blow dryer back with $5 because it was out of the six month warranty, and they would send a replacement. When I complained that it's not reasonable to be without a blow dryer for a minimum of 2 weeks and I have to pay to ship it back to them, plus the $5 fee when I could go out and buy a new one for $20 they said they would waive the $5 fee, send me a replacement & when I get it send the defective one back so they can test it. Quite frankly I'm a little afraid to use this dryer until I get the replacement.

incidentDescription:
On Thursday January 26, 2012, my Cuisinart FlavorBrew 12-cup Coffeemaker, model DCC-750BK caught on fire. I started the brew cycle and stepped into another room. During the brewing process, the coffee pot began began making a loud buzzing sound and I could smell burning/melting plastic. When I re-entered the kitchen, smoke was pouring out of the brew plate area at the bottom of the device. The brew plate was glowing bright red and small flames/sparks were coming out from beneath the front area of the brew plate. It was very frightening! If I hadn't been in the house at the time, there would have been a fire and smoke damage.

I'm concerned that is coffeemaker is a potential fire hazard. I'm reporting this incident because I'm concerned that my experience may not be an isolated occurrence.  And I want the Consumer Products Safety Commission and other consumers to be aware of the potential fire hazard. 

My Cuisinart FlavorBrew 12-cup Coffeemaker was purchased January 28, [2011].  It was in use for only one year.  It has a 3-year limited warranty.

productDescription: Charmglow Gas Grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
The context of the the following report is based on a post-recall, repair-kit retrofitted Charmglow grill:

As many grill owners know, recalls are important to follow and heed. Having purchase a Charmglow Home Depot Grill in 2005, we learned about a recall and received the retrofit kit after incident #1.

Incident #1 After lighting the grill last year, we noticed the smell of propane within minutes. The igniter had burned through the hose. We immediately found a recall on CPSC and notified the manufacturer. We installed the retrofit kit.

Incident #2 Two months after retro fit install, we were grilling happily on our patio- we had 7 guests and a two year old waiting for burgers and steak. Instead, we heard a whoosh and saw flames licking our from the interior of the grill. After running for safety, we called the FD and waited across the street for the inevitable propane explosion. Thankfully, one of our guests was able to extinguish the fire. What we have now is a charred patio area , frayed nerves and questions about the 'repair' kit, along with overall negligible consumer confidence in the manufacturer.

productDescription: Espresso maker with a water reservoir, coffee reservoir, coffee grinder, steam nozzle and hot water nozzle.
incidentDescription: I have the Jura Capresso model Impressa S7 espresso maker.  This model has a water reservoir which always contains water.  It is able to froth milk for cappucino, makes espresso, and supplies hot water for tea.  The hot water either comes out of a coffee spigot, a steam spigot, or a hot water spigot.  I was making espresso a few days ago, the unit first froths milk from a steam nozzle.  The steam did not shut off when it normally would.  It did shut off about 20 seconds after it normally would.  The coffee came out of the correct spigot after that.  The unit did something like this once before, at the time I called Capresso and I was told to wiggle a flap and clean it.  I was also told to change the fineness of the coffee grind setting.  I did this this time again and thought the problem was solved.  The next morning my wife was making espresso, the machine redirected all of the water through the frothing nozzle, no coffee came out.  The frothing nozzle alternated between boiled water and steam through the entire cycle.  I called Capresso and spoke to [redacted], I asked him if there was a recall on this unit. He said there isn't.  I explained what was happening. He told me I could send the unit in for repair.  I told him I had this unit reconditioned one year ago and don't want to do this on a yearly basis.  He told me to cycle the knobs on the unit from coffee to hot  water to steam and see if that will free a stuck valve.  In the process of doing this, the container I was using, filled up.  The unit stopped pouring water, I emptied the container and the steam nozzle started spraying steam suddenly.  I ran to put the container under the nozzle and scalded my finger.  There is no blister just a painful red spot, nothing to worry about but enough to think what if a family member was standing by the machine when it would start spraying steam.

productDescription: Kenmore canister vacuum with attachments
incidentDescription:
I received a Kenmore canister vacuum cleaner about 5 years ago.I very seldom used it because of the weight of the wands. It came with power beaters etc which I didn't need because of hard wood floors only. If I used this machine more then 20-25 times that is a lot.  Mainly I used my old 30+year old vacuum or electric brooms. On May 17th I got out said vacuum...placed it on the floor in the room to be cleaned.  I extracted the electric wire from the machine, plugged it into the outlet. I then proceeded to turn the machine (on switch is in the handle). I felt a tremble in my hand and immediately saw several sparks coming from the hose connector to the machine.I dropped the wand handle and quickly ran to unplug the electrical wire from the outlet   I could smell something burnt. After awhile I moved the canister to a safe spot,afraid it might start a fire. When my son came to visit he checked it out to discover that the connector hose had dislodged from its covering exposing electrical wires which in turn shorted out the start up wiring. The covering was still in the machine but the connector hose (with the electrical wires) was touching something which caused it to shoot sparks as it had.  I have pictures of the defective parts. We purchased a new handle, hose, connector unit in an attempt to replace the defective unit and that  is when we found out the start up unit burnt out also. 

I called Sears repair number and was told there was nothing they could do for me... since the hose connector  was not a recall.  Upon further investigation I found that in 1987 there was a recall for a Kenmore vacuum cleaner hose problem very, very similar to mine.  That is why I am writing to you.  I know it has been several years since the recall and even though different companies are manufacturing these machines for Sears perhaps their design plans are still flawed.   I think it should be looked into before there is a house fire or some injury occurs.  I  think I  was lucky enough to escape both.
I wonder how many other people have had this problem and just passed it off as a lemon of a machine. As I previously stated ... the machine was not abused or over used  for this to happen.
I will be glad to share any other information that you require.

Respectfully yours,
[REDACTED]

incidentDescription: Last week, while cleaning, the hand held portion of my Ergorapido turned itself on.  When it would not shut off, I set it on the counter to let the battery run itself out.  A short time later I smelled burning plastic.  It had burned a spot through the paper towel it was set on and burned a small spot in my butcher block counter top.  I tossed it in the sink and ran water over it.  It stopped running so I turned the water off.  In about 30 seconds, the water on the machine started to sizzle.  Then it came back on and the battery element on the back of it turned red and started to burn again.  I soaked it in water for about 5 minutes.  It stopped.  Once I turned the water off it started up again.  It  finally put it outside, in the middle of the driveway where it eventually burned itself out.  I wrote to Elerctrolux asking them about this but, other then acknowledging my e-mail, I have not had a reply.

productDescription: Perfect Flame Barbeque grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
My Perfect Flame Barbeque grill went up in flames.  While preheating, flames started going very high out of the unit and soon the fire was out of control.  The wires and the gas line were completely engulfed by the fire.  Thankfully my patio is made of cement and we had a calm day with no wind.  That doesn't happen very often in central Oklahoma.  A strong south wind would have caused untold troubles with a fire that size.

In January 2010, I received replacement burners and lid and replaced those parts as part of a recall.  My model number is SLG2008A.  It was difficult to replace the burners, since the bolts that held the original burners were completely void of any heads to put a screwdriver on.  Apparently the replacement parts only lasted about as long as the original parts did.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

I bought a new 2-4 cup Farberware Percolator from Bed Bath and Beyond in Garden City, Long Island on Merchants Boulevard.(UPC code 3205102243). Other Numbers on the box PK 4000SS, A/W #1498-00, Date code 1117 08
1 000 W 120V 60HZ

The bottom of the lid is so thin and knifelike that it sliced into my finger easily and caused a significant cut.  I brought the product back to the store and told them what happened and advised them of the danger present.  I believe this product should not be sold as it presents a danger every time the lid is handled.  The edge of the lid can easily cut through flesh.

I tried several times to contact the company.  The number for Farberware which you can get on line - 800-809-7166- refers you to another number 800-233-9054.  I tried this number several times.  One time, it put me on hold for an inordinate amount of time and I had to hang up.  The second time, it put me on hold and then a mesage in French came on which I did not understand and I did not continue to hold.  As yet, I have not notifed the company of their problem with the lid.

I feel this product is not safe to the consumer and should be addressed.  Although the cut on my finger healed, I could have been worse and lids present a danger.

productDescription: Andis Elevate Dryer 1875 Watt, this was the upgrade provided by the manufacturer after the failure of the first two units.
incidentDescription:
This is a DANGEROUS product.  I have experienced three separate units fail by electrical fire within each unit's 1 year warranty.

I was using my blow dryer when I noticed that I was having problem turning the switch on and off, the handle was heating up and then I saw flames and smoke.  I unplugged the blow dryer.  The item continued to smolder.  I removed it from my home due to the smoldering wires.

This is the THIRD dryer from ANDIS COMPANY where I have experienced an electrical malfunction and smoke/spark/flames.  I have used this item for personal use and less than 10 minutes per day. I have used in different homes so know my home wiring is not contributing to the problem. I reported the problem each time to the manufacturer and requested a replacement.  I returned the defective units hoping they were trouble shooting the problem.  This third failure shows the Manufacturer has not corrected the reported defect.

I purchased the first unit on 1/23/10.  It was a Model MI-5 1875 Watt Ceramic Hair Dryer.  I returned it to the company after it "burned out" with sparking and smoking.
This unit was replaced by the company on 1/13/11.

The second unit was another MI-5 Dryer.  It too "burned out" with sparking and smoking on 10/28/11.   I returned to ANDIS and they replaced with their top of the line MI-5 Elevate Dryer which they shipped out the same day.  This dryer last only 6 months before the failure described above.

Three wheel scooter; Golden Technology  DESCRIPTION: GC110D-SWI-BLU-BLK - LITERIDER - 3 WHEEL
Serial Number GL10H0313

VA Purchase order number is [REDACTED]
incidentDescription:
The decedent, a 93 year old male, was driving a motorized scooter on a sidewalk and then drove it on the grass, where he hit an object causing the scooter to tip over and then land on top of him.  


Per the medical records from the hospital, this incident resulted in "an acute broken displaced arthroplasty of the right knee with right thigh hematoma, right hemarthrosis superimposed on history of long-term warfarin therapy".  Seven days after the incident, while the decedent was hospitalized, he suffered a "catastrophic neurological event", suspected to be a stroke and he expired the next day.  

However, autopsy revealed the arthroplasty was not broken, only severely worn down.  There was no hemarthrosis.  There was no evidence of a stroke or subdural hematoma.  There was a very large hematoma to the right upper thigh, which was thought to have contributed to significant blood loss resulting in decreased perfusion and death.  The cause of death was ruled: "blunt force leg injury", with the manner being "accidental".

Now, as it was, the plastic handle had already burned me a few times and I always had to use a potholder to pick it up, but this burning smell was unbearable. I brought it to Macy's in Sherman Oaks, where they told me the kettle had been discontinued due to melting handles and other problems. Just from having it in my car for a short time, the smell was unbearable and lingered for days. It was awful. I couldn't bring the kettle back in my house so I put it in the recycling bin outside.
