productDescription: White, approximately 12 1/2 inches high, main section oscillates on a base that has a safety switch on the bottom surface.  The main section has power light in top center, lower on left is thermostat dial, on right dial for:  OFF, FAN, LO, HI. The front fan area has swerved horizontal lines, and 3 swerved intersecting vertical lines.  Name"OPTIMUS" in bold black capital letters at bottom of main section.  The back of the main section is a rectangular grill-type area, many horizontal lines and 3 vertical lines with a circle enclosing 3 smaller circles arranged vertically.
incidentDescription:
Purchased early in year 2012 from Menards: OPTIMUS oscillating heater with fan, 2 heat settings and thermostat.  I discarded box and receipt after 3 months as thought working well.  Yesterday when cleaning carpet in my mother's bedroom, I saw that the plug (without ground) had melted into the extension cord.  They are now fused (melted) together.  My mother used this heater daily, and I'm glad to have discovered this before disaster struck.
Thank you.

productDescription:
Weber Genesis E-330 Liquid Propane Gas Grill
Model 6531001
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
I have a Weber Genesis grill and was using it a few days ago (5/5/2012).  The fuel hose caught on fire which melted the rubber hose.  A hole erupted on the hose that then spewed propane out until I was able to shut it off.  Upon investigation, I determined that Weber incorrectly assembled the hose.  The rubber hose from the propane tank is connected to what they call a bulkhead.  From the bulkhead a metal flex tube is connected to route the fuel to the grill and side burner.  On this bulkhead they inserted the rubber hose where the metal one should have been.  The rubber hose touched the hot grill tray which caused the fire.

I was fortunate, this could have been much worse.

Repeated calls and e-mails to Weber have not been positive.  They refuse to accept responsibility which is why I am reporting this issue.  I am concerned that there may be other grills with the same issue.

Regards,

[REDACTED]

productDescription: Master Forge Outdoor Gas Grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
I purchased a Master Forge Outdoor Gas Grill, Model # L3218, Serial # L32001245.
Two weekends ago, I turned it on to pre-heat, went into the house, and moments later ran back outside when I saw flames engulfing the right side of the grill. I reached through the flames and shut off the burners, but I could hear the gas continuing to flow and the flames did not subside. I opened the front doors and saw the gas hose, still attached to the gas tank, but not the grill, flopping around on fire. I reached inside, released the tank restraining band, slid the tank rack out of the grill and shut the tank valve off. Fortunately I was not injured and only had my arm hair singed. The resulting damage to my grill however has rendered it completely useless and irrepairable.

While attempting to find out information on the company to file a complaint, I discovered that the Consumer Product Safety Commission in cooperation with Sagittarius Sporting Goods of China have announced a safety recall on the Master Forge 5-Burner Gas Grill, model #L3218 sold by Lowes Home Improvement between September 2009 and November 2009 because of a known problem where the rubber gas line may come in contact with the Grill's firebox causing it to melt, leading to a fire. I never received any such notice.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: grill scrubb brush: a flat brush with metallic bristles and a handle, used to clean debris off a grill before cooking outdoors
productType: Manual Cleaning Equipment (Excl. Buckets and Pails) (480)
incidentDescription:
Tonight for sunday night dinner we cooked burgers.

My 5 year old found a piece of metral bristle in her burger. We consider ourselves lucky since the bristle is probably small enough not to be noticed while chewing it with the burger's bread and lettuce but could also find itself in the stomach and create a performation.

Prior to putting the burgers on the grill, we cleaned our grill with a brush made by Brinkmann. The name of the product is "Grill Scrub Brush". It appears that the bristle in question broke loose from the brush while we were cleaning the grill surface. When my wife put the burgers on the grill, the bristle lodged into the meat, which eventually ended up on my daughter's plate. We consider ourselves very lucky that the sharp bristle did not end up being swallowed by her. Upon closer examination, the bristle in question was found to be brittle and could have easily broken in half. It appeared to be sharp enough, if swallowed, to potentially perforate the stomach or intestines.

The brush in question was bought last year and still looks functional, but we will definitely discard it and use a new one. It seems consumers need to be made aware of the potential danger of this brush.

productDescription: 12-cup programmable automatic coffee maker
incidentDescription:
Cuisinart coffee programmable coffee maker model DCC1200 purchased new in Nov. 2010 through Amazon.com.  On 5/4/12 after a two-hour brew and keep warm sequence, I was in another room and heard a loud sizzling and crackling sound coming from our kitchen.  The unit was apparently off, but bluish smoke was pouring from the unit and the remaining coffee in the carafe  (about two 5 oz. cups) was quite hot.  I quickly unplugged the unit before things got worse.  Thankfully, my kitchen counter top was not damaged and I was home to intervene.  It supposedly has a three year warranty, but other owners have lamented the hassle of repackaging the defective product for return and paying for round trip shipping costs totaling nearly $30.00 (for returned and replacement units).  

I will not have another Cuisinart coffee maker in my home- it's not worth risking a fire and endangering my family.  Multiple Cuisinart coffee maker failures across different models identical to my scenario have been reported through the CPSC saferproducts.gov web site.  Cuisinart should be compelled to recall and stop selling these defective units and back their product with full refunds regardless if under warranty; no questions, no hassles.  It is only a matter of time before Cuisinart is going to face property damage or loss of life claims from knowingly continuing to sell a dangerous product.

productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription: Purchased a BRINKMAN LP gas patio grill at Home Depot; the grill is labeled PORTICO COLLECTION and is model # 810-3260-S.  I took the unit home and assembled per the instructions and connected LP gas tank.  Started grill to grill fish in a basket.  Waited for grill to warm up with temperature set at medium low.  I was ready to place fish on grill and reached with one hand to grab the grill handle on the front to open the grill top.  The grill was so hot I dropped the handle as it was too hot to hold.  I received minor burns on two fingers.  This grill also was found to have very sharp edges on the sides of grill top.  I believe that this product represents a potential hazard and is improperly designed/manufactured.  I am returning product to Home Depot and advising them of potential issues.  If a small child were to walk by this grill while it was turned on and reached to grab the grill handle, I believe that they could suffer burns to their fingers/hands.  The grill shipping box indicates that it is "DESIGN CERTIFIED"; i am not sure if this is a industry ceretification or simply a play on words.  This product is dangerous and hazardous.

productDescription: Silver and black hand mixer with digital speed reading.  Details: Model#: HM820; Lot#: 2104; Mfg Date: 1137; "QC PASS 32"
incidentDescription:
When cleaning off my two-weeks-old mixer at my kitchen sink, I received a shock as I went to turn off the (grounded metal) faucet.  I had been running the mixer in a mixing bowl full of soapy water to help clean off the "beaters."  The mixer was not at all submerged, but my hands may have been a little wet.  I was plugged into a GFCI receptacle.  It was a low-current shock, and I did not experience any burning or muscle contraction (the GFCI also did not trip, though it has been tested to be functioning).

This is a consumer product and I was using it at home, but professionally I work as an Occupational Safety and Health Professional for an electrical contractor.  My opinion is that the device is leaking current, and we just never realized it until the conditions were just right (my hands were wet and I touched a grounded source--the faucet handle).

incidentDescription:
Hi there. I ordered a "ShedPal"to groom my Olde English Bulldog. I also bought one from "PetSmart", and returned because I received my ShedPal order in the mail. SO- these are popular and on the shelves at many pet stores. Regardless, I began to groom him with this battery operated handheld dog/cat/animal grooming tool. He seemed to be okay (besides the normal squirming associated with grooming him) when he, all of the sudden, jumped back 6feet darting into the wall because he got scared of the ShedPal around his (button like) tail area. After seeing this odd behavior I decided to take a better look at the ShedPal to see how it works...

That's when I saw it has a spinning ball type mechanism in the groomer machine that will burn/possible maim a human finger. This leads me to believe (because it was so easy to burn my own finger on this spinning ball that's not covered by anything what-so-ever), that is burned my dogs little button tail as well when I was grooming him. I am a young adult in my 20's, but I seriously worry about all of the (possible elderly, because they sell these things through an 888 phone #) people ordering this product that maybe can't see as well... It just seems very dangerous to me, and could hurt a human OR animal. If someone were to try to groom their cat, or long hair dog, I don't see how the hair doesn't get caught and tangled and ripped out too...?! A small dog or cat could be easily injured by this tool, or a child, or adult...

Please do something about this...?! thank you!!!

While the consumer was holding down the juicer, one of the two plastic flaps on the top panel of the juice broke and the debris went up in the direction of the consumer. The product continued to juice on its own for nearly another 20-30 seconds, the product began to smoke. The consumer unplugged the juicer from the outlet. By design, the 2 plastic flaps are on opposite sides of the juicer.  The consumer did not call the retailer as she is not sure of who they are. The consumer also did not find it necessary to call the fire department or her home insurance company. 

The consumer called the firm 2 days ago about the incident and was told they could not help her as the product is out of warranty. The consumer stated that there was no damage to the structure of her home.

productDescription: This is a four burner, Perfect Flame double lid gas grill.  It is metallic gray.  Three burners are located under one lid, a fourth burner is located under a separate lid that can be lit apart from the three burners.  the bottom portion of the grill is a gray cover.  The tank is accessed from the rear of the grill.
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
The Perfect Flame gas grill gas burners all began to significantly deteriorate over the course of three years of ownership/usage, with holes in the burner tubes that were approximately 3-4 inches in length and 1/2 to 3/4 in. in height.  This problem was seen in other Perfect Flame models that were the subject of a recall by the company; however, this product was not.  

The deterioration of all four burners allows large quantities of gas to escape unregulated, leading to large flames and the potential for fires inside the grill and outside.  On several occasions, the bottom of the grill would catch fire.  The flames on two of the four burners, when gas was left on medium, would rise approximately 6 inches to 1 ft. above the surface of the grill.

As was previously mentioned, the grill is approximately 3-4 years old.  It has been kept covered the entire time of ownership.

The Perfect Flame grill was subject to prior recalls, with the SLG model being recalled for similar reasons (November 18, 2009, Release #10-043).  The GAC, which I own, was subject to a recall for different reasons, although my date code (LO) is outside of the recall range.

productDescription:
Tassimo Home Coffee Brewer
TAS2001UC/ Serial #C100230/ FD9004
incidentDescription:
In (approximately) August, 2011, I purchased a Tassimo Home Brewer.  There was a recall due to the discs exploding in the machine.  I received the new part in early March, 2012 and used it according to the directions provided.

The discs continue to explode.  When this happens, HOT WATER and GRINDS SPEW from the machine.  I have taken pictures on various occasions to document this dangerous condition.

On April 27, 2012, I sent an e-mail to Tassimo Customer Service with the photos and on April 28th, I received a response that someone will be in touch with me within 24 hours.  Nobody contacted me so on May 3, 2012, I called Tassimo.  

After speaking with [REDACTED] and providing her with the information regarding the machine (TAS2001UC/ Serial #C100230/ FD9004) I was put on hold and transferred to [REDACTED].

[REDACTED] explained that although Tassimo had sent out the retrofit t-disc holder, they recognize that there are still problems.  He stated he will send us a newly retrofitted t-disc holder. Due to the number of discs that exploded, they will also be sending replacement coffee discs.

I explained to [REDACTED] that I am highly concerned about the safety of this machine - it is dangerous and that if Tassimo had already sent out retrofitted holders, why is it that they have created "newer" retrofitted holders?  He said he understands my concern, but he can assure me that the new part will solve the problem.

I believe that due to the recall and CONTINUED issues, the CPSC needs to be aware of this continued problem with this product.  Scalding water is a major safety issue and I do hope that the CPSC will continue to investigate these issues.

productDescription:
CUSTOMER SERVICE:  
I recently purchased and opened this carton, shipped from Distribution Center, 3820 Micro Drive, Millington TN 38053 
$94.94 -- Please credit back to my credit card.  
 
Magnifying Floor Lamp 
 
SKU # 200370-01
 
UPC: 0896368001502
 
Customer [REDACTED] 
Reference # [REDACTED] 
Last week I was planning to deliver this lamp to my elderly mother who is frail & lives alone.  It was to be a surprise for her for Mother's Day.  I unpacked the product and had it and the box & packing foam in the back end of my station wagon.  My car was parked inside my garage.  I left the back gate open, and was loading up her hot food and some other things to deliver to her.  I was inside my house (attached garage) for no longer than 8 - 10 minutes when I smelled smoke, which quickly became stronger & stronger.  I thought that neighbors were perhaps burning leaves or ??
 
Imagine my shock & horror, when I went out to my car with a kettle of hot food, and I saw heavy smoke billowing out of the back of my car!!!!!!!  
 
In that short time, less than 10 minutes, the mirror must have caught sunlight & started the shipping box on fire, melted a big hole in the Styrofoam into the carpeting of my station wagon, AND  left about 7 burned melted areas in my car's carpeting over the expanse of an area 14 x 16 inches wide.  I am left with these permanent deep blackened burn areas in my vehicle's carpeting.  These burns now hard as rocks.  
 
HOWEVER, I seriously question the safety of a product that caused this much damage in such a short time.  My mother could have sustained serious injury and/or death by fire had this occurred inside her home.  She could have lost her home as well.  She lives alone, has [REDACTED], and could not have exited the house on her own.
 
I would like a full refund of this product.  I am shipping it back to the Distribution Center today.  I was billed $94.94 for this item.  I am returning it in the original cartons, so that you can see for yourselves what damage was done to the shipping materials.  The burn hole in the exterior box is 5" x 3", and the Styrofoam melted-burned area is 6" x 6".  
 
This is obviously  a very dangerous and unsafe product and should be pulled off the market immediately!

productDescription:
Sanyo SK-CV8S, Convection Toaster Oven

The unit is a countertop toaster oven, which comes with a removable oven rack and several dishes to ease baking/heating.
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
Product: Sanyo SK-CV8S, Convection Toaster Oven

I am writing because this unit has a fundamental design flaw that should disqualify it from the market: the oven rack has no fasteners to prevent it from falling out when trying to remove items from the oven. That means when you go to pull a 400 degree baking dish out of the unit, you need to put your hand entirely inside the unit in order to extricate the dish. If you do what a normal user would want to do and slide out the rack a few inches so you don't have to put your hand within inches of the top heating rods, the entire rack tips forward and dumps your 400 degree food directly onto you!

I have had this incident happen to me several times to date, with items as relatively innocuous as toast (today) to items that present a real danger such as casserole (last month). I truly fear that if a consumer is not aware of this design flaw and goes to remove a hot dish from this convection oven with a child at his/her foot, there is a very real possibility of permanent burn injuries to that child.

After the rack fell completely out of the oven toward me the first time, I tried to be careful by not pulling the oven rack out too far. This, of course, brought my hand in contact with the top heating rods, scarring my left hand. The design flaw makes this product a "lose-lose" for users. If you want to pull your items out of the rack, you end up with your 400 degree food on your legs and feet. If you try to avoid the rack falling out, you end up burning your hands inside the unit.

I am taking the time to report this product because I truly believe you will see reports of burn injuries as a result of this product, with the unrestrained rack being responsible for most of these injuries.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription:
Eureka model AS1000A UPRIGHT VACUUM CLEANER
Serial number: UU321109005638
PURCHASED AT WAL-MART
incidentDescription:
I purchased a Eureka brand upright vacuum, model AS1000A.
Issues are as follows:

1. Regardless of carpet height setting on the vacuum, the brush continues to spin, even when using the hose with attachments in "Tool" mode. 
As all other vacuum cleaners I have purchased have an automatic brush shut off feature when switching to use hose and cleaning tools, I assumed this vacuum would do the same. It does not, and there is no warning regarding this in the user manual. I fortunately noticed a burning smell while cleaning upholstery, and looked at the vacuum cleaner to find the cord underneath the beater brush. 
Had I been a minute longer, it would have burned through to the bare wire. The insulation was burned almost completely through.
I called customer service and was told that, to help avoid the issue, I should change the height adjustment on the vacuum cleaner to "High Carpet". To make that change, you have to unlock (tilt the handle down) first, or the brush height will not change. I didn't know that, but it isn't in the owners manual either. 
Regardless, if I'm vacuuming high carpet (which I am) and the same situation presents itself, the brush still turns, and the potential for a burnt cord is still there, so the customer service persons "fix" is useless.

When reading the owners manual on how to use accessories on page 5, the first thing you read at the top of the page says: 
"How to use Accessories" ! "Handle must be in the upright position"
The next line: " Before Using Accessories" 
                        1. Raise Height Adjustment to "High Carpet".
                        2. Turn Air Path Selector Knob to "Tools".
**Notice the instruction to "tilt the handle back first" is not in the instructions**

If another consumer didn't know this (to tilt the handle back first), and followed those instructions to the letter, the height adjustment would not change. If the same situation that happened to me (3 times now) happened to them, they would suffer the same result or worse.

In my opinion, Eureka should recall these vacuum cleaners because there is a serious potential electrical safety hazard. I consider myself to be a fairly safety conscious person, and understand the importance of not running over a vacuum cord while vacuuming a carpet or floor. 
But if I'm using an attachment hose, and looking up while vacuuming drapes, or the back of a couch, or whatever, I shouldn't have to worry that if I accidentally pull the hose too hard, it could cause the vacuum cleaner to turn, and provide opportunity for the constantly spinning brush to come in contact with the cord.

productDescription: Cuisinart DCC 1200 Coffeemaker
incidentDescription:
A number of weeks ago I brewed a pot of coffee in my Cuisinart DCC-1200 coffeemaker. After starting the process I left the kitchen and went to another room. A short while later I heard a popping and crackling sound from the kitchen area. I went to investigate and I saw smoke coming from the coffeemaker and I smelled burning plastic. I unplugged the coffeemaker.
I called the Cuisinart customer service number and was told that the computers were down and that I could not be helped. I called the next day and was told that the computer was only processing new sales orders, not service orders. I waited several days and called again. This time I was told that the coffeemaker would be replaced. I was given a service order number and instructed to cut the electrical cord from the appliance and mail it in upon receipt of my replacement.
Weeks went by and I received no replacement unit. I called the Cuisinart customer service number and inquired about my replacement, which they explained had not yet been shipped. It's now a week later and I still don't have my replacement.

productDescription: Hair Dryer
brand: Revlon Travel Styler Worldwide Dual Voltage
incidentDescription:
Revlon Travel Styler Worldwide Dual Voltage Hair Dryer model RV417

My mother was using the hair dryer when it caught fire. Luckily she was not injured, but her hair and scalp could have easily been burned if she didn't unplug the dryer.

It appears that if fan stops blowing for any reason, the heating elements remain on, which causes them to overheat and ignite the hair dryer. 

The hair dryer should have a safety that only powers the heating elements if the fan is operating.

While drying her hair the user noticed the dryer was stopping and starting for no apparent reason.  She thought it had overheated.  She returned to using it.  The cord sparked at the base of the rubber fitting at the bottom of the handle.  The cord loosely passes through this fitting and the fitting is not molded to relieve strain on the cord.  

Inspection of the cord showed that the insulation had ruptured and the conductor inside was severed, allowing electricity to flow if the cord was in a particular position but opening the circuit in a hazardous manner as the cord is moved.  

It appears that the rubber fitting is supposed to be a substitute for a molded strain relief, however it is not properly engineered for daily use.

productDescription: Hamilton Beach Brew Station
incidentDescription:
My name is [REDACTED] and I'm reporting this on behalf of my mother in law (her address is listed in this report), [REDACTED]. According to [REDACTED] the following is a summary of what happened at her home on April 4, 2012:

About 2:45pm, my daughter [REDACTED] and I were home. She was sitting at the kitchen table and I was in the family room. All of a sudden all three of the smoke detectors in our home went off. As I jumped up to see what was making the detectors go off, my daughter turned to the kitchen and at the same time, we both saw flames coming out of the back of the Brew Station. My daughter instinctively yelled fire and I ran to the kitchen to help put the flames out. I unplugged it quickly (it was plugged in but was not in use/not turned on at the time) we struggled to get the flames out because they were coming out of the back of the unit, near the top rather than the bottom where the cord is at. We managed to get the Brew Station into the sink so we could douse more water on it to extinguish the flames entirely. It took a minute to get the flames out but we did. We took the Brew Station out to the garage in an attempt to remove the smoke and charred smell. The smell lingered in the house for some time afterward. As can be seen by the pictures of the unit, the fire clearly came from within the unit and near the top of the backside of the unit. Had we not been home, our kitchen and house would have clearly caught on fire. The unit is clearly ruined and has extensive damage - far more than ever imagined. I certainly hope this has not ever happened to anyone else and am now very concerned that the product was not safe to begin with. To think of what may have happened had we not been home to extinguish the fire so quickly, clearly we would have had far worse fire/smoke damage. I am very disappointed with this product. Coffee makers are likely one kitchen product which is used most frequently in a home.

productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
Perfect Flame brand gas grille. Model # 720-0522.  
The gas burners are catching on fire inside the housing where the gas valves are located. The rubber and plastic inside this housing are burning up. At first, only one burner was doing this. So I stopped using it. Then I was having ingniting troubles. I would have to turn the knob on and off a few times to get the other burners to ignite. When they would ignite the flame that would light the burners, the flame would not shoot out far enough to properly ignite the burners. Eventually all of the burners started to catch fire inside the valve housing. In each of these incicents, I was aware enough to turn the burners off before catching the entire grille on fire.

productDescription: 4 cup Mr. Coffee coffeemaker
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription: My 4 cup Mr. Coffee coffeemaker spontaneously turned itself on in the kitchen with no one anywhere near it. It hadn't been used in over 3 weeks and there had not been anyone in the room for over 3 hours. It was making a snapping sound and when I unplugged it from the wall, the entire unit was extremely hot. I live alone, so there was no one who could have accidently bumped it or hit the on button.

productDescription: Room Humidifier
model: Oscillating Ultrasonic Humidifier w/Warm&Cool Mist HUM-WM75
incidentDescription: This is a Homedics Oscillating Ultrasonic w/Warm&Cool Mist; model HUM-WM75.  Purchased the unit in January of 2011. The unit started to leak water around January of 2012.  Water is leaking under the unit through the base where holes are located for cooling. Looking through the holes you can see all of the wiring for the unit. The wiring appears to be directly where the unit is leaking. The potential for an electrical shock appears to be here. Looking at various sites which sold this unit this appears to be a very common problem that had been reported.

productDescription: weber genesis 330 natural gas grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription: I purchased a Genesis 330 by Weber.  I had the same problem as another incident previously posted by another consumer.  The knobs on this grill are so light to turn on that when you put the cover on, they turn on by the weight of the cover.  This caused the leaking of gas.  When I called the companyIi was given a detailed explanation on how to correctly put on a WEBER cover to avoid this problem.  I was told I had to hold out the cover so the cover did not touch is sensitve knobs.  To me these knobs are a danger waiting to happen.  I was not told by Weber that this had been reported previously by a consumer.  When I called to ask about this I was told that they knew nothing about the other complaint.  I find it hard to believe that a consumer would write a report to you before calling Weber as I did at least 10 times.  So, I am wondering if this is a problem that does not comply to safety standards or whether this could create a hazard that the compnay should tell consumers about.  I think this should be investigated.

productDescription: Ryobi 20 inch Self-Propelled Cordless 48V Electric Mower, Model RY14110
productSubCategory: Lawn Mowers, Leaf Blowers and Lawn Vacuums
incidentDescription:
I had completed using my mower, Ryobi 20 inch Self-Propelled Cordless 48V Electric Mower- Model RY14110, to trim my grass around noon on 4/15/2011.   I noticed that the battery was low, so I plugged it in without any extension cord and the battery charger LED switched to RED to indicate charging was required and started.

On 4/16/2011 before noon, my wife ran to me repoting she smelled a GAS leak and wanted me to confirm.  I checked the area and the source of the GAS smell was not our fireplace, but the mover which parked under my outdoor patio, near the fireplace exhaust vent.  On closer inspection, the battery was leaking clear fluid out the LED indicators, sides and had pooled beneath the battery.  The battery was also HOT to the touch.  The LED indicator on the charger was still, RED indicating it was still charging, even though the smart charger is supposed to shut off, when max charge is reached.  I immediately removed the Charger from the outlet and moved the mower away from my home and the patio area to limit the exposure to the strong fumes.

Hours later the bad fumes had largly subsided, but the battery was still hot to the touch.

incidentDescription: Plastic handle broke away from glass lid while crock pot was in use. Lid fell into stoneware crock, causing hot food to splatter on walls, floor, and onto my skin and clothes. I was burned by the metal edge of the lid as it fell, and also burned by the hot food.

productDescription: Power IQ Flat Iron, white in color, 1" tourmaline plates
productType: Hair Curlers, Curling Irons, Clips & Hairpins (1682)
incidentDescription: I was flat ironing my hair this morning. I purchased the Power IQ flat Iron with tourmaline plates back in 2010 from Sally Beauty Supply. About 3 months ago when using the same product my bangs got burned completely off! I thought maybe that time that my hair had still been wet from the shower and that it was my own fault. However after the incident this morning I have realized that this product now overheats and raises its temperature on its own. While flat ironing my bangs this morning they got burned again. Almost like I set fire to them. The flat iron has a digital temperature setting and I had it set at 400 degrees, but the flat iron can go up higher than that. But after my previous incident I never set it past 400. My hair was not wet as I had not taken a shower. Once I realized my bangs had gotten burned yet again I went to pick up the flat iron to inspect it. It was so hot that I could not even pick it up. I had to unplug it and wait for 10 minutes for it to cool down before I could even touch it again. The temperature had gotten up way past the alotted degrees. This is very unsafe! What if I had forgotten to unplug it? No telling how hot it could have gotten, probably would have burned my boyfriends house down. Not to mention now I have to go out it public with burned off hair and wait for it to grow back. Its publically humiliating and very frustrating as I paid about $70 for this product to malfunction and ruin my hair!

productDescription: coffee and espresso maker, also steams milk
incidentDescription:
The consumer stated that her coffee & espresso maker hasn’t been working properly since she purchased it.  The consumer turned on the coffee maker and she managed to make the coffee with no interruptions. Then the consumer tried to steam milk and it would not steam the milk. She turned off the coffee maker and waited for 10 minutes until it was cool enough to remove the coffee holder.  Pressure had build up behind the coffee holder causing it to emit a loud noise and it exploded causing coffee to spill everywhere. 

The consumer tried to use the machine again following the instructions on the manual and with the help of a mechanic. She waited for 20 minutes this time giving it a longer period of time to cool down. When she tried to remove the coffee holder the same incident happened. 

The consumer contacted the manufacture and they stated that the product was not working properly because she was using filter water. The representative informed her that she needs to use bottle water instead of filter water. She informed the Consumer that the minerals in the water are needed for the machine to work properly. 

While on the phone with the representative from the manufacture she tried to use the machine again with bottle water.  When she plugged the machine it turned on by itself, the representative indicated that it should not turn on when she by itself.  The representative informed the consumer that she would provide her with a $10 discount to purchase a new coffee maker and the consumer declined the offer. 

After 10 minutes of hanging up the call with the representative the consumer decided that she would no longer used the machine and proceeded to clean it realizing it was still extremely hot. The consumer burnt the palm of her left hand.  She treated the burn by placing ice on it.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

No photos were taken, no injuries or additional property damage were realized.  The complainant is very concerned about the safety issues involved with these heaters from his professional background/experience.

productDescription: Cuisinart Smart Stick Blender Turquoise color
incidentDescription:
I purchased a Cuisinart Smart Stick handheld blender (or immersion blender) from a reputable retailer.
Upon using the blender for the first time (when I say first time I mean this particular blender--I have used these before), I read the instructions first.  I made a milkshake in the plastic cup provided. I then unplugged the blender and disassembled it as the instructions read.  I brought the bottom part to the sink to clean it. I was using my left hand to remove some of the excess shake before rinsing and the blade snapped.  I at first thought my thumb was caught between the blades but then looked in horror and saw the blade was imbedded in my thumb.  I became hysterical as the blender was stuck to my finger.  I called my boyfriend and he calmed me down and talked me through getting the blender blade out of my thumb (I used my right hand and cut my right index finger deeply while doing so).  I was bleeding a lot, and wrapped both my thumb and index finger in a white towel.  My boyfriend was an hour away so he called my sister who woke her 1-year-old and came to get me.  She lives 15 minutes away.  She brought me to the emergency room.  This was approximately 8:15 pm.  I was hysterical because I had no idea how bad my thumb was.  They saw me right away at the hospital and said I would need stitches and everything else should be fine.  I ended up with 8 stitches to my left thumb and my right index finger was cut deeply but able to be bandaged vs. stitched.  I was sent home with care instructions which I have been following (redressing the wound daily, applying Bacitracyn).  I was told the stitches can come out 10 days later (Tuesday April 10th).  It is Tuesday April 10th today and I don't think they are ready to come out--but I will check with a doctor.  I contacted Cuisinart on Monday April 2nd and they said their Claims Dept. would be in touch within a couple of days.  It is now over a week later and I've heard NOTHING.  I am really angry that their defective product injured me, resulting in a hospital bill, an upcoming doctor's bill to remove stitches and left me unable to work--I have a home-based skincare studio (go to [REDACTED] for confirmation of this) and had to turn away clients which has been incredibly upsetting.

productDescription: Hamilton Beach toaster model 22504. Two-slot toaster, brushed metal finish.
incidentDescription:
Investigated a kitchen fire in a sprinkler apartment. The sprinkler system extinguished fire early on and its obvious
the fire started at the toaster. The plastic bottom melted out onto the counter top. We found burnt French bread in
the toaster. We also found the handle in the down position.

We got an exemplar and tried to start a fire with French bread. No luck despite repeataed cycles of toasting. All of
the heat is vented up and out of the toast slots. Recorded only ambient temperatures on the plastic bottom.

Next we introduced a fire at the printed circuit board where the power cord attached. Produced almost identical
fire damage to the kitchen. We think this started inside the control area and probably was NOT due to operator
misuse or error. Furthermore, we learned that the post-fire position of the toaster handle is a function of fire
damage, not the pre-fire position of the toaster handle. We are Certified Fire Investigators, not electrical engineers.
Consequently we're submitting this to CPSC for review.

incidentDescription: I use my grill that I bought at lowes in May of 2008 regularly.  The description is as follows;Perfect Flame Double Lid Four Burner Gas Grills, model number GAC 3615 Serial number 050627.  Since purchasing the grill, small flames are continuosly catching inside the grill which I thought were normal as the flames were not extremely big, I tought it was greese and fat falling from the items I was cooking, however, on 2 occasions, the grill completely caught fire and I had to throw water on it quickly.  Had I not been around it, the damages could of been significant as the flames were everywhere.  Again, I may of been naive but did not report it as I thought debris from old food was the cause, until I went on the lowes website and saw that my grill's model number was recalled.  Initially and incredibely,  when I visited the store, the manager refused to do anything about it as they said my serial number did not match the parameters of the recall.  I then called the lowes customer service to explain my situation, they said the store should of accepted my grill, that is where we stand now.  I am not sure if they will take it back, but regardless, I wanted to let you know, the exact description of the recall is what happened to me in and it was preety scary.

productDescription: Keurig Coffee Maker
incidentDescription: Keurig Model B77 Coffee Maker caught on fire and started smoking with bad odor.

productDescription: Cuisinart drip coffee maker, model number CBC-00 (from label on bottom)
incidentDescription:
I bought a Cuisinart CBC-00 drip coffee maker in the fall of 2010. It has worked fine for a year and a half. Then this past Saturday, 24 March 2012, it had been turned on for about an hour. I went to pour the last cup of coffee from the carafe when I saw heavy, acrid smoke coming out from the bottom of the unit and around the carafe heating plate. The light that's normally illuminated to show the unit is turned on was off. I immediately unplugged the coffee maker and took it outside, thinking it might be close to bursting into flames. The bottom third of the unit was very hot, the metal plate on the bottom of the case was extremely hot. It did slowly cool down, with no flame seen. The carafe heating plate was bulged up and badly warped.
The entire house reeked of acrid, electrical fire smoke all weekend. I shudder to think what could have happened if I had not been close by and caught the fire in its early stages.

productDescription: Cuisinart Classic 12-cup Programmable Coffeemaker DCC-1100 Series
incidentDescription:
On March 9, 2012 I brewed my coffee as I always did in the Cuisinart Classic 12-cup Programmable Coffeemaker DCC1100 series.  About 2 hours after the coffee automatically brewed I had left the room for a few minutes when my husband called me back to tell me that there was smoke coming from the unit and that the coffee was BOILING.  We unplugged the pot and put it outside on concrete so it wouldn't flare up in my kitchen.

I called Cuisinart and they offered to send me another pot, but I would have to let them charge me $10.00 for postage and handling (I didn't ask how they were going to collect this fee) and I would have to send the old one back (at my own expense).  I don't know if they would have charged me for a replacement pot if I didn't return the old one.  I said I would think about that offer.

I went online and searched for "Cuisinart coffeepot fires" and found MANY similar incidents for both this pot and other model numbers.  I can't believe this coffeemaker has not already been recalled!!

productDescription: Conair Infinity hair dryer
incidentDescription: I was using a 2 year old Conair Infinity hair dryer and it exploded in my hand, burning from my wrist and sending sparks all the way to my shoulder.  The sparks and flames came from the cord where it attaches to the hair dryer (where you hold the dryer!)

productDescription: 3 Burner Gas Grill /  Blue Ember Fiesta grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
To whom it may concern,
I"m writing in regards to some trouble we recently had with our Blue Ember Fiesta grill. In Wisconsin the grilling season is just beginning so I attempted to use our grill this weekend. Shortly after preheating, I noticed an irregular amount of smoke in the back yard. Smoke was coming our from the grill cover and bottom doors. I was going to lift the cover but could see flames so I left it closed and turned off the burners. I pulled it to the middle of the yard and left it to cool. I had our kitchen fire extinguisher ready but didn't deploy it. I was worried about opening the cover if I didn't have too to use the extinguisher. 
When it stopped smoking I looked it over. The inside was completely charred and black. The once nice clean stainless steel is now stained black and full of greasy grime. Half of the grease pan seems to have crumbled into pieces and is just gone. The remaining half is still hanging from the guide rail but is extremely brittle. My 20lb LP tanks is full of grime and the entire bottom storage areas is disgusting. It's like the hot grease caught fire and splattered all over.
 
After doing some research, I noticed this was not the only incident like this and found there's a recall on my particular grill. I would like to make some arrangements to correct the issues I'm having. I purchased this grill because of the stainless steel features, reasonable price, and ratings in consumer reports but after this issue I'm deeply concerned about the product.
 
Respectfully,
[redacted] 
Blue Ember Fiesta Gas Grill
Model-FG50069-U401
Serial #- 07013900
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: quartz infrared heater
incidentDescription:
The consumer  noticed that the print on the box indicated that the heater was safe for children & pets.  She also noticed a warning  label on the back of the heater indicating “Heater hot when in use do not let bare skin touch hot surface”.

When she put the heater into use she noticed the front grate where the heat comes out  and the ledge that’s a part of the case get very hot to touch. 

The consumer’s granddaughter whom is one years of age attempted to touch the infrared part of the heater. The consumer was able to get to her in time and there are no injuries reported. The heater was in use for an hour.

The consumer indicated that a child could be severely burned if their skin comes in contact with the heater.

The firm was contacted the week of 2/13/2012 and the representative that she spoke with was very rude and nasty the consumer stated.

The consumer contacted the BBB and reported the firm. The consumer plans to return the heater to the retailer.

productDescription: Eureka Upright Vacum
incidentDescription: Have a Eureka Upright Vacum Model# 5892 S# 0504024098. Several years ago while using this unit the handle would get very hot. It finally just stopped working.  I took the handle apart and noticed the switch in the handle was bunt.  I went to a vacum repair place and bought a replacement switch.  One year later the same thing happened again,the handle would get hot (around the switch), but this time smoke came out off the handle and the vacum would not shut off with the switch. Had to umplug from the wall. If I had not unpluged from the wall,Ibelieve the vacaum would have caught fire. Not safe!!!

productDescription: Brass Urn Fire Pit
incidentDescription:
I recently purchased a fire pit sold through Walmart, imported by Dewan & Sons and manufactured in India. The problem I am having is the threading on the grating handle is only about a ¼ inch total. This was not long enough to clear the support and grating and then fasten with a nut securely. The threading stripped and the handle popped off while the lid was being lifted off the fire pit resulting in the lid falling into the fire and casting burning material outwards at people standing around the pit.  I contacted the Importer and manufacturing contacts and was told they know of the issue and don’t care about the safety concern, that they don’t plan on changing the design and will continue to sell an unsafe product that will likely result in injury to all users including children standing around the fire pits making smores.
The site where the item can be found is here:
http://www.walmart.com/ip/Better-Homes-and-Gardens-Oil-Rubbed-Brass-Urn-Fire-Pit/17235792
The Importer/Manufacturers site is here:
http://dewansons.com
From talking with the manufacturer I believe this is an issue with most if not all of their fire pits currently for sale in the U.S. and they stated they are insured up to 5 million in losses per incident so they would rather continue making faulty dangerous products then have to make design changes that would cost them money.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription: gas smoker
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
model: Smoky Mountain A033141/ 25,000 BTU/hr vertical smoker
incidentDescription:
I am writing to you about a serious accident that occurred using a vertical smoker. The smoker was a gift years ago and I have used it quite often. 
It is Landmann / Great Outdoors Smoky Mountain Model #A033141, Serial #531000468, 25,000 BTU/hr vertical smoker, 16”x 24”x 45”. 
The accident occurred on February 5, 2012, when the propane flame went out and I went to open the door to the smoker to check the beef brisket I was preparing. The chamber had filled with gas, and a spark from the wood chip box inside the smoker ignited the gas before I could open the door. The latched door to the smoker exploded into me, and caused some serious damage. I was rushed to the hospital ER where I was given 12 stitches, a CAT scan and a few weeks of rehabilitation. The hair was burned off of my eyelids, eyebrows, and singed the left side of my head. 
I am 6’ 3” tall and weigh 220 lbs, and I fully believe that the blast could have killed a child. Doing some research online, I have found several recall notices for vertical smokers due to safety issues with these types of regulators (gas shut off after flame goes out). 
Thank you for your attention to this serious issue. I want to prevent this from happening to someone else if possible, especially a child.

productDescription: Model GBC976W (Gas Grill)

incidentDescription:
I had a UniFlame gas grill that is about 2.5 years old. The unit was well kept and in good working order. Model GBC976W

While grilling out, I left the grill unattended for 12 minutes. When I came back out I noticed that the grill brush that was 3 inches from the grill was melted. I then looked at the grill temp gage and notice it was complete spiked passed the temp of 750 degrees. The control knobs would not work to turn off the gas flow. I then attempted to turn the gas off at the tank. The tank valve was very hot and I was able to turn of the gas flow.

I reported the issue to Uniflame. They told me that the unit was out of the warranty period.
They wanted me to pay almost $100 to replace what they think might be a problem. My concern is since the unit could not have been turned off by the control knobs and the tank was very hot the safety feature should have turn the gas flow off. However since the unit was well over 750 degrees, I'm worried other might not be so lucky.

productDescription: 48" Free Standing Range, Bertazzoni 48" Professional Range Model X48 6G GGV X.  6-Bruner Natural Gas, Electric Griddle, Dual Gas Ovens
incidentDescription:
There was a grease fire on the griddle assembly.  The fire was extinguished using a fire extinguisher.  

The griddle design allows the grease to roll back under the griddle surface and drip on the heating elements.  Subsequently, we have raised the back of the griddle up by resting it on the back of the griddle "hole," and this helps, but grease still drips down the edges of the grease tray and puddles under it, then drips down the front face of the oven (inside the door) all the way to the floor.

A service technician has been out and determined that the unit is properly installed.

A Bertazzoni representative suggested raising screws in the back of the griddle burner assembly, but this would lead to further issues, such as batter flowing down the griddle since it is not flat.

The griddle needs a method to force the grease to drip into the grease tray and keep it from rolling back.  Additionally, the grease tray needs to be wider than the griddle so that it doesn't drip on the sides of the tray and down its sides.

productDescription: White oval slow cooker/[REDACTED]. Everstar brand, model ASC-615.
incidentDescription:
staAs we have done dozens of times, I put the ingredients for stroganoff into our Everstar Slow Cooker (model ASC-615).  I put the lid on, turned it on high, and left to go run errands.

When I came home 2 hours later, the lid to the cock pot was still sitting where I left it, but it was shattered. The handle was off, there was glass down in the food, and there was glass all over the stove. 

Nobody was in the room when it happened, fortunately, but my 3 small children were in the next room watching movies and my husband was in his office in the basement. The kids (ages 6,4, and 3) reported hearing "a glass being dropped--but when we went into the kitchen, we couldn't see it".  Thank goodness they weren't in the kitchen at the time!

Unprovoked, untouched, the glass lid exploded.  Someone could have been seriously hurt!

Upon disassembling the unit I traced the cause of the incident to a resistor which failed and began to arc, igniting the shrink tubing surrounding it.

productDescription: Revlon Curling Iron Model #RV052 Type RC52M with a .75" barrel, sold by Revlon and Manufactured by Helen of Troy
productType: Hair Curlers, Curling Irons, Clips & Hairpins (1682)
incidentDescription:
3/15/2012 I plugged in my curling iron (Revlon Model  #RV052 Type RC52M with a .75" barrel) and let it heat up as I do with every use. I began to curl my hair. On the second roll of hair near the crown of my head, and while holding the curling iron with my right hand, I heard a loud "snap" and a yellow fire ball blew out of the end of the handle. At the same time I received a terrible shock and burn to my right arm. Thank goodness my curling iron was plugged into an G.F.I. outlet, as it immediately cut the power to the curling iron and tripped the circuit breaker. I dropped the curling iron and looked at my arm and realized that I had been burned by this. I had received a shock and was obviously shook by this incident. I inspected the curling iron and where the cord meets the swivel end (to keep the cord from getting tangled), I saw that the cord had been literally blown out of the swivel and a couple of the copper wires were melted. 

I had not had any problems with this curling iron prior to this happening. No frays, no over heating, absolutely no problems prior to this. 

I did see my physician for the burn who told me that it was definitely an electrical burn and that I needed to watch it carefully for 24-48 hours to make sure that the tissue under my skin is not damaged. 

I did some research online on this model and there are numerous reports of the same thing happening to others as well.

productDescription: Propane Grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription: The gas regulator on my Char-Broil "Red Urban Infrared Grill" (Model # 463250210) failed.  When I opened the valve on the propane tank, gas started leaking out very rapidly.  I turned off the tank, disconnected the coupler, re-connected the coupler, and the same thing happened (I was checking to make sure that the coupler was connected properly).  The grill was purchased in June of 2010.  The original regulator (Char-Broil part number G352-3500-W1) was defective straight out of the box (same issue of gas leaking when the tank valve was opened).  Char-Broil sent a replacement part, which has now failed less than 2 years later.  The failure of this part allows propane to leak out very rapidly.  If the grill was on when this happened, there would be a serious risk of fire or an explosion.

productDescription:
Product Info:
Charmglow BBQ Grill (Gas)
Model: 720-0536
Purchased: April 2009
When not in use this grill remains covered.
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
I was in the process of cleaning the main burners and noticed that the small brackets that hold the rear end of the main burners in place have severe rust.  In trying to remove the burner, one of the brackets crumbled into flakes.  A second bracket is almost as bad- have not checked the other two. The burner is supposed to be screwed into these brackets.  At this point there no way to secure a screw into these brackets or what is left of them. The plastic knobs are highly flammable and when the knob caught on fire, my husband happened to look over and see it flaming high and melting onto our deck. We spoke to representatives of Char-Broil who refused to take responsibility even though we told them we would be reporting this issue to the Consumer Product Safety Commission. My husband suggested the problem could be resolved by placing a metal washer on the shaft behind the knob so that the heat or flame cannot get to the plastic knob. productDescription: Black & Decker countertop oven  model TRO480BS toaster oven
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
manufacturer: Applica Consumer Products, Inc. - NOTIFY SPECTRUM BRANDS
incidentDescription:
On 2/12/2012 I bought a Black & Decker countertop oven at Sear's.  The model  number is TRO480BS.  I used it for the second time (3/13/2012) today to toast a bagel. All three knobs were on the correct settings for toasting.  The timer has a picture of a bagel which must be a couple of minutes.  The timer went off and I took the bagel out.  As I walked away the glass door exploded sending hundreds of tiny pieces of glass all over my kitchen.  I luckily,  recently bought metal shelving unit and had placed  the oven lower than counter height and away from the high traffic area in my kitchen.  If I would have had this on the regular height kitchen counter the glass would have exploded onto my face arms and chest.  When I realized what had just happened I stepped on some pieces of glass and sustained several minor cuts on the bottom of my feet not realizing I was barefoot.
     I found the receipt and booklet and called Black & Decker immediately.  They were apologetic and said they would send a new oven out to me or a refund.  I took the replacement oven but am curious about incidents you may have received on this model oven.  They would forward my incident to engineering.  What I would like to know if this is an isolated incident or if there are other reports of this problem.
     Most ovens and toasters are kept at very little distance from one's face and body on a regular height kitchen counter.  An incident like mine would have sent me to the hospital with cuts on my arms and face.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: Gevalia CM500 12-cup Coffee Maker with glass carafe
incidentDescription: Immediately after brewing a pot of coffee, I lifted the lid to remove the old coffee filter and grounds.  The condensation on the lid slid down the lid and hit a baffle that's likely intended to reduce the mess on your countertop.  This baffle redirects the water back toward the heating element/percolator.  When the condensation hit the heating element, it shot the hot water toward me.  The water did not hit me in the face, but it cold have if it were pointed at me.  As it was, it just sprayed boiling water droplets on my hand.  I would consider it a design defect to have the hot water exit point on a location (the lid) that can lift to point it at you.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription: Holmes Ceramic Heater Model HCH4962
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription:
My Holmes Ceramic Heater (model HCH4062) was functioning normally without abnormal sounds or lack of heat output.  Suddenly a burst of flame, red glow, and smoke was produced at upper left of the front grill.  There was a brief electrical sound of a "short" or "sparking".  I unplugged the heater, but it continued to emit the smell of burning plastic and fumes for a few minutes.

I attempted unsuccessfully to first contact Holmes directly 3 ways as a courtesy to Holmes with information about the incident that company engineers might use to improve future products. 

1) I waited and waited on hold for customer support at 1-800-546-5637 without reaching a service representative.

2) I tried completing the online form 3 times. Each time I received error messages that did not indicate what was wrong with my form data.
https://secure.holmesproducts.com/contactus.aspx

3) I searched unsuccessfully for an email address at the holmesproducts.com web site.

I would have been happy to report to Holmes directly, but, since this failed, I decided to instead report the incident at www.saferproducts.gov.  It's unfortunate to have a heater burst into flame.  But by reporting the incident some good may come of it with better product design or component specification that make future consumers safer.

On 3/11/12, we returned home from an out of town trip and the grill had once again broken off and was being held by the tape, so it did not fall on the glass cooktop.  The break was once again where the clip was attached to a very thin section on the back of the grill.
This time when I went to the website for a new grill, this part was no longer listed.  
I began to search for other parts websites and found many, many other customers who have had the same problem.
This is a safety issue,as the grill could fall on a young child or break a glass cooktop.  I have notified Whirlpool of the issue and am awaiting a reply.
I would be happy to send you the broken part.

This would be a hazard for adults and children

productDescription: Vacuum cleaner
incidentDescription:
Consumer stated that the vacuum cleaner overheats.  The instructions were followed correctly but the vacuum cleaner does not operate properly .

Consumer is concerned that the safety device does not work and feels that this can be a fire hazard and burn hazard.

Consumer had contacted the manufacture with no resolution.  

UPDATE: The vacuum has a "Vacuum only" setting and a "Vacuum plus brush" setting. The original, and its replacement, both run hot enough to burn the hand.  There is an internal overheat sensor which suts the vacuum motor but not the brush motor, so it sounds like the machine is still working.  It took a long while to realize what was happening, since it sounded like it was still working.  There were frequent overheats in the first unit.  A second was purchased with same problem.  This is a burn and fire hazard.  It is not resolved by installing an overheat cutout switch.  Rather, the cutout is a tacit acknowledgement of the design flaw.

The consumer attempted to power off the heater and unplug it from the wall outlet, when she noticed the power cord was abnormally warm. The consumer stated that her unplugged the heater and the metal prong that goes in the wall outlet burned her finger. 

The consumer did not go to the doctor for her burn. The consumer placed the burn under cold water and was fine. The consumer believes this occurred due to the cord from the heater and not the outlet. The consumer stated that the product does not appear to be damaged and did not spread damage to the consumer’s home. 

The consumer took the product outside. The consumer did not find it necessary to call the fire department or her home insurance company. The consumer did some research and found recalls on similar models but hers was not included. The UL number is 1278. The consumer has not yet called the firm or the retailer.

productDescription: Cuisinart Brew Central DCC-1200, Black Chrome
incidentDescription:
We had been at home and having our usual morning coffee on the weekend.  Me and my wife each had a cup and the warming plate was still on, keeping the remaining pot of coffee warm.  A little later in the morning I heard a very loud hissing noise coming from the kitchen.  When I went to investigate, I found the noise was coming from the coffee maker.  It appeared that the coffee was starting to boil and there was foul smoke coming out of the machine.  I quickly unplugged it and took the whole unit outside and set it in my lawn.

There was plenty of coffee in the carafe and the warming plate should not get as hot as it did - to the point where something in the device started melting.  We worry what could have happened if I was not as close by as I was and it actually caught fire or the carafe exploded from the extreme heat.  We would often use the programmable feature of the coffee maker- so it is extra scary to think of what could have happened if we were asleep at the time.  This is actually a replacement unit sent to me by Cuisinart after the one we had bought in the store just stopped working.

I checked Amazon product reviews for this particular model and it looks like it is not just me- others have reported similar experiences.

It is the Cuisinart Brew Central 12-Cup Programmable Coffee Maker, Model DCC-1200

Also, noticed smoke smudge on the counter top after I moved the coffee maker.

incidentDescription:
Regarding the Cuisinart DTC-975 12 Cup Programmable Thermal Coffeemaker:
I have used this coffeemaker for about a year without any problems.  This morning I made coffee as usual.  A beeper will sound when the unit is finished and the coffee is ready.

The beeper sounded and I waited about another 30 minutes before going into the kitchen to pour myself a cup of coffee.  Upon entering the kitchen, I discovered coffee all over the counter top and on the floor.  The pot appeared to be properly seated in the coffeemaker.  When I took it out, hot coffee began pouring out of the filter basket onto the bottom of the coffeemaker.  It just missed my hand.  I grabbed another nearby pot to catch.  Upon opening the filter basket compartment, it was still full of liquid.

The thermal pot was only about 1/4 full, so this was not a case of it being overfilled.  It had stopped filling at that point for some inexplicable reason which resulted in the remainder of the coffee either running out onto the counter and floor or staying inside the filter compartment until the pot was removed.

No injuries were sustained but a major mess in the kitchen resulted.

productDescription: cuisinart electronic pressure cooker
incidentDescription:
2/13/2012 7:15 pm The cuisinart electric pressure cooker CPC-600 series came open as it was pressurizing. I had set the pressure cooker to cook on high pressure for 15 minutes.  It takes some time for the unit to build pressure and I had stepped away for a few minutes.  When I returned to check on the unit the red flashing indicator had not stopped flashing (to indicate that it had reached pressure and the timer had not yet started counting down).  There was steam and slight whistling sound coming from the red float valve that also indicates when the unit has reached full pressure.  Concerned about the steam and whistling from the float valve I was about to shut the unit down when the lid popped off.  The stew I was preparing erupted in approximately a 3ft radius scalding my left hand and burning my stomach covering the counters and the floor surrounding the cooking area of the unit. 

This was only the 3rd use of this pressure cooker.  I have cleaned the unit according to manufacturers instructions from the 2 previous uses. In the troubleshooting section of the instruction booklet it says that the reason air escapes from the float valve could be that food was stuck in the sealing ring. The other reason is that the sealing ring on the float wore out.  With this only being the 3rd use of the pressure cooker, I wouldn't think that the sealing ring would be worn out unless it was faulty to begin with.  I know I have taken care in cleaning the unit as I have been the only one who has operated and cleaned the machine.

productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
I purchased a new Weber model S310 gas grill and assembled it per the included instructions. During the first several uses I would find that the burner control knobs would come on while doing other tasks. Example grilling for two people and only turning on and starting just one burner and while cooking I would find that one or both of the other burners on and not lit. Also I would find the burner control knobs on while installing or removing the weather protective cover.
I now have to double and triple check that the burner control knobs are turned off whenever I am doing any tasks on or around the grill and make sure that the propane is turned off and stays that way until it is to be used and continue checking them while it is in use.
I called Weber Customer Service and was told that there is nothing wrong with the shutoff mechanisims.  
I also went to several stores that sell Weber Gas Grills and looked at 50 different 310 Grills and found that 40 of them operated the same as mine and the burner control knobs would not lock in the off position, but the other 10 would lock and there would be no inadverent unlocking of them.
When checking other models of Weber grills I found that they do have very positive locking of their burner controls and there is no inadvertant unlocking possible.
So I find that this style of grill is inherently UNSAFE and the potential for an explosion and or fire is very high. I beleive that the the burner control mechanisims should be recalled and replaced, before someone is injured.

productDescription: Space Heater
incidentDescription:
Complaint involves "Comfort Zone" heater, model cz792, manufacture date 07/10, purchased at Tractor Supply in St. Albans VT in fall of 2010.  I recently noticed that when the heater was set to it's lowest heat setting, the heater would stay on continuously instead of cycling on and off.  I unplugged the heater and stopped using it.  I disassembled the heater and found that the weighted (plastic) arm that is supposed to mechanically open a circuit on the thermostat had melted and was laying in the bottom of the heater (pictures available). This would cause the heater to remain "on" if it were tipped over.  I do not know if this melted arm somehow interfered with the operation of the thermostat causing the heater to stay "on" all the time when the thermostat was set to it's lowest setting.  

I also noted that the thermostat is wired to interrupt the "neutral" side of the incoming power instead of the "hot" side.  

Additionally, during troubleshooting I found that the main power/mode-select switch had several hundred ohms of resistance between the "hot" side contact and the respective outgoing contacts.

productDescription: Ryobi 20 inch Self-Propelled Cordless Electric Mower, Model #RY14110A, being sold exclusively at The Home Depot
productSubCategory: Lawn Mowers, Leaf Blowers and Lawn Vacuums
incidentDescription:
On June 4th, 2011, my wife and I purchased a Ryobi self propelled cordless electric lawn mower from HomeDepot.com. The lawn mower had received great reviews on the website up until that point and we were interested in a more ‘green’ option than a traditional gas mower. The mower was functional and we were satisfied with our purchase until August 2011.

One afternoon in August, I smelled a chemical smell in the garage. I investigated the smell and figured out it was coming from the lawn mower. The battery was hot, all of its lights were on, and it was covered in a clear fluid that we later determined to be battery acid. After unplugging the mower and waiting until the next morning, my wife called the customer service department at Ryobi. They stated that there had been a problem with the battery chargers and a new charger had been remanufactured. They assured us that a replacement battery and battery charger would be delivered within 3 weeks. 

Fast forward to January 2012, we have not received anything from Ryobi. 

Last night I decided to take a look at homedepot.com to see if any other customers had a similar problem. When I looked up the lawn mower, there were at least 20 other customers with the EXACT same story as us. Battery overcharged, leaked battery acid, called Ryobi, were assured they’d get a replacement, and no battery was ever replaced. Clearly Ryobi’s product is defective.  

In summary, we’ve lost almost $400 on a mower that doesn’t work, and quite possibly is a fire hazard. The battery acid leaked onto our garage floor, which was a safety hazard for me, my pets, and the environment. 

Even with the slew of negative reviews on HomeDepot.com, the store continues to sell the product. What is most questionable is that both my wife and I attempted to leave poor product reviews on the HomeDepot.com site, and they rejected both of our reviews because we included the fact that Ryobi had been terrible to deal with. If they rejected our reviews, how many other customers have had this same issue but could not be heard because HomeDepot.com is rejecting reviews from unsatisfied customers, thus keeping the rating for the product high? In addition, Ryobi’s issued no recalls and there’s A LOT of people left with broken lawnmowers and tons of frustration. How much longer will they sell the product before someone is injured?

incidentDescription:
In mid January 2012 the McDonnell & Miller RB-24 low water cut off on a barely 6 year old Burnham 203PVNI hot water boiler shorted out due to water leaking into the electrical circuit from the plastic threaded section that screwed into the water pipe. The electrical short overloaded the 24 v circuit causing the transformer (fan center) to burn out and generating a significant amount of smoke in the basement. More serious damage was prevented by the tripping of the Fuse panel circuit breaker. 

Plumber that repaired the damage noted that the Rb-24 units were "cheaply made" and had a history of unreliability. 

As to be noted was that the 24 v circuitry of the boiler does not have any fuses to protect from any circuit overloads which I consider a notable design flaw by Burnhan's. Electrical malfunctions are only protected by fuse panel circuit breakers.

productDescription:
A/C adapter (CT: 592C40EMFUT1JW) for HP Pavilion dv6000 laptop.
Note: This is not pertaining to the HP battery pack recall already in place for this model.  This complaint refers to the external A/C adapter that is plugged into the laptop and plugged into the wall.
My internal battery did not have the correct codes to fall under the recall, and it was not overheated during this incident. I'm referring strictly to the A/C adapter.
productType: Electric Wire or Wiring Systems (Excl Panelboards Recept (4062)
incidentDescription:
I own a HP Pavillion dv6000 laptop. I hadnt used it in several months because I bought a new HP laptop recently.  I put a DVD in to view and after less than 10 minutes into the DVD, I went to pickup the AC adapter external battery pack to move the whole laptop from the table to the floor and nearly burned my hand on the battery pack, so I quickly put it back down on the table and as I put it back down on the table I was burned by the end of the cord that enters the A/C pack.  The cord just outside of the adapter was very very hot. I could smell burning electrical wires and hear a buzz or sizzle coming from inside the A/C adapter. I quickly unplugged the adapter from the laptop and shut down the laptop for fear of a fire.
I visited this site to see if this product had been recalled, but they only thing HP has recalled on HP dv6000 laptops was the internal battery, and NOT the A/C adapter that you plug into the wall.  This is a major fire hazard. You can see where the cord has started to melt. If I left my laptop unattended it most certainly would have caught fire.  After only 10 minutes of a DVD playing the adapter was sizzling inside, and too hot to touch.  If the whole movie played unattended my house wouldve burned to the ground!
My internal battery is one of the non-recalled batteries CT: 6294102AXUWBJK, this internal battery was not hot at all during operation.  Only the external A/C adapter battery pack and the  thin cord leading from the laptop to the A/C adapter was extremely hot.  The thicker cord going from A/C adapter to the wall outlet was just warm.

My A/C adapter number is: CT: 592C40EMFUT1JW.

productDescription: Vacuum Cleaner
manufacturer: HMI INDUSTRIES INC. DBA HEALTH MOR
incidentDescription: We own a Filter Queen Vacuum and two Defenders systems, purchased in 2005.  We paid thousands of dollars for these 3 items.  The Filter Queen Vacuum has now started on fire in our home TWICE.  Once after the initial purchase and we received a new hose, wand and cleaning head in 2008 and now again the other night November 16, 2011.  We contacted the 800 # on the vacuum who directed us to a "company" 800#.  The individual we spoke with who finally called us back on Friday, November 18 said that we were part of a recall and they'd send us all new parts AGAIN.  I explained that it had this time burned my sons hand, ruined a 5’ X 7’ area rug and we no longer trusted ANY of these products in our home.  We had trusted them twice now and this was no longer acceptable, not to send us the new parts, that we wanted to return these three products and get our money back.  It is not fair to us that we would pay this much for their products, only to have them start on fire on us TWICE!!!!  We asked about why we weren't notified of any recalls??  I was originally told they had no idea and later told we must have thrown the notice away!. I then stated we must have been under TWO recalls OR they sent us faulty products the first time it caught on fire... they didn't know.  No one returned my call on Monday, however on Tuesday, November 22 when I got home from work there was a box with the new parts sitting outside my home.  I called and left a message for [REDACTED] to please call me first thing this morning, Wednesday, November 23... [REDACTED] just finally called me at 1:14pm and said his supervisor told him to send the new products.  I explained that I had told him NOT to send them as like I stated earlier, we no longer trusted Filter Queen or ANY of their products.  I am now going to seek legal advice as this is an extremely upsetting and serious matter to us, but apparently NO BIG DEAL to this company. I'm explained that I was hopeful that someone within their organization would understand just how serious this is and respectfully refund our money for the vacuum, two defenders, our carpet and the trauma they've put my kids through. This has went on for weeks and they are discussing paying us for the vacuum only, however, it has now been over a week (since December 20, 2011) since we’ve heard anything from Filter Queen/Health Mor. We’ve called, emailed, etc., numerous times since this whole nightmare started and are really appalled at the lack of concern from Health Mor over their product starting on fire now twice in our home, our son was burned (albeit not major, but he was burned)  we’ve never received a recall, etc.

I unplugged it.  I tried it again the next day and unfortunately it was still doing it.  I contacted the manufacturer (reference #4536568).  but they seem unfazed due to the age of the unit (9 years old). A minute or two later, the consumer was about to place his bread in the oven, but when he pulled the door handle it burned his left pointer finger.  The handle has a protective cover, but the consumer claims that the cover gets hot when the oven is used.  The consumer said that his injury was similar to a 3rd degree burn and it took over a week to heal.  The consumer applied some antibiotic ointment to his burn and treated himself at home.

The consumer contacted the manufacture and explained the incident a mfr., rep (name unknown).  The mfr., rep told the consumer that they will replace the product free of charge.  The consumer got his toaster replaced by the mfr, but the new toaster has the same issues.  The model that he received from the mfr. is different than the one that caused his burn.

The consumer believes that the door handle on the toaster is too close to the toaster and this causes the handle to get hot.  The consumer said that his mother uses a mitten or heating pad when she opens or closes the oven door.
The consumer feels that the toaster’s handle poses a burn hazard due to it design.
