productDescription: Calphalon 4 Qt Slow Cooker
incidentDescription: I used my Calphalon 4 qt slow cooker to make soup last night.  The soup cooked on high for 4 hours then warmed for an hour.  When we got ready to eat, I unplugged the [slow cooker].  After eating, I set a timer for 1 hour to let the soup cool before putting it away.  After that time, I put the soup away, rinsed the [slow cooker] and put it in the dishwasher, and then washed the lid by hand in warm water.  It didn't even feel warm to the touch.  I put it on my dish drying cloth on my counter to dry.  About 2a.m. I heard a pop.  I didn't realize until this morning what happened.  My [slow cooker] lid had just exploded -- not imploded, but exploded and put glass everywhere on my counter, window sill, sink, etc.  I called Calphalon and they are sending me a new lid, but I am wary and not sure how the lid could have just exploded especially after than many hours -- what if I or one of my kids would have been standing there? It could have been a serious danger.  I also just did some research online and I am not the first one this has happened to.

productDescription: Lithium Ion Battery (model: W-1,3.7v,1800mAh)
incidentDescription:
I have owned a Sprint/Sierra wireless hotspot since October 2010.
 Yesterday I noticed that the battery door on the unit had bulged and popped off on 1 side . After closer inspection,I realized that the Lithium Ion Battery (model: W-1,3.7v,1800mAh) was extremely hot and bulging on both sides.
After my discovery I immediately called Sprint and was told I could take it to Leesburg,VA store for replacement.I asked if this is a normal occurrence,and was told NO .

As I told the Sprint Rep,this appears to be a possible danger as battery could explode! She spoke with her supervisor and called me back again telling me I could call Sierra Wireless at 877-231-1144.(closed Sunday)      This is really passing the buck!
Upon further research of this issue,I went to the SPRINT.COM website to discover from Sprint forums that this has been an issue since 2010.see below link:
                   http://community.sprint.com/baw/message/388897    
Could these batteries explode or pose a fire hazard ? Is this what it will take for Sprint to recall and replace these. I am aware that [REDACTED] had this issue as I was one of the recalls.Should these battery incidents have not been kept quiet by your company?
As of Jan 30, I have spoken with a Sierra Wireless representative who is sending a battery at no charge. I am sure that if you had made Sierra wireless aware of this, 
 the problem may have been solved.

productDescription: Equipped with 106 square inches of cooking surface, this round-shaped electric grill features five removable cooking plates for exceptional versatility. The countertop appliance can function as a deep-dish pizza oven, a six-pocket quesadilla press, an omelet maker, or a pancake griddle--simply switch out the plates. Five come included: two ribbed grill plates, two quesadilla plates, and a 1-inch deep-dish plate for pizzas, griddling, baking, and more. The appliance's appeal lies not only in its simplicity and countertop convenience, but also in its fat-fighting ability. The cooking surface can be adjusted from flat to angled in order to help channel fat away from food and into the built-in drip tray. Even more, its triple nonstick coating allows for low-fat cooking while ensuring effortless food release. The unit also provides adjustable temperature control, a "ready" indicator light, and a 1-1/2-inch floating hinge to accommodate thicker sandwiches or steaks. Other highlights include embedded heating elements for consistent heat and rapid recovery time, an extended metal loop handle for raising and lowering the lid, cool-touch side handles, and a spatula for transferring food from the grill to a plate. To clean, simply wipe the outside of the appliance with a damp cloth and put the removable plates in the dishwasher. The 1500-watt grill measures 17-1/2 by 15 by 5-7/8 inches and carries a one-year limited warranty.
incidentDescription:
Hi,

  The below is a copy of the letter I sent the manufacturer.  I think this grill is hazardous.  I really like the concept but the plates fall out when hot all the time, mostly when you are lifting the grill open to get the food out or turn it.  When I went back and looked on amazon - other people are having the same issue - I have not placed a review on amazon so I am sure others haven't either.  I had this issue before and they replaced the defective plate but it keeps happening.  I am an engineer and I really do check the plates before cooking - I am not sure if the heat is expanding the latch or what.  To be honest - I have to think there must be a better locking mechanism out there.

  Sincerely,
 [redacted]
Hi,
  I have the George Foreman 360 Electric Nonstick Grill with 5 Interchangeable Grill Plates (I couldn't find it in the list below).  I also bought the heart-shaped waffle plates.  I have been pretty happy with one large exception.  I am very careful putting the plates in - I make sure they are in the right direction - tug on them to make sure they are stable - and they still sometimes fall out.  Today - I was grilling burgers and the top plate flew off when I lifted the opening.  This time the hinge cracked but is still somewhat usable but I think it is too big a safety hazard.  I am torn - do I invest more in these plates - or do I switch to another safer means of cooking (which seems to make more sense)  I like the grill a lot but you really need to come up with a locking mechanism for the plates that works. productDescription:
EdenPure GEN4 MODEL
Serial #:  CH00247896
Quartz infrared portable heater
incidentDescription:
("You can also report a potentially unsafe product to CPSC’s Office of Compliance at (301) 504-7520 or by sending an e-mail to sect15@cpsc.gov.")

I bought an EdenPure quartz infrared portable heater.  The appliance cord appeared to became hot enough to melt the outlet box, wall insulation, and wires.

I noticed a burning smell and smoke started to fill room.  I immediately turned the unit off and unplugged appliance from outlet.

EdenPure GEN 4 was the only appliance used on this circuit breaker as instructed.

We analyzed our wiring, circuit breaker did not pop yet meter indicated good working order, removed outlet box, rewired circuit, and did not find any evidence that would cause overheating which lead to

Further research of the EdenPure GEN4 appliance itself.
Plugged EdenPure into other circuits which also caused heating of the cord.  The heater cord was hot over a foot down the cord from the outlet.

Leading to further web research to draw indication that this may have or have not been a unique case:

Please note the following article from consumerreports.org
http://news.consumerreports.org/appliances/2011/02/one-melted-edenpure-space-heater-sparks-costco-recall-.html
"Meanwhile, if you bought an EdenPure US 1000 heater at Costco, you can take the retailer up on its refund offer. And if you experience any signs of overheating with any space heater, stop using it and notify the CPSC on the Report an Unsafe Product page of its website. "

Please note close-up photo of melted outlet is available upon request.

Would also like to note respiratory irritation directly connected to periods of time in which the appliance was running.

EdenPure
GEN4 MODEL
Serial #:  CH00247896
Customer service phone #:  1 800 219 8458

Thank You,
[REDACTED]

productDescription: Small "travel" humidifier that accepts a bottle of water on top.  Plugs in to wall using DC power converter.  Switch on item to adjust flow rate.
incidentDescription:
During the Christmas season I purchased a Mini-Humidifier from Target, sold as a house brand for $19.95. 

I used it for the first time this weekend, and left it on for a while because it appeared to be functioning normally.  I then realized that the product had a crack where the case had been improperly sonically welded, causing water to leak all over the dresser and on to a TV that was below it.  

Upon inspection, I saw that the manufacturer had not properly sealed the water champed, allowing water to leak out, onto the 24V DC power supply, potentially causing an electrical shock and/or fire hazard. 

I took the unit back to Target, and they refused to refund my money or replace it as it was considered a "seasonal" item.  

There are no UL / CSA or FCC/ CE compliance markings on the device itself, and in fact it was only the following: 

Mini Humidifier
Input Power DC24V 1A 24W
Model No. PNH01
Import Marketing Solutions
August, 2011

At the very least a product that uses water and input voltages above 12VDC are, I believe, required to have UL approval.  The fact that it leaks water due to poor design and manufacture is an potential fire and shock hazard for the consumer, and I recommend that Target be forced to issue a recall on this device, especially given their unwillingness to stand by the product.

productDescription: 12 cup Cuisinart Coffeemaker
incidentDescription:
Friday morning, December 23,2011, my wife got up at 6:00 am and went downstairs and started a pot of coffee, while I slept in for 15 more minutes.The coffee . had just finished brewing, as I prepared to take out the garbage and get the mornlng paper. I was exiting the kitchen door to go outside, when I smelled an electrical burning odor. I went to investigate, first checking the coffeemaker, then the basement and the rooms on the first floor.This took about 30 to 40 seconds. Finding nothing, I returned to the kitchen and I noticed thick blackish/grey smoke rolling out of the coffeemaker, near the warming plate or the underside of the unit. I unplugged the cord, noting that it was cool to touch. I took the unit outside and put it on the porch. On December 26,2011 I calleed the cousinart toll free number and talked to REDACTED, to
report the incident. I was able to get the serial number and the model number that was molded onto the plastic bottom of the unit so she could record that information I explained to her what had happened and that the unit was about 10 months old. She said that based on the serial number, that was correct. She then offered to send me a replacement unit. I informed her that I had already purchased a different model of a cousinart coffeemaker, because I liked their product. I was not after a replacement unit. All I wanted to do was make cousinart aware of the problem, and if I hadn't gotten up when I did, my house may have burned down. She offered me a replacement unit at least two more times, as I was trying to express my concern with the potential problem with the unit for others using the same unit. Feeling frustrated, I asked to speak to her supervisor. she put me on hold and after four or five minutes, a woman named REDACTED talked with me. I explained the situation to her and she also offered to send a replacement unit, rather than express concern over the incident itself.I explained that I had already replaced the unit, and that I only wanted someone at cousinart to be aware of the problem so they could take action as needed. I then asked to speak with her supervisor. She told me she had no supervisor. I asked to speak to a technition or an engineer, and she told me there was none available. I told her I needed to talk to someone in authority . She put me on hold for awhile, and when she came back on line, she gave me the name and number for REDACTED at REDACTED, who she identified as their REDACTED. I told her thanks, hung up, and called the number. The number rang 30-40 times with no response.  I hung up.

incidentDescription:
Approximately back in September I purchased a Motorcycle Battery Charge/Standby charger from Walmart in Neptune NJ. The charger was manufactured and distributed by Schumacher Electric Corporation. (http://www.batterychargers.com/)
I used the charger approximately 2 times for standby charging to keep my motorcycle battery, which was only about a year and a half old, healthy. Then a week later I connected the battery connectors to the charger with the quick connects connected and then plugged the charger into the wall. Nothing happened. The charger unit did not turn on and never began charging. I checked the quick connects which connect the charger unit to the charger tips to verify they were seated correctly. DUE TO FAULTY/DANGEROUS construction the connectors DO NOT connect properly. I checked them and they as always don't seat correctly. Then the charger unit made a small popping sound, then my battery exploded and I breathed in white presumably acidy smoke. The charger cords then baked to a crisp and almost caused a fire. My charger was ruined, my battery was ruined, and my side plastic of my motorcycle was ruined. I for two weeks contacted the company's customer service department regarding my claim for their defective product as I only wanted the $200 to replace the damaged property of mine. After two weeks of no response I filed a BBB complaint and long story short the company told me to [REDACTed] myself. They said there charger unit itself had ZERO imperfections and that too bad but they were denying my claim. I sent them my charger for them to examine as well as photo proof showing how their connectors are faulty and caused an electrical short. Then sent me back the broken charger as well as the burnt up/charred wires. I then just in the last week attempted to use the charger again with the different type of connectors (snap on type, no screw on which i used first). And that set of wires also overheated/melted but this time didn't cause my battery to explode. I'm trying to make people alert to the faulty and very dangerous product this company is selling. I'm also bringing this complaint to the Dept of Consumer Affairs so I can try to get my money for the damage their product cost me. Or I will proceed with BBB Arbitration and furthermore a Private Lawsuit against the company as their item caused problems, and I was forced to breathe in toxic fumes. I would like an investigation into the companies product as I've heard several similar stories regarding their products which are cheap china made crap causing overheating and fires. Thanks.

productDescription: back up battery
incidentDescription:
This letter is being sent to you about an incident concerning a BELKIN backup battery Mod.
#BU3DCOOl-12V, SN #BDC-11B42598D2.
In November, we were having problems with our TV signal. AT&T customer service was called
and a technician was sent out. The problem with our TV was fixed. Shortly thereafter, we
started having problems with our telephone. Again, I called customer service and was told we
needed an updated modem. The modem arrived along with a new backup battery referenced
above, which we really didn't need since the original backup battery was working fine. I then
installed both the new modem and the new battery.
On December 19, my wife had several messages on her cell phone from AT&T. The message
stated that several e-mails had been sent to us and that the referenced battery needed to be
replaced. We both checked our e-mails and our spam folders and we could not find any e-mails
from AT&T. A toll-free number[REDACTED] was also given to call. My wife called on
Tuesday, December 20th. The toll free number, as it turned out, was to the BELKIN company.
The representative asked for the serial number of the battery (80C-II84259802) and she was
told that was indeed a defective battery. My wife asked what the defect was and was told that
the battery would not provide back-up power in case of a power outage. She was told that a
new battery would be sent and should arrive in 3-5 days. The battery arrived late Thursday
evening, December 22nd. I did not install the battery on Thursday since we were led to believe
that the only problem with the battery was that it might not provide the backup needed in case
of a power outage.
On December 23rd, we were awakened by our dog barking at 4 a.m. We immediately could
smell the odor of burning wires. After a search of the house, we determined the smell was
coming from our office and, specifically, the battery. It was no coincidence that the same week
we were advised of a defect in the battery that we had this incident. My wife called tech
support for Belkin and all she was told was the battery we were sent was among a bad batch of
batteries. She kept questioning the agent at Belkin asking if the real problem with the battery
was a safety/fire hazard and not the original reason we were given and the lady said: "how can
I say this to you" and then immediately asked if there was anything else she could do for her.
Needless to say, we are very disappointed in the way this matter was handled by both the
BELKIN company and AT&T. If we had been told from the beginning that the battery was a
potential fire hazard, I would have immediately disconnected it and waited for the replacement
battery to arrive. Fortunately for us, we were home at the time, but, if we had not been home
we definitely would have had a fire with dire consequences for us. At this time, our perception
is that we were misled about the reason we were given regarding the defect in the battery and,
we are seriously considering other options for cable service. Enclosed you will find five photos
of the internal parts of the battery case.

productDescription: Counter top convection toaster oven

incidentDescription:
Last week, I bought a Black & Decker Convection Toaster Oven, Model No. CT04500S, Type 2. 
Our first use of the product was to toast some breads and that worked ok. Next time, we tried to broil some food. But after a few minutes, with a loud bang, the front glass panel  exploded and showered the kitchen floor with hundreds of small glass shards for upto about 10/12 ft. It was sheer luck that there was no serious injury to anyone because we were about 15/20 ft away from the counter on which the toaster rested. This product should be immediately removed from the market before it seriously hurts someone.

productDescription: Toast-R Oven (TRO 490B Type 1)
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
manufacturer: Applica Consumer Products, Inc. - NOTIFY SPECTRUM BRANDS
incidentDescription:
TO: Black and Decker:

In June I purchased your Toast-R Oven (TRO 490B Type 1) at Wal-Mart.
On December 9, 2001 I followed the instructions by turning the dial past the "10" mark and back again to the "light toast" mark to toast an English muffin. Within a few minutes, smoke began to appear from the toaster oven. I unplugged the toaster oven and found a burnt English muffin.  I plugged it back in to find that the element was still active. 
It appears that timer is defective as it sticks shortly before it is supposed to shut off causing the element to “stay hot” indefinitely. I can replicate the problem every time.  I have taken the toaster out of service. The only way to turn off the toaster oven is to manually force the timer to off when your food looks ready.
This is an extremely dangerous product that could endanger the lives and property of  an owner. 
Please let me know what I should do.
Thank you,
 [REDACTED}

productDescription: Cuisinart Brew Central DCC-1200 coffeemaker purchased March 2011
incidentDescription:
This is in reference to a Cuisinart Brew Central Coffeemaker, model DCC-1200, purchased in March 2011 from Amazon. I bought this because it was rated #1 in the Consumer Reports Dec. 2010 issue. This week it started to make a clicking noise after being on for about an hour, then began to smoke from the back of it. I caught it in time since I happened to be in the kitchen but I'm reporting this here because I believe it is a fire hazard. According to Consumeraffairs.com website, others have had the exact same thing happened. I reported it to Cuisinart today like they did but the company claims they know nothing about it. They would replace it with the same model but not refund the money unless I tried this model 3 times. Needless to say I will not try this again since I don't need my house to catch on fire. Just passing this info on to you.
Thanks, [REDACTED]

Hand held hair dryer - 1875W 
Black rubber
manufacturer: Yuyao Dewei Electric Appliance & Motor Co.
incidentDescription:
I bought a style elements hand held hair dryer several months ago for my son's girlfriend so when she flew out here, she wouldn't have to worry about packing hers along with a few other items to keep the weight down in her suitcase.

She arrived here on January 4, 2012 and used the hair dryer the next day.  Within a few minutes of drying her hair, she came to me and said that the hair dryer had gotten very hot.  That it was so hot that she had to cut it off immediately because it was burning her hand.  I tried it and within 10 seconds, I too had to shut off or risk getting burned.  It also had a terrible odor coming from it after being turned on.

I started searching the Internet and found another style elements sold through Big Lots with the same problem but did not see this model listed as being recalled.  I hope this product is recalled or some one is going to be seriously burned.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription:
Model # CF700WW05
Electric Mo. JFJ15A01
UL- E130543, 23FB, Listed Fan 52G
incidentDescription: The fan had been working that day, up until we noticed it wasn't and the power switch was still in the on position.  My husband shut off the switch and then tried going to a different speed, but that still didn't work.  The bedroom , where this fan is located in, also had a terrible oder; liked burnt plastic.  We aired out the room, which helped somewhat and just left the power to the fan off until our small grandkids left to go home.  My husband then disconnected the fan and took it down, only to find the capacitator had started to melt, which is what we were smelling.  This really upset me when I thought about what could of happened, since our 2 year grandson was sleeping in this room.  We are now leary of the remaining 6 ceiling fans we have.  All 7 fans were installed by a licensed electrician, during the construction of our home, back in 1996.  This was an incident that could of resulted in our home burning down and/or lives being taken.  We will never buy Emerson ceiling fans again !  This was also another inferior product, MADE IN CHINA !!!!!!  Why couldn't a safety switch (breaker) be installed on any electrical product that would shut down the unit as soon as it starts to overheat?  This would be inexpensive and save lives, provided they aren't manufactured in China.

productDescription: Kitchenaid Coffe Maker
incidentDescription:
The consumer stated that his coffee maker is a burn hazard as his coffee maker has a front door where the cup that holds the coffee grounds, has tendency to swing open posing a burn hazard. There is no mechanism to keep this door secured. The consumer also stated that the coffee maker has the coffee spill out of the rubber gasket atop where the coffee comes out of the coffee maker. This gasket is glued and the glue is now peeling, causing coffee to spill in all directions. The consumer stated that he has not been hurt by the product but the hot coffee has spilled on his foot. 

The consumer called the firm about the issue 3 times  as of two weeks ago. The consumer called the firm two weeks ago and told the consumer that they were aware of the problem. The consumer was informed that this coffee maker could have a new door and coffee pot but was currently unavailable. The consumer didn’t think that this was a viable solution. The consumer researched online how to order a replacement and found that these replacement parts were on sale. 

The consumer called back the firm’s 800 number and requested to speak with the corporate office. The consumer called the corporate office and told the consumer that they would send him the new model of that coffee maker. The firm called him back and advised him to mail back the old coffee maker in a pre posted envelope. 

The consumer received the “new” coffee maker and it is the exact same as his old one and poses the same hazard. Subsequently, the consumer has left 4 messages with the firm who have yet to call him back. The consumer has not had his home damaged by the product. The consumer stated that the product does not appear damaged.

productDescription: Blender to make soup
incidentDescription:
Purchased Cuisinart "Blend and Cook Soupmaker" for Christmas.  Works very well.  Used it three times.  After third use was placing jar in dishwasher when the loswer lip brushed a plate and 3/4 of the lip fell off.  I have photos of the broken part and have retained it for future review if needed.  My engineer brother in law viewed the photos and reported  "Very clean break.  Just what I'd expect of a "brittle material."  The neck is the weak point, but should not be that weak.  I'm surprised it would break easily .  If it is not a manufacturing defect, then it is poor engineering."  I reported it to Cuisinart but they merely stated that glass was not covered under the warranty.  I have ordered a replacement jar and will continue to use it, after careful inspection of the new jar.

My concern is that if the jar had failed in use it could have caused more than just a mess.  I am curious as to whether or not any other reports have been made of similar events.

productDescription: Cuisinart Coffeemaker
incidentDescription:

The consumer could hear the coffee maker from her bed which she thought was the coffee brewing. The consumer found that the coffee was boiling (hard boil) in the pot.

The consumer stated that the product was smoking a little bit. The consumer unplugged the coffeemaker and the smoking stopped. The consumer heard a little of a crackling noise after unplugging the coffeemaker. The noise continued until she poured water in the reservoir to cool it down.  The consumer stated that she was not injured by the product. The consumer stated that the product did not damage her house. 

The consumer stated that the coffeemaker does not look damaged on appearance. The consumer did not call the fire department after the incident happened. The consumer has yet to call the retailer and found numerous reports online about similar incidents with similar model numbers.  The consumer called the firm on December 12, 2011. The firm told the consumer they were going to send a replacement coffeemaker. The consumer  has yet to receive the replacement. (Received replacement evening of 12/21).

productDescription: edenpure gen 4 space heater
incidentDescription: I purchased a eden pure gen 4 space heater at Gemmins hardware store in Hudsonville Michigan on december 17th 2011 and took it to a friends house as a christmas present. Within two minutes of turning it on it began to smoke and then an acrid white toxic smoke began to pour out of the heater that rose up to the ceiling and filled the room with smoke a foot or two down from the ceiling. I took it out side and it continued to smoke. We had to open the doors and windows for over two hours with snow and temps in the low 30s. The smoke made our throats sore the next day as well and there was some lingering oder. I took the heater back to the store imediately and got antother and plugged it in out in the garage and it gave off a similar smell for a long time but didn't smoke. However I unplugged it and took it back to the store on monday the 19th as soon as it opened. My friend didn't want it in her house and I didn't trust it either. If the first one could suddenly pour out smoke while we were watching it then what's to prevent another from doing the same when there was no one to catch it. I believed there is a serious safety defect with these heaters and it needs to be corrected before some one is killed.

productDescription: humidifier
model: Cool Mist Ultasonic Humidifer Model HUM-CM50
incidentDescription:
Report of design defect
When replacing water in a "Cool Mist Ultrasonic Humidifier" Model HUM-CM50, distributed by HoMedics, http://www.homedics.com/?gclid=CNbljMi_ua0CFYUZQgodNnO0nQ I followed the instructions filling the water tank at the fill location on the bpttom of the tank and ther replaced the cap.  I then inverted the tank.  Again following the instructions, I picked up the water tank using the handle on the top as illustrated in the instruction manual.  The handle broke away from the water tank and crashed to the floor and broke.  Fortunatley it did not fall on my foot as the sharp edge of the bottom of the tank could cause serious injury.
This is a design defect that can easily result in the tank with sharp edges on the bottom side dropping with the weight of the water.  That sharp edge of the plastic tank could damage exposed flesh or if falls on the electric cord during the reinstallation of the tank potentially sever the insulation on the electric cord, the tank break and flood the floor with water causing and accidental electrocution of the product user.
The plastic foldable U-shaped handle is attached to the tank only by two small tabs approximately a 1/4 inch in length.  The installation of the handle at manufacture is simply by expanding the handle and then it returns to original shape.  With the added weight of the 1 gallon of water in the tank, the handle readily disengages from the retaining slots.  With the shape of the handle being U shaped and approximately 3 and 1/8 inches wide and only approximately 1 and half inches deep even a person with small hands  when inserting four fingers and picking up the tank will cause the width of the handle to expand and disengage the handle tabs from the slots.

PETSROLL 3 wheel scooter
The model is GoPet 
The serial number is P200908000672
incidentDescription:
While riding a PETSROLL 3 wheel scooter, the scooter became overbalanced rearward to the wheelie protection wheel and lost control, resulting in broken leg and ankle.  The reason control was lot is that the unit is driven by the front wheel and all braking, drive and steering is on the front wheel. if the unit becomes overbalanced backward and the front wheel leaves the ground, there is no way to control or stop the device. When overbalanced backward, the unit is practically impossible to return to the proper attitude. These units are imported from China and named PERTSROLL, ZAPPY 3, etc www.petsroll.net, www.zapworld.com/zappy-3-standard, etc.

productDescription: Cuisinart Brew Central Coffeemaker Model CBC-4400
incidentDescription:
This morning we heard sound coming from our Cuisinart Brew Central coffeemaker model CBC-4400 S/N 70531C. Upon investigation the coffee in the carafe was bubbling.  Then a white vapor was emanating from the left side of the base. Within seconds the strong smell of burning electrical components was evident.  I unplugged the coffeemaker and removed it to the back patio to cool or burnout.
An online Internet search showed the several other reports of Cuisinart fires had been reported.  We were lucky to be in attendance when this fire occurred. The coffeemaker has a two hour turnoff and our unit was still in within that time period.   Since the coffeemaker has a timer feature I recommend that it NOT BE USED.  To have the coffeemaker turn on during an unattended time would be a hazard.  The coffeemaker should have a high current and high temperature cutoff if it is equipped with a timer.  The unit should be deemed UNSAFE if plugged in and NOT ATTENDED!

productDescription: Free standing electric heater
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription:
On 12/20/2011 the heater made by Bionaire model # BCH9221 stopped blowing warm air. I removed the back panel looking for a blown fuse. There is no fuse in the unit. What I found was a burned neutral wire, melted case, and arching marks within the unit.

The unit has a single 16ga wire acting as the neutral for 2, 750 watt heat elements.
A single 16ga wire is rated for 13 amps

The heater is a 1500 watt heater
1500 watts / 120 volts = 12.5 amps

The 16 gauge neutral wire is under sized and has the potential of causing a fire within the unit.

productDescription: bialetti muka coffee maker   Two part unit that holds water and coffee in lower container and milk in the upper section, hot coffee is pumped up into upper section where coffee and heated milk are combined before pouring into cups
incidentDescription:
Bialetti Muka Expresso coffee maker has exploded twice sending hot coffee up to the ceiling and all over the kitchen counters. First incident occurred 2 years ago and the company sent us a replacement valve assembly to prevent a recurrence. This new valve was a different design and worked successfully until December 6th when the second valve exploded. Parts of the plastic/metal assembly  travelled upward with enough force to damage the stove exhaust hood and break a glass cover on one of the hood's lights. Hot coffee sprayed an area in an area about 24 inches in diameter on the ceiling above, and required repainting. More importantly, this coffee eruption was within 18 inches of a house guest waiting for the first cup of the day! Major burns would have occurred had he been closer to the stovetop.

The company response was to provide 2 replacement valves and an "I’m Sorry"

One question, unanswered by the company, was whether our altitude of nearly 9,000 ft would impact the release pressure of the valve assembly A possible cause?

I would like to see an independent evaluation of this product before some one is badly burned. THANKS

productDescription:
4-rack fully automatic food smoker with 2,288-cubic-inch interior
    500-watt cooking element; 125-watt smoking element; heats up to 280 degrees F
    Unique smoke without fire system features wood-flavored bisquettes that burn for 20 minutes each
    Runs for up to 8 hours without refueling; tray and drip bowl included; briquettes sold separately
    Measures 14-1/2 inches by 17 inches by 31 inches; 42 pounds; 1-year warranty
model: Bradley BTIS1 Original Fully Automatic 4-Rack Outdoor Food S
incidentDescription:
This is in regard to a Bradley BTIS1 Original Fully Automatic 4-Rack Outdoor Food Smoker 

Nearly caught my house on fire with this product, and please do note I am not alone, especially lately - check out the customer photos, reviews and their dates on the Amazon.com website: http://www.amazon.com/Bradley-BTIS1-Original-Automatic-Smoker/dp/B000FK2DNM/ref=cm_cr-mr-title

 Either this product is too difficult to use safely for most consumers, or I had a defective unit. I really believe it was the latter, but if it's the former, you're going to have a hard time keeping this product clean enough to be safe.

I bought this smoker in July (five months ago) and used the product according to directions. On the fifth use, it inexplicably overheated, melting the door seal. There was no fire that time.  I contacted Bradley.  Bradley sent out a replacement door seal, saying that the only way this can happen is if you improperly keep the vent closed, but they'd help me this time. I hadn't kept the vent closed, and said I was concerned it was a defective unit and a fire hazard. They continued to assert it must have been a closed vent. I crossed my fingers I had just not noticed my error.

It took me nearly 2 hours to replace the door seal, a dirty job that made me swear to myself I'd maintain the smoker perfectly so there would be no potential of user error going forward. Every single time I removed every single removable part and steel wool clean it. I wiped down the sides each time, and removed any obvious grease.

On about the fifth use after replacement of the door seal, my wife looked out the window just in time - the whole thing was ON FIRE. I unplugged it, doused the fire with water, and finished the turkey breast (not a greasy pork roast mind you, a turkey breast) in the oven.

I called up Bradley immediately, assuming the fire was proof I had a defective unit that would be quickly replaced. I figure, hey, they had a record of the first incident, so it shouldn't be much of a fuss. Ahem - no.  It would have to be reviewed.  I was asked to send in photos of the charred remains of the smoker.

After a week of chasing, I finally got to talk to [REDACTED], who is in charge of "fire incidents." I explained the situation, the previous problem, my exact experience and use of it, and he somehow determined, based only on AFTER photos of the charred remains of the unit that had been doused with water, that it was because of user error - that I hadn't cleaned the smoker thoroughly enough, and too much grease is why it caught fire. Then he offered me a "deep discount" that he didn't actually reveal.

I tried to engage him in simple logic. If you're saying this unit, that has caught fire, is NOT DEFECTIVE, and I'm saying that I've used this as responsibly as possible, what you are saying is either A) I am lying to you about how I maintained the product or B) that this product carries a very reasonable risk of a fire starting through normal customer use.

[REDACTED] didn't really want to say "A" but he essentially did when he refused to acknowledge the possibility of a defective unit. He said the chances of a defect were "slim to zero," explaining to me about how the components are each inspected before assembly. When I raised the possibility that it had been improperly assembled or perhaps my unit was otherwise defective, and offered to provide the unit to him somehow, he said there was no reason to do so. When I noted that I noticed others on Amazon were also having this issue, he literally laughed and said every product on Amazon has negative reviews from a few people.

This was pretty insulting given the time that I had invested in contacting the company to avoid a repeat of the overheating incident, and my earnest belief that I had used this product right and it was a defective unit. But at that point I realized that any company that would rather call a customer a liar than acknowledge the possibility that it could make a manufacturing error, was not worth a minute more of my time - other than helping assure other people aren't in my exact situation.

I wish I had taken others' warnings seriously on the Amazon website and not written them off as being posted by careless people who didn't bother taking care of the unit properly.

Consumers need to know that this product has the potential to catch fire, even if used very responsibly - and even if you are as careful as I was. I'm not some random Internet troll or someone in desperate need of a refund - I'm a regular suburban father who wouldn't bother submitting this if it were merely a product that stopped working.   This is about starting fires.

productDescription: Delonghi HHP1500 Safeheat Mica-Panel Heater.
incidentDescription:
I own a Delonghi HHP1500 Safeheat Mica-Panel Heater. I got this product from Home Depot about 3 years ago (2009).

Today I turned it on and was alarmed to see it SHOOT SPARKS like a tiny firework display from the main large flat micathermic panel. It is particularly dangerous because this is a SILENT heater and if you are not WATCHING the unit in action you may not notice sparking.
I believe what is happening is that after many continuous on-off-on-off cycles of heating, the insulation in the micathermic element is breaking down. If this is the correct analysis, then many of these units will FAIL SPARKING in similar way after several years of use -- and go from being very safe to very unsafe.

I will keep this unit for your investigation. I maybe able to send you a video of it sparking.

productDescription: batteries - Duracell AA Alkaline 1.5 V, Mar 2017, with the following number : 1D01D076
incidentDescription:
This toy is a pink plastic toy wand with a 5 pointed star on top that emits sounds and changes colors when switched on. The only marking on this toy is a decal which reads []REDACTED].  The wand was purchased in December for my grandchild as a Christmas gift and left at my home for her to play with when she visits from out of state. This year, she wanted to play with the wand and I realized the batteries were dead. I replaced the batteries with 2 new AA Duracells and then turned the unit on. It did not turn on, so I re-checked the loading of the batteries and tried the switch again. Suddenly, the handle became so hot, I instinctively dropped the wand to the floor. At this time I smelled plastic burning. Her grandfather came into the kitchen when he heard me yell. He grabbed it off the floor to keep the grandchild (age 3.5 years) from touching it and he burned his finger. He tossed it into the sink. He then secured kitchen gloves and removed the batteries as the wand was continuing to melt and heat and we could not stop it. 

This is a very dangerous toy. It could have caused severe burns to a child, could have started a fire. What disturbs me most is there is no information on this toy regarding where it was made, or who made it. This leads me to believe that it is an import. I am reporting this to perhaps save a child from injury and because I am sick of unsafe toys being imported into the United States that harm our children.

Yesterday morning upon entering daughter's room, I asked why it was so cold. She responded by using her remote at her bedside to initiate DeLonghi Heater, purchased last fall at a local retailer.
The unit turned on with fan and heat. I commented to her that her mouth did not appear as swollen as she'd just had braces applied 2 days before, a rather unpleasent experiance. We then both exclaimed,"What's that SMELL!?"!  Because the heater had just been turned on, I turned to look down and saw smoke billowing out  from the bottom rear left of the unit and less smoke wafting out the top of the unit, the whole time the unit continued operating as if all systems were "go". I quickly unplugged the unit and we both left the room to be able to breathe. The stench was toxic, simular to an electrical fire in my apartment in 1976, of which a stereo that had recently been repaired from a lightning strike, was identified as the culprit. Had I not been called into work that night, its probable I would've died in my sleep. I came home from working NICU to my windows completly blackened with toxic soot, my door warm to touch. I woke my neighbors on both sides and tried to climb from one's balcony to mine in attempt to rescue my 2 kittens, Gypsy and Jessica, but my neighbors kept saying I couldn't make it ( 3rd floor apt). The firemen arrived, they had head gear, and went in to rescue them, but it was too late. 
It was that kind of toxic stench that was billowing into my daughter's room from this "Delonghi SAFEHEAT" heater.
It was that unavoidable memory of sheer anguish, of their limp, lifeless bodies in my arms, that motivates me almost exactly 35 years later, to put my many other priorities aside (and 2 weeks before Xmas, there's plenty I need to be doing, believe me). 
For it maybe, that some good can come from the horrible death my kittens must have experianced so many years ago. I know how blessed I am to still have my child, braces and all, here with me today. And if my relating this alarming event can alert and perhaps prevent someone else's loved one from a simular tragic occurance, then some good will be done.
There is obvious plastic meltage on the unit.
Should pictures or the unit itself be desired, please advise.

productDescription: Dimplex calls this a compact electric stove, actually it is an electric space heater with simulated flames. The flames are created by light bulbs and a holagram, with no real fire. It plugs into the wall and is lightweight metal. Once the front door of the stove is open, there are three rocker switches to operate the features. The first switch is on-off and lights the flames only, without heat. The next switch turns the heat on low, with the heat emitting from the bottom of the stove toward the front. The second switch increases the heat to high, with a higher blower of heat from the bottom of the front. Turning off the first switch shuts down all heat and simulated flames.
incidentDescription: I only used this heater occassionally in the winter, since there is forced air furnace in my home. I have had to replace the on-off switch of this model DS3311 Dimplex compact Stove twice because the switch "froze" in the on mode and couldn't turn off. I had to unplug it.  Both times I noticed the switch plastic had melted around the prong that installs into the electric connection, separating the prong from the connection and leaving it frozen. I have the same problem now for the third time. The Dimplex company sent me a 3 new switches in October 2010 when this happened the first time and charged me $35, then when it happened again in March 2011, they asked if it had frozen and sent me 3 more new switches at no cost. (The set comes in 3, but the on-off switch is for the light bulb that simulates flames and the only one that continually malfunctions. The other two switches turn on the heat to high and then to low).  The second switch froze this week, this time in the off mode.  I believe this is a fire hazard and am asking that you recall the product. I noticed the power cord is very warm while the unit is operating. I am reluctant to try these switches anymore and hope you reply quickly, as I use the heater a few times a week in the winter. I originally paid $200 for it and never had this trouble with the other space heaters from other companies that are used more frequently than this. The way this unit is constructed makes it very difficult to remove the housing completely in order to replace parts. In following their directions, there is only a slim passage to reach into the interior works for replacing the switch. Their design is extremely inefficient and shows no forethought for future servicing. Thank you for your help. I hope the company can replace this with a safe product that looks the same, since the holagram flames look very realistic in this model.

productDescription:

Model DCC-1200
incidentDescription:
I have Cuisinart DCC-1200 Coffee Maker that was approximately 15 months old. After making a pot of coffee today, I went back to my desk. Within a few minutes, I heard loud snapping and popping sounds coming from the kitchen. I ran out there to see smoke billowing from the base of the DCC-1200 unit. Smoke was filling the kitchen. I quickly unplugged it and and placed it outside. I would guess it was only a minute or two from catching fire. I got the unit replaced under warranty from the store I purchased it from. 

Out of curiosity, I searched online to see if other Cuisinart DCC-1200 customers had the same problem. I was stunned to find dozens of people who have had the exact same thing happen to their Cuisinart Coffee Maker within the last two months. Many of them had their units actually catch fire. 

I called Cusinart customer service. They showed a very casual attitude regarding my news and said they are always improving their products. I am currently in the process of contacting the head of customer service at Cuisinart. I will keep climbing the ladder until I get action.

The Cuisinart DCC-1200 is clearly a dangerous product that MUST be recalled and taken off the market immediately!!! How many customers' home need to burn down and lives lost before this problem is addressed?

productDescription: Eureka Boss Upright Vacuum Cleaner, Bagless with dust wand.
incidentDescription:
I was using an Eureka Boss Upright vacuum cleaner, model # 5902BVZ, and noticed that the handle near the switch was getting progressively warmer. As I finished up the vacuuming it was down right hot to the touch and in switching it off it sparked from within the handle at the switch. When I tried to turn it back on to trouble shoot the problem it would spark and the power to the vacuum would cut in and out without the rocker switch moving sparking each time.

When I opened up the handle after I let it cool the wiring had melted through its insulation in 2 wires and the slide on "quick connect" connectors attached to the 3 way switch was charred. The handle was also melted where the wires were touching the inside plastic of the handle.

  As well as being charred in the connectors, the wire going into the connectors on two wires were also frayed and there was a pale greenish looking residue on the metal of the wires, like the metal was corroded which was also evident on the inside wall of the wire's insulation.

  I don't know if it's the wire's fault(improper gauge, low quality), the switches fault causing the wires to over heat or the connectors. Reading online I've come across many experiencing the same exact problem but all having different theories as to the culprit.

  I see this as a large hazard and a design flaw more than a "wear and tear" issue and Eureka should address this issue.

productDescription: "Comfort Zone" model CZ798, 120VAC 1500W electric space heater. Grey rectangular case, 14" tall, 9-3/4" wide, 6-3/4" deep inclusive of front-facing handles and rear louvers. Bears a label on the bottom stating "Made in China 07/11" with a "Conforms to UL STD #1278" statement, etc.
incidentDescription:
Electric space heater tipover switch melted during operation and dropped to the bottom of the space heater. Bimetallic tab-type thermostat glowed bright red during operation and ultimately welded itself closed, causing constant-on heater operation.  This is the third electric space heater to malfunction in this manner.

The "thermostat" mechanism carries the full current of the heater coils, and is a fire hazard due to contact pitting, resultant series resistance, and final always-on operation.  If left unattended, temperature will rise to dangerous levels.

productDescription: Rival slow cooker model SCV601, date code X264DH, stainless base, enameled pot
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription:
My Rival slow cooker, model SCV 601, date code X364DH, has had both its plastic handles on the base of the pot crumble, exposing sharp screws which become hot when the pot is used.  The screws cannot be accessed from the back to remove them.

The hazard is being cut by the sharp screws and/or being burned by the screws if the pot is plugged in.

I called customer service, and the apologetic rep said the unit was no longer under warranty, but she could offer 15% off a replacement pot. No replacement parts are available.

Similar failures have resulted in a recall, with replacement of the base unit, regardless of the age. (http://www.cpsc.gov/cpscpub/prerel/prhtml05/05236.html )   This recall should be expanded to include this unit.  The hazard for this uncovered unit is the same as the hazard described in the recall.  There are multiple reports of similar failures (search this model number on google).

productDescription: Krups IL Primo  Type 972/A Espresso Maker
incidentDescription:
While making Espresso, a loud whoosh was heard followed by a massive steam escape from the unit. No injuries.

Upon disassemble it was discovered the the four plastic (PBTP) mounting brackets that secure the boiler unit assembly to the appliance housing had cracked. The two halves of the boiler unit were separated by approximately 2mm.

The brackets are secured to the boiler assembly with the same screws that clamp the upper and lower halves of the boiler unit together. The brackets are approx 2mm thickness and over time deteriorated such that the bracket split and the material under the screw head broke away from the rest of the bracket on each of the four brackets. This resulted in the boiler unit not being secured to the chassis and being held in place by means not intended for that purpose. Once the material under the screw heads deteriorated further and fell away, there became a 2mm gap between the housing and screw head. Eventually the steam pressure inside the chamber during the boiling process caused the 2 halves of the boiler unit to separate by approx 2mm resulting in a massive steam escape and rendering the unit inoperable. 

The method of mounting the boiler unit to the chassis with a plastic bracket is not safe and should be designed with metal brackets.

My Delonghi heater was plugged into a 110V wall outlet, on a modern breaker-type electrical circuit. When I discovered the heater not producing heat, I traced the cord back to the wall and found the wall completely scortched above the plug. The Delonghi heater plug had one of its prongs completely melted off the end of the plug.

There were no other appliances on or connected to this circuit. The 20 amp hpuse circuit breaker did trip, fortunately.

My son in law is a practicing electrical engineer, and he is concerned that the 1500 watt space heater applance has a service cord much too small in diameter to carry a full load of current without overheating.

The outlet was inspected after removing power from the outlet, and the duplex outlet replaced. The house wirning is fully compliant with the local elctrical code (12 Guage wire with ground for a 20 amp circuit), and the electrical service panel is modern, having been updated within the last several years.

productDescription:
Freestanding Outdoor Stainless Steel Patio Heater - Gas Fired Infrared, Propane, 40,000BTU, 88" tall.
http://www.acefactorystore.com/proddetail.asp?prod=4304309&cat=192
productType: Gas or Lp Heaters, Other or Not Specified (392)
incidentDescription:
Having a party by the pool and in the late afternoon it was getting cool.  I lit the patio heater, using the knob (which creates a spark to ignite the pilot light).  It lit on the fourth or fifth try and then I turned the knob further to the low position.  Once the burner was lit, I turned it further to high, which was fully CCW.  I closed the lid covering the knob.  Many of the women at the party gathered around and started talking (four or five) and this went on for about 30 minutes.  
As they were standing there, the lower portion of the patio heater (where the propane tank is stored) exploded.  Flames shot out the lower vent holes at the very bottom of the unit and everyone jumped.
I ran over to the unit (I was about 15 feet away, facing the unit) and saw the propane cylinder was on fire, but still enclosed in the lower cylinder cover.  I first tried to open the burner valve cover to access the knob and shut off the upper flame.  The fire was shooting out of the grid and burning the entire upper section.  My finger burned as soon as I touched the cover, so I could not access the valve.
My attention turned to the burning propane cylinder.  I told everyone to get away, far away.  I blew hard through the hand-hole of the cylinder cover and was able to extinguish the flame.  I then opened the cylinder cover, which burned my hand further.  I then turned off the gas valve on top of the propane cylinder, burning all five fingers on my right hand (through my shirt I was using to protect my hand).
There was molten metal on the regulator that must have dripped down from the inside of the upper burner area.  I have no idea what melted.
Someone handed me a bottle of water, and I used it to extinguish the upper flame, that was still burning without propane feeding it.  
An hour or so later, I opened the door to the knob in the upper burner area and it was melted beyond recognition.
The patio heater is still sitting exactly as it was during the fire.

productDescription: Weber Genesis E-310 Natural Gas Grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
The incident relates to a new Weber natural gas grill purchased in the spring of 2011. In the ~20 times that we have used the grill and then put the cover back on (which came with the product), on 3 occasions, we have gone to our driveway/out back on the deck only to smell a strong odor of natural gas. Upon further investigation, we have figured out that the gas on the grill was turned on by the cover.. in other words, the amount of pressure needed to move the control knob to open the gas was so minimal, that replacing the cover over the grill was enough to turn it on. We are so lucky that someone did not walk back there with a cigarette, as we would have significant property damage and worse.. the potential for someone to get very hurt! As a Weber grill owner previously (last one we had for 10 years), not once did this happen on our old model!! That said, I am very sad to share the actual correspondence from Weber (below)... who first claims that they recommend that you shut off the gas after each use (although this warning/recommendation is NOT in the owner's guide), and the secondly, advises me "to be more careful". Very disappointing for a clear safety issue for their product, and one that clearly was not the same on prior models (where the same event did not occur) Actual correspondence with Weber Customer Service provided below : From: [REDACTED] To: support@weberstephen.com Subject: RE: Ticket: [REDACTED] Re: Weber Genesis E-310 - safety hazard Date: Mon, 14 Nov 2011 06:19:54 -0500 You see, this is very interesting to me being as we just replaced our old Weber of 10+ years with this one. On that one, there was more pressure required to turn the gas on with the control knobs, and not once in 10+ years did putting on the cover EVER turn on a knob. Seems to me that you did have a design that was different. In addition, in my previous email, I asked for the page # on the owner's guide that gives this warning. I read through the 20+ warnings and did not come across it. Please advise. Thanks for putting the blame on the consumer, surely not the customer service or concern I would expect from Weber. In an effort to prevent others from putting their life and property in jeopardy, I will be pursuing this with CPSC with fervor. Subject: Weber Genesis E-310 - safety hazard > > Dear Weber Support, > > I am writing to ask for assistance regarding a Weber Genesis E-310 (natural gas) that we purchased this spring 2011. productDescription: Farberware Electric percolating 12 cup coffee pot model FCP412G
manufacturer: Applica Consumer Products, Inc. - NOTIFY SPECTRUM BRANDS
incidentDescription:
This is the second time that my Farberware coffee pot has had a catastrophic failure.  The first incident happened on January 30, 2009.  I plugged in my Farberware superfast fully automatic 12 cup coffee pot into a GFI protected circuit - the consequence of which was an electrical explosion. One of the male connectors in the base of the unit separated from its insulated mounting and was pressed back into the base. That caused the a direct short when plugged into my outlet.

This first incident was to was "Farberware Superfast Fully Automatic" model number FCP 280 with the date code of 97 1105.  I made an immediate report to the CPSC and initially retained the destroyed GFI and coffee pot.  

After some period of time, after not having heard from the CPSC, I packaged up the unit and sent to Underwriter Laboratories for  failure analysis.  The implication of their analysis was that the coffee pot had been submerged and was corroded as a consequence of having been underwater.  This was not the case as my spouse and I have been the sole owners and users of that coffee pot from the inception.  We NEVER immersed the coffee pot.  A visual examination of the insulation piece that separated male side of the plugs at the base of the pot had cracked and separated such that it no longer held one side of the pin.  That is, it was a mechanical failure that allowed for this direct short having nothing to do with the UL allegation that an immersion was involved.

After that incident, we purchased a replacement coffee pot model FCP number 412G.  This one has failed in much the same way.  It is marked "QC passed" and 102 EE is embossed on its base.  I do not see a date code on it.  However, there is a stamping on it that says 102 EE.

On November 4, 2011, this reaplacement coffee pot also tripped the GFI; however it did not explode like the first incident.  There is obviously a dead short in this one too.  

I suspect that the replacement Farberware Coffee Pot suffers from a similar defect in design as the original one.  This time I am not sending it to UL for their failure analysis but will hold onto it assuming that you would have an interest in examining it.

productType: Hair Curlers, Curling Irons, Clips & Hairpins (1682)
model: H-9000 Pearl Ceramic Ultimate T Studio Style Professional
incidentDescription:
Remington Pearl Ceramic Ultimate T Studio 20 hair rollers.
1. The ends of each roller will burn fingertips. They did mine. One would think that companies that make hair rollers would want to use a heat resistant plastic to make the ends out of, since they know their customers are in contact with the ends of the rollers than any other part of the roller. 

2. These rollers sit on metal rods that heat up each roller. The last time I used the product I was unaware that some of the rollers had come off their places in the rods. I plugged unit in and went went few feet away back into the bedroom to do a few things while I waited for them to heat up.
  When I came back into bathroom I instantly smelled melting/burning plastic, lifted up the lid and found the rollers that weren't sitting on the rods like they should have been and the ends were in direct contact with the hot metal rods, and therefore melting as they were sitting against the rods.
  I unplugged it, carefully got the rollers back on the rods where they were supposed to be and swore to take it back after setting it down on my empty tub ledge to cool off. 
  I had planned on taking it back to Target where I bought it but then I got worried that even if I told the return clerk about what happened and made sure to tell them that they do not need to put them back on the shelf since they are a safety/fire risk and the ends are damaged now and the metal rods have melted plastic in some places; that the clerk would forget to pass that on to the next employee that handled it and it would be put back on the shelf.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

Luckily the spark went away from my face and I was not burned. However, I have searched online and found others have had similar problems with Revlon curling irons.

I contacted Revlon regarding the problem and they passed me along to the company they said makes these curling irons for them (Troy Industries). They offered me another curling iron which I said I really didn't want unless they could explain why the one I had malfunctioned and assure me that the same thing wouldn't happen to a new one. They said I would have to send them the curling iron so that their product safety review company could determine the cause of the malfunction. 

It seems strange to me that since others have had similar issues with their curling irons spanning over several years that they don't already know what the cause of the malfunction might be. I don't trust that they care or will follow through to make sure this product is made safe for the public. I hope you are able to follow through with them to see that this occurs.

Thank you,

[REDACTED]

incidentDescription:

Further investigation online revealed that this is not an isolated incident.  Link:  http://www.consumeraffairs.com/homeowners/cuisinart.html
Someone should look into these incidents before lives are lost.
Thank you!

productDescription: Avante Elite convection toaster oven
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
We purchased an Avante Elite convection toaster oven by T-FAL on 3-2-2010. This oven has a glass door on the top, covering a warming tray. The glass door has a 4 inch black handle attached to lift the door. Below the warming section is the regular convection/toaster oven with a separate handle. The Avante Elite sits on top of a 14 inch high microwave oven on a wooden kids play table at the side of our kitchen. 

At noon on 10-23-2011, we used the toaster function of the toaster oven to toast 4 slices of bread. We removed the toast and sat at our kitchen table which is 6 feet from the front of the Avante oven. Approximately ten minutes later there was a loud explosion sound and glass and the handle from the upper door of the Avante exploded into our kitchen. No one was near the oven, it was off at the time, and nothing hit it or dropped on it.  It just exploded! Glass pieces hit me sitting in my wheelchair at our table but did not injure me. For a few minutes following the original explosion, pieces of glass continued to fly off. We took numerous pictures of the glass and oven to document this catastrophic failure.

We were shocked by this amazing event. Frequently, our four young grandchildren eat at the table below the Avante. Luckily, they were not at our house today. If they had been sitting at the table, they would surely have been seriously injured by the flying glass and flying handle which weighs over 4 ounces. My daughter also has this model Avante oven in her house but she will stop using it immediately. 

I called T-FAL and started a report file with them about this incident. This is a very serious, dangerous failure of a common product which we felt the CSPS should know about.

productDescription: Apple MacBook Pro 17-inch widescreen notebook's OEM/stock Apple Rechargeable Battery
incidentDescription:
I bought two Apple MacBook Pro 17-inch laptops (Macintosh) for personal and office use.

Both of these computers came with the standard OEM factory parts, including the Apple-branded rechargeable lithium ion battery, as it should.

What should NOT happen is the following: In the 2 years of owning them, I have always exercised safe and very gentle operating and maintenance of the computers (I BABY THEM; I know how sensitive and delicate electronics can be, plus I never want to get even a scratch on the nice aluminum body).

I followed all the guidelines in the printed and electronic documentation included with the computers (including the user guide/manual). I always have and always do.

HOWEVER I noticed one day that the trackpad (built in touch pad) was difficult to operate and sometimes clicking was especially difficult. Soon I felt the computer was rocking back and forth. So I looked underneath and saw that the rechargeable battery had expanded/swollen out of its "normal" size. I knew something was wrong so I took it in to the "genius" bar at the Apple Store in Santa Monica, California (Third Street Promenade), where they brushed this incident off as "normal" and "the battery does that when it is consumed and no longer works. Time to buy a new battery." I replied that the battery still holds a solld 3 to 4 hour charge, and that System Profiler reports the battery status as "Normal" as far as charge-holding and discharging capacity. It was working fine for what it was made for, but not working fine as far as my computer's keyboard and trackpad operation. They suggested I spend $142 on a new battery (129 + 10.25% Tax). Or buy a bulk packaged battery from the genius bar for "only" $100. I denied their sales pitch and said that this was a manufacturing defect, and that I was worried it might further expand and burst. "Isn't this a health and safety issue? can't this cause a fire, and therefore possible damage and even death?" They didn't know what to say. I repeated that I would like a replacement free of charge for this manufacturing defect. They said no. So I left and continued to use the computer. The battery held a charge just fine. Well the next morning I came to my Office and the battery had indeed burst open, spewing some kind of chemical/gook all over my desk. It smelled like burning metal. I took it back to the genius bar, and they again said this was normal and that Apple is not responsible for it. Because my computer was "out of warranty" they felt they had no need to replace the now exploded Apple battery. 

A couple months later, I removed the Apple battery from my other 17-inch MacBook Pro, as I was leaving town for a couple weeks and feared a repeat of it blowing up in my house, possibly burning down the building. I placed in on my office desk and  when I came back from my trip, amazingly, the removed battery had somehow swollen up to the point of bursting the metal battery casing apart. No goo/liquid escaped this time, but the product was clearly unusable. I can see the cells inside bloated up. This is clearly not normal. This is a manufacturing defect that Apple is trying to cover up. If you google the phrase "Apple MacBook Pro Battery exchange" or even "Apple Macintosh PowerBook battery recall fires", you will see a lot of this happening in the past, and you'll see that up until 2008 or 2009, Apple admitted fault in their OEM laptop/notebook batteries, and said there is a risk of fire. They offered to replace such batteries for certain models/years, free of charge, no questions ask, regardless of Warranty status. This program for MacBook Pros (same model year as mine) is now closed. you can see the page still on Apple.com if you search the above. But they knew about the issues and HAD a recall, but ONLY for 15-inch MacBook Pros (as opposed to my 17-inch MB Pro), and they decided that they weren't responsible for any of them explooding, burning, catching fires, possibly destroying homes and possibly claiming human lives. Why? They fessed up before!

I called AppleCare (Customer Relations) and they interviewed me with a barrage of questions, it felt like a court deposition. They said they'd get back to me on what their "engineers find." I said okay, but never heard back from them. I called and left several kind but persistant messages. No callback, no reply, no replacement battery. No apology for possibly burning my house down while i slept. 

APPLE, YOU NEED TO DO THE RIGHT THING LEGALLY, MORALLY, and BEYOND. 

REPLACE ALL SWOLLEN BATTERIES FOR FREE WITHOUT HASSLE. 

DON'T LET THESE "normal" BATTERIES EXPLODE ON ANYONE ELSE.

Apple should issue a RECALL and offer one of their EXTENSION REPAIR PROGRAMS on their site apple.com and/or issue a full refund to owners who have already been FORCED to buy a new battery from Apple at almost $150 after tax per battery.

I thank you, APPLE COMPUTERS INC., for correcting this mistake in all fairness, and in accordance with U.S. Consumer Protection Laws.

productDescription: Black & Decker TRO355 toaster oven
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
manufacturer: Applica Consumer Products, Inc. - NOTIFY SPECTRUM BRANDS
incidentDescription:
I had a brand new Black & Decker model TRO355 toaster oven (an older model, circa 2006?) that was still in the original factory retail box.  This week (October 2011), I plugged in this toaster oven for the first time and used the toast function.  I could see through the front glass door that the upper and lower heating coils glowing red/orange.  But in about 1 or 2 minutes, there was a very loud explosion (louder than a firecracker)!  Fortunately, I was not looking through the glass door like I was doing just moments ago.  The front glass door blew open and there was smoke throughout the kitchen.  After yanking the power cord out of the AC outlet, I could see that the 2 bottom heating elements and 1 of the 2 top heating elements had exploded.  The metal sheath of each element was torn/twisted open and the coiled wire from inside the heating element was hanging out.  The white ceramic/porcelain insulators on the ends of each heating element had shattered.  There was white powder from those insulators everywhere inside the oven, on the kitchen counter, on the kitchen cabinets and on the floor.  There were small pieces of the white insulators in several places in the kitchen, up to about 4 feet away from the toaster oven.

This Black & Decker toaster oven was new and not tampered with or damaged in any way as far as I know.  I have looked on the internet and find at least a few other people who reported the exact same experience (explosion of the heating elements, white powder everywhere) and coincidentally was the same model:  TRO355.

I have had an older but very similar Black & Decker toaster oven that I used without any problems for over 10 years.  But this TRO355 was extremely dangerous and we are lucky that my spouse or I or my children were not injured by this incident.

productDescription: Toaster oven with convection, stainless steel.
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription: Toaster oven started emitting a smell and small amounts of smoke about a week before the main incident.  We though some food or other foreign material fell into one of the vents on top of the unit.  About a week later, my wife was using the unit to heat up some frozen waffles.  Smoke and flames were visible from the right side of the unit.  It was immediately unplugged and the flames were blown out.  I opened the case and discovered the fire was an electrical fire.  The main power lead enters the unit and is clamped to several smaller diameter wires.  One of these connections overheated and caught the plastic insulating cover over it on fire.  The main power lead was against the side of the metal case, so had the plastic totally melted away, it was possible the case of the unit could have become energized.

I contacted the manufacturer after my first toaster oven failed and they asked me to send them the end of the power cord and they sent me a new toaster oven, which is the one that I have now.  I am submitting this report to bring awareness to the problem associated with this product.
