manufacturer: WOLFGANG PUCK PRODUCTIONS, INC ( W.P. Productions Inc)
incidentDescription: Blender began to smoke and sparks came out from the bottom of the blender.

productDescription: Faberwear 8 cup electric coffee pot,
manufacturer: Applica Consumer Products, Inc. - NOTIFY SPECTRUM BRANDS
incidentDescription:
I have a 8 cup Faberwear electric coffee pot.  It is about 2 years old.  While cleaning it the handle fell off.  I don't understand how the handle was attached to the pot.  There is no hole where a screw goes into the body of the stainless steel pot.  The handle has a indent in which there is a screw that goes into a small plate, but the plate nor screw goes into the body of the pot.

I feel very fortunate that this happened while I was cleaning the pot and not when I was pouring a hot cup of coffee.

This is unbelievable to me...but then again not, after all it is made in China.

productDescription: 2 Electric Oil-Filled Heaters
incidentDescription: Really this is two reports in one. I bought two Honeywell Oil Filled electric Heaters model HZ-709-WM from WalMart in 2009. I gave one to my mother and kept one. The one I kept smoked and the venthole in front melted so I quit using it. My mother reported hers smoked with electrical smell and became afraid to use it. I contacted Honeywell and they are planning to replace them with them with identical units. I think I would rather have the $72.73 each I paid for them, but that was not offered.

productDescription: Magic Bullet Blender
incidentDescription: On October 19th in the evening I was using the Magic Bullet to make my daughter some baby food.  I have used this blender many times (10-15) in the past month as she just started eating table food.  I cut up sweet potatoes into small squares and put in two tablespoons of water along with the sweet potatoes into the tall cup.  I attached the steamer lid and placed it in the microwave for three minutes.  When the timer went off I removed the lid stirred up the potatoes then place the cross blade onto the cup.  I then placed them on the base and blended the potatoes.  I noticed they needed some more water to get the right consistency so I removed the cup from the base.  I banged the cup on the counter to get the sweet potatoes to slide down the cup so I wouldn't make a mess when I opened the lid.  I started to unscrew the cross blade attachment and it was giving me a hard time and all of a sudden as I unscrewed the contents exploded in a six-feet radius around my kitchen and on myself.  My husband came in to see what happened and I started to feel my skin burning.  He rushed me to the sink to run cold water on my skin.  It felt like my skin was falling off the burn was so intense.  We read online what to do for a burn so we covered my arm with loose gauze.  I woke up the next day (today) and I have an appointment to see the doctor to find out what else we can do.  I have two burn marks on my left wrist and hand.  One on the top of my hand just below the thumb the size of a quarter, red with white bumps in the middle.  One on my wrist the size of a dime and deep red.  Both of them are extremely tender and feel like large bruises.  My hand is also stiff.

productDescription:
(I purchased the items from http://www.rcplanet.com, so the code numbers are theirs.)

Battery: Align 6S1P 22.2V 2600mAh/25C/B AGNKX870008A

Charger: Align Intelligent Balance Charger RCC-6CX AGNKX850162A
incidentDescription: The incident involved a battery and charger manufactured by ALIGN Corp.,Ltd. The battery is for a radio-controlled helicopter. It is a 22.2v 2600mAh battery that connects to the charger via an interface board. When I connected the battery to the interface board (incorrectly, as it happens, but not illogically) the wiring immediately burst into flames at least 3 inches high. I burned a finger, but was fortunate to avoid more serious consequences.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: Marineland Visi-Therm 150 Watt Aquarium Heater.  Model VTX 150
productType: Heaters or Heating Systems, Other or Not Specified (393)
incidentDescription: I had a Marineland Visi-Therm 150 watt aquarium heater explode and catch fire.  I heard what sounded like a muffled fire cracker followed by rushing water.  When I ran into my living room I found water leaking out from below my aquarium.  When I opened the cabinet doors I saw the heater had exploded and cracked the compartment of my sump filter where it was located.  As the water rushed out and the heater was exposed to the air it ignited into a brief fire that self extinguished.  Overall I lost about 8 gallons of water onto the floor before I had a chance to shut everything down.  The water seeped through the floor and soaked some insulation, ceiling panels, carpet and drywall.  Had I not been home or if the heater was placed directly in the tank things could have been a lot worse.  I have a second Visi-Therm 100w that I have stopped using.  These are a dangerous product.  Marineland had a recall of a similar heater this year but not for this model.  It took 3 days of trying before I was able to reach someone at the customer service department to notify them of this incident.  I was told in order to file a claim I would need a letter on company letterhead from every vendor I purchased my items from stating replacement value.  Needless to say that will be impossible to get as most of these items were purchased online.  I am sending them the remains of the heater along with pictures and documention to support the replacement costs of the items damaged.  I fully intend to contact my Attorney General's office if they do not honor my claim.

I opened the back and found 2 burned wires that had melted and burned in half. The cord was fine the internal wires were smaller gauge than the heater cord. Could have started a fire but I had it hooked up to a ground fault circuit that tripped.

productDescription: Energizer rechargeable battery, AA.
incidentDescription: A remote control that contained Energizer rechargeable batteries suddenly sputtered and popped. Soon after, it began to leak. A battery had burst and leaked acid.

productDescription: Steam Mop manufactured by Shark and imported by Euro-Pro Operating,LLC.
incidentDescription:
Plugged in the Sharp Steam Pocket Mop Model S 3501 and was waiting for the mop to heat up prior to use. After waiting the minimal 30 second period to heat up and noticing steam was not being generated yet, allowed the unit to continue to heat. The time sequence was less than 3minutes when the unit suddenly popped and expelled hot steam from both sides of the water tank. Apparently there is no auto shut off trip mechanism if the unit overheats or builds up too much steam pressure. 

Fortunately there were no injuries but the potential for serious burns was present. 
This is the second unit I have owned and they have a tendency to periodically clog up but in the past the unit basically self cleaned itself and steam would flow normally into the steam mop head. This did not occur on 10/15 and as noted, the water tank unit exploded, expelled hot steam from both sides and is no longer functional.

battery pack case manufactured by MiLi model # H1-C10, originally purchased from IGear, approximiatly 2 years ago or so. You plug it in with the phone seated in it and it charges both the phone, and spare battery at the same time.
This morning I got up and unplugged the device, and set it on the kitchen table, as usual.  after about 10 minutes it went off like a roman candle, spewing sparks, and caught fire.  I flung it off the table, and luckily the IPhone disconnected, not damaging the phone.  The battery pack is a melted glob of plastic !

Luckily I was up at the time, and not driving or carrying it on my person !


Extreme fire hazard !!!!!

I can send pics if needed, and do still have the burned up mess !

productDescription: dehumidifier's
incidentDescription:
The consumer indicated that he had the dehumidifier plugged into the wall outlet on a low setting in a basement for estimating twelve hours when approximately  1 a.m. on 9/12/2011 the fire alarm went off alerting the consumer there was a fire in the home. 

After waking his wife he noticed that smoke was pouring from the basement door. He powered on the light to the basement and went down stairs where he noticed that thick black smoke was billowing from the from the front of the dehumidifier.

The consumer unplugged the plug from the wall outlet and while doing so it tripped the breaker. He noticed a orange glow so he grabbed the 
Dehumidifier by the handle and bean to take it outside .

While in going through the kitchen area to go outside the flame inside of the dehumidifier  and blew out approximately 5 feet high in the area. The consumer quickly grabbed a bowl of water from the kitchen sink and put the fire out. No proper authorities were contacted. 

The dehumidifier is placed outside of the home near the garage. While doing some research online he noticed there was a recall (see Release #11-088) and his model number was affected. The consumer went into the retailer on 9/11/2011 and the representative that he spoke with (name was not provided) advised the consumer to contact the firm for further assistance.

The representative then decided that he would honor a refund for the consumer. The consumer advised the representative that he did not want to accept the refund and instead took the dehumidifier back home.

The basement is full of smoke damage and has a strong plastic burning odor. The consumer indicated that he would contact the firm and that he may also contact his home owners insurance.

incidentDescription: We put water in the reservoir, started the brew, switched to steam the milk, but then when we switched back to brew, the filter holder and filter exploded off the coffee maker.  It shattered the carafe and sprayed hot water and grounds across our kitchen.  The filter holder was on tight so we do not know how it could have exploded off the coffee maker.

9/24/11 Consumer contacted the retailer and was advised that the toaster had not been recalled so he should report it to the Agency.

Consumer feels that this toaster is a fire hazard and should be reported.

productDescription: TABLE TOP CONVECTION OVEN
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
HAMILTON BEACH TABLE TOPP OVEN, TYPE 027, MODEL NO. 31197R, SERIES A2890BW. WHEN IN USE, THE HARD WIRED ELECTRIC CORD GETS SO HOT YOU CANNOT TOUCH IT. YOU HAVE TO WAIT UNTIL THE OVEN IS TURNED OFF AND COOLS DOWN. I CALLED HAMILTON BEACH CUSTOMER SERVICE (1-800-851-8900) AND WAS TOLD THERE IS NO RECALL ON THIS UNIT BECAUSE OF A FAULTY CORD, BUT THE CUSTOMER SERVICE REP WAS KIND ENOUGH TO OFFER TO SEND ME A MAILING LABEL TO RETURN THE OVEN AND THAT THEY WOULD EVALUATE IT AND SEND ME A NEW UNIT. I EXPLAINED THAT IT WASN'T THE OVEN THAT WAS FAULTY, ONLY THE ELECTRIC CORD. AND THAT MOST LIKELY THE CORD HAD ONLY THE MINIMUM SIZE WIRE AND THAT'S WHY IT GETS SO HOT. IT CANNOT HANDLE THE 1500 WATTS. THE CUSTOMER SERVICE REP SAID THEY JUST DON'T CHANGE THE CORD. I INDICATED THAT IF THEY JUST SEND ME ANOTHER TABLE TOP OVEN, IT WOULD HAVE THE SAME TYPE ELECTRIC CORD, CORRECT? THE REP SAID, "YES".

AGAIN, THE PRODUCT IS GOOD, BUT THE ELECTRIC CORD IS BAD. SO BAD THAT IF LEFT PLUGGED INTO THE ELECTRIC OUTLET, IT COULD VERY WELL CAUSE A FIRE. HAMILTON BEACH'S ANSWER TO SIMPLY EXCHANGE THE OVEN, WHICH HAS THE SAME TYPE ELECTRIC CORD, IS NOT PRODUCT SAFETY OR THE ANSWER TO THIS DANGEROUS PROBLEM.

productDescription: DeLonghi D895UX Cool-Touch ROTO Electric 1-1/2-Pound-Capacity Food Fryer
incidentDescription:
I own the Delonghi D895UX Deep Fryer as seen here:
http://www.amazon.com/DeLonghi-D895UX-Cool-Touch-Electric-2-Pound-Capacity/dp/B00004RGAW

This unit has a rubber drain hose that during normal operation is bent 90degrees upwards with a stopper in the end to keep oil from draining.  I have owned the unit approximately 5 years with minimal usage.  By design the rubber tube is bent, and at that bend the rubber tube has now cracked right at the bend.  I luckily noticed this when draining unit. But I am not sure when the crack started.  The problem that could easily occur is that while using the unit at temperatures up to 370 degrees F. the oil could start leaking out the bottom front onto ones counter top, floor... and on a person who tries to stop the flood of burning oil.  I can't imagine someones response to try and mitigate the leak would cause.
I contacted the company, they said that part was not allowed for consumer repair, and I would have to send the unit to them for repair at 100% my cost.  I told them that I believed this was a design flaw and a serious hazard, they did not offer to fix at their expense, stating that the warranty was over.
I believe this should be considered for a recall due to high potential for burn/fire hazard.  If you search about this fryer and leaking, it does bring up other reviews about this problem.

productDescription: Slow cooker style crock pot
incidentDescription:
We have a Cooks brand slow cooker model SC-702 purchased at [REDACTED] in Clearwater, Florida about a year ago.  The glass lid has a plastic handle attached to the top middle of the lid.  The plastic handle totally shattered into several pieces in my wife's hand while removing the lid from the hot pot. The lid fell to the kitchen floor and thankfully landed on a fatigue mat and did not break.  I searched the internet for a replacement handle and discovered that there are many accounts of this handle breaking in addition to the side handles breaking.  
We used this product according to manual directions and probably cooked a meal less than a dozen times.

productDescription: The product is an Aloha Breeze ceiling fan with a single glass light kit.  Their are 6 fan blades. 3 speeds with reverse operation. 25 year limited warranty. It is made by Aloha Housewares, Inc. Arlington, Texas
productType: Electric Chandeliers or Other Attached Light Fixtures (628)
incidentDescription: We purchased 2 of these fans for use in a small space.  The fan blades are primary colors on one side and pastels on the other.  My daughter spray painted the blades white.  She installed one of the fans in my galley kitchen and the other in a reading nook I have in my living room.  They were installed on Saturday, October 8, 2011.  They both worked fine.  In the middle of the night last night, October 12, 2011, I heard a crash in my kitchen.  When I got up to investigate I noticed white glass on the floor. When I looked around to see where it came from I saw that the glass globe of the ceilng fan had basically exploded.  Neither the fan nor the light were on at that time.

productDescription: electric coffeepot (superfast)
manufacturer: Applica Consumer Products, Inc. - NOTIFY SPECTRUM BRANDS
incidentDescription: Since Farberware changed their electric coffeepots to a 3 prong plug, it continuously pops my GFI breaker. I have exchanged the pots in the store 3 times and the manufacturer has sent me a new pot. I have had my GFI switch changed and it still happens. I bought a different brand of electric coffeepot, also with a 3 prong plug and it works fine. This has been going on over a year. I have given up on Farberware but I feel this is a serious defect and should be reported. My electrician says it is a problem with the coffeepot. I purchased the pots origionally at Bed Bath and Beyond and the manager there said they are getting alot of returns.

productDescription: Hoover U6485-900 Windtunnel Anniversary Self-Propelled Bagged Upright Vacuum Cleaner
model: Hoover U6485900 Windtunnel Anniversary Self-Propelled Bagged
incidentDescription: This is not a single incident, so there's really not a date attached to it.  Relatives have purchased a Hoover "Windtunnel Anniversary Self-Propelled Bagged Upright Vacuum Cleaner", model #U6485900.  I have been around when it has been used.  Having previously owned a number of brands of vacuums, including very powerful, modern units (e.g. Dyson), and various Shop-Vac and similar industrial models, I am shocked at the noise level near this unit while it is running.  It does not sound like there is something wrong with it, so I would presume that this is the normal noise level for this product, not a faulty unit.  I will say from experience that the noise level is comparable to, for example, an electric angle grinder, which requires use of hearing protection apparatus.  There is absolutely no way that this is a safe noise level for anything more than momentary exposure.  Perhaps there needs to be more strict monitoring and regulation of noise levels from home appliances, including vacuums, blenders, and other potentially-offending devices.

productDescription: The Shark Steam Mop is an electric powered mop.  Water in the reservoir gets heated when the unit is plugged in.  The motion of mopping back and forth is supposed to generate the steam, which is expelled through a microfiber fabric-covered detachable plastic mop head.  The steam heat and moisture are supposed to clean and sanitize hard surface floors.
incidentDescription:
While using my Shark Steam Mop S3501 yesterday, it worked normally for about 1 minute.  Then it ceased producing steam through the mop head.  I pumped the handle in an attempt to get it back to normal.  The mop head was cool to the touch (not hot as is normal when the unit is on), but the unit was plugged in, the power light was on, and the water tank full.  I unplugged it and went to eject the mop head to troubleshoot, but when I pressed the eject button, the attachment explosively shot off and steam started blasting from the bottom of the unit.  My fingers got slight steam burns, but if a person or pet had been standing in front of me and the mop, they would have been seriously burned.

We were able to replicate this scenario, but the second time, the mop head flew off on its own after just a few seconds, without the release button being pressed, and steam again started shooting everywhere--about a 2 foot long jet of steam.  This mop is seriously hazardous and seem to have some design flaws.  Mine is 8 months old and has been used fewer than a dozen times.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: HP Battery labeled 6A99902BBUJ0XE. Was in a Compaq laptop. Color is black.
incidentDescription: HP Battery labeled 6A99902BBUJ0XE, was feeling warm for a few months prior to incident, which caused me to purchase a cooling fan for the laptop it was being used in. Not too long after that the battery started to get irrationally hot. I could not remove the battery because of the heat. I turned off the laptop, but by the time it had cooled off, the cooling pad had melted and no longer functioned, the hinges for the laptop screen melted, the wires going to the screen may have caught fire (they looked slightly burnt), the fan on the laptop was melted, the couch and pants the laptop had been sitting on were slightly burnt, and the laptop was then rendered useless.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: Oven that is used to cook/bake food over just about any heat source.  It does not generate it's own heat.
incidentDescription: The stove is designed to sit over a heat source and bake/cook food in its interior.  The glass is not oven/heat safe glass.  It is ordinary glass. Received a "Style Elements" Hairdryer model # DW778, 125V-60Hz, 1875w manufactured by Yuyao Dewei Electric Appliance & Motor Company, China. It was purchased from a Big Lots store located in Garner NC in late August 2011.

incidentDescription: I purchased a Master Forge stainless steel portable gas grill from Lowes. The model # is GR4039-014247. Item # 0184640. There is excessive "blow back" when you attach and unattach a pound bottle of propane from the regulator. I was using the grill and the regulator froze and the burner all but went out. I turned the burner off and unscrewed the propane bottle. Unfortunately the flame was not quite extinguished when I unscrewed the bottle and the "blow back" ignighted in a very large ball of fire. My hair, eye brows and eye lashes got very singed as well as a vest I was wearing. I also got slightly burned on my arm. There are many reviews on Lowe's site about regulator problems with this grill, mostly concerning the regulator freezing when a one pound bottle is used. It seems to work OK with the adapter hose and the 20# tank. I tried twice to submit a review to Lowe's about this problem and was rejected both times.

productDescription: Helen of Troy Pro 1" Tangle Hot Air Brush

productDescription: Weber Spirit Gas Grill Model #310, serial # DE1326331
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
Weber Gas Grill model#310, serial number DE1326331.

Purchased at Home Depot, May 2010.  

On Tuesday, October 4th at approximately 5:10pm, the #2 control interface on the grill caught fire, flames shooting up out of the control interface and melting the knob.  Owner immediately shut off gas, threw baking soda on control pad and put fire out.  Called Wadsworth City Fire Department at approximately 5:20pm.  Chief [REDACTED] of the Wadsworth City Fire department inspected the grill.  His opinion at the time was a failure of the regulator connected to the control interface.  He may be reached at [REDACTED].

Called Weber Grill Company at approximately 6:30pm to report incident.  Weber representative attempted to indicate it was the fault of owner for not removing burners and running wire coat hanger through them.  Advised them we would file report with CPSC and Consumer Reports.

productDescription: Dehumidifiers
model: 580.54701400 (# on parts manual) # ownrs manual is 580.54701
incidentDescription:
Consumer said that he was upstairs two floor from the basement when he felt a strong burning odor.  Consumer rushed to the basement and found out that his dehumidifier was hot at touch.  Consumer was unable to turn off.  

Consumer unplugged the dehumidifier from the electric out.  Consumer did not had the product he disposal.

Consumer feels that his dehumidifier could pose a fire hazard, he also said if he wouldn’t be at home it would caught on fire.

09/10/2011 Consumer e-mailed and explained incident to mfr.  He hasn't here from mfr yet.

No Injury.

Further clarification of incident: Sears Kenmore Dehumidifier Model # 580.54701, (this is the model number given in the User's Manual. The number provided in the Parts Manual is 580.54701400). Dehumidifier is a 70 pint capacity model that can be used in cool temperatures. I owned the unit for approximately 7 years, setting it to cycle on and off every 3 hours during the warmer months. It was located in the basement with a hose attached that drained into a sump pump. Humidity setting was usually at 40%. Quite suddenly one evening, I began to smell something burning. I was on the second floor. Eventually traced problem to the dehumidifier which was extremely hot to the touch and emitting a strong, acrid smell. Unit was clearly turned "On"; the switches were illuminated but it was not running. Perhaps dehumidifier was in between cycles. I noticed small amount of water, perhaps condensation, on the upper part of the front grill. I immediately unplugged unit and when it cooled, threw it away. Unfortunately, it didn't occur to me to save my dehumidifier for future examination. I believe I caught this incident at the very beginning. Had I gone to bed or left the premises I have no doubt a fire would have ensued. I notified Sears Customer Service weeks ago but have not heard from them.

productDescription:

on first time of use, the new humidifier set off fire alarm waking two adults from sleep. after silencing the alarm and looking for the source, discovered the humidifier had produced smokey-appearing particulate haze in the bedroom. the hazy material in the air caused a feeling of raspy throat and bitter taste in one adult and mild asthma reaction in another adult.

inspecting the humidifier after the incident, there was a brownish discoloration to the water collected in the ultrasonic base unit and demineralization cartridge and some foreign material on the outside of the unit.  the foreign material on the outside of the unit had been noticed when the unit was un-boxed.

this humidifier was filled with clear tap water prior to its operation on this occassion, as well as another model humidifer in a second bedroom which operated without incident.

previously, Vicks brand humidifers as well as other brands have been operated in this same bedroom location for several years without incident

Vicks Model V5100N (on unit) or V5100JUV (on box), 1.5 gal capacity
Mfg by Kaz, Inc
Purchased at Drug Mart, Independence, OH on October 2, 2011
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: Krups digital convection toaster oven, model FBC412.
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
Krups FBC 412, Ref 575.04 digital convection toaster oven purchased in December 2008 for regular household use has a small wire in the rear of the unit that shorted out, causing the heating elements to fail.  The unit was approximately 12 minutes into the convection baking cycle, with temperature set 400 degrees F when a flame and sparks shot out from the rear vent.  The unit continued to run (convection fan and timer) however, the heating elements were not working.  No further sparks or flame developed.  The failed heating elements and burned wire were not readily evident since the unit continued to run, even when turned off and turned back on.  I'm concerned if the defect had gone undetected a fire could have resulted. 

I researched product recalls and did not find any.  The unit has always been used according to manufacturer instructions.

productDescription: Conair IONSHINE hair dryer - dark blue with silver letters that say CONAIR IONSHINE 1875 on the side of the dryer; black cord
incidentDescription:
I was drying my hair with my Conair IONSHINE  hairdryer when suddenly a bright blue-white flame about 4"-5" long shot noisily out of the place where the cord met the plug. It burned for a few seconds, and then the cord fell off the plug, at which time the flames stopped. I unplugged the plug from the socket. It looks like the cord melted at the attachment point. Black residue is all around the wall outlet and on the sink below.

I called the Conair Hotline, but they said they couldn't do anything because the dryer, based on model and serial number, is out of warranty. The warranty is for two years, but I only bought it 10 or so months ago. I was told that unless I had my receipt, (I do not), they couldn't help me. 

I can understand not replacing it if the motor died or no longer blew hot air. I know hair dryers don't last forever. But this is a safety issue, and I think they should replace it for me, although I'm not really sure I want another one of their products now.

Yesterday, about 10 minutes after starting the brew cycle, I heard a strange noise coming from the coffee maker, a bubbling, gurgling, hissing sound (which I later found out was due the coffee in the pot boiling and the hot plate burning). I checked the coffeemaker and saw smoke coming out from the hot plate. I removed the carafe and found the front half of the hot plate bright red. I immediately unplugged the coffee maker. Smoke continued to come out from around the hot plate along with a burning plastic smell. There was no damage to my countertop or any other surrounding appliances or the outlet. However, I feel if I had not been in the immediate vicinity this would not have been the case and quite likely could have led to a kitchen fire.
I called Cuisinart. They offered a replacement which I obviously didn't want. They refused to give me a refund.

productDescription: White 26 cu. side by side Frigidaire Refrigerator with ice maker. Ice and water in the door.
incidentDescription: Frigidaire Side by side refrigerator model FRS6LR5EW6, serial number 4A70605549. Saturday, October 1, 2011, my husband started smelling something like electric burning or hot wires. After several hours we narrowed it down to the kitchen. We started checking first with the light fixture because it was put in last week.Then we checked the microwave and stove which is electric. We checked the attic. Finally we decided it was the small freezer of my mother in laws. We disconnected and emptied the small freezer. We went to bed. After about an hour I started coughing as I have lung issues.  I came into the kitchen area and the smell was strong.  So I sat down and watched the kitchen in the dark and within 5 minutes, I heard the refrigerator cycle on and a small light appeared... then it dimmed and came back very strong.  It appeared on the wall and floor as if it was a flame. The freezer was thawing towards the back of the freezer area.  We lost approximately $200 in food. The refrigerator was purchased at Lowe's in Tulsa, OK, on or after August 2007. I believe it was in the spring of 2008.  I have reported it to Frigidaire. And was told to contact their recall center at 888-360-8556.

incidentDescription:
I have a Lasko Ceramic Air Heat Model 5536 (9212) and the cord heats up when it is plugged in and running.  

I used it for a while lthe winter of 2009-2010 without incident.  

However, last winter 2010it blew a circuit; so I unplugged it and didn't use it again.  I attributed that to too many things on same circuit.  

Today, I plugged in and the cord heated up at the outlet and and up to the appliance itself.  I didn't want to start a fire, so I unplugged it and don't plan to use it again.  

I checked recalls for this model but there wasn't one on your website.  I'll do more internet investigation but I thought I should alert CPSC about the possibility of this model starting a fire.

incidentDescription:
My battery for my 2008 15 inch MacBook Pro has expanded to the point of being a hazard. It has completely separated from the casing while in my lap top computer. I went to use it for homework and the battery had separated, exposing the insides and sharp edges. Prior to this, it was working fine and holding a normal charge. The small packet inside have expanded and look like it will explode and leak at any moment. 

I contacted Apple support and at first they said the battery was a hazard and they would take care of it. Then a supervisor got on the phone and told me that since my computer was 3 years old, it was normal. It was time for a new battery. I explained to the supervisor that my battery held a charge just fine prior to the sudden expansion. He said he was sorry and that it was normal.

productDescription: Gas grill (4 burners and 4 knobs)
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
The consumer stated that her gas grill, that is connected to her outdoor gas line, caught fire. The gas line comes out of her basement and her grill is sitting directly next to her home. The grill was on for about 20 minutes to 35 minutes. 

The grill was set to high at the time of the fire. The consumer's son in law was observing the grill and saw that there were flames coming out of the front door of the grill. The consumer's son in law tried to power of the grill by shutting off the knobs but that did not work. Her son in law shut off the gas line to the grill, which shut off the flames. The grill shows no signs of structural damage.
 
 The consumer home has not been damaged by the product. The consumer did not call the fire department after the incident. The consumer reported no injuries or smoke inhalation from anyone present. The consumer emailed the firm August 1st and explained that the grill caught fire. The consumer got a response August second, with the firm stating they had opened a case. 

On August 9th the consumer called the firm and told that the fire was caused by burner blockage of the grill. The consumer felt that none of this was relevant to her issue. Also on August 9th the firm told her that she should send them pictures via email.
 
 On the same date, the firm told her that she must take the burners apart which may have resulted in the fire. The firm told her that the burners must be cleaned every two to three times of usage. The consumer looked at the manual and read that this should only be done as a trouble shooting method if the flame wont ignite.

 The consumer asked for a written regulation that she needs to take apart the burners in writing. The consumer stated that the firm will not send her that requirement in writing. On August 9th the firm closed the case and have offered no further assistance. They firm did not respond to her last email on the 9th. The consumer has yet to call the retailer.

productDescription: Capresso coffee grinder Model 503
incidentDescription:
Last week, a huge "fire ball" - 3 to 4 inches large shot our of the electrical outlet while I had 2 appliances plugged in:  my coffee maker and my Capresso coffee grinder.  I switched outlets and continued making and grinding coffee.  I taped over the outlet from which the fireball came.

Two days later, I again had both appliances plugged in to another outlet.  The coffee maker was running. The grinder was not running, but it was plugged in.  A huge spark came out of the outlet and hit my jacket.  At that point, I pulled everything out of the outlet and we turned off the breakers.

I called the Scarsdale Fire Dept.  The Fire Dept examined the outlets and breakers and saw nothing unusual.  They questioned whether an applicance may have been at fault.

When the electrician came, he too examined the outlets and wiring.  He said everything was normal.  He thought there may have been an unusual power surge.  When he proceeded to test the 2 applicances:  the coffee maker and the coffee grinder, the grinder did not work in one outlet. He looked at the grinder and thought the plug may have been faulty.  At that point he saw that, at the point wheree the cord connects to the grinder, the rubber had worn away and the wiring was completely exposed.  

The cord is intended to be wrapped into a groove  at
 the base of the grinder and evidently, little by little the rubber wore away exposing the wires.  I think the grinder is about 2-3 years old. The electrician said that there should have been a piece of protective rubber at the point where the cord meets the unit

The Grinder is Capresso Model 503.
I emailed Capressor yesterday and have not received a response yet.
As I could have been seriously burned, or this could have started a fire, I am alerting you.

productDescription: Stainless Steel 3 burner Propane Grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
I have a gas grill--here are the Specifications
Manufacturer:  North American Outdoors (HK) Limited purchased at Target 
Purchase Date:  about 3-4 years ago, but did not use until about two years ago--remained in box
SN:  079681
Model #: BB10769A

On September 4, 2011 I lit the grill (all three burners), preheated it, and put all burners on "Low".  I placed six large chicken quarters on the grill and left it for 20 minutes.  When I returned, I noted a small amount smoke and assumed the grease from the chicken skin had caught fire.  When I reached the grill, I noted the temperature gauge was pinned at at the end of the scale--the scale stopped at 800 degrees F.  My first impression was that I had left it on high, but the knobs were all on low.  

I opened the grill and the chicken was charred, and an aluminum serving plate that I was preheating had melted and curled over the edge of the upper warming rack (I checked later and it appears aluminum melts at about 1250 degrees).  I tried to turn off the grill, but the first knob spun freely--apparently melted.  I reached to turn off the gas at the tank, but heat too intense.  I then got a rag to use as a hotpad and turned off the tank.  There was no evidence of a grease fire when I opened the grill, but each of the three burners was burning brightly.

The only explanation I have is that the pressure regulator of the grill failed, causing the extreme overheating.  Had I not intervened I feel sure there would have been a fire and/or explosion.  I received two second degree burns to my right hand, each about 1/2 inch in diameter.  Actually I feel very lucky and blessed that no worse injuries were sustained.

The grill has always been stored indoors.

model: Summer Smart Living Glazed Deco Flame Pot
incidentDescription:
We represent [REDACTED], a 23-year old male.  On June 29, 2011, [REDACTED] was injured with serious burns after the fuel receptacle exploded out of its ceramic pot.  

PLEASE NOTE THAT THIS IS NOT A SITUATION WHERE GEL WAS ADDED TO AN ALREADY BURNING POT.

[REDACTED] and his family had not lit the gel fuel pot that day.  Within about 5 minutes after the fuel pot had been lit (and without warning), a loud “pop” came from the pot and the fuel reservoir exploded into the air and onto the table.  When it landed, the flaming gel spilled along the table towards [REDACTED], and his arm became engulfed in flames.  We believe that the explosion was caused by the concentrated heat in the ceramic pot, which has no holes to circulate air.

The product label identifies the pot as “Summer Smart Living Glazed Deco Flame Pot,” and along with the Summer Smart Living Firepot Fuel Gel, was purchased at Giant - Store #0387, Rt 1 & 270, Lighthouse Plaza, in Rehoboth Beach, Delaware.  Both the Flame Pot and the Fuel Gel are distributed by American Sales Co., which we understand is a subsidiary of Ahold USA, Inc.   We believe that the gel may have been manufactured by Bird Brain, Inc., and perhaps the ceramic pot was also manufactured by Bird Brain.

productDescription: Cuisinart Exact Heat Toaster Oven Broiler  TOB-155 Series
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
On April 2,2011 I bought Toaster Oven Broiler from Sears.com. Unfortunately I didn't open package for another couple months. Sears has 90 days satisfaction warranty. In the end of August I tried to return the product because of safety issue, I burned my fingers twice and my wife three times. Sears refused to take product back, claiming expiration of 90 days, so under normal circumstances I wouldn't  dispute my fault with that. The problem is this product  is health hazard. Now here is the problem: on the front there is a handle that you grab to open up the door, right behind the handle there is a metal strip which is a part  of the door frame, this metal strip is about one inch wide and gets extremely hot, now space between the handle and the strip is about one inch. When you grab the handle you  will touch  this hot metal strip with your fingers (outside part between your knuckles and first joint) and burn yourself painfully. There is no way that normal size person can open that door without hurting itself. Now I went to Home Depot to see other models of toasters and amazingly I found  another model  made by the same company that looks almost identical and on the top that same metal strip there is plastic strip that provides insulation so you won't get burned. 
         I would like to add that during phone call conversation Sears.com was fully inform about this specific safety hazard yet as of today Sept. 6, 2011 it is still available on Sears.com.
         On Aug. 26, 2011 I received email from Sears Customer  Care, signed [REDACTED] that they won't take this product back because of 90 days policy, never mentioned or even thank for bringing  such as serious safety issue up.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription: 12 Cup Digital Coffee maker
incidentDescription:
There is an Error 5 that  displays on the Control Panel in the midst of 6 brewing 6 cups of coffee. To continue to brew the coffee and get rid of the error message she has to either reset the setting on the control panel and or unplug the plug from the wall outlet. 

She discovered how to reset the unit by reading the owner’s manual.
She noticed that the error 5 message would happen intermittently but for the last two weeks (estimating the week of 7/18/2011 it started occurring on a daily basis 

The Teflon coating on the heating plate bubbles up and in some areas on the heating plate the Teflon coating is worn off. The heating plate gets extremely hot to the touch.

 While doing some research n the internet on 7/30/2011 she noticed a recall (see release number 10-238) where she was experiencing the same hazard of the unit over heating but her model number was not included.

 She contacted the retailer on 8/1/2011 and was advised since it was over 30 days she could not return it. She indicated that she will continue to use the product with caution and she did not indicate if she would contact the firm.

productDescription:
Bird Brain Fire-Pot - Egg Shaped top and bottom cut off,

VERY easily tipped. And once it is tipped, continues to roll uncontrollably

Here is an image of the exact product we were using:
http://www.amazon.com/Bird-Brain-Firepot-Sepia-Pearl/dp/B002YQ5V9I/ref=pd_sim_ol_1
incidentDescription:
We bought a firepot and was using it on our table outside on the patio. I was leaning back in my chair and slipped backwards. When I fell backwards my foot caught the corner of the table and lifted the one side. This caused the firepot to roll over and toss fuel onto my fiance's skirt. She stood up startled, and the gel spread the whole way down her leg. She tried Stop Drop and Roll, to no avail, as soon as she would roll back, it would flash back up. Eventually she stood up and I ripped her skirt off piece by piece, burning my knuckles severely and other various parts of my fingers.

By the time we had her skirt ripped off, she was burnt from her hip to her knee all the way around the front/sides of her left leg. We were taken to the ER where she was discovered to have extensive 2nd degree and some 3rd degree burns. I had extensive 2nd degree burns to my hands. 

The worst part is, that the skirt did not have a single singed thread on it, meaning only the fuel caused her burns.

Not only is the Gel unsafe, but they are selling pots that are not designed properly. The one we purchased was the shape of an Egg with the bottom and top cut off. As soon as this thing tips, it wants to spin and roll. 

We have pictures and Hospital records that are available upon request.

productDescription: Sagittarius Gas Grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
The consumer stated that while he was using his gas grill on the deck of his backyard, flames came out of the air vent of the gas valve behind the panel of the grill. The consumer stated that the grill was on for about 15 minutes. The consumer was using 4 burners at the time of the incident and they were set to medium heat. The consumer has not been able to reach the manufacturer as of yet.

 The consumer got in contact with the retailer and was told that he needed to substantiate that he purchased the product from them, even though the product was sold exclusively at their store, before they can assist him. The consumer has not discussed with the retailer what they would be willing to offer. The grill shows signs of burning behind the panel of the grill and the wires behind the panel have melted; the igniter is also burned.

 At the time of the incident the consumer shut off the gas and the flames shut itself off. The grill did not damage the consumer's home. The consumer did not call the fire department at the time of the incident. The consumer that this grill was cited in recall release 10-099 for another hazard, but the consumer felt that this is issue is just as dangerous if not more dangerous than the hazard cited in the recall. The consumer feels that the grill is horribly built.

Consumer stated that the weight of this grill could not be supported by these inadequate wheels.

Consumer stated that if a child had been close by this incident may have caused injuries.

8/18/11 Consumer contacted the manufacturer and was advised that they would send out replacement wheels, he inquired if they had new designed wheels but they would not comment.

Consumer also contacted the retail store and was advise that someone would do a followup.

Consumer feels that this unit is a safety hazard and should be reported.

productDescription: Living Quarters 10" Fire Pot and 32 Oz. bottle of BirdBrain fuel gel
incidentDescription:
On August 1, 2011 [REDACTED] was severely burned when his friend was refilling a Living Quarters fire pot purchased from a Younkers store in Davenport, Iowa with BirdBrain fuel gel.  The flame had gone out and when his friend went to refill the fire pot reservoir. As he was doing so, it shot flames up into the plastic 32 ounce bottle of fuel gel causing it to be blown out of his hand, across the room, straying burning fuel gel around.  Some landed on [REDACTED] chest and quickly moved to his arms and head.  His two friends tried to put the fire out but suffered less severe burns while tearing his burning clothes off and trying to put the fire out.  The burning fuel gel had to eventually be smothered out by a sheet on a nearby couch.  The fuel gel was very difficult to extinguish.
[REDACTED] suffered 2nd and 3rd degree burns to his arms, chest, neck, face and head generally.  It is believed that the fire pot flame was out and that the fuel gel self ignited from the heat of the metal fuel gel reservoir.

productDescription: fuel burner. wave burner
incidentDescription: My partner and I were on our deck with a gel fuel fire pot (sold at bed bath and beyond) between us. the flame was getting very low so I, [REDACTED1], poured some more gel fuel in the candle and it exploded on my partner, [REDACTED2].  This caused a flash explosion and the gel fuel burst out and coagulated on her body.  I told her to drop and roll but it was like when one fire stopped, another would start. I could not get it out for awhile!  She went to the ER and spent the night in the hospital.  She suffered severe second degree burns to 13% of her body, mainly her left thigh.  I have read the NY times article and agree that this is a fairly new product to the market and the dangers and risks are NOT adequately displayed to the consumer.  If i would have known that this is basically an EXPLOSIVE device, we would never have purchased the product.   The product this involves is the exact product described in the NY times article sold at Bed Bath and Beyond.

productDescription:
Cuisinart DCC-1200 coffee maker, plastic housing, glass carafe, burner element, clock and timer for programmed brewing.
120V, 60 Hz, 1025 W
incidentDescription:
I had made coffee in my Cuisinart DCC-1200 electric coffee maker. I had poured myself a cup of coffee and left another couple of cups in the carafe on the coffee maker's heating element.  After some time I heard a strange sound from the direction of the coffee maker, as if something was bubbling.  I looked and saw that the coffee was boiling vigorously.  I ran to the coffee maker to turn it off and unplug it, and as I did so it began to smoke and release a smell as of burning plastic.  The bottom of the coffee maker was extremely hot, and the smoke appeared to be coming from the point where the cord enters the back of the machine.  Fearing that it might still burst into flame even though unplugged (and not wanting my kitchen to be filled with noxious fumes) I took it outside to cool off.

A searh of the internet revealed a number of other recent reports of identical problems with this and related models. See http://www.consumeraffairs.com/homeowners/cuisinart.html (Ignore the first item about a popcorn maker.)

Consumer said that the only way to reach the mfr is online.  Consumer did not have a computer or access to the internet.

productDescription:
Conair Ion Shine 1875
blue and gray color
model: Ion Shine 1875/ 205  125 can't make out the rest.
incidentDescription:
I had been drying my hair and turned the hair dryer off and hung it in the towel rack next to me.  I continued to get ready for the day in the bathroom where the hairdryer was.  I heard a loud "pop" sound in the direction of the hairdryer.  I looked toward the sound to see smoke and flames coming out the handle of my hairdryer.  I quickly unplugged it and carried it by the far end of the cord to outside.  I had this hairdryer for several years. The switch seemed to be touchy or sensitive.  When I would turn the switch on sometimes the hair dryer would not turn on immediately.  
I reported the incident to Conair since it was one of their products.  I was told that since it had been greater than two years since the purchase of the hair dryer they would not replace it.  The person on the phone asked to make sure that I didn't sustain any injury, which I did not.  I told the company representative that it wasn't a free replacement that I was looking for but to protect others who may use the same hair dryer.  I discussed with her my concern that if someone left the product plugged in and then left his or her home the product could catch fire and cause serious damage to someone or his or her home. She said she would pass my concern on to the marketing division.    This was the end of our conversation.  I reported this to the company in July of this year 2011.

The product is a Conair Ion Shine 1875 hair dryer

Sincerely,
[REDACTED]

productDescription: KitchenAid 2qt teakettle, black porcelain model number 51629 new.
incidentDescription:
Purchased a new kitchenaid 2qt teakettle and have found the design to be totally unsafe. The round ball like design causes the heat of a gas range, medium setting to over heat the top handle. The handle gets very hot and the metal logo insert is burning hot. This kettle was heated until boiling, no longer and was too hot to handle. On a very low flame the handle still gets quite hot. I have used quite a lot of teakettles but this is the worse.

 The second and most dangerous part is the poor design of the pour spout. If you pour cold water with this unit it pours well. If you pour boiling hot water, it will not break lip tension and will run down the front of the kettle and onto the counter, or your feet and floor. There is no way this unit has been safety tested.

This was item #51629

productDescription: Floor Stand Fan
model: Galaxy Floor Stand Fan Type 16-1P, Style PCO 2586
incidentDescription:
Subject: serious design problem

I am a mechanical design engineer and want to make you aware of a serious problem with the design of your Galaxy Floor Stand Fan Type 16-1P, Style PCO 2586.
My wife was lowering the motor fan head and lost her grip on the upper metal post which resulted in the top section slamming down on her hand pinching it severely. There was much bleeding and pain and she had to go to the emergency room at her doctors advice to check to see if she needed stitches and to ascertain if there was any other damage to her hand. They treated her and advised her that her hand was blistered and cut but no other damage was indicated. She also required a Tetanus shot. She now has it bandaged. The charge to us was her $75 deductible Emergency Room co-pay which was more than double the price we paid for your fan.
As a side note, I have also been pinched by this fan in the past as I lowered it gently but did not sustain any injury.
This design flaw could be easily corrected if the tapered releasing collar had a flared collar to protect ones hand. Many other pole mounted products have this safety feature such as Beach Umbrellas.
I have attached a photo of the damage to her hand and a photo showing your fan pinch point problem along with a photo of a typical beach umbrella flared collar.
We now worry that a small child could reach up and twist the release handle. Since their hand is much smaller it potentially could slam down, smash and/or break their fingers and not just damage the soft tissue of their hand.
Please consider recalling this product and reimburse anyone that was injured by it.
I am copying this e-mail to the Consumer Product Safety Commission so they have a record of it.

Thank You

productDescription: propane gas grill
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
Over this past weekend, I experienced a flash grease fire while grilling on my Weber Genesis Grill.  I am wondering if there has been a recall on this particular grill.  I am concerned as it appears there are several dangerous design flaws.  The design of the drip tray allows for food scraps to fall into the drip tray and over time grease collects on the food scraps rather than running down the drip tray to the left side aluminum drip pan as intended.  While grilling, grease dripped down onto the burners, catching fire, and transferring that fire to the drip tray.  In an instant the tray was on fire, and it was so intense I had to back away from the grill before I could remove the food on the grill.  The food on the grill fed the flames, which at this point was so hot inside the lower cabinet that it melted the plastic grommets around the door handles.  Toxic plastic fumes billowed from the grill.  This fire was right next to the propane tank, which you will see in the attached photos got hot enough to blacken the tank.  It was by the grace of God that the tank did not explode.  
 
I am not an engineer, however I have been grilling for many years.  Several things stand out to me.  First, the grease tray appears to be too close to the burners.  The grease tray itself should pitch to the center of the tray, not the side.  This would create a shorter distance for grease to travel to reach the aluminum grease pan. The doors should not have plastic components within close proximity to the heat source.  Being an enclosed space below the grill allows for heat build-up in a flash fire, creating a risk of exploding the propane tank.  
 
This is my four gas grill, and first grease fire.  I have had one other Weber grill, an [REDACTED] grill, and others.  I purposefully selected this grill after reading reviews and receiving personal recommendations of Weber Genesis users.  It was purchased for me as a Christmas gift this year.  I recognize now that the grease tray should be cleaned frequently, however, I never regularly cleaned the grease tray on past grills, and I suspect that most people are like me and do not clean the grease tray frequently.  
 
My concern is that someone will be seriously injured or could die from a propane explosion if they experience what I experienced this weekend

manufacturer: Sunbeam Products, Inc. d/b/a  Jarden Consumer Solutions
incidentDescription:
The Rival model SCR509 slow cooker (aka "Crock Pot") was filled with spaghetti sauce which had been cooking on the "high" heat setting for about four hours, and had reached full temperature.

Upon lifting the lid to stir the contents, the handle in the center of the lid separated from the lid without warning causing the lid, which was being held in one hand above the cooker, to fall uncontrollably down onto the top of the cooker and into the hot spaghetti sauce. This caused the hot oily liquid to splash across the surrounding area and onto my uncovered forearm and clothing. The lid then continued to fall from the top of the cooker and fell into the adjacent sink. It could not be stopped because it was too hot to touch with bare hands and covered with hot liquid.

Hot spaghetti sauce landing on my forearm caused first degree burns with blistering on the inside of the right forearm about three inches below the elbow, and minor burns on my chest where the hot liquid splashed onto my shirt. The glass lid sustained a dent to the metal rim with no obvious glass breakage. 

The cooker was immediately unplugged, and the food being prepared was disposed of after it cooled to room temperature because I could not determine with certainty that none of the broken plastic from the lid handle or any other parts had fallen into the food.

The lid handle is made of plastic which appears to have become brittle allowing a metal nut which is embedded in the plastic to separate from the handle. A metal machine screw fits through a hole in the center of the glass lid and into the metal nut and holds the handle and lid together.

My husband and 3 year old daughter were also on the bed and a few feet away.  In addition to the 40 lb falling weight glass shattered everywhere.

They thread with the ceiling mount but there is too much play in them so that they can be moved laterally when screwed in.  The failure mode is that because the bolts were slightly too small, they were able to vibrate loose over time.

productDescription: MacBook Rechargeable Battery (Designed by Apple in California, Assembled in China) Model Number A1280; Serial Number 6N841U7413CB
incidentDescription:
I have a MacBook laptop, which I purchased in early 2009. The laptop last year started to bulge a bit at its battery cover. Since it is a metal case, I thought that I had bent the bottom of the laptop when picking it up. However, two weeks ago, I noticed the bulge had grown quite a lot and my trackpad (mouse) would not click. So, I removed the MacBook Rechargeable Battery (model number A1280) and found that it had swollen substantially. When I replaced the cover without the battery, the laptop was working perfectly.

The laptop and battery are out of warranty because of age. However, the battery still holds a charge of a number of hours, and it has only reached around 270 cycles, which is less than the 300 cycle life. The swelling seems to be a manufacturing defect, as the battery still works. 

So, I took the battery and laptop to an Apple Store (in SoHo, Manhattan, New York). The specialist looked at it and said the battery had outlived its useful life and I would have to pay a hundred dollars to replace it. When I protested that the battery was within its cycle life and still held a charge, the lady told me that rechargeable batteries swell, indicating their life is over. I protested again, she insisted I buy a new battery so I can use the laptop without being plugged into a wall. I again refused, and she gave me the battery back. Of course, I am not using a potentially dangerous, swollen battery.

My battery's information: Serial Number 6N841U7413CB; Model Number A1280

I researched the problem, and have found numerous other complaints about the battery swelling, with different results. Mine is simply swollen. Some swell until they break open, exposing the individual cells. Others overheat.

http://www.cultofmac.com/apple-service-rep-swollen-macbook-battery-“normal”/77201

In June 2011, I contacted LG to tell them of the following issue:  after using the sweeper for ~5-10 minutes, the retractable cord begins to retract baack into the machine.  Eventually, I have to pull it back out and find that the cord has gotten so hot that it nearly burns my fingers.  The sweeper was sent in for repair and promptly returned to me with the note that they couldn't verify my complaint.  After verifying myself that it does indeed happen, another call was placed to LG.  Again, it was sent back for service.  Again, it was sent back with the attachment fixed (one of several things wrong with this machine) but the cord still not fixed.  This overheating cord is obviously a sign of something wrong, and I believe a serious safety issue due to the heat of if when it is pulled back out.

productDescription: Birdbrain brand, ceramic gel firepot. Blue ceramic with a lid. 7.48x7.48x11.81 inches. Firepot Gel brand is poured in to a removable, metal cylinder inside the pot and lights on fire with the firepot brand gel
model: Birdbrain Bee Hive hand-glazed ceramic firepot
incidentDescription: We lit a "birdbrain" brand ceramic gel firepot within 15 minutes without being disturbed or tampered with the gel from the pot exploded and landed on my husband the chair he was sitting on and a wicker planter. My husband caught on fire for several seconds rolling on the ground screaming trying to snuff out the fire. It went out but he ended up with 2nd degree burns on the entire back of his left hand and the back of his right leg, approximately  20 inches in length. The cushion of the chair he was sitting on was engolfed in flames along with a wicker planter.

productDescription: Back To Basics 2-Slice Egg & Muffin Toaster, Model # TEM-500.  Black.
incidentDescription: I was getting ready for bed around 9:30pm when I heard a loud noise in the kitchen.  It sounded like static coming from a radio.  I went into the kitchen and instantly smelled a strong electrical burning smell.  I walked around the kitchen and determined it was coming from the egg poacher on my Back To Basics Egg & Muffin 2-Slice Toaster, Model # TEM-500.  I unplugged it immediately and went to pick it up to move it, but the front portion (the egg poacher) was too hot to touch. It was still hot a 1/2 hour later.  I waited another hour and it had cooled off enough for me to remove it from the house.  It's important to note that the elapsed time from when noise started to when I unplugged it was under two minutes, so it heated up extremely fast. It was obvious that it would've started a fire if I had not been home to unplug it right away.  I did contact Back to Basics and report the issue and they told me the device is not meant to be left plugged in and that they have not heard other reports of this problem, however, I googled the issue and was able to find other complaints about the toaster either catching fire, or having a strong odor, loud noise and smoke.  Some of those complaints can be found here:  http://www.fixya.com/support/t2516135-paula_deen_toaster_egg_poacher_caught  They go all the way back to July of 2009.  One of those complaints listed this website as the official goverment product reporting system, so that is how I came about reporting the issue.  Back To Basics has asked me to send them the toaster back (they said they will email me a shipping label, which they have not done yet) and they will send me a new one, but I don't want to send it back if you need it for testing and I don't necessarily want to use the new one if this is a common problem, as it does not seem like an isolated incident according to other web complaints.  I have two dogs at home and I would hate to think what could have happened if I had not been home when this happened.

productDescription: Juicer extractor.  White plastic housing with clear top and side windows.  Made in China on the bottom.   The box says Aroma 1996.
incidentDescription:
( I filed this report originally on 3/31/2011, but I don't believe it was fully processed).  On 2/27/2011, I was using the Aroma ACJ-250 juicer extractor when it exploded with a "boom".  The light fixture above my head was shattered and fell onto me.  Sharp plastic and shredded metal shrapnel shot out in all directions, traveling 20 feet  to my left and 15 feet to my right.  The walls of the rooms were what contained the debris from traveling further.  My left hand was lacerated and my chest bruised from the force of the explosion.  Fruit juice and skin from my juicing efforts splattered and stained the ceiling, walls, cabinets, floor, my face clothing, body, everything I had on the counter and the rug in the adjoining room.  Basically, the entire kitchen was a stained mess.  It was a very traumatic event which stays with me.  I am SO fortunate my face wasn't over the juicer and that I did not lose an eye or sustain life threatening injuries.  I am relieved that my 10 year old son, who was helping me juice prior to the event had left the room and that no one else in our household or our pets got in the line of the trajectory pieces of shrapnel.  I found pieces of shrapnel for weeks after cleaning up on that day.  This was no way for me to have started my birthday.  My present in this is that I didn't get more seriously injured, but the "what ifs" haunt me.

My husband looked on line and found out this product had been recalled many years back, though that message did not reach me.  Since then, I learned that the company had no notification in service to alert consumers.  I have called Aroma housewares 5 times and left detailed messages with their legal department to discuss what happened to me, but they have never returned the call.
victimSeverity: Injury, First Aid Received by Non-Medical Professional

productDescription:
Ryobi Cordless Drill -  

HP 1802M
incidentDescription: Drill overheated while in use.  The trigger became hot and the drill lost its variable speed feature and worked only as a single speed.  I used the drill once in a while for a year after the incident and no longer used it after learning about the recall last week.

incidentDescription: Cuisinart coffee maker caught on fire. Smoke billows, burning smell. Very dangerous. Many many other consumers on the Internet are reporting the same thing.

productDescription: Logitech NTA2340 Remote Control Battery used in many of their remote controls.
incidentDescription:
My second NTA2340 battery has just started showing signs of not holding a charge and is slightly swollen. I have already had one Harmony One replaced because the battery swelled so much that it would not come out. After the replacement came, with basically nothing to lose, I put some "extra" effort into removing the first battery and now have it sitting on my desk. It has swollen to twice the thickness and the case is cracking. Now the battery in the replacement is doing the same thing. But this one I was able to get it out before it got stuck. I just sent a support eMail and we'll have to see what they say. I read in the forums that keeping in the charger can do this. Am I wrong to think that is "wrong"? I remember years ago Li-ion laptop batteries doing the same thing and the computer company had to recall them all.

This is a very bad situation. With all the reports of this being an issue, I am surprised that it was not been addressed in a recall and or this fixed? Like I said I'm on my second time with this.

productDescription: Wet 2 Straight, flat iron
productType: Hair Curlers, Curling Irons, Clips & Hairpins (1682)
incidentDescription: The consumer says that her grandaughter crawled into the bathroom.  the flat iron was plugged into the outlet.  The child pulled the cord, and the cord detached from the iron.  Her granddaughter received an electrical burn.  The consumer says that if a 9 month old 13 pound child can detach the cord from the iron than there is a serious problem with the iron.  The consumer says that the child may need surgery to prevent the area between the thumb and the first finger in order to prevent the skin area between those two fingers from fusing together as it heals.

productDescription:
Blue Ember propane grill model FGQ65079-U403
Serial # 08K005813
4 burner propane gill with electric ignition
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
In June 2010 my one year old Blue Ember grill (model FGQ65079-U403, serial # 08K005813) caught fire at the site of the propane tank during standard use. The household member using the grill at the time sustained minor burns to his legs, but was able to extinguish the fire prior to a major explosion or injury. After some research, it was made aware that recalls had taken place on a number of Blue Ember grill models, but the official recall did not include my grill. Though not included, my experience seems similar to those of consumers whose grill models had been recalled.

It has taken me one calender year to obtain assistance in correcting this issue directly from Blue Ember (Fiesta Grills). I have been told that, although my grill sustained extensive damage, the company will only replace parts, which I consider unacceptable due to continued safety concerns with the company.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: Bakers and Chefs Gas Grill. Appears to be a model called "Main Event". Has eight burners and two propane tanks (one tank for each bank of four). Silver in color. Date of production unknown, but believed to be made in the past five years or so.
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
I was in charge of grilling hamburgers at my church this evening. The grill the church had set up was a "Bakers & Chefs" model with eight (8) burners and two (2) propane tanks. Upon further investigation, it appears this model is called "Main Event" and is produced by a parent company called Grand Hall.

I followed the instructions on the grill to start it up. I have worked with many grills, both charcoal and gas, and had no difficulty getting the burners to ignite. Once I had waited for the grill to warm up, I placed the burgers on the grill. As they were cooking, huge flames jumped up through the grill grates. Many were over a foot tall. I was afraid to go in and flip or remove my burgers for fear of being burned. They seemed to occur regardless of where the dial was set--I had it set to "low" the entire time on one burner and this happened (the same thing happened when "high" was selected).

Eventually, I caught a break and managed to flip one of the burgers. When it was set down on the griddle, the huge flames began again. Most of them occurred right around the burger, but others jumped up in seemingly random locations.

I had to turn all the burners off and wait for the grill to cool down to safely remove my burgers, which were inedible.

While I understand flames are an inevitable part of any grilling experience, the amount and intensity of flames even on the lowest heat setting were unacceptable to me. I have been grilling since I was in my early teens and this is the first time I've ever been scared to place a tool on the grilling surface in fear of burning my arm or hand.

incidentDescription: I received notice from HP that some batteries from my Compaq Presario 700 laptop computer series were recalled. incidentDescription: 11 year old daughter suffered a laceration on her right ankle from the rear bolt on the housing cover for the chain.  Four stiches were required to suture the area.  The bolt is not covered in plastic or some other protective wrap.

productDescription: Cusinart DCC 1200 Coffee maker
incidentDescription: Made coffee as usual with the Cuisinart DCC-1200 coffee maker.  After about an hour of being on heard a popping/boiling sound and smelled fire.  The coffee maker had turned itself off as usual. I pulled the plug and ran it outside.  Coffee maker was clearly smoking from the warming plate.  Cuisinart gave no explanation but said they will replace with a new unit and provide a free UPS label for return.  Thank goodness I was there to hear/smell the coffee maker and get it outside before there was any damage.

productDescription: 4 burner propane grill, 2 sided, Perfect Flame model 3615
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
The propane tank connector started leaking very badly from where the fitting for the propane tank goes into the hose.  There is no signs of wear or abuse on the hose, as it is located under the grill and is only touched when changing out propane tanks.  This will be my 3rd propane tank on said grill and has just been replaced.  Luckily I noticed the leak and had not started the grill.  I saw the recalls on this grill when looking for replacement parts and wanted to notify you of this problem.  I have an LX date for the grill so it is not in the other recalls.

The connector was on properly, and was also double checked.  The leak was not where the tank connects, but behind the tank connection.

productDescription: The product is a Whirlpool/Gold Dehumidifier that is on wheels free standing about 25 inches tall and 13 inches wide.
incidentDescription: I have a Whirlpool Dehumidifier (Model # ADSOUSSl Serial # QU0419817) that I purchased about 4 years ago. On July 9th 2011 I returned home and noticed an odor coming from the workroom in the basement of my home. I found the Whirlpool Dehumidifier with smoke coming from the vents and a humming sound coming from the unit.  I disconnected the unit and carried it outside and smoke continued coming from the unit for several minutes, and the unit was extremely hot, and it is my opinion that if I had not returned when I did the unit would have erupted  into flames and I would have returned to a fire scene.

productDescription: 4 slice toaster
incidentDescription: For several years, I have owned and used a Corningware Electrics 4-slice Toaster.  Yesterday, it malfunctioned very badly, failing to pop up the toast until it was a smoking charred black mess that completely filled my house with heavy smoke.  My son noticed that it was beginning to fail several days ago, but didn't inform me of the situation. Had I not noticed, unplugged the toaster and put the toast in the sink with water, I'm certain that it would have continued to burn until the unit and subsequently my house would have caught fire.  The model number is TS-4318, the UL listing is E106413, Listed, 99N3.  It was purchased some time ago at the Boston Store in Milwaukee, Wisconsin for $50.00. However,  I am not looking for financial reimbursement.  I simply want you to be aware of this very grave potential fire hazard.  If you would like to examine the toaster, I will hold onto it for a bit, but either way, I would like to hear back from you that you have received this message.  I will also copy Better Homes with this email.  Thank you, [REDACTED]

incidentDescription: Dehumidifier malfunctioned causing smoke conditions inside the structure.

incidentDescription: I was blow drying my hair when sparks started shooting from the hair dryer.  If I had not been paying attention, my hair could easily have caught fire and caused serious bodily injury.

productDescription: Cellboost eIP2 Disposable Battery/Charger for "iPod", white plastic case, approximately 2" x 2".  Sealed inside case are 8 small batteries.
incidentDescription:
I purchased a Cellboost eIP2 disposable battery/charger for my iPod last year.  I opened the package, but had not used the device, and it was sitting on a wooden bookshelf in my study.  It was never exposed to heat or direct sunlight. On or about 20 July of this year, my wife and I heard what sounded like a gunshot inside our house, but when I checked the house from top to bottom, I found no broken windows or fallen objects.  Two days later I discovered the cause of the noise.  When I was in my study I noticed that the eIP2 sitting on a bookshelf had split open, and one of the 8 batteries inside had ruptured, leaving a black, powdery substance on the shelf.  No damage was done other than to the device itself, but under other circumstances and conditions there might have been propery damage or personal injury.  I called the telephone number on the package the eIP2 had come in, but received no answer on either the company's toll free or local numbers.  Failing to reach a company representative, I sent an email, but 6 days later I have received no response.  Since one of the batteries in the device had exploded, I was concerned that one or more of the other 7 batteries might do so as well, so I called our county fire marshall's office to seek guidance on how best to dispose of the device.  The person I talked with wasn't sure, but agreed that the device might pose a danger.  I finally was able to drop it off at a facility that accepted rechargeable batteries after explaining what had happened.  Here is info on the company that distributes the eIP2 and other Cellboost products:  

Compact Power Systems
[REDACTED] 
General Inquiries:
[REDACTED]

productDescription: Birdbrain Outdoor Fire Pot
incidentDescription: I used a Birdbrain Ceramic Firepot. Followed instructions on filling and lighting. It burned for about 10 minutes, then there was a loud pop. The ceramic pot broke, dumping the citronella fuel supplied with the pot. It spilled on the table, chair, outdoor carpet, and my friend's skirt. I was able to put out the flames quickly, but this could have been a serious accident including catastrophic fire and personal injury.

productDescription: Black & Decker TRO480BS Toast-R-Oven
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
manufacturer: Applica Consumer Products, Inc. - NOTIFY SPECTRUM BRANDS
incidentDescription: This report is on the Black & Decker TRO480BS Toast-R-Oven. This is the toaster you want if you want to burn down your house. I got this oven as a present 7 months ago and when it works right, it's a nifty little appliance.  It has this little quirk with the timer, however, where it doesn't always turn off when it's supposed to. There is a "Stay On" setting that is right next to the Off setting, and the catch between the 2 settings doesn't always engage.  We learned this early on with a mess of blackened toast, and so I am always super careful in setting the timer.  This morning I was making toast and the phone rang so I turned the toaster to off and walked away to answer the phone. I came back to find flames shooting out of the toaster and charring the underside of the cabinet above, even though all the settings on the toaster indicated that it was off.  It’s a very poorly engineered design. There should be 2 very separate knobs, one to engage for toasting – with a finite timer – and one to engage the “stay on” feature.

productDescription: Ezip 400 electric scooter
incidentDescription: My 13 yr old son was riding his Ezip 400 electric scooter when the throttle stuck in the fast position. The only way to stop the scooter was to shut off the master power. The way the scooter is designed to work is if you let go of the throttle the motor will disengage and the scooter will slow to a stop. I contacted the company Currie Industries and their primary concern was had my son dropped or crashed his scooter previously. Once I told them that he had not they agreed to ship me the necessary parts to fix the scooter but were going to charge me shipping and handling on the parts. The scooter was still within the 90 day warranty. I refused the new parts and the shipping and handling and returned the scooter to Walmart where I purchased it.

incidentDescription: I have a Hoover vacuum that I was using in my living room and the cord stretched slightly and I noticed a flash from the cord rewind chamber and the vacuum turned off and would not operate from that point. I checked on line for some information and found out that there was a recall on this vacuum (Hoover model #UH70210; MFG Code K09A). Through Hoover online I located my nearest repair location (Sears in Kingston, MA), where it was taken for repairs.
