productDescription: small, white, portable heater.  120V - 60 Hz - 1500 W
incidentDescription:
Good morning.  I am writing to express my concern with my DeLonghi Safe Heat Model 132 heater (Serial #13009).  I use this heater at work in my office, and during my vacation a safety inspection was conducted, which resulted in an email telling me that my heater was tipped over and it did not automatically shut off; therefore, the heater failed the safety test and has to be removed.     

The sticker directly adhered to the front of the heater specifically states:
         PTC Ceramic Thermal Cutoff: No need to worry about overheating.  Even when 
         the unit is accidently tipped over or covered by a curtain or blanket.  The PTC 
         ceramic thermal cutoff automatically shuts the unit off for complete peace of mind.

On the bottom of the heater it specifically states:  Q.C. PASSED

I have been in [email] contact with the manufacturer since July 6, 2011, and they not answered my questions on why the heater's automtic shutoff only works when the heater is tipped on its backside, and not when it is tipped on its front side.  They have also not explained why the marketing of the automatic shut off does not clearly inform the consumer that it only works when the heater is tipped on its back, and not when it is tipped on its front, as it seems to me that there would be a safety concern if the heater was tipped over in either position.

productDescription: Fire Pot also known as a napa candle
incidentDescription:
After noticing the gel from the fire pot was out he refilled it with the alcohol gel. Then a flame entered the bottle and caused it to explode and flew in every direction. The fire pot (also known as a Napa candle) was near a deck where it burned a hole threw a cushion of the patio furniture and umbrella, and his American flag.  The finish on the deck was destroyed (the location near where the where the fire pot was set). 

 It got into one person’s eyes (but was not on fire) and the victim receive severed burns to the abdomen, thighs and right hand. He immediately fell to the ground and rolled to put the fire out but when that did not help he then jumped into his Coi pond and that extinguished the flames. He was then taken to the University of North Carolina were he was kept in the Burn Unit for two days. He was diagnosed with having Superficial second degree burns. He had various skin grafts and was treated for the burns. 

The retailer was contacted on 5/24/2011 or 5/25/2011 to inform him of his injuries associated with the product. He discarded of the product and has not contacted the firm.  The product is a fancy styled vase and the center is a stainless still little tub and that is what you pour the gel into.  It is manufactured and sold by Napa Home and Garden Inc.

He indicated that it is a great product but the concerns with it are if you refill the gel while the fire pot is still hot it could pose as a potential fire hazard. So it’s safe to refill the gel when the fire pot in cool and not in use.

productDescription: A box fan
incidentDescription:
The fan was placed in the master bedroom window seal powered in the on position estimating about 4-5 hours. After arriving home they noticed that the fan had fell out of the window on to the floor and had burned itself up and melted the carpet. The bedroom is full of soot.

The Fire Department was contacted and they stated that they believed that the fan fell out of the window and fell onto the carpet and overheated and burned up. The day of the incident the weather was very windy which is believed to have caused the fan to fall out of the window. The master bedroom also experienced heavy smoke damage. 

A thermal imaging camera was used to determine if there was any fire/smoke in the home He contacted the insurance company, AAA Insurance, on 6/5/2011 took a report, pictures and also took the fan. The name of the representative was [REDACTED] and she indicated that the bedroom was considered to be a total loss. 

The only parts of the fan that remain are a chunk of motor cord and box portion of the fan is left.  While speaking with a next door neighbor he learned of the recent recall (see Release 11-183) but due to the fire he is unable to locate any model number that was located on the unit.He stated that he does not think he will contact the firm.

incidentDescription: Consumer wanted to report that her Kenmore gas grill caught flames yesterday while it was being operated outside on her deck. The product is solely a grill. The consumer called the retailer today and spoke with [REDACTED] at the number posted on the grill and was transferred to another woman who offered to send out a technician at the consumer's expense. However, the glass bowl breaks if foreign object falls into it while in operation, and its accessory attachment screw is prone to loosening and falling into the bowl. productDescription: OUTDOOR PROPANE GRILL
productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
I have recently bought a Chargriller outdoor BBQ grill and have noticed the unpainted interior shell is coated to prevent corrosion. I reviewed the manual and online data to verify what the coating is. It is stated by Chargriller that the coating is "vegetable based." That is the only detail available. I contacted Chargriller by email and inquired about the coating. They simply restated it was "vegetable based."

The reason I contacted Chargriller, and now sp.gov, is that I feel this coating MAY NOT  be vegetable based and may possibly be a toxic corrosion inhibiter instead. 2 reasons lead me to believe this:

1. While serving in the Navy, I worked on jet aircraft where we used toxic petroleum-based anti-corrosion coatings on almost all engine parts, fittings, and compartments. MSDS sheets I reviewed at the time stated the coatings were indeed quite toxic if ingested. The coating on the Chargriller has the exact same appearance, consistancy, and odor as the anti-corrosin coating I worked with in the Navy.

2. While working on my motorcycle, I recently used a rust-preventative spray made by [REDACTED]. This spray, which is also nasty if inhaled, ingested, or even has prolonged skin exposure, also has the same color, consistancy, and odor as the previously mentioned toxic anti-corrosion coatings as I used in the navy.

You cannot mistake the odor that these anti-corrosion coating give off. It's an acrid, skunk-like strong odor that gives you a headache very quickly. I have recontacted Chargriller for MSDS information on the coating they are using and I have not been contacted back. If Chargriller is, indeed, using a toxic coating, they are seriously endangering the health of consumers who use their grills. The basic research I have done on my own has shown that the compounds contained in anti-corrosion coatings can cause neurological damage, lung damage, and cancer in minute quantities. I would like to request that Chargriller be made to divulge the detailed nature of their grill coating and disclose any MSDS if available.

Thank you for your time
[REDACTED]

incidentDescription:
The other evening, I fired up the Weber Gas Grill and got it warmed up.  I turned the heat down once I had preheated it to burn off the crusty things.  I put on an ear of corn wrapped in foil to reheat it, and went inside.  Looking out the kitchen window as I was preparing to return with some other food stuffs, I notices some flames at the end of the grill where the propane tank is and the burner controls are located.  I thought perhaps there was some greasy stuff still on the grill still flaring up.

As I got closer, things did not look right.  I looked up  under the burner control panel and discovered that the all three burner controls were in flames.  They have plastic assemblies that were burning and dripping hot plastic.  Somewhat foolishly, I tried to dodge the dripping flaming hot plastic to shut off the propane tank.  I did get some flesh burned off a finger from the molten plastic in my pursuit.  I eventually got the cylinder off, and slowly the burner controls died down and I blew them out.  The controls below are a total loss and the burner knobs are trashed from melting by the heat below.

So from one perspective, no harm (less one burn), no foul as everything was contained.  However having a devious mind, the thought occurred to me that many folks have units like this sitting on a wooden deck.  The dripping plastic is like flaming tar balls and is burning all the way to the ground.  The splat will continue to burn on the surface it hits.  Potentially things could get real ugly.  We had stone and sand below our unit, so the supplemental fuel source was not a big deal.

productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
I have a Thermos bbq grill that has aluminum legs and sits in the floor or a table (about 2 feet high).  It has a red body about 15 inches square with fake coals, a gas burner and rack, and a red lid.  The propane bottle (about the size of a quart jar) screws onto the round control that has a knob that springs up (for off) and down (for on) and gives Off/ignition position/hi/med/low   settings.  
I hooked up the bbq and lit the burner with a long match.  A few minutes later, the flame was coming from the outside connection where the knob was.  It appeared to be coming from the narrow tube where the (regulator?) slid into the tube going to the bbq.    I blew out the flame and managed to turn the gas off.  It scared me quite a bit.

I did not use the bbq for a few years until yesterday (7/2/2011), I decided to try the bbq again, but a friend put a rubber o-ring between the parts to block the escaping gas.    I lit the bbq and 10 minutes later put the steaks on.  A few minutes later, I went to turn the steaks and found the bbq in flames right near the gas bottle again.  It was so bad the fire burned right through the plastic handle on the lid.  I could not turn the gas off to where the switch popped up to the off position, but managed to turn it to where the flame was out (using long handled bbq tongs).  Every few minutes it would flare up, but my friend was using my fire extinguisher on it and this would extinguish the flame for a few minutes,  We managed to unscrew the gas bottle from the bbq with oven mits, but the controls to the bbq - like the handle- were melted or burned beyond use.

A very strange thing was discovered.  My friend pulled the regulator? off the bbq after the bottle was unscrewed from it.  He poked into the tube where the gas flows into the bbq grill and was pulling strawlike material out (excelsior).  How this got there is quite a mystery, but obviously was there when the unit was purchased.  The excelsior was blocking the flow of gas somewhat, and the gas was escaping  (and flaming) through two small holes in the tube near the regulator.   I kept the excelsior and regulator and bbq for inspection if necessary.

I am trying to locate any other instances of a THERMOS bbq doing this and whether there is a recall or refund for the product.  (The steaks were cooked okay!)
Thank you.

productDescription: Krups electric coffee maker
incidentDescription:
This letter and report are to urge you to issue a safety recall for Krups electric coffee  maker, model KT 4065 which I believe is a newly designed product. You can see from the receipt, I purchased this coffee-maker five months ago; I began using it approximately four months ago, Early in use, the coffeemaker spilled hot fluid all over our kitchen counter on two occaSions, but I dismissed it Recently, it has it done this on a fairly regular basis, Enclosed is the actual coffee maker so you may test and verify the safety design defect in this product. Also enclosed is my receipt and the product booklet with warranty. Although this item is still under warranty, the terms indicate that Krups would repair or replace the item. Since this item is a huge safety hazard, I am not interested in another one of these.

Defective design, This coffee maker overflows the carafe spilling scalding hot fluid onto the counter or table. For families with small children who reach onto the counter, this is particularly dangerous. From my inspection, it appears that either the plastic lid to the carafe or the cone filter chamber is the culprit. The lid has a small trap door and very small entry holes for the water. I am a foodie and purchase high end appliances, cutlery, kitchen devices and am well versed in how to use them. The cause of the chronic overflow problem is definitely not:

(1 ) Lack of cleanliness. There was no excessive debris or calcification because we clean our coffee makers with white vinegar every 2 months. When this second spillover happened, I performed an extra deep vinegar soak and clean of all parts to make sure this would not happen again. It functioned fine for two mornings, then three days later the overflow occurred again. 

(2) The grind or type of coffee. We grind our coffee by hand where it is not too course, not too fine as we have for the past 4 years. We primarily use [REDACTED] Decaf or Breakfast blend. This was the coffee in use during the overflow incidents.

(3) The type of filter. We use the same filters we have always used. Two previous coffeemakers over the years have used the same cone type which we get at the grocery store nearby. I enclosed a few of those so that you can see for yourself
should you decide to test this. 

(4) The centering of the carafe. I have made 100% certain the carafe is centered directly under the cone (in fa~ there is a crevice that guides the carafe to keep it centered) and that the lid is correctly tightened on top with the thumb tab aligned
correctly.

(5) The water level. I have made 100% certain that I only fill the coffee maker up to the 10 cup level.

productDescription: 18 volts cordless electric drill
incidentDescription:
The consumer was using the drill for approximately 3 - 5 minutes to drill a hole in a log, when the drill exploded.  The consumer stated that he had been using the drill off and on that morning and the day before.  When the battery would wear down, the consumer recharged it and started using it again.

The consumer was drilling hole, when the drill exploded in his right hand.  The consumer was using both hands, but the right hand sustained more damage than his left hand.  The casing of the battery blew apart.  The battery is located underneath one's hands, when they are holding the drill.  The battery blew apart into several small pieces.  The consumer equated the incident to an explosive going off.  The consumer's mother drove him to the nearest emergency room (Pocono Medical Center).

X-rays were taken on the consumer's right hand, his wound was cleaned and approximately 3 to 5 sutures were applied his right hand.  The consumer was released the same day.  The consumer had follow-up care, which lasted approximately 2 months.

To this day, the consumer still experiences pain, he has scars and he stated that there is still some swelling to his right hand.


The week after the incident, the consumer contacted the manufacturer and explained the incident to a representative.  Their rep. asked the consumer about his injuries and asked him what amount he would considered as a claim for his pain and suffering.  The consumer said that he did not know initially, but he asked the company's rep. for a figure.  Their rep. did not provide him with a number, but the consumer said that he gave them a figure of $20,000.00.  The manufacturer has never offered the consumer any compensation for this incident. 

The consumer noted that the battery came with the drill and that the battery was made in China.  This product came with 1 battery and it was included in the packaging at the time of purchase.

NOTE:  The consumer said that his battery appears to be identical to the one mentioned in Release # 09-298.

incidentDescription: I built a new home which included a Heatliator built in natural gas fireplace. The fireplace features include a backup battery lighting system that lights the burner and provides heat in the event of a commercial power outage. The backup system works by using two D Alkaline disposable batteries in a battery pack under the firebox. I installed two backup batteries in the fireplace. After the first use, the batteries ruptured due to the heat and the fan unit which was running pulled the fumes from the two D Alkaline batteries into the room. I removed the cover of the fireplace to find a pool of acid in and under the battery pack and firebox floor. I called the builder who sent out a repair person who just removed the two batteries and left the acid which had now spread across the floor of the fireplace and had started reacting with the metal floor of the fireplace unit. The repair person advised the batteries should only be used in a power outage due to the heat causing them rupture under normal use. I asked why there is no sticker or label stating the batteries are only for emergency use and the repair person stated there should be as this is a common issue. I have contacted the manufacturer who sent another repair company out to replace the battery box and wiring that was damaged by the acid, and spray painted over the damaged metal floor of the firebox. During that visit I was told I should only use the battery pack during an electrical outage because the heat will damage the batteries installed. I am concerned that Heatilator is not labeling their battery backup product as emergency use only and therefore exposing consumers to fumes produced by ruptured batteries in the fireplaces they manufacture.

productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription:
This is a copy of an email sent to Weber regarding a fire hazzard with a Genesis grill.
FIRE HAZZARD

Weber Genesis Gas Grill
s/n DI1656236
purchase date 06/29/07

To Whom It May Concern,

At least early last year I had noticed a large burn mark on the left side frame panel and although I was not happy about the appearance I thought it came about because of the heat from the grill.
When I started to use the grill this year, flames started to come up outside the grill between the left side of the grill box and outside burner of the left side of the grill and therefore I shut it down immediately.
Upon inspection, I found two holes in the left side of the grill box and contacted your customer service department.  After providing a description of the problem they asked me to inspect the burner tubes and the crossover pipe.
The conclusion made was that there was a defect in the weld holding the middle tube causing it to come loose and burn a hole in the side of the grill.
The offer was made to replace the parts which I appreciate, but taking the entire grill apart is not a job for a layman.  
In addition, I feel that this is a dangerous condition precipitated by a poor design or weld which could have resulted in bodily injury.  
I was told that there was not a recall on this product which I will investigate further, and if there is not, I will try to initiate one.  I find it difficult to believe that this was a fluke and other consumers could be exposed to possible injury.
This is not my first Weber Grill and my other grill is at least twice the age and is still in very good condition.  I feel that offering parts to correct a dangerous situation and not offering the labor or a replacement is just a token gesture at best.
I have forwarded you the pictures you requested and will also forward the contents of this email to the CSPS.

On March 6, 2007, the US Consumer Product Safety Commission released a memo, Release #07-122, regarding a recall  on Weber Gas Grills and a Fire Hazard on a number of grills including the one which I own, model Genesis S-320 3780001.
Perhaps this condition should also be reviewed as well.

productDescription:
Kenmore Elite Trio Bottom Freezer Refrigerator
Model 795.7754*
25 cubic ft, bisque color
Upper refrigerator with french style doors
Bottom freezer drawer
Fresh water dispenser in refrigerator door
Automatic ice maker in freezer but no door dispenser
incidentDescription:
We own a Kenmore Elite Trio Bottom Freezer Refrigerator - Model 795.7754*
We have owned it just short of three years.  Over the weekend we opened the upper french-style doors and found both refrigerator lights out and smelled an odor of hot electrical burning.  We removed the light bulb cover and attempted to remove the bulbs.  They were too hot to touch.  After they cooled down, we removed the bulbs and observed the compartment that houses the light bulbs.  It is beginning to discolor.  Furthermore the glass bulbs were darkening and discoloring - but the filaments were still in tact.  After cooling, we placed the bulbs back in the sockets to see if they would once again illuminate.  They did but after several minutes, they became very hot again and again we smelled the odor of electrical burning.  We were able to determine that at least one of the two switches used to determine if the refrigerator doors are open or shut has gone bad - causing the scenario where the refrigerator senses that the door is open and thus keeps the light bulbs illuminated.  We have since removed the bulbs to open the circuit and prevent any fire hazard to our home.  We did an online search and found many other consumers who have experienced this problem.  Today we contacted Sears service center and were told that they knew nothing about the defect in their product.  Their only two solutions were to either purchase a one-year service agreement/warranty for a technician to make a service call and repair the refrigerator or schedule a service appointment without the agreement and pay for time and material.  Upon expressing our concern that this was a defect in their product and that it posed a fire hazard to our home and our family, we were simply told that they could do nothing about it.  The customer service representative couldn't understand why we didn't want to purchase a service agreement to remedy their defective product.  We are disappointed in Sears approach to resolving this issue and want to make others aware of the potential fire hazard they have in their homes.

This week we moved the dehumidifier away from the drain and disconnected the hose so it would drain into the collection bucket. We noticed that we were not getting any water in the bucket. Looked at the connections on top of the compressor, and you could see that it had been really hot under the cap. The current protection device had blown apart. The insulated crimp on connectors had become hot and the insulation had cracked. Other rubber grommets got brittle and cracked. There was a varnish substance covering everything under the cap. There were marks where the hot wires touched other things. Looked up this dehumidifier online and noticed a recall for it.

Model #: GE AHM40LKG1
Serial #: AM169722

productDescription: Shark (Euro-Pro Holdings LLC) Steam Mop Model S3501
incidentDescription:
We purchased a Shark Steam Mop (marketed by Euro-Pro Holdings LLC) in maybe May 2010.  This is a household device to mop floors with hot steam.  There is a steam generating component in the midsection of the handle (and a water tank) and the steam is channeled to a flexible mop head that is covered by a cloth pocket.

There is a one year warranty.

The mop stopped providing steam maybe last time my wife used it.  She didn't mention that to me before I used it today.  When I used it, I plugged it in to turn it on and waited for it to start producing steam.  You can lift and depress the upper handle to initiate the further production of steam (sometimes when there is low water or other conditions, steam production can be inhibited so patience is required).  I did this intermittently, not aggressively, for maybe a minute or two.

The unit was quiet however, meaning it was not producing steam.

Then it exploded and shot steam all over the floor in maybe a three foot jet.  The mop head broke from the handle, although the break point was actually a release or latched joint, so the explosion itself did not damage the unit.  You could describe it as the mop head explosively detaching.  I was very surprised, and because of the heat, force, and pressure involved I was glad that I was not manipulating the mop head when it explosively detached because I easily could have been scalded.

After unplugging and inspecting the unit and looking for a clog in the steam channel, I repeated the procedure once again, but without purposefully generating steam (I did not manipulate the handle).   The mop head explosively detached again after a short time (30 seconds?).

I then let the unit cool and disassembled the steam channel, as I assumed it was clogged.  In fact, on inspection, I saw that the upper steam channel (which is in direct proximity to the steam production unit) was designed as being plastic.  Part of the plastic had bubbled up like Styrofoam, and part of it had collapsed and melted.  In other words, instead of using a material that was unlikely to melt for the very hot upper steam channel, the designer of the mop used cheap plastic that melted around the time the warranty expired, collapsed around the small steam channel, and caused the unit to explode (or the mop head to explosively detach) in normal use.

I called Euro-Pro/Shark to talk to them.  A rep said that the model probably was out of warranty (by maybe a month or two) and that warranty service was therefore unavailable.  When I told him that I planned to report this to the consumer protection authorities, he referred me to another number 1-866-694-6406 that he said would generate a callback within 34 hours, and made some reference to burns or personal injuries.  I told him that I was not interested in compensation for personal injury, because luckily I was not injured.

However, this unit is basically a ticking time bomb in my opinion and should be recalled.  The melting of the plastic steam channel is a very predictable mode of failure, and it is outrageous that the most predictable mode of failure will very predictably cause the mop head to explosively detach.

I took pictures of the melted plastic piece (which is very small),  which are attached.  The pictures were taken after the channel was disassembled into basically four parts (two of which were plastic and had melted).  There is another choke point in the steam channel, but it is metal and I assume that it is a valve of some sort.  A picture of that also is attached.  I am holding onto the steam mop in case you want it, but it is extremely hazardous in this condition and will not function as intended. It just explodes.

Please encourage Euro Pro to recall all of their units that have an upper steam channel composed of plastic, as it is unreasonably susceptible of melting and causing a resulting explosion.

incidentDescription:
I have a Kitchen Aid 14-Cup Coffee Maker (model# KCM222CU) that I started using on 2/3/11. This morning (6/22/11), my husband set the timer to turn on at 5:30 AM, and then I went to get coffee from the maker at 7:45 AM.  I noticed that the coffee was abnormally hot, and then noticed that the maker had an error message on the screen.  Following the manufacturer's instructions, I turned off the machine, and the error message disappeared.  About an hour later I heard the coffee maker make a noise, and realized that although the unit was off the heating element under the carafe was still heating (much, much hotter than normal). I unplugged the unit several times, but each time I would plug it back in it would immediately heat up again (the unit was turned off the entire time).  Apparently the unit had gotten so hot that it had burned the carafe a bit around the metal ring on the glass portion.  I really think that had I not noticed that the element was still heating that the carafe would have eventually caught fire.

I contacted Kitchen Aid, and they didn't seem surprised to hear about the problem.  I think that they are well aware of the fire danger of this unit but continue to sell it to consumers.  I found comments on Amazon.com of at least one other user who had the same issue that I did.

productDescription: Hamilton Beach 10-Cup Food Processor
incidentDescription:
I had purchased a Hamilton Beach Food Processor (10 cup, DPCI: 072-04-0943) from Target, because it claims that it can be used to grate cheese.  

The food processor has a large blade at the top of the processor that spins very rapidly, and above that there's a locking plastic lid that contains a feeding tube.  When you put food down the tube, it's supposed to be processed by the blade.  The food processor will not start unless the lid is locked into place.  There's maybe a half-inch or so gap between the blade and the lid.

When I used it to grate cheese, I put the large disk on the motor and locked the lid into place.  I started the food processor and proceeded to put a block of cheese into the tube.  After about two spins of the blade (I did get a tiny amount of grated cheese, so it wasn't immediately), the cheese I had put into the tube was sucked down extremely quickly between the blade and the lid, in that 1/2 inch gap.  The block of cheese was about 2 or 3 inches wide, which caused the lid's locking mechanism to crack and the lid to fly off, hitting me.  The cheese flew across the room.  The most alarming thing is that the blade did not stop spinning after the lid was ripped off.  

I was not injured at all during this, just extremely shocked.  However, with the sharp, metal blade spinning exposed, it's entirely possible that someone using this machine could be injured.  I almost caught one of my fingers on the spinning blade.  Grating cheese is an approved use of this machine.  

I called Hamilton Beach to let them know what had happened with their product, left a detailed message with my name and number, and did not hear back from them.  I returned the product to Target and got a full refund.

I finished drying my hair, switched the dryer off, left it plugged in and walked into the other room. Less than a minute later I heard the hair dryer come on by itself! Fortunately I was just in the next room and went back into the bathroom to find the dryer on, and smoking. I was able to yank the cord from the wall without injury. My concern is, if I was unable to hear this happen, a fire would have absolutely started. 

When I retrieved the dryer, it was very hot to the touch and the switch was indeed in the off position. I still have the unit, but have replaced it. I'm taking the time to report this partially because of the danger and partially because when I was at CVS buying a replacement I was shocked to see they carry NO other brands except Conair and they still sell this model in question.

productType: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use) (3248)
incidentDescription: I have a Char-Broil COMMERCIAL SERIES LP/PROPANE powered outdoor grill. I grilled beef (Hamburger) on the grill at 600º for approximately (24) twenty-four minutes. When I determined that the beef was cooked properly, I closed both of the knob type valves that are fixed on the front of the grill to the closed position,  I opened the bottom storage door to close off the LP/PROPANE valve. Successfully closing off the the ignition source of fuel to the grill and burners, I pulled the beef off of the grate and closed the Stainless looking lid to the closed position and at that point visually the fire was completely extinguished from a visual perspective as well as I could tell.  I walked away from the grill appliance, went inside for approximately (2-3) two or three minutes when I looked outside and the grill appliance was blowing off a mix of dark gray smoke pouring out of the entire upper end of the fire-box with the lid still closed.  I checked the valves a second time making sure that all fuel sources had been completely closed off and they are closed. At this point the grill is on fire.  My next step was to contain the fire as effectively as possible, as I noticed that the thin perforated grate and the upper grill insert that sits inside of the thin perforated grate had caught on fire, I also noticed that the fire was burning below the thin perforated grate as well as burning on the top of the cooking surface.  I successfully extinguished the fire with wet kitchen towels, I used up (4) four towels to put the fire out.  The next day I uncovered the grill to take a look inside. What I found was that the run-off (fat) from the beef as it cooked had built up and baked itself to the thin perforated grate and the insert.  It appears visually like charcoal build up on the cooking surface of this type of grill cooking surface.  The cleaning history on this appliance is it gets the thin perforated grates and inserts pulled out every third time I cook on the grill. In total there are (4) pieces that get cleaned on the cooking surface.  This type of cooking surface gets a visual build up on the grate after (2-3) two or three uses.  I have used this appliance for about (13) months now and this is the first time that the entire firebox and grate had caught on fire after closing off all the fuel sources.  I also notice that on the top of the grate/cooking surface the the words PATENT PENDING are visible.  The good news is that that fire is out and we did not need the Snorkle truck. It was an incident that had serious potential to cause injuries and damages.
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: Cuisinart DCC-755bk coffeemaker, black, w/10-cup insulated metal carafe
incidentDescription:
My household possessed a Cuisinart DCC-755 coffeemaker.  Approximately a week ago, it began not wanting to turn on, or would run and turn off.  It gave up entirely today.  Upon opening it (removing 4 readily available screws on bottom that releases a base not attached to any function-related components), I was met with a burning smell and a fairly thick coat of white powder strewn about the inside of the unit.  The origin of the white powder is unclear, but it may be coming from a wire near the heating element for under the carafe.  Looking at one of the circuit boards, I also discovered scorch marks across an area of the board containing two large resistors and one small one.  Photographs were taken, but the webpage dialog for submitting them does not seem to be functionig properly on your site.

Investigating this on the web, I discovered that this failure seems to be the exact same syndrome (abrupt failure, burning, powder)  from others who have purchased this exact (and perhaps closely related) unit, some of whom had more dramatic burning, melted plastic, smoke, and the like.  Looking at the dates, it appears that the timing on many is similar as well, indicating that this may be an ongoing problem.  Thus, while we were relatively lucky with our unit, we seem to have dodged a bullet.  More importantly, as this was likely a popular unit due to being sold at Costo, it may represent an acute and ongoing concern for others, some of whom may be more unlucky than we were, perhaps much more.

Website of particular relevance to this:
http://www.consumeraffairs.com/homeowners/cuisinart.html

productDescription: Eureka Model 4870 upright vacuum cleaner, teal blue
incidentDescription: Was performing routing maintenance (belt replacment) on my Eureka 4870K vacuum s/n UU110827045860. Noticed power switch was not always working (stuck on or off). I removed the housing and discovered the crimp lugs on the power switch showed evidence of overheating (blackened, melting). Further the insulation on the wiring was melted back. Noted the plastic housing was sligtly melted inside in the vicinity of the switch. Also the exposed copper wire was oxidized. Replaced one crimp lug.  This is a safety defect. Either manufacturing (crimp not applied correctly, oxidation on wire prior to crimping) or a design defect (incorrectly sized wire, incorrect crimp lug). Mfr of crimp lug is TYCO, AMP p/n 2-520129-2, which is designed for 18-22 ga wire. productDescription: Black & Decker Spacemaker Oven model TROS 1000.
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
manufacturer: Applica Consumer Products, Inc. - NOTIFY SPECTRUM BRANDS
incidentDescription:
I purchased an under-the-counter Black and Decker toaster oven to replace the one I already had on May 30, 2010. It is model TROS1000. I was skeptical about buying it, in that there were quite a few reviews on amazon.com saying that people had trouble with the mounting system, and many said that the oven kept falling off the cabinet and they sent the oven back. But since some hadn't had that problem, and I liked my previous Black & Decker toaster oven, I decided to try it out. Well, I DID have problems with the mount and it DID fall down. There are two flimsy clips on the front of the mount to keep it in place. So I sent it back to Amazon.com and they sent me a replacement. I had the same problem with the second one, but was finally able to bend the clips so that the unit stayed in place. However, after some time, it began falling again. 

This is really quite dangerous because if the oven is hot, it can burn you or fall on something that's underneath it and possibly start a fire. 

So I contacted B&D via email and went back and forth with them on it. They ended up sending me a replacement oven, a $20 cheaper model (with no electronic controls) stating that they could substitute it out based on their warranty. So I asked for it to be escalated to management. They have finally said that they will refund my money, but frankly, I'm really concerned that they don't seem to care that people are having safety issues with this oven. 

On amazon.com alone, out of 301 customer reviews, 155 are 3 stars or less (out of 5 stars maximum), with many people talking about problems with the mount. This model has an identical mounting system to model TROS1500. 63 fall in the 1 star category.

Because it is an item that can get very hot, I feel that  even when the clips are working properly, the chance of bumping the unit and it falling are great. This is NOT the same mounting system I had on my previous B&D oven. 

I am going to return this and get my money back, but I hope you look into this matter. I hope a terrible accident doesn't have to happen before you make them fix this problem.

productDescription: KitchenAid 12" countertop toaster-oven-broiler
productType: Electric Counter-top Ovens, Broilers or Toaster Ovens (216)
incidentDescription:
On Sunday, May 22, 2011 I bought a KitchenAid 12" countertop toaster-oven from Target in Peoria, IL.  Got it home, set it up, plugged it in and set it for 350 degree Bake.  Less than 4 minutes later, I noticed a strong burning smell.  When I looked through the window into the oven I saw that it was ON FIRE!!!!  My husband came into the kitchen when I screamed.  He quickly unplugged the oven and took it outside of our home, setting it on a brick walkway.  It was several moments before the flames were extinguished.
We planned to return it to the store immediately, but it was too hot to safely put into our car.  30 minutes later it was still hot to the touch.  My husband noted that the hottest spot was not where we saw the initial flames.  The flames originated on the upper rear element, but the hot spot then appeared to be closer to the top front, as if the fire had spread.
The next day we returned it to the Target store where we bought it for a refund.  The only note made during the return was that the product was "defective".

The unit was faulty and replaced by the company with a new (?) unit on January 24, 2011.  It was replaced with the same model, serial number 01013.  The information the company has will be listed under Return Form 7004157393   Even though this was a serious problem which almost caused a home fire, the company goes by the original date of purchase, so even though this was a new (?) coffee maker sent to us by the company on January 24, 2011, and if they replace this one with a new one all warranties will expire in June of this year.
model: Cuisinart Classic 12-Cup Programmable Coffee maker DCC-1100
incidentDescription:
We purchased a Cuisinart Classic 12-Cup Programmable Coffee maker Model DCC-1100 Series in June of 2008.  This Coffee maker came with a three year guarantee. In January of 2011 the Coffee maker stopped working, so we contacted Cuisinart and paid $10.00 (plus an additional $14 for postage) to have the unit replaced. We received this new (?) unit on January 24, 2011. Last night, May 4, 2011, we ate dinner, then made a fresh pot of coffee. Within about a half an hour or so my granddaughter said she smelled something burning - it was mild for a few seconds, we immediately told her to go outside, and my husband and I looked for the source of the burning odor which was getting stronger by the seconds. As we got near the coffee maker it was clear that was the problem. My husband turned it off and immediately, unplugged the unit then took it out of the house. The coffee in the pot was close to boiling temperature. Thank God that we were in the next room and our granddaughter smelled it immediately or we would have had a serious fire. The strong burning odor in our home took over six hours to dissipate - with windows open, a ceiling fan and an exhaust fan running. I called the company and will deal with them as to replacing this with something safer, but I feel that the U S Consumer Product Safety Commission needs to look into this problem and possibly have the company recall the DCC-1100 Series Coffee makers. After talking with a company representative I looked online and was appalled at how many other consumers had the very same problem with this unit. (Actually consumers were complaining about some of Cuisinart’s other models as well - all with the heating plates - but the DCC-1100 was the one that had the most complaints) I am not satisfied at all dealing with their customer service supervisor and will pursue that, but the top priority is to have the USCPSC look into this and stop this company from just replacing units and not addressing the problem of this unsafe coffee maker. Peoples lives are in danger.  If we would not have been right there, if say my husband was sleeping and I took a shower, we would have had a fire! This happened last night at approximately 7:15 PM, and as I’m writing this at 12:21 PM today I still have a sore throat from the strong burning smell.  Please, please address this problem because the next family may not be as lucky as we were. Thank you so much for your time. We look forward to hearing from you.


At this time the company is willing to replace the item. They have told me they would be calling me back this evening, May 5, 2011, 7:00 PM.  I would, however, like to be assured that this safety issue is investigated.  This is a definite safety hazard that must be addressed. 

I am not alone in having the problems with this fire hazard. The following is a web site that lists many complaints about the very same problem with the Cuisinart Model DCC 1100.

http://www.consumeraffairs.com/homeowners/cuisinart.html
victimSeverity: Injury, No First Aid or Medical Attention Received

productDescription: Small standing humidifier, circular base, white, 8in wide by 1.5ft tall, removable upper water tank, blue LED lit window showing water level in tank
incidentDescription:
I often use a small humidifier made by Air Innovations, model number KS30U-06C. This week, as usual, I left the humidifier on while I was at work. I have never had any issue with this product in the past and I have in no way used this product in any way other than for its intended purpose. When I came home from work, my entire apartment was filled with a terrible smell, like something was burning. I immediately identified the source of the smell as coming from the Air Innovations humidifier. Under normal operation the unit senses when the water level in the tank is low and shuts off the internal components. On this day, the unit had run out of water but had failed to shut off its internal components allowing it to become extremely hot underneath the water tank where the operating components are located and to melt the plastic inside the unit. The unit's casing was also extremely hot to the touch. Under normal operation with a full tank of water the unit's LED indicator light is blue, showing that the the unit is in operation and has enough water. When the unit runs out of water, the unit shuts off and the LED indicator light turns red. On the day of this incident, the unit was out of water but the LED indicator light was still blue and the unit was still in operation, it failed to shut itself off.

If I hadn't intervened when I did, the unit would have melted straight through to the carpet and would have eventually started a fire. I contacted the company the next day and they, without any questions whatsoever, took down my address and offered to send me a similar model upon the return of the defective unit. I assume this action was made in an effort to avoid legal action.

I fear that this may happen to others and cause serious harm.
